For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Introduction This document describes the APIs provided by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace that are useable by applications. There are two basic types of API: Public cross-tenant APIs These are published by SAP in the SAP Business Accelerator Hub with documentation. They are mostly used by data contributors. In this guide, you can also find detailed instruction on how to use them. Generated tenant-local interfaces These are tenant-specific interfaces used by solution owners. They are also APIs, but differ based on the tenant. Rate Limiting This section describes the rate limit of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace APIs. Rate limiting restricts the number of incoming requests from callers to GTT APIs and within a specific time frame. It’s a protective measure that: prevents the GTT service from crashing due to the excessive load of requests ensures the availability and optimal performance of the GTT service for every client. We have defined the rate limits of following APIs according to tenant type: API Type of Tenant Limit IDOC interface: GTT_V2_EM_IDOC_Ingestion SOAP Message Interface: TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out Production The rate limit per tenant is 600 requests per minute. Test The rate limit per tenant is 600 requests per minute, 10000 requests per day. Write Service API: GTT_V2_HTTP_EVENT_INGESTION Production The rate limit per tenant is 600 per minute. Test The rate limit per tenant is 150 requests per minute, 10000 requests per day. Read Service API: GTT_V2_OData_Query Production The rate limit per tenant is 200 per minute.  Recommendation Before you start working through this document, ensure that you have the most recent version of this document available from the SAP Help Portal at: help.sap.com/gtt 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- API Type of Tenant Limit Test The rate limit per tenant is 60 requests per minute. When the rate limit is exceeded, you will receive an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response status code, and your requests are rejected. You can try executing requests again several minutes later. API Payload Limits To prevent APIs from being overloaded by the payload size, we have introduced API payload limits to regulate the API usage per message. The following tables list the size limit of different components in API payload: Public Tracking APIs API Request Body Response Body Provider API for Order Events Less than 40MB N/A Consumer API for Order Tracking Less than 40MB N/A Tenant-local Interfaces API Request Body without Attachment Attachment Response Body IDOC Service Less than 15MB Not supported N/A Read Service API No limit N/A The response body of read service API supports: 256 records at maximum for main entity in a query; 5000 records at maximum for each expanded entity of a single main entity; 20000 records at maximum for sum of each expanded entity for all main entity. Write Service API Less than 2MB Less than 10MB N/A SOAP Message Interface Less than 15MB Not supported N/A Here are examples of requests and responses for you to better understand the Read Service API size limit:  Note This will take effective as of December 13, 2025. There is no limit on API calls to fulfillment tracking apps, such as the "Track Shipments" app.  Example 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Public Cross-Tenant Tracking APIs This chapter describes how solution owners and data contributors exchange messages via the tracking APIs (or tracking interfaces) offered by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace provides two types of tracking APIs: Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT): enables solution owners to send a tracking request for an order to data contributors. Provider API for Order Events (GTT): enables data contributors (such as network partners or carriers) to post events for a tracked order. You can check out the above APIs on SAP Business Accelerator Hub . This chapter specifically describes the following two cases: how a solution owner sends a tracking request to a data contributor using the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT), and how a data contributor sends back the tracking data (that will later be converted to and processed as events in the GTT system) to a solution owner using the Provider API for Order Events (GTT). Sending Tracking Requests via Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT) As a solution owner, you can send a tracking request to a data contributor using the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT) . This chapter contains the following sections: Request Result Odata Response odata/v1/com.sap.gtt.app.gttft1.gttft1Service/Shipment? filter=filter1&$expand=processEvents, plannedEvents, freightUnitTPs 1 shipment was found and 5100 process events found on this shipment odata/v1/com.sap.gtt.app.gttft1.gttft1Service/Shipment? filter=filter1&$expand=processEvents, plannedEvents, freightUnitTPs 10 shipments were found and 2100 process events were found on each shipment. odata/v1/com.sap.gtt.app.gttft1.gttft1Service/Shipment? filter=filter1&$expand=processEvents, plannedEvents, freightUnitTPs,stops,trackingUnitTPs 1 shipment was found with 5000 process events, 5000 planned events, 5000 freightUnitTPs, 5000 stops, and 5000 trackingUnitTPs. Error: The response body Error: The response body Successful with data 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Prerequisites Configuration Testing the Integration Prerequisites To perform the tasks described in this chapter, you, as a solution owner, must have the following prerequisites: 1. You have onboarded on SAP Business Network for Logistics. 2. You have sent the invitation to the data contributor using the Invite Business Partners app. After the data contributor accepts the invitation using the Manage Invitations app, you two will be connected as business partners. 3. You have established a B2B connection to the external systems of the data contributor in the Configure Partner Connections app. 4. You have ensured that the data contributor has completed the Prerequisites and Configuration. Related Information Invite Business Partners Configure Partner Connections Configuration Context In the Manage Models app of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, the visibility provider integration information is already maintained for you in the GTT standard model “gttft1”. But if you want to integrate with your visibility provider in a user model or map user-defined fields in the standard model, do the following: Procedure 1. On the SAP Fiori launchpad, open the Manage Models app. 2. Select a model. 3. Go to the Visibility Provider Integration tab and open the edit mode. 4. Select a tracked process, and then turn on the Integration Switch. 5. In the Tracked Process / Events list on the left, you can see the tracked process event and event types. Use the value help to fill in the SAP Business Network for Logistics event type for actual events. 6. Select an event in the list, and then use the value help to fill in the fields or SAP Business Network for Logistics tracking fields on the right. 7. Save and deploy the model. On the SAP Fiori launchpad, open the Configure Partner Connections app, choose a partner connection that is active. If the data contributor you chose is a carrier, then the carrier must be onboarded onto SAP Business Network for Logistics. Note down its LBN ID with an “LBN#” prefix, such as "LBN#1234567". If the data contributor you chose is a network partner, then its corresponding carrier doesn’t have to be onboarded onto SAP Business Network for Logistics. Steps To test the integration in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, carry out the steps below: 1. On the SAP Fiori launchpad, open the Manage Models app. a. Select the GTT standard model “gttft1”. b. Switch to the Runtime view on the top right. c. In the Write Service tab, find the ShipmentEvent. Click the green section of this API endpoint. d. Click Try it out to test the API. e. In the Request Body text box, clear the existing request payload. Copy and paste the Sample Payload we provided and customize it to fit your needs. f. Execute the request. g. In the Responses section, it shows the response with the endpoint. 2. (Option 1) Back to the SAP Fiori launchpad, open the View Logs app. Open the Manage Message Logs app from the Quick Links section to check out the message processing status: a. Select the latest message on the list with the source type as External. The message contains the tracking request you just sent. You can drill down for more information. b. Back to the worklist page, refresh the page until you see a new message from your visibility provider. If the status is Success, then you have sent the tracking request successfully. 3. (Option 2) Back to the SAP Fiori launchpad, open the View Logs app. Open the Manage Integration Logs – Version 2.0 app from the Quick Links section to check out the message processing status. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Sending Events via Provider API for Order Events (GTT) As a data contributor, you can send back the tracking data (that will later be converted to and processed as events in the GTT system) to a solution owner using the Provider API for Order Events (GTT) . This chapter contains the following sections: Prerequisites and Configuration Monitoring Integration Prerequisites and Configuration Prerequisites To perform the tasks described in this chapter, you, as a data contributor, must have the following prerequisites: 1. You have onboarded on SAP Business Network for Logistics. 2. You have accepted the invitation from the solution owner using the Manage Invitations app. For more, see the application help of Manage Invitations. Configuration You need to use the System Connections app to complete the API implementations. For details, see the Connectivity section of Administration Guide for Logistics Providers. Related Information Provider API for Order Events (GTT) Monitoring Integration On the SAP Fiori launchpad, pen the View Logs app. Open the Manage Integration Logs – Version 2.0 app from the Quick Links section to view all integration logs for solution owner and data contributor transactions. For instructions on how to use the app, open the in-app help by selecting  within the Manage Integration Logs – Version 2.0 app. Generated Tenant-local Interfaces This chapter describes how to use the generated tenant-local interfaces in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. These APIs are provided for integration between the GTT system and other systems, which allows solution owners to access GTT services and perform CRUD (create, read, update, delete) operations on the GTT system via API requests. API Authentication You can use the following to authenticate your API calls to GTT service interfaces: HTTP Basic Authentication: You must create a technical user and maintain it in the System Connections app. For more, see Maintain Technical User in the System Connections App. 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 12 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Prerequisites To use these APIs, you must fulfill the following prerequisites: 1. Configure API authentication method. For more, see API Authentication. 2. Get the following information required in the API request URI: Server Address: You must provide the server address as the host in the request URI: For basic authentication, server address is the URL of your GTT Fiori Launchpad. It varies from hosted data centers. Do the following to get the server address: a. Go to your subaccount that has subscribed Global Track and Trace b. Click Services Instances and Subscriptions Global Track and Trace Go to Application c. After sign-in, you will see the URL. Model Information: Prepare the following model information needed in the resource path of the request URI: Model Namespace: It’s in the format of “com.<tenant name>.gtt.app.<model name>”. You can find the entire model namespace on the top of your target Model Details page. Write Service Name: It’s in the format of “<model name>WriteService”. Read Service Name: It’s in the format of “<model name>Service”. Model Name: You can find it on the target model card. After you finish the above tasks, you are ready to send API requests. In the sections followed, you can find examples of API request and response pair specific to different interface services. IDOC Service  Example Here are example server addresses specific to data centers for basic authentication: EU10: https:// <subdomain>.gtt.logistics.eu10.business-network.cloud.sap US20: https:// <subdomain>.gtt.logistics.us20.business-network.cloud.sap SA30: https:// <subdomain>.gtt.logistics.sa30.business-network.cloud.sap You must leave out “https://” when filing the information to an API request to avoid duplication.  Example In this guide, the standard model "gttft1" is used as the sample model. Report: data contributors can report events that are granted Report authorization. To enable the instance-based authorization, you need to: connect with your business partner (via the Invite Business Partners app or the Discover Business Partners app) for the tracked process user model field where you enter LBN ID, add LBN# as the prefix of its value to enable Read or Report authorization. For example, if the LBN ID is 10002424, you need to enter LBN#10002424. Instance-based Authorization Check for Write Service To check if a data contributor has Report authorization for an event, the GTT system will check if the event’s senderPartyId is equal to the tracked process’s partyId or to the LBN ID with the “LBN#” prefix. Not that events reported using Provider API for Order Events (GTT) are an exception, the GTT system won’t do this check for these events. For predefined event types, data contributors can only report GTTDelayedEvent and GTTOnTimeEvent. Authorization for instances can be inherited and checked through correlation. For example, suppose tracked process A observes tracked process B and tracked process B observes tracked process C. If you have authorization for tracked process C, you will also have authorization for B and A. Then events reported to C are also correlated to B and A. 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 51 This is custom documentation. Data contributors can only query user-defined process entities, user-defined event entities, GTTDelayedEvent and GTTOnTimeEvent. When querying process entities, you cannot filter/expand “QualifiedTrackingId” and user defined process entities. When querying event entities, you cannot filter/expand core entities and user-defined process entities. When querying any process entities, data will be filtered by process “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs. Note that at least one of process “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs should be equal to the user’s LBN ID. When querying any event entities, data will be filtered by “senderPartyId”, “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs. Note that at least one of “senderPartyId”, “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs should be equal to the user’s LBN ID. Notes There are several points to note: 1. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Response File tp2_20231218083335.zip SOAP Message Interfaces This section introduces SOAP message interfaces used by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out As a solution owner, you can create a freight order in TM embedded in SAP S/4HANA and send it for tracking in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Technical Name TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out Description You can use this inbound service provided by SAP Business Network for Logistics to create a freight order for tracking from your external system, such as TM embedded in SAP S/4HANA. This will enable you to track a freight order. For detailed configurations, see Using SOAP Messages. Frequently Asked Questions This section answers the questions that are frequently asked when you are using the tracking APIs. As a solution owner, can I request a new event type in the Provider API for Order Events (GTT)? Yes. You can report an incident on SAP ONE Support Launchpad categorized by component SBN-LBN-GTT to create a new event type. But before reporting the incident, please take a moment to familiarize yourself with the information below: 1. An event type means an action, such as Arrival or Departure. So it should not include any location-related information. 2. Location information could be maintained based on the stop ID (which is provided via the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT)), UNLOCODE, or IATACode. If you want to add an Arrival or Destination event, you can use the ARRIV_DEST event for both of these events. The exact location should then be maintained in the location ID. To foster standardization, please map your events to one of the existing event types. For a complete list of existing event types, see Event Code Descriptions. If you are unsure about which event type you should map with your event, you may also consider mapping it to the OTHER event type and adding a specific description for it. Does SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace support geo location tracking for direct integration with carriers (no visibility provider in between)? Yes. Carriers can also provide geo location updates via the Provider API for Order Events (GTT). Note that any event type can contain geo coordinates, such as Arrival, Departure, On Time, Delay, and so on. 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 59 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- As a solution owner, can I receive attachments from the data contributor as part of the Provider API for Order Events (GTT)? Yes. You have two options to achieve that. Option 1: The data contributor needs to maintain the fileName, mimeType, and fileURL that is publicly accessible. The GTT system will save the content from the URL provided as an attachment with the specified event. Option 2: The data contributor needs to maintain the fileName and fileContentBinaryObject to upload a Base64- encoded attachment. What is the size limit for attachments such as the proof of delivery that are sent by the data contributor? The total size of the attachment(s) in an event may not exceed 10 MB. As a solution owner, can I send a tracking request to multiple business partners regarding one specific document? Yes. You can achieve this in the Manage Models app by using the event-to-action function sendTrackingRequest. For more, see the corresponding part in the section Event to Action External Functions of Guide for Model Administrators. 5/12/26, 7:04 AM 60 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/GTT_Activate Your.content: Activate Your Account Generated on: 2026-05-12 06:47:35 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace | LBN Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_GTT_OPTION/8afff0118f9b4f1bb7d29f7b79c8f7d4?locale=en- US&state=PRODUCTION&version=LBN Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Introduction Welcome to SAP Business Network for Logistics! Your company has been invited to collaborate on the network by one of the business partners that you work with. What is the network and what are the benefits of joining? SAP Business Network for Logistics improves supply chain efficiency by connecting business partners on a collaborative network that supports jointly managing transactions, exchanging documents, and sharing insights across the value chain. For instance, upon invitation from a shipper, you – a carrier company – can activate your account on the network and collaborate with shippers on freight tendering, subcontracting, freight settlement, milestone reporting and dock appointment scheduling. SAP Business Network for Logistics is a cloud solution that provides your company with a range of apps which you can use to complete your daily tasks. For more information, see Introduction to SAP Business Network for Logistics - Video . This guide gives you information on how to activate your account for SAP Business Network for Logistics so you can sign in and start using the apps. If you have any issues following the steps, start by reading Frequently Asked Questions. Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process This guide gives an overview of the simplified onboarding process designed for data contributors and carriers who are ready to use SAP Business Network for Logistics. It provides detailed procedures for activating your account on the network, creating your business profile, adding users, and connecting with the business partner that invited you. If you have any issues performing the getting started tasks, see Frequently Asked Questions.  Note Instructions provided in this guide apply to both the production and test environments. If you’re invited by a shipper or solution owner from the production environment, you can follow these instructions to onboard to the production environment. Similarly, if the invitation comes from the test environment, you can use the same steps to onboard to the test environment.  Note Since release 2405, the account activation process for logistics providers has been simplified so that companies without an SAP Store account can also register as a carrier or data contributor on SAP Business Network for Logistics. You, as a logistics provider (carrier or data contributor), will receive an invitation from a shipper or solution owner to start your simplified account activation process. However, if the invitation was sent before release 2405 - which is before June 1, 2024, for invitation senders using the Europe data center (EU10), and before July 1, 2024, for those using the United States data center (US20) - the previous account activation process still applies. For more information, see Getting Started (Prior to Release 2405).  Note To help you get started easily, most procedures described in this document are also presented with step-by-step screenshots on the Carrier Learning Portal under Connect With Your Customer: 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Register (for Free) as a Carrier/Data Contributor on SAP Business Network for Logistics This topic provides step-by-step instructions on how to complete the registration for SAP Business Network for Logistics. Prerequisites Your company has been invited to collaborate on the network by one of the business partners that you work with. As the administrator of your company, you've received the following invitation email. If you don't receive it, check your SPAM/Junk Mail box. Email Subject / Sender Purpose Action to Take <Company_Name_Of_Inviter> would like to connect with you on SAP Business Network From: noreply@us.bn.cloud.ariba.com The email contains a link for registering an account on SAP Business Network for Logistics. See the following procedure. 1. After you received an email invitation from a shipper or a solution owner, click Get started in the email message. When SAP Business Network for Logistics shows the welcome page, click Create new account. 2. If you are creating a new account, verify the auto-populated email address and then click Proceed. 3. Follow the steps in the registration wizard. SAP Business Network asks for basic information about your business, such as your company name, address, and email address. You also create a username and password. The wizard performs automatic address validation to detect and correct any wrong or misspelled portion of a mailing address. A pop-up window shows a recommendation, which you can accept or reject. There is an ISO-based country- or region-specific drop-down list for state/province in the address section of the supplier profile. Select from the drop-down list (where available) instead of entering free text. Getting Started Create Account Connect Existing Account Account Administration Get Support  Note If the shipper or solution owner (inviter) has enabled “Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network” in Profile Settings for cross-data-center connections, you, as the invitee, will be prompted to choose a designated data center where your company profile will initially be maintained. Keep in mind that, to increase the visibility of your company’s service coverage, capabilities, and strengths, your company profile will also be replicated to other data centers. If you do not want your profile to be replicated to other data centers, you have the option to abort the registration.  Note 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- 4. Read the terms of use, choose the check boxes if you agree to the terms, and then choose Create account. 5. (Optional) Print the Summary page for your records. You can also print the terms of use. Results You’ve registered an account on SAP Business Network. Additionally, you'll receive several emails as described in Follow-up Emails. Follow-up Emails After registering for SAP Business Network for Logistics, you will receive several follow-up emails from SAP Business Network. These emails are sent from noreply@us.bn.cloud.ariba.com. Make sure your email software doesn’t block these email addresses to avoid them going to your SPAM/Junk Mail box. The table below shows the emails you should expect to receive and the actions to take after receiving them. Email Subject / Sender Purpose Action to Take Welcome to SAP Business Network From: noreply@us.bn.cloud.ariba.com Notifies you that your SAP Business Network account has been created and your company's tenant on the network is ready to use. The email contains the following: Your account information The sign in URL (embedded in the Sign in button) Proceed with the next task Sign In to SAP Business Network for Logistics. Sign In to SAP Business Network for Logistics This topic explains how to sign in to SAP Business Network for Logistics by clicking on the URL provided in the email Welcome to SAP Business Network, entering the user credentials, and accepting the terms and conditions. It also mentions that you can change the language displayed in the user interface. Prerequisites You've registered an account on SAP Business Network and received the emails described in Follow-up Emails. Procedure The person whose name is entered in the user account information section becomes the account administrator automatically. Account administrators can transfer the administrator role to another user later.  Note When double byte non-Latin characters (such as Chinese) are detected in an address, a warning is displayed. A Latin character translation must then be provided by the user, which is also validated for correctness. 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- 1. In the email Welcome to SAP Business Network, click the Sign in button. The sign-in page for the network is displayed. You’re recommended to bookmark this URL so you can sign in more easily next time. Additionally, when you add more users to the network in the future, you need to send this URL to the new users. 2. On the sign-in page, enter your user credentials and click Continue. E-Mail: enter the username listed in the email " Welcome to SAP Business Network". Password: enter the password that you set when you activated the initial user. 3. Change your password and then choose Save. 4. Open the sign-in page (with the URL you bookmarked in Step 1) then use the new password to sign-in to the home page of SAP Business Network for Logistics. 5. You are prompted to update your account information. Choose Update Now in the pop-up window and then open the Manage Business Profile app to complete your company profile. To increase your visibility to future business partners, be sure your company profile is completed accurately. For more information, see Create Your Company Profile. More Information The main window for SAP Business Network for Logistics opens. To change the language displayed in the user interface, click the user icon in the upper-right corner and choose Settings Language & Region . Create Your Company Profile You need to create your company profile for SAP Business Network for Logistics. The information in the profile is required to successfully connect to business partners. You also need to specify whether or not you'd like to make your profile visible to potential business partners and automatically accept connection requests. For detailed information, see Manage Business Profile. Configure a Technical User (Optional) A technical user is a token used for authentication and system connection. It is required only when you need to use the Write Service API provided by your solution owner on SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can create a technical user through the SAP ID service and maintain it in the System Connections app. Context  Note You, as the initial user and administrator of your company, can add additional administrators to help you complete the tasks hereafter. See Add Users for details.  Note A technical user is only required when you need to use the Write Service API provided by the solution owner connected with you on the network. If you only want to use the APIs in the API Accelerator Hub (see APIs for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace and APIs for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration ) or use the apps in the SAP Fiori Launchpad, skip this task. 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 5 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- A technical user is a role but not a person, nor a business user. It is a token used by selected services to access SAP Business Network for Logistics and authenticate system connection. Procedure Create a Technical User: 1. Go to the SAP ID service and create a user. Enter a unique email address that is not used by any of the users that you’ve created for SAP Business Network for Logistics. After registering the user, an email with the subject Activate Your Account for SAP.com will be sent to the email address. 2. Use the link in the email to activate the account. 3. On the Personal Information screen, note down the user ID, which starts with the letter P. You'll need it later. Maintain the Technical User in the System Connections app: 4. Sign in to SAP Business Network for Logistics. 5. In the SAP Fiori Launchpad window, open the System Connections app. 6. Choose Manage Alternate IDs. 7. Add an alternate ID as follows: Type: Technical User ID: the email address of the technical user 8. Choose Save. Add Users As an administrator, you can add users to your company's tenant on the network. The users you add will be able to sign in to the network with their own sign-in details and use the apps relevant to their roles. Procedure 1. Sign in to SAP Business Network for Logistics and open the User Management app. 2. Click Add on the right-hand side. 3. In the new entry, enter information about the user and assign user group(s) to the user. When you’re finished, click Save. Users assigned to the “…Admin” user group are administrators. They can perform administrative tasks using the following apps: Manage Business Profile Retention Management Blocking Store Define User Settings Manage Notification Settings System Connections 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 6 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Manage Invitations User Management Manage Integration Logs Users assigned to the “…All_Function” user group can access the following apps: Retention Management Blocking Store Define User Settings Manage Notification Settings Manage Invitations Manage Disputes Freight Orders for Confirmation Freight Orders for Reporting Review Freight Documents Invoice Freight Documents Freight Quotations Freight Requests for Quotation Manage Invoices Self-Book Dock Appointments Manage Freight Execution 4. Choose Save. Results After adding a user, the user receives an email with the subject “ Activate Your Account for User Profile” from ias@notifications.sap.com. The email contains a link to activate the user account, which is required for signing into the network. You need to send the network URL (see Sign In to SAP Business Network for Logistics) to the newly added users so they can sign in (after they’ve activated their user account).  Note If the user already exists in SAP Business Network for Logistics, no activation email will be sent because the user was already activated for the network.  Note You can edit the user group assignment for a user in the User Management app by clicking the  Edit icon for the user. The system will send an email to the user to notify the assignment change. You can also delete a user by selecting a user and choosing Delete Delete User . The deleted user can no longer access the apps in your company's tenant. 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Frequently Asked Questions This section answers the questions that are frequently asked when you get started with SAP Business Network for Logistics, including questions with invitation emails, registering and getting an account, signing in, and getting support. Invitation Email A business partner has invited me to join SAP Business Network for Logistics but I didn't receive the invitation email. Why? It is possible that your mail server blocked emails sent from noreply@us.bn.cloud.ariba.com. Try searching for the email in your SPAM/Junk Mail box. Registering and Getting Account What if my company needs more than one SAP Business Network for Logistics tenant? If your company needs more than one tenant, please contact your dedicated SAP onboarding specialist. Can I use the same user account to sign in to more than one SAP Business Network for Logistics tenant? Yes, you can use one user account to sign in to multiple tenants. This can occur when an email address that was used in a previous registration receives a new invitation. If you use this email address to register on the network again (most likely with a new company name), the system will create a separate tenant for you. When using your account (email address) to sign in to the network, you can switch between tenants, identified by company names, from the Switch Accounts icon in the upper-right corner. Important tips for using the same email across multiple registrations: User name: While you'll be asked to create a new user name (formatted as an email address) during registration, always use your original email address to sign in to the SAP Business Network for Logistics. Password: Similarly, you'll need to input a password again on the registration page. We recommend that you enter your original password. You have the option to enter a new password. But continue using your original password for sign-in purposes. Signing In What is the URL for signing in to SAP Business Network for Logistics? The sign-in URL is included in the email titled Welcome to SAP Business Network (described in Follow-up Emails). If you have added other users to your network (as described in Add Users), send the URL to them so that they can sign in with their own users/passwords. What is the user name/password I should use to sign in to SAP Business Network for Logistics? The initial user for the network is listed in the email titled Welcome to SAP Business Network. You can use this initial user (email address) and the password to sign in. For more information, see the application help: User Management 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- If you are not the initial user, your administrator can add you to the network. You'll receive an email with the subject " Activate Your Account for User Profile" from ias@notifications.sap.com. Click the activation link in the email to set a password. Then sign in with your email and password. What if I don't know the URL for signing in to the network? It is recommended that you keep the email that contains the sign-in URL ( the email with the subject Welcome to SAP Business Network) or create a bookmark for the URL in your web browser. What if I forget my password for signing in to SAP Business Network for Logistics? On the sign-in page, click Forgot Password. You'll receive the instructions for resetting your password. How can I reset my password? On the sign-in page, click Forgot Password. You'll receive the instructions for resetting your password. Getting Support My company's admin user for SAP Business Network for Logistics has left. Can SAP add me as the new admin user? Yes, we can add you as the admin user for your company. Please create a case on Ariba Help Center . How to create a case (report an issue) and get support? To create a case on Ariba Help Center , follow these steps: 1. Click the tile “SAP Business Network for Logistics – Carriers” under the For Suppliers section. 2. In the home page, try searching the knowledge base to get the answers for your issues first. 3. If the results still can’t resolve your issue, click Get Support Contact Support at the left-hand navigation pane, then, follow the workflow provided: a. Within Step 1: Enter a full description of the issue. b. Within Step 2: Browse the AI-generated resources based on your description to see if you can find solutions to your issue. If not, click Next to proceed. c. Within Step 3: Confirm the details. d. Within Step 4: Provide contact information. Click Webform to provide the required contact information.  Note When you report an issue that occurs in the onboarding process or some follow-up tasks related to onboarding, we recommend that you select General in the Confirm your issue field and then select the Issue area field from one of the following: Onboarding Services: General issues that occur during the onboarding process. Login: Issues that occur during the login process. Administration: Issues that occur during the usage of apps related to business partners. Carrier User Management: Issues that occur during the usage of the User Management app and the Define User Settings app. 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- 4. Submit the case. After you create a case on the Ariba Help Center , our support team will contact you using the email address you provided in the case creation form. We recommend adding itsm.notification-service@sap.com to your mailbox's allowed senders list to ensure you receive all correspondence. Do I have to provide an S-User ID when creating a case on Ariba Help Center? No, you don't. You can create cases on Ariba Help Center as a guest user. Getting Started (Prior to Release 2405) This guide gives you an overview of information on how to get started with SAP Business Network for Logistics. It provides detailed procedures for activating your account on the network, creating your business profile, adding users, and connecting with the business partner that invited you. If you have any issues performing the getting started tasks, see Frequently Asked Questions. Register (for Free) SAP Business Network for Logistics in SAP Store This topic provides step-by-step instructions on how to complete the registration for SAP Business Network for Logistics. Prerequisites Your company has been invited to collaborate on the network by one of the business partners that you work with. As the administrator of your company, you've received the following invitation email. If you don't receive them, check your SPAM/Junk Mail box. Email Subject / Sender Purpose Action to Take Invitation to Join SAP Business Network Logistics Provider, basic membership The email contains an SAP Store URL and a PO number for registering SAP Business Network for Logistics. See the procedure below.  Note If you've already received the Welcome to SAP Business Network email, please ensure that you enter your company's Business Network ID (BNO ID) in the Account ID field.  Note This section applies to logistics providers who received the invitation to the SAP Business Network for Logistics network before release 2405, which is before June 1, 2024, for invitation senders using the Europe data center (EU10), and before July 1, 2024, for those using the United States data center (US20). If the invitation you received was sent out after release 2405, see Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process.  Note You can also watch the Carrier Administrative Trainings videos to get step-by-step overview on account activating and administration. 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 10 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

The URL takes you to the SAP Business Network Logistics Provider solution page in SAP Store. 2. On the solution page, click View Pricing, and then click Start Now. If you haven’t signed in to SAP Store, this opens the Sign In page. If you've already signed in, proceed with Step 4. 3. On the Sign In page for SAP Store, do either of the following: If your company has already got an account for SAP Store, sign in. If your company doesn't have an SAP Store account, click Register to register an SAP Store account and follow the on-screen instructions to add company details. You'll then receive the emails as shown below. If you don't receive them, check your SPAM/Junk Mail box. In both emails, click the link to activate your account. Email Subject / Sender Purpose Action to Take Activate Your Account for SAP Store From: ias@notifications.sap.com Notifies you that an SAP Store account has been created for your company, and you need to activate the account. Click the link in the email to activate your SAP Store account. [PRIVATE] Your key to the SAP ecosystem From: notification-service@sap.com By activating this account, your company gets a unique S-User ID for obtaining SAP services and support. Click the link in the email to activate your S-User account. It is recommended that you take note of this S-User ID. You'll need it for obtaining SAP support in the future. 4. When you are on the Configure SAP Business Network Logistics Provider page, select contract terms and click Add to Cart. Make sure the start date is not in the past. 5. Confirm the order items and click Check Out. 6. On the checkout page, do the following: Account Details: this part is automatically filled. Please note the email address under Buyer Details. The welcome emails that you'll receive for accessing SAP Business Network for Logistics will be sent to that email address. If you want the emails to be sent to another person, you can add a technical contact here. Payment: the basic membership for SAP Business Network for Logistics is free of charge. Select Invoice and add tax information. Click Continue to Checkout Review. 7. On the Review Order Details page, fill in the PO number and click Place Order.  Note The PO number in the invitation email can be used for registering one tenant for SAP Business Network for Logistics. If your company needs more than one tenant, please contact your dedicated SAP onboarding specialist. 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 11 This is custom documentation. In the Privacy Settings section, specify the following: Make my business profile visible to potential business partners is by default No, which means your business profile is not visible to any company in SAP Business Network for Logistics. They can then find you in the network and invite you to connect to them. Frequently Asked Questions This section answers the questions that are frequently asked when you get started with SAP Business Network for Logistics, including questions with invitation emails, registering and getting an account, signing in, managing business profiles, and getting support. Invitation Email A business partner has invited me to join SAP Business Network for Logistics but I didn't receive the invitation email. Why? The reason might be either of the following: Your mail server has blocked emails sent from saplbn@mailsap.com. Try searching for the email in your SPAM/Junk Mail box. If your company has already registered and activated your account on the network, new invitations are sent to your existing account in the network. In this case, you won't receive an invitation email for registration again. You only need to accept the new invitation, as described in Accept Connection Request.  Note If the user already exists in SAP Business Network for Logistics, no activation email will be sent because the user was already activated for the network.  Note You can edit the user group assignment for a user in the User Management app by clicking the  Edit icon for the user. The system will send an email to the user to notify the assignment change. You can also delete a user by selecting a user and choosing Delete Delete User . The deleted user can no longer access the apps in your company's tenant. For more information, see the application help: User Management 5/12/26, 6:47 AM 18 This is custom documentation. Registering and Getting Account Why should I enter the PO number when placing the order in SAP Store? The PO number is used by SAP to identify you as an invited business partner of the network. You must enter this number to ensure successful registration. You can find the PO number in the invitation email. I encountered an issue when placing the order in SAP Store. What should I do? If you have issues or questions with SAP Store, please contact SAP Store customer support by clicking Need Help? in SAP Store. How do I know that my order in SAP Store has been successfully placed? You'll receive emails from SAP store with the subject SAP Store: Order request received and SAP Store: Your order is now fully processed. How do I know that my company has got an account for SAP Business Network for Logistics? SAP starts preparing your account on the network after you place the order in SAP Store. When this is complete, you'll receive the following welcome emails: Access information for SAP Business Network for Logistics: this email contains the specific URL for your company to sign in to the network and the initial user account to sign in. Activate Your Account for User Profile: this email enables you to activate the initial user account and set the password. I've registered SAP Business Network for Logistics in SAP Store but didn't receive the welcome emails. What should I do? After the registration, you should receive several emails as listed in Welcome Emails. If you didn't receive them, proceed as follows: 1. The welcome emails are sent to the email box that you provided during the registration. If you are not the owner of that email box, contact the owner to get the emails. 2. Check your SPAM/Junk Mail box. It is possible that your email server identified some emails as SPAM/Junk Mails. 3. If the above do not work, please contact your dedicated SAP onboarding specialist. What if my company needs more than one SAP Business Network for Logistics tenant? When a company is invited to join SAP Business Network for Logistics, the PO number in the invitation email can be used to register one SAP Business Network for Logistics tenant only. If your company needs more than one tenant, please contact your dedicated SAP onboarding specialist. What is the user name/password I should use to sign in to SAP Business Network for Logistics? The initial user for the network is listed in the access information email. You need to activate the user and set a password, as described in Welcome Emails. Then you can use this initial user (email) and the password to sign in. If you are not the initial user, your administrator can add you to the network. You'll receive an email with the subject " Activate Your Account for User Profile" from ias@notifications.sap.com. Sign on with your email and password. If you're asked to reset your password, just do it. If you don't remember the password, click Forgot password? and you'll receive an email for resetting it. After signing in, you'll see a page displaying your profile information. 3. Find your company's sign-in URL in the User Custom Attribute 1 field. Remember to bookmark the URL for future use. What if I forget my password for signing in to SAP Business Network for Logistics? On the sign-in page, click Forgot Password. You'll receive the instructions for resetting your password. How can I reset my password? On the sign-in page, click Forgot Password. You'll receive the instructions for resetting your password. If you have trouble identifying who the S-User is in your organization, you can contact the Customer Interaction Center (CIC). For more information, see the SAP for Me Online Help under Access and Authorizations . For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- This administration guide describes the steps you need to perform as an administrator to set up, configure, and administer SAP Business Network Logistics Provider. This guide addresses the following target audience: administrators, consultants, users and others involved with SAP Business Network Logistics Provider. About SAP Business Network Logistics Provider SAP Business Network for Logistics is an open network that connects business partners for inter-company collaboration. Freight collaboration and milestone reporting support you as a carrier or other logistics service provider to jointly manage the related transactions and exchange documents with your shippers. For more information, see Introduction to SAP Business Network for Logistics - Video . Technical Considerations Note that there are restrictions regarding the overall data volume that can be managed. Before starting your project, discuss your expected data volumes with your SAP technical contact. Browser Support This application only supports the standard browsers supported by SAP Business Technology Platform. For more information, see the Browser Support chapter in Feature Scope Description for SAP BTP, Cloud Foundry, ABAP, and Kyma Environments. Root Certificate for End User UI The browser certificate store must contain both the old root certificate ( DigiCert Global Root G2) and the new root certificate (DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5). Without this, the end user sign-in to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace will be impacted. To check if you are impacted, try to access the following URL: https://digicert-tls-rsa4096-root-g5.chain-demos.digicert.com . If your browser loads the page without warning, it trusts the DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 and no further action is required on your end. To ensure a smooth transition, you need to run the check and take action (where applicable) before April 23, 2026. Resolution for user sign-in to the BN4L Fiori Launchpad - How to import the certificate into my browser? The below steps might vary with the browser type and version: Download Root Certificate [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ] and Intermediate Certificate [DigiCert G5 TLS RSA4096 SHA384 2021 CA1 ]. Open Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. Open settings and search for security in the search box and click on it. Click on Manage Device Certificates / Manage Certificates.  Note A logistics provider can be a carrier in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration or a data contributor in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Go to the Trusted Root Certification Authorities tab and Import Digi Certificates using the Import button at the bottom. Go to the Intermediate Certification Authorities tab and Import Digi Certificates using the Import button at the bottom. Ensure that DigiCert Root and Intermediate is added in the list. For more information, see Switch to DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5. Product Availability This section describes certain product availability aspects. Availability - Languages The apps provided with SAP Business Network for Logistics support the following languages: English (US) – default Dutch German French Polish Portuguese (Brazilian) Russian Simplified Chinese Spanish Turkish Italian Japanese Arabic Bulgarian Czech Danish Greek Finnish Hebrew Croatian Hungarian Korean Malay 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 5 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Norwegian Romanian Slovak Serbian Swedish Thai Traditional Chinese In addition, selected documentation on SAP Help Portal supports the languages listed above. Onboarding and User Management A step-by-step guide will lead you through the process of registering SAP Business Network for Logistics, activating your account, signing in, and adding users. For more information, see Activate Your Account. Business Configuration SAP Fiori Launchpad Integration The SAP Fiori launchpad is delivered with the apps as part of the tenant onboarding process. The users that you have defined can access different applications using the Fiori launchpad. You can sign in to the Fiori launchpad using a URL with the following format: https://<your-subdomain>-site-entry.<domain-name>/sites#Shell-home Set Up Business Profile For your business partners to search and connect with you in the network, you must maintain your business profile using the Manage Business Profile app. For more information, see Manage Business Profile app. Manage Notification Settings You can schedule reminder notifications for some of the business processes for which you may need an alert using the Manage Notification Settings app. The system sends you notifications via emails. For more information, see Manage Notification Settings. Define User Settings You can define defaults that best suit the way you work using the Define User Settings app. The settings that you make in the app serve as the default settings in various other apps in your SAP Business Network for Logistics. For more information, see Define User Settings. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 6 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Manage Users As an administrator, you can use the User Management app to manage users in your company tenant, such as adding or deleting administrators or business users. For more information, see User Management. Manage Invitations from Business Partners To perform business in the network and to receive business documents from your business partners, you must first connect with them. An existing or potential business partner can send invitations to connect with you in the network. You can accept or reject the invitations using the Manage Invitations app. Navigate to the Manage Invitations app tile in the Fiori launchpad to access the app. For more information, see Manage Invitations. Freight Contracting You can participate in freight tendering when a known ordering party sends you a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ). You can accept or reject a freight RFQ. The freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics creates a freight quotation and sends it to the ordering party. The ordering party then evaluates your freight quotation and, according to their strategy, may or not award it to you. For more information, see the application help for Freight Contracting. Freight Orders for Confirmation If an ordering party wants to subcontract the transportation of goods to you, you will find the corresponding freight orders in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. This can also be a subsequent step to the tendering process, if your freight quotation was awarded. For more information, see the application help for the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) You can review and confirm ocean freight bookings that ordering parties ask you to execute in subcontracting in the Freight Bookings for Confirmation app. For more information, see the application help for the Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) app. Confirm Freight Bookings (Air) You can review and confirm air freight bookings that ordering parties ask you to execute in subcontracting in the Freight Bookings for Confirmation app. For more information, see the application help for the Confirm Freight Bookings (Air) app. Self-Book Dock Appointments You can book a dock appointment for a freight order in the Self-Book Dock Appointments app when the corresponding vehicle is about to reach a certain stop for loading or unloading. The appointments you booked will then be visualized in the Manage Dock Appointments app. This helps shippers have a precise estimate on the quantity of the upcoming dock appointments. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- For more information, see the application help for the Self-Book Dock Appointments app. Invoice Freight Documents You can view all the freight documents that are ready for invoicing using the Invoice Freight Documents app. You can view all the freight documents from one or more of your ordering parties using this app. You can select one or more of these freight documents and create a single invoice or a collective invoice for your ordering party for the services that you provided. For more information, see the application help for the Invoice Freight Documents app. Manage Invoices You can view all the invoices that you created in the freight collaboration option for your ordering party using the Manage Invoices app. For more information, see the application help for the Manage Invoices app. Review Freight Documents You can view all the freight documents that are ready for self-billing by the ordering party using the Review Freight Documents app. This app displays all the freight documents that you have received from one or more ordering parties. You can view the transportation charges in the freight document based on which the ordering party creates a self-billed invoice. You can create disputes against the freight documents for self-billing for additional unplanned freight costs using this app. For more information, see the application help for the Review Freight Documents app. Manage Disputes You can create disputes against the freight documents for self-billing for additional unplanned freight costs. Once the system creates a dispute, you can view this document in the Manage Disputes app. In this app, you can newly add a charge line for an additional charge encountered during the transportation or you can propose a change in an existing charge line. The ordering party can accept or reject your changes or propose another change and submit the dispute back to you. For more information, see the application help for the Manage Disputes app. Freight Orders for Reporting You can keep your ordering parties informed about the transportation of their freight using the Freight Orders for Reporting app. You can report when planned events in the freight order are completed. If a delay occurs, you can also use the app to report a new ETA (expected time of arrival), enabling the ordering party to replan if needed. Note that the Freight Orders for Reporting app has been deprecated and will be sunset on May 16, 2026. This app has been replaced with the new app Manage Freight Execution. For more information, see the application help for the Freight Orders for Reporting app. Manage Freight Orders The Manage Freight Execution app enables you to keep your ordering parties informed about the transportation of their freight. For example, if one of your shipments is delayed on-route, you can send the ordering party a new ETA (expected time of arrival) so they can replan if necessary. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- For more information, see the application help for the Manage Freight Execution app. Connectivity By implementing the APIs published by SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, your organization can receive and respond to business documents directly from your external system. To complete the API implementations, you – as an administrator – also need to perform the following steps using the System Connections app: 1. Set up Outbound Connections: Choose Manage Details. Enter the communication details and the authentication details to your external system. Then navigate back to Outbound Connections. Configure the supported services in your external system. To do so, choose Create, and select a service name and an operation name from the drop down menu. You can create an API or EDI communication based on the details provided under Manage Details. Activate the operation. 2. Set up Connection Settings: Choose Connection Settings. Under Outbound, in the Integration Platform dropdown list, you can choose between the following values: Neo (old) Multi-Cloud (new) Neo (old) is set as default. To enable outbound communication using the new integration platform, select Multi- Cloud (new). To authorize your inbound messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics, you need an OAuth token. To request the token from SAP, create a BCP ticket and use the component SBN-LBN-INT. Turn on the Enable Inbound Communication toggle and save. For more information about the APIs published by SAP Business Network for Logistics, go to:  Note The System Connections app is available for digital forwarders, carrier subnetworks, network partners, and carriers (B2B carrier/networks).  Note Ensure to allowlist the IP addresses of the integration platform. If you use Neo (old), you must allowlist the IP addresses listed under Regions and Hosts Available for the Neo Environment. If you use Multi-Cloud (new) for outbound connections, you must allowlist the IP addresses listed under Regions and API Endpoints Available for the Cloud Foundry Environment. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- SAP Business Accelerator Hub for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration SAP Business Accelerator Hub for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace For more information about EDI integration, see the guides published on SAP Help Portal at https://help.sap.com/docs/business- network-logistics-provider?task=integrate_task. Related Information System Connections (Data Contributor) Switch to DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 SAP Business Network for Logistics is switching its root Certificate Authority to DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 for the domain *.logistics.*.business-network.cloud.sap to enhance security and trust. This is in line with the root certificate replacement in the SAP BTP, Cloud Foundry Environment. To ensure a smooth transition, customers must take action before April 23, 2026. For more information, see SAP Note 3688060 . As part of our ongoing commitment to security and trust, SAP is updating the root Certificate Authority (CA). This update supports the broader adoption of our fifth-generation (G5) root CA and allows additional time for its inclusion in major browser and operating system trust stores, ensuring seamless and trusted connectivity. Am I Impacted? This change could impact B2B Connectivity: The sender systems must trust both the old root certificate ( DigiCert Global Root G2) and the new root certificate ( DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5). Without this, the inbound communication to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace will be impacted. For information about a possible impact on the end user UI, see Browser Support. Resolution for B2B Connectivity to BN4L: Case 1: When sender system is S/4HANA (On-Premise & Private Cloud) 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Upload this Root Certificate to all relevant SSL Client PSEs*. 3. For detailed steps, see SAP KBA 3238733 - How to Import a Certificate Into a STRUST PSE's Certificate List In a NetWeaver AS ABAP. 4. [DigiCert Global Root G2] should remain as is. 5. ICM restart should be necessary post change in STRUST, only if you are running old releases of Netweaver 700/701 and 64x. See SAP KBA 2746647 - SSSLERR_PEER_CERT_UNTRUSTED after importing the target certificate. Since Netweaver AS ABAP 710 and AS ABAP 702, ICM restart is no longer necessary. Case 2: When sender system is SAP NetWeaver PI (On-Premise & Private Cloud) 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Import this Root Certificate to TrustedCAs view of NetWeaver Java Key Storage. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 10 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

Case 3: When WebDispatcher is placed in front of Cloud Integration endpoint 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Import this Root Certificate to Trusted Certificates through Web Administration Interface of SAP WebDispatcher. 3. See SAP Help - PSE Management in Web Administration Interface of SAP Web Dispatcher, section [Trusted Certificates]. Case 4: When sender system is a non-SAP service/software 1. Consult your vendor for confirmation that it should trust [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ] for outbound TLS communication. 2. Particularly, in case of a customer written Java program, JDK version should be higher than the following: SAP JVM 8.1.097 SapMachine 11.0.22 SapMachine 17.0.10 SapMachine 21.0.2 Oracle JDK 8u401 Oracle JDK 17.0.10 OpenJDK 17.0.10 OpenJDK 21.0.2 For more information, see the following SAP Notes: 3688060 3587968 3566727 3472211 Migration to New Integration Platform (Freemium Customer) SAP Business Network for Logistics is run on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) leveraging the various services provided by the platform. SAP BTP offers a variety of application environments that customers and internal SAP organizations can choose from, to build SAP applications and business solutions in the cloud. One critical service used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is the SAP Cloud Integration (previously known as SAP CPI) which acts as the single integration platform for all customers and partners for SAP Business Network for Logistics. This platform is owned and managed by the SAP Business Network for Logistics development team. Freemium customers can maintain necessary connectivity configurations using the System Connections app, and monitor their integration logs using the Manage Integration Logs app. SAP Cloud Integration used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is hosted in the Neo environment of SAP BTP. SAP BTP, Neo environment is the oldest of the application environments and is built on a proprietary SAP technology stack. The Neo environment in SAP BTP has been deprecated and will be sunset for internal SaaS applications (see SAP Note 3351844 ). Data Storage Security SAP Business Network for Logistics stores data in tenant-specific database schemas. Access to the databases are preconfigured with the infrastructure environment. The databases contain many different types of data including the following: Personal data (for example, user names, email addresses, and so on) Operational business data Preferences and configurations This data is updated continuously whenever required or requested. Data Protection and Privacy Introduction Data protection is associated with numerous legal requirements and privacy concerns. In addition to compliance with general data protection and privacy acts, it is necessary to consider compliance with industry-specific legislation in different countries/regions. SAP provides specific features and functions to support compliance with regard to relevant legal requirements, including data protection. SAP does not give any advice on whether these features and functions are the best method to support company, industry, regional, or country-specific requirements. Furthermore, this information should not be taken as advice or a recommendation regarding additional features that would be required in specific IT environments. Decisions related to data protection must be made on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration the given system landscape and the applicable legal requirements.  Note SAP does not provide legal advice in any form. SAP software supports data protection compliance by providing security features and specific data protection-relevant functions, such as simplified blocking and deletion of personal data. In many cases, compliance with applicable data protection and privacy laws will not be covered by a product feature. Definitions and other terms used in this document are not taken from a particular legal source.  Caution The extent to which data protection is supported by technical means depends on secure system operation. Network security, security note implementation, adequate logging of system changes, and appropriate usage of the system are the basic technical requirements for compliance with data privacy legislation and other legislation. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 16 This is custom documentation.
