Glossary The following terms are general to SAP products. Not all terms may be relevant for this SAP product. Term Definition Artificial Intelligence (AI) The simulation of human intelligence processes by machines and computer systems – typically by learning, coming to its own conclusions, appearing to understand complex content, engaging in natural dialogs with people, enhancing human cognitive performance (also known as cognitive computing) or replacing people on execution of nonroutine tasks. Applications include autonomous vehicles, automatic speech recognition and generation and detecting novel concepts and abstractions (useful for detecting potential new risks and aiding humans to quickly understand very large bodies of ever-changing information) Automated Decision Making The ability to make decisions by technological means without human involvement. Blocking A method of restricting access to data for which the primary business purpose has ended. Business Purpose The legal, contractual, or in other form justified reason for the processing of personal data to complete an end-to-end business process. The personal data used to complete the process is predefined in a purpose, which is defined by the data controller. The process must be defined before the personal data required to fulfill the purpose can be determined. Consent The action of the data subject confirming that the usage of his or her personal data shall be allowed for a given purpose. A consent functionality allows the storage of a consent record in relation to a specific purpose and shows if a data subject has granted, withdrawn, or denied consent. Data Subject Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person ("data subject"). An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier, or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person. Deletion Deletion of personal data so that the data is no longer available. End of Business Defines the end of active business and the start of residence time and retention period. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 17 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Term Definition End of Purpose (EoP) The point in time when the processing of a set of personal data is no longer required for the primary business purpose, for example, when a contract is fulfilled. After the EoP has been reached, the data is blocked and can only be accessed by users with special authorizations (for example, tax auditors). End of Purpose (EoP) check A method of identifying the point in time for a data set when the processing of personal data is no longer required for the primary business purpose. After the EoP has been reached, the data is blocked and can only be accessed by users with special authorization, for example, tax auditors. Personal data Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person ("data subject"). An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier, or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person. Processing of Personal Data Processing means any operation or set of operations which is performed on personal data or on sets of personal data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, recording, organisation, structuring, storage, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure or destruction. Purpose The information that specifies the reason and the goal for the processing of a specific set of personal data. As a rule, the purpose references the relevant legal basis for the processing of personal data. Residence period The period of time between the end of business and the end of purpose (EoP) for a data set during which the data remains in the database and can be used in case of subsequent processes related to the original purpose. At the end of the longest configured residence period, the data is blocked or deleted. The residence period is part of the overall retention period. Retention period The period of time between the end of the last business activity involving a specific object (for example, a business partner) and the deletion of the corresponding data, subject to applicable laws. The retention period is a combination of the residence period and the blocking period. Sensitive personal data A category of personal data that usually includes the following type of information: Special categories of personal data, such as data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data, biometric data, data concerning health or sex life or sexual orientation. Personal data subject to professional secrecy Personal data relating to criminal or administrative offenses 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 18 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Term Definition Personal data concerning insurances and bank or credit card accounts Technical and organizational measures (TOM) Some basic requirements that support data protection and privacy are often referred to as technical and organizational measures (TOM). The following topics are related to data protection and privacy and require appropriate TOMs, for example: Access control: Authentication features Authorizations: Authorization concept Read access logging Transmission control / Communication security Input control / Change logging Availability control Separation by purpose: Is subject to the organizational model implemented and must be applied as part of the authorization concept. Consent The processing of personal data (including its collection or its transfer) is based on purposes, legitimated by the fulfilment of a contract, a legal obligation, a vital interest, a public interest, a legitimate interest or a consent. In some cases, the data subject may also be the user. This SAP product provides functionality to capture consent of data subjects before collecting personal data, where no other legal ground exists. This allows data subjects to give and withdraw consent to process their personal data. Where data is processed for a purpose different than the original purpose or a privacy statement was changed, likely a new consent needs to be collected. Consent in the SAP Business Network for Logistics The terms of personal data collection are outlined in a Privacy Statement. Users are required to read and accept the Privacy Statement when signing in to the SAP Business Network for Logistics for the first time. Users can read the Privacy Statement and withdraw the consent at any time. To do that, click the user icon in the upper-right corner of the app window and choose Settings Privacy Statement . Read Access Logging Read Access Logging is considered as an additional safeguard in the protection of personal data, because it helps to identify potential illegitimate access to personal data. Read access to sensitive personal data is partially based on legislation, and it is subject to logging functionality. Read access logging (RAL) is used to monitor and log read access to sensitive personal data that was disclosed via user interface, which can be extended to read access to other personal data. Data may be categorized as sensitive by law, by external company policy, or by internal company policy. When these read accesses are logged, you should be able check which user accessed personal data on which access channel and the date and time, depending on the configuration. Read access logging enables you to answer questions about who accessed particular data within a specified time frame. That logging also includes downloading attachments or files, logs for such events shall contain information to identify the attachment. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 19 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Additionally, as for Read Access Logging across system boundaries, the respective “access” shall be logged as soon as sensitive personal data crosses the boundary from a trusted to an un-trusted area. Here are some examples of such questions: Who accessed the data of a given business entity, for example a bank account? Who accessed personal data, for example of a business partner? Which employee accessed personal information, for example religion? Which accounts or business partners were accessed by which users? Furthermore, log records can be viewed and queried, but access to them is restricted by adequate authorizations. The personal data for which read access shall be logged and the retention period of logs, can be configured. Products built using Java with an SAP HANA database as a back end use the audit trails and audit policies for change logging. For more information, see the Auditing Activity section in the SAP HANA Security Guide. This product uses the Log4J API for change logging. For more information, see JDBC Appender . This product uses a log façade for change logging. For more information, see the Appenders section of the Logback documentation . Java-based NetWeaver products use the security audit log of the SAP NetWeaver Application Server (AS) Java for change logging. For more information, see the Security Audit Log of the AS Java. Cloud products using SAP HANA XS and SAP HANA standalone use the audit trail and audit policies for change logging. For more information, see the Auditing Activity section in the SAP HANA Security Guide. Personal Data Record The feature provides data associated to the Data Subject. It is in the duty of the customer to check, whether all the data reported shall get handed over to the data subject, because the report might contain internal customer information or information on other third parties. Data subjects have the right to receive information regarding their personal data undergoing processing. The personal data record feature helps you to comply with the relevant legal requirements for data protection by allowing you to search for and retrieve personal data for a specified data subject. The search results are displayed in a comprehensive and structured list containing all personal data of the data subject specified, organized according to the purpose for which the data was collected and processed. The extracted data can be downloaded in form of a report, that provides configuration and extensibility functionality. The access to the personal data record is only allowed with authorization. Personal Data Record in the SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace uses the Next Generation Data Privacy Integration service for the retrieval of personal data. To implement this service, you must first subscribe to the SAP Data Privacy Integration Next Generation service (application plan name: ngdpi) in your SAP Cloud Platform subaccount. After subscribing, assign the DPI_NextGen_Information_DataPrivacy_Administrator role collection to users handling personal data management to ensure they have the appropriate permissions for managing personal data securely. For more information about the Next Generation Data Privacy Integration service, refer to the following resources: https://help.sap.com/docs/data-privacy-integration/end-user-information/what-is-data-privacy-integration-nextgen? q=nextgen&version=Cloud https://help.sap.com/docs/data-privacy-integration/security/assigning-roles-to-users- b90280f5f6904d008a3ebb8ac3809094?q=nextgen 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 20 This is custom documentation. file://api-specs/split/GTT_Administratio.content: Deletion of Personal Data Simplified Blocking and Deletion The processing of personal data is subject to applicable laws related to the deletion of this data when the specified, explicit, and legitimate purpose for processing this personal data has expired. If there is no longer a legitimate purpose, that requires the retention and use of personal data, it must be deleted irrecoverably. Blocking is necessary when the original retention period has expired but additional applicable extended and overruling (mandated by law) retention periods are still in place. After the expiration of the longest retention period, the data must be deleted. Deletion of Personal Data When considering compliance with data protection regulations, it is also necessary to consider compliance with industry-specific legislation in different countries. A typical potential scenario in certain countries is that personal data shall be deleted after the specified, explicit, and legitimate purpose for the processing of personal data has ended, but only if no other retention periods are defined in legislation, for example, retention periods for financial documents. Legal requirements in certain scenarios or countries also often require blocking of data in cases where the specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes for the processing of this data have ended, however, the data still has to be retained in the database due to other legally mandated retention periods. Sometimes, transactional data are personal data with relation to a master data object, e.g. a sales order with reference to a business partner. Therefore, the challenge for deletion and blocking is first to handle transactional data and finally other data, such as business partner data. Deletion of Personal Data in the SAP Business Network for Logistics The administrator of a company can specify retention periods using the Retention Management app. For more information, see Retention Management. Once the residence period ends, the data moves to the blocking period. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a data protection officer, can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the system deletes the data. The data protection officer can use the Blocking Store app provided by SAP Business Network for Logistics to access all the documents that are in the blocking period. To view a document, the user can download the document in a text file format. For more information, see Blocking Store. Change Log Creation and change of personal data need to be documented. Therefore, for review purposes or as a result of legal regulations, it may be necessary to track the changes made to this data. When these changes are logged, you should be able to check which user made which change, the date and time, the previous value, and the current value, depending on the configuration. Furthermore, log records can be viewed and queried, but access to them is restricted by adequate authorizations. The personal data for which changes shall be logged and the retention period of logs, can be configured.. Change Logging in the SAP Business Network for Logistics SAP Business Network for Logistics supports change and audit log. When you change any personal information, the system updates the audit log. Users with the required authorization can request for the change log. To request for a log, the authorized user must create an SAP support message in the component BC-NEO-AUDITLOG. For more information about how to request for audit logs, see Audit Log Viewer for the Cloud Foundry Environment. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 21 This is custom documentation. Monitoring and Troubleshooting Error Handling If you encounter technical issues or require support, follow the procedure to report a case. Report a Case through SAP for Me To report a case through SAP for Me, you need an S-User ID to sign in. If you don't have the sign-in credentials of your S-User, contact a user administrator in your organization. If you have trouble identifying who the user administrator is in your organization, please call the Customer Interaction Center (CIC) . For more information, see the SAP for Me Online Help under Access and Authorizations . Procedure 1. Open the SAP for Me application . Sign in with your S-User ID. 2. Navigate to Services & Support Get Support . 3. In the Get Support app, select a relevant customer and report your issue. For detailed process, see Get Support Application Online Help . If you use a component to categorize your issue, use SBN-LBN. Report a Case on Ariba Help Center If you set up your logistics provider account via the simplified onboarding process, you won’t have an S-User ID. In this case, you can report a case on Ariba Help Center. Procedure 1. Sign in to Ariba Help Center then choose Carrier Help Center. 2. Select Contact us, enter keywords pertaining to the issue in the search box and then press Enter. 3. Browse the populated results. If the results provided do not resolve your issue, click Create a Case at the lower-right corner. 4. Enter information on the case creation form. 5/12/26, 6:56 AM 22 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 3 -- 5. Click One last step once you complete the case creation form, choose the contact method, and then click Submit. After you create a case on the Ariba Help Center , our support team will contact you using the email address you provided in the case creation form. We recommend adding itsm.notification-service@sap.com to your mailbox's allowed senders list to ensure you receive all correspondence. file://api-specs/split/GTT_Getting Start.content: Getting Started Guide for Solution Owners Generated on: 2026-05-12 06:45:29 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace | LBN Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_GTT_OPTION/527aed4c3a9d4fb8a7fd9e9221018b03?locale=en- US&state=PRODUCTION&version=LBN Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/12/26, 6:45 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 9 -- Introduction Welcome to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace! What is the network and what are the benefits of joining? SAP Business Network for Logistics improves supply chain efficiency by connecting business partners on a collaborative network that supports jointly managing transactions, exchanging documents, and sharing insights across the value chain. Then business users can capture, process and store tracking information about tracked business processes, query any tracked process, and display its retrieved data from end to end. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace is a cloud solution that provides your company with a range of solution owner apps which you can use for completing your daily tasks. This getting started guide for administrators leads you through the onboarding and initial setup process so you and your colleagues can sign in and start using the apps. If you have any issues following the steps in this guide, start by reading Frequently Asked Questions. Welcome Emails After purchasing a solution for SAP Business Network for Logistics in SAP Store, the contact IT person of your company will receive several emails from SAP. These emails provide instructions and links for activating accounts, setting up global accounts, and accessing onboarding instructions and documents. The emails are sent from notification@sapnetworkmail.com and no.reply.provisioning@sap.com. Make sure your email software doesn’t block these email addresses to avoid it going to your SPAM/Junk Mail box. The table below shows the emails you should expect to receive and the actions to take after receiving them. If you don’t have access to the emails listed here, start by reading Frequently Asked Questions. Email Purpose Action to Take An email for activating your Identity Authentication account Notifies you that an Identity Authentication tenant has been created for you on SAP BTP, and you need to activate your account. The Identity Authentication is an identity provider for user authentication and authorization management. You won't receive this email if: Your company has already got an Identity Authentication tenant; or You are an SAP partner that purchased the cloud test&demo license for the solution. 1. In the email, choose Click here to activate your account to activate your account and set password. 2. In the email, click the link text Administration Console to go to the administration console for SAP Identity Authentication Service. Sign in with your email and the password you just set. You're recommended to bookmark this URL so you could sign in more easily in the future. 3. If the onboarding tasks need to be performed by another person, you need to add that person as the 5/12/26, 6:45 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 9 -- Email Purpose Action to Take administrator of the Identity Authentication tenant. To do that, choose Users & Authorizations Administrators in the menu pane. Then choose +Add and User at the bottom of the pane in the middle, and grant the user the Manage Groups authorization. A welcome email from SAP BTP for your global account Notifies you that your global account on SAP BTP is ready to use. Set up your global account as described in Set Up Your Global Account in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. Welcome to SAP Business Network for Logistics, global track and trace option Notifies you that your SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace is ready to use. The email contains onboarding instructions and document links. In the email, click the document links. You'll refer to these documents to perform administration tasks and use the apps. You can bookmark the document links for future use. Getting Started After receiving the welcome emails, you can get started with the initial administrative tasks, as described in the table below. Task Procedure Set up a test environment to test the connection and data exchange between solution owner and data contributor. 1. Set up a test solution owner tenant and a test data contributor tenant, and connect the two. For detailed procedure, refer to the following section in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners: Solution Owner Onboarding 2. As a test solution owner, you can connect to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace with your backend SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) or TM on SAP S/4HANA. For detailed information, see How to Send Documents from SAP ERP to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Set up the production use as a solution owner. This is only applicable for customers licensed with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. SAP partners with the cloud test&demo license cannot set up the solution for production use. 1. Set up your company's production solution owner tenant for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. For detailed procedure, see Solution Owner Onboarding in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners.  Note Dependent on your purchase solution, you are entitled to set up different types of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace tenants. For more information, see Onboarding. 5/12/26, 6:45 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 9 -- Task Procedure After the setup, you'll be able to sign in to your tenant to use the solution owner apps. 2. You can connect to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace with your backend SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) or TM on SAP S/4HANA. For detailed information, see How to Send Documents from SAP ERP to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. 3. Invite the data contributors that you already know and/or discover new data contributors and invite them to connect with you on the network. For detailed procedure, see Inviting Data Contributors to Connect with You on the Network. You can then collaborate with connected data contributors on tracking business processes. Inviting Data Contributors to Connect with You on the Network Context A data contributor is an individual or organization that provides logistics information and reports milestone events to you. Data contributors can include carriers, warehouse providers, visibility providers, LSPs (Logistics Service Providers), customs brokers, or other parties involved in the movement of goods. Note that you may not have to invite all the logistics information providers to your network. For example, if you receive information from visibility providers, then you don't have to invite the corresponding carriers to connect with you on the network. Prerequisites You're onboarded onto SAP Business Network for Logistics. To perform the tasks described in this section, you must be assigned with the following roles. Application Identifier Role Template Description lbnplatform-bprepo- live!b18679 BPEditTemplate The assigned user can edit company profile in the Manage Business Profile app. InviteBPProcessTemplate The assigned user can invite business partners in the Invite Business Partners app. BusinessPartnerDiscoveryTemplate The assigned user can search for and invite business partners in the Discover Business Partners app.  Note 5/12/26, 6:45 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 9 -- Create Your Company's Business Profile You need to create your company’s business profile. This is required as a prerequisite to inviting business partners onto your network. 1. Sign in toSAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. For more information, see Sign In to the Network in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. 2. In the SAP Fiori Launchpad window, when a message box opens reminding you that your company's business profile is incomplete, choose Open Manage Business Profile App in the message box. You can also open the app later by clicking the Manage Business Profile app tile in the SAP Fiori Launchpad window. 3. In the Manage Business Profile app, click Edit in the upper right-hand corner. 4. In the Header and Contact Details sections, enter at least a company name, an address, and a business contact person. To enter address and business contact, click Add on the right-hand side. 5. Save your business profile by clicking Save in the lower right-hand corner. Inviting Data Contributors to Connect with You You can invite data contributors to connect with you on the network using either of the following apps: Discover Business Partners App Use this app to invite data contributors that have already joined the network, no matter whether you know them or not. You can search for data contributors by different criteria and can select suitable ones to send connection invitations. To invite a data contributor with the app, proceed as follows: 1. In the SAP Fiori Launchpad window, open the Discover Business Partners app by clicking the app tile. 2. Discover and invite data contributors. 3. After the data contributor accepts your invitation, update data contributor's LBN ID. 4. Assign technical user roles to data contributor's technical user. Invite Business Partners App Use this app to send connection invitations to data contributors that you already know. It is especially useful when you want to invite a number of data contributors all at once. For example, you have just onboarded to the network and want to invite all the data contributors that already exist in your backend SAP TM system. To invite data contributors with the app, proceed as follows: 1. In the SAP Fiori Launchpad window, open the Invite Business Partners app by clicking the app tile. 2. Add new data contributors to your data contributors list. 3. Submit connection invitations. 4. After the data contributor accepts your invitation, update data contributor's LBN IDs. For more information on role assignment, see Solution Owner Onboarding in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners: 5/12/26, 6:45 AM 5 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 9 -- 5. Assign technical user roles to data contributor's technical user. Next Steps For more information about the administrative tasks and track and trace activities, explore the user assistance by calling up the in- app help via the  Open Help icon on the SAP Fiori Launchpad. The following sections in the user assistance may be of interest to you: Role Activity Document SAP Consultant Modeling and testing the tracking scenairo Guide for Model Administrators Connecting to SAP S/4HANA How to Send Documents from SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace Sending documents to other SAP systems How to Send Documents from SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace to Other Systems Business User Getting started with fulfillment tracking apps Fulfillment Tracking Apps in the guide Application Help IT Administrator Monitoring message transactions Guide for Message Log Administrators Frequently Asked Questions This section answers the questions that are frequently asked when you get started. It covers questions about onboarding, user authentication, subscription failures, signing in, inviting business partners, and getting support. Welcome Emails What if I didn't receive the email for activating my Identity Authentication account? An Identity Authentication tenant is provided to customers who haven't got an existing tenant. If you are an SAP partner with the cloud test&demo license of the product, you can use SAP ID Service (S-user or P-user) as the identity provider. If you are a customer, your company may have already got an Identity Authentication tenant. To find your company's existing tenants and administrators, see Viewing Assigned Tenants and Administrators or create an incident with component BC-IAM-IDS. Then ask the administrator to grant you the Manage Groups authorization of the tenant so that you could proceed with the onboarding. What if the activation link in the email for activating Identity Authentication account is invalid or already used? Please follow the advice in SAP note 2637748 or create an incident with component BC-IAM-IDS. Onboarding 5/12/26, 6:45 AM 6 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 9 -- If I have an existing Identity Authentication tenant that SAP offered me in the past, can I use it for SAP Business Network for Logistics? Yes. The same tenant can be used for multiple SAP cloud solutions. If your company has already got an Identity Authentication tenant, you won't get a new one upon the purchase of SAP Business Network for Logistics. Do I need a standalone Cloud Foundry subaccount for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace? Yes, we recommend that you use a standalone Cloud Foundry subaccount. What if my subscription to the global track and trace apps fail? If your subscription fails, please follow the instructions displayed in the error message on your screen. What is the URL for signing in to SAP Business Network for Logistics? After performing the onboarding process, you can find the sign-in URL as follows: 1. In the SAP BTP cockpit, go to the subaccount that you created for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. 2. In the left-hand pane, choose Services Instances and Subscriptions . 3. In the Subscriptions table, click the  Go to Application icon to the right of the app name Global Track and Trace, Solution Owner. This displays the sign-in page for the network. You’re recommended to bookmark the URL so you can sign-in more easily in the future. If you have added other users for your apps, send this URL to them so that they could sign-in with their own sign-in credentials. If I'm not the admin user, how can I confirm the URL for my company tenant? If you don't know your company tenant name or who is the administrator, you can follow the steps from Viewing Assigned Tenants and Administrators. What is the sig-in user name/password I should use to sign in to SAP Business Network for Logistics? If you are the administrator who receives the email for activating your Identity Authentication account, use that user (email) and the password you set to sign in to the network. If during the onboarding process, you, as an administrator, have added other users in Identity Authentication, each of them will either receive the “Activate Your Account for User Profile” email or receive the user (email) and initial password from you (dependent on the option you selected when creating the new user). That is the user credential they should use to sign in to the network. The number of apps that each user can see after the sign-in is dependent on the role collections assigned to the user. For more information, see Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users. What if I forget my password for signing in to SAP Business Network for Logistics? On the sign-in page, click Forgot Password. You'll receive the instruction for resetting your password. After signing in, I saw an empty page with a message "Where to". What should I do? The reason might be: 5/12/26, 6:45 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 9 -- When you entered your username and password on the sign-in page, the page has timed out. In that case, reopen the sign- in page and sign in again. You haven't subscribed Global Track and Trace, Solution Owner. In that case, go to your subaccount in SAP BTP and subscribe the app. If the issue still exists, please create an incident with component SBN-LBN-GTT. After signing on, I saw an empty page with a message "Authorization Request Error". What should I do? You may try the following: If you use Identity Authentication as the IdP forSAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, make sure you have performed the steps as described in Establish Trust Between Your Subaccount and Identity Authentication Tenant. Make sure you have created the user in SAP ID Service or Identity Authentication and assigned the user the appropriate role collections. If the issue still exists, please create an incident with component SBN-LBN-GTT. Can I add business user roles into the role collection that I assign to the technical user? Do not add any business user roles into the role collection you assign to the technical user. Although the system allows you to do it when adding the roles, you won't be able to open the business user apps on SAP Fiori Launchpad. For more, see Create a Technical User and Assign Role Collection. Inviting Business Partners How do I know the status of the connection invitation that I sent to a business partner? If you use the Invite Business Partners app to submit an invitation, you can check its status in the Status column: After an invitation is submitted, the invitee is moved to the In Progress worklist. The status Invitation email sent to business partner means that SAP has sent an email to invite the business partner to register to the network. The status Routed to business partner means the invitee has registered to the network and received your invitation, but not yet accepted (or rejected) it. After the invitee accepts (or rejects) your invitation, the invitee is moved to the Accepted (or Rejected) worklist, and the status changes to Accepted (or rejected). If you use the Discover Business Partners app to send the invitation, when your search for the business partner, you'll see the Connection Status in business partner information changes to Connected after the invitee accepts your invitation. I've sent an invitation to a business partner using the Invite Business Partners app, but the business partner didn't receive it. What should I do? You may first check the business partner's email address. If it's correct, then create an incident with component SBN-LBN-BP-OB. I've sent an invitation to a business partner using the Invite Business Partners app, but would like to resend it because the business partner contact email is incorrect or has changed. What should I do? If the invitation is still in progress, you may try recall it in the In Progress worklist and then submit a new invitation with the correct email address. If the recall fails, please create an incident with component SBN-LBN-BP-OB. 5/12/26, 6:45 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 9 -- After I invite a business partner, what should the business partner do to connect with me? To get started with the network and connect with you, the business partner can refer to the following step-by-step guide on SAP Help portal: Activate Your Account The guide is available in multiple languages. Select a language option beside the title. Getting Support How to create an incident (report an issue) and get support? If you encounter technical issues or require technical support, you may create an incident (report an issue) using the Get Support app, which is part of the Services & Support dashboard in SAP for Me. Sign in with your S-User ID. For detailed process, see Get Support Application Online Help . If you use a component to categorize your issue, use SBN-LBN-OB (for onboarding relevant issues) or SBN-LBN-GTT (for other issues with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace). If you don't know your S-User ID, see the next question. To create an incident, I need to provide my S-user ID. What if I don't know my S-user ID? If you don't have the sign-in credentials of your S-User, contact a user administrator in your organization. If you have trouble identifying who the user administrator is in your organization, please call the Customer Interaction Center (CIC) . For more information, see the SAP for Me Online Help under Access and Authorizations . Miscellaneous Why is it not possible to upload my company logo to my business profile? When uploading your company logo in the Manage Business Profile app, verify if the logo meets size limitation: 2 MB 5/12/26, 6:45 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 9 --

file://api-specs/split/GTT_SAP_BN4L_Prem.content: PUBLIC Integration Platform Migration Guide for Premium Users of SAP Business Network for Logistics Relevant for the following company roles: • Shippers of SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration • Solution owners of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace • Network owners and network participants of SAP Business Network Material Traceability Document Version: 1.7 Date: 2025-06-21 -- 1 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 2 / 18 Table of contents Introduction ................................................................................................................................................................. 3 Overview ....................................................................................................................................................................... 4 Who Is the Target Audience of this Guide? ................................................................................................... 6 Data Center-Specific Integration Platform..................................................................................................... 7 How to identify your tenant’s data center? .................................................................................................................................... 7 Why Migrate? .............................................................................................................................................................. 7 Changes for Premium Users ................................................................................................................................. 8 Existing Connections in SAP Business Network for Logistics ............................................................................................ 8 Configuration Changes.................................................................................................................................................................................. 9 Inbound to SAP Business Network for Logistics ..................................................................................................................................................... 9 Outbound from SAP Business Network for Logistics ....................................................................................................................................... 12 Monitoring of Integration Logs .......................................................................................................................... 17 Test Case for Smoke Testing ............................................................................................................................. 17 Other Configurations Apps ................................................................................................................................. 18 Support ........................................................................................................................................................................ 18 -- 2 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 3 / 18 Introduction SAP Business Network for Logistics is run on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) leveraging the various services provided by the platform. SAP BTP offers a variety of application environments that customers and internal SAP organizations can choose from, to build SAP applications and business solutions in the cloud. One critical service used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is the SAP Cloud Integration (previously known as SAP CPI) which acts as the single integration platform for all customers and partners of SAP Business Network for Logistics. This platform is owned and maintained by the SAP Business Network for Logistics development team. Customers and partners can maintain necessary connectivity configurations using apps such as ‘System Connections’, ‘Configure Partner Connections’, etc. Customers can also monitor the messages relevant to them via ‘Manage Integration Logs’. SAP Cloud Integration used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is hosted in Neo environment of SAP BTP. SAP BTP, Neo environment is the oldest of the application environments and is built on a proprietary SAP technology stack. The Neo environment in SAP BTP has been deprecated and will be sunset for internal SaaS applications (see SAP Note). SAP Cloud Integration is also offered in a multi-cloud foundation in SAP BTP, and this is the new platform that will be used by SAP Business Network for Logistics. In accordance with SAP BTP’s decision to sunset Neo environment, SAP Business Networks for Logistics has decided to stop the support of the existing Neo integration platform on July 18, 2025, as part of our July 2025 release. This means that the connectivity to your backend transportation management system (TMS) will stop working if you don’t migrate your connections to the new integration platform before the mentioned date. This applies for our premium customers connecting to SAP Business Network for Logistics from SAP S/4HANA system using SOAP messages. This guide provides a comprehensive list of changes that a premium customer must do to migrate from the old integration platform to the new one. For a solution owner in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, this impacts the integration platform used for location replication via the DRF framework in SAP Business Network for Logistics. As a result, you need to migrate your existing connections (from your SAP-backend systems) to the new integration platform in SAP Business Network for Logistics hosted in SAP BTP, multi-cloud environment. Please note that this does not impact the connectivity from your backend SAP system to your SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace tenant via destinations created in your sub-account. No changes are required over there. We understand the critical role that connectivity plays in SAP Business Network for Logistics. The primary focus is not to disrupt the existing integrations between your backend systems and SAP Business Network for Logistics. So, your existing configurations will stay intact and continue to work until you migrate to the new integration platform or till the end of support of the old integration platform (July 18, 2025). In the meanwhile, we have made it possible for you to migrate from the old platform to new one using the configuration apps in SAP Business Network for Logistics. This requires some changes in SAP Business Network for Logistics configuration apps as well as in your backend systems. You might also need to update your firewall/SAP Cloud Connector configurations as the subaccount of integration platform and the IP range will be different for the new integration platform. We urge you to migrate as soon as possible because the new platform is much more stable, and the old platform will go into a maintenance mode. New platform features will be focused on the new integration platform. Please note: You mustn’t delete your existing configurations in your System Connections app at any step of the migration activity. Your existing connections are required for the connectivity of any existing documents in the network. If you delete the existing connection, connectivity for your existing documents in the network will stop to work. -- 3 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 4 / 18 Additionally, we recommend performing the migration activities in your test tenants first and then monitor if all the integration scenarios are working correctly. Proceed with the changes in your productive tenants accordingly. Overview The below diagram depicts a high-level integration architecture for customers connecting directly from their SAP backend system to SAP Business Network for Logistics. As shown below, your backend systems are connected to the network via connections created in your System Connections app that point to the existing integration platform, which is SAP Cloud Integration – Neo environment. When you use a direct connection, you’ll require an SAP Cloud Connector configuration to allowlist the calls coming to your SAP backend landscape from a cloud application. Migrating to a new integration platform means that you need to create a new connection in your System Connections app and change the destination and authentication configurations in your backend system as well as your SAP Cloud Connector configurations. -- 4 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 5 / 18 For a customer integrating to SAP Business Network for Logistics via their own cloud integration platform such as an SAP Cloud Integration tenant, the configuration changes will be mainly in the SAP Cloud Integration platform (in addition to a new connection in the System Connections app). No changes are required in your SAP Cloud Connector tenant. The steps to enable this switch from the old connection to the new one is detailed out in the following sections. -- 5 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 6 / 18 Who Is the Target Audience of this Guide? This guide captures detailed steps for customers who configured connectivity in SAP Business Network for Logistics before August 17, 2024 in the Neo integration platform. You can identify the integration platform used for your connection in the System Connections app by looking at the ‘Neo’ or ‘Multi-Cloud’ tag in the UI. New customers can refer to our administration guide and SAP Community blog which capture the configuration steps in detail. Destination URLs and configurations for ‘Multi-Cloud’ integration platform are updated over there. Important Notes: For customers of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, a migration is only required if you have set up location replication from SAP Data Replication Framework (SAP DRF) in your backend system using the LocationBulkReplicationRequest SOAP message. You only need to follow the configuration changes mentioned in the Inbound to SAP Business Network for Logistics chapter and can ignore the Outbound from SAP Business Network for Logistics section. For customers of SAP Business Network Material Traceability, a migration is only required if you have enabled an inbound connection to the network for the PostMaterialTraceabilityEventNotification or MaterialTraceabilityEventNotificationMessage SOAP message using configurations in the System Connections app. You only need to follow the configuration changes mentioned in the Inbound to SAP Business Network for Logistics chapter and can ignore the Outbound from SAP Business Network for Logistics section. -- 6 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 7 / 18 Data Center-Specific Integration Platform SAP Business Networks for Logistics is available in two different data centers – EU and US. There are dedicated integration tenants for customers in each data center – one for EU and one for US. In this migration guide, you’ll see a mention of endpoints/IP addresses of these two data centers. Please ensure that you update your configurations by referring to the data center where your tenant is hosted. How to identify your tenant’s data center? If you are unsure about your tenant’s datacenter, this can be identified from the ‘eu10’/’us20’ tag in the host URL of your SAP Business Networks for Logistics tenant. URL in SAP Business Network for Logistics Data Center https://shipper01.lbn.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/ EU https://lbn-shipper01.lbn.cfapps.us20.hana.ondemand.com/ US Why Migrate? Apart from the sunset of integration platform, the migration to the new platform has its benefits. Listing some of these below: • Improved data persistence resources for integration logs: In the current integration platform, resources for database are limited and at the maximum possible limit. Customers rely on integration logs and payload download feature to debug/validate any integration issues. If the DB memory limit is breached, integration scenarios would work fine but there would be discrepancies in the way logs/payloads are stored. Migrating to the new platform will ensure proper log monitoring and payload download. • Improved security for communication between SAP Business Networks for Logistics apps: Better authentication protocols will be deployed for communication between SAP Business Networks for Logistics backend apps and the new integration platform. • New features: Improvements to platform features will be based on the new integration platform. Some of these upcoming features include hourly auto-reprocessing of failed/escalated logs. • Self-configuration to set up inbound communication for freemium customers: Freemium customers such as ‘carriers’ used to rely on the ticketing process to set up inbound authentication/communication to SAP Business Networks for Logistics. This was true for both API and EDI communications. Part of this was because of a lack of support from the older integration platform. In upcoming releases, we intend to make these provisioning available via configuration apps for freemium customers. -- 7 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 8 / 18 Changes for Premium Users Existing Connections in SAP Business Network for Logistics Your existing connections in the System Connections app will be untouched. Even though new connections will be used to connect from your backend system to SAP Business Network for Logistics via the new integration platform, existing documents created in your SAP Business Network for Logistics apps (such as Freight Orders for Confirmation, Freight Orders for Settlement, etc.) refer to the old connections to communicate back to your SAP backend systems. This means that a confirmation message for a freight order created prior to the migration will work only if the original connection is unchanged. The existing connections in SAP Business Network for Logistics that point to the old integration platform will be highlighted and have a differentiator called ‘Neo’ as follows: Note: Any new connection created in the app since June 22, 2024, will be marked with a new ‘Multi-cloud’ differentiator and you need to use the API URLs and configurations mentioned in this guide for any new connection. -- 8 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 9 / 18 Configuration Changes For customers of SAP Business Network for Logistics who wish to connect their backend TMS system – SAP Transportation Management standalone (SAP TM) or TM in SAP S/4HANA, the following changes are required to migrate from the old platform to the new one. Inbound to SAP Business Network for Logistics • The most significant change is that the SAP Business Network for Logistics endpoint will be changed to the new integration platform. This means that configurations for outbound from your SOAMANAGER or SAP PI/PO or SAP Cloud Integration system must be updated. You must use the following new URL for Provider SOAP APIs in SAP Business Network for Logistics: Data Center Inbound SOAP URL EU https://api.logistics.eu.business-network.cloud.sap/cxf/lbn/b2b/soap/v1 US https://api.logistics.us.business-network.cloud.sap/cxf/lbn/b2b/soap/v1 -- 9 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 10 / 18 • You must generate new key-pairs (client certificates -. p12 files) to authenticate the inbound communication to SAP Business Network for Logistics. You must not continue to use the existing client certificates. The new key-pairs must be uploaded in the ‘STRUST’ transaction and the same must be updated in the SOAMANAGER configuration: • As the endpoint is now changed, this means that SSL certificates are also different and must be updated in the STRUST configuration. Navigate to the host URL mentioned above (depending on your data center) in a browser. If prompted for a credential, click on Cancel. Click on the configure/secure icon in the URL bar and navigate to the Certificate viewer. Download the root certificate and upload it in STRUST. -- 10 of 10 --

You can continue to edit the existing connections. There is a differentiator in the UI to help you identify between old and new connection types. For old connections, a banner is present – ‘This connection’s integration platform has been deprecated’. Any new connection created in the System Connections app since the release will point to the new integration platform. You won’t be able to create new connections in the System Connections app that point to the older platform. -- 1 of 8 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 12 / 18 Outbound from SAP Business Network for Logistics • In the System Connections app, open ‘Manage Cloud Connector Details’. Maintain a new cloud connector location ID and an email ID. You need to add the new integration platform’s sub-account in your SAP Cloud Connector configuration. To add the new platform in your SAP Cloud Connector, the authentication is enabled via email ID instead of S-User ID. This is the email linked to your S-User in the SAP ID service. The existing location ID must not be re-used, and a new location ID must be added. This is because the existing connection should remain as mentioned before. • In the ‘Outbound from Network’ tab, maintain the backend system URL for service interfaces. • In the ‘Configure Connections’ tab, maintain the ‘Active Authentication Type’. − If you choose ‘Cloud Connector with Basic Authentication’, maintain the location ID and email ID that you configured above. − If you choose ‘Client Certificate’, please note that the certificate chains are different for the old platform and the new one. ‘Download Certificate Chain’ will contextually download the old/new certificate chain -- 2 of 8 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 13 / 18 depending on which connection you’ve chosen. Make sure that you download from the new connection and use the same for your Outbound from Network authentication. This certificate must be configured in your intermediate cloud integration system (for example: SAP Cloud Integration) for authenticating the calls from SAP Business Network for Logistics to your integration system. • Changes in your Cloud Connector tenant If you are directly connecting to your ABAP backend systems from SAP Business Network for Logistics, you need to add the new SAP Cloud Integration sub-account in your cloud connector. The existing connection that you created refers to the old integration tenant and you need to re-do the process for the new platform as well. Please note that the old configuration in your SAP Cloud Connector tenant must not be changed/deleted as it’s required for the execution of existing documents. Your existing connection will remain as-is: Additionally, you need to add the new SAP Business Network for Logistics integration subaccount as well. − For customers in EU10 data center, the configuration is as below: -- 3 of 8 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. We’ve also added a new column to make this clear to customers. The app also supports the reprocessing of messages failed/escalated in both these platforms. Test Case for Smoke Testing • SAP S/4HANA backend to Network – Once the configuration changes are done, check if the messages have been received in your shipper tenant. You should be able to see these messages in the Manage Integration Logs app as well. − For example: In your SAP S/4HANA system, open a Road Freight Order. − Send the freight order to SAP Business Network for Logistics by Subcontracting -> Send to Carrier. − Check if the Freight Order is created in the carrier’s Freight Order for Confirmation app in SAP Business Network for Logistics. • Network to SAP S/4HANA – For any outbound from SAP Business Network for Logistics, check if the confirmation messages have been received successfully in your SAP S/4HANA backend and if the log is visible in your Manage Integration Logs app. − For example: Confirm the Freight Order created in the previous step from your carrier app. − Check if the Freight Order status is updated in your backend SAP S/4HANA system. • In case of any failures, please check the integration logs in your SRT_MONI/SXI_MONI transactions in the SAP S/4HANA backend, integration logs in your intermediate cloud integration platform (if any) and Manage Integration Logs in SAP Business Network for Logistics in the respective order. -- 7 of 8 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. file://api-specs/split/GTT_uide for Mode.content: Guide for Model Administrators Generated on: 2026-05-12 07:01:40 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace | LBN Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_GTT_OPTION/53fd87f0f8fd43a7921edb9874f40567?locale=en- US&state=PRODUCTION&version=LBN Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Introduction About This Document This documentation describes how to perform all the tasks required to manage version 2 models for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. This involves using the following apps: Manage Models (MM) app Check Processes and Events (CPE) app Target Audience The target audience for this guide is Administrator – Data Models (GTT). Prerequisites You are able to sign in to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace as an Administrator – Data Models (GTT). About Global Track and Trace The main purpose of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace is to track processes that are influenced by business events. All tracked processes and business events have a common core behavior and share a common set of basic attributes. Therefore, SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace consists of the following: A core engine: provides generic functionality to track processes, handle business events and provide the modeling environment described in this document. GTT apps: enrich the core engine’s generic functionality by adding domain specific semantics in terms of data and behavior. Basic Terms The applications of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace deal with the following central objects and terms: Tracked Process A tracked process comprises the following: Involved parties acting in or being affected by the process. Track multiple other processes. A set of planned events that are expected to happen within the tracked process.  Note Planned events are called “milestones” in SAP ERP applications like SAP Event Management. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- A set of events that actually happened against the process. This could be a realization of a planned event or also an unplanned event. Event Events can be planned events or unplanned events that might occur during a process. When an event happens, it becomes an actual event. An actual event needs to be matched against a planned event of that process. If not, it becomes an unplanned event. Planned Event A planned event: Has a fixed semantic. Has a planned date and time (with time zone), a tolerance window, a planned location, and other planned data. Examples include: goods issued (planned date: 2016-07-06; planned location: gate 1) goods received (planned date: 2016-07-07; planned location: pack station 801) Unplanned Event A unplanned event: Has a fixed semantic as well. Is not planned, but can be foreseen that it occurs with a certain likelihood, but cannot be planned thus has no planned data. Examples include: delay in delivery, damage of goods. Or is a piece of information at an arbitrary point in time, such as the current position and temperature of a container. Actual Event An actual event: Is an event that actually happened. Is either matched against a planned event of a process and complements planned data with actual data or becomes an unplanned event of the process. Triggers changes of attributes of a tracked process. Timestamps Every event, planned or actual, has two timestamps: 1. (planned/actual) business timestamp: the time at which the event physically happens. 2. (planned/actual) technical timestamp: the time at which a user reports the event in the system. Usually, the timestamps for the same event are different, with the time of the business timestamp before that of the technical. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The timestamp uses the UTC time. The event status is determined by comparing the planned business timestamp with that of the actual. Example 1: The times in the timestamps for an “arrival” event are as follows: Planned business timestamp: 2:00 pm Actual business timestamp: 2:30 pm Actual technical timestamp: 3:00 pm The comparison of planned and actual business timestamps determines the event status: Planned business timestamp: 2:00 pm Actual business timestamp: 2:30 pm So the event status is Late. Reporting an Event Again: The situation is more complicated if the same event is reported again, or even multiple times. Then the sequence of actual events is determined by the setting you made when you created or edited the tracked process for Affect Planned Event Status By. You can select either: Actual Business Timestamp or Actual Technical Timestamp. For more information, see Create Tracked Process. But in either case, the new timestamp must be later than the previous one, otherwise it is ignored. Example 2: As in the previous example, the times in the timestamps for an “arrival” event are as follows: Planned business timestamp: 2:00 pm Actual business timestamp 1: 2:30 pm (So the event status is Late.) Actual technical timestamp 1: 3:00 pm The event is reported for a second time with the following timestamps: Actual business timestamp 2: 1:00 pm Actual technical timestamp 2: 4:00 pm If you set: Affect Planned Event Status By actual business timestamp, then: The actual business timestamp is used to determine the sequence of actual events. As the second actual business timestamp (1:00 pm) is before that of the first (2:30 pm), the second timestamp is ignored.  Note For simplicity in the following examples, only one planned business timestamp is used to determine the event status. In practice, rather than a single planned business timestamp, a range is used from the planned business earliest timestamp to the planned business latest timestamp. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- So, the actual business timestamp remains as 2:30 pm and the event status remains Late. If you set: Affect Planned Event Status By actual technical timestamp, then: The actual technical timestamp is used to determine the sequence of actual events. As the second actual technical timestamp (4:00 pm) is after that of the first (3:00 pm), the second timestamp is valid and the actual technical timestamp becomes 4:00 pm. Event status is then determined by comparing the second event’s actual business timestamp with that of the planned. As the actual business timestamp (1:00 pm) is before the planned business timestamp (2:00 pm), the event status becomes Early. Structure Different models can be created in the MM app. Each model must contain one or more tracked process types and event types. Each tracked process type and event type contain some predefined core model fields that you cannot change. You can add user- defined fields to each tracked process type and event type. For each tracked process type, some event types can be specified as an: Admissible Planned Event type: specifies the event types that can be used in planned events of a tracked process with this process type. Admissible Unplanned Event type: specifies the event types that can be used in unplanned events of a tracked process with this process type. As shown in the following diagram, some other field types can be defined: Tracked process type Event type Field type Model Overview Page The MM app starts by opening the Model Overview page. This lists up to 20 models. The model count is displayed at the bottom. For example: (20/100) indicates that 20 models are displayed of a total of 100. If there are more than 20 models, click the More button to see the next 20. The information on each model is displayed on a model card. To find your model, you can simply check the list or search by typing its model name. To select your model, click its model card. Also, on the Model Overview page, you can do the following: 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 5 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Create a model Import a model Export a model Delete a model Refresh the latest data of models on the page by clicking the Refresh icon. On the top right, a Sample Codes menu is provided with a direct link to download the sample codes: For Fulfillment Tracking Apps: links to the following GTT repository in the SAP Samples organization on GitHub.com where you can download the SAP ERP sample codes of fulfillment tracking apps: https://github.com/SAP-samples/logistics- business-network-gtt-standardapps-samples Help and Support There are several ways you can find help and support on the Fiori launchpad of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Built-In Support Built-in support provides efficient, simplified and guided support channels, you can search for knowledge, ask for needed information, get help from recommended solutions. Currently, expert chat is not supported. To access the built-in support service on the Fiori Launchpad, click the icon  on the right corner of the screen. You will see a welcome page where you can sign in, and a list of recommended links for the page. To gain full access to the built-in functions, you must activate your S-user. For more, see Activating Built-In Support Services. For more information on how to use this tool, refer to Built-In Support on SAP Help Portal. In-app Help When you launch the app, you can turn on the in-app help that provides on-screen explanations of key fields and areas on the screen. To turn on the in-app help, on the top right on the screen, click the  icon. Once the in-app help is turned on, you can: search the displayed help topics for the text that you type; click the  icon to see the help texts on that topic; click the link tiles to see the documentation of this app on SAP Help Portal; hide the Help Topics panel by clicking the  button on the bottom right. Standard and User Models You have a choice of two types of model: 1. Standard models are predefined and delivered in the product. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 6 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- 2. User models are created by model administrators. The standard model is consumed by the Fulfillment Tracking apps. It provides: standard tracked processes with model fields, planned and unplanned events in the Tracked Process tab standard field types with model fields in the Field Type Pool tab standard event types with model fields in the Event Type Pool tab standard code lists with model codes in the Code List tab standard IDOC mapping in the IDOC Integration tab standard visibility provider mapping in the Visibility Provider Integration tab standard planned event extensions in the Planned Event Extension tab standard declaration and script in the Event to Action tab. You cannot delete a standard model. You can edit it to create user-defined tracked processes, field types, event types, code lists, planned event extensions, and event-to-action scripts. User-defined fields in the standard model also support IDOC mapping and visibility provider mapping. The standard model is integrated with LBN code lists. The Model Card The information displayed on the model card includes: Name: in lower case with numerals except as the first character. For example, process17 or salesorder317. The name must be unique in the tenant. Draft version status: Blank: the model’s draft version is the same as the deployed version. Draft: displayed as . The model’s draft version is different from the deployed version. Deployed version status: Blank: the model has not been deployed. Active: displayed as . The deployed version is active, meaning that the write/read services of the model are running. Inactive: displayed as . The deployed version is inactive, meaning that the write/read services of the model are disabled. Description: up to 255 characters describing the model. Namespace: identifies the model and includes its name. This is unique across SAP Business Network for Logistics.  Note The name of user-defined tracked processes, field types, event types, code lists, and planned event extensions must start with the case-insensitive letters “ZZ”. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Last Operation Status: The icon for each stage is color-coded, so you can see its status at a glance: green for success, red for error, and orange for warning and pending. Deployment Success Deployment Warning Deployment Pending Deployment Error Deletion Pending Deletion Error Event to Action Log: For more, see Enable/Disable Event to Action Log of the Model. Off: the Event to Action Log is disabled. On: the Event to Action Log is enabled. Email Rules: takes you to the Email Rules page where you can create and define email rules for email notifications. For more, see Define the Rule on the Configuration UI Import Model Context You can import a single model from a JSON file that is sized below 2MB. Procedure 1. On the Model Overview page, click the Import button 2. In the pop-up dialog, click the Browse… button to select a JSON file to upload. Once you have selected your file, click Import. 3. When the file is uploaded, you see one of the following three kinds of messages: Error: The message identifies what went wrong, such as a broken file, an unreadable file or one with incompatible data structure. It may also suggest what to do next. Warning: When the name of the uploaded model already exists in the MM app, you must confirm whether to overwrite the existing model or abort the upload. Success: Your imported model was created successfully. Export Model Context You can export a single model as a JSON file. Procedure 1. On the Model Overview page, select the model you want to export, then click the Export button. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- 2. A pop-up dialog appears. If the model is already deployed, you can choose to export either the draft version or the deployed version. If the model is not deployed, you can only export the draft version. 3. After you have chosen the version you want, click Export. The exported JSON file is automatically downloaded to your browser. You can find it in your local download file path Delete Model Context You can delete one model at a time. Procedure 1. On the Model Overview page, select the model you want to delete, then click the Delete button. 2. A confirmation message box appears. You can choose to continue or abort. 3. If you continue, you get a success message when deletion is complete. If you meet an error, the Last Operation Status becomes Deletion Error, and you can view the model history to check the details. Related Information View the Model History Create and Deploy a Model Create a Model from Scratch Context The MM app allows you to create a model from scratch. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. 2. On the Model Overview page, click the Create button. The detail page of a blank model then appears. 3. On the Model Details page, you can do the following: In the Header tab, fill in the model header information. See Model Header for details. In the Tracked Process tab, create one or more tracked processes. In each tracked process, create user-defined fields, planned events and unplanned events. See Tracked Process for details. In the Field Type Pool tab, create field types. They can be used as the Composition type when you define user- defined fields for a tracked process. See Field Type for details. In the Event Type Pool tab, create event types. They can be used when you define planned/unplanned events for a tracked process. See Event Type for details. In the Code List tab, create code lists. They can be used as the Code List type when you define user-defined fields for a tracked process. See Code List for details. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- In the IDOC Integration tab, define the IDOC integration mapping rules for a tracked process. See IDOC Integration for details. In the Visibility Provider Integration tab, define the visibility provider integration mapping rules for a tracked process. See Visibility Provider Integration for details. In the Planned Event Extension tab, create planned event extension fields. See Planned Event Extension for details. In the Event to Action tab, define the event-to-action rules for the model. (This replaces the business rules used in the Version 1 of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace.) See Event to Action (Business Rules) for details. 4. Save your model configuration. Edit an Existing Model Context The MM app allows you to import and edit a model. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. 2. On the Model Overview page, you can either: import the model you want to edit by clicking the Import button, or select an existing model. The detail page of a model then appears. 3. On the top right, click the Edit button. 4. On the Model Details page, you can do the following: In the Header tab, edit the model header information. See Model Header for details. In the Tracked Process tab, edit tracked processes or create new ones. In each tracked process, edit/create user- defined fields, planned events and unplanned events. See Tracked Process for details. In the Field Type Pool tab, edit field types or create new ones. They can be used as the Composition type when you define user-defined fields for a tracked process. See Field Type for details. In the Event Type Pool tab, edit event types or create new ones. They can be used when you define planned/unplanned events for a tracked process. See Event Type for details. In the Code List tab, edit code lists or create new ones. They can be used as the Code List type when you define user-defined fields for a tracked process. See Code List for details. In the IDOC Integration tab, edit the IDOC integration mapping rules for a tracked process or define new ones. See IDOC Integration for details. In the Visibility Provider Integration tab, edit the visibility provider integration mapping rules for a tracked process or define new ones. See Visibility Provider Integration for details. In the Planned Event Extension tab, edit planned event extension fields or create new ones. See Planned Event Extension for details. In the Event to Action tab, edit the event-to-action rules for the model or define new ones. See Event to Action (Business Rules) for details. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 10 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --
