file://api-specs/split/GTT_uide for Mode.content: 5. Save your model configuration. Deploy a Model Context When you have created a model, you can deploy the model directly. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. 2. On the Model Overview page, click the model you want to deploy. The detail page of the model then appears. 3. On the Model Details page, click the Deploy button on the top right. The model is then deployed. Model Header Context In the Header tab, you can fill in the following basic information about the model: Name Description Namespace Correlation Level. Correlation level: is the level of event correlation propagation between tracked processes within a model. is specified as an integer from 1 to 5. Each tracked process has a list of observed tracked processes. You can add a tracked process to the observed tracked process list by the tracked process creation/update event or by some other actual events. For example, suppose there is an event correlation chain between tracked processes A, B, and C, which means that tracked process A observes tracked process B and tracked process B observes tracked process C. If the model is configured to have 1 level of correlation, then events reported to tracked process C are also correlated to B. If the model is configured to have 2 levels of correlation, then events reported to tracked process C are also correlated to both A and B. And so on. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 11 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Note that the event correlation chain between tracked processes breaks up in the following two cases: When tracked processes are of the same type: In this example, if tracked processes A and C are of the same type, then the event correlation chain breaks up between B and A. So events reported to tracked process C are correlated to B, but not to A. When the actual event’s event type is not defined as an admissible planned or unplanned event in this tracked process: In this example, if a Proof of Delivery planned/unplanned event has been defined in tracked processes C and A, but not in B, then when the Proof of Delivery actual event is reported to C, the event correlation chain breaks up between B and C. So the Proof of Delivery actual event reported to C won’t be correlated to B and A, even if there is a Proof of Delivery planned/unplanned event defined in A. Also note that the authorization for instances can also be inherited and checked through correlation. So in this example: If you have authorization for tracked process C, you will also have authorization for B and A. Then events reported to C are also correlated to B and A. If you don’t have authorization for tracked process C, the system will check if you have authorization for B. If so, events will be reported to B and correlated to A. Otherwise, the system will check if you have authorization for A. If tracked process C doesn’t exist, the system will check if you have authorization for B. If so, events will be reported to B and correlated to A. Otherwise, the system will check if you have authorization for A. Procedure To complete the model header, do the following: 1. Fill in the mandatory field: Name. It must meet the following requirements: It's unique from other models in the same tenant. It starts with a lowercase letter and then lowercase letters or numbers. It cannot start with letters “gtt”. It's less than 50 characters. 2. When the model name is set, the Namespace will be filled automatically. 3. Fill in the Description. 4. Fill in the Correlation Level in the range from 1 to 5. Tracked Process 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 12 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- A tracked process is the main object in the model. Each model must have at least one tracked process. The name of the tracked process must be unique in the model. You can create/edit/delete your own tracked process. You can have at most 200 tracked processes in a model. In the Tracked Process tab, user-defined tracked processes are listed on the left. Select one tracked process in the list. On the right, there are different views of the tracked process: Field Lists Admissible Planned Events Admissible Unplanned Events. Related Information Basic Terms Create Tracked Process Context You can create a tracked process in the Tracked Process tab. Procedure 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the Create button above the list. 2. Fill in the following: Name: mandatory and must be unique in this model. Description Tracking ID Type: mandatory and must be unique across models in the whole tenant. Affect Planned Event Status By: mandatory. You can select either the Actual Business Timestamp or Actual Technical Timestamp in the drop-down list. The first one is the default. Your selection decides the timestamp the system uses to process the last reported actual event. In turn, this affects the planned event status. For more, see Timestamps. Sort Planned Events By: mandatory and you can select either First Planned Business Timestamp then Payload Sequence or First Payload Sequence then Planned Business Timestamp in the drop-down list. The first one is the default. Your selection decides the sequence of planned events that is used for the tracked process status calculation. You can see the displayed sequence in the Planned Events tab of the CPE app. 3. Click OK. Edit Tracked Process Context After a tracked process is created, you can edit the tracked process attributes. Procedure 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 13 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the tracked process that you want to change. 2. Click the Edit button above the list. 3. In the pop-up dialog, you can edit its name, description and tracking ID type, and change your selection in Affect Planned Event Status By and Sort Planned Events By. 4. When your editing is complete, click OK. The Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Delete Tracked Process Context You can delete a tracked process. Procedure 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the tracked process that you want to delete. 2. Click the Delete button above the list. 3. There are two situations: If this tracked process is not used by other objects, before deletion, a warning message box pops up to ask you if you want to delete the tracked process, its fields, admissible planned events, and admissible unplanned events. Otherwise, a Where Used List pops up to ask you if you want to delete the tracked process and all the data in the places where this tracked process is used. 4. If you click the OK button, the deletion takes effect immediately and the Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Field Lists In the Tracked Process tab, by default, the content of Field Lists is displayed with two tables: User Model Fields: This table contains the user-defined fields in this tracked process. You can create/edit/delete these fields for this tracked process. Core Model Fields: This table contains all the fields from the predefined core model's process types. You cannot modify them. Besides, in a standard tracked processes of the standard model "gttft1", you can also see a Standard Model Fields table. It contains the standard fields in this tracked process. You can edit a string-type or code list-type standard field to add a role attribute. You can have at most 200 fields in a tracked process. Edit Standard Model Fields Context To edit a standard model field, do the following: 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 14 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Click the pencil icon  at the end of the field that needs to be changed in the Standard Model Fields table. 2. Edit in the pop-up dialog. You can only do the following changes: Change the visibility attribute of the field: If you set a field as Visible, it's available in the following UI interfaces of this app, otherwise, it's not: Filters and the worklist settings Information tab of the detail pages. This complements the adapting UI functionality for hiding fields. Assign role attribute: You can edit a string-type or code list-type standard field to add a role attribute. For more information on role attributes, see Specify Attributes in the Role Using “ReadServiceAttributeTemplate” 3. Click OK to save changes. The Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 4. Save your model configuration. Create User Model Field Context To create a user model field, do the following: Procedure 1. Click the Create button above the User Model Fields table. 2. In the pop-up dialog, fill in the following information: Field Explanation Name* The name must be unique in one tracked process. Label  Note While most fields can be hidden using your model configuration, some types of fields will always remain visible in fulfillment tracking apps. These include: Fields Integrated with Master Data: Fields linking to master data (for example, location or business partner master data) must be shown. Combined Fields: fields that combine data from source (for example, Departure Location / Departure Time). These are considered essential for the core functionality and data integrity of the tracking applications and cannot be hidden. Code List Fields with Colors or Icons: Fields that use visual indicators for status (for example, Delay Status, Transportation Mode). Location-Relevant Timestamp fields: Timestamps tied to a geographical location (for example, Actual Arrival At). 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 15 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Field Explanation Type* You can select one of the following types: String: You must also specify the length. Enter a number from 1 to 4000. UUID Boolean Integer Decimal: You must also specify the precision and scale. For Precision, enter a number from 1 to 34. Date Timestamp Association to One: associates to a tracked process, or linked to a tracked process. If you choose this type, you must select a process type. Association to Many: associates to more than one tracked process, based on an Association to One field of this tracked process. If you choose this type, you must select a process type and one of its Association to One field. You can also input values freely to create new fields directly. Composition: an item-level table with a structure. If you choose this type, you must select a field type that you defined in the Field Type Pool tab. Code List: a code list with the string type and a value range. If you choose this type, you must select a code list that you defined in the Code List tab. Attachments: Supported file types are: jpeg, jpg, gif, png, pdf, doc, docx, xls, and xlsx. The maximum file size limit is 10 MB. Attachments-type fields don’t support IDOC integration mapping. Only the event’s attachments- type fields support visibility provider integration mapping. DPP The abbreviation for data protection and privacy. It includes the following selectable values: Personal Identifiable Information and Data Subject ID. There must be only one "Data Subject ID" in one tracked process. Fields annotated as "Data Subject ID" include the properties of "Personal Identifiable Information". Changes to the fields annotated as "Data Subject ID" trigger updates of the PDM data visibility, Audit Log Viewer read log and Audit Log Viewer change log. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 16 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Field Explanation Changes to the fields annotated as "Personal Identifiable Information" trigger updates of the PDM data visibility and Audit Log Viewer change log. For more information, refer to the chapters Security: General and Security: Data Protection and Privacy in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. Grant Only string-type fields can be granted Read or Report. Read: If this field is granted "Read" and the user's LBN ID is equal to this field, then you can read this tracked process where the field exists. Report: If this field is granted "Report" and the user's LBN ID is equal to this field, then you can write this tracked process where the field exists. Role Attribute A role attribute can only be specified to a string-type or code list-type field. It's used to check if a user role has authorization to read this tracked process based on the value of the role attribute defined in SAP BTP cockpit. You can assign at most nine attributes, from gttUserAuthAttribute001 to gttUserAuthAttribute009, to nine different fields in a tracked process. To use this function, you must add the role ReadServiceAttributeTemplate to your role collection and specify attributes in this role in SAP BTP cockpit. For more, see the section Specify Attributes in the Role Using “ReadServiceAttributeTemplate” in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. Readable When reading the tracked process, this field is readable by the OData service. Writable When writing the tracked process, this field is writable. Visible This attribute controls the visibility of the fields in fulfillment tracking apps: If the box is checked, the field is displayed in the fulfillment tracking apps by default. You can hide it with the Adapt UI. If the box is unchecked, the field can't be displayed in the fulfillment tracking apps, even with the Adapt UI. A field must be readable in order to be visible. * mandatory field 3. Click OK to create this field. 4. Save your model configuration. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 17 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Edit User Model Field Context To edit a user model field, do the following: Procedure 1. Click the pencil icon  at the end of the field that needs to be changed in the table. 2. Edit in the pop-up dialog. 3. Click OK to save changes. The Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 4. Save your model configuration. Delete User Model Field Context To delete one or more user model field, do the following: Procedure 1. Select the fields that you want to delete. Multiple selection is supported. 2. Click the Delete button above the User Model Fields table. 3. The To Be Deleted Objects dialog pops up to ask you if you want to delete the selected fields and all the data in the places where these fields are used. 4. Click OK. Fields you selected are removed immediately, and the Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Add URL for User Model Field Context To add a URL for a user model field, do the following: Procedure 1. On the Model Details page, click the Edit button on the top right. 2. Select a user model field whose type is not "Composition", "Attachments", or "Association to Many". 3. Click the Add URL button above the User Model Fields table. 4. Fill in the name and address. The address supports variables. Variables should be in curly brackets, such as {Field1}. The following fields can be used as variables:  Note In the fulfillment tracking apps, after you add a field that is created in the standard model "gttft1" with Adapt UI, deleting it or marking it unreadable in the standard model will lead to errors and improper display of this field. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 18 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- A user model field whose type is not "Composition", "Attachments", or "Association to Many" in this tracked process. A user model field whose type is not "Composition", "Attachments", or "Association to Many" in the associated tracked process, if the type of the field that the URL is added for is "Associate to One". Delete URL for User Model Field Context To delete a URL for a user model field, do the following: Procedure 1. On the Model Details page, click the Edit button on the top right. 2. Find the field whose URL you want to delete. Click the icon in the URLs column. 3. In the pop-up, select the URL that you want to delete. 4. Click the deletion icon . The URL is removed immediately. 5. Click OK. 6. Save your model configuration. Admissible Planned Events To define planned events, you can use admissible planned events. In the Tracked Process tab, click the drop-down of the Content view on the right and switch to the Admissible Planned Events view. All the admissible planned events are listed on the right side of this page. By default, the content of Admissible Planned Events is displayed with a User Model Planned Event Types table. It contains the user-defined planned events in this tracked process. You can add/edit/delete these planned events. Besides, in a standard tracked process for the standard model "gttft1", you can also see a Standard Model Planned Event Types table. It contains the standard planned events in this tracked process. You can only edit these planned events. You can have at most 200 admissible planned events in a tracked process. Create Admissible Planned Event  Note If you want to navigate to the external systems from the fulfillment tracking apps, you must add URLs for user model fields in the standard model “gttft1”. You can add either of the following two types of address: Address with a fixed URL prefix. For example: www.sap.com/?zzdeliveryNo={variable} Address with a URL prefix variable. For example: {URL prefix variable}/?zzdeliveryNo={variable} 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 19 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Context Before doing this task, you must first define one or more event types in the Event Type Pool tab. To create an admissible planned event, do the following: Procedure 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the drop-down of the Content view on the right and switch to the Admissible Planned Events view. 2. Click the Add button above the User Model Planned Event Types table. A pop-up dialog appears. 3. In the Details tab, fill in the following information: Field Explanation Event Type* Select an event type that you defined in the Event Type Pool tab. Note that If the event type is already used by another admissible planned event in the same tracked process, this event type is not selectable and you are not able to select it as an admissible planned event again. The events that inherit GTTDelayedEvent and GTTOnTimeEvent won’t be displayed in the drop- down list. Default Business Tolerance It's used to calculate the earliest planned business timestamp and the latest planned business timestamp, if they are not provided in the event payload. Enter a number that is greater than or equal to 0. The default is 0. Default Technical Tolerance It's used to calculate the earliest planned technical timestamp and the latest planned technical timestamp, if they are not provided in the event payload. Enter a number that is greater than or equal to 0. The default is 0. Periodic Overdue Detection* It's used to define how often you want the system to check the status of overdue events. For example, if you enter 10 minutes, then the system will check the status of overdue events every 10 minutes. Enter a number that is greater than or equal to 5. Max Overdue Detection* It specifies the maximum times that you want the system to check the status of overdue events. For example, if you enter 3, the system will check the overdue events three times and then ignore them even if they are still overdue. Enter a number that is less than or equal to 5. Affect Planned Event Status By Select in the drop-down: 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 20 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/GTT_uide for Mode.content: Field Explanation Actual Business Timestamp: the default. Actual Technical Timestamp Inherit from Tracked Process: inheriting the configuration from your tracked process definition. Your selection decides the timestamp that the system uses to process the last reported actual event. In turn, this affects the planned event status. 4. In the Match Actual Event tab, you can define how an actual event matches an admissible planned event when the actual event is sent to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Define the Match Location value by clicking the switch control. On: The location is used as a match key between the planned event and actual event. The check box of locationAltKey is then enabled in the Match Planned Event tab. Off: The location is not a match key between the planned event and actual event. The check box of locationAltKey is disabled in the Match Planned Event tab. Below the location match condition, you can define match conditions between planned event extension fields and actual event fields. You can add/edit/delete a match condition. The field you added/deleted here will also enable/disable the check box of this field displayed in the Match Planned Event tab. To add a match condition, do the following: a. Click the Add icon  . b. On the left, choose a planned event extension field you defined in the Planned Event Extension tab, the match operator is set as equal by default. On the right, choose an actual event field. The two match fields must be of the same type. Click the Delete icon on the right to delete a corresponding match condition. 5. In the Match Planned Event tab, you can define how a planned event matches an existing admissible planned event when a planned event update or tracked process update is sent to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. You can define the match value by using the check box. The check box of eventType is enabled by default and cannot be changed. Fields that are not defined in the Match Actual Event tab won’t be displayed here. If you don't maintain anything here, the system will fall back to the match conditions in the Match Actual Event tab when matching planned events. 6. Click OK to close the dialog and add a planned event if all checks in the dialog pass. 7. Save your model configuration.  Note If a planned event extension field you used here doesn’t exist in the event types that inherit GTTDelayedEvent, then the system will add this extension field to the event types that inherit GTTDelayedEvent.  Note In the GTT standard model “gttft1”, you cannot change the event type, event match key, and standard fields in the Match Actual Event and Match Planned Event tabs for the events below: standard admissible planned events user-defined admissible planned events with a standard event type. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 21 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Edit Admissible Planned Event Context To edit an admissible planned event, do the following: Procedure 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the drop-down of the Content view on the right and switch to the Admissible Planned Events view. 2. Click the pencil icon  at the end of the planned event that needs to be changed in the table. 3. Edit in the pop-up dialog. 4. Click OK to save changes. The Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Delete Admissible Planned Event Context To delete an admissible planned event, do the following: Procedure 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the drop-down of the Content view on the right and switch to the Admissible Planned Events view. 2. Select the planned events that you want to delete. Multiple selection is supported. 3. Click the Delete button above the User Model Planned Event Types table. 4. Click OK. Planned events you selected are removed immediately, and the Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Admissible Unplanned Events To define unplanned events, you can use admissible unplanned events. In the Tracked Process tab, click the drop-down of the Content view on the right and switch to the Admissible Unplanned Events view. All the admissible unplanned events are listed on the right side of this page. By default, the content of Admissible Unplanned Events is displayed with two tables: User Model Unplanned Event Types: This table contains the user-defined unplanned events in this tracked process. You can add/edit/delete these unplanned events. Core Model Unplanned Event Types: This table contains all the unplanned events from the predefined core model's event types. They are: GTTDelayedEvent, GTTOnTimeEvent, GTTDeletionEvent, and GTTUpdatePlanEvent. You cannot modify them. Besides, in a standard tracked process for the standard model "gttft1", you can also see a Standard Model Unplanned Event Types table. It contains the standard unplanned events in this tracked process. You cannot modify them. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 22 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- You can have at most 200 admissible unplanned events in a tracked process. Create Admissible Unplanned Event Context Before doing this task, you must first define one or more event types in the Event Type Pool tab. To create an admissible unplanned event, do the following: Procedure 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the drop-down of the Content view on the right and switch to the Admissible Unplanned Events view. 2. Click the Add button above the User Model Unplanned Event Types table. A pop-up dialog appears. 3. In the Details tab, select a event type that you defined in the Event Type Pool tab. 4. In the Match Actual Event tab, you can define how an actual event matches an admissible unplanned event when the actual event is sent to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Here, you can add/edit/delete a match condition between: an actual event field and a string field. Only constants, empty and null fields are allowed. an actual event field and a tracked process field. The two match fields should be of the same type. "Attachments", "Composition", "Association to One" and "Association to Many" types are excluded. If the type is "Code List", the two match fields must come from the same code list. For tracked process fields, only standard and user-defined fields are supported. an actual event field and a sub-field in the tracked process composition field. The match condition works when the actual event field matches one of the sub-fields of the composition field. (Composition field means that the field's type is "Association to One" or "Association to Many".) 5. Click OK to close the dialog and add a unplanned event if all checks in the dialog pass. 6. Save your model configuration. Edit Admissible Unplanned Event Context To edit an admissible unplanned event, do the following:  Note The settings here don’t apply to unplanned events whose event type is GTTUpdatePlanEvent. If there's a referred planned event in the actual event payload, the settings also don’t apply to the following actual events: actual events whose event type is GTTOnTimeEvent or GTTDelayedEvent; actual events that inherit GTTOnTimeEvent or GTTDelayedEvent. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 23 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Procedure 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the drop-down of the Content view on the right and switch to the Admissible Unplanned Events view. 2. Click the pencil icon  at the end of the unplanned event that needs to be changed in the table. 3. Edit in the pop-up dialog. 4. Click OK to save changes. The Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Delete Admissible Unplanned Event Context To delete an admissible unplanned event, do the following: Procedure 1. In the Tracked Process tab, click the drop-down of the Content view on the right and switch to the Admissible Unplanned Events view. 2. Select the unplanned events that you want to delete. Multiple selection is supported. 3. Click the Delete button above the User Model Unplanned Event Types table. 4. Click OK. Unplanned events you selected are removed immediately, and the Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Field Type You can create/edit/delete user-defined field type in the Field Type Pool tab. It is used to define the composition of user-defined fields for tracked processes, field types and event types. You can have at most 200 field types in a model. In the Field Type Pool tab, the field types are listed on the left. The User Fields table on the right changes according to the field type you select on the left. Create Field Type Context To create a field type, do the following: Procedure 1. Click the Create button above the Items List. 2. Select the target Tracked Process. 3. Fill in the Name of the field type. The name must be unique in the model. 4. Click the OK button to close the dialog if all the checks pass. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 24 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- 5. On the right side, the User Model Fields table contains user model fields that only belong to this field type. You can have at most 200 user model fields in a field type. You can create/edit/delete user model fields for this field type. To create a user model field, click the Create button above the User Model Fields list. Fill in the name and label. Select a type and define this field’s scope (key, writable, readable and visible) by using the check boxes. For more information on these attributes, see Create User Model Field. To edit a user model field, refer to Edit User Model Field. To delete a user model field, refer to Delete User Model Field. To add a URL for a user model field, refer to Add URL for User Model Field. To delete a URL for a user model field, refer to Delete URL for User Model Field. Edit Field Type Context You can change the field type's name and the tracked process that it belongs to. Procedure 1. Click the Edit button above the Items List. 2. Change the selection of the target Tracked Process. 3. Change the Name of the field type. 4. Click the OK button to close the dialog if all the checks pass. Delete Field Type Context You can delete a field type. Procedure  Note A field type's user model field does not support the "Association to Many" type. If a string field is specified as the primary key (by checking the Key box in the creation dialog), only the following types of characters are supported in its value: letters numbers hyphens underscores If the value contains characters of other types, an error will appear when the system is trying to read the data. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 25 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- 1. Select the target field type. 2. Click the Delete button above the Items List. 3. The selected field type is removed if it is not referred by other objects. 4. Otherwise, before deletion, a Where Used List pops up to ask you if you want to delete the field type and all the data in the places where this field type is used. 5. If you click the OK button, the deletion takes effect immediately and the model detail page is changed to the edit mode. 6. Save your model configuration. Event Type Event type is used in the planned events and unplanned events of a tracked process. There are two types: Core model event types: including the GTTDelayedEvent, GTTOnTimeEvent, GTTDeletionEvent, and GTTUpdatePlanEvent User-defined event type. Besides, in the standard model "gttft1", you can also see standard event types and the corresponding standard model fields. You cannot modify them. You can create/edit/delete your own user-defined event type. You can have at most 200 event types in a model. In the Event Type Pool tab, user-defined event types and core model event types are listed on the left. Select an event type in the list. Then on the right side, the field list is displayed in two tables: The table at the top contains all user-defined fields used in this event type. The table at the bottom contains fields that are inherited from the core model event type. Create Event Type Context You can create an event type in a tracked process, including attributes such as the event type name, description, inherited event, and field list. Procedure 1. Click the Create button above the list on the left. 2. Select a tracked process in the drop-down list. 3. Fill in the event type name and description. The name is mandatory and should be unique in the model. In the Inherit drop- down list, the default value Event is provided. You can also change it based on your requirement. 4. Click the OK button to close dialog if all checks pass. 5. On the right side, two tables appear. The first contains user fields that only belong to this event type. The other contains all fields from the inherited event. You can have at most 200 user model fields in an event type. You can create/edit/delete user fields for this event type. To create a user model field, click the Create button above the User Model Fields list. Fill in the name and label. Select a type and define this field’s scope (writable, readable and visible) by using the check boxes. For more information on these attributes, see Create User Model Field. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 26 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- To edit a user model field, refer to Edit User Model Field. To delete a user model field, refer to Delete User Model Field. To add a URL for a user model field, refer to Add URL for User Model Field. To delete a URL for a user model field, refer to Delete URL for User Model Field. Edit Event Type Context After the event type has been created, you can edit its attributes. Procedure 1. Click the event type you want to change on the left side. 2. Click the Edit button above the list. 3. In the pop-up dialog, you can edit its tracked process, name, description and inherited event. 4. After editing is complete, click the OK button and save changes to the model. And the Model Details page is changed to edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Delete Event Type Context To delete an event type, do the following: Procedure 1. Select an event type that you want to delete. 2. Click the Delete button above the list. 3. If the event type is not used in other places, the deletion takes effect immediately and the model detail page is changed to the edit mode. 4. Otherwise, before deletion, a Where Used List dialog pops up to ask you if you want to delete the event type and all the data in the places where this event type is used. If you click the OK button, the deletion takes effect immediately and the model detail page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration.  Note a. A field type's user model field does not support the "Association to Many" type. b. For event types that inherit GTTDelayedEvent, if a field has the same name with a planned event extension field, its properties such as type will be copied from the planned event extension field. The properties cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 27 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Code List You can create/edit/delete code list in a tracked process. Each code list is a collection of code with a name. The code list is consumed as the type of a model field for a tracked process, field type, and event type. Code list fields can receive empty value. You can have at most 200 code lists in a model. In the Code List tab, code lists are displayed in alphabetical order. Click a code list, then the table on the right displays the corresponding collection of codes and their names. Create Code List Context To create a code list, do the following: Procedure 1. In the Code Lists tab, click the Create button above the list. 2. Fill in the name. The name of code list should be unique in one model. 3. Click OK. 4. After the creation is complete, you can create/edit/delete codes for this code list. You can have at most 200 codes in a code list. To create a code in the code list, do the following: a. Click the Add button above the table. b. A new row with two empty inputs will be added on the bottom of the table. c. Fill in code and name. The code should be unique in one code list. If the code is left empty, this line will not be saved to model. d. Save your model configuration. To edit a code in the code list, do the following: a. Click Edit on the top right to change the Model Details page to the edit mode. b. Change the name and code in the table. c. Save your model configuration. To delete a code in the code list, do the following: a. Click Edit on the top right to change the Model Details page to the edit mode. b. In the User Model Codes table, click the Delete icon at the end of the line that you want to delete. c. The deletion takes effect immediately. d. Save your model configuration. To import codes in a code list, do the following: a. Click the Import button above the table. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 28 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- b. A pop-up dialog appears. Select an LBN Code List that you want to import. You can preview the codes of the selected LBN code list in the table below. c. Click OK to import the codes. d. Save your model configuration. Edit Code List Context You can edit a code list’s name. Procedure 1. Select the code list item you want to change. 2. Click the Edit button above the list. 3. In the pop-up dialog, you can edit its Name. 4. After changes are complete, click OK to save changes to model. And the Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Delete Code List Context To delete a code list, do the following: Procedure  Note The following LBN code lists are provided: Carrier Reference Document Type Event Reason Code Descriptions Incoterm Descriptions Location Type Descriptions Shipper Reference Document Type Shipping Type Descriptions Traffic Direction Descriptions Transportation Means Standard Code Descriptions Transportation Modes For more, see the Code Lists document. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 29 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- 1. Select the code list item that you want to delete. 2. Click the Delete button above the list. 3. If the code list is not used in other places, the deletion takes effect immediately and the model detail page is changed to the edit mode. 4. Otherwise, before deletion, a Where Used List dialog pops up to ask you if you want to delete the code list and all the data in the places where this code list is used. If you click the OK button, the deletion takes effect immediately and the model detail page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. IDOC Integration IDOC Integration maintains mapping rules between ERP IDOC and tracked process user-defined fields. It defines: ERP Object Type Application Object Type the mapping of tracked process event and IDOC the mapping of tracked process actual event and ERP Event Code the mapping of events’ IDOC Segment/IDOC Field and tracked process user-defined fields On the IDOC Integration tab, you can select a specific tracked process to display or edit its related properties. On the right of the tracked process selection, there is an IDOC integration switch for this tracked process. The default state of this switch is OFF. You can change the state in the edit mode. When the switch state is: OFF, the related configuration view is not visible. These mapping properties are not checked. ON, you can see below the tracked process mapping, a Tracked Process / Events table and a User Model Fields table. When saving a draft model, these selected and filled items are checked before saving or deploying it. In the tracked process mapping part, you can select ERP Object Type and fill in Application Object Type. ERP Object Type You can select: Purchase Order Header Purchase Order Item Inbound Delivery Header Inbound Delivery Item Sales Order Header Sales Order Item Outbound Delivery Header Outbound Delivery Item Freight Unit 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 30 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/GTT_uide for Mode.content: Shipment Others Your selection can decide the value help lists of Event Code, IDOC Segment, and IDOC Field. Application Object Type This is a mandatory field. Your entry specifies the application object type in the ERP system for IDOC Integration. Tracked Process / Events table This includes tracked process event and event types. You are free to input your own value or use value help to define IDOC and ERP Event Code. Event code must be unique in a model. User Model Fields table There are Field column, IDOC Segment column and IDOC Field column in the tree table. You are free to input your own values or use value help to define related properties according to your selected ERP Object Type. To Set up IDOC Integration Context To set up the IDOC integration, do the following: Procedure 1. In the IDOC Integration tab, select a tracked process. 2. Set the Integration Switch to ON for IDOC integration. 3. Select an ERP Object Type. 4. Fill in the Application Object Type. 5. For the IDOC column in the Tracked Process / Events table: If your ERP object type value is: “Others”, then use the value help or input a value manually Otherwise, the corresponding is automatically filled in for you. 6. For the Event Code column in the Tracked Process / Events table, use value help or input a value manually. 7. For the IDOC Segment and IDOC Field columns in the User Model Fields table, use value help or manually enter your own values. Visibility Provider Integration Visibility Provider Integration is used for mapping visibility provider generic interface with a tracked process and its actual events. In the Visibility Provider Integration tab, you can select a specific tracked process to display or edit related properties. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 31 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- On the right of the tracked process selection is an Integration Switch for this tracked process. The default state of this switch is OFF. You can change the state in the edit mode. When the switch state is: OFF, the related configuration view is not visible. These mapping properties are not checked. ON, you can see below the Tracking Indicator, the Generate Event for Tracking Request Failure switch, a Tracked Process / Events table, and a User Model Fields table. When saving a draft model, these selected and filled items are checked before saving or deploying it. Generate Event for Tracking Request Failure switch This switch allows you to automatically generate an event called “GTT Tracking Request Error Event” when your tracking request is rejected by your business partner. The event contains an error message that your business partner sent to you. You can use the information for troubleshooting. The event will be displayed in: the Check Processes and Events app’s Other Events table, which contains a core model field Error Message to display the error. the fulfillment tracking apps’ Events table, which contains a field Event Reason Text to display the error. You can also view this error in the Error Message field of the Event Details page. For more, see Guide for Transportation Planners. Tracked Process / Events table In this table, there are tracked process events and event types. For event types, you can use value help to define the LBN Event Type. To see the full list of supported LBN event types, see Event Code Descriptions in the Code Lists document. Standard/User Model Fields table For the tracked process event, the table includes LBN Tracking Fields column and the tracked process' Fields column. You can select the tracked process field. You cannot input values freely in the edit mode. For the event type events, the table includes the event's user-defined Field column and LBN Tracking Fields column. You can select the LBN tracking field. You cannot input values freely in the edit mode.  Note In the standard model “gttft1”, you can: change the mapping of standard event types with LBN event types. But if you do so, you will no longer benefit from future upgrades of the standard model. map user-defined event types with LBN event types. But if you do so, you will no longer benefit from future upgrades of the standard model. change the mapping of the tracked process’s standard fields with the LBN tracking fields. But if you do so, you will no longer benefit from future upgrades of the standard field mapping of this tracked process. If you change the standard field mapping of the “Shipment” and “TrackingUnit” tracked processes, see Reference: Standard Field Mapping of "Shipment" and "TrackingUnit" Tracked Processes for the upgrades, and manually update the field mapping accordingly. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 32 This is custom documentation. In the Visibility Provider Integration tab, select a tracked process. 2. Set the Integration Switch to ON for visibility provider integration. 3. Use value help to fill in the LBN Event Type for actual events. 4. Use value help to fill in the Field or LBN Tracking Fields. These fields are applied to all the planned events in the model. You can create/edit/delete user defined planned event extension fields in the Planned Event Extension tab. You can have at most 200 planned event extension fields in a model. Create Planned Event Extension Fields Context To create a planned event extension field, do the following: Procedure 1. Click the Create button above the User Model Fields table. 2. Fill in the following: Name: should be unique in the planned event extension Label Type: supports String, UUID, Boolean, Integer, Decimal, Date, and Timestamp 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 36 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Visible Readable Writable For more on these attributes, see the relevant information in Create User Model Field. 3. Click OK to create this field. The model detail page is changed to the edit mode. 4. Save your model configuration. Edit Planned Event Extension Fields Context You can edit the name, label, type, and readable or writable attributes of a planned event extension field. Procedure 1. Select the field that needs to be changed in the table. 2. Click the Edit button above the table. Or click the pencil icon  at the end of the field that needs to be changed in the table. 3. Edit in the pop-up dialog, then click the OK button to save changes. And the Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 4. Save your model configuration. Delete Planned Event Extension Field Context To delete one or more planned event extension user model field, do the following: Procedure 1. Select the fields that you want to delete. Multiple selection is supported. 2. Click the Delete button above the User Model Fields table. 3. The To Be Deleted Objects dialog pops up to ask you if you want to delete the selected fields and all the data in the places where these fields are used. 4. Click OK. Fields you selected are removed immediately, and the Model Details page is changed to the edit mode. 5. Save your model configuration. Event to Action (Business Rules) Under the Event to Action tab, you can add a script incorporating logic (business rules) to your model. For more information about the script, see Appendix: Event to Action Script. In the standard model “gttft1”, the script is divided into four sections: Standard Declaration, User Script Before Standard Script, Standard Script, and User Script After Standard Script. Standard sections are not editable. You can only edit the user script 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 37 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- sections. In the display mode, you can click the eyeglass icon to view the script in a pop-up dialog. Add a Script to Your Model Context To add a script to your model, do the following. Procedure 1. On the Model Details page, click the Event to Action tab. 2. You can click Help to open the documentation and find information on writing scripts. 3. Click the Edit button on the top right. Write or paste your script in the window. You can click the pencil icon  to edit the script in a pop-up dialog. 4. Click Validate Code to check your script for errors. If there are no errors, you get a success message. If an error is found, click Open Validation Details to see the line number and type of error. Once you have corrected the error, click Validate Code again. 5. When you have finished your script, you have several options: Cancel: you can choose whether to discard all changes and return to the previous script, or not. Save: to save your script in the model. Translation In the MM app, the following model meta-data fields support multilingual translation: Description of the model Label of user model field in Planned Event Extension, Tracked Process, Field Type and Event Type Description of tracked process Description of event type Name of code in code list Supported Language English (US) is the default language and the default fallback language. To see the full list of supported languages, see the section Product Availability in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. Translation Dialog Context 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 38 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- The translation dialog allows you to manage the translation of different languages. Procedure 1. On the Model Details page, click the Edit button on the top right. 2. Click the Tracked Process tab. 3. To maintain a translation for a tracked process description: a. Select a tracked process from the list. b. Click the Edit button. c. In the pop-up dialog, i. If a translation of the description exists in the current logon language, it is displayed in the Description Input Control. ii. If a translation of description does not exist in the logon language but a fallback language exits, the description in the fallback language is shown as a placeholder in Description Input Control. d. When editing is complete, click Save. 4. To maintain translations for both a tracked process description and fields’ label in a tracked process: a. Click Translate button above the User Model Fields table. b. In the pop-up dialog, a translation of each field is displayed in one line. The first line is a description of this tracked process. Subsequent lines are user fields’ label in this tracked process. In the filter, you can select which language needs to be modified. For example, if you select German in the Language Drop Down List, a new column is added to the table below. c. Add translation in the column of special line. d. Click OK to save your changes. Deployed Models When a model is deployed, two additional views become available: Runtime View: displays deployment information such as API details and deployment history log. Deployed View: displays the deployed version of the model details. Runtime View When a model is deployed, you can see the runtime information of the deployed model. The Runtime view contains the following information: Write Service API Read Service API Write Service 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 39 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- In the Runtime view, select the Write Service tab to see the Write Service API details. The Write Service section is displayed in the following order: Tracked process types appear in alphabetical order. And in each tracked process type, the tracked process event is displayed first and followed by user-defined events in alphabetical order. Core events appear at the end in alphabetical order. The Write Service section contains the following information and functions that are offered to consume the Write Service API: API Endpoint: allows you to test the API against the data available in the tenant account. Resources: a list of the resources available for the API. API operations: HTTP POST method can be used to all these resources. Try it out: consume and test the selected API. You can view the response of the API in JSON format in the Response body section. Schemas: The schema for the resources. Trying Out API Context To try out an API, do the following: Procedure 1. In the Servers drop-down, you can see the API endpoint for the Try it out function. 2. In the API documentation, choose the required resource and its HTTP method. To test the API, click Try it out. 3. Enter the request payload in JSON format in the Request body text box. 4. Click Execute to execute the request. 5. In the server response section, it shows the response with the endpoint. Read Service Please see Read Service in API Documentation. Deployed View After a model has been deployed, you can see its deployed version in the Deployed view. On the Model Details page, click the Deployed button on the top right. The Deployed view has the same layout and content as the Draft view. The difference is the deployed view is read-only because you cannot modify the content of the deployed version of the model. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 40 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/GTT_uide for Mode.content: More Tasks On the top right of Model Details page, there is an Additional Options icon  that contains the following actions: Activate/Deactivate the Model Delete Business Data of the Model Export Business Data of the Model Enable/Disable the Model Cache Enable/Disable Event to Action Log of the Model View the Model History Activate/Deactivate the Model Context When a model is deployed, you can activate/deactivate the model to expose/conceal the Write Service and Read Service APIs for consumption. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. Select a deployed model. 2. On the Model Details page, switch to the Runtime or Deployed view. 3. Click the Additional Options icon  and select: Activate: to expose the API for consumption Deactivate: not to expose the API for consumption. 4. Click OK in the confirmation box. 5. The deployed version of the model is then active/inactive. If it’s active, you can read the model metadata and business data, and write the business data. If it’s inactive, you can only read the model metadata. Delete Business Data of the Model Context When a model is deployed, you can delete the business data of the logical system you specified, including the tracked processes with corresponding events. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. Select a deployed model. 2. On the Model Details page, switch to the Runtime or Deployed view. 3. Click the Additional Options icon  and select Delete Business Data. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 41 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- 4. Select All or Specified Logical System. If you choose the latter, enter the logical system name. 5. Click Delete. Export Business Data of the Model Context When a model is deployed, you can export the business data of the model, including the tracked processes with corresponding events, and download the files in the ZIP format. To use this function, you must have the DataModelAdminTemplate role to your role collection. For more, see the Available Roles for Solution Owners section in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. Select a deployed model. 2. On the Model Details page, switch to the Runtime or Deployed view. 3. Click the Additional Options icon  and select Export Business Data. 4. In the pop-up, select a time type that you want the time range of your exported business data to be based on: the Last Changed Time of tracked processes or the Creation Time of tracked processes. 5. Specify the time range for the data you want to export with the Start Time and End Time filters. The duration between the start time and the end time cannot exceed 365 days. 6. Select the tracked process(es) that you want to export. If you don't select any, all tracked processes will be exported. 7. Click Request Export. A confirmation box pops up. Click OK to confirm. A request is then generated under the Requests table. The following columns are displayed: Exported File: displays the request and the file that is exported within this request. Each request is named after the date and time when it is created. You can click  after each request to see the time type, time range and tracked processes you previously specified. If no tracked process is selected in the last step, the Tracked Process field in the pop-over is left empty. But it indicates that all tracked processes are exported. Once the request is completed, expand the request and you can see a list of exported files in the ZIP format that you can download. Each file represents a tracked process and its events. The maximum file size is 100 MB. If the data for a tracked process exceeds this limit, a new file will be created. Completed Time: shows when the request is completed. Status: shows the processing progress of the request: The progress icon  means the request is being processed. The completion icon  means the request is successfully processed. The warning icon  means the request fails to be processed. You must generate a new export request. 8. When the request is completed, select a file that you want to download.  Note The requests will be automatically deleted after 7 days. If the number of requests exceeds 10, only the latest 10 requests are kept. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 42 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- 9. Click Download. The file will then be saved to your local device. When you extract the file, you’ll see a collection of JSON files in the resulting folder. Enable/Disable the Model Cache Context When a model is deployed, you can enable/disable the model cache. The default is Enabled. If you change the model cache switch from Enabled to Disabled or from Disabled to Enabled, the change needs at most 15 minutes to take effect. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. Select a deployed model. 2. On the Model Details page, switch to the Runtime or Deployed view. 3. Click the Additional Options icon  and select Enable/Disable Model Cache. 4. Click OK in the confirmation box. 5. The model cache is then enabled/disabled. If it is Enabled, when you make any changes to the model and redeploy it, the model cache in the runtime needs at most 15 minutes to expire. New changes will take effect thereafter. The same applies to the Configure Partner Connections app. If it is Disabled, when you make any changes to the model and redeploy it, new changes will take effect at once. The same applies to the Configure Partner Connections app. Enable/Disable Event to Action Log of the Model Context When a model is deployed, you can enable/disable the logging of certain items related to your event-to-action script. These items are recorded in message logs and event logs. They include: the Event to Action Log statements the payload sent to the tracking API through the function sendTrackingRequest the payload sent to SAP Transportation Management through the function forwardEventToTM.  Caution In production tenants, enabling the model cache is strongly recommended to ensure optimal message processing performance. Disabling the model cache in production tenants significantly slows down the message processing and could lead to a great number of pending messages in the Manage Message Logs app.  Note This also applies to the Configure Partner Connections API cache. By default, the cache is enabled when calling Configure Partner Connections API internally. When you enable/disable the model cache, the Configure Partner Connections API cache is enabled/disabled at the same time. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 43 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The default is Disabled/Off. Once enabled, the system will start logging the above-mentioned items within 15 minutes. You can see the logs on the Correlation Details page of the Manage Message Logs app and the Manage Event Logs app. For instructions, see View Correlation Payload and Logs. Procedure 1. Launch the MM app. Select a deployed model. 2. On the Model Details page, switch to the Runtime or Deployed view. 3. Click the Additional Options icon  and select Enable/Disable Event to Action Log. 4. Click OK in the confirmation box. 5. The Event to Action Log is then enabled/disabled. View the Model History Context When a model is deleted, deployed, activated/deactivated, or meets deployment/deletion error, you can see the history details about the model. Procedure 1. On the Model Details page, click the Additional Options icon  and select History. 2. The history log is displayed in chronological descending order by the action time. 3. The history log entries are grouped by weeks. Click the group title to collapse/expand the group. 4. The history log entry contains the information of the administrator who performed the action, action time and description. Check Processes and Events Check Processes and Events (CPE) displays a tracked process with its event data based on a deployed GTT metadata model. The app is used to display all the tracked processes that have been deployed, to test the models, and to check the data displays details of all its events for a selected tracked process displays the data for standard and user-defined fields in the model. When you launch the CPE app, the overview page is displayed that lists all active process types with high-level information about each. Click a specific process type to see its data details on the Process List page. Help and Support There are several ways you can find help and support on the Fiori launchpad of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Built-In Support 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 44 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Built-in support provides efficient, simplified and guided support channels, you can search for knowledge, ask for needed information, get help from recommended solutions. Currently, expert chat is not supported. To access the built-in support service on the Fiori Launchpad, click the icon  on the right corner of the screen. You will see a welcome page where you can sign in, and a list of recommended links for the page. To gain full access to the built-in functions, you must activate your S-user. For more, see Activating Built-In Support Services. For more information on how to use this tool, refer to Built-In Support on SAP Help Portal. In-app Help When you launch the app, you can turn on the in-app help that provides on-screen explanations of key fields and areas on the screen. To turn on the in-app help, on the top right on the screen, click the  icon. Once the in-app help is turned on, you can: search the displayed help topics for the text that you type; click the  icon to see the help texts on that topic; click the link tiles to see the documentation of this app on SAP Help Portal; hide the Help Topics panel by clicking the  button on the bottom right. Filters You can apply one or more filters to reduce the number of process types displayed. You can also use value proposal search in selected filters. When you start typing, matching elements are displayed, and you can select them. By default, the following filters are shown: Process Type: the type of a tracked process. Model Namespace: the full unique technical name of the model. Last Deployed At: the range of start to end date that the model was last deployed. When you have completed your filter selection, click Go. You have the following options to alter how filters are displayed: You can hide the filters by clicking the  icon. You can pin the filters to the top of the screen by clicking the pin  icon. You can change the default filters, by clicking the Adapt Filters button. Views You can select a view, also called a variant. The view determines the number of process types listed on the overview page. There are two types, either: 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 45 This is custom documentation. To create your own view: Click Adapt Filters and the Settings icon  to personalize your filter and table settings respectively. Click the drop-down icon  to the right of the Standard view. Click Save As in the view selector. Enter a name for your view (case sensitive). You can also choose Set as Default and Apply Automatically. Save your view. You can click Manage in the view selector to change the view settings. Process List From the overview page, click a specific process type to see data details of that process type on the Process List page. By default, these filters are displayed: Alternative Key: the unique identifier of the tracked process in SAP Business Network for Logistics. It follows the pattern: scheme:party:system:type:id Scheme: “xri://sap.com/id”, a fixed value Party: LBN ID of the business partner System: name of the logical system that the tracked process comes from Type: business or document type of the tracked process ID: tracking ID of the tracked process Tracking ID: the document number of the tracked process Logical System: an application system in which the applications are coordinated to work in one common database, and from which the tracked process comes from Lifecycle Status: the lifecycle status of the tracked process. Select from the drop-down list one or more of: Business Active: the default value when a tracked process is created. It indicates that the relevant data of the tracked process is used in the ongoing business. End of Business: defines the end of active business and the start of residence time and retention period. When one of the last planned events is reported, the lifecycle status of the tracked process changes to “End of Business” automatically. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 46 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Process Status: the actual status of a tracked process, decided by the status of the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned”. Select from the drop-down list one or more of: As Planned: the initial status of a tracked process, also the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is reported on time. Delayed: the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is expected to be late. Early: the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is early reported. Late: the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is late reported. Overdue: the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is overdue. Overdue indicates that the current timestamp exceeds the latest planned technical timestamp. You can use the value proposal search in selected filters by clicking the icon . The case insensitive search is supported for the following conditions: “contains” “starts with” “ends with”. When you start typing, matching elements are displayed, and you can select them. To change the default filters, click Adapt Filters. More filters are provided, such as: Estimated Status: the estimated status of a tracked process, decided by the estimated status of the last unreported planned event whose status is not unknown. For details, see Important Terms. ID: the technical key of a tracked process. Party ID: the LBN ID of a solution owner or a data contributor. Tracking ID Type: the equivalent to the tracked process type. In the table of Processes, you can change the default columns with the Settings icon to display the View Settings screen. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings icon. You can also drill down further for more information. Other Events Other events include: GTTUpdatePlanEvent Unplanned events: display all the actual event data that has been reported without any reference to a planned event. You can change the default columns and sorting with the Settings icon. You can also drill down further for more information. Attachments This tab is displayed only when you create a user model field with its type as "Attachments" in the Tracked Process tab of the MM app. A Refresh button is displayed on the top right. Click the button to update the data shown.  Note The field “timeZone” supports the time zone IDs that are defined by IANA Time Zone Database. When setting values for the “timeZone” and “timeZoneId” fields, you should only provide a value for one of them. If you maintain the value of the parameter GTT_OTL_TIMEZONE in the Tracked Process EM IDOC, it will be automatically converted to the corresponding time zone ID. For more information on the mentioned IDOC, see IDOC Service.  Note The "Actual Business Timestamp" is for the planned event’s last correlated event*. *last correlated event: When an actual event is matched with a planned event successfully and the status of this planned event is calculated based on this actual event, then this actual event is considered as the last correlated event of this planned event. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 48 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Planned Event Details On the Process Details page, select a planned event from the Planned Events table to see the Planned Event Details page. There are two tabs: Planned Data: It covers the information about the planned event including the core fields, standard fields and the user- defined fields. Actual Data: Only displayed if an actual event is reported with reference to this planned event. The information is held in a table.
