Related Information Event Details Appendix: Event to Action Script An event-to-action script allows you to incorporate logic (business rules) into your model. This section explains about the structure and syntax of the script. To add your script to a model, see the section Add a Script to Your Model. To know more about the notification service, see the guide How to Send Notifications. Lexical Structure The lexical structure of a programming language is the set of elementary rules that specifies how you write programs in that language. It is the lowest-level syntax of a language. It specifies such things as what variable names look like, the delimiter characters for comments, and how one program statement is separated from the next. This section documents the lexical structure of the event-to-action script. Character Set Case Sensitivity This script is a case-sensitive language. This means that language keywords, variables, function names, and other identifiers must always be typed with a consistent capitalization of letters. The while keyword, for example, must be typed “while,” not “While” or “WHILE.” Similarly, online, Online, OnLine, and ONLINE are four distinct variable names. Whitespace This script recognizes the following characters as whitespace: space(\u0020) tab(\t) carriage return: (\r) line feed (\n) Comments This script supports the following styles of comments: Any text between a double slash "//" and the end of a line is treated as a comment and is ignored. Any text between the characters "/*" and "*/" is also treated as a comment. These comments may span multiple lines but may not be nested. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 52 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Literals A literal is a data value that appears directly in a program. The following are all literals: Identifiers and Reserved Words Identifiers An identifier is simply a name. Identifiers are used to name variables and functions and to provide labels for certain loops in the script code. An identifier must begin with a letter, or an underscore "_". Subsequent characters can be letters, digits, or underscores. The following are all legal identifiers: Reserved Words The script reserves a number of identifiers as the keywords of the language itself. You cannot use these words as identifiers in your programs: actualEvent plannedEvent trackedProcess break function return case do if switch var else continue 12 // The Integer number 1.2 // The float number "hello world" // A string value true // A Boolean value false // The other Boolean value null // A null value [1,2,3,4,5] // An array a a_b_c x11 _test 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 53 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- false while finally true for Semicolons Like many programming languages, we use the semicolon ";" to separate statements from each other. This is important to make the meaning of your code clear. Without a separator, the end of one statement might appear to be the beginning of the next, or vice versa. Values and Variables String Literals To include a string literal in a program, simply enclose the characters of the string within a matched pair of double quotes ("). The maximum size for a string is 10M. Here are examples of string literals: There are three functions for a string literal: 1. Function length() returns the length of a specified string. For example: 2. Function search()searches for a specified string value and returns the position of the match. If no matches are found, the function returns -1. For example: 3. Function substring() extracts the characters in a string from the start character to the end character and returns a new substring. To use this function, the following points should be noticed: The start index is mandatory. If the end index is not specified, the function extracts from the start character to the end of the string. The start character is included in the substring, but the end one is not. Only integers are input as indices. Subtractive integers are recognized as 0. The index 0 suggests the first character. "testing" "π is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter" var str = “circle”; str.length(); // returns 6 var str = “π is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter”; str.search("is"); // returns 2 str.search("t"); // returns 5 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 54 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- If the start index is greater than the end index, such as str.substring(4, 1), the indices will automatically swap places to str.substring(1, 4). Here are examples: Boolean Values A boolean value represents true or false, on or off, yes or no. There are only two possible values of this type. The reserved words true and false evaluate to these two values. null Value null is a language keyword that evaluates to a special value that is usually used to indicate the absence of a value. Object Value An object is a composite value. It aggregates multiple values (primitive values or other objects) and allows you to store and retrieve those values by name. An object is an unordered collection of properties, each of which has a name and a value. Property names are strings, so we can say that objects map strings to values. This string-to-value mapping goes by various names. The maximum size for an object is 100M. Function containsProperty() checks if an object contains a property. The syntax of this function is: For example: Array Value An array is an ordered collection of values. Each value is called an element, and each element has a numeric position in the array, known as its index. An array element may be of any type, and different elements of the same array may be of different types. Array elements may even be objects or other arrays, which allows you to create complex data structures, such as arrays of objects and arrays of arrays. There are two functions for an array value: 1. Function array.size() returns the size of the array. 2. Function array.push(x) adds the element x to the array as the last element. var str = “π is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter”; str.substring(2, 4); // returns “is” str.substring(5); // returns “the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter” object.containsProperty(“propertyName”) o.containsProperty(“x”) 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 55 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Numbers A number value can be an integer of float. A number value can be transformed to a string in this way: Timestamp Value There are four functions for a timestamp value: 1. Function timestamp.minusDays(x) subtracts the number of days (x) in the timestamp. 2. Function timestamp.plusDays(x) adds the number of days (x) in the timestamp. 3. Function timestamp.minusMinutes(x) subtracts the number of minutes (x) in the timestamp. 4. Function timestamp.plusMinutes(x) adds the number of minutes (x) in the timestamp. Expressions and Operators Property Access Expressions A property access expression evaluates to the value of an object property or an array element. 1. Syntax for an Object value property access: Here are some examples: 2. Syntax for Array value property access: Here are some examples: Invocation Expressions An invocation expression is the syntax for calling (or executing) a function or method. It starts with a function expression that identifies the function to be called. The function expression is followed by an open parenthesis, a comma-separated list of zero or num.toString() expression . identifier var o = toObject(“{x:1,y:{z:3}}”); //An example object o.x; //=>1 o.y.z; //=>3 expression [ expression ] var o = toObject(“ {x:1,y:{z:3}}”); //An example object var a = [o,4,[5,6]]; // An example array that c a[0].x; //=>1 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 56 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- more argument expressions, and a close parenthesis. Here are some examples: Operators Operators are used for arithmetic expressions, comparison expressions, logical expressions, assignment expressions, and more. Here are all allowed operators: Operator Operation Example + Positive number +1 - Negate number -1 +,- Add, subtract 1+2 1-2 <,<=,>,>= Compare a>=b == Test for equality a==b != Test for inequality a!=b ^ Power 2^3 == 8 && Compute logical AND true && false || Compute logical OR true || false ! Invert boolean value !true = assignment a=1 Statements Declaration Statements The “var” statement declares a variable. Here is the syntax: Return Statement toObject(“( )”); //toObject is the function expression; “( )” is the argument expression var uuid = toUUID("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"); var date = toDate("2010-05-04"); var timestamp = toTimestamp("2013-06-25T16:22:52.966Z"); var name [ = value] 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 57 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- The return statement terminates the execution of the code block immediately. Conditions Conditional statements execute or skip other statements depending on the value of a specified expression. These statements are the decision points of your code, and they are also sometimes known as “branches.” The “if” statement is the fundamental control statement that allows script to make decisions, or, more precisely, to execute statements conditionally. This statement has 3 forms: 1. The first form’s syntax is: 2. The second form of the “if” statement introduces an else clause that is executed when the expression is false. Its syntax is: 3. The third form’s syntax is: Loops (while) The script supports “while” statement for loop. It has the following syntax: To execute a “while” statement, the interpreter first evaluates the expression: If the value of the expression is false, then the interpreter skips over the statement that serves as the loop body and moves on to the next statement in the program. If the expression is true, the interpreter executes the statement and repeats, jumping back to the top of the loop and evaluating the expression again. The continue statement terminates the execution of the statements in the current iteration of the current loop and continues the execution of the loop with the next iteration. The breakstatement terminates the current loop statement and transfers the program control to the statement following the terminated statement. if (expression) statement if (expression) statement1 else statement2 if (expression) statement1 else if(expression2) statement2 else statement2 while (expression) statement 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 58 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- For example: Event to Action Log Statement The Event to Action Log statement begins a code line with “?” and is followed by a variable. For example: To see your event-to-action logs, you should do the following in the MM app first: 1. Deploy the model 2. Enable the Event to Action Log of the model. After the message processing, the logs are displayed on the Correlation Details page of the Manage Message Logs app and the Manage Event Logs app. For instructions, see View Correlation Payload and Logs. Related Information Deploy a Model Enable/Disable Event to Action Log of the Model User-Defined Function You can define your own functions. It must follow the syntax below: For example: var i = 0; var n = 0; while (i < 5) { i = i+1; if (i == 3) { continue; } n = n+i; if( n > 8) { break; } } var test = "gtttest5"; ?test ; function functionName(param1, param2, param3…..) { statement } 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 59 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Samples Notification service can be enabled by the event-to-action script. For details, see the section Implement the Script in the guide How to Send Notifications. System Embedded Constants There are some predefined system constants that you can invoke directly in the script. They include the following: trackedProcess The constant trackedProcess is an object of the tracked process. For its object structure example, see Example of trackedProcess Object. Function getFinalPlannedEvents() under the trackedProcess object returns a list of events that are flagged as final event. For example: actualEvent The constant actualEvent is an object of the actual event received. For its object structure example, see Example of actualEvent Object. plannedEvent The constant plannedEvent is an object of the planned event. For its object structure example, see Example of plannedEvent Object. Function isReported() under plannedEvent object returns a Boolean value: true or false. For example: modelNamespace The constant modelNamespace is a string value of the current model namespace. For example: function sample(a, b){ ?a; ?b; return a+b; } var c=sample(1,3); // c is 4 after execution  Note You cannot use system embedded functions in your user-defined functions. trackedProcess.getFinalPlannedEvents(); plannedEvent.isReported(); 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 60 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

System Embedded Functions There are some predefined system functions that you can invoke directly in the script. System embedded functions are divided into two groups: Event to Action Internal functions: are used within SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Event to Action External functions: interact with third-party systems in their operations. Event to Action Internal Functions Event to Action Internal functions are used within SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. They include: toTimestamp Function toTimestamp converts a timestamp in string format into a timestamp value. toDate Function toDate converts a date in string format into a date value. toUUID Function toUUID converts a UUID in string format into a UUID value. if(modelNamespace + ".SalesOrder.SalesOrderEvent" == actualEvent.eventType) { … } /** * Convert a timestamp in string format into TimestampValue. * * @param timeString - A timestamp in string format. Example: "2013-06-25T16:22:52.966Z". * @returns TimestampValue */ toTimestamp(timeString) /** * Convert a date in string format into DateValue. * * @param dateString - A date in string format. Example: "2019-05-04". * @returns DateValue */ toDate(dateString) /** * Convert a UUID in string format into UUIDValue. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 61 This is custom documentation. file://api-specs/split/GTT_uide for Mode.content: event table Parameter (Field) Description Value Type Default Logic eventTypeCode A coded representation of the type of a transportation event such as Departure, Arrival, or Proof of Delivery. For example, in a road freight order, typically one of the following code values can occur: Arrival: ARRIV_DEST Delayed: DELAYED Departure: DEPARTURE Proof of Delivery: POD Proof of Pickup: POPU Loading Begin: LOAD_BEGIN Loading End: LOAD_END Coupling: COUPLING Decoupling: DECOUPLING String (20) Follow the mapping of Event Type to Event Code in the IDOC Integration tab of the MM app. eventReasonCode A coded representation of the reason of a transportation event. For example, in a road freight order, typically one of the following code values can occur: Breakdown: BRKDWN Others: OTHERS Traffic: TRAFFC Waiting at Location: WTGLOC String (20) Use the value of the current event’s eventReasonCode field. eventReasonText A text string that contains the reason of a transportation event. Free input String (255) Use the value of the current event’s eventReasonText field. 5/12/26, 7:01 AM 81 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Parameter (Field) Description Value Type Default Logic referenceEventTypeCode A coded representation of a specific milestone referring to another event during the transport execution. For example, a delayed event refers to an arrival event. For example, in a road freight order, typically one of the following code values can occur: Arrival: ARRIV_DEST Departure: DEPARTURE Proof of Delivery: POD Proof of Pickup: POPU Loading Begin: LOAD_BEGIN Loading End: LOAD_END Coupling: COUPLING Decoupling: DECOUPLING String (20) For delayed events and events that inherit GTTDelayedEvent, follow the mapping of refPlannedEventType to Event Code in the IDOC Integration tab of the MM app. For other events, this field will be empty. recipientSystemLocationInternalID A proprietary identifier for a location where the even was reported. String (20) If the current event matches with a planned event, the value will be the planned event’s locationAltKey. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/12/26, 6:50 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 5 -- Introduction This guide describes the configurations you need to perform before you can integrate with Ariba Network. After you set up the integration, you can navigate from Ariba Network to the Monitor Inbound ASNs (MIA) app in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace to view the inbound delivery details. Perequisites You have purchased SAP Business Network Commerce Automation. You have purchased SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace and finished the onboarding process. For more information about the onboarding process, see Onboarding. You have an administrator role of your subaccount and subscribe to the MIA app. You have downloaded and installed sample codes for the MIA app. Procedure To set up for the integration, do the following: Submit the Required Information to Ariba Network Establish Trust Configure Role Collections and Add Ariba Network Buyer Platform Users Submit the Required Information to Ariba Network Context To submit the required information on Ariba Network, do the following: Procedure 1. Download the global track and trace SP SAML Metadata, then submit a Service Request to request enablement. a. In the SAP BTP cockpit, go to your subaccount. b. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Overview page, click Trust Configuration in the Security tab in the left-hand navigation area. c. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Trust Configuration page, click SAML Metadata to download the SP SAML Metadata. 2. Create a service request in SAP Ariba a. Go to https://connectsupport.ariba.com/ to create an SAP Ariba Service Request. You create an SAP Ariba Service Request to enable SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace for your Ariba Network account. Sign in with the SAP Ariba credential provided to you.  Note 5/12/26, 6:50 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 5 -- b. In the Incidents & Service Requests tab on the top, click Create a Service Request. c. In the search box, enter Where is my order enablement and click the Search  icon, then click the Continue to next step popup on the bottom right. d. Click the Issue/Configuration tile to go to the Create a Service Request page. e. Fill in the required information in each step. f. After you complete all steps, click Review at the bottom left to check the information that you filled in. g. Click Submit to create your service request. 3. Download the Ariba Network IdP SAML Metadata. After your service request has been processed, you will receive a notification that contains the Ariba Network IdP SAML Metadata from Ariba Support. Establish Trust Context To estabilishe the trust, do the following Procedure 1. In the SAP BTP cockpit, go to your subaccount. 2. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Overview page, click Trust Configuration in the Security tab in the left- hand navigation area. 3. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Trust Configuration page, click New Trust Configuration. 4. In the New Trust Configuration popup, click Upload to import the Ariba Network SAML IdP Metadata that you downloaded. 5. Check the validity of the Ariba Network IdP SAML Metadata by clicking “Show Details”. If one of the following attributes is empty, the SAML Metadata is considered invalid: Origin Key Subject Issuer Entity ID Single Sign-On URL (Redirect Binding) Single Sign-On URL (Post Binding) Single Logout URL (Post Binding) If you do not have permission to create a Support Request, ask your Designated Support Contact to log one for you. An SAP Ariba Support representative will follow up to enable SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace.  Note Upload your global track and trace SP SAML Metadata using the Attachments field. 5/12/26, 6:50 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 5 -- In this case, you must contact Ariba Support team in step 2 of Submit the Required Information to Ariba Network and ask them to provide a valid one. 6. Fill in the Name (for example: Ariba IDP) and uncheck the Create Shadow Users During Logon box, then click Save. Configure Role Collections and Add Ariba Network Buyer Platform Users Context To configure role collections and add Ariba Network buyer platform users, do the following: Procedure 1. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Overview page, click Role Collections in the Security tab in the left-hand navigation area. 2. On the Subaccount: <subaccount_name> Role Collections page, click the Add icon on the top right. 3. In the pop-up, fill in the Name, then click Create. 4. After creating the role collection, click the name to navigate to its details page, then click Edit. 5. In the Roles tab, select the role with its name and template as AppManageInboundASNsDisplayTemplate, then click Add. 6. In the Users tab, provide the following information as exemplified in the screenshot, then click Save. Fill in ID with the user's E-mail of Ariba Network buyer accounts. Choose the name of the Identity Provider that you configured (which is not "Default Identity Provider"). 5/12/26, 6:50 AM 4 This is custom documentation. TABLE OF CONTENTS INTRODUCTION ............................................................................................................................................... 3 PREREQUISITES .............................................................................................................................................. 3 API OVERVIEW ................................................................................................................................................ 4 MIGRATION OF INTEGRATION PLATFORM ................................................................................................. 4 STEP 1: CONFIGURE OUTBOUND CONNECTIONS ..................................................................................... 5 Special Considerations While Maintaining Communication Details .......................................................... 6 Authenticating Outbound Requests from Network ...................................................................................... 7 STEP 2: TEST OUTBOUND CONNECTIVITY ............................................................................................... 10 STEP 3: CONFIGURE INBOUND CONNECTIONS ....................................................................................... 11 Provider API Endpoints for Inbound Scenarios ......................................................................................... 13 STEP 4: EMAIL NOTIFICATION FOR INTEGRATION ERRORS ................................................................. 14 OPERATIONAL MONITORING ...................................................................................................................... 15 -- 2 of 10 -- 3 INTRODUCTION SAP Business Network for Logistics provides a network for shippers and carriers to collaborate for freight quotation, order confirmation, tracking, invoice, disputes and dock appointment use cases. SAP Business Network for Logistics provides web UI access to carriers for users to act on a defined process. Additionally, if you wish to get these documents in your systems, you may use the public APIs of SAP Business Network for Logistics to get the data and act on it. This document provides information on how to connect to SAP Business Network for Logistics as a carrier using REST APIs. The following subset of processes are supported via APIs: • Freight Tendering (Road) • Freight Subcontracting (Road) • Freight Booking (Ocean and Air) • Order Tracking • External Planning • Settlement For more general information, see the carrier introduction presentation and the carrier introduction video. Note: All activities mentioned in this guide have to be done in both the test and productive environments. PREREQUISITES To set up API integration with SAP Business Network for Logistics, you must meet the following requirements: • Carrier tenant is available in the test and productive environments. For more information about the process of registering SAP Business Network for Logistics, activating your account, logging on, and adding users, see the Activate Your Account guide. • In case your API server uses IP filtering, you need to add the IP ranges to the allow list as mentioned in the administration guide for logistics providers, to enable SAP Business Network for Logistics integration tenants to connect to your API server. Please make sure the API server is accessible on the internet. • It is expected that a carrier sets up an API server on their side for information exchange. Carriers have to set up the API connection once and shippers can use the same API connection for communication. The following diagram outlines the API communication between the involved parties: -- 3 of 10 -- 4 API OVERVIEW All APIs between the shipper and SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration are SOAP. All APIs between SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and the carrier are REST. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration provides APIs for the following B2B processes: You can find all the carrier-facing REST APIs on the right-hand side of the image. For more information, see the following documents: • Processes in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration • Carrier APIs (Rest APIs) in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration MIGRATION OF INTEGRATION PLATFORM The integration platform used in SAP Business Network for Logistics is announced for sunset, and a new platform is enabled for customers and partners. If you are an existing customer who has setup API connectivity with the network, there are certain migration efforts required from your end. There’s a detailed migration guide explaining the necessary steps required. We urge you to migrate to the new platform as soon as possible. For new customers, we’ve updated the endpoints and other details in our official product documentation on SAP Help Portal, the SAP Business Accelerator Hub documentation and also in this guide. For more information, see the Integration Platform Migration Guide for Freemium Users of SAP Business Network for Logistics relevant for carriers. -- 4 of 10 -- 5 STEP 1: CONFIGURE OUTBOUND CONNECTIONS Precondition: You have developed an API service in your backend server/transportation management system that can receive messages from SAP Business Network for Logistics in the published API format. On the Manage Network tab of your SAP Fiori launchpad, select the System Connections app. Choose Manage Details in the upper right corner. Under the Communication Details tab, choose Add and select the HTTPS option from the dropdown menu. -- 5 of 10 -- 6 Enter the following data in the New Communication Details window: For more information, see Specifying the Authentication Details and Base URLs for Your System’s Endpoints. Special Considerations While Maintaining Communication Details Due to disparity in the API designs of earlier SAP Business Network for Logistics APIs, there’s a difference in how destination URLs need to be configured for different scenarios. Earlier designs for ‘Consumer API for Freight Subcontracting’ and ‘Consumer API for Freight Tendering’ capture several pieces of information, such as shipper LBN ID, originator system ID and document ID, in the URL path especially for update, notification and cancellation scenarios. Hence the communication detail only expects the base URL to be maintained for all operation types (including create) of these two APIs. The URL path captured in the standard API documentation will be appended to the base URL configured in the communication details. In the more recent API designs, such as tracking and freight booking, a different approach is followed. All necessary information is captured in the request body. Hence no URL path calculation is required. This means that the entire URL can be configured in the communication details. SAP Business Network for Logistics reads this configuration as-is, and no change is done while sending the request. The difference in handling of communication details during runtime of different APIs is captured below: Consumer API Communication Details - Base URL/Entire URL Freight Tendering Base URL Freight Subcontracting Base URL Freight Booking for Confirmation Entire URL Order Tracking Entire URL Request for Planning in External System Entire URL Examples: Freight Subcontracting create scenario: If your API system is configured to accept a POST request at ‘https://carrier-api-system/api/v1/LbnFreightOrderForSubcontracing’, you need to capture the URL in the communication details as ‘https://carrier-api-system/api/v1/’. Freight Booking create scenario: If your API system is configured to accept a POST request at ‘https://carrier-api-system/api/v1/FreightBookingRequest’, you need to capture the entire URL in the communication details. -- 6 of 10 -- 7 Authenticating Outbound Requests from Network SAP Business Network for Logistics enables carriers to configure either a network-to-network authentication or a shipper-specific authentication for API request from the network to your backend system. • Network-to-network – common authentication for all shippers in the network • Shipper-specific – you expect a unique authentication credential for requests sent by each shipper from the network If you wish to set up a network-to-network authentication, you can follow the steps below. Under the Authentication Details tab, choose Add and select the required option from the dropdown menu and provide the credential details. Go back to the entry page of the System Connections app and create outbound connections for all API services that you provide: For a list of available services, see Assigning Authentication Details and a Base URL to a Service. -- 7 of 10 -- 8 Enter the following data for the new service: Please note that you need to maintain an “Authentication Detail” only if your integration design assumes a network-to-network authentication, this is, if you have a single authentication for all the shippers in SAP Business Network for Logistics. [Image: Configuration where carriers have a network-to-network authentication with SAP Business Network for Logistics] -- 8 of 10 -- 9 If you expect each shipper to send a unique authentication to your API system, you can leave this field blank, and shippers have a different configuration application where they’ll provide the same. [Image: Configuration where carriers expect a shipper-specific authentication from SAP Business Network for Logistics] -- 9 of 10 -- 10 STEP 2: TEST OUTBOUND CONNECTIVITY After configuration, you should directly perform a connection test to your API server. To test the service, in the Services table, select Post freight order for subcontracting and choose Test Service in the upper-right corner, then select With Default Payload: The system generates a test freight order and attempts to send a call to your API server. The below window is shown with the test freight order ID: Using the ID of the created document (for example API_TEST_xVdlBk8sz6), open the Manage Integration Logs app to view the test result. Please refer to the chapter OPERATIONAL MONITORING for more details. -- 10 of 10 --

For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Introduction This document describes the APIs provided by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace that are useable by applications. There are two basic types of API: Public cross-tenant APIs These are published by SAP in the SAP Business Accelerator Hub with documentation. They are mostly used by data contributors. In this guide, you can also find detailed instruction on how to use them. Generated tenant-local interfaces These are tenant-specific interfaces used by solution owners. They are also APIs, but differ based on the tenant. Rate Limiting This section describes the rate limit of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace APIs. Rate limiting restricts the number of incoming requests from callers to GTT APIs and within a specific time frame. It’s a protective measure that: prevents the GTT service from crashing due to the excessive load of requests ensures the availability and optimal performance of the GTT service for every client. We have defined the rate limits of following APIs according to tenant type: API Type of Tenant Limit IDOC interface: GTT_V2_EM_IDOC_Ingestion SOAP Message Interface: TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out Production The rate limit per tenant is 600 requests per minute. Test The rate limit per tenant is 600 requests per minute, 10000 requests per day. Write Service API: GTT_V2_HTTP_EVENT_INGESTION Production The rate limit per tenant is 600 per minute. Test The rate limit per tenant is 150 requests per minute, 10000 requests per day. Read Service API: GTT_V2_OData_Query Production The rate limit per tenant is 200 per minute.  Recommendation Before you start working through this document, ensure that you have the most recent version of this document available from the SAP Help Portal at: help.sap.com/gtt 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- API Type of Tenant Limit Test The rate limit per tenant is 60 requests per minute. When the rate limit is exceeded, you will receive an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response status code, and your requests are rejected. You can try executing requests again several minutes later. API Payload Limits To prevent APIs from being overloaded by the payload size, we have introduced API payload limits to regulate the API usage per message. The following tables list the size limit of different components in API payload: Public Tracking APIs API Request Body Response Body Provider API for Order Events Less than 40MB N/A Consumer API for Order Tracking Less than 40MB N/A Tenant-local Interfaces API Request Body without Attachment Attachment Response Body IDOC Service Less than 15MB Not supported N/A Read Service API No limit N/A The response body of read service API supports: 256 records at maximum for main entity in a query; 5000 records at maximum for each expanded entity of a single main entity; 20000 records at maximum for sum of each expanded entity for all main entity. Write Service API Less than 2MB Less than 10MB N/A SOAP Message Interface Less than 15MB Not supported N/A Here are examples of requests and responses for you to better understand the Read Service API size limit:  Note This will take effective as of December 13, 2025. There is no limit on API calls to fulfillment tracking apps, such as the "Track Shipments" app.  Example 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Public Cross-Tenant Tracking APIs This chapter describes how solution owners and data contributors exchange messages via the tracking APIs (or tracking interfaces) offered by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace provides two types of tracking APIs: Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT): enables solution owners to send a tracking request for an order to data contributors. Provider API for Order Events (GTT): enables data contributors (such as network partners or carriers) to post events for a tracked order. You can check out the above APIs on SAP Business Accelerator Hub . This chapter specifically describes the following two cases: how a solution owner sends a tracking request to a data contributor using the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT), and how a data contributor sends back the tracking data (that will later be converted to and processed as events in the GTT system) to a solution owner using the Provider API for Order Events (GTT). Sending Tracking Requests via Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT) As a solution owner, you can send a tracking request to a data contributor using the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT) . This chapter contains the following sections: Request Result Odata Response odata/v1/com.sap.gtt.app.gttft1.gttft1Service/Shipment? filter=filter1&$expand=processEvents, plannedEvents, freightUnitTPs 1 shipment was found and 5100 process events found on this shipment odata/v1/com.sap.gtt.app.gttft1.gttft1Service/Shipment? filter=filter1&$expand=processEvents, plannedEvents, freightUnitTPs 10 shipments were found and 2100 process events were found on each shipment. odata/v1/com.sap.gtt.app.gttft1.gttft1Service/Shipment? filter=filter1&$expand=processEvents, plannedEvents, freightUnitTPs,stops,trackingUnitTPs 1 shipment was found with 5000 process events, 5000 planned events, 5000 freightUnitTPs, 5000 stops, and 5000 trackingUnitTPs. You have onboarded on SAP Business Network for Logistics. 2. You have sent the invitation to the data contributor using the Invite Business Partners app. After the data contributor accepts the invitation using the Manage Invitations app, you two will be connected as business partners. 3. You have established a B2B connection to the external systems of the data contributor in the Configure Partner Connections app. 4. You have ensured that the data contributor has completed the Prerequisites and Configuration. Related Information Invite Business Partners Configure Partner Connections Configuration Context In the Manage Models app of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, the visibility provider integration information is already maintained for you in the GTT standard model “gttft1”. But if you want to integrate with your visibility provider in a user model or map user-defined fields in the standard model, do the following: Procedure 1. On the SAP Fiori launchpad, open the Manage Models app. 2. Select a model. 3. Go to the Visibility Provider Integration tab and open the edit mode. 4. Select a tracked process, and then turn on the Integration Switch. 5. In the Tracked Process / Events list on the left, you can see the tracked process event and event types. Use the value help to fill in the SAP Business Network for Logistics event type for actual events. 6. Select an event in the list, and then use the value help to fill in the fields or SAP Business Network for Logistics tracking fields on the right. 7. Save and deploy the model. If the data contributor you chose is a carrier, then the carrier must be onboarded onto SAP Business Network for Logistics. Note down its LBN ID with an “LBN#” prefix, such as "LBN#1234567". If the data contributor you chose is a network partner, then its corresponding carrier doesn’t have to be onboarded onto SAP Business Network for Logistics. Steps To test the integration in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, carry out the steps below: 1. On the SAP Fiori launchpad, open the Manage Models app. a. Select the GTT standard model “gttft1”. b. Switch to the Runtime view on the top right. c. In the Write Service tab, find the ShipmentEvent. Click the green section of this API endpoint. d. Click Try it out to test the API. e. In the Request Body text box, clear the existing request payload. Copy and paste the Sample Payload we provided and customize it to fit your needs. f. Execute the request. g. In the Responses section, it shows the response with the endpoint. 2. (Option 1) Back to the SAP Fiori launchpad, open the View Logs app. Open the Manage Message Logs app from the Quick Links section to check out the message processing status: a. Select the latest message on the list with the source type as External. The message contains the tracking request you just sent. You can drill down for more information. b. Back to the worklist page, refresh the page until you see a new message from your visibility provider. If the status is Success, then you have sent the tracking request successfully. 3. (Option 2) Back to the SAP Fiori launchpad, open the View Logs app. Open the Manage Integration Logs – Version 2.0 app from the Quick Links section to check out the message processing status. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Sending Events via Provider API for Order Events (GTT) As a data contributor, you can send back the tracking data (that will later be converted to and processed as events in the GTT system) to a solution owner using the Provider API for Order Events (GTT) . This chapter contains the following sections: Prerequisites and Configuration Monitoring Integration Prerequisites and Configuration Prerequisites To perform the tasks described in this chapter, you, as a data contributor, must have the following prerequisites: 1. You have onboarded on SAP Business Network for Logistics. 2. You have accepted the invitation from the solution owner using the Manage Invitations app. For more, see the application help of Manage Invitations. Configuration You need to use the System Connections app to complete the API implementations. For details, see the Connectivity section of Administration Guide for Logistics Providers. Related Information Provider API for Order Events (GTT) Monitoring Integration On the SAP Fiori launchpad, pen the View Logs app. Open the Manage Integration Logs – Version 2.0 app from the Quick Links section to view all integration logs for solution owner and data contributor transactions. For instructions on how to use the app, open the in-app help by selecting  within the Manage Integration Logs – Version 2.0 app. Generated Tenant-local Interfaces This chapter describes how to use the generated tenant-local interfaces in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. These APIs are provided for integration between the GTT system and other systems, which allows solution owners to access GTT services and perform CRUD (create, read, update, delete) operations on the GTT system via API requests. API Authentication You can use the following to authenticate your API calls to GTT service interfaces: HTTP Basic Authentication: You must create a technical user and maintain it in the System Connections app. For more, see Maintain Technical User in the System Connections App. 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 12 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Prerequisites To use these APIs, you must fulfill the following prerequisites: 1. Configure API authentication method. For more, see API Authentication. 2. Get the following information required in the API request URI: Server Address: You must provide the server address as the host in the request URI: For basic authentication, server address is the URL of your GTT Fiori Launchpad. It varies from hosted data centers. Do the following to get the server address: a. Go to your subaccount that has subscribed Global Track and Trace b. Click Services Instances and Subscriptions Global Track and Trace Go to Application c. After sign-in, you will see the URL. Model Information: Prepare the following model information needed in the resource path of the request URI: Model Namespace: It’s in the format of “com.<tenant name>.gtt.app.<model name>”. You can find the entire model namespace on the top of your target Model Details page. Write Service Name: It’s in the format of “<model name>WriteService”. Read Service Name: It’s in the format of “<model name>Service”. Model Name: You can find it on the target model card. After you finish the above tasks, you are ready to send API requests. In the sections followed, you can find examples of API request and response pair specific to different interface services. IDOC Service  Example Here are example server addresses specific to data centers for basic authentication: EU10: https:// <subdomain>.gtt.logistics.eu10.business-network.cloud.sap US20: https:// <subdomain>.gtt.logistics.us20.business-network.cloud.sap SA30: https:// <subdomain>.gtt.logistics.sa30.business-network.cloud.sap You must leave out “https://” when filing the information to an API request to avoid duplication.  Example In this guide, the standard model "gttft1" is used as the sample model. Report: data contributors can report events that are granted Report authorization. To enable the instance-based authorization, you need to: connect with your business partner (via the Invite Business Partners app or the Discover Business Partners app) for the tracked process user model field where you enter LBN ID, add LBN# as the prefix of its value to enable Read or Report authorization. For example, if the LBN ID is 10002424, you need to enter LBN#10002424. Instance-based Authorization Check for Write Service To check if a data contributor has Report authorization for an event, the GTT system will check if the event’s senderPartyId is equal to the tracked process’s partyId or to the LBN ID with the “LBN#” prefix. Not that events reported using Provider API for Order Events (GTT) are an exception, the GTT system won’t do this check for these events. For predefined event types, data contributors can only report GTTDelayedEvent and GTTOnTimeEvent. Authorization for instances can be inherited and checked through correlation. For example, suppose tracked process A observes tracked process B and tracked process B observes tracked process C. If you have authorization for tracked process C, you will also have authorization for B and A. Then events reported to C are also correlated to B and A. 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 51 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- If you don’t have authorization for tracked process C, the system will check if you have authorization for B. If so, events will be reported to B and correlated to A. Otherwise, the system will check if you have authorization for A. If tracked process C doesn’t exist, the system will check if you have authorization for B. If so, events will be reported to B and correlated to A. Otherwise, the system will check if you have authorization for A. Instance-based Authorization Check for OData Read Service 1. Solution owners have Read authorization for their instances. 2. Data contributors can only query user-defined process entities, user-defined event entities, GTTDelayedEvent and GTTOnTimeEvent. When querying process entities, you cannot filter/expand “QualifiedTrackingId” and user defined process entities. When querying event entities, you cannot filter/expand core entities and user-defined process entities. When querying any process entities, data will be filtered by process “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs. Note that at least one of process “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs should be equal to the user’s LBN ID. When querying any event entities, data will be filtered by “senderPartyId”, “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs. Note that at least one of “senderPartyId”, “partyId” and READ annotation specified LBN IDs should be equal to the user’s LBN ID. Notes There are several points to note: 1. It’s not supported that “/”,”//” “;”, “%”, “\” appear in the key of the query entity. 2. It’s recommended to keep the layer of the navigation or expand no more than 3 layers. 3. The max limit of number of records in the response is 256. 4. For $expand, the use of a same entity name is not supported.  Example Unsupported example: https://< Server Address >/api/outbound/odata/v1/com.gttsampleso01.gtt.app.sof.sofService/ SalesOrderItem(id=guid’6d49b8f3-5599-5cbf-b9d0-b06bfb4e24a9', altkey='/;\%-12345678  Example Not suggested example: https://< Server Address >/api/outbound/odata/v1/com.gttsampleso01.gtt.app.sof.sofService/ TrackedProcess(guid'6d49b8f3-5599-5cbf-b9d0-b06bfb4e24a9')? $expand=plannedEvents/lastProcessEventDirectory/event/references 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 52 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Response File tp2_20231218083335.zip SOAP Message Interfaces This section introduces SOAP message interfaces used by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out As a solution owner, you can create a freight order in TM embedded in SAP S/4HANA and send it for tracking in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Technical Name TransportationOrderGenericTrackedProcessRequest_Out Description You can use this inbound service provided by SAP Business Network for Logistics to create a freight order for tracking from your external system, such as TM embedded in SAP S/4HANA. This will enable you to track a freight order. For detailed configurations, see Using SOAP Messages. Frequently Asked Questions This section answers the questions that are frequently asked when you are using the tracking APIs. As a solution owner, can I request a new event type in the Provider API for Order Events (GTT)? Yes. You can report an incident on SAP ONE Support Launchpad categorized by component SBN-LBN-GTT to create a new event type. But before reporting the incident, please take a moment to familiarize yourself with the information below: 1. An event type means an action, such as Arrival or Departure. So it should not include any location-related information. 2. Location information could be maintained based on the stop ID (which is provided via the Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT)), UNLOCODE, or IATACode. If you want to add an Arrival or Destination event, you can use the ARRIV_DEST event for both of these events. The exact location should then be maintained in the location ID. To foster standardization, please map your events to one of the existing event types. For a complete list of existing event types, see Event Code Descriptions. If you are unsure about which event type you should map with your event, you may also consider mapping it to the OTHER event type and adding a specific description for it. Does SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace support geo location tracking for direct integration with carriers (no visibility provider in between)? Yes. Carriers can also provide geo location updates via the Provider API for Order Events (GTT). Note that any event type can contain geo coordinates, such as Arrival, Departure, On Time, Delay, and so on. 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 59 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- As a solution owner, can I receive attachments from the data contributor as part of the Provider API for Order Events (GTT)? Yes. You have two options to achieve that. Option 1: The data contributor needs to maintain the fileName, mimeType, and fileURL that is publicly accessible. The GTT system will save the content from the URL provided as an attachment with the specified event. Option 2: The data contributor needs to maintain the fileName and fileContentBinaryObject to upload a Base64- encoded attachment. What is the size limit for attachments such as the proof of delivery that are sent by the data contributor? The total size of the attachment(s) in an event may not exceed 10 MB. As a solution owner, can I send a tracking request to multiple business partners regarding one specific document? Yes. You can achieve this in the Manage Models app by using the event-to-action function sendTrackingRequest. For more, see the corresponding part in the section Event to Action External Functions of Guide for Model Administrators. 5/12/26, 6:33 AM 60 This is custom documentation. How to connect to Network Partner in Business Network for Logistics as a shipper or Network Owner RavishShettyR Product and Topic Expert 2022 Nov 03 9:39 AM 8 Likes  3,224 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Introduction Business Network for logistics(BN4L) has integration to certain list of the B2B carriers and visibility partners. This document will describe the step by step on how to setup the connection from your account to network partner B2B Carrier – Is nothing but a carrier in your system. Carrier Business users instead of using LBN Web UI, will be using carrier’s IT system. LBN will be integrated to carrier system Network Partner – Also called as a digital forwarder, is another network of carriers. They act on behalf of the carriers for digitally transacting document. LBN will be integrated to Network partner and network partner there on to the carriers.   -- 1 of 10 -- The required configurations for setting up the connections to B2B carriers and Network partners are similar. In this document, we will cover only the steps involved to connect to Network partners. Step1: Discover the Network Partner and establish relationship Step2: Configure connection parameters in BN4L Step3: Testing with Network partners Step1: Discover the Network Partner and establish relationship Pre-requisite: You have established connection to all the carriers, that you wish to collaborate or require tracking information. You can find in the below link on how to establish connection to your carriers. FC:https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_FC_OPTION/185742008f2c477ca789b93675b0ec6c/ a1c5c34037a94fd68fbc24b... GTT:https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_GTT_OPTION/d0802f41861a4f81a3610d873fdcf14 8/a1c5c34037a94fd68fbc24... -- 2 of 10 -- Navigate to Discover Business Partners tile Search for the network partner that wish to connect to. Fourkites, inc. is used as an example -- 3 of 10 -- View detail information for Fourkites, Inc and click on Request for connection. The connection request is routed to the network partner. The network partner will receive a connection request and the network partner will accept/reject depending on your contract with the network partner. To proceed further, the network partner must accept the request. Step 2: Configure connection parameters in BN4L Once the network partner accepted your request, you may proceed with the next steps. In most -- 4 of 10 -- cases, the network partner also would have onboarded you into their systems and would have generated a user credential to access their systems. This credential must be maintained in BN4L for communicating digitally with network partner via BN4L. Maintaining Network Partner Credential Navigate to configure partners connection app Click on Manage credential and maintain the credential provided to you by the network partner -- 5 of 10 -- BN4L support Basic, OAuth and APIkey credentials. Depending on the type of credential provided by the network partner, maintain the entries accordingly . Even for P44, the credential must be maintained as mentioned in the below screenshots. In addition, if you are using tracking for via P44 LTL scenario, you would have to maintain additional values with project44 tab. In P44 terms it is called as capacity provider account. P44 uses the details mentioned in the capacity provider account to retrieve tracking information from carrier system. -- 6 of 10 -- In case you are setting up connection to P44, follow the below mentioned guide: https://help.sap.com/doc/96e23bc983664cc998bd044a66c7b5cd/LBN/en- US/SAP_LBN_FC_p44_guide.pdf Mapping Carriers to Network Partner After maintaining the credential, you must map carriers to network partner. You have an option to map all the carriers to the same network partner for each scenario. -- 7 of 10 -- Depending on the network partner, the list of supported services by the network partner can be seen in drop down. This list will vary from one network partner to another.(These list of services is configured by network partner and integration is built based on supported list). You may select a specific scenario that you wish to setup. BN4L will route the calls to network partner entries endpoints based the transaction data values, mainly transportation Mode( Air , Ocean, Road ) and shipping type( FCL, LCL, FTL, LTL ). -- 8 of 10 -- Note: It is highly recommended to pass the Transportation Mode and Shipping type, if available in the transaction data . Map the network partner credential that was created earlier. After creation, you will have an entry as below. The information can be read as all carriers will be routed to Fourkites for shipment tracking of all modes. -- 9 of 10 -- Step 3: Testing with Network Partners Integration testing must be done on a project basis involving representatives from SAP and network partner organisation. The above setup can be achieved in test and productive environment. In the test environment, you may use one of test carrier tenants in your global account. This test carrier tenant must be mapped to one of the network partner carriers by the network partner. In productive tenants, the carrier that you wish to collaborate must be shared with network partner. Network partner does the mapping between the LBN carriers and the Network partner carriers. In addition, check the logs in Manage Integration Log app for successful communication with network partners Summary By doing above configuration you have enabled connection to Network partner. You can trigger the payload from FC or GTT and see that the calls are going to the network partner. LABELS Technology Updates Add tags Comment -- 10 of 10 --

................................................................................................................................. 4 Should I Do this Migration?................................................................................................................................... 4 Why Migrate? .............................................................................................................................................................. 4 Configuration Changes for Freemium Users ................................................................................................. 4 Outbound from SAP Business Networks for Logistics............................................................................................................ 5 Inbound to SAP Business Network for Logistics ......................................................................................................................... 7 API Connectivity ............................................................................................................................................................................................................................... 7 EDI Connectivity ............................................................................................................................................................................................................................... 9 Monitoring of Integration Logs .......................................................................................................................... 10 Support ........................................................................................................................................................................ 10 -- 2 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 3 / 10 Introduction SAP Business Network for Logistics (SAP BN4L) is run on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) leveraging the various services provided by the platform. SAP BTP offers a variety of application environments that customers and internal SAP organizations can choose from, to build SAP applications and business solutions in the cloud. One critical service used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is the SAP Cloud Integration (previously known as SAP CPI) which acts as the single integration platform for all customers and partners for SAP Business Network for Logistics. This platform is owned and managed by the SAP Business Network for Logistics development team. Freemium customers can maintain necessary connectivity configurations using the ‘System Connections’ app and monitor their integration logs via ‘Manage Integration Logs’. SAP Cloud Integration used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is hosted in Neo environment of SAP BTP. SAP BTP, Neo environment is the oldest of the application environments and is built on a proprietary SAP technology stack. The Neo environment in SAP BTP has been deprecated and will be sunset for internal SaaS applications (see SAP Note). SAP Cloud Integration is also offered in a multi-cloud foundation in SAP BTP, and this is the new platform that will be used by SAP Business Network for Logistics. In accordance with SAP BTP’s decision to sunset Neo environment, SAP Business Networks for Logistics has decided to stop the support of the existing Neo integration platform on July 18, 2025, as part of our July 2025 release. This means that the connectivity to your backend transportation management system (TMS) will stop working if you don’t migrate to the new integration platform. This would require some configuration changes in your backend TMS and in your System Connections app in SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can read more about this change in this announcement. This guide provides a comprehensive list of changes that a premium customer must do in order to migrate from the old integration platform to the new one. We understand the critical role that connectivity plays in SAP Business Network for Logistics. The primary focus is not to disrupt the existing integrations between your backend systems and SAP Business Network for Logistics. So, your existing configurations will stay intact and continue to work until you migrate to the new integration platform or till the end of support of the old integration platform. In the meanwhile, we have made it possible for you to migrate from the old platform to the new one using the configuration apps in SAP Business Network for Logistics. This requires some changes in SAP Business Network for Logistics configuration apps as well as in your backend systems. You might also need to update your firewall/SAP Cloud Connector configurations as the IP range will be different for the new integration platform. We urge you to migrate as soon as possible to leverage the improved log capacity and other new features. Note: We recommend performing the migration activities in your test tenants first and then monitor if all the integration scenarios are working correctly. Proceed with the changes in your productive tenants accordingly. Data Center-Specific Integration Platform There will be a separate integration platform for customers onboarded to EU/US data centers. In this migration guide, you’ll see a mention of endpoints/IP addresses of these two data centers. Please ensure that you update your configurations by referring to the data center where your tenant is hosted. -- 3 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 4 / 10 How to Identify Your Tenant’s Data Center? If you are unsure about your tenant’s datacenter, this can be identified from the ‘eu10’/’us20’ tag in the host URL of your SAP Business Networks for Logistics tenant. URL in SAP Business Network for Logistics Data Center https://carrier01.lbn.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/ EU https://lbn-carrier01.lbn.cfapps.us20.hana.ondemand.com/ US Should I Do this Migration? The steps mentioned in this guide are only targeted for B2B carriers/partners of SAP Business Network for Logistics. If you are only using the UI in the network, you need not do any of the below mentioned changes. Why Migrate? Apart from the sunset of the old integration platform, the migration to the new platform has its benefits. Here’s why a B2B carrier should do this migration: • Improved data persistence resources for integration logs: In the current integration platform, resources for database are limited and at the maximum possible limit. Customers rely on integration logs and payload download feature to debug/validate any integration issues. If the DB memory limit is breached, integration scenarios would work fine but there would be discrepancies in the way logs/payloads are stored. Migrating to the new platform will ensure proper log monitoring and payload download. • Improved security for communication between SAP Business Network for Logistics apps: Better authentication protocols will be deployed for communication between the SAP Business Network for Logistics backend apps and the new integration platform (agnostic to customers) • New features: Improvements to platform features will be based on the new integration platform. Some of these upcoming features include hourly auto-reprocessing of failed/escalated logs. • Self-configuration to set up inbound communication for freemium customers: Freemium customers such as ‘carriers’ used to rely on a ticketing process to set up inbound authentication/communication to SAP Business Network for Logistics. This was true for both API and EDI communications. Part of the reason was a lack of support from the older integration platform. In upcoming releases, we’ll make these provisionings available via System Connections apps for freemium customers. Configuration Changes for Freemium Users New integration platform means new destination URLs and authentication to connect to SAP Business Network for Logistics. There’ll be no changes to our API/EDI message definitions. So, your existing developments/integrations should work out of the box. -- 4 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 5 / 10 Outbound from SAP Business Networks for Logistics Configurations maintained in your System Connections app are used for the outbound communication from SAP Business Networks for Logistics to your backend system. However, you need to explicitly select the new integration platform for the outbound communication from the network. This is because the new integration platform is hosted in a different cloud infrastructure. Hence, you might need to update your allowlisting rules, if any, at your side to allow communications from the new platform. Please find the IP ranges for the new integration platform below: Data Center NAT IPs (Outbound from Network) LB IPs (Inbound to Network) EU 18.198.196.89, 18.193.21.232, 3.65.9.91, 52.29.190.137, 18.197.134.65, 3.67.182.154, 3.67.255.232, 3.66.249.150, 3.68.44.236, 52.59.128.222, 52.28.241.88, 18.184.81.94, 3.67.200.70, 3.68.51.135, 3.124.174.204, 3.68.31.37, 3.67.58.183, 3.67.0.172, 3.67.244.62, 3.126.117.58, 3.66.100.105, 3.68.13.226, 3.126.45.133, 3.67.249.135, 18.194.183.183, 3.126.229.22, 18.193.180.19, 3.64.227.236, 18.153.123.11, 3.121.37.195, 3.73.215.90 -- 5 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 6 / 10 3.67.246.74, 3.66.68.201, 3.68.0.70, 52.28.56.202, 3.126.95.250, 3.66.68.127, 18.195.244.40, 3.67.107.121, 3.67.24.253, 18.193.50.255, 3.121.35.143 US 40.90.195.191, 20.57.129.106, 20.57.128.95, 20.57.128.118, 40.90.209.71, 20.72.210.109, 20.72.209.240, 20.72.209.187, 40.90.200.224, 40.90.201.197, 40.90.201.85, 40.90.200.237 40.91.120.100 Once you’ve updated your firewall configurations (if you have any) to allowlist new IP ranges to enable the communication from the network via the new integration platform, you need to navigate to ‘Connection Settings’ in your System Connections app and select ‘Integration Platform’ as ‘Multi-Cloud (new)’ from the dropdown list. -- 6 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 7 / 10 Click on Save. Confirm the warning pop-up. Now your integration scenarios should be executed via the new ‘multi-cloud’ platform. Regarding the Services that you’ve configured in the main page - Outbound Connections, no changes are required as these will be read by the new integration platform as-is. Inbound to SAP Business Network for Logistics API Connectivity To use the integration platform for your inbound communication to SAP Business Network for Logistics, you need to change the destination URLs for all provider APIs. The host URL of integration platform varies based on your data center: Data Center Host/Base URL EU10 https://api.logistics.eu.business-network.cloud.sap/ US20 https://api.logistics.us.business-network.cloud.sap/ The URL path remains the same and can be obtained from SAP Business Accelerator Hub documentation. You’d need new OAuth 2.0 credentials to authenticate the calls to the new integration platform. With the latest release of SAP Business Network for Logistics, it’s now possible to provision OAuth 2.0 credentials from the System Connections app directly by selecting the Provider APIs you wish to connect with. -- 7 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 8 / 10 In the System Connections app, proceed as follows: 1. Choose Connection Settings. 2. Under Inbound, activate the Enable Inbound Connections toggle. 3. Select Integration Platform as Multi-Cloud. 4. Select the desired APIs from the Provider API dropdown. 5. Save your settings. 6. Wait for some time as the credentials are generated and necessary roles are assigned. You should be able to copy the Client ID, Client Secret, Authentication URL and Host URL once created. This would also be available any time in the Connection Settings window. The authentication URL varies based on the data center. You can copy it from the UI or refer to the table below: -- 8 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 9 / 10 Data Center OAuth 2.0 Token URL EU https://bn4lintegrationsuiteliveeu10- d2q5jmpt.authentication.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/oauth/token?grant_type=client_credentials US https://bn4lintegrationsuiteliveus20- 0gohdecj.authentication.us20.hana.ondemand.com/oauth/token?grant_type=client_credentials EDI Connectivity If you’ve already requested an SFTP polling scheduler before, please raise a support incident with SAP asking to migrate to the new platform. You can create an incident in SAP support portal categorized by component SBN-LBN-INT and title as ‘SAP BN4L Integration Platform Migration: Request for transferring SFTP polling schedulers to new integration platform’ with the following information: • EDI message format (ANSI X12 or EDIFACT) • LBN ID • Polling schedule: Start and end time on the same date (for example, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.). That is, if the start time is on 22 September, the end time cannot be on 23 September, according to your time zone. • Polling frequency (for example, every 30 minutes) Please note that SFTP polling is not yet enabled as a self-service and must be set up by SAP. -- 9 of 10 -- © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. See Legal Notice on www.sap.com/legal-notice for use terms, disclaimers, disclosures, or restrictions related to this material. 10 / 10 Monitoring of Integration Logs The Manage Integration Logs app in your tenant is updated to support the integration logs from both, the old ‘neo’ and the new ‘multi-cloud’ integration platform. We’ve also added a new column to make this clear to customers. The app also supports the reprocessing of messages failed/escalated in both these platforms. Support If you encounter any issues during the migration process, refer to the following blog article. This article summarizes frequently asked questions about the migration: https://community.sap.com/t5/supply-chain-management-blogs-by-sap/faq-neo-to-multi-cloud-cpi- migration-for-business-network-for-logistics/ba-p/14079631 For any further queries, open a ‘Medium’ priority incident in the ‘SBN-LBN-INT’ component with the title – ‘Concerns related to SAP BN4L integration platform migration – <CustomerName>’. -- 10 of 10 --

Start testing integration with SAP Business Network for Logistics without SFTP server aboppre Associate 2023 Jan 26 7:41 AM 11 Likes  1,451 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Introduction SAP Business Network for Logistics provides capabilities of freight tendering, tracking and dock appointment scheduling by connecting business partners in the network. To set up EDI integration with the network carriers need an SFTP server for information exchange. For carriers who are interested in testing EDI integration without such an SFTP server we offer the option to test EDI Outbound messages by sending them as email. This blog describes the required configuration in the System Connections app to use this functionality. Setting up email communication in the System Connections app   -- 1 of 4 -- On the Manage Network tab of your SAP Fiori launchpad, select the System Connections app. Choose Manage Details in the upper right corner. Under the Communication Details tab, choose Add and select the Email option from the dropdown menu. -- 2 of 4 -- Enter all required data in the New Communication Details window. An email containing an IFTMIN/ANSI 204 message will be sent to each email address in the Recipients field. Go back to the entry page of the System Connections app and create three different outbound connections for the Freight Subcontracting All service, one for each of the following operations: Post freight order for subcontracting cancellation Post freight order for subcontracting Put freight order for subcontracting -- 3 of 4 -- For details how to create these services, see our How-to guides for ANSI or EDIFACT. Here you can also find information how to adjust your configuration for productive usage. Summary By following the above steps, you can start testing the integration with SAP Business Network for Logistics without an SFTP server. You may use the comments section to provide feedback on this article and help in improving the content. Additional you may post your queries in the comment or in the community Q&A.
