SAP Business Network For Logistics - Carrier Side Integration - API vs EDI Jeff-Gebo Product and Topic Expert 2023 Mar 07 12:39 AM 38 Likes  14,931 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Introduction SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) provides capabilities of freight tendering, subcontracting, settlement, tracking and dock appointment scheduling by connecting business partners in the network. By joining the network, a carrier can connect and transact with any shipper on the network. BN4L comes by default with a web portal that our carriers can use to transact with shippers they are collaborating with. Of course, this often means they have to do the "swivel seat" style of integration, meaning manually copying the data from our portal and pasting it into their own systems...not very fun to be sure but not horrible if you only have a small number of transactions. Most carriers I have met would rather get away from this method of "integration" once the transaction numbers start to increase. BN4L provides two options for building integrations - API and EDI. Both have their pros and cons as you will soon read.   -- 1 of 6 -- API Pros Performance - nothing can beat the speed of a system-to-system API integration. Transactions can flow back and forth between shipper and carrier in a matter of seconds. Functional Coverage - Most functionality in the web portal is also supported with APIs with a couple of exceptions. Invoice Disputes and Dock Appointment Scheduling are only available in the web portal. New processes to the industry like quotes/spot bids and external planning are only available for integration with APIs. API Cons Development Skills Required - APIs require some development and/or robust middleware to implement. On top of that, your own systems must be API enabled to build the integrations. To our SAP customers this might sound trivial, but many carriers are working on older systems that don't support the latest integration possibilities. Takes Time to Implement - building an API integration can take time and requires close collaboration with a shipper who can send test data. A middleware solution can help ease some of this burden, and should be considered, but it will still take time to build a robust API integration. Why does it take a long time? For one, the payloads are large and somewhat complex, it's not enough to be an API developer, you need to also understand the data and the business process. EDI Pros Standards Based - EDI has been around for a long time and is how logistics integrations have operated for decades. There is tons of knowledge in the industry around EDI and even older carrier systems support it. ANSI has defined the North American standard for -- 2 of 6 -- EDI and after that they helped define the UN/EDIFACT standard used in much of the rest of the world. Relatively Easy to Implement - because it is so well known and based on standards it is easier to implement than API. Every carrier I have worked with to date has EDI experts employeed. EDI Cons Performance - BN4L EDI uses SFTP and batch jobs to build the integration, and due to this it is much slower than API. What API can do in seconds EDI can do in minutes to hours. Functional Coverage - BN4L currently only supports EDI for Road tendering (FTL & LTL - 204, 990, 214, 210 & 997). There is no support for quotes (AKA Spot Bids) with EDI for Road as this process wasn't around when EDI standards were defined. Ocean booking EDI support will be rolled out slowly this year starting with the 300 in the March 2023 release. Air booking support is planned but not yet on the roadmap. Above shows our Freight Order APIs and EDI support for Road FTL / LTL. -- 3 of 6 -- Things Shippers Should Know and Consider Not all carriers can build an API integration even if they wanted to, they just aren't there yet. EDI is the best many of them can do. Most carriers can't support API integration for quotes/spot bids and will have to use the web portal to respond to these. There are some exceptions - but only the most technically sophisticated carriers can support this. The LTL industry by and large will not build API integrations, they will only do EDI. Maybe this will change in the future as API standards for LTL are being worked on. Things Carriers Should Know and Consider EDI is a great place to start for integration, but you should start thinking about how to take the next step to support API integration. The speed and functionality over API integration can be a differentiator. New processes that like quotes and external planning are only available for integration over API, and if you don't invest and move forward you could be left behind. Look at the FinTech industry did to banking, the same thing is already starting to happen with CarrierTech. Make sure to invest in your technology as it truly is the new battle ground for carriers. Consider joining a standards body that is defining industry API standards...these will only come about if those with deep industry knowledge make it happen. In Conclusion When it comes to shipper/carrier integrations EDI has dominated for decades and continues to be the most used integration in the industry, and BN4L will continue to grow its support for it. That said, there is no doubt that a well built API integration can be a differentiator in that it can perform orders of magnitude faster, and newer innovative processes like quotes/spot bids and external planning are only supported for integration over API. Carriers who wisely invest in a -- 4 of 6 -- Comments technology platform that can integrate over APIs can now and into the future will certainly have advantages over those who can only do EDI. Learn More BN4L EDI Setup Guide & Specs BN4L Carrier API Docs BN4L Carrier / Partner API Integration Guide For further questions and feedback related to the blog, please check the Q&A area and feel free to post your questions in the link with the tag SAP Business Network for Logistics. Great to see that both API and EDI are available. sschrist Discoverer 2023 Mar 22 7:29 PM Great info, Jeff. justyna Participant 2023 Mar 28 2:51 PM Great blog post, thank you Jeff! -- 6 of 6 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: SAP Community > Products and Technology > Supply Chain Management > SCM Blog Posts by SAP > SAP Business Network For Logistics - Road EDI Inte... SAP Business Network For Logistics - Road EDI Integration Tips and Tricks Jeff-Gebo Product and Topic Expert 2023 Jul 26 10:45 PM 16 Likes  12,622 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Introduction SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) provides collaboration capabilities for shippers and carriers - freight tendering, subcontracting, settlement, tracking and dock appointment scheduling can all be collaborated on. A carrier on our network can connect and transact with any shipper on the network. BN4L comes by default with a web portal that our carriers can use to collaborate with shippers they are connected to. Optionally, carriers can build an integration from BN4L to their own systems using EDI or API. If you haven’t yet read my blog on EDI vs API integration I highly recommend doing so. Over the past year and a half, I have worked with hundreds of carriers who are building these integrations, both EDI and API. Over the course of this work with carriers going the EDI integration route I have identified common issues and questions that they have. My hope is that the below list will assist in speeding up EDI integrations for new carrier integrations. Note: I work with North American carriers so I am focused on ANSI EDI, that said we also support EDIFACT for the rest of the world.   -- 1 of 10 -- EDI ANSI Common Issues & Questions 204 The first question I get from a carrier is always this: What are your ISA/GS IDs (AKA sender / receiver IDs)? In BN4L we use the LBN ID of the shipper and carrier. The LBN ID is a unique ID (10 digit numeric value) of the shipper and carrier the uniquely identifies them on the network. Each will typically have two of these. One for the test landscape and another for the production landscape. Like any good integrator you will first build and test your integration on the test landscape then move to production once everything has been successfully tested. Ok, then there is the second related question – what is the qualifier? Ours is “ZZ”. You can find all of this documented in our 204 Spec Guide. PRO TIP: Never download our guides, just bookmark the link – we are making improvements all the time and upgrade our guides regularly. 990 -- 2 of 10 -- The easiest of all the EDI inbound messages but almost everyone misses this one segment, you need to send the Sender System ID! Why? Because a shipper can possibly have multiple systems connected to their BN4L tenant and due to that we need the carrier to send back this segment so we can route the message to the proper system. If only I had a dollar for every time I emailed the below snippet, I could retire. LOL! Learn more in the 990 spec guide. ---------------------------- You are missing the following segment: N9*06*”Sender System ID”~ You can get the sender system ID value from the 204 segment: L11*SenderSystemId*06~ 210 This one is more complex – the most difficult of all the inbound messages. First you need to send back three N9 segments – the Sender System ID, the Bill From Party and the Purchasing Party. The Bill From Party and Purchase Party are the business partner IDs as maintained in the shippers system. If you don’t get these correct the invoice won’t process successfully. Sometimes carriers forget to send the C3 segment with the currency code. Most difficult about the 210 is how we require the L1 segments to be formatted. I’m not going to go into detail on that in this blog, I will create a separate one just for L1 segment. Suffice to say, take the advice I mention below about the L1 segment – again, I email this snippet out all the time to carriers trying to integrate with the 210: ---------------------------- You are missing the following segments: -- 3 of 10 -- N9*06*Sender System ID~ N9*12*BillFromParty~ N9*CN*PurchasingParty~ You can get these from the 204 in the following segments: L11*SenderSystemId*06~ L11*PurchasingParty*CN~ L11*BillFromParty*12~ With the 210 please pay special attention to how we format the L1 – look at the examples on page 30 of the 210 spec guide. PRO TIP: You need to ask the shipper you are integrating with which BN4L Charge Codes they support for your use case with them. They should be able to send you that list. 214 for Freight Collaboration Tracking (not GTT) This one isn’t too bad, but not used quite as much because a lot of our shippers choose a Visibility Provider (like Project44, FourKites or Shippeo to name a few) to get order tracking data. That said, more and more carriers are setting up the 214 with us…I imagine this will become more popular over time. In addition to the Sender System ID we need the Stop ID or Location ID. Stop ID is just 1, 2, 3 (depends on number of stops), or better yet send the Location ID which can be found in the 204. Below is the email snippet I send out regularly to carriers and as always the 214 Spec Guide which has examples is your friend. -- 4 of 10 -- ------------------------------- You are missing the following segment: L11*SenderSystemId*06~ You can get the sender system ID value from the 204 segment: L11*SenderSystemId*06~ You also need to send a Stop ID or Location ID. The location ID can be found in the 204 N1-04 position. Send as: L11*Location ID*LU~ 997 We currently only support the 997 for confirmation of the files you send to BN4L - these are the 990, 214 and 210. It is on our roadmap to support 997 confirmations for a 204 (hopefully will be delivered sometime this year). With our 997 we have one thing that needs to be known by carriers - that is the sender ISA / GS ID is "LBN". Why? Well because we did receive your file, but it may not have been routed all the way to the shipper's TM. This 997 only means that it was received by BN4L. (Why "LBN" and not "BN4L" well, BN4L used to be called Logistics Business Network, LBN for short). Summary -- 5 of 10 -- Comments EDI Integration can be easy if you consider these common issues and answers to common questions listed here. I’ve seen this integration setup as quickly as a day…I’ve also seen it take weeks. My hope is with this info we can get more carriers integrated in days. Feel free to ask any questions below on this in the comments. Happy integrating! PS - we now support the 300 and 301 for Ocean. Are you a carrier interested in this? Let me know! For further questions and feedback related to the blog, please check the Q&A area and feel free to post your questions in the link with the tag SAP Business Network for Logistics. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Application Help Generated on: 2026-05-12 06:36:52 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration | LBN Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_FC_OPTION/185742008f2c477ca789b93675b0ec6c?locale=en- US&state=PRODUCTION&version=LBN Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration improves supply chain efficiency by connecting business partners on a collaborative network that supports jointly managing transactions, exchanging documents, and sharing insights across the value chain. For instance, upon invitation from a shipper, a carrier can onboard onto the network and collaborate with shippers on freight tendering, invoicing and milestone reporting. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration runs on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), utilizing one of the following infrastructures: Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Frankfurt, Germany Microsoft Azure infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Washington state, US Google Cloud infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Dammam, Saudi Arabia The data used in the solution is also stored in the respective data center. Information for shippers: Collaborative managed transactions supported in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration are tailored to the relevant SAP backend systems. For freight collaboration scenarios, SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration offers out-of-the-box connectivity to shippers with the following systems: SAP Transportation Management (on-premise) or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA (on-premise) SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition SAP Logistics Management For more information about supported releases, see SAP Note 2620322 . In addition, out-of-the box connectivity is delivered for truck carrier networks, including project44 for visibility services and B2B carrier connectivity for freight tendering and subcontracting. Selected digital freight forwarders support on-demand road transportation with real-time pricing and subcontracting. To learn more about the SAP Business Network add-ons for project44 visibility services, see the Feature Scope Description for project44 Add-Ons and the Configuration and Application Guide for project44 Add-Ons. Shipper Apps and APIs With SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, you as a shipper can use the apps to get started on the network, including connecting your systems (for example a transportation management system) to the network. Additionally, you can perform your daily tasks in the areas of dock appointment management, freight order tracking, freight settlement, and dispute handling.  Note The following documentation uses the term SAP S/4HANA to refer to both SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition and SAP S/4HANA (on-premise). If any of the information provided applies to only SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA, this will be clearly specified.  Note These apps are also suitable for logistics service providers that are performing the role of a shipper. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Prerequisites To use a new app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section. Shipper APIs As a shipper, you can use the APIs in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration to perform your daily tasks in the areas of freight contracting, freight booking, freight tracking, dock appointment scheduling, and freight settlement. For more information, see https://help.sap.com/doc/e1b2026259d84fc29e6e6760da815011/LBN/en- US/7ccd8fd6e75249b991c8d62706fe90ff.html. General Settings The General Settings app enables you as the shipper admin to configure the general settings related to freight collaboration at an ordering party level. You can also set up tolerance rules that would enable the settlement clerk at the shipper organization to auto-approve certain amounts by applying the tolerance rules to disputes created from invoices or self-billing documents. When an invoice contains discrepancies that would result in a dispute, you can define and assign tolerance ranges and tolerance groups so that you do not have to check each order manually. The system can then approve charge lines automatically. Lines that are not approved must be reviewed manually by the user. This app contains the following main areas: Define Appointment and Dispute Settings You can configure the appointment and dispute settings for an ordering party in this tab. For more information, see Appointment and Dispute Settings. Define Tolerance Range You can define the tolerance range itself by creating an upper limit and a lower limit. The tolerance values can be specified in either amounts (e.g. lower limit of EUR 10, upper limit of EUR 15) or percentages (e.g. lower limit of 2%, upper limit of 2%). Define Tolerance Groups Once you have defined the tolerance range, you can group them together. You can define item level tolerance ranges for each charge code. You can add a tolerance range for the rate amount and final amount for each charge code. You can also define the tolerance ranges for the total document amount proposed by the carrier. In this scenario, for each currency, you can specify the tolerance range. For more information on how tolerance is applied on dispute documents, see Applying Tolerance Check.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note You must specify a lower limit and an upper limit, either of which can be expressed as an amount or a percentage. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Appointment and Dispute Settings SAP Business Network for Logistics enables you to configure the dock appointment and dispute settings for an ordering party. As part of the dock appointment settings, you can also define the guest user access settings. Guest User Access In the General Settings app, in the Define Appointment and Dispute Settings tab, you can choose the Guest Access button to define the type of URL you want to send to the guest carrier user. You can choose one of the following options: Dynamic URL When you select this option, the system sends a URL to the carrier which is specific to the document you send to the carrier for dock appointment scheduling. The carrier can enter the document reference to view the document. Static URL When you select this option, the system sends a URL to the carrier which is generic. The carrier can enter the following details and view the document: Document Type and ID Email ID User Name Company Name We recommend you to select the dynamic URL by default. If you select the static URL, anyone with the link and valid document reference can access the document. Ordering Party Settings To define the ordering party settings, in the General Settings app, in the Define Appointment and Dispute Settings tab, choose the Add Ordering Party button. Once you add an ordering party, you can define the following settings: Dock Appointment Scheduling You can enable one of the following settings for the dock appointment creation process in the SAP Business Network for Logistics system: On Freight Order Creation  Note The system applies the settings you specify here to all the ordering parties. Once you specify the above settings, the system displays the type of URL you have chosen on the header area in the tab view. In the detailed view, you cannot view this information. If you select the dynamic URL option and later change the setting to static URL, the guest user can use both the dynamic and static URLs to access the document. However, if you select the static URL and later change the setting to dynamic URL, the guest user can only use the latest dynamic URL to access the document.  Note The system only displays those ordering parties that you have maintained in the Manage Locations app with the object type as Business Partner. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- The system creates an appointment when a freight order is created. In other words, the system creates an appointment for a freight order that is yet to be confirmed. On Freight Order Confirmation The system creates an appointment only when a freight order is confirmed. On Appointment API The system creates an appointment based on the appointment API and not on the freight order. If you select On Freight Order Creation or On Freight Order Confirmation, the system still allows you to create appointments using the Appointment Provider API (GenericAppointment_In). If you select On Appointment API, appointments can only be created using the API. Settlement Dispute Management in External System You can enable or disable dispute management in external system for freight orders and freight bookings. Enable for Freight Order When you enable this setting for freight orders, then the disputes created for the subsequent documents will be created in your external system. Enable for Freight Booking When you enable this setting for freight bookings, then the disputes created for the subsequent documents will be created in your external system. Enable Automatic Submission of Disputes You can enable or disable automatic approval of disputes. If you have enabled this setting, and if the dispute is within the specified tolerance range, the system automatically approves the disputes sent by your carrier. If the dispute is not within the specified tolerance range, you must manually approve the dispute. Note that if you have defined both document tolerance and item tolerance, then both tolerances must be within the specified tolerance range for the dispute to be automatically submitted. If you have defined only document tolerance or item tolerance, then the respective tolerance must be within the specified tolerance range for the dispute to be automatically submitted. Enable Mandatory Attachments for Invoice Submission You can enable or disable mandatory attachments during carrier invoice submission. If you enable this setting, during carrier invoicing, the carrier must mandatorily add attachments before submitting the document. If you disable this setting, adding an attachment is optional for the carriers. Enable Subsequent Invoice with Same Charge Type  Note To add an ordering party, you must have already created a location in the Manage Locations app with the Object Type as Business Partner.  Note It can take up to 15 minutes until any change is reflected in the carrier's Manage Invoices app. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 5 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- You can enable or disable subsequent invoice with same charge type. When you enable this setting, the carrier can add a subsequent charge for a charge type which has already been invoiced. If you disable this setting, the carrier cannot add a subsequent charge. Reference Documents You can specify whether you want to send reference documents to external system as notes. If you enable this setting, you can also specify the note type for reference documents in the field that appears below. This note type that you specify here will be used to send the reference documents as a note. Enable Tax Code Validation When you enable this setting, if the carrier enters a tax code in the invoice, the system validates this tax code with the tax codes that you have maintained in the Assign Charge Codes app. Tolerance Group Assignment You can assign one tolerance group to each individual carrier that you have onboarded on the freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics. When you assign a tolerance group to a carrier, the tolerance group should be sufficient for consumption in terms of charge lines and the respective currencies. For example, if you have a very good relationship with a particular carrier, you can define a group in which all the charge codes are automatically approved. Approval Conditions You can enable a multi-step dispute approval process within your organization before submitting the dispute to the carrier. A dispute document can either be approved in a single step by a basic user at the first level or sent to supervisors or managers at the next levels for review based on the settings that you specify. The additional approval steps are enabled only when the disputed amount exceeds the threshold amount or percentage specified the settings. Based on the range of the disputed amount, you can define multiple approver groups for various dispute amount ranges to approve the dispute. You can specify the approval conditions for an ordering party as follows: 1. Choose Add to add a new approval condition. Add Approver Conditions pane appears on the right. 2. In the Approver Group section, specify the following: Scenario Displays dispute scenario by default. Approver Group Specify the name of the approver group. The name that you specify here must be the same as you have specified in the user group in IAS Portal. You can assign all the users for this approver group to the IAS user group. For more information on assigning user groups, see Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users.  Note Use a note type that is different from the default note type as the system uses the default note type to send the carrier notes to your external system.  Note This is a mandatory field. You can specify alpha numeric values. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 6 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Notification Language Select a language, from the drop-down menu, in which you want to receive the email notification. An email notification is sent to the approvers in this group whenever a dispute requires their approval. Notification Emails Specify the email ID to which the email notification must be sent. You can specify multiple email IDs by choosing the add icon. Note that the system only sends email notifications about the dispute approval to these users. Not all these users may have the authorization to approve or reject the disputes. You must maintain those settings in the IAS portal. 3. In the Conditions section, specify the following: Currency Select the same currency that you have specified for the document currency, from the drop-down menu. Threshold Range Select a threshold amount or a threshold percentage from the drop-down menu. Specify a threshold amount or percentage as appropriate. Purchasing Group Specify the name of the purchasing group. Administrative Data Displays the administrative data such as created on, created by, changed on, and changed by. Applying Tolerance Check When a dispute is created or updated in the carrier tenant for a freight order or invoice and then sent to you for review, a tolerance check is applied based on your tolerance settings. You can enable tolerance for the entire document amount or the individual charge item amount. Tolerance Check Formula The system uses the following formulae to check whether the amounts are within the specified tolerance range: For Tolerance Amounts Do not specify commas and spaces. You can only specify _ (underscore) and – (hyphen) special characters.  Note For an ordering party, you must specify the same currency and threshold range factor (amount or percentage) across all approval conditions. In other words, when you create subsequent approval conditions, you must specify the same currency and threshold range factor (amount or percentage) that you specify in your first approval condition. You cannot enter the same combination of condition attributes in two approval groups. In other words, you cannot specify the same currency, threshold range, and purchasing group combination that you specified in the previous entry. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- If you have maintained the tolerance range in amounts, the system uses the following formulae for calculation: Freight Order Amount – Lower Tolerance Amount Freight Order Amount + Upper Tolerance Amount If the amount proposed by the carrier is in between the above values, then the tolerance check is approved. If the freight order amount is USD 50 and the upper limit is USD 5 and lower limit is USD 5, then if the carrier specifies the amount to be within USD 45(50-5) and USD 55(50+5) then it passes tolerance check. For Tolerance Percentages If you have maintained the tolerance range in percentages, the system uses the following formulae for calculation: Freight Order Amount – (Lower Tolerance Percentage * Freight Order Amount) Freight Order Amount + (Upper Tolerance Percentage * Freight Order Amount) If the amount proposed by the carrier is in between the above values, then the tolerance check is approved. For example, if the freight order amount is USD 50 and the upper limit is 5 % and lower limit is 5 %, then if the carrier specifies the amount to be within USD 47.5(50-2.5) and USD 52.5(50+2.5) then it passes tolerance check. Document Tolerances If you have defined document tolerances in your tolerance group for a carrier, a tolerance check is applied on the total document amount proposed by the carrier. In other words, if the carrier sends a disputed document to you and the total freight document amount proposed by the carrier on the header area falls within the defined tolerance range, then the system updates the information button on the header dispute status with this information. Item Tolerances If you have defined item tolerances in your tolerance group for a carrier, the system applies a tolerance check according to the following criteria: If the charge codes listed in a freight document are present in the defined tolerance group, the tolerance check is applied for those charge codes. If the charge codes are not specified in that group, no tolerance check is applied and you must approve those lines manually. For a charge code that matches the group, the currencies are then checked. In the General Settings app, the Rate Amount and the Final Amount, for example, can be maintained in different currencies. If the currencies match, a second check is applied according to a defined formula. For a given currency, you can maintain a limit as either an amount or a percentage, and different formulas are applied accordingly. If the carrier’s proposed value in the invoice lies within the start and end limits according to the respective formula, the charge line is considered to be within tolerance. Every rate amount and final amount that falls within the tolerance limit is assumed to be approved by the system’s tolerance check. The line is then marked with a green bar and receives the status Approved by tolerance check. This means you do not have to approve these lines manually. If the tolerance check does not meet your expectations, you can override it by clicking  (Edit)and entering your changes. If you do so, however, you must consider the following: If you edit the line, the tolerance check will not be applied to that line in subsequent rounds. (However, if you do not edit the line and it does not pass the tolerance check in the first round, the check can be applied in all subsequent rounds of the dispute life cycle process.) 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- If all the lines are approved by the tolerance check, the dispute status remains as For review. (It only changes to Resolved if you click Submit Dispute.) If a line is dependent on other lines and the other lines are approved by the tolerance check, the dependent line is not necessarily approved by the check unless it falls within the tolerance limits. If you add a new line, the same tolerance check is applicable. In this case, however, the freight order value is considered as 0. Only if it matches the currencies and falls within the tolerance limits is the new line also considered as approved by the tolerance check. Combination of Settings If you have specified the settings for both document tolerance and item tolerance, then the system checks the tolerances at both levels in the disputed document and updates the status as follows: For the charge lines within tolerance range, the status is updated as Approved by Tolerance Check. For the charge lines outside tolerance range, there is no status update. For the charge lines for which tolerance is not defined, there is no status update. On the header status, in the information button, a message is displayed whether the tolerance is within the set tolerance range or not. If you have specified the settings only for document tolerance or item tolerance, then the system checks the tolerances as appropriate based on your settings. Example You have specified the following settings in the tolerance group: Document Tolerance Amount Currency Tolerance Definition Selected Tolerance Range EUR Example1 10.00 EUR to 100.00 EUR Item Tolerance Amount Charge Code Rate Amount Tolerance Range Final Amount Tolerance Range ADMIN_FEE 10.00 EUR to 50.00 EUR 10.00 EUR to 50.00 EUR INSPECTION_FEE 10.00 EUR to 50.00 EUR 10.00 EUR to 50.00 EUR Freight document amount is EUR 100. If the carrier sends a disputed document to you, the system checks the tolerances at both levels in the document as you have maintained both document tolerance and item tolerance. If the total document amount proposed by carrier is within EUR 90 (100-10) to EUR 200 (100+100), the document tolerance check is approved. If both the rate amount and the final amount of the administration fee and inspection fee are within EUR 90 (100-10) to EUR 150 (100+50), then the system updates the status of these charge lines as Approved by Tolerance Check and the charge line is highlighted in green. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Manage Locations You can use the Manage Locations app to manage location master data either manually replicated from another system or created from scratch using the app. Location master data can then be consumed by other apps, such as Docking Location Settings, in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. You can set up a location replication using the Data Replication Framework (DRF) in the SAP S4/HANA source system. For more information, see the Business Configuration section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. Location master data consists of not only the address information, but also the business purpose of a location. Additionally, the master data of a location can include one or more alternative IDs so that the location becomes cross-platform identifiable. The main features of this app include: View a location Create a location Upload locations Edit a location Creating a Location To create a location, proceed as follows: 1. Click Create on the upper-right corner of the Locations table. The Create New Location page opens. 2. On the Create New Location page, enter the following details: Source: Source of the location. Valid values are: SAP SCM Logistic Location: Locations from one of the following systems:  Note If the subsequent invoice contains a charge that is already invoiced, the subsequent invoice is not applicable for document tolerance. If the subsequent invoice contains a charge that is already invoiced, that charge is not applicable for item tolerance.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note The Manage Locations app implements all security features and data protection-relevant functions documented in the "Security and Data Protection and Privacy" section of the Administration Guide. A location master data record enters the blocking period if it has not been accessed for three consecutive years. The blocking period lasts for another three years, during which only audit specialists can access the record. The record will then be automatically deleted when the end of the blocking period is reached. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 10 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Business Working Hours This worksheet contains all the information in the gate Business Hours tab in the Manage Entities app. You can view the following columns: Gate reference Time period reference Start date End date Working days Start time End time Note that you can edit all the fields in this worksheet similar to the edit option in gate in the Manage Entities app. Upload Gates Microsoft Excel To upload the gates in a Microsoft Excel file, perform the following: 1. You can use the gates file that you previously downloaded using the Download option to edit the existing data. Alternatively, you can download the template by choosing Gate Excel Export Template option to add new gates. This template contains the same worksheets and columns similar to the downloaded gates Microsoft Excel file. However, it does not contain any data. Note that you can only use either the template or the downloaded file to upload into the system. 2. Upload the Excel file by choosing Gate Excel Upload . Upload entities dialog box appears. 3. Select the edited file that you want to upload from your computer and choose Proceed. The system displays the confirmation message indicating the number of gate entities that will be uploaded. It will also display the error log if some of the entities are in error state. You can download the error log to investigate the issue. 4. Choose Confirm to upload the entities. Displays whether the entities are uploaded. If they are uploaded, you can view them in the Gate tab in the app. For gate entities in active and inactive statuses, you can only edit the Contact Person, Phone Number, and Arrival Lead Time fields. All the other fields are non-editable similar to the edit option in gate in the Manage Entities app.  Note There are a few columns that are hidden in the worksheets. These columns contain technical information. You cannot edit these columns Adding of Enable Sharing option is currently not available in the Microsoft Excel file. You cannot edit the status of the gate in the Microsoft Excel file. You can only change the status in the Manage Entities app. You can only upload Microsoft Excel files with a maximum of 2500 entries. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 91 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Defining Yard Settings Yard settings define operational parameters such as business hours, gates, and docking locations, crucial for efficient yard management. To define the settings for a yard, proceed as follows: 1. Choose the Yard tab on the left pane. 2. Choose the Add Yard button. The create yard pane appears on the right. a. Define settings for the following sections: b. Details c. Business Hours d. Gates e. Docking Locations 3. Choose Save to save the yard settings as a draft. Choose Save and Activate to activate the yard settings. Details Enter the following information in the details section: Location ID Select a location ID. You maintain location master data in the Manage Locations app. Time Zone Enter a time zone. Yard ID Specify a yard ID. Remarks You can enter the additional information about the yard in this section. Business Hours  Note The following fields cannot be changed any longer after the yard was activated: Yard ID Location ID Description Address Time Zone 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 92 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Choose the add icon in this section to add an entry of business hours. Enter the following information: Period Specify the duration for which the entry of business hours is valid. Working Days Specify the working days of the yard. Working Hours Specify the working hours for the specified working days. To add another entry of validity period, choose the add icon. You can create up to 10 entries per validity period. Gates Choose the add icon in this section to add entries of gates. The system displays the list of active gates in the same time zone that you have maintained in the Manage Entities app. You can select the gates that you want to add to the yard. Once you add one or more gates to the yard, you must use the Assign Default button to assign one of the inbound gates and one of the outbound gates as the default gate. Note that if you assign an inbound/outbound gate as the default gate, you need not assign any other gates as the default gate. If you do not assign the default gates, then the system does not allow you to activate the yard. Docking Locations Choose the add icon in this section to add entries of docking locations. The system displays the list of active docking locations in the same time zone that you have maintained in the Manage Entities app. You can select the docking locations that you want to add to the yard. Viewing a Yard Displays detailed information about a yard's status, location, business hours, gates, and docking locations. To view the yard settings, proceed as follows: 1. Choose the Yard tab on the left pane. 2. Enter the yard ID in the search bar on the left pane to search for a specific yard. 3. Choose a yard from the results.  Note You can add only one entry of business hours for a yard.  Note The system displays active gates in the same time zone that are either shared with yards or active gates in the same time zone that are yet to be associated with a yard.  Note The system displays only the active docking locations in the same time zone. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 93 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The system displays the detail view of the settings on a right pane. The detail view consists of a header and other sections. Header The header section displays the following information: Yard ID Location ID Yard Icon Displays the yard icon. Also displays a shared sign on this icon when a yard has enabled sharing with business partners. You can view the sharing details by choosing this icon. The system displays the Yard ID, Location ID, Shared By, and Permissions. Status Displays one of the following statuses: Draft This status appears after you create a yard and choose the Save button. You can delete a yard only when it is in a draft status. Active This status appears when you activate a draft or an inactive yard or when you choose the Save and Activate button while creating a new yard. Inactive This status appears when you deactivate a yard by choosing the Deactivate button. Note that deactivation may take some time and you may have to refresh your page to get the updated status. You cannot deactivate a yard that is associated with active gates. Decommissioned This status appears when you close a yard by choosing the Decommission button. You can only decommission yards that are in the inactive status. Once you decommission a yard, you cannot activate it or perform any actions. Details The details section displays the following information: Location ID Description Displays the location description. The system retrieves this information once from the master data of the associated location when the location has been assigned to the yard. Address Displays the location address. The system retrieves this information once from the master data of the associated location when the location has been assigned to the yard. Time Zone 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 94 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Displays the time zone of the location. The system retrieves this information once from the master data of the associated location when the location has been assigned to the yard. Yard ID Remarks Displays additional information about the yard in this section. Share Entity You can share the yard details with your business partner. Based on the settings you provide here, the business partner can either view or view and edit the yard details. This section displays the following information: Created By Displays the details of who created the yard sharing. Share Entity With Displays the business partners with whom the yard has been shared with. Permissions Displays whether the business partner can only view or edit the yard settings. Business Hours This section displays the business hours of the yard. This section displays the following information: Period Displays the duration for which the entry of business hours is valid. Working Days Displays the working days of the yard. Working Hours Displays the working hours for the specified working days. Gates Displays the list of gates in the same time zone that are associated with the yard. This section displays the following information for each entry: Gate ID  Note You can only share active yards with your business partners. That is, when you create a yard, save, and activate the setting, you can edit the yard settings and add sharing details. As a prerequisite, you must establish a relationship with the business partner (shipper) with whom you want to share your yard. To do so, use the Invite Business Partners app and add a new invitee as a shipper. The shipper must operate in the same data center as you. For more information, see Add New Business Partners. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 95 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Description Direction Working Hours Default Gate Displays whether the gate is a default gate Docking Locations Displays the list of docking locations that are associated with the yard. This section displays the following information for each entry: Docking Location ID Description Working Hours Uploading and Downloading Yards SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration enables you to simplify the entity management process especially when you have lot of entities to be processed. You can view, edit, and upload entities using a Microsoft Excel file. This feature enables you to work on multiple entries simultaneously thereby saving a lot of time. You can download and upload the entities in Microsoft Excel format. In the Yard tab, in the worklist area on the left, you can view the Excel button. When you choose this button, you can select one of the following options: Download You can download all the yard entities in Microsoft Excel. Upload You can upload the edited Microsoft Excel template containing the yards that you want to add. Export Template You can download this Microsoft Excel template file to add the yards and upload it in the system. Download Yards Microsoft Excel The downloaded yards Microsoft Excel file contains the following worksheets: Yard This worksheet contains all the information in the yard Details tab in the Manage Entities app. You can view the following columns: Yard reference As the yard information has been split across different worksheets in this Microsoft Excel file, the system has created this reference ID in the Microsoft Excel file. When you switch to another worksheet, you can use this reference ID to logically map the relevant data. Yard ID 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 96 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Location ID Time zone Business Working Hours This worksheet contains all the information in the yard Business Hours tab in the Manage Entities app. You can view the following columns: Yard reference Time period reference Start date End date Working days Start time End time Note that you can edit all the fields in this worksheet similar to the edit option in yard in the Manage Entities app. Docking Location Association This worksheet contains the associations between the yard and docking locations. You can view the Yard Reference and the associated Docking Location Reference in this worksheet. Note that you can edit both the above fields are editable. Docking Location This worksheet contains the Docking Location Reference, Docking Location ID, and Description. Note that all the fields in this worksheet are non-editable similar to the edit option in yard in the Manage Entities app. Gate Association This worksheet contains the associations between the yard and gate. You can view the Yard Reference and the associated Gate Reference in this worksheet. Note that you can edit both the above fields are editable. Gate This worksheet contains the Gate Reference, Gate ID, Description, and Direction. Note that all the fields in this worksheet are non-editable similar to the edit option in yard in the Manage Entities app. Upload Yards Microsoft Excel To upload the yards in a Microsoft Excel file, perform the following: 1. You can use the yards file that you previously downloaded using the Download option to edit the existing data.  Note For yard entities in draft status, you can edit all the above fields. For yard entities in active and inactive statuses, all the above fields are non-editable similar to the edit option in yard in the Manage Entities app. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 97 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Alternatively, you can download the template by choosing Yard Excel Export Template option to add new yards. This template contains the same worksheets and columns similar to the downloaded yards Microsoft Excel file. However, it does not contain any data. Note that you can only use either the template or the downloaded file to upload into the system. 2. Upload the Excel file by choosing Yard Excel Upload . Upload entities dialog box appears. 3. Select the edited file that you want to upload from your computer and choose Proceed. The system displays the confirmation message indicating the number of yard entities that will be uploaded. It will also display the error log if some of the entities are in error state. You can download the error log to investigate the issue. 4. Choose Confirm to upload the entities. Displays whether the entities are uploaded. If they are uploaded, you can view them in the Yard tab in the app. Manage Dock Appointments You, as a shipper, can use this app to manage (view, edit, cancel) the dock appointments that carriers have booked for loading or unloading services in the docking locations of your organization. In this app, you can also apply instance-based authorization. This helps you to restrict the shippers who can access the dock appointments of a certain docking location to only those that are involved in the management of that location. The main features of this app include: Reschedule a dock appointment Cancel a dock appointment Create a dock appointment Reserve a time slot Docking Locations You can view all docking locations in the overview page. The system displays the details of each docking location in a card format. You can filter the docking locations based on the Location ID, Description, and Address.  Note There are a few columns that are hidden in the worksheets. These columns contain technical information. You cannot edit these columns. Adding of Enable Sharing option is currently not available in the Microsoft Excel file. You cannot edit the status of the yard in the Microsoft Excel file. You can only change the status in the Manage Entities app. You can only upload Microsoft Excel files with a maximum of 2500 entries.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 98 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Each docking location card displays the following information: Location ID Displays the location ID of the docking location. Note that the system retrieves the docking location details that you have created in the Docking Location Settings app. Description Displays the description for the docking location that you have specified in the Docking Location Settings app. Address Displays the address of the docking location that you have specified in the Docking Location Settings app. Booked Appointments Displays the number of future active appointments booked in this docking location in the current week. Ready for Booking Displays the number of documents that are ready for booking an appointment in the current week. Current Week Slot Utilization Displays the number of appointments in this docking location for the current week. Detail View (Manage Dock Appointments) The detail view of a docking location consists of a calendar view and a table view. Calendar View When you choose a docking location in the worklist page, the system by default opens the calendar of appointments for the docking location. You can view the appointment calendar for the entire docking location in the All tab. You can also view the individual appointment calendar for each loading point available in the selected docking location by choosing the various tabs with the loading point ID. Non- working hours are displayed as greyed-out in 15-minute intervals, based on the validity period of the loading point. You can switch between the day, week, and month view for the loading point calendars. Based on the view that you choose, the system displays the appointments for the specific day, week, or month. Note that the system applies this setting across all the loading point calendars in the docking location. The system displays all the appointments for the day along with the freight order details. Note that in the month view of the calendar, if there is no space to display all the appointments, the system displays some of the appointments in a dialog box. You can also resize this dialog box as desired. In the calendar view, you can view an icon in the upper right corner of the calendar. When you choose this icon, the system displays the details of calendar and appointments color coding. The following are the descriptions of various icons used in the calendar view. Icon Description Arrival 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 99 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Icon Description Check-In Begin Check-In On Hold Checked In Loading Unloading Executed Overdue Grouped Blocked Time You can drag and drop an appointment in the calendar to reschedule an appointment. You can use the static search option on the header area to search for booked appointments based on a given freight order ID, appointment ID, or reference document ID. The search is globally conducted for all loading points in the All tab, and separately conducted in the individual appointment calendar for each loading point. The number of matches found in the search is indicated in parentheses, like (1), at the end of the tab name, and the best appointment match is displayed in the Maintain Appointment view. If you have, for example, several appointments that are based on the same freight order, you get several hits for the same freight order, and the system randomly selects one appointment to be displayed as the best match.  Note You can drag and drop to reschedule only those appointments which have time slots in multiples of 30 minutes (for example, 9:00 – 10:00 or 9:30 – 10:30). If the time slots are not in multiples of 30 minutes (for example, 8:45 – 9:45 or 8:15 – 9:15), then you cannot drag and drop to reschedule appointment. However, you can select the appointment and change the time using input boxes. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 100 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --
