file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Discover Business Partners Finding the right business partners is always a challenge. However, this will be easier once your partners-to-be have joined SAP Business Network for Logistics. As a simple yet powerful app in SAP Business Network for Logistics, Discover Business Partners helps you search the network for logistics service providers, then from the results, invite suitable ones to be your business partners. Prerequisites To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. Search for Business Partners To search for business partners on the network, enter a key word, for example the company name, in the search box and then press Enter . You can also use faceted search on the left pane to narrow down your search results. When using faceted search, you can even leave the search box empty. This is useful if you want to explore your potential partners in a specific region or industry. Result A set of matched results are returned. You can click to open the details page of a matched result. Send Request for Connection To send a request for connection to your potential business partners, proceed as follows: 1. Click to select the company to which you want to send the request for connection from the Matched Results table. 2. Choose Request for Connection. The request for connection is sent to the selected companies. Results A request for connection is sent to the selected company. Once the company accepts your request, you will become business partners. After you’ve set up a partnership with a business partner via this app, you must update the business partner’s LBN ID in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). To do this, see Updating Business Partner’s LBN ID. References If the uploaded Microsoft Excel file contains the same charge type or a condition type repeated more than once, the system does not upload the entire file.  Note If the business partners you are trying to connect with operates in a different data center, you must first ensure that your company profile is available across all data centers of SAP Business Network for Logistics. For more information, refer to Profile Settings.  Note If the companies that match your search conditions are not found, see Discover Business Partners App and refer to "Why companies that match my search conditions are not returned in the Matched Results table?" 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 31 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Manage Business Profile Manage Invitations Updating Business Partner’s LBN ID To update the LBN ID in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) for a logistics service provider who’s become your business partner, proceed as follows in SAP TM: 1. Go to the Manage Business Partner transaction (transaction BP). 2. Set the filter criteria to find the business partner for which you want to update the LBN ID and then double-click the business partner to open its Display Organization page. 3. Navigate to the Identification tab. In the Identification Numbers section, IDType field, enter LBN001. 4. In the Identification Number field, enter the LBN ID and save your changes. Invite Business Partners The Invite Business Partners app is designed for managing all the business partners that you want to be part of your network. You can use this app to select and invite business partners to join your business network and check their participation status. If you have access, you can navigate to the Discover Business Partners app to find more potential business partners. You may have business with many partners in your system and you may want to persist your business with them in SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can download the Excel template available in the app and fill the details of the business partners using this template. You can then upload the template back in the app. If you are using SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system, you can download these business partners from SAP TM system and upload them in Invite Business Partners. For more information, see Downloading Carrier Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). You can select one or more of these business partners from your system and invite them to join your network. When you submit these partners, a back-end team manages your connection invitation. For more information, see Connection Invitations. When a business partner accepts an invitation to connect with your network, the system updates the unique LBN ID of the partner. If you are using SAP TM system, you can update these LBN IDs of partners in SAP TM system by downloading the partner list from the  Note To use these apps, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note You must make sure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non purpose-related way in the Microsoft Excel file. The file size of each business partners Excel cannot be larger than 2MB, and the maximum number of rows in each file is 5000. A digital freight forwarder is managed as a business partner in both the SAP Business Network for Logistics and SAP Transportation Management system. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 32 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Discover Business Partners app and uploading the list in your SAP TM system. For more information, see Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). The Discover Business Partners app consists of the following areas: Filter bar You can filter the business partner based on one more of the filter options (Business Partner ID and Business Partner) that appear on the header area. Worklists by status The business partners are categorized based on their invitation response status: To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted, and Rejected. Worklist (Manage Business Partners) There are different ways to manage all the business partners and to set filters. To search for a specific business partner, you can use the filter bar in the header. The system also displays preconfigured worklists (To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted, Rejected) based on the business partner's invitation response status. Filter Bar With the filter bar, you can do the following: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for business partners. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper-left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. To Be Submitted The To Be Submitted worklist displays all the business partners that you have uploaded or added in the app but have not yet submitted to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitations. This worklist also displays connection invitations that have been rejected. The worklist displays the following details for each invitation: System ID Business Partner ID Invitee Company Role SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code)  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 33 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Phone number Email Language City Country/Region Zip code Status In Progress The In Progress worklist displays all the business partners that you have submitted to the back-end team to manage the connection invitations. These business partners have not yet responded to your invitation to connect with your network. You can recall your invitation in this worklist if needed. The In Progress worklist has the same columns as the To Be Submitted worklist. Accepted The Accepted worklist displays all the business partners who have accepted your invitation to join your business network. You can select one or more business partners in the Accepted tab and download them in Microsoft Excel format. The Accepted worklist has the same columns as the In Progress worklist along with the unique LBN ID of the business partner. Rejected The Rejected worklist displays all the business partners who have rejected your invitation to join your business network via Discover Business Partners. The Rejected worklist has the same columns as the Accepted worklist. Using the settings icon on each worklist, you can control the number of columns displayed in the To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted, and Rejected tabs. You can also sort and filter the business partners in these worklists based on various attributes. Add New Business Partners You can add new business partners to the Invite Business Partners app in one of the following ways: Manual entry  Note A rejected invitation is displayed on the To Be Submitted worklist with the status "Returned by LBN OPS team" if it was submitted via the Invite Business Partners app. A rejected invitation is displayed on the Rejected worklist if it was submitted via the Discover Business Partners app. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 34 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- On the To Be Submitted tab, you can manually add a new business partner to the Invite Business Partners app by choosing Add Invitee Business Partner . You can also add a shipper to the app by choosing Add Invitee Shipper . When adding a shipper, you must provide the shipper's LBN ID. Using this method, you can specify the language of your connection invitations. Supported languages are: English Arabic Bulgarian Chinese Simplified Chinese Traditional Croatian Czech Danish Dutch Finnish French German Greek Hebrew Hungarian Italian Japanese Korean Malay Norwegian Polish Portuguese (Brazilian) Romanian Russian Serbian Slovak Spanish Swedish Thai Turkish Manual entry with an Excel template 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 35 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- You can download the Excel template available in the Invite Business Partners app by choosing the Download Excel Template button. You can fill the details of the business partners using this template. You can then upload this template back in the Invite Business Partners app. Downloading business partner Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system You can download the list of business partners in your SAP TM system and upload the Excel file in the Invite Business Partners app. For more information, see Download Carrier Excel from SAP Transportation Management System. You can select one or more business partners in the To Be Submitted worklist and delete them from the Invite Business Partners app. Note that you cannot delete the business partners that you have submitted to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitation. Connection Invitations Once you have a list of business partners added to the Invite Business Partners app, you can select one or more partners from the To Be Submitted worklist and choose Submit. Once you choose Submit, the system instantaneously sends a request to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitation. The system moves the submitted business partners to the In Progress worklist. Shippers in both production and test environments can use the Invite Business Partners app to send connection invitations to business partners. If the invitees are not yet on the network, they can activate their accounts via a simplified account activation process and collaborate with the inviter in the respective environment (either production or test). You can refer your invitees to the following resource for their account activation: Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process. Note that business partners need your contact information when you send them an invitation to join your business network. If you have not maintained a default address in the Manage Business Profile app, the system does not allow you to submit business partners. For more information on adding a default address, see Edit Company Profile. The back-end team sends an invitation to the business partners requesting them to connect with your network. The business partner can view this connection invitation using the Manage Invitations app and choose to accept or reject the invitation. For more information, see Manage Invitations. When the business partner accepts or rejects an invitation, you will be notified of the same and the system moves the business partner to the accepted or rejected worklist as appropriate. If a partner accepts your invitation, the partner connects with your network and you can perform business transactions with this partner. If a business partner rejects your invitation, the partner is not connected with your network and you cannot perform any business transactions with this partner. You can find the rejected invitation from the To Be Submitted worklist and resend it if you want to.  Note When you upload a business partner Excel in the Invite Business Partners app, the system automatically filters out the erroneous business partner records and selects only the correct business partner records. For example, in the downloaded Excel file, if there are business partners that already exist in the Invite Business Partners app with the status as In Progress, Accepted or Rejected, or if some of the entries do not contain any of the mandatory fields, the system ignores such entries and uploads all the other entries. When you upload a business partner Excel, the system performs a validation. If there are no validation errors, the business partner Excel is uploaded. If there are validation errors, the system displays the erroneous entries in an error log. The system allows you to download this error log. You must make sure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non purpose-related way in the Microsoft Excel file. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 36 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- The system updates the unique LBN IDs of the business partners who have accepted your connection invitation. You can view this LBN ID in the Accepted worklist for each business partner. If you are using SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system, you can update these LBN IDs of business partners in SAP TM system by downloading the business partner list from the Invite Business Partners app and uploading the list in your SAP TM system. For more information, see Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). Recall Invitations You can recall a submitted invitation as long as its status remains "In Progress". To recall the invitation, switch to the In Progress worklist, click to open the invitation that you want to recall, and then choose Recall on the details page. After being recalled, the invitation returns to the To Be Submitted worklist and becomes editable. The business partner cannot view the recalled invitation using the app until you submit it again. Downloading Business Partner Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) You can download the business partners from the SAP TM system and upload them to the Invite Business Partners app. Context In SAP TM system, you must perform the following steps to download the business partner Excel: Procedure 1. Execute the report /SCMTMS/R_LBN_CARR_LIST_DWNLD in transaction SE38. 2. Enter your SAP TM organization ID in the Organizational ID field and execute. The system determines the hierarchy of this organization and retrieves all the freight agreements that are valid at the time of searching. The system then determines the valid business partners from these agreements. Note that if you select the Show Application Log checkbox, the system displays the detailed information about the business partner determination process. 3. Alternatively, instead of entering an organization ID and retrieving multiple business partners, you can also enter the business partner IDs in the Carrier IDs field and execute. The system retrieves the details of all the business partners that you have entered. 4. Select all the business partners that you want to download and then choose Download. The system downloads the Excel file. Next Steps Once you download the Excel file, in the Invite Business Partners app, choose the Upload Business Partners button to upload this Excel. Once you upload the Excel file with a list of partners, the system updates the To Be Submitted worklist in the app with the partner details in the Excel.  Note You can't recall an invitation when its status is "Invitation email sent to business partner". 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 37 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) You can update the SAP TM system with the unique LBN IDs of the business partners who have accepted to connect with your business network. Context To do so, you must perform the following: Procedure 1. Download the list of business partners with their LBN IDs from the Accepted worklist in the Invite Business Partners app. The system downloads the list of partners in a CSV format. 2. In the SAP TM system, execute the report /SCMTMS/R_LBN_ID_BP_UPD in transaction SA38. 3. Browse for the CSV file that you have downloaded and upload the file. The system updates the business partner IDs for the partners in the system. Note that you can choose whether you want the system to process the upload job in the background or foreground. If you choose to process the upload job in the foreground, the system displays the error logs if there are any. Configure Partner Connections You can use the Configure Partner Connections app to establish a B2B connection to the external systems of your business partners. Using this configuration, SAP Business Network for Logistics can directly send documents to your partner’s external systems. Prerequisites SAP Business Network for Logistics must support the desired business partner for B2B connectivity. This means that your company must agree on B2B integration with your carrier. Then, you must invite your network partner to join SAP Business Network for Logistics using the Invite Business Partners app. Only then will the network partner be visible in the Configure Partner Connections app. The process of using the Configure Partner Connections app to create a connection and to authenticate messages includes the following steps: 1. Manage Credential Details 2. Create Partner Connection  Note System IDs may consist of alphanumerical characters and the underscore ( _ ) character. You can check the Specification tab of the Excel for further guidance. The system checks all records when you upload your Excel, and displays the errors on the Upload Business Partners screen. You can correct the errors in your Excel and upload it again.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 38 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Create Partner Connection Context Using the Configure Partner Connections app, you now need to map the connection details with your business partners and establish a B2B connection. Procedure 1. In the Configure Partner Connections app, choose Create. 2. Provide the following information: Field Explanation Usage (as maintained in Manage Credential Details) Business Partner ID Type* ID type of your individual connected business partner or of all connected business partners. A business partner is an entity with which the LBN customer does business (freight contracting, and order execution). You can maintain the following ID types: LBN ID SCAC P44_EU Motor Carrier Number US DOT GLN VAT SAPBPID – SAP Business Partner Number You can choose between general ID types (Any LBN ID or Any Alternate ID) and specific ID types (such as LBN ID, SCAC, or GLN) for a connection with your business partners. Any LBN ID applies this setting to all business partners that are onboarded in the network and connected to your tenant. You can configure alternate business partner ID types to initiate tracking for your shipments. Onboarding of these business partners to SAP Business Network for Logistics is not required. Business Partner ID Value* Unique identifier representing the business partner. Based on the business partner ID type, you choose the business partner ID value: If you choose LBN ID, the field name is Business Partner (LBN ID). If you choose a different ID than LBN ID, the field name is Business Partner ID Value. Network Partner (LBN ID) LBN ID of your network partner. A network partner is an entity which does data transfer/integration to business partners. Network partners will have many business partners in their network and have built integrations to business partner systems. You must provide this information if you receive the data via a network partner. Service* A service is defined based on the combination of the following information coming from a shipper: SAP Business Network for Logistics supports the transportation modes Road and Ocean with the following services: 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 39 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Field Explanation Usage (as maintained in Manage Credential Details) Tracking type: Specifies if the tracking is based on a device or vehicle (such as the vehicle’s license plate) or based on a shipment indicator (such as a bill of lading) Transportation mode (such as Road) Scenario (such as tracking) Shipping type (such as LTL - less than truck load, or FTL - full truck load) Resource Road Tracking FTL (Removed) Shipment Road Tracking LTL Shipment Tracking All Shipment Road Tracking FTL Resource Road Tracking LTL (Removed) Shipment Ocean Tracking FCL Resource Ocean Tracking FCL (Removed) Shipment Ocean Tracking LCL Resource Ocean Tracking LCL (Removed) Resource Tracking All (Removed) Freight Tendering All Freight Subcontracting All Supply Chain Risk Freight Ocean Booking All Freight Air Booking All Freight Road Subcontracting FTL Freight Road Subcontracting LTL Freight Road Tendering FTL Freight Road Tendering LTL Freight External Planning All Business Partner Credential Credential provided to you by your business partner, which is maintained in the Manage Credential Details view. You must maintain this field if you communicate directly with your business partner’s system. Network Partner Credential Credential provided to you by your network partner, which is maintained in the Manage Credential Details view. You must provide this information if you are communicating with your business partner via a network partner.  Caution Resource tracking related services have been removed on August 17th, 2024. You can use the shipment tracking related services instead.  Note Only those services that are supported by your business partner will be shown in the dropdown box. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 40 This is custom documentation. Manage Credential Details Context The Manage Credential Details view is a secure storage for you to maintain all the credentials that you receive from your business partner or network partner with whom you would like to enable B2B communication. A network partner can consist of a network of business partners (in this case of carriers) that provides services like tracking, freight tendering, and subcontracting. SAP Business Network for Logistics supports the following credential types: Basic OAuth 2.0 API Key project44 For more information, see the Configuration and Application Guide for project44 add-ons. Procedure 1. In the Configure Partner Connections app, choose Manage Credential Details. 2. Select the tab with the credential type that you want to use for maintaining the credential details. 3. Choose Add and complete the dialog. 4. (Optional): To change the credential details, select the row and choose Edit. System Connections (Shipper) Use the System Connections app for shippers to create a connection and to authenticate inbound and outbound messages between SAP Business Network for Logistics and your on-premise SAP Transportation Management standalone system or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA.  Note This feature is only available for SAP Business Network for Logistics standard APIs and not for custom API integrations. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 41 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- You can use the app in combination with each of the following exchange infrastructures between SAP Business Network for Logistics and your SAP backend system: SAP Cloud Integration SAP Process Integration Direct integration using SOA Manager The process of using the System Connections app to create a connection and to authenticate messages includes the following steps: 1. Creating a Connection. 2. Authenticating Inbound Messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics. 3. Authenticating Outbound Messages from SAP Business Network for Logistics. 4. Activating the Connection. Creating a Connection By creating a connection in the System Connections app, you can then specify the details required for authenticating inbound and outbound messages between SAP Business Network for Logistics and your SAP backend system. If you need to connect multiple backend systems, create a connection for each system. Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, click Add in the Connections column. 2. In the New Connection dialog box, select a connection type from the list. The following connection types are available: ABAP-based SAP system Qualtrics SAP Analytics Cloud SAP Cloud ALM 3. Enter the following information for the new connection. a. Connection ID: meaningful name of the connection b. System ID: ID of the system you’re connecting, for example, QW9.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note Specify the source system ID as it appears in your external system (such as SAP Transportation Management). The format must be specified exactly as it appears in the external system. For example, QM7_910. If you use another system ID or change the system ID afterwards, this can have severe consequences. Your processes might stop working.  Caution 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 42 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- c. Logical System ID: logical system ID of the system you’re connecting, for example, QW9CLNT170. The Logical System ID field is only available to the ABAP-based SAP system connection type. This setting helps users using both the freight collaboration and global track and trace solutions avoid duplicated tracking records. 4. Click Add. The certificate is signed by SAP Passport Certification Authority. For more information, see Configuring a Certificate for API Authentication. Alternatively, you can use a client certificate that’s signed by one of the following third-party certification authorities. Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, select the connection and on the Inbound to Network tab, click Add. 2. In the Add Certificate dialog, enter a meaningful name for the certificate details, and upload the client certificate. a. Note, you can use a certificate for only one connection. b. Make sure you upload the same client certificate to your SAP backend system. This step establishes trust between the systems. 3. When the certificate expires, you need to get a new one and repeat these steps to upload it. To receive notifications about certificate expiration, subscribe to the system notification service. Securing the communication between SAP Business Network for Logistics and your on-premise system with Client Certificate, Basic Authentication, or using Cloud Connector with Basic Authentication. Related Information Mapping the URLs of your SAP On-Premise System to Service Interfaces Securing Communication Between SAP Business Network for Logistics and your SAP On-Premise System Mapping the URLs of your SAP On-Premise System to Service Interfaces The first step in authenticating outbound messages from SAP Business Network for Logistics to your on-premise SAP Transportation Management standalone system or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA is to map the URLs of your on-premise system to the service interfaces (message types) you want to use. Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, select the connection and then on the Outbound from Network tab, click Add Destination. 2. In the Add Destination dialog, select a service interface and enter the corresponding URL of your on-premise system (see the following table for more information). Related Information Securing Communication Between SAP Business Network for Logistics and your SAP On-Premise System The second step in authenticating outbound messages from SAP Business Network for Logistics to your on-premise SAP Transportation Management standalone system or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA is to secure the connection with either client certificate authentication or Cloud Connector.  Note The Cloud Connector only supports inbound connections using HTTP; it doesn't support HTTPS. Administrators can choose between using HTTP or HTTPS when the Cloud Connector communicates with on-premise systems. Please refer to Supported Protocols of Cloud Connector for more details. If you select Cloud Connector with Basic Authentication as the Active Authentication Type, remember that you should configure the destination service URL with only the HTTP protocol. This URL corresponds to the virtual host set in your Cloud Connector's Cloud To On-Premise notification. This applies regardless of whether you've configured an HTTP or HTTPS port in your backend SAP S/4HANA system using SOAMANAGER configurations. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 46 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Using client certificate authentication can be used with all exchange infrastructures, however, you must use it if you use the exchange infrastructure SAP Cloud Integration. Note, to use client certificate authentication, you must add a range of your system's IP addresses to an allowlist. For more information about adding IP addresses to an allowlist, see Country/Region Availability. Using basic authentication is possible in case your integration layer supports basic authentication. Using Cloud Connector is recommended. For more information about the advantages of using Cloud Connector, see Cloud Connector. Note, Cloud Connector is incompatible with the exchange infrastructure SAP Cloud Integration. Related Information Using Client Certificate Authentication Using Cloud Connector with Basic Authentication Using Basic Authentication Using Client Certificate Authentication To apply a client certificate, follow these steps: Procedure 1. Open the System Connections app, locate the connection for which you want to apply or renew the client certificate, and then switch to the Outbound from Network tab on the right pane. 2. Choose Configure Connections. a. In the General tab, double confirm the Active Authentication Type is Client Certificate. b. Click Download Certificate Chain to download the client certificate (p7b files). If the expiration of the certificate is distant, the active certificate (CertChain_Active_TimeStamp.p7b) is downloaded. If the certificate is about to expire, both the active certificate and the new certificate (CertChain_New_TimeStamp.p7b) are downloaded. Both certificates are functional. 3. Extract the p7b file using KeyStore Explorer. We recommend extracting the new certificate if it's downloaded. Otherwise, extract the active one. 4. Locate the leaf certificate in the Certificate Hierarchy section and click Export to export it as a .cer file. 5. Open the .cer file in a text editor and copy the content. 6. Go to the SAP BTP cockpit, choose the subaccount that host your SAP Cloud Integration application. 7. Create an integration instance: a. Select Process Integration Runtime in the Service dropdown list, select Integration-flow in the Plan dropdown list and then specify the instance name. b. Set Roles to ESBMessaging.send, set Grant-types to Client Credentials, and then click Create. 8. In the newly created integration instance, click Create in the Service Key section to create a service key that applies the new client certificate: a. Set the Key Type to External Certificate. b. Paste the content you copied in step 5 into the External Certificate field. c. Save the service key. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Using Cloud Connector with Basic Authentication SAP Business Network for Logistics can be used in combination with Cloud Connector to enable secure communication with your SAP on-premise system (in this case SAP Transportation Management standalone or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA). Prerequisites You have an SAP user account, for example an S-user or P-user in SAP ID service (https://accounts.sap.com ). The S-user ID is provided in the order form to your SAP Account Manager. To obtain a P-user ID, go to https://www.sap.com/index.html and register a new user using his or her email address. If a user has already been registered with the SAP ID service (for example, at SAP Community or SAP Developer Center ) using the same email address, the user does not need to register again. For more information about creating a user, see Create SAP User Accounts. You have installed Cloud Connector. For more information about installing Cloud Connector, see Installation. Context After completing the prerequisites, complete the following steps in the System Connections app: Procedure 1. Specify a location ID and SAP User to use with the Cloud Connector. a. Click Manage Cloud Connector Details. b. On the Locations tab, click Add and enter a location ID. You can also search for a location ID. Later on, you'll need to enter the location ID when adding the SAP Business Network for Logistics subaccount to Cloud Connector (see Next Steps below). c. Set the status to Released. This allows you to assign the location ID to an interface. d. On the SAP Users tab, click Add. In the SAP User ID or Email ID column, enter an email ID or the SAP user that you created earlier (see Prerequisites above). You can search also for an SAP user ID, or email ID. e. Click Save. 2. Configure your connection. a. Select the Configure Connections button in the Outbound from Network tab. b. In the General tab, select Cloud Connector with Basic Authentication from the Active Authentication Type drop down list. c. Select Email ID and Location ID from the corresponding dropdown lists. d. Click Save. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Maintaining SAC Connection To enable secured access to SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), you must establish mutual trust between your Identity Authentication tenant and a tenant for the embedded analytics toolsets. Context In the System Connections app, proceed as follows: Procedure 1. To add a connection, choose Add in the Connections view. Select SAP Analytics Cloud as the connection type, enter a connection ID and a system ID. 2. In the Trust Configurations view, select a name identifier for the trust configuration, and upload an XML file with the metadata. Save your entries. The Status will show In Progress. 3. Select Refresh Status a few times until the status changes to active or inactive. Status Description In Progress Trust configuration is in progress. SAP Business Network for Logistics is uploading the metadata file. Active Trust is established Inactive Error status on trust configuration 4. Choose Download SAML Metadata to download the metadata file for the SAC tenant. For more information, see the Administration Guide for SAP Business Network, intelligent insights add-on on SAP Help Portal at https://help.sap.com/viewer/product/SAP_LBN_II_OPTION, and choose Authorize Users for Embedded Analytics Toolsets. Maintaining SAP Cloud ALM Connection You can maintain the system URL and the credentials for a connection to your instance of SAP Cloud ALM so that the Manage Integration Logs app can send integration message logs to SAP Cloud ALM. Context In the System Connections app, proceed as follows: Procedure 1. To add a connection, choose Add in the Connections view. Select SAP Cloud ALM as the connection type, enter a connection ID and a system ID. 2. Choose Maintain Authentication Details, then Add. Save your entries. 3. In the main view, maintain the system URL for SAP Cloud ALM and the authentication alias. Save your entries. 4. Activate the connection. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- You – as a shipper – connect your TM systems to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration using the System Connections app. You do so by creating a connection and configuring your inbound and outbound connections in the app. This facilitates a flow of messages between the two systems. To facilitate easy transition between the two systems, you can configure navigation links to business documents in your external systems (such as SAP Transportation Management standalone or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA). Context In the System Connections app, under the same connection where you – as a shipper – have configured an inbound and outbound connection from the TM system, you can maintain the navigation links for business documents (freight orders and ocean freight bookings). To configure a link to a business document, complete the following steps: Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, locate the connection for which you want to create business document links on the left pane. 2. Select Create Document Links in the upper-right corner. This opens the Configure Document Links panel. Then select Create. 3. In the Create Document Link dialog box, enter the following data: Field Purpose Example Value Document Type You can navigate to the following business documents in your external system: From the Manage Disputes app, you can navigate to freight orders. From the Track Freight Movement app, you can navigate to ocean freight bookings. Freight order Base URL Contains the protocol, host, domain, and port of the external target system. https://uit210-tms001.au.sap.corp Path Path to the app in the external target system. /sap/bc/ui5_ui5/ui2/ushell/shells/abap/FioriLaunchpad.html#FreightOrder- changeRoad  Note You can create document links only for connections of the ABAP-based SAP system type.  Note To find the Logical System Name, start transaction SE16. Configure Survey Delivery Settings You as a shipper, may want to send event-based experience management surveys on a regular basis to your customers and carriers to get their feedback on the event execution experience. SAP Business Network for Logistics enables you to configure the delivery settings for the surveys that you maintain in the Qualtrics system. Note that to maintain a connection from your SAP Business Network for Logistics system to the Qualtrics system, you must maintain the appropriate settings in the System Connections app. For more information, see Maintaining Qualtrics Connection. You can create a user account in Qualtrics and create surveys based on the templates provided by SAP Business Network for Logistics. For more information on creating surveys in Qualtrics, see Customer Delivery Experience Management with Qualtrics . In the Configure Survey Delivery Settings app, based on the settings you have defined, the system sends emails to the email IDs that you have maintained at regular intervals. You can also assign a survey to a specific scenario, location, carrier, and trigger condition. Once the recipients receive the email, fill and submit the survey, the Qualtrics system collates all the feedback and provides the information on their experience. You can use this information to evaluate their experience. The Configure Survey Delivery Settings app consists of the following areas: Filter bar Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter the survey configurations using one or more of the following filters: Location Carrier Survey Name Trigger Condition Delivery Schedule Survey Delivery Configuration Worklist You can view the list of survey configurations that you have already created. When you choose a configuration, the system displays the details on the right pane. Note that when you choose the location name and carrier name you can view the additional details of the location in a dialog box. If you have chosen All Carriers in the carrier setting, you cannot view the additional details. Defining a Survey Delivery Configuration To define a survey delivery configuration, choose Create. The Create New Survey Delivery Configuration pane appears on the right. On this pane, enter the following information: Scenario  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 58 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Select a scenario from the drop-down menu that contains the list of pre-defined business scenarios. Note that as of now, Customer Delivery is the only available scenario. Location Select a location from the input help. Note that these are the locations that you have maintained in the Manage Locations app. Carrier Select either All Carriers or a carrier from the input help that contains the list of carriers. Note that the system selects All Carriers by default when you create a new survey delivery configuration. Trigger Condition Specify on what event you want the delivery to be triggered. Select one or more events from the drop-down menu that contains the pre-defined events. When you select more than one event, the system triggers email delivery on the occurrence of each event based on the delivery schedule and delivery frequency settings. Survey Name Contains the list of survey names. These are the surveys that you have created in the Qualtrics system. Select a survey that must be sent for this scenario. Recipients Enter the list of email addresses to which the survey email must be sent. When you choose the input help, the system displays the list of email addresses that you have maintained in the Manage Locations app for the selected location. You can select one or more email addresses from the input help to which the survey email must be sent. Delivery Schedule Specify whether you want the delivery to be done every n events or every n days. You define the value of n in the Delivery Frequency field. Note that the system selects Every N Events by default when you create a new survey delivery configuration. Delivery Frequency Specify a number. The value that you specify here aligns with the Delivery Schedule. For example, if you have selected the Delivery Schedule as Every N Events and specified the Delivery Frequency as 10, then the system schedules the survey email to be sent on completion of every 10 events. Note that the system selects 1 by default when you create a new survey delivery configuration. When you choose Save, the system saves the survey delivery configuration.  Note All the above fields are mandatory. You cannot maintain more than one survey delivery configuration for a specific combination of scenario, location, and carrier. For example, if you have created a survey delivery configuration with the scenario as Customer Delivery, location as Location A, and carrier as Carrier X, you cannot create another survey delivery configuration with the same attributes. However, you can create a configuration with the scenario as Customer Delivery, location as Location A, and carrier as All Carriers. In this case, when a survey must be sent to the carrier X, the settings with the carrier as Carrier X takes precedence over the settings for all carriers. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 59 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- More Information Maintaining Qualtrics Connection Configure Survey Delivery Settings Customer Delivery Experience Management with Qualtrics Dock Appointment Scheduling Dock appointment scheduling in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration allows shippers to book appointments for loading and unloading services. Integration with external systems like SAP EWM and SAP TM is possible, and APIs are available for appointment creation and cancellation. As a shipper, you can use dock appointment scheduling functionality in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration to book dock appointments for a loading point on behalf of the carrier for loading or unloading services in the docking locations of your organization. You can create dock appointments for confirmed freight orders in SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can also integrate dock appointment scheduling functionality in SAP Business Network for Logistics with external systems such as SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM), Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) on SAP S/4HANA, SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM), and Transportation Management on SAP S/4HANA. For this integration, SAP offers APIs to trigger appointment creation and cancelation from an external system to SAP Business Network for Logistics system and send the appointment confirmation from SAP Business Network for Logistics system to your external system. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Prerequisites Before shippers can start booking dock appointments, they need to take some settings in other apps, such as the Manage Locations or General Settings app. You must create a location master data in the Manage Locations app. For more information on creation of a location, see Creating a Location Settings to Enable Appointment Booking To book appointments with the Manage Dock Appointments app and to enable the carriers to self-book dock appointments, you must enable certain settings. The carrier can create a dock appointment before or after confirming a freight order based on your settings. To enable you and the carrier to book dock appointments for a confirmed freight order, you must perform the following: 1. In the Manage Locations app, you must create a location with the following settings: Specify Object Type as Business Partner. Specify the source system ID as it appears in your SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system. Note that the format must be specified exactly as it appears in the SAP TM system. For example, QM7_910. In the External ID field, enter the business partner ID of the business partner associated with the purchasing organization as it appears in the SAP Transportation Management system. Note that in the General Settings app, the system represents the ordering party ID in the format <source system ID>: <external ID>. For more information, see Creating a Location. 2. In the Docking Location Settings app, you must maintain this location as a loading or unloading point and as an active location. For more information, see Manage Entities. You can also enable a carrier or a warehouse operator to create an appointment for a freight order that has not yet been confirmed. To do so, along with the above-mentioned settings, in the General Settings app, you must perform the following: 1. In the Define Appointment Settings tab, add the ordering party by selecting the entry with the system ID and external ID that you created. 2. For this ordering party, under the Maintain Appointment setting, enable the option On Freight Order Creation button. Enabling Role-Based Access Role-based access configuration for the Manage Dock Appointments app involves creating a role from a role template and setting specific location attributes. To enable role-based access of Manage Dock Appointments app and Manage Gate Operations app, proceed as follows: 1. Create a role using the AttributedLocationTemplate role template. You can find this role template under the lbn-live!t1590 application identifier. 2. For the newly-created role, set the location_id attribute in AttributedLocationTemplate to <Source System>:<External ID> of the docking location that you want the shipper to access, for example QM7_910: LBN_WDF. You can find the Source System and External ID of a location in the Manage Locations app. 3. Add this role to the role collection that has been assigned to the shipper. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 61 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Result In the Manage Dock Appointments app, shippers who have the AttributedLocationTemplate role template assigned can only access the dock appointments in the docking location that matches the location_id attribute set in AttributedLocationTemplate. In the Manage Gate Operations app, shippers who have the AttributedLocationTemplate role template assigned can only access gate logbooks associated to the yard location that matches the location_id attribute set in AttributedLocationTemplate. Integration of Dock Appointment Scheduling with Freight Orders Integration of dock appointment scheduling with freight orders in the transportation management (TM) system streamlines logistics by automatically creating and updating appointments based on changes in freight order details. The dock appointment scheduling functionality is integrated with the freight orders from your external systems such as your transportation system. The system uses an inbound message from your transportation system to create a freight order for the carrier in your SAP Business Network for Logistics system. If you have maintained the relevant settings for the carrier in the General Settings app, the system created appointment requests for this freight order. For more information on the settings, see General Settings. Confirming a Freight Order When a carrier confirms a freight order using the Freight Orders for Confirmation app in SAP Business Network for Logistics, the system creates appointment requests for this freight order. When you make any changes to a confirmed freight order in your transportation system or in SAP Business Network for Logistics, the system updates the appointments accordingly. The following table describes what happens when you update a freight order: Freight Order Update Type Appointment Status Notification Change of arrival or departure dates System updates the open and provisional appointments System cancels the confirmed appointments Exception: If the changed dates match the start and end date of the scheduled appointment, the appointment will not be canceled. System triggers notification on cancellation Change of docking location or loading point System updates the open and provisional appointments System cancels the confirmed appointments System triggers notification on cancellation Change of document references No change in status. System updates the document references.  Note In the Manage Dock Appointments app, shippers who do not have the AttributedLocationTemplate role template assigned can access all docking locations. In the Manage Gate Operations app, shippers who do not have the AttributedLocationTemplate role template assigned can access all gate logbooks. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 62 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Freight Order Update Type Appointment Status Notification Other changes No change in status. System updates the changes. Canceling or Rejecting a Freight Order When you cancel a freight order from your transportation system or when a carrier rejects a freight order from the Freight Orders for Confirmation app, the system cancels the relevant appointment requests and the booked appointments. The appointments will not be visible on the Self-Book Dock Appointments app for the carrier and the Manage Dock Appointments app. In addition, an appointment is automatically canceled if one of the following is changed: Arrival dates Departure dates Loading point Docking location Reconfirming a Freight Order When you reconfirm a canceled freight order from your transportation system or when a carrier reconfirms a rejected freight order from the Freight Orders for Confirmation app, the system reopens the relevant appointment requests for booking. Preferred Slots / Slots Preferred by Shipper If the shipper provides the relevant acceptable and requested date and time information, it will be displayed when you maintain an appointment. The requested dates correspond to the Loading of Cargo Start Date/Time and Loading of Cargo End Date/Time fields of the respective stop in the transportation management (TM) system. The UI fields are related to the TransportationOrderRequest message type in TM where start date time and end date time are inside the RequestedLoadingDateTimePeriod and RequestedUnloadingDateTimePeriod tags. The acceptable dates correspond to the Start Date/Time Confirmed by Carrier and End Date/Time Confirmed by Carrier fields of the respective stop in the transportation management (TM) system. The UI fields are related to the TransportationOrderRequest message type in TM where start date time and end date time are inside the AcceptableLoadingDateTimePeriod and AcceptableUnloadingDateTimePeriod tags. Additional Address to Fix Loading Point The subcontracting process passes the loading point ID and unloading point ID from the transportation management system (TM) to SAP Business Network for Logistics. This is done through the Location field under Additional Address at Source Location or Additional Address at Destination Location in TM, which is sent through the InternalID fields under  Note If the changed dates match the start and end date of the scheduled appointment, the appointment will not be canceled. If the start and end date of the scheduled appointment is within the range of the new acceptable start and end date, the appointment will also not be canceled. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 63 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- DetailedLoadingLocation or DetailedUnloadingLocation in the Provider API to Create Freight Order for Subcontracting (TransportationOrderRequest_Out). If the internal ID matches an existing loading point ID, the system preselects and fixes this loading point. It then cannot be changed by the shipper or carrier in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Manage Entities Manage Entities app allows users to define and manage attributes for loading points, docking locations, gates, and yards. You can use this app to define and view the following settings: Loading Point You can define the attributes of a loading point and manage the business hours and block time. Docking Location The loading points situated in the same geographical location are grouped into one docking location. You can define the attributes of a docking location and manage the corresponding loading points. Gate You can define the attributes of a gate and manage the business hours. Yard You can define the attributes of a yard and maintain the corresponding gates and docking locations. Defining Loading Point Settings Loading point settings define operational parameters such as business hours, capacity, and time slot booking for efficient management of loading and unloading activities. To define the settings for a loading point, proceed as follows: 1. Choose the Loading Point tab on the left pane. 2. Choose the Add Loading Point button. The create loading point pane appears on the right. 3. Define settings for the following sections: Details Business Hours Block Time 4. Choose Save to save the loading point as a draft. Choose Save and Activate to activate the loading point settings.  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 64 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Details Enter the following information in the Details section: Loading Point ID Enter the loading point ID. The loading point ID is the identification of a single loading point for differentiation. You must always book a dock appointment for a specific loading point. That’s why you need to create a loading point. A loading point can have several areas (for example, doors), which are represented by the capacity. You must always assign the loading point to a docking location in order to select a loading point for appointment booking. Location ID Select a location ID (optional). You maintain location master data in the Manage Locations app. The location ID is composed of the source system and the external ID as follows: app. The location ID is composed of the source system and the external ID as follows:<Source System>: <External ID>. It is retrieved from the location master data one time at the beginning. After activation it cannot be changed anymore even if the values in the Manage Locations app change. Capacity Specify the number of loading/unloading activities that can be performed concurrently at the loading point. In a logistics setting, a capacity value of 10 typically indicates that there are 10 doors available in the loading area, allowing 10 trucks to be loaded or unloaded simultaneously. However, the exact meaning of capacity depends on how your operational entities – such as loading points and docks – are defined and modeled within your system. For instance, if each door is represented as a loading point in your configuration, then the capacity assigned to each loading point is 1. Address The following fields cannot be changed any longer after the loading point was activated: Under Location Details: Loading Point ID Location ID Description Address Capacity Activity Type Under Time Details: Time Zone Time Slot Booking Time Slot Duration  Note The location ID of the loading point is not used to determine the loading point of the appointment. Instead, the location ID of the docking location is used to determine the docking location for appointment booking. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 65 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Activity Type Specify whether you can perform loading, unloading, or both activities in this loading point. Time Zone Appointment Date Change If you enable this indicator, the carriers can change the date of a dock appointment. You can specify a range for the loading point so that carriers can change the date within the specified range. Note that a date change is only possible before the cut-off time. Advance Up To Specify the number of days up to which the carrier can advance the dock appointment date. Postpone Up To Specify the number of days up to which the carrier can postpone the dock appointment date. Time Slot Booking Time slot booking is disabled by default so that you cannot specify a time slot duration. While booking an appointment, you do not have to select a time slot and the appointment is valid at any time of the day of the appointment date. The time slot duration is set to 0. If you enable time slot booking for this loading point, you can define the time slot duration for which this loading point can be booked. Time Slot Duration You can select a time slot duration for which the loading point can be booked. You can enter a duration between 5 minutes and 23:59 hours. Restrict Maximum Duration of Consecutive Time Slots You can define whether the maximum duration of all consecutive time slots is restricted. This setting ensures that the sum of time slots to be booked by your carrier cannot exceed the maximum consecutive duration of all adjacent time slots. This restriction only affects the booking for the carrier when they select more than one time slot. They can always book at least one time slot. As the shipper, you can always exceed the maximum duration. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Max. Consecutive Timeslot Duration . Maximum Consecutive Duration You can define the maximum duration of all adjacent time slots. Use Derived Appointment Duration If you enable the Use Derived Appointment Duration toggle, the system forces carrier users to book appointment durations based on input from an external system. 1. This can, for example, come from the TransportationOrderRequest message type in SAP Transportation Management or transportation management (TM) in SAP S/4HANA, using the RequestedLoadingDateTimePeriod and/or RequestedUnloadingDateTimePeriod fields. 2. Additionally or instead, you can add a custom implementation and provide the LoadingDuration and UnloadingDuration fields within the TransporationStage. As a prerequisite, you must implement the  Note This setting that you maintain for a loading point, takes precedence over the settings you specify for the Enable Appointment Date Change in the docking location. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 66 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- following SAP Notes: 3680384 - Scheduling Settings Simulation Interface 3662698 - Loading and Unloading Duration in TransportationOrderRequest_Out 2474555 - Additional SOA Documentation for Enterprise Services "Transportation Order" If both options are implemented, the LoadingDuration and UnloadingDuration fields take precedence. 3. Another option is through the Provider API for Dock Appointment Scheduling (GenericAppointment_In), using the RequestedStartDateTime and RequestedEndDateTime fields. For more information about the setup and the underlying processes, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Use Derived Appointment Duration . Overbooking You can enable or disable overbooking for this loading point. When you enable overbooking, the system allows the user to book appointments even after the available slots are booked. If you enable overbooking, the system displays the following: Overbooking Limit If you enable the overbooking setting, you must specify the overbooking limit. Overbooking limit refers to the number of appointments that can be booked once the available slots are booked. Note that as of now you can set the overbooking limit up to 50. Overbooking for Carriers If you enable the overbooking setting, you must either enable or disable the overbooking option for the carriers. When you enable the overbooking option for carriers, the carriers can book appointments even after the available slots are booked. Note that the overbooking limit that you set here applies for the carriers as well when you enable this setting Capacity and Time Slot At You can specify the level at which you want to enable the capacity and time slot settings. You can select one of the following options: Loading Point Level Validity Period Level Working Hours Level Based on the setting you specify here, you can maintain the capacity and time slot at the respective levels. Assignment Details Assignment with Docking Locations If you enable this setting, the loading point can be associated with multiple docking locations in the same time zone. If you disable this setting, the loading point can be associated with only one docking location in the same time zone. Assigned Docking Locations You can select the docking locations in the same time zone with which you want to share the loading point.  Note After loading point activation, this field can only be changed to a lower level ( Loading Point Validity Period Working Hours , and the settings defined for the newly selected level will be used. It can't be changed back to a higher level.  Note The Microsoft Excel upload feature only works if you have selected the Loading Point Level option. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 67 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- After selecting the relevant docking locations, you can assign the loading point to these additional docking locations. To do so, you need to edit the docking location, choose the + icon, and select the loading point from the list under Add Loading Point. Remarks You can enter the additional information about the loading point in this section. Validity Period Choose the add icon in this section to add an entry of validity period. Enter the following information: Period Specify the duration for which the entry of validity period is valid. Working Days Specify the working days of the loading point. Working Hours Specify the working hours for the specified working days. To add another entry of validity period, choose the add icon. You can create up to 10 entries per validity period. It is recommended that you specify the working hours in accordance with the time slot that you have maintained for this loading point. Deleting Validity Periods To delete an entry of validity period, choose the delete icon that appears next to the entry. You can also choose Delete from the details pane that appears on the right when you select the entry of validity period. Note that you cannot delete an entry of validity period if the entry contains appointments in the future. You can only delete an entry that either does not contain any future appointments or contains appointments in the past. Modifying Validity Periods You can select an entry of validity period and modify the details on the right pane. Modifying Periods You can increase or reduce the period.  Note You can add multiple entries of validity period per working day for a loading point. However, the combination of period and working days specified in an entry of validity period must not overlap with the consecutive entries.  Note You can only reduce a period that does not contain any future appointments or contains appointments that are in the past. You cannot reduce the period, if the period that you are reducing contains appointments that are in the future. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 68 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Modifying Working Days You can add a working day for the selected entry of validity period. Note that the system allows you to delete a working day for a time period only when the deleted working day does not contain any future appointments. Modifying Working Hours You can increase or reduce the working hours. Block Time You can block time for special occasions, such as public holidays, maintenance, or cleaning. Choose the add icon in this section to add a time block. The system displays the block time pane on the right. Description Specify a description for the time block. Disable Appointment Booking Specify whether you want to disable appointment booking only for the carriers or for all. If you select For All, both you and the carriers cannot book appointments during the blocked time. If you select For Carriers, only the carriers cannot book an appointment during the blocked time. The blocked time will be available for you to book an appointment. Max. Capacity When you enable the Max. Capacity toggle, the maximum capacity is blocked for this loading point, and the capacity in the dropdown above is disabled because it is no longer relevant. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Maximum Capacity Blocker . Including Overbooking When you enable the Include Overbooking toggle, the capacity maintained under Overbooking Limit is blocked for this loading point. You can only enable this toggle when the Max. Capacity toggle is enabled. Capacity In the dropdown menu, you can view the capacity that you have specified for this loading point. You can select a capacity that you want to block from the dropdown menu. If you have enabled Capacity and Time Slot At as Validity Period Level, you can view and modify the Capacity and Time Slot Duration in this pane.  Note When you modify the working hours, there might be inconsistencies in the start and end time of the time slots. Hence, it is recommended that you modify the working hours in multiples of the time slot duration. You cannot modify the working hours, if the selected entry of validity period contains appointments that are in the future. If you have enabled Capacity and Time Slot At as Working Hours Level, you can view and modify the Capacity and Time Slot Duration in this pane. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 69 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Date and Time You can specify the start and end date and time, and you can choose between single blocks and recurring blocks. Single Block: Creates a single occurrence of the time block. Recurring Block: Creates multiple occurrences based on the specified recurrence interval and the recurrence end date. You can specify a daily, weekly or monthly recurrence interval, such as every third week on a specific day of the week. For monthly recurrence intervals, you can choose between the following options: Day: A specific day of the week, such as every first Monday of the month. Date: A calendar date, such as 1 for the first day of the month. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Announcing Recurring Block Times . All Day Event When you enable the All Day Event toggle, you can create a block for an entire day or for several days in a row. Note: When creating an All Day Event, ensure that the duration of the appointment is less than the chosen recurrence interval. For instance, if your appointment lasts two days, the earliest possible recurrence is every three days or more. This means the recurrence interval must always be longer than the appointment duration. Start Date and Time Specify the start date and time for the time block. End Date and Time Specify the end date and time for the time block. View History When you enable the View History toggle, the system also displays the appointments that are in the past. By default, time blocks in the past are hidden. You can block the time for a loading point that has been shared with multiple docking locations. When you do so, the system blocks the entire capacity of the loading point for the blocked period across all the docking locations with which the loading point has been shared.  Note Duration The maximum duration of a single block is 31 days. If you want to block your loading point for more than 31 days, you can use the Deactivate option of the loading point or use a recurring block. For more information, see the status Inactive under Header on this page. The maximum duration of a recurring block depends on the recurrence pattern: Daily: The maximum duration is 31 days, and it can occur up to every 31 days. The duration must be shorter than the recurrence frequency. The recurrence end date can be set up to one year from the start date. Weekly: The maximum duration is 24 hours, and it can occur up to every 6 weeks. The recurrence end date can be set up to one year from the start date. Monthly: The maximum duration is 24 hours, and it can occur up to every 12 months. It must be shorter than the recurrence frequency. The recurrence end date can be set up to three years from the start date. 5/12/26, 6:36 AM 70 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Releasing a Time Block If the docking locations that share the loading point are in the same tenant, then the user can release the block. If the docking locations that share the loading point are in different tenants, then only the user who created the time block can release the same. Viewing a Loading Point Loading point settings provide detailed information about the configuration and status of loading points, including capacity and time slots. To view the loading point settings, proceed as follows: 1. Choose the Loading Point tab on the left pane. 2. Enter the loading point ID in the search bar on the left pane to search for a specific loading point. 3. Choose a loading point from the results.
