For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration improves supply chain efficiency by connecting business partners on a collaborative network that supports jointly managing transactions, exchanging documents, and sharing insights across the value chain. For instance, upon invitation from a shipper, a carrier can onboard onto the network and collaborate with shippers on freight tendering, invoicing and milestone reporting. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration runs on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), utilizing one of the following infrastructures: Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Frankfurt, Germany Microsoft Azure infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Washington state, US Google Cloud infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Dammam, Saudi Arabia The data used in the solution is also stored in the respective data center. Information for shippers: Collaborative managed transactions supported in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration are tailored to the relevant SAP backend systems. For freight collaboration scenarios, SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration offers out-of-the-box connectivity to shippers with the following systems: SAP Transportation Management (on-premise) or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA (on-premise) SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition SAP Logistics Management For more information about supported releases, see SAP Note 2620322 . In addition, out-of-the box connectivity is delivered for truck carrier networks, including project44 for visibility services and B2B carrier connectivity for freight tendering and subcontracting. Selected digital freight forwarders support on-demand road transportation with real-time pricing and subcontracting. To learn more about the SAP Business Network add-ons for project44 visibility services, see the Feature Scope Description for project44 Add-Ons and the Configuration and Application Guide for project44 Add-Ons. Data Protection and Privacy You use the Data Protection and Privacy apps to manage personal and sensitive personal data of employees, individual customers, and contacts. Data processing systems store master data or transactional data used to perform business processes and to document them. In many cases, it involves the personal data of employees, individual customers, and contacts. In many countries, the storage, disclosure, and removal of such personal data from data storage systems must be in accordance with statutory data protection  Note The following documentation uses the term SAP S/4HANA to refer to both SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition and SAP S/4HANA (on-premise). If any of the information provided applies to only SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA, this will be clearly specified. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- laws. One requirement in many countries is that the personal data can only be stored if a clear business reason for this data retention exists. Most data protection legislation proscribes fixed retention periods, defining how long data can be stored in data systems, after which it must be deleted. In addition, legislation in many countries stipulates that the data protection officer must disclose the personal data of individuals, when requested for it. Retention Management SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration restricts the access of personal data on completion of its business purpose. That is, not all the user groups can access the personal data after the expiration of originally defined residence period. The Retention Management app enables you to define rules for residence and blocking of personal data for apps that belong to a specific application group. These rules restrict the usage of documents containing personal data. In the Retention Management app, you define the residence period and the blocking period. The residence period and blocking period are together called as the retention period. Defining Residence and Blocking Periods To define the residence period and blocking period of various applications, perform the following: 1. Sign in to the Fiori Launchpad and choose the Retention Management tile. 2. Select an application type.  Note You must familiarize yourself with the following important definitions relevant for using the Retention Management app: Residence Period The period between the end of business and the end of purpose for a data set during which the data remains in the database and can be used in case of subsequent processes related to the original purpose. At the end of the residence period, the data is blocked. Blocking Period The period between the residence period and the deletion of the data is the blocking period. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a data protection officer, can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the data is deleted. Retention Period The period between the end of the last business activity involving a specific object and the deletion of the corresponding data, subject to applicable laws. For example, in the Freight Requests for Quotation app, business partner is a master data and the end of purpose of this master data is until the business partner is in the network. The retention period is a combination of the residence period and the blocking period. Data Subject An identified or identifiable natural person. An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- 3. Enter a residence period. The residence period is the period between the end of business and the end of purpose for a data set during which the data remains in the database and can be used in case of subsequent processes related to the original purpose. At the end of the residence period, the data is blocked. Note that if you do not specify a residence period, the system by default assigns a residence period of 12 months for the application type. 4. Enter a blocking period. The blocking period is the period between the residence period and the deletion of the data is the blocking period. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a Data Protection Officer (DPO), can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the data is deleted. Note that if you do not specify a blocking period, the system by default assigns a blocking period of 12 months for the application type. 5. Choose Save. The system stores the residence and blocking periods for the specific application type. Blocking Store Once the residence period ends, the data moves to the blocking period. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a data protection officer, can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the system deletes the data. The data protection officer can log into the Fiori Launchpad and choose the Blocking Store app to access all the documents that are in the blocking period. To view a document, the user can download the document in a text file format by choosing the Download button. Identifier Displays the unique identifier for the document. Status Displays the status of the document, for example, in blocking period. End of business Displays the date when the document got into the end of business state. App name Displays the name of the app with which the data is associated. Administration information Personal Data Record  Note For the Define User Settings application type, the system displays only the Data Subject ID field. You must enter the identifier of the person in which the system stores the personal settings. When you choose Delete, the system deletes the personal settings of the individual from the system. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Data subjects have the right to receive information regarding their personal data undergoing processing. The personal data record feature helps you to comply with the relevant legal requirements for data protection by allowing you to search for and retrieve all personal data for a specified data subject. The search results are displayed in a comprehensive and structured list containing all personal data of the data subject specified, organized according to the purpose for which the data was collected and processed. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration uses Personal Data Manager for information and retrieval of personal data. A user with the right role can access the Fiori Launchpad of Personal Data Manager and search for the transactions that have the data of the data subject. To access the Fiord Launchpad of Personal Data Manager, use an URL of the following format: https://<your-subdomain>- pdm-portal.<domain-name>/sites For more information about Personal Data Manager, see the Administration Guide for Shippers. Audit Log Personal data is subject to frequent changes. Therefore, for review purposes or as a result of legal regulations, it may be necessary to track the changes made to this data. When these changes are logged, you should be able to check which employee made which change, the date and time, the previous value, and the current value, depending on the configuration. It is also possible to analyze errors in this way. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration supports change and audit log. When you change any personal information, the system updates the audit log. Users with the required authorization can request for the change log. To request for a log, the authorized user must create an SAP support message in the component BC-NEO-AUDITLOG. For more information about how to request for audit logs, see Audit Log Viewer for the Cloud Foundry Environment. Manage Business Profile Whether you are a shipper, solution owner, or logistics provider, you will land on the company profile page in SAP Business Network when opening the Manage Business Profile app. On this page, you can manage and adjust your company information as per your needs. This enables potential partners and relevant stakeholders to know more about your company’s service coverage, capabilities, and strength. You can maintain the basic information about your company. This includes but is not limited to the type of organization, year founded, and annual revenue to help shippers and solution owners evaluate you as a potential logistics provider. The Product and Service Categories, Ship-to or Service Locations, and Industries sections of your company profile allow you to provide detailed information about the products or services you offer, the locations you ship to or provide services, and the industries you serve. This information is critical because shippers and solution owners usually discover your company based on the product and service categories and ship-to or service locations. The Additional Addresses section provides you with an effective and intuitive way to add and manage addresses beyond the primary business address, such as branch offices, regional offices, warehouses, or other physical sites associated with your company. Including these addresses provides a comprehensive overview of your company's geographical reach and operational scope. The Contacts section enables you to create multiple individual contacts and assign them one or multiple roles, such as Sales Representative, Marketing Manager, and Technical Contact, designating them as companywide contacts. This guarantees that their contact details are readily available to all current and potential trading partners on the network. More Information 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 5 This is custom documentation. On the Company Profile page, click a pencil icon to edit the information in a section, and enter or revise values as necessary. Note the following constraints and guidelines when you edit your company profile: Company D-U-N-S Number—A nine-digit number issued by Dun & Bradstreet, Inc. to identify each corporate location of an organization. You can obtain a D-U-N-S number or look up your company’s existing number on Dun & Bradstreet’s website, https://www.dnb.com . Supplier Legal Form—Choose the type of business entity or legal status of your company from the dropdown. The list of values varies per country/region. Year Founded—Enter the year in yyyy format. For detailed information, see Creating Additional Addresses. 4. To add contact information to your company profile, select Contacts from the left navigation pane. For detailed information, see Managing Contact Information. Creating Additional Addresses To add an additional address to your company profile, follow these steps: 1. Select Additional Addresses from the left navigation pane of the Company Profile page. 2. On the Additional Addresses page, click Create. 3. On the Create Address page, specify the following fields: Address Name (Mandatory): Give a unique name to easily identify this address. Address Type: Specify the type of address. Country/Region (Mandatory): Specify the country or region where the address is located. Address Line 1 (Mandatory): Enter the primary address information. Address Line 2 (Optional): Include additional address details, if applicable. Address Line 3 (Optional): Include further address details, if necessary. Fax Number: If applicable, provide a fax number. Email: This field is mandatory for email communication regarding this address. 4. Once all required information is entered, click Save. The new address will appear in the Addresses table. 5. Repeat the process to add more addresses. Managing Contact Information Companywide Contact Companywide contacts have their contact information accessible to both current and potential business partners on the network. Assign individuals in your company as companywide contacts. This ensures that your business partners know the right people to contact for various issues or questions. To do this, follow these steps: 1. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane of the Company Profile page. 2. Click Create in the upper right corner of the Contact Personnel with Companywide Assignments table. 3. On the Create Contact Personnel Entry page, specify the basic information and address of the contact. The basic information includes Contact Name, Email, Business Title, Phone, Fax, and Company Assignment. Each contact must have a name, phone number, and email. The Company Assignment field specifies the companywide roles assigned to a contact. If this field is specified, the contact is designated as a companywide contact for the selected role, and their contact information is accessible to all business partners on the network. Each contact personnel can be assigned with multiple companywide roles. 4. After providing the necessary information, click Create. 5. To edit a contact, click Edit in the upper right corner of the table. 6. To delete a contact, Click Delete in the upper right corner of the table. After a contact is deleted, all its assignments will be removed as well. Profile Settings You can specify the visibility and availability of your company profile on the Profile Settings page. If you are a shipper or solution owner, before trying to connect with business partners that operate in a different data center, you must first make your company profile available across all data centers of SAP Business Network for Logistics. Steps to Configure Profile Settings 1. Open your company profile. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- 2. Click the Options menu in the upper-right corner of your profile and select Profile settings. 3. On the Profile Settings page, locate the section labeled Search Results Visibility: a. Toggle Show my profile in search results to allow your profile to appear in search results. This setting determines whether your company profile is visible to potential business partners in their search results. Once your company profile becomes visible, shippers or solution owners can discover your company on the network and send you connection requests for further partnership. Default value: Yes b. Toggle Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network to allow profile data replication across data centers. This setting determines whether your profile data will be replicated to other data centers in SAP Business Network for Logistics. For carriers and data providers, this setting is enabled by default. Shippers and solution owners need to enable it manually. 4. Click Save to confirm your settings. Results Once Show my profile in search results is enabled, your profile will become searchable and visible to potential business partners. Otherwise, your company profile will not be shown in any search results, and thus, no business partners can reach you for further connections. Once Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network is enabled, your company profile data will be replicated across all data centers of SAP Business Network for Logistics. Future updates to your profile will also be automatically synchronized across all data centers. For shippers and solution owners, enabling this setting allows for establishing cross- data-center connections. If this setting is not enabled, your company profile will be only available in the data center where you initially onboarded. As a result, no cross-data-center connections can be established. Carrier Apps and APIs With SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, you as a carrier can use the the apps to get started on the network and to perform your daily tasks in the areas of freight tendering, subcontracting, dock appointment scheduling, milestone reporting and freight settlement. The SAP Business Network Logistics Provider, basic membership page is the central entry point for logistics providers (carriers and data contributors) to find all relevant assets regarding activation, integration and operation of SAP Business Network for Logistics. Carrier APIs As a carrier, you can use the APIs in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration to perform your daily tasks in the areas of freight contracting, freight booking, freight tracking, and freight settlement.  Note Once enabled, this setting cannot be reversed.  Note These apps are also suitable for logistics service providers that perform the role of a carrier who receives freight requests for quotation or freight orders from an ordering party. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- For more information, see https://help.sap.com/doc/e1b2026259d84fc29e6e6760da815011/LBN/en- US/15db9545fb79453c90e49ebad6cc57fc.html. Define User Settings (Carrier) The Define User Settings app allows you to define defaults that best suit the way you work. The settings that you make in the app serve as the default settings in various other apps for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. Distance In this section, you can define the default unit of measurement for distance. The system uses this setting in other apps in your area. Notification Subscriptions In this section, you can subscribe to notifications for various scenarios and specify the email address and preferred language for receiving the notifications. Note that you cannot subscribe to a scenario without maintaining an email address. When you subscribe to notifications for a scenario, the system can send email notifications based on the settings you make in the Manage Notification Settings app. For more information on managing notification settings, see Manage Notification Settings (Carrier). Manage Notification Settings (Carrier) You can use this app to schedule reminder notifications for some of the business processes for which you may need an alert. The system sends you notifications via emails. The Manage Notification Settings app consists of the following areas: List of scenarios This area displays the scenarios for which you can configure alerts. Filter You can use this filter to filter the scenarios. When you select a scenario from this drop-down menu, the system displays only that specific scenario. Configuration details The system displays the following in this area: Configurations The system displays notification types and the settings that you can configure for each type. On-event notification refers to the email notification that you receive at the time when a target event happens, for example, when you receive an invitation from a shipper. Post-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive after the target event happens, for example, after you have received the invitation. Upload Locations You can fill the details of locations using an Excel template and then upload this template back to the app. To do this, follow these steps: 1. Choose Upload to open the Upload Locations page. 2. Click Upload on the up-right corner, then download the Excel template available by choosing Download Excel Template. 3. If you want the system to verify your entries, set Calibrate coordinates when saving to Yes before you upload your file. By default, Calibrate coordinates when saving is set to Apply global settings, meaning that how the system handles coordinates for the location records you are uploading is determined by the option you choose in the Generate geo- coordinates automatically setting, which can be found in the Settings dialogue box. Header The Header section displays the address information. General This section displays the basic information of a location. Global settings for Geo-Coordinates You can use Generate geo-coordinates automatically in the Settings dialogue box to define how the system handles geo- coordinates for all location records. (Applies to locations created after you enable this option) Enable Risk Monitoring If you have configured the risk monitoring service provider in Configure Partner Connections, you can determine whether or not to use the service provider to monitor risks at a certain location in Manage Locations. For example, when you set Calibrate coordinates when saving to No in a location record, the system does not generate or calibrate coordinates for the record even if Generate geo-coordinates automatically is set to Generate or Overwrite.  Note Risk information is not displayed in Manage Locations. Procedure To enable risk monitoring for a specific location, follow these steps: 1. Click the location record for which you want to monitor risks to open its details page. 2. Choose Edit on the upper-right corner. 3. Click to select the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox and then choose Save. Alternatively, you can enable risk monitoring for multiple locations at once. To do this, select the location records, and then choose Risk Monitoring Enable . Results The risk monitoring service provider starts monitoring risks at the location. If you’ve subscribed for the intelligent insights add-on, you can view the risk information on each target location in the Logistics Execution Insights app. To notify the service provider to stop monitoring risks at a location, uncheck the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox in the corresponding location record. To stop using the risk monitoring feature for all locations in your supply chain, uncheck the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox in each location record where you previously enabled the feature in Manage Locations and then deactivate the risk monitoring service provider in Configure Partner Connections. More Information Editing a Location Creating a Location Self-Book Dock Appointments You, as a carrier, can use this app to book a dock appointment for a freight order when the corresponding vehicle is about to reach a certain stop for loading or unloading. The appointments you booked will then be visualized in the Manage Dock Appointments app. This helps shippers have a precise estimate on the quantity of upcoming dock appointments. Process When you confirm a freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app, the system updates the Self-Book Dock Appointments app with this freight order, so that you can create an appointment for this freight order. Note that to perform this, the ordering party must have enabled the relevant settings. Alternatively, the ordering party can enable you to update the Self-Book Dock Appointments app with a freight order that has not yet been confirmed. In other words, once the ordering party sends the freight order from SAP Transportation Management system, the freight order is updated in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app, with the status as New. Before you confirm this order, the  Note You can also configure this setting when creating a new location record. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 95 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- system lists this freight order in the Ready for Booking table in the Self-Book Dock Appointments app. You can select and create an appointment for this order. Note that the system allows you to cancel only those appointments for which the associated gate logbooks are in the status Ready for Check-In or Cancelled. Worklist (Self-Book Dock Appointments) The Self-Book Dock Appointments app consists of the Ready for Booking tab and the Booked Appointment tab. Ready for Booking The Ready for Booking tab consists of all freight documents that are ready for maintaining an appointment. You can view the following information on this tab: Location Loading Point Ordering Party / Reference Document License Plate Activity Type Displays whether you can perform loading, unloading, or both activities. Arrival Date and Time Departure Date and Time Appointment Status Displays whether the document has a canceled appointment or the appointment is yet to be booked Means of Transport Booking Cut-Off Displays the cut-off date and time for booking an appointment Location ID Freight Order Reference Documents Booked Appointment The Booked Appointment tab consists of all freight documents with an appointment. You can view the following information on this tab: Loading Point  Note For more information, you can watch the following video: How to Self-Book Dock Appointments (English only). 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 96 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Ordering Party / Appointment License Plate Freight Order ID Reference Documents Appointment Start Date and Time Appointment End Date and Time Gate ID Gate Location Planned Check-In Date and Time Displays the planned date and time of vehicle check-in Docking Location Group ID Displays the group ID if the document is part of a grouped appointment You can use the following features to filter the freight documents for appointment: Status In the Ready for Booking tab, you can filter the freight documents for appointment based on the one of the following statuses: All Not Booked Canceled Search You can search for a specific document for appointment using the search field. View History When you enable this toggle, the system also displays the appointments that are in the past. Personalization You can choose the personalization icon to manage your settings. You can perform the following: Columns You can add or remove columns that are displayed on the table. Sort You can do an ascending or descending sort of a column in the table. Filter You can filter the documents for appointment based on the loading type values. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 97 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Group You can group the documents for appointment based on one or more of the attributes specified in the input help. Export to Spreadsheet You can choose the export to spreadsheet button to download the dock appointments in Microsoft Excel format. This feature is available in both Ready for Booking and Booked Appointment tab. Maintaining a Dock Appointment Context The Ready for Booking table lists documents for which you can maintain an appointment. These include: Documents that have a stop matching of one of active loading points but do not have an appointment booked Documents whose appointment has been canceled To maintain a dock appointment, select an eligible document from the list, and then choose Maintain Appointment to proceed with the appointment creation process. You cannot update appointments in the past. For more details, proceed as follows: Procedure 1. Select the document from the Ready for Booking table, and then choose Maintain Appointment. You can also click the document to view its details page. Additionally, booking cut-off times that are less than 24 hours away are highlighted in orange. This helps you better prioritize your appointment booking. 2. On the Maintain Appointment page, specify the Loading Point and Date fields (only loading points with the matching activity type will be available). The system displays a list of available time slots and the slots preferred by your shipper (acceptable and requested ones). If the shipper does not allow carriers to change the appointment date, you are not able to edit the Date field. Note that the system displays DST STARTS when the day light savings time begins and DST ENDS when the day light savings time ends. 3. Depending on the duration of the loading or unloading activity, choose one or more consecutive time slots from the Time Slot list. Note that if the shipper has disabled the time slot option for a loading point, you may not be able to view the time slots for the appointments at this loading point. In such scenarios, you can maintain the appointment without selecting a time slot. The shipper can restrict the maximum duration of consecutive time slots. This ensures that the sum of bookable time slots cannot exceed the total duration of all adjacent time slots. However, you can always book at least one time slot. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Max. Consecutive Timeslot Duration . If your shipper uses the Derived Appointment Duration feature, the following applies: When you book an appointment, the booked time slots must match the calculated duration from the shipper. If an exact match is not possible, you must ensure that the booked time is not exceeded by more than one time slot. Example: If the derived appointment duration is set to 27 minutes, and a single time slot has 15 minutes, you must select two consecutive time slots of 15 minutes. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 98 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Use Derived Appointment Duration . 4. On the Information tab, enter the following under Driver Details: Driver Name Driver Phone Number Additional Driver Name Additional Driver Phone Number You can also click the Ordering Party link to open the quick view page. Hyperlinks on the quick view page enable you to perform various operations. For example, you can click Email to launch an email program. 5. On the Information tab, enter the following under Resource Details: License Plate / Country or Region of Registration (of the truck) Truck ID Trailer ID 6. If there is any additional information about the appointment, enter it in the Notes section. Notes are intended to provide additional information related to the business document or business process. We recommend you to avoid entering sensitive personal data. 7. If there are any attachments that you want to add to the appointment, choose the Add button under the Attachments section. You can only upload files that meet the following criteria: Files of the formats: jpg, jpeg, gif, png, pdf, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, tiff, tiff-fx Image files less than 6MB file size Document files less than 5MB file size File name less than 150 characters including file extension 8. Choose Maintain. Results A dock appointment has been maintained for the document. You can find this appointment on the Booked Appointments table. From there, you can access the appointment and view the details. After you maintain a dock appointment, shippers can view your appointment using the Manage Dock Appointments app. Maintaining a Grouped Appointment When you select a docking location in the calendar view, you can select two or more documents from the Ready for Booking tab and maintain multiple appointments in a single group with the same time slot. Note that the system enables you to create a grouped appointment only when the following attributes of the selected documents are same: Location Loading Point (only loading points with the matching activity type will be available) 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 99 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Activity Type Transport Means Description Transport Means Type Arrival Date and Time Departure Date and Time To maintain multiple appointments in a single group, proceed as follows: 1. Select two or more documents with the similar attributes from the Ready for Booking tab and choose Maintain Appointment. Note that as of now, you can only select up to 20 documents to create a grouped appointment. 2. You can view multiple appointments that are created under the Grouped Appointments tab. You can perform the following: You can add or remove documents here. When you choose Add, the system displays the list of documents that contain similar attributes. You can select the documents and choose Add to Group. You can choose the appointment ID to switch to a different appointment that is not the current appointment. You can choose the freight order under the Freight Order column to navigate to the freight order in SAP Business Network for Logistics. 3. On the Scheduling tab, specify the Loading Point and Date (only loading points with the matching activity type will be available). Note that if the shipper has disabled the option to change the appointment date for carriers, you may not be able to edit the Date field. 4. Depending on the duration of the loading or unloading activity, choose one or more consecutive time slots from the Time Slot list. Note that if the shipper has disabled the time slot option for a loading point, you may not be able to view the time slots for the appointments at this loading point. In such scenarios, you can maintain the appointment without selecting a time slot. The shipper can restrict the maximum duration of consecutive time slots. This ensures that the sum of bookable time slots cannot exceed the total duration of all adjacent time slots. However, you can always book at least one time slot. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Max. Consecutive Timeslot Duration . If your shipper uses the Derived Appointment Duration feature, the following applies: When you book an appointment, the booked time slots must match the calculated duration from the shipper. If an exact match is not possible, you must ensure that the booked time is not exceeded by more than one time slot. Example: If the derived appointment duration is set to 27 minutes, and a single time slot has 15 minutes, you must select two consecutive time slots of 15 minutes. For more information, see the following blog: SAP Business Network for Logistics - Dock Appointment Scheduling: Use Derived Appointment Duration . 5. On the Information tab, enter the following under Driver Details: Driver Name Driver Phone Number Additional Driver Name Additional Driver Phone Number 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 100 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: 6. On the Information tab, enter the following under Resource Details: License Plate / Country or Region of Registration (of the truck) Truck ID Trailer ID 7. Choose Maintain. Results A grouped appointment has been maintained for documents. You can find this appointment on the Booked Appointments table. From there, you can access the appointment and view the details. You can also edit or cancel the appointment from there. When you edit or cancel, you can choose whether you want to edit or cancel only the current appointment or all the appointments in the group. After you maintain a dock appointment, shippers can view your appointment using the Manage Dock Appointments app. Viewing an Appointment You can access the list of maintained appointments in the Booked Appointment tab. When you select an appointment, the system displays the appointment details. The detail view of an appointment consists of a header and several sections. Header The system displays the following information in this section: Location Note that when you choose the location, the system displays the additional details of the location that is assigned to the docking location, such as time zone, address, and remarks. Loading Point Appointment Start Date and Time Appointment End Date and Time Information The system displays the following information under this section: General You can view the Ordering Party, Activity Type, Dangerous Goods, Incoterm, and Incoterm Location. Note that when you choose the ordering party, the system displays the additional details of the ordering party. Booking Details  Note Once you maintain the grouped appointment, you can edit the grouped appointment and add notes and attachments. Note that when you do so, the notes and attachments are added only to the current appointment and not all the appointments in the group. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 101 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- You can view the Loading Point, Remarks, and Business Hours of the loading point. Active Vehicle Resource You can view the active vehicle resource details such as Transport Means Type, Vehicle Category Code, Vehicle Type Code, and Vehicle Resource ID. Driver Details You can view the driver details such as Driver Name, Additional Driver Name, and Driver Phone Number. Resource Details You can view the License Plate / Country or Region of Registration (of the truck), Truck ID and Trailer ID. Admin Data You can view the Created By, Changed By, Created On, and Changed On details. Guest User You can view the guest user details such as Name, Company Name, and Email ID. Reference Documents You can view the reference document details such as reference document ID, stop details, and arrival and departure date and time. When you choose a freight order, the system navigates to the freight order in SAP Business Network for Logistics. The link is only available if the appointment was created based on a freight order that exists in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Stops Displays the visual representation of the freight order execution flow with the source location, intermediate stop locations, and destination location. You can see the appointment ID created in SAP Business Network for Logistics, the expected dates for departure and arrival, and the activity type performed for the appointment, such as loading or unloading. When you choose a stop, the system displays the following stop details in a dialog box: Arrival Date and Time Displays the expected arrival date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. Departure Date and Time Displays the expected departure date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. Requested Start Date and Time Displays the requested start date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. Acceptable Start Date and Time Displays the acceptable start date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. Requested End Date and Time Displays the requested end date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. Acceptable End Date and Time Displays the acceptable end date and time defined in the corresponding freight order. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 102 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- The following Appointment Details are displayed for all appointments created in SAP Business Network for Logistics but not for the currently displayed appointment and not for external appointments: Appointment ID Displays the appointment ID if the appointment was created by SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can use this ID to search for the appointment in its corresponding docking location in the Manage Dock Appointments app. Appointment Start Date and Time Displays the start date and time of the appointment after it was booked. Appointment End Date and Time Displays the end date and time of the appointment after it was booked. Cargo You can view the following cargo details: Cargo Item Displays the description of the cargo item. Type Displays whether the cargo item is a package, product, or a container. Logistical Details Displays the quantity, gross weight, gross volume, and dimensions. Equipment Details Displays the equipment type and equipment group. Reference Documents Displays the reference document details. Special Requirements Displays the following: Dangerous Goods If the ordering party has provided dangerous goods information, you can view this information from the Cargo section by choosing Yes in the Dangerous Goods column. This opens a window containing details about the item type, relevant regulations, and more detailed information such as storage instructions, control temperature, and emergency temperature. Temperature Requirements Other Details Displays the following: Over-Dimensional Non-Stackable High Value 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 103 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Notes You can view the additional information about the appointment that you have added. Attachments You can view the attachments that you have added. You can edit or cancel the appointment by choosing the Edit and Cancel Appointment buttons respectively. Note that the system allows you to cancel only those appointments for which the associated gate logbooks are in the status Ready for Check-In or Cancelled. Enabling Docking Location-Based Access You can apply location-based authorization in the Self-Book Dock Appointments app to control user access to appointments belonging to a specific docking location. In other terms, you can assign a docking location to a user ID. When you do so, the user can view only those documents for appointment that belong to the docking location ID. To enable location-based authorization, navigate to the User Management app. Create and assign a user group to control user access to specified docking locations in the Self-Book Dock Appointments app. For more information, see Create a User and Assign User Groups. Maintaining a Dock Appointment (Guest User) You as a customer or a carrier, who is not on SAP Business Network for Logistics (but your shipper is on the network), may want to pick up a shipment from a shipper’s warehouse. You may also want your carrier to do this on your behalf. To do so, you must maintain the dock appointment details in the SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration system. The shipper can provide a guest user access to you and can enable you to maintain the appointment details in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration using an API. Once the shipper provides you a guest user access, the system generates an URL and sends it to you in an email. To validate the authenticity of the accessing personnel, when you navigate to the URL, the system prompts you to enter additional appointment information such as the purchase order number. Once you pass the security validation, you can view the appointment details. You can select the time slots yourself and save the appointment. You can also invite your carrier to access this appointment and select the time slots. To do so, you must perform the following: 1. Choose the Add Carrier button. A dialog box appears. 2. Enter the carrier details in this dialog box and proceed. The system sends an email to the carrier with the URL for guest user access of the appointment. The carrier can navigate to the URL, access the appointment details, and select the time slots. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 104 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Note that only the URL that you receive as a customer contains the Add Carrier button. The URL that the carrier receives does not contain this button. Freight Orders for Reporting The Freight Orders for Reporting app enables you to keep your ordering parties informed about the transportation of their freight. For example, if one of your delivery trucks is delayed on-route, you can send the ordering party a new ETA (expected time of arrival) so they can replan if necessary. Additionally, the app lets you upload and send documents, such as proof of deliveries, to your ordering parties. Note that this app has been deprecated and will be sunset shortly. This app has been replaced with the new app Manage Freight Execution. The reporting app contains the track relevant freight orders irrespective of whether the orders are relevant for confirmation or not. In the Freight Orders for Reporting app, you can view the events that you reported manually and the events reported by the visibility provider. The manually reported data and the events reported by the visibility provider are synchronized to the ordering party’s Track Freight Movement app and SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) or SAP S/4 HANA system. The Freight Orders for Reporting app consists of a main view and a detail view. When you open the app, the main view is displayed. It has two screen areas: Filter bar Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter the freight orders by one or more of the following options: Freight Order Ordering Party Reporting Status Displays one of the following statuses: Ready for Reporting When you confirm a freight order, the system sends this freight order to the Freight Orders for Reporting app with this status. Reporting in Progress  Note As of now, in the Freight Orders for Reporting app, you can report only arrival and departure events. Alternatively, you can keep your ordering parties in the loop during the transportation of their freight by sending them visibility data (including real-time location, estimated ETA, event status, and time of event completion) via a supported visibility provider. For more information about supported visibility providers, visit the SAP Community wiki for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration , and the homepage for SAP Business Network for Logistics . You can report events for a freight order even when you have not reconfirmed a freight order that has been updated by the ordering party. In the worklist, you can view the tag Updated for such updated freight orders. Also, a message appears on the worklist when there are freight orders updated by the ordering party and you have not yet confirmed these freight orders. You can use the link in the message to navigate and view the list of freight orders with pending reconfirmation. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 105 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- When you start reporting the events in the freight order then the system sets the status of this freight order as Reporting in Progress. Reporting Completed When you have reported all planned events in the freight order, then the system sets the status of this freight order as Reporting Completed. Reporting in Progress (freight order reconfirmation required) After you start reporting the events in the freight order, if any changes are done to this freight order, then the system sets this status. Canceled If the freight order is canceled, the system updates the status of this freight order as Canceled. Driver Name License Plate Delay Departure Date Arrival Date Source Location Destination Location Received On Orders Pending Reconfirmation Consignee Party Name Destination Address Source Address Vendor ID Proof of Delivery Status You can select one of the following options: Reported at Last Stop When you select this filter option, you can view all freight orders for which you have reported the proof of delivery at the last stop. Not Reported at Last Stop When you select this filter option, you can view all freight orders for which you have not reported the proof of delivery at the last stop. Worklists You can use the following worklists Events to Report, Skipped Events, and All. From each worklist, you can click on a freight order to navigate to its detail view. The detail view has two screen areas: Header 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 106 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- The header displays information such as the freight order ID, ordering party, and the reporting status of the freight order. Sections In the Reporting section, you can report the planned events in freight order, as well as upload both proof of delivery and proof of pickup documents. You can also display extra details in the Information, Contacts, Notes, and Drivers and License Plate sections. Worklists (Freight Orders for Reporting) To restrict the number of freight orders that are displayed, you can use the preconfigured worklists (Events to Report, Skipped Events, All). All The All worklist displays the information available on the Events to Report and Skipped Events worklists. Additionally, the All worklist lists freight orders that you have finished reporting, as well as canceled freight orders. For each freight order, the following information is displayed: Ordering party and freight order ID You can view the freight order details in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Note that you can navigate and view only those freight orders that you have confirmed in your Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Reporting status Driver and license plate Number of reference documents Event type and location of the current event that you must report Scenario type Planned time of the current event that you must report By how long the event is delayed Date of arrival Date of departure Source location Destination location The number of skipped events within the freight order Events to Report The Events to Report worklist displays the freight orders – and the events within the freight order – that you must report. For each freight order, the following information is displayed: Ordering party and freight order ID You can view the freight order details in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Note that you can navigate and view only those freight orders that you have confirmed in your Freight Orders for Confirmation app. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 107 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Reporting status Drivers and license plate Number of reference documents Event type and location of the current event that you must report Scenario type Planned time of the current event that you must report By how long the event is delayed Date of arrival Date of departure Source location Destination location Skipped Events The Skipped Events worklist displays freight orders that include one or more events that you’ve skipped. This means when you skip an event on the Events to Report worklist, you can easily find the freight order later on when you’re able to report the skipped event. For each freight order, the following information is displayed: Ordering party and freight order ID You can view the freight order details in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Note that you can navigate and view only those freight orders that you have confirmed in your Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Reporting status Drivers and license plate Number of reference documents Scenario type The number of skipped events within the freight order Date of arrival Date of departure Source location Destination location Export to Spreadsheet You can choose the export to spreadsheet button to download the dock appointments in Microsoft Excel format. This feature is available in both Ready for Booking and Booked Appointment tab. Detail View (Freight Orders for Reporting) The detail view of a freight order consists of a header and several sections. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 108 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Header The header displays information about the freight order. The following fields may be of interest to you: Freight order details You can view the freight order details in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Note that you can navigate and view only those freight orders that you have confirmed in your Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Reporting status (Ready for reporting, Reporting in progress, Reporting in progress (freight order reconfirmation required), Reporting completed, Canceled) The status of a freight order changes from Ready for reporting to Reporting in progress when you report any event (or if you skip an event or mark an event as unable to report). The status changes from Reporting in progress to Reporting completed only when you have reported the final time (the time of completion) for all events or marked any events that you cannot report to unable to report. Contact details of the ordering party Information The Information section displays general data about the freight order. Reporting The Reporting section displays all the events in the freight order. Report Final Time You can report a final time for the event Report Delay You can report a delay to the shipper. You can specify the duration of delay, reason for delay, and additional details. Report Proof of Pickup For a departure event, you can report a proof of pickup. Note that you must upload a minimum of one attachment. Report Proof of Delivery For an arrival event, you can report a proof of delivery. Note that you must upload a minimum of one attachment. Report Exception You can report exceptions to the shipper in case of unforeseen events such as damages or other issues. Note that you have an option to upload an attachment. Unable to Report When you are unable to report an event, you can notify the shipper by choosing this option. Note that you can select any time zone when you report a final time. However, the system converts it to the local time zone of the respective source or destination location while displaying it in the Freight Orders for Reporting app and the shipper’s Track Freight Movement app. Contacts 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 109 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- If provided by the ordering party, the Contacts section displays the company name of the ordering party along with the phone number and the email address of the contact person. This section also displays the contact details for each individual stop (stop number and location). Notes The Notes section displays comments left by the ordering party. Drivers and License Plate The Drivers and License Plate section displays the driver and vehicle license plate information that was provided in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Reporting Events in a Freight Order While your company transports freight for an ordering party, use the Freight Orders for Reporting app to report when planned events in the freight order are completed. If a delay occurs, you can also use the app to report a new ETA (expected time of arrival), enabling the ordering party to replan if needed. Prerequisites Before you can report the events of a freight order, the freight order must be confirmed in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Once the system creates a freight order in the ordering party’s Track Freight Movement app, this freight order is also available in the Freight Orders for Reporting app. Context You can report an event from both the Events to Report worklist and from the Reporting section in the detail view of the freight order. Using the worklist is useful for reporting the events of multiple freight orders while they are executed during the day. Whereas, using the Reporting section is useful for reporting several events for one freight order. If you don't have the information required to report an event, you can skip the event and report it later. For more information, see Skipping an Event. Procedure 1. Open the Freight Orders for Reporting app. 2. On the Events to Report worklist, report the first event of the freight order. a. Optional: If the event cannot be completed at the planned time due to a delay, you can inform the ordering party. To do so, select Report Delay from the inline menu of the freight order and enter the details of the delay in the Report Delay dialog box. Note, if you don’t know the duration of the delay, you can leave the Expected Time and Delay fields empty. b. When the event is complete, select Report Final Time from the inline menu of the freight order and complete the Report Final Time dialog box. Enter the final time, time zone, reason for delay, and additional details. Note, if you report a time that is earlier than when the freight order was received in the app, the time may not be saved by the shipper's system. After reporting the final time of the event, the data for the next planned event is displayed on the worklist. 3. Repeat step 2 for all events in the freight order. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 110 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: To see an overview of the events you have reported for the freight order, click the freight order to display the Reporting section. Next Steps When you receive electronic copies of the proof of delivery and proof of pickup documents, you can use the app to upload and send them to the ordering party. For more information, see Sending Proof of Delivery and Proof of Pickup Documents to the Ordering Party Skipping an Event If you don't have the information to report an event that is listed on the Events to Report worklist, you can skip the event and report it later. This enables you to carry on reporting the rest of the events in the freight order. To skip an event, on the Events to Report worklist choose Skip Event from the inline menu of the freight order.  Note When the ordering party makes any changes, subcontracts, and executes the freight order in the SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system, the system does the following: Updates the reporting app with these changes. Sets the status of the reporting app to Reporting in Progress (freight order reconfirmation required). To report events in the reporting app, you must reconfirm this freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. When the ordering party sends the freight order for subcontracting, you can confirm the order in Freight Orders for Confirmation app and start reporting events in the Freight Orders for Reporting app. The freight order status is set to Ready for Reporting in the reporting app. Meanwhile, if the ordering party changes the order details in SAP TM and executes it, System creates the order in the ordering party’s Track Freight Movement app. In this case, the status of freight order in the reporting app becomes Reporting in Progress (freight order reconfirmation required). In this scenario, the ordering party must perform the subcontracting process again in the SAP TM system. Only after this is done, you can view the updated freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. When you reconfirm this freight order, the system updates the status Ready for Reporting in the reporting app. When the ordering party creates a freight order and subcontracts the order in SAP TM, the system updates this freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. When you confirm this order, it appears in the reporting app and also in the ordering party’s Track Freight Movement app. After this is done, when the ordering party makes any changes to this freight order in SAP TM system and executes the freight order, the system updates the order only in the Track Freight Movement app and not the reporting app. However, the status of this freight order becomes Reporting in Progress (freight order reconfirmation required) in the reporting app. In this scenario, the ordering party must perform the subcontracting process again in the SAP TM system. Only after this is done, you can view the updated freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. When you reconfirm this freight order, the system updates the status Ready for Reporting in the reporting app.  Note You can skip an event even after you have reported a delay. You cannot skip the last event of a freight order. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 111 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- When you skip an event, the freight order is listed on the Skipped Events worklist. This ensures that you don’t forget to report the event. When you’re able to report the final time of the skipped event, click the freight order to display the Reporting section and enter the final time for the event. If you'll never be able to provide the final time of the skipped event, you can mark the event as unable to report. By doing so, the freight order will no longer be listed on the Skipped Events worklist. And, if the skipped event is the only outstanding unreported event in the freight order, the reporting status will change to Reporting completed. To mark an event as unable to report, go to the Reporting section in the details view of the freight order and select Unable to Report from the inline menu of the event. Sending Proof of Delivery and Proof of Pickup Documents to the Ordering Party To upload and send the ordering party proof of delivery and proof of pickup documents, go to the Reporting section in the details view of the freight order and upload the documents to the relevant events. For a proof of delivery document, choose Upload Proof of Delivery from the dropdown menu of the relevant arrival event. Enter the final date and time, time zone, and upload relevant attachments and choose Report. Note that the time zone that you specify while uploading a proof of delivery, will be converted to the local time zone of the destination location while the system displays it in the shipper’s Track Freight Movement app. For a proof of pickup document, choose Upload Proof of Pickup from the dropdown menu of the relevant departure event. Enter the final date and time, time zone, and upload relevant attachments and choose Report.
