file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Reporting Status Displays a status based on the event reporting in a freight document. You can view one of the following statuses: Ready for Reporting When a freight document is made available in the Manage Freight Execution app, the initial status is set as Ready for Reporting. Reporting in Progress When the carrier starts reporting events in the freight document then the reporting status is set as Reporting in Progress. Reporting Completed When the carrier has reported all planned events in the freight document or marked the remaining events as Unable to Report, then the reporting status is set as Reporting Completed. Current Status Displays the current status of execution based on the latest planned event reported. You can view whether the execution is as planned, early, on time, or late. You can view one of the following statuses: As Planned This status appears when no event has been reported for the freight document and the reporting deadline has not yet lapsed. Early This status appears when the latest planned event has been reported and it has occurred ahead of time. On Time This status appears when the latest planned event has been reported and it has occurred on time. Late This status appears when the latest planned event has been reported and it has occurred late. Overdue This status appears when the latest planned event has not been reported by the reporting deadline. Delayed This status appears when a delayed event is reported on either the latest planned event or at the document-level. Estimated Status Displays the estimated status of execution based on the latest estimate received for a planned event. You can view whether the execution is running early, running on time, or running late. Note that this is relevant before the planned event has been reported. You can view one of the following statuses: Running Early 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 121 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- When the latest planned event has been estimated to happen before time. Running on Time When the latest planned event has been estimated to happen on time. Running Late When the latest planned event has been estimated to happen late. Proof of Delivery Status Displays whether the proof of delivery has been reported at the last stop. You can view one of the following statuses. Reported at Last Stop Not Reported at Last Stop Reporting Events While your company transports freight for an ordering party, you can use the Manage Freight Execution app to report planned and unplanned events in the freight document. You can also perform the following when you report an event: Report an estimate for any planned event, enabling the ordering party to replan if needed. If a delay occurs, you can also use the app to report a delay at both the document-level and at a planned event-level. You can report proof of pick-up and proof of delivery with attachments. You can report additional events for the supported event types at any stop. You can report an event directly from the worklist page or the detailed view page for a freight document. When you choose the Report button, you can choose one of the following options. Planned Event You can report a planned event as follows: 1. Select an event for which you want to report. You can view the list of events planned by the ordering party for you. Note that the system pre-selects the next planned event. You can change the selection as required. 2. Enter the final time or estimated time along with the time zone. 3. Optionally, you can enter a reason code and description. 4. Optionally, you can also add an attachment. 5. Optionally, you can add an estimate for events planned in the future. Unplanned Event You can report an unplanned event as follows: 1. Select an event from the supported event types. 2. Optionally, select a stop at which this unplanned event must be reported. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 122 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- 3. Enter the final time along with the time zone. 4. Optionally, you can enter a reason code and description. 5. Optionally, you can also add an attachment. 6. Optionally, you can add an estimate for events planned in the future. Unable to Report Remaining Events You can choose this option if you will never be able to provide the final time of the event. Events History Header When you choose the View Events History button in the detailed view page, you can view all events reported during the freight execution in a card format. This includes all the planned and unplanned events that have been reported multiple times. For each event, you can view the following information in a card format: Event type Current status When a final time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Estimated status When an estimated time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Location Planned on Final time When a final time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Estimated time When an estimated time is reported for the planned event, you can view this information. Business partner Attachment Reason Code When a reason code is available for the planned event, you can view this information. Reason Code Description When a reason code description is available for the planned event, you can view this information. Events Overview When you navigate to additional options in the Events Overview sub-tab and choose the View History button in the planned event card, you can view all the events that have already been reported for that specific planned event on the right pane. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 123 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Invoice Freight Documents You can view all the freight documents that are ready for invoicing using the Invoice Freight Documents app. You can view all the freight documents from one or more of your ordering parties using this app. You can select one or more of these freight documents and create a single invoice or a collective invoice for your ordering party for the services that you provided. The Invoice Freight Documents app consists of a main view and a detail view. When you launch the app, the system displays the main view with the following areas: Filter bar Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter the freight documents to restrict the number of freight documents displayed. You can filter based on freight documents based on one or more of the following attributes: Freight document Departure date Ordering Party Arrival date Arrival location Document status Customer account Reference document ID Reference document type Changed on Created on Departure location Gross amount Gross amount currency Purchasing group Mode of transport Worklists You can use the following worklists: To be Invoiced, Invoicing in Process, Awaiting Ordering Party's Response, Completely Invoiced, and All. From the main view, you can navigate to the detail view of a freight document. The detail view has the following areas: Header You can view information such as the general details, freight document amount, invoiced amount, and invoice status. Sections You can view further details of the freight document in the following sections: Information 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 124 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Cargo Stages Charges Business Partners Notes Attachments Worklist (Invoice Freight Documents) To restrict the number of freight documents displayed, you can use the preconfigured worklists (To be Invoiced, Invoicing in Process, Awaiting Ordering Party's Response, Completely Invoiced, All) that are based on the invoice status of the freight document. All The All worklist displays all freight documents that are settlement relevant. The system displays the following information for each freight document: Ordering party and freight document Displays the ordering party details and the freight document ID. Also displays a warning message if the freight document contains zero amount. Customer account Displays the customer account ID. Departure date and time Arrival date and time Departure location Arrival location Arrival location time zone Mode of transport Purchasing group Reference documents To be Invoiced The To be Invoiced worklist displays all freight documents that are not yet invoiced. This worklist displays the same information as the All worklist. Invoicing in Process The Invoicing in Process worklist displays all freight documents for which you have already created an invoice. This worklist displays the same information as the To be Invoiced worklist. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 125 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Awaiting Ordering Party's Response The Awaiting Ordering Party's Response worklist displays those freight documents which are not yet responded by the ordering party. This worklist displays the same information as the Invoicing in Process worklist. Completely Invoiced After an invoice has been created for a freight document in your Transportation Management (TM) system (TM in SAP S4 HANA 1809 onwards), the status of the freight document becomes Completely Invoiced. These invoices are displayed in the Completely Invoiced worklist in the Invoice Freight Documents app. This worklist displays the same information as the Awaiting Ordering Party's Response worklist. Document Statuses You can view the document statuses Updated, Settled Outside, and Cancelled, as appropriate, as a label in the worklist. When the ordering party makes any changes to a freight document with the status as Invoicing in Process in their transportation system, these changes are updated and the freight document status is set as Updated. When the ordering party cancels a freight document in their external system, you can view the Cancelled label for the freight document in the worklist. In the ordering party's external system, when a freight order that has been sent for confirmation to the carrier has been cancelled, the corresponding freight order is cancelled in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app, Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean), and the Invoice Freight Documents app. Note that the freight document can be cancelled only when there is no active dispute or an invoice document corresponding to the freight document. When you settle a freight document outside of SAP Business Network for Logistics in your external system, you can view the Settled Outside label for the freight document in the worklist. Create Invoice You can select one or more of these freight documents and create a single invoice for your ordering party using the Create Invoice button. For more information, see Creating Invoices from Freight Documents. Note that this button is available only in the following tabs: All To be Invoiced Completely Invoiced Create Collective Invoice You can select two or more of these freight documents and create a collective invoice for your ordering party using the Create Collective Invoice button. For more information, see Creating a Collective Invoice. Note that this button is available only in the following tabs: All To be Invoiced 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 126 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Completely Invoiced Mark or Unmark as Settled Outside You can settle a freight document outside of SAP Business Network for Logistics in your external system. When you do so, you can select one or more relevant freight documents and choose the mark or unmark as settled outside icon. From the drop down menu, you can choose the option Mark as Settled Outside. Note that once you mark a freight document as settled, it no longer appears in the To be Invoiced tab. You can use the Document Status filter to view the marked documents in the All tab. You can also undo this action by choosing the Unmark as Settled Outside option from the drop down menu. Note that you can only select up to 100 freight documents from the worklist while choosing one of these options. Export to Spreadsheet You can choose the export to spreadsheet button to download the freight documents in Microsoft Excel format. Note that when you use this feature, the applied filters are considered for data selection. Detail View (Invoice Freight Documents) The detail view of a freight document for settlement consists of a header and several sections. Header You can view the following important information about the freight document: General Details Displays the freight document ID, document status, contact details, delivery date, and purchasing group. When you choose the contact, the system displays the phone number, email, and address of the ordering party. Freight document amount Displays the sum of all amounts in the freight document Invoiced amount Displays the total amount of charges that are currently invoiced in the freight document. Note that this amount does not include the charges that are yet to be invoiced. Invoicing status Displays the status of the invoice, that is, whether the invoice is yet to be invoiced, in process, awaiting ordering party's response, completely invoiced, or submitted. Information The Information section displays the following subsections: General Displays the total distance, duration, service level, and freight agreement details. Departure Location Displays the date and time and address. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 127 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Arrival Location Displays the date and time and address. Active Vehicle Resource Displays the mode of transport, means of transport, vehicle code, vehicle type code, and vehicle resource ID. Administrative Data Displays the administrative information. Invoice Details Section You can view the following information for each invoice associated with the freight document: Invoice Displays the invoice IDs of the included invoices. You can navigate directly to the displayed invoices from this section. Invoice Date Gross Amount Displays the total gross invoice amount of the invoice. That is, if you have a collective invoice, the gross invoice amount is the total of gross amounts from all the included freight documents. Note that the gross amount is the sum of net amount and tax amount. Document Status Displays the status of the invoice, that is whether it is a draft or if it has been submitted. Disputes Reference Documents Section Displays the document type and document ID of the reference documents. Cargo The Cargo section displays information on the cargo items involved, such as type, locations, quantity, gross weight, net weight, dimensions, and gross volume. Stages You can view the transportation stages in this tab. You can view the details such as item, type, locations, quantity, gross weight, net weight, dimensions, and gross volume for each stage.  Note You can view the details of all cargo item types such as container, package, product, and service. You can navigate through the entire cargo item hierarchy. For example, from a container to the packages, package to the products or services and so on to view the respective details. The ordering party can implement a business add-in (BAdI) to display only the main cargo items. Any notes sent by the ordering party with text type LBNMI will be discarded as it is a technical text type used to display main cargo items. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 128 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Charges The Charges section displays the following information: Charge description Displays the charge type details for each stage in each freight document. Charge types are the classification of charges for which you charge the ordering party. Charge type (Transportation System) Classification of charge line that indicates the type of charges such base rate, surcharge, or discount, as specified in the ordering party's SAP Transportation Management system. Rate amount/unit Displays the flat rate amount or rate amount per unit, for example, USD 20 per 1 kg. Quantity Displays the total quantity relevant for calculating the final amount. Final amount Displays the final amount that has been derived from the rate amount, quantity, and calculation method. When you select a charge line, you can view the following additional details specific for the selected charge: Transportation charges You can view the charge details such as line number, charge type, calculation methods, and payment terms. Line number Charge description Displays the classification of charges for which you charge the ordering party. These are the transportation mode- specific codes that are predefined by SAP Business Network for Logistics. Calculation method Displays the logic with which the system calculates the charges. Payment terms Displays the conditions of payment you agreed with your ordering party with respect to goods supplied or services provided. Logistical reference Displays the item or stage information for a charge line (for container, package, product, or stage) from which the system obtains the logistical data. Calculation basis Displays the actual base or factor with which the system calculated the charges. You can view the calculation basis for rates belonging to a rate table. Exchange rates Displays the exchange rate information that is used as the basis for currency conversion. Notes 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 129 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Displays the notes specified for the charge line. Business Partners You can view the various business partners associated with the freight document. The system displays the role of the business partner (whether the business partner is a carrier or an ordering party). The system also displays the address of the business partner. Notes You can view the comments added by the ordering party. Attachments You can view the attachments added by the ordering party. Creating Invoices from Freight Documents You can view all the freight documents from one or more of your ordering parties using the Invoice Freight Documents app. You can select one or more of these freight documents and create a single invoice or a collective invoice for your ordering party for the services that you provided. To create an invoice or a collective invoice from freight documents, perform the following: Creating an Invoice To create an invoice, you must select a freight document from the worklist page and choose Create Invoice. Alternatively, you can also choose Create Invoice on the header area of the detail view of a freight document. You can also select multiple freight documents from the worklist page and choose Create Invoice. The system creates individual invoices, one each for all the selected freight documents. Creating a Collective Invoice  Note You can only upload files that fulfil the following criteria: Files must be of one of the formats: jpg, gif, png, .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx Image files must be less than 6MB file size Document files must be less than 5MB file size File name must be less than 150 characters including file extension  Note If you already have an invoice in draft version for a freight document, you cannot create a new invoice. You cannot create an invoice or a collective invoice for a freight order with the document status as Cancelled. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 130 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: To create a collective invoice, you must select two or more freight documents from the worklist page and choose Create Collective Invoice. For more information about collective invoice creation, see Creating a Collective Invoice. Note that if you already have a collective invoice in draft version for the selected freight documents, you cannot create a new collective invoice. Exclusion of Zero Charges When you create an invoice from a freight document that includes a planned charge with a zero amount, these zero charges are excluded by default in the invoice document. Also, in the Manage Invoices app, you can view a message in the Charges tab that indicates the same. You can review and manually include these charges if needed. Note that this exclusion applies only to planned charges and not unplanned charges. Creating a Collective Invoice When you select two or more freight documents and create a collective invoice, the system attempts to combine multiple freight documents that you have selected into a single invoice document. However, if certain conditions are different between the selected freight documents, the system cannot create a combined invoice. In this case, the system creates multiple invoices. Split and Consolidation Criteria The system uses the following split and consolidation criteria when it attempts to create a collective invoice: Account Invoicing party Payee Document currency Calculation level Payment terms Item currency Note that the system makes a split with no specific document of priority. Example You have two freight documents for invoicing for which you want to create a collective invoice. You select the freight documents in the worklist screen and choose Create Collective Invoice. However, the document currency in the first freight document does not match the document currency in the second freight document. In this case, the system creates two invoices.  Note If a freight document is being invoiced item wise or stage wise, and if an invoice has been created only for some items or stages, then you can create an invoice for the remaining items or stages. However, you can create a subsequent invoice only after the ordering party accepts or rejects the first invoice. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 131 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Creating Subsequent Invoices A carrier can submit subsequent invoices for an individual freight document. A carrier may want to invoice only a few charge lines for the charges he has actually incurred and then submit a second invoice for the remaining charges he has subsequently incurred. Alternatively, the carrier may want to charge all the lines in one invoice and then later add his unplanned charges in a subsequent invoice. In the freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics, multiple invoices can be created for the same freight document. A subsequent invoice can only be created for an individual freight document on the following conditions: There is no active invoice for that given freight document. If the carrier creates an invoice but does not submit it to SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) and then tries to create a second invoice, an error message is returned informing him that an invoice already exists. An invoice has already been submitted to the SAP TM system. Only when the first invoice has been submitted to the SAP TM system can a second invoice be created, but the invoicing cannot be done for the lines that have already been invoiced. When the subsequent invoice is submitted from the freight collaboration option, it creates the subsequent invoice in SAP TM after the previous invoice has been transferred for Accruals. The carrier can choose to exclude certain lines from an invoice – either because he wants to invoice it later or he has not incurred that charge – by clicking the cross icon. This will ensure that only a few charge lines are invoiced but not others. Excluded lines can be part of a subsequent invoice. A further condition of subsequent invoicing relates to parent and child lines. If a parent line is part of one invoice, all its dependent lines are also expected to be part of the same invoice, so parent and child lines always appear as part of one invoice. They cannot be split and invoiced in different invoices. If the carrier chooses to exclude a child line but not the parent line, a warning message is displayed informing the carrier that the excluded line has a reference in that invoice and that after the invoice has been submitted, it will no longer be possible to invoice the excluded child line. Adding a Subsequent Charge When you create a subsequent invoice, you can add a subsequent charge for a charge type which has already been invoiced. In the Charges tab, for each charge line, you can choose the icon to add a subsequent charge. When you choose the icon, you can enter a new subsequent charge and the old invoice amount is displayed below. The rate amount has been disabled for subsequent charges. You can add the additional amount in the Final Amount field and submit the invoice. For example, if the already invoiced amount for the charge type Basic Freight is EUR 100, and you enter EUR 50 as the subsequent charge, then the final invoiced amount for Basic Freight will be EUR 150. Review Freight Documents You can have a billing process in place with your ordering party where you do not submit an invoice to your ordering party for the transportation services you provide. Instead, your ordering party pays you automatically in a self-billing process, based on the information in the freight document.  Note This feature is available only if the ordering party has enabled the necessary settings for you. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 132 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- You can create disputes against the freight documents for self-billing for unplanned freight costs. To create a dispute case, you can use the Review Freight Documents app. You can view all the freight documents for which you have not yet created any disputes in the No Disputes tab. When you navigate to the detailed view of the freight document, you can review the freight document charges and other details. You can create a dispute if you have any unplanned charges or if you have incurred additional charges for an existing charge line. When you choose Create Dispute, the system creates a new dispute document and you can make changes to the document. When you change a value in a charge line or add a new charge line, the system displays a dropdown menu in the Dispute Reason column, from which you must select a reason for the dispute. You can choose to save your changes and submit them later. When you have saved the changes and not submitted the dispute yet, you can choose to either cancel the changes or delete the entire dispute document. Once you submit the document, you cannot delete the dispute document. Once the system creates a dispute, you can view this document in the Manage Disputes app. For more information on the Manage Disputes app, see Manage Disputes. Manage Invoices You can use the Manage Invoices app to view all the invoices that you created for your ordering party in the freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can select one or more freight documents and create a single invoice or a collective invoice for your ordering party for the services that you provided using the Invoice Freight Documents app. For more information, see Invoice Freight Documents. Status Displays one of the following invoice statuses: Draft This status appears when you create a new invoice and the invoice is not yet submitted to the ordering party. Submitted This status appears when you submit the invoice to the ordering party. Note that when the invoice is submitted to the ordering party and an invoice has been created in the ordering party’s external system, you can view an information button next to the Submitted status. In Dispute This status appears when there is a dispute for an invoice document as a result of differences and potential disputes between what the ordering party expects to pay against what you expect to be paid. API Invoice Error This status appears when there is any error in the Provider API for Invoicing. Therefore, this status appears on an invoice when the relevant disputed document has been resolved and now needs to be reviewed by the carrier and any relevant tax lines can be edited before the invoice is submitted to the SAP Transportation Management system. Editing and Submitting Invoices You can view all the freight documents from one or more of your ordering parties using the Invoice Freight Documents app. You can select one or more of these freight documents and create a single invoice or a collective invoice for your ordering party for the services that you provided. For more information about invoice creation process, see Creating Invoices from Freight Documents. For more information about collective invoice creation process, see Creating a Collective Invoice. When you create one or more invoices from one or more freight documents, the system uses the data from the freight document and fills it in the corresponding fields in the invoice. The system assigns Draft status to the newly created invoice. Editing an Invoice Before you submit an invoice to the ordering party, you can edit an invoice directly in the app or you can download a Microsoft Excel file of the invoice, edit the downloaded file, and then upload the edited file back in the app. Using either method, the system allows you to perform the following: Edit the invoice ID and invoice date Edit rate amount and final amount Add a tax charge line and specify the following: Tax type (maximum of 3 characters) Percentage Final amount Note that for only for tax charge lines, you can specify the final amount as zero. Resubmitting Invoices You can reopen a submitted invoice to make any necessary changes and then resubmit the invoice. Context If an invoice for a freight document contains certain errors such as, an incorrect tax charge type, the invoice might not appear in the SAP Transportation Management system when you submit it. In this case, the customer can inform the carrier that the invoice has not been created in SAP Transportation Management and then ask the carrier to reopen the invoice, make the necessary changes and resubmit the invoice. Procedure 1. Go to the Submitted worklist tab to reopen an invoice that has already been submitted. 2. Choose the Reopen button. The system then changes the invoice status to Error to indicate that the invoice is in progress again and the invoice appears on the Error worklist tab. 3. Make the necessary changes, such as excluding all 0 amounts or adding tax codes, and choose Save to save the invoice. The invoice status remains as Error. 4. Choose Submit to resubmit the invoice. The invoice status then changes to Submitted. Results Once the invoice has been corrected and resubmitted, it is created in the SAP Transportation Management system.  Note You only need to reopen an invoice if the invoice has failed in SAP Transportation Management. Otherwise, you should not reopen invoices that have already been submitted. If you reopen an invoice that was created in the SAP Transportation Management system without any errors and then try to resubmit it, the system rejects the invoice as the invoice ID is identified as a duplicate. This ensures that the process is not interrupted.  Note The invoice ID is read-only, but you can modify the Charge fields, and Notes and Attachments can also be edited. The Reopen button appears only on invoices that have been submitted, but have not yet reached the ordering party’s external system.  Note When you reopen an invoice, the status of the invoice is set as In Error. Manage Disputes As a carrier, you can have a self-billing process in place with the ordering party, wherein you do not submit an invoice for the transportation services. Instead, the ordering party settles automatically based on the information in the freight document. In this process, you can have differences and potential disputes between what the ordering party expects to pay against what you expect to be paid. To keep good business relationships, you need to work closely with the ordering party to resolve these differences in a collaborative way. You need to get clarification on the differences and converge on an understanding with the ordering party on how to resolve the differences. You can create disputes against the freight documents for self-billing for additional unplanned charges, rates, quantities, and final amounts. Creating and Reviewing Disputes from Ordering Party You can create disputes against the freight documents for self-billing for additional unplanned freight costs. To create a dispute case, you can use the Review Freight Documents app. Once the system creates a dispute, you can view this document in the Manage Disputes app. For more information on creating a dispute, see Creating a Dispute. In the Manage Disputes app, you can view all the newly created disputes that are yet to be submitted in the New tab. You can navigate to the dispute details and propose changes in the Charges tab. You can newly add a charge line for an additional charge encountered during the transportation or you can propose a change in an existing charge line.  Note Notes are intended to provide additional information related to the business document or business process. You’re recommended to avoid entering sensitive personal data.  Note You can attach documents related to the business document or business process in this section. You’re recommended to avoid attaching sensitive personal data. You can only upload files that fulfil the following criteria: Files must be of one of the formats: jpg, gif, png, .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx Image files must be less than 6MB file size Document files must be less than 5MB file size File name must be less than 150 characters including file extension  Note It is highly recommended that when you change the rate amount, quantity, or final amount, you also change the others accordingly. You can choose to save your changes and submit them later. When you have saved the changes and not submitted the dispute yet, you can choose to either cancel the changes or delete the entire dispute document. Once you submit the document, you cannot delete the dispute document. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 159 This is custom documentation. Based on the action performed by you or the ordering party, the system displays the following document statuses in the header area: New This status appears when you have newly created a dispute document. To be approved This status appears when the ordering party has taken an action on the disputes raised by you and submits it back to you for your approval. Submitted This status appears when you submit your disputes to the ordering party for approval. Resolved This status appears when both you and the ordering party have converged on an understanding and resolved the differences. Based on the action performed by you or the ordering party, the system displays the following statuses at the disputed charge line: Disputed by carrier This status appears when you propose a change in an existing charge line or added an unplanned charge. Disputed by ordering party This status appears when the ordering party proposes a change on a charge line disputed by you and submits the dispute back to you. You could either accept the ordering party's proposal or propose another change. When you accept the proposal, the system changes the status of the charge line as Accepted by carrier. When you propose another change, the system changes the status as Disputed by carrier. Accepted by ordering party This status appears when the ordering party accepts the dispute proposed by you and submits the dispute back to you. When all the disputed lines are accepted by the ordering party, then the dispute document is set to status Resolved. You do not have to take an action on the resolved charge lines. Rejected by ordering party This status appears when the ordering party rejects your proposal and submits the dispute to you. Note that when the ordering party rejects your proposal, you can either accept the rejection or propose another change. When you accept the rejection, the system changes the status of the charge line as Accepted by carrier. When you propose another change, the system changes the status as Disputed by carrier. Rejection accepted by carrier This status appears when the ordering party rejects your proposal and you accept the ordering party's rejection. Accepted by carrier This status appears when you accept the ordering party’s proposal and submit the dispute to the ordering party.  Note 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 160 This is custom documentation. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Invoice Process Settings You can select the invoice process settings. On dispute resolution, when you submit the dispute to the ordering party, a dialog box appears and you can choose one of the following options for the invoice: Submit the invoice with updated charges to the ordering party If you select this option, once the dispute is resolved between you and the ordering party, the invoice with the updated charges related to this dispute will be submitted to the ordering party. If there are taxes in the invoice, you can modify the taxes before resolving the dispute so that the invoice is submitted to the ordering party with the appropriate tax amounts. Update the invoice and set the status as Ready for Submission If you select this option, once the dispute is resolved between you and the ordering party, the invoice related to this dispute will be updated and the status will be set as Ready for Submission. You can navigate to the invoice in the Manage Invoices app and submit it. Set the invoice status as Rejected by Dispute If you select this option, once the dispute is resolved between you and the ordering party, the invoice related to this dispute will be set as Rejected by Dispute. You can create and submit a new invoice. An information message indicating the status of the invoice after dispute resolution appears on the header area of the dispute details page. If you want to modify the invoice process settings, you can do so using the link available in the information message. Acknowledgement Message After Dispute Resolution A dispute is resolved when the shipper or the carrier accepts all charges proposed by the other party. For example, the carrier proposes charges and the shipper accepts these charges. When the party that has the document accepts all the charges, then the system updates these charges in the freight document in the shipper's SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system and the dispute status is updated as Submitted for confirmation. When the resolved charges that have been agreed upon by the shipper and the carrier in the freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics are updated in the shipper's SAP TM system, the system displays an acknowledgment message that the charges have been updated. If the charges are not updated, the system displays a failure message. Success message When a successful acknowledgment message is received in the freight collaboration option, the status of the shipper's dispute is set to Resolved. Then, the carrier dispute is set to Resolved, after which the carrier invoice status is updated to Submitted (for an invoicing dispute) and the carrier invoice is submitted to the SAP TM system. When the ordering party rejects a dispute document, you can re-submit the dispute document by adding a note for the rejected charge line without modifying the rate amount. Note that this is relevant only for disputes from SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. The ordering party has rejected the dispute document with the reason as attachment missing. In this scenario, you can add an attachment without modifying the rate amount and submit the dispute document.  Note This setting is applicable only when there is a change in the invoice post dispute process. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 161 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 3 -- When the system receives an acknowledgment message from the SAP TM system, it sets the dispute status changed as Resolved. Failure message If the SAP TM freight document update fails, TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In will fail with errors, and the acknowledgment message (TransportationOrderChargeElementConfirmation_Out) will not be triggered. The shipper must process this error in Forward Error Handling (FEH), which has already been registered and implemented on the inbound side for TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In. FEH is configured to perform error handling. Therefore, the error message is forwarded to FEH post-processing, which the shipper can access by choosing the red flag. You user launches the transaction sxi_monitor in the shipper's system and provides the interface name as TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In. Error message If TransportationOrderChargeElementConfirmation_Out message contains any error, it will set the dispute status as In Error. The error must be addressed in the SAP TM system and the dispute can be re-triggered. This will resend the TransportationOrderChargeElementRequest_In message to update the charges again. Dispute Inconsistencies During Freight Document Updates Updates in self-billed freight documents are reflected in the dispute document in the carrier's system and are marked as inconsistent. When a carrier, creates a dispute on a self-billed freight document and the ordering party also makes changes to the self-billed freight document in their SAP Transportation Management system, the system notifies the carrier that the carrier is disputing on a document that has recently been changed. The system displays the following message to the carrier: Some of the charges have inconsistent values due to changes in the freight document. Also, the system highlights the relevant lines and indicates as Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted). The carrier can accept the new charges or create a new dispute with the new frame of reference. When the carrier chooses Merge charges, the line that was previously marked as being Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted) is no longer in dispute and the system no longer highlights the line. If other lines are in dispute, the system continues this process. However, if there are no other disputed lines and if the carrier submits the document, the dispute status changes to Submitted for confirmation. If the document is with the ordering party, the disputed line is highlighted and marked as Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted). The document is editable in the ordering party's system but not in the carrier's system. If there are disputed lines that are inconsistent, the system displays the following message to the ordering party: Some of the charges have inconsistent values due to changes in the freight document. When the ordering party accepts the charges, the line that was previously marked as being Inconsistent (Updated) or Inconsistent (Deleted) is no longer in dispute, and the system no longer highlights the line. If other lines are in dispute, the system continues this process.  Note The system does this only for disputes on self-billed freight documents. Also, the system does this only for disputes that are managed by the ordering party in their SAP Business Network for Logistics system and not in their external transportation system. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 162 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 3 -- However, if there are no other disputed lines and if the document is submitted by the ordering party, the dispute status changes to To be reviewed and is sent to the carrier for approval. The carrier can view the updated charges. APIs for Planning in External System As a carrier, you can use the APIs in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration for planning in external system. The ordering party creates transportation requirements from a sales order, purchase order, or delivery documents in their SAP Transportation Management system and sends it to you and requests you to perform planning activities in your system. Once you create a planned freight document in your system, you can send the document containing the transportation requirements back to the ordering party. You can perform these activities using the following APIs: Consumer API to Request for Planning in External System Provider API to Create Planned Freight Document from External System For more information, see https://help.sap.com/doc/e1b2026259d84fc29e6e6760da815011/LBN/en- US/e3d67b2e9ec847a5b6942021a74b2523.html. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 163 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 3 --

Freight Settlement Invoice Submission After Dispute Resolution A carrier invoice is ready for submission after disputes are resolved. The carrier can then review the invoice, adjust the tax lines (if needed) based on the resolved amount, and submit the invoice. Update Carrier Dispute The system sends an email notification to you when the shipper sends a dispute document for your approval. The notification email includes a link to the dispute document. Resolve Carrier Dispute The system sends an email notification to you when the shipper resolves a dispute document. The notification email includes a link to the dispute document. Pending Invoice Submitted The system sends an email notification to you when the pending invoice document has been submitted after receiving the corresponding freight document from your shipper. Invoice with API Error The system sends an email notification to you when the invoice document fails during processing in SAP Business Network for Logistics with an error. Invoice Submission Pending The system sends an email notification to you when the invoice document is not yet submitted to your shipper as the corresponding freight document is not available in SAP Business Network for Logistics. Manage Network Invitations An invitation has been sent to you from a shipper. The notification includes a link that you can click to view the invitation and respond to it. Update Freight Booking The system sends an email notification to you when a shipper sends an updated freight booking. Cancel Freight Booking The system sends an email notification to you when a shipper sends a cancellation of a freight booking. Related Information Define User Settings (Carrier) Configure Notification Settings (Carrier) Prerequisites To enable reminder notifications, make sure you also maintain an email address and subscribe to the notification(s) you need in the Define User Settings app. For more information, see Define User Settings (Carrier) Context You can configure the following types of notifications in the Manage Notification Settings app, where applicable. On-Event Notification On-event notification refers to the email notification that you receive at the time when a target event happens, for example, when you receive an invitation from a shipper. You can activate or deactivate on-event notification by setting the activation toggle to Yes or No, respectively. Pre-Event Notifications Pre-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive before the target event happens, for example, before dock appointment booking cut-off. You can schedule pre-event notifications by adding notification periods and specifying notification frequency within each period, as described below: Notification period: The period within which email notifications will be sent in a specified frequency. You only specify the start of the period, for example, 30 days before the event, which means the notification period starts from 30 days before the event till the start of the next period or the event time.  Note To enable email notifications for the above scenarios, you need to activate the settings in this app and subscribe to notifications for the scenarios in the Define User Settings app. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 13 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Frequency: The frequency to receive notifications within the specified period. For example, setting the frequency to every 5 days means within the specified period, you'll receive an email notification every 5 days. Post-Event Notifications Post-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive after the target event happens, for example, after you have received the invitation. You can schedule post-event notifications by adding notification periods and specifying notification frequency within each period, as described below: Notification period: The period within which email notifications will be sent in a specified frequency. You only specify the end of the period, for example, 30 days after the event, which means the notification period starts from the end of the previous period or the event time, to 30 days after the event. Frequency: The frequency to receive notifications within the specified period. For example, setting the frequency to every 5 days means within the specified period, you'll receive an email notification every 5 days.  Example The schedule shown below Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 60 days Every 10 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days Yes 15 days Every 3 days Yes specifies the following schedule: Within the period from 60 days before the event to 30 days before the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Within the period from 30 days before the event to 15 days before the event, receive a notification every 5 days. Within the period from 15 days before the event till the event time, receive a notification every 3 days. In the same example, if you deactivate the "30 days" period, as shown below: Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 60 days Every 10 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days No 15 days Every 3 days Yes Then the "30 days" period is ignored and the schedule changes to: Within the period from 60 days before the event to 15 days before the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Within the period from 15 days before the event till the event time, receive a notification every 3 days.  Example The schedule shown below 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 14 This is custom documentation. System Connections (Carrier) Use the System Connections app for carriers and partners to complete the implementation of SAP Business Network for Logistics APIs. By implementing the freight tendering, subcontracting and tracking APIs published by SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, your organization can receive and respond to freight tendering documents, subcontracting documents, and tracking requests directly from your system. To complete the API implementations, you – as an administrator – also need to perform the following steps using the System Connections app: Specify the authentication details and base URLs for your system’s endpoints. Assign authentication details and a base URL to each API operation that you’ve implemented. Enable inbound communication to SAP Business Network for Logistics. The app has the following areas: Outbound Connections This area lists the outbound-from-network API services to which you can assign authentication details and a base URL. In addition, you can see the active or inactive status of the operations. Manage Details This area enables you to manage (create, edit and delete) your base URLs (communication details) and your authentication details (OAuth 2.0 and basic credentials). Connection Settings This area enables you to call LBN endpoints for inbound and outbound connections. For more information about the APIs published by SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, go to SAP Business Accelerator Hub . Specifying the Authentication Details and Base URLs for Your System’s Endpoints 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 21 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Configure communication and authentication details for your system's API or EDI endpoints by specifying base URLs, protocols (HTTPS/SFTP/Email), and authentication methods (Basic, API Key, OAuth 2.0) to enable secure integration with SAP Business Network for Logistics. Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, click Manage Details. 2. In the Communication Details section, click Add and complete the dialog. You can choose between the following options: HTTPS (for API) SFTP (for EDI) Email (for EDI) 3. In the Authentication Details section, click Add and complete the dialog. When creating API communication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name An identifier for the details Base URL The endpoint URL for the communication The API call made to your system uses the HTTPS protocol. When creating EDI communication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name Enter a name to identify the authentication details in this app. Address Enter the host name or IP address of the SFTP server and an optional port, for example, my.host.org:22. You can configure this parameter by entering a dynamic expression such as ${property.property_name} or ${header.header_name}. Message Format You can choose EDIFACT or ANSI X12 from the drop-down list. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 22 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Attribute Description Message Type For EDIFACT, you can choose between the following options: IFTMIN All Inbound Messages For ANSI X12, you can choose between the following options: 204 213 300 303 997 All Inbound Messages Known Host Key Enter a base64-encoded string of your SFTP server. This is used to authenticate your server. SAP Business Network for Logistics can also retrieve the known host key and insert it for you. As a prerequisite, you must have entered the address (including the port) of the SFTP server. Message Version The D96A message version is selected by default corresponding to EDIFACT. The V4010 message version is selected by default corresponding to ANSI X12. No version will be displayed for message type All Inbound Messages. Description The Instructions of Transport description is selected by default corresponding to EDIFACT message type IFTMIN. The Load Tender description is selected by default corresponding to ANSI X12 message type 204. The description will not be shown for message type All Inbound Messages. Directory Enter the relative path to write the file to a directory. Example: parentdirectory/childdirectory File Name Enter the name of the file to be written. The entry is valid only for LBN outbound message types. Additional allowed placeholders: %DOCUMENT_ID% %MESSAGE_TYPE% %TIMESTAMP% %SHIPPER_LBN_ID% %CONTROL_NUMBER% The placeholder %CONTROL_NUMBER% is only available for ANSI X12 997 messages. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 23 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Attribute Description You can combine these placeholders with any fixed strings and in any order (<string 1><placeholder 1><string 2><placeholder 2> <string 3>). Examples: LBN_%MESSAGE_TYPE%_%DOCUMENT_ID%_%TIMESTAMP%.edi %TIMESTAMP%_%SHIPPER_LBN_ID%.edi When creating Basic authentication details, the provided user name and password are used for authentication during the API call to your system. When creating API Key authentication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name An identifier for the details API Key Attribute Enter the key for the request header. API Key Value Enter the token to be used for authentication. The API key represents the name of the token that a client provides when making API calls. The token is sent as request header. When creating OAuth 2.0 authentication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name Enter a name to identify the authentication details in this app. Grant Type Valid values are: Client Credentials (default) and Client Certificate. Authentication URL Enter the URL of the OAuth 2.0 authorization server that issues the access token. Client ID Enter the ID of the client that you’re connecting to. Client Secret Secret key of the client that you’re connecting to. OAuth 2.0 uses a multiple-step authentication pattern: Client credentials (Client ID and Client Secret) are used by the client application to initially request an access token. The access token is then used to authorize the client (for as long as the token is valid) to access the server’s resources (for example, the resources that are used in the associated integration flow). In many OAuth 2.0 scenarios, the access token is issued (or generated) by an authorization server. Client Authentication Select Send as Body Parameter or Send as Request Header. This enables access to your system. If you select Send as Body Parameter, the Client ID and Client Secret are sent in the request body to the authentication server. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 24 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Attribute Description If you select Send as Request Header, the Client ID and Client Secret are sent as a part of the authorization header to the authentication server. Valid values are: client credentials and client certificate. Client Certificate When you select Send as Body Parameter, the Client ID goes in the request body to the authentication server. If you choose Send as Request Header, the Client ID becomes part of the authorization header sent to the authentication server. Specify the path of the client certificate (key pair file) in the Key Pair File field. Enter its password in the Password field. Include Scope Select the checkbox to provide the OAuth 2.0 scope information that will be included in the request body. Scope Enter the scope that you defined for the endpoint. Content Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded is selected by default. Worklists by status The invitations are categorized based on the invitation statuses: New, Accepted, and Rejected. Worklist (Manage Invitations) There are different ways to work on the invitations and to set filters. To restrict the number of invitations displayed, you can use the filter bar in the header and the preconfigured worklists (New, Accepted, Rejected) based on the status of the invitation. Filter Bar With the filter bar, you can do the following: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for invitations. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. Worklists New The New worklist displays all invitations that you have not yet responded to. This worklist displays the following details for each invitation: Invitation Number Inviter Inviter LBN Network ID Invitation From Phone number Email  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 31 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- City Country/Region Address Accept and reject options Accepted The Accepted worklist displays all the invitations that you have accepted. This worklist displays the following details for each invitation: Invitation Number Inviter Inviter LBN Network ID Invitation From Phone number Email City Country/Region Address Administration information such as Accepted On and Accepted By Rejected The Rejected worklist displays all the invitations that you have rejected. This worklist displays the following details for each invitation: Invitation Number Inviter Inviter LBN Network ID Invitation From Phone number Email City Country/Region Address Administration information such as Rejected On and Rejected By  Note Using the  Settings icon on each worklist, you can control the number of columns displayed in the New, Accepted, and Rejected worklists. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 32 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- You can schedule alerts for the invitations that you receive from potential business partners. On the event of receiving or automatically accepting an invitation, you can specify whether you want to receive a notification in an email using the Manage Notification Settings app. For more information, see Manage Notification Settings (Carrier). Viewing an Invitation Context To view an invitation, perform the following: Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Invitations app. 2. You can view all the new invitations in the New worklist. (Optional) You can retrieve a specific invitation or a set of invitations using the various search filter options such as the inviter's company name, email, city, country/region, that appear on the header area. The system also categorizes the invitations based on various attributes and displays them in the following tabs: New: Displays all new invitations from potential business partners. Accepted: Displays invitations that you have accepted. Rejected: Displays invitations that you have rejected. Accepting or Rejecting an Invitation Context You can accept or reject the invitations from potential business partners to connect with their business network. When rejecting, you can indicate a rejection reason to the inviter. If you accept an invitation, you can connect with the inviter's business network and the system notifies the inviter of the same. If you reject an invitation, you cannot connect with the inviter's business network and the system notifies the inviter of the same. To accept or reject an invitation, perform the following: Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Invitations app. You can view all the new invitations in the New worklist. You can directly accept or reject the invitations in this worklist. 2. Alternatively, you can search for and retrieve a specific invitation using search filter options in the header. Once you retrieve the invitation, you can respond to the invitation by choosing the Accept or Reject button. Results Once you accept or reject an invitation, you can view the details of the invitation in the Accepted or Rejected worklist as appropriate. You cannot view this invitation anymore in the New worklist.  Note 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 33 This is custom documentation. Default value: No Freight Contracting You can participate in freight contracting when a known ordering party sends you a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ). Subsequently, if the freight quotation was awarded, then you can find the corresponding freight documents in the Freight Orders for Confirmation, Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean), and Confirm Freight Bookings (Air). Your options for responding to the received freight RFQ are determined by the tendering setup implemented by the ordering party. Your response options depend on the following settings: Is the price negotiable? If so, you can propose a new price. Are the dates and times negotiable? If so, you can propose new dates and times. Does the ordering party require you to respond? If a response is unrequired (indicated by Accept Automatically: Yes) then the freight RFQ will be automatically accepted when the response time runs out, unless you reject it beforehand. If a response is required and you want the job then you must accept the freight RFQ before the response time runs out. When you accept or reject a freight RFQ, the SAP Business Network for Logistics creates a freight quotation and sends it to the ordering party. The ordering party then evaluates your freight quotation and, according to their strategy, may or not award it to you. Accepting a Freight Request for Quotation If you agree with the price and the dates given by the ordering party, you can accept a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ) without proposing a change. Context You can also accept a freight RFQ that you previously rejected or accepted with a change, as long as the freight RFQ has not been closed by the ordering party. If you want to propose a new price or new dates, see Accepting a Freight Request for Quotation with a Change. Procedure 1. Open the Freight Requests for Quotation app. 2. Within a worklist (New, Responded To, or All), select one or more open freight RFQs (a freight RFQ is open if its remaining time has not ran out). To accept a single freight RFQ, you can also use the detail view. 3. Choose Accept. Note that if one or more of the selected freight RFQs contain zero prices from the ordering party and if you have not maintained any price, the system displays a warning message before you proceed to Accept. The ordering party expects you to enter a price before you accept. Next Steps Your ordering party will now evaluate your freight quotation and reply to it. If they award it to you, they will ask you to confirm the related freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Accepting a Freight Request for Quotation with a Change You can accept a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ) with a change. Context If the ordering party wants to receive proposals for alternative prices or dates to those which they specified in the freight request for quotation (freight RFQ), then you can make a proposal by accepting the freight RFQ with a change. And, as long as the remaining time has not run out and the freight RFQ has not been closed by the ordering party, you can accept a freight RFQ and make a date or price proposal for freight RFQs that you previously rejected or accepted.  Note The ordering party can maintain a setting in their transportation management system to either enable or disable you from modifying the price proposal currency. Based on this setting, when you accept a freight request for quotation with change, the system either enables you to modify the price proposal currency or does not allow you to do so. You can view these details in the information icon next to the price proposal currency, in the dialog box, which appears when you choose the Accept with Change button in the freight request for quotation. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 41 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Open the Freight Requests for Quotation app. 2. Within a worklist (New, Responded To, or All), look for the open freight RFQ for which you want to enter changes (a freight RFQ is open if its remaining time has not ran out). Alternatively, you can also open the detail view of the freight RFQ. 3. Choose Accept with Change. 4. Enter your your proposal price and the currency. 5. Enter your date proposals. For each stop, the earliest start and the latest end for all activities at that location are displayed, such as driving on the premises, loading, completing paper work. These dates might be prefilled by your ordering party. In the proposal fields in the middle, you can see if the ordering party would prefer a timeframe for your activities. If these are empty, you can enter your own proposal in these fields. 6. Choose Accept with Change. Next Steps Your ordering party will now evaluate your freight quotation and reply to it. If they award it to you, they will ask you to confirm the related freight order in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Rejecting a Freight Request for Quotation You can reject a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ) if you are unable to or do not want to take over this transport. Context As long as the remaining time to respond hasn't ran out and the freight RFQ has not been closed by the ordering party, you can reject a freight RFQ, even if you previously accepted it. Procedure 1. Open the Freight Requests for Quotation app. 2. Within a worklist (New, Responded To, or All), select one or more open freight RFQs (a freight RFQ is open if its remaining time has not ran out). To reject a single freight RFQ, you can also use the detail view. 3. Choose Reject and select a rejection reason. Note, the reject reason will be assigned to all selected freight RFQs and recorded in each automatically generated freight quotation. 4. Choose Reject. Responded To (Open) The Responded To (Open) worklist displays all freight orders that you've already responded to. The Responded To (Open) worklist displays the same information as the All worklist. You can select one or more freight orders and choose to either Confirm or Reject from the worklist page. You can choose to export the worklist into a spreadsheet by choosing the Export to Spreadsheet icon on the top right corner of the worklist table. You can view the unit of measure along with total gross weight, total gross volume, and total quantity. However, when you download the freight orders in a Microsoft Excel sheet, the system still displays the unit of measures for these attributes in separate columns to enable easy sorting. Some of the fields that are not relevant for documents with the document category as Shipment Not Relevant.  Note 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 52 This is custom documentation. The following fields may be of particular interest for you: General details Displays the freight order ID, document category, ordering party, and consignee party. Document category displays whether the document is a freight order or a shipment. When you choose the ordering party or consignee party, you can view the address and contact details. Price (Negotiable or Non-negotiable) Whether the price is negotiable or not depends on the ordering party's decision. Submitted price Remaining time (Confirm Automatically: Yes/No) If it says Confirm Automatically: Yes, the network will automatically confirm the freight order for you unless you reject it before the remaining time runs out. The remaining time is not a mandatory field. Depending on the ordering party's setup, you may not be restricted by a dedicated response due date time. Your latest response (Confirmed, Confirmed with Change, Rejected, Confirmed Automatically) Contact details of the ordering party Freight order status (New, New (updated), Updated, Confirmed, Confirmed with change, Automatically confirmed, Rejected Canceled, Cancellation confirmed) Information The information tab contains the General section and the Reference Documents section. You can view the following details in these sections: You can view a message that highlights the number of notes in the notes section and you can also navigate to the notes section when you choose View All. General Displays the following information: Freight Order ID Total Distance Total Duration Response Due Date And Time Number Of Loading Stops Number Of Unloading Stops Some of the fields and tabs that are not relevant for a shipment document are not displayed in freight orders with the document category as Shipment. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 53 This is custom documentation. Mode of Transport SAP Transportation Management System SAP Business Network for Logistics System 03 - Ocean 01 - Ocean 01 - Road 03 - Road 05 - Air 04 - Air  Note If the ordering party has entered dangerous goods information in their SAP Transportation Management (TM) system, this information is transferred to SAP Business Network for Logistics.
