Note that you can add reference documents with the document types such as Global Location Number, Motor Carrier Number, United States Department of Transportation, and so on for executing carriers so that the ordering party can use this information for tracking purposes. You can also download the reference document details in a spreadsheet. You can view the following details in this document: Document ID Document Type Code Document Type Description Created On (UTC) Created By Cargo and Service Items This section displays the following data about the cargo items involved: Service Items In this sub-section, the system displays the number of document services and cargo services. When you choose the number, you can view the additional details of all the document services and cargo services in a dialog box. Cargo In this sub-section, the system displays the cargo item ID as the combination of Item ID with the parent hierarchy separated by colon as the prefix in freight documents with the document category as Shipment. Cargo Item / Description Displays the description of the cargo item. Type Displays whether the cargo item is a package, product, or a container. Note that if the cargo item is a container, the system displays this field as Type/ID. You can enter the container ID in the field next to container cargo type. Logistical Details Displays the quantity, gross weight, gross volume, and dimensions. Also displays the normalized quantity. Equipment Details Displays the equipment type and equipment group. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 55 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Special Requirements Displays the following: Dangerous Goods If the ordering party has provided dangerous goods information, you can view this information from the Cargo section by choosing Yes in the Dangerous Goods column. This opens a window containing details about the item type, relevant regulations, and more detailed information such as storage instructions, control temperature, and emergency temperature. Temperature Requirements Reference Document You can view the following: Customer purchase order details Document ID and document type of the SAP Enterprise Resource Planning (SAP ERP) reference documents such as inbound delivery, outbound delivery, sales order, and purchase order document associated in the SAP Transportation Management system. Other Details Displays the following: Over-Dimensional Displays whether the cargo item is over-dimensional Non-Stackable High Value Seal Details When you choose this button, you can view the seal details in a dialog box. You can view the seal numbers and seal parties. Note that this button appears only in container line items. Cargo Services This field is visible when cargo services are available for a cargo item. Choosing it displays the detailed information. Stops and Stage Details When you select a cargo item and choose View Stage and Stop Details, you can view the stop and stage details for the cargo item. In the Stop Details tab, for each stop within the stop sequence, the address of the ordering party is displayed.  Note You can view the details of all cargo item types such as container, package, product, and service. You can navigate through the entire cargo item hierarchy. For example, from a container to the packages, package to the products or services and so on to view the respective details. The ordering party can implement a business add-in (BAdI) to display only the main cargo items. Any notes sent by the ordering party with text type LBNMI will be discarded as it is a technical text type used to display main cargo items. You can view the aggregated dangerous goods information for the filtered items at the main cargo item level. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 56 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- You can toggle between the Loading and Unloading buttons to view the information specific to the activity. The Loading tab displays the following details: Loading start date and time Loading end date and time Acceptable start date and time Acceptable end date and time Cargo items to be loaded The Unloading tab displays the following details: Unloading start date and time Unloading end date and time Acceptable start date and time Acceptable end date and time Cargo items to be unloaded Charges The Charges section displays the following information: Charge description Displays the charge type details for each stage in each freight document. Charge types are the classification of charges for which you charge the ordering party. Charge type (Transportation System) Classification of charge line that indicates the type of charges such base rate, surcharge, or discount, as specified in the ordering party's SAP Transportation Management system. Rate amount/unit Displays the flat rate amount or rate amount per unit, for example, USD 20 per 1 kg. Quantity Displays the total quantity relevant for calculating the final amount. Final amount Displays the final amount that has been derived from the rate amount, quantity, and calculation method. When you select a charge, you can view the following additional details specific for the selected charge: Transportation charges You can view the charge details such as line number, charge type, calculation methods, and payment terms. Line number Charge description 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 57 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Displays the classification of charges for which you charge the ordering party. These are the transportation mode- specific codes that are predefined by SAP Business Network for Logistics. Calculation method Displays the logic with which the system calculates the charges. Payment terms Displays the conditions of payment you agreed with your ordering party with respect to goods supplied or services provided. Logistical reference Displays the item or stage information for a charge line (for container, package, product, or stage) from which the system obtains the logistical data. Calculation basis Displays the actual base or factor with which the system calculated the charges. You can view the calculation basis for rates belonging to a rate table. Exchange rates Displays the exchange rate information that is used as the basis for currency conversion. Notes Displays the notes specified for the charge line. Tour The Tour section displays the stop sequence. For each stop, you can view the following information: Stop number Location You can click the link to view both the main and additional address of the location. Arrival and departure date and time Activity Distance to next location Time to next location Contacts If provided by the ordering party, the Contacts section displays the company name of the ordering party along with the phone number and the email address of the contact person. This section also displays the contact details for each individual stop (stop number and location). Notes The Notes section displays the comments previously left by the ordering party and yourself, as well as enabling you to add new notes. Note: When you add a new note, it is only sent when you confirm or reject the freight order. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 58 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Attachments The Attachments section displays the attachments the ordering party has sent you, as well as letting you upload your own attachments. Drivers and Resource Details The Drivers and Resource Details section enables you to provide the names of the drivers who will drive the vehicle as well as provide the vehicle license plate. You can specify the following details: Driver Details: Name and mobile numbers of the driver and additional driver Resource Details: Truck license plate and country or region of registration, truck ID, and trailer ID Confirming a Freight Order If you agree with the price and the dates given by the ordering party, you can confirm a freight order without proposing a change. Context You can confirm a freight order that fulfills the following criteria: The Freight Order Status is New, New (Updated), Confirmed, Confirmed with Change, and Confirmed Automatically even if the arrival date is in the past. The Freight Order Status is Rejected, Canceled or Cancellation Confirmed along with a future arrival date. You can also confirm a freight order that you previously rejected or confirmed with a change, as long as the freight order has not been closed by the ordering party. Procedure  Note Notes are intended to provide additional information related to the business document or business process. You’re recommended to avoid entering sensitive personal data. Any notes sent by the ordering party with text type LBNMI will be discarded as it is a technical text type used to display main cargo items.  Note The mobile number, truck ID, and trailer ID details are sent to the ordering party to their SAP Transportation Management system. The driver mobile number and the truck ID details that you enter here are used for tracking purposes. This section is not available in consignment orders. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 59 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- 1. Open the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. 2. Within a worklist (New, Responded To, or All), select one or more open freight orders. To confirm a single freight order, you can also use the detail view. 3. Choose Confirm. After confirming the freight order, the Confirm button changes to Send Update (unless there is still remaining time available). Clicking Send Update enables you to send information to the ordering party that you were unable to provide when confirming the freight order. Confirming a Freight Order with a Change You can confirm a freight order with a change. Context If the ordering party wants to receive proposals for alternative prices to those which they specified in the freight order, then you can make a proposal by confirming the freight order with a change. And, as long as the remaining time has not run out and the freight order has not been closed by the ordering party, you can confirm a freight order and make a price proposal for freight orders that you previously rejected or confirmed. Procedure 1. Open the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. 2. Within a worklist (New, Responded To, or All), look for the open freight order for which you want to enter changes. Alternatively, you can also open the detail view of the freight order. 3. Choose Confirm with Change. 4. Enter your price proposal. 5. Choose Confirm with Change. Rejecting a Freight Order You can reject a freight order if you are unable to or do not want to take on the transportation. Context As long as the remaining time to respond hasn't run out and the freight order has not been closed by the ordering party, you can reject a freight order, even if you previously confirmed it. You can reject a freight order as long as the arrival date and time has not passed.  Note The ordering party can maintain a setting in their transportation management system to either enable or disable you from modifying the price proposal currency. Based on this setting, for the direct tendering scenario, when you confirm a freight order with change, the system either enables you to modify the price proposal currency or does not allow you to do so. You can view these details in the information icon next to the price proposal currency, in the dialog box, which appears when you choose the Confirm with Change button in the freight order. Note that when you change the price proposal currency, the system automatically updates the settlement currency to be the same as the updated price proposal currency. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 60 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

When the response time is over and the shipper sends a cancelation, it is displayed in the All worklist with status Cancelation confirmed. Confirming a Cancelation If the ordering party cancels a freight order, you should confirm the cancelation to actively acknowledge the change. Context To confirm a cancelation, proceed as follows: Procedure 1. Open the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. 2. Within the New worklist, select one or more canceled freight orders. To confirm a cancelation for a single freight order, you can also use the detail view. 3. Choose Confirm. Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) The Confirm Freight Bookings app for ocean freight allows you to review and confirm ocean freight bookings that ordering parties ask you to execute. The Confirm Freight Bookings app consists of a main view and a detail view. The main view has two screen areas: Filter bar Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter ocean freight bookings by one or more of the following fields: Freight Booking ID Ordering Party Departure Date Departure Location Arrival Date Arrival Location Port of Loading Port of Discharge 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 61 This is custom documentation. From the main view, you can navigate to the detail view, which has two screen areas: Header You can display data such as booking details, port details, and status. Sections You can display further details in the General Info, Cargo, Capacity, Locations, Date and Time, Stages, Contacts, Attachments, and Notes sections. The New worklist displays the same information as the All worklist. You can select one or more freight bookings from the New worklist and choose Confirm or Reject. Rejected The Rejected worklist displays all freight bookings that you've rejected. The Rejected worklist displays the same information as the All worklist. From the All tab and New tab, you can select a freight booking with the status as New and choose to either Confirm or Reject from the worklist page. Note that you cannot confirm or reject freight bookings with the document category as Shipment. You can choose to export the worklist into a spreadsheet by choosing the Export to Spreadsheet icon on the top right corner of the worklist table. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Enter the number of confirmed containers per container type Unit of Measurement Displays the unit of measurement for the confirmed container count Cargo Capacity Displays the cargo capacity in TEU if maintained in the source system Unit of Measurement Displays the unit of measurement of the cargo capacity Locations For each stop, the system displays the following information: Stop Number Location Planned Arrival Date and Time Planned Departure Date and Time Activities Overview Distance to Next Stop Time to Next Stop You can choose View All Transportation Activities, to view the following information: Header You can view the booking details, port details, and status. Stops You can view the details of each stop and the activities in each stop in a table format. The system displays the following information for each stop: Date and Time Displays the planned arrival and planned departure date and time. Next Stop Details Displays the distance to next stop and time to next stop. Activities Displays the following information in a table format: Item ID Activity Cargo Details Gross Weight Gross Volume 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 71 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Quantity Length x Width x Height Special Requirements Date and Time Displays the date and time details for each stop. Depending on the type of stop, the system displays the date and time information. The following are the different types of stops: Pick-Up Location Indicates the source location of the first pre-carriage stage. Delivery Location Indicates the destination location of the last on-carriage stage. Port of Loading Indicates the source location of the first main carriage stage. Port of Discharge Indicates the destination location of the last main carriage stage. The system displays these dates and times in the time zone of their respective stop location. Note that the system receives this time zone information for a location from the transportation management system. If there is no time zone associated with a location in the transportation management system, then the system receives this time zone information from the location master in the SAP Business Network for Logistics system. If there is no time zone associated with a location in the location master, then the system by default displays the time zone as UTC for that location. Stages Displays the following information: Stage Type Displays whether the stage is a pre-carriage, on-carriage, or main carriage stage. Transport Specifies the mode of transport and means of transport details. The mode of transport specifies one of the following values: Maritime transport Road transport Air transport The mode of transport specifies one of the following values:  Note The port pick-up date, cargo cut-off date, and VGM cut-off date fields are not available in freight orders with the document category as Shipment. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 72 This is custom documentation. You can also toggle the view between the attachments that you have uploaded, the attachments from the ordering party, and the all the attachments. Note that this section is not available in freight bookings with the document category as Shipment.  Note Attachment file type must be base 64 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 74 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Notes The Notes section displays the notes the ordering party has sent you. You can as well enter your own notes. Managing an Ocean Freight Booking You can perform the following actions on a freight booking: Confirming a Freight Booking You can confirm a freight booking with the status as New. You can confirm a freight booking either from the worklist page or the freight booking details page. You can select one or more freight bookings from the New worklist and choose Confirm. You can also enter information in the editable fields in the freight booking details page and then confirm a freight booking. Note that once you confirm a freight booking, the status of the freight booking changes to Confirmed. Confirming a Freight Booking with a Change You can confirm a freight booking with a price proposal. For more information, see Confirming a Freight Booking with a Change. Updating a Freight Booking You can update a freight booking with the status as Confirmed. In the details page of a confirmed freight booking, you can update the information and choose Update. In the Stages tab, you can now specify an UN/LOCODE for a location for which there is no location details or UN/LOCODE specified. Rejecting a Freight Booking You can attach documents related to the business document or business process in this section. You’re recommended to avoid attaching sensitive personal data. You can only upload files that fulfil the following criteria: Files must be of one of the formats: jpeg, gif, png, .pdf, .doc, .docx, .xls, .xlsx Image files must be less than 6MB file size Document files must be less than 5MB file size When you mention the file path, you must mention the file name along with the extension.  Note Any notes sent by the ordering party with text type LBNMI will be discarded as it is a technical text type used to display main cargo items. You can enter notes when you reject a freight order. The ordering party can view these rejection notes in their transportation system. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 75 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- You can reject a freight booking with the status as New or Confirmed. You can reject a new freight booking from the worklist page or the freight booking details page. You can select one or more freight bookings from the New worklist and choose Reject. You can also reject a confirmed booking from the freight booking details page. Confirming a Freight Booking with a Change Context If the ordering party wants to receive proposals for alternative prices to those which they specified in the freight booking, then you can make a proposal by confirming the freight booking with a change. And, as long as the remaining time has not run out and the freight booking has not been closed by the ordering party, you can confirm a freight booking and make a price proposal for freight bookings that you previously rejected or confirmed. Procedure 1. Open the Freight Bookings for Confirmation (Ocean) app. 2. Within a worklist (New, Confirmed, Rejected, or All), look for the open freight booking for which you want to enter changes. Alternatively, you can also open the detail view of the freight booking. 3. Choose Confirm with Change. 4. Enter your price proposal and select a currency. 5. Choose Confirm. The Confirm Freight Bookings app consists of a main view and a detail view. The main view has two screen areas: Filter bar Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter air freight bookings by one or more of the following fields:  Note You cannot confirm, update, or reject freight bookings with the document category as Shipment.  Note The ordering party can maintain a setting in their transportation management system to either enable or disable you from modifying the price proposal currency. Based on this setting, for the direct tendering scenario, when you confirm a freight booking with change, the system either enables you to modify the price proposal currency or does not allow you to do so. You can view these details in the information icon next to the price proposal currency, in the dialog box, which appears when you choose the Confirm with Change button in the freight booking. You cannot view the Confirm with Change button if the ordering party has not maintained the necessary settings in their transportation management system. When you change the price proposal currency, the system automatically updates the settlement currency to be the same as the updated price proposal currency. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 76 This is custom documentation. Sections You can display further details in the Information, Cargo, Capacity, Locations, Date and Time, Stages, Contacts, Attachments, and Notes sections. Worklist (Confirm Freight Bookings (Air)) To restrict the number of air freight bookings displayed, you can use the preconfigured worklists (All, New, Confirmed, Rejected, and Canceled) according to the status of the freight booking. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 77 This is custom documentation. Document category displays whether the document is a freight booking or a shipment. When you choose the ordering party, consignee party, departure location, or arrival location, you can view the address, and address details. Airport Details Displays the Airport of Departure and Airport of Destination information. When you choose the airport of departure or destination, you can view the address and contact details. Status Displays one of the following confirmation statuses: New New (Updated) Displays this status when the ordering party sends an update on a freight booking that you have not yet confirmed. Manage Locations You can use the Manage Locations app to manage location master data either manually replicated from another system or created from scratch using the app. Location master data can then be consumed by other apps, such as Docking Location Settings, in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. You can set up a location replication using the Data Replication Framework (DRF) in the SAP S4/HANA source system. For more information, see the Business Configuration section of the Administration Guide for Shippers. Location master data consists of not only the address information, but also the business purpose of a location. Additionally, the master data of a location can include one or more alternative IDs so that the location becomes cross-platform identifiable. The main features of this app include: View a location Create a location Upload locations Edit a location  Note To use this app, you must add one or several roles to your role collection. The required role templates and application identifiers are described in the Available Roles for Shippers section of the Administration Guide for Shippers.  Note The Manage Locations app implements all security features and data protection-relevant functions documented in the "Security and Data Protection and Privacy" section of the Administration Guide. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 88 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Creating a Location To create a location, proceed as follows: 1. Click Create on the upper-right corner of the Locations table. The Create New Location page opens. 2. On the Create New Location page, enter the following details: Source: Source of the location. Valid values are: SAP SCM Logistic Location: Locations from one of the following systems: SAP Extended Warehouse Management SAP Transportation Management SAP ERP Location: Locations from an SAP ERP system Others: Locations from other systems Location Type: Type of the location This field is available when Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location. Object Type: Business purpose of a location. This field is configurable when Source is set to SAP ERP Location or Others. When Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location, the system automatically sets Object Type to Logistic Location. Valid values for the Object Type field are:: Business Partner Customer Plant Shipping Point Supplier If none of the values above fits the location’s business purpose, you can change Source to SAP SCM Logistic Location as an alternative. This will set Object Type to Logistic Location at the backend and make Location Type configurable. The Location Type field provides you with a broader list of types pertaining to various business purposes, such as port and hub. Description: Descriptive information about the location Source System/External ID: Source system from which the location master data is copied and the corresponding ID. A location master data record enters the blocking period if it has not been accessed for three consecutive years. The blocking period lasts for another three years, during which only audit specialists can access the record. The record will then be automatically deleted when the end of the blocking period is reached.  Note You can also maintain the information of an ordering party in this app by setting the Object Type field to Business Partner. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 89 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- If you are creating a location from scratch, set the Source System part to LBN, and set the External ID part to the location ID you previously prepared. If you are importing a location from SAP Transportation Management (TM), set the Source System to the business system name of your TM system and set the External ID to the location ID in TM. For locations that have its object type set to “Business Partner”, you can find the business system name of your TM system and the location ID in the SOAP request message sent to LBN. In this request, the MessageHeader.SenderBusinessSystemID attribute specifies the business system name and the internal ID of the sender (the MessageHeader.SenderParty.InternalID attribute) specifies the location ID. Alternatively, you can run transaction code SLDCHECK in TM to view the business system name. Logical System: You can also use the Logical System field to identify the system from which the location master data is replicated. The Logical System field is is optional in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. If you’ve only purchased the freight collaboration solution, leave this field empty. If you’ve purchased both freight collaboration and global track and trace, refer to the configuration for global track and trace to maintain the logical system ID. If you leave Generate geo-coordinates automatically with the default option, the system generates geo-coordinates for locations when both the latitude and longitude coordinates are missing. For more information, see Global settings for Geo-Coordinates. 5/12/26, 6:38 AM 90 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: Application Help Generated on: 2026-05-12 06:52:37 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace | LBN Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_LBN_GTT_OPTION/98d177f964dc42f8916622380de9d0c3?locale=en- US&state=PRODUCTION&version=LBN Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace The aim of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace is to capture, process and store tracking information about tracked business processes. Then, it allows business users to get real-time transparency of the execution of those processes. They can query any tracked process and display its retrieved data from end to end. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace is a cloud service solution based on SAP Business Technology Platform. It's integrated with the following SAP S/4HANA systems: SAP S/4HANA (on-premise) SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition Both two systems have the Transportation Management (TM) component embedded, which can work with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. To learn more about the SAP Business Network add-ons for project44 visibility services, see the Feature Scope Description for project44 Add-Ons and the Configuration and Application Guide for project44 Add-Ons. Solution Owner Apps This chapter provides application help on all the apps used by solution owners as part of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Overview The following apps are available for Solution Owners: Model Management App Description Manage Models to create and deploy a GTT metadata model that meets the business requirements for events and logic Check Processes and Events to display, dynamically and in a user-friendly way, a tracked process with its event data, based on a deployed GTT metadata model Business Operations  Note The following documentation uses the term SAP S/4HANA to refer to both SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition and SAP S/4HANA (on-premise). If any of the information provided applies to only SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA, this will be clearly specified.  Note The apps provided with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace run on desktops, as well as tablet devices that have a screen format wide enough to display the overview section and the detailed section of the screen, side-by-side. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- App Description View Logs to have an at-a-glance overview of the available logs and their statuses Manage Message Logs to view all the technical logs for all the message data, phase by phase and, if necessary, retrigger certain events or their correlations for the message Manage Event Logs to view all the technical logs for all the event data, phase by phase and, if necessary, retrigger one or multiple events or their correlations Manage Integration Logs to monitor the inbound and outbound integration messages related to location replication and visibility providers that are processed by SAP Business Network for Logistics Fulfillment Tracking App Description Track Shipments to monitor the real-time execution status of LE-TRA shipments and freight documents from SAP S/4HANA and report events manually Monitor Inbound ASNs to monitor the fulfillment status of inbound ASNs/deliveries Monitor Outbound Deliveries to monitor the fulfillment status of outbound deliveries Track SO Fulfillment to monitor the fulfillment status of sales orders Track PO Fulfillment to monitor the fulfillment status of purchase orders For more information on the Fulfilment Tracking apps, see Fulfillment Tracking Apps. In addition, SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace incorporates apps that are, or will be, standard across SAP Business Network for Logistics, including: Manage Network App Description Invite Business Partners to invite business partners already known to join their business network and check their participation status System Connections to create a connection and to authenticate inbound messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics from your on-premise SAP Transportation Management standalone system or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA Configure Partner Connections to establish a B2B connection to the external systems of your business partners Manage Business Profile to view and edit your company profile such as contact details and business partner type Manage Notification Templates to create a template for a notification email of an event, such as that a sales order has been created, for use with the notification service Manage Locations to manage location master data either manually copied from another system or created from scratch 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- App Description Discover Business Partners to search onSAP Business Network for Logistics and select suitable business partners, they may or may not already know, to invite to join their business network Retention Management App Description Blocking Store to access restricted data during its blocking period Retention Management to define rules that determine the residence and blocking periods of personal data Further, the Reminder service is introduced that allows you to create a template email for an event, such as that a sales order has been created, and automatically send to the involved parties of a tracked process, an email based on the template. It uses the Manage Notification Templates app to create the template and the Manage Models app to set up the notifications. Fulfillment Tracking Apps Fulfillment tracking apps monitor the fulfillment status of: sales orders, purchase orders, outbound and inbound deliveries, shipments in SAP S/4HANA freight units and freight orders in TM in SAP S/4HANA. Fulfillment tracking apps are ready-to-consume standard apps based on the GTT standard model. The standard model allows extensibility to add user-defined tracked processes, field types, event types, code lists, planned event extensions, and event-to- action scripts. If you want to send documents from SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, refer to How to Send Documents from SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace and make sure that you meet the requirements for the product version mentioned in its Prerequisites section. The sample codes for the fulfillment tracking apps are available in the following GTT repository in the SAP Samples organization on GitHub.com: https://github.com/SAP-samples/logistics- business-network-gtt-standardapps-samples . You can find a document explaining how to download and install the sample codes in the repository. On the contrary, If you want to send documents from SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace to other SAP systems, refer to How to Send Documents from SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace to Other Systems. Based on your business needs, you can perform the following configuration tasks to enhance the functionality and the usability of fulfillment tracking apps: Adapting the UI  Note The sample codes are not provided as part of standard delivery, but only as an example to show you how to set up the SAP S/4HANA extractors for use with fulfillment tracking apps. They are not standard codes and you can customize them for your business scenarios. You should determine what documents with certain condition need to be sent to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace for tracking. You don't need to send unnecessary ones. For example, if you only need the sales order, then you don't have to implement the purchase order. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Navigate to Fulfillment Tracking Apps from External Systems Define My Tracking Status. Track Shipments App A standard app : for transportation planners to monitor the real-time execution status of LE-TRA shipments from SAP S/4HANAand freight documents from TM in SAP S/4HANA and report events manually. To know how to synchronize actual events back to TM in SAP S/4HANA in the Fulfillment Tracking apps, see Synchronize Actual Events Back to TM in SAP S/4HANA. For more information on how to use this app, see Guide for Receiving Specialists. Track PO Fulfillment For information on how to use this app, see Guide for Purchasers. Adapting the UI This section describes how to adapt the UI of the fulfillment tracking apps. When you are in the adaptation mode, you have many options to adapt the UI to your liking. You can also adapt and save certain views. The content in this section is an excerpt from Adapting SAP Fiori UIs at Runtime - Key User Adaptation, and adapted for the use in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. It might not be updated timely. You can check out more details and timely updates on this function with the link provided. Prerequisites You have added the roles of fulfillment tracking apps and and two flexible UI configuration roles “UIConfigureTemplate” and “FlexKeyUser”to the role collection in SAP BTP cockpit. For the role templates and application identifiers, see Available Roles for Solution Owners. You have started the UI Adaptation mode. To do that, click Adapt UI in the user actions menu. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 6 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Overview Header Bar Version History If the user interface of the current app has been adapted previously, you can switch to a recent version or to the original app. Just click on the title of the current version to expand the version history, then select a version from the dropdown list to display it. Activate New Version Use  to activate the current draft or a selected version that is not currently active, so it becomes a new version. Discard Draft This option is only available when you display a draft that has not yet been activated. Use  to discard all UI changes that you did in draft mode. You can then start adapting the UI again, based on the last activated version. Publish Version This option is only available when you display an unpublished version. Use  (Publish Version) to publish a version of a changed app to a target subaccount. UI Adaptation and Navigation modes When UI Adaptation is activated, you can edit the current screen on which you started the adaptation mode, but you cannot navigate using a button (for example, to another list item, screen, or dialog box triggered by the button). To interrupt the adaptation mode and reach these "hidden" elements, choose Navigation. Now you can navigate on the UI as usual, for example to reveal other areas. Please note: Any changes you make while you're in the Navigation mode (for example setting a filter) will not be saved later. So make sure you choose UI Adaptation again before you make further changes that you want to preserve. Visualization mode This highlights all or certain supported key user changes that have been made on the UI and are part of the current UI. When you click on a highlighted change, you see details about all changes made to this element, including a timestamp for when the changes were saved. When you're in this mode, you will also see a dropdown list in the header bar that lets you filter for certain change types. By default, you see All Changes. More Actions Use  (More Actions) to display a menu containing additional actions. This menu contains actions for translating UI changes. These actions, as well as the  icon are only visible if you have the AdminFlexKeyUser role. Undo and Redo Use  to undo and  to redo the changes you made during your current session. Feedback Use  (Feedback) to share your feedback on key user adaptation with the development team at SAP. Save Draft Use  (Save Draft) to save your UI changes. The changes are saved as drafts and are not visible to end users until you activate them. Exit When you're done with your UI changes, use  (Exit) to exit the UI adaptation mode and return to your running app. For the specific kinds of changes you can make on the UI, check the subpage of this chapter. Security UI adaptation should not be used as a means to fulfill security requirements. UI changes affect only the visibility of the respective elements on the UI. Example: If you remove a field, it doesn't show up on the UI any longer. However, no other security measures 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- are applied that prevent a user from accessing the data associated with the removed field. If you want to restrict access to certain data for security reasons, this has to be done in the back-end system via roles and authorizations. Making UI Changes When you're in the adaptation mode of a worklist page or detail page, you can edit all UI elements (such as fields, groups of fields, or sections) that get highlighted when you hover over or select them. The optional changes that you can make on the elements appear in the context menu after you select them. You can also move a UI element by dragging and dropping. Check out the following video for an overview of how to make UI changes: Open this video in a new window Moving a UI Element To move a UI element, just drag and drop it. When you drag a UI element, dashed boxes indicate where you can drop it. Drag the element to its new location (indicated by a space) and drop it. You can also cut and paste UI elements: Right-click the UI element and choose Cut from the context menu. The element gets grayed out and a dashed box indicates where you can paste it. Right-click within the dashed box at the position where you want to paste the cut element and choose Paste from the context menu.  Note Different fields, groups or sections may support different kinds of changes depending on the apps’ predefined settings. For example, you can rename one certain field, but for others, you may not be able to rename them. You can also make changes on the elements on the popups and dialogues. After you add a field that is created in the standard model "gttft1" with Adapt UI, deleting it or marking it unreadable in the standard model will lead to errors and improper display of the field. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Removing a UI Element Select a UI element it and press Delete or choose Remove from the context menu. The element is then removed from the UI, it's not permanently deleted from the app. You can add it again at any point within its original container. Exception: When you delete a group of fields, the grouping information (group title and order of fields) gets lost, but the fields are still available and can be added. Adding a UI Element Right-click the UI element container where you want to add an element and choose Add from the context menu (for example, Add: Field). Select the available elements that you want to add and choose OK. To add a new group, choose Create: Group from the context menu. The following example is provided to show you how to add a UI element: Example: Adding the Events Table. Renaming a UI Element You can change editable text of a UI element. If you double-click it and the text (such as the title of a group of fields or a field label) gets highlighted, you can rename it. Just edit the text and press Enter . You can also right-click the element and choose Rename from the context menu. Resetting Changes By clicking  in the header bar, you can discard all the UI changes you made and return to the current activated version where you can make the changes again from the start. Creating a Public View You can create a view on the worklist page or for tables on the detail page, and make it public so that it’s available in users’ view list. To do this, select Public when you create a view and save. Click Save & Exit to exit the UI Adaptation mode and return to the running app where you can see the created view in your view list. Embedding Content Currently, this is not supported in fulfillment tracking apps.  Note A UI element container (for example a group) must contain at least one UI element. This means that the Remove option is disabled for a UI element if it's the only one in the container. Either add another UI element first or delete the entire container. You can't remove a field within filter and the worklist settings with this function. If you want to hide some fields within, you can mark them as Invisible. For more, see Edit Standard Model Fields.  Caution Removing a field does not prevent users from accessing the data associated with the field. The field is merely removed from the UI and no other security measures are applied. If you want to implement security requirements to restrict access to certain data, this has to be done in the back-end system.  Note In the original app version, under the Information tab, you can add standard and core model fields，standard compositions that are not displayed by default. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Example: Adding the Events Table This section gives you step-by-step instructions on how to add a UI element using the example of adding the Events table in the Track Shipments app. So, you can add other elements in the same way, such as user-defined tracking status tag, user-defined group on the header, fields in the Information section, and so on. Before you start, make sure that you have added the ""FlexKeyUser" role to your role collection mentioned in the Prerequisites section of Adapting the UI. Context To add the Events table in the Track Shipments app, do the following: Procedure 1. Launch the TS app. 2. Click one of the shipments to go to the Shipment Details page. 3. Choose Adapt UI from the user actions menu. Now you are in the UI Adaptation mode. 4. Click one of the tabs to show the context menu with available action options. 5. Click the Add icon. 6. Choose Events from the available content in the pop-up and click OK. 7. Activate the new version: a. Click  icon on the top left of the page b. Enter a name for the new version and confirm 8. Click Save & Exit on the top right of the page. Results The Events tab with a table in it is added to the right of the tab you clicked. You can change its position by dragging and dropping. Navigate to Fulfillment Tracking Apps from External Systems SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace supports navigation from external systems to worklist pages and detail pages of fulfillment tracking apps. If you want to navigate to worklist pages, see Navigate to Worklist Pages of Fulfillment Tracking Apps from External Systems. If you want to navigate to detail pages, see Navigate to Detail Pages of Fulfillment Tracking Apps from External Systems. Navigate to Worklist Pages of Fulfillment Tracking Apps from External Systems  Note Generally, the UI element that you want to add must be of the same type with the one you click in this step. If you want to add a user-defined group on the header, you should click one of the existing group there. If you want to add the tracking status tag, click one of the existing tag, such as delay status tag. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 10 This is custom documentation. Data Contributor Apps This chapter provides application help on all the apps used by data contributors as part of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- App Description Manage Locations to manage location master data either manually replicated from another system or created from scratch using the app System Connections to receive and respond to order and event tracking documents directly from your system by implementing the order and event tracking APIs published by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace Manage Invitations to manage all the invitations you receive from the solution owners to connect with their business network Settings App Description Define User Settings to define the default settings in various other apps in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace Retention Management App Description Blocking Store to access restricted data during its blocking period Retention Management to define rules that determine the residence and blocking periods of personal data Business Operations App Description Manage Integration Logs to view all integration logs for solution owner and data contributor transactions User Management Prerequisite To access the User Management app, you must be an administrator user of SAP Business Network for Logistics. If you don’t know who is your company’s administrator user, create an incident with component SBN-LBN-BP-OB and provide your company’s subdomain in the incident. The subdomain can be found in your sign-in URL as follows: https://<subdomain>.lbn.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/sites About the app The User Management app allows an administrator to perform user management tasks including the following: Add or delete users in your company's tenant Add users to user groups  Note This app is available for data contributors only. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 93 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The User Management app consists of the following areas: Filter bar You can filter the users based on one or more of the filter options, such as First Name, Last Name and Email that appear in the header area. Worklists Include an All Users list and other user lists categorized by user groups. Worklist (User Management) There are different ways to work on the users and to set filters. To restrict the number of users displayed, you can use the filter bar in the header and the worklists for different user groups. Filter Bar With the filter bar, you can do the following: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for users. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. Worklists All Users The All Users worklist contains all the users in the current tenant. This worklist displays the following details for each user: First name Last name Email  Note The user groups are pre-defined and you are not able to modify them.  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 94 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- User group(s) The system displays all the user groups to which the user belongs. This worklist contains the option to change user information, including first and last names, and the assigned user groups. You can do so by clicking the  Edit icon in the worklist. You can also add a user by choosing the Add button and delete a user by selecting the user and choosing Delete Delete User . User Lists by User Groups Each worklist displays all the users that belong to a specific user group. These worklists display the same user information as the All Users worklist. The worklists contain the option to change user information, delete a user, and remove a user from the current user group. To edit a user, click the  Edit icon for the user. To delete a user, select the user in the worklist and choose Delete Delete User . To remove a user from the current user group, select the user in the worklist and choose Delete Delete Mapping . For example, by choosing Delete Mapping in the ABC worklist, you remove the user from the ABC user group. Create a User and Assign User Groups Prerequisites You are a tenant administrator, that is, you have already been assigned to the admin user group either by the system or by another administrator in your company. Context As an administrator, you can create users in your company's tenant and assign users to user groups so that they have access to relevant apps. Procedure 1. Launch the User Management app. 2. In the All Users worklist, choose the Add button. A new empty row is added at the top of the list table. 3. In the new row, enter the user names, user email, and select the user group(s) you want to assign to the user. Users assigned to the “…Admin” user group are administrators. They can perform administrative tasks using the following apps: Manage Business Profile Retention Management Blocking Store Define User Settings Manage Notification Settings System Connections Manage Invitations 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 95 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- User Management Manage Integration Logs Users assigned to the “…All_Function” user group can access the following apps: Retention Management Blocking Store Define User Settings Manage Notification Settings Manage Invitations Manage Disputes Freight Orders for Confirmation Freight Orders for Reporting Review Freight Documents Invoice Freight Documents Freight Quotations Freight Requests for Quotation Manage Invoices Self-Book Dock Appointments Manage Freight Execution 4. Choose the Save button. Results The new user is created and added to the specified user groups in your company's tenant. The system will send an activation email to the user for setting the password.  Note When assigning user groups, consider the following security considerations: Grant the user only the authorization that is necessary. Ensure that authorization is removed as soon as it is no longer needed (for example, if an employee leaves the company).  Note If the new user's email domain is different from yours, you'll be prompted to confirm it.  Note If the user already exists in SAP Business Network for Logistics, no activation email will be sent because the user was already activated for the network. Users must sign out and sign in again to see the apps respective to their newly assigned user groups. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 96 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- You need to send the network URL to the newly added users so they can sign in to the network with their own user credentials (after they’ve activated their user accounts). Edit User Information You, as a tenant administrator, can change the information for existing users in your company's tenant. Context The following user information can be changed: First and last names User group assignments Procedure 1. Launch the User Management app. You can view all your users in the current tenant in the All Users worklist. To narrow down the list, use the filter bar, search box, or go to the worklist for a specific user group. 2. To edit a user, in any worklist, click the  Edit icon for the user, make your changes, and choose Save. Results If the user group assignment for an existing user is changed, the system will send an email to the user to notify the change. Users must sign out and sign in again to see the apps respective to their newly assigned user groups. Delete a User Context You, as a tenant administrator, can delete a user from the current tenant. The deleted user can no longer access the apps in your company's tenant. Procedure 1. Launch the User Management app. You can view all the users in the All Users worklist. To narrow down the list, use the filter bar or search box. 2. To delete a user, in any worklist, select the user and choose Delete Delete User . 3. In the confirmation dialog box, click OK.  Note You can't delete your own account.  Note 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 97 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Manage Locations You can use the Manage Locations app to manage location master data either manually replicated from another system or created from scratch using the app. Location master data can then be consumed by other apps in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. You can set up a location replication using the Data Replication Framework (DRF) in the SAP S4/HANA source system. For more information, see Configurations for Location Replication. Location master data consists of not only the address information, but also the business purpose of a location. Additionally, the master data of a location can include one or more alternative IDs so that the location becomes cross-platform identifiable. The main features of this app include: View a location Create a location Upload locations Edit a location Viewing a Location To view a location, proceed as follows: 1. By default, you can use the following fields to filter locations: External ID Source System Object Type Description Country/Region City Data Processing Status If the user also exists in other tenants of SAP Business Network for Logistics, the deletion only removes the user from the current tenant.  Note The Manage Locations app implements all security features and data protection-relevant functions documented in the "Security and Data Protection and Privacy" section of the Administration Guide. A location master data record enters the blocking period if it has not been accessed for three consecutive years. The blocking period lasts for another three years, during which only audit specialists can access the record. The record will then be automatically deleted when the end of the blocking period is reached. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 98 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Additional Information You can also adjust the filter bar by chooosing Adapt Filters. 2. Click the location from the filter results to open the details page. The detail view of the location consists of a header and other sections. Header The Header section displays the address information. General This section displays the basic information of a location. This includes the business purposes, the longitude/latitude coordinates, and the revision history. Geographical Coordinates and Map This section displays the geographical coordinates of the location. It also identifies the location on the map. Alternative Location IDs This section displays a list of type-specific alternative IDs of the location. Contact Information This section displays the contact information related to the location. Additional Information This section displays the contact information related to the location. More Information You can do the following with the filter bar: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for locations. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box.  Note 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 99 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Creating a Location To create a location, proceed as follows: 1. Click Create on the upper-right corner of the Locations table. The Create New Location page opens. 2. On the Create New Location page, enter the following details: Source: Source of the location. Valid values are: SAP SCM Logistic Location: Locations from one of the following systems: SAP Extended Warehouse Management SAP Transportation Management SAP ERP Location: Locations from an SAP ERP system Others: Locations from other systems Location Type: Type of the location This field is available when Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location. Object Type: Business purpose of a location. This field is configurable when Source is set to SAP ERP Location or Others. When Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location, the system automatically sets Object Type to Logistic Location. Valid values for the Object Type field are:: Business Partner Customer Plant Shipping Point Supplier If none of the values above fits the location’s business purpose, you can change Source to SAP SCM Logistic Location as an alternative. This will set Object Type to Logistic Location at the backend and make Location Type configurable. The Location Type field provides you with a broader list of types pertaining to various business purposes, such as port and hub. Description: Descriptive information about the location Source System/External ID: Source system from which the location master data is copied and the corresponding ID. If you are creating a location from scratch, set the Source System part to LBN, and set the External ID part to the location ID you previously prepared. The default Standard view cannot be changed.  Note You can also maintain the information of an ordering party in this app by setting the Object Type field to Business Partner. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 100 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: If you are importing a location from SAP Transportation Management (TM), set the Source System to the business system name of your TM system and set the External ID to the location ID in TM. For locations that have its object type set to “Business Partner”, you can find the business system name of your TM system and the location ID in the SOAP request message sent to LBN. In this request, the MessageHeader.SenderBusinessSystemID attribute specifies the business system name and the internal ID of the sender (the MessageHeader.SenderParty.InternalID attribute) specifies the location ID. Alternatively, you can run transaction code SLDCHECK in TM to view the business system name. Logical System: You can also use the Logical System field to identify the system from which the location master data is replicated. This is a mandatory field if you want to use the location in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. The logical system ID you enter here must be the same one that you used when configuring the replication of location master data via the Data Replication Framework. For more information, see Replicating Locations from SAP S/4HANA via Data Replication Framework (DRF). Make sure you enter the logical system ID correctly so that it matches the source system of the location. Otherwise, there can be duplicate records in your location master data. (Optional) Address: Country/Region State City District Street/House Number Zip Code (Optional) Geographical Coordinates And Map: Longitude: Longitude coordinate of the location Latitude: Latitude coordinate of the location (Optional) Time Zone (Optional) Alternative Location ID: Type: Type of the alternative ID. ID: Alternative ID in the specified type.  Note You can enter the coordinates in the Longitude and Latitude fields manually. If you want the system to verify your entries, set Calibrate coordinates when saving to Yes before you save your changes. You can also choose Generate Longitude and Latitude Coordinates to create the coordinates according to the address information you’ve entered. By default, Calibrate coordinates when saving is set to Apply global settings, meaning that how the system handles coordinates for the location record you are working on is determined by the option you choose in the Generate geo-coordinates automatically setting, which can be found in the Settings dialogue box. If you leave Generate geo-coordinates automatically with the default option, the system generates geo-coordinates for locations when both the latitude and longitude coordinates are missing. For more information, see Global settings for Geo-Coordinates. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 101 This is custom documentation. Use the following fields to filter locations: Location ID Description Location Type Country/Region City 2. Click the location from the filter results to open the details page. 3. Choose Edit on the upper-right corner of the details page. System Connections (Data Contributor) Use the System Connections app for data contributors to complete the implementation of SAP Business Network for Logistics APIs. By implementing the tracking APIs published by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, your organization can receive and respond to tracking requests directly from your system. To complete the API implementations, you – as an administrator – also need to perform the following steps using the System Connections app: Specify the authentication details and base URLs for your system’s endpoints. Assign authentication details and a base URL to each API operation that you’ve implemented. Enable inbound communication to SAP Business Network for Logistics. The app has the following areas: Outbound Connections This area lists the outbound-from-network API services to which you can assign authentication details and a base URL. In addition, you can see the active or inactive status of the operations. Manage Details 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 102 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- This area enables you to manage (create, edit and delete) your base URLs (communication details) and your authentication details (OAuth 2.0 and basic credentials). Connection Settings This area enables you to call LBN endpoints for inbound and outbound connections. For more information about the APIs published by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, go to https://api.sap.com/package/LbnGlobalTrackAndTrace?section=Overview . Specifying the Authentication Details and Base URLs for Your System’s Endpoints Configure communication and authentication details for your system's API or EDI endpoints by specifying base URLs, protocols (HTTPS/SFTP/Email), and authentication methods (Basic, API Key, OAuth 2.0) to enable secure integration with SAP Business Network for Logistics. Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, click Manage Details. 2. In the Communication Details section, click Add and complete the dialog. You can choose between the following options: HTTPS (for API) SFTP (for EDI) Email (for EDI) 3. In the Authentication Details section, click Add and complete the dialog. When creating API communication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name An identifier for the details Base URL The endpoint URL for the communication The API call made to your system uses the HTTPS protocol. When creating EDI communication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name Enter a name to identify the authentication details in this app. Address Enter the host name or IP address of the SFTP server and an optional port, for example, my.host.org:22. You can configure this parameter by entering a dynamic expression such as ${property.property_name} or ${header.header_name}. Message Format You can choose EDIFACT or ANSI X12 from the drop-down list. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 103 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Attribute Description Message Type For EDIFACT, you can choose between the following options: IFTMIN All Inbound Messages For ANSI X12, you can choose between the following options: 204 213 300 303 997 All Inbound Messages Known Host Key Enter a base64-encoded string of your SFTP server. This is used to authenticate your server. SAP Business Network for Logistics can also retrieve the known host key and insert it for you. As a prerequisite, you must have entered the address (including the port) of the SFTP server. Message Version The D96A message version is selected by default corresponding to EDIFACT. The V4010 message version is selected by default corresponding to ANSI X12. No version will be displayed for message type All Inbound Messages. Description The Instructions of Transport description is selected by default corresponding to EDIFACT message type IFTMIN. The Load Tender description is selected by default corresponding to ANSI X12 message type 204. The description will not be shown for message type All Inbound Messages. Directory Enter the relative path to write the file to a directory. Example: parentdirectory/childdirectory File Name Enter the name of the file to be written. The entry is valid only for LBN outbound message types. Additional allowed placeholders: %DOCUMENT_ID% %MESSAGE_TYPE% %TIMESTAMP% %SHIPPER_LBN_ID% %CONTROL_NUMBER% The placeholder %CONTROL_NUMBER% is only available for ANSI X12 997 messages. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 104 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Attribute Description You can combine these placeholders with any fixed strings and in any order (<string 1><placeholder 1><string 2><placeholder 2> <string 3>). Examples: LBN_%MESSAGE_TYPE%_%DOCUMENT_ID%_%TIMESTAMP%.edi %TIMESTAMP%_%SHIPPER_LBN_ID%.edi When creating Basic authentication details, the provided user name and password are used for authentication during the API call to your system. When creating API Key authentication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name An identifier for the details API Key Attribute Enter the key for the request header. API Key Value Enter the token to be used for authentication. The API key represents the name of the token that a client provides when making API calls. The token is sent as request header. When creating OAuth 2.0 authentication details, you need to enter the following information: Attribute Description Name Enter a name to identify the authentication details in this app. Grant Type Valid values are: Client Credentials (default) and Client Certificate. Authentication URL Enter the URL of the OAuth 2.0 authorization server that issues the access token. Client ID Enter the ID of the client that you’re connecting to. Client Secret Secret key of the client that you’re connecting to. OAuth 2.0 uses a multiple-step authentication pattern: Client credentials (Client ID and Client Secret) are used by the client application to initially request an access token. The access token is then used to authorize the client (for as long as the token is valid) to access the server’s resources (for example, the resources that are used in the associated integration flow). In many OAuth 2.0 scenarios, the access token is issued (or generated) by an authorization server. Client Authentication Select Send as Body Parameter or Send as Request Header. This enables access to your system. If you select Send as Body Parameter, the Client ID and Client Secret are sent in the request body to the authentication server. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 105 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Attribute Description If you select Send as Request Header, the Client ID and Client Secret are sent as a part of the authorization header to the authentication server. Valid values are: client credentials and client certificate. Client Certificate When you select Send as Body Parameter, the Client ID goes in the request body to the authentication server. If you choose Send as Request Header, the Client ID becomes part of the authorization header sent to the authentication server. Specify the path of the client certificate (key pair file) in the Key Pair File field. Enter its password in the Password field. Include Scope Select the checkbox to provide the OAuth 2.0 scope information that will be included in the request body. Scope Enter the scope that you defined for the endpoint. Content Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded is selected by default. Assigning Authentication Details and a Base URL to a Service Prerequisites You have specified the communication details (base URL) and authentication details (basic or OAuth 2.0 credentials, or API key). To test the service, select it in the table and choose one of the two methods from the Test Service drop down. With Default Payload An internal shipper tenant is used to trigger the payload. The payload content is static with the intention of testing the connection from SAP Business Network for Logistics to your carrier system. With Custom Payload An internal shipper tenant is used to trigger the payload. You can modify the payload content to the extent of changing the order details with the intention of testing various scenarios. However, the order ID and the shipper LBN ID will always be fixed by SAP Business Network for Logistics. The test service will not work with any other shipper tenant. You will find a sample payload shippers would send from their system here . The service test is only available for test tenant types for the following operations: Post freight request for quotation Post freight request for quotation cancellation Post freight quotation notification Post freight order for subcontracting 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 109 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Post freight order for subcontracting cancellation Post freight booking request Freight booking shipping instruction Delete order for tracking Post freight booking request cancellation Put order for tracking Put freight order for subcontracting Post freight order for subcontracting Post freight document generic request Put location data Delete location data Automating EDI Pulling This feature allows you to schedule automated EDI pulling operations for ANSI and EDIFACT inbound messages. You can run the pulling job during a specific time period each day or on specific days of the week. Prerequisites Ensure you set the Service Name to EDI Inbound All and the Operation Name to Pull EDI in the Create Service dialog when using the System Connections app to create a connection service. Procedure 1. Specify the recurrence type of the EDI pulling service by using the Recurrence toggle. Daily (default): The service runs every day. Weekly/On Days: The service runs on selected days of the week. 2. Set the time period during which the service runs based on the selected recurrence type by specifying the Recur Start Time and Recur End Time. 3. Choose the interval for the service from the Interval drop-down list. 4. Choose your time zone from the Timezone drop-down list. This setting applies to the time period you set in step two.
