file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: To enable inbound connections for Multi-Cloud, proceed as follows: Procedure 1. In the System Connections app, on the Configuration Settings view, activate the Enable Inbound Connections toggle. For new users, the toggle is disabled by default. 2. Select the integration platform. You can choose between Multi-Cloud and Neo (deprecated). Neo is selected by default. 3. (For Multi-Cloud only) Select the Provider APIs to which you want to have access, and save. You can update the Provider API selection later. 4. View the service credentials (client ID, client secret, authentication URL, and host URL). You can copy them and enter them when you create the OAuth 2.0 authentication details. For more information, see: Specifying the Authentication Details and Base URLs for Your System’s Endpoints. For more information, refer to the instructions in the provider API specification of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, under https://api.sap.com/package/LbnGlobalTrackAndTrace?section=Overview . To enable inbound connections for Neo, proceed as in step 1. By default, inbound communication is authenticated with OAuth 2.0. To acquire the OAuth 2.0 credentials for Neo (deprecated), create an incident with component SBN-LBN-INT. Manage Alternate IDs (Data Contributor) You can maintain alternate identifiers of your other accounts in the network. These identifiers shall be used in specific integration scenarios or in specific transaction flows in the network. Additionally, the LBN ID of your tenant can be seen above the Alternate IDs table as a read-only field. SAP Business Network for Logistics supports the following alternate identifiers (alternate IDs): DUNS ID (Data Universal Numbering System ID) SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) Registration Number USDOT (US Department of Transportation) MC Number (Motor Carrier Number) Others GLN (Global Location Number) Technical User To create your own alternate IDs, proceed as follows: 1. Choose Manage Alternate IDs. 2. Select an alternate ID type from the dropdown menu and type in the required value. 3. Choose OK. You can also delete or change existing entries. Define User Settings 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 111 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- The Define User Settings app allows you to define defaults that best suit the way you work. The settings that you make in the app serve as the default settings in various other apps for .SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace Distance In this section, you can define the default unit of measurement for distance. The system uses this setting in other apps in your area. Notification Subscriptions In this section, you can subscribe to notifications for various scenarios and specify the email address and preferred language for receiving the notifications. Note that you cannot subscribe to a scenario without maintaining an email address. When you subscribe to notifications for a scenario, the system can send email notifications based on the settings you make in the Manage Notification Settings app. For more information on managing notification settings, see Manage Notification Settings. Manage Invitations The Manage Invitations app allows you to manage all the invitations you receive from potential business partners to connect with their business network. The app consists of the following areas: Filter bar You can filter the invitations based on one or more of the filter options, such as inviter's company name, email, city, country/region, that appear in the header area. Worklists by status The invitations are categorized based on the invitation statuses: New, Accepted, and Rejected. Worklist (Manage Invitations) There are different ways to work on the invitations and to set filters. To restrict the number of invitations displayed, you can use the filter bar in the header and the preconfigured worklists (New, Accepted, Rejected) based on the status of the invitation. Filter Bar With the filter bar, you can do the following: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for invitations. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later.  Note This app is available for data contributors only. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 112 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. Worklists New The New worklist displays all invitations that you have not yet responded to. This worklist displays the following details for each invitation: Invitation Number Inviter Inviter LBN Network ID Invitation From Phone number Email City Country/Region Address Accept and reject options Accepted The Accepted worklist displays all the invitations that you have accepted. This worklist displays the following details for each invitation: Invitation Number Inviter Inviter LBN Network ID Invitation From Phone number Email City Country/Region Address  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 113 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Administration information such as Accepted On and Accepted By Rejected The Rejected worklist displays all the invitations that you have rejected. This worklist displays the following details for each invitation: Invitation Number Inviter Inviter LBN Network ID Invitation From Phone number Email City Country/Region Address Administration information such as Rejected On and Rejected By Viewing an Invitation Context To view an invitation, perform the following: Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Invitations app. 2. You can view all the new invitations in the New worklist. (Optional) You can retrieve a specific invitation or a set of invitations using the various search filter options such as the inviter's company name, email, city, country/region, that appear on the header area. The system also categorizes the invitations based on various attributes and displays them in the following tabs: New: Displays all new invitations from potential business partners. Accepted: Displays invitations that you have accepted. Rejected: Displays invitations that you have rejected. Accepting or Rejecting an Invitation  Note Using the  Settings icon on each worklist, you can control the number of columns displayed in the New, Accepted, and Rejected worklists. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 114 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Context You can accept or reject the invitations from potential business partners to connect with their business network. When rejecting, you can indicate a rejection reason to the inviter. If you accept an invitation, you can connect with the inviter's business network and the system notifies the inviter of the same. If you reject an invitation, you cannot connect with the inviter's business network and the system notifies the inviter of the same. To accept or reject an invitation, perform the following: Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Invitations app. You can view all the new invitations in the New worklist. You can directly accept or reject the invitations in this worklist. 2. Alternatively, you can search for and retrieve a specific invitation using search filter options in the header. Once you retrieve the invitation, you can respond to the invitation by choosing the Accept or Reject button. Results Once you accept or reject an invitation, you can view the details of the invitation in the Accepted or Rejected worklist as appropriate. You cannot view this invitation anymore in the New worklist. Settings on Invitations You can specify the visibility of your company profile and how you process connection requests in the app. To do this, click Settings on Invitations on the upper-right concern then specify the followings: Automatically accept connection requests (invitations) Determines whether you want the app to automatically accept connection requests from potential business patterns. Default value: No Manage Notification Settings You can use this app to schedule reminder notifications for some of the business processes for which you may need an alert. The system sends you notifications via emails. The Manage Notification Settings app consists of the following areas: List of scenarios This area displays the scenarios for which you can configure alerts. Filter You can use this filter to filter the scenarios. When you select a scenario from this drop-down menu, the system displays only that specific scenario. Configuration details The system displays the following in this area: 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 115 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Configurations The system displays notification types and the settings that you can configure for each type. On-event notification refers to the email notification that you receive at the time when a target event happens, for example, when you receive an invitation from a shipper. Post-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive after the target event happens, for example, after you have received the invitation. Subscribers The system displays the list of users who have subscribed to notifications for the current scenario. The subscription is made in the Define User Settings app. Scenarios As a data contributor, you can schedule email notifications for the following scenario: Scenario Group Scenario For receiving email notifications when, before or after ... Business Operations Integration Error V2 The system now sends an email notification to you when an integration error occurs. Related Information Define User Settings Configure Notification Settings Prerequisites To enable reminder notifications, make sure you also maintain an email address and subscribe to the notification(s) you need in the Define User Settings app. For more information, see Define User Settings Context You can configure the following types of notifications in the Manage Notification Settings app, where applicable. On-Event Notification On-event notification refers to the email notification that you receive at the time when a target event happens, for example, when you receive an invitation from a shipper. You can activate or deactivate on-event notification by setting the activation toggle to Yes or No, respectively. Pre-Event Notifications  Note To enable email notifications for the above scenarios, you need to activate the settings in this app and subscribe to notifications for the scenarios in the Define User Settings app. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 116 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Pre-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive before the target event happens, for example, before dock appointment booking cut-off. You can schedule pre-event notifications by adding notification periods and specifying notification frequency within each period, as described below: Notification period: The period within which email notifications will be sent in a specified frequency. You only specify the start of the period, for example, 30 days before the event, which means the notification period starts from 30 days before the event till the start of the next period or the event time. Frequency: The frequency to receive notifications within the specified period. For example, setting the frequency to every 5 days means within the specified period, you'll receive an email notification every 5 days. Post-Event Notifications Post-event notifications refer to the notifications you receive after the target event happens, for example, after you have received the invitation. You can schedule post-event notifications by adding notification periods and specifying notification frequency within each period, as described below: Notification period: The period within which email notifications will be sent in a specified frequency.  Example The schedule shown below Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 60 days Every 10 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days Yes 15 days Every 3 days Yes specifies the following schedule: Within the period from 60 days before the event to 30 days before the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Within the period from 30 days before the event to 15 days before the event, receive a notification every 5 days. Within the period from 15 days before the event till the event time, receive a notification every 3 days. In the same example, if you deactivate the "30 days" period, as shown below: Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 60 days Every 10 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days No 15 days Every 3 days Yes Then the "30 days" period is ignored and the schedule changes to: Within the period from 60 days before the event to 15 days before the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Within the period from 15 days before the event till the event time, receive a notification every 3 days. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 117 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- You only specify the end of the period, for example, 30 days after the event, which means the notification period starts from the end of the previous period or the event time, to 30 days after the event. Frequency: The frequency to receive notifications within the specified period. For example, setting the frequency to every 5 days means within the specified period, you'll receive an email notification every 5 days. Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Notification Settings app. 2. In the scenario list, select the scenario for which you want to set notifications. 3. To activate on-event notification, for On-Event Notification, set the toggle to Yes. To deactivate, set it to No. 4. To configure pre-event or post-event notifications, do the following: a. Expand the Pre-Event Notifications or Post-Event Notifications area. b. To add a notification period, choose the Add button. Then in the Add Notification Period dialog box, specify the start (pre-event) or end (post-event) of the period and the frequency, and choose Save. You can add multiple periods according to your needs.  Example The schedule shown below Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 15 days Every 3 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days Yes 60 days Every 10 days Yes specifies the following schedule: Within the period from the event time to 15 days after the event, receive a notification every 3 days. Within the period from 15 days after the event to 30 days after the event, receive a notification every 5 days. Within the period from 30 days after the event to 60 days after the event, receive a notification every 10 days. Note that for the invitations scenario, the notifications stop as soon as the invitation is accepted or rejected. In the same example, if you deactivate the "30 days" period, as shown below: Notification Period Frequency Activated for User 15 days Every 3 days Yes 30 days Every 5 days No 60 days Every 10 days Yes Then the "30 days" period is ignored and the schedule changes to: Within the period from the event time to 15 days after the event, receive a notification every 3 days. Within the period from 15 days after the event to 60 days after the event, receive a notification every 10 days. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 118 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- c. To edit or delete a notification period, choose the Edit or Delete button. To deactivate a period, set Activated for User to No. Manage Freight Execution The Manage Freight Execution app enables you to view the execution of the freight documents by tracking planned and unplanned events that occurred during freight execution. You can also report various planned and unplanned events. Also, you can perform the following in this new app: Planned milestone events You can view the milestones planned by the ordering party Planned and unplanned events You can report various planned and unplanned events. Estimate You can report an estimate for any planned event. Delay You can report delays at both the document-level and at an event-level. Proof of pick-up and delivery You can submit proof of pick-up and proof of delivery with attachments. Additional events You can report additional events for the supported event types at any stop. Event history You can view all the events reported by you and all other business partners. You can also view the event history for a specific planned event. Attachments You can view all the attachments specific to the freight execution in the Attachments tab. This app contains the track relevant freight documents irrespective of whether the documents are relevant for confirmation or not. This app also contains documents that are ready for tracking from the SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. In this app, you can view the events that you reported manually and the events reported by other business partners. The manually reported data and the events reported by the APIs are synchronized to the SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) or SAP S/4 HANA system. Note that you can report events for a freight order even when you have not reconfirmed a freight order that has been updated by the ordering party. This app consists of a main view and a detailed view. When you open the app, the main view is displayed. It consists of two screen areas: Filter bar 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 119 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Using the filter bar in the header, you can filter the freight documents by one of the following criteria to restrict the number of freight documents displayed: Freight Document Freight Document Type Departure Location Arrival Location Departure Date Arrival Date Created On Reference Documents Mode of Transport Category of transportation, for example, road, ocean, air, and so on. Reporting Status Displays the reporting status based on the documents that are ready for reporting. For more information on current status, see Freight Execution Statuses. Execution Status Displays whether the freight is Ready for Execution or In Transit. For more information, see Freight Execution Statuses. Current Status Displays the current status of execution based on the latest planned event reported. You can view whether the execution is as planned, early, on time, or late. For more information on current status, see Freight Execution Statuses. Estimated Status Displays the estimated status of execution based on the latest estimate received for a planned event. You can view whether the execution is as running early, running on time, or running late. Note that this is relevant before the planned event has been reported. For more information on estimated status, see Freight Execution Statuses. Arrival Country The last arrival location of a freight document. Carrier Container Dangerous Goods Departure Country IMO Number The International Maritime Organization (IMO) number is a unique identifier assigned to propelled, seagoing vessels of 100 gross tons and above. It consists of the three letters "IMO" followed by unique seven-digit numbers. License Plate Number Proof of Delivery Status 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 120 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

Worklists You can use the following worklists: All, Ready for Execution, Execution In Progress and Executed. From the main view, you can navigate to the detailed view of a freight document. Worklist (Manage Freight Execution) To restrict the number of freight documents displayed, you can use the preconfigured worklists (All, Ready for Execution, Execution In Progress, and Executed). Common Apps This chapter provides application help on the apps used by both solution owners and data contributors as part of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Manage Business Profile Whether you are a shipper, solution owner, or logistics provider, you will land on the company profile page in SAP Business Network when opening the Manage Business Profile app. On this page, you can manage and adjust your company information as per your needs. This enables potential partners and relevant stakeholders to know more about your company’s service coverage, capabilities, and strength. You can maintain the basic information about your company. This includes but is not limited to the type of organization, year founded, and annual revenue to help shippers and solution owners evaluate you as a potential logistics provider. The Product and Service Categories, Ship-to or Service Locations, and Industries sections of your company profile allow you to provide detailed information about the products or services you offer, the locations you ship to or provide services, and the industries you serve. This information is critical because shippers and solution owners usually discover your company based on the product and service categories and ship-to or service locations. The Additional Addresses section provides you with an effective and intuitive way to add and manage addresses beyond the primary business address, such as branch offices, regional offices, warehouses, or other physical sites associated with your company. Including these addresses provides a comprehensive overview of your company's geographical reach and operational scope. The Contacts section enables you to create multiple individual contacts and assign them one or multiple roles, such as Sales Representative, Marketing Manager, and Technical Contact, designating them as companywide contacts. This guarantees that their contact details are readily available to all current and potential trading partners on the network. Managing Contact Information Companywide Contact Companywide contacts have their contact information accessible to both current and potential business partners on the network. Assign individuals in your company as companywide contacts. This ensures that your business partners know the right people to contact for various issues or questions. To do this, follow these steps: 1. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane of the Company Profile page. 2. Manage Integration Logs The Manage Integration Logs app allows you to monitor the inbound and outbound messages that are processed from SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can view the integration logs using this app. For solution owners, to navigate to this app, you need to launch the View Logs app first on the SAP Fiori launchpad. Then click Manage Integration Logs in the Quick Links section. This can be integration logs between SAP Business Network for Logistics and SAP S/4HANA or any other backend SAP system (such as SAP Transportation Management) or any API or EDI system of carriers, network partners, network participants, or similar. Since SAP Business Network for Logistics follows a single integration system design for all customers and other partners, the Manage Integration Logs app aims to provide a visibility into integration logs for a particular customer or partner. Only the technical parties involved in an integration log can view the same in the app, ensuring data separation across all customers. The app also provides access to customer-facing payloads and enables the reprocessing of failed integration logs. The app provides standard SAP Business Network for Logistics integration logs only. For instructions on how to use the app, open the in-app help by selecting . Shippers and solution owners can use the following features: You can search based on document ID and date/time. The following statuses are available: Completed: The system assigns this status to a message when SAP Business Network for Logistics was able to process the document successfully. Failed: The system assigns this status to a message when there is a validation error that occurred during the first step of processing of the message. This can happen if there is a payload issue, missing mandatory fields, or a missing configuration. Retry: Depending on the nature of the error and the settings in the consuming application, an integration log can go to retry mode. In such cases, the log retries for a couple of times ranging from a couple of minutes to 30 minutes, after which the status goes into a final status – Completed or Escalated. Escalated: The system assigns this status to a message when the processing failed in backend of an app, or in an external API, or in the customer’s backend SAP system. This usually denotes a connectivity failure at any of the above mentioned places. Reasons could be that a service is not available for a long period, or that there is an authentication issue, or some basic connectivity failure due to misconfigurations, or technical failures in a backend system. You can find a more detailed error information when you click the icon in the Log Details column. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 137 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- The Error column displays the error code and description that the affected app sends when a call to SAP Business Network for Logistics fails. The description provides you with a more concrete context of the issue. You can sort or filter by error code to identify the logs with common failures, and take corrective actions (such as reprocessing the messages, fixing the root cause of the issue, informing SAP support about the error). Reprocessing: The system assigns this status to a message while it's being reprocessed. After you solve the configuration or connectivity issue in SAP Business Network for Logistics and select the Reprocess button, the system moves the message to this status. While a message has this status, you should just wait for it to complete reprocessing. The overall status is derived from the latest status of an individual log associated with the scenario. Flow Direction Systems involved in message flow The Manage Integration Logs app allows you to monitor the inbound and outbound messages that are being sent between the different systems involved. The following flow directions are available: SAP S/4HANA to Network Network to SAP S/4HANA Network to External System External System to Network Network to Network Error Codes The Manage Integration Logs app categorizes and displays error codes for communication failures between different systems. The Manage Integration LogsSAP Business Network for Logistics app displays error codes when the communication between the different systems involved (SAP Business Network for Logistics, SAP S/4HANA or any other backend SAP system, such as SAP Transportation Management, or any API or EDI system) fails. The Manage Integration Logs app can categorize integration log errors based on the error response captured. When an error occurs in a backend SAP Business Network for Logistics app, this app provides an error code in the response, which can then be shown in the Manage Integration Logs app under Error along with their translated descriptions. SAP Business Network for Logistics tries to capture the HTTP response codes while communicating to an external system, and for internal systems where it doesn’t find a category code. We categorize the error messages as far as possible. You can sort or filter by error code to identify the logs with common failures, and take corrective actions (such as reprocessing the messages, fixing the root cause of the issue, informing SAP support about the error).  Note SAP S/4HANA can be either SAP S/4HANA (on-premise) or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition. Both two systems have the Transportation Management (TM) component embedded, which can work with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Network refers to a product or solution within the SAP Business Network family. External System refers to a non-SAP system. Contact your visibility provider or carrier. 5002 Request body format error 5003 Time zone format incorrect Reprocessing Integration Messages When integration messages fail to reach the target system, this is reported in a message log. Depending on the kind of error, it can help to reprocess an integration message. However, not all integration messages can be reprocessed. You can manually reprocess integration messages with the status Failed or Escalated. To do so, proceed as follows: 1. Select a message, or multiple messages, in the table. 2. Choose Reprocess. When an escalated/failed message is reprocessed, newer logs are created in the internal integration system. When you try to reprocess an already reprocessed message, the Manage Integration Logs app refers to the latest logs in the internal integration system. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 148 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- The reprocessing of a message is limited to 29 days. After 30 days, you won’t be able to reprocess the message or download the payload. Log details are available to be viewed for 90 days. For reprocessing purposes, there are two columns available: Reprocessed: Indicates whether an integration message has already been reprocessed or not. Reprocessable: Indicates whether a message log can be reprocessed or not. Not all messages with status Failed or Escalated are eligible for reprocessing. This is usually determined by a uniqueness check of a combination of several fields such as Sender, Document ID, Document Type, and Source System. In certain cases, the check is also extended to additional information, such as Event Type or Reported Time. An integration message with status Failed or Escalated is the latest one in chronological order when grouped together with Sender, Document ID, Document Type, and Source System. Example: A subcontracting request (TransportationOrderRequest) is sent from the transportation management (TM) system of a shipper to SAP Business Network for Logistics and fails. The same document is updated in the TM system and sent again. In such cases, SAP Business Network for Logistics would allow the reprocessing of the latest message only. The older integration messages will have the Reprocessable value set to No. The same applies when the latest integration message from the TM system has the status Completed. Older messages with status Failed or Escalated are not eligible for reprocessing. Hence, the Reprocessable value is set to No. In certain cases, such as an event notification in a tracking scenario, the event type and the reported time are also considered. Example: If multiple events reported by a carrier or a carrier system fail in SAP Business Network for Logistics, all of these are relevant for reprocessing. In the uniqueness check, event type and reported time information is considered too. Thus, for the same freight order ID, shipper, document type (TransportationEventBulkNotification), and source system, it’s possible to reprocess escalated logs for DepartureEvent, ArrivalEvent, etc. And for all these event logs, the Reprocessable value is set to Yes. Automatic Reprocessing of Integration Messages In addition to the conditions mentioned above, integration messages must meet the following prerequisites to be auto- reprocessed: The messages are reprocessable. The messages have not been reprocessed earlier (either manually or automatically). Either the sender or the receiver of the message has a tenant of type Default (productive tenant). Auto-reprocessing is not supported for test tenants. The messages failed with an error code that is eligible for auto-reprocessing. Automatic reprocessing is supported for the following error codes: Error Codes Eligible for Auto-Reprocessing Error Code Description 102 Missing necessary connectivity configurations at customer side 107 Missing necessary tenant configurations 108 Missing necessary connectivity configurations 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 149 This is custom documentation. Retention Management SAP Business Network for Logistics restricts the access of personal data on completion of its business purpose. That is, not all the user groups can access the personal data after the expiration of originally defined residence period. The Retention Management app enables you to define rules for residence and blocking of personal data for apps that belong to a specific application group. These rules restrict the usage of documents containing personal data. In the Retention Management app, you define the residence period and the blocking period. The residence period and blocking period are together called as the retention period. Business Activity The relevant data is used in ongoing business, such as contract creation, delivery or payment. End of Business Defines the end of active business and the start of residence time and retention period.  Note You should familiarize yourself with the following important definitions before using the Retention Management app. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 150 This is custom documentation. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: In SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, it is updated by the “lastChangeDateTime” value in the tracked process and “creationDateTime” in the event. Residence Period The period between the end of business and the end of purpose for a data set during which the data remains in the database and can be used in case of subsequent processes related to the original purpose. At the end of the residence period, the data is blocked. For the settings of residence period in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, refer to Defining Residence and Blocking Periods. End of Purpose The point in time when the processing of a set of personal data is no longer required for the primary business purpose, for example, when a contract is fulfilled. After the EoP has been reached, the data is blocked and can only be accessed by users with special authorizations (for example, tax auditors). In SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, the value of end of purpose is calculated by the blocking store background job: End of Purpose = End of Business + Residence Period When the residence period is finished, the tracked process and event lifecycle reach end of purpose. Blocking Period The period between the residence period and the deletion of the data. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a Data Protection Officer (DPO), can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the data is deleted. For the settings of blocking period in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, refer to Defining Residence and Blocking Periods. Retention Period The period between the end of the last business activity involving a specific object and the deletion of the corresponding data, subject to applicable laws. Retention Period = Residence Period + Blocking Period Deletion The data is deleted and no longer exists in the database. In SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, the value of date of deletion is calculated by the blocking store background job: Date of Deletion = End of Business + Residence Period + Blocking Period Notes Blocking store background job operates automatically once a day at 12 a.m. UTC. So any changes of the life cycle status of tracked processes and events take effect after 12 a.m. UTC each day. End of Business is updated if an event is reported to a tracked process. The end of business dates of this tracked process and its correlated tracked processes are also updated and consistent with the end of business date of the latest reported event. The life cycle status of tracked process is not updated if you directly change the “lifeCycleStatus_code” value of this tracked process. It is only updated by the blocking store background job. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 151 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 3 -- When considering compliance with data protection regulations, it is also necessary to consider compliance with industry- specific legislation in different countries/regions. A typical potential scenario in certain countries/regions is that personal data shall be deleted after the specified, explicit, and legitimate purpose for the processing of personal data has ended, but only as long as no other retention periods are defined in legislation, for example, retention periods for financial documents. Legal requirements in certain scenarios or countries/regions also often require blocking of data in cases where the specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes for the processing of this data have ended, however, the data still has to be retained in the database due to other legally mandated retention periods. In some scenarios, personal data also includes referenced data. Therefore, the challenge for deletion and blocking is first to handle referenced data and finally other data, such as business partner data. Defining Residence and Blocking Periods Context To define the residence period and blocking period of various applications, do the following: Procedure 1. Login to the SAP Fiori Launchpad and choose the Retention Management tile. 2. Select an application type. 3. Enter a residence period. Note that if you do not specify a residence period, the system by default assigns a residence period of 12 months for the application type. 4. Enter a blocking period. Note that if you do not specify a blocking period, the system by default assigns a blocking period of 12 months for the application type. 5. Choose Save. Results The system stores the entered residence and blocking periods for the specific application type. Blocking Store Once the residence period ends, the data moves to the blocking period. In the blocking period, only users with appropriate authorization, such as a data protection officer, can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the system deletes the data. The data protection officer can log into the SAP Fiori Launchpad and choose the Blocking Store app to access all the documents that are in the blocking period. To view a document, the user can download the document in a text file format by choosing the Download button. Identifier: Displays the unique identifier for the document. Status: Displays the status of the document, for example, in blocking period. End of business: Displays the date when the document reached the end of business state. App name: Displays the name of the tracked process type / event type with which the data is associated.  Note If you have any questions, log your incident in SAP Support Launchpad with component “SBN-LBN-BP-OB”. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 152 This is custom documentation. To turn on the in-app help, on the top right on the screen, click the  icon. In the navigation URLs, the filtering settings should be defined as the URL parameters,and the filtered results would be automatically displayed as you navigate to these pages. Typically, the pattern of this navigation URL is: <URL to the worklist page of the app>?<key>=<value> If you want to specify multiple filters or multiple values for one filter, the navigation URL patterns are as follows: For multiple filters: <URL to the worklist page of the app>?<key_1>=<value_1>&<key_2>=<value_2> For one filter with multiple values: <URL to the worklist page of the app>?<key_1>=<value_1>& <key_1>=<value_2> For detailed instructions on how to define the URL parameters for the navigation, see Define the URL Parameters for Filtering the Worklists of Fulfillment Tracking Apps. You can also find some URL Parameters examples in List of URL Parameters Examples. Define the URL Parameters for Filtering the Worklists of Fulfillment Tracking Apps Context To define the URL parameters for filtering the worklists of fulfillment tracking apps, do the following: Procedure 1. Decide on a filter to be defined in the navigation URL. 2. Define the key of the parameter. It is the field name of the filter. Generally, each filter in the apps corresponds to one user model field, standard model field or core model field in the standard model “gttft1”. To find the field name, do the following: Go to the standard model in the Manage Models app. Click the target tracked process or field type and find the corresponding field in the User Model Fields, Standard Model Fields or Core Model Fields sections. Use the field name, not the description. The type of the field may influence the name of the key. For details, see List of URL Parameters Examples. 3. Define the value of the parameter. It consists of the operator and the field value, for example, “>2021”. The type of the field supports different operators. For details, see List of URL Parameters Examples. List of URL Parameters Examples The examples of the URL parameters are sorted according to the types of the fields and listed as follows: UUID For this type, the key is the field name. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- GoodsReceipt Delivered Return ManifestReady ReceivedFromShipper ConsigneeNotified Stage-Level Observation Between Tracked Processes Introduction When a tracked process observes another tracked process at stage level, the event correlation follows the following rules: For actual events that can match a planed event in the observing tracked process, they can be correlated to the observing tracked process from the observed tracked process. For actual events that cannot match a planned event in the observing tracked process, only those of the observed stages can be correlated to the observing tracked process from the observed tracked process. In such case, the correlation starts after the first planned event is reported for the observed tracked process, and the actual event must: be correlated to the observing tracked process. match a planned event of the observing tracked process. The correlation stops once the Arrival event on the last stop of the observed stages is reported for the observed tracked process. In the fulfillment tracking apps, those correlated events from the observed tracked process can be displayed in the timeline or events table of the observing tracked process. The stage-level observation applies to the following observation scenarios: FreightUnit observes Shipment FreightUnit observes TrackingUnit Shipment observes TrackingUnit OutboundDelivery observes Shipment InboundDelivery observes Shipment 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 23 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Here is an example that helps you better understand the event correlation for the stage-level observation: In this example, tracked process A is assumed to observe tracked process B. For tracked process A, there are two stops, each has a planned event. For tracked process B, there are three stops. There are two planned events (planned Arrival and Departure events) on stop 2. The observed stage is from stop 1 to stop 2. Case 1 The Departure event is reported on stop 1 of tracked process B. This Departure event can be correlated to tracked process A because the Departure event of tracked process B can match a planned event in tracked process A. Case 2 After departure, an unplanned Location Update event is reported on stop 1 of tracked process B. This unplanned Location update can be correlated from tracked process B to tracked process A, because: This Departure event matches the Departure event on stop 1 of tracked process A. The Departure event has already reported and correlated to tracked process A. Case 3 The Arrival event on stop 2 of tracked process B is reported. This Arrival event can be correlated from tracked process B to tracked process A. Meanwhile, tracked process A stops getting actual events that cannot match its planned events from tracked process B because its Arrival event on the last stop of the observed stage has been reported. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 24 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Case 4 The Departure event on stop 2 of tracked process B is reported. This Departure event cannot be correlated from tracked process B to tracked process A because this Departure event cannot match a planned event of tracked process A, and this actual event is not on the observed stage. As a result, All actual events on the observed stage (from stop 1- stop 2) can be correlated from tracked process B to tracked process A. All actual events from stop 2 to stop 3 cannot be correlated from tracked process B to tracked process A. Deactivating Stage-Level Observation By default, the stage-level observation is activated. You can use the flag “gttft1_StageLevelObserveSwitchOn” in the event-to-action script to deactivate it. As a result, the observing tracked process receives all actual events correlated from the observed tracked process. To deactivate the stage-level observation, do the following: 1. Go to the standard model “gttft1” of the Manage Models app. 2. In the User Script before Standard Script section of the Event to Action tab, set the value of “gttft1_StageLevelObserveSwitchOn” to “false”. By default, the value is set to “true”. Delay Status Shows if a tracked process or an event is delayed or not. A tracked process is shown as Delayed when one of its planned events is delayed. Event Status Event status is determined by comparing the planned business timestamp with that of the actual. Event Status Description As Planned The initial status for the planned event. Delayed At least one "Delay" event or an event that inherits "GTTDelayedEvent" is reported with reference to the unreported planned event, without the "on-time" event to restore its status. Reported Early The planned event has been reported and the actual business time is earlier than the earliest planned business time. Reported On Time The planned event has been reported and the actual business time is between the earlier and latest planned business time. Reported Late The planned event has been reported and the actual business time is later than the latest planned business time. Reported An unplanned event has been reported. Overdue The planned event is not reported but the current timestamp exceeds the latest planned technical timestamp. Process Status The actual status of the tracked process, decided by the status of the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned”. See the following table for status description. Process Status Description As Planned The initial status of a tracked process, also the status when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” has been reported. Delayed A tracked process is "Delayed" when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is expected to be late. Early A tracked process is "Early" when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” has been reported and its actual business time is earlier than the earliest planned business time. Late A tracked process is "Late" when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” has been reported and the actual business time is later than the latest planned business time. Overdue A tracked process is "Overdue" when the last planned event whose status is not “As Planned” is overdue. It indicates that the current timestamp exceeds the latest planned technical timestamp, but the last planned event hasn't been reported. Estimated Status Description Running Early The estimated time is earlier than the earliest planned business time. Running Late The estimated time is later than the latest planned business time. Running On Time The estimated time is between the earliest and the latest planned business time. Invite Business Partners The Invite Business Partners app is designed for managing all the business partners that you want to be part of your network. You can use this app to select and invite business partners to join your business network and check their participation status. If you have access, you can navigate to the Discover Business Partners app to find more potential business partners. You may have business with many partners in your system and you may want to persist your business with them in SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can download the Excel template available in the app and fill the details of the business partners using this template. You can then upload the template back in the app. If you are using SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system, you can download these business partners from SAP TM system and upload them in Invite Business Partners. For more information, see Downloading Carrier Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). You can select one or more of these business partners from your system and invite them to join your network. When you submit these partners, a back-end team manages your connection invitation. For more information, see Connection Invitations. When a business partner accepts an invitation to connect with your network, the system updates the unique LBN ID of the partner. If you are using SAP TM system, you can update these LBN IDs of partners in SAP TM system by downloading the partner list from the Discover Business Partners app and uploading the list in your SAP TM system. For more information, see Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). The Discover Business Partners app consists of the following areas: Filter bar You can filter the business partner based on one more of the filter options (Business Partner ID and Business Partner) that appear on the header area. Worklists by status The business partners are categorized based on their invitation response status: To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted, and Rejected. Worklist (Manage Business Partners) There are different ways to manage all the business partners and to set filters. To search for a specific business partner, you can use the filter bar in the header. The system also displays preconfigured worklists (To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted,  Note You must make sure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non purpose-related way in the Microsoft Excel file. The file size of each business partners Excel cannot be larger than 2MB, and the maximum number of rows in each file is 5000. A digital freight forwarder is managed as a business partner in both the SAP Business Network for Logistics and SAP Transportation Management system. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 41 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Rejected) based on the business partner's invitation response status. Filter Bar With the filter bar, you can do the following: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for business partners. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. To Be Submitted The To Be Submitted worklist displays all the business partners that you have uploaded or added in the app but have not yet submitted to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitations. This worklist also displays connection invitations that have been rejected. The worklist displays the following details for each invitation: System ID Business Partner ID Invitee Company Role SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) Phone number Email Language City Country/Region Zip code Status  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed.  Note A rejected invitation is displayed on the To Be Submitted worklist with the status "Returned by LBN OPS team" if it was submitted via the Invite Business Partners app. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 42 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- In Progress The In Progress worklist displays all the business partners that you have submitted to the back-end team to manage the connection invitations. These business partners have not yet responded to your invitation to connect with your network. You can recall your invitation in this worklist if needed. The In Progress worklist has the same columns as the To Be Submitted worklist. Accepted The Accepted worklist displays all the business partners who have accepted your invitation to join your business network. You can select one or more business partners in the Accepted tab and download them in Microsoft Excel format. The Accepted worklist has the same columns as the In Progress worklist along with the unique LBN ID of the business partner. Rejected The Rejected worklist displays all the business partners who have rejected your invitation to join your business network via Discover Business Partners. The Rejected worklist has the same columns as the Accepted worklist. Using the settings icon on each worklist, you can control the number of columns displayed in the To Be Submitted, In Progress, Accepted, and Rejected tabs. You can also sort and filter the business partners in these worklists based on various attributes. Add New Business Partners You can add new business partners to the Invite Business Partners app in one of the following ways: Manual entry On the To Be Submitted tab, you can manually add a new network data contributor to the Invite Business Partners app by choosing Add Invitee. Using this method, you can specify the language of your connection invitations. Supported languages are: English Arabic Bulgarian Chinese Simplified Chinese Traditional Croatian Czech Danish A rejected invitation is displayed on the Rejected worklist if it was submitted via the Discover Business Partners app. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 43 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Dutch Finnish French German Greek Hebrew Hungarian Italian Japanese Korean Malay Norwegian Polish Portuguese (Brazilian) Romanian Russian Serbian Slovak Spanish Swedish Thai Turkish Manual entry with an Excel template You can download the Excel template available in the Invite Business Partners app by choosing the Download Excel Template button. You can fill the details of the business partners using this template. You can then upload this template back in the Invite Business Partners app. Downloading business partner Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system You can download the list of business partners in your SAP TM system and upload the Excel file in the Invite Business Partners app. For more information, see Download Carrier Excel from SAP Transportation Management System.  Note When you upload a business partner Excel in the Invite Business Partners app, the system automatically filters out the erroneous business partner records and selects only the correct business partner records. For example, in the downloaded Excel file, if there are business partners that already exist in the Invite Business Partners app with the status as In Progress, Accepted or Rejected, or if some of the entries do not contain any of the mandatory fields, the system ignores such entries and uploads all the other entries. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 44 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- You can select one or more business partners in the To Be Submitted worklist and delete them from the Invite Business Partners app. Note that you cannot delete the business partners that you have submitted to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitation. Connection Invitations Once you have a list of business partners added to the Invite Business Partners app, you can select one or more partners from the To Be Submitted worklist and choose Submit. Once you choose Submit, the system instantaneously sends a request to the back-end team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection invitation. The system moves the submitted business partners to the In Progress worklist. Solution owners in both production and test environments can use the Invite Business Partners app to send connection invitations to business partners. If the invitees are not yet on the network, they can activate their accounts via a simplified account activation process and collaborate with the inviter in the respective environment (either production or test). You can refer your invitees to the following resource for their account activation: Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process. Note that business partners need your contact information when you send them an invitation to join your business network. If you have not maintained a default address in the Manage Business Profile app, the system does not allow you to submit business partners. For more information on adding a default address, see Edit Company Profile. The back-end team sends an invitation to the business partners requesting them to connect with your network. The business partner can view this connection invitation using the Manage Invitations app and choose to accept or reject the invitation. For more information, see Manage Invitations. When the business partner accepts or rejects an invitation, you will be notified of the same and the system moves the business partner to the accepted or rejected worklist as appropriate. If a partner accepts your invitation, the partner connects with your network and you can perform business transactions with this partner. If a business partner rejects your invitation, the partner is not connected with your network and you cannot perform any business transactions with this partner. You can find the rejected invitation from the To Be Submitted worklist and resend it if you want to. The system updates the unique LBN IDs of the business partners who have accepted your connection invitation. You can view this LBN ID in the Accepted worklist for each business partner. If you are using SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system, you can update these LBN IDs of business partners in SAP TM system by downloading the business partner list from the Invite Business Partners app and uploading the list in your SAP TM system. For more information, see Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). Recall Invitations You can recall a submitted invitation as long as its status remains "In Progress". When you upload a business partner Excel, the system performs a validation. If there are no validation errors, the business partner Excel is uploaded. If there are validation errors, the system displays the erroneous entries in an error log. The system allows you to download this error log. You must make sure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non purpose-related way in the Microsoft Excel file. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 45 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- To recall the invitation, switch to the In Progress worklist, click to open the invitation that you want to recall, and then choose Recall on the details page. After being recalled, the invitation returns to the To Be Submitted worklist and becomes editable. The business partner cannot view the recalled invitation using the app until you submit it again. Downloading Business Partner Excel from SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) You can download the business partners from the SAP TM system and upload them to the Invite Business Partners app. Context In SAP TM system, you must perform the following steps to download the business partner Excel: Procedure 1. Execute the report /SCMTMS/R_LBN_CARR_LIST_DWNLD in transaction SE38. 2. Enter your SAP TM organization ID in the Organizational ID field and execute. The system determines the hierarchy of this organization and retrieves all the freight agreements that are valid at the time of searching. The system then determines the valid business partners from these agreements. Note that if you select the Show Application Log checkbox, the system displays the detailed information about the business partner determination process. 3. Alternatively, instead of entering an organization ID and retrieving multiple business partners, you can also enter the business partner IDs in the Carrier IDs field and execute. The system retrieves the details of all the business partners that you have entered. 4. Select all the business partners that you want to download and then choose Download. The system downloads the Excel file. Next Steps Once you download the Excel file, in the Invite Business Partners app, choose the Upload Business Partners button to upload this Excel. Once you upload the Excel file with a list of partners, the system updates the To Be Submitted worklist in the app with the partner details in the Excel. Updating LBN IDs in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM)  Note You can't recall an invitation when its status is "Invitation email sent to business partner".  Note System IDs may consist of alphanumerical characters and the underscore ( _ ) character. You can check the Specification tab of the Excel for further guidance. The system checks all records when you upload your Excel, and displays the errors on the Upload Business Partners screen. You can correct the errors in your Excel and upload it again. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 46 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- You can update the SAP TM system with the unique LBN IDs of the business partners who have accepted to connect with your business network. Context To do so, you must perform the following: Procedure 1. Download the list of business partners with their LBN IDs from the Accepted worklist in the Invite Business Partners app. The system downloads the list of partners in a CSV format. 2. In the SAP TM system, execute the report /SCMTMS/R_LBN_ID_BP_UPD in transaction SA38. 3. Browse for the CSV file that you have downloaded and upload the file. The system updates the business partner IDs for the partners in the system. Note that you can choose whether you want the system to process the upload job in the background or foreground. If you choose to process the upload job in the foreground, the system displays the error logs if there are any. Assign Technical User Roles to Data Contributor's Technical User Prerequisites You must have the administrator role for your subaccount on SAP BTP. Context If you are using SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, your connected data contributor will send you the email address of its technical user after accepting your connection request. You need to grant the technical user the technical user roles. This needs to be performed for each data contributor that's connected with you. Procedure 1. Go to your subaccount in the SAP BTP cockpit. 2. In the left-hand pane, choose Role Collections under Security. 3. Choose the technical user role collection (you've created it in the task Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users). 4. Go to the Users section and choose Edit. 5. Enter the email address of the technical user and select Default identity provider. 6. Save your changes. Related Information Assign Users to Role Collection  Note Make sure the role collection contains all the technical user roles as listed in Available Roles for Solution Owners. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 47 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- System Connections (Solution Owner) Use the System Connections app for solution owners to create a connection and to authenticate inbound messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics from your on-premise SAP Transportation Management standalone system or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA. You can use the app in combination with each of the following exchange infrastructures between SAP Business Network for Logistics and your SAP backend system: SAP Cloud Integration SAP Process Integration Direct integration using SOA Manager The process of using the System Connections app to create a connection and to authenticate messages includes the following steps: 1. Creating a Connection. 2. Authenticating Inbound Messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics. 3. Activating the Connection. Configurations for Location Replication To replicate locations, you need to do some configurations first before using the System Connections app. Replicating Locations from SAP S/4HANA via Data Replication Framework (DRF) Context You can use the Manage Locations app to manage location master data, which was manually copied or replicated from SAP S/4HANA or created from new using the app. Location master data can then be used by the System Connections app in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Master Data Replication in the Source System To set up master data replication, you must configure the replication of master data via the Data Replication Framework (DRF) in the SAP S/4HANA source system. DRF uses SOAP service - LocationBulkReplicationRequest to replicate location master data from the source system to SAP Business Network for Logistics. Procedure 1. Define the business system for the SAP Business Network for Logistics tenant to which you want to replicate business partners. a. In the source system, go to Customizing for Data Replication using transaction DRFIMG. b. Go to Define Custom Settings for Data Replication Define Technical Settings Define Technical Settings for Business Systems . 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 48 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- c. There are two ways of making the location replication configuration: i. Create a business system using your LBN ID and Logical System ID as values. Concatenate LBN ID and the Logical System ID with delimiter “##”. For example, 100000000001##SYSCLNT001. ii. Follow the steps below: 1. Ensure that you are using a Cross Customising Client and run transaction drfimg. 2. Navigate to Data Replication > Define Custom Settings for Data Replication > Define Technical Settings > BAdI Determination of Local System Name. Execute this BAdI. 3. Enter 189 as the BO type and Location as the description. g. Create a new communication channel called Replication via Services.  Note Once these configurations are made, it would be applicable for all data replication settings via DRF. The logical system would be used in all these settings.  Note The logical system ID you entered here (string after the delimiter “##”) will also be used if you manually create individual location records in the Manage Locations app at a later time. Impl to assign the target system (identified by its LBN ID – as maintained in the business system) to the outbound implementation. e. Optional: If you only want to replicate one default language description, select the outbound implementation and navigate to Assign Language. f. Choose Activate. 3. Optional: Set up filter object criteria. a. On the SAP Easy Access screen, choose Cross-Application Components Processes and Tools for Enterprise Applications Master Data Governance Data Replication Define Filter Criteria (transaction DRFF). b. For information about a possible impact on the end user UI, see Browser Support. Resolution for B2B Connectivity to BN4L: Case 1: When sender system is S/4HANA (On-Premise & Private Cloud) 1. Case 2: When sender system is SAP NetWeaver PI (On-Premise & Private Cloud) 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Case 3: When WebDispatcher is placed in front of Cloud Integration endpoint 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. See SAP Help - PSE Management in Web Administration Interface of SAP Web Dispatcher, section [Trusted Certificates]. Case 4: When sender system is a non-SAP service/software 1. Consult your vendor for confirmation that it should trust [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ] for outbound TLS communication. 2. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Communication from and to your SAP backend system is based on B2B messages using SOAP and REST protocols. For authentication at SAP Business Network for Logistics, client certificates are used. Therefore, these certificates must be requested as a prerequisite. Several possible ways in which such key pairs (public and private key, sometimes also just called certificates) can be generated are listed below. A *.p12 file will be generated as a result. You may use any of the following options: Private and public key creation with the Identity Authentication service SAP Cloud Integration: keystore Trust manager – STRUST Private and public key creation with a third-party tool Creating a Private and Public Key with the Identity Authentication Service Before communication from and to your SAP backend system can take place, authentication with public and private keys, or certificates, must take place. The identity authentication service is one option for doing this. Perform the following steps: 1. Obtain access to the Identity Authentication service. There are three possible ways in which you can achieve this: You have already purchased an Identity Authentication service tenant. You can purchase such a service tenant here: < https://www.sapstore.com/solutions/40132/SAP-Cloud-Platform-Identity-Authentication>. While subscribing to a productive license for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, you have been provisioned with an Identity Authentication service tenant and details tenant, and a URL is sent to the S-User used for the license subscription. If you have subscribed for a test license for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, and you have not purchased an Identity Authentication service tenant, you may request a key pair from SAP by raising an incident to the component SBN-LBN-INT. (In this case, you can skip the steps in this section.) When using the Identity Authentication service, the certificates are signed by SAP Passport CA. 2. Follow the steps below to generate a *.p12 file from your Identity Authentication service tenant. Perform the following actions to generate a key pair. The following process is only for an SAP Business Network for Logistics productive license. a. Access the tenant's administration console for the Identity Authentication service by using the console's URL. Note the following points: The URL has the pattern https://<tenant ID>.accounts.ondemand.com/admin. The tenant ID is automatically generated by the system. The first administrator who created the tenant receives an activation email with a URL. This URL contains the tenant ID. b. Under Applications and Resources, choose Applications, click the pencil icon for Add Application, and assign the new application the name CertificateGeneration, for example. Then search for CertificateGeneration and click on Certificate for API Authentication. c. Enter the Common Name, Password, and Confirmed Password and click on Generate. The browser downloads the certificate to your local system. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 53 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The result is that you will have a signed certificate – a *.p12 file. Further information is available here: API Authentication SAP Cloud Integration: Keystore Before communication from and to your SAP backend system can take place, authentication with public and private keys, or certificates, must take place. The SAP Cloud Integration keystore is one option for doing this. If you have access to an SAP Cloud Integration tenant, you can use the available keystore functionality. Further information on generating the certificate is available here: Creating a Key Pair/SSH Key Pair. Trust Manager – STRUST Before communication from and to your SAP backend system can take place, authentication with public and private keys, or certificates, must take place. Trust manager – STRUST is one option for doing this. Follow the steps described in Configuring SAP NetWeaver AS for ABAP to Support TLS to configure STRUST certificates. Here, you will also find the information on Personal Security Environment (PSE) creation and certificates. Further information is available here: Configuring the Web Service Runtime. For additional information on this topic, check out this SAP blog on How to order an SSL certificate . Creating a Private and Public Key with a Third-Party Tool Before communication from and to your SAP backend system can take place, authentication with public and private keys, or certificates, must take place. Third-party tools are available for doing this. Create a new *.p12 file (private key and certificate), such as OpenSSL, and get it signed by a supported certificate authority (CA). Certificates created using the Identity Authentication service are already signed by SAP Passport CA. Any other certificates which are not yet signed by a CA need to be signed by one of the SAP Business Network for Logistics-supported CAs. Related Information Authenticating Inbound Messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics Configuring Links to Business Documents in Source Systems Context If your business documents in the source systems are sent to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace for tracking, you may need to switch between the two systems to view the information and perform necessary tasks. To facilitate the navigation, the in- app navigation is enabled so that you can go to the business document in the source systems directly from the fulfillment tracking apps with a single click. For this to work properly, you must configure document links first in the System Connections app. Procedure 1. Launch the System Connections app and click Add. 2. In the New Connection dialog, enter the following data and click Add: Connection Type: select "ABAP-based SAP system or external systems". You can create document links only for connections of the ABAP-based SAP system or external systems type. Connection ID: enter any value. System ID: enter any value. You can provide the path as follows: Path: /sap/bc/ui2/flp#OutboundDelivery-displayInWebGUI?OutboundDelivery={{trackingId}} Authenticating Inbound Messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics To authenticate inbound messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics from your SAP backend system, complete the following steps in the System Connections app. Prerequisites You've acquired a client certificate that's signed by SAP or a third-party certification authority: You’re recommended to use an SAP client certificate, which you can request from your Identity Authentication account on SAP BTP. Before you can delete an ABAP-based connection, you must first delete the certificates within the inbound connection manually. Then choose Delete Connection. SAP Business Network for Logistics will show a warning about the impact on existing documents. The connectivity will be permanently terminated once you delete an ABAP-based connection. There might be some existing documents in the network created using the connection. After deletion, this connection will be lost forever. 2.
