Manage Alternate IDs (Solution Owner) You can maintain alternate identifiers of your other accounts in the network. These identifiers shall be used in specific integration scenarios or in specific transaction flows in the network. Additionally, the LBN ID of your tenant can be seen above the Manage Alternate IDs table as a read-only field. SAP Business Network for Logistics supports the following alternate identifiers (alternate IDs): DUNS ID (Data Universal Numbering System ID) SCAC (Standard Carrier Alpha Code) Registration Number USDOT (US Department of Transportation) MC Number (Motor Carrier Number) Others GLN (Global Location Number) Technical User To create your own alternate IDs, proceed as follows: 1. Choose Manage Alternate IDs. 2. Select an alternate ID type from the dropdown menu and type in the required value. 3. Choose OK. You can also delete or change existing entries. Configure Partner Connections You can use the Configure Partner Connections app to establish a B2B connection to the external systems of your business partners. Using this configuration, SAP Business Network for Logistics can directly send documents to your partner’s external systems. Prerequisites 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 71 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- SAP Business Network for Logistics must support the desired business partner for B2B connectivity. This means that your company must agree on B2B integration with your data contributor. Then, you must invite your network partner to join SAP Business Network for Logistics using the Invite Business Partners app. Only then will the network partner be visible in the Configure Partner Connections app. The process of using the Configure Partner Connections app to create a connection and to authenticate messages includes the following steps: 1. Manage Credential Details 2. Create Partner Connection Manage Credential Details Context The Manage Credential Details view is a secure storage for you to maintain all the credentials that you receive from your business partner or network partner with whom you would like to enable B2B communication. A network partner can consist of a network of business partners (in this case of data contributors) that provides services like tracking. SAP Business Network for Logistics supports the following credential types: Basic OAuth 2.0 API Key project44 For more information, see the Configuration and Application Guide for project44 add-ons. Procedure 1. In the Configure Partner Connections app, choose Manage Credential Details. 2. Select the tab with the credential type that you want to use for maintaining the credential details. 3. Choose Add and complete the dialog. 4. (Optional): To change the credential details, select the row and choose Edit. Create Partner Connection Context Using the Configure Partner Connections app, you now need to map the connection details with your business partners and establish a B2B connection. Procedure 1. In the Configure Partner Connections app, choose Create. 2. Provide the following information: 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 72 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Field Explanation Usage (as maintained in Manage Credential Details) Business Partner ID Type* ID type of your individual connected business partner or of all connected business partners. A business partner is an entity with which the LBN customer does business (freight contracting, and order execution). You can maintain the following ID types: LBN ID SCAC P44_EU Motor Carrier Number US DOT GLN VAT SAPBPID – SAP Business Partner Number You can choose between general ID types (Any LBN ID or Any Alternate ID) and specific ID types (such as LBN ID, SCAC, or GLN) for a connection with your business partners. Any LBN ID applies this setting to all business partners that are onboarded in the network and connected to your tenant. You can configure alternate business partner ID types to initiate tracking for your shipments. Onboarding of these business partners to SAP Business Network for Logistics is not required. Business Partner ID Value* Unique identifier representing the business partner. Based on the business partner ID type, you choose the business partner ID value: If you choose LBN ID, the field name is Business Partner (LBN ID). If you choose a different ID than LBN ID, the field name is Business Partner ID Value. Network Partner (LBN ID) LBN ID of your network partner. A network partner is an entity which does data transfer/integration to business partners. Network partners will have many business partners in their network and have built integrations to business partner systems. You must provide this information if you receive the data via a network partner. Service* A service is defined based on the combination of the following information coming from a solution owner: Tracking type: Specifies if the tracking is based on a device or vehicle (such as the vehicle’s license plate) or based on a shipment indicator (such as a bill of lading) Transportation mode (such as Road) Scenario (such as tracking) SAP Business Network for Logistics supports the transportation modes Road and Ocean with the following services: Resource Road Tracking FTL (Removed) Shipment Road Tracking LTL Shipment Tracking All Shipment Road Tracking FTL Resource Road Tracking LTL (Removed) Shipment Ocean Tracking FCL 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 73 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Field Explanation Usage (as maintained in Manage Credential Details) Shipping type (such as LTL - less than truck load, or FTL - full truck load) Resource Ocean Tracking FCL (Removed) Shipment Ocean Tracking LCL Resource Ocean Tracking LCL (Removed) Resource Tracking All (Removed) Shipment Air Tracking All Shipment Tracking Parcel Resource Tracking Parcel (Removed) Shipment Rail Tracking All Business Partner Credential Credential provided to you by your business partner, which is maintained in the Manage Credential Details view. You must maintain this field if you communicate directly with your business partner’s system. You must provide this information if you are communicating with your business partner via a network partner. * mandatory fields You can either save or save and activate your changes. 3. It will be sent as header parameters in a Consumer API. Depending on your scenario, you can agree with your business partners or network partners to provide additional information. In SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, the LBN ID of your business partner is only mapped with one alternate ID, which is used when sending a tracking request via a Consumer API. It is of the highest priority and will overwrite the current alternate ID used in the Consumer API. 4. Save your entries. In the Configure Partner Connections app, choose Manage Credential Details. 2. Select the OAuth 2.0 tab. 3. Choose Add and complete the dialog: Name Credential Type: Network Partner Credential Grant Type: Client Credentials Authentication URL, Client ID, Client Secret: Refer to your email from project44. Client Authentication: Send as Body Parameter Scope Included: No 4. Back to the Partner Connections worklist page, choose Create. APIs and not for custom API integrations. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 75 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- 5. Complete the dialog: Business Partner ID Type: For ocean, parcel, road LTL and road LTL tracking, choose SCAC or LBN ID. For air tracking, choose Any Alternate ID. Network Partner (LBN ID): Project44, Inc. – Unified Service: For ocean tracking, choose Shipment Ocean Tracking FCL or Shipment Ocean Tracking LCL. For air tracking, choose Shipment Air Tracking All. For parcel tracking, choose Shipment Tracking Parcel. For road LTL tracking, choose Shipment Road Tracking LTL. For road FTL tracking, choose Shipment Road Tracking FTL. Status: Active Enable EDIFACT IFTSTA for Event Tracking The message type EDIFACT IFTSTA supports both inquiries of shipment status and responses for consignment status, making it suitable for use in both inbound and outbound connections. This message type can be leveraged to track the following business events in the global track and trace solution: Code Code Description DEPARTURE Departure UNLOAD_END Unloading End ARRIV_DEST Arrival OUT_FOR_DELIVERY Out for Delivery LOAD_END Loading End DELAYED Delay Configuration The GLNID is crucial for identifying both parties in IFTSTA communication. To set up EDIFACT integration for the IFTSTA message type, this identifier for both parties must be consistently maintained in the following apps: Configure Partner Connections  Note For road FTL tracking, you can also choose other Business Partner ID types listed in Create Partner Connection, depending on the requirements of your carrier or visibility providers. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 76 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- System Connections Maintaining GLNIDs as Customer Headers in Configure Partner Connections Solution owners must maintain their GLNID and that of their data contributors. Use customer headers in the Configure Partner Connections app for this purpose. To maintain GLNIDs in Configure Partner Connections, follow these steps: 1. Open the partner connection in which you want to enable the EDIFACT IFTSTA message type. 2. Scroll down to the Custom Headers section and click the plus sign. 3. Enter SHIPPER_GLNID as the key and enter your GLNID as the value. 4. Enter CARRIER_GLNID as the key and enter the GLNID of the data contributor you work with as the value. 5. Save your changes. 6. Repeat these steps if you want to enable EDIFACT IFTSTA in other partner connections. Maintaining GLNIDs as Alternative Identifiers in System Connections Both solution owners and data contributors must maintain their GLNID in the System Connections app. To maintain GLNIDs in System Connections, follow these steps: 1. Choose Manage Alternate IDs. 2. Select GLN from the dropdown menu and enter your GLNID. 3. Choose OK. Limitations In an inbound connection, if RFF+ZZ8 (stopId) is not provided, the stopId is converted to an empty string, instead of NULL. If an EDI file contains more than one event types, multiple messages with the same message number are sent to the global track and trace solution. The address name field of a location is not supported in an IFTSTA message. UNLOCODE and IATACODE are not supported in an IFTSTA message. A delay event can only refer to an arrival or departure event, and no event reason code is available in the delay event. More information You can refer your data contributors to this implementation guide for B2B IFTSTA integration: https://help.sap.com/doc/df3dd1c3edd44250b0c27c9c71159459/LBN/en-US/SAP_LBN_EDI_HowToGuide_GTT.pdf For detailed information about the IFTSTA messages used in the global track and trace solution, see the following Message Implementation Guide: https://help.sap.com/doc/9cc21c6fda37437eaee763d114d5bbfe/LBN/en-US/SAP_LBN_IFTSTA_D01C_GTT.pdf 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 77 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Manage Notification Templates The Manage Notification Templates app enables you to create and maintain email notification templates that you can use to notify your business partner on the occurrence of an event. This app enables you to create a customized notification template and maintain language specific notification email texts for this template. You can also specify the recipients of these emails in these templates. Creation of a Notification Template To create a notification template, perform the following: 1. Choose Create. The Create Notification Template dialog box appears. 2. Enter a template ID and template description. 3. Select the Global Track and Trace application and choose OK. The system creates the template. When you select this template, you can view and maintain the email templates in different languages. You can use the Delete button to delete one or more templates. Note that you must set one of the templates as default and the default template cannot be deleted. To maintain email templates in different languages you must select the notification template, perform the following: 1. Choose Add. The Add Language dialog box appears. 2. Select a language from the drop-down menu. 3. Enter a value from the Insert Placeholder button. Note that when you choose this button, the system displays a list of placeholders. Choose the appropriate placeholder for the email contacts. 4. Choose OK. A new window appears. 5. Enter an email subject and email body in the respective fields. Note that you can also enter a value from the Insert Placeholder button. When you choose this button, the system displays a list of placeholders. Choose the appropriate placeholder. 6. Choose Save. The system saves the language specific email template text. Similarly, you can add multiple language email template texts to a template. Note that the system sets the first language template that you create as the default template. Once you create two or more language templates, you select a template and use the Set As Default button to choose a different default template. Manage Locations 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 78 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- You can use the Manage Locations app to manage location master data either manually replicated from another system or created from scratch using the app. Location master data can then be consumed by other apps in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. You can set up a location replication using the Data Replication Framework (DRF) in the SAP S4/HANA source system. For more information, see Configurations for Location Replication. Location master data consists of not only the address information, but also the business purpose of a location. Additionally, the master data of a location can include one or more alternative IDs so that the location becomes cross-platform identifiable. The main features of this app include: View a location Create a location Upload locations Edit a location Viewing a Location To view a location, proceed as follows: 1. By default, you can use the following fields to filter locations: External ID Source System Object Type Description Country/Region City Data Processing Status Additional Information You can also adjust the filter bar by chooosing Adapt Filters. 2. Click the location from the filter results to open the details page. The detail view of the location consists of a header and other sections.  Note The Manage Locations app implements all security features and data protection-relevant functions documented in the "Security and Data Protection and Privacy" section of the Administration Guide. A location master data record enters the blocking period if it has not been accessed for three consecutive years. The blocking period lasts for another three years, during which only audit specialists can access the record. The record will then be automatically deleted when the end of the blocking period is reached. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 79 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Header The Header section displays the address information. General This section displays the basic information of a location. This includes the business purposes, the longitude/latitude coordinates, and the revision history. Geographical Coordinates and Map This section displays the geographical coordinates of the location. It also identifies the location on the map. Alternative Location IDs This section displays a list of type-specific alternative IDs of the location. Contact Information This section displays the contact information related to the location. Additional Information This section displays the contact information related to the location. More Information You can do the following with the filter bar: Specify filters to narrow down the worklists and search for locations. Add or remove the filters displayed on the filter bar by choosing Adapt Filters. Save the current filter settings as a view and apply it later. After you specified filters (and pressed Enter ) and/or adapted filter display, the current view name shown in the upper- left corner displays a * sign, indicating the view has been changed. Save the view by either of the following: Click the view name to open the My Views box and choose Save or Save As. In the Adapt Filters dialog box, choose Save. Next time when you want to apply the view, just select the view name in the My Views box. Creating a Location To create a location, proceed as follows: 1. Click Create on the upper-right corner of the Locations table. The Create New Location page opens.  Note The default Standard view cannot be changed. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 80 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: 2. On the Create New Location page, enter the following details: Source: Source of the location. Valid values are: SAP SCM Logistic Location: Locations from one of the following systems: SAP Extended Warehouse Management SAP Transportation Management SAP ERP Location: Locations from an SAP ERP system Others: Locations from other systems Location Type: Type of the location This field is available when Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location. Object Type: Business purpose of a location. This field is configurable when Source is set to SAP ERP Location or Others. When Source is set to SAP SCM Logistic Location, the system automatically sets Object Type to Logistic Location. Valid values for the Object Type field are:: Business Partner Customer Plant Shipping Point Supplier If none of the values above fits the location’s business purpose, you can change Source to SAP SCM Logistic Location as an alternative. This will set Object Type to Logistic Location at the backend and make Location Type configurable. The Location Type field provides you with a broader list of types pertaining to various business purposes, such as port and hub. Description: Descriptive information about the location Source System/External ID: Source system from which the location master data is copied and the corresponding ID. If you are creating a location from scratch, set the Source System part to LBN, and set the External ID part to the location ID you previously prepared. If you are importing a location from SAP Transportation Management (TM), set the Source System to the business system name of your TM system and set the External ID to the location ID in TM. For locations that have its object type set to “Business Partner”, you can find the business system name of your TM system and the location ID in the SOAP request message sent to LBN. In this request, the MessageHeader.SenderBusinessSystemID attribute specifies the business system name and the internal ID of the sender (the MessageHeader.SenderParty.InternalID attribute) specifies the location ID. Alternatively, you can run transaction code SLDCHECK in TM to view the business system name.  Note You can also maintain the information of an ordering party in this app by setting the Object Type field to Business Partner. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 81 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Logical System: You can also use the Logical System field to identify the system from which the location master data is replicated. This is a mandatory field if you want to use the location in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. The logical system ID you enter here must be the same one that you used when configuring the replication of location master data via the Data Replication Framework. For more information, see Replicating Locations from SAP S/4HANA via Data Replication Framework (DRF). Make sure you enter the logical system ID correctly so that it matches the source system of the location. Otherwise, there can be duplicate records in your location master data. (Optional) Address: Country/Region State City District Street/House Number Zip Code (Optional) Geographical Coordinates And Map: Longitude: Longitude coordinate of the location Latitude: Latitude coordinate of the location (Optional) Time Zone (Optional) Alternative Location ID: Type: Type of the alternative ID. ID: Alternative ID in the specified type. (Optional) Contact Information: Contact information related to the location. (Optional) Additional Information: Additional information about the location. For more detail, see Define Additional Information. 3. Choose Save. Result  Note You can enter the coordinates in the Longitude and Latitude fields manually. If you want the system to verify your entries, set Calibrate coordinates when saving to Yes before you save your changes. You can also choose Generate Longitude and Latitude Coordinates to create the coordinates according to the address information you’ve entered. By default, Calibrate coordinates when saving is set to Apply global settings, meaning that how the system handles coordinates for the location record you are working on is determined by the option you choose in the Generate geo-coordinates automatically setting, which can be found in the Settings dialogue box. If you leave Generate geo-coordinates automatically with the default option, the system generates geo-coordinates for locations when both the latitude and longitude coordinates are missing. For more information, see Global settings for Geo-Coordinates. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 82 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- The newly-created location master data can be consumed by other apps in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Upload Locations You can fill the details of locations using an Excel template and then upload this template back to the app. To do this, follow these steps: 1. Choose Upload to open the Upload Locations page. 2. Click Upload on the up-right corner, then download the Excel template available by choosing Download Excel Template. 3. Fill the details of the locations you want to upload in the template. 4. In Choose File, locate the modified Excel template and then choose Upload. Editing a Location To edit a location, proceed as follows: 1. Use the following fields to filter locations: Location ID Description Location Type Country/Region City 2. Click the location from the filter results to open the details page. 3. Choose Edit on the upper-right corner of the details page. Enable Risk Monitoring If you have configured the risk monitoring service provider in Configure Partner Connections, you can determine whether or not to use the service provider to monitor risks at a certain location in Manage Locations.  Note You can enter the geographical coordinates for the location records in the Longitude and Latitude columns manually. If you want the system to verify your entries, set Calibrate coordinates when saving to Yes before you upload your file. By default, Calibrate coordinates when saving is set to Apply global settings, meaning that how the system handles coordinates for the location records you are uploading is determined by the option you choose in the Generate geo- coordinates automatically setting, which can be found in the Settings dialogue box. If you leave Generate geo-coordinates automatically with the default option, the system generates geo-coordinates for locations when both the latitude and longitude coordinates are missing. For more information, see Global settings for Geo-Coordinates.  Note 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 83 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Prerequisites You have configured the risk monitoring service provider in Configure Partner Connections. Procedure To enable risk monitoring for a specific location, follow these steps: 1. Click the location record for which you want to monitor risks to open its details page. 2. Choose Edit on the upper-right corner. 3. Click to select the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox and then choose Save. Alternatively, you can enable risk monitoring for multiple locations at once. To do this, select the location records, and then choose Risk Monitoring Enable . Results The risk monitoring service provider starts monitoring risks at the location. If you’ve subscribed for the intelligent insights add-on, you can view the risk information on each target location in the Logistics Execution Insights app. To notify the service provider to stop monitoring risks at a location, uncheck the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox in the corresponding location record. To stop using the risk monitoring feature for all locations in your supply chain, uncheck the Enable supply chain risk monitoring checkbox in each location record where you previously enabled the feature in Manage Locations and then deactivate the risk monitoring service provider in Configure Partner Connections. More Information Editing a Location Creating a Location Manage Custom Codes You can use the manage custom codes feature to extend the drop-down list for the following fields: Country/Region State Location Type Risk information is not displayed in Manage Locations. Instead, it’s displayed on the map view of the Logistics Execution Insights app. You use Manage Locations to specify a group of target locations where you want to monitor risks.  Note You can also configure this setting when creating a new location record. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 84 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Time Zone Role of Contact This feature is useful if the drop-down list of a field does not contain the code you want to select. For example, you do not find the region code you need in the drop-down list of Country/Region. To create a custom code, proceed as follows: 1. Choose the Manage Custom Codes button. 2. On the Manage Custom Codes page, select the field for which you want to extend the list, and then choose Create. 3. Specify the name, language, and description of the code, and then choose Save. Results After you create a custom code, you can find it from the Custom category when you expand the corresponding drop-down list. If needed, you can also remove it or edit its description on the Manage Custom Codes page. Global settings for Geo-Coordinates You can use Generate geo-coordinates automatically in the Settings dialogue box to define how the system handles geo- coordinates for all location records. In Generate geo-coordinates automatically, you have the following options: Off (Default): Do not generate geo-coordinates automatically even if they are missing. Generate: Generate geo-coordinates for locations when both the latitude and longitude coordinates are missing. (Applies to all locations including the existing ones) Overwrite: Generate geo-coordinates for locations when coordinates are missing or overwrite them if they already exist. (Applies to locations created after you enable this option) Archiving Locations If you have location records that are no longer used regularly, you can archive these records for future reference or regulatory compliance.  Note Options in Generate geo-coordinates automatically only take effect for location records where you leave Calibrate coordinates when saving with the default option Apply global settings. The Calibrate coordinates when saving setting in location records takes precedence over Generate geo-coordinates automatically in the Settings dialogue box. For example, when you set Calibrate coordinates when saving to No in a location record, the system does not generate or calibrate coordinates for the record even if Generate geo-coordinates automatically is set to Generate or Overwrite.  Note To archive locations, you must have the LocationArchiveTemplate role. 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 85 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- To archive location records, select the records you want to archive on the Locations list and then choose Archive. You can view the locations you’ve archived on the Archived Locations list by choosing Archived Items at the up-right corner. To restore archived location records, select the records you want to restore on the Archived Locations list, and then choose Restore. You can view the restored locations after you switch to the standard Locations list. Define Additional Information The Additional Information section contains a list of additional information associated to a location record. This section enables you to define necessary custom characteristics or references by adding your information items. An information item comprises a name, the type of the item, and the corresponding value. Type: Type of the additional information item. It can be either Text or Alternative ID. Name: Name of the additional information item. If you set Type to Alternative ID, the name of the item must be set to one of the following values: GLN DUNS UN/LOCODE IATA Airport Code Value: Value that corresponds to this additional information item. If you have a location that contains multiple ports or airports, you can maintain multiple UN/LOCODEs and IATA Airport Codes for this location in this section. But to ensure that the actual event matches with the correct planned/unplanned event, be aware of the following event match rules: For planned events, when multiple location records are found with the same UN/LOCODE or IATA Airport Code, the system will match the actual event with the planned event that has the same location alternative key. For unplanned events, the UN/LOCODE or IATA Airport Code maintained in the Alternative Location IDs section of the Manage Locations app is superior to the one maintained in the Additional Information section. For example, when two location records (A and B) are found with the same UN/LOCODE, but the UN/LOCODE in Location A is maintained in the Alternative Location IDs section and the UN/LOCODE in Location B is maintained in the Additional Information section, the system will take Location A as the superior one, and match the actual event with the unplanned event that has Location A. Discover Business Partners Finding the right business partners is always a challenge. However, this will be easier once your partners-to-be have joined SAP Business Network for Logistics. As a simple yet powerful app in SAP Business Network for Logistics, Discover Business Partners helps you search the network for logistics service providers, then from the results, invite suitable ones to be your business partners. Search for Business Partners 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 86 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- To search for business partners on the network, enter a key word, for example the company name, in the search box and then press Enter . You can also use faceted search on the left pane to narrow down your search results. When using faceted search, you can even leave the search box empty. This is useful if you want to explore your potential partners in a specific region or industry. Result A set of matched results are returned. You can click to open the details page of a matched result. Send Request for Connection To send a request for connection to your potential business partners, proceed as follows: 1. Click to select the company to which you want to send the request for connection from the Matched Results table. 2. Choose Request for Connection. The request for connection is sent to the selected companies. Results A request for connection is sent to the selected company. Once the company accepts your request, you will become business partners. After you’ve set up a partnership with a business partner via this app, you must update the business partner’s LBN ID in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM). To do this, see Updating Business Partner’s LBN ID. References Manage Business Profile Manage Invitations Updating Business Partner’s LBN ID To update the LBN ID in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) for a logistics service provider who’s become your business partner, proceed as follows in SAP TM: 1. Go to the Manage Business Partner transaction (transaction BP). 2. Set the filter criteria to find the business partner for which you want to update the LBN ID and then double-click the business partner to open its Display Organization page. 3. Navigate to the Identification tab. In the Identification Numbers section, IDType field, enter LBN001. 4. In the Identification Number field, enter the LBN ID and save your changes.  Note If the business partners you are trying to connect with operates in a different data center, you must first ensure that your company profile is available across all data centers of SAP Business Network for Logistics. For more information, refer to Profile Settings.  Note If the companies that match your search conditions are not found, see Discover Business Partners App and refer to "Why companies that match my search conditions are not returned in the Matched Results table?" 5/12/26, 6:52 AM 87 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Assign Technical User Roles to Data Contributor's Technical User Prerequisites You must have the administrator role for your subaccount on SAP BTP. Context If you are using SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, your connected data contributor will send you the email address of its technical user after accepting your connection request. You need to grant the technical user the technical user roles. This needs to be performed for each data contributor that's connected with you. Procedure 1. Go to your subaccount in the SAP BTP cockpit. 2. In the left-hand pane, choose Role Collections under Security. 3. Choose the technical user role collection (you've created it in the task Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users). 4. Go to the Users section and choose Edit. 5. Enter the email address of the technical user and select Default identity provider. 6. Save your changes. file://api-specs/split/SAP Business Netw.content: SAP Business Network for Logistics- Best Practice This site is dedicated to collecting all best practices for SAP Business Network for Logistics.  Pre-Implementation Think about the solution as a whole rather than focusing on BN4L only. A back-end system (e.g. TM, S/4Hana, EWM, YL etc.) is a leading system that determines how various logistics processes, data flow and collaboration with trading partners via BN4L will look like. Build all these scenarios coming from the back-end system into the BN4L and not vice versa. Review Activate Road Map Viewer to get familiar with SAP Activate phases that provide clear guidance at every step of the implementation journey. Consider customer’s existing and future processes in their back-end system as well as back-end limitations and compatibility with BN4L. Review Tips and Tricks blog and this document with best practices prior the implementation. Telling the narrative from BN4L point of view quite often doesn't reflect the reality of projects where BN4L is implemented as it doesn’t reflect needs and scenarios of customer’s back-end. Supply Chain Logistics Maturity Model introduces a structured framework developed by SAP to help logistics leaders assess and improve their supply chain operations. This resource can be leveraged by our customers ahead of their IT transformation initiatives to assess their current maturity level and define strategic next steps.  Shipper Onboarding Shipper onboarding includes initial configuration of global BTP account which includes subaccounts creation and subscription to applications for BN4L, user management or establishing trust between subaccounts and Identity Authentication tenant. FC, GTT External  Network Partners There are two types of network partners that SAP collaborate with within BN4L solution. Tracking Collaboration Integrate with SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) for event reporting purpose. LSPs / carriers onboarded to this type of network partners are able to share tracking information and report events to customers through BN4L. Visibility service providers / visibility data aggregators Transacting Collaboration Integrate with SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) for transacting purpose. SAP Business Network for Logistics: Get your first, API integrated example from Shipper in 3 steps Saif Product and Topic Expert 2023 Aug 29 11:51 PM 15 Likes  6,668 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Getting started with Carrier API Integration in 3 simple steps The SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration solution connects shippers and their logistics partners on a secure network for optimized collaboration and insights, integrated tightly with core business processes for efficiency and resilience. More details can be found here. Carrier Integration involves 3 key entities/systems. S/4HANA Transportation Management system - owned by Shipper. SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) - Both Shipper and Carrier are part of this. Carrier / Network Partner's system - owned by Carriers or Network partners.   -- 1 of 7 -- As shown above, there are 2 integration patterns: Outbound from TM & SAP BN4L: Whenever there is a change or a business event in TM, it triggers the call to SAP BN4L which then routes it to a specific carrier webhook based on the configuration. Inbound into TM & SAP BN4L: This is triggered by Carriers or Network Partners when they call SAP BN4L's APIs. Note: SAP BN4L also supports EDI in addition to API and also a Web portal Interface. In this post, we will focus on the first pattern of receiving orders from a Shipper. 1. Preparing webhook - by Carrier As seen above, in order for carriers to receive the business events/changes, a webhook is required to be hosted by carriers and configured in BN4L. There are many platforms such as pipedream, webhook.site, Postman, Make, SAP's Integration Suite or even a simple nodejs application hosting a webhook on Business Technology platform (BTP). While there are a number of ways listed below to create a webhook, the intent of this blog is to give a quick turnaround for carriers to receive examples and messages from SAP BN4L to build the integration. For simplicity's sake, I use an iPaas provider pipedream. This is easy and convenient to create a webhook to test the end-end integration. -- 2 of 7 -- 2. Configure System Connections - by Carrier Pre-requisite: SAP BN4L provides a portal for carriers, which carriers receive access to once ordered via sapstore. The process is explained here. Carrier user will need the necessary authorization to be able to access and manage connections in the portal. Make sure you also enable Inbound communication. Make sure you have accepted the invitation from the Shipper. -- 3 of 7 -- Access the System Connections app and configure the webhook that you created in the previous step for the scenario that you wish to test. In the case below, I chose the "Freight Subcontracting All" option as an example. -- 4 of 7 -- 3. Configure Partner Connections - by Shipper Once you are done with Step 2, contact your shipper to configure the connection to your configured webhook. Pre-requisite: Shipper has access to SAP BN4L and has onboarded with one of the scenarios described. Shipper user has relevant roles to access "Configure Partner Connections" and ""app. Shipper sends an invite to the carrier and makes sure the tenants are connected. Shipper accesses the "Configure Partner Connections" app and establishes a connection with the scenario endpoint configured by carrier in their tenant in step 2 and also activates the connection. -- 5 of 7 -- Note: You can repeat steps 2 and 3 for other scenarios and operations. That's it..!! Ask your Shipper to send some test orders and voilà! you will receive the orders to the configured webhook. You can also access the "Manage Integration Logs" application to monitor the integration and also access the payload. Conclusion While the above may not be a productive setup, it allows the participants of the network(Shippers-Carriers/ Network Partners) to quickly understand the behavior of the system and enables you to develop and validate against production-like orders from your shippers in a very short time. -- 6 of 7 -- Comments For further questions and feedback related to the blog, please check the Q&A area and feel free to post your questions in the link with the tag SAP Business Network for Logistics. TABLE OF CONTENTS INTRODUCTION ............................................................................................................................................... 3 PREREQUISITES .............................................................................................................................................. 4 PROCESS DESCRIPTION................................................................................................................................ 5 STEP 1: IFTSTA (OUTBOUND) ....................................................................................................................... 6 STEP 2: TEST OUTBOUND CONNECTIVITY ............................................................................................... 10 STEP 3: IFTSTA (INBOUND) WITH SFTP POLLING .................................................................................... 10 STEP 4: EMAIL NOTIFICATION FOR INTEGRATION ERRORS ................................................................. 14 OPERATIONAL MONITORING ...................................................................................................................... 15 -- 2 of 10 -- 3 INTRODUCTION Note: As of today, SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace (GTT) supports the following B2B standards and corresponding messages: EDI/B2B Message Standard Message Type Version Description EDIFACT IFTSTA D01C Shipment Status Inquiry EDIFACT IFTSTA D01C Shipment status Update EDIFACT IFTSTA supports both inquiries of shipment status and responses for the status of a consignment, making it suitable for use in both inbound and outbound connections. To set up EDIFACT integration for the IFTSTA message type, you, as a data contributor, must configure an SFTP connection in the System Connections app. Additionally, the GLNID for both parties (solution owner and data contributor) must be consistently maintained in the Configure Partner Connections and System Connections. This implementation guide provides detailed instructions on what needs to be done. Note: We strongly recommend that you perform all activities mentioned in this guide in both the test and productive environments. -- 3 of 10 -- 4 PREREQUISITES To set up EDI integration with SAP Business Network for Logistics, you must meet the following requirements: • The data contributor tenant is available in the test and productive environments. For more information about the process of registering SAP Business Network for Logistics, activating your account, logging on, and adding users, see the Activate Your Account guide. • Both the solution owner and data contributor must maintain alternate identifiers (such as the GLNID in the System Connections app. The GLNID is crucial for identifying both parties in IFTSTA communication. For more information, see Manage Alternate IDs (Data Contributor) | SAP Help Portal. • The solution owner you work with has maintained the GLNID of both parties in the Configure Partner Connections app. For more information, see Enable EDIFACT IFTSTA for Event Tracking. • In case your SFTP server uses IP filtering, you need to add specific IP ranges to the allow list based on the data center you’re onboarded to. Otherwise, the Cloud Integration tenants cannot connect to your SFTP server. For more information, see Regions and Hosts Available for the Connectivity Platform. • It is expected that data contributor set up an SFTP server on their side for information exchange. Data contributors have to set up the SFTP connection once and solution owners can use the same SFTP connection for communication. Data contributors must enter a base64-encoded string of their SFTP server in the Known Host Key field of the System Connections app. See also Specifying the Authentication Details and Base URLs for Your System’s Endpoints. The following diagram demonstrates the SFTP communication between the involved parties. • Ensure that you use different folders for Test and Prod on your SFTP server. -- 4 of 10 -- 5 PROCESS DESCRIPTION The process flow below illustrates a sequence of events for exchanging UN/EDIFACT messages which are supported by SAP Business Network for Logistics. The supported message types are also listed in the Introduction section. -- 5 of 10 -- 6 STEP 1: IFTSTA (OUTBOUND) On the Manage Network tab of your SAP Fiori launchpad, select the System Connections app. Choose Manage Details in the upper-right corner. Under the Communication Details tab, choose Add and select the SFTP option from the dropdown menu. -- 6 of 10 -- 7 Enter the following data in the Add EDI Communication window: For more information, see Specifying the Authentication Details and Base URLs for Your System’s Endpoints. Hint: The file name can consist of particular placeholders that you replace when creating the file name and fixed parts. For example, LBN_%DOCUMENT_ID%_%TIMESTAMP%.edi Available placeholders: • %DOCUMENT_ID% • %MESSAGE_TYPE% • %TIMESTAMP% • %SHIPPER_LBN_ID% Under the Authentication Details tab, choose Add and select the BASIC option from the dropdown menu. Enter the following data in the New Basic Authentication Details window: -- 7 of 10 -- 8 Go back to the entry page of the System Connections app and create outbound connection for the following service and operation Service Operation Corresponding EDIFACT Message Shipment Tracking All Put order for tracking EDIFACT IFTSTA To do so, create a new service: -- 8 of 10 -- 9 Enter the following data for the new service: -- 9 of 10 -- 10 STEP 2: TEST OUTBOUND CONNECTIVITY After configuring the outbound connection, you should directly perform a connection test to your SFTP server. To test the service, select Shipment Tracking All from the Service table and choose Test Service in the upper-right corner, then select With Default Payload: The system generates a test freight order and attempts to send an EDI file to your SFTP server. The following window is shown with the test freight order ID: Using the ID of the created document (for example API_TEST_2EseTjcRHq), you can find the corresponding test document in the Manage Integration Logs app and view the test result. Please refer to the chapter OPERATIONAL MONITORING for more details. STEP 3: IFTSTA (INBOUND) WITH SFTP POLLING On the Manage Network tab of your SAP Fiori launchpad, select the System Connections app. -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/SAP_LBN_p44_FSD_P.content: SAP Business Network, project44 Add-Ons Feature Scope Description PUBLIC Document version: LBN 2.0 15 February 2025 -- 1 of 10 -- 2 TABLE OF CONTENTS 1 ABOUT THIS DOCUMENT.............................................................................................................. 3 2 INTRODUCTION .............................................................................................................................. 4 2.1 project44 Add-Ons for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration ..........................................5 2.2 project44 Add-Ons for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace ......................................6 3 FEATURES ...................................................................................................................................... 7 3.1 SAP Business Network, project44 FTL Visibility Add-On ...............................................................8 3.2 SAP Business Network, project44 LTL Visibility Add-On ...............................................................8 3.3 SAP Business Network, project44 Ocean Visibility Add-On ..........................................................9 3.4 SAP Business Network, project44 Air Visibility Add-On ............................................................. 10 3.5 SAP Business Network, project44 Parcel Visibility Add-On........................................................ 10 3.6 SAP Business Network, project44 Rail Visibility Add-On ............................................................ 11 4 GEOGRAPHIC AND CARRIER NETWORK AVAILABILITY ....................................................... 12 -- 2 of 10 -- SAP Business Network, project44 Add-Ons 3 1 ABOUT THIS DOCUMENT This feature scope description covers the project44 add-ons for SAP Business Network. It defines the real-time visibility content services that are available for the following: • SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration • SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace Note that the service scope and capabilities described in this documentation cover only the respective project44 add-ons. -- 3 of 10 -- SAP Business Network, project44 Add-Ons 4 2 INTRODUCTION SAP is extending the reach of SAP Business Network with project44 add-ons that provide real-time visibility content. These add-on services leverage the project44 multi-mode carrier network with its established B2B connectivity to carrier and logistics provider systems, truck telematics, electronic logging devices, and so on. With the add-ons for project44 visibility services, SAP Business Network users can benefit from the availability of actual shipment execution insights, such as real-time shipment location and event status for full truck loads, and real-time milestone status for less than truck load shipments. This allows for a holistic view of both planned and actual shipment status, as well as automatic business event detection. project44 visibility content is available to SAP Business Network users through supplementary, add-on licenses from SAP. -- 4 of 10 -- SAP Business Network, project44 Add-Ons 5 2.1 project44 Add-Ons for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration delivers out-of-the-box, native connectivity to the project44 Advanced Visibility Platform™. The following add-ons are available as ready-to-run scenarios: • SAP Business Network, project44 FTL visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 LTL visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 ocean visibility add-on The visibility add-ons allow usage of project44 real-time visibility data with the SAP Business Network for Logistics, Track Freight Movement app, for full truckload (FTL), less than truck load (LTL) and ocean shipment tracking. They enable project44 actual shipment visibility data to be leveraged, including truck and vessel location for full truck loads and full container and less than container ocean shipments (with geocoordinates and timestamps), event status and milestone status (with location and timestamp) for less than truck load. Predicted estimated time of arrivals (ETAs) are also available for road shipments. In this way, the Track Freight Movement app for shippers, brings together both planned and actual shipment information to provide users with an accurate overview of the freight order execution status for improved logistics and resource capacity planning. -- 5 of 10 -- SAP Business Network, project44 Add-Ons 6 2.2 project44 Add-Ons for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace SAP offers add-on licenses to enrich execution status of tracked process with project44 real-time visibility content into SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace (GTT). Solution owners can, for example, receive visibility data from the project44 Advanced Visibility Platform. Visibility data from project44 is available with out-of-the-box integration for tracking across different shipment modes. The following add-ons may be purchased for users to view project44 visibility data in GTT tracked processes: • SAP Business Network, project44 FTL visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 LTL visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 ocean visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 air visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 parcel visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 rail visibility add-on Each project44 add-on license: • includes only the right to use the corresponding project44 content and data with a GTT tracked process • is separate and must be purchased individually. Note 1. The following are not included with the project44 add-on licenses or with the license for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace: • out-of-the-box integration of the GTT solution with project44 for rail. • a GTT model template customized for a project44 scenario for rail. • configuration and/or extensions such as business partner setup and locations. 2. When creating the partner connection in the Configure Partner Connections app, solution owners can choose “Project44, Inc. – Unified” as the network partner. -- 6 of 10 -- SAP Business Network, project44 Add-Ons 7 3 FEATURES The following SAP Business Network, project44 add-ons are available to shippers or solution owners: Figure 1: Available SAP Business Network, project44 add-ons SAP Business Network Add-ons for project44 content services Global Track and Trace With integration and ready-to-use scenarios for: • SAP Business Network, project44 FTL visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 LTL visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 ocean visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 air visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 parcel visibility add-on Custom integrations provided by project44, with proper implementation project scoping exercise: • SAP Business Network, project44 rail visibility add-on Freight Collaboration With out-of-the-box integration and ready-to- use scenarios for: • SAP Business Network, project44 FTL visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 LTL visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 ocean visibility add-on -- 7 of 10 -- SAP Business Network, project44 Add-Ons 8 3.1 SAP Business Network, project44 FTL Visibility Add-On Feature Description Shipment tracking initiation • Initiate tracking with o a carrier identifier (such as SCAC code), a carrier reference number, (such as bill of lading), and a tracked object (such as license plate) o a carrier identifier and a carrier reference number and source and destination information with planned business time. Note that which identifier and document should be used to initiate tracking depends on the carrier. Real-time shipment location tracking • Geolocation updates are received every 15-minutes by default. Event status tracking and predictive estimated time of arrival • Receive enriched data with applied predictive analytics for accurate arrival, departure, ETA, and other logistical information. • View dynamic, predictive estimated time of arrival times for the next stop. ETAs dynamically change with every data point and are responsive to real-time conditions including traffic patterns, weather, and road conditions. • In the US, driver hours of service are factored into predictive driver idle time and further refine the accuracy of the dynamic ETA. • The information received from project44 may vary due to different carriers. 3.2 SAP Business Network, project44 LTL Visibility Add-On Feature Description Shipment tracking initiation • Initiate tracking with a carrier via o a SCAC code o a SCAC code and a bill of lading (BOL) number o a SCAC code and a master bill of lading number o a SCAC code and a progressive rotating order number -- 8 of 10 -- SAP Business Network, project44 Add-Ons 9 o a SCAC code and a pickup reference number and source and destination information. Milestone tracking • Receive milestone updates from project44 via APIs, such as arrival, delay, delivered, departure, and pick-up. • Milestone status updates are triggered as they occur. • The information received from project44 may vary due to different carriers. 3.3 SAP Business Network, project44 Ocean Visibility Add-On Feature Description Shipment tracking initiation • Initiate tracking of a container with o a SCAC code and a container number o a SCAC code, a bill of lading (BOL) number, and a container number o a SCAC code, a booking reference number, and a container number. Note that SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace supports tracking of a shipment (with a BOL number or booking reference number) that has only one container. Near real-time container tracking • Receive container level data from carriers and ports including location, and container status. • Port and terminal milestones are passed in near real-time as they occur. Note that the system tracks only port-to-port milestone updates and does not track on-road information. And the information received from carriers may vary. -- 9 of 10 -- SAP Business Network, project44 Add-Ons 10 3.4 SAP Business Network, project44 Air Visibility Add-On Feature Description Shipment tracking initiation • Initiate tracking of a shipment with a master air waybill (MAWB) number. Note that SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace supports tracking of a shipment that has only one flight. Milestone tracking • Receive milestone updates from cargo airlines, terminals, and aircraft tracking systems for the entire flight; such as airport of origin, in-flight and airport of destination milestones including shipping manifest, departure and arrival. • Receive predictive estimated time of arrival and flight exceptions. • Airport and terminal milestones are passed in near real-time as they occur. Note that the system tracks only port-to- port milestone updates and does not track on-road information. And the information received from cargo airlines, terminals, and air tracking systems may vary. Near real-time in-flight location tracking • Receive in-flight tracking data (including geo-location) via aircraft tracking systems connectivity. 3.5 SAP Business Network, project44 Parcel Visibility Add-On Note: Refer to Section 4 Geographic and Carrier Network Availability for additional information on standard and custom integration availability. Feature Description Parcel tracking initiation • Initiate tracking with a parcel tracking number, a carrier identifier, and source and destination information. Real-time parcel shipment tracking • Receive milestone updates via direct parcel carrier provider connectivity, such as available for pick-up, out for delivery, held, delivered, and missed delivery window. • Milestone status updates are triggered as they occur. • The information received from project44 may vary due to different carriers. -- 10 of 10 --

Introduction This document explains the required organizational and configuration steps for the consumption of project44 services through SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration as well as SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. For tracking-related scenarios, SAP recommends using SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. SAP is extending the reach of the SAP Business Network with project44 add-ons that provide real- time visibility content. These add-on services leverage the project44 multi-mode carrier network with its established connectivity to carrier and logistics provider systems, truck telematics, electronic logging devices, and so on. With the add-ons for project44 visibility services, SAP Business Network users can benefit from the availability of actual shipment execution insights, such as real-time shipment location and event status for full truck loads, and real-time milestone status for less than truck load shipments. This allows for a holistic view of both planned and actual shipment status, as well as automatic business event detection. project44 visibility content with business partner systems are available to SAP Business Network for Logistics users through supplementary, add-on licenses from SAP. SAP Business Network for Logistics provides tracking capabilities with the integration of project44 content, covered by the following add-ons: • SAP Business Network, project44 FTL visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 LTL visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 ocean visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 air visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 parcel visibility add-on • SAP Business Network, project44 rail visibility add-on* * No standard integration into SAP Business Network for Logistics available; custom integrations provided by project44, with proper implementation project scoping exercise. For more information on how to leverage the project44 add-ons for customer projects, see the slides for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace and project44. 2. Contact your project44 solution architect or customer success manager for onboarding details. • Setup of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace solution owner tenant as mentioned in the Onboarding chapter of the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. -- 5 of 10 -- 6 3. Configuring Connection Between Business Partners and project44 If all your business partners that use project44 services have LBN IDs, you are now ready to create a partner connection for each business partner. Creating a Partner Connection Specific to Each Service for Each Business Partner The partner connection with each business partner is created in the Configure Partner Connections app. When filling out the Create New Partner Connection dialog, the Network Partner Credential is the project44 credential that was added as an OAuth network partner credential in Section 3 above. The Service is the project44 service with which the business partner is connected. And so, the partner connection in the Configure Partner Connections app is created unique to each service and for each business partner ID type and alternate ID. Thus, you map the business partner, project44, service, and credentials together to route calls from SAP Business Network for Logistics to project44. -- 2 of 10 -- 13 In SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, one LBN ID of project44 is only mapped with one of its alternate IDs. If project44 asks you to use another one for a particular business context, you can update the alternate ID as required by providing the key-value pair information under Custom Headers. For more details, refer to Configure Partner Connections (freight collaboration) or Configure Partner Connections (global track and trace). -- 3 of 10 -- 14 6. Configuration and Testing for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration 6.1 Scenario Specific Configuration for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration With the B2B collaboration add-on, SAP Business Network enables the collaborative processing of FTL and LTL shipments with carriers. Note: For tracking-related scenarios, SAP recommends using SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. To differentiate different scenarios, SAP Business Network for Logistics relies on the following fields: • Transportation Mode – The transportation mode must be maintained in the freight order document (SAP Transportation Management standalone or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA) • Shipping type –The shipping type must be maintained in the freight order document (SAP Transportation Management standalone or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA) Based on the scenario, additional data is required from the SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system: a. Road FTL Tracking b. Road FTL Tendering & Subcontracting c. Road LTL Subcontracting d. Ocean tracking i. project44 has to mark the webhook as the default for ocean tracking scenarios. This has to be done one time with an email request to project44 [implementation@project44.com] FTL Tendering and Subcontracting Scenario As the first step in the tendering process, you – as an ordering party – create a request for freight quotation (RFQ) in your SAP TM system. When you publish this RFQ, the system sends the RFQ to SAP Business Network for Logistics. SAP Business Network for Logistics uses the data in the RFQ and creates a tendered shipment and a tender in project44 with the details of the origin, destination, truck type, and so on. The system creates the tender and tendered shipment. You can view the tendered shipment ID and tender ID in the document reference details of the RFQ. Note that the carrier for which you have created the RFQ must be a project44 carrier. This carrier can view this tender and send one of the following responses: • Accept • Accept with Rate Quote • Reject Once the carrier responds to the tender from the project44 system, SAP Business Network for Logistics creates a quotation based on this response and sends it to your SAP TM system. You can either award or cancel the quotation. -- 4 of 10 -- 15 When you accept the response, the SAP TM system sends a freight order for confirmation to the carrier in SAP Business Network for Logistics for subcontracting which in turn triggers a dispatch in the project44 system. When you send a cancellation, the system cancels the dispatch in the project44 system. When you cancel the RFQ, the system updates the status to cancelled in SAP Business Network for Logistics and deletes the corresponding tendered shipment and tender in project44. Response Required Scenario In your SAP TM system, you can control whether you require a response from your carrier before the carrier starts the dispatch. If you do not require a response from the carrier, the carrier begins the dispatch directly after the system creates an RFQ. If you require a response, then the carrier triggers the dispatch only after the carrier receives the freight order for confirmation. LTL Subcontracting Scenario In the LTL scenario, you have precontracted rates with the carrier. Hence the carrier starts the dispatch directly without any RFQs. Once you send the freight order from your SAP TM system, the system creates a shipment in project44, and the carrier begins the dispatch. Note that if you cancel the freight order in your SAP TM system, using the shipment ID, the system cancels the dispatched shipment in project44. -- 5 of 10 -- 16 SAP Business Network, project44 FTL visibility add-on All freight orders created in your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system can be tracked with the project44 add-on for FTL visibility. You must ensure that the carrier is assigned to the freight order and that the carrier is available in the project44 network. When the freight order is set to In Execution, it is sent to SAP Business Network for Logistics, and you can display it in the Track Freight Movement app. To use FTL tracking in SAP Business Network for Logistics, you must provide the following information in your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system when creating the freight order: • On the Stages tab: Source Location and Destination Location Also, either the Planned Departure Time or Planned Arrival Time must be in the future, and the arrival time must be later than the departure time. • On the Terms and Conditions tab: Shipping Type must be FTL (18). • On the General Data tab: Registration Country/No. Note: It is now possible in LBN for shippers to maintain a default shipping type in the Assign Codes app. So, when no shipping type is maintained for a shipment, the default value will be used, assuming that one has been maintained. The following events are supported for FTL: • Departure • Delay • Arrival at Destination • Expected Time of Arrival The reported events are sent to your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system and are visible on the Execution tab of the freight order. SAP Business Network, project44 LTL visibility add-on All freight orders created in your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system can be tracked with the project44 add-on for LTL visibility. You must ensure that the carrier is assigned to the freight order and that the carrier is available in the project44 network. When the freight order is set to In Execution, it is sent to SAP Business Network for Logistics, and you can display it in the Track Freight Movement app. -- 6 of 10 -- 17 To use LTL tracking in SAP Business Network for Logistics, you must provide the following information in your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system when creating the freight order: • Under the Stages tab: Source Location and Destination Location. The arrival time must be further in the future than the departure time. It is only possible for the departure time to be in the past. The arrival time, at least, must be in the future. Only one stage (with source location and destination location) is supported within the LTL process. Multiple stages are not supported. • Under the Terms and Conditions tab: Shipping Type must be LTL (17). • Under the Document References tab: Tracking can only start when the freight order that’s sent to the carrier includes the following in the Document Types for Business Transaction field: - PRO number: ‘BN’ (Consignment identifier, carrier assigned) - Bill of lading: ‘T50’ (Bill of Lading) Note: It is now possible in LBN for shippers to maintain a default shipping type in the Assign Codes app. So, when no shipping type is maintained for a shipment, the default value will be used, assuming that one has been maintained. The following events are supported for LTL: • Departure • Delay • Arrival at Destination The reported events are sent to your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system and are visible under the Execution tab of the freight order. SAP Business Network for Logistics receives the attachment related to an event from project44 as a URL for proof of pickup and proof of delivery. This URL will be accessible in the Track Freight Movement app. Additionally, the carrier can upload the attachments in the Freight Orders for Reporting app. SAP Business Network, project44 ocean visibility add-on All ocean bookings created in your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system can be tracked with the project44 add-on for ocean visibility. You must ensure that the carrier is assigned to the ocean booking and that the carrier is available in the project44 network. When the ocean booking is set to In Execution, it is sent to SAP Business Network for Logistics, and you can display it in the Track Freight Movements app. To use ocean tracking in SAP Business Network for Logistics, you must provide the following information in your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system when creating the freight order: If you want your carriers to upload attachments (proof of pick-up, proof of delivery) as part of the reporting, they can do so in the Freight Orders for Reporting app. -- 7 of 10 -- 18 • Under the Stages tab: Source Location and Destination Location. The locations should mandatorily have a UN/LOCODE maintained. This is later used to correlate the events reported by project44 onto TM planned events. Only one stage (with source location and destination location) is supported. Multiple stages are not supported. • Under the Terms and Conditions tab: Shipping Type must be FCL (full container load) or LCL (less than container load). • Under the Notes tab: A note with text type ‘Container ID’ must be created with the container ID of the ocean booking as the value. This is a custom text type. Note that you must separate multiple container IDs using commas. Note: It is now possible in LBN for shippers to maintain a default shipping type in the Assign Codes app. So, when no shipping type is maintained for a shipment, the default value will be used, assuming that one has been maintained. The system supports multiple events for ocean tracking. The following are some of the important events: • Departure • Arrival at Destination • Gate-In End • Gate-Out End • Loading End • Unloading End • Return The reported events are sent to your SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system and are visible on the Execution tab of the freight order. If you want your carriers to upload attachments (proof of pickup, proof of delivery) as part of the reporting, they can do so in the Freight Orders for Reporting app. -- 8 of 10 -- 19 6.2 Testing in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration Tracking Initialization – flow from SAP Business Network for Logistics to project44: Trigger a freight order out from TM system by setting Execution status or from ECC. The order will be pushed to the project44 system. Successful orders sent can be verified by logging in to project44. The URL to log in to project44 (https://na12.api.project44.com) would likely have been maintained by you in the Configure Partner Connections app. Event flow from project44: You may get events from the project44 system based on your requirements. Simulated events are supported only for Road FTL. For other scenarios, the testing has to be done manually with project44. Road FTL: The simulation of events must be requested from SAP with an incident categorized by component SBN-LBN-INT. To create an incident, open https://launchpad.support.sap.com/#incident/create. And this option is available only in the shipper test tenant. To test with real road orders, you might have to obtain the vehicle ID, license plate (truck) or driver mobile no. from project44 which are relevant for your carrier executing the orders. As mentioned above, these vehicle identifiers have to be maintained in the SAP TM or ECC system. This information has to flow from your system to SAP Business Network for Logistics to project44 during tracking initialization. When the initialization of tracking is done in the p44 system, the events will flow to your system. To monitor if the messages are being processed from SAP Business Network for Logistics as expected, you may view them in the Manage Integration Logs app (freight collaboration) or in the Track Freight Movement app (freight collaboration). Example of how to maintain Shipment in TM to maintain these identifiers: Road LTL: Simulation currently not available You must obtain a real (not test) Shipment identifier (T50 – Bill of lading, T67- Pro Number) from project44 and maintain it in the SAP TM system in the document reference section of the freight -- 9 of 10 -- 20 order or shipment. This information must be sent during initialization. After project44 receives it and when the actual event occurs, the events from project44 will be sent which can be validated using the Manage Integration Logs app. Example of how to maintain Shipment in SAP TM to maintain these identifiers: Ocean: Simulation currently not available You must obtain the real container ID (CONTAINER_ID) or Bill of lading (T50) from project44 and maintain it in TM freight order document reference or in global track and trace. This must be sent during track initialization. Based on the real ocean events, the events will be reported from project44. To monitor if the messages are being processed from SAP Business Network for Logistics as expected, you may view them in the Manage Integration Logs app (freight collaboration) or in the Track Freight Movement app (freight collaboration). -- 10 of 10 --

But if you want to integrate with your visibility provider in a user model or map user-defined fields in the standard model, do the following: 1. Launch the Manage Models app. Select a model. 2. In the Tracked Process / Events list on the left, you can see the tracked process event and event types. "value": [Action Required] Contact project44 for a valid House Air Waybill number or Master Air Waybill number. } ] } -- 9 of 10 -- 30 Sample Payload for Parcel Tracking { "altKey": [Action Required] Fill the alternative key in the following pattern: <scheme>:<party>:<system>:<type>:<id>. For example, "xri://sap.com/id:LBN#10000000001:QX8CLNT912:FT1_SHIPMENT:6100079522". "actualBusinessTimestamp": [Action Required] Fill in the current timestamp in UTC time format, for example, "2022-07- 01T00:00:00Z". “serviceAgentLbnId”: [Action Required] Fill in the data contributor’s identifier that you noted down in the prerequisite. Provide at least two stops: one for the point of departure and the other for the destination. Make sure all the locations mentioned in planned events are described here. { “stopId”: “locationId”: “locationType_code”: “ordinalNo”: }, …… ], “trackedObjects”: [ { "idType_code": "PACKAGE_EXT_ID", "value": [Action Required] Use a real parcel tracking number. } ] } -- 10 of 10 --
