Tips & Tricks with SAP Business Network for Logistics Saif Product and Topic Expert 2024 Sep 10 5:20 AM 12 Likes � 6,131 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Common queries/issues/know-hows in Business Network for Logistics and their resolution/explanation. 1. Technical IDs in APIs for Carrier Integration Technical ID in Consumer API for Subcontracting � � -- 1 of 10 -- Technical ID in Consumer API for Order Tracking The constant at the end, FC, indicates that the shipper is using Freight Collaboration for Tracking process. Carriers have to make sure that they report events with the exact technical ID for successful reporting. Technical ID in Consumer API for Booking Confirmation Technical ID in Consumer API for Order Tracking - Freight Booking Note that even though it is a Freight Booking, the technicalID uses Freight Order as the constant in the technicalId. TechnicalID in consumer API for Subcontracting TechnicalID in consumer API for Tracking - Freight Order TechnicalID in consumer API for Booking Confirmation TechnicalID in consumer API for Tracking - Freight Booking -- 2 of 10 -- Location ID in Consumer API for Order Tracking The Location Object Type constant can have different values depending on how a shipper configures the location master. Carriers should discuss with their shippers on possible values if relying on this field or if planning to report events with locationID. The Location code is shipper-specific code as mastered in their TM system. Technical ID in Consumer API for Order Tracking - Global Track and Trace Shipment The constant that indicates Tracking ID type differs for different tracked processes. The one above is commonly used as it is part of standard GTT model for Shipment Tracked process. If a customer uses a custom GTT model, this value could differ. The constant at the end, GTT, indicates that the shipper is using Global Track & Trace for the tracking process. 2. Exception occurred while creating or updating the location Sometimes you see this error when a shipper initiates a tracking request. The error is not specific but does indicate a possible problem. Location ID in consumer API for Tracking TechnicalID in consumer API for tracking - GTT -- 3 of 10 -- When a shipper initiates a tracking request, it is considered an A2A call and the system tries to update the location master data from TM into BNL. In this particular case, the shipper maintained a faulty UNLOCODE for the location. (3 characters as opposed to standard 5 characters). So, if this error is seen, shippers should check the location master. 3. No matching stop found while reporting events Carrier reports events via Tracking APIs and all the logs in BNL and CPI show it was successful. However, events are not seen reported against the Freight Order - Execution tab in TM. On checking srt_moni you will notice some error logs: As the error indicates, the shipper would have configured mandatory stopIDs for one or more events. This configuration is available in: Log in srt_moni -- 4 of 10 -- Sometimes shippers fail to convey this requirement to carriers that they have mandated stopIDs. BNL accepts events with or without stopID and reports it as planned or unplanned respectively. Carriers can choose to send stopIDs, locationID, or UNLOCODE/IATACode. If the carrier sends locationID or UNLOCODE/IATACode, BNL looks up the stopIDs and delegates it to TM. Usually carriers prefer to use UNLOCODE/IATACode as this is an industry-standard code and they do not have to deal with shipper-specific codes. 4. AccessToken fetch error One of the scenarios where this error is seen is when a Network Partner is involved and is responding to a Freight Booking confirmation via the API. You will notice that the API call itself gives a 200 OK and also gives a JSON response, but the error will be seen in Manage Integration Logs app as below. Freight booking API has fields, documentRecipientParty, senderParty, and recipientParty. The values in these fields differ in the consumer and provider calls, that the Network Partner makes. The error occurs when there is a mismatch in the value sin those fields resulting in token issues. To understand the usage, refer this blog. -- 5 of 10 -- 5. Attachments sent via APIs and application behavior. General Attachments: Can be sent by carriers via their confirmation call or even updates to confirmation call. This can be done until the orders go into execution by the carrier (In certain versions of TM or S/4HANA confirmation updates can be sent even while the order is in execution). These attachments can be seen by the shipper in the attachment section against the orders in TM. Carriers can also see these attachments in FOFC (Freight Order for Confirmation) app in BNL. -- 6 of 10 -- If any updates to confirmation are made while the order is in execution, the attachments are seen by the carrier in BNL, but they will not get processed by the shipper and cannot be seen in TM (only on certain versions of TM). Event Attachments: These are sent by carriers when reporting events via API. If attachments are sent against planned events, these are seen by the carrier in FOFC app. Shippers can also see these attachments in the TFM (Track Freight Movement) app in BNL and also in TM in the attachment section of each event. (Not in the general attachment section) (egs: DEPARTURE planned event) Attachments in Freight Order for Confirmation app Attachments shown in Track Freight movement app -- 7 of 10 -- If attachments are sent against unplanned events, these are seen by the shipper in the TFM app in BNL and also in TM in the attachment section of the event. The carrier cannot see the attachment sent for unplanned events in FOFC BNL app. 6. Timezones and event reporting Scenario UI/API FC GTT Location has timeZone and event reported without timeZone (API) API UTC reported time is converted to location Timezone UTC reported time converted to users local timezone. -- 8 of 10 -- Location has no timeZone and event reported without timezone (API) API Cannot create Locations without Timezone. UTC reported time converted to users local timezone. Location has TimeZone & event reported with a different timeZone (API) API UTC reported time is converted to location Timezone UTC reported time converted to users local timezone. Location has no TimeZone & event reported with a different timeZone (API) API Cannot create Locations without Timezone. UTC reported time converted to users local timezone. Location has TimeZone & event reported with a different timeZone (UI) UI UTC reported time is converted to location Timezone The time reported is considered to be for the timezone given and the user sees converted local Time Location has no TimeZone & event reported with a different timeZone (UI) UI Cannot create Locations without Timezone. The time reported is considered to be for the timezone given and the user sees converted local Time Unplanned Events with timeZone API Converts it to the time based on the timeZone sent and shows that timezone as well in the UI. UTC reported time converted to users local timezone. 7. invalid_client, Bad Credentials error while reporting events via API Sometimes when a carrier reports events the below error is seen. The credentials used are also correct. -- 9 of 10 -- This happens when the shipper is subscribed to FC but the carrier is reporting event with the technicalId suffixed with GTT or vice versa. egs: "xri://sap.com/id: LBN#10010005000:BS_SAP:FreightBooking:65000000550:GTT". To resolve this, the carrier has to make sure the right suffix is sent after discussing with the shipper. 8. FreightOrder with altKey does not exist error While reporting events, carriers sometimes see this error in the MIL app. The call itself to report events will respond with a 200 OK. This happens when the Order is not set to "Ready for Transportation Execution" by the shipper. To resolve this, ask the shipper to change the status of the Order, following which events can be reported. 9. JSON parse error: Cannot deserialize value of type com.sap.lbn.trackingservice.domain.input.generic.TransportationMode from String "04": not one of the values accepted for Enum class: [01, 03] This error is seen in MIL(Manage Integration Logs) app when a carrier is trying to report events via API. Error in MIL app -- 10 of 10 --

file://api-specs/split/Tips & Tricks wit.content: This is because the carrier is reporting the event to FC (Freight Collaboration) with transportMode as "04". As the error suggests, FC only supports reporting events for modes 01(Maritime) and 03(Road) only. However, GTT supports more modes in the reporting API. 10. Carrier Document references reported via tracking are not seen in TM Carriers while reporting events via API might also want to send some document references, however, due to a limitation in the TM interface- TransportationEventBulkNotification_In these document references cannot be mapped and chance cannot be pushed to TM. So, if a customer has a use case to receive document references while the order is in execution, they can consider sending an update to confirmation and pass the document references, so that it can be updated in TM against the order. 11. Location ID exists already while configuring Cloud Connector details BNL allows shippers to configure the technical user and the Cloud Connector Location ID in the System Connections app. This configuration can be reused across tenants if it's within the same Global Account. However if the tenants belong to different Global Accounts, BNL recognizes that the configuration already exists with the same location ID or the User and throws this error. -- 1 of 7 -- If it's in the same GA, you don't need to add it again, but rather reuse the config. If its in a different GA, then due to the current limitation that the configuration is not seen in the dialog above, you will have to check if there is any tenant that uses this config and either remove it if unused or configure a different locationID. 12. FC and GTT both for Tracking There are instances where a customer might use both Freight Collaboration and Global Track and Trace for Tracking depending on the capability of the carrier. The use case could be that a few carriers prefer to manually report events via the Freight Orders for Reporting app in carrier portal and a few carriers integrate to report events via GTT. When both are active, by default 2 consumer requests go out to the integrating carrier, one from FC and another from GTT (can be differentiated by the suffix to technicalId). To avoid this, the shipper can deactivate, /SCMTMS/CO_CPX_TORGNTRCKPR_OUT SOAP interface to avoid the FC consumer request from going out. However, they have to make sure the trackingRelevanceIndicator is active so that manual reporting in FC works. 13. Instance Authorization Check Failed in GTT while reporting events -- 2 of 7 -- This error is seen when a carrier is reporting events. The call itself would be successful, but the error could be seen in logs. This happens when the carrier LBN ID sent by the carrier does not match the serviceAgenLbnId maintained by the solution owner/shipper. In the particular case above, carrier is reporting at FU level and the FU did not have a serviceAgenLbnId maintained. 14. 108 Missing necessary connectivity configurations or CLOUD_CONNECTOR parameter not found in the Partner Directory for the partner ID (LBN ID) You might be familiar that customers are recommended to move to Multi-Cloud integration platform. However, we also caution not to delete old, Neo configuration in System Connections app. This error is seen, if a document was exchanged while having Neo config and then the Neo Config was deleted and the Multi-Cloud config was retained. This issue will not be seen on Newly created document objects which are exchanged on the same integration platform config. 15. SOAP messages not generated for SAP TM to BNL scenarios In some cases, after the setup, you may encounter that SOAP messages not are not getting trigerred and no logs are seen in srt_moni. In this case check for 2 customizations: 1. PPF setting for /SCMTMS/TOR - The right action profile should be maintained. -- 3 of 7 -- 2. Also make sure the right settings for integration and output options are maintained here for the scenarios that are failing. -- 4 of 7 -- Note 1: Before applying any of the above suggestions, make sure to perform a test in your non-production environment as each scenario could be different. Note 2: This blog will be updated regularly with more Tips & Tricks. If you are interested in receiving updates, make sure to subscribe and bookmark the blog. One of the best BN4L articles! zbaumann1 Discoverer 2025 May 01 9:30 PM This is super helpful! One question regarding attachments - here, you talk about attachments coming through to the shipper from the carrier. Is it possible for the shipper to attach files in API messages to the carrier in FC? Saif Product and Topic Expert 2025 May 02 5:55 AM @zbaumann1 Yes, that's possible. Typically, Shippers would attach files in the TM system, which is then passed on to the carrier via the consumer APIs. As an example, look at the attachment node in this spec for Subcontracting. You can explore other consumer APIs, which will have an equivalent attachment node, through which carriers can expect shipper's documents. -- 6 of 7 -- zbaumann1 Discoverer 2025 May 07 7:42 PM Thank you @Saif ! Would the inclusion of attachments in the freight order be automatic, or is there extra configuration required? EmilyZhang Associate EmilyZhang 2025 Aug 15 7:05 AM Super good blog! Learned a lot from this article. One question regarding stopID, one of the carrier asked if they can use a sequence of incremented numbers as the stopID used in the tracking event API. I can learn from this No.3 issue that the stopID is maintained in Shipper TM system and sometimes it will be failed to convey this to carrier, so carrier can send back the stopID, locationID, or UNLOCODE/IATACode. Which is already mapped with the stopID in TM system. But for my understanding, if they would like to use a sequence of incremented numbers as the stopID, they must have a integration layer to map the stopIDs with the stopID in TM system. It will make more efforts to the task. Is my understanding correct? Or would you please advise? -- 7 of 7 --

Understanding Network Partner Integration in SAP Business Network for Logistics Saif Product and Topic Expert 2024 Mar 28 9:52 AM 9 Likes  4,863 Views Edit SAP Managed Tags Introduction SAP Business Network for Logistics connects stakeholders across the logistics ecosystem for seamless digitalized collaboration and advanced insights. Logistics Network has a Business Partner persona termed as a Network Partner, which allows entities to partner with SAP’s Logistic Network, to provide their services as visibility providers or even bring their network and integrate with SAP Business Network for Logistics.   -- 1 of 10 -- As depicted above, Shippers can leverage the network by connecting with existing Business Partners and reduce integration efforts and costs through instant access to vast, ever-growing carrier networks and/or already established B2B connectivity. Network Partners can play multiple roles on the network. They can either be a visibility provider, connect with the carrier/shipper and provide near real-time updates/milestone events, or they can also extend the network with their ecosystem of carriers and facilitate services such as tendering, subcontracting, tracking and settlement. In this blog we will explore how subcontracting and tracking are supported by some of the network partners on the network. The Set-up Onboarding Network partners are onboarded to the network through an invitation process by SAP. If an organization intends to be a part of the network, they can write to sap.dsc.network.enablement@sap.com, describing their request. Network Partners can also be onboarded to the network proactively, through an invitation process by SAP based on a shipper's request. Once the setup is done, network partners will get access to a portal with administration applications to support user management and integration configuration, and additional applications if the network partner supports other logistics processes such as subcontracting. Portal Preview: -- 2 of 10 -- Note: Network Partners will also need to explicitly request for technical user a.k.a oauth client credentials. Once this is received, integration work can begin. Business Partner Setup and Configure Partner Connections This is an important step in establishing connectivity with the Network Partner over the network. There are 3 key aspects to consider: 1. Business Partner set up in Shipper’s Transportation Management. 2. SAP Business Network for Logistics set up with the Carrier and Network Partner. 3. Configure Partner Connection pattern used. Scenario 1: Network Partner offers subcontracting and other Logistics processes. There are multiple ways in which the solution allows the Business Partner set up. Approach 1: Onboard all carriers to BNL / use specific carrier LBN ID along with network Partner in CPC In this approach, the shipper onboards each carrier they do business with, from the Network Partner’s network to BNL, and establishes a connection with the Network Partner. -- 3 of 10 -- Things to consider: In this approach, the Orders/Bookings will be seen in the carrier’s portal, and it will also be forwarded to the network partner. Business Partner mapping and BNL setup Configure Partner Connections config -- 4 of 10 -- Since there is a Network Partner involved for the subcontracting process, there is very little value added to onboard the carrier, unless there is a specific Business Process that requires the carrier to be on BNL, which the network Partner cannot support. The carrier would be active on BNL for another shipper, so this unnecessarily creates orders in their tenant for which they are not expected to respond (Since Network Partners do it on their behalf). High effort to onboard all carriers as most of them might not be expected to use BNL for this shipper. This approach does not work for subcontracting via Freight Orders (Road). Example: Booking Consumer API - (Parties) Booking Confirmation Provider API - (Parties) -- 5 of 10 -- Approach 2: Connect with the Network Partner via a dummy/test carrier. In this approach, the shipper uses a dummy/test carrier and establishes a connection with the Network Partner. The setup is similar to approach 1, however here the LBN ID of the test carrier is mapped to carrier Business Partners in TM. In CPC, a specific connection is made as shown below. This routes orders to the test carrier and also forwards the order/booking to the network partner. Business Partner mapping and BNL setup -- 6 of 10 -- Things to consider: While this is okay for testing purposes, this does not add any value in production as orders/bookings are unnecessarily sent to the test carrier. This approach does not work for subcontracting via Freight Orders (Road). Example Scenario: Refer to approach 1. Approach 3: No carrier onboarding. Direct connection with Network Partner In this approach, the shipper maps the LBN ID of the Network Partner to the Carrier Business Partner in TM. And then, maintains the configure partner connects as shown below with Business Partner ID Type as, “Any LBN ID”. So, this config, allows the orders/bookings to be routed to Network Partner without any intermediate carrier. This enables direct routing of orders/Bookings to Network Partners without onboarding carriers to BNL. Configure Partner Connections Config -- 7 of 10 -- Things to consider: In this approach, there is no need to onboard carriers to Business Network for Logistics since the Network Partner interacts with the shipper on their behalf. TM can have multiple BPs per carrier based on business requirements and each of them would be mapped to Network Partner's LBN ID. Business Partner mapping and BNL setup Configure Partner Connections config -- 8 of 10 -- This is the only approach that is currently supported for Freight Orders subcontracting (Road) via Network Partner. Examples: Booking (Ocean/Air) Booking Consumer API: Booking Confirmation Provider API Freight Order (Road) Subcontracting Consumer API - (Parties) -- 9 of 10 -- Subcontracting Confirmation Provider API - (Parties) Scenario 2: Network Partner offers Tracking only. In this case, typically, shippers would execute subcontracting and other planning processes with a carrier or freight forwarder and would work with a network partner to receive tracking data/milestone events. The CPC application supports several ways to configure this scenario. 2 broad approaches are: Approach 1: A typical setup in TM would be that the shipper would have a BP representing the carrier or the LSP. The carrier or the LSP would also be onboarded to BNL along with the network Partner. Approach 2: The shipper would have a BP representing the carrier in TM. Carriers are not onboarded to BNL and the shipper receives tracking data from the Network Partner directly. -- 10 of 10 --

These options relate to how a Network Partner wishes to track and also how a Business partner is set up in TM by the shipper. Example 1: If a shipper wants to utilize a visibility provider’s tracking services for all their shipments and assuming that all the carriers the shipper is doing business with are not onboarded to BNL, but have an alternate ID in the shipper’s TM the below pattern can be used. -- 1 of 5 -- Example 2: If a shipper has more than one visibility provider and wants to utilize their tracking services for their shipments and assuming that all the carriers the shipper is doing business with are not onboarded to BNL, but they do have a specific alternate ID in the shipper’s TM, the below pattern can be used. Here, the shipper will have to identify a specific alternate ID using which they can distinguish the orders being sent to specific visibility providers. -- 2 of 5 -- Depending on the supportability of the network partner, appropriate service can be configured. Note: The payload examples shown above are only focused on sending and receiving the right business partner details. For detailed payload structure, refer the specifications for Freight Collaboration and Global Track and Trace. What should be the strategy with Network Partners? This blog shows the supportability of the solution, the different variations, and how the APIs behave when a Network Partner is involved. It is important to determine the right strategy that works for a shipper. To do that, the below questions need to be answered as part of designing the solution. 1. What scenarios are in scope for the Shipper-Carrier/LSP-Network Partner trio? -- 3 of 5 -- 2. Are all carriers/LSPs in scope also in scope of the Network Partner? Is there a direct B2B connectivity scenario with one or more carriers / LSPs? 3. How is the Business Partner setup done across the components - SAP TM / S/4HANA, SAP Business Network for Logistics, and in the Network Partner's system? 4. What are the common identifiers across these components? So, it is imperative to have a design that answers the above, and then a suitable approach or a combination of approaches can then be deployed. Version Date Description 1.0 2026-04-30 Initial version for SAP Integrated Business Planning 2605 Configuring Business Network Collaboration To integrate the SAP Integrated Business Planning solution with the SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution, you must configure the settings described in this document. The settings are applicable to both SAP Integrated Business Planning and the SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration buyer account. Integrating SAP Integrated Business Planning with SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration enables you to exchange product activity messages and product replenishment messages. You can monitor inbound and outbound messages in SAP IBP using the Message Monitoring Overview and Message Monitoring apps. To see the interfaces related to Business Network Collaboration, make sure that your user is assigned to the recipient ARIBA_RECIPIENTS. You can do this in the Assign Recipients to Users app. For more information, see Message Monitoring. Related Information More information about the SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution is available in the buyer administration guide, which you can access from the Help section of your SAP Ariba dashboard. Setting Up SAP Integrated Business Planning When a cXML message is sent to the SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution, the sending system must authenticate itself. The SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution offers two ways of doing this: either by using a client certificate or a “shared secret” password. The authentication method must be defined in both SAP Integrated Business Planning and SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration. Related Information  Note Until three months after the publication of a new release of SAP Integrated Business Planning, we publish regular documentation updates on the SAP Help Portal. If you use a local PDF copy or a paper printout of this document, make sure that you have the latest version. You can find it at http://help.sap.com/ibp2605.  Note The SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution is licensed separately. 5/9/26, 9:33 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Authentication Using Client Certificate Authentication Using Shared Secret Authentication Using Client Certificate To use a client certificate to authenticate your SAP Integrated Business Planning system, complete the following steps. 1. Create a Communication System To enable integration with the SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution, you need to define a new communication system. 2. Maintain Certificate Trust List To enable the integration with the SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution, you need to add the certificate you've downloaded from the Public Certificate Repository of SAP Business Network to the certificate trust list in SAP Integrated Business Planning solution (SAP IBP). 3. Create a Communication Arrangement You create a new communication arrangement based on communication scenario SAP_COM_0201 (Planning – Ariba Network Integration). 4. Download Certificate from Communication System To enable the integration with the SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution using client-certificate-based authentication, you need to download the certificate from the communication system you've created in the SAP Integrated Business Planning (SAP IBP) solution for this purpose. Later, you will upload this certificate in SAP Business Network. Create a Communication System To enable integration with the SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution, you need to define a new communication system. Procedure 1. In the Communication Systems app, enter a system ID and system name. These values can be defined freely. 2. As the host name, enter certservice-2.ariba.com. 3. In the Users for Outbound Communication section, click the plus icon (). 4. In the New Outbound User popup, set the authentication method to SSL Client Certificate and the client certificate to Client Default. 5. Save your changes. 6. Based on the host name used in the communication system, download the ECC certificate for it from the Public Certificate Repository of SAP Business Network at https://support.ariba.com/item/view/192337 and save it on your local machine. You've created a communication system and downloaded the correct certificate from the Public Certificate Repository of SAP Business Network at https://support.ariba.com/item/view/192337 . Procedure 1. In the Maintain Certificate Trust List app, click the plus icon () to add a certificate. 2. In the Upload Certificate popup, choose Browse, select the certificate you've downloaded, and choose Upload. 3. Supported cXML Versions The SAP Integrated Business Planning solution supports specific cXML versions for the messages that are exchanged between SAP Integrated Business Planning and the SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution. The following cXML versions are supported by IBP: ProductReplenishmentMessage: cXML version 1.2.035 ProductActivityMessage: cXML version 1.2.036 Security The SAP Integrated Business Planning solution always uses direct connectivity to connect to the SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution by executing the following actions: SAP Integrated Business Planning pushes cXML messages to SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration (synchronous) The Polling Agent of Ariba Network Integration 1.0 for SAP Integrated Business Planning fetches pending messages from SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration (synchronous) SAP Integrated Business Planning communicates with SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration solution through the HTTPS protocol, encrypting transmitted data. Authentication with Shared Secret Password The shared secret password is stored in the secure storage ABAP DB in SAP Integrated Business Planning. file://SBN/split/Buyer Value Prop - Test.content: Managed Gateway for Spend and Network – Test Central Supplier Integration SAP 2025 -- 1 of 10 -- 2 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Agenda • Overview of the Managed Gateway for Spend & Network • Test Central Overview • Data Flow through the Managed Gateway for Spend & Network • Integration Project Overview • Considerations for Using Test Central • Overall Process, Roles and Responsibility for setting up Test Central -- 2 of 10 -- 3 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Overview of the Managed Gateway for Spend & Network Managed Gateway for Spend & Network is the supplier integration engine for the SAP Business Network • Primary Goal: To simplify integration management across multiple relationships and significantly decrease the integration timeline • Secondary Goals: • Provide a growing list of industry and regional standards • Provide flexibility in the context of standardization via an extension framework • Provide self-testing capabilities using Test Central • Provide robust monitoring and transaction tracking Network Effect and Scale • Eliminate point-to-point integration • Eliminate linear resource scale • Reduce new relationship connection to days • 100% of relationships are integrated once initially connected • Increase user experience and satisfaction -- 3 of 10 -- 4 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Test Central Introduction Test Central empowers suppliers to independently validate their integration with the SAP Business Network—streamlining and accelerating project timelines. By enabling self-service testing, suppliers can confirm key aspects of their setup without direct involvement from buyers. Key Capabilities • Connectivity Validation Verify system-level connectivity with SAP’s Managed Gateway for Spend & Network to ensure a stable technical handshake. • Schema Compliance Confirm that transaction files are properly structured and conform to industry standards and SAP’s data specifications. • Document Choreography Document choreography allows suppliers to self-test against document flow leveraging buyer specific requirements. • Buyer-Specific Transaction Rules Ensure your transactions align with the unique business rules and configuration requirements of each buyer on the network. By leveraging these features, suppliers can perform thorough, realistic testing and confidently move forward in the integration process— without waiting on buyer-side interaction. -- 4 of 10 -- 5 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Data Flow through the Managed Gateway for Spend & Network -- 5 of 10 -- 6 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Data Flow through the Managed Gateway for Spend & Network -- 6 of 10 -- 7 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Integration Project Overview -- 7 of 10 -- 8 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Considerations for using Test Central • Test Central is enabled individually for each Buyer account • Suppliers can only access Test Central POs if they have a Trading Relationship with Buyer • Test Central Purchase Orders validate against Buyer’s SAP Business Network Configuration only, not a Buyer’s B&I or ERP configuration • Test Central Documents will have a “TC_” Prefix • Purchase Orders from Test Central are not copied into Buyer’s ERP • You will see “test data” in the SAP Business Network • Invoices will be rejected in Buyer’s ERP, or treated as non-PO invoices (if supported) -- 8 of 10 -- 9 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Overall Process, Roles and Responsibility for setting up Test Central Task IS/IA/DS Buyer Supplier Discuss Test Central Process R/A C I Agreement to use Test Central C R/A I Enable Managed Gateway in Production and Test Manage Profile >> Managed Gateway >> Enable Managed Gateway A/C R I Create Test Plan with Buyer based on type of POs in scope C R/A I Work with Buyer to create/select specific PO examples for each PO type to be used in Test Central R A I Prep the Purchase Orders for Test Central R/A I I Load the Purchase Orders in Test Central R/A I I Submit JIRA ticket for tracking Test Central Setup R/A I I Confirm Test Central Ready for Supplier Use R/A I C R = Responsible -The person or people who actually do the work to complete the task. They are responsible for action/implementation. Responsibility can be shared. A = Accountable (or Approver) -The one ultimately answerable for the correct and thorough completion of the task. Whoever is Accountable must sign off or approve work that Responsible provides. There must be exactly one Accountable person per task. C = Consulted-Those whose opinions are sought before a decision or action is taken. Typically, they are subject-matter experts, and there is two-way communication. I = Informed -Those who are kept up to date on progress or decisions. They receive information but are not necessarily consulted or responsible for the work. Communication is usually one-way. -- 9 of 10 -- 10 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Thank you. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide for BTP.content: SAP Business Network on BTP Buyer Administration Guide Generated on: 2026-05-06 06:48:45 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network for Procurement | Cloud Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/ARIBA_NETWORK/3c2416ce48504cfdb28ae12258c367c6?locale=en- US&state=PRODUCTION&version=RTC Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 1 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Introduction SAP Business Network on BTP for buyers introduce significant improvements to the site performance and operational efficiency. User experience of the Default Transaction Rules page, Notifications page, Email notifications, Invoice Details page, Purchase Order Details page, and System IDs and Endpoints page are enhanced.. SAP Business Network adapted SAPUI5 technology to improve user experience intuitiveness, navigation, content organization, and visual consistency across its applications. This release adapts SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) thus offering the ability to compose end-to-end business processes. This guide applies to: SAP Business Network SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Restrictions Experimental features are not part of the officially delivered scope that SAP guarantees for future releases. This means that experimental features may be changed by SAP at any time for any reason without notice. Experimental features are not for productive use. You may not demonstrate, test, examine, evaluate, or otherwise use the experimental features in a live operating environment or with data that has not been sufficiently backed up. The purpose of experimental features is to get feedback early on, allowing customers and partners to influence the future product accordingly. By providing your feedback (e.g. in the SAP Community), you accept that intellectual property rights of the contributions or derivative works shall remain the exclusive property of SAP. For more information, see Disclaimers and Other Legal Information. SAP Business Network on BTP for Buyers Buying organizations use SAP Business Network to find suppliers from which they want to purchase products or services and invite suppliers to form trading relationships. After the supplier accepts the invitation, the buying organization can look at the supplier’s customer catalogs and place orders. Buyers can also easily search for suppliers and their products on the network catalog irrespective of the trading relationship between buyer and supplier. Suppliers receive the orders and return invoices. As a buying organization, you can do the following on SAP Business Network: Search for or invite suppliers that have the products and services you need to form trading partnerships. Send orders and receive invoices. Run reports on your suppliers.  Note The functionality remains the same compared to previous release. This document covers only the user interface changes that are part of this release. This document does not cover all the features, but only those features that are part of early customer access (EAC). The document will be updated as and when new features are delivered. This document should be read in conjunction with the classic SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Enhancements from Legacy SAP Business Network Buyer User Interface The following enhancements are made to the user interface, compared to the legacy SAP Business Network user interface The Default Transaction Rules page is improved for better organization, search, and user experience. You can easily find and configure rules in a structured and intuitive layout. Enhanced the look and feel of the Notifications page, supported multiple email addresses up to ten, and improved the information displayed in the email notifications. Configured notification alerts for the following: send a notification to the requestor when orders are not delivered to private suppliers. send a notification when orders are undeliverable. Redesigned the Invoice Details page, Purchase Order Details, and System IDs and Endpoints page with a clear layout and organized information with various sections to improve visibility and easy navigation. Simplified the navigation steps: To access the newly designed default transaction rules page, click the Configure transaction rules tile under the Setup Actions section on the SAP Business Network homepage. To access the newly designed notification settings page, click the Configure email notifications tile on the SAP Business Network homepage. The Settings page is redesigned and the tasks are grouped under different tabs. The existing Account settings Manage Profile Business Application IDs and End Points (cXML and OData Setup) link is renamed to System IDs and End Points (Document Routing). The new Display Invoice permission is added to the Permissions section of the Create Role page. The View All link on the Purchase Orders tile and Invoices tile is hidden as the Analytics dashboard features are not available for the first release of the Next Generation Cloud Platform for buyers. Also, the Reports Analytics menu option on the SAP Business Network homepage is not available for buyers. The existing Inbox and Order Access permission is renamed to Display Invoice permission. The Display Invoice permission allows you to view invoice tiles and lists and access the invoice details page. Users with Inbox and Order Access permission will have the Display Invoice permission automatically. Inbox and Order Access permission remains as is, for backward compatibility. The Purchase Order Details page has been redesigned for easier reading and with the ability to search for relevant fields so buyers and suppliers can act efficiently. Account Administrator Responsibilities One person in your organization acts as the account administrator. The administrator is responsible for: Setting configuration options. See SAP Business Network Configuration. (Optional) Adding additional users to the account. See SAP Business Network Users and Roles.  Note If any of these tiles are not visible on the screen, click View All Tasks and then select the appropriate option. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 3 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- (Optional) Creating a test account for testing document flow with suppliers. See Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network. Getting Started with the SAP Business Network on BTP User Interface for Buyers The SAP Business Network application user interface for buyers has the following key components: 1. —The default page you see when you sign in to SAP Business Network. Click Home to access your home page from anywhere in the application. 2. Menu bar—Provides access to the various pages in the application. Some menus go directly to a page, while others provide a dropdown list of commands. The menu bar that you see may vary depending on your account’s entitlements. 3. Header bar—Provides helpful menus and commands. Use the dropdown on the top-left corner of the header bar to switch between different SAP Business Network web applications. Click the Account Settings icon to choose one of the following commands from the dropdown: ANID (Ariba Network ID)—A number that uniquely identifies your company on SAP Business Network. You might need this number to contact some support services. Company Profile—Review and manage your company profile on SAP Business Network. Manage Profile—Configure company settings such as locale settings, cXML settings, document routing preferences, system notifications, country/region-based invoice rules, payment settings, application end points, and quote automation rules. Settings—Access configurations for users and roles, self-service customization, the unit of measure master list, and your audit log. Also manage purge requests. Services—Manage your SAP Business Network services. Switch to Test Account—Change from production to test account modes. Saved Suppliers— View and remove suppliers that are saved. Admin can view the saved suppliers of all users. Announcements— Create and publish announcements. Logout—Exit SAP Business Network when you are done with your session. Click the Notifications icon to view the list of notifications for the logged in user. Click the Help  icon to navigate directly to the SAP Product Support Help Center. 4. Search bar—Provides capabilities to search for trading partners and network catalog products on SAP Business Network. Trading partners search. See Searching for Trading Partners on SAP Business Network. Discovery search. See Searching for Products in Network Catalog from Various Suppliers. This option is not available for RTC. 5. The Overview section displays the default tiles for your business role, or tiles that you have configured. 6. The Setup Actions section offers you recommended tasks and information resources for first time users. 7. The Highlights section provides widgets to show at a glance current information for your business activities.  Note 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Home Page You can navigate back to the SAP Business Network home page by clicking Home on the menu bar. Depending on your permissions, the Home dashboard can display the following content items. Only the Alerts and Messages content item is not permission-based. Notifications This content item displays important information about SAP Business Network, and reminders about your account. A yellow icon is shown for alerts that require your attention soon, and a red icon is shown for alerts that require your immediate attention. You can permanently delete any item that does not have an icon by clicking the trash can icon. Shipment Tracking. See Tracking Shipments from the Home Dashboard. Be sure to respond promptly to alerts in the Alerts and Messages content item. Overview Section The SAP Business Network Home page displays the all the configured tiles in the Overview section, by default. Depending on the configuration in Wrokbench, the tiles are displayed. You can reveal additional tiles with the More button. You can also configure which tiles are to be displayed from the Workbench. For more information, see The Workbench  Note The user interface now has the Feedback button on the right for users to share their feedback by means of a 1-minute survey. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 5 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Setup Actions The Setup Actions tile bar directs you to complete important configuration tasks for your account. For example, Update company profile, Upload company logo, Upload vendors, Manage active relationships, or Configure transaction rules, Add roles and users, or Configure email notifications. Click View All Tasks to view the list of actions that are not visible as tiles. Highlights Section The Highlights section displays role-based widgets. These widgets help you focus on important tasks, insights, key performance indicators, and benchmarks for your business. To customize the contents of your Home page, see Customizing Your Home Page Widgets. Shipment Tracking Widget The Shipment tracking widget allows you to quickly track the status of shipments. Enter a purchase order number and click Track to view shipment status information. Purchase Orders Widget The Purchase Orders widget shows you the total value of purchase orders you have created in each month of the selected year. Data is displayed in your preferred currency. Click View all to view additional details on the Analytics dashboard. You must have the Analytics dashboard access permission and the analytics functionality must be activated to access the Analytics dashboard. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 6 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Invoices Widget The Invoices widget shows you the total value of invoices you have received in each month of the selected year. Data is displayed in your preferred currency. Click View all to view additional details on the Analytics dashboard. You must have the Analytics dashboard access permission and the analytics functionality must be activated to access the Analytics dashboard. Supplier Enablement Widgets The Enablement summary, Full enablement progress, and Light enablement progress widgets enable you to quickly check the real-time enablement progress for your potential suppliers that are planning to use either an enterprise account or a standard account. To view the widgets, you must have at least one of the following permissions assigned to your account: Supplier Enablement Configuration, Supplier Enablement Program Administrator, Supplier Enablement Report Administration, or Supplier Enablement Task Management Update Company Profile The buyer company profile on SAP Business Network on BTP provides information about your company and its business. You can review and manage information in the Company Profile to help suppliers learn about your company. Your Company Profile page consists of the following sections: Section Description Quick Navigation Tabs Use the navigation tabs to go to different sections. About Us An overview of your company information is displayed at the top of your profile. You can edit details such as the company name, website, DUNS number, number of employees, year founded, annual revenue, legal form, address, and business type. Product and Services The data for Product and Service Categories and Receiving Locations are retrieved from SAP Business Network Discovery activities and cannot be edited. You can specify Industries for your company. Company Showcase You can showcase your company by adding marketing collateral in the form of attachments, customer presentations, case studies or external links. This helps suppliers learn more about your company.  Note Purchase order and invoice amounts specified in non-USD currencies are converted to USD for the purpose of aggregation using the currency exchange rate at the time the transaction document is created. The aggregated amount is further converted to your user-specified currency for display in widgets. Therefore, you may see a difference between the original amounts displayed in the workbench and the aggregated amount displayed in widgets. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 7 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Buyers with the Company Information permission can click Edit available at the top of each section to edit the information contained in the section. The options in the upper-right corner includes commands for viewing your public profile and obtaining a public profile URL. Edit the Company Profile Follow these steps to Edit your company profile: 1. Click Edit for the section that you want to edit information, enter or revise values as needed, and save your changes. 2. You can edit the following fields in the About Us section: Company Name—A name by which your company is to be known. DUNS Number—A nine-digit number issued by Dun & Bradstreet, Inc. to identify each corporate location of an organization. You can obtain a DUNS number or look up your company’s existing number on Dun & Bradstreet’s website, https://www.dnb.com . Address Information—Complete address of the company including country, region, city, along with the postal code. Short Description—A short description about your company. Long Description—A detailed description about your company. Business Type—Check the business types that apply to your company. Number of Employees—The approximate number of people who work for your organization. Founded—Enter the year when the company was founded in yyyy format. Revenue—Select a currency range. If you prefer not to state your annual revenue, scroll to the bottom of the list and select Contact company for information. Legal Form—Choose the type of business entity or legal status of your company from the dropdown. The list of values varies per country/region. Stock Symbol—A symbol that represents the stock of your company Legal Name—Name by which the company is legally registered. Website URL—Website URL of your company. 3. In the Product and Services section, you can edit only the Industries by selecting the industries your company serves. 4. In the Company Showcase section, you can either add an external link or an attachment. Choose Attachment to attach any files you want to make available to suppliers, such as customer presentations, case studies, and certifications. Choose External link to enter a URL and a description for each additional site. You must preface URLs with “https://”. For example: https://www.Your-Company.com/service. Additional Entities The Additional Entities page enables businesses to add organizational units—such as branches, affiliates, and subsidiaries—and manage business address types, including Sold From (supplier company address), Remit To (supplier remittance address), Sold To (buyer company address), and Bill To (buyer billing address), in one centralized location on their respective company profile. By centralizing address management, businesses ensure consistent and accurate address entities across invoicing, payments, and shipments. For more details, see Understanding Additional Entities 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 8 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Understanding Additional Entities In addition to showing your organizational structure, Additional Entities simplify address management. Instead of maintaining multiple addresses separately, you can centrally manage all address types—Sold From and Remit To (when acting as suppliers), or Bill To and Sold To (when acting as buyers). This helps ensure address information remains consistent and accurate across business processes like invoicing, payments, and shipments. When adding an entity, you’ll enter key details like the legal name, address, tax information (if applicable), and the network collaboration function—which defines how the entity participates in transactions. Available functions include: Sold From – A supplier entity selling goods to buyers. Remit To – A supplier entity where buyers remit payments after receiving an invoice. Bill To – A buyer entity to whom suppliers issue invoices. Sold To – A buyer entity that receives goods from suppliers. Assigning the correct function ensures addresses are used appropriately in transactions, improving operational accuracy and efficiency. How Additional Entities Are Used When Acting as Suppliers Country Configuration (formerly Legal/Regulatory Profile): In countries that require registration with local tax authorities for electronic invoicing, you must set up a country-specific configuration in SAP Business Network. During setup, your organization’s address and tax details are pulled from Additional Entities based on the selected country and company name. You must first create and maintain this information in Additional Entities before the country configuration can be created. Remittance and Bank Information Setup: You can link your Remit To address with specific remittance preferences and bank details. These are automatically included in invoices to ensure buyers receive accurate payment instructions. Invoice Creation: When creating invoices, you’ll select from a predefined list of addresses—Sold From, Remit To, Sold To, and Bill To— maintained under Additional Entities. This ensures that invoices use consistent and validated address data. When Acting as Buyers Document Routing Configuration: If you use multiple ERP systems, you can define routing rules that reference Bill To addresses maintained in Additional Entities. These rules determine which ERP system or business unit should receive and process documents like purchase orders or invoices. Managing Sold To Entities Prerequisites 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 9 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context Previously, the default Sold To address was created or set as default in: Account Settings Manage Profile Default Transaction Rules Now, all address creation, editing, and default assignment are centralized in: Company Profile Additional Entities You can still access legacy pages, but they now redirect or provide links back to the Additional Entities page to manage Sold To data. Procedure Create a Sold To Entity 1. In the Additional Entities section, click Create. 2. On the Create New Additional Entity page, provide the following information: Company and location information: Company (Legal) Name Contact Name Country/Region, City, State, Postal Code Address Lines 1-3 Network collaboration information: From the Functions dropdown, select Sold To. (Optional) Check Make this address default. Identification information Enter an Internal ID, which is used to recognize the entity within your organization, such as a company code, address ID, or other internal reference. Usage information: a. Select one or more categories. Categories define the context and purpose of the identifiers you are about to enter. Common categories include: GlobalUniqueID: For globally recognized identifiers like DUNS or Global Location Numbers (GLN). TaxID: For country-specific tax identification numbers (VAT ID, GST ID, for example). Peppol: For organizations using the Peppol e-invoicing network (Peppol ID, Leitweg ID, for example). The categories you select determine which sections and fields are shown below. b. Fill in the required identifiers for each category.  Note The first Sold To address you create is automatically set as the default. Its default status can’t be changed directly. To update the default, overwrite the existing default address with new values. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 10 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --
