file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide for BTP.content: This permission… Enables a user to… Transaction Data Export for Deleted Data Download ZIP files of deleted transaction documents. Grants access to this area: Quick Links Deleted Transactions Transaction Monitoring Visibility Access the Transaction Document Report job type for Upload/Download without having the administrator role. Grants access to this area: Quick Links Upload/Download User Administration Create, delete, and manage users and roles. Grants access to this area: Manage Users Create and Publish Announcements Create and publish announcements. Grants access to this area: Account Settings Manage Announcements Quick Links Create Announcement Multifactor Authentication Multifactor authentication is a two-step verification process where you are required to authenticate yourself a second time using a time-based verification code. As compared to the single step authentication process, the multifactor authentication process provides enhanced security. If multifactor authentication is enabled for critical fields, you are required to perform the two-step verification process while attempting to update the values of critical fields such as email addresses, phone numbers, remittance information and so on. With multifactor authentication enabled for sign in, you are required to perform the two-step verification process to sign in to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network administrators can now enable the following functionalities for users in their organization by selecting the desired users from a table: Require multi-factor authentication for critical fields Require multi-factor authentication for login Prerequisites  Note This permission is for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer accounts only.  Note This permission is visible only to users assigned the Administrator role.  Note Only buyer administrators with the required permissions can disable multifactor authentication for sign ins. SAP Business Network does not prompt newly created users to complete the multifactor authentication setup immediately after a successful sign in. New users are recommended to set up multifactor authentication for sign in after they change their initial password. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 91 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- When multifactor authentication is enabled for your organization, you must install an authenticator application such as SAP Authenticator from iTunes (for iOS devices) or from Google Play (for Android devices) in your hand-held devices to generate a time-based verification code (also called time-based one-time password). The time-based verification code setup is also compatible with third-party authenticators such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator. Setting Up Multifactor Authentication (Buyer User) Context You can set up multifactor authentication after your SAP Business Network administrator has enabled the feature. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Personal Information. The Personal Information page appears. 3. Below the User Name text box, click the Set up multi-factor authentication link. The Set up Multi-factor Authentication page appears. 4. Download and install SAP Authenticator or any compatible authenticator application such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator on your hand-held device. 5. Open the authenticator application that you have installed on your mobile device and do either one of the following: a. Scan the QR code displayed on the page, and enter the code in the Time-based Verification Code input box, or b. Enter the secure key displayed on the page in the Time-based Verification Code input box. 6. Click Done. SAP Business Network Roles A user with the Administrator role can create a role with certain permissions and assign the role to a buyer user. A role defines a user function within SAP Business Network, such as Purchase Order Generator. Each role has a unique name and set of associated permissions that specify what users who are assigned to the role can see and do in SAP Business Network. A role can be assigned to any number of users. Using the Administrator Role After you complete registration, SAP Business Network creates a single default role named Administrator. The Administrator role is automatically linked to the user name and sign in that you entered during registration. The Administrator role should be assigned to the individual at your organization who is responsible for setting configuration options, managing supplier relationships and contacts, and maintaining the account over time. The account administrator serves as the primary point of contact for users with questions or problems. As the SAP Business Network account administrator, you control who can sign in to your organization’s SAP Business Network account and which areas of the service each user can access. To do this, you create roles and then add users. As a best practice, create roles that reflect the way your company does business to prevent confusion for your account users and maximize the efficiency of your team once roles are in place. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 92 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Only one SAP Business Network user can be assigned to the Administrator role. You cannot modify this role, but you can assign it to another user. The account administrator can assign user management capabilities to non-administrator buyer users, called user administrators. For more information, see the following topics: Transferring Administration Ownership Assigning User Management Capabilities to Users SAP Business Network Predefined Roles Predefined roles are visible only in accounts that were created before roles and permissions were introduced on SAP Business Network. If you registered with SAP Business Network after roles and permissions were implemented, Administrator is the only predefined role. To minimize disruption to these older users, SAP Business Network provides a small set of predefined roles to be used as templates for custom roles. SAP Business Network assigned the Full Access role to all preexisting users when it introduced roles and permissions. Administrators for these older supplier accounts should review the predefined roles and their permissions and consider using them as the basis for custom roles. The predefined roles are listed in the following table: This Role… Grants a User Access To… Administrator All areas of the account, including Settings Users and test account management Catalog Manager Catalogs Customer Catalogs Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Catalog Service Full Access All areas of SAP Business Network, except areas that are reserved for administrators Purchasing Manager Give access to incoming and outgoing transaction documents and the following configuration pages: Account Settings Manage Profile Default Transaction Rules Account Settings Manage Profile cXML Setup Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications (transaction-related notifications only) Vendor Manager Supplier Enablement Current Relationships Supplier Enablement Contacts Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Supplier Account Settings Company Profile Product Manager Catalogs Network Catalog Product Approver Catalogs Network Catalog The Administrator role includes all available permissions. These permissions grant the Administrator role access to all areas of your SAP Business Network account. Setting Up Multifactor Authentication Using a New Device (Buyer User) 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 93 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Context When you change your mobile device, you can reset the multifactor authentication that had been configured using your old device. Using the verification code from the old device, you can set up multifactor authentication on your new device. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Personal Information. The Personal Information page appears. 3. Below the User Name text box, click the Reset multi-factor authentication link. 4. Enter the verification code from your old mobile device. 5. Set up multifactor authentication again, using a new QR code on your new mobile device. 6. Click Done. Deleting a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can delete roles that they no longer need. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. You have informed users about role changes that will affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. No users can be assigned the role you want to delete. To change a user to another role, see Reassigning Users to a Different Role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, you can perform a search for the role you want to delete, if necessary. Search for a Permission using the search filters. Or, scroll down and locate the role you want to delete. 3. In the Actions column of the roles results table, click the Delete  icon. Results SAP Business Network deletes the role and returns to the Users page. Changing a User’s Role and Resetting the Password You can select a different role for an existing user or reset the password. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 94 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Context Users can forget their sign in information if they do not sign in to SAP Business Network regularly. SAP Business Network provides a secure and relatively quick way for users to recover sign in information. However, even with this process in place, loss of user names and passwords can cause frustration and lost productivity for you and your users. If you do not want to reset a user’s password, instruct him or her to click Forgot Your Password? on the SAP Business Network Sign In page. After a user submits a user name, SAP Business Network Accounts Services sends the user an email containing steps to reset the password. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Cick Edit for the user whose password you want to reset. 4. Do one of the following: To change a user’s role, select a different role in the Role Assignment section and click Save. To reset the user’s password, click Reset Password. 5. Click Save. SAP Business Network returns to the Users page. Results If you reset the user’s password, SAP Business Network sends an email to the user containing a new randomly-generated password. The password update takes effect immediately. Managing Multifactor Authentication for Users Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage User Authentication. 3. Select the desired multifactor authentication check boxes. 4. Select the users (from the table) for which you want to manage multifactor authentication. 5. Click the following buttons depending on what you wish to do: Enable: Enables multifactor authentication for the selected users. Disable: Disables multifactor authentication for the selected users. Reset: Resets multifactor authentication for the selected users. These users must either enter the secure key displayed on the user interface, or scan a new QR code during their next sign in session. Send Email Reminder: Sends a reminder email to the selected users. Unlock: Unlocks the selected users. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 95 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- 6. Click Save. Requesting Removal of Personal Data for a Buyer User SAP Business Network users can request the administrator for their account to remove their personal information from the system. If your request is approved, your personal information is removed, and you can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites If you are currently assigned the Administrator role for your account, you can't perform this task until after you transfer the Administrator role to another user. See Transferring Administration Ownership. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Manage Profile. 2. Click Personal Information. The Personal Information page opens. 3. In the Personal information usage section, check the Request to remove my personal information option. 4. Click Save. Results The administrator is notified of your request, and they can approve or reject it. Assigning User Management Capabilities to Users The current account administrator can create a role with the User Administration permission and assign it to non-administrator buyer users, called user administrators. User administrators can perform administrative functions, such as tasks relevant to user management and buyer user access to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles page, click the  icon. 3. Enter a distinctive name for the role. Enter a description to record your intentions for this role. 4. Go to the last page of permissions, and select the User Administration permission. 5. Click Save. 6. Click Manage Users. 7. On the Manage Users page, select the user you want to assign the user administrator role to. 8. Choose Actions Edit . 9. In the Role Assignment area of the Edit User page, select the user administrator role you created. 10. Click Save. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 96 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Transferring Administration Ownership The current account administrator can reassign ownership of the SAP Business Network account to another person. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Context Account administrators can quickly and easily transfer the Administrator role to another user. After the Administrator role is transferred to a new user, SAP Business Network sends a notification to the new account administrator, alerting them that they now have the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Select the user you want to transfer the Administrator role to. 4. Choose Actions Make Administrator . The Assign a Role page opens. 5. Select a new role for your account, and click Assign. Updating Users Using an Excel Template Account and user administrators can update multiple users using an Excel template. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Click the Upload Users button on the Manage Users page. 4. Click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 5. Click the Download template link on the Upload File dialog box. Alternatively, if you already have an uploaded Excel template you can reuse it by selecting the download icon ( ) in the File column on the Upload Users page 6. Open the Excel template and fill out or update the required fields and click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 7. Click the Browse button on the Upload Files dialog box, choose the Excel template from your computer and enter a descriptive name. 8. Click the Upload button.  Note If you do not know who the account administrator is, contact SAP Business Network Support. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 97 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- 9. Click the Refresh Status button on the Upload Users page and wait until it shows status Completed. If the status is Completed With Errors or Failed, select the download icon ( ) in the Log column to see the reasons for errors and to correct them. 10. Click the Done button. This opens the Manage Users page where you can see the updated users. SAP Business Network Users Access to a buyer account is secured with individual user identities and levels of permissions. A user is an SAP Business Network sign in (user name and password) that enables one individual in your organization to sign in to your account. The administrator adds users to the SAP Business Network account and assigns each user exactly one role, which typically corresponds to the user’s real-world job responsibilities. Best Practices in Managing User Accounts When the administrator of an SAP Business Network account creates users and assigns roles, it is mandatory that the administrator assigns a unique user name with an appropriate assigned role for each individual who needs to access the account. Users must not share their user name or password with other users. This is important for SAP Business Network and your company in managing data privacy and integrity on SAP Business Network. For security, account administrators and users who have PCard access but are not the PCard owner are required to update their password every 90 days. As a best practice, users should not share their secret question and secret answer. To ensure your organization and users have secure accounts on SAP Business Network, create individual user accounts for different roles in the organization. By default, add one role per user. Users can have multiple related roles, depending on the tasks assigned to the user. How Roles Control User Interface Access Every user can see the Configuration Personal Information area, which contains basic contact information and a preferred language setting for that specific user. Beyond that, the only areas that a user is permitted to see are those allowed by their role permissions. For example, if the administrator created a role that included the Contact Administration permission, a user assigned to that role could see only the Configuration Personal Information area and the Supplier Enablement Contacts area of your SAP Business Network account. While users can update their own personal information, the administrator is responsible for overall user maintenance, which includes deleting users or reassigning user sign ins when individuals leave the company, and resetting user passwords. Related Information SAP Business Network Roles Deleting a User If a user has left the company, you can delete the user to prevent its further use to access SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 98 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Context When an employee leaves the company or changes jobs and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account, the administrator should either delete the user or reassign the user’s sign in to another individual. If you want to retain the user’s setup and data, reassign the sign in. See Reassigning a User Sign In. If you want to delete the user’s setup and data, perform this procedure. User deletion is permanent. There is no way for SAP Business Network or you to recover a deleted user. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Search for the user you want to delete. See Creating a User for the steps to perform. 4. In the user results table, check the checkbox for the user you want to delete. 5. In the Actions column, click the Delete  icon in the row of the user you want to delete. Results SAP Business Network deletes the account and refreshes the page content. It does not maintain a record of deleted users. Prevention of Manual Sign In by SAP Business Network Buyer Users Buyers whose SAP Business Network accounts are configured for single sign-on (SSO) corporate authentication can prevent users from signing into the SAP Business Network manually, outside of the single sign-on (SSO) configuration. This SAP Business Network feature is applicable to all buyers who use single sign-on (SSO) corporate authentication for accessing the SAP Business Network. This feature does not affect SAP Business Network suppliers. Preventing users from signing in manually enhances the security of SAP Business Network accounts using single sign-on (SSO) authentication. When this feature is enabled, users cannot sign in to the SAP Business Network in any way other than through single sign-on (SSO). They cannot sign in by entering the URL buyer.ariba.com directly into a browser. Even users with the Administrator role cannot sign in manually. Users who try to sign in manually will receive an error message that says The user name and password pair you entered was not found. If this feature is not enabled, users can use their user name and password to manually sign in to the SAP Business Network. Enabling This Feature This feature is disabled by default. To enable this feature, ask your Designated Support Contact to log a case (formerly Service Request). An SAP Business Network Support representative will follow up to complete the request. Enabling the feature involves SAP Business Network setting an option in the single sign-on (SSO) configuration for the SAP Business Network account to disable manual sign in. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 99 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Enabling Multifactor Authentication for Sign In Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage User Authentication. The Multi-factor Authentication User Setup page is displayed. 3. Select the box Require multi-factor authentication for sign in. 4. Click Yes in the dialog box that appears. 5. Select the desired users by checking the boxes against their user names from the table, and click Enable. Configuring Retention Period for Revoked Users in Your Organization As an administrator, you can configure the retention period of user data for revoked users in your organization. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Users . 3. Click Manage User Deletion. 4. Enter a retention period between 1 and 999 in the Retention period in months box. The data of all revoked users in your organization will be retained for a period that you configure here. 5. Click Save. After the retention period is over, user data will be deleted permanently from SAP Business Network. You cannot act upon a revocation request unless you configure the retention period first. Revoked users' data is available for you to view for purposes such as regulatory audits. All the data of an organization (including users' data - both revoked as well as deleted) is deleted when an organization is permanently deleted. Modifying a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can edit a role's name, description, and assigned permissions.  Note Only the selected users are enabled for "multifactor authentication for sign in". If you do not select any user from the table, none of the users in your organization will be enabled for multifactor authentication. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 100 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide for BTP.content: Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. You have informed users about role changes that can affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, search for a Permission using the search filters, or scroll down and locate the role you want to modify. 3. In the Role Name column of the search results table, select the role you want to modify. 4. Check Show me all the available permissions and select the permissions you want or uncheck the permissions you don't want for that role. 5. Choose Save. SAP Business Network applies your changes to all users assigned to the role. Changes take effect for each user at their next sign in. Reassigning Users to a Different Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can change the role assigned to users. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. You have informed users about role changes that will affect them.SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, scroll down to the role you want to investigate. 3. Click the role in the Role Name column. 4. Scroll down to the Assigned Users table. 5. Using the checkboxes, select the users you want to move to another role. 6. Click Move to another role. 7. Click Save to return to the Manage Roles page. Approving or Rejecting a Buyer User's Request to Remove Their Personal Information As an administrator, you can approve or reject a user's request to remove their personal information from SAP Business Network. If you approve the request, the user's personal information is removed, and they can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 101 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. In the Users table, select the user who requested revocation of access. In the AN Access column, the value is Revocation request pending. 4. Click Actions, and choose one of the following actions: Accept Revocation Request Reject Revocation Request 5. Click OK. SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass Description This section covers onboarding an SAP Fieldglass supplier on SAP Business Network and vice versa. Buyers can onboard the suppliers either in SAP Fieldglass or SAP Business Network ensuring unified user experience for suppliers across SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network. If SAP Ariba Buying that is part of SAP Ariba Procurement solutions uses SAP Fieldglass (restricted access) for service procurement, buyer cannot onboard a supplier on SAP Fieldglass. The buyer can leverage the SAP Business Network onboarding feature to onboard and manage suppliers. For more information on buyers and suppliers connection, see the How Buyers and Suppliers Connect section in the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide. Onboarding SAP Business Network Supplier on SAP Fieldglass  Note Buyer can invite a supplier on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass only if the buyer exists on both. Only the active supplier accounts can be integrated. Synchronization of supplier profile is not supported between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. After the supplier registers in SAP Fieldglass by approving the collaboration type as Service and establishes a connection with the buyer in SAP Fieldglass, a situation may arise wherein the buyer deletes the relationship or the supplier rejects the approved releationship in SAP Business Network. In that case, the relationship in SAP Fieldglass continues and it is not automatically deleted, you must manually deactivate the relationship. Only one remote external identity provider (IDP) is allowed to login to SAP Business Network. Therefore, while connecting to SAP Fieldglass, use only the SAP Fieldglass IDP. The Copy SES option on SAP Business Network is not supported in this integration scenario. Creation of service sheets from Orders tile is not supported for SAP Fieldglass suppliers. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 102 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Description This section explains onboarding a SAP Business Network supplier on SAP Fieldglass, which is mandatory in the following situations: If a buyer that uses SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass sends a purchase order containing serviceable items, to a supplier in SAP Business Network If a buyer uses SAP Ariba Buying to manage service orders, then the buyer can leverage the SAP Business Network onboarding feature to onboard and manage suppliers. The suppliers on SAP Business Network can create a new account or use the existing account and link that to a new or existing account on SAP Fieldglass. SAP Ariba Buying that is part of SAP Ariba Procurement solutions uses SAP Fieldglass (restricted access) for service procurement. After the supplier is registered on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass, the supplier can use the SAP Business Network portal to view the service orders and navigate to SAP Fieldglass to manage the statement of work. If the buyer has a trading relationship with a supplier, then they can send a service collaboration request to the supplier to onboard them on SAP Fieldglass. The supplier can approve or reject the request. On approval, the supplier gets a notification to either create a new account or use an existing account on SAP Fieldglass. When the supplier creates a new account or uses an existing account, the supplier account in SAP Business Network is linked to the supplier account in SAP Fieldglass and single-sign-on is enabled. Prerequisites Ensure that the buyer exists on both SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. Ensure that the buyer has a trading relationship with a supplier. Only then the buyer can send a service collaboration request to the supplier to onboard them on SAP Fieldglass. Ensure that the buyer Fieldglass ID (FGID) is included in SAP Business Network in the Fieldglass configuration section. In the buyer profile, ensure that the Enable Supplier Onboarding option is selected while configuring SAP Fieldglass. Restrictions Buyer can invite a supplier on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass only if the buyer exists on both the applications. Synchronization of supplier profile is not supported between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. There is always one-to-one link between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass account. User Interface Changes for Buyer The Configure Fieldglass Routing URL screen includes a new field Fieldglass ID. Purchase Order Invoices Through SAP Business Network, buyers and suppliers can seamlessly integrate their invoicing processes on a single network. By enabling the appropriate invoice rules, buyers can allow suppliers to: Create standard invoices against purchase orders. Create non-PO invoices and credit memos. Create invoices against contracts by accessing the customers’ contract collaboration sites. Invoice Routing Status Level Invoice routing status levels describe invoice validation against your invoicing rules. Status Level Definition Obsoleted The supplier canceled the invoice. Queued SAP Business Network received the invoice but has not processed it. Sent SAP Business Network sent the invoice to a queue. The invoice is awaiting pickup by you. Acknowledged Your application has acknowledged the receipt of the invoice. Unassigned Applies only to ICS invoices (invoices sent from an invoice conversion service provider). Indicates an unknown supplier. SAP Business Network either did not find an order matching the invoice or cannot verify the supplier ID. For information about invoice conversion, see the SAP Business Network Guide to Invoice Conversion. Invoice Details Page The Invoice Details page is redesigned to enhance usability and information clarity. The layout and label clarity are improved for easy navigation and understanding. Information is organized into various sections to improve visibility. You can navigate directly to the required sections of the details page by clicking on the respective tabs at the top of the Invoice Details page instead of scrolling through the page to search for the  Note If your supplier’s account is suspended, you cannot receive invoices or other incoming documents from this supplier. SAP Business Network displays a message at the top of the supplier’s basic profile if their account is suspended. SAP Business Network suspends your supplier’s account for failure to remit payment for network transaction service fees. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 117 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 9 -- required information. Clicking a line item on the Invoice Details place displays the selected line item details. All the existing functionalities like Resend invoice, Download attachment, Download cXML, and Print are now available on the new Details page. Types of Invoices Invoice type Description Material Also called purchase order-based, these are standard invoices routed through SAP Business Network that do not contain any service lines (lines that require a service sheet). Service Another type of standard invoice, these are based on service sheets that suppliers create from service lines in service purchase orders routed through SAP Business Network. Service sheets and service invoices can include both services and material goods. Lean Service These are invoices routed through SAP Business Network. A single invoice can be created for all the Lean Service line items in a purchase order. Limit Service These are invoices routed through SAP Business Network. A single invoice can be created for all the Limit Service line items in a purchase order. Limit Order A Limit Order line item is defined as the fulfillment of a service or material delivery at a price limited by a predetermined amount within a time period specified by the buyer. These are invoices routed through SAP Business Network. A single invoice can be created for all the Limit Order line items in a purchase order. Non-PO These invoices reference purchase orders that were not routed through SAP Business Network. Non-PO invoices also allow suppliers to invoice purchase orders that have expired and been deleted, or to generate an invoice that does not have a corresponding purchase order. Non-PO invoices can be issued to a buying organization even if the supplier doesn’t already have an active trading relationship with the buying organization. In that case, the buyer provides the supplier with buyer customer code to allow sending a non-PO invoice (quick enablement through invoice). Credit memo A credit memo represents an amount owed to a buyer by a supplier, typically from an earlier transaction such as a purchase order or a contract invoice. The amount due is a negative number. There are four types of credit memos: PO-based header level credit memos, PO-based line-level credit memos, non-PO credit memos, and dynamic discounting credit memos. Line-level credit memos can be based on a change in quantity or a price adjustment (price decrease). Line-level debit memo Line-level debit memos represent an amount owed to a supplier by a buyer from an earlier transaction. Line-level debit memos are always due to a price adjustment (price increase). 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 118 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 9 -- Invoice type Description Blanket purchase order based A blanket purchase order (BPO) is a type of contract that buyers create that forms an agreement to spend a specific amount with a supplier for critical items or services. If the blanket purchase order is used to purchase specific items (item level BPO), and the customer has not enabled their invoicing site or the BPO for collaborative invoicing, then suppliers can create an invoice directly from the BPO the same way as they can from a regular purchase order. If the BPO is a customer catalog, supplier level or commodity contract, and the buyers are either not using an SAP Ariba invoicing solution, or are using an SAP Ariba invoicing solutions for which collaborative invoicing has been disabled, then suppliers can view the BPO, but must create a non-PO invoice with the contract ID as reference to invoice against the BPO. Contract-based A buying organization using an SAP Ariba invoicing solution can allow collaborative invoicing for suppliers. In that case, suppliers punch in to the buyer’s invoicing solution to either create the entire invoice in the buyer’s invoicing site, or they punch in to retrieve the contract information and add items from the contract to the invoice, but finalize the invoice in and submit the invoice from the SAP Business Network - just as a standard invoice. If suppliers create the entire invoice in the buyer’s invoicing site, SAP Business Network compliance rules do not apply, since the supplier is subject to the invoicing processes and rules configured for the buyer’s invoicing solution. Self billing SAP Business Network can automatically transmit self-billing invoices to suppliers and buyers based on data in purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and goods receipts using an automated process. Invoicing - Buyer's Perspective  Note Service sheet is not supported for blanket purchase orders in SAP Business Network. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 119 This is custom documentation. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click Update Company Profile. Alternatively, go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Click the Additional Entities tab. You'll see the Additional Entities table that lists all the entities that you have added. The table view shows the following details: Company Name: The name of the organizational entity. Default Address: Whether this address is the default address or not. Location: A combination of City and Country for easy identification. Click the Chart icon to switch to the Chart View. The Chart View offers a two-level visual overview of your company’s structure: Parent organization Name Location (Country and City) Linked Entities (Number of additional entities) BNO ID (Unique SAP Business Network organization ID) Functions (Role in business transactions: Always Supplier) Linked entities Name A default Bill To entity cannot be deleted, but its details can be overwritten. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 13 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Location (Country and City) BNO ID (Unique SAP Business Network organization ID) Functions (Role in business transactions, such as Sold From or Remit To) Chart View is useful for quickly understanding how different entities are connected within your company. Company Contacts By default, the main company contact is set to the account creator (administrator). However, you can update this information at any time to reflect your company’s most appropriate general contact. Click the Contacts tab in the Update Company Profile page. In the Company Contact Information section, update Email, Phone, Fax of your company as needed. In the Individual Company Contacts section, you can create the contact details of a person with company-wide assignments. Here you can enter the contact name, business title, company assignment, address, email, phone number for the contact. The Inviter Contact checkbox when selected can be used as the Inviter Contact when adding a vendor. Show or Hide Company Profile When you create a public posting on SAP Business Network Discovery, your company profile information is, by default visible to suppliers. If you want to prevent suppliers from viewing your company profile information, then you can hide it. Showing your company profile in postings can help potential suppliers feel more comfortable with doing business with your organization, resulting in increased responses to your posting. Although you can choose to hide your company profile information, SAP recommends that you show it. To show or hide you company profile, select of deselect the Make my profile visible to supplier in postings option in the Settings tab. You can also replicate this settings to global regions by selecting the Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network. Upload Company Logo Prerequisites Before uploading your logo, ensure the following: You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Your logo file meets these requirements: Format: GIF (static only; no animation) Maximum size: 200 KB Dimensions: Up to 250 × 250 pixels Background: Remove any excess area surrounding your logo. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 14 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Context You might want to add your logo so suppliers can tell who the customer is at a glance. Logos also appear on all emails and faxes sent to suppliers registering through the supplier enablement method. Logos do not appear on cXML or EDI orders. Your test account and production account each use their own logo. You might want to create a logo for your test account that clearly indicates that the orders are test orders. You cannot configure different logos to display to your suppliers. To save an existing logo on your computer, right-click it and select Save As in your web browser. Procedure 1. Click Upload Company Logo on the Home page. Alternatively, go to Account Settings Company Profile . 2. Click the Edit company logo icon in the top-left corner of the page. 3. In the Upload Company Logo dialog box, click Browse to select your logo file. 4. Click Open to preview the logo. 5. Click Save to apply your changes. Your logo is updated immediately. Email Notifications Notifications are triggered by events that occur on SAP Business Network. For example, invoice received or updated, undelivered purchase orders, and so on. Buyers on SAP Business Network can specify which notifications to receive so that they are informed about events and activities related to their account. Notifications help monitor account activity and document updates related to transactions, such as purchase orders, order confirmations, ship notices, and invoices. Elements present in the classic SAP Business Network user interface have been added to the new user interface to maintain parity. Based on the notification type,SAP Business Network delivers these notifications in two places: on the SAP Business Network Portal (Online) and to a specified email address. Notifications related to transaction documents, such as purchase orders, order confirmations, ship notices, and invoices are delivered on SAP Business Network. To view these notifications, buyers can click the Quick Links icon and select Notifications. Changes to the User Interface The Notifications table displays the following: Field Name Description Document Type Displays the document type: Purchase Order Invoice Order Confirmation Ship Notice Status Displays the status of the notification as: Failed Rejected Received 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 15 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Field Name Description Updated From Displays the name of the sender who sent the notification. Subject Displays the subject line of the message. Order/Doc Number Displays the order number or document number. Date Displays the date and time when the notification was sent. Implementation Details Business End User Tasks To view notifications for your SAP Business Network account: 1. Go to Quick Links and select Notifications. The Notifications page appears. 2. Select a notification and click more details. 3. Select any notification to view the message details. A panel appears with the full details of the notification. Configure Email Notifications You can configure email notifications for various transactional documents or enablement tasks and select the events that trigger these notifications. You can also configure the email addresses where notifications are to be sent. You can specify up to 10 email addresses. To configure email notifications, follow these steps: 1. Click Configure email notifications under the Setup Actions section in the Home page of the SAP Buyer Portal. If this option is not visible on screen, click View All Tasks and then selectConfigure email notifications 2. Click Saved Version and select Draft to edit the configurations.. 3. The Notifications page displays all theavailable notification configurations under the Network Notifications tab. The events that trigger the notification are grouped as per the document type, such as purchase orders, order confirmations, ship notices, and invoices or as per the enablement tasks such as upload/download, relationship, or master data management notifications. The following table describes these groups and the various tasks that can be enabled for notifications under each group: Group Tasks Description Order Notifications Undeliverable Orders Send a notification when orders are undeliverable. Order Status Update Send a notification to the order requester on the order when the order status changes. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 16 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Group Tasks Description Orders Not Delivered Send a notification to the order requester when orders are not delivered to private suppliers. Invoice Notifications Invoice Received Send a notification when an invoice is received. Duplicate Invoice Alert Send a notification when an invoice is duplicate. Catalog Updates Send a notification when a supplier publishes a new catalog or uploads a new catalog version. Order Confirmation Notifications Orders Confirmation Rejected Send a notification when an order confirmation is rejected. Service Sheet Notifications Service Sheet Received Send a notification when service sheets are received or updated. Pending Queue Notifications Pending Queue Notifications Send a notification when items delivered through pending queue are not acknowledged. Upload/Download Planning Collaboration Send a notification when a document download is ready. Relationship Notifications Supplier Send a notification when a supplier accepts trading relationship with your company. Ship Notice Notifications Reminder of Non-shipped Order Items Send reminders of non-shipped order items. Payment Remittance Status Updates Send a notification only when payment remittance status changes. Payment Proposal Send a notification when a payment proposal is undeliverable. Data Deletion Criteria for Buyers On the Configuration page, the administrator for your SAP Business Network account and other users with appropriate permission can specify the retention period for transaction documents. Additionally, SAP Business Network automatically deletes buyer master data after a period of inactivity following contract termination. You may need to delete old transaction documents to satisfy regulatory needs in your country/region or business requirements in your organization. If you request recurring deletion of transaction data, any transaction document sets older than the retention period are subject to deletion every month. Each document set includes transaction documents and any associated attachments. You can also request one-time deletion of transaction data. This operation is similar, but happens only once, not every month. For example, you can delete your transaction data older than January 1, 2018. Types of Transaction Documents That Can Be Deleted The following transaction documents can be deleted: Purchase orders (orders and blanket orders) Order confirmations Ship notices Receipts Service sheets Invoices, credit memos, and debit memos Payment documents SAP Business Network for Supply Chain transaction documents Notifications Quote requests and quote messages Associated attachments Workflow for Deleting Transaction Documents The following diagram shows the workflow for deleting transaction documents from SAP Business Network:  Note If a buyer account is deleted from the SAP Business Network, the posted RFx transactions get automatically deleted. Suppliers associated with the deleted RFx now can't view any of the deleted RFx transactions. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 18 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Workflow for Deleting Transaction Documents from SAP Business Network About Transaction Document Sets Each transaction document is part of a larger transaction document set, a sequence of related documents sent between the buyer and supplier (for example, purchase order, order confirmation, ship notice, receipt, invoice, and so on). Buyers and suppliers maintain their own data retention period. When all documents in a particular set are older than the specified data retention period, only then are they ready to be deleted. If any document in a set isn't older than the data retention period, the entire set is retained. Transaction Document Set For example, say that your company retains transaction documents for 36 months. A purchase order was created 60 months ago. However, an invoice associated with the purchase order was created only 30 months ago. Since the document set (the purchase order and invoice) isn't older than the retention period of 36 months, both the purchase order and the invoice are retained, not deleted. Documents are identified for deletion according to the data retention period that you specify (for example, 18 months). The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. On the first day of each month, the system finds any document sets older than the data retention period. If all documents in a particular set are older than the data retention period, that set is identified for deletion. The identified set is queued for deletion and deleted within 1 month after being identified.  Note SAP Ariba retains transaction data for a reasonable time after the 30-day grace period. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 19 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- When the system deletes a document, it’s deleted permanently; it can’t be restored. You can’t perform any operations against deleted documents (for example, searching). Data Deletion Restrictions This feature doesn't affect archived invoices, which are stored separately. Once a document has been identified for deletion, it’s deleted regardless if you later opt out of data deletion. Please carefully configure the retention period for transaction documents. Deletion of transaction documents is an irreversible process. You can’t retrieve any transaction documents after they're deleted by the system. If you're using long-term archiving services, we strongly recommend that you specify a retention period for transaction documents that is greater than or equal to the longest archiving retention period legally required by countries/regions where you operate. If the system deletes your invoices, you can't search for those invoices in SAP Business Network. Your archived invoices, however, continue to be retained by TrustWeaver or Sovos (third-party systems that SAP Business Network uses to archive invoices) for the full legal retention period. Data Deletion Notifications You can enable the following notifications for data deletion: Notification Type Notifications Data Identification and Deletion Send a notification when the transaction documents have been identified for deletion Send a notification after deletion of transactions Automatic Deletion of Master Data for Inactive Buyer Accounts Buyer accounts and their data are automatically deleted when their contract with SAP Ariba is terminated. When a buyer account's contract with SAP Ariba is terminated, the account status becomes Expired and SAP Business Network sends a notification to the buyer account administrator. The buyer account administrator can request reactivation of their account at this time. After 60 days of expiry, if the account has not been reactivated, the buyer account and all of its data is permanently deleted. Account deletion is irreversable.  Note Documents that have been identified for deletion can still be searched until they're deleted.  Note Accounts that have used archiving services at any time are not subject to the automatic deletion of master data due to inactivity; the account is expired but the master data is maintained.  Note Buyers who only use SAP Business Network Discovery are considered inactive after 3 years of inactivity.  Note When a buyer account is deleted, they're still visible to their suppliers with the identifier Deleted by SAP Ariba, and suppliers can still access transactions involving the deleted buyer. No company is able to perform new transactions with a deleted buyer. When the buyer and all its related suppliers are deleted, all remaining retained data is permanently deleted. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 20 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Data Deletion Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. A transaction document is identified for deletion when all documents in its transaction document set, the sequence of related documents exchanged between the buyer and supplier, are older than the data retention period. The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. Buyers and suppliers maintain their own data retention period. Consequently, your suppliers can retain copies of documents that have been deleted from your account. Requesting a One-Time Deletion of Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Buyers You can request to delete transactions older than a certain date on a one-time basis for your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Data Deletion Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. A transaction document is identified for deletion when all documents in its transaction document set, the sequence of related documents exchanged between the buyer and supplier, are older than the specified date. The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. Buyers and suppliers maintain their own data retention period. Consequently, your suppliers can retain copies of documents that have been deleted from your account. To receive an email notification when transaction documents for your deletion request are available to download, the administrator needs to set up notifications. All transactions created or last updated before that date are identified for deletion as soon as possible. 5. Click Done. Canceling a Request for Deletion of Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Buyers You can cancel a request to delete transaction data. After the request is canceled, you can request a new recurring or one-time deletion at any time. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Data Deletion Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Data Deletion Criteria.  Tip You can click History log on the Data Deletion Criteria page to view deletion requests that already have run or been canceled.  Restriction Once a transaction document set has been identified for deletion, it’s deleted regardless if you later cancel the deletion request. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 23 This is custom documentation. Click Done. Downloading ZIP Files for Deleted Transactions for SAP Business Network Buyers You can download transaction documents from your SAP Business Network account for 30 days after they were identified for deletion. SAP Business Network collects the transaction documents into ZIP files for download. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Transaction Data Export for Deleted Data permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. You have 30 days to download ZIP files for transaction documents identified for deletion. After that, the documents are permanently deleted. Procedure 1. Click Quick links, and choose Deleted Transactions in the Document Archive section. The Deleted Transactions page appears. If files are available for download, they appear in separate tables for recurring deletion and one-time deletion. Deleted Transactions Page 2. To download a ZIP file, go to the Action column and click the  Download icon.  Tip You can click History log on the Data Deletion Criteria page to view deletion requests that have been canceled.  Tip You can filter the table of ZIP files to show files for which download has not yet started. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 24 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Default Transaction Rules For documents entered on the SAP Business Network portal, the transaction rules are applied when the documents are created. If there are errors or incomplete information, the user cannot move to the next stage to submit the document to the buyer. For integrated documents, the rules are applied after the documents are received and processed. The network sends the relevant error messages as notifications on the SAP Business Network portal and the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network if the supplier investigates the document's status. The look and feel and the user experience of the Default Transaction Rules page is significantly improved in NextGen release. The rules are organized so that support, services, and buyers can easily search and identify specific rules they need to implement for their business needs. Each business rule is labeled with a unique rule ID for better identification. The default transaction rule page includes a new Production Status indicator to identify the rules that are out of sync between test and production accounts and to identify the rules that are candidates for migrating test accounts to production. In cases where the rules differ from the production environment, you can easily identify potential synchronization issues. Additionally, you can track rule modifications that require evaluation, testing, and eventual promotion to the production environment. Administrators can add comments providing the business rationale for the rule changes and share them with your team, services, or support for enhanced monitoring and traceability.
