Override supplier's routing method for orders that match buyer's conditions. Mark purchase order as received when the receipt displays close for receiving Default Rule Status: Off Prevent sending duplicate purchase orders to suppliers. Check this rule to prevent a duplicate of any type of existing order from posting to hosted or integrated suppliers. Such orders include purchase orders, change orders, scheduling agreements, scheduling agreement releases, or blanket orders. If all of the following information in a new order is the same as in an existing order, this rule rejects the new order as a duplicate: Buyer ANID Supplier ANID System ID Order number Order version Order type When SAP Business Network rejects a duplicate order, the buyer receives a status message that the document was rejected as a duplicate. The message provides the reason for rejection, and includes certain information from the duplicate order, such as the order ID, payload ID, and supplier ANID. Default Rule Status: Off Order Confirmation Rules Order Confirmation Rules You can configure these transaction rules for order confirmations Enable suppliers to send order confirmation Uncheck this rule to prevent suppliers from sending order confirmation for all types of orders, such as material orders, service orders, and both these orders at item-level. When this rule is checked, you can override the following rules:  Note This rule does not remove existing duplicate orders. This rule does not apply to new orders with the delete request type. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 31 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Allow suppliers to confirm an order multiple times: The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release. This rule has the following options: Yes No – Allows suppliers to confirm the order only once, for the entire order. Suppliers can't confirm the order at the line-item level. The Confirm only once at line-item level. rule is available only when No is first checked. Allows suppliers to confirm the order only once, either for the entire order or at the line-item level. This rule applies to material orders and service orders independently. If you don't check this rule, the suppliers can only confirm the entire purchase order once. For the suppliers to reconfirm an order when this rule is No, you must send a changed order to the supplier. Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders - Select this rule if you want the suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders to you. To restrict the suppliers from sending you order confirmations for material orders, clear this rule setting. Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the line-item level - Select this rule to allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the line-item level or at the header level. If you don't check this rule, then the suppliers can only confirm or reject the entire order. Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for service orders - Select this rule to allow suppliers to send order confirmations for service orders to you. To restrict your suppliers from sending you order confirmations for service orders, click to clear this rule setting. Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for service orders at the line-item level - Select this rule to allow suppliers to send order confirmations for service orders at the line-item level or at the header level. If you don't check this rule, your suppliers can only confirm or reject the entire order. Allow Supplier to enter service details for OC - Select this rule to allow suppliers to send service details for order confirmation. Default Rule Status: On Require suppliers to fully confirm line items before fulfillment The order confirmation can be for a purchase order, scheduling agreement, or scheduling agreement release. When you select this rule it enables a subrule called Check Delivery Date. Select the Check Delivery Date subrule to evaluate whether the supplier’s delivery or completion date for a line item matches the buyer’s need-by date from the order. If the dates are different, the line item isn't considered fully confirmed. When this rule is selected with the subrule Check Delivery Date, a supplier can't create a service entry sheet or invoice from an order confirmation that has the status Confirmed With New Date or Confirmed With Changes. Uncheck this subrule to not consider the delivery date when evaluating whether a line item is fully confirmed. For scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases, this rule is only applied to Firm schedule lines.  Note When you change the default setting and clear this rule, SAP Business Network automatically unchecks the Require suppliers to create an order confirmation for the PO before creating an invoice rule. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 32 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Only confirmation statuses against Firmschedule lines need to be different from Confirmed With Changes or Confirmed With New Date. The overall confirmed quantity for Firmschedule lines needs to be equal to or greater than the item’s quantity. Default Rule Status: Off Require delivery dates for order confirmations Select this rule if you want the suppliers to provide delivery dates on order confirmations. The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release. Default Rule Status: Off Require an estimated shipping date on order confirmations Select this rule if you want the suppliers to specify estimated shipping dates when changing order confirmation line items. The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release. Default Rule Status: Off Do not allow suppliers to reject entire purchase orders Select this rule if you want the suppliers to fully reject the purchase order. Partial rejections aren't allowed when this rule is selected. Default Rule Status: Off Do not allow suppliers to change line-item description on order confirmations Select this rule if you do not want the suppliers to change line item descriptions on order confirmations. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to increase item quantities on order confirmations Select this rule if you do not want SAP Business Network to check item quantities on order confirmations, and suppliers can modify the item quantity on order confirmations for line items they're confirming. The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release. Default Rule Status: Off Apply line-item quantity tolerance to order confirmations This rule allows you to specify the maximum quantity by which your supplier can fall below or exceed the quantity requested for an item in a purchase order when creating an order confirmation. Underdelivery and overdelivery tolerance values are entered as percentages.  Note This rule is not enforced for unplanned lean-service items or material items in an order confirmation. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 33 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- When quantity tolerances are set, your suppliers can't enter quantities that are outside these tolerances when creating order confirmations. To determine whether a quantity is within tolerance, order confirmation quantities are compared with the required quantity on the purchase order line item or scheduling agreement release line item. While entering quantities on an order confirmation, if your supplier enters a quantity that is outside the permitted tolerance, a message displays to indicate the error. Tolerance checks are performed only when a quantity tolerance value is included for either underdelivery or overdelivery in the Apply line item quantity tolerance to order confirmations transaction rule or in control keys within the line item cXML. The underdelivery and overdelivery values are evaluated independently, so it's possible to have a value in one and not in the other. A value of 0 for either underdelivery or overdelivery means that it is not possible to create an order confirmation that exceeds the requested quantity in that direction. For example, say a purchase order line item requests a quantity of 10, and the transaction rule says that up to 10% underdelivery is allowed and 0% overdelivery is allowed. In this case, an order confirmation can be created with a quantity of either 9 or 10. Any other quantity is outside the allowed tolerances. If no tolerance value is included, the default system behavior applies – underdelivery is permitted, and overdelivery isn't permitted. (Having an empty value for overdelivery isn't permitted – instead, the system adds 0 as a default value.) The presence of tolerance values affects order statuses in the following ways: Orders for which there's underdelivery, but within tolerance, have a status of Partially Confirmed. Orders for which there's overdelivery, but within tolerance, have a status of Fully Confirmed. Default Rule Status: On Apply line-item unit price tolerance to order confirmations You can specify a tolerance percentage for the line item unit price. Your supplier is allowed to specify any line item unit price within this tolerance limit for confirmed line items on the order confirmation. By default the line item price tolerance is blank, which means that there's no restriction on increasing the line item unit price. A tolerance value of 0% applies only to the upper end tolerance of the unit price. The supplier is therefore allowed to modify the lower limit of the unit price irrespective of the 0% tolerance value specified in the rule. This rule also requires you to allow suppliers to edit the Unit Price, Unit Price Quantity, and Unit Conversion fields for advanced pricing details. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to change the currency for unit price on order confirmations Select this rule if you wanr the suppliers to change the unit price currency on order confirmations.  Note This tolerance is applied only to your suppliers who are enabled with the entitlement Enforce Control Keys for All Suppliers. Enablement for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain includes this entitlement.  Note This tolerance is applied only to your suppliers who are enabled with the entitlement Enforce Control Keys for All Suppliers. Enablement for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain includes this entitlement. This rule isn't enforced for the Expected Value of an unplanned lean service or a material item. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 34 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Note When this rule is not selected, the suppliers can't change the unit price currency on order confirmations. This rule has a dependency on the Apply line item unit price tolerance to order confirmations rule. Default Rule Status: On Apply line-item subtotal amount tolerance to order confirmations Specify a tolerance in percentage by which the line item subtotals can be increased, based on a corresponding increase to the unit price of a line item. The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release. When a tolerance is specified, SAP Business Network allows your suppliers to increase line item subtotals on order confirmations within the percentage limit. This rule must be checked to allow your suppliers to edit the Unit Price, Unit Price Quantity, and Unit Conversion fields for advanced pricing details in an order confirmation. Default Rule Status: Off Apply line-item delivery date tolerance to order confirmations This rule allows you to impose tolerances in days for early and late delivery. When this rule is checked, it's applied to purchase order line items, scheduling agreement line items, and scheduling agreement release line items. When delivery tolerances are set, your suppliers can't enter delivery dates that are outside the delivery tolerances when creating order confirmations. While entering delivery dates on an order confirmation, if the supplier enters a delivery date that is outside the permitted tolerance, a message is displayed to indicate this exceeded tolerance. To determine whether a delivery date is within tolerance, order confirmation estimated delivery dates are compared with the required delivery (or Need By) date on the purchase order line item. For example, say that a purchase order line item has a required delivery date of May 8, and the Apply line item delivery date tolerance to order confirmations rule sets tolerances of an upper limit of 3 days and a lower limit of 5 days. When the supplier creates an order confirmation for the line item, delivery dates between May 3 and May 11 are within tolerance. Anything outside that range causes a message to be displayed on the user interface.  Note This rule is enforced for the Expected Value of an unplanned lean service or a material item.  Note This tolerance is applied only to your suppliers who are enabled with the entitlement Enforce Control Keys for All Suppliers. Enablement for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain includes this entitlement.  Note This tolerance is applied only to your suppliers who are enabled with the entitlement Enforce Control Keys for All Suppliers. Enablement for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain includes this entitlement. This rule isn't enforced for unplanned lean-service items or material items in an order confirmation. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 35 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Tolerance checks are only performed when a delivery date tolerance value is included for either early or late delivery in the Apply line item delivery date tolerance to order confirmations business rule. A value of “0” for either early or late delivery means that items can't be delivered either before or after the requested delivery date. Tolerance checks aren't performed if there's no required delivery date specified on a purchase order, or if the supplier doesn't enter an estimated delivery date when submitting an order confirmation. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to change advanced pricing details on order confirmations at the line-item level Select this rule to allow the suppliers to alter the values in the Unit Quantity Price, Unit Conversion, Unit Price, and Pricing Description fields on order confirmations. Default Rule Status: On Require suppliers to provide a reason when they reject an order Select this rule to display the Rejection Reason field in the Reject Order dialog box after a supplier tries to reject an order. The suppliers can select from a list of reasons, or choose Other and enter a comment describing the reason for rejecting the order. The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release. Default Rule Status: Off Require suppliers to provide a reason when they reject an order at the line-item level If this rule is checked, your suppliers must specify a Rejection Reason when they reject a line item. Your supplier can select from a list of reasons, or choose Other and enter a comment describing the reason for rejecting the line item. The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to enter the estimated shipping date on order confirmations at the line-item level Select this rule to allow suppliers to enter the estimated shipping date on order confirmations at the line-item level. Default Rule Status: On Allow suppliers to enter comments on order confirmations at the line-item level for confirmed or backordered items Select this rule to allow suppliers to enter comments on order confirmations at the line-item level for confirmed and back ordered items.. Default Rule Status: On Require suppliers to enter a comment at the order confirmation line item level when there are any changes 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 36 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Select this rule to allow suppliers to provide comment on why the change was made if the supplier changes an item's unit price, supplier part ID, or description, during order confirmation. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to edit the Supplier Part ID and Auxiliary Part ID fields on order confirmations at the line-item level Select this rule to allow suppliers to change the supplier part ID and auxiliary part ID for line items on order confirmations. When the rule is unchecked, suppliers can't edit the Supplier Part or Auxiliary Part ID fields for line items on order confirmations. Default Rule Status: On Allow suppliers to edit estimated shipping dates, delivery dates, and quantities on the Items to Confirm tab Select this rule to allow suppliers to enter the estimated shipping dates, delivery dates, and quantities on Items to Confirm tab. Default Rule Status: Off Allow check for estimated shipping or delivery dates in the past when order confirmations are submitted Select this rule to allow suppliers to check for estimated shipping or delivery dates in the past when order confirmations are submitted Default Rule Status: Off Require that if suppliers confirm orders with item sets, they do so at the child-line level If you select this rule then suppliers are required to confirm orders with item sets at the child-line level.. Default Rule Status: Off Require suppliers to explicitly confirm temporary unit prices in the order confirmation If you select this rule, then the suppliers can no longer confirm an entire order if it contains temporary unit prices. Suppliers must first explicitly confirm each temporary unit price.  Note This rule can be checked only when transaction rule Allow suppliers to enter comments on order confirmations at the line- item level for confirmed or backordered items is selected. If both rules are selected and later Allow suppliers to enter comments on order confirmations at the line-item level for confirmed or backordered items is not selected, this rule automatically becomes deselected.  Note This rule isn't enforced for the Expected Value of an unplanned lean service or a material item. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 37 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Default Rule Status: Off Enable enhanced order confirmation integration capabilities Select this rule to allow suppliers to enable enhanced order confirmation integration capabilities Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to include attachments with order confirmations Select this rule to allow suppliers to attach files to order confirmations. Default Rule Status: Off Copy Delivery Date from Purchase Order Select this rule to allow suppliers to copy delivery date from purchase order to order confirmations. Default Rule Status: Off Require suppliers to include the Polish invoice title for invoices and credit memos in EDI or cXML invoices Default Rule Status: Off Service Sheet Rules The following is the list of transactions rules that are you can configure in SAP Business Network on BTP: Require suppliers to create an order confirmation before creating a service sheet - Requires suppliers to partially or fully confirm an order before creating any service sheets from it. Default Rule Status: Off Require suppliers to provide start and end dates on service sheets - Select At line level if you want the suppliers to include both start and end dates for service sheet line items. The rule applies only to service items, not material items. Check At header level if you want the suppliers to include both start and end dates at the service sheet header. When you select either of the options, the subrule Do not allow service sheets for services that are still in progress is available. Both options apply whether suppliers create service sheets manually or whether SAP Business Network creates them automatically when an order is flipped to an invoice. Default Rule Status: Off Require suppliers to provide approver information on service sheets - Requires suppliers to provide the email address of the person at your company responsible for approving the service sheet (to ensure that the work was completed according to the service sheet description) when creating a service sheet. Default Rule Status: On Allow suppliers to send service sheet attachments - Allows suppliers to add attachments to service sheets. Service sheets only support attachments at the header level. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 38 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Your procurement application can download service sheet attachments (MIME multipart messages) - Allows your procurement application to download header-level service sheet attachments if you allow suppliers to add them. If you select this option, then the Send URLs to view attachments on SAP Business Network, is not available. Require suppliers to send service sheet attachments - Requires suppliers to add at least one attachment to each service sheet. There is no way for suppliers to add attachments to service sheets uploaded as CSV files. If you check this rule for suppliers who upload service sheets as CSV files, their uploads will fail and they must log into SAP Business Network and edit and resubmit the failed service sheets with attachments. Allow suppliers to add ad hoc line items to service sheets - Allows suppliers to add items to service sheets that were not included in the original order. If you place unplanned service orders and your SAP Business Network buyer account is not integrated with SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, you should check this setting, so that suppliers can add items as they fulfill the orders. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to increase item quantities on service sheets - If you select this rule, suppliers can increase item quantities on service sheets up to the tolerance level you specify. The default exception tolerance is 0%. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to change the unit of measure on service sheets - Allows suppliers to change the unit of measure on service sheets. You cannot set an exception tolerance when this rule is checked. Allow suppliers to change the unit price on service sheets - Allows suppliers to change unit prices on service sheets without restriction. You cannot set an exception tolerance when this rule is checked. If you do not select this rule, suppliers can only change unit prices on service sheets within the tolerance level you specify. To set unit price tolerance, select Check Price Tolerance. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to include taxes, freight, special handling, discounts, allowances, and charges on automatically- generated service sheets - Allows suppliers to include other charges such as taxes, freight, special handling, discounts, allowances, and charges on automatically-generated service sheets if your procurement application supports them. These charges also appear on the related invoice. If your procurement application does not support the processing of additional charges on a service sheet, you should not select this rule. If this rule is not selected, additional charges are excluded from automatically-generated service sheets. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to create multiple service sheets for an amount-based service item - Allows suppliers to create multiple service sheets for an amount-based service item. If you select this rule, suppliers can create multiple service sheets on amount-based lines on a service purchase order. If this rule is not selected, suppliers can create only one service sheet for amount-based lines on a service purchase order. If a supplier attempts to create multiple service sheets against an amount-based service line purchase order when the rule is not selected, SAP Business Network displays an error message. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to enter advanced pricing details at the line-item level on service sheets - When this rule is selected, it allows the suppliers to enter the values in the Price Unit Quantity, Unit Conversion, Price Unit, and Pricing Description fields at line item level . Default Rule Status: Off  Note 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 39 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Allow suppliers to change advanced pricing details at the line-item level on service sheets - When this rule is selected, it allows the suppliers to alter the values in the Price Unit Quantity, Unit Conversion, Price Unit, and Pricing Description fields on order confirmations. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to include multiple parent PO lines per service sheet - Allows suppliers to include multiple parent PO lines per service sheet. If you select this rule, suppliers won't be prompted to select an outline item when they create a service sheet or an invoice for the order. Instead, all parent PO lines are automatically added to the service sheet and the invoice. If the rule is not selected, suppliers can include only one parent PO line per service sheet. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to reuse service sheet numbers - Allows suppliers to reuse a service sheet number if the service sheet has been rejected or failed. Select at least one of the options, Canceled, Rejected, Failed in External System, or Failed. If you do nto select this rule, suppliers can’t reuse service sheet numbers. If a service sheet is rejected, canceled or failed, they must use a new number when they resubmit it. Default Rule Status: Off Do not allow creation of service entry sheet for expired purchase orders - When this rule is selected, it does not allow the suppliers to create a service entry sheet for the purchase orders that are expired. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to cancel service sheets that they create - Allows suppliers to cancel a service sheet if its status is, Canceled, Rejected or Failed. Suppliers can reuse the service sheet numbers if you enable the Allow suppliers to reuse service sheet numbers rule in the default transaction rules. Default Rule Status: Off Require suppliers to provide account assignment information - Select this rule to ensure that the suppliers can submit service sheets only after they replace the value U (Unknown) with the appropriate account assignment category values. Buyers can specify U (Unknown) as the value for the account assignment category for service line items on purchase orders. Suppliers can punch in to SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing to retrieve the appropriate value for the account assignment category and then submit their service sheets. Default Rule Status: Off Allow suppliers to use the indicator for final service entry sheet - Allows suppliers to indicate in a service sheet that it will be the final service sheet generated against the line item in a purchase order even if the service is not complete. You must have SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA directly connected to SAP Business Network to receive the final service sheet indicator in service sheets. Default Rule Status: Off Require suppliers to create service entry sheets where the line item quantity is not zero- Prevents suppliers from creating service entry sheets where the line item quantity is zero. Default Rule Status: Off Do not allow part number to exceed specified characters for ad hoc line items - You can prevent suppliers from specifying part numbers (for ad hoc line items in service sheets) which exceed the configured number of characters. The maximum allowed number is 99. Default Rule Status: Off Require suppliers to provide description for ad hoc line items - Requires suppliers to provide descriptions for ad hoc line items. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 40 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules SAP Ariba provides a set of default country/region-specific invoicing rule templates that you can use as a starting point when defining invoice rules. Country/region-based rule templates reflect the current knowledge of invoice requirements for those countries/regions. SAP Ariba strongly recommends buyers implementing country/region-based invoice rules to consult with their tax and legal advisors to determine the applicability of any business rule they implement. Enablement Process for Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules You can use the country/region-based invoicing rule templates to add countries/regions for which you want to implement specific invoice rules. By default, country/region-based invoice rules are disabled and no country/region-based invoice rules are activated. Follow these general steps to enable and activate country/region-based invoice rules: 1. Using the country/region-based invoicing rule templates, add the countries/regions for which you want to implement specific invoice rules and review the country/region's invoice rules set. 2. Based on legal requirements for a country/region, edit the invoicing rules set for the country/region. 3. View the final invoice rules that get applied based on the rules defined on the default transaction rule, supplier group rule, and country/region-based invoice rule levels. 4. You might want to discuss any changes to the invoicing rules with your suppliers to avoid unnecessary invoice rejections as a result of the new invoice rule enforcement. 5. If you are ready to put the rules in production, uncheck the rule Ignore country-based invoice rules: If you want to enable country/region-based invoice rules for all suppliers that do not belong to a supplier group, uncheck Ignore country-based invoice rules on the Default Transaction Rules page. If you want to enable country/region-based invoice rules by supplier group, uncheck Ignore country-based invoice rules on supplier group level. Suppliers can review the rules that are applied to their invoices by the country/region of origin after you have enabled country/region-based invoice rules for them. Related Information Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules Automatic Invoice Creation from Receipts SAP Business Network buyers in the United States, Australia, and South Africa can enable a country/region-based invoice rule to automatically create invoices from receipts. The Enable automatic invoice creation from receipts rule, effective only when Require suppliers to include only received quantities on invoices is checked, causes SAP Business Network to automatically create an invoice when you send a receipt for material goods. This rule ensures that invoices are based on goods that you have received. Before invoices can be automatically generated on behalf of a supplier, based on receipts sent from you, the supplier must agree to automatic invoicing by completing the Automatic Invoice Creation Acceptance page for each buyer that has enabled the country/region-based rule. When the supplier logs in to SAP Business Network, an alert notifies them of the need for confirmation of automatic invoicing against receipts. When you enable automatic invoice creation, SAP Business Network automatically generates a standard invoice or line-item credit memo when you send a receipt for received quantities. Partial invoicing is also supported. The date assigned to the invoice is the system date. Each automatically generated invoice has references to the related receipt and purchase order. When SAP Business Network generates an invoice automatically based on a receipt you submit, it gathers information for the invoice from the order, the receipt, and the supplier's company profile. Header-level information for the invoice comes from the order. If the tax information is not present on the order, the VAT information is obtained from the supplier's company profile. Item- level information for the invoice comes from the order with the exception of Order Line Number and Quantity, which come from the receipt. All taxes for invoices generated automatically from receipts must come from the purchase order. Taxes can be specified at the header-level of the order or at the line-item level, but not in both places. To ensure that line item level taxes for standard invoices are copied from the purchase order, check the Copy tax from purchase order to standard invoice rule. (Note that this rule does not apply to line item credit memos. For line item credit memos, taxes at line item level default from the invoice and not from the purchase order, even when this rule is enabled.) The rule Include allowances and charges in the unit price must be unchecked to ensure correct calculation of line item unit prices when the purchase orders have taxes and charges applied on the line items. All taxes should be specified as a percentage rate on the order. The percentage is applied to all invoices generated for the order. If the tax is specified as a flat amount on the order, it is also applied to all invoices generated for the order, which could result in higher taxes than intended. Allowances and charges for invoices generated automatically from receipts must come from the order. Allowances and charges can be specified at the header-level of the order and at the line-item level. Like taxes, all allowances and charges should be specified as a percentage rate on the order. The percentage is applied to all invoices generated for the order. If an allowance or charge is specified as a flat amount on the order, it is applied to every invoice generated from a receipt, which could result in cumulatively higher allowances or charges than intended. Invoice Number for Automatically-Generated Invoices There are two methods SAP Business Network uses to assign invoice numbers to invoices created automatically from receipts:  Note You can view the invoice rules for countries/regions that are in an “Active” status. The rules belonging to countries/regions that are in an inactive status are not available in the downloaded CSV file. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 51 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Receipts with Delivery Note Information: If the buyer uses the SAP ERP to create a receipt from a ship notice coming from SAP Ariba, the Delivery Note field on the receipt is auto-populated with the packing slip ID from SAP Business Network. In that case, the invoice number for an automatically-generated invoice or line-item credit memo is based on the delivery note information, with a four-digit number appended to it. Receipts without Delivery Note Information: If a receipt does not include delivery note information, the invoice number is a system-generated unique number that starts with "A" (for example, "AI7VCKN40"). Restrictions The following receipts do not result in an automatically-generated invoice: Receipts for items from multiple orders. Receipts for items from a purchase order that contains both services and material goods. Buyers and cXML-enabled suppliers must upgrade to cXML 1.2.030 or later to support the ShipNoticeIDInfo child element in the ReceiptRequestHeader element. All items in a receipt must have either positive or negative quantities and must be either of type "received" or "returned". Otherwise, the receipt will be rejected. All taxes, allowances, and charges must be specified on the order as a percent rate, not as a flat amount. The Enable automatic invoice creation from receipts country/region-based invoice rule is supported only for United States, Australia, and South Africa. The rule only applies to suppliers that invoice through the SAP Business Network and not through an integrated ERP system. In addition to required business rules that the buyer must select to enable automatic invoice creation from receipts, there are other rules that affect the fulfillment flow. The following default transaction rules, if checked, affect the workflow for automatic invoicing from receipts: Allow suppliers to increase item quantities Allow suppliers to increase line item subtotals Require suppliers to fully confirm line items before fulfillment Require suppliers to create an order confirmation for the PO before creating an invoice Require suppliers to create a ship notice for the PO before creating an invoice For example, if the first two rules are unchecked, the invoice quantities and subtotals cannot be increased from the order. If the last three rules are checked, an order confirmation, ship notice, and receipt must be created in sequence for an order before SAP Business Network can automatically create an invoice on behalf of the supplier. Related Information Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules Catalog Validation Preferences SAP Business Network enables suppliers to check their customer catalogs against your catalog validation preferences before publishing the customer catalog to you. The supplier’s ability to qualify their customer catalog for your organization increases the likelihood that you can upload their customer catalogs without encountering errors. You can set the following validation preferences: Specify the UNSPSC (United Nations Standard Products and Services Code) code version that you support. If the supplier’s UNSPSC version is different, SAP Business Network automatically converts the commodity codes in the customer catalog to your supported version. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 52 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Set an option to allow 0 price values. SAP Business Network’s standard customer catalog checking produces an error for 0 price values. Set an option to disable Unit of Measure (UOM) checking. This enables you to upload suppliers' customer catalogs without encountering an error if the customer catalog UOM codes differ from those you support. If you customize your UOM maps, you should disable UOM checking. Set an option to disable commodity code checking. This enables you to download suppliers' customer catalogs without encountering an error if the customer catalog commodity codes differ from those you support. If you customize your commodity code maps, you should disable commodity code checking. Related Information Setting Catalog Validation Preferences About Overriding Your Rules and Preferences for a Supplier Setting Catalog Validation Preferences You can configure catalog validation preferences for your SAP Business Network account. Suppliers can check their customer catalogs against your catalog validation preferences before publishing their customer catalogs to you. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Catalog Validation Preferences. The Catalog Validation Preferences page appears. Catalog Validation Preferences Page 3. To convert UNSPSC codes in the supplier's customer catalogs to the version supported in your Ariba Buyer configuration, choose Change and select the version number. 4. To disable some validation checking, choose one or more of the following: Disable commodity code (UNSPSC) checking to ignore differences between the commodity codes specified in customer catalogs and commodity codes you support 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 53 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Disable Unit of Measure (UOM) checking to ignore differences between the UOM specified in customer catalogs and UOM you support Ignore zero (0) price values to ignore items with a price of 0 If you do not select a UNSPSC version, SAP Business Network validates against its “pinned” version, which is 13.5. 5. Click Save. Audit Logs for Buyers You can access classic and standard audit logs. To view audit logs, click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings. Under Audit Log, choose Classic for the legacy audit log or Standard for the Intelligent Configuration Manager audit log. These are the available classic audit logs: Transaction Rule Changes – This log tracks changes to default transaction rules. Supplier Group Membership Changes – This log tracks changes to supplier groups. Profile Changes – This log tracks changes to user profiles. User Access – This log tracks user access activity, which includes the number of failed access attempts since the last successful sign in and their reasons. Currency Preference Changes – This log tracks changes to currency preferences. For more information about the standard audit log, see Managing SAP Ariba Audit Information. Audit Logs Audit logs for switching data centers and enabling or disabling SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network routing in SAP Business Network Entries are added to the audit log when a user enables or disables SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network routing in SAP Business Network. Entries are added to the audit log when a user switches between SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network data centers in SAP Business Network. Only SAP Business Network users with administrator or viewer privileges can view the audit log entries. Audit logs for test and production accounts are separate and independent of each other. The following are the functional features: When users switch data centers and enable or disable SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network routing, these comments are entered in the SAP Business Network audit log.  Note This log can be exported to a PDF file with a maximum of 500 records. If you need additional records, change the search criteria to filter for a specific time period, user, or other field. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 54 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Audit Log Operations and Comments Operation Comments in the Audit Log Description User enables SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network routing X Data Center was enabled for SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway SSO to SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway X Data Center was enabled X is the default data center for selected location User disables SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network routing X Data Center was disabled for SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway SSO to SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway X Data Center was disabled User switches between SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network data centers X Data Center was disabled for SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway SSO to SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway X Data Center was disabled X is the currently configured data center Y Data Center was enabled for SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway SSO to SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway Y Data Center was enabled Y is the new data center that the user switches to Viewing Audit Log Entries How to view audit log entries To view the audit log information go to Settings Audit Log . To generate the audit log in PDF format click the Export to PDF button. Unit of Measure Data for Your Account You can use the unit of measure CSV template to define the unit of measure codes that you use in your business, as well as provide additional information such as the symbol, name, and description for each code. Unit of measure codes can be based on ISO or UN/CEFACT standards, or they can be any arbitrary codes defined by your company. If unit of measure codes are company-specific, it's important to provide additional information about the codes to suppliers so they can understand what the codes mean in purchase orders and other SAP Business Network documents. The unit of measure CSV template has the following four header rows at the top of the template: Row 1: Character encoding (for example, 8859_1). Row 2: Field names (Code, Name, Symbol, and Description). Row 3: Whether the field is required or optional. Row 4: Data type and maximum length (for example, "String 100"). The first three fields in the template, Code, Name, and Symbol, are required. The Description field is optional. The fields can be rearranged in any order as long as the field names are not changed.  Note If there is no symbol for a code, we recommend that you repeat the Code value in the Symbol field. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 55 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- The following table shows an example of unit of measure information that you can add to the CSV template: Code Name Symbol Description 2N dB decibel decibel 2P kbyte kilobyte kilobyte 2Q kBq kilobecquerel kilobecquerel 2R kCi kilocurie kilocurie DZN dozen DOZ dozen PK pack PK pack TP ten pack TP ten pack Language Support The unit of measure master list supports multiple languages. Fill in the template in a separate CSV file for each locale. To activate a master list, upload strings for at least the English locale. Enabling or Disabling Unit of Measure Codes You can disable and enable unit of measure codes that you uploaded to your account. If you disable a unit of measure code, suppliers can't find it anymore in the application, although they can still enter it. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Before you can enable or disable unit of measure codes, you must first upload them to your account. When you upload unit of measure codes, they are enabled by default. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Enable or disable codes. The Enable or disable unit of measure codes page appears. 3. Select Code or Name from the list. 4. Type the start of a code or name, and then click Search. 5. Select one or more codes. 6. Click Enable to enable the selected codes, or click Disable to disable them. 7. Click Done.  Restriction Once you upload a unit of measure code to your account, you cannot delete it. However, you can update the Name, Symbol, and Description fields for a unit of measure code. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 56 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Uploading Unit of Measure Data You can use the unit of measure CSV template to upload additional unit of measure information to your account for use in SAP Business Network documents. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Fill in the CSV template with information about unit of measure information codes for one or more locales. To activate the list in your account, upload strings for at least the English locale. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Upload or download master list. 3. For the locale of the CSV file you are uploading, click Upload. 4. Click Browse to select a CSV file, and then click Upload. 5. Repeat steps and for other locales, as needed. 6. Click Done. Downloading the Unit of Measure Template You can download a CSV template to populate it with unit of measure codes to upload to your SAP Business Network account. To support different locales, save a different version of the file for each locale. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . The Master List page appears. Master List Page  Note To verify the data you uploaded, click Download. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 57 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Download template, and save the file to your computer. Activating the Analytics Functionality in Your SAP Business Network Buyer Account You activate the analytics functionality in your SAP Business Network buyer account from the Configuration page. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Analytics Configuration. 3. Click Submit to configure and activate the analytics functionality. If the operation fails, click Retry. You can retry the operation for a maximum of 4 times. Contact SAP Ariba Customer Suppor for help if the operation fails after the maximum number of tries. UI Customization This feature allows buyers to create custom attributes that display additional data that is relevant for their business but not available as part of SAP Business Network in a self-service manner and add them to a customization project. The buyers can edit or create standard and custom attributes and display them in the specific section of the transactional documents, such as invoice, purchase order, advance ship notice, and order confirmation. Customization helps the buyers to collect additional information, that are not captured as part of standard default fields. For example, if the orders include the fixed bin location for items, you can customize ship notices to include that field, too. The data from the fields that you add are sent as extrinsics in cXML documents. Depending on the country or industry specific rules, customers may require additional fields in transactional documents. The buyers can determine if the customizations are applicable for a supplier group or a multiple supplier groups. You can also control the behavior of fields, such as adding notes, warnings or page hints or hide field lables and values for the amount and subtotal fields. When you customize the user interface, the following conditions are applicable: SAP Business Network creates an audit log for all the customizations done and user who performed it. The audit log stores information about the projects created and also the fields customized to have a control. The buyer can assign the customization project to a supplier group or multiple supplier groups. The buyer can create a copy of the customization projects and assign that to a different supplier. The buyer can add, edit, or remove customization projects. Implementation Details General Prerequisites 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 58 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Ensure that the admin has the following permissions to customize a project and add custom attributes:: ADMIN_TS_CUSTOMIZATION ADMIN_CUSTOMIZATION ADMIN_TS ADMIN_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTES CUSTOMIZATION ATTRIBUTE EDITOR CUSTOMIZATION EDITOR CUSTOMIZATION PUBLISHER Restrictions The following restrictions are applicable for creating custom attributes: Custom attributes can be created in a centralized library and added to the customization project. Custom attributes can also be created while creating the customization project. These attributes are automatically saved to the library and can be added to other customization projects. Each customer must have their own custom field library. Custom fields created by the customer in their own library are accessible only by them (not by other customers). Attributes can be deleted from the library, only if they are not yet included in a published project. User can select the area of the chosen document to be customized with additional attributes. The custom fields that are added must not override system-required fields. The transactional document types have their own transaction rules that limit the types of values a supplier is allowed to enter UI Customization must not override a Transaction Rule. Different versions of the projects are available that the buyer can track and restore. Buyer can edit field level and section level of a document type in a project. Configuration Business End User Tasks Follow these steps to customize the user interface: 1. Login to the SAP Business Network as an editor. 2. Navigate to Users Settings to open the Settings page. 3. Scroll down to the Integration section and select Customization Self-service to open the Customization Self-service page. 4. Click Create to create a new project. 5. Enter a name for the project, select the supplier account and then select the document type for which you want to add additional fields or customize the attributes.  Note 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 59 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- 6. Select one of the document customization areas from the following options: Document display CSV Excel PDF Workbench 7. Click Create. When you create a project for a document type, all the fields available in the document template for that document are included to the project. Click View details to list the different sections and fields available for that project. To customize a document refer to . Add Attributes After you create a project, you can view the different sections of the document by clicking the View details link. Expand the section to view the fields and select a field to view the attributes. Adding an Attribute To add an attribute, follow these steps: 1. Click View details for a project you created for a document type. 2. Expand a section and select a field to list the attributes of the field. 3. Click Create Create Attribute to open the Create Attribute page. 4. Enter a attribute name and then enter the description. You can select mutiple suppliers. This release support the following document types: Invoice Order Confirmation Purchase Order Ship Notice Service Entry Sheets  Note Document display option is common for all the documents. Other options in the customization area differs depending on the document selected. For example, if you select Ship Notice as document type, then the customization area displays CSV, PDF, Excel, and Items to Ship, whereas, if you select Order Confirmation, the customization area displays Excel and Items to Confirm.  Note The Create Add Existing Attribute option allows you to add or edit an existing attribute to a field. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 60 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/BuyerAdminGuide for BTP.content: 5. Select the attribute type. You can select one from the following options: Extrinsic: captures data from suppliers. This attribute is sent in cXML as extrinsic element. Characteristic: contains detailed information about the item that can be used across different industries. For example, material characteristics like size, color, colorcode and so on. Static 6. Select the data type. You can select from the following options: String Boolean Integer Decimal Date DateTime Money Email Phone URL Address 7. Enter the Key name, which is the name of the field by which it is stored in the backend. This cannot be edited later. 8. Enter the label. 9. Click Save to create the new attribute either to the customization project and to the library. The system validates the field name within the project and within the centralized library if it is unique and displays the newly created attribute in the subsection, which you can edit. Customizing a Field You can customize an existing field or a newly created filed to control the behavior and appearance in documents. You can do any of the following customizations for a field: Default values: Set a default value. Default value can be dynamic (based on extrinsic from the PO, in the INV case). Flippable Values: Set this field if you want to select a field from a document and map it to a field in another document (example Purchase Order), so that the data is automatically populated. Required: Make a field required with or without a condition. Required fields display with an asterisk. To change your shared secret, you must enter the current value in the Current Shared Secret text box. If you forget your shared secret, SAP Business Network Customer Support must reset it. Your website and SAP Business Network use this certificate for cXML authentication. You can also use the backup certificate if your primary certificate becomes invalid. Digital certificates require more setup steps, they cost money, and they expire over time. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- The SAP Business Network audit service, logs selected user and administration actions performed in SAP Business Network applications. It also logs user interface audit actions like create, download, purge, or delete audit reports. The audit actions are divided into the following categories: Generic audit actions - purge, delete and download audit reports Inegrated audit actions - create audit reports For more information about audit logs for buyers, see Audit Logs for Buyers. For more information about audit logs for suppliers, see Audit Logs for Suppliers. The SAP Business Network on BTP audit service enables administrators and security personnel to take a detailed look at what occurs in their SAP Business Network site, reproduce potential malicious activities of users and administrators, monitor administrative activities, like configuration changes, and retrieve forensic evidence if a security breach occurs. The SAP Business Network audit service records activities and events relevant for security auditing. You can access audit service records for evaluation in the form of security audit reports. In legacy SAP Business Network Audit Classic is where you can view the audit logs. In SAP Business Network on BTP, all audit logs are now written to BTP and retrieved from BTP. The main difference of audit between SAP Business Network on BTP and legacy SAP Business Network is that in legacy SAP Business Network the audit events were generated in a synchronous manner, providing a real-time view of the audit trail. Whereas in SAP Business Network on BTP you first need to create an audit repor, download it to view them. To view audit logs, click Account Settings Settings and then choose Audit Log Standard from the Compliance section. Implementation Details General Prerequisites Ensure that the user have the following permissions to access audit logs: User Administration Audit Log Administration Business End User Tasks The SAP Business Network audit service log entries contain identifying information, such as user, event type, date, and time. When users change data, the SAP Business Network audit service records both the old and new value. The SAP Business Network audit service creates a log entry when a user, integration tool, or scheduled event performs the following actions: Changes a user's authorization Exports or downloads data Creates, edits, or deletes data Authenticates a user Changes system configuration Accesses or changes sensitive information The SAP Business Network audit service also records user consent to privacy policies, including the version number of the policy and whether the policy was a custom privacy policy or the SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Privacy Statement. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 78 This is custom documentation. SAP Business Network Users and Roles By creating roles and then adding users to them, the SAP Business Network administrator controls who can sign in to your organization’s account and which areas of the service each user can access. Mass Uploading Users Using an Excel Template Account and user administrators can create and update users through mass upload using an Excel template. Using an Excel template, user administrators can perform the following actions: create or update users, assign roles, assign business units, authorization profile assignments. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. For the mass upload capability using an Excel template, all required fields must be filled out in the Excel template before uploading it. List of the required fields in the Excel template: Action User Name Corporate User Name (if SSO is enabled) Email Address First Name Last Name Has Limited Access; if this value is set to "No", at least one role must be assigned Only Excel files in the .XLSX format can be uploaded Only five roles, business units, and authorization profiles can be assigned using an Excel template. These roles, business units, and authorization profiles must exist already, and cannot be created using Excel upload. If additional ones are needed, they can be added from the user interface. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 81 This is custom documentation. The number of users entered in the Excel file must not exceed 500. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Click the Upload Users button on the Manage Users page. 4. Click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 5. Click the Download template link on the Upload File dialog box. 6. Open the Excel template and fill out the required fields. 7. Click the Browse button on the Upload Files dialog box, choose the filled out Excel template from your computer and enter a descriptive name. 8. Click the Upload button. 9. Click the Refresh Status button on the Upload Users page and wait until it shows status Completed. If the status is Completed With Errors or Failed, select the download icon ( ) in the Log column to see the reasons for errors and to correct them. 10. Click the Done button. This opens the Manage Users page where you can see the uploaded users. Revoke User Access and Remove a User's Personal Information SAP Business Network users can request the administrator for their account to remove their personal information from the system. If approved, the user can’t sign in to SAP Business Network any longer, and their personal information is no longer visible to users, including in transaction documents shared and exchanged with business partners. Restrictions Comments or attachment files associated with transaction documents aren’t affected when users remove personal information. Therefore, avoid entering personal information in comments or attached files. After a user’s revocation of user access request is approved, their personal information is pseudonymized in SAP Business Network transaction documents. However, transaction documents that were integrated with other systems (such as an ERP) or downloaded before the request was approved may still have the user’s personal information. The customer needs to take additional action, including informing impacted business partners, to remove it. If a customer needs to re-identify a user that has been pseudonymized for legal purposes, the administrator of the account can provide that information. Reassigning a User Sign In If a user has left the company, you can reassign that user’s sign-in to another individual, to retain the user setup and data. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions.  Note For audit and compliance purposes, the user's personal information is still visible to the user who is the administrator for your SAP Business Network account. 5/6/26, 6:48 AM 82 This is custom documentation. If you want to retain the user’s setup and data, reassign the sign-in. If you want to delete the user’s setup and data, delete the user. Procedure 1. Sign in using the user’s user name and password. If you do not know the password, click Help Support to contact SAP Business Network Support. 2. Choose Account Settings Manage Profile . 3. On the Configuration page, choose Personal Information. 4. Change the user name and password and optionally other information. 5. Click OK. 6. On the Configuration page, choose Notifications. 7. Make any modifications to notification emails based on the user sign in reassignment. 8. Click OK. A user signs in to the SAP Business Network portal to request the removal of their personal information. 2. The administrator for the account receives an email notifying them of the user's request. 3. The administrator signs in to the SAP Business Network portal and approves or rejects the user's request. 4. If the administrator approved the request, the user's personal information is removed. 5. If the administrator approved the request, the user can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Configure Retention Period and Manage Deletion of Revoked Users in SAP Business Network As a buyer administrator, configure a retention period for revoked users. SAP Business Network users can request the administrator of their account to remove their personal information from the system. This is called a revocation request. If the request is approved, users cannot sign in to SAP Business Network any longer, and their personal information is no longer visible to other users. As an administrator, you can configure a retention period for the user data of all the revoked users in your organization. The data of revoked users is automatically removed from SAP Business Network after this retention period is reached. In the meantime, you can view the list of revoked users in the Revoked Users tab. You must have configured the retention period before accepting or rejecting any revocation request. If the retention period for an organization is not configured, SAP Business Network prompts you to configure the retention period before you can act on a revocation request. You can change the retention period at any time before the previously configured retention period is reached. The newly configured retention period takes effect immediately. The retention period must be configured in months, and must be between 1 and 999 months. SAP Business Network Permissions A permission grants access to a certain area of the SAP Business Network user interface. Each role includes one or more permissions. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Change in the Names of SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network SAP has renamed SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network to SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network respectively. This document uses the revised names. This change is effective from the SAP Ariba 2302 release and it does not affect the functionality of SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network. The UI components of SPRO nodes contain the short name, Managed Gateway for Spend&Network. The content on the Performance Assistant pages associated with the SPRO nodes displays the name as SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. Also, the name Ariba Network is renamed as SAP Business Network throughout the SPRO menu components. Exceptions The product name Ariba Network adapter for SAP NetWeaver is not updated in this document. The names of the integration scenarios that contain the name Ariba Network are not updated in this document. The technical names of the ABAP objects in the SPRO nodes associated with the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, addons for SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA and SAP Business Network are not renamed. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide This guide is for SAP Ariba administrators or business users responsible for setting up SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA with SAP Ariba solutions and SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA buyers can integrate SAP Ariba solutions with SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and use the functionalities integrated across SAP Ariba solutions. Buyers can find information about the system requirements, data flows, and prerequisites that they require before sending master data and transaction data through the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. SAP Ariba recommends that you read this guide first and then the following guides to know more about the supported functionalities. This guide applies to: SAP Ariba Buying SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing SAP Ariba Invoice Management SAP Ariba Catalog SAP Business Network Commerce Automation  Caution SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network is not audited for compliance with the Payment Card Industry Standard (PCI). You should not submit Purchasing Card (PCard) data in transactions sent to the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. SAP Ariba may reject transactions that include data in the field designated for PCard use. 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 2 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- SAP Ariba Contracts SAP Ariba Collaborative Sourcing SAP Ariba Discount Management SAP Ariba Invoice Management SAP Business Network SAP Ariba Payables SAP Ariba Spot Buy Catalog SAP Ariba strategic sourcing solutions SAP Ariba Sourcing SAP Ariba Supplier Information and Performance Management SAP Ariba Supplier Lifecycle and Performance SAP Ariba Supplier Risk Related Guides SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Configuration Guide SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Migration Guide Introduction You've decided to integrate your SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system with SAP Business Network and SAP Ariba solutions to efficiently manage supplier interactions across the spend management lifecycle. The SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network simplifies and accelerates the integration. This document is intended for business users and administrators and provides an overview of the supported functionalities. In addition, it includes information about software components, access rights, and system requirements on SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA side before you can begin the integration process. Please note that this guide does not provide process descriptions on how to carry out the integration. Refer to the following documents for information about: Installation and configuration of SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA add-on Integration steps on the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Configuration requirements on the SAP Business Network and SAP Ariba solutions. Unless otherwise specified, references to SAP ERP in this documentation also apply to SAP S/4HANA. 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 3 This is custom documentation. SAP Help Portal Overview of the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Solution for Buyers SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network provides a simple and efficient Integration-as-a-Service (IaaS) solution. SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network facilitates the integration of buyers' SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA systems with SAP Business Network and SAP Ariba solutions. By leveraging the SAP Cloud Platform integration, SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network: Supports the configuration on the basis of the core ERP capabilities Supports certificate-based or basic user name and password based authentication for connectivity Offers tools such as: Document Validator tool to validate documents for schema, content and transformation Supplier Reporting to view the integration status of their suppliers Transaction Tracker to search and track transaction status Test Central to help users perform self-test before moving to a production environment In addition, SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network: Simplifies integration by using a guidance-based setup Reduces the integration deployment time 5/6/26, 7:27 AM 4 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Provides an integrated test framework to verify various scenarios configured in the system Facilitates smoother upgrade of the solution Aligns with SAP standard software delivery processes by supporting download through the SAP Service Marketplace and by addressing issues with standard SAP Notes and correction instructions Uses the single sign-on functionality to enable buyers to access their SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network account from their SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, or SAP Ariba strategic sourcing solutions account.
