file://SBN/split/CIG and SBN Overview 2_.content: Change in the quantity of the line items Deletion of line items Addition of line items Buyers can maintain consistency in the line items in the ship notice and inbound delivery document. SAP ERP can process the edited ship notice for the following changes: Quantity Delivery date Gross weight Gross weight unit of measure Volume Volume unit of measure Supplier batch ID Integrated suppliers can also make updates to the ship notices and send the edited ship notices to the SAP ERP system from their back-end systems. Starting SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, Release 2505 (Q2 2025, SP 23), cancellation and deletion of inbound deliveries when Advanced Ship Notices (ASN) are canceled in SAP Business Network is supported. Previously, when an ASN was canceled in SAP Business Network, the inbound deliveries in SAP ERP were not deleted or canceled. After an ASN order was canceled, characters_1 was added at the end of the ID which was not available in SAP ERP. This feature enhances CL_ARBCIG_DISP_DELV_NOTIF_IMPL to fetch the inbound deliveries with the old ASN ID without_1 from the EKES table. The system now deletes multiple inbound deliveries when it's available. Component Information in Ship Notices Buyers integrated with SAP Business Network, SAP Business Network for Supply Chain for Buyers, and SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network can process component information in ship notices from SAP Business Network. Component suppliers on SAP Business Network send the component information in ship notices created against the subcontracting purchase orders. The inbound delivery that SAP ERP creates contains the component information. The component information helps buyers and suppliers track the shipment for components efficiently. To customize the component information, use the methods, PRE_PROCESSING and POST_PROCESSING in the BAdI, ARBCIG_ADVANCE_SHIPMENT_NOTICE with the parameter, CT_LECOMP. For more information on how to customize, see Ship Notice. Important: SAP Ariba can process the component information only for buyers using SAP ERP 6.0 EhP4 and higher. Packaging Information with Handling Units 5/6/26, 7:29 AM 81 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Buyers integrated with SAP Business Network, SAP Business Network for Supply Chain for Buyers, and SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network can process handling units in the packaging information sent in ship notices from suppliers from SAP Business Network. A handling unit is the base unit containing the delivery item and packaging material. The handling unit has a unique standard identification number that stores detailed information of the delivery item. Handling units are used for multiple-level packaging. Handling units help warehouse agents in the logistics of shipping items to suppliers. Buyers create packaging instructions for material items on the SAP ERP system. The packaging instructions contain detailed information of how to pack the material items for shipping. Packaging instructions help in associating the handling units automatically. Buyers define the packaging instructions containing the hierarchy of the multiple levels of packing units. The packaging instruction determines each handling unit in packing and shipping goods to the buyers. As a buyer, you define the master data for the materials with the packaging instructions on the SAP ERP system. For example, as a buyer, you create the packaging instructions containing the packing units for shipping bottles (finished material type, FERT). In the packaging instruction, you specify the following packing hierarchy: Define the material (packaging material type, VERP) for the box and the packing instruction specifying that the bottle is packed in the box. Each small box is a handling unit. Define the material (packaging material type, VERP) for the carton and the packing instruction specifying that the carton contains the box. The carton is also a handling unit. Define the material (packaging material type, VERP) for the pallet and the packing instruction specifying that the pallet contains the carton. The pallet is also a handling unit. After the buyer has uploaded the packaging instructions on SAP Business Network, the packing hierarchy is available for the supplier. When buyers create a purchase order, buyers can include material items having handling units with the packaging information. When a supplier creates a ship notice on SAP Business Network against the purchase order, the supplier selects items, and specifies how the items are packed for shipment. Suppliers use the packaging information that the buyers have uploaded on SAP Business Network while specifying the items to be packed in a shipment. Suppliers can ship items to be delivered in multiple packages, but stored as a unit. Each set of delivery items can be packed in multiple packages. The delivery items are packed together in the packaging material (box, carton, rack, etc.). Each packaging material is associated with a unique code, Packaging Code. The packaging code stores the details and specifications about the items and packaging material. For example, suppliers could pack items for delivery in boxes or cartons, and then further pack them in containers or pallet. Suppliers can view the packaging code of the items packed in each of the boxes, cartons, or containers. When buyers create the inbound delivery on the SAP ERP system, the inbound delivery stores the information about handling units in the packaging information. 5/6/26, 7:29 AM 82 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Supporting Integration of Packing Information in Ship Notices from SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Packaging Instructions Fields Auxiliary Packaging Materials in the Packaging Information Supporting Integration of Packing Information in Ship Notices from SAP Business Network The following describes the workflow to integrate the packaging information with handling units for delivery items against ship notices from suppliers on SAP Business Network: 1. The SAP ERP buyer enables the necessary parameter for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Ensure that you also maintain the required settings for the packaging information. For more details, see Prerequisites and Restrictions for Packaging Information with Handling Units. 2. Define the master data for the materials with the packaging instructions in the SAP ERP system. The SAP ERP buyer creates the packaging information for the material item on the SAP ERP system. You define the packaging instructions containing the hierarchy of the multiple levels of handling units. The hierarchy determines each handling unit when packing and shipping goods to the buyers. For example, as a buyer, you create the packaging instructions containing the packing units for shipping bottles. In the packaging instruction, you specify the following packing hierarchy: Define the material for the box and the packing instruction specifying that the bottle is packed in the box. Each small box is a handling unit. Define the material for the carton and the packing instruction specifying that the carton contains the box. The carton is also a handling unit. Define the material for the pallet and the packing instruction specifying that the pallet contains the carton. The pallet is also a handling unit. When buyers define the master data for packaging material items, buyers can also specify the auxiliary packaging materials (packaging material category D) on the SAP ERP system. Buyers can include the auxiliary packaging materials when creating the packaging instructions for shipping material items. 3. Go to SPRO and run the task, Export Packaging Data for Handling Units to SAP Business Network, or use the Transaction code, ARBCIG_ASN_HU_EXP to extract the packaging information for the material items available on the SAP ERP system. Save the packaging information as an Excel file on your local system. The Excel file must be in a .xlsx format. If you are using SAP ERP 6.0 EHP0 to EHP3, ensure that you open the Excel file and save the file as an Excel Workbook (*.xlsx). Ensure that .xlsx is in lower case alphabets. If you are using SAP ERP 6.0, EHP4 and higher, you do not need to save the file as an *.xlsx. The file is already in the *.xlsx format.  Note Ensure that you create the packaging instructions for the materials before you run the program to extract the packaging information available on the SAP ERP system.  Note You must run the task, Export Packaging Data for Handling Units to SAP Business Network, each time there is a new material or changes to the packaging information for the material items available on the SAP ERP system. SAP Ariba does not support uploading partial master data of handling units. 5/6/26, 7:29 AM 83 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- 4. Go to the SAP Business Network buyer account and download the template for the packaging information. You can download the Excel template on the Upload/Download Download page. 5. Copy the packaging data from the saved Excel file available on the SAP ERP system to the SAP Business Network Excel template. Save the changes. The Excel file containing the packaging information you upload on SAP Business Network must have the following: The Excel worksheet name containing the packaging data is ʻInstructions’. The Excel file contains the SAP Ariba banner. The Excel file contains all the necessary fields that SAP Business Network requires to send the packaging information with handling units in ship notices to SAP ERP. 6. Go back to the SAP Business Network buyer account and upload the saved Excel file containing the packaging information with handling units. You upload the Excel file on the Upload/Download Upload page. Ensure that the file has been uploaded successfully. 7. On the SAP ERP system, create a purchase order for the finished material goods. Ensure that you set the confirmation control key in the Confirmation tab for suppliers to create ship notices. For example, 0004-Inbound delivery. 8. The supplier confirms the purchase order and sends the order confirmation to the buyer. 9. The supplier creates a ship notice against the purchase order. To pack items, the supplier does the following: Click Pack Items. If you have more than one packaging information, select the required packaging information available in the Choose packaging instructions field. The supplier views the handling units for line items available in the packaging information that the buyer has uploaded on SAP Business Network. The supplier defines the quantity to be shipped in each handling unit. For example, when the supplier creates a ship notice against the purchase order for ten bottles, the packaging instruction displays the packing hierarchy for packing the ten bottles. Suppliers can specify the following to pack ten bottles: Define each bottle to be packed in a small box. You define ten small boxes containing the ten bottles. Define ten small boxes to be packed in one carton. Define one carton to be packed in a pallet. 10. The buyer receives the ship notice containing the packaging information from the supplier on SAP Business Network. 11. The buyer creates the inbound delivery on the SAP ERP system. The inbound delivery additionally stores the packaging information with the handling units for the box, carton, and pallet for the finished material item against the ship notice from SAP Business Network. When a supplier sends a ship notice containing changes, SAP ERP processes the changes in the inbound delivery. 12. The buyer creates the goods receipt against the inbound delivery on the SAP ERP system and sends the receipt to the supplier on SAP Business Network. 13. The supplier creates an invoice and sends the invoice to the buyer. SAP Business Network Packaging Instructions Fields The Packaging Instructions template contains the following fields. 5/6/26, 7:29 AM 84 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Field Description Required Packaging Specification ID A unique ID for the packing instruction document. The Packaging Specification ID for a material item is the same for all the packaging levels. Required Material Buyer Part ID for the material item. When there are multiple material items to be packed, this material item denotes the final material item used to pack. Optional Material Description Description of the material item. Optional Capacity Quantity of the packing unit. Required Unit Unit of measure for the quantity specified for the packing unit. Required Packaging Level Level of packaging. Used when there are multiple packages for a material item. Specify 1 as the highest level of the packing hierarchy. Required Packaging Material Packaging material used at each packing level. For example, box, carton, pallet Required Packaging Material Description Description of the packaging material item used at each packing level. Optional Maximum Capacity The maximum capacity of the packing unit. Required Minimum Capacity The maximum capacity of the packing unit. Required Length The length of the package or material item. Used when specifying the dimension of the package. Required Unit Length The length of the package or material item per unit. Used when specifying the dimension of the package. Required Net Weight The total weight of the package or material item. Used when specifying the dimension of the package. Required Gross Weight The total weight, including packaging. Required Unit Gross Weight The gross weight per unit of the item. Required 5/6/26, 7:29 AM 85 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Field Description Required Total Volume The total volume, including packaging. Required Unit Total Volume The total volume per unit of the item. Required Parent Packaging Material The parent packaging material. Used when there are multiple packages for a material item. Specify the parent to the immediate level of the packing hierarchy. For example, you have packed one box in a carton. Here the carton is the parent packaging material for the box. Valid values: Yes, No, or blank. Is Printable Set to No. To print the handling units. Required packaging material. Valid values: Yes if you are defining the handling units for other packaging material. By default, the value is set to No for auxiliary packaging material. Is Default Set to Yes. Applicable when the material is associated to multiple packing instructions. Contains information about the default option. Buyers can edit this value in the packaging instructions to specify when the material is associated to multiple packaging instructions. Required for auxiliary packaging material. Default value: Yes Auxiliary Packaging Materials in the Packaging Information Starting SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network 2003 (Q1 2020) release. buyers integrated with SAP Business Network, SAP Business Network for Supply Chain for Buyers, and SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network can include the auxiliary packaging materials in the packaging specification. The auxiliary packaging materials that buyers send with the packaging instruction from the SAP ERP system help suppliers to adhere to the packaging structure in the ship notices. When buyers define the master data for packaging material items, buyers can also specify the auxiliary packaging materials (packaging material category D) on the SAP ERP system. Buyers can include the auxiliary packaging materials when creating the packaging instructions for shipping material items.  Note 5/6/26, 7:29 AM 86 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Buyer can include the following item types in the packaging instructions: M - Materials packed P - Packaging material that is used to package the material I - Subordinate packing instructions (for multilevel packaging) Buyers can run the Export Packaging Data for Handling Units to SAP Business Network report to export packaging instructions from the ERP system to SAP Business Network. The packaging instructions that this report exports include the auxiliary packaging material information as well. Starting SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Release 2205 (Q2 2202), the assignment of parent packaging material to auxiliary packaging materials is supported. On the Export Packaging Data for Handling Units to SAP Business Network report, the following enhancements are supported: Extract the auxiliary material with the assignment to parent packaging material. Filter the packing instructions based on check profile, handling unit groups, and date of creation of packing instructions. Run the extraction program in the background to extract a large volume of packing instructions. Also, the packing instructions extract displays the ERP system ID associated with the packing instructions. The packing instructions extracted from the ERP system is saved as a Microsoft Excel file either on the local system or on the SAP application server that buyers can import to SAP Business Network. Buyers can make the necessary changes before uploading on SAP Business Network. Buyers can change the packaging instruction to specify the default packaging instruction when the downloaded file contains multiple packing instructions for the same material. Suppliers can choose the packaging instructions containing the auxiliary packaging materials when they create a ship notice on SAP Business Network. Starting SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Release 2205 (Q2 2202), SAP Business Network uses the auxiliary packaging materials at specific packaging hierarchy levels as specified in the packing instructions. In addition, the suppliers in SAP Business Network can include empty packaging material as auxiliary packaging material or as handling units with zero load quantity to the ship notice and integrate the ship notice with the buyer’s ERP system. Prerequisites and Restrictions General prerequisites for ship notices To use confirmation control keys to validate delivery quantity tolerances when suppliers create ship notices against standard purchase orders, configure the confirmation control keys in purchase orders and order confirmations. When creating purchase orders, ensure that you maintain the following fields in the Confirmations tab. Choose a value in the Conf. Control field for the order confirmation. Check the Acknowl.Reqd field. Buyers must assign a packaging material type to each packaging material they create on the SAP ERP system.  Note Every time buyers upload the updated packing instructions to SAP Business Network, it replaces the existing packing instructions that you have uploaded to SAP Business Network. So, you must upload the packing instructions in the full load mode only. 5/6/26, 7:29 AM 87 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Maintain the Confirmation control keys for the order confirmations and ship notices. Ensure that you also maintain the Confirmation categories for order confirmations(AB) and ship notices (LA). Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain must configure the required shipping configuration to create the outbound delivery for components. Ensure that you extend the components to the sales view. To send the component ship notice to two different locations (two-step movement), configure the item Category Determination for delivery items. Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain require this configuration. Restrictions Duplicate Packing Slip IDs for ship notices are not supported in SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. For more information on the control keys, see cXML User's Guide in the Product Documentation > For Users section of the Learning Center. You also need to configure the SAP ERP to accept attachments and comments in ship notices. SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Ensure that you maintain the necessary parameters for the document type, ShipNoticeRequest to send and receive ship notices. SAP Business Network Ensure that you enable the necessary rules for the suppliers to send ship notices. Specify the rules in the Default Transaction Rules page in your SAP Business Network buyer account. Additionally, you must also enable the transaction rule Allow suppliers to edit existing ship notices in the Default Transaction Rules and Supplier Group Transaction Rules sections. Suppliers can edit an existing ship notice only if this rule is checked. This rule is disabled by default.  Note Although SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network supports the time tolerances in ship notices, SAP Business Network currently does not support this functionality. 5/6/26, 7:29 AM 88 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Ensure that you enable the necessary settings to send control keys at the line item level for ship notices in the purchase orders. The control key setting allows suppliers and you to override the default transaction rule you specify in the SAP Business Network buyer account. Ensure that your suppliers use the same Packing Slip ID (PackageID) in the ship notice while editing the ship notice. Ensure that you enable the Require all items in a ship notice to have the same transport terms value transaction rule to prevent the creation of a single Advanced Shipping Notice (ASN) with different Incoterms, storage location, or inbound delivery header-level details. For more information on the transaction rules for SAP Business Network, see SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide for SAP Business Network on the SAP Help Portal. Restrictions Suppliers on SAP Business Network can update multiple fields while editing the ship notice. However, SAP ERP integrated with SAP Business Network and SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network can process changes to only the following fields for existing line items in the ship notice: Quantity Delivery date Gross weight Gross weight unit of measure Volume Volume unit of measure Supplier Batch ID Buyers cannot edit the ship notices that have been created on the SAP ERP system in SAP Business Network. Only one inbound delivery can be created for a single ASN, and all line items must share the same Incoterm, storage location, and inbound delivery header-level details. Sending an ASN with different Incoterms, storage location, or inbound delivery header-level details is not supported and can result in multiple inbound deliveries and data inconsistencies. Save the packaging information as an Excel file on your local system. The Excel file must be in .xlsx format. Run the task each time there is a new material or changes to the packaging information for the material items available on the SAP ERP system. If you are using SAP ERP 6.0 EHP0 to EHP3, ensure that you open the Excel file and save the file as an Excel Workbook (*.xlsx). Ensure that .xlsx is in lower case alphabets. If you are using SAP ERP 6.0, EHP4 and higher, you do not need to save the file as a *.xlsx. The file is already in the *.xlsx format. Copy the packaging data from the saved Excel file available on the SAP ERP system to the SAP Business Network Excel template. However, if you use the Excel file saved on your SAP ERP system, ensure that you make the following format changes that SAP Business Network requires: Ensure that the worksheet name containing the packaging data is renamed from ʻSheet 1’ to ʻInstructions’. Ensure that you insert three blank rows above the existing Row 1 in the Excel file. You require this step as the template on SAP Business Network contains the SAP Ariba banner, and the Excel file that SAP ERP extracts does not contain the SAP Ariba banner. 5/6/26, 7:29 AM 90 This is custom documentation. Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers Content -- 2 of 10 -- Change in the Names of SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network SAP has renamed SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network to SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network respectively. This document uses the revised names. This change is effective from the SAP Ariba 2302 release and it does not affect the functionality of SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network. The UI components of SPRO nodes contain the short name, Managed Gateway for Spend&Network. The content on the Performance Assistant pages associated with the SPRO nodes displays the name as SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. Also, the name Ariba Network is renamed as SAP Business Network throughout the SPRO menu components. Exceptions • The product name Ariba Network adapter for SAP NetWeaver is not updated in this document. • The names of the integration scenarios that contain the name Ariba Network are not updated in this document. • The technical names of the ABAP objects in the SPRO nodes associated with the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, addons for SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA and SAP Business Network are not renamed. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers Change in the Names of SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network PUBLIC 3 -- 3 of 10 -- SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers This guide is for SAP Ariba administrators responsible for installing and setting up SAP ERP with SAP Business Network and SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network for suppliers. To integrate SAP ERP with SAP Business Network and SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, suppliers must first download and install the required components for SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, Supplier AddOn for SAP ERP. This guide applies to: • SAP Business Network Related guides SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway how to guide for suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network configuration guide for ERP integration for suppliers 4 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers -- 4 of 10 -- Overview of Integrating SAP ERP with SAP Business Network using the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network For suppliers to integrate SAP ERP with SAP Business Network using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network requires installation of the following components: • SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Supplier AddOn for SAP ERP: The add-on is installed on SAP ERP system. The add-on enables SAP ERP to communicate with SAP Business Network through SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. • SAP Cloud Platform cloud connector (cloud connector): The cloud connector allows you to efociently and securely transfer data between SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and SAP ERP. The cloud connector is a software component to connect to cloud applications. For more details on the cloud connector, see https://help.sap.com/viewer/ cca91383641e40ffbe03bdc78f00f681/Cloud/en-US/e6c7616abb5710148cfcf3e75d96d596.html. • SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network: The gateway allows you to map and transform the data. You can monitor the transactions between SAP ERP and SAP Business Network. The following table lists the steps that you must perform to integrate SAP ERP with SAP Business Network using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network: Step Environment Description Enable SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Enable SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend manage- ment and SAP Business Network setting on SAP Business Network. Download add-on and cloud connector SAP ERP You can download the following software from SAP Service Market- place : • SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Supplier AddOn for SAP ERP You can download SAP Cloud Platform cloud connector from SAP De- velopment Tools page. Install and configure cloud connector and add-on SAP ERP Install the cloud connector and the add-on for SAP ERP. Currently, the supported encoding for data is UTF-8. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers Overview of Integrating SAP ERP with SAP Business Network using the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network PUBLIC 7 -- 7 of 10 -- Installing the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Supplier AddOn for SAP ERP This chapter describes the add-on components you must download and install to use SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. The add-on for SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network allows you to send or receive documents from SAP Ariba and SAP ERP. Downloading and Installing the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Supplier AddOn from SAP ONE Support Launchpad [page 8] Downloading and Installing the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Supplier AddOn from SAP ONE Support Launchpad You can download and install the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network software components for SAP ERP from the SAP Software Download Center or the Maintenance Planner. Go to the SAP ONE Support Launchpad at https://launchpad.support.sap.com . See the SAP Note, 1841471 for general instructions about how to install the add-on. The authorizations allow the users to send SAP information for transactions to SAP Business Network and SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. To define the required authorizations, use the authorization objects, class, and program that SAP Ariba provides. You must use the following out-of-the-box authorization objects for SAP ERP users. SAP Ariba provides the following authorization objects and classes: • ACIS: Authorization object class • ARBCIS_CLS: Authorization Object for Ariba Class Objects • ARBCIS_PRG: Authorization object for program execution • ARBCIS_SPR: Authorization Object for SPRO Node SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers Defining Authorizations PUBLIC 11 -- 1 of 6 -- Configuring the SAP Cloud Connector Connect SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network with your SAP ERP using SAP Cloud Connector (cloud connector).  Note If you are using the same SAP ERP as a buyer and as a supplier, you cannot use the cloud connector configured for buy-side to connect with SAP ERP configured for sell-side. To connect SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network with your SAP ERP as a supplier, you must configure the cloud connector once again for the sell-side. The cloud connector serves as the link between SAP Cloud Platform and existing on-premise systems. The cloud connector runs as on-premise agent in a secured network and acts as a reverse invoke proxy between the on- premise network and SAP Cloud Platform. Due to its reverse invoke proxy support, you don't need to configure the on-premise firewall to allow external access from the cloud to internal systems. New installation and configuration You must install and configure cloud connector for test and production environments. For information on how to install and configure cloud connector, see Cloud Connector. Add the new subaccounts and configure cloud connector to connect to SAP ERP.  Note For high availability, you must configure multiple subaccounts. Refer Table 1: Subaccount information. 4. Enter the following information: • Subaccount User: Enter the P user ID and password that you received in the email when SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network was enabled on SAP Ariba solution. • Display Name: (Optional) Enter a name to easily recognize the subaccount in the user interface. • Location ID: (Optional) Enter the same LocationID that you had previously configured in SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. The location ID must be unique per subaccount and should be an identifier that can be used in a URL. • Description: (Optional) Enter a brief description of the connection. 5. Click Save. After configuring the subaccounts, you must configure cloud connector to allow SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network to access SAP ERP. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers Change in the Names of SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway and Ariba Network PUBLIC 3 -- 3 of 10 -- SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers This guide helps SAP Ariba supplier administrators understand the integration of suppliers' SAP ERP with SAP Business Network using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. This guide applies to: • SAP Business Network Related Guides • SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers • SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Configuration Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers 4 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers -- 4 of 10 -- SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers Overview of Integrating SAP ERP with SAP Business Network Using the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network [page 5] Software Components [page 6] High-Level Steps for Integrating SAP ERP with SAP Business Network [page 7] Supported Transactions [page 8] Forward Error Handling [page 12] Overview of Integrating SAP ERP with SAP Business Network Using the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Suppliers on SAP Business Network can use SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network to integrate their SAP ERP with SAP Business Network. Suppliers using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network have the following benefits: • Simple SPRO based configuration for SAP ERP add-on. • Simplified integration by using a guidance-based setup on the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network portal. • Smoother upgrade of the solution. • Aligned with SAP standard software delivery processes by supporting download through the SAP Service Marketplace and by addressing issues with standard SAP Notes and correction instructions. • Access to SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network account from SAP Business Network, using the single sign-on functionality. The maximum size of attachments is configurable per user. You can set the limit for attachments between 10 MB and 100 MB. The attachments limit applies to the total size of all attachments associated with the transaction document. If the attachments are encoded in the base64 encoding schemes, the base64 encoding increases the actual size of attachments by approximately 35%. Therefore, the actual limit on the size of attachments is 65% of the configured limit. For example, if the maximum allowed limit is set to 10000 KB, the actual total size of all the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers PUBLIC 5 -- 5 of 10 -- attachments users can add is 6500 KB. If you attempt to add attachments that exceed this limit, SAP Business Network displays a warning and does not allow you to add attachments. Prerequisites and Restrictions [page 6] Prerequisites and Restrictions Prerequisites You must download the following components for the integration: • SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Supplier AddOn for SAP ERP • SAP cloud connector Restrictions Integrating supplier SAP ERP with SAP Business Network using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network has the following restrictions: • Integration of SAP S/4HANA on-premise with SAP Business Network using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network is not supported in the current release. • Only SAP EHP4 for SAP ERP 6.0 onwards is supported. • Only the following transactions are supported: • Sales order • Order confirmation • Outbound delivery • Billing document • Multi ANID and multi-ERP are not supported. • Mediated connectivity is not supported. Software Components To integrate SAP ERP with SAP Business Network using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, you need the following components: • SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Supplier AddOn for SAP ERP : The add-on is installed on the SAP ERP system. The add-on enables SAP ERP to communicate 6 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers -- 6 of 10 -- with SAP Business Network and SAP Ariba solutions through SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. • SAP Cloud Platform cloud connector (cloud connector): The cloud connector allows you to efociently and securely transfer data between SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network and SAP ERP. The cloud connector is a software component to connect to cloud applications. For more details on the cloud connector, see this document. Supported Systems This section lists the supported systems and the supported software in this release of SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network.  Note SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network supports only Unicode systems. Currently, the supported encoding for data is UTF-8. SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network supports the following versions of SAP ERP: • SAP ERP (SAP_BASIS 700 SP27 is the SAP Basis version for all the following SAP ERP versions) SAP EHP4 for SAP ERP 6.0 (SAP_APPL 604 SP12) SAP EHP5 for SAP ERP 6.0 (SAP_APPL 605 SP09) SAP EHP6 for SAP ERP 6.0 with non-HANA database (SAP_APPL 606 SP05) SAP EHP6 for SAP ERP 6.0 with HANA database (SAP_APPL 606 Minimum supported version) SAP EHP7 for SAP ERP 6.0 (SAP_APPL 617 Minimum supported version) SAP EHP8 for SAP ERP 6.0 (SAP_APPL 618 Minimum supported version) • SAP_BS_FND 701: Support Package 12 Transport Layer Security SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network requires the minimum Transport Layer Security version, TLS 1.2. High-Level Steps for Integrating SAP ERP with SAP Business Network To integrate SAP ERP with SAP Business Network using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, you must do the following high-level steps: • Download the components for SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers PUBLIC 7 -- 7 of 10 -- • Set up the SAP Cloud Connector. • Enable SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network on SAP Business Network. • Set up the global settings to connect to the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network on the SAP ERP system. • Set up the supported transactions on the SAP ERP system. • Create integration projects on SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. • Test and deploy the connection to the SAP Ariba solution. For details about installation and configurations, see SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers and SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network configuration guide for ERP integration for suppliers. Supported Transactions The integration of SAP ERP with SAP Business Network using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network supports the following transactions in the current release: Sales Order [page 8] Order Confirmation [page 9] Outbound Delivery [page 11] Billing Document [page 11] Sales Order Buyers create a purchase order to request for products or services using their SAP ERP and send them to suppliers on SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network then sends the purchase order to the supplier SAP ERP using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. The inbound purchase order is then converted to sales order in the supplier SAP ERP. The SAP ERP add-on supports the following features for sales order: • Creation of sales order from purchase order data. • Creation of standard sales order. • Updation of the sales order when there are updates to the purchase order. • Consumption of payment terms from purchase order for sales order and invoice.  Note If payment terms are not maintained in purchase order, the payment terms from customer master in supplier ERP is used for sales order and invoice. 8 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers -- 8 of 10 -- • Deletion and addition of line-items in a sales order are allowed simultaneously. • Standard sales order with reference to buyer purchase order with multiple comments at header and line level. • Attachments. • Partner functions such as ShipTo and BillTo addresses. Prerequisites • Configure the pricing condition type to EDI1 for sales order. • Assign customer to the sales organization data. • Create customer material information. • Define purchase order types. • In SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, maintain payment terms in customer master data under Sales Area Data Billing Documents . Restrictions SAP ERP add-on for suppliers does not support the following for sales orders: • Service, consignment, subcontracting, return, blanket, scheduling agreement, and scheduling agreement release. • Sales order with non-catalog items. • Consumption of control keys. • Order confirmation instructions and advanced ship notice instructions. • Line payment card details. • SAP ISO UOM code to AN UOM cXML code conversion. • Partner functions such as SoldTo addresses. • Cancellation of sales order. • Price-Based Quantity in sales order. • Display of purchase order Material Short Text in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA although it is visible in the sales order proxy payload. Order Confirmation In response to a sales order, suppliers send order confirmation to buyers. The supplier SAP ERP sends order confirmation to buyers regardless of the buyer’s Enhanced Order Confirmation settings (whether they want to receive confirmations in allDetail or detail) on SAP Business Network. Order confirmation documents can have the following states on SAP Business Network: At header level: SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers PUBLIC 9 -- 9 of 10 -- • detail • rejected • all detail At line-item level: • accepted • rejected • backordered • detail SAP ERP add-on supports sending order confirmations to SAP Business Network, and has the following features: • Order confirmation can be sent to completely accept, partially accept, or completely reject a sales order. • Multiple order confirmations can be sent for a single sales order. • Order confirmation creation is triggered only for the following conditions: • If there is a rejection reason set at any of the items. • Atleast one of the schedule lines must have confirmed quantity greater than zero. • Order confirmation update is triggered only for the following changes in sales order: • New item or schedule line added or removed • Change in order quantity • Change in confirmed quantity • Change in schedule date • Change in shipping date • Change in Net Price • Assigning a rejection reason • Order confirmation can have partial and full delivery schedule lines for line items. • Order confirmations are supported only for SAP Business Network initiated purchase orders. • Comments are supported at the header and line-item levels. • Attachments are supported at the header and line levels. Restrictions SAP ERP add-on for suppliers does not support the following for order confirmations: • Updating order confirmation. • Partial line item rejection with header or line notes. • Multiple supplier SAP Business Network ID. • Unit of Measure (UOM) other than the ISO standard. • If an order confirmation fails in SAP Business Network, the subsequent order confirmation updates cannot be sent. In such a scenario, you must use the pre-processing methods of the BAdI provided for order confirmation. For more information, see Supported Transaction Customization of SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network configuration guide for ERP integration for suppliers. 10 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/CIGOverviewSup_Part2.pd.content: Outbound Delivery Suppliers create an outbound delivery to notify the buyers that their orders are about to be shipped. SAP ERP add-on for suppliers supports the following features for outbound delivery: • Complete and partial outbound delivery only against standard sales orders. • Comments at the header and line-item levels. Restrictions SAP ERP add-on for suppliers does not support the following for outbound delivery: • Multi ANID with respective shipping point for one customer. • Update and cancellation of outbound delivery. • Service, consignment, subcontracting, return, blanket, scheduling agreement, and scheduling agreement release. • Attachments. • Serial number and Buyer Batch ID. • Single outbound delivery for multiple sales orders. • Packing or handling unit for material for outbound delivery. • Unit of Measure (UOM) other than the ISO standard. Billing Document Buyers create a purchase order to request for products or services using their SAP ERP and send them to suppliers on SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network then sends the purchase order to the supplier SAP ERP using SAP Business Network. The inbound purchase order is then converted to a sales order in the supplier SAP ERP. Suppliers create a billing document against sales orders sent by buyers. SAP ERP add-on for suppliers supports the following features for billing document: • Billing document referring to a single sales order. • Billing document for outbound delivery. • Credit memos for single sales order. • Billing document with taxes at header and line-item level. • Comments at the header and line levels. • Billing document with special handling charges at header and line-item level. • Billing document with shipping charges at the header level. • Partner functions such as ShipTo and BillTo addresses. SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers PUBLIC 11 -- 1 of 8 -- Restrictions SAP ERP add-on for suppliers does not support the following for billing documents: • Single billing document for multiple sales orders. • Single billing document referring to multiple outbound deliveries. • Line-level credit memos for multiple sales orders. • Standard invoice referring to single or multiple sales orders, when PO reference is not readily available, as in case of credit memo. • Non-PO invoice. • Invoice cancellation. • Credit memo for return orders. • Partial credit memo. • Discounts. • Attachments. • Shipping charges at the line-item level. • Partner functions such as SoldTo addresses. • Mapping due amount. Forward Error Handling Forward error handling (FEH) functionality allows the monitoring and processing of errors asynchronously on SAP ERP. When a document sent from an SAP Ariba solution to SAP ERP fails for any reason, it can be checked and processed again on SAP ERP. When FEH is enabled, the error message for every failed inbound transaction is transferred to Post Processing Ofoce (PPO). Status update request (SUR) for the transaction is sent to the sender when the transaction is successful or when the message is discarded. With FEH enabled and the business processes configured, if the system detects an error in an inbound transaction, the user can read the message and do one of the following: • Update the required information and reprocess the transaction. For example, if the error is due to a mapping error, the user can edit the payload and process the transaction again. The user can correct the error and reprocess the transaction until it is successful. An SUR is sent to the sender when the transaction is successful. • Reprocess the transaction immediately. For example, if the error is because the purchase order is still open, the user can submit the transaction for reprocessing. An SUR is sent to sender when the transaction is successful. • Discard the message in FEH if the sender has to take action on the transaction. In this case, a rejection message is sent to the sender as an SUR. Prerequisites • Activate FEH. • Define process data. • Define postprocessing. 12 PUBLIC SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers -- 2 of 8 -- • Define resolution stategy. • Define business process. • Assign proxy method to FEH. Before Guided Integration for Trading Partners was available, supplier integration was a high-touch process involving the SAP integration team. It could take weeks, or even months, for you and your buyer to be fully integrated to transact business smoothly. Buyers could set default transaction rules in SAP Business Network to define their business processes, but you had no equivalent tool, which made it difocult for you to determine which buyers to integrate with. Guided Integration for Trading Partners gives you this capability. You can use Guided Integration for Trading Partners to discover which of your existing buyers you can easily integrate with for additional business processes. After discovering buyers, you can use Guided Integration for Trading Partners to integrate your business processes quickly and independently, and as a result, you become enabled for additional types of commerce collaboration with your existing buyers. Prerequisites You need one of the following permissions to use Guided Integration for Trading Partners: • Integration Management Full Access • Integration Management Read-Only Access Restrictions You must have a SAP Business Network Enterprise Platinum account to use Guided Integration for Trading Partners. Workflow Follow these steps to find existing buyers to integrate with for additional business processes: 1. Go to Guided Integration for Trading Partners. See Entering Guided Integration for Trading Partners [page 5]. 2. Complete the questionnaire to define your business processes. See Questionnaire for Guided Integration for Trading Partners [page 8]. 3. Use the compatibility dashboard to search for buyers. See View Your Compatibility with Your Trading Partners [page 12]. 4. Compare and reconcile your template for a document type with a prospective buyer’s template. See Compare and Reconcile Templates with Guided Integration for Trading Partners [page 16]. Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners PUBLIC 11 -- 1 of 10 -- View Your Compatibility with Your Trading Partners Use the compatibility dashboard to check compatibility with your buyers. Prerequisites You must have one of the following permissions: • Integration Management Read-Only Access • Integration Management Full Access After you complete the integration management questionnaire, you can use the compatibility dashboard to search for existing buyers to integrate with for additional business processes. You use this dashboard to compare the information from your integration profile with the business rules set by your buyers. The dashboard helps you locate compatibilities and incompatibilities with prospective buyers and find new buyers to integrate with for different business processes. It also helps you identify gaps in your business processes that you may want to address to be compatible with more buyers. The following are some examples of these types of gaps: • Order confirmations document – You do not update order confirmations when there are changes to previously- confirmed information like the order quantity. However, a majority of your existing buyers want their suppliers to be able to do this. • Invoice document – You only send invoices for orders transmitted from SAP Business Network. A buyer you would like to do business with for invoices requires their suppliers be able to send invoices from orders not transmitted from SAP Business Network (that is, non-PO invoices). For information about the compatibility dashboard, see Using the Guided Integration for Trading Partners Compatibility Dashboard [page 12]. Compare and Reconcile Templates with Guided Integration for Trading Partners Compare your business processes with those of a prospective buyer and resolve any incompatibilities. Prerequisites You must have one of the following permissions: • Integration Management Read-Only Access • Integration Management Full Access Buyers and suppliers use cXML to transact business by sending and receiving documents with SAP Business Network. Buyers and suppliers need compatible business processes for these transactions to succeed. For example, suppose you are a supplier who sells t-shirts that buyers purchase to customize and resell. If a buyer purchases t-shirts from you, they need to be able to include the quantity for each size and color. If size and color are not already fields in your purchase order document, you will need to add them to be compatible with these buyers. Do the following two tasks to identify and resolve incompatibilities with selected buyers: 1. Compare templates for a document type. You can use different types of templates to do the comparison. Following are descriptions of these templates: • SAP Supplier Super Template – You have your own SAP Supplier Super Template for each document type. This is a customized template that matches all your buyer relationships in SAP Business Network. This template contains the common cXML for all buyers that you have a relationship with for the document type. SAP Business Network creates your initial SAP Supplier Super Template using the buyers you transacted with during the last 12 months for the document type. If you have no transactions with any buyers during the last 12 months for the document type, you will not have a SAP Supplier Super Template for the document type. When you add buyers for a document type, you can use Guided Integration for Trading Partners to update your SAP Supplier Super Template to include any new fields these added buyers require. • SAP Golden Template – Each document type has a SAP Golden Template. This is a standard template that matches the most used fields in SAP Business Network. For example, the SAP Golden Template for purchase orders contains the common fields buyers use for purchase orders. SAP Business Network automatically generates the SAP Golden Template for each document type. When generating these templates, it uses intelligence derived from a cross section of existing buyer and supplier relationships across different industries. • Buyer Template – This template is specific to a buyer for a document type. It is generated on the fly based on your transaction documents for this document type with this buyer. If the Buyer Template is not available in SAP Business Network, you can upload a local version of it. The template will not be available if you do not have any transaction documents for this document type with 16 PUBLIC Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners -- 6 of 10 -- this buyer yet. You will need to continue to upload a local version of the Buyer Template until you have transaction documents for this document type with this buyer. • Document Type Definition (DTD) Template – cXML is thoroughly defined by a set of Document Type Definitions (DTDs). DTDs for all versions of cXML are available on cXML.org. The DTD template is the cXML.org template for the document type. Since DTDs define the syntax and order of all cXML fields for a document type, you may want to use the DTD template to find missing fields and attributes in your SAP Supplier Super Template. 2. Reconcile differences between templates. After comparing templates, you can reconcile any differences. If you have the Integration Management Full Access permission, you can save the reconciled template, download it, and share it with your middleware teams. Your middleware teams may need to make additional modifications to the template. For information about comparing and reconciling templates, refer to Comparing and Reconciling Templates with Guided Integration for Trading Partners [page 17]. Comparing and Reconciling Templates with Guided Integration for Trading Partners Compare your business processes with those of a prospective buyer, and then reconcile any incompatibilities. Prerequisites You must have one of the following permissions: • Integration Management Read-Only Access • Integration Management Full Access Procedure 1. From the Integration Overview page, click Reconcile and Download Template. The Reconcile Template page opens with the document type displayed at the top of the page. If needed, you can select a different document type from the pulldown menu. A default template that is suitable for you appears as My Latest Template in the My Workspace panel. Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners PUBLIC 17 -- 7 of 10 -- Click the Document Type Definition (DTD) link at the bottom of the page to view, and optionally download, the Document Type Definition (DTD) cXML reference file for the document type. Note that you can only download the DTD file by clicking this reference link; you cannot download it by selecting Document Type Definition Template from the Source column. 2. Choose a Source template. The choices for the Source template include the following: • SAP Supplier Super Template – Customized template that matches all your buyer relationships in SAP Business Network. • SAP Golden Template – Standard template that matches the most used fields in SAP Business Network. • Buyer Template – The template specific to a buyer for this document type. • Document Type Definition Template – The standard cXML template that defines the document type. 18 PUBLIC Guided Integration for Trading Partners Guided Integration for Trading Partners -- 8 of 10 -- 3. Choose a My Workspace template. The choices for the My Workspace template include the following: • Draft Template – The last draft template you saved for the selected document type. • My Latest Template – The latest template you saved for the selected document type. • SAP Supplier Super Template – Customized template that matches all your buyer relationships in SAP Business Network. • SAP Golden Template – Standard template that matches the most used fields in SAP Business Network. • Upload Supplier Template – Upload your template to use it to compare and reconcile. Network に対する⾃動処理連携: お取引先様による⾃動処理連携とは何か? ⾃動処理連携とは、お取引先様のERPをSAP Business Networkと電⼦的に接続する、⼈⼿を 介さない処理⽅法を指します。 バイヤー様の全ての購買処理が弊社標準のcXMLフォーマットをもってSAP Business Network で処理される場合、お取引先様はcXMLやEDIまたはCSVやPOFlipとして知られているネット ワークポータル(ブラウザ経由の⼿作業)などその他の⽅法を⽤いて購買処理を実施致します。 何故⾃動処理連携なのか? システムからシステムへ データが送信される場合、 それはより早く、より正確 (45-60%)で、反復処理に 適しており、⽐較的安価で、 更にバイヤー様とお取引先 様の満⾜度が向上します。 誰が⾃動処理連携を実施す るべきか? これはお取引先様の選択に なります。お取引量が⾃動 処理連携実施の有無に影響 しますが、しかしお取引先 様がSAP Business Networkを介してバイヤー 様との間でその実施を望む かどうかを決断します。 左の図は、システム間、つ まり B2B のデータ処理に焦 点を当てて、⾃動処理連携 がどのように機能するのか を⽰しています。 バイヤーERP & Enablement Lead (NxL) Integration Advisor (IA) Integration Specialist (IS) バイヤー様側 お取引先様側 • お客様のプロジェクトチームと協⼒して⾃動処 理連携の戦略、計画及び作業予定を⽴案します。 • “Buyer Readiness Verification” (BRV)の作成 を主導します。 • タイムリーな⾃動処理連携対応メンバーのアサ インメントの為、⾃動処理連携管理の為のメン バー配置を調整します。 • SBN上での⾃動処理連携に⻑けた専⾨家とし て活動します。 • ⾃動処理連携に関連する書類を検証するため のソリューションテストを実⾏します。 • ⾃動処理連携に関連する書類を準備します。 • 初期導⼊中は、単⼀の問い合わせ窓⼝として、 IS(Integration Specialist)と共にお取引先様 の作業をサポートします。 • 他のメンバーに知識を共有します。 • 既に定められたエスカレーションパスに従い、 問題点をエスカレーションします。 • 各お取引先様の⾃動処理連携プロジェクトを、 カタログのサポートを含めて能動的に管理しま す。 • 失敗した、または却下されたテスト通信のトラ ブルシューティングを⾏います。 • お取引先様の進捗やマイルストーンの達成につ いて週次で報告します。 注意事項︓ SIチーム(お取引先様の⾃動連係対応チーム)はシェアードサービスの位置づけの為、複数のバイヤー様プロジェクトを同時並⾏で対応しています。対象の地域や対応内容の複雑さ、 ⾃動連係対象のお取引先様社数などの条件に応じて、同じ担当者または複数の担当者が割り当てられる場合があります。SIチームでは、バイヤー様の業務⽬標達成を最⼤限サポートする為に、 プロジェクト毎にSI担当者のアサインメントを決定しています。 -- 7 of 10 -- 8 INTERNAL | SAP AND CUSTOMERS ONLY ⾃動処理連携におけるバイヤー様側の各担当内容 ビジネスリード SBN Admin テクニカルリード テストリード • プロジェクト調整に関するバイ ヤー様側の主な連絡先 • プロジェクトスケジュールに関 する合意を提供 • 予定されたプロジェクト会議へ の参加 • 業務処理に関する質問への回答 • テスト⼿順書の調整 • 完了したテスト⼿順書の評価 • テストが完了したことの確認 • ⾃⾝のアカウントに対する ベンダーマスターの設定お よびサプライヤー様の適 • バイヤー様側システムと SBN間での注⽂書処理成功 の為の連携を実施 • サプライヤー様がテスト実 施可能となった際の連絡 • バックエンドシステムへの ⾃動処理連携に関する技術 的な詳細を提供 • 購買データ処理失敗に関す るトラブルシューティング を⽀援 • テストシナリオに対する評価と確 認 • テスト⼿順書の要件に沿ったPOの 作成 • テスト⼿順書へのPO番号の記⼊。 (バイヤー様とお取引先様が合意済 みのもの)。 • 必要に応じて、バイヤー様側テク ニカルメンバーを投⼊ • オーダー確認や事前出荷通知 (=ASN)、請求書、クレジットメ モがきちんとSBNからバイヤー様 ERPに向かって処理さてたことを 検証する。 • 返信された処理結果に応じたテス ト⼿順書の更新 注意事項︓これらのロールは御社社内のお⼀⼈または複数の⽅より担当されることがございます。 -- 8 of 10 -- 9 INTERNAL | SAP AND CUSTOMERS ONLY お取引先様はどのようにSAP Business Networkと接続するのか? CIG*=“Cloud Integration Gateway” • ⾃動処理連携実施のお取引先様⽅にとっての接続⽅法 • cXMLのEDIデータフォーマットをサポート • HTTPSの通信プロトコルをサポート • ご⾃⾝で実施する、お取引先様からSAP Business Networkへの接続テストツール • 購買データ処理およびその処理エラーに関する追跡 注意事項︓お取引先様とBusiness Network間データ通信を実現する場合には、CIGをご利⽤いただいても結構ですが、直接cXMLフォーマットをご利⽤いただい てHTTPS⼿順で通信をすることも可能です。 *CIG: 「SAP Integration Suite, Managed gateway」にも呼ばれることをどうぞご了承ください。 -- 9 of 10 -- 10 INTERNAL | SAP AND CUSTOMERS ONLY 補⾜事項: Integration Kit – Solution Blueprint Solution Blueprintはバイヤー様のプロジェクト要件を概説する、バ イヤー様固有の業務範囲定義書であり、お取引先様の⾃動処理連携に 関するさまざまな業務および技術的側⾯を⽂書化しています。 Solution Blueprintは次の⽬的で使⽤されています: • スムーズかつ迅速な準備を促進するために、バイヤー様とお取引 先様の双⽅から考えられる全ての⾃動処理連携に関する要件を特 定して⽂書化する。 • ⾃動処理連携にかかる開発の設計開始の前段階に、あらゆる側⾯ から例外や懸念事項を特定、分析、⽂書化する。 • ⾃動処理連携に関するシステムの詳細をカバーする。 • プロジェクト追跡に関する詳細 – プロジェクトの予定表と作業⽇ 程、テスト計画、プロジェクトのリスク、作業⼈員確保の要件と 可⽤性、ベストプラクティス、次の作業内容などをカバーします。 本件の取り組みは、アサインされたSAP⾃動処 理連携スペシャリストによって対応されます。 割り当てられた担当⼈員は、全ての責任を遂⾏ する為の正しいスキルと知識を持っていること が前提となります。 ・業務運営に関する知識 ・顧客とのやり取りで経験が豊富な開発者 -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/INT Integration Overvie.content: INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Integration for SAP Business Network -- 1 of 10 -- 2 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Introduction to SAP Business Network Integration: What is Trading Partner Integration? Integration is connecting a trading partner’s ERP to the SAP Business Network by an electronic method via a touchless process. While all of your transactions are submitted to the Network using our native language, cXML, your trading partner may choose to transact using cXML, EDI, or use other methods such as CSV, or using the Network Portal, also known as POFlip. Trading Partner ERP Customer ERP Purchase Orders Invoices Why integrate? When data is transferred from system to system, it is faster, more accurate (45- 60%), more repeatable, less expensive (60-75%), and improves both trading partner and buyer satisfaction. Who should integrate? It’s the trading partner’s choice! Transaction volume can be used to help prioritize but trading partners will confirm whether they wish to integrate a particular buyer relationship on the Network. The image to the left shows how the integration works, focusing on system to system, or B2B, transacting. -- 2 of 10 -- 3 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only How can Trading Partners Transact over the SAP Business Network? Manual Semi-Automated Automated data entry performed by trading partner some set up work required by buyer and trading partner set up work to configure system to system data transmission using the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway Network Portal CSV cXML EDI PIDX OAGIS • The manual conversion of using the Network User Interface to create a order confirmation, advanced ship notice, invoice, credit, or other document from an order, also known as “POFlip” • Comma Separated Value/Variable (CSV) file represents structured way of data stored as plain text file. CSV invoice upload supports the transfer, transformation and loading of comma delimited files representing a trading partner’s order confirmations, ship notices, invoices, and credits to be rendered as cXML invoices for their Customers. • The Commerce eXtensible Markup Language (cXML) is an open language defined by public Document Type Definitions (DTDs). These DTDs define cXML so that it is extremely flexible. It is the Network’s native language, created by SAP Ariba in 1999, intended for the communication of business documents between procurement applications, e- commerce hubs, and trading partners. Electronic data interchange (EDI) is the concept of businesses electronically communicating information that was traditionally communicated on paper, such as purchase orders and invoices. Technical standards for EDI exist to facilitate parties transacting such instruments without having to make special arrangements. • ANSI ASC X12 version 004010 American National Standards Institute Accredited Standards Committee X12 • UN EDIFACT version D96A with syntax version 3 and Syntax levels UNOC United Nations Electronic Data Interchange For Administration Commerce And Transport • Petroleum Industry Data eXchange (PIDX) provides a global forum for delivering the process, information and technology standards that facilitates seamless, efficient digital business within the oil and gas industry and its trading community. • Open Applications Group Integration Specification (OAGIS): OAGIS defines a common content model and common messages for communication between business applications. This includes application- to-application (A2A) and business-to-business (B2B) integration. -- 3 of 10 -- 4 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only What is the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway? While you’re working through your Systems Integration Testing (SIT), we want to confirm that we have properly identified and understand the requirements for integrated trading partners, so they can be accurately documented. This process is critical in creating a system to best support your business outcome objectives. Testing with buyers Testing with trading partners We test with buyers to validate our understanding of the solution scope and the requirements for integrated trading partners. We test with trading partners to validate the trading partner’s mapping against buyer’s requirements. Integration testing is required. -- 3 of 10 -- 14 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Testing Key Takeaways and Considerations buyer and individual trading partner Who What When Where Why How Solutions Testing •• Buy Side integration resource with buyer resource involvement • Design and Realize Phases • Buyer’s Network TEST Environment • Validate the solution • Identify technical requirements that may be difficult for integrated trading partners to fulfill • Obtain verified samples to use in integrated documentation • Posting integrated documents to the Network Mapping Testing with Trading Partners • Facilitate an integration project using the established process • Explore Phase for initial connectivity testing • Realize Phase for completing test scripts • Buyer’s and Trading Partner’s Business Network TEST Environments • Validate the trading partner mapping to ensure buyer’s requirements are met • Identify technical requirements that may be difficult for specific integrated trading partners to fulfill • Status calls facilitated by Sell Side Integration resource with • Posting integrated documents to the Business Network • Sell Side integration resource with buyer resource involvement • Trading Partners • Buy Side integration resource acts as an integrated trading partner to perform test scripts for validating the solution scope -- 4 of 10 -- 15 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Timing during Project Implementation Prepare Explore & Realize Deploy & Run The work done to set up the integration workstream is in parallel with the overall project deployment and enablement. The integration resources will work with the customer and all of the SAP project team contacts to determine the appropriate roll out for each project. In the case where there are not adequate resources to support an integration workstream in parallel with a project implementation, the set up work prior to engaging trading partners should still take place in order to position the program for integrations in the future. The integration workstream milestones will overlap with the implementation and enablement project plans. Typical timelines for the pilot integration wave, once build is complete and stable includes 4 weeks of buy side work to perform solutions testing and creating the integration specifications for trading partners. After this work is completed, typical timelines for trading partners is 12 weeks. In many cases, the integrated pilot wave will have a later go live date than Portal/POFlip trading partners. -- 5 of 10 -- 16 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Keys to Success How can I have a successful integration program with my trading partners? • Remember that it’s a partnership between you, us, and your trading partner! • Follow our recommended best practices • Mitigate common challenges • Be engaged in meetings to discuss status through accurate and timely reporting • Collaborate with us in establishing project governance and escalation paths Follow Best Practices Mitigation Reporting & Meetings Project Governance -- 6 of 10 -- 17 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Keys to Success: Follow Best Practices Pilot Wave Future Waves During Implementation, you want to include a sampling of integrated trading partners (the “pilots”) by buying channel, business process, and transaction format (cXML, EDI, PIDX, etc.) to verify the requirements. For future waves of trading partners, you want to expand the proven process, best practices, and solution verification of the pilot to larger waves of trading partners. • Integrated Trading Partners • typically represent the bulk of your PO & Invoice transaction volumes. They are key to unlocking your adoption goals to attain business objectives. • require additional lead time to plan and staff their resources to support integration in time for your Go Live. • Have understanding on current business processes with the trading partner • Early business level discussions and engagement are needed to provide the integrated trading partner with visibility into: • Future state of business process • Alignment on scope of spend category, buying channel, business unit • Document choreography and SAP Business Network requirements • Procurement Content (catalogs, contracts) • Timing, Partnership, Expectations, and Alignment • Larger waves of integrations can be managed when adequate planning is conducted and lead time is provided to trading partners • Any new additional changes to Business Network requirements, is considered a change in scope therefore Implementation Team members may need to be re-engaged -- 7 of 10 -- 18 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Keys to Success: Mitigate Common Challenges Resources have day jobs… Resources can’t answer questions… The timeline is too short! Who cares about trading partners? I have more changes… Integration Requires… • Dedicated resources (including 3rd party consulting teams) without competing priorities within the project implementation • The right individuals to support at the technical and business levels, including input to the test scripts • Creating plans with timelines that meet the buyer’s and trading partner’s ability to agree and commit, with clearly defined contingencies • Considering trading partners as stakeholders when designing the solution and creating project plans with timelines • No changes to design and requirements after sign off without an impact assessment and adjust to timeline -- 8 of 10 -- 19 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Keys to Success: Reporting & Meetings In order to keep you up to date on progress, we have a few channels available to engage with your resources. There are standard reports the integration team will leverage to provide status updates, call out risks and action items, and confirm things are moving as expected. Weekly Buyer Status Weekly Trading Partner Status • Review project status • Review exception status of trading partners • Discuss resolution to obstacles • Review status of action items • Review project status with each trading partner • Discuss resolution to obstacles • Review status of action items -- 9 of 10 -- 20 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Gradient in Shape Gradient in Shape Keys to Success: Establish Project Governance Having a Governance process in place assists with overcoming obstacles related to: • Disengaged or non- responsive resources • Knowledge of who to go to when challenges arise • Levels of escalation to have complex decisions quickly resolved Teamwork Communication Gradient in Shape Accountability -- 10 of 10 --

Transaction volume can be used to help prioritize, but trading partners will confirm whether they wish to integrate a particular buyer relationship on the SAP Business Network. Why Integrate? Electronic communication is faster, more accurate (45-60%), more repeatable, less expensive (60-75%) and improves both trading partner and buyer satisfaction. file://SBN/split/INT Integration Overvie.content: 11 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only When does all of this happen? Prepare Explore & Realize Deploy & Run The work done to set up the integration workstream is in parallel with the overall project deployment and enablement. The integration resources will work with the customer and all of the SAP project team contacts to determine the appropriate roll out for each project. In the case where there are not adequate resources to support an integration workstream in parallel with a project implementation, the set up work prior to engaging trading partners should still take place in order to position the program for integrations in the future. The integration workstream milestones will overlap with the implementation and enablement project plans. Typical timelines for the pilot integration wave, once build is complete and stable includes 4 weeks of buy side work to perform solutions testing and creating the integration specifications for trading partners. After this work is completed, typical timelines for trading partners is 12 weeks. In many cases, the integrated pilot wave will have a later go live date than Portal/POFlip trading partners. -- 1 of 10 -- 12 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Why should I support trading partner integration? While you’re working through your Systems Integration Testing (SIT), we want to confirm that we have properly identified and understand the requirements for integrated trading partners, so they can be accurately documented. This process is critical in creating a system to best support your business outcome objectives. Testing with buyers Testing with trading partners We test with buyers to validate our understanding of the solution scope and the requirements for integrated trading partners. We test with trading partners to validate the trading partner’s mapping against buyer’s requirements. Trading Partner integration testing is required. -- 2 of 10 -- How can I have a successful trading partner integration program? -- 3 of 10 -- 14 INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Remember - It’s a partnership!
