file://SBN/split/Invoice error messages_.content:  English  FAQ KB0394765 Invoice error messages Symptom How do I troubleshoot an invoice error? Resolution Below is a list of possible error messages produced by the SAP Business Network for invoices. These messages are generated if invoice processing detects errors when suppliers submit invoices through any channel (online, cXML, EDI, or CSV). To search the list, press CTRL+F on your keyboard and then enter the text of the error message. If you receive an ANERR message, try the steps described here. Error No. Error Message Meaning and suggested resolution 1 INVOICE_DUPLICATE An invoice with the same ID has already been received. If the invoice is not a duplicate, resubmit it with a different ID. 2 INVOICE_NO_ID The invoice number is blank in the submitted invoice. Enter an invoice number, and resubmit the invoice 3 SHIPPING_IN_LINE_ERROR The isShippingInLine element indicates shipping information is provided at the line level. The invoice indicates that shipping information is provided at line item level but the invoice header also contains shipping information. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 4 SUMMARY_AND_DETAIL The InvoiceDetailHeaderIndicator contradicts the InvoiceDetailOrder element. The InvoiceDetailHeaderIndicator element indicates that the invoice is a summary invoice. The InvoiceDetailOrder element can appear in only a detail invoice. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 5 DETAIL_AND_SUMMARY The InvoiceDetailHeaderIndicator contradicts the InvoiceDetailHeaderOrder element. The InvoiceDetailHeaderIndicator element indicates that the invoice is a detail invoice. The InvoiceDetailHeaderOrder element can appear in only a summary invoice. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 6 INV_ROLE_IN_SHIPPING The Contact role in the InvoiceDetailShipping element is not a valid value. Check the cXML specification or DTD for the list of valid roles for the Contact -- 1 of 7 -- element. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 7 INV_ROLE_IN_PARTNER The Contact role in the InvoicePartner element is not a valid value. Check the cXML specification or DTD for the list of valid roles for the Contact element. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 8 INV_LINE_DUPLICATE There are multiple invoice line items with the same ID. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 9 ASN_NOT_FOUND The invoice references a nonexistent shipping notice document. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 10 NO_PCARD_INVOICE This customer does not allow suppliers to generate invoices for PCard orders. 11 PCARD_INF_ONLY PCard order invoices are for information only. The isInformationOnly attribute in the InvoiceDetailRequestHeader must be set to yes. 12 PO_NOT_FOUND Cannot find the PO referenced in the invoice. Correct the PO number and resubmit the invoice. 13 PO_OBSOLETE The invoice references an obsolete, replaced, or duplicate PO. Use the current version of the PO and resubmit the invoice. 14 MULTIPLE_PO The Order ID matches multiple purchase orders. Use the DocumentReference element in cXML to reference the purchase order. You must provide the payloadID of the PO you want to invoice. 15 NON_PO_INVOICE This customer does not accept invoices for orders sent outside of the SAP Business Network. The invoice references a PO that does not exist in the SAP Business Network. Change the PO number and resubmit the invoice. 16 HEADER_WITH_ACCOUNT_IN_LINE The isAccountingInLine indicator must be set to false if the isHeaderInvoice element is set to true. The header invoice cannot have accounting specified at the line-item level. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 17 CREDIT_DEBIT_MEMO_NOT_HEADER The isHeaderInvoice indicator must be set to true for a credit or debit memo. A credit or debit memo must be a header invoice. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 18 CREDIT_MEMO_PAYMENT Payment terms are not allowed in a credit memo. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 19 SHIPPING_NO_CONTACT The shipFrom or shipTo contact roles are missing from the InvoiceDetailShipping element. The InvoiceDetailShipping element must contain Contact elements with both -- 2 of 7 -- shipFrom and shipTo roles. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 20 DELETE_NO_REFERENCE A delete invoice must contain a DocumentReference for an existing invoice. An invoice with the delete operation must reference an existing invoice. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 21 NET_PAYMENT_INVALID The net payment terms in the invoice do not match the net payment terms in the PO. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 22 DISCOUNT_PAYMENT_INVALID The discount payment terms in the invoice do not match the discount payment terms in the order. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 23 QUANTITY_INVALID_NUMBER The quantity value is not a valid number. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 24 LINE_NUMBER_LINE_ITEM_REF_INVALID The lineNumber attribute of a InvoiceDetailItemReference is not a valid number. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 25 PO_LINE_QUANTITY_INVALID The quantity of a line item exceeds the buying organization's quantity limits. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 26 PO_LINE_UOM_INVALID The unit of measure of an invoice line item does not match the unit of measure of the original PO line item. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 27 PO_LINE_PART_ID_INVALID The supplier part ID in the invoice does not match the supplier part ID of the original PO line item. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 28 PO_LINE_CURRENCY_INVALID The unit price currency of an invoice item does not match the unit price currency of the original PO line item. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 29 PO_LINE_PRICE_INVALID The unit price of an invoice item does not match the unit price of the original PO line item. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 30 PO_LINE_NOT_FOUND The invoice line item does not exist in the original PO. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 31 CREDIT_MEMO_DUE_POSITIVE The Due Amount must be negative for a credit memo. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 32 DEBIT_MEMO_DUE_NEGATIVE The Due Amount must be positive for a debit memo.Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 33 EXCEPTION An exception occurred while processing the invoice. The invoice contained unexpected errors. 34 INVALID_REF_HEADER Invalid DocumentReference element in the InvoiceDetailRequestHeader. Check the -- 3 of 7 -- cXML specification or DTD for the list of valid values. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 35 INVOICE_UPDATE The invoice status has been successfully updated. 36 INVOICE_UPDATE_WITH_PAYMENT The invoice status has been successfully updated. 37 INVOICE_VALIDATION_FAIL Invoice validation failed. The submitted invoice contains errors and is invalid. Check for errors in the invoice history for more information on the failure. 38 INVOICE_RECEIVED The invoice was successfully received. 39 BLANK_PERIOD_START_DATE The startDate attribute cannot be blank. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 40 BLANK_PERIOD_END_DATE The endDate attribute cannot be blank. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 41 MISSING_UNIT_RATE The UnitRate is required for labor items. The UnitRate is not specified in InvoiceDetailServiceItem with InvoiceLaborDetail. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 42 MISSING_QUANTITY The Quantity is required for labor items. The Quantity is not specified in InvoiceDetailServiceItem with InvoiceLaborDetail. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 43 INVALID_TIMECARD_REFERENCE Invalid TimeCardReference value for labor item. The invoice references a time sheet that does not exist on the SAP Business Network. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 44 MULTIPLE_TIMECARD_FOUND Multiple time sheets match TimeCardReference in a labor item. 45 MISSING_PERIOD The Period in the labor item is a required value. The Period value is not specified in InvoiceDetailServiceItem with InvoiceLaborDetail. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 46 PERIOD_NO_MATCH The Period in InvoiceDetailServiceItem with InvoiceLaborDetail does not match the period in the time sheet specified by the InvoiceLaborDetail InvoiceTimeCardDetail TimeCardReference element. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 47 MISSING_PAYCODE The Pay code is a required value in the labor item. UnitRate TermReference with termName (payCode) is not specified in InvoiceDetailServiceItem with InvoiceLaborDetail. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. -- 4 of 7 -- 48 CAN_NOT_SAVE_CHANGES Cannot save changes to the invoice. Changes to the invoice conflict with other changes made by the system. The invoice will reprocess in the next scheduled time frame. 49 PSFT_INVOICE_STATUS_UPDATE The status of the invoice has been successfully updated. 50 PSFT_INVOICE_STATUS_RESET The invoice has been successfully reset to its initial status. 51 NO_CANCEL_INVOICE This customer does not allow invoice cancelation. 52 PO_LINE_AMT_OVER_BILLING The subtotal of a line item exceeds the buying organization's line item subtotal limits. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 53 INVOICE_NET_AMT_OVER_LIMIT The net amount exceeds the buying organization's net amount limits.Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 54 INVOICE_UPDATE_COMMNETS The invoice status has been successfully updated with comments from your customer. 55 INVOICE_STATUS_UPDATE The invoice status has been successfully updated by your customer. 56 UNIT_PRICE_MISSING The unit price is missing for a line item. 57 MISSING_ORDER_ID Order ID is required by this buying organization. Enter an order ID and resubmit the invoice. 58 TAX_INFO_MISMATCH The tax information at invoice line {0} does not match the tax information in the PO. This customer requires that the PO tax information match the tax information included in the invoice. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 59 TAX_SUMMARY_WRONG The tax information in the summary does not match the total from the line item. The Tax Summary information is wrong. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 60 TAX_SUM_INCORRECT The total tax does not equal the sum of all tax lines. The tax total is calculated incorrectly at the specified line item. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 61 BILL_TO_REQUIRED The bill-to information is missing or incomplete. Your customer requests this information. Complete the bill-to information and resubmit the invoice. 62 CUSTOMER_VAT_ID_REQUIRED The Customer VAT ID is missing. Your customer requests this information. Enter a valid Customer VAT ID and resubmit the invoice. 63 REMIT_TO_REQUIRED The remit-to information is missing or incomplete.Your customer requests this -- 5 of 7 -- information. Complete the remit-to information and resubmit the invoice. 64 SUPPLIER_VAT_ID_REQUIRED The Supplier VAT ID is missing. Your customer requests this information. Enter the Supplier VAT ID and resubmit the invoice. 65 TAX_POINT_DATE_REQUIRED_AT_LINE The Supply Date in the VAT entry is missing from the line. Your customer requests this information. Enter the Supply Date and resubmit the invoice. 66 ITEM_DESCRIPTION_REQUIRED The Item Description is missing from the line. Your customer requests this information. Enter the Item Description and resubmit the invoice. 67 VAT_REQUIRED_AT_LINE The VAT information is missing from the line. Your customer requests this information. Enter the VAT information and resubmit the invoice. 68 VAT_PERCENTAGE_MISSING_AT_LINE The VAT rate is missing from the line. Your customer requests this information. Enter the VAT rate and resubmit the invoice. 69 VAT_REQUIRED_AT_SUMMARY The VAT information in the invoice summary is missing. Your customer requests this information. Enter the VAT information in the invoice summary and resubmit the invoice. 70 VAT_PERCENTAGE_MISSING_AT_SUMMARY The VAT rate in the invoice summary is missing. Your customer requests this information. Enter the VAT rate in the invoice summary and resubmit the invoice. 71 TAX_POINT_DATE_REQUIRED_AT_SUMMARY The Supply Date in the VAT entry in the invoice summary is missing. Your customer requests this information. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 72 TAX_AMOUNT_INVALID_AT_LINE The VAT amount for the line item is not a valid value. Your customer requests this information. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 73 TAX_AMOUNT_INVALID_AT_SUMMARY The VAT amount in the invoice summary is not a valid value. Your customer requests this information. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 74 TAXABLE_AMOUNT_INVALID_AT_LINE The VAT taxable amount for the line item is not a valid value. Your customer requests this information. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 75 TAXABLE_AMOUNT_INVALID_AT_SUMMARY The VAT taxable amount in the invoice summary is not a valid value. Your customer requests this information. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 76 SHIP_FROM_MISSING_AT_LINE The Ship From information for the line item is missing or incomplete. Your customer requests this information. Complete the Ship From information and resubmit the invoice. -- 6 of 7 -- 77 SHIP_TO_MISSING_AT_LINE The Ship To information for the line item is missing or incomplete. Your customer requests this information. Complete the Ship To information and resubmit the invoice. 78 SHIP_FROM_MISSING_AT_HEADER The Ship From information is missing or incomplete in the invoice header. Your customer requests this information. Enter the Ship From information in the invoice header and resubmit the invoice. 79 SHIP_TO_MISSING_AT_HEADER The Ship To information is missing or incomplete in the invoice header. Your customer requests this information. Enter the Ship To information in the invoice header and resubmit the invoice. 80 INVALID_LINE_NUMBER The invoiceLineNumber attribute value is not a valid value. The line number in the invoice is not a number. Correct the error and resubmit the invoice. 81 MISSING_REASON_FOR_ZERO_RATE_VAT See Also Keep in mind that this list is not exhaustive as you might receive custom rejection messages from your customer. If this happens,you need to reach out to your customers directly for more information. SAP Business Network Enterprise account fee model A supplier enterprise account on SAP Business Network unlocks extended capabilities to enhance collaboration with your customers. You can automate more transactions, gain insight, improve compliance, and benefit from extended support and services. The enterprise account fee model is detailed below. Did you know? 93.1%of active suppliers on SAP Business Network transact for free* As a supplier on SAP Business Network, you pay fees only under the following conditions: Fee or no fee? 1. You have an enterprise account. 2. You meet both of these thresholds in any customer relationship: a. You have transacted over US$50,000 worth of orders or invoices. b. You have exchanged at least five documents. The flowchart below illustrates if and how the transaction fee is charged. Do I have an enterprise account? NO No fees are applicable on a standard account YES Have I transacted over $50,000 with at least one customer? NO There are no fees YES Have I exchanged five or more documents on the network? NO There are no fees YES Without service sheets The fee is 0.155% of your transactions amount. With service sheets The fee is 0.35% of your transactions amount. Fee model If your enterprise account is chargeable, the fee comprises two components: the transaction fee, based on document value, and the subscription fee, based on the number of documents. Transaction Fee (Billed quarterly) The transaction fee is a percentage of the value of purchase orders or invoices exchanged, whichever is greater. 0.155% of transacted value for relationships without service sheets (3) 0.35% of transacted value for relationships with service sheets (3) Capped at $20,000 per customer relationship Subscription Fee (Billed annually) The subscription fee is a set amount based on your account level, determined by the number of annual documents (1) you transact across all customer relationships. Number of documents per year Subscription level Yearly fee 5 to 24 documents or <$250,000 (2) Bronze $50 25 to 99 documents Silver $750 100 to 499 documents Gold $2,250 >500 documents Platinum $5,500 1. Only purchase orders (POs), invoices, and service sheets are considered chargeable documents. All other documents (order confirmations, ship notices, and more) are excluded from the document volume count. 2. Suppliers transacting less than $250,000 annually are automatically placed at the lowest annual fee level, regardless of the number of documents transacted. 3. Service sheets are used to record services as they are actually performed with reference to the specifications from the PO. In general, you can enter an invoice for a PO only after the service entry sheet has also been accepted. Only accepted service sheets are charged. Examples of total annual cost • A supplier that exchanged 32 documents with a total transaction value of $120,000 in a customer relationship without service sheets is placed at the bronze level and pays $236 per year ((120,000 * 0.155%) + 50). • A supplier that exchanged 250 documents with a total transaction value of $600,000 in a customer relationship without service sheets is placed at the gold level and pays $3,180 per year ((600,000 * 0.155%) + 2,250). • A supplier that exchanged 80 documents with a total transaction value of $250,000 in a customer relationship including service sheets is placed at the silver level and pays $1,625 per year ((250,000 * 0.35%) + 750). • A supplier that exchanged three documents with a total transaction value of $120,000 doesn’t pay any fees. When your transaction value or document volume exceeds the free threshold, you become a chargeable supplier and owe subscription fees. Your first bill for SAP Business Network When this occurs, SAP Business Network totals your historical monthly document counts across all customer relationships, up to three months if available, and annualizes that amount to determine your subscription level for the next year. The date your transactions first become chargeable is your anniversary date. Each year on that date, your subscription level is reevaluated. This reevaluation is based on your total number of documents transacted during the previous 12 months. Additional resources Calculate your fees Use our online fee calculator to get an estimate of the yearly fees for your enterprise account. Get supplier assistance Find more information and support on our help center by clicking the question mark icon ( ? ) in the top-right corner of your supplier login page. If you’re not transacting in U.S. dollars, please use the tables below to find the corresponding amount in your local currency. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide This guide describes how the administrator for a seller account can update company information and configure additional users. Supplier administrators must maintain complete and accurate company information to be matched to new prospective buyers. This guide applies to: SAP Business Network SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network Discovery Related guides SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Configuring Document Routing Managing Subscription Services Types of SAP Business Network Accounts You have the choice to do business using one of two SAP Business Network account types: Standard or Enterprise. Some suppliers choose to transact on the SAP Business Network using a fee based Enterprise account due to their historical volume of transactions or to leverage certain functionality that is only available with an Enterprise account. If you are unsure which account type to choose, register a free of charge standard account. You can always upgrade to an Enterprise account if your business needs change. When a buyer has an active subscription for SAP Business Network Supplier Chain Collaboration, suppliers can only register as an enterprise account. See, SAP Business Network Registration. Temporary Account Support for Suppliers Supplier account administrators who prefer to manage new registrations on behalf of their company can claim ownership of their email domain and configure the registration options—including the option to allow creation of temporary accounts. Supplier account administrators who prefer to manage new registrations on behalf of their company can claim ownership of their email domain and configure the registration options, including the option to allow creation of temporary accounts. A Temporary Standard Account allows suppliers to register on SAP Business Network with limited functionality. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain has adapted the SAPUI5 technology to improve user experience intuitiveness, navigation, content organization, and visual consistency. Supplier Displays the name of the supplier. Document Number The document ID with a link to the relevant document for the quality notification or quality inspection. Customer Part Number A unique identifier that a buyer assigns to a product or item. Supplier Part Number An alphanumeric identifier assigned by a supplier to every product it sells. The supplier part number is used by a company as part of its master data for the products that it buys from that supplier. Customer Batch A batch of a product that is batch-managed by the customer. The customer creates the batches for a product in the customer's back-end system and transmits them to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Supplier Batch Batch of a finished product (primary product or co-product) that the supplier defined so as to identify a particular finished-product quantity in the work order. Date Received The date and time the quality notification was sent to the recipient. Event Type Quality Notifications: Displays the status of the quality notification as Created, Updated, Completed, and Closed. Quality Inspections: Receive alerts for submitted quality inspection results, requests, or usage decisions. Customer Relationships To begin transacting business with a customer on SAP Business Network, your customer needs to send you a relationship request. You can either accept or reject the relationship request. This two-step process ensures that buying organizations are not inundated with customer catalogs, and that suppliers’ product and service offerings are treated confidentially. In SAP Business Network, users or members of the same organization often create multiple accounts for various reasons. Sometimes, users forget they have already registered and sign up again, while different departments or teams may create separate accounts for each member within the same organization. Additionally, accounts are often registered under different emails, usernames, or roles (such as individual and team accounts). These duplicate accounts lead to fragmented user data, increased administrative overhead, and other challenges for both users and the platform. This feature enables users to identify multiple accounts linked to the same organization or individual. See, Linking to a Child Account. Account Linking If you have multiple SAP Business Network accounts, you might benefit from setting up an account linking as Parent and Child accounts. Account Linking benefits include the following: One individual can handle service management tasks for the entire organization, saving time and effort. The administrator for the parent account can align the subscription terms for all subsidiaries’ services to start and end on the same date, so that all subscription expirations and renewals occur at the same time. Realignment can occur whether or not subsidiary accounts have already subscribed to services on their own. The administrator for the parent account can pay for all subsidiaries’ subscriptions in a single payment. The administrator of the Parent account has Child Account Access permissions which enable users to automatically sign on to a child account without having to enter a user name and password. In addition to these benefits, you can also control the visibility of your accounts to potential business partners. By default, both the parent and child accounts are visible to potential business partners when they perform a search for you on SAP Business Network. However, you can control the visibility of your child accounts by configuring the Allow buyer organizations to search this account setting. When this setting is enabled, business partners can search for both parent and child accounts on SAP Business Network. When this setting is unchecked, business partners can search and view only the parent accounts on SAP Business Network. Service Management in Account Linking The administrator for a parent account can work with SAP Business Network Customer Support to manage services for child accounts. This includes subscribing to, updating, renewing, and canceling services on behalf of the child accounts. The parent account administrator can view the status of each child account’s subscriptions in the Service Subscriptions My Subsidiaries’ Services section of the parent account.  Note Suppliers from any Data Centre can now establish parent-child relationships with suppliers from any other centre. For example: Suppliers from KSA can now establish a parent-child relationship with the suppliers in the US.  Note You cannot create an account hierarchy in your test account.  Note 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 110 This is custom documentation. Archiving ensures invoices remain unaltered, secure, and legally compliant, supporting long-term retention requirements mandated by country- or region-specific regulations. The following rules are applicable for archiving invoices: Invoices are archived in ZIP format at configurable frequencies, twice a day, daily, weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly. Archived invoices are retained for three months within the SAP Business Network buyer’s account. Both PDF and cXML formats are archived, which is configurable. Archiving begins after a 30-day lag period to account for the average invoicing cycle, unless immediate archiving is explicitly requested. Archived files can be downloaded from the Archived Invoices page or automatically delivered to a buyer-maintained repository.  Note You can either configure additional options or Save. a. If applicable, activate the following options in the Non-Catalog Order Routing Preferences: Activate the Route non-catalog orders as catalog orders with part numbers option. Implementation Details General Prerequisites Ensure that the following prerequisites are met: Ensure that administrator or a user has Archive Access permission. A valid HTTPS URL (with SSL certificate) if automatic delivery of archive files is required. Enable PDF generation through SAP Business Networksupport if human-readable copies are required. Ensure that the designated repository supports WORM technology (Write Once, Read Many) or equivalent secure storage methods for legal compliance. Restrictions The following restrictions are applicable: Failed or rejected invoices cannot be archived. Archive files are automatically deleted after three months. Notifications and PDF generation are out of scope unless explicitly enabled. Pending queue implementation is not included in standard archiving. Compliance Considerations Ensure that you meet the following compliance considerations before configuring invoices for archiving: Archival periods are defined by local regulations (typically, invoices must be retained for several years beyond issuance). All electronic signatures, certificates, and verification protocols must also be archived. Data integrity must be preserved through: Digital signatures (ensuring proof of non-alteration). Secure access control. Immutable storage (e.g., WORM). Configuring Archival Settings Follow these steps to configure invoice archive: 1. Deletion Settings for Transaction Data (Suppliers) The administrator for your SAP Business Network account and other users with appropriate permission can specify the retention period for transaction documents. Additionally, SAP Business Network automatically deletes supplier master data after an extended period of inactivity. You may need to delete old transaction documents to meet regulatory needs in your country/region or business requirements in your organization. If you request recurring deletion of transaction data, the system deletes any transaction document sets older than the retention period every month. Each document set includes transaction documents and any associated attachments. You can also request a one-time deletion of transaction data. This operation is similar, but it happens only once, not every month. For example, you can delete your transaction data older than January 1, 2018. Types of Transaction Documents That Can Be Deleted The following transaction documents can be deleted: Purchase orders (orders and blanket orders) Order confirmations Ship notices Receipts  Note If a supplier account is deleted from the SAP Business Network, the RFx transactions responded by the supplier are not deleted immediately. The RFx transactions get deleted only after the buyers' and the suppliers' accounts associated with that RFx are deleted. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 135 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Service sheets Invoices, credit memos, and debit memos Payment documents SAP Business Network for Supply Chain transaction documents Quote requests and quote messages Associated attachments Workflow for Deleting Transaction Documents The following diagram shows the workflow for deleting transaction documents from SAP Business Network: Workflow for Deleting Transaction Documents from SAP Business Network Data Deletion Restrictions This feature doesn't affect archived invoices, which are stored separately. Once a document has been identified for deletion, it’s deleted even if you later opt out of data deletion. Please carefully configure the retention period for transaction documents. Deletion of transaction documents is an irreversible process. You can’t retrieve any transaction documents after they're deleted by the system. If you're using long-term archiving services, we strongly recommend that you specify a retention period for transaction documents that is greater than or equal to the longest archiving retention period legally required by countries/regions where you operate. If the system deletes your invoices, you can't search for those invoices in SAP Business Network. Your archived invoices, however, continue to be retained by TrustWeaver or Sovos (third-party systems that SAP Business Network uses to archive invoices) for the full legal retention period. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Notification Type Notifications Data Identification and Deletion Send a notification when the transaction documents have been identified for deletion Send a notification after deletion of transactions Requesting Recurring Deletion of Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can request to delete transactions older than a certain age in months on a recurring basis every month for your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Data Deletion Configuration permission. See Permissions You Can Assign to Users. A transaction document is identified for deletion when all documents in its transaction document set are older than the data retention period. The transaction document set is the sequence of related documents exchanged between the buyer and supplier. The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. Buyers and suppliers maintain their own data retention period. Consequently, your buyers may keep copies of documents that you have deleted from your account. To receive an email notification when transaction documents for your deletion request are available to download, the administrator needs to set up notifications. Procedure 1. Go to Account settings Settings Compliance . 2. Select Deletion Settings for Transaction Data. The Deletion Settings for Transaction Data page appears. 3. In the Recurring Deletion tab, click the Set Up Now button in the Recurring Deletion Setting section. 4. In the popup, for Delete Transactions Older Than ___ Months, enter a number equal to or greater than 18. 5. Click Save.  Caution Once a transaction document set has been identified for deletion, it’s deleted even if you later opt out of data deletion.  Tip You can go to the Setting Change Log table in the Recurring Deletion tab to view changes to the recurring deletion settings.  Note 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 137 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Requesting a One-Time Deletion of Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can request to delete transactions older than a certain date on a one-time basis for your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Data Deletion Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions. A transaction document is identified for deletion when all documents in its transaction document set are older than the data retention period. The transaction document set is the sequence of related documents exchanged between the buyer and supplier. The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. Buyers and suppliers maintain their own data retention period. Consequently, your suppliers may keep copies of documents that you have deleted from your account. To receive an email notification when transaction documents for your deletion request are available to download, the administrator needs to set up notifications. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Settings Compliance . 2. Select Deletion Settings for Transaction Data. The Deletion Settings for Transaction Data page appears. 3. In the One-Time Deletion tab, click the Set Up button. 4. In the popup, for Delete Transactions Before, select a date older than 18 months. All transactions created or last updated before that date are identified for deletion as soon as possible. 5. Click Save. After the request is canceled, you can request a new recurring or one-time deletion at any time. SAP Business Network uses your data to help you analyze your business activities in the analytics dashboard. When a recurring deletion request deletes transactions, the data used in analytics are also deleted.  Caution Once you identify a transaction document set for deletion, it’s deleted even if you later opt out of data deletion.  Tip You can go to the History Log table in the One-Time Deletion tab to view one-time deletion requests that already have run, been removed, or completed. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 138 This is custom documentation. file://SBN/split/SBN BTP Supplier Admin.content: Analytics Data Export The administrator for your SAP Business Network account can request to export the analytics data from your account. Analytics data refer to your master data and transaction data (purchase orders, invoices, credit memos, and debit memos) used by SAP Business Network to provide analytics features such as the analytics dashboard. SAP Business Network exports analytics data in separate CSV (Comma-Separated Values) files, and you can download them. The data export and download won't affect the original data on SAP Business Network. Requesting Analytics Data Export for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can request to export your analytics data from your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are the administrator of your SAP Business Network account. You know the ANID of your SAP Business Network account. You have a secured email box for receiving encrypted email notifications when the requested data is ready for download. Context SAP Business Network uses part of your master data and transaction data (purchase orders, invoices, credit memos, and debit memos) to help you analyze your business activities in the analytics dashboard. If you want to export the data used in analytics, you can make a request. Procedure Create a case on component SBN-AN-ANL to request the analytics data export from your SAP Business Network account. Ensure to provide the ANID of your SAP Business Network account and a secured email box for receiving encrypted email notifications. For information on how to create a case, see Get Support Application Online Help . Results An SAP support representative verifies that you are the account administrator, then sends an encrypted email including a URL and a shared access key for downloading the requested data. You have 7 days to download the data. After that, the download package is deleted. The original data are unaffected and remain on SAP Business Network. Click your user initials at the top right of the home page and choose Company Profile from the menu. 3. In the Overview tab, locate the About Us section and click Edit. 4. GIRO: A standardized economic activity code that identifies the primary business activity a supplier is legally registered to perform in Chile, such as manufacturing, retail, or professional services. These codes are issued and maintained by the Chilean Internal Revenue Service (SII). This field is mandatory for Chilean suppliers. Click the  icon to select from the applicable code list. For a complete list of official economic activity codes and their descriptions, see https://www.sii.cl/ayudas/ayudas_por_servicios/1956-codigos-1959.html . Short Description: A brief summary of your company. Long Description: A more detailed overview of your company. Business Type: Select one or more types that represent your business. Additional Entities Understanding Additional Entities How Additional Entities Are Used Managing Sold From Entities Managing Remit To Entities Understanding Additional Entities Additional entities represent your company’s organizational units such as branches, affiliates, or subsidiaries that operate under your main organization. They allow you to present a transparent view of your company structure on SAP Business Network so trading partners can better understand how your organization is set up. When adding an additional entity, you provide key details such as the legal name, address, and tax information, and define its network collaboration function. By entering and maintaining address information here, you can manage all business addresses centrally instead of keeping them in separate locations. This centralized approach is built on the Global Address Book (GAB) framework, which provides a unified model for managing address data across SAP Business Network. Through this shared framework, Additional Entities ensure consistency and accuracy of address information across invoicing, payments, and shipments.  Note Currently, each certification is limited to a maximum of two versions. If you have reached the limit and want to add a new one, you have to delete an older one first. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 25 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Each additional entity includes an address and a collaboration function that defines how this address is used in business transactions. The function specifies the business role of the entity within the network, ensuring each address serves its correct purpose in transactional processes Collaboration functions include: Sold From: Supplier entity selling goods to buyers. Remit To: Supplier entity where buyers remit payments after receiving an invoice. Bill To: Buyer entity to whom suppliers issue invoices. Sold To: Buyer entity that receives goods from suppliers. Assigning the appropriate function helps ensure address information is applied correctly across transactions and supports consistent, efficient operations. Related Information How Additional Entities Are Used How Additional Entities Are Used The information managed in Additional Entities supports a range of configurations and transactional processes. Depending on your role on SAP Business Network, these use cases may apply: When Acting as Suppliers Country Configuration (formerly Legal/Regulatory Profile): In countries that require registration with local tax authorities for electronic invoicing, you must set up a country-specific configuration in SAP Business Network. During setup, your organization’s address and tax details are pulled from Additional Entities based on the selected country and company name. You must first create and maintain this information in Additional Entities before the country configuration can be created. Remittance and Bank Information Setup: You can link your Remit To address with specific remittance preferences and bank details. These are automatically included in invoices to ensure buyers receive accurate payment instructions. Invoice Creation: When creating invoices, you’ll select from a predefined list of addresses maintained under Additional Entities. This ensures that invoices use consistent and validated address data. When Acting as Buyers Document Routing Configuration: If you use multiple ERP systems, you can define routing rules that reference Bill To addresses maintained in Additional Entities. These rules determine which ERP system or business unit should receive and process documents like purchase orders or invoices. Related Information Understanding Additional Entities 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 26 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Managing Sold From Entities A Sold From entity represents the supplier organization or branch that ships goods or delivers services to a buyer. It identifies the physical or legal location where the sale originates and is used in business transactions to support tax calculation, regulatory compliance, and fulfillment processing. Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Procedure Create a Sold From Entity 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile Additional Entities . 3. In the Additional Entities table, click Create. 4. On the Create New Additional Entity page, provide the following information: Company and location information: Company (Legal) Name Contact Name Country/Region, City, State, Postal Code Address Lines 1-3 Network collaboration information: From the Functions dropdown, select Sold From. (Optional) Check Make this address default. Identification information Enter an Internal ID, which is used to recognize the entity within your organization, such as a company code, address ID, or other internal reference. Usage information: a. Select one or more categories. Categories define the context and purpose of the identifiers you are about to enter. Common categories include: GlobalUniqueID: For globally recognized identifiers like DUNS or Global Location Numbers (GLN). TaxID: For country-specific tax identification numbers (VAT ID, GST ID, for example). The categories you select determine which sections and fields are shown below. b. Fill in the required identifiers for each category.  Note You can add up to 20 Sold From entities. To set a new default, first deselect the current default address. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 27 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- 5. Click Create. The entity will now appear in the Additional Entities table. Edit or Delete an Entity 6. Select an entity in the Additional Entities table, then click Edit or Delete. Related Information Understanding Additional Entities Country Configuration Managing Remit To Entities A Remit To entity represents the supplier location where payments should be sent. It appears on invoices to inform buyers where to remit payment and may include associated bank and remittance details to ensure accurate processing. Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Now, address management is handled under Company Profile Additional Entities , while payment configuration remains on the Settlement page. Because the functions are split across two areas, direct navigation links are available to help you move between address management and payment configuration as needed. Procedure Create a Remit To Address 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile Additional Entities . 3. In the Additional Entities table, click Create.  Note The Tax IDs are displayed based on the country of the selected address.  Note You can set up the legal profile, which is now referred to as country configuration, for a Sold From entity. For details, see Creating a Country Configuration.  Note A Sold From entity linked to a Country Configuration cannot be edited or deleted. See Country Configuration for details. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 28 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- 4. On the Create New Additional Entity page, provide the following information: Company and location information: Company (Legal) Name Contact Name Country/Region, City, State, Postal Code Address Lines 1-3 Network collaboration information: From the Functions dropdown, select Remit To. (Optional) Select Make this address default. Identification information Enter an Internal ID, which is used to recognize the entity within your organization, such as a company code, address ID, or other internal reference. 5. Click Create. The entity will now appear in the Additional Entities table. Edit or Delete an Entity 6. To edit or delete an entity, select its row and click Edit or Delete. Add or Update Remittance Information 7. From the Additional Entities tab, click Go to Remittances to configure payment details.  Note Deleting a Remit To entity will also remove the remittance information linked to it.  Note These configurations are currently available only on the Settlement page. Address information must be managed in Company Profile Additional Entities . 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 29 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Country Configuration Country Configuration refer to supplier accounts registered with the country-specific tax authorities for electronic invoicing procedures. Suppliers must create and maintain a country-specific configuration for your organization in SAP Business Network. Country Configuration was formerly called as Legal/Regulatory Profile in SAP Business Network. During the creation of a country configuration, your organization's address and tax related information are retrieved from Additional Entities for the selected country and company name. To create a country configuration, the supplier must have created the company's address and maintain the tax identifiers under Additional Entities. It is only then you can select the company name during the country configuration. You can also edit and delete the country configuration. Related Information Creating a Country Configuration Editing a Country Configuration Deleting a Country Configuration Creating a Country Configuration Learn how to create a country configuration. Procedure 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. 2. Navigate to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Country Configuration. 4. Choose Create. 5. Select the country/region and the company name. 6. Choose Continue. For the selected country and company name, some of the fields are prepopulated. This information is captured from the company details provided under Additional Entities. 7. Enter details for the required fields. The fields displayed are country-specific and hence vary for every country. 8. Choose Create. Results You can also edit and delete the country configuration. For more information, see: Editing a Country Configuration Deleting a Country Configuration Editing a Country Configuration 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 30 This is custom documentation. Go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Country Configuration. 4. Navigate to the country configuration of the required country. The configuration screen of the selected country is displayed. 5. Choose Edit at the top right of the configuration screen. The Tax Identification Numbers section is non-editable. 6. Continue to edit the required fields. 7. Choose Save. Deleting a Country Configuration Learn how to delete a country configuration. Context You can delete a country configuration in two ways: 1. Navigate to the required country configuration on the Country Configuration home screen. 2. Choose Delete at the top right. 1. Open the required country configuration on the Country Configuration home screen. 2. Choose Delete at the top right. Contacts Efficient communication is a cornerstone of successful business interactions, and maintaining accurate contact information is paramount to achieving this goal. Within SAP Business Network, the contact management feature empowers organizations to effectively manage both the main company contact and individual contacts. Main Company Contact: The Main Company Contact includes essential contact information for the company, specifically the general email, phone, and fax numbers. Each account has one main contact, defaulted to the information of the account creator (administrator), and you have the flexibility to edit and update this information as needed. Individual Company Contacts: In addition to the main company contact, you can create multiple individual contacts and assign them one or more roles, such as Sales Representative, Marketing Manager, or Technical Contact. Assigning a role designates the contact as a companywide 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 31 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- contact, which is visible to all trading partners on SAP Business Network. If no role is assigned, the contact is considered private. You can later assign them to specific customers. Customer-Specific Contacts: SAP Business Network allows you to assign contacts to specific customers. These contacts are visible only to the designated customer and serve as the primary point of contact for them, improving personalized communication. Editing the Main Contact The main company contact includes essential contact information for your company, specifically the general email address, phone number, and fax number. Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context Each account has one main contact, which defaults to the information of the account creator (administrator). You can edit and update this information as needed. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane. 4. Click the Company Contact Information tab, and then click Edit in the upper-right corner of the page. 5. Update Email, Phone, and Fax of your company as needed. Related Information Contacts Managing Companywide Contacts Managing Customer-Specific Contacts Managing Companywide Contacts Designating a contact as companywide makes their information accessible to both current and potential trading partners on SAP Business Network. Prerequisites  Note Your contact information will be available in supplier contact reports that buyers can download, visible on buyers' Supplier Enablement screens, and consumed by other SAP Ariba applications like SAP Ariba Buying, SAP Ariba Sourcing, and SAP Ariba Supplier Lifecycle and Performance. However, your trading partners won’t see it in your company profile. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 32 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context Assigning individuals in your company as companywide contacts ensures your trading partners can easily reach the right people for various issues or inquiries. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane. 4. Scroll down to the Contact Personnel section and click Create in the upper-right corner of the Contact Personnel with Companywide Assignments table. 5. On the Create New Contact with Companywide Assignment page, provide the following details: Basic Information: Contact Name (mandatory) Email (mandatory) Phone (mandatory) Business Title Fax Company Assignment: Assigning a role here designates the contact as a companywide contact. Address Information: Country/Region State City Address Line 1 Address Line 2 Address Line 3 Postal Code 6. After providing the necessary information, click Create to save the contact. 7. To edit a contact, click Edit in the upper right corner of the table. 8. To delete a contact, Click Delete in the upper right corner of the table.  Note If you assign a companywide role to the contact, their information will be visible to all trading partners on SAP Business Network. You can assign multiple roles to a contact, if necessary. If no companywide role is assigned, the contact is considered private and will not be visible to trading partners. You can later assign them to a specific customer. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 33 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- After a contact is deleted, all its assignments will be removed as well. Related Information Contacts Managing Customer-Specific Contacts Managing Customer-Specific Contacts Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission to edit your company profile. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to assign this permission to you. The individual contact to be assigned to specific customers have been added to the Contact Personnel with Company Assignments table. For details, refer to Managing Companywide Contacts. Context Assign individual contacts to specific customers to act as the main point of contact. This helps personalize communication and strengthens relationships. Note that contacts can only be assigned to customers with an existing trading relationship. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane. 4. Scroll down to the Customer-Specific Assignments section, select a customer from the table, and click Edit. 5. On the Edit Customer-Specific Assignment page, select personnel from the drop-down list to assign them as the specified contact for the selected customer, and then click Save. Related Information Contacts Managing Companywide Contacts Managing Profile Visibility Your company profile on SAP Business Network helps buyers discover and evaluate your business. You can customize what information is visible, manage global profile reach, control extended profile sharing, and define who can contact your company. How to Access Visibility Settings 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click your user initials at the top right of the home page and choose Company Profile from the menu.  Note Customers will only see their own customer-specific assignments, along with any companywide contacts you provide. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 34 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- 3. Click the Settings tab. 1. Profile Sections Control the visibility of specific sections on your company profile. Showing more sections helps buyers better understand your capabilities. Section Visibility Options Certifications Sustainability Ratings Assessments Organization Structure Visible to all: Anyone can see this section. Visible to trading partners only: Only visible to trading partners with active relationships. Hidden: Not visible to other users. Always Visible Sections Always Invisible Sections About Us Product and Service Categories Ship To or Service Locations Industries Company Showcase Social Media Keywords Contacts 2. Search Results These settings control your visibility in buyer search results and across global SAP Business Network data centers. Show my profile in search results Appear in buyer search results to increase visibility and business opportunities. Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network Make your profile discoverable in all regional data centers of SAP Business Network. 3. Extended Profile Decide who can access extended information about your company. Your extended profile includes details from multiple configuration areas, such as: My Account Company Profile Electronic Order Routing  Note To appear in global searches, you must enable both options above. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 35 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Electronic Invoice Routing Settlement This information can be downloaded by buyers as an Excel file. Visibility Options: Make my extended profile available to all SAP Business Network buying organizations Make my extended profile available ONLY to my current and pending SAP Business Network customers 4. Contact Preferences Define how others can reach out to your company or account administrator. Allow buyers to contact my company using Trading Partner Search Lets buyers send messages directly via search. Your email address remains private, and you'll be notified of new messages. Allow other suppliers to contact my account administrator During supplier registration, SAP Business Network checks existing profiles for potential matches (based on company name, aliases, DUNS number, or tax ID). If your company is identified as a match and this setting is enabled, the registrant can email your administrator to request account access credentials. Public Profile Your public profile on SAP Business Network is the version of your company profile that is visible to anyone with your public profile URL. Always Visible Sections These sections are always visible to anyone who accesses your public profile: About Us – Key company details, such as company name, location, founding year, revenue, employee count, and legal form. Products & Services – Your offerings, industries served, and shipping/service locations. Company Showcase – Content that showcase your strengths and advantages. Social Media – Links to your company’s social media platforms. Configurable Sections You can control the visibility of the following sections using your profile settings. Assessments – Business-related evaluations, such as human rights assessments. Certifications– Your company’s official accreditations and compliance with recognized standards.  Note Pending customers mean trading partners who have sent you a relationship request. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 36 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Sustainability Ratings – Your company’s performance on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria as assessed by third-party rating providers. Organization Structure – Overview of your company’s organizational hierarchy. You can show these sections to all trading partners with or without an existing relationship, or only to those with an existing relationship, or just hide them from all trading partners. Always Hidden Sections The following items are never visible on your public profile: Company Keywords Contacts How to View or Share Your Public Profile To view your public profile, go to the Company Profile page and click View My Public Profile in the upper-right corner. To share your profile, click the More options () menu and copy your public profile URL. Profile Data Federation This feature enables your company profile data to be replicated across SAP Business Network's global data centers, making your profile visible to trading partners in different regions. For more information, refer to How Profile Data Federation Works and Enabling Profile Data Federation. How Profile Data Federation Works Profile data federation replicates your company profile data across all global data centers of SAP Business Network, enabling trading partners in different regions to find and view your company profile, thereby facilitating potential business opportunities. To understand how profile data federation works, consider two trading partners located in different regions: Trading Partner A is based in the United States (US) data center. Trading Partner B is based in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) data center. For Trading Partner B to view Trading Partner A’s profile, Trading Partner A’s profile data must be replicated from the US data center to the KSA data center. To make this happen, Trading Partner A must enable profile data federation. For details about how to enable profile data federation, refer to Enabling Profile Data Federation. Once enabled, an initial replication synchronizes your company profile data across all global data centers of SAP Business Network. Future updates are automatically synchronized to ensure your profile remains consistent and up to date across all data centers.  Note Profile data federation is only available to companies that are not sole proprietors. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 37 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- Enabling Profile Data Federation Profile data federation allows your company profile to be visible across all global data centers of SAP Business Network. This makes it possible for trading partners in different regions to find and view your company profile, facilitating potential business opportunities. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See Permissions You Can Assign to Users. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. This opens the Company Profile page. 3. Click the Options menu in the upper-right corner of your profile and select Profile settings. 4. On the Profile Settings page, locate the section labeled Search Results Visibility: a. Optional: Toggle Show my profile in search results to allow your profile appear in search results. This setting determines whether your company profile is visible to trading partners in their search results. To enable global searchability, turn on this setting along with Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network. Currently, this setting is unavailable to buyers. b. Toggle Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network to enable profile data federation. This setting determines whether your profile data will be replicated to other data centers of SAP Business Network. For suppliers, this setting is enabled by default. Buyers need to enable it manually. Once enabled, this setting cannot be reversed. 5. Click Save to confirm your settings. Results Your company profile will be replicated and visible across all data centers of SAP Business Network. Future updates to your profile will be automatically synchronized globally. If Show my profile in search results is enabled, your profile will also become searchable across all global regions. Company Profile Experience for Promote Suppliers with a promote subscription on SAP Business Network enjoy exclusive features that enhance their company profiles and foster trust with potential buyers. Active Supplier Status Showcase your active platform engagement and readiness for new business opportunities. For more information, refer to Active Supplier Status. Verified Business Badge Confirm your company’s authenticity and legitimacy with trusted third-party partners. By becoming a verified supplier, you gain a competitive advantage over unverified businesses. For more information, refer to Business Verification. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 38 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Company Showcase Promote your company by adding marketing materials such as customer presentations, case studies, and website links. For more information, refer to Company Showcase. Related Information Buying the Promote Subscription Business Verification Trust is the foundation of successful business relationships. SAP Business Network is dedicated to creating a secure and reliable platform for suppliers and buyers. To mitigate risks associated with unverified businesses, we’ve introduced the Business Verification feature, designed to foster trustworthy, long-lasting partnerships within the network. Understanding Business Verification Business verification is a crucial process that confirms the authenticity and legitimacy of a supplier company. This process is typically carried out in collaboration with reputable third-party organizations, CDQ and Dun & Bradstreet , which specialize in validating business information. The Verification Process Once you submit the verification request: 1. We first verify your business details with CDQ. If your information matches their record, your business is verified. 2. If there is no match or discrepancies are found with CDQ, we check if you have provided a DUNS number. If available, we use it to verify your business details with Dun & Bradstreet. 3. Once your business is successfully verified through either CDQ or Dun & Bradstreet, a verification badge ( ) will be added to your profile. The business details verified include: Company Name Primary Address (Country, State, City, Address Line 1, and Postal Code) Tax ID or VAT ID DUNS Number (if Dun & Bradstreet is the verifier) Benefits of Verifying Your Business Enhanced Credibility The verification badge demonstrates to prospective buyers that you are who you say you are on the world’s largest B2B network. This can give you a competitive edge over businesses that have not undergone the verification process. Increased Visibility 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 39 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Verified businesses enjoy increased visibility in search results. Stronger Trust Verification confirms the accuracy of your business details, reducing fraud risks and building trust with potential customers. Qualifying for Business Verification To qualify for business verification, ensure the following: You have bought the promote subscription for your SAP Business Network supplier account. If your organization has a parent-child hierarchy, you must be part of the parent organization, as only parent organizations can initiate business verification. The verification badge is granted exclusively to the parent organization. You have the Company Information permission to edit your company profile. Only users with this permission can start the verification process. If you don't have this permission, contact your organization’s administrator to assign it to you. Verifying Your Business Maintaining an accurate, up-to-date, and verified profile can significantly enhance your credibility with potential buyers. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you through the verification process: Prerequisites Ensure you've bought the promote subscription for your SAP Business Network supplier account. Ensure you're part of the parent organization if your organization has a parent-child hierarchy. Ensure you have the Company Information permission to edit the company profile. Only users with this permission can initiate the verification process. Contact your organization’s administrator to assign the necessary permission if needed. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. This opens the Company Profile page. 3. Click Verify your business under the Promote suggestions section at the top of the Overview page. The system will check for any missing required or recommended information. If any details are missing, a popup will guide you to add the necessary information. 4. Add required and recommended information: Required information: Number of Employees Year Founded Revenue Legal Form 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 40 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --
