file://SBN/split/SBN BTP Supplier Admin.content: Business Type Recommended information: DUNS Number Adding a DUNS number can increase your chances of successful verification. If your business cannot be verified through CDQ, the system will use the DUNS number for verification with Dun & Bradstreet. Without a DUNS number, Dun & Bradstreet verification will not be attempted. If you don't know your DUNS number, click Find my DUNS number and use the Lookup DUNS Number service to search based on your company name and address. If your existing company name and address don't match the records in the D&B database for the DUNS number you’re adding, you need to accept the updates from D&B. Upon acceptance, your company name and address will automatically update to match the D&B records and will become non-editable unless you clear your DUNS number. In addition to the mandatory updates, you can also import other optional updates such as Website URL and Short Description from D&B to enrich your profile data. 5. Confirm your business details: Company Name Primary Address DUNS Number (if available) 6. Add and confirm your tax information. If you already have a tax ID or VAT ID, double-check to confirm it's correct. Your tax information is used solely for verification and will not be publicly displayed or shared. 7. Click Verify to submit your verification request. Verification Process 1. SAP Business Network verifies your details with CDQ. 2. If CDQ cannot verify, and you’ve provided a DUNS number, verification proceeds with Dun & Bradstreet. Verification Result Success A blue checkmark badge ( ) is displayed against your company name on your profile. This badge will also appear in search results and SAP applications, like Guided Sourcing. Buyers can search for trading partners by verified status. Failure Handling Click View Verification Summary on the result page to check the failure cause. To reinitiate the verification process, follow steps in Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure. Notifications: You'll receive an in-app notification regarding your verification result. Click the bell icon in the top-right corner of the SAP Business Network portal to view it. Disclaimer 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 41 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- SAP does not verify the accuracy of Third-Party Verification Information and is not responsible for any losses, direct or indirect, that may arise from it. Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure If your business fails third-party verification, you can reinitiate the process to ensure successful verification. The verification badge boosts your visibility in search rankings, builds trust with buyers, and helps you stand out among competitors. Procedure 1. On the verification result page, click View Verification Summary to access the summary page of your verification. If the result page is closed, go to your Company Profile and click Verify your business under the Promote suggestions section at the top of the Overview page. This will also open the summary page of your last verification. 2. On the Verification Summary page, review the failure cause and click Edit and Resubmit to return to the business information review page. 3. On the business information review page: a. Update your tax information. b. Click Company Profile in the error message strip to update your company name, address, or DUNS number. 4. After resolving all inconsistencies, click Verify to resubmit your verification request. Business Verification Troubleshooting Business verification issues can occur for various reasons. Below are common scenarios and guidance to resolve them: What Should I Do Upon Verification Failure? Verification through third-party services may fail for various reasons. Below are common causes and the steps you can take to address them: Common Reasons for Verification Failure: Incomplete or Incorrect Data: The data you provided is incomplete or incorrect, or the reference data has discrepancies due to outdated or incorrect official records. Data Not Found: The provided identifier is invalid, does not match the business, or is from a country or type not yet supported by the verification service. Network or Server Error: Temporary technical issues may prevent the verification process from completing. Actions to Take: 1. Review and correct your submitted data. Ensure that the following fields are correct:  Note If you have a DUNS number, we recommend adding it to your profile. This will enable verification with Dun & Bradstreet (D&B) if verification with CDQ is unsuccessful. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 42 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Company Name: Make sure it matches the official name on your business registration. Primary Address: Verify that all address fields are accurate and complete. VAT or Tax ID: Double-check that your VAT or tax identifiers are valid and match the format required by the system. 2. Cross-check your data with official records. The official data sources that CDQ replies on include: Business Registers: for example, Companies House (UK), Handelsregister (Germany) VAT Databases: for example, VIES (EU VAT Information Exchange System) Tax Authorities: for example, IRS (USA), CRA (Canada) Before resubmitting, refer to your local business register, VAT database, or tax authorities. Make sure the details on your SAP Business Network profile exactly match those found in these official sources. This can include checking any identifiers, registration numbers, or business names that are critical to the verification process. 3. Contact your local authority. If there are any errors in the official records, reach out to your local business registry or tax authority for help. 4. Submit a new verification request. Once you’ve reviewed and corrected any discrepancies, you can resubmit your verification request. Make sure that all the information is up to date and accurate to increase the chances of success. For detailed instructions on resubmitting your verification request, refer to Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure. 5. Escalate the issue. If your verification continues to fail despite your efforts to correct the data, or if you believe the failure is due to an issue with the verification process, you can escalate the issue to SAP Support. We'll work with the verification partner to investigate and improve the service if needed. Please provide: The submitted (correct) data (Company Name, Address, and Identifier). Any official reference sources (for example, business registry extracts) to assist in the investigation. A brief explanation of the issue. Synthetic Examples for Escalation Cases to CDQ Example 1 Abbreviation Not Recognized Submitted: Name: ABC Corp, Address: 123 Main St, London, WC2N 5DU, UK. Reference: Name: ABC Corporation, Address: 123 Main Street, London, WC2N 5DU, UK. Issue: The abbreviation “Corp” was not recognized as equivalent to “Corporation.” Resolution: Escalate the case to CDQ to review the fuzzy comparison logic. Example 2 Missing or Incomplete Reference Data Submitted: Name: XYZ GmbH, VAT Number: DE123456789, Address: Musterstr. 12, 10115, Berlin, Germany. Reference: The business is not found in the current data source. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 43 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Issue: The reference source may not have up-to-date or complete records. Resolution: Escalate the issue with the input data for analysis and, if needed, review the reference source’s coverage. Example 3 Regional Variations Submitted: Name: ABC Ltd, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing Street, London, UK. Reference: Name: ABC Limited, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing St, London, UK. Issue: The matching algorithm fails to reconcile regional address formatting differences. Resolution: Escalate the case for review and possible algorithm refinement. Example 4 Identifier Not Recognized Submitted: Name: Tech Innovations Inc., Identifier: US TIN 123456789. Reference: Name: ABC Limited, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing St, London, UK. Issue: The system does not support U.S. Taxpayer Identification Numbers (TIN). Resolution: Escalate the case to assess expanding identifier support. Detailed Cases of Intended Verification Failure with CDQ 1. VAT Number Issues Reason: Invalid VAT number format or structure (for example, missing check digits). VAT number not found in the database. Example: A supplier submits VAT Number ESX12345678, which does not follow the correct format for Spain (2 letters + 8 digits). Resolution: Confirm the VAT number with the local tax authority. 2. Address Inconsistencies Reason: Missing critical address fields (for example, postal code, street name). Significant mismatches in address details between the input and reference. Example: Input address is “Main Road, Berlin, Germany”, but the reference requires the house number and postal code (for example, “123 Main Road, 10115, Berlin, Germany”). Resolution: Provide a complete address, including postal code and house number. 3. Business Name Discrepancies Reason: Placeholder or dummy names (for example, “Unknown Supplier”). Major differences between the submitted name and reference data. Example: Submitted: Tech INNVOITASNO, Reference: Tech Innovators GmbH. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 44 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Resolution: Ensure that the official name match the business register. 4. Identifier Does Not Match Business Reason: The identifier belongs to a different business. Example: VAT Number DE987654321 is submitted for “XYZ GmbH”, but the reference shows it belongs to “ABC GmbH”. Resolution: Provide the correct identifier for your business. 5. Data Source Limitations Reason: The identifier is from a country or type not yet supported by the verification service. Example: A supplier provides a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) from the USA, which is not yet supported. Resolution: Escalate to CDQ if necessary. Why Do I Lose My Verification Badge? Your verification badge can be removed for the following reasons: Updating Verified Business Information If you update any of the following verified business details, your badge will be removed: Company name Primary address (Country, State, City, Address Line 1, and Postal Code) Tax ID or VAT ID For businesses verified with Dun & Bradstreet, changing or removing your DUNS number will also result in the loss of the verification badge. However, if your business is verified with CDQ, altering your DUNS number will not affect your badge. After making any updates to these details, you must go through the verification process again to regain your badge. Expired Promote Subscription If your promote subscription expires and is not set to auto-renew, your badge will be removed. To restore it, you need to renew your subscription and reinitiate the verification process. To regain your verification badge, follow the steps outlined in Verifying Your Business to reinitate the verification process. Active Supplier Status Suppliers who actively engage on SAP Business Network are awarded an icon on their company profile. This status boosts credibility with potential buyers and demonstrates readiness for new business opportunities.  Note If your promote subscription is set to auto-renew, you will not lose your badge. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 45 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Eligibility Criteria To qualify for Active Supplier status, you must have the promote subscription for your SAP Business Network supplier account and meet at least one of the following requirements: Complete at least one successful transaction (invoice or order) within the last three years. Only transactions within this timeframe are considered. Maintain at least one active trading relationship. Status Activation and Maintenance Activation The Active Supplier status is automatically activated when the eligibility criteria are met. The Active Supplier icon is prominently displayed under your company name on your profile, visible to the public. Maintenance If you no longer meet the criteria, your status will change to Inactive Supplier. The Inactive Supplier icon is not visible to the public. To regain Active Supplier status, you must once again fulfill the eligibility requirements. Notifications You receive both an in-app and email notifications once the Active Supplier status is activated. Company Showcase You can add company showcase materials, including customer presentations, company website, best practices, case studies, and more, in the form of attachments or external links, to your profile to promote your company and attract new business opportunities. This feature is now exclusive to SAP Business Network, promote subscribers. For promote subscribers, you can add and manage company showcase materials on your company profile to enhance visibility and showcase your expertise. For non-promote users, you can only view or delete existing company showcase materials. To continue using the full functionality, you will need to buy the SAP Business Network, promote subscription. Users and Roles The account administrator can create users, roles and assign specific roles to users so they can perform different activities. An SAP Business Network user’s role typically corresponds to their functional role in your company. Administrators also maintain user list, assign user roles and permissions, delete users, and transfer administrative rights. The Manage Users and Manage Roles pages are redesigned to help administrators and users with the User Administration permission. Administrators can perform the following: View, create, manage, revoke, and deactivate or activate sub-users  Note Existing company showcase materials will remain visible to buyers, even without a promote subscription. However, you’ll need to subscribe to the promote package in order to upload new assets or make changes to your current showcase. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 46 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- Manage revocation period Manage and assign roles Supplier Administrators and users with User Administration permission: Upgrading to a supplier Enterprise account will list additional enterprise-only permissions. If you downgrade to a supplier Standard account, you can't activate the additional supplier enterprise-only permissions. In addition, a supplier can have a paid premium subscription such as bronze. Each of the subscription level may have different premium permissions. Removing the premium subscription will remove the premium permissions. Managing Users and Roles Administrators can create, edit and revoke users by navigating to Account Settings Settings Manage Users . The Manage Users contains the Active (N), Deactivated (N), and Revoked (N) tables where N represents the number of users. The Active (N) table is displayed by default. 1. On the Active (N) table, you can choose the following options: Create a new user. Select an existing user to Revoke their access to SAP Business Network. Import Users using an Excel file. The following table is an example of an active user: Active User User Name Email Address First Name Last Name Created On username@example.com emailaddress@example.com John Doe Aug 14, 2024, 12:00:05 PM 2. The Deactivated (N) table contains a list of users whose accounts were deactivated on SAP Business Network. Deactivated users temporarily do not have access to SAP Business Network. If required, you can select a user name and choose Reactivate to reactive the user account. The reactivated user is moved to the Active (N). The following table is an example of a deactivated user: Deactivated User User Name Email Address First Name Last Name Deactivated On username@example.com emailaddress@example.com John Doe Aug 14, 2024, 12:00:05 PM  Note If an enterprise-only permission is added to a role for a user who has downgraded to a Standard account, the permission is removed from the role. Re-upgrading to an Enterprise account does not restore the permission that was removed. If necessary, the removed permission must be reassigned to the role.  Note You can download a template to add a list of users with their contact information. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 47 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- 3. The Revoked (N) table contains a list of users whose accounts were revoked and no longer have access to SAP Business Network. The following table is an example of a revoked user: Revoked User User Name Email Address First Name Last Name Suspended On Revocation Status username@example.com emailaddress@example.com John Doe Aug 14, 2024, 12:00:05 PM Approved Revoking and Deleting Users: Users can be revoked from their roles and be placed for account deletion. A retention period is available for administrators if they want to revoke users from accessing SAP Business Network. By default, the retention period has no value. A user cannot be revoked if there is no retention period set. If the retention period is set, a user can be revoked, and after the retention period has passed, the user will be deleted from the system. To create and assign roles to a user, go to Account Settings Settings Manage Roles . The Manage Roles page contains the Custom Roles (N) and Pre-defined Roles (N) tables where N represents the total number of roles. 1. On the Custom Roles (N) table, you can Create a new role with permissions, or Delete an existing role. Created roles are considered custom roles and can be edited or deleted. 2. The Pre-defined Roles (N) table contains a list of roles that are managed by SAP Business Network. If you have users assigned to a default role, the list of role will appear in the Default Roles (N). You cannot delete or edit the default roles that are managed by SAP Business Network. Mass User Upload: Option to upload an .xlsx file containing a list of users for creating or updating users on SAP Business Network. You can upload an .xlsx file of up to 100 users for each upload.  Caution Choosing Revoke will remove the selected user’s access to SAP Business Network. You can retrieve the user data within the configured retention period, but you can’t retrieve it once the confirmed retention period has passed. This action cannot be reversed.  Note If you are deleting a role, ensure that there are no users assigned to the selected role.  Note Your upload may fail if the spreadsheet file exceeds the maximum number of users, has any file errors, or the buyer and supplier have different templates. When updating users on SAP Business Network, ensure that the list of users on the spreadsheet file matches the same email address, same user name, same first name, and same last name. However, the phone number cannot be updated. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 48 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Transferring Administrator Roles to Another User: A sub-user with User Administrator and Transfer Administrator Ownership permissions can make any user and themselves an administrator by checking the Make Admin of the user detail page. Customer Assignment (Supplier Administrators Only): If a sub-user with assigned customers becomes an administrator, the assigned customers are removed from the sub-user, and all customers are moved to the parent user account. If the administrator user is changed back to a sub-user account, the parent user retains all assigned customers as the default. Updated email notifications for requests to reset account passwords or if there are changes in administrator roles. Implementation Details General Prerequisites You meet any of the following requirements: You are an administrator for your company's organization or are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. Have the User Administration/Transfer Ownership permission to transfer authorization roles to another user. Managing Roles Use this procedure to create or update roles to assign to users so they can perform different activities. An SAP Business Network user’s role typically corresponds to their functional role in your company. Prerequisites Only the account administrator can manage users and roles. Context You can assign a role to any number of users. Each role has a unique name and a set of associated permissions that specify what the assigned users can see and do in SAP Business Network. For example, you might create an Invoice Generator role for people who handle incoming purchase orders and create invoices. You can assign multiple roles to a single user. When users have multiple roles, the Roles section in the Manage Users lists the multiple assigned roles. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings, and choose Settings Manage Roles . 2. Perform one of the following actions in the Manage Roles page. Click Create to create a new role.  Restriction You can create a maximum of 10 custom roles. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 49 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Select a the right-arrow against the role and click Edit that you want to update. Select a role and click Delete to delete a role. 3. Enter a distinctive name for the role. 4. (Optional) Enter a description to record your intentions for this role. Descriptions can be very useful later, if you want to review or revise the structure of your roles. 5. In the Permissions section, click Add and select one or more permissions for the role. Each role must have at least one permission. SAP Business Network does not display the administrator-specific permissions in the list. 6. In the Users section, click Add and select one or more users for the created role. 7. Click Save to create or update the role. Next Steps You assign roles to people when you create users in your account. Duplicate Account Check Process for Administrators SAP Business Network automatically performs a duplicate check when users attempt to create new accounts. When SAP Business Network determines that your account matches the details provided by a user attempting to create a new account, they are given the option to contact you to request access. As the account administrator, you receive an email notification that includes the contact information of the requester and a message from them. In an offline process, you should contact this user by email or phone to determine if they should be granted access to your account. If the result of the offline process is to NOT grant the user access, no further action is required by you, the administrator. If the result of the offline process is to grant access to the user, you must add the user to your account and ensure appropriate permissions are granted. The new supplier user receives two email notifications - one containing their user name, the other including a temporary password for their first time signing in. If the new supplier has issues accessing the account, you can assist them by resetting the password or by logging a service request with SAP Product Support. Managing Users  Note If you modify a role that is already assigned to users, those users will notice the permission changes the next time they sign in to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network doesn't notify users when you change a role. Therefore, we recommend telling users before you make changes.  Remember Before you can delete a role, you need to reassign associated users to a different role. You cannot delete roles that are currently assigned to users. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 50 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SBN BTP Supplier Admin.content: A user is a user name and password combination that a single individual in your company enters when signing into SAP Business Network. You assign roles to each user to give them access to different areas of your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites Only the account administrator can manage users and roles. Context Create a unique user name for each user who needs to access the account. Users should not share their user name or password with other users. This is important for SAP Business Network and your company in managing data privacy and integrity on SAP Business Network. To ensure your company and users have secure accounts on SAP Business Network: Users can have multiple roles, depending on the tasks they need to perform. All users should store their user name and password (sign in information) in a safe place. Users can forget their sign in information if they do not sign in to SAP Business Network regularly. SAP Business Network provides a secure and quick way for users to recover sign in information and reset passwords. When an employee leaves the company or changes jobs, and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account in their name, we recommend either deleting the user or reassigning the user’s sign in to another individual. If you reassign the sign in, you retain the user’s setup and data. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings and choose Settings Manage Users . 2. Perform one of the following actions: On the Manage Users page, click the Create User button to create a new user. Select the right-arrow next to the user details that you want to edit, and then click Edit. 3. Enter a user name, email address, first and last name, and optionally an office phone number for the user. 4. In the Roles section, click Add and choose one or more roles for the user.  Recommendation Create roles before you begin to create users.  Restriction You can create a maximum of 6000 users. When an account has more than 1000 users, SAP Business Network displays a simplified version of the Manage Users page.  Note Because SAP Business Network doesn't notify users when you change their assigned roles, we recommend telling users before you make changes.  Note When users create transaction audit reports or submit documents such as invoices, order confirmations, and ship notices, SAP Business Network captures the user’s first and last name, so ensure that these values are correct. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 51 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- 5. In the Customer Assignment section, click Add and select customer assignment. 6. Click Save. Results After you create a user, SAP Business Network sends an email message to that user with a randomly-generated password and a link to SAP Business Network. New users need to sign in and change the password to something they can remember. Next Steps Users who forget their user name or password can go to the sign in page, click Forgot User name or Password, and follow the instructions for regaining access to their account. Administrators can also reset passwords for users. Exposing or Hiding a User Account Use this procedure to make a user visible to or hidden from your customers. You might make a user visible to customers if you want that user to be a customer contact at your company. Context By default, your supplier user accounts are not visible to or searchable by your customers. If you participate in sourcing events, you can provide account visibility so that your customers can pre-approve the user accounts for punch-in. Providing visibility makes it easier for your customer to create accounts. You can hide an exposed account at any time. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings, and choose Settings Manage Users . 2. Click the right-arrow against the user. 3. Click Show Contact or Hide Contact to expose or hide the acccount. Resetting a User’s Password Use this procedure to reset passwords for users who forget their password. Prerequisites Only the account administrator can reset passwords for users. Context If you have a security concern about a user's account, you can force that user's password to reset. For security purposes, account administrators and users who have PCard access but are not the PCard owner are required to update their password every 90 days. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings, and choose Settings Manage Users . 2. Click the right-arrow against the user whose password you want to reset, and click Request reset password. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain sends an email to the user with a link to reset the password. The password update takes effect immediately. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 52 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Transferring the Account Administration Role If you're leaving your company or moving to a new position, you need to transfer ownership of the SAP Business Network account by choosing a new administrator. This ensures that your company doesn't experience interruptions in access to the account or in transactions with your customers. Prerequisites The current administrator needs to transfer the Administrator role to an existing user. Context The person who registered an account for your company on SAP Business Network is automatically assigned the Administrator role. We recommend assigning the Administrator role to the individual who is responsible for configuring your account, maintaining customer relationships, managing users, and subscribing to services. As the account administrator, you control who can sign in to your company's SAP Business Network account and which activities users can perform. The administrator also serves as the primary point of contact for other users in your company's SAP Business Network account who have questions or problems. Users contact the administrator to reset their password, to update their roles and permissions, or to give them access to the test account. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Manage Users . 2. Click the right-arrow against the user who you want to make the new administrator. 3. Click Make Admin. SAP Business Network displays the Assign yourself to a Role page. 4. Choose a new role for your account, and click Transfer. SAP Business Network displays a warning message that indicates the name of the new account administrator. 5. Click Confirm to transfer the account administrator role. Results SAP Business Network logs you out of your account and sends an email notification to the new account administrator, alerting them that they now have the Administrator role. Revoke User Access and Remove a User's Personal Information SAP Business Network users can request the administrator for their account to remove their personal information from the system. If approved, the user can’t sign in to SAP Business Network any longer, and their personal information is no longer visible to users, including in transaction documents shared and exchanged with business partners.  Restriction You can have only one administrator for your SAP Ariba account.  Note If you aren't sure who the administrator of an account is, contact SAP Business Network Customer Support. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 53 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Restrictions Comments or attachment files associated with transaction documents aren’t affected when users remove personal information. Therefore, avoid entering personal information in comments or attached files. After a user’s revocation of user access request is approved, their personal information is pseudonymized in SAP Business Network transaction documents. However, transaction documents that were integrated with other systems (such as an ERP) or downloaded before the request was approved may still have the user’s personal information. The customer needs to take additional action, including informing impacted business partners, to remove it. If a customer needs to re-identify a user that has been pseudonymized for legal purposes, the administrator of the account can provide that information. Retention Period for Revoked Users As a supplier administrator, configure a retention period for revoked users. SAP Business Network users can request the administrator of their account to remove their personal information from the system. This is called a revocation request. The request is auto-approved and users cannot sign in to SAP Business Network any longer, and their personal information is no longer visible to other users. As an administrator, you can configure a retention period for the user data of all the revoked users in your organization. The data of revoked users is automatically removed from SAP Business Network after this retention period is reached. In the meantime, you can view the list of revoked users in the Revoked Users tab. You must have configured the retention period before accepting or rejecting any revocation request. If the retention period for an organization is not configured, SAP Business Network prompts you to configure the retention period before you can act on a revocation request. You can change the retention period at any time before the previously configured retention period is reached. The newly configured retention period takes effect immediately. The retention period must be configured in months, and must be between 1 and 999 months. After the retention period is over, user data will be deleted permanently from SAP Business Network. You cannot act upon a revocation request unless you configure the retention period first. Revoked users' data is available for you to view for purposes such as regulatory audits. All the data of an organization (including users' data for revoked) is deleted when an organization is permanently deleted. Multifactor Authentication  Note For audit and compliance purposes, the user's personal information is still visible to the user who is the administrator for your SAP Business Network account.  Note Only users with non-administrator roles can request revocation of their access from SAP Business Network. Administrators cannot raise a revocation request. If administrators want to request revocation of their access from SAP Business Network, they must transfer their administrator role to another user. Transaction documents such as invoices created by users before they were revoked will remain unchanged in SAP Business Network even after revocation and subsequent permanent deletion of such users. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 54 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- SAP Business Network buyer and supplier administrators can configure multi-factor authentication settings at the organization and user level on the Account Security page. Multifactor authentication is a two-step verification process where you are required to authenticate yourself a second time using a time-based verification code. As compared to the single step authentication process, the multifactor authentication process provides enhanced security. If multifactor authentication is enabled for critical fields, you are required to perform the two-step verification process while attempting to update the values of critical fields such as email addresses, phone numbers, remittance information and so on. With multifactor authentication enabled for sign in, you are required to perform the two-step verification process to sign in to SAP Business Network. The role name Proposals and Contracts Access has been renamed to _ARIBA_SOURCING_ACCESS_CUSTOM_ROLE_. Administrators can access the multi-factor authentication settings by navigating to Account Settings Settings Account Security . The following changes have been made to the Account Security page: The Account Security page contains a Configuring Multi-Factor Authentication Settings section for administrators to configure multi-factor authentication settings for their users. Administrators can activate and configure multi-factor authentication settings for all their users. On the Account Security page, administrators can edit the following fields: Activate Multi-Factor Authentication for all users: Multi-Factor Authentication Login Multi-Factor Authentication for Critical Fields Maximum multi-factor authentication attempts before user lockout: Value is 5 attempts. Grace period to skip activating multi-factor authentication: Value is 24 hours. Multi-factor authentication lockout duration: Value is 1 hour. Save and Cancel buttons. The following multi-factor authentication fields are: Field Description Activate multi-factor authentication for all users: Choose one or more options: Multi-factor authentication login Multi-factor authentication for critical fields  Note The values are fixed and cannot be modified.  Note The master account will be automatically activated for multi- factor authentication when the organization's multi-factor authentication is activated. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 55 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Field Description Number of invalid multi-factor authentication attempts allowed before lockout: The maximum number of times the user can attempt multi-factor authentication before lockout. Grace period to skip activating multi-factor authentication: The maximum number of hours the user can skip activating their multi-factor authentication. Multi-factor lockout duration: The maximum number of hours the user must wait to retry multi- factor authentication after an invalid attempt. Save Save and apply your settings for multi-factor authentication. Cancel Cancel and discard your changes. To configure the multi-factor authentication at the user level, go to Account Settings Settings Manage Users and select a user to view their user profile. Depending on the configuration changes to the multi-factor authentication settings, the administrator can choose the following options for the user: When the Multi-Factor Authentication Login and Multi-Factor Authentication for Critical Fields are activated, a Manage Authentication button is available on the selected user's detail page. Administrators can choose Manage Authentication Enable/Disable or Manage Authentication Reset Authentication for their users. Implementation Details General Prerequisites You meet any of the following requirements: The master account may disable their own multi-factor authentication by navigating to Account Settings User Account . This option is not available for sub-users.  Note This value is fixed and cannot be modified.  Note This value is fixed and cannot be modified.  Note This value is fixed and cannot be modified.  Example Scenarios for Multi-Factor Authentication 1. If configuring at the organization level and the options Multi-factor authentication login and/or Multi-factor authentication login are activated, the option to activate and deactivate multi-factor authentication are available on the user's profile. 2. If configuring at the organization level and the options Multi-factor authentication login and/or Multi-factor authentication login are deactivated, the option to activate and deactivate multi-factor authentication are not available on the user's profile. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 56 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- You are an administrator for your company's organization or are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. Have the User Administration/Transfer Ownership permission to transfer authorization roles to another user. Notifications You specify which notifications you want receive in order to stay informed about different events and activities that affect your SAP Ariba account. You can use notifications to monitor catalog access activity, learn about matching business opportunities on SAP Business Network Discovery, and troubleshoot problems with your account. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain has adapted the SAPUI5 technology to improve user experience intuitiveness, navigation, content organization, and visual consistency. Elements present in the classic SAP Business Network for Supply Chain user interface have been added to the new user interface to maintain parity. Improvements have been made for the Notification list page, search, permissions, settings, email notifications, and authorizations for buyers and suppliers on SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Buyers and suppliers can configure their email notification to get notified of any relevant events or invoice status change of their documents. Once you configure your email notifications, users receive an email notification of the updates or changes done in the SAP Business Network. The email alert enables customers to take proactive actions in events that need their attention. Suppliers or buyers on SAP Business Network can enter up to ten comma-separated email addresses of their users to be notified of their order document statuses. After entering the email addresses, the recipients are automatically notified of the status of the order documents. For information about the notifications that you want to receive through email, notifications sent to your email, see Configuring Email Notifications. Suppliers can configure the following notifications: Network Service Order Order Inquiry Invoice Catalog Subscriptions Order Confirmations Service Sheet Pending Queue Planning Collaboration Upload/Download Relationship Ship notice Goods Receipt Payments Components Ship Notice Supplier Enablement task overdue reminder 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 57 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- The functions of the unsubscribe process remain the same as in the legacy SAP Business Network user interface. Configuring Email Notifications A centralized email notification provides consistency and clarity for buyers and suppliers so that they can take appropriate action. The email notification includes a subject line, email message, a link to view relevant documents on SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, and a link to sign in to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. To access the Notifications page, navigate to Account Settings Settings Notifications and select the appropriate tab. Ensure that you have necessary permission to configure the email notification. Restrictions You can specify up to 10 valid email addresses, separated by comma. User Tasks 1. Log in to the supplier account. 2. Click the user name icon, click Settings, and then click Notifications under Account administration. 3. Click Edit and activate or deactivate email notifications and select the status for which you want to receive notifications. 4. In the notification settings, add one or multiple email addresses to receive notifications. 5. Click Save. Network Service Notification Network Service Notification section is available to suppliers on the Notifications page with the following option: Notification Type Field Description Network Service Send a notification in advance of planned network downtime, unplanned downtime, and new releases When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address whenever there is a problem in the network, planned downtime and for new releases. Suppliers can enter up to ten comma-separated emails. Default value: No. Order Notifications Order Notifications The Order Notification section has the following options: 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 58 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Notification Type Field Description Undeliverable Orders Send a notification when orders are undeliverable When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when the orders are undeliverrable. New Purchase Orders Send a notification when a new order is received When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when a new order is received. Purchase Orders Changed Send a notification when an order is changed When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when an order is modified. Order Inquiry Notifications Order Inquiry Notifications The Order Inquiry Notifications section has the following options: Notification Type Field Description Order Inquiries Send a notification when purchase order inquiries are received When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when the order inquiries are received. Undeliverable Order Inquiries Send a notification when purchase order inquiries are undeliverable When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when order inquiries are undeliverable. Invoice Notifications Description Suppliers can configure and receive email notifications for relevant events in the network. When supplier submit the invoices on SAP Business Network, if there are any document failures or status of the invoice changes, the suppliers are alerted of them, either immediately or at a configured frequency, so that they can appropriate actions: The supplier can choose the frequency to receive the notification. For example, immediately or one notification (daily digest) per day. User can subscribe to the notification that they would like to receive. For example, receive notification when invoice status is changed or updated. Prerequisites None. Restrictions 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 59 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- The supplier cannot choose to receive notification on invoices that are automatically created from receipts and service sheets. The supplier cannot choose the type of status changes to be included in the notification. The Invoice Notifications section has the following options: Notification Type Field Description Invoice Status Change Send a notification when invoice statuses change When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when invoice statuses change. Invoice Failure Send a notification when invoices are undeliverable or rejected When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when invoices are not delivered or rejected by the buyer. Invoice Created Automatically from Receipts Send a notification when an invoice is automatically created from a goods receipt When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when an invoice is automatically created from GRN. Catalog Subscriptions The Catalog Subscriptions section has the following options: Notification Type Field Description Catalog Subscriptions Send a notification when a customer subscribes to my catalog or when procurement customer sends status updates on catalogs When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when a customer subscribes to the catalog or when procurement customer sends status updates on catalogs. Order Confirmation Notifications The Order Confirmation Notifications section has the following options: Notification Type Field Description Order Confirmation Failure Send a notification when order confirmations are undeliverable When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when the order confirmations are undeliverable. Reminder of Unconfirmed Orders Send reminders of unconfirmed orders When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address giving a reminder on the orders that are not confirmed. Service Sheet Notifications The Service Sheet Notifications section has the following options: 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 60 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

Pending Queue Notifications The Catalog Subscriptions section has the following options: Notification Type Field Description Pending Queue Send a notification when items delivered through pending queue are not acknowledged When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when the items delivered through pending queue are not acknowledged. Other Notifications This section describes the options available for Planning Collaboration, Upload or Download and Relationship notifications. The Planning Collaboration Notifications section has the following options: Notification Type Field Description Planning Collaboration Updates Send a notification immediately when buyers share planning collaboration updates When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when the buyers share planning collaboration updates. Send a periodic digest notification summarizing planning collaboration updates sent by buyers When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications periodically, that summarizes the planning collaboration updates sent by the buyers. The Upload/Download section has the following options: Notification Type Field Description Upload/Download Send a notification when a document download is ready When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when the document that they have downloaded is ready to view. The Relationship Notifications section has the following options: 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 61 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Notification Type Field Description Customer Requirements Change Send a notification when a buying organization creates a trading relationship with my company When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when the buying organization creates a trading relationship with the supplier organization. The Customer Requirements Change section has the following options: Notification Type Field Description Add Supplier Email on my Supplier Information Portal Send a notification when a customer has shared or updated Master Data or Business Requirements on my Supplier Information Portal When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when the customer shares master data or business requirements on the supplier information portal or updae them. The Supplier Enablement task overdue reminder section has the following options: Notification Type Field Description Add Supplier Email for task overdue reminder Send a notification when a supplier enablement task is overdue When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when supplier enablement task is overdue. Ship Notice Notifications The Ship Notice Notification section has the following options: Notification Type Field Description Ship Notice Failure Send a notification when ship notices are undeliverable When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address. Suppliers can enter up to ten comma- separated emails. Reminder of Non-Shipped Orders Send reminders of non-shipped orders When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address. Suppliers can enter up to ten comma- separated emails. Ship Notice Accepted with Changes Send a notification when ship notices are accepted with changes When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when ship notices are accepted with changes. Ship Notice Declined Send a notification when ship notices are declined When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications to their email address when ship notices are declined. Goods Receipt Notifications The Goods Receipt Notifications section has the following options: 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 62 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Notification Type Field Description Reminder of Non-received Order Items Send reminders of non-received order items When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications reminding them of the order items that are not received. Payments Notifications The Payments Notification section has the following options: Notification Type Field Description Payment Proposal SendWhenPaymentProfileActive When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications when payment profile is active. Payment Remittance Send a notification when payment remittances are undeliverable or their status changed When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications when payment remittance is undeliverable or the payment remittance status is changed. Send a notification when payment remittances or payment proposals are received When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications when payment remittance or payment proposals are received. Payment Remittance Status Updates Send a notification only when payment remittance status changes When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications when payment remittance status is updated. Remittance Batch Send a notification when a remittance batch is delivered to the bank When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications when payment remittance batch is delivered to the bank. Remittance Batch Errors Send a notification when a remittance batch has errors or failed to be sent to the payment provider When set to Yes, suppliers receive notifications when payment remittance batch has errors or failed. Messaging This feature provides in-portal messaging with email notifications for buyers and suppliers on SAP Business Network. Users can start conversations within the portal and continue participating offline through email, ensuring timely and uninterrupted collaboration. Users can send and track messages related to specific business documents, such as purchase orders or invoices, or initiate general, document-independent conversations. Messages sent online or by email are captured and displayed in the same conversation, ensuring consistent visibility, auditability, and continuity of communication for all participants. Built with SAPUI5 technology, the feature provides a consistent and intuitive user experience that supports flexible communication workflows. With this capability, users can: Communicate with trading partners using online messages or email, based on user preference and business context. Send and receive messages related to specific documents (in-context) or general topics (context-free). Receive notifications for new messages and reply directly from email or within SAP Business Network. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 63 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- Access and manage all conversations from a centralized Message Center with complete message history. Improve collaboration efficiency and accelerate resolution of procurement and invoicing issues. For more information on the Messaging feature, refer to Overview of the Messaging Feature. Changes to Existing Functionality The previous broadcast messaging function has been replaced by the Announcements feature, which buyers can use to share important updates with multiple suppliers. For more information on Announcements, refer to Announcements for Trading Partner Communication. In this release, the Messaging feature does not support country/region-based or company code-based message routing configurations. User Interface Changes A  Message icon appears in the top-right corner of the SAP Business Network portal. Clicking this icon opens the Message Center, where users can view, reply to, or create conversations. When new messages are received, a red badge with a number appears on the icon, indicating the count of unread messages. On purchase order and invoice Details pages, a Send Message button has been added, which allows users to message trading partners directly within a document’s context. Overview of the Messaging Feature The Messaging feature enables buyers and suppliers on SAP Business Network on BTP to communicate directly with each other using online messaging and email messaging. It supports structured, auditable communication related to procurement and invoicing activities by ensuring that all message exchanges are centrally stored, traceable, and accessible in one place. The feature is available to all buyer users and all supplier users. Buyers and suppliers can use Messaging to clarify purchase order details, follow up on order status, and resolve invoicing or payment issues. By moving these conversations from offline channels into SAP Business Network, the feature improves visibility, accountability, and collaboration efficiency. Online Messaging Online messaging allows buyers and suppliers to communicate directly within SAP Business Network using the Message Center. It provides a centralized, real-time workspace for all conversations, ensuring full message history and visibility for all participants. There are two types of online conversations: In-Context Conversations: Linked to a specific business document (including purchase orders and invoices) and initiated from the document's Details page. These conversations allow users to discuss and resolve document-related issues while maintaining a clear audit trail. Context-Free Conversations: General, document-independent conversations initiated directly from the Message Center, allowing users to communicate more broadly with trading partners. All online conversations, regardless of type, are stored and managed in the Message Center for easy tracking, access, and follow- up. Email Messaging 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 64 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Email messaging allows users to participate in message conversations directly from their email clients while keeping all communication synchronized with the Message Center in SAP Business Network. When a new message is posted, SAP Business Network sends an email notification to all conversation participants who have an SAP Business Network account. By default, SAP Business Network includes the latest two messages of a conversation in the email. Recipients can reply directly from email, and their responses are processed by SAP Business Network and added to the corresponding conversation thread. For more information, see Email Messaging. Benefits Using the Messaging feature helps trading partners: Reduce processing delays and manual coordination in procurement and invoicing workflows. Resolve disputes more efficiently with centralized, traceable message history. Maintain a complete audit trail of buyer–supplier interactions across online and email channels. Availability and Prerequisites The Messaging feature is available to buyer and supplier organizations using SAP Business Network on BTP. To allow unregistered and registered suppliers to respond to interactive email-order emails, ensure that standard enablement using interactive email-order is turned on for the SAP Business Network buyer account. Glossary of Messaging Terms Term Definition Conversation A collection of one or more messages grouped by a common subject. Each conversation includes the subject, participants, and the sequence of exchanged messages. In-context conversation A conversation linked to a specific business document, such as a purchase order or invoice. It enables trading partners to communicate directly about that document. Context-free conversation A general conversation not tied to any business document. It is initiated from the Message Center and used for broader or document-independent communication. Message / Post The content exchanged within a conversation. Messages (also knows as posts) appear in chronological order within the Message Center, forming a single communication thread. Message Center The central workspace where users can create, view, and manage all conversations. It is accessed by clicking the  icon in the top- right corner of the SAP Business Network portal. The Messaging User Interface The following example shows the Message Center user interface: 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 65 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 5 of 10 -- Element on Screen Description Search bar Allows you to search for specific messages. Create Starts a new conversation. Delete Deletes a conversation. Available only to administrators in the initiator’s organization. Conversation list on the left panel Displays all conversations, including: In-context conversations: Linked to a specific business document. The Reference field on the conversation details screen indicates the document linked to the conversation. Context-free conversations: General conversation not linked to any business document. Edit Subject Edits the subject of a conversation. Close Conversation Makes a conversation read-only. Available only to the initiator or administrators in the initiator’s organization. Reopen Reopens a closed conversation open for further communication. Available only to the initiator or administrators in the initiator’s organization. Email Messaging Email messaging extends the SAP Business Network Messaging capability by allowing buyers and suppliers to participate in message conversations directly from their email clients. In addition to the online messaging channel, users can receive email notifications for newly created messages and send responses by replying to those emails. All email-based responses are captured and displayed in the corresponding online message thread, ensuring that all communication remains contextual, auditable, and accessible to all conversation participants.  Note The data shown in this example screenshot is for testing purposes only and does not represent real customer data. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 66 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 6 of 10 -- This capability is available to all buyer users and supplier users and supports both document-related conversations, such as those initiated from purchase orders or invoices, and context-free conversations. Buyer and supplier administrators can configure the email addresses that should receive message notifications. When a new message is posted, SAP Business Network sends an email notification to all conversation participants who have an SAP Business Network account. By default, SAP Business Network includes the latest two messages of a conversation in the email. Recipients can reply directly from email, and their responses are processed by SAP Business Network and added to the corresponding conversation thread. Adding a Participant to an Email Conversation Buyers and suppliers can include participants who don't have access to SAP Business Network by including the email address of the participant in the carbon copy (Cc) field of an email client. When the participant responds, buyers and suppliers can continue the conversation by responding to the emails. When a participant is included in an email, it must contain the Messaging Policy consent statement to ensure that the participant consents to the Messaging Policy of the SAP Ariba Cloud Services. When any subuser is deleted, SAP Business Network deletes all personal information of the subuser and stops sending any email notifications to the subuser. In this scenario, when a participant (either a buyer subuser or a supplier subuser) of a conversation is deleted, the Messaging feature deletes the details of the participant. SAP Business Network doesn't delete any conversation. Any other user having access to the document in SAP Business Network can participate in the conversation. Adding Attachments to a Message While initiating a message or responding to a message, a buyer or supplier can add attachments to the message. You can also add attachments while replying to an email message. All participants of a conversation can view the list of attachments either online in SAP Business Network or in the email message. You can download attachments either in SAP Business Network or from the email message. You can add a maximum of 5 attachments to a message. The size of each attachment can't exceed 10 MB. SAP Business Network rejects all email messages containing more than 5 attachments or if the size of any attachment exceeds 10 MB. Attachments having executable file extensions aren't allowed. Standard account suppliers can also add attachments while replying to a message via email. Supplier End User Tasks Initiating a Context-Free Conversation You can start a conversation that is not linked to any specific business document. These are called context-free conversations and are created directly from the Message Center. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen.  Note When a user initiates a message from SAP Business Network, the user can add only one participant. However, when the responding participant replies to a message via an email client, multiple participants can be added. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 67 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 7 of 10 -- The Message Center is displayed. 2. In the left panel of the Message Center, click Create. The Create New Conversation dialog opens. 3. Enter the following details: Recipient: Enter the name of the organization you want to contact. You can also click the  icon to choose from a list of organizations with which you have an active trading or sourcing relationship. Subject: Provide a brief subject for your conversation (maximum 20 characters). Start Message: Type your initial message (maximum 1024 characters). Message content must not include lewd, harassing, discriminatory, or illegal material. Attachment: Select files to attach, if needed. You can attach up to five files, with a maximum size of 10 MB per file. 4. Click Create to start your conversation Results The conversation is created and displayed in the Message Center You can continue exchanging messages with the recipient within this thread. Initiating an In-Context Conversation After a business document is created and sent, you can start a conversation with your trading partner in the context of that document. These are called in-context conversations. Context You can exchange in-context messages for the following document types: Purchase Orders PO-Based Invoices Non-PO Invoices Procedure 1. Open the required document, such as a purchase order or invoice. 2. On the document Details page, click Send Message. The Messages popup appears. 3. Click New message. The Create New Conversation dialog opens. 4. Enter the following details:  Note Files attached to messages cannot be deleted or recalled once sent. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 68 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 8 of 10 -- Recipient: Enter the name of the organization you want to contact. You can also click the  icon to choose from a list of organizations with which you have an active trading or sourcing relationship. Subject: Provide a brief subject for your conversation (maximum 20 characters). Start Message: Type your initial message (maximum 1024 characters). Message content must not include lewd, harassing, discriminatory, or illegal material. Attachment: Select files to attach, if needed. You can attach up to five files, with a maximum size of 10 MB per file. 5. Click Create to start your conversation Results You can start exchanging messages with the recipient within this thread. If you click Send Message again from the document’s Details page, the existing conversation opens automatically. You can also access the same conversation from the Message Center. Viewing and Replying to Online Messages You can view and reply to online messages directly from the Message Center. Context Any user in your organization can access the Message Center and participate in a conversation. Within each conversation thread, participants are identified by their user name followed by the name of their company. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, select the conversation you want to view. The conversation thread appears on the right. 3. Enter your reply in the text box and click the  Send icon to send it. 4. Optional: To attach files, click the  Attachment icon and select the files you want to upload. Unsubscribing from Email Notifications for Online Messages As a supplier, you can unsubscribe from email notifications that are sent when new conversation messages are posted.  Note Files attached to messages cannot be deleted or recalled once sent.  Note You can upload up to 5 files, and each file can be up to 10 MB in size. Files attached to messages cannot be deleted or recalled once sent. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 69 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Context By default, when buyers and suppliers communicate using the Message Center, the Messaging feature sends an email notification for each message. If you do not want to receive an email for every message, you can unsubscribe using the steps below. Procedure 1. Open the notification email. 2. Click the Unsubscribe link for email message notification. Results After unsubscribing, you will no longer receive email notifications for new conversation messages. To resume receiving email notifications, contact your SAP Business Network account administrator and ask them to add your email address back to the notification list. Supplier Administrator Tasks Closing a Conversation To prevent accidental replies, the conversation initiator or an administrator from the initiator’s organization can close a conversation, making it read-only. Prerequisites You are either the conversation initiator or an administrator from the initiator’s organization. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. In the left panel of the Message Center, select the conversation that you can close. 3. Click Close Conversation in the top-right corner of the screen. 4. In the confirmation dialog, click Close to confirm. Results The conversation becomes inactive and you’re not able to send new messages until reopened. Related Information Reopening a Conversation Reopening a Conversation 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 70 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SBN BTP Supplier Admin.content: You can reopen a closed conversation if you need to continue communicating with the recipient. Prerequisites You are either the conversation initiator or an administrator from the initiator organization. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, click the closed conversation you want to reopen. 3. Click Reopen Conversation at the top-right corner of the conversation details screen. 4. In the confirmation dialog, click OK to confirm. Results The conversation is active again, and you can continue exchanging messages with the recipient. Deleting a Conversation If a conversation is no longer needed, an administrator from the initiator organization can delete it. Once deleted, the conversation cannot be resumed and will be permanently removed from the system in accordance with the system’s data retention policy. Prerequisites You are an administrator from the initiator organization. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, select a conversation that you want to delete. 3. Click Delete at the top right of the panel. Results The conversation is removed from the conversation list and cannot be resumed. Deleting a Message from a Conversation An administrator from the initiator organization can delete individual messages from a conversation.  Note Checkboxes are disabled for conversations that were not initiated by your organization. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 71 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- Prerequisites You must be an administrator from the initiator organization. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, open a conversation that was initiated by a user from your organization. 3. Under the message you want to remove, click Delete. Results The selected message is deleted from the conversation. The recipient can no longer view the message. Configuring a Supplier Account to Receive Email Notifications As a supplier administrator, use this procedure to configure email addresses for a supplier account to receive certain kinds of email notifications. Context Supplier accounts can receive email notifications for the following types of messages: Document-specific messages Purchase order-related messages. Invoice-related messages Default email notifications for all messages You can specify a maximum of three comma-separated email addresses to receive the notifications. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Account Administration Notifications . 2. On the Notifications page, click the Messaging tab. 3. Choose your next step. Send notifications when purchase order messages are received. In the Global document-specific settings section, check the Send notifications to these addresses checkbox, and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. Send notifications when invoice messages are received. Check the Send notifications when invoice messages are received checkbox, and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. Send notifications for all types of buyer messages received. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 72 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- In the Global default settings section, check the Send notifications when customer messages are received checkbox and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. If global document-specific settings aren't defined, or if those email addresses are unsubscribed from receiving notifications, the Messaging feature sends the notifications to the specified email addresses. Send all notifications to the SAP Business Network administrator. Check theSend all notifications to the SAP Business Network administrator checkbox. If you enable both global default settings, the Messaging feature sends notifications to the SAP Business Network Supplier Administrator only when the email addresses in Global document-specific messages are unsubscribed. Send notifications when context-free messages are sent or received. In the Context-free settings section, check the Send context-free message notifications to these addresses checkbox and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. 4. Click Save. 5. Click Close. Quality Notifications Improvements have been made for the Notification list page, search, permissions, settings, email notifications, and authorizations for buyers and suppliers on SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain has adapted the SAPUI5 technology to improve user experience intuitiveness, navigation, content organization, and visual consistency. Elements present in the classic SAP Business Network for Supply Chain user interface have been added to the new user interface to maintain parity. Buyers and suppliers can access the redesigned Notification list page by navigating to Quality Notification from the shellbar. Changes to the User Interface Quality Notification List Page The Notification list page displays search filters and a Notifications (N) table where N represents the total number of quality notifications.  Note You must have SAP Business Network for Supply Chain and the quality collaboration entitlement to configure the quality collaboration rules. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 73 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- The Notification list page includes a view dropdown menu where you can save filter preferences, refine your search, and save your settings as a custom view. The default Standard view displays all your notifications. To change a view, select the  down navigation arrow and choose Go. A My Views popup dialog appears with the following options: Standard (default) 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 74 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 4 of 10 -- Save As - Save your customized view. After clicking Save As, a Save View popup menu appears for you to enter a unique name, choose to set as a default view and/or apply the filters automatically each time you access the Notification list page. Manage - Manage your customized views. A Manage Views popup dialog appears with a list of the View, set a view as the Default, use Apply Automatically to load the Notification list page with applied filters, and review who created the custom views in the Created By column. You can delete a custom view by selecting  Delete View next to the respective view. Some filters, such as Customer batch, have a  value help icon. Choosing the  value help icon opens a Search and Select popup dialog. The Search and Select popup dialog includes filters to help define your search for specific quality notification documents. The Search and Select pop up dialog includes an Items (N) table where N represents the total number of statuses that match your filter parameters. You can also define conditions to help modify your search results. For more information on defining conditions, see Define Conditions. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 75 This is custom documentation. Quality notification type Search for one or more quality notification types. You can choose the  value help icon to search and select a value or to define conditions. Priority Filter your quality notifications by choosing the following priorities: Critical High Low Medium Urgent You can choose one or multiple levels of priorities. Creation date Choose a date period from the  date range pickericon. The Notifications table includes the following fields: Field Description Supplier deviation no. A unique ID or document number provided by the supplier in SAP Business Network. Customer (Supplier view) Displays the name of the customer in the supplier's system. Supplier (Buyer view) Displays the name of the supplier in the buyer's system. Priority Displays the status of the quality notification as: 1 (Low) 2 (Medium) 3 (High) 4 (Urgent)  Note Choose a From and To date range.  Note Choose the value for X in days or weeks.  Note Choose or enter the number of days for Before Today and After Today. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 78 This is custom documentation. Ver Displays the version number of the purchase order. If an quality notification document has changed or is modified, a document version number appears. Original quality notifications begin with the version number 1. Creation date (Preferred Time Zone) Displays the creation date in your local time zone. Supplier part no. Alphanumeric identifier assigned by a supplier to every product it sells. The supplier part number is used by a company as part of its master data for the products it buys from that supplier. Customer batch A batch ID of a product that is batch-managed by the customer. Customer deviation no. A unique ID set by the customer in their backend system (S4 or SAP ERP). Due date (Preferred Time Zone) Displays the due date in your local time zone. Last changed (Preferred Time Zone) Displays the date and time the quality notification has changed in your local time zone. Quality notification type Displays the type of the quality notification.
