file://SBN/split/SBN BTP Supplier Admin.content: Buyers and suppliers can export and print quality notifications in PDF and cXML format from the details page at the top of page in the Download option. Visual Filters When viewing the Quality Notifications list page, an option to display your filtered search results as a visual chart. Selecting the  Visual Filters icon displays your filters as a horizontal graph chart based on Quality Notification by Status and Quality Notification by Quality Notification Type as shown in the following image: You can modify how the data is displayed in both the Quality Notification by Status and Quality Notification by Quality Notification Type charts by choosing the  value help icon next to the chart titles. The Quality Notification by Status and Quality Notification by Quality Notification Type charts includes the following user interface changes: A  value help icon to help refine your search. Choosing the  value help icon next to the chart title opens the Status search and select and the Quality notification type pop up dialogs. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 81 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 1 of 10 -- The Status search and select and the Quality notification type pop up dialogs includes an Items (N) table where N represents the total number of statuses that match your filter parameters. A Go button is available to apply your selected filters to display on the Visual Filters charts. A Show Filters is available to help you further refine your search for specific quality notifications. To display all the available filters, select Show All Filters. Possible values are: 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 82 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 2 of 10 -- Search and Select Filters Supplier Customer Customer location Purchase order no. Ship notice no. Customer part no. Supplier batch Customer batch Supplier part no. Supplier deviation no. Customer deviation no. Supplier action Status Quality notification type Priority Creation date You can also define conditions to help modify your search results. When filtering for quality notifications, you can define conditions for the Quality Notification by Status and Quality Notification by Quality Notification Type charts. Choosing the  value help icon opens a Define Conditions pop up window for the respective filter option. After defining conditions, these conditions are applied to the filtered options. Example: Condition Company Code equal to =001 The following table describes the possible options for defining conditions: Section Condition Include contains equal to between starts with ends with 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 83 This is custom documentation. Choosing the  View Settings opens a View Settings pop up dialog. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 84 This is custom documentation. The Columns tab includes a search bar, a  Filters icon, and a Columns with a (X/N) counter where X represents the visible columns, and N represents the total number of available columns. Implementation Details General Prerequisites To configure relevant quality collaboration business rules, buyer administrators must go to Account Settings Default Transaction Rules . You have SAP Business Network for Supply Chain activated for your SAP Business Network account. Buyers have the following permission assigned: Permission/Role Description Quality Collaboration Access Allow buyers to view the Quality collaboration tab. Supplier administrators have the following permissions assigned: Permission Description Quality Notification Access Suppliers with this permission can only view quality notifications. Quality Notification Creation Suppliers with this permission can create new quality notifications. Related Information Creating and Editing Quality Notifications for Suppliers Using the Visual Filters Chart Prerequisites When viewing the Quality Notifications list page, an option to display your filtered search results as a visual chart is available on the header level. Select the  Visual Filters icon to display your filters as a horizontal graph chart based on Quality Notification by Status and Quality Notification by Quality Notification Type. You have the following permissions assigned to your account: Buyer Permission Description Quality Collaboration Access Allow buyers to view the Quality collaboration tab. Supplier Permission Description Quality Notification Access Suppliers with this permission can only view quality notifications. Quality Notification Creation Suppliers with this permission can create new quality notifications. Procedure 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 86 This is custom documentation. Choose the  value help icon next to the Quality Notification by Status and Quality Notification by Quality Notification Type chart titles. Viewing Quality Notifications for Buyers and Suppliers Buyers and suppliers can view details and additional information for each quality notification. Quality Notification Details and Header You can select a quality notification from the Notifications table of the Quality Notification list page to view the details of the quality notification. The selected quality notification details page appears with header information, a Back button to return to the Quality Notification list page, a Download button to export as a cXML or PDF file, and a  Share icon to send the quality notification to an email. Selecting the  Send to e-mail icon opens a draft email message from your default email application. The Quality Notification details page includes the Details, Defects, Partner information, and History tabs. Each tab includes the following information: Details tab contains the Customer and part, Notification detail, Problem description, Return information, Required task, and Activity log sections. Defects tab displays a Defects (N) table where N represents the number of defects identified in the quality notification. The Defects table includes the following fields: Field Description Number Numerical identifier of the defect. Title Subject line of the complaint. Defect category Defect grouping. Number of defects Number of defects found in the quality notification. Comment Displays the comments left in the quality notification. Also appears as a  Comment icon which opens a pop up dialog after clicking on it. Defect subcategory Defect subgrouping.  Note You have the following permissions assigned to your account: Buyer Permission Description Quality Collaboration Access Allow buyers to view the Quality collaboration tab. Supplier Permission Description Quality Notification Access Suppliers with this permission can only view quality notifications. Quality Notification Creation Suppliers with this permission can create new quality notifications. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 89 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 9 of 10 -- Field Description Search Search for a specific defect in the quality notification. Selecting on the defect opens the Defects details panel. It displays additional information of the specific defect as: Comments: Comments left by your supplier. Causes: The Causes table describes the problems found in the defects. The fields include the defect Number, the Title of the defect, a Cause category and Cause subcategory that describes the root cause, and Comment if applicable. Also appears as a  Comment icon which opens a pop up dialog after clicking on it. A Search bar is available to help you search for a specific cause. Additional Impacted Batches: The Additional Impacted Batches table includes batch information impacted by the defects. The fields include the impacted batch Number, the Customer location the defect took place, Customer part no., and Customer batch. Required tasks: The Required tasks table contains a list of tasks required to help mitigate or reduce defects. Activity log: The Activity log includes additional information on how the goods are handled. Partner Information tab: The Partner Information displays contact, shipping, and billing information for buyers and suppliers. The General section includes the From and To contact information that displays the name, email, address, and phone number. If the quality notification is initiated by the supplier, the From section displays the supplier's contact information. The To section displays the buyer's contact information. If the quality notification is initiated by the buyer, the From section displays the buyer's contact information. The To section displays the supplier's contact information. The Contact Information section displays the name, address, phone number, and email for the Seller Party Contact, Buyer Party Contact, and User Contact. The Shipping and Billing Information section displays the name, address, phone number, and email for the Bill To and Ship To contacts. History tab: Displays the Status, Event, Changed by, and the Date and time of the quality notification documents routed in SAP Business Network.  Note The user contact information is displayed after the supplier sends the quality notification.  Note Buyers with the Quality Collaboration Access permission can only view the quality notifications. 5/6/26, 6:55 AM 90 This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SBN Supplier Account _.content: 2 Get your results This calculator will help you determine your: Subscription level We offer five subscription levels: Premium, Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Platinum. Estimated annual fee The data you provide will help you estimate your annual fee. This calculator provides an estimate of subscription and transaction fees for SAP Business Network based on the information you provide and the current, generally applicable fees schedule for SAP Business Network enterprise accounts. This calculator applies to the usual global fee model (exceptions exist in Brazil, Chile, Peru, and southern Africa - see specific fee schedules). Please note that fees are billed only in the following currencies: USD, CAD, AUD, SGD, JPY, EUR, GBP, CHF, and ZAR. The calculator automatically switches to the relevant currency once you choose your country. Frequently asked questions Why would some suppliers need to pay fees to use SAP Business Network? SAP invests significantly in SAP Business Network to ensure it offers suppliers and other trading partners more value and support than any other collaboration product in the industry. This includes providing suppliers with onboarding services and support in multiple languages and locations worldwide, which requires investment from our customers as well. In addition, SAP bundles value-added functionality, services, and support into subscriptions tailored to suppliers’ level of participation How do suppliers obtain access to specific features or services available at their subscription level? We offer five subscription levels: Premium, Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Platinum. The subscription level each supplier receives is aligned with the financial volume and number of documents they transact on SAP Business Network as well as their technology usage. Many of the subscription features and services are available directly on SAP Business Network, so suppliers can access them by simply logging / / Overview Features Promote subscription Pricing Customer stories Support Log in All products SAP Business Network Suppliers Pricing -- 1 of 2 -- in to their accounts. For answers to more specific questions regarding subscription services or billing, suppliers may sign into their SAP Business Network account to contact support through the help center. How are supplier fees calculated? To understand how fees are calculated, please download the subscription overview and fee schedule above. You can also try the fee calculator that can help you estimate fees based on your expected SAP Business Network activity. How are “transaction volume” and “document counts” calculated? Transaction volume is calculated as the total financial value in the applicable currency, including any taxes such as value-added taxes (VAT), of all non-PO invoices plus the total financial value of all POs, excluding canceled orders, or all invoices generated from a PO, whichever is greater, sent over SAP Business Network for the preceding 12 months. To avoid double counting, PO-based invoices sent through SAP Business Network are not included in the transaction volume. Which documents are included in these annual counts? Only purchase order and invoice, both PO- and non-PO-based, documents are included in the annual counts. / / Overview Features Promote subscription Pricing Customer stories Support Log in All products SAP Business Network Suppliers Pricing -- 2 of 2 --

Supplier Administration Guide Content PUBLIC 3 -- 3 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide This guide describes how the administrator for a seller account can update company information and configure additional users. Supplier administrators must maintain complete and accurate company information to be matched to new prospective buyers. This guide applies to: • SAP Business Network • SAP Business Network for Supply Chain • SAP Business Network Discovery Related guides Managing your SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Configuring Document Routing Managing Subscription Services Types of SAP Business Network Accounts You have the choice to do business using one of two SAP Business Network account types: Standard or Enterprise. Some suppliers choose to transact on the SAP Business Network using a fee based Enterprise account due to their historical volume of transactions or to leverage certain functionality that is only available with an Enterprise account. If you are unsure which account type to choose, register a free of charge standard account. You can always upgrade to an Enterprise account if your business needs change. Converting a Fully-Enabled Enterprise Account to a Standard Account [page 5] Deleting Your SAP Business Network Account [page 6] 4 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 4 of 10 -- Converting a Fully-Enabled Enterprise Account to a Standard Account Use this procedure to convert your SAP Business Network account from a fully-enabled Enterprise account to a Standard account. Prerequisites You must be the administrator of a single-organization enterprise account. For multi-organization accounts and suppliers that are part of Quadrem Network billing plan, contact SAP Ariba Network Operations. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Convert to Standard account. 2. Review the information on the Account change eligibility check screen. 3. Click Check eligibility now to continue. 4. A green checkmark in the status indicates that you have met all the requirements to convert your account. The Convert now option appears only after you pass all the eligibility criteria(s). 5. After you click the Convert now option, a Download reports popup appears prompting you to download any reports you might need later. 6. Click Convert now to convert your fully-enabled Enterprise account to a Standard account. You see an Account converted screen on successful conversion of your enterprise account into standard account.  Note If your account does not meet one or more eligibility criteria(s), a red crossmark appears in the status column. You must review and take appropriate action to resolve the criteria(s) marked with red cross. 7. After you resolve the failed criteria(s), you can select Re-check eligibility to re-evaluate your eligibility for converting your account. You can also select Stay with Enterprise account to continue using the enterprise account. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 5 -- 5 of 10 -- Deleting Your SAP Business Network Account Use this procedure to delete your SAP Business Network account. This procedure also applies to SAP Business Network Supplier mobile app. Prerequisites • You must be the account administrator. • You must pay any outstanding fees on your account. • You must delete all credit card information from your account. • You must use only active email addresses listed for your account. • You must convert your Enterprise account to a Standard account. See, Downgrade your Enterprise account to a Standard account • You must reject all trading relationships . • You must delete all the links with other accounts under Account Hierarchy • You must delete all sub-user accounts. • You must delete all the Archived invoices. Context If you are finished using SAP Business Network to conduct transactions over the internet, you can delete your account. However, there is no charge to keep your account open when you have no established trading relationships. You may want to maintain an active account to connect with future customers who use SAP Business Network, or find new customers using SAP Business Network Discovery. Procedure 1. Login to the supplier account as an administrator. 2. Navigate to Users Settings Users . 3. Click Account Deletion. Results After you submit the account deletion request, you will receive a confirmation email with the subject line: Action Required:Confirm Account Deletion Request. Click the link included in the email to confirm the request. 6 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 6 of 10 --  Note • The link will expire in 5 mins. After that, the account will be expired and none of the users will be able to log on to the account. For this reason, it is highly recommended that the you inform all account users and customers of the account deletion prior to deleting the account. If you are planning on deleting your account so that your email address can be used as a username on another SAP Business Network account, please change your username to a different username before deleting the account because you will not be able to use username attached to the deleted account again. Usernames must be in the format of an email address, but the email address does not need to be a valid email. • There is no charge to keep your account open when there are no trading relationships established. You can keep your account open to connect with future customers who use Ariba or find new customers using SAP Business Network Discovery. There is a grace period of 60 days when you are still able to restore your account after an account deletion request. Once the grace period is over, your account gets permanently deleted and cannot be retrieved. If you want to restore your account within 60 days of submitting the deletion request, you must create a Case with SAP Support . Your Company Profile The trading partner company profile helps you win more business by standing out to potential customers across the entirety of SAP Business Network. You can update and maintain information in the Company Profile about your business, including products and services offered, your experience and expertise, and highlights of your accomplishments and values. Additionally, you can control whether or not you want to appear in search results. By default, your profile is visible to all potential and existing customer relationships. About This Profile [page 8] Network Catalog Access [page 8] Profile Settings [page 8] Organizational Structure [page 11] Editing Your Company profile [page 12] How to Add Sustainability Ratings to Your Company Profile [page 12] Showing or Hiding Your Company Profile in Search Results [page 13] Adding Economic Activity Code (GIRO) to Your Company Profile [page 14] Showcasing Assessments on Your Company Profile [page 15] Certifications [page 15] Contacts [page 19] Profile Data Federation [page 23] Company Profile Experience for Promote [page 24] SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 7 -- 7 of 10 -- About This Profile The About This Profile link, located under the company name on your profile, provides key details about your registration history. It reveals the following information: • Member of SAP Business Network Since: Indicates the year you joined SAP Business Network. It reflects your maturity and experience on the platform. A longer membership suggests greater stability and reliability. • Registration Type: Shows how you registered with SAP Business Network. There are two possible registration methods: • Invited: Another buyer invited you to join the platform. This indicates a trusted recommendation and potential endorsement. • Walk-up: You proactively self-registered on the platform. This demonstrates your initiative to engage with the SAP Business Network community. Network Catalog Access Your company profile displays a Network Catalog link under the company name. This link becomes active once you upload products to your network catalog. When potential buyers view your company profile, they can click the link to access a pre-filtered search page that lists a complete suite of your network catalog offerings, including pricing information and specifications. If no products are uploaded, the link stays inactive. For instructions on uploading products to your network catalog, refer to Managing Network Catalog. Profile Settings As a supplier on SAP Business Network, your company's public profile is accessible to all users on SAP Business Network. To attract potential buyers and assist your existing buyers in effective planning, it is crucial to maintain a comprehensive and accurate profile. You have the flexibility to manage the visibility of additional information about your company beyond the basic details, control your profile's appearance in search results, manage buyer access to your extended profiles, and regulate who can initiate contact with you. These objectives can be accomplished by configuring the profile settings. To access these settings, follow these steps: 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. 3. Click on the Options menu located in the upper-right corner of your company profile. 4. Select Profile settings from the dropdown menu. Refer to the table below for a description of each profile setting: 8 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 8 of 10 -- Profile Setting Description Profile Visibility Choose between Show or Hide for each item that you want to display or hide on your public profile. The following items are always visible to all users visiting your public profile: • Basic Info • Product and Service Categories • Ship-to or Service Locations • Industries • Marketing Collateral • References • Social Media The following items are always invisible in your public profile: • Keywords • Contacts The following items are configurable to be either shown or hidden in your public profile based on your business needs: • Credentials (Certifications and Sustainability Ratings): You have options to show it to all trading partners with or without an existing trading relationship with you, or only to your existing trading partners. The default is to show it to all trading partners. • Assessments: The default setting is Show. • Activity Data: The default setting is Show. Organization Structure Choose the required visibility setting from the following op- tions: • Show: Organization structure is visible to all trading part- ners on SAP Business Network. • Hide: Organization structure is hidden from all trading partners on SAP Business Network. • Show to my trading partners only: Organization struc- ture is visible to only the trading partners with whom the supplier has a relationship. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 9 -- 9 of 10 -- Profile Setting Description Search Results Visibility Show my profile in search results Choose whether your company will appear in search results when SAP Business Network Discovery users and Trading Part- ners search for suppliers. To increase your company’s visibility for new business opportunities, ensure that this option is ena- bled. Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network When enabled, your profile data will be replicated across global data centers of SAP Business Network and visible in those regions. For details, see Profile Data Federation [page 23]. For suppliers, this setting is enabled by default. Buyers need to enable it manually. Once enabled, this setting cannot be reversed.  Note As a supplier, to enable your profile searchable across global data centers, you must also toggle on Show my profile in search results in addition to enabling Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network. Extended Profile Visibility Choose whether your extended profile is available to all buyers on SAP Business Network or only to those who already have an established relationship with you or have sent you a relation- ship request. The extended profile includes details such as your catalog and transaction capabilities, which you can set up within the Electronic Order Routing, Electronic Invoice Routing, and Settlement sections. To access these configurations, click on the Account Settings icon and then proceed to Settings Network Settings on your SAP Business Network portal. Buyers have the ability to download your extended profile. The information in the downloaded file is sourced from various con- figuration areas, including My Account, Company Profile, and settings within Electronic Order Routing, Electronic Invoice Routing, and Settlement. 10 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SBN Supplier Administra.content: • You have 30 days to download ZIP files for transaction documents identified for deletion. After that, the documents are permanently deleted. Procedure 1. Click ..., and choose Deleted Transactions in the Document Archive section. The Deleted Transactions page appears. If files are available for download, they appear in separate tables for recurring deletion and one-time deletion. Figure 6: Deleted Transactions Page 2. To download a ZIP file, go to the Action column and click the  Download icon.  Tip You can filter the table of ZIP files to show files for which download has not yet started. Transaction Data Download The administrator for your SAP Business Network account and other users with appropriate permission can request to download your account's transaction data at any time for any period up to 90 days. If you would like to be notified by email when ZIP files are available to download, ask your administrator to set up notifications [page 34]. The following transaction documents can be downloaded: • Purchase orders (orders and blanket orders) • Order confirmations SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 91 -- 1 of 10 -- • Ship notices • Receipts • Service sheets • Invoices, credit memos, and debit memos • Payment documents • SAP Business Network for Supply Chain transaction documents • Notifications • Quote requests and quote messages SAP Business Network maintains transaction documents in cXML (Commerce eXtensible Markup Language) format, and you can download them in ZIP files. For more information about cXML, see the cXML Reference Guide at cXML.org . Downloading Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Suppliers [page 92] Downloading Transaction Data for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can download transaction documents from your SAP Business Network account at any time. Prerequisites • You need the Download Current Transactions permission to perform this task. • The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. • To receive an email notification when requested documents are ready for download, the administrator needs to set up notifications [page 34]. • After your download request is processed, you have 7 days to download ZIP files for the requested transaction documents. After that, the ZIP files are deleted. The original transaction documents are unaffected and remain on SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Choose ... Current Transactions . The Current Transactions page appears. 2. Select a start date and an end date for transaction documents. The date range can be up to 90 days. 3. Click Request. 4. After your request is processed, you should receive an email notification informing you whether ZIP files are available for download. 5. If ZIP files are available, choose ... Current Transactions again. 92 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 2 of 10 -- 6. To download a ZIP file, go to the Action column and click the  Download icon.  Tip You can filter the table of ZIP files to show files for which download hasn't started yet. Analytics Data Export The administrator for your SAP Business Network account can request to export the analytics data from your account. Analytics data refer to your master data and transaction data (purchase orders, invoices, credit memos, and debit memos) used by SAP Business Network to provide analytics features such as the analytics dashboard. SAP Business Network exports analytics data in separate CSV (Comma-Separated Values) files, and you can download them. The data export and download won't affect the original data on SAP Business Network. Requesting Analytics Data Export for SAP Business Network Suppliers [page 93] Requesting Analytics Data Export for SAP Business Network Suppliers You can request to export your analytics data from your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites • You are the administrator of your SAP Business Network account. • You know the ANID of your SAP Business Network account. • You have a secured email box for receiving encrypted email notifications when the requested data is ready for download. Context SAP Business Network uses part of your master data and transaction data (purchase orders, invoices, credit memos, and debit memos) to help you analyze your business activities in the analytics dashboard. If you want to export the data used in analytics, you can make a request. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 93 -- 3 of 10 -- Procedure Create a case on component SBN-AN-ANL to request the analytics data export from your SAP Business Network account. Ensure to provide the ANID of your SAP Business Network account and a secured email box for receiving encrypted email notifications. For information on how to create a case, see Get Support Application Online Help . Results An SAP support representative verifies that you are the account administrator, then sends an encrypted email including a URL and a shared access key for downloading the requested data. You have 7 days to download the data. After that, the download package is deleted. The original data are unaffected and remain on SAP Business Network. API Management API management allows supplier organizations access to the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from within their SAP Business Network accounts. APIs for supplier organizations are published on the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. You can access the SAP Ariba Developer Portal and perform the configurations necessary to access, create, and authenticate API applications after you sign in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. You can: • use single sign-on (SSO) to access the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from the Account Settings page in SAP Business Network • access APIs that are created for use by supplier organizations • view details about APIs, including, but not limited to product documentation, runtime URLs, endpoint information, and swagger documentation For more information, see SAP Ariba APIs. Configuring Your API Client ID [page 95] Accessing the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from SAP Business Network [page 95] 94 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 4 of 10 -- Configuring Your API Client ID Use this procedure to configure your API client IDs in SAP Business Network. Context SAP Business Network is a calling application in the context of accessing supplier-oriented APIs from the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. Therefore, you must provide a client ID in the API Client ID Configuration section. The API client ID is required to enable the SAP Ariba Developer Portal to identify that this is a genuine and secure connection between SAP Business Network and the portal. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Account Registration . 2. Click the API Management tab. 3. In the API Client ID Configuration section, click Add. 4. Enter the Client ID. For more information, see Help for the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. 5. Click Add. 6. Click Save. Next Steps After you finish configuring your API client ID, click Close to return to your Home dashboard. Accessing the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from SAP Business Network Use this procedure to access the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You must have the API Development Access permission to be able to view the section Ariba Developer Portal (Automatic Sign In) and to access the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 95 -- 5 of 10 -- Context SAP Business Network allows supplier organizations access to the SAP Ariba Developer Portal from within SAP Business Network. If you have the API Development Access permission, you do not require any further sign-on credentials to access the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. Your sign-on session to SAP Business Network is sufficient.  Note Supplier users with administrator privileges have the API Development Access permission by default. The supplier administrator must first sign in to the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. The supplier organization is created in the SAP Ariba Developer Portal only after the supplier administrator signs in to the portal. Subsequently, supplier administrators can create users and selectively assign roles with the API Development Access permission. For more information, see Users and Roles [page 42]. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Account Registration . 2. Click the API Management tab. 3. In the Ariba Developer Portal (Automatic Sign In) section, click the link Developer Portal. 4. In the SAP Ariba APIs sign-in page, click SAP Business Network Supplier SSO. For more information, see Help for the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. Dun & Bradstreet Integration Dun & Bradstreet (D&B) integration allows you to synchronize your company information from the D&B database and auto-populate it into your company profile. The information that you can synchronize from D&B include: • Company name • Company address • Website URL • Company descriptions  Note To use this feature, your company must be registered with D&B and has a valid Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) number. Even though entering the DUNS number is optional, we highly recommend you use the D&B integration to auto-populate the company information from D&B database. This would help maintain accurate and consistent user data across SAP Business Network. 96 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 6 of 10 -- Steps to Synchronize Company Information from D&B • If you don’t have a DUNS number on your profile: 1. Navigate to Account Settings Company Profile . 2. Click the pencil icon to the right of your company name to open the Edit Company Information page. 3. On Basic info tab, fill out the DUNS Number field. 4. If the entered DUNS number is already in use by another account, click Use a different DUNS number. 5. If you don’t know your DUNS number, click Find my DUNS number to search using your company name and address. 6. After you enter or select a DUNS number, the system checks your company name and address against D&B records: • If the details don’t match, you’ll be prompted to accept updates from D&B. • If you choose not to accept the updates, select Remove My DUNS Number to clear it from your profile. 7. Once you accept the updates, your company name and address fields are auto-populated with the information from D&B and become non-editable unless you remove your DUNS number. 8. Optionally, import additional updates (Website URL, Short Description, Long Description) from D&B to enrich your profile. • If you already have a valid DUNS number on your profile: • The system verifies whether your company name and address match D&B’s records. • If the details don’t match: 1. An alert appears on your profile’s Overview page. 2. Click Review and sync now in the alert to open the Edit Company Information page and update your details or DUNS number. 3. Follow steps 3 to 8 from the section above to synchronize your profile. • If you have an invalid DUNS number on your company profile: 1. An alert on the Overview page notifies you of the invalid DUNS number. 2. Click Update your DUNS number now in the alert to open the Edit Company Information page. 3. Follow steps 3 to 8 from the first section to correct your DUNS number and synchronize your profile with D&B. file://SBN/split/SBN Supplier Administra.content: Profile Setting Description Contact My Company The Do not allow buyers to contact my company using Trading Partner Search setting grants you the ability to de- cide whether potential buyers can directly send you messages through the Trading Partner Search results. This secure communication method ensures the confidential- ity of email addresses while monitoring all interactions in a central location. You receive an email notification when a new message arrives. The Allow other suppliers to contact my account administrator setting grants you with the ability to decide whether users who are in the process of registering an SAP Business Network profile can contact your administrator to request an account sign in. During registration, SAP Business Network performs an auto- mated search across all registered suppliers based on the company name, aliases, DUNS number, and tax ID to deter- mine if the registrant’s company is already registered. If SAP Business Network finds your company as a match and you choose this profile visibility option, the registrant can send an email message to your account administrator requesting a user name and password for their SAP Business Network account. Organizational Structure Viewing the organizational hierarchy of suppliers on SAP Business Network enhances visibility and understanding of supplier relationships and can be used to improve collaboration and decision-making with trading partners. You can view your organizational structure on SAP Business Network by navigating to Account Settings > Company Profile and choosing Organization Structure from the left pane. You can view your organizational hierarchy at the following three levels: • Parent organization • Linked child organizations • Additional addresses Clicking an element at the parent or child organization levels displays the following details: • Name of the organization • Address of the organization • Relationship count • SAP Business Network organization ID or BNOID • Account type SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 11 -- 1 of 10 -- Clicking an element at the additional address level displays the following details: • Name of the address • Address of the organization Editing Your Company profile Use this procedure to edit your Company Profile information and ensure that it’s complete and accurate to attract the most qualified customers. Prerequisites You must have the Company Information permission. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Company Profile. 2. On the Company Profile page, click a pencil icon to edit the information in a section, and enter or revise values as necessary. 3. Click Save. 4. Click Close. How to Add Sustainability Ratings to Your Company Profile Add sustainability ratings to your Company Profile to increase trust and provide transparency on environmental, sustainability, and governance practices to buyers. Context You can now add third-party sustainability ratings in your SAP Business Network Company Profile to increase trust and provide transparency on your environmental, suistaintability, and governance practices to existing and prospective buyers. Buyers can search for and discover trading partners based on these ratings. 12 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 2 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. 2. In the Sustainability ratings section, click the edit icon. 3. Click Add sustainability rating. 4. Do one of the following: • Click Enter rating to manually enter sustainability rating information, then click Add. • Click Import from EcoVadis to import your sustainability rating directly from EcoVadis. 5. Optionally Browse for and Add an attachment to support your rating.  Note Attachments must be in PDF format and can't exceed 10 MB. 6. Click Done. Showing or Hiding Your Company Profile in Search Results If you want to prevent potential customers on SAP Business Network from finding your company through search, use this procedure to hide your Company Profile in search results. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Company Profile. The Company Profile page appears. 2. Navigate to the upper right corner of the Company Profile page and choose the  Options button. The Options popover window appears. 3. Toggle the Show my profile in search results option as desired. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 13 -- 3 of 10 -- Your changes are automatically saved. Adding Economic Activity Code (GIRO) to Your Company Profile Adding economic activity code to your profile is mandatory for Chilean suppliers. You can also view and change the selected economic activity code. When you select the applicable economic activity code, it appears in the GIRO field of your company profile. Field Description GIRO Code related to an activity that involves the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services. For a list of official economic activity codes and their descriptions, see https://www.sii.cl/ayudas/ ayudas_por_servicios/1956-codigos-1959.html . Procedure Follow these steps to change your selected economic activity code. 1. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. 2. Click view details link to view the GIRO description. 3. Click the edit icon to change your GIRO code. 4. Use the drag down option or the search filter to select the applicable GIRO code or description. 5. Click Save. 14 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 4 of 10 -- Showcasing Assessments on Your Company Profile On your SAP Business Network company profile, you can showcase completed assessments related to your products, services, and business practices. This enhances your credibility and makes it easier for buyers to access your assessment responses. To adjust these settings, go to Options Profile settings Profile Visibility and manage the Assessments section. If you choose to show the Assessments section and have shared the assessments with a buyer, they can directly access and view these assessments on your company profile. Even if you haven't shared assessments with a specific buyer, they can still request access to these assessments through the Assessments section on your company profile, irrespective of their current trading or sourcing relationship with you. For added convenience, if you've enabled the Auto share completed assessments with my buyers upon request setting, any assessment sharing requests from buyers with existing trading or sourcing relationships will be automatically handled. However, if a sharing request comes from a buyer without an established relationship, you'll need to manually grant access to your assessments. You'll receive both an in-app notification and an email notification when a buyer initiates an assessment sharing request from your company profile. This ensures you stay informed and can manage these requests promptly. Related Information Self-Assessment Questionnaire Certifications Certifications are essential credentials that highlight your company's expertise, credibility, and compliance with industry standards. Displaying them on your SAP Business Network profile helps demonstrate your commitment to quality and build trust with current and potential customers. SAP Business Network supports a wide range of certification types, including: • Supplier Diversity Certifications for businesses owned and operated by underrepresented groups. Categories include: • Small Business • Women-owned Business • Minority-owned Business • Veteran-owned Business • LGBT-Owned Business • Disability-Owned Business Each category includes specific certification programs. For example, Small Business certfications may include: • Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 15 -- 5 of 10 -- • 8(a) Business Development Program • HUBZone (Historically Underutilized Business Zone Program)  Note Supplier Diversity certifications are country-specific. Available options are filtered based on your company’s primary address. • Environmental Certifications for businesses that demonstrate environmentally responsible practices, such as reducing waste, conserving energy, and reducing pollution. • Energy Certifications that recognize efforts in energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy sources like solar and wind. • Social Enterprise Certifications for businesses committed to creating positive social or environmental impact in their communities. • Quality Certifications that reflect a commitment to quality management systems and continuous process improvement. • Security Certifications that demonstrate strong information security practices and effective risk management. • Other Certifications that do not fit into the above categories. Managing Certifications on Your Company Profile Adding certifications to your SAP Business Network profile help build trust and credibility with current and potential buyers. Certifications can also improve your visibility, as buyers can search for them when looking for new suppliers. Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context You can add a wide range of certification types, including Supplier Diversity, Environmental, Energy, Social Enterprise, Quality, Security, and Other types. For descriptions about each certification type, see Certifications [page 15]. 16 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 6 of 10 -- Procedure Adding a Certification: 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Click the Certifications tab. 4. Click Add in the upper-right corner. 5. In the Add New Certification dialog box: • Select a certification from the predefined list. • If your certification isn’t listed, check My certification is not in the list, then enter the certification name and choose the appropriate certification type. • Click Browse to upload your certification document. • Accepted file formats: .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .pdf • Maximum file size: 10 MB 6. Fill in the required certification details: • Effective Date • Expiration Date • Certification Number • Certified By • Certified Location • Additional Information (optional) 7. Click Add to save the certification.  Note Before adding a certification, ensure you have obtained it legitimately and have the right to display it publicly. Managing Existing Certifications 8. Once added, you can manage certifications from the Certifications list page: • Check the certification status: • Self-Reported indicates that the certification is supplier-reported and not verified by SAP Business Network or third parties. • An alert ( ) icon appears if a certification has expired. • Download a certification: Click the Download icon next to the document. • Edit, update, or remove a certification: Click the More options ( ) icon and choose: • Manage Details View and edit certification information. On the certification details page: • Click the Edit ( ) icon to update certification details. • Click Add New Version to upload a new recertified version. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 17 -- 7 of 10 --  Note You can add up to two versions per certification. To add a new one after reaching the limit, you must delete an older version first. Showing multiple versions highlights your ongoing commitment to quality and helps strengthen buyer confidence. • Click the Delete ( ) icon to delete a specific version. • Click Delete Certification to remove all versions of the certification. • Add New Version Upload another version to show continued certification. • Delete Remove all versions of the certification. Responding to Certification Requests from Buyers Prerequisites To respond to certification requests from buyers, supplier users must have the Company Information permission to edit their company profiles. Context As a supplier, it is essential to promptly respond to certification requests from buyers. Doing so not only helps establish trust with buyers but also provides you with a competitive advantage within the marketplace. Procedure 1. Upon receiving a certification request notification through your SAP Business Network portal, click the Add option within the notification. If the requested certification is not already present in your profile, clicking Add in the notification will open the Add Certification dialog box. This dialog box allows you to input the details of the new certification you want to add. If the requested certification is already part of your profile, clicking Add in the notification will open the Add New Version dialog box. In this dialog box, you can add a new version to the existing certification. 2. Click Browse to add your certification file. Provide details about the certification, including Certification Number, Certified By, Certified Location, Effective Date, Expiration Date, and Additional Information. Once you've entered these details, click Add.  Note Currently, each certification is limited to a maximum of two versions. If you have reached the limit and want to add a new one, you have to delete an older one first. 18 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 8 of 10 -- Results The certification is now added to your profile and is visible to all visiting buyers. An in-app notification is sent to the requester to inform them of the update. Contacts Efficient communication is a cornerstone of successful business interactions, and maintaining accurate contact information is paramount to achieving this goal. Within SAP Business Network, the contact management feature empowers organizations to effectively manage both the main company contact and individual contacts. Main Company Contact: The Main Company Contact includes essential contact information for the company, specifically the general email, phone, and fax numbers. Each account has one main contact, defaulted to the information of the account creator (administrator), and you have the flexibility to edit and update this information as needed. Individual Company Contacts: In addition to the main company contact, you can create multiple individual contacts and assign them one or more roles, such as Sales Representative, Marketing Manager, or Technical Contact. Assigning a role designates the contact as a companywide contact, which is visible to all trading partners on SAP Business Network. If no role is assigned, the contact is considered private. You can later assign them to specific customers. Customer-Specific Contacts: SAP Business Network allows you to assign contacts to specific customers. These contacts are visible only to the designated customer and serve as the primary point of contact for them, improving personalized communication.  Note Your contact information will be available in supplier contact reports that buyers can download, visible on buyers' Supplier Enablement screens, and consumed by other SAP Ariba applications like SAP Ariba Buying, SAP Ariba Sourcing, and SAP Ariba Supplier Lifecycle and Performance. However, your trading partners won’t see it in your company profile. Editing the Main Contact The main company contact includes essential contact information for your company, specifically the general email address, phone number, and fax number. Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 19 -- 9 of 10 -- Context Each account has one main contact, which defaults to the information of the account creator (administrator). You can edit and update this information as needed. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane. 4. Click the Company Contact Information tab, and then click Edit in the upper-right corner of the page. 5. Update Email, Phone, and Fax of your company as needed. Related Information Contacts [page 19] Managing Companywide Contacts [page 20] Managing Customer-Specific Contacts [page 22] Managing Companywide Contacts Designating a contact as companywide makes their information accessible to both current and potential trading partners on SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context Assigning individuals in your company as companywide contacts ensures your trading partners can easily reach the right people for various issues or inquiries. 20 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 10 of 10 --

Select Contacts from the left navigation pane. 4. Scroll down to the Contact Personnel section and click Create in the upper-right corner of the Contact Personnel with Companywide Assignments table. 5. On the Create New Contact with Companywide Assignment page, provide the following details: Basic Information: • Contact Name (mandatory) • Email (mandatory) • Phone (mandatory) • Business Title • Fax • Company Assignment: Assigning a role here designates the contact as a companywide contact.  Note • If you assign a companywide role to the contact, their information will be visible to all trading partners on SAP Business Network. You can assign multiple roles to a contact, if necessary. • If no companywide role is assigned, the contact is considered private and will not be visible to trading partners. You can later assign them to a specific customer. Address Information: • Country/Region • State • City • Address Line 1 • Address Line 2 • Address Line 3 • Postal Code 6. After providing the necessary information, click Create to save the contact. 7. To edit a contact, click Edit in the upper right corner of the table. 8. To delete a contact, Click Delete in the upper right corner of the table. After a contact is deleted, all its assignments will be removed as well. Related Information Contacts [page 19] Managing Customer-Specific Contacts [page 22] SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 21 -- 1 of 10 -- Managing Customer-Specific Contacts Prerequisites • You have the Company Information permission to edit your company profile. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to assign this permission to you. • The individual contact to be assigned to specific customers have been added to the Contact Personnel with Company Assignments table. For details, refer to Managing Companywide Contacts [page 20]. Context Assign individual contacts to specific customers to act as the main point of contact. This helps personalize communication and strengthens relationships. Note that contacts can only be assigned to customers with an existing trading relationship. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Go to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Contacts from the left navigation pane. 4. Scroll down to the Customer-Specific Assignments section, select a customer from the table, and click Edit. 5. On the Edit Customer-Specific Assignment page, select personnel from the drop-down list to assign them as the specified contact for the selected customer, and then click Save.  Note Customers will only see their own customer-specific assignments, along with any companywide contacts you provide. Related Information Contacts [page 19] Managing Companywide Contacts [page 20] 22 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 2 of 10 -- Profile Data Federation This feature enables your company profile data to be replicated across SAP Business Network's global data centers, making your profile visible to trading partners in different regions. For more information, refer to How Profile Data Federation Works [page 23] and Enabling Profile Data Federation [page 23]. How Profile Data Federation Works Profile data federation replicates your company profile data across all global data centers of SAP Business Network, enabling trading partners in different regions to find and view your company profile, thereby facilitating potential business opportunities. To understand how profile data federation works, consider two trading partners located in different regions: • Trading Partner A is based in the United States (US) data center. • Trading Partner B is based in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) data center. For Trading Partner B to view Trading Partner A’s profile, Trading Partner A’s profile data must be replicated from the US data center to the KSA data center. To make this happen, Trading Partner A must enable profile data federation. For details about how to enable profile data federation, refer to Enabling Profile Data Federation [page 23]. Once enabled, an initial replication synchronizes your company profile data across all global data centers of SAP Business Network. Future updates are automatically synchronized to ensure your profile remains consistent and up to date across all data centers.  Note Profile data federation is only available to companies that are not sole proprietors. Enabling Profile Data Federation Profile data federation allows your company profile to be visible across all global data centers of SAP Business Network. This makes it possible for trading partners in different regions to find and view your company profile, facilitating potential business opportunities. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See Permissions You Can Assign to Users [page 54]. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 23 -- 3 of 10 -- Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. This opens the Company Profile page. 3. Click the Options menu in the upper-right corner of your profile and select Profile settings. 4. On the Profile Settings page, locate the section labeled Search Results Visibility: a. Optional: Toggle Show my profile in search results to allow your profile appear in search results. This setting determines whether your company profile is visible to trading partners in their search results. To enable global searchability, turn on this setting along with Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network. Currently, this setting is unavailable to buyers. b. Toggle Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network to enable profile data federation. This setting determines whether your profile data will be replicated to other data centers of SAP Business Network. For suppliers, this setting is enabled by default. Buyers need to enable it manually. Once enabled, this setting cannot be reversed. 5. Click Save to confirm your settings. Results • Your company profile will be replicated and visible across all data centers of SAP Business Network. • Future updates to your profile will be automatically synchronized globally. • If Show my profile in search results is enabled, your profile will also become searchable across all global regions. Company Profile Experience for Promote Suppliers with a promote subscription on SAP Business Network enjoy exclusive features that enhance their company profiles and foster trust with potential buyers: • Active Supplier Status Showcase your active platform engagement and readiness for new business opportunities. For more information, refer to Active Supplier Status [page 32]. • Verified Business Badge Confirm your company’s authenticity and legitimacy with trusted third-party partners. By becoming a verified supplier, you gain a competitive advantage over unverified businesses. For more information, refer to Business Verification [page 25]. • Marketing Collateral Promote your company by adding marketing materials such as customer presentations, case studies, and website links. For more information, refer to Marketing Collateral [page 32]. 24 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 4 of 10 -- Related Information Buying the Promote Subscription Business Verification Trust is the foundation of successful business relationships. SAP Business Network is dedicated to creating a secure and reliable platform for suppliers and buyers. To mitigate risks associated with unverified businesses, we’ve introduced the Business Verification feature, designed to foster trustworthy, long-lasting partnerships within the network. Understanding Business Verification Business verification is a crucial process that confirms the authenticity and legitimacy of a supplier company. This process is typically carried out in collaboration with reputable third-party organizations, CDQ and Dun & Bradstreet , which specialize in validating business information. The Verification Process Once you submit the verification request: 1. We first verify your business details with CDQ. If your information matches their record, your business is verified. 2. If there is no match or discrepancies are found with CDQ, we check if you have provided a DUNS number. If available, we use it to verify your business details with Dun & Bradstreet. 3. Once your business is successfully verified through either CDQ or Dun & Bradstreet, a verification badge ( ) will be added to your profile. The business details verified include: • Company Name • Primary Address (Country, State, City, Address Line 1, and Postal Code) • Tax ID or VAT ID • DUNS Number (if Dun & Bradstreet is the verifier) Benefits of Verifying Your Business • Enhanced Credibility SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 25 -- 5 of 10 -- The verification badge demonstrates to prospective buyers that you are who you say you are on the world’s largest B2B network. This can give you a competitive edge over businesses that have not undergone the verification process. • Increased Visibility Verified businesses enjoy increased visibility in search results. • Stronger Trust Verification confirms the accuracy of your business details, reducing fraud risks and building trust with potential customers. Qualifying for Business Verification To qualify for business verification, ensure the following: • You have bought the promote subscription for your SAP Business Network supplier account. • If your organization has a parent-child hierarchy, you must be part of the parent organization, as only parent organizations can initiate business verification. The verification badge is granted exclusively to the parent organization. • You have the Company Information permission to edit your company profile. Only users with this permission can start the verification process. If you don't have this permission, contact your organization’s administrator to assign it to you. Verifying Your Business Maintaining an accurate, up-to-date, and verified profile can significantly enhance your credibility with potential buyers. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you through the verification process: Prerequisites • Ensure you've bought the promote subscription for your SAP Business Network supplier account. • Ensure you're part of the parent organization if your organization has a parent-child hierarchy. • Ensure you have the Company Information permission to edit the company profile. Only users with this permission can initiate the verification process. Contact your organization’s administrator to assign the necessary permission if needed. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. This opens the Company Profile page. 26 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 6 of 10 -- 3. Click Verify your business under the Promote suggestions section at the top of the Overview page. The system will check for any missing required or recommended information. If any details are missing, a popup will guide you to add the necessary information. 4. Add required and recommended information: Required information: • Number of Employees • Year Founded • Revenue • Legal Form • Business Type Recommended information: • DUNS Number • Adding a DUNS number can increase your chances of successful verification. If your business cannot be verified through CDQ, the system will use the DUNS number for verification with Dun & Bradstreet. Without a DUNS number, Dun & Bradstreet verification will not be attempted. • If you don't know your DUNS number, click Find my DUNS number and use the Lookup DUNS Number service to search based on your company name and address. • If your existing company name and address don't match the records in the D&B database for the DUNS number you’re adding, you need to accept the updates from D&B. Upon acceptance, your company name and address will automatically update to match the D&B records and will become non-editable unless you clear your DUNS number. • In addition to the mandatory updates, you can also import other optional updates such as Website URL and Short Description from D&B to enrich your profile data. 5. Confirm your business details: • Company Name • Primary Address • DUNS Number (if available) 6. Add and confirm your tax information. If you already have a tax ID or VAT ID, double-check to confirm it's correct. Your tax information is used solely for verification and will not be publicly displayed or shared. 7. Click Verify to submit your verification request. Verification Process 1. SAP Business Network verifies your details with CDQ. 2. If CDQ cannot verify, and you’ve provided a DUNS number, verification proceeds with Dun & Bradstreet. Verification Result • Success SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 27 -- 7 of 10 -- • A blue checkmark badge ( ) is displayed against your company name on your profile. • This badge will also appear in search results and SAP applications, like Guided Sourcing. Buyers can search for trading partners by verified status. • Failure Handling Click View Verification Summary on the result page to check the failure cause. To reinitiate the verification process, follow steps in Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure [page 28]. • Notifications: • You'll receive an in-app notification regarding your verification result. Click the bell icon in the top-right corner of the SAP Business Network portal to view it. • Disclaimer SAP does not verify the accuracy of Third-Party Verification Information and is not responsible for any losses, direct or indirect, that may arise from it. Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure If your business fails third-party verification, you can reinitiate the process to ensure successful verification. The verification badge boosts your visibility in search rankings, builds trust with buyers, and helps you stand out among competitors. Procedure 1. On the verification result page, click View Verification Summary to access the summary page of your verification. • If the result page is closed, go to your Company Profile and click Verify your business under the Promote suggestions section at the top of the Overview page. This will also open the summary page of your last verification. 2. On the Verification Summary page, review the failure cause and click Edit and Resubmit to return to the business information review page. 3. On the business information review page: 1. Update your tax information. 2. Click Company Profile in the error message strip to update your company name, address, or DUNS number.  Note If you have a DUNS number, we recommend adding it to your profile. This will enable verification with Dun & Bradstreet (D&B) if verification with CDQ is unsuccessful. 4. After resolving all inconsistencies, click Verify to resubmit your verification request. 28 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 8 of 10 -- Business Verification Troubleshooting Business verification issues can occur for various reasons. Below are common scenarios and guidance to resolve them: What Should I Do Upon Verification Failure? [page 29] Why Do I Lose My Verification Badge? [page 31] What Should I Do Upon Verification Failure? Verification through third-party services may fail for various reasons. Below are common causes and the steps you can take to address them: Common Reasons for Verification Failure: • Incomplete or Incorrect Data: The data you provided is incomplete or incorrect, or the reference data has discrepancies due to outdated or incorrect official records. • Data Not Found: The provided identifier is invalid, does not match the business, or is from a country or type not yet supported by the verification service. • Network or Server Error: Temporary technical issues may prevent the verification process from completing. Actions to Take: 1. Review and correct your submitted data. Ensure that the following fields are correct: • Company Name: Make sure it matches the official name on your business registration. • Primary Address: Verify that all address fields are accurate and complete. • VAT or Tax ID: Double-check that your VAT or tax identifiers are valid and match the format required by the system. 2. Cross-check your data with official records. The official data sources that CDQ replies on include: • Business Registers: for example, Companies House (UK), Handelsregister (Germany) • VAT Databases: for example, VIES (EU VAT Information Exchange System) • Tax Authorities: for example, IRS (USA), CRA (Canada) Before resubmitting, refer to your local business register, VAT database, or tax authorities. Make sure the details on your SAP Business Network profile exactly match those found in these official sources. This can include checking any identifiers, registration numbers, or business names that are critical to the verification process. 3. Contact your local authority. If there are any errors in the official records, reach out to your local business registry or tax authority for help. 4. Submit a new verification request. Once you’ve reviewed and corrected any discrepancies, you can resubmit your verification request. Make sure that all the information is up to date and accurate to increase the chances of success. For detailed instructions on resubmitting your verification request, refer to Reverifying Your Business After Verification Failure [page 28]. 5. Escalate the issue. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 29 -- 9 of 10 -- If your verification continues to fail despite your efforts to correct the data, or if you believe the failure is due to an issue with the verification process, you can escalate the issue to SAP Support. We'll work with the verification partner to investigate and improve the service if needed. Please provide: • The submitted (correct) data (Company Name, Address, and Identifier). • Any official reference sources (for example, business registry extracts) to assist in the investigation. • A brief explanation of the issue. Synthetic Examples for Escalation Cases to CDQ Example 1 Abbreviation Not Recognized • Submitted: Name: ABC Corp, Address: 123 Main St, London, WC2N 5DU, UK. • Reference: Name: ABC Corporation, Address: 123 Main Street, London, WC2N 5DU, UK. • Issue: The abbreviation “Corp” was not recognized as equivalent to “Corporation.” • Resolution: Escalate the case to CDQ to review the fuzzy comparison logic. Example 2 Missing or Incomplete Reference Data • Submitted: Name: XYZ GmbH, VAT Number: DE123456789, Address: Musterstr. 12, 10115, Berlin, Germany. • Reference: The business is not found in the current data source. • Issue: The reference source may not have up-to-date or complete records. • Resolution: Escalate the issue with the input data for analysis and, if needed, review the reference source’s coverage. Example 3 Regional Variations • Submitted: Name: ABC Ltd, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing Street, London, UK. • Reference: Name: ABC Limited, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing St, London, UK. • Issue: The matching algorithm fails to reconcile regional address formatting differences. • Resolution: Escalate the case for review and possible algorithm refinement. Example 4 Identifier Not Recognized • Submitted: Name: Tech Innovations Inc., Identifier: US TIN 123456789. • Reference: Name: ABC Limited, Address: Flat 2, 10 Downing St, London, UK. • Issue: The system does not support U.S. Taxpayer Identification Numbers (TIN). • Resolution: Escalate the case to assess expanding identifier support. Detailed Cases of Intended Verification Failure with CDQ 1. VAT Number Issues • Reason: • Invalid VAT number format or structure (for example, missing check digits). • VAT number not found in the database. • Example: A supplier submits VAT Number ESX12345678, which does not follow the correct format for Spain (2 letters + 8 digits). 30 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 10 of 10 --
