file://SBN/TestCentral/How to use the BU.title: How to use the BUYER_TC_Scenario_Tracker Template
file://SBN/TestCentral/How to use the BU.content: How to use the BUYER_TC_Scenario_Tracker Template Key Takeaways  Always check if buyer has a file already created in CPR  Allows you to confirm what has already been loaded so you do not duplicate scenarios  No duplicating the buyer’s scenario tracker since it’s already been created  Consolidate scenarios whenever possible  Do not make test scenarios mandatory within Test Central. Test Scenarios will be made “mandatory” through enforcement of test plan.  Ensure Test Scenario Name/Description match the Test Case name/Description/Expected Result & Test Scenario Name/Description in Test Central setup  Ensure PO Modifiable Fields tab is accurate when Doc Characteristics are selected during Test Scenario creation  Add notes in Notes field to advise which are modifiable in which scenario  Ensure PO Modifiable Fields are present in the cXML payload or the Test Scenario will not work correctly 1. Access the Test Central section of the TPS Warehouse: Test Central a. Click on Internal Guides and Documents -> Functional Documents -> TC Set Up Tracking folder b. Open BUYER_TC_Scenario_Tracker_template and SAVE A COPY i. If you do not save a copy, changes will be made to the original document -- 1 of 4 -- • You need somewhere on your computer to save files for Test Central however that makes the most sense for you • Replace BUYER with the buyer’s name and remove template so it says as *Buyers Name*_TC_Scenario_Tracker 2. Populate the buyer’s scenario tracker according to the instrcutions below for each tab Tabs 1. Instructions and Examples: an example of how to use the Test Scenarios tab -- 2 of 4 -- 2. Test Scenarios tab: Populate this tab with the sample PO data you are putting into Test Central for your Buyer. Template Columns  Test Scenario Name – Descriptive Name of Test Scenario, this appears in Test Central. You must follow this format: [BUYER] [REGION] [PO TYPE]  Sample Document - Transaction order for scenario with samples to reference (included on PO's Loaded to TC Tab)  Description – Description of Purchase Order, this appears in Test Central  Notes – Notes for Admin  Active – TRUE for active scenarios [TRUE]  Mandatory – Indicate if scenario is required by the system [FALSE] 3.PO – Modifiable Fields tab: Fields that are editable on a Test Scenario for the supplier when creating test POs in Test Central Template Columns  Field Name – Name of field/cXML tag  Level – Indicate if field is header or detail (line)  Notes – Instructions on who and how the field may be modified -- 3 of 4 -- 4.POs Loaded to TC: Sample cXML payloads that have been edited and used in corresponding test cases • Template Columns  The number of columns will vary depending on the scenarios and samples provided  Each column will contain the first row with a heading that ties back to the Test Scenarios tab  Key Takeaways  Update samples with variables prior to pasting in template  Update column names with corresponding Test Scenario Names & Test Scenario #  Ensure you delete all cXML samples and replace them with your buyer’s corresponding cXML payloads -- 4 of 4 --

file://SBN/TestCentral/Internal Test Cen.title: Internal Test Central Instructions
file://SBN/TestCentral/Internal Test Cen.content: INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Managed Gateway for Spend & Network- Test Central Setting up Test Central and adding buyer specific scenarios for Test Central SAP June, 2025 -- 1 of 57 -- 2 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Agenda • Overall Process, Roles and Responsibility for setting up Test Central • Standard Buyer-Initiated Project utilizing Test Central • Supplier-Initiated Project utilizing Test Central • Determine if the Buyer has Test Central enabled and if Test Scenarios have been previously configured • Setting up Buyer and Supplier Accounts to utilize Test Central with your Admin Access • Determining Relevant PO Types via Buyer Integration Kit for Accurate cXML Configuration in Test Central • Exporting, Editing and Saving cXML for POs to use for Test Central Scenarios • Demo of editing cXML • BUYER_TC_Scenario_Tracker_Template & PO samples • Tracking Scenarios with JIRA and CPR • Accessing Admin Area in Managed Gateway for Spend&Network • Creating Test Cases • Creating Test Scenarios • Confirming Set up was successful • Troubleshooting -- 2 of 57 -- 3 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Roles and Responsibilities Involved in the Test Central Set Up Process Task IS Buyer Supplier Discuss Test Central Process and Caveat R/A C I Agreement to use Test Central C R/A I Enable Managed Gateway in Production and Test Manage Profile >> Managed Gateway >> Enable Managed Gateway A/C R I Create Test Plan with Buyer based on type of POs in scope C R/A I Work with Buyer to create/select specific PO examples for each PO type to be used in Test Central R A I Prep the Purchase Orders for Test Central R/A I I Load the Purchase Orders in Test Central R/A I I Submit JIRA ticket for tracking Test Central Setup R/A I I Confirm Test Central Ready for Supplier Use R/A I C R = Responsible -The person or people who actually do the work to complete the task. They are responsible for action/implementation. Responsibility can be shared. A = Accountable (or Approver) -The one ultimately answerable for the correct and thorough completion of the task. Whoever is Accountable must sign off or approve work that Responsible provides. There must be exactly one Accountable person per task. C = Consulted-Those whose opinions are sought before a decision or action is taken. Typically, they are subject-matter experts, and there is two-way communication. I = Informed -Those who are kept up to date on progress or decisions. They receive information but are not necessarily consulted or responsible for the work. Communication is usually one-way. -- 3 of 57 -- Standard Buyer-Initiated Project utilizing Test Central Following today’s current process, majority of assigned projects are initiated by the buyer. Not much changes aside from advising the use of TC for majority of testing, and set up on the backend for TC if needed -- 4 of 57 -- 5 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Pre-Kickoff Activities •Project assigned to IS via Atlas. •Along with your normal pre-work activities, confirm if the Buyer is enabled for Test Central. •Check system settings, Check Test Central and/or the Buyer’s CPR folder for the Buyer_TC_Scenario_Tracker to view any existing Test Scenarios previously created by another IS. Initial Kickoff Call •IS schedules a kickoff call with Buyer and Supplier to review blueprints/ guidelines as usual •Communicate that Test Central will be used for testing—it is not optional. •If Buyer pushes back, notify Shannon and consider a separate call with the Buyer to present the Value Prop Slide Deck. Follow-Up Call: Test Plan Alignment •Include Buyer and Supplier to align on: •Connectivity setup (if applicable) •Test Plan and Test Central •Focus discussion on: o Identify which production Purchase Orders can be leveraged by the IS to configure Test Central o Confirm Test Plan and that all tests outlined in the Test Plan can be supported using these selected POs Configuration & Setup •Once Transaction Numbers for Test Case Payloads are confirmed, follow the Engineering PowerPoint to: •Set up Test Central •Create test cases and scenarios •Save and upload the Buyer TC Scenario Tracker to their CPR folder and attach to the JIRA ticket for tracking (engineering slide deck) Testing Preparation & Execution •Continue with project as normal until testing phase. •Before testing begins: •Review Test Central with Supplier (if not already done) to ensure they are prepared to complete testing independently. •Share the Supplier-Facing Test Central Instruction Guide when appropriate •It’s recommended to introduce the guide in a dedicated call ahead of testing. Alternatively, share the guide and offer to sch edule a follow-up call for questions and clarification, depending on the IS’s preference Final Testing & Go-Live •After Supplier completes testing in Test Central, reengage Buyer to send at least on end -to-end test. •Proceed to Production deployment as usual. •Project complete! Buyer Initiated Project - Sequence of Events -- 5 of 57 -- Supplier-Initiated Project utilizing Test Central -- 6 of 57 -- 7 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Project Kickoff • Project is assigned to the IS • IS initiates a call with the supplier to discuss project, introduce Test Central, discuss connection setup, and share relevant buyer documentation • IS confirms the PO types currently in Prod between both (if any are there) and begins to develop the Buyer’s TC Scenarios Tracker and export cXML from the Production POs to configure Test Central according to Buyer documentation • Work with supplier to configure Managed Gateway and Connection (if needed) Buyer Engagement • IS should involve Buyer before Supplier’s Testing begins to confirm all necessary PO Types are set up in Test Central • i.e. There is SAP Rush PO and B&I PO (according to buyer documentation) in Production, you want to confirm with Buyer if ther e are any other PO types they will be sending to supplier, change orders, cancel orders, etc. • Review and confirm Buyer’s Test plan with both parties if there is one in the buyer’s CPR folder • If not, use a generic test plan • Advise buyer they will be needed for end-to-end testing once TC Testing is complete Testing Execution • Check if the Buyer is enabled for Test Central by checking system settings and/or the Buyer’s CPR folder for the Buyer_TC_Scenario_Tracker to view any existing Test Scenarios previously created by another IS. • If the Buyer is not set up for TC, follow along with the Engineering Slide Deck to set up Test Central • IS finalizes Test Central setup and gives the go-ahead for supplier testing. • Supplier utilizes Test Central to send Test POs per the test plan • IS assists supplier with testing/troubleshooting if needed • IS does NOT send test POs for supplier – they need to do this on their own Final Validation • Upon supplier confirmation of testing completion, IS reconnects with Buyer to execute at least one end-to-end test from their system (exact details at Buyer/Supplier discretion). • Once Buyer and Supplier validate successful testing, IS assists with Production deployment as needed. Supplier Initiated Project - Sequence of Events -- 7 of 57 -- 8 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only • Current PO (types) in Prod between buyer and supplier (if any) • If not – what PO types are going to be used • If there are no POs currently in Prod, then the Buyer will need to send at least 1 PO for each PO type in Test • Confirm what documents supplier should be sending back • These are not in any way related in Test Central and there is no set up in Test Central needed • These documents will flow through the connection supplier has set up as normal testing without TC • Review Buyer’s Test Plan with buyer and supplier and confirm what PO types/scenarios should be included. • Adjust as needed and provide copy to both parties as you normally do • Advise Buyer they will need to send at least 1 PO from their test system to ensure success in end-to-end process • Timeline/Go Live Date • Discussion should be similar to what you currently have around timeline/go live date • Confirm any hard go live dates with Buyer • Ideally, TC Testing should cut testing in half (6 weeks down to 3 weeks) – Of course this Depends on how many Test scenarios in scope, supplier’s availability to complete testing on their own , any is sues etc. Supplier Initiated - Discussion with Buyer and Supplier regarding PO Samples for TC -- 8 of 57 -- 9 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Hi Buyer Team, I’ve been assigned as the SAP Integration Resource to support your supplier, [Supplier Name] (Supplier ANID), to facilitate [Supplier Name]’s migration from manual invoice handling to automated electronic invoice. This initiative stems from a recent supplier consultation, and we're leveraging the Managed Gateway for Spend and Network’s Test Central feature to conduct testing—allowing us to proceed without requiring a direct Target resource to generate Purchase Orders. To ensure comprehensive test coverage, it would be extremely valuable to have someone from [Buyer Name] confirm which Purchase Orders [Supplier Name] should use during testing. This will help us account for all relevant scenarios and reduce any gaps in validation. Would someone from your team be available to join a brief call with me and [Supplier Name]’s technical resource to align on this? Below is my availability for next week: Thanks, Your Name Supplier initiated project - Email Templates for reaching out to Buyer for TC Discussion -- 9 of 57 -- Determine if the Buyer has Test Central enabled and if Test Scenarios have been previously configured Do not miss this step!!! -- 10 of 57 -- 11 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only • As time goes this will naturally be built up from those adding their scenarios and eventually no new test scenarios will need to be added to TC by an IS. • We do not want multiple scenarios of the same PO type which is why it is very important to check what is already there before adding any new Test Scenarios in TC • Confirm PO Types that have already been loaded for the Buyer • Check Buyer’s CPR folder – There should be a Buyer_TC_Scenario_Tracker with the Buyer’s Name in their CPR folder • Check Test Central for previously configured POs – Check on the Admin side by searching in Test Scenarios for the Buyer’s name – If the buyer and supplier have an established trading relationship and supplier has managed Gateway enabled, you can go to their Test Central, click on the Buyer’s Name and OrderRequest in Document Type to confirm what is already added Confirm PO Scenarios have already been loaded for Buyer in TC -- 11 of 57 -- Setting up Buyer and Supplier Accounts to utilize Test Central with your Admin Access If Managed Gateway/Test Central is not configured for the Buyer & Supplier, you’ll need to follow these steps -- 12 of 57 -- 13 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Once Buyer confirms the use of Test Central, make sure they Enable Managed Gateway for Spend & Network in buyer’s Test account. This does not mean that Buyer must use Managed Gateway, it is just confirmation that Buyer allows Suppliers to use Test Central for testing purposes. The buyer can turn this on by logging into their SAP Business Network Test account, going to the Settings menu, clicking on Manage Profile, SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Setup and enabling Managed Gateway for Spend & Network. If this is already enabled, you can go straight to Managed Gateway Admin and check “TC Send to AN” (slide 16). If Managed Gateway is not already enabled, you need to follow the above steps to have Buyer enabled Managed Gateway in their Test Account. Instruct Buyer to Enable Managed Gateway in their SAP Business Network -- 13 of 57 -- 14 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Supplier will need to enable Managed Gateway in both Test and Production prior to utilizing Test Central. G o to the Settings menu on the top right. Select Electronic Order Routing -> Configure SAP Integration, Managed Gateway -> check the box to Enable Managed Gateway for Spend&Network and click Save. They need to repeat the same process in their Production Account Instruct Supplier to Enable Managed Gateway in their SAP Business Network -- 14 of 57 -- 15 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Prior to the supplier utilizing Test Central to send Purchase Orders, they will need to confirm their Electronic Order Routing for POs is set up according to how they’d like to receive POs. Using Test Central to send Test POs does not necessarily mean they have to receive the POs via the Managed Gateway. They can elect to receive POs via Online, Email or cXML set in the Business Network. Test Central will check the supplier’s Electronic Order Routing settings and send the PO to them however they have set. Instruct Supplier to change Order Routing if needed -- 15 of 57 -- 16 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only • Be sure to enable the "TC Send transactions to AN" option located under Trading Partner Properties in Managed Gateway Admin. • This critical step ensures that Purchase Orders sent from Test Central are properly routed through the buyer’s SAP Business Network account. • if you do not have this access, reach out to Shannon or Sumedha • Outbound document flow if “TC Send to AN” is enabled: – Managed Gateway Test Central -> Buyer’s SAP Business Network Account -> Supplier’s SAP Business Network Account (to check routing method) -> Managed Gateway Transaction Tracker -> Supplier • Outbound document flow if “TC Send to AN” is not enabled: – Managed Gateway Test Central -> Managed Gateway Transaction Tracker -> Supplier via project/connection set up in Managed Gateway Enable Buyer’s TC POs to flow through their SAP Business Network -- 16 of 57 -- Determining Relevant PO Types via Buyer Integration Kit for Accurate cXML Configuration in Test Central -- 17 of 57 -- 18 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Check Production to confirm there are current POs flowing between buyer and supplier Log into the supplier’s production account to check any POs between the supplier and buyer for the last year -- 18 of 57 -- 19 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only You’ll want to simultaneously be looking at the buyer’s Transaction Guidelines/Integration Blueprints and their EDI/cXML Deltas/Transaction Samples to see what types of Purchase Orders they could potentially send to suppliers. Knowing this information will help you to know exactly what you’re looking for when searching in the SAP Business Network. For this example, My Buyer is Target. I checked the project record in Atlas to confirm the CPR link. I checked Target’s CPR to find their Integration Blueprint and Transaction Samples for EDI since my supplier is using EDI. 1. I see that their transaction sample tabs showing B&I PO, SAP Rush PO, and SAP Direct PO so I am going to want to be aware of that when checking the business network for POs between the two. -- 19 of 57 -- 20 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only I logged into Admin and went to the Supplier’s Production Account 2. I clicked ‘Show More’ of the filter to be able to filter on additional values. • Enter the Buyer you are working with in Customers • Change Creation date to at least the last 365 days • Click Apply and view results -- 20 of 57 -- 21 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only I sorted on the Order Number and changed the Items shown to 100 to be able to see more POs. I went through the pages until I saw a change in the PO # format based on the transaction samples i.e. 700 vs 97 • I saw noted in the blueprint that their B&I POs start with 7 • I checked the other types of POs and it seems the SAP Rush POs start with the 97 • Therefore, I am going to start off with these two types of POs for Target and my supplier • **You can also export the search results to an excel file if it’s easier for you to review that way -- 21 of 57 -- Exporting, Editing and Saving cXML for POs to use for Test Central Scenarios -- 22 of 57 -- 23 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only 1. Export the cXML for each type of PO we need -- 23 of 57 -- 24 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only 2. Save it as an .xml file with the Name format: [BUYER] [REGION] [PO TYPE] PO so you can edit it in a cXML editor such as Notepad++, or Oxygen • Notepad works as well, but it’s easier to confirm you’re Creating Test Cases in Test Case Repository -- 42 of 57 -- 43 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Once you have entered the Details on the Purchase Order, ensure you check Active then click on the pencil next to Payload to add the scrubbed cXML. It is VERY important to confirm: • Document has Generic header • From ID, To ID, Sender ID, PrivateID, SystemID,VendorID, etc. should be removed from the header and replaced with #SENDERID#, #FROMID#, etc. • Remove any supplier identifying information • Supplier Name, Supplier Identifying Product Information, supplier specific locations, etc. • Remove any document Numbers and replace with #DOCUMENTID# • such as OrderID,MasterAgreement, etc. • Dates should be changed because these will be autogenerated by Test Central • Order ID and Order Date – Example: OrderRequestHeader orderDate="#DATETIME#" orderID="#DOCUMENTID#“ • For Service PO, if there is a Service End Date in the cXML of PO, please change that to 10 years after today's date so that Service PO does not expire. – Example: <Period startDate="2021-02-01T00:00:00- 00:00"endDate="2031-02-28T00:00:00-00:00"/> Click Save! file://SBN/TestCentral/Quick Guide for T.content: Quick Guide for Troubleshooting Test Scenarios not appearing in a supplier’s Test Central If a buyer‘s Test Scenarios aren’t displaying in the supplier’s Test Central, return to the Admin Area and verify the following: • Your Test Cases and/or Test Scenarios are marked as Active • Each Test Scenario is associated with the correct Buyer • ANID is the most accurate way to confirm the Buyer is correct • The Test Case/Scenario has been deployed to the Data Center corresponding to your supplier's location If all those are correct and you are still not seeing the Test Scenarios in supplier’s Test Central, act as supplier in Managed Gateway/Test Central: • Ensure a project is created in Managed Gateway • If a project exists, but it is set to All – recreate a project with the same connection and set customer to the specific buyer • Ensure you’re selecting OrderRequest, ChangeOrderRequest, CancelOrderRequest in Document Type when creating a Test Script If you’re still unable to see the buyer’s Test Scenarios in the supplier’s Test Central, reach out to an SME NAMER/LAC: • Jessica Roth – jessica.roth@sap.com • Sumedha Gupta – sumedha.gupta@sap.com APAC/EMEA: • Dean Worth – dean.worth@sap.com -- 1 of 1 --

file://SBN/TestCentral/Supplier How To U.content: INTERNAL – SAP and Partners Only Step-by-Step Guide for Integration Testing with Test Central SAP June, 2025 -- 1 of 23 -- 2 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only • Managed Gateway for Spend&Network Data Flow • Electronic Order Routing in the SAP Business Network • Configure Managed Gateway for Spend&Network • Creating a New Project and/or Connection to be used for Test Central • Creating a Test Script with one or more Test Scenarios for a particular Buyer • Test Central Dashboard and statuses • Troubleshooting a failed Test Central Purchase Order • Test Central Purchase Order in the SAP Business Network • Summary Agenda -- 2 of 23 -- 3 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only The Managed Gateway for Spend & Network Data Flow Managed Gateway for Spend & Network is a self-service platform that empowers suppliers to seamlessly configure and integrate with the SAP Business Network. It enables efficient transaction processing with buyers while providing enhanced visibility and control over connectivity and data exchange. Positioned between the supplier’s ERP system and their SAP Business Network account, the Managed Gateway offers advanced tool s and functionality beyond the standard legacy integration available within SAP BN. It delivers a more transparent view of integrat ion status and transactional flows Below is a general overview of the system architecture, although specific configurations may vary based on each buyer –supplier relationship. With Managed Gateway for Spend & Network, you can: - Streamline integration between your ERP system and the SAP Business Network, enabling seamless management of one or multiple buyer relationships. - Validate and test transaction documents independently against buyer transaction rules and validations to ensure accuracy befo re transmitting. - Track and monitor the entire integration lifecycle, providing real-time visibility into document flow and connection status -- 3 of 23 -- 4 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Configure your Managed Gateway For Spend & Network account Log into your SAP Business Network Test account, and go to the Settings menu on the top right. Select Electronic Order Routing -> Configure SAP Integration, Managed Gateway -> check the box to Enable Managed Gateway for Spend&Network and click Save. You’ll need to repeat the same process in your Production Account. You can now log in to the Managed Gateway by clicking on the Log in to Managed Gateway for Spend&Network link shown here. -- 4 of 23 -- 5 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Change Document Routing in SAP Business Network to Managed Gateway Navigate to Electronic Order Routing from the Settings menu and verify that Document Routing is configured to use Managed Gateway for Spend and Network.* This setting can be applied at the default level, impacting all buyer relationships, or at the buyer level, allowing configuration for individual buyer connections. -- 5 of 23 -- 6 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Create your project in Managed Gateway For Spend & Network Select "Create a New Integration Project“ and enter a Project Name and select which customer you’re integrating with. -- 6 of 23 -- 7 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Choose an existing connection or add a new connection Choose an existing connection by selecting the down arrow to the left of the connection Name in the Reusable Connections section and click Save or click Add New Connection on the right to set up a new connection. -- 7 of 23 -- 8 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Choose an existing connection or add a new connection If you choose to Add New Connection, you’ll be prompted to enter your connection details. -- 8 of 23 -- 9 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Configure Document Mapping The Mapping step shows what documents are mapped, the format/version of the document, and in which direction the documents are set up. Things to consider: • Send direction is From the Supplier to the Buyer • Receive direction is From the Buyer to the Supplier • Be sure to add 824 and 997 to receive status updates • cXML connections do not require document mapping and will skip this section -- 9 of 23 -- 10 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Confirm you are ready to use Test Central Once your project status is updated to ‘In Testing’, go to Test Central to start submitting test Purchase Orders on behalf of your buyer. -- 10 of 23 -- 11 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Creating a Test Script First, you will need to give your Test Script a name and a description. This is up to the supplier’s discretion as they’re the one creating the Test Scripts. Next, select the Customer you’d like to test with and the OrderRequest from the Document Type list and click Apply, then Add. You will get a pop up with a list of possible scenarios to choose from. (screenshot on next slide) -- 11 of 23 -- 12 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Select Test Scenario to add to Test Script Below is a screenshot of the popup with Optional Test Scenarios. Please make sure you do not test with StandardOrderRequest. This Document Type is not specific to a buyer and will therefore not have buyer specific information. Select the test scenario that includes the Name of the Buyer that you are testing with. -- 12 of 23 -- 13 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Test Scripts with multiple Purchase Order Scenarios You can include multiple Purchase Order types within a single Test Script. This allows all associated documents to be submitted simultaneously and treated as part of one unified test. For the Script to be marked as Completed, each scenario within the Test Script must successfully run to completion. To modify a specific scenario, simply click the pencil icon to edit its details -- 13 of 23 -- 14 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Modifying Line Items on a Test Central Purchase Order Once you click into the specific test scenario, you can edit each line item and/or Add more lines to the Test Purchase Order. Select Close and your line items will be saved. For address-related fields, simply enter the relevant Address ID to display on the PO. The full address does not need to be manually entered. Best Practice Tip: To ensure a meaningful and successful integration test, it's important for suppliers to update the buyer’s test Purchase Order with their actual product data, including item names, SKUs, pricing, and quantities. Here's why: •Realistic Simulation: Updating the PO reflects the actual products and formats used in production, allowing us to closely mimic live transaction behavior. •Accurate Validation: It helps confirm that product data flows correctly between systems— ensuring everything from unit of measure to tax and pricing logic is configured as expected. •Fewer Surprises: Testing • with real data helps identify potential mapping or formatting issues before go-live, reducing the risk of failed transactions later. •Streamlined Onboarding: If the test is successful, transitioning to production will be smoother and faster, with fewer adjustments needed. -- 14 of 23 -- 15 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Complete and Send your Test PO via the Test Script Click Save to send your Test Purchase Orders listed in the Test Scenarios -- 15 of 23 -- 16 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Test Central Dashboard The Test Central Dashboard will show you the list of Test Scripts you have submitted and their Status. The status can either be Completed, In Progress, or Failed. Click on Select to Edit, see Results, or Delete a script. -- 16 of 23 -- 17 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only In Progress Test Script In Progress – Pass/Fail Yellow Clock, In Progress, 0% • Test ID will be generated and shown here once the Purchase Order is sent. -- 17 of 23 -- 18 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Failed - Pass/Fail red X, overall testing 0% Failed Test Script and Troubleshooting -- 18 of 23 -- 19 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only If your test POs fail, you can go to the Transaction Tracker to view more details and resolve the error. Failed Test Script and Troubleshooting -- 19 of 23 -- 20 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Completed Test Script Completed – Pass/Fail green check, overall testing 100% -- 20 of 23 -- 21 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Example of TC PO Showing in SAP Business Network Some of the benefits of utilizing Test Central is that the Purchase Order flows into the Supplier and Buyer’s SAP Business Ne twork accounts. Below is a screenshot of a supplier’s SAP Business Network Test Account with Purchase Orders generated in Test Central. Purch ase Orders generated in Test Central will always start with “TC_”. -- 21 of 23 -- 22 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Summary – Wrap Up Congratulations— a Test Purchase Order has been successfully submitted on the buyer’s behalf! Confirm your test scenarios in the system against the test plan developed with the Buyer to ensure all required scenarios are complete. You can now repeat these steps with any buyer who uses Test Central for integration testing. Best Practice Tip For a thorough end-to- end validation, have the buyer send at least one Purchase Order directly from their Test system before moving to Production. This helps confirm real- world readiness and system compatibility. -- 22 of 23 -- 23 INTERNAL – SAP and P artners Only Thank you. -- 23 of 23 --

file://SBN/TestCentral/Supplier Objectio.title: Supplier Objections and Responses
file://SBN/TestCentral/Supplier Objectio.content: Common Supplier Objections and Responses Key Message to Reinforce with Suppliers Test Central gives suppliers more control, not more responsibility. It removes delays, reduces rework, and lets you test thoroughly—without risking buyer systems or production data. Objection: This sounds like extra work for our technical team. Response: In practice, it’s less work. Test Central provides ready-made PO templates and automated validation feedback, so your team spends less time troubleshooting and re-submitting documents. You also avoid repeated coordination with buyers just to get test POs issued. Objection: What if we do something wrong and it impacts the buyer? Response: That risk is removed by design. Test Central validates documents automatically and provides immediate feedback before anything reaches production. SAP resources remain involved throughout testing, and nothing you send through Test Central affects live transactions or buyer systems. Objection: We’ve successfully onboarded without Test Central before. Why do we have to use it now? Response: That’s true—and Test Central builds on that success. It removes bottlenecks like waiting for buyer availability and manual PO creation. The goal isn’t to change what works, but to make testing faster, more predictable, and less dependent on external coordination. Objection: We don’t have time to learn a new tool Response: Test Central is designed to be lightweight. Suppliers use it only to generate test POs; the interface is simple, and SAP provides clear instructions and support. Most suppliers become productive quickly, and the time saved during testing far outweighs the short learning curve. Objection: What if Test Central doesn’t reflect real buyer POs? Response: All Test Central scenarios are built using actual buyer PO samples provided by the buyer. These are scrubbed only to remove sensitive or supplier-specific data. Structurally and functionally, the POs you test with mirror real production documents. You also are able to add/remove/edit line items specific to your actual product data to ensure real life test scenarios. -- 1 of 2 -- Objection: We prefer buyers to control testing. Response: Buyers still control the scope and final validation. Test Central simply lets you handle the early and middle stages independently. Buyers still perform end-to-end testing from their ERP before go-live, ensuring nothing changes from a governance perspective. Objection: What if our team needs help during testing? Response: You’re not on your own. SAP Integration Resources remain engaged throughout testing and troubleshooting. In addition, Test Central’s automated validations help you identify issues immediately, often without needing buyer or SAP intervention. We also have a guide for sending test POs with Test Central and troubleshooting if needed. Objection: Does this mean we must use Managed Gateway for everything? Response: No. Managed Gateway must be enabled and you must create a connection for at least one document to flow through to allow Test Central usage, but you can still receive POs via your preferred routing method—cXML, email, or online—based on your SAP Business Network configuration. Test Central reads what routing you have configured for the particular buyer and sends documents via that route. Objection: Will this slow down our go-live? Response: Actually, it usually accelerates it. Because you can complete most testing independently, overall timelines are shorter. Many projects see testing duration reduced significantly because dependencies on buyer availability are minimized. Objection: I don’t see how this benefits us since it’s giving us more work. What’s in it for us as a supplier? Response: • Faster testing cycles • Fewer rejections late in testing • Clear validation feedback • Less back-and-forth with buyers • Greater confidence before go-live Ultimately, Test Central helps you get to production faster with fewer surprises. -- 2 of 2 --

file://SBN/TestCentral/Supplier TC Cheat.title: Supplier TC Cheat Sheet
file://SBN/TestCentral/Supplier TC Cheat.content: Supplier Cheat Sheet: Testing With Test Central A quick guide for suppliers connecting to SAP Business Network via SAP Managed Gateway What Is Test Central? A safe test-only environment where you can send test POs on behalf of the buyer and send back your documents (OC/ASN/INV/Credit Memos) to make sure everything works before real testing begins. Why We’re Using Test Central 1. Make sure everything works before involving the buyer • Confirm you can receive the buyer’s PO through your Managed Gateway connection • Check your documents are well-formed, valid, and meet cXML/EDI standards • Verify your documents pass the buyer’s transaction rules in the SAP Business Network 2. Fix issues faster • You can send as many test POs as needed until everything passes—no waiting on the buyer 3. Faster onboarding, fewer escalations • You test on your own schedule, which speeds up the entire project What Does Change? • The only thing really changing for you is that you will be completing a portion of the testing by generating POs on behalf on the buyer without having to wait for them to send from their system What Does NOT Change? • SAP still runs the kickoff call and reviews all requirements • SAP can demo how to use Test Central • SAP supports you through testing, troubleshooting, and getting to go‑live • The buyer will send at least 1 test from their systems to confirm end-to-end testing is successful -- 1 of 3 -- What You Need To Do Follow this simple 5-step workflow for each Test Scenario: 1. Generate and send the Test PO in Test Central The Test PO will flow to you as it is defined in the Default Order Routing or if the buyer has a Custom Order Routing • You can edit line items of the different Test POs generated in Test Central 2. Process the PO in your system Receive and process the PO into your system exactly as you would if the buyer was sending the test PO • Confirm your connection can receive buyer POs through Managed Gateway • Check that all fields map correctly 3. Send back the required documents Respond to the Test PO with the documents that were confirmed during the kickoff call, such as: • Order Confirmation (OC) • Advance Ship Notice (ASN) • Invoice • Credit Memo These documents help verify that your transactions are: • Well-formed and valid (cXML/EDI) • Aligned with the buyer’s business rules in the SAP Business Network 4. Track progress for each Test Scenario Use the agreed-upon Test Plan to track which documents you have submitted. This makes it easy for SAP and the buyer to review results and identify anything that needs adjustment. -- 2 of 3 -- 5. Repeat if needed — this is normal If a document doesn’t pass validation the first time, don’t worry. Test Central is designed for multiple test cycles, so you can correct issues and resend until everything passes. If anything is unclear at any step, please ask — SAP is here to support you through testing and help you reach a successful go-live. -- 3 of 3 --

file://SBN/TestCentral/Supplier Test Cen.title: Supplier Test Central FAQ
file://SBN/TestCentral/Supplier Test Cen.content: Supplier Test Central FAQ 1. What if we already tested our connection with another customer? Each buyer sends different requirements based on their business practices. Testing with buyer specific scenarios in Test Central ensures your integration works for this specific buyer. 2. What is Test Central? A safe, test‑only environment in the SAP Business Network where you can receive test POs and send back your documents (OC, ASN, Invoice, Credit Memo) to confirm everything works before involving the buyer, helping shorten the overall testing timeline. 3. Why am I sending POs on behalf of the buyer? This lets you test faster. You don’t need to wait for the buyer to generate POs — you can create and send as many test POs as needed on your own schedule. 4. Will Test Central affect my production setup? No. Everything you do in Test Central stays in the test environment. 5. What documents do I need to send? Your SAP Integration Resource will confirm the documents in scope during the kickoff (e.g., OC, ASN, Invoice, Credit Memo). 6. Are Test Central POs real? They look and behave like real POs but are non‑ERP, test‑only documents and do not post to the buyer’s ERP. 7. How do I know if my documents passed validation? Test Central provides automated status updates. Your documents must be: • Well-formed (technically correct) • Valid against cXML/EDI standards • Aligned with the buyer’s SAP Business Network transaction rules If anything fails, Test Central provides an error message so you can correct and resend -- 1 of 3 -- 8. What if my documents fail? This is normal and would happen if the buyer was sending the test POs as well. Fix the issue in your system and send another test PO or test document. Test Central allows unlimited retries with no down time since you’re the one sending the Test PO. 9. How many test cycles can I complete? As many as necessary. You can create multiple Test POs to adjust mapping, routing, or formatting on your documents. 10. Do I need Managed Gateway enabled to use Test Central? Yes. You must have a connection in the Managed Gateway to use Test Central. 11. How do I know which scenarios to test? Your SAP Integration Resource will review and confirm the Test Plan with you and the buyer, outlining all required scenarios and documents. You can mark progress directly in the plan. 12. Do I still need to do end-to-end testing after Test Central? Yes — but only at the very end. After testing with Test Central is complete, the buyer sends at least one PO from their ERP to confirm your documents are accepted by their ERP. 13. How long does Test Central testing take? It depends on your availability and how quickly you address errors, but most suppliers complete the majority of testing in about two weeks or less, since they can test independently. 14. Do I need to change my mapping for Test Central? No special mapping is needed for Test Central. The POs you test with come directly from the buyer’s real Production samples, so they match what you’ll receive in both Test and Production when the buyer sends a PO themselves. -- 2 of 3 -- You may make small fixes if validations fail, but the mapping you build in Test Central is the same mapping used for end-to-end testing and Production. Nothing is temporary — you are building your final live integration. 15. What if I use EDI instead of cXML? Test Central supports both. 16. Who supports me during Test Central testing? Your SAP Integration Resource will: • Demo how Test Central works • Guide you through setup • Help troubleshoot errors • Support you through all test cycles • Confirm you're ready for end-to-end testing and go-live You are not testing alone. 17. What happens after I finish Test Central testing? The buyer sends at least one PO from their ERP to verify your documents flow correctly and pass their ERP validations. After this confirmation, the process continues exactly as it always has: • Move the connection to Production (if applicable) • Update your Order Routing settings in your SAP Business Network Production account • Make any necessary updates in your internal systems • Proceed to go-live on the agreed-upon date 18. What if I still have questions? Just ask your SAP Integration Resource. We’re here to support you, clarify expectations, and make the testing process as smooth and quick as possible. -- 3 of 3 --

file://SBN/TestCentral/Talking points fo.url: file://SBN/TestCentral/Talking points for Introducing Test Central.pdf
file://SBN/TestCentral/Talking points fo.title: Talking points for Introducing Test Central
file://SBN/TestCentral/Talking points fo.content: Talking points for Introducing Test Central in a project • Test Central is now our standard approach to testing during Integration Projects • Testing tool in the Managed Gateway for Spend & Network that allows suppliers to generate purchase orders on behalf of the buyer • Reduces buyer workload while allowing suppliers to complete most testing smoothly and efficiently. • Supports a more predictable and repeatable testing process, reducing delays caused by buyer system availability, approvals, or competing priorities. • Configured on the backend as a one-time setup per buyer per PO type, allowing the same Test PO scenarios to be reused for every future supplier integration. • Suppliers use these POs to test their documents (OC/ASN/INV) to check their documents are: – Well formed and valid according to industry – Align with a buyer’s SAP BN business transaction rules • Supports all Test Scenarios, enabling ~80% of testing without buyer involvement • SAP resources remain engaged for oversight, troubleshooting, and progress support. • Provides immediate feedback through automated validations and assertions, helping suppliers quickly correct errors without repeated back-and-forth with buyers or SAP resources. • Buyer only needs to enable Managed Gateway (if not already enabled) and provide PO examples for each PO Type that needs set up in Test Central (if not already set up) and for at least one end to end test after supplier completes testing with Test Central -- 1 of 1 --

file://SBN/TestCentral/Test Central - Ho.url: file://SBN/TestCentral/Test Central - How to Guide for Suppliers.pdf
file://SBN/TestCentral/Test Central - Ho.title: Test Central - How to Guide for Suppliers
file://SBN/TestCentral/Test Central - Ho.content: Step-by-Step Integration Guide for Using Test Central - Suppliers September 2025 -- 1 of 23 -- • Managed Gateway for Spend&Network Data Flow • Electronic Order Routing in the SAP Business Network • Configure Managed Gateway for Spend&Network • Creating a New Project and/or Connection to be used for Test Central • Creating a Test Script with one or more Test Scenarios for a particular Buyer • Test Central Dashboard and statuses • Troubleshooting a failed Test Central Purchase Order • Test Central Purchase Order in the SAP Business Network • Summary Agenda -- 2 of 23 -- The Managed Gateway for Spend & Network Data Flow • Managed Gateway for Spend & Network is a self-service platform that empowers suppliers to seamlessly configure and integrate with the SAP Business Network. It enables efficient transaction processing with buyers while providing enhanced visibility and control over connectivity and data exchange. • Positioned between the supplier’s ERP system and their SAP Business Network account, the Managed Gateway offers advanced tools and functionality beyond the standard legacy integration available within SAP BN. It delivers a more transparent view of integration status and transactional flows • Below is a general overview of the system architecture, although specific configurations may vary based on each buyer–supplier relationship. With Managed Gateway for Spend & Network, you can: - Streamline integration between your ERP system and the SAP Business Network, enabling seamless management of one or multiple buyer relationships. - Validate and test transaction documents independently against buyer transaction rules and validations to ensure accuracy before transmitting. - Track and monitor the entire integration lifecycle, providing real-time visibility into document flow and connection status -- 3 of 23 -- Configure your Managed Gateway For Spend & Network account • Log into your SAP Business Network Test account, and go to the Settings menu on the top right. Select Electronic Order Routing -> Configure SAP Integration, Managed Gateway -> check the box to Enable Managed Gateway for Spend&Network and click Save. You’ll need to repeat the same process in your Production Account. You can now log in to the Managed Gateway by clicking on the Log in to Managed Gateway for Spend&Network link shown here. -- 4 of 23 -- Change Document Routing in SAP Business Network to Managed Gateway • Navigate to Electronic Order Routing from the Settings menu and verify that Document Routing is configured to use Managed Gateway for Spend and Network.* This setting can be applied at the default level, impacting all buyer relationships, or at the buyer level, allowing configuration for individual buyer connections. **You can still choose to receive POs through online or email so you do not need to change New & Change/Cancel Orders to Managed Gateway unless you have a connection set up -- 5 of 23 -- Create your project in Managed Gateway For Spend & Network • Select "Create a New Integration Project“ and enter a Project Name and select which customer you’re integrating with. -- 6 of 23 -- Choose an existing connection or add a new connection • Choose an existing connection by selecting the down arrow to the left of the connection Name in the Reusable Connections section and click Save or click Add New Connection on the right to set up a new connection. -- 7 of 23 -- Choose an existing connection or add a new connection • If you choose to Add New Connection, you’ll be prompted to enter your connection details. -- 8 of 23 -- Configure Document Mapping • The Mapping step shows what documents are mapped, the format/version of the document, and in which direction the documents are set up. • Things to consider: • Send direction is From the Supplier to the Buyer • Receive direction is From the Buyer to the Supplier • Be sure to add 824 and 997 to receive status updates • cXML connections do not require document mapping and will skip this section -- 9 of 23 -- Confirm you are ready to use Test Central • Once your project status is updated to ‘In Testing’, go to Test Central to start submitting test Purchase Orders on behalf of your buyer. -- 10 of 23 -- Creating a Test Script • First, you will need to give your Test Script a name and a description. This is up to the supplier’s discretion as they’re the one creating the Test Scripts. Next, select the Customer you’d like to test with and the OrderRequest from the Document Type list and click Apply, then Add. You will get a pop up with a list of possible scenarios to choose from. (screenshot on next slide) -- 11 of 23 -- Select Test Scenario to add to Test Script • Below is a screenshot of the popup with Optional Test Scenarios. Please make sure you do not test with StandardOrderRequest. This Document Type is not specific to a buyer and will therefore not have buyer specific information. Select the test scenario that includes the Name of the Buyer that you are testing with. -- 12 of 23 -- Test Scripts with multiple Purchase Order Scenarios • You can include multiple Purchase Order types within a single Test Script. This allows all associated documents to be submitted simultaneously and treated as part of one unified test. For the Script to be marked as Completed, each scenario within the Test Script must successfully run to completion. To modify a specific scenario, simply click the pencil icon to edit its details -- 13 of 23 -- Modifying Line Items on a Test Central Purchase Order • Once you click into the specific test scenario, you can edit each line item and/or Add more lines to the Test Purchase Order. Select Close and your line items will be saved. • For address-related fields, simply enter the relevant Address ID to display on the PO. The full address does not need to be manually entered. Best Practice Tip: To ensure a meaningful and successful integration test, it's important for suppliers to update the buyer’s test Purchase Order with their actual product data, including item names, SKUs, pricing, and quantities. Here's why: •Realistic Simulation: Updating the PO reflects the actual products and formats used in production, allowing us to closely mimic live transaction behavior. •Accurate Validation: It helps confirm that product data flows correctly between systems— ensuring everything from unit of measure to tax and pricing logic is configured as expected. •Fewer Surprises: Testing • with real data helps identify potential mapping or formatting issues before go-live, reducing the risk of failed transactions later. •Streamlined Onboarding: If the test is successful, transitioning to production will be smoother and faster, with fewer adjustments needed. -- 14 of 23 -- Complete and Send your Test PO via the Test Script • Click Save to send your Test Purchase Orders listed in the Test Scenarios -- 15 of 23 -- Test Central Dashboard • The Test Central Dashboard will show you the list of Test Scripts you have submitted and their Status. The status can either be Completed, In Progress, or Failed. Click on Select to Edit, see Results, or Delete a script. -- 16 of 23 -- In Progress Test Script • In Progress – Pass/Fail Yellow Clock, In Progress, 0% • Test ID will be generated and shown here once the Purchase Order is sent. -- 17 of 23 -- • Failed - Pass/Fail red X, overall testing 0% Failed Test Script and Troubleshooting -- 18 of 23 -- • If your test POs fail, you can go to the Transaction Tracker to view more details and resolve the error. Failed Test Script and Troubleshooting -- 19 of 23 -- Completed Test Script • Completed – Pass/Fail green check, overall testing 100% -- 20 of 23 -- Example of TC PO Showing in SAP Business Network Some of the benefits of utilizing Test Central is that the Purchase Order flows into the Supplier and Buyer’s SAP Business Network accounts. Below is a screenshot of a supplier’s SAP Business Network Test Account with Purchase Orders generated in Test Central. Purchase Orders generated in Test Central will always start with “TC_”. -- 21 of 23 -- Summary – Wrap Up • Congratulations— a Test Purchase Order has been successfully submitted on the buyer’s behalf! • Confirm your test scenarios in the system against the test plan developed with the Buyer to ensure all required scenarios are complete. • You can now repeat these steps with any buyer who uses Test Central for integration testing. Best Practice Tip For a thorough end-to- end validation, have the buyer send at least one Purchase Order directly from their Test system before moving to Production. This helps confirm real- world readiness and system compatibility. -- 22 of 23 -- Thank you. -- 23 of 23 --

Creating Test Case(s) and a corresponding Test scenario.pdf ☐ Confirm Original PO Test Case exists ☐ Confirm Cancel PO Test Case exists ☐ Add Test Case: o Document Type = ChangeOrderRequest o Parent Doc Type = OrderRequest -- 3 of 5 -- ☐ In Document Characteristics: o Only Enable Order Operation • Set value = delete • Do NOT mark modifiable or mandatory ☐ Save scenario Data Center Replication ☐ Create Test Cases/Scenarios in US Data Center ☐ Create Test Case/Scenarios in EU Data Center Supplier Visibility Validation (MANDATORY) - Quick Guide for Troubleshooting Test Scenarios.pdf ☐ Log in as Supplier ☐ Open Test Central ☐ Create Test Script o Select Buyer o Document Type = OrderRequest, ChangeOrderRequest o Click Apply → Add ☐ Confirm: o Buyer appears in Customer list o Test Scenarios are visible in popup window after selecting Customer & Document Types o Scenarios are selectable and line items are editable Tracking & Documentation - How to use the BUYER_TC_Scenario_Tracker Template.pdf ☐ Update Buyer_TC_Scenario_Tracker o Replace *Buyer* with Buyer’s name o Test Scenarios tab o PO – Modifiable Fields tab o POs Loaded to TC tab ☐ Save tracker to: o Buyer CPR → Integration Kit → Test Central folder • Create folder if not already there o Notes in Atlas on SI/BSSI/BRP records -- 4 of 5 -- Final Confirmation ☐ No duplicate PO scenarios created in Test Central ☐ No scenarios marked Mandatory ☐ Supplier can successfully see scenarios ☐ Instruct supplier to begin sending Test PO according to Test Plan -- 5 of 5 --

Supplier Administration Guide Content PUBLIC 3 -- 3 of 10 -- SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide This guide describes how the administrator for a seller account can update company information and configure additional users. Supplier administrators must maintain complete and accurate company information to be matched to new prospective buyers. This guide applies to: • SAP Business Network • SAP Business Network for Supply Chain • SAP Business Network Discovery Related guides Managing your SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Configuring Document Routing Managing Subscription Services Types of SAP Business Network Accounts You have the choice to do business using one of two SAP Business Network account types: Standard or Enterprise. Some suppliers choose to transact on the SAP Business Network using a fee based Enterprise account due to their historical volume of transactions or to leverage certain functionality that is only available with an Enterprise account. If you are unsure which account type to choose, register a free of charge standard account. You can always upgrade to an Enterprise account if your business needs change. Converting a Fully-Enabled Enterprise Account to a Standard Account [page 5] Deleting Your SAP Business Network Account [page 6] 4 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 4 of 10 -- Converting a Fully-Enabled Enterprise Account to a Standard Account Use this procedure to convert your SAP Business Network account from a fully-enabled Enterprise account to a Standard account. Prerequisites You must be the administrator of a single-organization enterprise account. For multi-organization accounts and suppliers that are part of Quadrem Network billing plan, contact SAP Ariba Network Operations. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Convert to Standard account. 2. Review the information on the Account change eligibility check screen. 3. Click Check eligibility now to continue. 4. A green checkmark in the status indicates that you have met all the requirements to convert your account. The Convert now option appears only after you pass all the eligibility criteria(s). 5. After you click the Convert now option, a Download reports popup appears prompting you to download any reports you might need later. 6. Click Convert now to convert your fully-enabled Enterprise account to a Standard account. You see an Account converted screen on successful conversion of your enterprise account into standard account.  Note If your account does not meet one or more eligibility criteria(s), a red crossmark appears in the status column. You must review and take appropriate action to resolve the criteria(s) marked with red cross. 7. After you resolve the failed criteria(s), you can select Re-check eligibility to re-evaluate your eligibility for converting your account. You can also select Stay with Enterprise account to continue using the enterprise account. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 5 -- 5 of 10 -- Deleting Your SAP Business Network Account Use this procedure to delete your SAP Business Network account. This procedure also applies to SAP Business Network Supplier mobile app. Prerequisites • You must be the account administrator. • You must pay any outstanding fees on your account. • You must delete all credit card information from your account. • You must use only active email addresses listed for your account. • You must convert your Enterprise account to a Standard account. See, Downgrade your Enterprise account to a Standard account • You must reject all trading relationships . • You must delete all the links with other accounts under Account Hierarchy • You must delete all sub-user accounts. • You must delete all the Archived invoices. Context If you are finished using SAP Business Network to conduct transactions over the internet, you can delete your account. However, there is no charge to keep your account open when you have no established trading relationships. You may want to maintain an active account to connect with future customers who use SAP Business Network, or find new customers using SAP Business Network Discovery. Procedure 1. Login to the supplier account as an administrator. 2. Navigate to Users Settings Users . 3. Click Account Deletion. Results After you submit the account deletion request, you will receive a confirmation email with the subject line: Action Required:Confirm Account Deletion Request. Click the link included in the email to confirm the request. 6 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 6 of 10 --  Note • The link will expire in 5 mins. After that, the account will be expired and none of the users will be able to log on to the account. For this reason, it is highly recommended that the you inform all account users and customers of the account deletion prior to deleting the account. If you are planning on deleting your account so that your email address can be used as a username on another SAP Business Network account, please change your username to a different username before deleting the account because you will not be able to use username attached to the deleted account again. Usernames must be in the format of an email address, but the email address does not need to be a valid email. • There is no charge to keep your account open when there are no trading relationships established. You can keep your account open to connect with future customers who use Ariba or find new customers using SAP Business Network Discovery. There is a grace period of 60 days when you are still able to restore your account after an account deletion request. Once the grace period is over, your account gets permanently deleted and cannot be retrieved. If you want to restore your account within 60 days of submitting the deletion request, you must create a Case with SAP Support . Your Company Profile The trading partner company profile helps you win more business by standing out to potential customers across the entirety of SAP Business Network. You can update and maintain information in the Company Profile about your business, including products and services offered, your experience and expertise, and highlights of your accomplishments and values. Additionally, you can control whether or not you want to appear in search results. By default, your profile is visible to all potential and existing customer relationships. About This Profile [page 8] Network Catalog Access [page 8] Profile Settings [page 8] Organizational Structure [page 11] Editing Your Company profile [page 12] How to Add Sustainability Ratings to Your Company Profile [page 12] Showing or Hiding Your Company Profile in Search Results [page 13] Adding Economic Activity Code (GIRO) to Your Company Profile [page 14] Showcasing Assessments on Your Company Profile [page 15] Certifications [page 15] Contacts [page 19] Profile Data Federation [page 23] Company Profile Experience for Promote [page 24] SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 7 -- 7 of 10 -- About This Profile The About This Profile link, located under the company name on your profile, provides key details about your registration history. It reveals the following information: • Member of SAP Business Network Since: Indicates the year you joined SAP Business Network. It reflects your maturity and experience on the platform. A longer membership suggests greater stability and reliability. • Registration Type: Shows how you registered with SAP Business Network. There are two possible registration methods: • Invited: Another buyer invited you to join the platform. This indicates a trusted recommendation and potential endorsement. • Walk-up: You proactively self-registered on the platform. This demonstrates your initiative to engage with the SAP Business Network community. Network Catalog Access Your company profile displays a Network Catalog link under the company name. This link becomes active once you upload products to your network catalog. When potential buyers view your company profile, they can click the link to access a pre-filtered search page that lists a complete suite of your network catalog offerings, including pricing information and specifications. If no products are uploaded, the link stays inactive. For instructions on uploading products to your network catalog, refer to Managing Network Catalog. Profile Settings As a supplier on SAP Business Network, your company's public profile is accessible to all users on SAP Business Network. To attract potential buyers and assist your existing buyers in effective planning, it is crucial to maintain a comprehensive and accurate profile. You have the flexibility to manage the visibility of additional information about your company beyond the basic details, control your profile's appearance in search results, manage buyer access to your extended profiles, and regulate who can initiate contact with you. These objectives can be accomplished by configuring the profile settings. To access these settings, follow these steps: 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. 3. Click on the Options menu located in the upper-right corner of your company profile. 4. Select Profile settings from the dropdown menu. Refer to the table below for a description of each profile setting: 8 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 8 of 10 -- Profile Setting Description Profile Visibility Choose between Show or Hide for each item that you want to display or hide on your public profile. The following items are always visible to all users visiting your public profile: • Basic Info • Product and Service Categories • Ship-to or Service Locations • Industries • Marketing Collateral • References • Social Media The following items are always invisible in your public profile: • Keywords • Contacts The following items are configurable to be either shown or hidden in your public profile based on your business needs: • Credentials (Certifications and Sustainability Ratings): You have options to show it to all trading partners with or without an existing trading relationship with you, or only to your existing trading partners. The default is to show it to all trading partners. • Assessments: The default setting is Show. • Activity Data: The default setting is Show. Organization Structure Choose the required visibility setting from the following op- tions: • Show: Organization structure is visible to all trading part- ners on SAP Business Network. • Hide: Organization structure is hidden from all trading partners on SAP Business Network. • Show to my trading partners only: Organization struc- ture is visible to only the trading partners with whom the supplier has a relationship. SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide PUBLIC 9 -- 9 of 10 -- Profile Setting Description Search Results Visibility Show my profile in search results Choose whether your company will appear in search results when SAP Business Network Discovery users and Trading Part- ners search for suppliers. To increase your company’s visibility for new business opportunities, ensure that this option is ena- bled. Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network When enabled, your profile data will be replicated across global data centers of SAP Business Network and visible in those regions. For details, see Profile Data Federation [page 23]. For suppliers, this setting is enabled by default. Buyers need to enable it manually. Once enabled, this setting cannot be reversed.  Note As a supplier, to enable your profile searchable across global data centers, you must also toggle on Show my profile in search results in addition to enabling Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network. Extended Profile Visibility Choose whether your extended profile is available to all buyers on SAP Business Network or only to those who already have an established relationship with you or have sent you a relation- ship request. The extended profile includes details such as your catalog and transaction capabilities, which you can set up within the Electronic Order Routing, Electronic Invoice Routing, and Settlement sections. To access these configurations, click on the Account Settings icon and then proceed to Settings Network Settings on your SAP Business Network portal. Buyers have the ability to download your extended profile. The information in the downloaded file is sourced from various con- figuration areas, including My Account, Company Profile, and settings within Electronic Order Routing, Electronic Invoice Routing, and Settlement. 10 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide -- 10 of 10 --
