All rights reserved. 5 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the Edifact format. Initially the uses segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION A message from the buyer to the seller, specifying details of the buyer's request to change a Purchase Order. SAP Business Network receives Purchase Order Changes from Buyer in the form of cXML OrderRequest documents. Suppliers are able to select their preferred method of receiving Purchase Orders Change. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDIFACT, SAP Business Network maps to the D.96A ORDCHG Purchase Order Change message. Suppliers can select EDIFACT as their preferred method for receiving Purchase Order Changes. SAP Business Network uses EDIFACT Syntax version 3 and Syntax levels UNOC. Due to Syntax version 3 requirements, SAP Business Network always sends a UNA segment. SAP Business Network does not use functional groups. The envelope structure is UNA-UNB-UNH. CONTRL message acknowledgements are required by SAP Business Network. The complete contents of the OrderRequest are preserved as much as possible in this ORDCHG implementation. However, EDIFACT imposes limitations on element sizes as well as element and segment repetitions, where cXML does not. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard Edifact Rules, defined in D.96A, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. This segment FTX+PRD, specified via C108 4440_1="itemCategory", identifies the item category for an item in C108 4440_2. The item category specifies how a component or material is procured. Possible values are: - materialUnknown: Refers to procuring a material without specifying the material number. - text: Refers to procuring a free-form text item. - stockTransfer: Refers to transfer of stock from one plant to another. - materialGroup: Refers to procuring a material without specifying the value or quantity. - subcontract: Procuring a material by providing component information to a contract manufacturer that makes the finished product. - consignment: Managing a material through a special process where the payment to supplier is withheld until the material or service is consumed by the buyer. - thirdParty: Procuring a material from a third-party vendor. - limit: Indicates that there is an expected limit for unplanned services or material covered by this item. -- 7 of 10 -- ORDCHG Purchase order change request message Outbound Version UN/EDIFACT D.96A Implementation Guideline 2.18 Sep-26, 2025 © 2016-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. The buyer's ERP system determines the subcontracting type based on the material provision indicator determined to support the regular subcontracting refurbishments or replacements scenarios. Possible values are: - regular: Standard subcontracting scenario. - refurbWithoutChange: Refurbishment without changed material. - refurbWithChange: Refurbishment with changed material. - replacement: Replacement of the materials. -- 8 of 10 -- ORDCHG Purchase order change request message Outbound Version UN/EDIFACT D.96A Implementation Guideline 2.18 Sep-26, 2025 © 2016-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the Edifact format. Initially the uses segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION A message specifying details for goods or services ordered under conditions agreed between the seller and the buyer. SAP Business Network receives Purchase Orders from Buyer in the form of cXML OrderRequest documents. Suppliers are able to select their preferred method of receiving Purchase Orders. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDIFACT, SAP Business Network maps to the D.96A ORDERS Purchase Order message. Suppliers can select EDIFACT as their preferred method for receiving Purchase Orders. SAP Business Network uses EDIFACT Syntax version 3 and Syntax levels UNOC. Due to Syntax version 3 requirements, SAP Business Network always sends a UNA segment. SAP Business Network does not use functional groups. The envelope structure is UNA-UNB-UNH. CONTRL message acknowledgements are required by SAP Business Network. The complete contents of the OrderRequest are preserved as much as possible in this ORDERS implementation. However, EDIFACT imposes limitations on element sizes as well as element and segment repetitions, where cXML does not. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard Edifact Rules, defined in D.96A, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- ORDERS Purchase order message Outbound Version UN/EDIFACT D.96A Implementation Guideline 2.16 Sep-26, 2025 © 2016-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. This segment FTX+PRD, specified via C108 4440_1="itemCategory", identifies the item category for an item in C108 4440_2. The item category specifies how a component or material is procured. Possible values are: - materialUnknown: Refers to procuring a material without specifying the material number. - text: Refers to procuring a free-form text item. - stockTransfer: Refers to transfer of stock from one plant to another. - materialGroup: Refers to procuring a material without specifying the value or quantity. - subcontract: Procuring a material by providing component information to a contract manufacturer that makes the finished product. - consignment: Managing a material through a special process where the payment to supplier is withheld until the material or service is consumed by the buyer. - thirdParty: Procuring a material from a third-party vendor. - limit: Indicates that there is an expected limit for unplanned services or material covered by this item. -- 6 of 10 -- ORDERS Purchase order message Outbound Version UN/EDIFACT D.96A Implementation Guideline 2.16 Sep-26, 2025 © 2016-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Application Advice Transaction Set (824) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide the ability to report the results of an application system's data content edits of transaction sets. The results of editing transaction sets can be reported at the functional group and transaction set level, in either coded or free-form format. It is designed to accommodate the business need of reporting the acceptance, rejection or acceptance with change of any transaction set. The Application Advice should not be used in place of a transaction set designed as a specific response to another transaction set (e.g., purchase order acknowledgment sent in response to a purchase order). NOTES SAP Business Network sends Application Advice Messages to Buyers in the form of the cXML StatusUpdateRequest Messages. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps from the ANSI X12 004010 824 Application Advice. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. INTRODUCTION This Draf t Standard f or Trial Use contains the f ormat and establishes the data contents of the Warehouse Stock Transf er Shipment Advice Transaction Set (943) f or use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. This transaction set provides a receiving location with detail inf ormation concerning product being shipped to that location. The transaction set can be used to provide f or customary and established business and industry practice relative to the billing f or goods and services provided. NOTES Sap Business Network allows suppliers to send Warehouse Stock Transf er Shipment Advices to Buyers in the f orm of cXML ShipNoticeRequest documents. As a service to suppliers pref erring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 943 (Warehouse Stock Transf er Shipment Advice) transaction set. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Warehouse Stock Transfer Shipment Advice Transaction Set (943) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used by a depositor or an agent of the depositor to advise the recipient that a transfer shipment has been made. This transaction set provides a receiving location with detail information concerning product being shipped to that location. The transaction set can be used to provide for customary and established business and industry practice relative to the placement of a Warehouse Shipping Order. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Warehouse Stock Transfer Shipment Advices from Buyers in the form of cXML ShipNoticeRequest documents. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network converts the cXML document to the ANSI X12 004010 943 Warehouse Stock Transfer Shipment Advice document. Suppliers can select EDI as their preferred method for receiving Warehouse Stock Transfer Shipment Advice. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1) but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Inventory Inquiry/Advice Transaction Set (846) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Warehouse Inventory Adjustment Advice Messages to Buyers in the form of the cXML ProductReplenishmentMessage. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 947 Warehouse Inventory Adjustment Advice document. On receiving the 947 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML ProductReplenishmentMessage. The final cXML document is internally posted to process the actual Warehouse Inventory Adjustment Advice. If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. SAP Business Network does not currently implement the 824 Application Advice. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. N9*8X is used in conjunction with N903 as the inventory quantity type* to specify the quantity in N902 and the unit of measurement* in C040. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *UserNote (Unit or Basis for Measurement Code (355)*) Code specifying the units in which a value is being expressed, or manner in which a measurement has been taken. Note that an unknown unit of measrement code will be processed as "ZZ" (mutually defined). Please refer to APPENDIX - CODELISTS "355 Unit or Basis for Measurement Code (UOM)" for supported codes. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *UserNote (Inventory quantity type) - Supported values are: N903 = "SubcontractingStockInTransferQuantity": The quantity of inventory of stock that has been transferred to a vendor of type subcontracting using a special movement type. N903 = "UnrestrictedUseQuantity": The quantity of inventory that is unrestricted stock, which is the physical stock that is always available at a plant/storage location that can be consumed for stock movements and available for material requirements planning. N903 = "BlockedQuantity": The quantity of inventory that is blocked stock, which is not counted as unrestricted stock. N903 = "QualityInspectionQuantity": The quantity of inventory that is under quality inspection. N903 = "PromotionQuantity": The quantity of inventory that is reserved for promotions. N903 = "StockInTransferQuantity": The quantity of inventory that is moving between plants or from one company code to another. N903 = "IncrementQuantity": The quantity used to increment (add to) stock. N903 = "RequiredMinimumQuantity": Minimum stock level at which the stock must be maintained. N903 = "RequiredMaximumQuantity": Maximum stock level at which the stock must be maintained. N903 = "StockOnHandQuantity": The calculated value of different Stock types dependent on the customer, location, and material. N903 = "WorkInProcessQuantity": Inventory that has begun the manufacturing process and is no longer included in raw materials inventory, but is not yet a completed product. On a balance sheet, work in progress (WIP) is considered to be an asset because money has been spent towards a completed product. N903 = "IntransitQuantity": The stock in transit is the quantity of a material that was withdrawn from the stock of the issuing plant but has not yet arrived at the receiving plant. N903 = "ScrapQuantity": The quantity represents the Scrap of a material that is expected to occur during production if the material is a component. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of Purchase Order Change Acknowledgment Transaction Set (865) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide for customary and established business and industry practice relative to a seller's acknowledgment of a buyer's purchase order. This transaction set can also be used as notification of a vendor generated order. This usage advises a buyer that a vendor has or will ship merchandise as prearranged in their partnership. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Order Confirmations to Buyers in the form of the cXML ConfirmationRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 865 Purchase Order Change Acknowledgment document. On receiving the 865 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML ConfirmationRequest. The final cXML document is internally posted to process the actual order confirmation. If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. SAP Business Network does not currently implement the 824 Application Advice. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Functional Acknowledgment Transaction Set (997) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to define the control structures for a set of acknowledgments to indicate the results of the syntactical analysis of the electronically encoded documents. The encoded documents are the transaction sets, which are grouped in functional groups, used in defining transactions for business data interchange. This standard does not cover the semantic meaning of the information encoded in the transaction sets. NOTES SAP Business Network requires EDI Suppliers to respond to e.g Purchase Orders (850), Purchase Order Change Requests (860), etc. with a Functional Acknowledgment to confirm that they received the messages. Currently, each transaction set must be acknowledged. Suppliers are expected to return their acceptance or rejection codes according to the supported segments and codes in this guideline. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- 997 Functional Acknowledgment Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.5 Feb-21, 2023 © 2016-2023 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Functional Acknowledgment Transaction Set (997) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to define the control structures for a set of acknowledgments to indicate the results of the syntactical analysis of the electronically encoded documents. The encoded documents are the transaction sets, which are grouped in functional groups, used in defining transactions for business data interchange. This standard does not cover the semantic meaning of the information encoded in the transaction sets. NOTES SAP Business Network responds to EDI transactions, e.g., Invoices (810) with a Functional Acknowledgment to confirm that the messages were received. Currently, each transaction will be acknowledged. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Inventory Inquiry/Advice Transaction Set (846) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Inventory Inquiry/Advice Messages to Buyers in the form of the cXML ProductReplenishmentMessage. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 846 Inventory Inquiry/Advice document. On receiving the 846 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML ProductReplenishmentMessage. The final cXML document is internally posted to process the actual Inventory Inquiry/Advice. If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. SAP Business Network does not currently implement the 824 Application Advice. Example: QTY*33*14*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*1N: Scrap allowed (Scrap Quantity) is used as the quantity representing the scrap of a material that is expected to occur during production if the material is a component. (Inventory only) Example: QTY*1N*16*EA>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*IQ: In-Transit Quantity (Intransit Quantity) is used as the quantity of a material that was withdrawn from the stock of the issuing plant but has not yet arrived at the receiving plant. (Inventory only) Example: QTY*IQ*200*EA>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*17: Quantity On Hand (Stock On Hand Quantity) is used as the calculated value of different stock types dependent on the customer, location, and material. (Inventory only) Example: QTY*17*1000*EA>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*37: Work In Progress (Work In Progress Quantity) is used as the inventory that has begun the manufacturing process and is no longer included in raw materials inventory, but is not yet a completed product. On a balance sheet, work in progress (WIP) is considered to be an asset because money has been spent towards a completed product. (Inventory only) Example: QTY*37*10*EA>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*57 and QTY*70: Minimum Order Quantity (57) and Maximum Order Quantity (70) (Order Quantity minimum and maximum) are used paired as the quantity range the customer must order. The trading partners are alerted if the order quantity is not within the required quantity range during order entry. (Inventory only) Example: QTY*57*1*EA>1~ QTY*70*10000*EA>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*33: Use Quantity Available for Sale (Unrestricted Use Quantity) as the quantity of inventory that is unrestricted stock, which is the physical stock that is always available at a plant/storage location that can be consumed for stock movements and available for material requirements planning. Examples: QTY*33*14*EA>1~ QTY*33*14*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*3Y: Use Subcontracting Stock Transfer In Quantity as the quantity of inventory of stock that has been transferred to a vendor of type subcontracting using a special movement type. Examples: QTY*3Y*15*EA>1~ QTY*3Y*15*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*69: Use Incremental Quantity as the quantity to increment (add to) stock. Examples: QTY*69*200*EA>1~ QTY*69*200*EA>2~ -- 9 of 10 -- 846 Inventory Inquiry/Advice Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.16 Nov-21, 2025 © 2017-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 30 QTY M 1 Inventory/ConsignmentInventory Quantity _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*72: Use Minimum Stock Level (Required Minimum Quantity) as the minimum stock level at which the stock must be maintained. Examples: QTY*72*50*EA>1~ QTY*72*50*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*73: Use Maximum Stock Level (Required Maximum Quantity) as the maximum stock level at which the stock must be maintained. Examples: QTY*73*800*EA>1~ QTY*73*800*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*77: Use Stock Transfer In (Stock In Transfer Quantity) as the quantity of inventory that is moving between plants or from one company code to another. Examples: QTY*77*25*EA>1~ QTY*77*25*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*QH: Use Quantity on Hold (Blocked Quantity) as the quantity of inventory that is blocked stock, which is not counted as unrestricted stock. Examples: QTY*QH*10*EA>1~ QTY*QH*10*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*XT: Use Protected Quantity (Quality Inspection Quantity) as the the quantity of inventory that is under quality inspection. Examples: QTY*XT*500*EA>1~ QTY*XT*500*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*XU: Reserved Quantity (Promotion Quantity) is used as the the quantity of inventory that is reserved for promotions. Examples: QTY*XU*400*EA>1~ QTY*XU*400*EA>2~ -- 10 of 10 --

REF*8X is required to identify the type of time series for this QTY*7K loop. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *User Note (Time series type): Supported values for REF02 are: "manufacturingOrder": An order that initiates the manufacturing process to track the status of manufacturing from Raw Material to Finished Goods status. "purchaseOrder": Subcontracting purchase order from the backend ERP system. "supplierForecast": Forecast created by the supplier based on the Demand Supply situation in the backend ERP system. Typically, the supplier creates the forecast for components based on the Finished Goods Demand. "shipment": Supplier shipment quantity from supplier's location and customer's location to ship the quantities requested. "projectedStock": Stock that is expected to be available in the location at the end of this day. "firmReceipt": Total quantity that the supplier wants to deliver to the customer in period so that the total demand from the customer is covered. "plannedReceipt": Total quantity that the supplier wants to deliver to the customer in a period so that the raw net demands of the buyer are covered. It is a planned quantity that is subject to changes. "forecastConfirmation": Total quantity that the supplier wants to deliver to the customer in the period so that the total demand from the customer is covered. "capacityConfirmation": Quantity of production output of a specific resource that supplier commits to attain. "capacityShiftRuns": Number of shifts a specific production resource can run. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Inventory Inquiry/Advice Transaction Set (846) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Inventory Inquiry/Advice Messages from Buyers in the form of the cXML ProductActivityMessage. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 846 Inventory Inquiry/Advice document. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1) but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. All rights reserved. 5 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Inventory Inquiry/Advice (MO / PO) Transaction Set (846) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Inventory Inquiry/Advice (MO / PO) Messages to Buyers in the form of the cXML ProductReplenishmentMessage. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 846 Inventory Inquiry/Advice (MO / PO) document. On receiving the 846 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML ProductReplenishmentMessage. The final cXML document is internally posted to process the actual Inventory Inquiry/Advice (MO / PO). If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. SAP Business Network does not currently implement the 824 Application Advice. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. "purchaseOrder": Subcontracting purchase order from the backend ERP system. "supplierForecast": Forecast created by the supplier based on the Demand Supply situation in the backend ERP system. Typically, the supplier creates the forecast for components based on the Finished Goods Demand. "shipment": Supplier shipment quantity from supplier's location and customer's location to ship the quantities requested. "projectedStock": Stock that is expected to be available in the location at the end of this day. "firmReceipt": Total quantity that the supplier wants to deliver to the customer in period so that the total demand from the customer is covered. "plannedReceipt": Total quantity that the supplier wants to deliver to the customer in a period so that the raw net demands of the buyer are covered. It is a planned quantity that is subject to changes. "forecastConfirmation": Total quantity that the supplier wants to deliver to the customer in the period so that the total demand from the customer is covered. "capacityConfirmation": Quantity of production output of a specific resource that supplier commits to attain. "capacityShiftRuns": Number of shifts a specific production resource can run. (Inventory only) Example: QTY*IQ*200*EA>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*17: Quantity On Hand (Stock On Hand Quantity) is used as the calculated value of different stock types dependent on the customer, location, and material. (Inventory only) Example: QTY*17*1000*EA>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*37: Work In Progress (Work In Progress Quantity) is used as the inventory that has begun the manufacturing process and is no longer included in raw materials inventory, but is not yet a completed product. (Inventory only) Example: QTY*37*10*EA>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*57 and QTY*70: Minimum Order Quantity (57) and Maximum Order Quantity (70) (Order Quantity minimum and maximum) are used paired as the quantity range the customer must order. (Inventory only) Example: QTY*57*1*EA>1~ QTY*70*10000*EA>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*33: Use Quantity Available for Sale (Unrestricted Use Quantity) as the quantity of inventory that is unrestricted stock, which is the physical stock that is always available at a plant/storage location that can be consumed for stock movements and available for material requirements planning. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Inventory Inquiry/Advice Transaction Set (846) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Inventory Inquiry/Advice Messages from Buyers in the form of the cXML ProductActivityMessage. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 846 Inventory Inquiry/Advice document. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1), but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- 846 Inventory Inquiry/Advice (SMI) Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 2.8 Nov-21, 2025 © 2017-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. "originCountryCode": The country of origin for a batch of material or goods. "shelfLife": Duration that a product is expected to remain within its approved product specification after production date. It is used for information purposes only. The lexical representation for duration is the ISO 8601 extended format PnYn MnDTnH nMnS, where nY represents the number of years, nM the number of months, nD the number of days, T the date/time separator, nH the number of hours, nM the number of minutes, and nS the number of seconds. For example, to indicate a duration of 60 days, one would write: P0Y0M60D. "expirationDate": The date on which when a batch of material/goods becomes expired*. "inspectionDate": The date on which when a batch of material/goods will be inspected*. "productionDate": The date on which when a batch of material or goods is produced*. *Batch number related dates: Date expressed as format CCYYMMDDHHMMSS[timezone] _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Example: REF*BT*batchQuantity*10>A1~ REF*BT*productionDate*20171210100000-0500*0L>A1~ REF*BT*expirationDate*20181231100000-0500*0L>A1~ REF*BT*inspectionDate*20180101100000-0500*0L>A1~ REF*BT*originCountryCode*US>A1~ REF*BT*shelfLife*P0Y0M1DT2H3M4S>A1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ For detailed information about the BatchGroup composition, please refer to these subsequent sections within this document: BATCH GROUP BATCH GROUP – UNIQUE SEQUENTIAL COUNTER -- 2 of 10 -- 846 Inventory Inquiry/Advice (SMI) Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 2.8 Nov-21, 2025 © 2017-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 42 BATCH GROUP This Implementation Guideline provides batch information in the ANSI X12 846 4010 message for each material produced in a single manufacturing run. It is received from the Buyer in the form of <Batch> loop(s)* for each <ProductActivityDetails> in the cXML ProductActivityMessage document. *Currently only one <Batch> loop (BatchGroup) per product is supported. BatchGroup composition: LEVEL A (1st) <Batch> The <Batch> itself carries the batch IDs, its related quantity, country of origin and relevant dates. Additionally, the <Batch> loop can contain multiple <PropertyValuation> loops for further properties and its associated values. LEVEL B (2nd) <PropertyValuation> Each <PropertyValuation> loop contains one <PropertyReference> and multiple <ValueGroup> loops. The <PropertyReference> contains multiple <IdReference>, one for each identified property reference. LEVEL C (3rd) <ValueGroup> Each <ValueGroup> loop contains one <IdReference> for the identified value group reference and multiple <PropertyValue> loops. LEVEL D (4th) <PropertyValue> Each <PropertyValue> loop contains multiple <Characteristic> for this property value. LEVEL Z (5th) Contains the content, sent via the respective REF BatchGroup segment. Since the ANSI X12 846 4010 standard does not provide such a detailed loop structure for batch information, one <Batch> loop under <ProductActivityDetails> is represented in the ANSI X12 846 message as one BatchGroup under the LIN group by using 4 specified REF BatchGroup segments, one for each level along with a UniqueSequentialCounter*. *Please refer to the next section BATCH GROUP – UNIQUE SEQUENTIAL COUNTER. <Batch> Occurence 0..1 <PropertyValuation> Occurence 0..n <PropertyReference> Occurence 0..1 <IdReference> Occurence 0..n <ValueGroup> Occurence 0..n <IdReference> Occurence 0..1 <PropertyValue> Occurence 0..n <Characteristic> Occurence 0..n <ProductActivityDetails> Occurence 1..1 REF*BT REF*ADB REF*ADC REF*ADD LIN LEVEL A LEVEL B LEVEL D LEVEL Z LEVEL C COUNTER A1 LEVEL Z LEVEL Z COUNTER A1-B1-Z1 COUNTER A1-B1-C1-Z1 COUNTER A1-B1-C1-D1-Z1 -- 2 of 10 -- 846 Inventory Inquiry/Advice (SMI) Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 2.8 Nov-21, 2025 © 2017-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 43 BATCH GROUP – UNIQUE SEQUENTIAL COUNTER This counter is sent on each specified REF BatchGroup segment via (C040 127 with 128=”0L”). It uniquely identifies the correct position of each REF BatchGroup segment within one BatchGroup. The counter (C040 127 with 128=”0L”) is composed of 1 to 5 sections as follows: [Level ID] Each level within one BatchGroup is identified by a specific alphanumeric character (A – D & Z). [Level Sequence] The numerical suffix serves as a sequential level counter per direct parent level. Each REF BatchGroup segment contains at least one of these sections in its counter. Example only 1st level composition (Batch - REF*BT): A1 [Section Separator] The higher the Level ID of the respective REF BatchGroup segment is, the more sections are included in its counter composition. Sections are separated by a minus sign (-). The counter always starts with the section of the 1st level in the BatchGroup hierarchy, followed by the section(s) for each subsequent level until the Level ID of the respective REF BatchGroup segment is reached. Example 5 level composition (Characteristic - REF*ADD): A1-B1-C1-D1-Z1 Example BATCH GROUP* – UNIQUE SEQUENTIAL COUNTER REF Segment Level ID Level Sequence Example REF*BT A 0..1* REF*BT*Supplier Batch ID*Buyer Batch ID*0L>A1~ REF*BT*batchQuantity*10*0L>A1~ REF*BT*originCountryCode*US*0L>A1~ REF*BT*productionDate*20161210100000-0500*0L>A1~ REF*BT*expirationDate*20171231100000-0500*0L>A1~ REF*BT*inspectionDate*20160101100000-0500*0L>A1~ REF*BT*shelfLife*P0Y0M1DT2H3M4S*0L>A1~ REF*ADB B 0..n REF*ADB*domainA1B1Z1*ID-A1B1Z1*0L>A1-B1-Z1~ REF*ADB*domainA1B1Z2*ID-A1B1Z2*0L>A1-B1-Z2~ REF*ADB*domainA1B2Z1*ID-A1B2Z1*0L>A1-B2-Z1~ REF*ADC C 0..n REF*ADC*domainA1B1C1Z1*ID-A1B1C1*0L>A1-B1-C1-Z1~ REF*ADC*domainA1B1C2Z1*ID-A1B1C2*0L>A1-B1-C2-Z1~ REF*ADC*domainA1B2C1Z1*ID-A1B2C1*0L>A1-B2-C1-Z1~ REF*ADD D 0..n REF*ADD*charA1B1C1D1Z1*ID-A1B1C1D1-01*0L>A1-B1-C1-D1-Z1~ REF*ADD*charA1B1C1D1Z2*ID-A1B1C1D1-02*0L>A1-B1-C1-D1-Z2~ REF*ADD*charA1B1C2D2Z1*ID-A1B1C1D2-01*0L>A1-B1-C1-D2-Z1~ REF*ADD*charA1B1C2D1Z1*ID-A1B1C2D1-01*0L>A1-B1-C2-D1-Z1~ REF*ADD*charA1B2C1D1Z1*ID-A1B2C1D1-01*0L>A1-B2-C1-D1-Z1~ *Currently only one BatchGroup per LIN is supported. All rights reserved. 5 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Invoice Transaction Set (810) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide for customary and established business and industry practice relative to the billing for goods and services provided. NOTES SAP Business Network allows suppliers to send invoices to buying organizations in the form of cXML InvoiceDetailRequest documents. As a service to suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 810 (Invoice) transaction set and translates it to a cXML InvoiceDetailRequest. Because the 810 implementations ultimately map to an InvoiceDetailRequest, it must conform to its rules. On receiving an 810 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and then converts it to the cXML InvoiceDetailRequest. The final cXML document is internally posted to process the actual invoice. 810 documents must strictly conform to these implementation guidelines. The 810 is implemented using ANSI X12 Version 004010. There are two layout templates for invoices: Detailed (Regular Invoice) and Header Invoice. A Detailed Invoice addresses the line items of one purchase order. A Header Invoice covers many purchase orders without listing specific line items. There are three types of invoices: Standard, Credit Memo and Debit Memo. Each layout template and invoice type have particular requirements (content that must be present in order to be valid). There are also some content requirements for 810 itself to be satisfied. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 5 of 10 -- 810 Invoice Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 2.27 Mar-19, 2026 © 2018-2026 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 16 BIG M 1 Beginning Segment for Invoice Example: BIG*20170103*InvoiceID*20151230*PurchaseOrderID***DI*00*NA~ To indicate the beginning of an invoice transaction set and transmit identifying numbers and dates. There are two layout templates of invoices: Regular and Header. A Regular Invoice addresses the line items of one purchase order. A Header Invoice covers many purchase orders without listing specific line items. There are three types of invoices: Standard [BIG07=DI/FD], Credit Memo [BIG07=CR/CN] and Debit Memo [BIG07=DR/DC]. Summary Invoices can use only the Regular layout template. A Credit Memo submitted in Regular form is called "Line Level Credit Memo", a Debit Memo submitted in Regular form is called "Line Level Debit Memo". Both include item details. *UserNote [DC]: "Line Level Debit Memo" feature must be enabled in SAP Business Network. Header Invoices reference one whole Purchase Order on each line item of the invoice. The line items of each Purchase Order are not detailed. Each Purchase Order requires an occurrence of the IT1 Group. Regular Invoices are identified by specifying order and/or master agreement identifications at the invoice header level. Used with BIG07=DI (Standard Invoice), BIG07=FD (Standard Summary Invoice), BIG07=CN (Line Level Credit Memo) and BIG07=DC (Line Level Debit Memo). Header Invoices are identified by NOT specifying any order and/or master agreement identifications at the invoice header level and the usage of IT1 where 235=PO/VO. Specifically, BIG03-04 must be null. Header level REF segments identifying orders or master agreements must not be present. Used with BIG07=DI (Standard Invoice), BIG07=CR (Credit Memo) and BIG07=DR (Debit Memo). _____________________________________________________________________________________________ In case the 810 is a Credit Memo or Line Level Credit Memo, SAP Business NetworkSAP Business Network will default all amounts to negative. Only line level order-related references (IT1/REF*PO/AH/VN) will be considered. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *UserNote [NONPO]: External Purchase Order related invoice It is allowed to send non-PO Invoice or Credit/Debit Memo transactions without specific order reference. This can be any external purchase order that was not routed through SAP Business Network. Otherwise it is not used. 1 Schedule Agreement Example: REF*AH*Agreement ID*1~ To specify order-related references. Agreement Number [REF*AH]: Used in conjunction with DTM*LEA. REF03 is used as agreement type indicator. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Purchase Order Number [REF*PO]: Can be provided to support order numbers longer than 22 chars. If REF*PO is present, then REF02 overrides the order number provided in BIG04. This can be used in conjunction with DTM*004. If BIG04 include "NONPO" (external purchase order related invoice), this reference will be ignored. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Vendor Order Number [REF*VN]: Comparable to BAK08 in the X12 855 4010 message type. Can be used in conjunction with DTM*008. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Single and Multiple Purchase Order (PO) Scenarios: Single PO Scenario - Header level order-related references BIG03-04 and REF*PO or REF*AH or REF*VN must be provided. Line level order-related reference (IT1/REF*PO/AH/VN) must be null. Multiple PO Scenario - BIG03-04 must be null. Additionally order-related references (REF*PO/AH/VN) at header must also be null. Only line level order-related references (IT1/REF*PO/AH/VN) will be considered. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Invoice Source Document: Using the REF segment with the qualifiers AH, PO, and VN defines the source document referenced in the invoice. This information can be mandatory when the appropriate rule is set in the SAP Business Network. Below is a breakdown of the logic sequence for determining the value: 1. If the value of BIG04 equals "NONPO", invoice relates to an External Purchase Order. 2. If REF*PO segment exists or BIG04 is provided and does not equal "NONPO", invoice relates to a Purchase Order. 3. If REF*AH segment exists and BIG04 is not provided, the invoice relates to a Contract. 4. If REF*VN segment exists and BIG04 is not provided, the invoice relates to a Sales Order. 5. When none of the above conditions are met, the invoice relates as a document with no order information. Please note that multiple conditions may potentially apply. In such cases the first matching condition in the list takes precedence. Example: BIG*20170102*Invoice ID*20151230*PurchaseOrderID***DI*00*~ ... REF*AH*Agreement ID*1~ REF*VN*Vendor Order ID~ The invoice will relate to a Purchase Order as BIG04 is provided and does not equal "NONPO". -- 10 of 10 --

[timezone] = Please refer to APPENDIX - CODELISTS 623 Time Code. Example: REF*SI*Tracking ID*20170106060000ED~ To specify identifying information. This reference is used only with N1*SF and N1*ST. REF02 identify the carrier assigned reference number for their part of the shipment (shipment tracking number). In addition to this, REF03 can be used to provide a relating shipment tracking date. Carrier PRO number: This is the carrier assigned reference ID / tracking ID for their part of this shipment. Conceptually, this is a tracking number. Different carriers have different names for shipment identifiers. Some call it a way bill number, others call it a PRO number, and still others call it a bill of lading. They all represent tracking numbers. Example: N1*SF*Ship-From~ REF*SI*Tracking ID*20170106060000ED~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Tracking Number Date Note: Note that a complete date/time/zone is recommended. Otherwise it will be automatically calculated and might lead to wrong data. Timestamps in cXML are represented as a date with a time, and an offset to UTC. If you do not specify a time, it will be taken as noon (12:00) on the date specified. If you do not specify the time code (zone), then it will be defaulted to UTC (+00:00). -- 2 of 10 -- 810 Invoice Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 2.27 March-19, 2026 © 2018-2026 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 44 IT1 M 1 Baseline Item Data Example: IT1*1*50*EA*10.00**SN*Serial ID*VP*Supplier Part ID*VS*Supplier Supplemental Part ID*BP*Buyer Part ID*MG*Ma nufacturer Part ID*MF*Manufacturer Name*CH*Country Code ISO*EN*EAN ID*EA*European Waste ID*C3*UNSPS C ID~ To specify the basic and most frequently used line item data for the invoice and related transactions. The contents of the IT1 group depend on whether this is a Regular Invoice, referencing one order with its line items, or is a Header Invoice with each invoice line item citing a whole order. In the case of Regular Invoices, we distinguish between regular item and service item. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ A Regular Invoice uses IT101, 02, 03, and 04, and product/service ID qualifiers which can be used in any order. Allowed product/service ID qualifiers for regular items: SN, UP, VP, VS, BP, MG, MF, C3, and CH Allowed product/service ID qualifiers for service items: SH, VS, BP and C3 Conditions: 1. IT101, 02, 03 and 04 are all required. 2. If VS is used, then VP (regular item) or SH (service item) is required. 3. If either MF or MG is used, the other is required. 4. If line item is a service item, then SH is mandatory. Product/service ID qualifiers SN, UP, VP, MG, MF, CH, EN or EA are not allowed to be used along with SH. 5. If CH is used, it qualifies an ISO-3166 country code. Do not use the country name. 6. Only SN is allowed to repeat. With all others, only the last occurrence is captured. 7. If C3 is used, the Classification domain is automatically identified as "UNSPSC". If you like to specify other Classification domains, please refer to the subsequent REF*8L segment "Reference - Classification". Example 1: Regular Invoice citing a PO line item. IT1*10*20*EA*10.00**SN*Serial ID*VP*Supplier Part ID*VS*Supplier Supplemental Part ID*BP*Buyer Part ID*MG*Manufacturer Part ID*MF*Manufacturer Name*CH*Country Code ISO*EN*EAN ID*EA*European Waste ID*C3*UNSPSC ID~ Example 2: Regular Invoice citing a PO service line item. IT1*10*30*EA*15.00**SH*Supplier Service Part ID*VS*Supplier Supplemental Service Part ID*BP*Buyer Service Part ID*C3*UNSPSC ID~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Header Invoices reference one whole Purchase Order on each line item of the invoice. The line items of each Purchase Order are not detailed. Each Purchase Order requires an occurrence of the IT1 Group. A Header Invoice does not use IT101, but does require IT102-IT104, and uses product/service ID qualifiers PO and VO. The following conditions must be met: 1. IT102 = should be "1" (one purchase order) 2. IT103 = should be "ZZ" 3. IT104 = Invoiced amount of purchase order being referenced - required 4. At least one of PO or VO order number is required. Both can be used. Example 3: Header Invoice citing a purchase order. IT1**1*ZZ*100.00**PO*Purchase Order ID*VO*Supplier Order ID~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ UserNote [Serial Numbers]: Multiple serial numbers are supported. You can use SN with a serial number as many times as you wish. IT1 is a limited resource. Additional serial numbers can be added using REF*SE. Any serial numbers specified in IT1 with SN are combined with REF*SE. You can use either implementation or both. -- 4 of 10 -- 810 Invoice Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 2.27 March-19, 2026 © 2018-2026 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. The usage of this segment [REF*FJ] is highley recommended*. Invoice Line Item Number [REF*FJ] Supplier defined ID for the current invoice line. Should be unique across all invoice lines within an invoice. It is recommended that you either map them directly from your invoicing system, if available in integer form, or generate these numbers in your outbound invoice map using an accumulator. Required for both Regular and Header Invoice lines. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *Please note: The "Invoice Line Item Number" [REF*FJ] throughout an Invoice document is always mandatory for the SAP Business Network. Additionally, this number should be unique to ensure the correct and faultless transfer to the buyer system. If REF*FJ is not sent, SAP Business Network copies the mandatory "Invoice Line Item Number" value from IT101 (IT1_350) value to fulfill at least the first requirement. This is the "Purchase Order Line Item Number" value. This scenario only works with unique "Purchase Order Line Item Number" values throughout the 810 document. Service Entry Number [REF*ACE] is used to refer to the service sheet line related to this line item. REF04 refers to the line number in the related ServiceEntryRequest for the item. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Fine Line Classification (Item type / Composite item type): The item type specifies whether the line item is a grouped item having child items or an independent line item. Possible values: "composite" to identify an item group, "item" to identify an independent line item or "lean" Indicate that no child item is expected for the line. The composite item type specifies whether a parent item uses group-level pricing. Possible values are "groupLevel" or "itemLevel". REF04 indicate the line number of the corresponding parent line item. This is a mandatory field and applicable only for a line item with itemType="item". Example: REF*FL*item**LI>1~ REF*FL*composite*groupLevel~ REF*FL*composite*itemLevel~ REF*FL*lean~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Ship Notice/Manifest Number [REF*MA] Shipment ID of an earlier Advance Ship Notice [ASN]. This would be BSN02 [396] "Shipment Identifier" from an 856 previously sent. If you are using this, then it is recommended to include a Manifest/Ship Notice Date [DTM*111] which would match its counterpart in BSN03 (date) and BSN04 (time) from the 856. It is also possible to add the related line number by using C040 where 128=LI. Example: REF*MA*Ship Notice ID**LI>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Receiving Advice Number [REF*RV] Receipt ID of an earlier Receiving Advice. This would be BRA01 [127] from an 861 previously sent. It is also possible to add the related line number by using C040 where 128=LI. Example: REF*RV*Receipt ID**LI>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Master Agreement Number [REF*AH] is used in conjunction with DTM*LEA. REF03 is used as agreement type indicator. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ REF*VN represents the Supplier's Order Number and can be used in combination with DTM*008. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ REF*PO represents the Purchase Order Number. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ UserNote [Serial Numbers]: Multiple serial numbers are supported. Additional serial numbers can be added using IT1 (235="SN"). IT1 is a limited resource. Any serial numbers specified in IT1 with SN are combined with REF*SE. You can use either implementation or both. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *UserNote [PO Scenarios]: Single and Multiple Purchase Order (PO) Scenarios Single PO Scenario - Header level PO related references BIG03-04 and REF*PO or REF*AH or REF*VN must be provided. Line level PO related reference (IT1/REF*PO/AH/VN) must be null. Multiple PO Scenario - BIG03-04 must be null. Additionally PO related references (REF*PO/AH/VN) at header must also be null. Supplier Order Date [DTM*008] corresponds to DTM*ACK from earlier 855. Date of the goods Shipment [DTM*011] should match DTM*011 from an earlier 856. Manifest/Ship Notice Date [DTM*111] from earlier 856. Should match BSN03 + BSN04. Delivery Note Date [DTM*192] is used in conjunction with REF, where REF01=KK. Service Entry Date [DTM*472] is used in conjunction with REF, where REF01=ACE. Agreement Date [DTM*LEA] is used in conjunction with REF, where REF01=AH. Product Movement Date [DTM*514] is used in conjunction with REF, where REF01=4M. Reference Date [DTM*214] is used for the blanket order or contract item. The usage of this date is optional in most cases, and must be defined by the trading partners involved in the transaction. Procurement software might use this date in reconciling an invoice against a blanket order or contract. For the service item it can indicate the date at which the service line item is being invoiced. Inspection Date [DTM*517] represent the date when the transfer of goods or the delivery of services occurs according to legal tax definitions. The usage of this date is optional in most cases, and must be defined by the trading partners involved in the transaction. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Nonconformance Report (842) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Nonconformance Report Messages to Buyers in the form of the cXML QualityNotificationRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 842 Nonconformance Report document. On receiving the 842 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML QualityNotificationRequest. The final cXML document is internally posted to process the actual Nonconformance Report. If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. SAP Business Network does not currently implement the 824 Application Advice. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- 842 Nonconformance Report Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 2.8 Dec-09, 2024 © 2017-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Nonconformance Report (842) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Nonconformance Report Messages from Buyers in the form of the cXML QualityNotificationRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 842 Nonconformance Report document. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1) but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- 842 Nonconformance Report Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 2.8 Jun-18, 2024 © 2017-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. Example: BNR*00*QN1*20170629*152900~ To indicate the beginning of a Nonconformance Report Transaction Set. The Nonconformance Report Message defines a nonconformance notification for one or more defects associated with a line item on a purchase order or a ship notice. A code is used to classify each item according to the type of problem or defect. The details of the problem or defect can contain causes, tasks, activities, codes, code groups, and descriptions. Transaction set purpose code "Original" [BNR01=00] - Is used to create a new Nonconformance Report. Transaction set purpose code "Replace" [BNR01=05] - Is used to update an existing Nonconformance Report. -- 3 of 10 -- 842 Nonconformance Report Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 2.8 Jun-18, 2024 © 2017-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Warehouse Shipping Order Transaction Set (940) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide for customary and established business and industry practice relative to the placement of purchase orders for goods and services. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Purchase Orders from Buyer in the form of cXML OrderRequest documents. Suppliers are able to select their preferred method of receiving Purchase Orders. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 940 Warehouse Shipping Order document. Suppliers can select EDI as their preferred method for receiving Warehouse Shipping Orders. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1), but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. All rights reserved. 6 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Purchase Order Change Request Transaction Set (860) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide the information required for customary and established business and industry practice relative to the placement of purchase order change. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Purchase Orders from Buyer in the form of cXML OrderRequest documents. Suppliers are able to select their preferred method of receiving Purchase Order Change Requests. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 860 Purchase Order Change Request document. Suppliers can select EDI as their preferred method for receiving Purchase Order Change Request. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1), but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 6 of 10 -- 860 Purchase Order Change Request - Buyer Initiated Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 3.2 Oct-24, 2025 © 2016-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. SAP Business Network Orders currently supports payment terms only by the number of days from the invoice date, and a discount and/or premium. You can put the discount and/or late penalty in the same ITD segment, or use multiple ITD segments. A discount uses ITD03 and ITD05. A penalty uses ITD07 and ITD15. ITD12 is optional for both terms. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ITD01: Optional to identify the type of terms you are defining. ITD02: All payment terms are based on the Invoice Date. ITD03: Required for discount terms (ITD01=52). Must be used in combination with ITD05. This value is read as a percentage. If you mean 2.25% then ITD03=2.25, not 0.0225. ITD05: Required for discount terms [ITD01=52]. Must be used in combination with ITD03. This is the number of days from the Invoice Date (ITD02=3, BIG01). ITD07: Required for penalty terms (ITD01=05). Must be used in combination with ITD15. This is the number of days from the Invoice Date after which penalty terms apply. ITD12: Optional for discount and penalty terms (ITD01=05 or 52). Used to provide payment terms description. ITD15: Required for penalty terms (ITD01= 05). Must be used in combination with ITD07. This is the penalty terms percentage to be applied ITD07 days after the Invoice Date (ITD02=3). The ITD15 value is always set to 0. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Example 1: Penalty (ITD01=05) ITD*05*3*****30********0~ You should use this code if no discount is offered, but a late payment penalty exists. Note that ITD07 and ITD15 become mandatory. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Example 2: Discount (ITD01=52) 2% discount for prompt payment in < 10 days ITD*52*3*2**10~ ITD03 and ITD05 are required. -- 1 of 10 -- 860 Purchase Order Change Request - Buyer Initiated Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 3.2 Oct-24, 2025 © 2016-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. "isNotERS" - The order or line item is not flagged for Evaluated Receipt Settlement. "allowed" - Invoice is allowed "notAllowed" - Invoice is not allowed Example: N9*KD*INVValue*isERS~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Invoice verification types: The only supported value in N903 in combination with N902="INVVerification" is: "goodsReceipt" - Indicates that invoice verification for this item is based on the goods receipt. All rights reserved. 6 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Purchase Order Transaction Set (850) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide for customary and established business and industry practice relative to the placement of purchase orders for goods and services. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Purchase Orders from Buyer in the form of cXML OrderRequest documents. Suppliers are able to select their preferred method of receiving Purchase Orders. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 850 Purchase Order document. Suppliers can select EDI as their preferred method for receiving Purchase Orders. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1) but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 6 of 10 -- 850 Purchase Order Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 3.2 Oct-24, 2025 © 2016-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company.
