Examples: N9*KD*ASNLowerQtyTolerancePercent*5.0~ N9*KD*ASNUpperQtyTolerancePercent*5.0~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Invoice instructions: Supported values in N903 in combination with N902="INVValue" are: "isERS" - The order or line item is flagged for Evaluated Receipt Settlement, indicating that the system will post an invoice for it automatically based on goods receipts. "isNotERS" - The order or line item is not flagged for Evaluated Receipt Settlement. "allowed" - Invoice is allowed "notAllowed" - Invoice is not allowed Example: N9*KD*INVValue*isERS~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Invoice verification types: The only supported value in N903 in combination with N902="INVVerification" is: "goodsReceipt" - Indicates that invoice verification for this item is based on the goods receipt. The invoice item can then be matched up uniquely with the goods receipt item. Goods-receipt-based invoice verification makes sense when you expect a delivery to be made and posted in several parts. Example: N9*KD*INVVerification*goodsReceipt~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Invoice and/or Service sheet unit price update options: Specifies whether a buyer or supplier is allowed to update the unit price while creating an invoice. Supported values in N903 in combination with N902="INV_unitPriceEditable" for the invoice or N902="SES_UnitPriceEditable" for the service sheet are: "yes" - The buyer or supplier is allowed to edit unit price. The new price must be within price tolerance. "no" - The unit price is not editable regardless of transaction rules defined in the network hub. Examples: N9*KD*INV_unitPriceEditable*yes~ N9*KD*SES_UnitPriceEditable*no~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Service sheet instructions: Supported values in N903 in combination with N902="SESValue" are: "allowed" - Service sheet is allowed "notAllowed" - Service sheet is not allowed Example: N9*KD*SESValue*allowed~ -- 8 of 10 -- 850 Purchase Order Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 3.2 Oct-24, 2025 © 2016-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 116 REF O 12 Party Reference Example: REF*AP**Accounts receivable ID~ To specify identifying information. Not used if N1*DA. All reference identifiers are optional, and most all can be used. Care should be taken to avoid ambiguity and duplication. Some of the special cases are shown below. For further detailed correlation between party and its references please refer to APPENDIX - CODELISTS 128 Reference Identification Qualifier. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ REF*AP: The Accounts Receivable Identification Number should only be used for the Buyer (N1*BY) / Bill To (N1*BT) / Sold To (N1*SO) and / or Ship To Party (N1*ST). Example: N1*BY*Buyer Name~ REF*AP*Buyer Accounts Receivable ID~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ REF*PB: The Payer's Bank Account Identification Number should be used for the Buyer (N1*BY) / Bill To (N1*BT) and / or Sold To Party (N1*SO). Example: N1*SO*Sold To Name~ REF*AP*Sold To Bank Account ID~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ REF*BAA: The Supplier Tax Identification Number should only be used for the Remit To Party (N1*RI). REF*RT and REF*PY: Payee's Bank Routing Identification Number (financial institution) and Payee's Bank Account Identification Number should be paired and are recommended for the Remit To Party (N1*RI), but allowed at all parties. Example: N1*RI*Remit To Name~ REF*BAA*Supplier Tax ID~ REF*RT*Payees Bank Routing ID~ REF*PY*Payees Bank Account ID~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ REF*4B, REF*4C, REF*9S and REF*KK: The Loading Point, Storage Location, Transportation Zone and cRADCRS Indicator should only be used for the Sold To (N1*SO) and / or Ship To Party (N1*ST). Example: N1*ST*Ship To Name~ REF*4B*1234~ REF*4C*5678~ REF*9S*ABCD~ REF*KK*RAD~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ REF*YD: The Buyer Additional Identification Number should only be used for the Buyer Party (N1*BY). REF*ZA: The Supplier Additional Identification Number should only be used for the Supplier Corporate (N1*SU) / Supplier Account (N1*SE) / Message From (N1*FR) / Bill From (N1*BF). SAP Business Network Orders currently supports payment terms only by the number of days from the invoice date, and a discount and/or premium. You can put the discount and/or late penalty in the same ITD segment, or use multiple ITD segments. A discount uses ITD03 and ITD05. A penalty uses ITD07 and ITD15. ITD12 is optional for both terms. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ITD01: Optional to identify the type of terms you are defining. ITD02: All payment terms are based on the Invoice Date. ITD03: Required for discount terms (ITD01=52). Must be used in combination with ITD05. This value is read as a percentage. If you mean 2.25% then ITD03=2.25, not 0.0225. ITD05: Required for discount terms [ITD01=52]. Must be used in combination with ITD03. This is the number of days from the Invoice Date (ITD02=3, BIG01). ITD07: Required for penalty terms (ITD01=05). Must be used in combination with ITD15. This is the number of days from the Invoice Date after which penalty terms apply. ITD12: Optional for discount and penalty terms (ITD01=05 or 52). Used to provide payment terms description. ITD15: Required for penalty terms (ITD01= 05). Must be used in combination with ITD07. This is the penalty terms percentage to be applied ITD07 days after the Invoice Date (ITD02=3). The ITD15 value is always set to 0. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Example 1: Penalty (ITD01=05) ITD*05*3*****30********0~ You should use this code if no discount is offered, but a late payment penalty exists. Note that ITD07 and ITD15 become mandatory. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Example 2: Discount (ITD01=52) 2% discount for prompt payment in < 10 days ITD*52*3*2**10~ ITD03 and ITD05 are required. -- 1 of 10 -- 850 Purchase Order Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 3.2 Oct-24, 2025 © 2016-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Purchase Order Transaction Set (850) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide for customary and established business and industry practice relative to the placement of sales orders for goods and services. NOTES SAP Business Network allows suppliers to send sales order to buying organizations in the form of cXML SalesOrderRequest documents. As a service to suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 850 (Purchase order) transaction set and translates it to a cXML SalesOrderRequest. Because the 850 implementations ultimately map to an SalesOrderRequest, it must conform to its rules. On receiving an 850 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and then converts it to the cXML SalesOrderRequest. The final cXML document is internally posted to process the actual sales order. 850 documents must strictly conform to these implementation guidelines. The 850 is implemented using ANSI X12 Version 004010. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- 850 Sales Order Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.8 May-29, 2024 © 2021-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Purchase Order Acknowledgment Transaction Set (855) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide for customary and established business and industry practice relative to a seller's acknowledgment of a buyer's purchase order. This transaction set can also be used as notification of a vendor generated order. This usage advises a buyer that a vendor has or will ship merchandise as prearranged in their partnership. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Order Confirmations to Buyers in the form of the cXML ConfirmationRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 855 Purchase Order Acknowledgment document. On receiving the 855 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML ConfirmationRequest. The final cXML document is internally posted to process the actual order confirmation. If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. SAP Business Network does not currently implement the 824 Application Advice. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- 855 Purchase Order Acknowledgment Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 2.16 May-22, 2025 © 2016-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Planning Schedule with Release Capability (830) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Planning Schedule with Release Capability Messages to Buyers in the form of the cXML ProdutReplenishmentMessage. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 830 Planning Schedule with Release Capability document. On receiving the 830 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML ProdutReplenishmentMessage. The final cXML document is internally posted to process the actual Planning Schedule with Release Capability. If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. SAP Business Network does not currently implement the 824 Application Advice. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. All rights reserved. 22 QTY O >1 Quantity Example: QTY*QH*100*EA>1~ To specify inventory related quantity categories. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *Note: Inventory Category Code: This element is required to indicate the ownership of the inventory for the related quantity, except for QTY where QTY01=1N/17/37/57/70/IQ. C001/1081="1" (Inventory): Inventory that is in the possession of the buyer, and is owned and managed by the buyer. Example: QTY*33*14*EA>1~ C001/1081="2" (Consignment Inventory): Inventory that is in the possession of the buyer, but is owned by the supplier. Example: QTY*33*14*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*1N: Use Scap allowed (Scrap Quantity) as the quantity representing the scrap of a material that is expected to occur during production if the material is a component. Example: QTY*1N*16*EA~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*17: Use Quantity On Hand (Stock On Hand Quantity) as the calculated value of different stock types dependent on the customer, location, and material. Example: QTY*17*1000*EA~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*37: Use Work In Progress (Work In Progress Quantity) as the inventory that has begun the manufacturing process and is no longer included in raw materials inventory, but is not yet a completed product. On a balance sheet, work in progress (WIP) is considered to be an asset because money has been spent towards a completed product. Example: QTY*37*10*EA~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*57 and QTY*70: Use Minimum Order Quantity (57) and Maximum Order Quantity (70) (Order Quantity minimum and maximum) paired as the quantity range the customer must order. The trading partners are alerted if the order quantity is not within the required quantity range during order entry. Example: QTY*57*1*EA~ QTY*70*10000*EA~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*3Y: Use Subcontracting Stock Transfer In as the quantity of inventory of stock that has been transferred to a vendor of type subcontracting using a special movement type. Examples: QTY*3Y*15*EA>1~ QTY*3Y*15*EA>1~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*33: Use Quantity Available for Sale (Unrestricted Use Quantity) as the quantity of inventory that is unrestricted stock, which is the physical stock that is always available at a plant/storage location that can be consumed for stock movements and available for material requirements planning. Examples: QTY*33*14*EA>1~ QTY*33*14*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*69: Use the Incremental Quantity as the quantity to increment (add to) stock. Examples: QTY*69*200*EA>1~ QTY*69*200*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ -- 2 of 10 -- 830 Planning Schedule with Release Capability Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.15 Nov-21, 2025 © 2017-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 23 QTY O >1 Quantity QTY*72: Use Minimum Stock Level (Required Minimum Quantity) as the minimum stock level at which the stock must be maintained. Examples: QTY*72*50*EA>1~ QTY*72*50*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*73: Use Maximum Stock Level (Required Maximum Quantity) as the maximum stock level at which the stock must be maintained. Examples: QTY*73*800*EA>1~ QTY*73*800*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*77: Use Stock Transfer In as the quantity of inventory that is moving between plants or from one company code to another. Examples: QTY*77*25*EA>1~ QTY*77*25*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*IQ: Use In-Transit Quantity (Intransit Quantity) as the quantity of a material that was withdrawn from the stock of the issuing plant but has not yet arrived at the receiving plant. Example: QTY*IQ*200*EA~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*QH: Use Quantity on Hold (Blocked Quantity) as the quantity of inventory that is blocked stock, which is not counted as unrestricted stock. Examples: QTY*QH*10*EA>1~ QTY*QH*10*EA>2~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ QTY*XT: Use Protected Quantity (Quality Inspection Quantity) as the the quantity of inventory that is under quality inspection. All rights reserved. 31 FST M 1 Forecast Schedule Example: FST*100*D*F*20160101*20160131***REC*plannedReceipt~ To specify the forecasted dates and quantities. *UserNote FST (Time Series Type): FST09 in combination with FST08="REC" is required if FST02=D to indicate the replenishment Time Series Type for Forecast and SMI processes. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ FST09="forecastConfirmation": Used as a reply of a former 830 Forecast Time Series Type (where FST08="13") to specify the total quantity that the supplier wants to deliver to the customer in the period so that the total demand from the customer is covered. Only in this case it is also allowed to use FST02=C without FST08 and FST09. Examples: FST*100*C*F*20170605*20170606~ or FST*100*D*F*20170605*20170606***REC*forecastConfirmation~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ FST09="supplierForecast": Used as a forecast created by the supplier based on the Demand Supply situation in the backend ERP system. Typically, the supplier creates the forecast for components based on the Finished Goods Demand. Only in this case it is also allowed to use FST02=D without FST08 and FST09. Examples: FST*100*D*F*20170605*20170606~ or FST*100*D*F*20170605*20170606***REC*supplierForecast~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ FST09="capacityConfirmation": Used as the quantity of production output of a specific resource that supplier commits to attain. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Planning Schedule with Release Capability (830) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Planning Schedule with Release Capability Messages from Buyers in the form of the cXML OrderRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 830 Planning Schedule with Release Capability document. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1), but it does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- 830 Planning Schedule with Release Capability (Order) Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.12 Feb-26, 2026 © 2020-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Planning Schedule with Release Capability (830) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Planning Schedule with Release Capability Messages from SAP Business Network Buyers in the form of the cXML ProductActivityMessage. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 830 Planning Schedule with Release Capability document. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1), but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. This transaction set can be used by a transportation carrier to provid e shippers, consignees, and their agents with the status of shipments in terms of dates, times, locations, route, identif ying numbers, and conveyance. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Transportation Carrier Shipment Status Messages by means of the cXML TransportConf irmation document conf orm to its rules. As a service to Logistic Service Providers pref erring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps f rom the ANSI X12 004010 Transportation Carrier Shipment Status Message document. Logistic Service Providers can select ANSI X12 as their pref erred method f or sending Transportation Carrier Shipment Status Message documents. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1) but does require a 997 to be returned f or each f unctional group received (other than type FA). Date/Time Note: Note that a complete date/time/zone is recommended. Otherwise it will be automatically calculated and might lead to wrong data. Timestamps in cXML are represented as a date with a time, and an offset to UTC. If you do not specify a time, it will be taken as noon (12:00) on the date specified. AT7*AV: Use status "Collected" if the requested consignment is collected and ready to be shipped. It is recommended to provide updated or new information, such as transport related dates (AT703, AT705 - AT707), Carrier reference number (L11*CN) and tracking information (L11**2I) and/or dimensions (AT8). Transport related dates should only be used if status is "Acc epted" or "Collected". Destination location related date (AT705 - AT707): AT7*XB*AG and AT7*AV*AG:: Use "Consignee Related" for the expected delivery date for the material to be received at the partner location. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example f iles used in this guide are examples only. In the f ollowing chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally , you will f ind a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation f ocuses on an explicit version, i.e. , the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draf t Standard f or Trial Use contains the f ormat and establishes the data contents of the Receiving Advice/Acceptance Certif icate Transaction Set (861) f or use within the context of an Electronic Data Inter- change (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide f or customary and established busi - ness and industry practice relative to the notif ication of receipt or f ormal acceptance of goods and services. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Receiving Advice/Acceptance Certif icate Messages to Buyers in the f orm of the cXML ReceiptRequest Messages. As a service to Suppliers pref erring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 861 Receiving Advice/Acceptance Certif icate document. On receiving the 861 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML ReceiptRequest. The f inal cXML document is internally posted to perf orm the notif ication of receipt or return of goods and services . If an error arises at the application level, an email notif ication is sent to the Supplier, advising the f ailure and the reason. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetition of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Receiving Advice/Acceptance Certificate Transaction Set (861) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide for customary and established business and industry practice relative to the notification of receipt or formal acceptance of goods and services. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Receiving Advice/Acceptance Certificate Messages from SAP Business Network Buyers in the form of the cXML ReceiptRequest Messages. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 861 Receiving Advice/Acceptance Certificate document. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1), but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- 861 Receiving Advice/Acceptance Certificate Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.13 Oct-21, 2025 © 2017-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Warehouse Stock Transfer Receipt Advice Transaction Set (944) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used by a receiving location to advise a depositor or an agent of the depositor that a transfer shipment has been received. This transaction set provides the depositor or the depositor's agent with detail information concerning product that has been received. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Warehouse Stock Transfer Receipt Advice to Buyers in the form of the cXML ReceiptRequest documents. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 944 Warehouse Stock Transfer Receipt Advice document. On receiving the 944 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML ReceiptRequest. The final cXML document is internally posted to perform the actual fulfillment update. If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Warehouse Stock Transfer Receipt Advice Transaction Set (944) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide for customary and established business and industry practice relative to the placement of purchase orders for goods and services. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Warehouse Stock Transfer Receipt Advice from Buyer in the form of cXML ReceiptRequest documents. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 944 Warehouse Stock Transfer Receipt Advice document. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1) but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Report of Test Results (863) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Report of Test Results Messages from Buyers in the form of the cXML QualityInspectionDecisionRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 863 Report of Test Results (QualityInspectionDecision) document. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1), but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Report of Test Results (863) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Report of Test Results Messages from Buyers in the form of the cXML QualityInspectionRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 863 Report of Test Results (QualityInspectionRequest) document. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1) but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. Otherwise it is not used. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *UserNote (PSD C001_649_1): Characteristic type A buyer uses inspection characteristics to describe the inspection criteria for materials, parts, and products. This allows the buyer to plan inspections systematically, uniformly, and economically. An inspection request can contain different types of characteristics, some required, optional, or conditional. Supported values are: "1": required - The inspection of this characteristic is required to create an inspection decision. "2": optional - The inspection of this characteristic is not required to create an inspection decision. "3": afterAccept - This conditional inspection characteristic must be inspected if the previous required characteristic was accepted. "4": afterRejection - This conditional inspection characteristic must be inspected if the previous required characteristic was rejected. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *UserNote (PSD C001_1018_2): Quantitative indicator "1" indicates that this characteristic uses a numerical measurement. Otherwise it is not used. In that case the characteristic uses a non-numerical, qualitative measurement. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *UserNote (PSD C001_649_2): Recording type It indicates how the valuation will be sent for this characteristic. Supported values are: "1": singleResult - Single values for each inspection characteristic. "2": summarizedRecording - Summarized values for each inspection characteristic. "3": noCharacteristicRecording - No characteristic record. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Report of Test Results (863) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Report of Test Results to Buyers in the form of the cXML QualityInspectionResultRequest. This is a fulfillment document to the cXML QualityInspectionRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 863 Report of Test Results (QualityInspectionResult) document. On receiving the 863 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML QualityInspectionResultRequest. The final cXML document is internally posted to perform the actual fulfillment update. If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. SAP Business Network does not currently implement the 824 Application Advice. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Price/Sales Catalog Transaction Set (832) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Sales Catalog Messages to Buyers in the form of the CIF file embedded in the cXML message CatalogUploadRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 832 Sales Catalog document. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Ship Notice/Manifest Transaction Set (856) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to list the contents of a shipment of goods as well as additional information relating to the shipment, such as order information, product description, physical characteristics, type of packaging, marking, carrier information, and configuration of goods within the transportation equipment. The transaction set enables the sender to describe the contents and configuration of a shipment in various levels of detail and provides an ordered flexibility to convey information. The sender of this transaction is the organization responsible for detailing and communicating the contents of a shipment, or shipments, to one or more receivers of the transaction set. The receiver of this transaction set can be any organization having an interest in the contents of a shipment or information about the contents of a shipment. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Ship Notices to Buyers in the form of the cXML ShipNoticeRequest. This is a fulfillment document to the cXML OrderRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 856 Ship Notice / Manifest document. On receiving the 856 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML ShipNoticeRequest. The final cXML document is internally posted to perform the actual fulfillment update. If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. Depending of the code entered on BSN05 you can send the packaging hierarchy superordinated (0001) or subordinated (0002) to the item hierarchy. Note that using the HL Tare loop at this place is only allowed, if you use and indicate the Standard Pack Structure with 0002. If you use the Pick and Pack Structure with 0001, please refer to the documented "Hierarchical Level - Tare (BSN05 = 0001)" loop before the HL Item loop. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ The Tare level is optional in general, but if it is used then always as a parent level in combination with the following Pack level (child level). Packaging information at this level specifies the 1st level of packaging in this ASN (e.g. pallet level). All rights reserved. 142 856 MESSAGE STRUCTURES – HIERARCHICAL STRUCTURE CODE (BSN05) This Implementation Guideline provides 3 different options to structure an ANSI X12 856 message, which SAP Business Network sends to the Buyer in the form of a cXML ShipNoticeRequest document. Note: To ensure that the Buyer receives the correct cXML ShipNoticeRequest document structure including all content, it is strongly recommended to use the destined indicator “Hierarchical Structure Code” (BSN05) via Segment BSN at Element 1005 on the ANSI X12 856 message. Option 1 (Simple Structure) BSN05 = 0004 for Shipment, Order, Item In the simple structure format, no packaging levels - neither Pack nor Tare HL loops - are indicated. The Item HL loop is the only detail information sent, listing the purchase order line items that were shipped. This format does not include any unique identification of logistic handling units or any packaging hierarchy. It is used as the default structure if the BSN05 element is not used. [Note Default Structure*] Packaging information in this case is optional and limited to only a general description of the packaging form and its physical dimensions on item hierarchy. Option 2 (Pick and Pack Structure) BSN05 = 0001 for Shipment, Order, Packaging, Item In the pick and pack structure format, packaging levels - Tare and/or Pack HL loops - are mandatory. The item level information is subordinated to the packaging level. A shipped line item can appear multiple times in the message for the same purchase order line item if it is separated into multiple packages. A shipped line item always relates to a unique package with its respective dispatch quantity per pack. In this case packaging information on tare and/or pack hierarchy must include the label / SSCC as the unique identification of the logistic handling unit and the packaging form and/or its physical dimensions. BSN05 = 0001 is mandatory Option 3 (Standard Pack Structure) BSN05 = 0002 for Shipment, Order, Item, Packaging In the standard pack structure format, packaging levels - tare and/or pack HL loops – are mandatory. The package level information is subordinated to the item level. The purchase order line items that were shipped are listed with their total shipped quantity. Each related package is transmitted subsequently with its dispatch quantity of this item at HL Pack loop. In this case packaging information on tare and/or pack hierarchy must include the label / SSCC as the unique identification of the logistic handling unit and the packaging form and/or its physical dimensions. BSN05 = 0002 is mandatory [Note Default Structure*] If you use Tare and/or Pack HL loops in your message, you must enter the correct code 0001 or 0002 according to the hierarchical structure of your message. If you do not enter a code, SAP Business Network defaults it to Simple Structure (0004 = Shipment, Order, Item). -- 2 of 10 -- 856 Ship Notice/Manifest Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 3.2 Aug-28, 2025 © 2017-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 143 HIERARCHICAL LOOPS The 856 uses hierarchical loops (HL) to represent the supplier’s physical shipment in electronic form to identify dependencies among and the content of hierarchically related groups of data segments. The HL segment is used to identify levels of detail information using a hierarchical structure, such as relating line-item data to order data. The HL segment defines a top-down/left-right ordered structure. ▪ HL01 shall contain a unique alphanumeric number for each occurrence of the HL segment in the transaction set. For example, HL01 could be used to indicate the number of occurrences of the HL segment, in which case the value of HL01 would be "1" for the initial HL segment and would be incremented by one in each subsequent HL segment within the transaction. ▪ HL02 identifies the hierarchical ID number of the HL segment to which the current HL segment is subordinate. ▪ HL03 indicates the context of the series of segments following the current HL segment up to the next occurrence of an HL segment in the transaction. For example, HL03 is used to indicate that subsequent segments in the HL loop form a logical grouping of data referring to shipment, order, or item-level information. ▪ HL04 indicates whether or not there are subordinate (or child) HL segments related to the current HL segment. -- 3 of 10 -- 856 Ship Notice/Manifest Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 3.2 Aug-28, 2025 © 2017-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 16 BSN M 1 Beginning Segment for Ship Notice Example: BSN*00*Ship Notice ID*20160111*131459*0001*PL*B44~ This segment is used to identify and specify a message. BSN01: A "replace" Ship Notice (BSN01=05) allows a supplier to correct an error in a Ship Notice or to add additional information learned later. In either case, a "replace" document must be complete: All data from the original should be discarded by the recipient. A "replace" Ship Notice must have the same shipment identification number (SID) (BSN02) as the previous version of the notice. This provides an unambiguous and direct connection between all versions of the Ship Notice. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ BSN02: This value does not vary as a particular Ship Notice is updated. (BSN01=03) or (BSN0=05) describing the same shipment must share a SID with the "original" Ship Notice (BSN01=00). Examples: BSN*00*Original SID1*20160111*131459*0004*PL*B44~ BSN*05*Original SID1*20160111*131459*0004*PL*B44~ BSN*03*Original SID1*20160111*131459*0004*PL*B44~ In case of delete / cancellation (BSN01="03") the original SID value you sent via BSN01 will be automatically updated by the SAP Business Network with the attachment of "_1" for further functionality. BSN*03*Original SID1*20160111*131459*0004*PL*B44~ leads to shipmentID value "Original SID1_1" in the SAP Business Network. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ BSN03/04: It is recommended to additionally use DTM*111 for the notice date. Please refer to segment "DTM Date/Time" either at header or at HL Shipment level. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *User Note (BSN05) If you use Tare and/or Pack HL loops in your message, you must enter the correct code 0001 or 0002 according to the hierarchical structure of your message. If you do not enter a code, SAP Business Network defaults it to Simple Structure (0004 = Shipment, Order, Item). Read more about it here: _____________________________________________________________________________________________ For the supported structures and how to use BSN05 correctly, please refer to this subsequent section within this document: 856 MESSAGE STRUCTURES – HIERARCHICAL STRUCTURE CODE (BSN05) For HL loop usage description and examples, please refer to these subsequent sections within this document: HIERARCHICAL LOOPS HIERARCHICAL LOOPS EXAMPLES For packaging usage description and examples, please refer to this subsequent section within this document: DOCUMENTED EXAMPLE -- 6 of 10 -- 856 Ship Notice/Manifest Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 3.2 Aug-28, 2025 © 2017-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. Example: DTM*011*20160111*141010*ET~ To specify pertinent dates and times. Date/Time Note: Note that a complete date/time/zone is recommended. Otherwise it will be automatically calculated and might lead to wrong data. Timestamps in cXML are represented as a date with a time, and an offset to UTC. If you do not specify a time, it will be taken as noon (12:00) on the date specified. If you do not specify the time code (zone), then it will be defaulted to UTC (+00:00). _____________________________________________________________________________________________ It is allowed to send date/time information either here or at HL Shipment level. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ The Shipped Date (DTM*011) is mandatory, except for "deletion" (BSN01=03). The Estimated Delivery Date (DTM*017) is mandatory, except for "deletion" (BSN01=03). The Manifest/Ship Notice (DTM*111) is actually optional, as it must be sent in BSN03 (Date) and BSN04 (Time). However, it is recommended to use DTM*111 with DTM04 (time zone) to achieve an exact result. Other dates are optional. All rights reserved. 21 HL M 200000 Hierarchical Level - Shipment TD1 O 20 Carrier Details (Total Number of Packaging) Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage 01 103 Packaging Code O AN 3/5 O AN 3/5 Code identifying the type of packaging (3 or 3+2 characters) If the Data Element is used, then Part 1 is always required.* Part 1 (1-3): Packaging Form - mandatory Part 2 (4-5): Packaging Material - optional Please refer to APPENDIX - CODELISTS 103 Packaging Code. 02 80 Lading Quantity C N0 1/7 C N0 1/7 Total number of packaging Example: TD1*PLT*1~ To specify the transportation details relative to commodity, total number of packaging. This TD1 segment can be used only for the count of packages in the message. Do not mix with weight or volume information. For weight and volume information, please refer to the respective TD1 segments. If your packaging hierarchy includes only 1 level, e.g. non-palletized cartons, only 1 TD1 segment is allowed. You can repeat the segment if your packaging hierarchy includes 2 levels, e.g. cartons unto pallets. In this case it is strongly recommended to send the first TD1 for the parent packaging level, e.g. pallets, followed by a second TD1 for the child level, e.g. cartons. TD101: The packaging type is not required and will be ignored. You can optionally send it, but you should either send MXD or an empty value in case the Packaging Code is different throughout the message per package level. Examples: Example - 4 cartons (1 level) TD1*CTN*4~ Example - 1 carton and 3 boxes (1 level) TD1*MXD*4~ or TD1**4~ Example - 2 pallets (parent level), 4 cartons (child level) TD1*PLT*2~ TD1*CTN*4~ Example - 2 pallets (parent level), 1 carton and 3 boxes (child level) TD1*PLT*2~ TD1*MXD*4~ or TD1*PLT*2~ TD1**4~ -- 1 of 10 -- 856 Ship Notice/Manifest Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 3.2 Aug-28, 2025 © 2017-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. It is recommended to use this TD1 segment for the total gross and net weight only. But instead of TD1 is also allowed to use the preceding MEA segment for the same. However, do not mix it with the TD1 segments for total number of packaging or volume information. For total number of packaging and volume information, please refer to the respective TD1 segments. Some call it a way bill number, others call it a PRO number, and still others call it a bill of lading. They all represent tracking numbers. If carrier information is being supplied here, the identification of the carrier is required. Both the coded identification (TD502-03) and the carrier name (TD505) are required in combination with the tracking number. You can also provide the URL and the date related to the tracking number (TD508). Please refer to the REF*CN segment in this guideline. Example: DTM*011*20160111*141010*ET~ To specify pertinent dates and times. Date/Time Note: Note that a complete date/time/zone is recommended. Otherwise it will be automatically calculated and might lead to wrong data. Timestamps in cXML are represented as a date with a time, and an offset to UTC. If you do not specify a time, it will be taken as noon (12:00) on the date specified. If you do not specify the time code (zone), then it will be defaulted to UTC (+00:00). _____________________________________________________________________________________________ It is allowed to send date/time information either here or at main header. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ The Shipped Date (DTM*011) is mandatory, except for "deletion" (BSN01=03). The Estimated Delivery Date (DTM*017) is mandatory, except for "deletion" (BSN01=03). The Manifest/Ship Notice (DTM*111) is actually optional, as it must be sent in BSN03 (Date) and BSN04 (Time). However, it is recommended to use DTM*111 with DTM04 (time zone) to achieve an exact result. Other dates are optional. Example: DTM*011*20160111*1410*ET~ DTM*017*20160112*1400*ET~ DTM*111*20160111*131459*ET~ -- 1 of 10 -- 856 Ship Notice/Manifest Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 3.2 Aug-28, 2025 © 2017-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements f or digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 f ormat. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example f iles used in this guide are examples only. In the f ollowing chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally , you will f ind a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation f ocuses on an explicit version, i.e. , the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draf t Standard f or Trial Use contains the f ormat and establishes the data contents of the Ship Notice/Manif est Transaction Set (856) f or use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (E DI) environment. The transaction set can be used to list the contents of a shipment of goods as well as additional inf ormation relating to the shipment, such as order inf ormation, product description, physical characteristics, type of packaging, marking, carrier inf ormation, and conf iguration of goods within the transportation equipment. The transaction set enables the sender to describe the contents and conf iguration of a shipment in various levels of detail and provides an ordered f lexibility to convey inf ormation. The sender of this transaction is the organization responsible f or detailing and communicating the contents of a shipment, or shipments, to one or more receivers of the transaction set. The receiver of this transaction set can be any organizatio n having an interest in the contents of a shipment or inf ormation about the contents of a shipment. NOTES Copy Ship Notice SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Ship Notices to Buyers in the f orm of the cXML ShipNoticeRequest. This is a f ulf illment document to the cXML OrderRequest. As a service to send a Copy Ship Notice to other members in the supply chain pref erring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network converts the cXML document to the ANSI X12 004010 856 Ship Notice / Manif est document. Component Shipment SAP Business Network receives Ship Notices f rom Buyers in the f orm of the cXML ShipNoticeRequest. This is a f ulf illment document to the cXML OrderRequest. As a service to (Component) Suppliers pref erring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network converts the cXML document to the ANSI X12 004010 856 Ship Notice / Manif est document. All rights reserved. 123 856 MESSAGE STRUCTURES – HIERARCHICAL STRUCTURE CODE (BSN05) This Implementation Guideline currently provides 3 dif f erent options to structure an ANSI X12 856 message, which SAP Business Network receives in the f orm of a cXML ShipNoticeRequest document. Option 1 (Simple Structure) BSN05 = 0004 for Shipment, Order, Item In the simple structure f ormat, no packaging levels - neither Pack nor Tare HL loops - are indicated. The Item HL loop is the only detail inf ormation sent, listing the purchase order line items that were shipped. This f ormat does not include any unique identif ication of logistic handling units or any packaging hierarchy. It is used as the def ault structure if packaging is not used. Packaging inf ormation in this case is optional and limited to only a general description of the packaging f orm and its physical dimensions on item hierarchy. Option 2 (Pick and Pack Structure) BSN05 = 0001 for Shipment, Order, Packaging, Item In the pick and pack structure f ormat, packaging levels - Tare and/or Pack HL loops - are mandatory. The item level inf ormation is subordinated to the packaging level. A shipped line item can appear multiple times in the message f or the same purchase order line item if it is separated into multiple packages. A shipped line item always relates to a unique package with its respective dispatch quantity per pack. In this case packaging inf ormation on tare and/or pack hierarchy must include the label / SSCC as the unique identif ication of the logistic handling unit and the packaging f orm and/or its physical dimensions. BSN05 = 0001 is mandatory Option 3 (Standard Pack Structure) BSN05 = 0002 for Shipment, Order, Item, Packaging In the standard pack structure f ormat, packaging levels - tare and/or pack HL loops – are mandatory. The package level inf ormation is subordinated to the item level. The purchase order line items that were shipped are listed with their total shipped quantity. Each related package is transmitted subsequently with its dispatch quantity of this item at HL Pack loop. In this case packaging inf ormation on tare and/or pack hierarchy must include the label / SSCC as the unique identif ication of the logistic handling unit and the packaging f orm and/or its physical dimensions. BSN05 = 0002 is mandatory -- 3 of 10 -- 856 Ship Notice/Manif est Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.9 Feb-19, 2024 © 2019-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 124 HIERARCHICAL LOOPS The 856 uses hierarchical loops (HL) to represent the supplier’s physical shipment in electronic f orm to identif y dependencies among and the content of hierarchically related groups of data segments . The HL segment is used to identif y levels of detail inf ormation using a hierarchical structure, such as relating line-item data to order data. The HL segment def ines a top-down/lef t-right ordered structure. ▪ HL01 shall contain a unique alphanumeric number f or each occurrence of the HL segment in the transaction set. For example, HL01 could be used to indicate the number of occurrences of the HL segment, in which case the value of HL01 would be "1" f or the initial HL segment and would be incremented by one in each subsequent HL segment within the transaction. ▪ HL02 identif ies the hierarchical ID number of the HL segment to which the current HL segment is subordinate. ▪ HL03 indicates the context of the series of segments f ollowing the current HL segment up to the next occurrence of an HL segment in the transaction. For example, HL03 is used to indicate that subsequent segments in the HL loop f orm a logical grouping of data ref erring to shipment, order, or item-level inf ormation. ▪ HL04 indicates whether or not there are subordinate (or child) HL segments related to the current HL segment. -- 4 of 10 -- 856 Ship Notice/Manif est Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.9 Feb-19, 2024 © 2019-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 15 BSN M 1 Beginning Segment for Ship Notice Example: BSN*00*Ship Notice ID*20190111*131459*0001*PL*B44~ This segment is used to identify and specify a message. BSN01: A "replace" Ship Notice (BSN01=05) allows to correct an error in a Ship Notice or to add additional information learned later. In either case, a "replace" document is complete: All data from the original should be discarded by the recipient. A "replace" Ship Notice has always the same shipment identification number (SID) (BSN02) as the previous version of the notic e. This provides an unambiguo us and direct connection between all versions of the Ship Notice. A "duplicate" Ship Notice (BSN01=07) indicates the copy of the original Ship Notice to another member in the supply chain. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ BSN02: This value does not vary as a particular Ship Notice is updated. (BSN01=03) or (BSN0=05) describing the same shipment always share a SID with the "original" Ship Notice (BSN01=00). Examples component shipment from a buyer to a supplier: BSN*00*Original SID1*20190111*131459*0004*PL*B44~ BSN*05*Original SID1*20190111*131459*0004*PL*B44~ BSN*03*Original SID1*20190111*131459*0004*PL*B44~ Example copy ship notice from SAP Business Network to another member in the supply chain: BSN*07*Original SID1*20190111*131459*0004*PL*B44~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ *User Note (BSN05) Depending upon your preference and if packaging is used, it is indicated by the Pick and Pack Structure (0001 = Shipment, Order, Packaging, Item) or the Standard Pack Structure (0002 = Shipment, Order, Item, Packaging). Packaging is sent via Tare and/or Pack HL loops in this message. Otherwise, SAP Business Network defaults it to the Simple Structure (0004 = Shipment, Order, Item). INTRODUCTION This Draf t Standard f or Trial Use contains the f ormat and establishes the data contents of the Motor Carrier Load Tender (204) f or use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. This transaction set can be used to allow shippers or other interested parties to of f er (tender) a shipment to a f ull load (truckload) motor carrier including detailed scheduling, equipment requi rements, commodities, and shipping instructions pertinent to a load tender. It is not to be used to provide a motor carrier with data relative to a Less-than-Truckload bill of lading, pick-up notif ication, or manif est. NOTES SAP Business Network sends Transport Instruction Messages by means of the cXML TransportRequest document conf orm to its rules. As a service to Logistic Service Providers pref erring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 Motor Carrier Load Tender document. Logistic Service Providers can select ANSI X12 as their pref erred method f or receiving Instruction Motor Carrier Load Tender documents. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1), but does require a 997 to be returned f or each f unctional group received (other than type FA). All rights reserved. 15 L11 O 50 Business Instructions and Reference Number Example: L11*trackingNumber*CN*Carrier Shipment ID~ To specify instructions in this business relationship or a reference number. L1102=CI: The Unique Consignment Identifier is always required and must be returned in the transport confirmation 204 via LX/AT7/L11**CI. It is the mandatory and unique identifier for this consignment, which is a collection of packages going f rom a single originating party to a single destination party. The collection of packages or consignment items are specified in detail via S5 loop where the Stop Sequence Number (S501) > 0. Example: L11*Consignment ID*CI~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ L1102=CN: Carrier's Reference Number (PRO/Invoice) If already known this segment is used to identify the carrier assigned shipment identifier in L1103. In this case L1101 specifies the related type or domain, e.g. trackingNumber. Example: L11*trackingNumber*CN*Carrier Shipment ID~ L1102=2I: Tracking Number If already known this segment can be used to provide the URL of the related tracki ng number (L11**CN) in L1103. In this case L1101 specifies the related Tracking number date. Example: L11*20160111*2I*Tracking URL Text' _____________________________________________________________________________________________ L1102=UN: Hazard information: If hazard information is used, 2 segments L11**UN are present. L11*Hazard Description*UN is used for gen eral dangerous goods description in L1103. In this case L1101 is used as a hardcoded value to indicate the description. L11*Domain*UN is used for additional dangerous goods classification. In this case L1101 is used as a text identification to specify the domain responsible for the classification (code) in L1103. Examples: L11*Hazard Description*UN*Hazard Description TEXT~ L11*UNDG*UN*Hazard Classification~ or L11*Hazard Description*UN*Flammable liquids, toxic, n.o.s~ L11*UNDG*UN*1992~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Special reference numbers related to this transport request and the transport logistic process chain: L1102=SI: The Shipper's Identifying Number for Shipment (SID) L1102=BM: The Bill of Lading Number L1102=6A: The Consignee Reference Number Examples: L11*SID*SI~ L11*Bill Of Lading ID*BM~ L11*Consignee Reference ID*6A~ _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Optional document message numbers and dates from former messages related to this transport request within the whole process chain and further optional reference numbers and dates related to former messages, such as: L1102=AH: The Agreement Number -> Example: L11*Agreement ID*AH~ L1102=PO: The Purchase Order Number to relate to a former 850 -> Example: L11*Purchase Order ID*PO~ -- 5 of 10 -- 204 Motor Carrier Load Tender Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.9 Feb-19, 2024 © 2017-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Motor Carrier Load Tender (204) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. This transaction set can be used to allow shippers or other interested parties to offer (tender) a shipment to a full load (truckload) motor carrier including detailed scheduling, equipment requirements, commodities, and shipping instructions pertinent to a load tender. It is not to be used to provide a motor carrier with data relative to a Less-than-Truckload bill of lading, pick-up notification, or manifest. NOTES SAP Business Network sends Transport Instruction Messages by means of the cXML TransportRequest document conform to its rules. The cXML TransportRequest document can contain multiple Consignment loops. As a service to Logistic Service Providers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 204 004010 Motor Carrier Load Tender document. Logistic Service Providers can select ANSI X12 as their preferred method for receiving Instruction Motor Carrier Load Tender documents. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1) but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- 204 Motor Carrier Load Tender (Multi-Consignment) Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.0 Sep-20, 2024 © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. If the buyer does not provide an own identifaction, then the same sequential consignment counter from S501 is sent in L1101. -- 1 of 10 -- 204 Motor Carrier Load Tender (Multi-Consignment) Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.0 Sep-20, 2024 © 2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. Conceptually, this is a tracking number. Different carriers have different domains for shipment identifiers. Some call it a way bill number, others call it a PRO number, and still others call it a bill of lading. They all represent tracking numbers. If a Postal Address City or the two-char ISO-3166 Country Code via N4 segment is used, then one Street (N301) is also used. *UserNote (State or Province Code) If the country code (N404) is US or CA, then the state or province code (N402) is also required and must be a valid state or province digraph. If the country code (N404) is not US or CA, then the state or province code must not be used on (N402). In that case the state or province code can optional be specified by using N406, always in combination with N405="SP". All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Production Sequence Transaction Set (866) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Production Sequence Messages to Buyers in the form of the cXML ComponentConsumptionRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 866 Production Sequence document. On receiving the 866 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML ComponentConsumptionRequest. The final cXML document is internally posted to process the actual Production Sequence. If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. SAP Business Network does not currently implement the 824 Application Advice. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Shipping Schedule (862) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. NOTES SAP Business Network receives Shipping Schedule from Buyers in the form of cXML OrderRequest documents. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network maps to the ANSI X12 004010 862 Shipping Schedule document. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1), but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard ANSI X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- 862 Shipping Schedule Outbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.22 Sep-25, 2025 © 2016-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company.
