All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are actually used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Warehouse Shipping Advice Transaction Set (945) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide for customary and established business and industry practice relative to the placement of purchase orders for goods and services. NOTES SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Ship Notices to Buyers in the form of the cXML ShipNoticeRequest. This is a fulfillment document to the cXML OrderRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network accepts the ANSI X12 004010 945 Warehouse Shipping Advice document. On receiving the 945 (documented here), SAP Business Network validates the EDI content, returns a 997 to the Supplier, and converts it to the cXML ShipNoticeRequest. The final cXML document is internally posted to perform the actual fulfillment update. If an error arises at the application level, an email notification is sent to the Supplier, advising the failure and the reason. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard X12 Rules, defined in 004010, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional O Optional Optional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- 945 Warehouse Shipping Advice Inbound Version ANSI X12 004010 Implementation Guideline 1.9 Dec-01, 2025 © 2021-2025 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. Each nested 0310 loop "Item Loop" represents either items associated with that package when packaging is used or items within the transaction set when packaging is not used. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the ANSI X.12 format. Initially the used segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION This Draft Standard for Trial Use contains the format and establishes the data contents of the Warehouse Shipping Advice Transaction Set (945) for use within the context of an Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) environment. The transaction set can be used to provide for customary and established business and industry practice relative to the placement of purchase orders for goods and services. NOTES Copy Warehouse Shipping Advice SAP Business Network allows Suppliers to send Warehouse Shipping Advice documents to Buyers in the form of the cXML ShipNoticeRequest. This is a fulfillment document to the cXML OrderRequest. As a service to send a Copy to other members in the supply chain preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network converts the cXML document to the ANSI X12 004010 945 Warehouse Shipping Advice document. Warehouse Shipping Advice SAP Business Network receives Warehouse Shipping Advice documents from Buyers in the form of the cXML ShipNoticeRequest. This is a fulfillment document to the cXML OrderRequest. As a service to Suppliers preferring to transact via EDI, SAP Business Network converts the cXML document to the ANSI X12 004010 945 Warehouse Shipping Advice document. SAP Business Network does not require or accept interchange acknowledgements (TA1) but does require a 997 to be returned for each functional group received (other than type FA). INTRODUCTION CONTRL is a message syntactically acknowledging or rejecting, with error indication, a received interchange, functional group or message. A CONTRL message can be used to: a) acknowledge or reject a received interchange, functional group or message and list any errors contained therein, or b) acknowledge only the receipt of an interchange. This requires that the UNB, UNZ, and the UNA if used, be checked. All rights reserved. 4 PREFACE This document outlines the requirements for digital data interchange using the Edifact format. Initially the uses segments and their meaning within a message are described. The example files used in this guide are examples only. In the following chapter all segments are described in detail. Additionally, you will find a document example as well as a branching diagram. This documentation focuses on an explicit version, i.e., the segments are documented as they would possibly occur in practice. Thus, the maximum number of repetitions of the individual segments is limited to the ones which are used. This does, however, not constitute a limitation, but rather a more detailed description of the example used. INTRODUCTION CONTRL is a message syntactically acknowledging or rejecting, with error indication, a received interchange, functional group or message. A CONTRL message can be used to: a) acknowledge or reject a received interchange, functional group or message and list any errors contained therein, or b) acknowledge only the receipt of an interchange. This requires that the UNB, UNZ, and the UNA if used, be checked. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard Edifact Rules, defined in D.3, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- CONTRL Syntax and service report message Outbound Version UN/EDIFACT D3 Implementation Guideline 1.2 Mar-01, 2023 © 2018-2023 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. INTRODUCTION A message claiming payment for goods or services supplied under conditions agreed between the seller and the buyer. The United Nations Standard Invoice Message, with correct data qualification, serves also as the specification for Debit Note and Credit Note messages. Throughout this document, the reference to 'Invoice' may be interpreted as conveying the wider meaning of 'Invoice/Credit Note/Debit Note'. SAP Business Network implements invoices with the cXML InvoiceDetailRequest document. The INVOIC implementation must ultimately map to an InvoiceDetailRequest and conform to its rules. There are two layout templates for invoices: Detailed (Regular Invoice) and Header Invoice. A detailed invoice addresses the line items of one purchase order. A header invoice covers many purchase orders without listing specific line items. There are three types of invoices: Standard, Credit Memo and Debit Memo. Each layout template and invoice type has particular requirements: content that must be present in order to be valid. There are also some content requirements for INVOIC itself to be satisfied. This document is intended to assist suppliers to start testing INVOIC messaging with the minimal requirements. It addresses the base data content for the invoice and what must be included in an INVOIC message. This document does not attempt to explain how every possible cXML construct is represented in the INVOIC. USING THIS GUIDELINE The DETAILED SEGMENT DESCRIPTION shows the Standard Edifact Rules, defined in D.01B, and the User Rules, recommended by SAP Business Network. Unused segments are not shown. The codes defining in detail Segment and Element usages are: Status Standard Usage SAP Business Network Usage M Mandatory Must Use / Required by SAP Business Network C Conditional Conditional X Not Used Not Used Descriptions for segments have been provided alongside and detailed explanation will follow in a future release. -- 4 of 10 -- INVOIC Invoice message Inbound Version UN/EDIFACT D.01B Implementation Guideline 1.15 Aug-12, 2024 © 2017-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 5 TRIANGULAR TRANSACTIONS VAT with Triangular Transactions involves integrating four things with a Tax Detail: 1) Tax Point Date, which refers to the date on which VAT becomes due. 2) Payment Date, which indicates the date when payment must be made. 3) Triangular Transaction indicator, that this VAT tax charge represents a triangular transaction. 4) Triangular Transaction Law Reference, a text string identifying the relevant triangulation law for the transaction. Since these data are not provided within the TAX group, they must be gathered from RFF group. To implement this, the TAX segment must have a category of VAT. TAX07 (3446) contains the relevant VAT Registration Number. An RFF group with qualifier VA contains a matching VAT Registration Number. This is how the RFF group is connected to the TAX group. The RFF group contains one of both DTM segments with qualifiers 131 and 140 to provide the dates. TAX03.01 (5289) may optionally contain the code "TT", which tags it as a Triangular Transaction. (Point 3 above.) TriangularTransactionLawReference is captured from FTX01(4451)="TXD" and FTX02(4453)="4". -- 5 of 10 -- INVOIC Invoice message Inbound Version UN/EDIFACT D.01B Implementation Guideline 1.15 Aug-12, 2024 © 2017-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 15 BGM M 1 Beginning of message Example: BGM+380+INVOIC ID+9' A segment by which the sender must uniquely identify the invoice by means of its type and number and when necessary its function. There are two layout templates of invoices: Regular and Summary. A regular invoice addresses the line items of one purchase order. A summary invoice covers many purchase orders without listing specific line items. There are three types of invoices: Standard, Credit Memo and Debit Memo. Every type can use the Regular or Summary layout. Credit Memos submitted in Regular form are called "Line Level Credit Memos", Debit Memos submitted in Regular form are called "Line Level Debit Memos"*. Summary Invoices reference one whole Purchase Order on each line item of the invoice. The line items of each Purchase Order are not detailed. Each Purchase Order being covered in a Header Invoice requires an occurrence of Group 26, LIN. Regular Invoices are identified by BGM document name code "380" [Standard Invoice] and by specifying order and/or master agreement identifications at the invoice header level. Summary Invoices are identified by BGM document name code "381" [Credit Note], "383" [Debit Note] or "385" [Standard Summary Invoice] and by NOT specifying any order and/or master agreement identifications at the invoice header level. Header level RFF segments identifying orders or master agreements must not be present. *User Note: (Line Level Debit Memo) is reserved for future use - not supported yet. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Example: Standard Invoice [Regular Form] BGM+380:::Document Name+RE12345+9' ... INVOIC D01B requires at least one NAD to identify the invoice sender. The recommended qualifier is II for “Issuer of invoice". If you wish to specify a distinctive Remit-To, then you should include qualifier RE. If either NAD+SF or NAD+ST is used, then the other is required. If NAD+CA is used, then NAD+SF and NAD+ST are both required. Note that only the Name (C058/3124) is actually required. The postal address is optional in itself and not required with most NAD groups, but it is recommended for NAD+SF and particularly NAD+ST if used. If any element from a Postal Address (NAD C080 - NAD 3207) is being provided, then Street (C059/3042), City (3164) and the two- char ISO-3166 Country code (3207) are all required and become mandatory. If the country code (3207) is US or CA, then the country-sub-entity (C819/3228) is also required. Within a postal address, party name (C080/3036) is supposed to represent specific recipient name(s) of a package or envelope. This may also include intra-office routing information, such as a department, a floor, office, or cube number. Use of party name (C080/3036) is entirely optional. The final recipient of goods (NAD+UD) is used for reporting Value-Added Tax (VAT) in a "Triangular Transaction". This party may be used with RFF (SG3) with qualifier VA ("VAT registration number"). In addition to this, DTM+89 can be used to provide a shipment tracking date. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Carrier identification number: This RFF can provide multiple identifiers for the same carrier. The use of an identification domain is required. All identification provided by RFF+CN must correspond to the same company. Please refer to APPENDIX - CODELISTS 6345 Currency identification code. 6343 Currency type code qualifier C an..3 C an..3 4 Invoicing currency Example: MOA+128:100.00:EUR:4' A segment specifying any monetary amounts relating to the product, e.g. item amount, insurance value, customs value. Subtotal amount (MOA+289) The invoice subtotal of the current line item (unit price times quantity). Optional for regular and summary invoices but mandatory for service items. Tax amount (MOA+176) The tax amount for the current line item (including taxes on shipping, and special handling charges). Optional for regular and summary invoices. Gross amount (MOA+128) The sum of subtotal, taxes, special handling, shipping and all other charges for the current line item, before discounts. Optional for regular and summary invoices. Net amount (MOA+203 / MOA+38) The gross amount minus allowances and discounts for the current line item. MOA+203 is used to provide net amount for regular invoices only. MOA+38 is used to provide net amount for summary invoices only. Optional for regular and summary invoices. Total line item amount without tax - (MOA+125). This element is used to summarize the total line item amount without tax. The total amount includes: Subtotal, shipping and special handling amount, total charges and total allowances (including discounts - ALC+A++++DI'). This element does not include taxes. -- 1 of 10 -- INVOIC Invoice message Inbound Version UN/EDIFACT D.01B Implementation Guideline 1.15 Aug-12, 2024 © 2017-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 76 NAD M 1 Name and address Example: NAD+CA+CA-ID::92+Name1:Name2:Name3:Name4:Name5+AddrName1:AddrName2:AddrName3:AddrName4:Add rName5+Street1:Street2:Street3:Street4+City+:::TX+Postcode+US' A segment identifying names and adresses of the parties, in coded or clear form, and their functions relevant to the line item. If either NAD+SF or NAD+ST is used, then the other is required. If NAD+CA is used, then NAD+SF and NAD+ST are both required. MF is used with regular invoices only, and is paired with MF in C212, in PIA. They must be used together. Note that only the Name (C058/3124) is actually required. The postal address is optional in itself and not required with most NAD groups, but it is recommended for NAD+SF and particularly NAD+ST if used. If any element from a Postal Address (NAD C080 - NAD 3207) is being provided, then Street (C059/3042), City (3164) and the two- char ISO-3166 Country code (3207) are all required and become mandatory. If the country code (3207) is US or CA, then the country-sub-entity (C819/3228) is also required. Within a postal address, party name (C080/3036) is supposed to represent specific recipient name(s) of a package or envelope. This may also include intra-office routing information, such as a department, a floor, office, or cube number. Use of party name (C080/3036) is entirely optional. -- 6 of 10 -- INVOIC Invoice message Inbound Version UN/EDIFACT D.01B Implementation Guideline 1.15 Aug-12, 2024 © 2017-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. All rights reserved. 79 RFF M 1 Reference - Additional carrier/shipment identification Example: RFF+CN:Tracking ID::trackingNumber' A segment identifying the reference by its number and where appropriate a line number within a document. This reference is used only with NAD+CA or NAD+SF and NAD+ST. If it is paired with NAD+CA it provides the carrier identification number. If it is used with NAD+SF and NAD+ST it identifies the carrier assigned reference number for their part of the shipment (shipment tracking number). In addition to this, DTM+89 can be used to provide a shipment tracking date. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Carrier identification number: This RFF can provide multiple identifiers for the same carrier. The use of an identification domain is required. All identification provided by RFF+CN must correspond to the same company. Example: NAD+CA++Carrier' RFF+CN:Legal company name::companyName' RFF+CN:Carrier ID-1::182' RFF+CN:Carrier ID-2::16' _____________________________________________________________________________________________ Carrier assigned reference number: Identifier that appears on this shipment and through which additional detail about the shipment may be retrieved. Defined by the carrier. Conceptually, this is a tracking number. Different carriers have different names for shipment identifiers. Some call it a way bill number, others call it a PRO number, and still others call it a bill of lading. They all represent tracking numbers. To specify more precisely what kind of identifier this is, a domain can apply. Example: NAD+SF++Ship-from' RFF+CN:Tracking ID-1::trackingNumber' DTM+89:20160203:102' RFF+CN:Tracking ID-2::billOfLading' DTM+89:20160203:102' -- 9 of 10 -- INVOIC Invoice message Inbound Version UN/EDIFACT D.01B Implementation Guideline 1.15 Aug-12, 2024 © 2017-2024 SAP SE or an SAP affiliate company. This document covers product-specific information only. For general information about SAP Business Technology Platform, see the documentation on SAP Help Portal at: https://help.sap.com/viewer/product/BTP/Cloud Target audience: administrators, consultants, users and others involved with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. 8 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Solution Owners Overview -- 8 of 66 -- 3 About Global Track and Trace The aim of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace is to capture, process and store tracking information about tracked business processes. Then, it allows business users to get real-time transparency of the execution of those processes. They can query any tracked process and display its retrieved data from end to end. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace is a cloud service solution based on SAP Business Technology Platform. It's integrated with the following SAP S/4HANA systems: • SAP S/4HANA (on-premise) • SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition Both two systems have the Transportation Management (TM) component embedded, which can work with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace.  Note The following documentation uses the term SAP S/4HANA to refer to both SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition and SAP S/4HANA (on-premise). If any of the information provided applies to only SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition or SAP S/4HANA, this will be clearly specified. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace offers a rich set of features. Some of the major highlights include: • a simple architecture that enables models with embedded logic (business rules) • built-in mapping support for documents from SAP S/4HANA systems It also features a streamlined modeling and tracking process that is intuitive and easier to use. It includes flexible logic (business rules) that can be embedded in the models together with new fully-integrated testing functionality with color-coded GUI-based end-to-end log tracing and drill down. If you've subscribed for the intelligent insights add-on for SAP Business Network, you can use it to get insights on your supply chain execution based on tracked process data. To learn how to set up the integration, see Setting Up Intelligent Insights for Global Track and Trace.  Note You can leverage SAP Analytics Cloud to perform real-time analysis on the tracked processes you’ve created. The Manage Analytic Models app from the intelligent insights add-on enables you to create highly customizable analytic models based on tracked processes. By using these models, you can create various analytic stories to achieve the best data-driven decision-making experience. For more information about SAP Analytics Cloud, see SAP Analytics Cloud. For more information about Manage Analytic Models, see Manage Analytic Models. Administration Guide for Solution Owners About Global Track and Trace PUBLIC 9 -- 9 of 66 -- 3.1 Technical Considerations Note that there are restrictions regarding the overall data volume that can be managed. Before starting your project, discuss your expected data volumes with your SAP technical contact. 3.2 Browser Support This application only supports the standard browsers supported by SAP Business Technology Platform. For more information, see the Browser Support chapter in Feature Scope Description for SAP BTP, Cloud Foundry, ABAP, and Kyma Environments. Root Certificate for End User UI The browser certificate store must contain both the old root certificate (DigiCert Global Root G2) and the new root certificate (DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5). Without this, the end user sign-in to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace will be impacted. To check if you are impacted, try to access the following URL: https://digicert-tls-rsa4096-root-g5.chain-demos.digicert.com . If your browser loads the page without warning, it trusts the DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 and no further action is required on your end. To ensure a smooth transition, you need to run the check and take action (where applicable) before April 23, 2026. Resolution for user sign-in to the BN4L Fiori Launchpad - How to import the certificate into my browser? The below steps might vary with the browser type and version: • Download Root Certificate [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ] and Intermediate Certificate [DigiCert G5 TLS RSA4096 SHA384 2021 CA1 ]. • Open Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. • Open settings and search for security in the search box and click on it. • Click on Manage Device Certificates / Manage Certificates. • Go to the Trusted Root Certification Authorities tab and Import Digi Certificates using the Import button at the bottom. • Go to the Intermediate Certification Authorities tab and Import Digi Certificates using the Import button at the bottom. • Ensure that DigiCert Root and Intermediate is added in the list. For more information, see Switch to DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5. 10 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Solution Owners About Global Track and Trace -- 10 of 66 -- 3.3 Product Availability This section describes certain product availability aspects. Administration Guide for Solution Owners Onboarding PUBLIC 13 -- 13 of 66 -- 4.1 Solution Owner Onboarding This section is applicable to customers who have purchased the SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace solution. It describes the technical steps needed to set up production use. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace is a solution deployed on SAP Business Technology Platform. You are entitled to use a global account on SAP BTP and create subaccounts in it. In your subaccount, you subscribe to the apps for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. You also configure roles and bundle them into role collections for user management. Task Overview  Note If you have any issues performing the tasks below, see Frequently Asked Questions [page 40]. The following tasks are necessary to set up the solution owner production or test tenant in SAP Business Network for Logistics: 1. Set up global account, create solution owner subaccount, and subscribe to apps: 1. Set Up Your Global Account [page 14] 2. Create a Subaccount [page 15] 3. Subscribe to Apps [page 17] 2. Create and authorize users: 1. Establish Trust Between Your Subaccount and Identity Authentication Tenant [page 18] 2. Create Users in Identity Authentication [page 21] 3. Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users [page 24] 4. Create a Technical User and Assign Role Collection [page 22] 3. Sign in, maintain business profile and technical user: • Sign In to the Network [page 33] • Maintain Technical User in the System Connections App [page 35] 4.1.1 Set Up Your Global Account Your global account on SAP Business Technology Platform is the entry point for managing the resources, landscape, and entitlements for your company and projects in a self-service manner. 14 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Solution Owners Onboarding -- 14 of 66 -- As your company's admin, you should have received a welcome email from SAP BTP for your global account. (If needed) Add Members to Your Global Account 4.1.2 Create a Subaccount Prerequisites You have the administrator role in the global account. Context You need a subaccount in your global account to subscribe apps for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. You cannot use the same subaccount to subscribe to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Administration Guide for Solution Owners Onboarding PUBLIC 15 -- 15 of 66 -- Procedure Follow the procedure in Create a Subaccount. When you specify the subaccount details, pay attention to the following: Field Description Display Name Enter a name for the subaccount. Use a name that is easy for you to distinguish. Description (Optional) Enter a description for your subaccount. Subdomain The subdomain will become part of the URL for accessing subscribed applications. The subdomain must be less than 50 characters. It can contain only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (not allowed at the beginning or at the end) and it must be unique within your global account. Do not start the subdomain with a digit if you are going to use solution owner apps for Global Track and Trace with this subaccount. Note that you cannot change the subdomain once you spec- ify it. Region (Provider) Choose the desired region for your subaccount. The region you select determines the data center where your data will be hosted. • Select Europe (Frankfurt) cf-eu10 for the Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Frankfurt, Germany (Recommended) • Select US West (WA) cf-us20 for the Microsoft Azure infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Washington state, US • Select KSA (Dammam) GCP Public Sector cf-sa30 for the Google Cloud infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Dammam, Saudi Arabia  Note To establish cross-data-center connections with your business partners, you must enable Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network in Profile Settings. Used for production Select this option if your account is for productive use. Do not select this option if it is for non-productive purposes, such as development and testing. 16 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Solution Owners Onboarding -- 16 of 66 -- Field Description Enable beta features We recommend not to enable the beta features. To get the tenant-specific URL for accessing SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, see Sign In to the Network [page 33]. 4.1.4 Establish Trust Between Your Subaccount and Identity Authentication Tenant To enable secure access to your subaccount, you need to establish trust between your subaccount and the Identity Authentication tenant. Context SAP Cloud Identity Services - Identity Authentication is an identity provider supported by SAP BTP. It is where the business users for SAP BTP are stored. SAP Business Network for Logistics uses Identity Authentication as the identity provider. To enable secured access to your subaccount, you must establish mutual trust between your subaccount and Identity Authentication tenant. With the purchase of the productive license, your company is provided with a tenant for Identity Authentication, if it hasn't already got one. You or your colleague receives an email for activating the account. The email contains a link to the administration console for Identity Authentication. By activating the account, you are the administrator of the account and can assign administrator roles to other users.  Note If the activation link in the email is invalid or already used, follow the advice in SAP note 2637748 . To find your company's existing Identity Authentication tenants and their administrators, see Viewing Assigned Tenants and Administrators. For further questions on Identity Authentication tenant URL or administrator, create an incident with component BC-IAM-IDS. 18 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Solution Owners Onboarding -- 18 of 66 -- Procedure You can establish the trust using automatic method. For prerequisites and detailed steps, see: • Automatic method: Establish Trust and Federation Between SAP Authorization and Trust Management Service and Identity Authentication 4.1.4.1 Migration of Authentication from XSUAA to IAS For existing customers, we recommend that you migrate the authentication from XSUAA to IAS to consume new capabilities in the future, such as Joule, SAP's generative AI copilot. SAP Cloud Identity services are SAP's strategic solution for enterprise-grade identity and access management (IAM) in customers' SAP cloud landscapes. As the de-facto standard for authentication and authorization on SAP BTP, SAP Authorization and Trust Management service (XSUAA) is used by many applications and reuse services that are developed by SAP, partners, and customers. However, they often rely indirectly on SAP Cloud Identity services as XSUAA delegates part of its responsibilities to the following SAP Cloud Identity services: • Identity Authentication Service (IAS): provides authentication-related service • Identity Provisioning: manage users and their authorization assignments in XSUAA Going forward, SAP Cloud Identity services are the strategic IAM solution for SAP cloud products and the new IAM features will be mostly available in SAP Cloud Identity services. For SAP Business Network for Logistics to consume new IAM features like Authorization Management in SAP Cloud Identity services, it requires the migration of the authentication from XSUAA to IAS. However, this is done at tenant level depending on the features you would like to use. Prerequisites Ensure you have fulfilled the following prerequisites: • If you already have an IAS tenant, you must establish OpenID Connect (OIDC) trust between your subaccount and the Identity Authentication tenant. For more information, see Establish Trust Between Your Subaccount and Identity Authentication Tenant. • If you already have SAML-based trust configuration in your subaccount, you should migrate to OIDC-based trust configuration. For more information, see Migration from SAML Trust to OpenID Connect Trust with SAP Cloud Identity Services. Administration Guide for Solution Owners Onboarding PUBLIC 19 -- 19 of 66 -- Procedure To migrate, you must raise a ticket in the component SBN-LBN-GTT-COR to request the migration support. You need to provide the following details in the ticket: • Title: Migrate from XSUAA to IAS-based Authentication • Details • Subaccount ID • Subaccount Domain Results After the migration, the previous default identity provider that you used to sign in (usually with your S-User ID) to the apps subscribed in your subaccount will no longer work. You need to create the users in your IAS tenant, adjust the role collections in your subaccount and use your IAS tenant to sign in. Here is the comparison of the sign-in interface before and after the migration: This doesn't affect the technical user as long as the parameter Default for Noninteractive Logon is switched on when establishing the trust. It is also used for calling GTT read/write service directly. Each tenant can only have one technical user, and it must be unique. Context A technical user is a role but not a person, nor a business user. It is a token used by selected services to access the SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace and authenticate system connection. Do not use your technical user's account to sign into SAP Fiori Launchpad. In this task, you'll create a technical user and assign technical user role collection to it. Create a Technical User 1. Sign in to the administration console for SAP Cloud Identity Services. 2. Choose the User Management tile. 3. Click Add and fill in the required fields in the dialog box. Enter a unique email address that is not used by any of the users that you’ve created for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. After registering the user, an email with the subject Activate Your Account for SAP.com will be sent to the email address. 4. Use the link in the email to activate the account. 5. On the Personal Information screen, note down the user ID, which starts with the letter P. You'll need it later. 22 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Solution Owners Onboarding -- 22 of 66 -- Assign Role Collection to the Technical User 1. Go to your subaccount in the SAP BTP cockpit. 2. In the left-hand pane, choose Role Collections under Security. 3. Choose the technical user role collection in the task: Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users [page 24]. Make sure that you only assign the roles under For Technical Users [page 31] to the technical user.  Note A technical user can only be assigned with following two groups of roles: • Technical user role: make sure the role collection you assign to the technical user contains all the following technical user roles as listed under Technical User Roles in For Technical Users [page 31]: • ReadServiceIntegrationTemplate • WriteServiceIntegrationTemplate • MetadataServiceIntegrationTemplate • ReadServiceAttributeTemplate • LocationProcessTemplate • ERP integration role: if you want to use the technical user for ERP integration, make sure the role collection you assign to the technical user also contains the following ERP integration role as listed under ERP Integration Role in For Technical Users [page 31] : • EMIDocIntegrationTemplate Don't add any business user roles into the role collection you assign to the technical user. 4. Go to the Users section and choose Edit. 5. Enter the email address of the technical user and select Default identity provider. 6. Save your changes. For more information, see Assign Users to Role Collection. 4.1.5.2 Create a Business User and Assign Role Collection Prerequisites To assign role collection to a business user, you must have the administrator role for your subaccount. In addition to compliance with general data protection and privacy acts, it is necessary to consider compliance with industry-specific legislation in different countries/regions. SAP provides specific features and functions to support compliance with regard to relevant legal requirements, including data protection. SAP does not give any advice on whether these features and functions are the best method to support company, industry, regional, or country-specific requirements. Furthermore, this information should not be taken as advice or a recommendation regarding additional features that would be required in specific IT environments. Decisions related to data protection must be made on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration the given system landscape and the applicable legal requirements.  Note SAP does not provide legal advice in any form. SAP software supports data protection compliance by providing security features and specific data protection-relevant functions, such as simplified blocking and deletion of personal data. In many cases, compliance with applicable data protection and privacy laws will not be covered by a product feature. Definitions and other terms used in this document are not taken from a particular legal source.  Caution The extent to which data protection is supported by technical means depends on secure system operation. Network security, security note implementation, adequate logging of system changes, and appropriate usage of the system are the basic technical requirements for compliance with data privacy legislation and other legislation. Administration Guide for Solution Owners Security: Data Protection and Privacy PUBLIC 47 -- 47 of 66 -- Term Definition Artificial Intelligence (AI) The simulation of human intelligence processes by machines and computer systems – typically by learning, coming to its own conclusions, appearing to understand complex content, engaging in natural dialogs with people, enhancing human cognitive performance (also known as cognitive computing) or replacing people on execution of nonroutine tasks. Appli- cations include autonomous vehicles, automatic speech rec- ognition and generation and detecting novel concepts and abstractions (useful for detecting potential new risks and aiding humans to quickly understand very large bodies of ever-changing information) Automated Decision Making The ability to make decisions by technological means with- out human involvement. Blocking A method of restricting access to data for which the primary business purpose has ended. Business Purpose The legal, contractual, or in other form justified reason for the processing of personal data to complete an end-to-end business process. The personal data used to complete the process is predefined in a purpose, which is defined by the data controller. The process must be defined before the per- sonal data required to fulfill the purpose can be determined. Consent The action of the data subject confirming that the usage of his or her personal data shall be allowed for a given pur- pose. A consent functionality allows the storage of a consent record in relation to a specific purpose and shows if a data subject has granted, withdrawn, or denied consent. Data Subject Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natu- ral person ("data subject"). An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identifica- tion number, location data, an online identifier, or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person. Deletion Deletion of personal data so that the data is no longer avail- able. End of Business Defines the end of active business and the start of residence time and retention period. 48 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Solution Owners Security: Data Protection and Privacy -- 48 of 66 -- Term Definition End of Purpose (EoP) The point in time when the processing of a set of personal data is no longer required for the primary business purpose, for example, when a contract is fulfilled. After the EoP has been reached, the data is blocked and can only be accessed by users with special authorizations (for example, tax audi- tors). End of Purpose (EoP) check A method of identifying the point in time for a data set when the processing of personal data is no longer required for the primary business purpose. After the EoP has been reached, the data is blocked and can only be accessed by users with special authorization, for example, tax auditors. Personal data Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natu- ral person ("data subject"). An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identifica- tion number, location data, an online identifier, or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person. Processing of Personal Data Processing means any operation or set of operations which is performed on personal data or on sets of personal data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, re- cording, organisation, structuring, storage, adaptation or al- teration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmis- sion, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure or destruction. Purpose The information that specifies the reason and the goal for the processing of a specific set of personal data. As a rule, the purpose references the relevant legal basis for the proc- essing of personal data. Residence period The period of time between the end of business and the end of purpose (EoP) for a data set during which the data remains in the database and can be used in case of sub- sequent processes related to the original purpose. At the end of the longest configured residence period, the data is blocked or deleted. The residence period is part of the over- all retention period. Retention period The period of time between the end of the last business activity involving a specific object (for example, a business partner) and the deletion of the corresponding data, subject to applicable laws. The retention period is a combination of the residence period and the blocking period. In some cases, the data subject may also be the user. This SAP product provides functionality to capture consent of data subjects before collecting personal data, where no other legal ground exists. This allows data subjects to give and withdraw consent to process their personal data. To do that, click the user icon in the upper-right corner of the app window and choose Settings Privacy Statement . 7.3 Read Access Logging (RAL) Read Access Logging is considered as an additional safeguard in the protection of personal data, because it helps to identify potential illegitimate access to personal data. Read access to sensitive personal data is partially based on legislation, and it is subject to logging functionality. Read access logging (RAL) is used to monitor and log read access to sensitive personal data that was disclosed via user interface, which can be extended to read access to other personal data. Data may be categorized as sensitive by law, by external company policy, or by internal company policy. When these read accesses are logged, you should be able check which user accessed personal data on which access channel and the date and time, depending on the configuration. Read access logging enables you to answer questions about who accessed particular data within a specified time frame. That logging also includes downloading attachments or files, logs for such events shall contain information to identify the attachment. Additionally, as for Read Access Logging across system boundaries, the respective “access” shall be logged as soon as sensitive personal data crosses the boundary from a trusted to an un-trusted area. Here are some examples of such questions: • Who accessed the data of a given business entity, for example a bank account? • Who accessed personal data, for example of a business partner? • Which employee accessed personal information, for example religion? • Which accounts or business partners were accessed by which users? Furthermore, log records can be viewed and queried, but access to them is restricted by adequate authorizations. The personal data for which read access shall be logged and the retention period of logs, can be configured. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace includes a feature that logs accesses of sensitive personal data in the system. The feature helps to analyze data access of sensitive personal data. The Audit Log Viewer allows you to access audit logs. • To view the GTT audit logs for a given time period, see the section Access the Audit Log Viewer [page 55]. • For more information on the Audit Log Viewer, see the Audit Log Viewer for the Cloud Foundry Environment. 7.4 Personal Data Record The feature provides data associated to the Data Subject. It is in the duty of the customer to check, whether all the data reported shall get handed over to the data subject, because the report might contain internal Administration Guide for Solution Owners Security: Data Protection and Privacy PUBLIC 51 -- 51 of 66 -- customer information or information on other third parties. Data subjects have the right to receive information regarding their personal data undergoing processing. The personal data record feature helps you to comply with the relevant legal requirements for data protection by allowing you to search for and retrieve personal data for a specified data subject. The search results are displayed in a comprehensive and structured list containing all personal data of

The extracted data can be downloaded in form of a report, that provides configuration and extensibility functionality. The access to the personal data record is only allowed with authorization. Subscribe to SAP Data Privacy Integration Next Generation Service The Manage Personal Data app uses the Next Generation Data Privacy Integration service to extract personal data stored about a data subject. To use this service, subscribe to the SAP Data Privacy Integration Next Generation service (application plan name: ngdpi) in your SAP Cloud Platform subaccount. After subscription, assign the DPI_NextGen_Information_DataPrivacy_Administrator role collection to users handling personal data management to ensure they have appropriate permissions for managing personal data securely. The company that owns the data is the data controller. If a data subject wants to know which data is stored about him or her, he or she shall contact their data controller. You can use the following user roles: • DP&P Specialist: is authorized to deal with requests from data subjects concerning their personal data using the Retention Management app • Audit Specialist: is authorized to view, for the purpose of DP&P auditing, all GTT data including personal data using the Blocking Store app  Note You can use annotations to identify any data that you wish to classify as being personal data or sensitive personal data. For more information, see the Guide for Model Administrators documentation that is available from the SAP Help Portal under https://help.sap.com/gtt. Set up Access to Personal Data To set up access for DP&P Specialists to view the personal data of data subjects, you must do the following: 1. Assign the business users to the user group You assign the user group TT_DATA_PRIVACY_SPECIALIST or TT_AUDITOR to a user using the Administration Console for SAP Identity Authentication Service. 2. View assigned roles You can see the assigned role in the user’s role list in the User Management app. Retrieve Personal Information To retrieve personal information about a data subject, you, as the DP&P specialist, must do the following: Prerequisite: You must be able to access the Manage Personal Data app of the Next Generation Data Privacy Integration service. 1. Start the Manage Personal Data app. To do so, in your SAP Cloud Foundry subaccount find the Data Privacy Integration tile and click Go to Application. 2. In the Data Subject Search page, enter the email address of the data subject as the Data Subject ID and then press the Enter key or click the Go button. 52 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Solution Owners Security: Data Protection and Privacy -- 52 of 66 -- 3. If any personal information is found for the data subject, the data subject is listed in section Data Subjects, with one or more links to an application(s). The following links may appear: 1. Solution BP Management for business partner management. 2. Master Data Management for master data management. 3. Metadata-service for metadata service (that is model management). 4. Core Engine for tracked processes. An example is shown in the following screenshot: 4. Click the link of the application, and you are navigated to the second page of the app. 5. Click the area with the application name and the email address (that is the Data Subject ID), a new pane with some detailed information is displayed on the right. 6. In the section Where the data subject’s personal data is used, click the link View List to open further detailed information in a new pane on the right. This pane displays business transactions made by the data subject in an application. 7. Retrieve the personal data and make it available securely to the data subject. For more information about the Next Generation Data Privacy Integration service, refer to the following resources: • https://help.sap.com/docs/data-privacy-integration/end-user-information/what-is-data-privacy- integration-nextgen?q=nextgen&version=Cloud • https://help.sap.com/docs/data-privacy-integration/security/assigning-roles-to-users- b90280f5f6904d008a3ebb8ac3809094?q=nextgen 7.5 Data Retention In SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, business data that needs to be deleted can be found in the following: 1. Model deployment history 2. Tracked processes and Events 3. Message logs Administration Guide for Solution Owners Security: Data Protection and Privacy PUBLIC 53 -- 53 of 66 -- 1. Model Deployment History A model administrator can delete any model. This results in the immediate and permanent deletion of the model, tracked processes and all data including deployment (or change) history and any data annotated as being DPP-relevant. 2. Tracked Processes and Events See the section Retention Management. 3. Message Logs The Manage Message Logs app contains a DP&P-related option for setting the retention period for message logs of all the messages that have been sent to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. Message logs older than the specified retention period are deleted along with any personal data they may contain. Prerequisite You must have a user with the role: Message Log Administrator. Procedure 1. In the SAP Fiori Launchpad, open the Manage Message Logs app. 2. Click the Retention button. 3. In the Retention Period area, enter the retention period in days. The default is 30 days. You must enter an integer between 1 and 30 inclusive. 4. Click Save. Result The retention period for message logs is changed to the value you saved. 7.6 Change Log Creation and change of personal data need to be documented. Therefore, for review purposes or as a result of legal regulations, it may be necessary to track the changes made to this data. When these changes are logged, you should be able to check which user made which change, the date and time, the previous value, and the current value, depending on the configuration. Furthermore, log records can be viewed and queried, but access to them is restricted by adequate authorizations. The personal data for which changes shall be logged and the retention period of logs, can be configured.. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace includes a feature that logs changes of personal data in the system. The feature helps to analyze modification of personal data. 54 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Solution Owners Security: Data Protection and Privacy -- 54 of 66 -- The Audit Log Viewer allows you to access change logs. • To view the GTT change logs for a given time period, see the section Access the Audit Log Viewer [page 55]. • For more information on the Audit Log Viewer, see the Audit Log Viewer for the Cloud Foundry Environment. 7.7 Tasks for Audit Specialists Audit specialists are authorized to view, for the purpose of DP&P auditing, all GTT data and can do the following: • Access the Audit Log Viewer [page 55] • View Blocked Master Data [page 56] 7.7.1 Access the Audit Log Viewer Context Prerequisites: To access the audit log viewer, you need to be assigned: • the role solution administrator and • the role audit specialist Procedure 1. Sign in to the SAP BTP cockpit. 2. Choose your global account and cloud foundry subaccount. 3. Choose Subscriptions. 4. Find the tile, Audit Log Viewer, and click Go to Application. 5. Fill in your account information and sign in. 6. Select the Time Range and click Reload. You can see the audit logs for your selected time range. 7. To view the information for all users, navigate to the Users list. Administration Guide for Solution Owners Security: Data Protection and Privacy PUBLIC 55 -- 55 of 66 -- Results You can see the audit logs for your selected time range. Depending on your authorization, the list displays all users from either the solution participant or solution owner.  Note The list includes blocked users but not deleted users. Business Network Global Track and Trace, including: • Leading documents (Leading Tracked Processes): number of leading tracked processes generated for tracking targeted business processes • Documents (Tracked Processes): number of tracked processes generated for tracking targeted business processes • Documents (Events): number of events generated for tracked processes • Consumed SAP S/4HANA memory • Storage: data storage size for all generated tracked processes and events To monitor the above usage analytics, go to your global account's or subaccount's Usage Analytics page in the SAP BTP cockpit. Then in the Service Usage table, select the service SAP Global Track and Trace. For more information on monitoring usage in SAP BTP, see: • Monitoring Usage and Consumption Costs in Your Global Account • View Subaccount Usage Analytics 8.2 Error Handling If you encounter technical issues or require support, follow the procedure to report a case. Report a Case through SAP for Me To report a case through SAP for Me, you need an S-User ID to sign in. If you don't have the sign-in credentials of your S-User, contact a user administrator in your organization. If you have trouble identifying who the user administrator is in your organization, please call the Customer Interaction Center (CIC) . For more information, see the SAP for Me Online Help under Access and Authorizations . Procedure 1. Open the SAP for Me application . Sign in with your S-User ID. Administration Guide for Solution Owners Monitoring and Troubleshooting PUBLIC 59 -- 59 of 66 -- 2. Navigate to Services & Support Get Support . 3. In the Get Support app, select a relevant customer and report your issue. For detailed process, see Get Support Application Online Help . If you use a component to categorize your issue, use SBN-LBN. Report a Case on Ariba Help Center If you set up your logistics provider account via the simplified onboarding process, you won’t have an S-User ID. In this case, you can report a case on Ariba Help Center. Procedure 1. Sign in to Ariba Help Center then choose Carrier Help Center. 2. Select Contact us, enter keywords pertaining to the issue in the search box and then press Enter. 3. Browse the populated results. If the results provided do not resolve your issue, click Create a Case at the lower-right corner. 4. Enter information on the case creation form.  Note • Select the solution or add-on you’re using from the Issue type dropdown list, then choose the most relevant Issue area. • Enter your company's Business Network ID (BNO ID) in the Account ID field. 5. Click One last step once you complete the case creation form, choose the contact method, and then click Submit. After you create a case on the Ariba Help Center , our support team will contact you using the email address you provided in the case creation form. We recommend adding itsm.notification-service@sap.com to your mailbox's allowed senders list to ensure you receive all correspondence. 8.3 Accessibility Features To optimize your experience, our apps have features and settings that help you use the software efficiently. Administration Guide for Solution Owners Monitoring and Troubleshooting PUBLIC 61 -- 61 of 66 -- 9 Extensibility Features SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace offers extensibility that allows you to adapt the standard business software to your business requirements. The extensibility attributes include: • Custom Field [page 62] • Custom Business Logic [page 62] • Integration [page 64] 9.1 Custom Field In the Manage Models app, you can add custom fields for tracked processes, event types and other data types to provide supplementary information and display these fields in the fulfillment tracking apps. For more, see Guide for Model Administrators. The fulfillment tracking apps also support key user extensibility that allows you to customize their user interface. For more, see Adapting the UI. 9.2 Custom Business Logic In SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, you can use the event-to-action scripts to define custom business logic as per your business needs. It's applicable to the following cases: • Define your tracking and execution status • Configure email notifications • Generate public shipment links • Set up the stage-level observation • Display the single route view on the map Event to Action An event-to-action script allows you to incorporate logic (business rules) into your model. For more, see Event to Action (Business Rules). 62 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Solution Owners Extensibility Features -- 62 of 66 -- My Tracking Status “My Tracking Status” can reflect how your tracking process goes. You can display it in the Track Shipments, Monitor Inbound ASNs and Monitor Outbound Deliveries apps to identify shipments, inbound and outbound deliveries with exceptional tracking status. You can define it in a way that better meets your individual business needs. For more, see Define My Tracking Status. My Execution Status Apart from the standard execution status designed by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, “My Execution Status” is provided for you to define the execution status in a way that can better meet your individual business needs. You can display it in the Track Shipments app to monitor your shipments. For more, see Define My Execution Status. Email Notifications You can use the email notification service to send email automatically in cases such as when an event occurs. For more, see How to Send Notifications. Public Link Public links allow you to share the shipment details to guest users. After receiving the link, they can view the shipment information without the need to sign in. By default, the generation of public links is disabled. You can enable it in the event-to-action script. For more, see Generate Public Links for Shipments. Stage-Level Observation Stage-level observation affects the event correlation between tracked processes. When a tracked process observes another tracked process at stage level, the event correlation follows a set of rules. By default, it's enabled. You can disable it in the event-to-action script. For more, see Stage-Level Observation Between Tracked Processes. Single Route View on Map In the Track Shipments app, there are two views available on the map, a default view and a single-route view. The former view shows both planned and actual routes. The latter shows only the actual route. You can disable the single route view in the event-to-action script. For more, see Guide for Transportation Planners. Administration Guide for Solution Owners Extensibility Features PUBLIC 63 -- 63 of 66 -- Carrier Name The field is introduced for you, solution owner, to define custom carrier names that are displayed in the Track Shipments app. It helps you recognize carriers easily. To do so, do the following: • In the standard model of the Manage Models app, define cusom carrier names in the code list CarrierDescription. For more, see Code List. • In the Event to Action tab, add the following script under User Script Before Standard Script:  Sample Code if (scriptForShipment && SHIPMENT_EVENT == actualEvent.eventType){ trackedProcess.carrierDescription_code = trackedProcess.serviceAgentLbnId; As a result, the code names can be displayed as the Carrier Name in the standard Track Shipments app. You can also filter shipments by these custom carrier names with the Carrier Name filter. These carrier names can be different from what is manintained by carriers themselves. 9.3 Integration You can map custom fields to LBN tracking fields under the Visibility Provider Integration. Then use the following APIs to provide the values for these fields: • Provider API for Order Events (GTT) • Consumer API for Order Tracking (GTT) For more about the mapping, see Visibility Provider Integration. You can configure the IDOC related settings for custom fields, event types, etc.. For more, see Sample Code Configuration Guide for Integration with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace . Custom fields can also be forwarded back to your TM system together with actual events.
