-- 1 Introduction About This Document This document describes all aspects of the notification service.  Recommendation Before you start working your way through this document, ensure you have the most recent version of this document that is available from the SAP Help Portal at: help.sap.com/gtt About the Notification Service The notification service: • allows you to create a template email for an event, such as that a sales order has been created, then when the event occurs, automatically send emails based on the template to the involved parties • is available with Version 2 of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace Prerequisite You are able to sign in to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace and use the following apps: • Manage Models (MM) app • Manage Notification Templates (MNT) app • View Logs (VL) app • Manage Message Logs (MML) app How to Send Notifications Introduction PUBLIC 3 -- 3 of 26 -- 2 Create Email Template Context To create the email template, do the following: Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Notification Templates (MNT) app. 2. Click the Create button. The Create Notification Template popup then appears. 3. Enter the information required including a: • name for the template • description • select the Global Track and Trace application 4. When you are finished, click Ok. 5. To create the email, click Add and enter the following information. For an example, see below • Language: select from the drop-down list. English (US) is the default. • Recipients: enter ^{recipients1} • Subject: enter a title such as: “Reminder Service Test Email” • Body: enter the text for the email. For an example, see the following. 6. When you are finished, click Ok. Recipients example ^{recipients1} Subject example Reminder Service Test Email 4 PUBLIC How to Send Notifications Create Email Template -- 4 of 26 -- Body text example Dear Tester, This is a sample email for test use. User-defined placeholder: ^{UserDefined_Placeholder} Application-defined placeholder: SolutionOwner_BusinessProfileName: Test Company is ~{SolutionOwner_BusinessProfileName} SolutionOwner_Address: No.1 Lane 2 Street 3, City 4, China is ~{SolutionOwner_Address} SolutionOwner_PostalCode: 200000 is ~{SolutionOwner_PostalCode} SolutionOwner_Website: www.asdf.com is ~{SolutionOwner_Website} SolutionOwner_Mobile: 0987654321 is ~{SolutionOwner_Mobile} SolutionOwner_Fax: 0123456789 is ~{SolutionOwner_Fax} System-defined placeholder: LOGO is ${BP_LOGO} Best Regards SAP Business Network for Logistics Team How to Send Notifications Create Email Template PUBLIC 5 -- 5 of 26 -- 3 Define the Rule in the Event-to-Action Script You can write a rule for an email template that includes variables, such as placeholders, that refer to different attributes of a tracked process. When your rule is processed, the variables in the template are replaced by specific values in each email so the reader has all the relevant information from the tracked process. You can define email rules in an event-to-action script within a GTT metadata model using the Manage Models (MM app). This chapter describes the various parts of the script, how to use them in the rule and how to implement the script. Optionally, you can also define email rules on the Email Rules page of the Manage Models app. You don't have to write codes in this way. For more, see Define the Rule on the Configuration UI [page 14]. 3.1 Placeholders In the script, you can use three different types of placeholders: Type Format Description System-defined ${<placeholder_name>} Defined by notification service. You cannot make changes. If you have any problems, log your incident in ServiceNow with component SBN-LBN-PER. Application-defined ~{<placeholder_name>} Defined by the GTT system. You cannot make changes. If you have any problems, log your incident in ServiceNow with component SBN-LBN-GTT-COR. User-defined ^{<placeholder_name>} 3.1.1 System-defined Placeholders The following system-defined placeholder is available: ${BP_LOGO} 6 PUBLIC How to Send Notifications Define the Rule in the Event-to-Action Script -- 6 of 26 -- You can apply a logo, for example the solution owner’s, in the Manage Business Profile app as follows: 3.1.2 Application-defined Placeholders The following application-defined placeholders are available: 1. ~{<SolutionOwner_BusinessProfileName>} 2. ~{<SolutionOwner_Website>} 3. ~{<SolutionOwner_Address>} 4. ~{<SolutionOwner_PostalCode>} 5. ~{<SolutionOwner_Mobile>} 6. ~{<SolutionOwner_Fax>} How to Send Notifications Define the Rule in the Event-to-Action Script PUBLIC 7 -- 7 of 26 -- You can set values for these placeholders in the Manage Business Profile app as follows: 3.1.3 User-defined Placeholders You can define them for use in your script. For example, to create a user-defined placeholder: “Userdefined_Placeholder”, you must add the following script in Event to Action: var userDefPlaceholders = toObject("{}"); var directMailTemp = reminderService.generateDirectMailTemplate(); userDefPlaceholders.Userdefined_Placeholder = "User-defined placeholder"; 8 PUBLIC How to Send Notifications Define the Rule in the Event-to-Action Script -- 8 of 26 -- directMailTemp.userdefinedPlaceholders = userDefPlaceholders; Then you can use “Userdefined_Placeholder” in email templates. For example, as follows: This is defined by ^{ Userdefined_Placeholder}. For more, see the section Appendix: Event to Action Script in Guide for Model Administrators. 3.2 Create Mail Object Use the following function to generate Direct Mail Template objects. var directMailTemp = reminderService.generateDirectMailTemplate(); Properties and Functions Use the following functions to generate Direct Mail Template properties and functions. var userDefPlaceholders = toObject("{}"); var directMailTemp = reminderService.generateDirectMailTemplate(); userDefPlaceholders.Userdefined_Placeholder = "User-defined placeholder"; directMailTemp.templateId = "invite"; directMailTemp.locale = "en"; directMailTemp.recipients = ["jane@doe.com", "jack@ryan.com"]; directMailTemp.userdefinedPlaceholders = userDefPlaceholders; directMailTemp.templateRecipientIgnore = false; directMailTemp.post();  Note • templateId: to identify the name of the email template, which is created in the Manage Notification Templates (MNT) app • locale: to identify the language version of the email template, which is created in the Manage Notification Templates (MNT) app. You can refer to the language code in the following table: Language Language Code Arabic ar Bulgarian bg Chinese cn Czech cs Danish da German de Greek el English en Spanish es Finnish fi How to Send Notifications Define the Rule in the Event-to-Action Script PUBLIC 9 -- 9 of 26 -- Language Language Code French fr Croatian hr Hungarian hu Italian it Hebrew iw Japanese ja Korean ko Malay ms Dutch nl Norwegian no Polish pl Portuguese (Brazil) pt_br Romanian ro Russian ru Serbian sh Slovakian sk Swedish sv Thai th Turkish tr Chinese (Trad.) zh_tw • recipients: recipients of the email. The value type should be Array. • templateRecipientIgnore: to decide the recipients of the email template. The value type should be Boolean. The default value is false. • If the value is false, two groups of recipients will receive the email: • all recipients in the recipient field maintained in the template • recipients listed in the payload in Event to Action • If the value is true, only the recipients listed in the payload in Event to Action will receive the email. • post(): to send the email 10 PUBLIC How to Send Notifications Define the Rule in the Event-to-Action Script -- 10 of 26 -- 3.3 Implement the Script Context To implement your completed script, do the following: Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Models (MM) app. 2. Select your model and click to open it. 3. Click the Event to Action tab. 4. Input the script. For example: var userDefPlaceholders = toObject("{}"); var directMailTemp = reminderService.generateDirectMailTemplate(); userDefPlaceholders.UserDefined_Placeholder = "User-defined placeholder"; userDefPlaceholders.recipients1 = "name0.surname0@company.com,name1.surname1@company.com";//You can only enter a string value. Use "," to seperate multiple recipients. directMailTemp.templateId = "invite"; directMailTemp.recipients = ["name2.surname2@company.com ", " name3.surname3@company.com "]; directMailTemp.userdefinedPlaceholders = userDefPlaceholders; directMailTemp.post(); 5. When you are ready, click the Deploy button. How to Send Notifications Define the Rule in the Event-to-Action Script PUBLIC 11 -- 11 of 26 -- 3.4 Send Email Context To send the emails generated from the template, do the following: Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Models (MM) app. 2. Click the Runtime button. 3. When you are finished, click Try it out. 4. In the Request body, input the following but change the altKey to that of your own model: { "altKey": "xri://sap.com/id:LBN#10002424:QM7_910:testtype:41003_10", "actualBusinessTimestamp": "2020-05-24T09:00:00.213+01:00" } 5. Under the input box, click Execute. 6. If your mail address is in the script, after a delay you will receive an email like the following: 12 PUBLIC How to Send Notifications Define the Rule in the Event-to-Action Script -- 12 of 26 --  Note The email subject line is truncated by the sender client as follows: • Microsoft Outlook client: 255 characters • Google Mail client: 998 characters How to Send Notifications Define the Rule in the Event-to-Action Script PUBLIC 13 -- 13 of 26 -- 4 Define the Rule on the Configuration UI Prerequisites • You have created email templates in the Manage Notification Templates app. For more, see Create Email Template [page 4]. • You must have at least one of the following roles: • DataModelAdminTemplate • EmailRulesProcessTemplate For more, see the Available Roles for Solution Owners section in the Administration Guide for Solution Owners. Context In addition to defining rules in the event-to-action script, you can also define rules on the configuration UI without the need to write codes. If the rules are met, an email will be automatically sent to designated recipients. The rules defined in these two ways are independent. Procedure 1. Launch the Manage Models app 2. Click Email Rules on the standard model card. The Email Rules page appears. 3. On the left-side of the panel, there is an Email Rules table. Click the Add icon on the top right to create a rule first. A table row is added.  Note You can only create one rule at a time. You can’t create another rule before the current rule is defined and saved. You can create a maximum of 15 rules. Optional: You can also import rules from your local file with the icon  on the top right. The existing rules with the same description as the imported ones will be overwritten. The status of all imported rules is set to Inactive. You can activate them as needed. 4. On the right panel of the page, click Edit on the top right to edit General Information and Rule Settings. a. For General Information, provide the following: 14 PUBLIC How to Send Notifications Define the Rule on the Configuration UI -- 14 of 26 -- • Description: the description of the email rule, displayed in the Description column of the table on the left. • Status: you can activate and deactivate the rule with the switch. The status is displayed in the Status column of the table on the left. b. For Rule Settings, you can specify the context, conditions and action triggered of a rule in the following three sections: • When: sets the context under which the conditions of a rule should be checked. You can understand the context here as: when a <target event >is reported and correlated to the <target tracked process>. You must specify the relevant event and tracked process with the following fields: • Current Event: select a target actual event or a tracked process event • Correlated Tracked Process: the tracked process that the current event is correlated to. • If: specifies the conditions that must be met for the rule to be processed. Click the Add icon to add the condition and choose either of the following: • Compared to Model Field Value: this means you want the attribute to be compared to a model field value. It allows you to select a field available in your model in the Value Column. • Compared to Specific Value: this means you want the attribute to be compared to a specific value. It allows you to enter a value manually in the Value column. Then provide the condition details: • Attribute: select a field available in the pop-up. The fields in the drop-down list are available fields of the current event, or matched planned event of the current event, or correlated tracked process of the current event. • Operator: select an operator from the drop-down list. The available operators in the list changes based on the field type of the attribute that you choose. • Value: the value that you want the attribute to be compared to.  Note You can add a maximum of 15 conditions. • Then: the action of the rule. When the conditions are met, an email will be sent to designated recipients. The following information you provide determines the style, language, recipients, and content of the email: • Email Template ID: select an email template from the drop-down list. All email templates that you maintained in the Manage Notification Templates app are available here. For more, see Create Email Template [page 4]. • Language: select a language from the drop-down list. All languages that you maintained for the email template are available here. • Recipients: enter the email accounts of the recipients. To add multiple email accounts, press "Enter" after you input each one. You can also specify recipients in the placeholder section followed. For more, see Add Recipients [page 17]. • User-Defined Placeholders In the placeholder section, you can provide values for user-defined placeholders that you have maintained in the selected email template. Click the Add icon and choose either of the following: • Model Field Value: this means the value you want to add for the placeholder is a model field value. It allows you to select a field available in your model. • Specific Value: this means the value you want to add for the placeholder is a specific value. It allows you to enter a value manually. How to Send Notifications Define the Rule on the Configuration UI PUBLIC 15 -- 15 of 26 -- Then provide the placeholder details in the following columns: • Placeholder Name: The name of user-defined placeholders that you maintained in the email template on the Manage Notifications Template app. • Value: The value that will populate the user-defined placeholders in your email. • Show As: You can specify how to populate a placeholder in the email template. When the value is a code list, you can choose one of the following options from the drop-down list: • Code: The codes of code list entries will be shown in the generated email. • Name: The names of code list entries will be shown in the generated email. When the value is the location alternative key, you can choose one of the following options from the drop-down list: • Text: The location alternative key itself will be shown in the generated email. • Location: You can further choose the location details from the drop-down list to the right, such as "Email Address". In this case, the system will use the location alternative key to search for location maintained in the master data and return the "Email Address" only that you previously selected. As a result, the email address will be shown in the generated email. When the value is the business parter's LBN ID, the system can get the master data of the mapped business partner and you can decide to show what information in the placeholder. You can choose one of the following options from the drop-down list: • Text: The business partner's LBN ID will be shown in the generated email, such as “LBN#1234567”. • Business Partner: You can further choose the business partner details from the drop- down list to the right. It includes the Website, Business Profile Name and the following headquarter information as shown in the screenshot: • Postal Code • Mobile Number • Phone Number • Fax Number • Email 16 PUBLIC How to Send Notifications Define the Rule on the Configuration UI -- 16 of 26 -- If you choose "Email", then the email will shown in the generated email.  Note If business partners weren't onboarded on the same data center as yours, their master data retrieved might be incomplete. You can also use the user-defined placeholders to embed public links in email notifications. For more, see Example: Embed Public Links in Email Notifications [page 19]. 5. Save your changes. The email rule is created successfully. You can export your email rules in a JSON file with the icon  . You can also save your email rules as a tile on the home page of GTT Fiori Launchpad for quick access. For more, see Save a Tile [page 20]. 4.1 Add Recipients You can add recipients in the email rules so that they can receive email notifications. There are two ways of adding them: How to Send Notifications Define the Rule on the Configuration UI PUBLIC 17 -- 17 of 26 -- Using the Application-Defined Placeholder (Recommended) This applies to the case when you have inserted the application-defined placeholder ~{GTT_Default_Recipients} in the Recipients field of your email template. For more, see Create Email Template [page 4]. If you have done so, on the configuration UI, you can enter email accounts of the recipients on the Recipients field when creating a rule. To add multiple recipients, press “Enter” on your keyboard after you input each email account. Using a User-Defined Placeholder This applies to the case when you have added a user-define placeholder in the Recipients field of your email template, for example, ^{recipients}. For more, see Create Email Template [page 4]. If you have done so, in the placeholder section of the configuration UI. Provide the following information: • Placeholder Name: enter the user-defined placeholder name that you maintained in the Recipients field of your email template. In the given example, it's "recipients". • Value: there are two cases, depending on whether you choose "Model Field Value" or "Specific Value" when adding the row: • When you choose "Model Field Value", then you can click the value help icon to select an available field. The value of the designated field is filled in the user-defined placeholder in the trigger email. • When you choose "Specific Value", then enter the email accounts of the recipients and they are automatically filled in the user-defined placeholder in the triggered email. To add multiple email accounts, use “,” to separate them without any space in between. 4.2 Example: Recommended Rule Settings for Planned Event Overdue Notifications Context If you want the system to send email notifications in the case when a planned event is overdue, for example, the planned Departure event of the Shipment tracked process, here are the recommended rule settings: Procedure 1. Create an email rule and provide its general information. For details, see Define the Rule on the Configuration UI [page 14]. 18 PUBLIC How to Send Notifications Define the Rule on the Configuration UI -- 18 of 26 -- 2. Switch to the Rule Settings tab, define the context, condition, and the action of the rule in the following sections respectively. a. In the When section, provide the following required information: • Current Event: Select "GTT Overdue Event" from the list after clicking the value help icon. • Correlated Tracked Process: Select the tracked process that the current event is correlated to. In this example, select "Shipment". b. In the If section, click + and then select Compared to Specific Value. Provide the required information as follows: • Attribute: Select "Event Type" under Matched Planned Event. • Operator: Select "is equal to". • Value: Fill in the combination of model namespace, tracked process, and event type, separated by full stop ".". You can find the relevant information in the Manage Models app. • Model Namespace: you can find the namespace (example: com.lbngttapps.gtt.app.gttft1) on the model card of a model. • Tracked Process: the tracked process in which the event type is defined. You can find the name of each tracked process (example: Shipment) in the Event Type Pool tab of the model. • Event Type: you can find the name of each event type (example: Departure) under the corresponding tracked process in the Event Type Pool tab of the model. In this example, fill in “com.lbngttapps.gtt.app.gttft1.Shipment.Departure”. c. In the Then section, provide the required information. For details, see Define the Rule on the Configuration UI [page 14]. 3. Save your changes. 4.3 Example: Embed Public Links in Email Notifications Prerequisites You have enabled generating shipment links for public sharing via the event-to-action script in the Manage Models app. For instructions, see Generate Public Links for Shipments in Application Help. Context You can embed public links of shipments in email notifications, so recipients can receive the links in the email and access the shipment details directly with them. How to Send Notifications Define the Rule on the Configuration UI PUBLIC 19 -- 19 of 26 -- Procedure 1. In the Manage Notification Templates app, maintain a user-defined placeholder for public links in the email template body. It's must be in the format of "^{ Userdefined_Placeholder}", for example, ^{public_link}. For more, see Create Email Template [page 4]. 2. In the Manage Models app, create an email rule that uses the above email template. For more, see Define the Rule on the Configuration UI [page 14]. 3. In the placeholder section at the bottom of the Rule Settings page, click Add icon and choose Model Field Value. Provide the following information: a. Placeholder Name: enter the name of the user-defined placeholder for public links that you maintained in the Recipients field of your email template. In the given example, it's "public_link". b. Value: select the field "Shipment.ShipmentEvent.publiclink". 4. Save the rule. 4.4 Save a Tile You can save your email rules in a model as a tile on the home page of GTT Fiori Launchpad. When you click the tile, it brings you back to the Email Rules page in the Manage Models app. To save your email rules as a tile: 1. On the Email Rules page, click the  icon on the upper right corner and choose Save as Tile. 2. In the popup, enter a title. Optionally, you can provide a subtitle and description and choose a group on which the tile is displayed on your launchpad. 3. Click Save. To delete a saved tile, click the user icon in the upper-right corner of the home page and choose Edit Home Page. 20 PUBLIC How to Send Notifications Define the Rule on the Configuration UI -- 20 of 26 -- 5 Check Email Status Context To check the status of the email, do the following: Procedure 1. Launch the View Logs app. 2. Click the header tile of Message Log View card. Then you navigate to the Manage Message Logs app. 3. Click the message of the event you want to check. 4. The Message Details page appears. 5. In the Process Flow diagram, click the block below the Correlation stage. 6. The Correlation Details page appears. 7. In the Logs list of Process History, click Event to Action External. You can find the status of reminder service here. How to Send Notifications Check Email Status PUBLIC 21 -- 21 of 26 -- 6 Send SAP Qualtrics Feedback Survey Context After the goods are delivered and relevant events are reported in the GTT system, to send the link of a Qualtrics feedback survey about carriers to your customers, do the following: Procedure 1. Go to the official website of SAP Qualtrics: https://qualtrics.com/ to create a survey project. For more information on how to create a survey project, go to https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/standard-elements/ embedded-data/#SettingValuesFromAContactList . The survey can contain Embedded Data fields used as parameters of the survey. 2. Launch the Manage Notification Templates app to create a notification template. For more information on how to create a template, see the section Manage Notification Templates in the guide Application Help. The notification template contains the Qualtrics survey URL and the parameters defined in Embedded Data fields. 22 PUBLIC How to Send Notifications Send SAP Qualtrics Feedback Survey -- 22 of 26 -- 3. Launch the Manage Models app. Input scripts in the Event to Action tab of the corresponding model to define the conditions of the survey notification. Then deploy the model. 4. If the conditions are met, the notification email will be sent to your customers. 5. After the customers fill in the survey, you can analyze the feedback result. document covers the frequently asked questions (FAQs) for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. They are particularly useful when you are getting started. • FAQs for Solution Owners [page 4] • FAQs for Data Contributors [page 31] • FAQs for Common Apps [page 38] Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) About the FAQs PUBLIC 3 -- 3 of 44 -- 2 FAQs for Solution Owners As a solution owner, you can find frequently asked questions in the following sections about using SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace in general and its applications. 2.1 General Here you will find some frequently asked general questions about using SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. How can I find GTT documents? GTT documents are available on the web from: help.sap.com/gtt. Some of the documents can be downloaded for ease of use. However, they are updated regularly, sometimes between releases, with, for example, the latest features and details of the most recent bug fixes. So, before you start to read a particular document, please always check online to ensure that you have the latest version. What should I do if I experience problems with the GTT system? Your GTT system has been set up by your technical team and is run by your system administrator. If you experience issues while using your GTT system, please contact your system administrator. Which browsers are supported? SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace apps support the standard browsers supported by SAP BTP. For more information, see Browser Support chapter in Feature Scope Description for SAP BTP, Cloud Foundry, ABAP, and Kyma Environments. Which languages are supported? GTT apps support the following languages: • English (US) – default • Dutch • German • French • Polish • Portuguese (Brazilian) • Russian • Simplified Chinese • Spanish • Turkish • Italian • Japanese 4 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners -- 4 of 44 -- • Arabic • Bulgarian • Czech • Danish • Greek • Finnish • Hebrew • Croatian • Hungarian • Korean • Malay • Norwegian • Romanian • Slovak • Serbian • Swedish • Thai • Traditional Chinese • Ukranian How do I change the app language? The app language is defined by the language setting in your Web browser. You can also change the language by clicking the user button in the upper-right corner of the Fiori Launchpad window and choosing Settings. Then choose Language & Region and select the language that you want. Where can I find a glossary for the terms used in the apps and user assistance? You can find term definitions in the SAP terminology database: 1. Go to http://sapterm.com and click Look up SAP terminology. 2. Enter the search criteria: 1. Enter the term. 2. Select the source and target language. 3. Select the Advanced Search checkbox and choose the SBN-LBN-GTT component. 3. Click Search. Is there any in-app help available? Yes. To see it, on the Fiori Launchpad, click the green question mark (?) on the top right. This turns on a short description of each app. How many days before the new features in the test tenants sent to the productive tenants? The release of new features in the test tenants usually happens one month prior to the productive release for testing purposes. For example, if a feature is planned to be released in November, this feature will be released in test tenants in October first, then sent to productive tenants in November. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners PUBLIC 5 -- 5 of 44 -- Where can I see the release notes about the new features released in the test and productive tenants of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace? For the release notes of: • the productive tenants, see What's New for Production Tenants • the test tenants, see What's New for the Test Tenants Will I receive any notifications of updates after the release of features in the test and productive tenants of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace? Unfortunately, there is no option to subscribe to updates on the above-mentioned pages. But you can check the release schedule and dates in the Release Schedule. The updates are usually maintained on Monday after the release weekend. Is there any downtime when the new features are released in the productive tenants of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace? No, it happens seamlessly. How can I export data to external systems from SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace? You have the following four options: Option 1) Query ODATA Read Service 2) Forward via Event- to-Action Script 3) Export via Data Ex- port APIs 4) Replicate Data to SAP Business Network, intelligent insights add-on Definition SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace provides a Read Serv- ice API (ODATA) that populates all its data. It’s the same service that is also used by the tracking applications for collecting all data (process/events). You can also push data from SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace via event- to-action scripts. For example, when the last event is reported, a certain status is reached, or for every update, you can for- ward the relevant data to a defined endpoint. SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace provides data export APIs that you can use to export data. The tracked process, including its events is exported altogether. All files that correspond to one tracked process type will be wrapped within one zip file. You can integrate SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace to Intelligent In- sights with a single switch. After the in- tegration, you can di- rectly send data from SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace to Intelligent Insights for further analysis. In Intelligent Insights, you can configure your an- alytic scenarios using embedded toolsets. 6 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners -- 6 of 44 -- Option 1) Query ODATA Read Service 2) Forward via Event- to-Action Script 3) Export via Data Ex- port APIs 4) Replicate Data to SAP Business Network, intelligent insights add-on Advantages • Well-organized data format. • Comprehensive filter conditions. • Data is returned synchronously. • Synchronized call. • Better perform- ance than option 1. • You can export the data as per limited filtering. • No impact on event processing. • Asynchronized call. • No need to purchase SAP Analytics Cloud li- cense, as it is al- ready included in the add-on serv- ice. • Standard integra- tion. • Further exporting data from Intelli- gent Insights is also possible. Disadvantages • Limitation of 256 records per call. • Performance not as good as the other options. • Attachment is not directly sup- ported. • This may impact the performance of your event processing as the forwarding action takes additional time. • Attachment is not directly sup- ported. • Data is returned asynchronously as the request is running with a background job. You need to re- quest the data and you get it af- ter the job is fin- ished. • Compared to ODATA Read Serv- ice, it returns a ZIP file, so you need to write ex- tra codes to get the content of these files. • Attachment is not directly sup- ported. • Need to purchase SAP Business Network, intelli- gent insights add- on. • Not very benefi- cial if you have al- ready purchased SAP Analytics Cloud or cross reference some data outside SAP Business Network for Logistics. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners PUBLIC 7 -- 7 of 44 -- • Also, on the right side menu, please feel free to provide any comments that might help us to improve this section, such as corrections or suggestions for other FAQs. 2.2 Fulfillment Tracking Apps Here you can find frequently asked questions that are common to following fulfillment tracking apps: Track Shipments, Monitor Inbound ASNs, Monitor Outbound Deliveries, Track SO Fulfillment, Track PO Fulfillment. Can I share tracking links with my business partners or customers? As a solution owner of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, you can share the tracking links of the fulfillment tracking apps with your business partners or customers through the notification service. For more, go to http://help.sap.com/gtt and search for the guide: How to Send Notifications. So far, business partners can view the links only by being an internal user of your tenant. For more, see the section Create Users in Identity Authentication in Administration Guide for Solution Owners. You can also configure which tracked process this partner can see by applying attribute-based authorization. For more, see the section Specify Attributes in the Role Using “ReadServiceAttributeTemplate” in Administration Guide for Solution Owners. If this partner collaborates with multiple solution owners in the network, the partner will have to log onto different solution owners’ tenants to see the corresponding shipments. We also plan to provide an app for business partners to view the shipments directly. For more, see the road map . What are the prerequisites of using fulfillment tracking apps with integration to SAP S/ 4HANA? For the prerequisites of integrating SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace with SAP S/4HANA, see the Prerequisites section in How to Send Documents from SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace For the prerequisites of using sample codes for SAP S/4HANA extractors, see Requirements section of the GTT repository in the SAP Samples organization on GitHub.com What’s the difference between event status Delayed, Reported Late and Overdue? • Status Delayed indicates that a Delay event is reported. • Status Reported Late indicates that an actual event is reported to occur later than the expected time window. • Status Overdue indicates that no actual event has been reported when the expected time window is overdue. Can I report a planned event many times? Yes, and all its actual events are displayed in the Reporting History dialogue. How do fulfillment tracking apps get the geographical coordinates information? For reported events, the geographical coordinates in the event payload are used first. If they are not provided, the location information that you maintained in the Manage Locations app will be used. 8 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners -- 8 of 44 -- For unreported planned events, the location information that you maintained in the Manage Locations app is used. How can I define user-defined tracked processes / field types / event types / code lists / planned event extensions? There are two steps: • Go to the Manage Models app. Create user-defined tracked processes / field types / event types / code lists / planned event extensions in the GTT standard model “gttft1”. For instructions, go to http:// help.sap.com/gtt to search for Guide for Model Administrators. • Enhance data extractors for user-defined tracked processes / field types / event types / code lists / planned event extensions. If you use SAP S/4HANA to extract the data, you can refer to sample codes on GitHub.com:https://github.com/SAP-samples/logistics-business-network-gtt-standardapps-samples . How does the observing tracked process receive events from the observed process in stage level observation? Now the observing tracked process always receives reported planned events propagated from the observed tracked process, and only receives unplanned events of the assigned stages. In this case, no important information is lost. For example, when a freight unit observes a shipment, the freight unit always gets the reported planned events propagated from the shipment but starts to get the unplanned events of the assigned stages from the shipment only when the first planned event is reported. It stops getting these unplanned events once the last stop’s arrival event is reported.  Note In the GTT system, the stage level observation applies to the following observation relationship between tracked processes: • OutboundDelivery observes Shipment • InboundDelivery observes Shipment • FreightUnit observes Shipment • FreightUnit observes TrackingUnit • FreightOrder observes TrackingUnit What actual events can be sent from the SAP S/4HANA system to the GTT system? To know types of actual events for each tracked process that can be sent from SAP S/4HANA to the GTT system, refer to the following sections in Sample Code Configuration Guide for Integration with SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace on Github.com: • 4.12.3 Define Event Types for Purchase Order Item • 4.13.3 Define Event Types for Inbound Delivery Header • 4.13.4 Define Event Types for Inbound Delivery Item • 4.15.3 Define Event Types for Outbound Delivery Header • 4.15.4 Define Event Types for Outbound Delivery Item • 4.16.2 Define Event Types for Shipment Header • 4.17.2 Define Event Types for Freight Unit Header • 4.18.2 Define Event Types for Road Freight Order/Ocean Booking/Air Booking Header Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners PUBLIC 9 -- 9 of 44 -- What is the size limit for attachments that I can upload when reporting an event? The total size of attachments cannot exceed 10MB. 2.2.1 Track Shipments App Here you will find some frequently asked questions about the Track Shipments (TS) app. What does the TS app enable me to do? This app allows you to monitor the real-time execution status of LE-TRA shipments and freight documents from SAP S/4HANA and report events manually. The tasks associated with this app include the following: • Displays a list of all the available shipments • Monitors the milestone fulfillment status of shipments including Loading Start, Check-in, Loading End, Departure, Proof of Delivery, Arrival, etc. • Reports planned and unplanned events for the shipment • Monitors the real-time location and status of the shipments and the relevant freight units • Tracks the carbon emissions of the shipments • Supports parcel tracking and container tracking in the TM scenario • Supports navigation to the Monitor Inbound ASNs, Monitor Outbound Deliveries, Track SO Fulfillment and Track PO Fulfillment apps. Can I customize the filters and columns on the worklist page? Yes. You can find the other filters not displayed by default by clicking the Adapt Filters button, and other columns not displayed by default by clicking the Settings icon. Then you can change the default settings and save your own variants. Can I customize the tables on detail pages? Yes. You can customize the table settings by clicking the Settings icon and save the customized table as a variant. What event types are displayed in the Tracking Timeline tab? Beside the following event types, all the other event types of the "Shipment" or all the other admissible event types of the "FreightUnit" tracked process in the standard model "gttft1" can be displayed in the timeline: • Location Update • Technical Use • Estimated Time Update • event types marked "For Internal Use Only" • "Delay" and "On Time" with reference to a planned event • GTT Tracking Request Error Event What event types are used to draw the planned and actual routes in the map on the Shipment Details page? Beside the following event types, all the other event types of the "Shipment" or all the other admissible event types of the "FreightUnit" tracked process in the standard model "gttft1" with valid geographical coordinates are used to draw the routes: 10 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners -- 10 of 44 -- • Technical Use • Manifest Ready • Flight Booked • event types marked "For Internal Use Only" • Customs Hold Start • Customs Hold End • Other • Slot Booking • Subsequent Vehicle Ready What is the sorting logic of the events in the Tracking Timeline tab? Planned events are sorted by planned sequence. The sequence is calculated by the system and decided by the configuration of the Sort Planned Events By setting of the "Shipment" and "FreightUnit" tracked processes in the GTT standard model “gttft1”. Unplanned events are sorted by the actual business timestamp. Why can’t I see the Attachments button in the Tracking Timeline tab? The Attachments button only appears after you upload the attachments when you report the event. Why can’t I see the emission information on the Shipment Details page? The emission information only appears in the Emissions tab when the relevant emission event is reported. Can I view the details of an actual event in the app? Yes. In the Tracking Timeline tab of detail pages, you can click an actual event in the Reporting History dialog or Show Details button to navigate to the Event Details page to view the actual event details. Does container tracking work with project44? Yes, if the container ID is provided, project44 can support tracking multiple containers. What event types of the “Shipment” tracked process can be synchronized back to TM in SAP S/4HANA? Please see Supported Event Types and Fields. How to stop events from synchronizing back to TM in SAP S/4HANA? In the standard model “gttft1”, the events that are synchronized back to TM in SAP S/4HANA are defined in the standard declaration of the Event to Action tab. To stop certain events from synchronizing back, you must add your own script in the “User Script Before Standard Script” section to overwrite the standard declaration. For example, you can add the following script to stop the “Departure” and “Arrival” events from synchronizing back to TM in SAP S/4HANA:  Sample Code if (DEPARTURE_EVENT == actualEvent.eventType || ARRIVAL_EVENT == actualEvent.eventType ) { eventForwardToTM = false; } Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners PUBLIC 11 -- 11 of 44 -- Why can’t I see planned events' locations on the map of my shipment? There are tree possibilities: 1. You didn’t maintain the planned events’ locations in the Manage Locations app. In this case, go to the app to maintain them. For details, see Creating a Location section in Manage Locations. 2. You have maintained the location information such as logical system, object type and external ID incorrectly in the Manage Locations app. In this case, identify the wrong information and correct it. The major steps are as follows: 1. Go to the Check Processes and Events app to find your shipment. 2. In the Planned Events tab of the Process Details page, find the Location Alternative Key of the location used in the event. For example, if you can’t see the departure location “SP_0001” on the map, then you need to find the location alternative key of the “Departure” event in the table. The format of a location alternative key is: xri://sap.com/id:LBN#<your tenant's LBN ID>:<location's logical system>:Location:<location's object type>:<location's external ID>. 3. Go to the Manage Locations app to find the corresponding location information of “SP_0001” that you have maintained. 4. Compare the logical system, object type and external ID of the location “SP_0001” in the Manage Locations app with the ones in the location alternative key to identify the wrong information and correct it. 3. You have maintained the locations, but their geo coordinates are missing. In this case, add the geo coordinates in the Manage Locations app. When can I initiate tracking for my shipment? You can initiate tracking when the shipment has at least one tracked object or one carrier reference document. Related Information Guide for Transportation Planners 2.2.2 Monitor Inbound ASNs App Here you will find some frequently asked questions about the Monitor Inbound ASNs (MIA) app. What does the MIA app enable me to do? This app allows you to monitor the inbound ASN/delivery fulfillment status. The tasks associated with this app include the following: • Displays key and user-defined information tracked for an inbound ASN/delivery process • Displays the tracking timeline to reflect the latest status of the events of an inbound ASN/delivery process • Displays the real-time transportation route in the map view of the inbound ASN/delivery • Displays the relationships between inbound ASN/delivery and shipment. If you use TM in SAP S/4HANA) to manage the inbound ASN fulfillment, it displays the relationships between inbound ASN/delivery items and freight unit items. 12 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners -- 12 of 44 -- • Supports navigation to the Track Shipments (TS) app to check the shipment and freight unit details • Supports navigation to the Track PO Fulfillment (TPOF) and Track SO Fulfillment (TSOF) apps. What does ASN stand for? It stands for "Advanced Shipping Notification" sent by the supplier to the buyer. What is the inbound delivery? It is a document generated in the buyer' s SAP S/4HANA system to store the content from the inbound ASN. Can I customize the filters and columns on the worklist page? Yes. Beside the following event types, all the other admissible event types of the "InboundDelivery" tracked process in the standard model "gttft1" with valid geographical coordinates are used to draw the routes: • "Technical Use" event type • "Manifest Ready" event type • "Flight Booked" event type • event types marked "For Internal Use Only" • "Other" event type What is the sorting logic of the events in the Tracking Timeline tab? Related Information Guide for Receiving Specialists 2.2.3 Monitor Outbound Deliveries App Here you will find some frequently asked questions about the Monitor Outbound Deliveries (MOD) app. What does the app enable me to do? The Monitor Outbound Deliveries (MOD) app allows you to monitor the fulfillment status of outbound deliveries. The tasks associated with this app include the following: • Displays key and user-defined information tracked for an outbound delivery process • Displays the tracking timeline to reflect the latest status of the events of an outbound delivery process • Displays the real-time transportation route of the outbound delivery in a map view • Displays the relationships between outbound delivery and shipment. Go to the Visibility Provider Integration tab of the MM app to map visibility provider interfaces with a tracked process and its actual events. You can maintain the recipient in two ways: • First go to the Manage Notification Templates app to choose system-defined /application-defined placeholders or define user-defined placeholders in the Recipients field, and then go to the Manage Models app to set the value of placeholders in the Event to Action script. • Or go to the Manage Models app to directly define a Recipient value in the recipients payload in the Event to Action script. You cannot maintain the sender. The sender is the system email address of SAP Business Network for Logistics. Why can’t I deploy a model? If you can’t deploy a model, a model validation error or technical communication error will pop up. You can check the detailed error message and what you should do in the History view of the model. What does correlation level mean? Correlation level: • is the level of event correlation propagation between tracked processes within a model • is specified as an integer from 1 to 5 Each tracked process has a list of observed tracked processes. You can add a tracked process to the observed tracked process list by the process creation/update event or by some other actual events. For example, suppose tracked process A observes tracked process B and tracked process B observes tracked process C. • If the model is configured to have 1 level of correlation, then events reported to tracked process C are also correlated to B. • If the model is configured to have 2 levels of correlation, then events reported to tracked process C are also correlated to both tracked processes A and B. • And so on. For which tracked process can I initiate tracking? You can initiate tracking for any tracked process through visibility providers, such as shipment, delivery, and so on. To initiate tracking, you need to use the function sendTrackingRequest in the event-to-action script. For more, see Guide for Model Administrators. Related Information View Logs 2.6 Manage Message Logs App Here you will find some frequently asked questions about the Manage Message Logs (MML) app. What does the MML app enable me to do? This app allows assigned users to view all the technical logs for all the message data, phase by phase and, if necessary, retrigger certain events or their correlations for the message. The tasks associated with this app include the following: • Displays a list of all the messages used to update a process or for business actual event reporting • Displays log details for each message including its process flow and payload • Displays log details for each event including its process history and payload • Displays log details for each correlation about its process history, phase by phase • Enables historical events and correlations, within a retention period, to be retriggered. How does the MML app receive the external source types? SAP ERP messages are sent with the predefined support of IDOC adapter. Visibility Provider messages are sent with the Visibility Provider adapter. The other external messages need to call the write service directly. What is the Tracking ID? The Tracking ID, which is parsed from the message payload, refers to the tracked process ID. What is the Message No.? The Message No. is the message identification number given by the source system. 22 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners -- 22 of 44 -- What is the Source ID? The Source ID is the source system ID identified by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace or the LBN ID of the visibility provider. What does the source type Internal mean? Internal indicates that the message is generated by SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. What does the Event Type mean? The type of events that the message creates, such as the process update event, process deletion event, and actual business event. What does the status Pending mean? The status Pending means that the message processing is not finished. You need to wait and refresh the Message Details page for the result. What does the status Not Relevant mean? The status Not Relevant means that the event is correlated with the observing tracked process but does not match any admissible planned or unplanned events. For example, suppose that the tracked process “Delivery” observes the tracked process “Shipment”. When the event “Geolocation Update” is correlated with the tracked process “Delivery” but there is no admissible planned or unplanned events designed for this event, the status of this event then becomes “Not Relevant”. What does the Retention button enable me to do? You can use it to control the log volume by setting the retention period. The default and maximum period is 30 days. What does the Retrigger button enable me to do? The Retrigger button allows you to retrigger a selected process event, actual event or correlation, but not including an overdue event type. Retriggering: • reprocesses the selected item from phase one to the last phase • allows you to fix an error then retrigger the item with the error and in so doing, clear the error • generates a new entry in the Process History tab on the Event Details page or Correlation Details page Note that if you retrigger an event on the Event Details page, it will restart all its following correlations. If you retrigger a correlation on the Correlation Details page, it will only restart the selected correlation. This app allows assigned users to view all the technical logs for all the event data, phase by phase and, if necessary, retrigger one or multiple events or their correlations. The tasks associated with this app include the following: • Displays a list of all the events (tracked process events and actual events), and their correlations • Displays log details for each event including its process flow, process history and payload • Displays log details for each correlation about its process history, phase by phase • Enables historical events and correlations, within a retention period (which is configured in the MML app), to be retriggered • Enables the setup of rules to retrigger certain events and correlations automatically. What does the Auto Retrigger Rules button enable me to do? It allows you to set up rules to retrigger certain events and event correlations automatically. How often does the system run my auto retrigger rule? After you activate the rule, the system will filter the events and event correlations based on the rule and retrigger them every five minutes.  Note Some FAQs for the MML app also apply to the MEL app. For more, see Manage Message Logs App [page 22]. Related Information Manage Event Logs 2.8 Invite Business Partners App Are you a solution owner with a question about your Invite Business Partners app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. I want to upload a business partner Excel file. What is the size restriction for the file? The size of each business partner Excel file cannot be larger than 2 MB, and the maximum number of rows in it is 5,000. 24 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners -- 24 of 44 -- If I have, for instance, five business partners in a business partner Excel file, can I upload only three of them? No, you cannot select multiple business partners from a business partner Excel file and upload them. There is missing data in the business partner Excel file. However, the system still uploads the data. Why? The system uploads the Excel data because there is no Excel validation. However, when you save the uploaded data in your app, this may result in an error. How can I edit the business partner details? When you upload a business partner, you can edit the business partner details before saving using the in-line editing capability. You can also edit the business partner details later by selecting the business partner and choosing Edit. How do I enter missing business partner data before saving it in my network tenant? You can use one of the following ways to provide missing business partner data before saving: • Maintain the missing data in the source system (for example, your SAP Transportation Management system) and re-export the business partner data to Excel. • Manually enter the missing business partner data in the business partner Excel file before uploading the file to your network tenant. • Manually enter the missing business partner data using the in-line edit functionality in your network tenant before saving the data. Why do I get an error message when I save business partner data? The error message appears for one of the following reasons: • You have not entered the business partner details completely. For example, you may not have entered any data in the Business Partner ID field, which is mandatory. • You have already uploaded this business partner in your app and chosen to submit the business partner to the backend team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection request. If I accidentally delete a business partner, will I be able to re-upload the business partner? Yes, you can re-upload a business partner if you have not previously chosen Submit for the business partner. When you select a business partner and choose Submit, the system instantaneously sends a request to the backend team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection request. Hence, you are not able to re-upload such business partners. What happens if I re-upload an existing business partner? When you re-upload an existing business partner, the system overwrites the existing business partner details with the new details. Can I create multiple business partners with the same system ID and business partner ID? No, you cannot create multiple business partners with the same IDs. The system uses the combination of the system ID and business partner ID as the unique identifier of a business partner. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners PUBLIC 25 -- 25 of 44 -- Why am I not able to edit business partner data once I submit the business partner? Once you submit the business partner data, the system instantaneously sends a request to the backend team of SAP Business Network for Logistics to manage the connection request. After this process, you cannot make any changes as these changes will not be updated in the administrator app. Can I re-submit business partner data? No, you cannot re-submit business partner data. What happens when a business partner accepts my invitation? When a business partner accepts your invitation to connect with you, the system updates the Accepted tab with the details of this business partner. You are now connected with this business partner and you can participate in business transactions with the business partner. What happens when a business partner rejects my invitation? When a business partner rejects your invitation to connect with you, the system updates the Rejected tab with the details of this business partner. You are not connected with this business partner and you cannot participate in business transactions with the business partner. A business partner has rejected my invitation. Can I contact this business partner through my network tenant? No, you cannot contact a business partner directly through your network tenant. Why is the Download Business Partners button available only on the Accepted tab? You use the Download Business Partners button to download the list of business partners with their network IDs that the system updates after they accept the connection invitation. You use this list to update the network IDs in your SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) system. Can I partially download some of the business partners from the Accepted tab? Yes, you can select one or more business partners on the Accepted tab and download them in Microsoft Excel format. You must maintain a system connection to exchange messages between your system and your network tenant. 26 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Solution Owners -- 26 of 44 -- How do I get informed when a certificate is about to expire? To receive a notification about an expiring certificate, you need to register with the Cloud System Notification Subscriptions application. For more information, go to https://support.sap.com/en/my-support/systems- installations/cac.html . How can I renew a certificate when it expires? To renew a certificate, you must delete the old certificate once the validity expires and add a new certificate. Is it mandatory to have a certificate in my system that must be signed by one of the certificate authorities (CAs) available in the load balancer? Yes, it is mandatory to have a certificate signed by one of the CAs available in the load balancer. If you have a certificate that is signed by a different CA, you must create a ticket. The backend team of SAP Business Network for Logistics will upload your certificate to the network. Can I provide multiple certificates for a connection? Yes, you can provide multiple certificates for a connection. Can I have multiple connections for a system? Yes, you can have multiple connections for a system. Can I provide a message type of my own? No, you cannot provide a message type of your own. Can I maintain multiple system connections with the same combination of system ID and connection ID? The system uses the combination of a system ID and connection ID as a unique identifier for a connection. Hence you cannot use the same combination of IDs more than once. Can I edit a system connection once it is created? Yes. Only connection ID and system ID cannot be changed once created. Is it mandatory to maintain a destination in the Outbound from Network section? No, you do not need to maintain a destination for connection unless you need to send a document or a message from your network tenant to your system. Will the connection status automatically be updated if the status of the external system undergoes a change? That is, if the external system is removed from the landscape? No, there will not be any automatic updates in this scenario. The backend team of SAP Business Network for Logistics must manually change the connection status. For more information, see Browser Support chapter in Feature Scope Description for SAP BTP, Cloud Foundry, ABAP, and Kyma Environments. Which languages are supported? GTT apps support the following languages: • English (US) – default • Dutch • German • French • Polish • Portuguese (Brazilian) • Russian • Simplified Chinese • Spanish • Turkish • Italian • Japanese Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Data Contributors PUBLIC 31 -- 31 of 44 -- • Arabic • Bulgarian • Czech • Danish • Greek • Finnish • Hebrew • Croatian • Hungarian • Korean • Malay • Norwegian • Romanian • Slovak • Serbian • Swedish • Thai • Traditional Chinese • Ukranian How do I change the app language? You can also change the language by clicking the user button in the upper-right corner of the Fiori Launchpad window and choosing Settings. Then choose Language & Region and select the language that you want. Where can I find a glossary for the terms used in the apps and user assistance? You can find term definitions in the SAP terminology database: 1. Go to http://sapterm.com and click Look up SAP terminology. 2. Enter the search criteria: 1. Enter the term. 2. Select the source and target language. 3. Select the Advanced Search checkbox and choose the SBN-LBN-GTT component. 3. Click Search. Is there any in-app help available? Yes. To see it, on the Fiori Launchpad, click the green question mark (?) on the top right. This turns on a short description of each app. How many days before the new features in the test tenants sent to the productive tenants? The release of new features in the test tenants usually happens one month prior to the productive release for testing purposes. For example, if a feature is planned to be released in November, this feature will be released in test tenants in October first, then sent to productive tenants in November. 32 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Data Contributors -- 32 of 44 -- Where can I see the release notes about the new features released in the test and productive tenants of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace? For the release notes of: • the productive tenants, see What's New for Production Tenants • the test tenants, see What's New for the Test Tenants Will I receive any notifications of updates after the release of features in the test and productive tenants of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace? Unfortunately, there is no option to subscribe to updates on the above-mentioned pages. But you can check the release schedule and dates in the Release Schedule. The updates are usually maintained on Monday after the release weekend. Is there any downtime when the new features are released in the productive tenants of SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace? No, it happens seamlessly. Yow now have several options including: • On the left menu, you can click on the apps that your role can use. If you do so, you’ll see more FAQs covering that app. • On the right side menu, you can print this page. This printout includes the answers to any questions you have currently selected. • Also, on the right side menu, please feel free to provide any comments that might help us to improve this section, such as corrections or suggestions for other FAQs. 3.2 User Management App Are you a data contributor administrator with a question about your User Management app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. Is this app relevant for all data contributors? Yes. This app is relevant for data contributors that have purchased SAP Business Network Logistics Provider, basic membership. How can I see a given record in the display? Validate if you have any filters applied. There are also tabs that you could click into to reduce the searchable list down to a smaller set. How can I edit a given record? Tell your administrator to grant you the necessary access rights. You can find the list of the access rights inCreate a User and Assign User Groups . What happens after I create a user in this app? The new user is created in your company's tenant and added to the specified user groups. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Data Contributors PUBLIC 33 -- 33 of 44 -- The system will send an activation email to the user so that he or she can set the password and access the relevant apps. Note that if the user already exists in SAP Business Network for Logistics, no activation email will be sent because the user was already activated for the network. What happens after I delete a user in this app? The user is deleted from your company's tenant and can no longer access the apps in the tenant. The app shows some existing user groups for assignment. Can I create or modify user groups? The user groups are predefined and cannot be created, modified, or deleted by users. Related Information User Management 3.3 System Connections App Are you a data contributor with a question about your System Connections app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. Where can I find information about APIs for SAP Business Network for Logistics? Go to SAP API Hub athttps://api.sap.com/package/LbnGlobalTrackAndTrace?section=Overview Where can I find information about OAuth 2.0 authentication for inbound-to-network communication? For more information about OAuth 2.0 authentication, please report an incident under component SBN-LBN- INT. Can I add to the list of supported API operations? The list of operations is fixed and cannot be added to. Related Information System Connections (Data Contributor) 34 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Data Contributors -- 34 of 44 -- 3.4 Manage Invitations App Are you a data contributor with a question about your Manage Invitations app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. I have received new invitations for connections. Is there a stipulated time frame within which I must respond to these invitations? No, there are no restrictions on the response time. I have rejected an invitation accidentally. Can I resend a response or must I contact the SAP Business Network for Logistics team and place a request for that specific invitation? Once you accept or reject an invitation, you cannot reverse it as the system updates the business partner instantaneously. Also, there is no option to submit a request to the SAP Business Network for Logistics team. Is it mandatory to provide a rejection reason when I reject an invitation? No, it is not mandatory. However, when you specify a rejection reason, it would help the inviter understand the issues. What happens once I accept an invitation? When you accept an invitation from the inviter, the system notifies the inviter that you have accepted it. You can connect with the inviter’s network to perform business transactions. What happens once I reject an invitation? When you reject an invitation, the system notifies the inviter that you have rejected it. You cannot connect with the inviter’s network to perform any business transactions. When I receive a new invitation, will I be notified? No, you will not receive any alert or notification when you receive a new invitation. All the new invitations will be displayed on the New tab until you send a response. Why can't I locate my invitation? You can try the following: • Check if you have any filters or searches applied to the current page that could limit your list if you are searching for something specific that does not match the business partner you want to connect with. • Click around to the tabs with other status tags. For example, click the Accepted or Rejected tab to search for your invitation. Can I restrict the number of invitations displayed? No, you cannot restrict the display of invitations. The invitations are grouped based on the response status and you can view them on the corresponding tabs. I need to verify the details of the inviter before responding to the invitation. Where can I find more information? The system does not currently enable you to access additional inviter details. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Data Contributors PUBLIC 35 -- 35 of 44 -- Related Information Manage Invitations 3.5 Define User Settings App Are you a data contributor with a question about your Define User Settings app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. Which user settings can be personalized? You can set the distance unit of measure to either miles or kilometers. You can also subscribe to various notification services. What happens when I set the distance unit of measure? Once you set the distance unit of measure to miles or kilometers, the system applies this setting to all the business documents that you create subsequently. Note that the system does not apply this setting to the documents that you have already created. How can I get an email alert for a specific functionality? You can subscribe to notifications for a specific functionality in the Define User Settings app. The list of users subscribed to a notification will display in the Manage Notification Settings app. The list of options and their description is available at Manage Notification Settings. What are the scenarios for which I can subscribe to a notification service? The available scenarios are listed under Scenarios. To subscribe, select the checkbox under Subscribed. The list of scenarios and their description is available at Manage Notification Settings. What happens when I subscribe to a notification service? Once you subscribe to the notification service for a scenario, the system can send email notifications based on the settings you make in the Manage Notification Settings app. What do I need to do before I subscribe to a scenario? You must specify an email address. I have specified an email address but I do not want to subscribe to a scenario at present. Is that possible? Yes, you can maintain an email address without subscribing to a scenario. Do I need to maintain an email address even if I do not want to subscribe to a scenario? No, you do not need to maintain an e-mail address unless you want to subscribe to a scenario. 36 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Data Contributors -- 36 of 44 -- How do I change the app language? The app language is defined by the language setting in your Web browser. You can also change the language by clicking the user button in the upper-right corner of the Fiori launchpad window and choosing Settings. Then choose Language & Region and select the language that you want. Related Information Define User Settings Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Data Contributors PUBLIC 37 -- 37 of 44 -- 4 FAQs for Common Apps Here you can find frequently asked questions about the applications in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace that are used by both solution owners and data contributors. 4.1 Blocking Store App Do you have a question about your Blocking Store app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. How can I view the personal data during the blocking period? You can use the Blocking Store app to view the personal data during the blocking period. Note that you can access the Blocking Store app only if you have the required authorization. What happens to the document once it reaches the end of the blocking period? Once the blocking period is over, all the personal data of the document is deleted permanently. Related Information Blocking Store 4.2 Retention Management App Do you have a question about your Retention Management app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. What is the residence period and when does it start? It is the period between the end of business and the end of purpose for a data set. During the residence period, data remains in the database and can be used in case of subsequent processes related to the original purpose. At the end of the residence period, the data is blocked. Once the business document reaches the end of business, it enters the residence period. What is the blocking period and when does it start? The blocking period is the period between the end of the residence period and the deletion of the data. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a data protection officer, can access the data. At the end of the blocking period, the data is deleted. 38 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Common Apps -- 38 of 44 -- What is the retention period? The retention period is a combination of the residence period and the blocking period. It is the period between the end of the last business activity involving a specific object and the deletion of the corresponding data, subject to applicable laws. What is the end of purpose? The end of purpose for a business document is the point in time at which the primary processing purpose ends, such as a contract being fulfilled. For example, in the Freight Requests for Quotation app, a business partner is an item of master data. The end of purpose of this master data is the point in time at which the data is no longer relevant for business activities. How do I maintain the residence and blocking periods? And can I maintain different residence and blocking periods for each application? You can maintain the residence and blocking periods using the Retention Management app. You can specify the residence and blocking periods in months for an application type. If you do not specify a residence or a blocking period, the system sets it to 12 months by default. Yes, you can maintain different residence and blocking periods for each application. Related Information Retention Management 4.3 Manage Business Profile App Do you have a question about your Manage Business Profile app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. How do I edit or update the company profile? When you choose the Manage Business Profile tile on SAP Fiori Launchpad, the system opens the company profile page. You can edit or update the profile information by choosing the Edit icon in each section. How do I add multiple company addresses? Follow the instructions on Creating Additional Addresses. Why is it mandatory to maintain a default address? The default address is the address that will be displayed to other business partners in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. The default address is also the address that will be displayed when you launch the Manage Business Profile app. In general, the corporate address is chosen as the default address. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Common Apps PUBLIC 39 -- 39 of 44 -- My corporate address has changed. What should I do? After you launch the Manage Business Profile app, choose the Edit icon in the first section on your company profile and then enter your new address on the Address tab. Can I add a contact person for each of my addresses? No, you cannot add a contact person for each address. Is it mandatory to maintain sensitive data such as gross revenue in the profile? No, most information that you specify on the company profile page is optional. However, if you specify your business details, the business partner can use this information to analyze your business prospects before connecting with you. What are alternate identifiers and why should I specify them? Alternate identifiers are standard industry codes or compliance details, for example the DUNS Number. If you maintain this information, the business partner can verify your credibility and eligibility before connecting with you. Related Information Manage Business Profile 4.4 Manage Integration Logs App Are you a solution owner or a data contributor with a question about your Manage Integration Logs app? If so, take a look at these FAQs. One of the messages had a Failed status. Can I reprocess this message? Yes, after you solve the configuration or syntax issues pertaining to that business document, you can choose to reprocess this message. Only messages where the value in the Reprocessable column is set to Yes can be reprocessed. After I reprocessed a message, I am not able to view the log. Why? When you reprocess a message with the status Failed or Escalated, the system updates the status to Reprocessing. After the reprocessing has run, this message is updated to a final status of Failed, Escalated, or Completed. Where can I find the Manage Integration Logs - Integration Message Flow View version 1.0 app? The Manage Integration Logs - Integration Message Flow View (version 1.0) app has been sunset. You must switch to the new Manage Integration Logs (version 2.0) app. To start using the new app (as a shipper, solution owner or network owner), ask your system administrator to add the ManageIntegrationLogsDisplayTemplate and ManageIntegrationLogsTemplate roles to your role collection. If you are a carrier, data contributor or network participant, your role settings are managed by 40 PUBLIC Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) FAQs for Common Apps -- 40 of 44 -- SAP Business Network for Logistics. The app shall be visible in your SAP Fiori launchpad. For any queries or concerns, please report an incident in SAP for Me categorized by component SBN-LBN-INT. Can I reprocess my logs after 30 days? No. The reprocessing of a message is limited to 29 days. After 30 days, you won’t be able to reprocess the message or download the payload. In the app, these messages are highlighted in grey. What is the difference between status and overall status? In the Documents tab, integration logs are aggregated based on the LBN IDs of the parties involved, the document ID, and the scenario. The overall status of an entry in the Documents tab is derived from the latest status of an individual log that's part of the aggregation. The Documents tab is only displayed for shippers, solution owners, and network owners. How can I configure email notifications for failed or escalated messages? Data contrnibutors can schedule email notifications for the Integration Error V2 scenario as outlined in Manage Notification Settings.
