Welcome to SAP Business Network for Logistics! Your company has been invited to collaborate on the network by one of the business partners that you work with. What is the network and what are the benefits of joining? SAP Business Network for Logistics improves supply chain efficiency by connecting business partners on a collaborative network that supports jointly managing transactions, exchanging documents, and sharing insights across the value chain. For instance, upon invitation from a shipper, you – a carrier company – can activate your account on the network and collaborate with shippers on freight tendering, subcontracting, freight settlement, milestone reporting and dock appointment scheduling. SAP Business Network for Logistics is a cloud solution that provides your company with a range of apps which you can use to complete your daily tasks. For more information, see Introduction to SAP Business Network for Logistics - Video . This guide gives you information on how to activate your account for SAP Business Network for Logistics so you can sign in and start using the apps. If you have any issues following the steps, start by reading Frequently Asked Questions [page 11]. Activate Your Account Introduction PUBLIC 3 -- 3 of 30 -- 2 Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process This guide gives an overview of the simplified onboarding process designed for data contributors and carriers who are ready to use SAP Business Network for Logistics. It provides detailed procedures for activating your account on the network, creating your business profile, adding users, and connecting with the business partner that invited you.  Note Instructions provided in this guide apply to both the production and test environments. If you’re invited by a shipper or solution owner from the production environment, you can follow these instructions to onboard to the production environment. Similarly, if the invitation comes from the test environment, you can use the same steps to onboard to the test environment.  Note Since release 2405, the account activation process for logistics providers has been simplified so that companies without an SAP Store account can also register as a carrier or data contributor on SAP Business Network for Logistics. You, as a logistics provider (carrier or data contributor), will receive an invitation from a shipper or solution owner to start your simplified account activation process. However, if the invitation was sent before release 2405 - which is before June 1, 2024, for invitation senders using the Europe data center (EU10), and before July 1, 2024, for those using the United States data center (US20) - the previous account activation process still applies. For more information, see Getting Started (Prior to Release 2405) [page 14]. If you have any issues performing the getting started tasks, see Frequently Asked Questions [page 11].  Note To help you get started easily, most procedures described in this document are also presented with step-by-step screenshots on the Carrier Learning Portal under Connect With Your Customer: • Getting Started • Create Account • Connect Existing Account • Account Administration • Get Support 4 PUBLIC Activate Your Account Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process -- 4 of 30 -- 2.1 Register (for Free) as a Carrier/Data Contributor on SAP Business Network for Logistics This topic provides step-by-step instructions on how to complete the registration for SAP Business Network for Logistics. Prerequisites Your company has been invited to collaborate on the network by one of the business partners that you work with. As the administrator of your company, you've received the following invitation email. If you don't receive it, check your SPAM/Junk Mail box. Email Subject / Sender Purpose Action to Take <Company_Name_Of_Inviter> would like to connect with you on SAP Busi- ness Network From: noreply@us.bn.cloud.ariba.com The email contains a link for registering an account on SAP Business Network for Logistics. See the following procedure. 1. After you received an email invitation from a shipper or a solution owner, click Get started in the email message. When SAP Business Network for Logistics shows the welcome page, click Create new account.  Note If the shipper or solution owner (inviter) has enabled “Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network” in Profile Settings for cross-data-center connections, you, as the invitee, will be prompted to choose a designated data center where your company profile will initially be maintained. Keep in mind that, to increase the visibility of your company’s service coverage, capabilities, and strengths, your company profile will also be replicated to other data centers. If you do not want your profile to be replicated to other data centers, you have the option to abort the registration. 2. If you are creating a new account, verify the auto-populated email address and then click Proceed. 3. Follow the steps in the registration wizard. SAP Business Network asks for basic information about your business, such as your company name, address, and email address. You also create a username and password. The wizard performs automatic address validation to detect and correct any wrong or misspelled portion of a mailing address. A pop-up window shows a recommendation, which you can accept or reject. There is an ISO-based country- or region-specific drop-down list for state/province in the address section of the supplier profile. Select from the drop-down list (where available) instead of entering free text.  Note The person whose name is entered in the user account information section becomes the account administrator automatically. Account administrators can transfer the administrator role to another user later. Activate Your Account Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process PUBLIC 5 -- 5 of 30 --  Note When double byte non-Latin characters (such as Chinese) are detected in an address, a warning is displayed. A Latin character translation must then be provided by the user, which is also validated for correctness. 4. Read the terms of use, choose the check boxes if you agree to the terms, and then choose Create account. 5. (Optional) Print the Summary page for your records. You can also print the terms of use. Results You’ve registered an account on SAP Business Network. Additionally, you'll receive several emails as described in Follow-up Emails [page 6]. 2.2 Follow-up Emails After registering for SAP Business Network for Logistics, you will receive several follow-up emails from SAP Business Network. These emails are sent from noreply@us.bn.cloud.ariba.com. Make sure your email software doesn’t block these email addresses to avoid them going to your SPAM/Junk Mail box. The table below shows the emails you should expect to receive and the actions to take after receiving them. Email Subject / Sender Purpose Action to Take Welcome to SAP Business Network From: noreply@us.bn.cloud.ariba.com Notifies you that your SAP Business Network account has been created and your company's tenant on the network is ready to use. The email contains the following: • Your account information • The sign in URL (embedded in the Sign in button) Proceed with the next task Sign In to SAP Business Network for Logistics [page 7]. 6 PUBLIC Activate Your Account Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process -- 6 of 30 -- 2.3 Sign In to SAP Business Network for Logistics This topic explains how to sign in to SAP Business Network for Logistics by clicking on the URL provided in the email Welcome to SAP Business Network, entering the user credentials, and accepting the terms and conditions. It also mentions that you can change the language displayed in the user interface. Prerequisites You've registered an account on SAP Business Network and received the emails described in Follow-up Emails [page 6]. Procedure 1. In the email Welcome to SAP Business Network, click the Sign in button. The sign-in page for the network is displayed. You’re recommended to bookmark this URL so you can sign in more easily next time. Additionally, when you add more users to the network in the future, you need to send this URL to the new users. 2. On the sign-in page, enter your user credentials and click Continue. • E-Mail: enter the username listed in the email "Welcome to SAP Business Network". • Password: enter the password that you set when you activated the initial user. 3. Change your password and then choose Save. 4. Open the sign-in page (with the URL you bookmarked in Step 1) then use the new password to sign-in to the home page of SAP Business Network for Logistics. 5. You are prompted to update your account information. Choose Update Now in the pop-up window and then open the Manage Business Profile app to complete your company profile. To increase your visibility to future business partners, be sure your company profile is completed accurately. For more information, see Create Your Company Profile [page 8]. More Information The main window for SAP Business Network for Logistics opens. To change the language displayed in the user interface, click the user icon in the upper-right corner and choose Settings Language & Region .  Note You, as the initial user and administrator of your company, can add additional administrators to help you complete the tasks hereafter. See Add Users [page 9] for details. Activate Your Account Getting Started with SAP Business Network for Logistics via New Onboarding Process PUBLIC 7 -- 7 of 30 -- 2.4 Create Your Company Profile You need to create your company profile for SAP Business Network for Logistics. The information in the profile is required to successfully connect to business partners. You also need to specify whether or not you'd like to make your profile visible to potential business partners and automatically accept connection requests. For detailed information, see Manage Business Profile. 2.5 Configure a Technical User (Optional) A technical user is a token used for authentication and system connection. It is required only when you need to use the Write Service API provided by your solution owner on SAP Business Network for Logistics. If your company didn't have an S-User ID before registering SAP Business Network for Logistics, check the email with the subject "[PRIVATE] Your key to the SAP ecosystem" (see Step 3 in Register (for Free) SAP Business Network for Logistics in SAP Store [page 14]). The email contains the S-User ID for your company. The password is set when the email receiver activates the account using the link provided in the email. For more information, watch a short video S-Users Management in Carrier Administrative Trainings . It’s also possible that your company already had an S-User ID before registering SAP Business Network for Logistics. In that case, you need to contact a user administrator in your company for S-User sign-in credentials. If you have trouble identifying who the S-User is in your organization, you can contact the Customer Interaction Center (CIC). For more information, see the SAP for Me Online Help under Access and Authorizations . You'll also find more useful information on the SAP Help Portal for SAP Business Network logistics providers. Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Document History -- 4 of 34 -- 2 Overview  Recommendation Before you start working your way through this document, ensure you have the most recent version of this document that is available from the SAP Help Portal at: https://help.sap.com/docs/business-network-logistics-provider About This Guide This administration guide describes the steps you need to perform as an administrator to set up, configure, and administer SAP Business Network Logistics Provider. This guide addresses the following target audience: administrators, consultants, users and others involved with SAP Business Network Logistics Provider.  Note A logistics provider can be a carrier in SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration or a data contributor in SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace. About SAP Business Network Logistics Provider SAP Business Network for Logistics is an open network that connects business partners for inter-company collaboration. Freight collaboration and milestone reporting support you as a carrier or other logistics service provider to jointly manage the related transactions and exchange documents with your shippers. For more information, see Introduction to SAP Business Network for Logistics - Video . 2.1 Technical Considerations Note that there are restrictions regarding the overall data volume that can be managed. Before starting your project, discuss your expected data volumes with your SAP technical contact. Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Overview PUBLIC 5 -- 5 of 34 -- 2.2 Browser Support This application only supports the standard browsers supported by SAP Business Technology Platform. For more information, see the Browser Support chapter in Feature Scope Description for SAP BTP, Cloud Foundry, ABAP, and Kyma Environments. Root Certificate for End User UI The browser certificate store must contain both the old root certificate (DigiCert Global Root G2) and the new root certificate (DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5). Without this, the end user sign-in to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace will be impacted. To check if you are impacted, try to access the following URL: https://digicert-tls-rsa4096-root-g5.chain-demos.digicert.com . If your browser loads the page without warning, it trusts the DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 and no further action is required on your end. To ensure a smooth transition, you need to run the check and take action (where applicable) before April 23, 2026. Resolution for user sign-in to the BN4L Fiori Launchpad - How to import the certificate into my browser? The below steps might vary with the browser type and version: • Download Root Certificate [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ] and Intermediate Certificate [DigiCert G5 TLS RSA4096 SHA384 2021 CA1 ]. • Open Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. • Open settings and search for security in the search box and click on it. • Click on Manage Device Certificates / Manage Certificates. • Go to the Trusted Root Certification Authorities tab and Import Digi Certificates using the Import button at the bottom. • Go to the Intermediate Certification Authorities tab and Import Digi Certificates using the Import button at the bottom. • Ensure that DigiCert Root and Intermediate is added in the list. For more information, see Switch to DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 [page 14]. 2.3 Product Availability This section describes certain product availability aspects. 6 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Overview -- 6 of 34 -- Availability - Languages The apps provided with SAP Business Network for Logistics support the following languages: • English (US) – default • Dutch • German • French • Polish • Portuguese (Brazilian) • Russian • Simplified Chinese • Spanish • Turkish • Italian • Japanese • Arabic • Bulgarian • Czech • Danish • Greek • Finnish • Hebrew • Croatian • Hungarian • Korean • Malay • Norwegian • Romanian • Slovak • Serbian • Swedish • Thai • Traditional Chinese In addition, selected documentation on SAP Help Portal supports the languages listed above. Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Overview PUBLIC 7 -- 7 of 34 -- 3 Onboarding and User Management A step-by-step guide will lead you through the process of registering SAP Business Network for Logistics, activating your account, signing in, and adding users. For more information, see Activate Your Account. 8 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Onboarding and User Management -- 8 of 34 -- 4 Business Configuration SAP Fiori Launchpad Integration The SAP Fiori launchpad is delivered with the apps as part of the tenant onboarding process. The users that you have defined can access different applications using the Fiori launchpad. You can sign in to the Fiori launchpad using a URL with the following format: https://<your-subdomain>-site-entry.<domain-name>/sites#Shell-home Set Up Business Profile For your business partners to search and connect with you in the network, you must maintain your business profile using the Manage Business Profile app. For more information, see Manage Business Profile app. Manage Notification Settings You can schedule reminder notifications for some of the business processes for which you may need an alert using the Manage Notification Settings app. The system sends you notifications via emails. For more information, see Manage Notification Settings (Carrier). Define User Settings You can define defaults that best suit the way you work using the Define User Settings app. The settings that you make in the app serve as the default settings in various other apps in your SAP Business Network for Logistics. For more information, see Define User Settings (Carrier). Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Business Configuration PUBLIC 9 -- 9 of 34 -- Manage Users As an administrator, you can use the User Management app to manage users in your company tenant, such as adding or deleting administrators or business users. For more information, see User Management. Manage Invitations from Business Partners To perform business in the network and to receive business documents from your business partners, you must first connect with them. An existing or potential business partner can send invitations to connect with you in the network. You can accept or reject the invitations using the Manage Invitations app. Navigate to the Manage Invitations app tile in the Fiori launchpad to access the app. For more information, see Manage Invitations. Freight Contracting You can participate in freight tendering when a known ordering party sends you a freight request for quotation (freight RFQ). You can accept or reject a freight RFQ. The freight collaboration option for SAP Business Network for Logistics creates a freight quotation and sends it to the ordering party. The ordering party then evaluates your freight quotation and, according to their strategy, may or not award it to you. For more information, see the application help for Freight Contracting. Freight Orders for Confirmation If an ordering party wants to subcontract the transportation of goods to you, you will find the corresponding freight orders in the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. This can also be a subsequent step to the tendering process, if your freight quotation was awarded. For more information, see the application help for the Freight Orders for Confirmation app. Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) You can review and confirm ocean freight bookings that ordering parties ask you to execute in subcontracting in the Freight Bookings for Confirmation app. For more information, see the application help for the Confirm Freight Bookings (Ocean) app. 10 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Business Configuration -- 10 of 34 -- Confirm Freight Bookings (Air) You can review and confirm air freight bookings that ordering parties ask you to execute in subcontracting in the Freight Bookings for Confirmation app. For more information, see the application help for the Confirm Freight Bookings (Air) app. Self-Book Dock Appointments You can book a dock appointment for a freight order in the Self-Book Dock Appointments app when the corresponding vehicle is about to reach a certain stop for loading or unloading. The appointments you booked will then be visualized in the Manage Dock Appointments app. This helps shippers have a precise estimate on the quantity of the upcoming dock appointments. For more information, see the application help for the Self-Book Dock Appointments app. Invoice Freight Documents You can view all the freight documents that are ready for invoicing using the Invoice Freight Documents app. You can view all the freight documents from one or more of your ordering parties using this app. You can select one or more of these freight documents and create a single invoice or a collective invoice for your ordering party for the services that you provided. For more information, see the application help for the Invoice Freight Documents app. Manage Invoices You can view all the invoices that you created in the freight collaboration option for your ordering party using the Manage Invoices app. For more information, see the application help for the Manage Invoices app. Review Freight Documents You can view all the freight documents that are ready for self-billing by the ordering party using the Review Freight Documents app. This app displays all the freight documents that you have received from one or more ordering parties. You can view the transportation charges in the freight document based on which the ordering party creates a self-billed invoice. You can create disputes against the freight documents for self-billing for additional unplanned freight costs using this app. For more information, see the application help for the Review Freight Documents app. Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Business Configuration PUBLIC 11 -- 11 of 34 -- Manage Disputes You can create disputes against the freight documents for self-billing for additional unplanned freight costs. Once the system creates a dispute, you can view this document in the Manage Disputes app. In this app, you can newly add a charge line for an additional charge encountered during the transportation or you can propose a change in an existing charge line. The ordering party can accept or reject your changes or propose another change and submit the dispute back to you. For more information, see the application help for the Manage Disputes app. Freight Orders for Reporting You can keep your ordering parties informed about the transportation of their freight using the Freight Orders for Reporting app. You can report when planned events in the freight order are completed. If a delay occurs, you can also use the app to report a new ETA (expected time of arrival), enabling the ordering party to replan if needed. For more information, see the application help for the Freight Orders for Reporting app. Note that the Freight Orders for Reporting app has been deprecated and will be sunset on May 16, 2026. This app has been replaced with the new app Manage Freight Execution. Manage Freight Orders The Manage Freight Execution app enables you to keep your ordering parties informed about the transportation of their freight. For example, if one of your shipments is delayed on-route, you can send the ordering party a new ETA (expected time of arrival) so they can replan if necessary. For more information, see the application help for the Manage Freight Execution app. 12 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Business Configuration -- 12 of 34 -- 5 Connectivity  Note The System Connections app is available for digital forwarders, carrier subnetworks, network partners, and carriers (B2B carrier/networks). By implementing the APIs published by SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace, your organization can receive and respond to business documents directly from your external system. To complete the API implementations, you – as an administrator – also need to perform the following steps using the System Connections app: 1. Set up Outbound Connections: • Choose Manage Details. • Enter the communication details and the authentication details to your external system. Then navigate back to Outbound Connections. • Configure the supported services in your external system. To do so, choose Create, and select a service name and an operation name from the drop down menu. You can create an API or EDI communication based on the details provided under Manage Details. • Activate the operation. 2. Set up Connection Settings: • Choose Connection Settings. • Under Outbound, in the Integration Platform dropdown list, you can choose between the following values: • Neo (old) • Multi-Cloud (new)  Note Ensure to allowlist the IP addresses of the integration platform. • If you use Neo (old), you must allowlist the IP addresses listed under Regions and Hosts Available for the Neo Environment. If you use Multi-Cloud (new) for outbound connections, you must allowlist the IP addresses listed under Regions and API Endpoints Available for the Cloud Foundry Environment. Neo (old) is set as default. To enable outbound communication using the new integration platform, select Multi-Cloud (new). • To authorize your inbound messages to SAP Business Network for Logistics, you need an OAuth token. To request the token from SAP, create a BCP ticket and use the component SBN-LBN-INT. • Turn on the Enable Inbound Communication toggle and save. For more information about the APIs published by SAP Business Network for Logistics, go to: • SAP Business Accelerator Hub for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Connectivity PUBLIC 13 -- 13 of 34 -- • SAP Business Accelerator Hub for SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace For more information about EDI integration, see the guides published on SAP Help Portal at https:// help.sap.com/docs/business-network-logistics-provider?task=integrate_task. Related Information System Connections (Carrier) 5.1 Switch to DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 SAP Business Network for Logistics is switching its root Certificate Authority to DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 for the domain *.logistics.*.business-network.cloud.sap to enhance security and trust. This is in line with the root certificate replacement in the SAP BTP, Cloud Foundry Environment. To ensure a smooth transition, customers must take action before April 23, 2026. For more information, see SAP Note 3688060 . As part of our ongoing commitment to security and trust, SAP is updating the root Certificate Authority (CA). This update supports the broader adoption of our fifth-generation (G5) root CA and allows additional time for its inclusion in major browser and operating system trust stores, ensuring seamless and trusted connectivity. Am I Impacted? This change could impact B2B Connectivity: The sender systems must trust both the old root certificate (DigiCert Global Root G2) and the new root certificate (DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5). Without this, the inbound communication to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace will be impacted. For information about a possible impact on the end user UI, see Browser Support [page 6]. Resolution for B2B Connectivity to BN4L: Case 1: When sender system is S/4HANA (On-Premise & Private Cloud) 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Upload this Root Certificate to all relevant SSL Client PSEs*. 3. For detailed steps, see SAP KBA 3238733 - How to Import a Certificate Into a STRUST PSE's Certificate List In a NetWeaver AS ABAP. 4. [DigiCert Global Root G2] should remain as is. 5. ICM restart should be necessary post change in STRUST, only if you are running old releases of Netweaver 700/701 and 64x. See SAP KBA 2746647 - SSSLERR_PEER_CERT_UNTRUSTED after importing the target certificate. Since Netweaver AS ABAP 710 and AS ABAP 702, ICM restart is no longer necessary. Case 2: When sender system is SAP NetWeaver PI (On-Premise & Private Cloud) 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Import this Root Certificate to TrustedCAs view of NetWeaver Java Key Storage. 14 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Connectivity -- 14 of 34 -- 3. For detailed steps, see SAP KBA 2056672 - How to import server certificates in PI system. Case 3: When WebDispatcher is placed in front of Cloud Integration endpoint 1. Download [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ]. 2. Import this Root Certificate to Trusted Certificates through Web Administration Interface of SAP WebDispatcher. 3. See SAP Help - PSE Management in Web Administration Interface of SAP Web Dispatcher, section [Trusted Certificates]. Case 4: When sender system is a non-SAP service/software 1. Consult your vendor for confirmation that it should trust [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ] for outbound TLS communication. 2. Particularly, in case of a customer written Java program, JDK version should be higher than the following: • SAP JVM 8.1.097 • SapMachine 11.0.22 • SapMachine 17.0.10 • SapMachine 21.0.2 • Oracle JDK 8u401 • Oracle JDK 17.0.10 • OpenJDK 17.0.10 • OpenJDK 21.0.2 For more information, see the following SAP Notes: • 3688060 • 3587968 • 3566727 • 3472211 5.2 Migration to New Integration Platform (Freemium Customer) SAP Business Network for Logistics is run on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) leveraging the various services provided by the platform. SAP BTP offers a variety of application environments that customers and internal SAP organizations can choose from, to build SAP applications and business solutions in the cloud. One critical service used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is the SAP Cloud Integration (previously known as SAP CPI) which acts as the single integration platform for all customers and partners for SAP Business Network for Logistics. This platform is owned and managed by the SAP Business Network for Logistics development team. Freemium customers can maintain necessary connectivity configurations using the System Connections app, and monitor their integration logs using the Manage Integration Logs app. SAP Cloud Integration used by SAP Business Network for Logistics is hosted in the Neo environment of SAP BTP. SAP BTP, Neo environment is the oldest of the application environments and is built on a proprietary SAP technology stack. The Neo environment in SAP BTP has been deprecated and will be sunset for internal SaaS applications (see SAP Note 3351844 ). SAP Cloud Integration is also offered in a multi-cloud foundation in SAP BTP, and this is the new platform that will be used by SAP Business Network for Logistics. Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Connectivity PUBLIC 15 -- 15 of 34 -- In accordance with SAP BTP’s decision to sunset Neo environment, SAP Business Network for Logistics has decided to stop the support of the existing Neo integration platform on July 18, 2025, as part of our July 2025 release. This means that connectivity to your backend transportation management system (TMS) will stop working if you don’t migrate to the new integration platform. This requires some configuration changes in your backend TMS and in your System Connections app in SAP Business Network for Logistics. You can read more about this change in this announcement . There is a comprehensive guide capturing the list of changes that a freemium customer must do to migrate from old integration platform to the new one. We understand the critical role that connectivity plays in SAP Business Network for Logistics. The primary focus is not to disrupt the existing integrations between your backend systems and SAP Business Network for Logistics. So, your existing configurations will stay intact and continue to work until you migrate to the new integration platform or till the end of support of the old integration platform. In the meanwhile, we have made it possible for you to migrate from the old integration platform to new one using the configuration apps in SAP Business Network for Logistics. This requires some changes in SAP Business Network for Logistics configuration apps as well as in your backend systems. You might also need to update your firewall/SAP Cloud Connector configurations as the IP range will be different for the new integration platform. We urge you to migrate as soon as possible to leverage the improved log capacity and other new features.  Note We recommend performing the migration activities in your test tenants first and then monitor if all the integration scenarios are working correctly. Proceed with the changes in your productive tenants accordingly. For more information, see the Integration Platform Migration Guide for Freemium Users. 5.3 Regions and Hosts Available for the Connectivity Platform Available data centers, and required IP ranges to be allowlisted Data Center-Specific Integration Platform SAP Business Network for Logistics can be hosted on the following data centers • Frankfurt, Germany (EU10) • Washington, US (US20) • Dammam, Saudi Arabia (SA30) There are dedicated integration tenants for customers in each data center. Based on which data center you’re onboarded to, the IP ranges of our integration platform differs. How to identify your tenant’s datacenter? For more information about security on SAP Business Technology Platform, see Data Privacy and Security in the (SAP BTP) documentation on SAP Help Portal. 6.1 User Administration, Authentication, and Authorizations It's important to consider the security-aspects of creating and configuring users and roles for the applications. Consider the following security aspects: • Grant users only the minimum level of authorization that's necessary. • Remove a user's authorization as soon as it's no longer required, for example, if an employee leaves the company. Related Information • Assign Users to Role Collections • Delete Users from Role Collections 6.2 Session Security Protection SAP Business Network for Logistics is restricted to operating with Secure Socket Layer (SSL) and activated cookie handling only in the browser. 6.3 Network and Communication Security SAP Business Network for Logistics uses the HTTPS protocol to encrypt communication between the browser and the service. Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Security and Data Protection and Privacy PUBLIC 21 -- 21 of 34 -- 6.4 Data Storage Security SAP Business Network for Logistics stores data in tenant-specific database schemas. Access to the databases are preconfigured with the infrastructure environment. The databases contain many different types of data including the following: • Personal data (for example, user names, email addresses, and so on) • Operational business data • Preferences and configurations This data is updated continuously whenever required or requested. 6.5 Data Protection and Privacy 6.5.1 Introduction Data protection is associated with numerous legal requirements and privacy concerns. In addition to compliance with general data protection and privacy acts, it is necessary to consider compliance with industry-specific legislation in different countries/regions. SAP provides specific features and functions to support compliance with regard to relevant legal requirements, including data protection. SAP does not give any advice on whether these features and functions are the best method to support company, industry, regional, or country-specific requirements. Furthermore, this information should not be taken as advice or a recommendation regarding additional features that would be required in specific IT environments. Decisions related to data protection must be made on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration the given system landscape and the applicable legal requirements.  Note SAP does not provide legal advice in any form. SAP software supports data protection compliance by providing security features and specific data protection-relevant functions, such as simplified blocking and deletion of personal data. In many cases, compliance with applicable data protection and privacy laws will not be covered by a product feature. Definitions and other terms used in this document are not taken from a particular legal source.  Caution The extent to which data protection is supported by technical means depends on secure system operation. Network security, security note implementation, adequate logging of system changes, and appropriate usage of the system are the basic technical requirements for compliance with data privacy legislation and other legislation. 22 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Security and Data Protection and Privacy -- 22 of 34 -- Generic Fields You need to make sure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non purpose-related way, for example, in free-text fields, through APIs or customer extensions, through notes and attachments in the apps, Microsoft Excel uploads and so on. Note that these are not subject to the read access logging (RAL) example configuration. Please do not include sensitive personal data (for example, social security numbers) or personal data (for example, addresses) since the attribute field is not set up with appropriate data protection measures. 6.5.2 Glossary The following terms are general to SAP products. Not all terms may be relevant for this SAP product. Term Definition Artificial Intelligence (AI) The simulation of human intelligence processes by machines and computer systems – typically by learning, coming to its own conclusions, appearing to understand complex content, engaging in natural dialogs with people, enhancing human cognitive performance (also known as cognitive computing) or replacing people on execution of nonroutine tasks. Appli- cations include autonomous vehicles, automatic speech rec- ognition and generation and detecting novel concepts and abstractions (useful for detecting potential new risks and aiding humans to quickly understand very large bodies of ever-changing information) Automated Decision Making The ability to make decisions by technological means with- out human involvement. Blocking A method of restricting access to data for which the primary business purpose has ended. Business Purpose The legal, contractual, or in other form justified reason for the processing of personal data to complete an end-to-end business process. The personal data used to complete the process is predefined in a purpose, which is defined by the data controller. The process must be defined before the per- sonal data required to fulfill the purpose can be determined. Consent The action of the data subject confirming that the usage of his or her personal data shall be allowed for a given pur- pose. A consent functionality allows the storage of a consent record in relation to a specific purpose and shows if a data subject has granted, withdrawn, or denied consent. Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Security and Data Protection and Privacy PUBLIC 23 -- 23 of 34 -- Term Definition Data Subject Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natu- ral person ("data subject"). An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identifica- tion number, location data, an online identifier, or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person. Deletion Deletion of personal data so that the data is no longer avail- able. End of Business Defines the end of active business and the start of residence time and retention period. End of Purpose (EoP) The point in time when the processing of a set of personal data is no longer required for the primary business purpose, for example, when a contract is fulfilled. After the EoP has been reached, the data is blocked and can only be accessed by users with special authorizations (for example, tax audi- tors). End of Purpose (EoP) check A method of identifying the point in time for a data set when the processing of personal data is no longer required for the primary business purpose. After the EoP has been reached, the data is blocked and can only be accessed by users with special authorization, for example, tax auditors. Personal data Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natu- ral person ("data subject"). An identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identifica- tion number, location data, an online identifier, or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of that natural person. Processing of Personal Data Processing means any operation or set of operations which is performed on personal data or on sets of personal data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, re- cording, organisation, structuring, storage, adaptation or al- teration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmis- sion, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure or destruction. Purpose The information that specifies the reason and the goal for the processing of a specific set of personal data. As a rule, the purpose references the relevant legal basis for the proc- essing of personal data. 24 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Security and Data Protection and Privacy -- 24 of 34 -- Term Definition Residence period The period of time between the end of business and the end of purpose (EoP) for a data set during which the data remains in the database and can be used in case of sub- sequent processes related to the original purpose. At the end of the longest configured residence period, the data is blocked or deleted. The residence period is part of the over- all retention period. Retention period The period of time between the end of the last business activity involving a specific object (for example, a business partner) and the deletion of the corresponding data, subject to applicable laws. The retention period is a combination of the residence period and the blocking period. Sensitive personal data A category of personal data that usually includes the follow- ing type of information: • Special categories of personal data, such as data reveal- ing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data, biometric data, data concerning health or sex life or sexual orientation. • Personal data subject to professional secrecy • Personal data relating to criminal or administrative of- fenses • Personal data concerning insurances and bank or credit card accounts Technical and organizational measures (TOM) Some basic requirements that support data protection and privacy are often referred to as technical and organizational measures (TOM). The following topics are related to data protection and privacy and require appropriate TOMs, for example: • Access control: Authentication features • Authorizations: Authorization concept • Read access logging • Transmission control / Communication security • Input control / Change logging • Availability control • Separation by purpose: Is subject to the organizational model implemented and must be applied as part of the authorization concept. 6.5.3 Consent Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Security and Data Protection and Privacy PUBLIC 25 -- 25 of 34 -- The processing of personal data (including its collection or its transfer) is based on purposes, legitimated by the fulfilment of a contract, a legal obligation, a vital interest, a public interest, a legitimate interest or a consent. In some cases, the data subject may also be the user. This SAP product provides functionality to capture consent of data subjects before collecting personal data, where no other legal ground exists. This allows data subjects to give and withdraw consent to process their personal data. Where data is processed for a purpose different than the original purpose or a privacy statement was changed, likely a new consent needs to be collected. Consent in the SAP Business Network for Logistics The terms of personal data collection are outlined in a Privacy Statement. Users are required to read and accept the Privacy Statement when signing in to the SAP Business Network for Logistics for the first time. Users can read the Privacy Statement and withdraw the consent at any time. To do that, click the user icon in the upper-right corner of the app window and choose Settings Privacy Statement . 6.5.4 Read Access Logging Read Access Logging is considered as an additional safeguard in the protection of personal data, because it helps to identify potential illegitimate access to personal data. Read access to sensitive personal data is partially based on legislation, and it is subject to logging functionality. Read access logging (RAL) is used to monitor and log read access to sensitive personal data that was disclosed via user interface, which can be extended to read access to other personal data. Data may be categorized as sensitive by law, by external company policy, or by internal company policy. When these read accesses are logged, you should be able check which user accessed personal data on which access channel and the date and time, depending on the configuration. Read access logging enables you to answer questions about who accessed particular data within a specified time frame. That logging also includes downloading attachments or files, logs for such events shall contain information to identify the attachment. Additionally, as for Read Access Logging across system boundaries, the respective “access” shall be logged as soon as sensitive personal data crosses the boundary from a trusted to an un-trusted area. Here are some examples of such questions: • Who accessed the data of a given business entity, for example a bank account? • Who accessed personal data, for example of a business partner? • Which employee accessed personal information, for example religion? • Which accounts or business partners were accessed by which users? Furthermore, log records can be viewed and queried, but access to them is restricted by adequate authorizations. The personal data for which read access shall be logged and the retention period of logs, can be configured. Products built using Java with an SAP HANA database as a back end use the audit trails and audit policies for change logging. For more information, see the Auditing Activity section in the SAP HANA Security Guide. This product uses the Log4J API for change logging. For more information, see JDBC Appender . This product uses a log façade for change logging. For more information, see the Appenders section of the Logback documentation . 26 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Security and Data Protection and Privacy -- 26 of 34 -- Java-based NetWeaver products use the security audit log of the SAP NetWeaver Application Server (AS) Java for change logging. For more information, see the Security Audit Log of the AS Java. Cloud products using SAP HANA XS and SAP HANA standalone use the audit trail and audit policies for change logging. For more information, see the Auditing Activity section in the SAP HANA Security Guide. 6.5.5 Personal Data Record The feature provides data associated to the Data Subject. It is in the duty of the customer to check, whether all the data reported shall get handed over to the data subject, because the report might contain internal customer information or information on other third parties. Data subjects have the right to receive information regarding their personal data undergoing processing. The personal data record feat

file://api-specs/split/Administration Gu.content: ure helps you to comply with the relevant legal requirements for data protection by allowing you to search for and retrieve personal data for a specified data subject. The search results are displayed in a comprehensive and structured list containing all personal data of the data subject specified, organized according to the purpose for which the data was collected and processed. The extracted data can be downloaded in form of a report, that provides configuration and extensibility functionality. The access to the personal data record is only allowed with authorization. Personal Data Record in the SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration uses Personal Data Manager for retrieval of personal data. To use Personal Data Manager, you must choose the Personal Data Manager tile in the (SAP BTP) cockpit to enable this functionality. A user with the right role can access the Fiori launchpad of Personal Data Manager and search for the transactions that have the data of the data subject. To access the Fiori Launchpad of Personal Data Manager, use a URL with the following format: https://<your-subdomain>.personal-data-manager-portal.cfapps.<landscape>.hana.ondemand.com For more information about Personal Data Manager, see the Administration Guide for Shippers in the SAP Help Portal for SAP Business Network for Logistics. 6.5.6 Deletion of Personal Data Simplified Blocking and Deletion The processing of personal data is subject to applicable laws related to the deletion of this data when the specified, explicit, and legitimate purpose for processing this personal data has expired. If there is no longer Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Security and Data Protection and Privacy PUBLIC 27 -- 27 of 34 -- a legitimate purpose, that requires the retention and use of personal data, it must be deleted irrecoverably. Blocking is necessary when the original retention period has expired but additional applicable extended and overruling (mandated by law) retention periods are still in place. After the expiration of the longest retention period, the data must be deleted. Deletion of Personal Data When considering compliance with data protection regulations, it is also necessary to consider compliance with industry-specific legislation in different countries. A typical potential scenario in certain countries is that personal data shall be deleted after the specified, explicit, and legitimate purpose for the processing of personal data has ended, but only if no other retention periods are defined in legislation, for example, retention periods for financial documents. Legal requirements in certain scenarios or countries also often require blocking of data in cases where the specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes for the processing of this data have ended, however, the data still has to be retained in the database due to other legally mandated retention periods. Sometimes, transactional data are personal data with relation to a master data object, e.g. a sales order with reference to a business partner. Therefore, the challenge for deletion and blocking is first to handle transactional data and finally other data, such as business partner data. Deletion of Personal Data in the SAP Business Network for Logistics The administrator of a company can specify retention periods using the Retention Management app. For more information, see Retention Management. Once the residence period ends, the data moves to the blocking period. In the blocking period, only users with special privileges, such as a data protection officer, can access the data. At the end of the configured blocking period, the system deletes the data. The data protection officer can use the Blocking Store app provided by SAP Business Network for Logistics to access all the documents that are in the blocking period. To view a document, the user can download the document in a text file format. For more information, see Blocking Store. 6.5.7 Change Log Creation and change of personal data need to be documented. Therefore, for review purposes or as a result of legal regulations, it may be necessary to track the changes made to this data. When these changes are logged, you should be able to check which user made which change, the date and time, the previous value, and the current value, depending on the configuration. Furthermore, log records can be viewed and queried, but access to them is restricted by adequate authorizations. The personal data for which changes shall be logged and the retention period of logs, can be configured.. 28 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Security and Data Protection and Privacy -- 28 of 34 -- Change Logging in the SAP Business Network for Logistics SAP Business Network for Logistics supports change and audit log. When you change any personal information, the system updates the audit log. Users with the required authorization can request for the change log. To request for a log, the authorized user must create an SAP support message in the component BC-NEO- AUDITLOG. For more information about how to request for audit logs, see Audit Log Viewer for the Cloud Foundry Environment. Products built using Java with an SAP HANA database as a back end use the audit trails and audit policies for change logging. For more information, see the Auditing Activity section in the SAP HANA Security Guide. This product uses the Log4J API for change logging. For more information, see JDBC Appender . This product uses a log façade for change logging. For more information, see the Appenders section of the Logback documentation . Java-based NetWeaver products use the security audit log of the SAP NetWeaver Application Server (AS) Java for change logging. For more information, see the Security Audit Log of the AS Java. Cloud products using SAP HANA XS and SAP HANA standalone use the audit trail and audit policies for change logging. For more information, see the Auditing Activity section in the SAP HANA Security Guide. Report a Case through SAP for Me To report a case through SAP for Me, you need an S-User ID to sign in. If you don't have the sign-in credentials of your S-User, contact a user administrator in your organization. If you have trouble identifying who the user administrator is in your organization, please call the Customer Interaction Center (CIC) . For more information, see the SAP for Me Online Help under Access and Authorizations . Procedure 1. Open the SAP for Me application . Sign in with your S-User ID. 2. Navigate to Services & Support Get Support . 3. In the Get Support app, select a relevant customer and report your issue. For detailed process, see Get Support Application Online Help . If you use a component to categorize your issue, use SBN-LBN. Report a Case on Ariba Help Center If you set up your logistics provider account via the simplified onboarding process, you won’t have an S-User ID. In this case, you can report a case on Ariba Help Center. Procedure 1. Sign in to Ariba Help Center then choose Carrier Help Center. 2. Select Contact us, enter keywords pertaining to the issue in the search box and then press Enter. 3. Browse the populated results. If the results provided do not resolve your issue, click Create a Case at the lower-right corner. 4. Enter information on the case creation form.  Note • Select the solution or add-on you’re using from the Issue type dropdown list, then choose the most relevant Issue area. 30 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Monitoring and Troubleshooting -- 30 of 34 -- • Enter your company's Business Network ID (BNO ID) in the Account ID field. 5. Click One last step once you complete the case creation form, choose the contact method, and then click Submit. After you create a case on the Ariba Help Center , our support team will contact you using the email address you provided in the case creation form. We recommend adding itsm.notification-service@sap.com to your mailbox's allowed senders list to ensure you receive all correspondence. 7.2 Accessibility Features To optimize your experience, our apps have features and settings that help you use the software efficiently. Learn more about these features and settings and find out how to use them.  Note SAP Business Network for Logistics is based on SAPUI5. For this reason, accessibility features for SAPUI5 also apply. See the accessibility documentation for SAPUI5 on SAP Help Portal at Accessibility for End Users. For more information on screen reader support and keyboard shortcuts, see Screen-Reader Support for SAPUI5 Controls and Keyboard Handling for SAPUI5 Elements. About This Guide This administration guide describes the steps you need to perform as an administrator to set up your system and to set up the connection to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration.  Note This document describes only about the following: • Integration of SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration with SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) or TM in SAP S/4HANA. • Integration to SAP identity providers. • Usage of SAP Cloud Integration as the integration platform between SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration with SAP TM or TM in SAP S/4HANA This document covers application-specific information only. For general information about SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), see the documentation on SAP Help Portal at https://help.sap.com/CP. This guide addresses the following target audience: • System administrators • Key users  Note The SAP Cloud Platform brand is retired. For more information, see A Robust Platform for RISE with SAP . About Freight Collaboration SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration improves supply chain efficiency by connecting business partners on a collaborative network that supports jointly managing transactions, exchanging documents, and sharing insights across the value chain. For instance, upon invitation from a shipper, a carrier can onboard onto the network and collaborate with shippers on freight tendering, invoicing and milestone reporting. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration runs on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP), utilizing one of the following infrastructures: • Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Frankfurt, Germany • Microsoft Azure infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Washington state, US 10 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Shippers Overview -- 10 of 132 -- • Google Cloud infrastructure, hosted in a data center in Dammam, Saudi Arabia The data used in the solution is also stored in the respective data center. For more information about using the functions and features provided by SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, see the Application Help. Administration Guide for Shippers Overview PUBLIC 11 -- 11 of 132 -- 2 Browser Support This application only supports the standard browsers supported by SAP Business Technology Platform. For more information, see the Browser Support chapter in Feature Scope Description for SAP BTP, Cloud Foundry, ABAP, and Kyma Environments. Root Certificate for End User UI The browser certificate store must contain both the old root certificate (DigiCert Global Root G2) and the new root certificate (DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5). Without this, the end user sign-in to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace will be impacted. To check if you are impacted, try to access the following URL: https://digicert-tls-rsa4096-root-g5.chain-demos.digicert.com . If your browser loads the page without warning, it trusts the DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 and no further action is required on your end. To ensure a smooth transition, you need to run the check and take action (where applicable) before April 23, 2026. Resolution for user sign-in to the BN4L Fiori Launchpad - How to import the certificate into my browser? The below steps might vary with the browser type and version: • Download Root Certificate [DigiCert TLS RSA4096 Root G5 ] and Intermediate Certificate [DigiCert G5 TLS RSA4096 SHA384 2021 CA1 ]. • Open Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. • Open settings and search for security in the search box and click on it. • Click on Manage Device Certificates / Manage Certificates. • Go to the Trusted Root Certification Authorities tab and Import Digi Certificates using the Import button at the bottom. • Go to the Intermediate Certification Authorities tab and Import Digi Certificates using the Import button at the bottom. • Ensure that DigiCert Root and Intermediate is added in the list. Context You need a subaccount in your global account to subscribe apps for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. If you purchased SAP Business Network Global Track and Trace as well, we advise that you use the same subaccount as you use for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration to share master data and avoid double onboarding of your carriers. Use a subaccount that has not yet been used to subscribe to SAP Business Network Asset Collaboration or SAP Business Network Material Traceability. You cannot use the same subaccount to subscribe to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. Procedure Follow the procedure in Create a Subaccount. When you specify the subaccount details, pay attention to the following: Field Description Display Name Enter a name for the subaccount. Use a name that is easy for you to distinguish. Administration Guide for Shippers Onboarding PUBLIC 17 -- 17 of 132 -- Field Description Subdomain The subdomain will become part of the URL for accessing subscribed applications. The subdomain must be less than 50 characters. It can contain only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (not allowed at the beginning or at the end) and it must be unique within your global account. Do not start the subdomain with a digit if you are going to use solution owner apps for Global Track and Trace with this subaccount. Note that you cannot change the subdomain once you spec- ify it. Region (Provider) Choose the desired region for your subaccount. For detailed procedure, see Add Members to Your Subaccount. 4.1.3 Establish Trust Between Your Subaccount and Identity Authentication Tenant To enable secure access to your subaccount, you need to establish trust between your subaccount and the Identity Authentication tenant. Context SAP Cloud Identity Services - Identity Authentication is an identity provider supported by SAP BTP. It is where the business users for SAP BTP are stored. SAP Business Network for Logistics uses Identity Authentication as the identity provider. To enable secured access to your subaccount, you must establish mutual trust between your subaccount and Identity Authentication tenant. With the purchase of the productive license, your company is provided with a tenant for Identity Authentication, if it hasn't already got one. You or your colleague receives an email for activating the account. The email contains a link to the administration console for Identity Authentication. By activating the account, you are the administrator of the account and can assign administrator roles to other users.  Note If the activation link in the email is invalid or already used, follow the advice in SAP note 2637748 . To find your company's existing Identity Authentication tenants and their administrators, see Viewing Assigned Tenants and Administrators. For further questions on Identity Authentication tenant URL or administrator, create an incident with component BC-IAM-IDS. Procedure You can establish the trust using automatic method. Procedure See Create a New User in the Identity Authentication document. 4.1.6 Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users Prerequisites You have the administrator role for your subaccount. Context SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration provides multiple roles that contain role definitions to determine user authorizations. You can group the roles into role collections and assign them to users. To learn more about roles and role collections, see Working with Role Collections.  Note When you assign roles, consider the following security considerations: Administration Guide for Shippers Onboarding PUBLIC 21 -- 21 of 132 -- • Grant users only the minimum level of authorization that is necessary. • Ensure that authorization is removed as soon as it is no longer needed (for example, if an employee leaves the company). Procedure 1. Begin by familiarizing yourself with the roles available for the apps of SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. You’ll see that there is often a role for displaying information in an app and another role for editing or updating information. Knowing which roles are available should help you plan how best to organize the roles into the role collections that you’ll then assign to the users. To see the roles for shipper apps, go to Available Roles for Shippers [page 23]. If you need to set up a carrier tenant for testing purpose, see the carrier app roles at Available Roles for Carriers [page 33]. 2. Create one or more role collections for organizing the roles that you'll assign to users. To do so: 1. In your subaccount, go to Security Role Collections . 2. Create a new role collection by clicking the  Create New Role Collection icon. 3. Select the collection you've created and click Edit. 4. Add roles to the role collection. To do that, under Roles, click in the Role Name field. You can open the Application Identifier dropdown menu to find multiple roles for your solution. From the list of roles, select the ones you want to add to the role collection. 5. Assign users to the role collection by specifying user email and identity provider under Users. For more information, see Assign Users to Role Collections. You can also assign user groups to the role collection. For more information, see Assign User Groups to Role Collections. Note that it is mandatory to assign user groups for dispute internal approval workflow notification to work. For more information, see Internal Approval Process.  Note When adding users to a role collection, make sure the user already exists in the specified identity provider. To create a user in your Identity Authentication tenant, see Create Users in Identity Authentication [page 21]. 6. Save the role collection. Results After being assigned the roles, the user can then sign in to the network to access the authorized apps. Context You can get the tenant-specific URL forSAP Business Network Freight Collaboration and sign in. Administration Guide for Shippers Onboarding PUBLIC 27 -- 27 of 132 -- Procedure 1. In the SAP BTP cockpit, go to your subaccount. 2. In the left-hand navigation area, choose Services Instances and Subscriptions . 3. In the Subscriptions table, click the  Go to Application icon to the right of the shipper apps application name. This displays the sign-in page for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration on the network.  Recommendation You’re recommended to bookmark the URL so you can sign in more easily in the future. 4. Enter your business user name (email) and password and sign in.  Note If your IdP is Identity Authentication, your user name can be found in the email with the subject “Activate Your Account for User Profile” from notification@sapnetwork.com. You set the password when you activated your account by clicking a link in that email. If you forget your password, you may reset it by clicking Forgot Password? on the sign-in page. The main window of SAP Business Network for Logistics opens. A message box is displayed reminding you to maintain your company's business profile. You can choose Open Manage Business Profile App to maintain at least a company name, an address, and a contact person, or do it later. English is the default language displayed in the user interface. You can change it by clicking the user icon in the upper-right corner, choosing Settings, and specifying a different supported language in the Language & Region section. Supported languages are: • Arabic • Bulgarian • Chinese Simplified • Chinese Traditional • Croatian • Czech • Danish • Dutch • Finnish • French • German • Greek • Hebrew • Hungarian • Italian • Japanese • Korean • Malay • Norwegian • Polish 28 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Shippers Onboarding -- 28 of 132 -- • Portuguese for Brazil • Romanian • Russian • Serbo-Croatian • Slovak • Spanish • Swedish • Thai • Turkish Next Steps • Copy the tenant-specific URL and send it to the other users that you have created in the previous task. Then the users can access the URL in a web browser and sign in to the freight collaboration solution with their own user names (emails) and passwords. • Connect your backend SAP Transportation Management system or Transportation Management embedded in SAP S/4HANA. For detailed information, see Connectivity [page 40]. • Perform other administrative tasks, for example, maintain your company's business profile in the Manage Business Profile app, invite carriers to connect with you in the Discover Business Partners or Invite Business Partners app, configure notification settings in the Manage Notification Settings app, etc. For more information, see Business Configuration [page 62] and Configuring Additional Services [page 72]. 4.2 Scenario 2: Test/SI Tenant Onboarding Using Identity Authentication This section describes the procedures needed to set up a test environment for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration using Identity Authentication as the identity provider. The customer or partner license for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration provides you with subscriptions for both shipper apps and carrier apps for test use, which enable you to create a test shipper tenant and a test carrier tenant to test the connection and collaboration. file://api-specs/split/Administration Gu.content: Network Freight Collaboration is a solution deployed on SAP Business Technology Platform. With the purchase of the solution, you are entitled to use a global account on SAP BTP and create subaccounts in it. In your subaccount, you subscribe to the apps for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. You configure roles and bundle them into role collections for user management.  Note To perform the tasks in this section, make sure your company has got an Identity Authentication tenant. Administration Guide for Shippers Onboarding PUBLIC 29 -- 29 of 132 -- Task Overview  Note If you have any issues performing the tasks below, see Frequently Asked Questions. 1. Set Up a Shipper (Test) Tenant [page 30] 2. Set Up a Carrier (Test) Tenant [page 32] 3. (As the Shipper) Invite the Carrier to Connect with You on the Network [page 36] 4. (As the Carrier) Accept the Connection Request from the Shipper [page 37] 5. (As the Shipper) Enter the Carrier's LBN ID in Your System [page 38] 4.2.1 Set Up a Shipper (Test) Tenant Prerequisites To begin the setup, the following prerequisites must be fulfilled: • You have an administrator role of your global account. For more information on accessing your global account, see Set Up Your Global Account [page 16]. • You have an existing tenant for Identity Authentication and you are the administrator or you have been assigned to the Manage Groups role of the account. Context In this task, you'll create a shipper tenant, assign a shipper user to it, and maintain the shipper company’s business profile. Procedure 1. Create a subaccount for the shipper. See Create a Subaccount [page 17] for more information. 2. Add entitlements for the following apps to your subaccount. See Configure Entitlements and Quotas for Subaccounts. • Authorization Apps for Freight Collaboration (Plan: test or default) • Shipper Apps for Freight Collaboration (Plan: test or si) 3. Configure a shipper user using Identity Authentication as the identity provider. a. Follow the procedure in Establish Trust Between Your Subaccount and Identity Authentication Tenant [page 19] to establish the trust. 30 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Shippers Onboarding -- 30 of 132 -- b. Follow the procedure in Create Users in Identity Authentication [page 21] to create a user. Skip this step if you want to use your current user in Identity Authentication. 4. Subscribe to apps from your subaccount. a. In the left-hand navigation area of the subaccount, choose Services Service Marketplace . Here you see the apps entitled to your subaccount. b. Subscribe to the apps in the following sequence by clicking the tile and choosing Create. 1. Authorization Apps for Freight Collaboration (Plan: test or default) 2. Shipper Apps for Freight Collaboration (Plan: test or si)  Note If you can't see the above app tiles, ask your global account administrator to add the entitlements of these apps to your subaccount. For more information, see Configure Entitlements and Quotas for Subaccounts.  Note In case you need to unsubscribe these apps, make sure you unsubscribe Shipper Apps for Freight Collaboration before unsubscribing Authorization Apps for Freight Collaboration. Otherwise, the unsubscription will fail. 5. Configure a role collection and assign it to the shipper user as described in Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users [page 21]. You may add roles according to your needs by referring to Available Roles for Shippers [page 23]. 6. Sign in to the shipper tenant. a. In the left-hand navigation area of the shipper subaccount, choose Services Instances and Subscriptions . b. In the Subscriptions table, click the  Go to Application icon to the right of the shipper apps application name. This displays the logon page. You’re recommended to bookmark the URL so you can sign in more easily in the future. c. Sign in using the email and password of the shipper user that you've configured. The SAP Fiori Launchpad window for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration opens. You'll see a label "Test" (for customer license) on the header bar of the window, reminding you the tenant is not for productive use. 7. Maintain a business profile for the shipper. a. In the SAP Fiori Launchpad window, if you see a message box indicating that your company's business profile is incomplete, click Open Manage Business Profile App in the message box. This will direct you to the company profile for the shipper. b. Specify the company name, address, and contact person in the company profile. For detailed information, refer to Edit Company Profile. 8. Record the company name and LBN ID of the shipper. This LBN ID will be assigned to the business partner Identification in the backend SAP TM or SAP S/4HANA system. You can find the LBN ID by choosing Manage Alternate IDs in the System Connections app. Administration Guide for Shippers Onboarding PUBLIC 31 -- 31 of 132 -- 4.2.2 Set Up a Carrier (Test) Tenant Context In this task, you'll create a carrier tenant, assign a carrier user to it, and maintain the carrier company’s business profile. If you want to create more carrier tenants for testing, you can do so the same way. Use a subaccount that has not yet been used to subscribe to SAP Business Network Asset Collaboration or SAP Business Network Material Traceability. You cannot use the same subaccount to subscribe to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. Procedure 1. Create a subaccount for the carrier. See Create a Subaccount [page 17] for more information. 2. Add entitlements for the following apps to your subaccount. See Configure Entitlements and Quotas for Subaccounts. • Authorization Apps for Freight Collaboration (Plan: test or default) • Carrier Apps for Freight Collaboration (Plan: test or si) 3. Configure a carrier user using Identity Authentication as the identity provider. a. Follow the procedure in Establish Trust Between Your Subaccount and Identity Authentication Tenant [page 19] to establish the trust. b. Follow the procedure in Create Users in Identity Authentication [page 21] to create a user. Skip this step if you want to use your current user in Identity Authentication. 4. Subscribe to apps from your subaccount. a. In the left-hand navigation area of the subaccount, choose Services Service Marketplace . Here you see the apps entitled to your subaccount. b. Subscribe to the apps in the following sequence by clicking the tile and choosing Create. 1. Authorization Apps for Freight Collaboration (Plan: test or default) 2. Carrier Apps for Freight Collaboration (Plan: test or si)  Note If you can't see the above app tiles, ask your global account administrator to add the entitlements of these apps to your subaccount. For more information, see Configure Entitlements and Quotas for Subaccounts.  Note In case you need to unsubscribe these apps, make sure you unsubscribe Carrier Apps for Freight Collaboration before unsubscribing Authorization Apps for Freight Collaboration. Otherwise, the unsubscription will fail. 32 PUBLIC Administration Guide for Shippers Onboarding -- 32 of 132 -- 5. Configure a role collection and assign it to the carrier user as described in Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users [page 21]. You may add roles according to your needs by referring to Available Roles for Carriers [page 33].  Note A carrier in the productive environment can use the User Management app to assign roles to users, but the app is not applicable for a test-type carrier that subscribed Carrier Apps for Freight Collaboration (plan: test or si). 6. Sign in to the carrier tenant. a. In the left-hand navigation area of the carrier subaccount, choose Services Instances and Subscriptions . b. In the Subscriptions table, click the  Go to Application icon to the right of the carrier apps application name. This displays the logon page. You’re recommended to bookmark the URL so you can sign in more easily in the future. c. Sign in using the email and password of the carrier user that you just configured. The SAP Fiori Launchpad window for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration opens. You'll see a label "Test" (for customer license) on the header bar of the window, reminding you the tenant is not for productive use. 7. Maintain a business profile for the carrier. a. In the SAP Fiori Launchpad window, if you see a message box indicating that your company's business profile is incomplete, click Open Manage Business Profile App in the message box. This will direct you to the company profile for the carrier. b. Specify the company name, address, and contact person in the company profile. For detailed information, refer to Edit Company Profile. c. By default, the carrier’s company profile you just specified is not visible to any business partners on the network. For testing purposes, you can make it visible by following the instructions provided in the Profile Settings section.  Note If you want to get email notification when a connection request is automatically accepted, subscribe to and configure the Invitation Auto-Accepted notification scenario in the Manage Notification Settings and Define User Settings apps. 8. Record the company name and LBN ID of the carrier. You'll use them in the next tasks. • Company name: Specified in the carrier’s company profile in step 6. • LBN ID: Displayed by choosing Manage Alternate IDs in the System Connections app. 4.2.2.1 Available Roles for Carriers SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration provides the following roles for carriers: Administration Guide for Shippers Onboarding PUBLIC 33 -- 33 of 132 -- Role Application Identifier The Role Enables the User to App Name BPDisplayTemplate lbnplatform-bprepo- live!b18679 Open the app and display the company profile Manage Business Profile BPEditTemplate Open the app and edit the company profile Manage Business Profile ManageInvitationsDispl ayTemplate Open the app and display the invitations from shippers Manage Invitations ManageInvitationsProce ssTemplate Open the app and accept or reject the invitations from shippers Manage Invitations ManageIntegrationLogsD isplayTemplate lbn- manageIntegrationLogsB roker-live!b18679 Open the app and view the message logs.
