What is the network and what are the benefits of joining? SAP Business Network for Logistics improves supply chain efficiency by connecting business partners on a collaborative network that supports jointly managing transactions, exchanging documents, and sharing insights across the value chain. For instance, by inviting carriers to connect with you on the network, you – a shipper company – can collaborate with carriers on freight tendering, subcontracting, freight settlement, milestone reporting and dock appointment scheduling. SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration is a cloud solution that provides your company with a range of shipper-specific apps which you can use for completing your daily tasks. This getting started guide for administrators leads you through the onboarding and initial setup process so you and your colleagues can sign in and start using the apps. If you have any issues following the steps in this guide, start by reading Frequently Asked Questions [page 10]. Getting Started Guide for Shippers Introduction PUBLIC 3 -- 3 of 16 -- 2 Welcome Emails After purchasing a solution for SAP Business Network for Logistics in SAP Store, the contact IT person of your company will receive several emails from SAP. These emails provide instructions and links for activating accounts, setting up global accounts, and accessing onboarding instructions and documents. The emails are sent from notification@sapnetworkmail.com and no.reply.provisioning@sap.com. Make sure your email software doesn’t block these email addresses to avoid it going to your SPAM/Junk Mail box. The table below shows the emails you should expect to receive and the actions to take after receiving them. If you don’t have access to the emails listed here, start by reading Frequently Asked Questions [page 10]. Email Purpose Action to Take An email for activating your Identity Au- thentication account Notifies you that an Identity Authentica- tion tenant has been created for you on SAP BTP, and you need to activate your account. The Identity Authentication is an iden- tity provider for user authentication and authorization management. You won't receive this email if: • Your company has already got an Identity Authentication tenant; or • You are an SAP partner that pur- chased the cloud test&demo li- cense for the solution. 1. In the email, choose Click here to activate your account to activate your account and set password. 2. In the email, click the link text Administration Console to go to the administration console for SAP Identity Authentication Service. Sign in with your email and the password you just set. You're recommended to bookmark this URL so you could sign in more easily in the future. 3. If the onboarding tasks need to be performed by another person, you need to add that person as the ad- ministrator of the Identity Authen- tication tenant. To do that, choose Users & Authorizations Administrators in the menu pane. Then choose +Add and User at the bottom of the pane in the middle, and grant the user the Manage Groups au- thorization. A welcome email from SAP BTP for your global account Notifies you that your global account on SAP BTP is ready to use. Set up your global account as descri- bed in Set Up Your Global Account in the Administration Guide for Shippers. 4 PUBLIC Getting Started Guide for Shippers Welcome Emails -- 4 of 16 -- Email Purpose Action to Take Welcome to SAP Business Network for Logistics - Shipper Notifies you that your SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration is ready to use. The email contains onboarding instruc- tions and document links. In the email, click the document links. You'll refer to these documents to per- form administration tasks and use the apps. You can bookmark the document links for future use. Getting Started Guide for Shippers Welcome Emails PUBLIC 5 -- 5 of 16 -- 3 Getting Started After receiving the welcome emails, you can get started with the initial administrative tasks, as described in the table below.  Note Dependent on your purchase solution, you are entitled to set up different types of SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration tenants. For more information, see Onboarding. Task Procedure Set up a test environment to test the shipper-carrier connec- tion and the exchange of data between the two parties. 1. Set up a test shipper tenant and a test carrier tenant, and connect the two. For detailed procedure, refer to the following section in the Administration Guide for Shippers: • Scenario 2: Test/SI Tenant Onboarding Using Iden- tity Authentication, if you want to use your Identity Authentication tenant. 2. As a test shipper, connect to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration with your backend SAP Transpor- tation Management (SAP TM) or TM on SAP S/4HANA. For detailed procedure, see Connectivity in the Adminis- tration Guide for Shippers. Set up the production use as a shipper. This is only applicable for customers licensed with SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. SAP partners with the cloud test&demo license cannot set up the solution for production use. 1. Set up your company's production shipper tenant for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. For detailed procedure, see Scenario 1: Shipper On- boarding in the Administration Guide for Shippers. After the setup, you'll be able to sign in to your tenant to use the shipper-specific apps. 2. Connect to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration with your backend SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) or TM on SAP S/4HANA. For detailed procedure, see Connectivity in the Adminis- tration Guide for Shippers. 3. Invite the carriers that you already know and/or dis- cover new carriers and invite them to connect with you on the network. For detailed procedure, see Inviting Carriers to Connect with You on the Network [page 7]. You can then collaborate with connected carriers on freight tendering, subcontracting, freight settlement, milestone reporting and dock appointment scheduling. 6 PUBLIC Getting Started Guide for Shippers Getting Started -- 6 of 16 -- 3.1 Inviting Carriers to Connect with You on the Network Prerequisites • You're onboarded onto SAP Business Network for Logistics. • To perform the tasks described in this section, you must be assigned with the following roles. Application Identifier Role Template Description lbnplatform-bprepo-live! b18679 BPEditTemplate The assigned user can edit company profile in the Manage Business Profile app. InviteBPProcessTemplate The assigned user can invite busi- ness partners in the Invite Business Partners app. BusinessPartnerDiscoveryTempl ate The assigned user can search for and invite business partners in the Discover Business Partners app.  Note For more information on role assignment, see Scenario 1: Shipper Onboarding in the Administration Guide for Shippers: Create Your Company's Business Profile You need to create your company’s business profile. This is required as a prerequisite to inviting business partners onto your network. 1. Sign in toSAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. For more information, see Sign In to the Network in the Administration Guide for Shippers. 2. In the SAP Fiori Launchpad window, when a message box opens reminding you that your company's business profile is incomplete, choose Open Manage Business Profile App in the message box. You can also open the app later by clicking the Manage Business Profile app tile in the SAP Fiori Launchpad window. 3. In the Manage Business Profile app, click Edit in the upper right-hand corner. 4. In the Header and Contact Details sections, enter at least a company name, an address, and a business contact person. To enter address and business contact, click Add on the right-hand side. 5. Save your business profile by clicking Save in the lower right-hand corner. Getting Started Guide for Shippers Getting Started PUBLIC 7 -- 7 of 16 -- Inviting Carriers to Connect with You You can invite carriers to connect with you on the network using either of the following apps: Discover Business Partners App Use this app to invite carriers that have already joined the network, no matter whether you know them or not. You can search for carriers by different criteria and can select suitable carriers to send connection invitations. To invite a carrier with the app, proceed as follows: 1. In the SAP Fiori Launchpad window, open the Discover Business Partners app by clicking the app tile. 2. Discover and invite carriers. 3. After the carrier accepts your invitation, update carrier's LBN ID. Invite Business Partners App Use this app to send connection invitations to carriers that you already know. It is especially useful when you want to invite a number of carriers all at once. For example, you have just onboarded to the network and want to invite all the carriers that already exist in your backend SAP TM system. To invite carriers with the app, proceed as follows: 1. In the SAP Fiori Launchpad window, open the Invite Business Partners app by clicking the app tile. 2. Add new carriers to your carriers list. 3. Submit connection invitations. 4. After the carrier accepts your invitation, update carrier's LBN IDs. 8 PUBLIC Getting Started Guide for Shippers Getting Started -- 8 of 16 -- 4 Next Steps For more information about the administrative tasks and freight collaboration activities, explore the user assistance by calling up the in-app help via the  Open Help icon on the SAP Fiori Launchpad. The following sections in the user assistance may be of interest to you: Business Area Document Section Post-onboarding business configurations In the Administration Guide for Shippers: • Business Configuration • Configuring Additional Services Subcontracting and tendering Assign Charge Codes Configure Tolerance (General Settings) Dock appointment scheduling Manage Locations Manage Dock Appointments Docking Location Settings (Manage Entities) Settlement Manage Disputes from Carrier Getting Started Guide for Shippers Next Steps PUBLIC 9 -- 9 of 16 -- 5 Frequently Asked Questions This section answers the questions that are frequently asked when you get started. It covers questions about onboarding, user authentication, subscription failures, signing in, inviting business partners, and getting support.  Note To find more questions and answers on the network and the apps, go to SAP Library for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration on SAP Help Portal at https://help.sap.com/fc. Then under Use, select Frequently Asked Questions. Welcome Emails What if I didn't receive the email for activating my Identity Authentication account? As described in Welcome Emails [page 4], an Identity Authentication tenant is provided to customers who haven't got an existing tenant. If you are an SAP partner with the cloud test&demo license of the product, you can use SAP ID Service (S-user or P-user) as the identity provider. If you are a customer, your company may have already got an Identity Authentication tenant. To find your company's existing tenants and administrators, see Viewing Assigned Tenants and Administrators or create an incident with component BC-IAM-IDS. Then ask the administrator to grant you the Manage Groups authorization of the tenant so that you could proceed with the onboarding. What if the activation link in the email for activating Identity Authentication account is invalid or already used? Please follow the advice in SAP note 2637748 or create an incident with component BC-IAM-IDS. Onboarding If I have an existing Identity Authentication tenant that SAP offered me in the past, can I use it for SAP Business Network for Logistics? Yes. The same tenant can be used for multiple SAP cloud solutions. If your company has already got an Identity Authentication tenant, you won't get a new one upon the purchase of SAP Business Network for Logistics. Do I need a standalone Cloud Foundry subaccount for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration? Yes, we recommend that you use a standalone Cloud Foundry subaccount. 10 PUBLIC Getting Started Guide for Shippers Frequently Asked Questions -- 10 of 16 -- Why does my subscription to the authorization apps or shipper apps fail? Subscription failure can be caused by various reasons. Please make sure you subscribe authorization apps before subscribing shipper apps. An error may occur if you subscribe both Shipper Apps for Freight Collaboration and Shipper Apps(Test or SI) for Freight Collaboration in the same subaccount. In that case, you need to create two subaccounts to subscribe them separately. If your subscription fails and you don't know the reason, please follow the instructions displayed in the error message on your screen. What is the URL for signing in to SAP Business Network for Logistics? After performing the onboarding process, you can find the sign-in URL as follows: 1. In the SAP BTP cockpit, go to the subaccount that you created for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. 2. In the left-hand pane, choose Services Instances and Subscriptions . 3. In the Subscriptions table, click the  Go to Application icon to the right of the app name Shipper Apps for Freight Collaboration. This displays the sign-in page for the network. You’re recommended to bookmark the URL so you can sign-in more easily in the future. If you have added other users for your apps, send this URL to them so that they could sign-in with their own sign-in credentials. If I'm not the admin user, how can I confirm the URL for my company tenant? If you don't know your company tenant name or who is the administrator, you can follow the steps from Viewing Assigned Tenants and Administrators. What is the sig-in user name/password I should use to sign in to SAP Business Network for Logistics? If you are the administrator who receives the email for activating your Identity Authentication account, as mentioned in Welcome Emails [page 4], use that user (email) and the password you set to sign in to the network. If during the onboarding process, you, as an administrator, have added other users in Identity Authentication, each of them will either receive the “Activate Your Account for User Profile” email or receive the user (email) and initial password from you (dependent on the option you selected when creating the new user). That is the user credential they should use to sign in to the network. The number of apps that each user can see after the sign-in is dependent on the role collections assigned to the user. For more information, see Organize Roles Together and Assign Them to Users in the Administration Guide for Shippers. What if I forget my password for signing in to SAP Business Network for Logistics? On the sign-in page, click Forgot Password. You'll receive the instruction for resetting your password. After signing in, I saw an empty page with a message "Where to". What should I do? The reason might be: • When you entered your username and password on the sign-in page, the page has timed out. In that case, reopen the sign-in page and sign in again. Getting Started Guide for Shippers Frequently Asked Questions PUBLIC 11 -- 11 of 16 -- • You haven't subscribed Authorization Apps for Freight Collaboration. In that case, go to your subaccount in SAP BTP and subscribe the app. If the issue still exists, please create an incident with component SBN-LBN-OB. After signing on, I saw an empty page with a message "Authorization Request Error". What should I do? You may try the following: • If you use Identity Authentication as the IdP for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, make sure you have performed the steps as described in Establish Trust Between Your Subaccount and Identity Authentication Tenant. If the issue still exists, please create an incident with component SBN-LBN-OB. Inviting Business Partners How do I know the status of the connection invitation that I sent to a business partner? If you use the Invite Business Partners app to submit an invitation, you can check its status in the Status column: • After an invitation is submitted, the invitee is moved to the In Progress worklist. The status Invitation email sent to business partner means that SAP has sent an email to invite the business partner to register to the network. The status Routed to business partner means the invitee has registered to the network and received your invitation, but not yet accepted (or rejected) it. • After the invitee accepts (or rejects) your invitation, the invitee is moved to the Accepted (or Rejected) worklist, and the status changes to Accepted (or rejected). If you use the Discover Business Partners app to send the invitation, when your search for the business partner, you'll see the Connection Status in business partner information changes to Connected after the invitee accepts your invitation. I've sent an invitation to a business partner using the Invite Business Partners app, but the business partner didn't receive it. What should I do? You may first check the business partner's email address. If it's correct, then create an incident with component SBN-LBN-BP-OB. I've sent an invitation to a business partner using the Invite Business Partners app, but would like to resend it because the business partner contact email is incorrect or has changed. What should I do? If the invitation is still in progress, you may try recall it in the In Progress worklist and then submit a new invitation with the correct email address. If the recall fails, please create an incident with component SBN-LBN-BP-OB. After I invite a business partner, what should the business partner do to connect with me? To get started with the network and connect with you, the business partner can refer to the following step-by- step guide on SAP Help portal: 12 PUBLIC Getting Started Guide for Shippers Frequently Asked Questions -- 12 of 16 -- • Activate Your Account The guide is available in multiple languages. Select a language option beside the title. Getting Support How to create an incident (report an issue) and get support? If you encounter technical issues or require technical support, you may create an incident (report an issue) using the Get Support app, which is part of the Services & Support dashboard in SAP for Me. Sign in with your S-User ID. For detailed process, see Get Support Application Online Help . If you use a component to categorize your issue, use SBN-LBN-OB (for onboarding relevant issues) or SBN- LBN-FC (for other issues with SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration). If you don't know your S-User ID, see the next question. To create an incident, I need to provide my S-user ID. What if I don't know my S-user ID? If you don't have the sign-in credentials of your S-User, contact a user administrator in your organization. If you have trouble identifying who the user administrator is in your organization, please call the Customer Interaction Center (CIC) . For more information, see the SAP for Me Online Help under Access and Authorizations . Miscellaneous Why is it not possible to upload my company logo to my business profile? When uploading your company logo in the Manage Business Profile app, verify if the logo meets size limitation: 2 MB Getting Started Guide for Shippers Frequently Asked Questions PUBLIC 13 -- 13 of 16 -- Important Disclaimers and Legal Information Hyperlinks Some links are classified by an icon and/or a mouseover text. Introduction This guide explains how you can verify (view, edit, and modify) an invoice using a Microsoft Excel file. By doing so, you can automate the process and reduce human efforts and errors. You can generate an invoice for the selected freight orders for settlement and then download the invoice as a template in Microsoft Excel format, edit the downloaded file, and then upload it back to the app. Invoice Upload Guide Introduction PUBLIC 3 -- 3 of 12 -- 2 Accepted File Upload Formats The system only accepts the upload of Microsoft Excel files of xlsx format only. 4 PUBLIC Invoice Upload Guide Accepted File Upload Formats -- 4 of 12 -- 3 Invoice Upload Options Once you generate the invoice as a Microsoft Excel file of xlsx format using the download invoice option in the Manage Invoices app, you can upload the invoice in the following manner 1. Edit the editable fields in the downloaded Microsoft Excel file. 2. Save your changes. 3. Upload the invoice back to the app. Invoice Upload Guide Invoice Upload Options PUBLIC 5 -- 5 of 12 -- 4 Editable Invoice Fields The following fields are editable in the downloaded invoice: • Invoice date • Invoice ID • Rate amount • Final amount • Note • Deletion indicator If you want to delete a charge, you must choose Yes in the Deletion Indicator. 6 PUBLIC Invoice Upload Guide Editable Invoice Fields -- 6 of 12 -- 5 Downloading an Invoice Template Procedure 1. On the Fiori launchpad, choose the Manage Invoices tile. 2. Search for the invoice that you want to edit using the invoice ID and open the invoice. 3. Download the invoice template by choosing Download/Upload Invoice Download Invoice . Results The system downloads a Microsoft Excel file in the .xlsx format with all the information of the invoice. Invoice Upload Guide Downloading an Invoice Template PUBLIC 7 -- 7 of 12 -- 6 Uploading an Invoice Procedure 1. Export invoice details from your billing software as a PDF or a Microsoft Excel file. 2. Enter data from the exported file into the downloaded invoice template. You can also have a custom program to automatically insert the contents of your exported file into the downloaded invoice template. 3. Save your changes. 4. On the Fiori launchpad, choose the Manage Invoices tile. 5. Search for the invoice that you want to edit using the invoice ID and open the invoice. 6. Upload the edited file by choosing Download/Upload Invoice Upload Invoice . 7. Choose the saved Microsoft Excel .xlsx file for upload. When you upload the invoice, the system validates the following: • Whether the invoice file has been uploaded for the right invoice in the app. • Whether a duplicate charge type has been entered for the same logistical reference. • Whether a new charge type has been entered without a rate. • Whether the invoice ID or invoice date is blank. Results If there are validation errors, the system displays the errors in an error log and you can download the error log for future reference. If there are no validation errors, the system uploads the invoice. You can attach relevant documents for the new and existing charges. After the Microsoft Excel file has been uploaded, you can view the uploaded values in the app screen. You can also further modify these values. 8 PUBLIC Invoice Upload Guide Uploading an Invoice -- 8 of 12 --  Note If you want to save the uploaded values, you must explicitly choose Save. You can also completely abort your upload operation by choosing Cancel. You must make sure that no personal data enters the system in an uncontrolled or non purpose-related way in the Microsoft Excel file. All rights reserved. -- 1 of 10 -- Content 1 About This Document. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .3 2 Features. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 4 2 PUBLIC Feature Scope Description Content -- 2 of 10 -- 1 About This Document This feature scope description shows you which features and product documentation are available for SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. Further restrictions may apply based on your license agreement with SAP. Functions and capabilities described in the documentation of this product may exceed the functional scope of the product to explain integration with other SAP products that must be licensed separately. Documentation The following product documentation is available for the freight collaboration solution: • This feature scope description • Getting Started Guide for Shippers • Administration Guide for Shippers • Activate Your Account (for carriers) • Administration Guide for Logistics Providers Feature Scope Description About This Document PUBLIC 3 -- 3 of 10 -- 2 Features Introduction SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration provides an environment for logistics business partners (shippers and carriers) to work together collaboratively. The network supports business processes for subcontracting freight orders, tendering, and invoicing. The network also supports the process of onboarding onto the network. Features for shippers Feature Description Manage network • Join the network. • Maintain your company profile. • Invite carriers onto the network to work with you. • Invite shippers to work with you. (Note, the shippers must already be onboarded). • Set up the connection between your system (for exam- ple a transportation management system) and the net- work. • Subscribe to notifications so you are prompted when your SAP Cloud Integration certificate expires. • Search the network for carriers and logistics service providers, then from the results, invite suitable ones to be your business partners. • Establish a connection yourself between a test shipper account and a test carrier account. • Activate services and define authentication details for establishing external API communication for your carri- ers and network partners. file://SBN/split/OC Supply chain monitor.content: Order confirmation deviation monitoring with Supply chain Monitor Key learnings for suppliers SCC Seller Integration EMEA Team, SAP April 03, 2026 -- 1 of 10 -- This documentation describes in general the Order confirmation deviation monitoring and approval process in SAP Business Network. It is not intended to substitute a buyer’s specific requirements described in the Integration guidelines. Please always consult your Seller Integration Functional Lead on buyer side who will help you to get the full buyer’s specification of the process. Disclaimer -- 2 of 10 -- -- 3 of 10 -- Order confirmation deviation in Supply Chain Monitor What is Order confirmation deviation monitoring in Supply chain monitor, how it works from the supplier POV Deviations - what kind of deviations, how deviation is recognized (control keys, tolerance in rules) -- 4 of 10 -- Per rule, a buyer can allow suppliers to send an Order Confirmation that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval Example of Control keys section in PO Example of Tolerances section in Transaction rules: * Please find more details about tolerances in cXML Solution guide. Order Confirmation deviation - types of deviation Supply Chain monitor allows to control three types of deviations in Order confirmation: Delivery date (*Date deviations are not recognized for purchase order line items with multiple schedule lines) Quantity Unit price Deviation is identified based on tolerances set by buyer either in Control keys sent within Purchase order, or tolerances set in the Transaction rules in buyer’s SAP Business Network account. -- 5 of 10 -- Whenever a deviation is recognized for Order confirmation, the item that deviates is marked as below. Supplier can also receive a notification when deviation is recognized (more details in section OC Approval slide 11) -- 6 of 10 -- Order Confirmation Approval flow Approval flow – options that buyer can take: approve, approve and change PO, reject. Approval request message – routing and email notifications - PO confirmation status on SAP Business Network – behavior, implications to further process (ASN, Invoice) -- 7 of 10 -- Buyers can choose between two configurations for a deviation approval: Single-level deviation approval - Provides a single level of approval. Buyers approve deviations directly in the buyer portal. Multilevel deviation approval - Provides multiple levels of approval. Buyers approve deviations first in the buyer portal, then in their backend ERP system. The configuration type defines which actions are allowed per deviation type. The following actions are available: Approve - Buyer approves the deviation and updates the item’s confirmation in their ERP. Approve and Update - Buyer approves the deviation and updates the order in their ERP with the confirmation information. Supplier receives updated order accord to order confirmation data. Reject - Buyer rejects the deviation and nothing is updated in the ERP. Items revert to being unconfirmed in SAP Business Network. Order Confirmation Approval flow -- 8 of 10 -- Following Approval statuses are available for Order confirmation: Awaiting approval – deviation is recognized and awaiting buyer’s approval action. Approved – either no deviation is recognized (Order confirmation accepts PO as is) therefore OC is automatically approve OR buyer approved the deviation. Approved awaiting change PO – buyer approved the deviation and triggered change PO. Supplier will receive change PO. Awaiting supplier reconfirmation - in certain cases supplier is required to reconfirm after change PO triggered by buyer (more details in section Transaction rules implications 17) Rejected – buyer rejected the deviation Each time the Approval status of Order Confirmation changes a notification is sent by email to the supplier if notifications are set-up (see slide 11 for more detail) IMPORTANT NOTE: In case a supplier submits Order confirmation with deviation that falls within tolerance limit set by a buyer, the Order confirmation deviation w be automatically Approved. Order Confirmation Approval flow – OC Approval status -- 9 of 10 -- Approval status is visible in the Order confirmation message -> Related Documents: Order Confirmation Approval flow – OC Approval status After a buyer action the Order confirmation deviation, the approval status changes: -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/OC Supply chain monitor.content: Example of the notification email: Order Confirmation Approval flow – Notifications In case a supplier would like to receive information about Order confirmation approval status, there are two options available in SAP Business Network account: Route cXML message to designated URL on supplier side. This option is available in Account Settings n Settings n Electronic order routing in supplier’s SAP Business Network account: * Currently there is no option to route ApprovalRequest to Cloud Integration Gateway on supplier side. Set notification via email. Account Settings n Settings n Notifications n Network -- 1 of 10 -- Order Confirmation deviation Approval flow - sample workflow -- 2 of 10 -- Order Confirmation Structure Order Confirmation cXML structure compatible with Supply chain monitor -- 3 of 10 -- Integrated suppliers can use the cXML ConfirmationRequest schema with both type = “allDetail” or “detail” on the header level to confirm the PO and indicate a deviation. type=“detail” on header - in case the buyer enabled the enhancement for order confirmation capabilities for hosted and integrated suppliers, SAP Business Network will automatically enhance the structure with PO item data and trigger the OC deviation process ConfirmationRequest with type=“accept” on header level is automatically recognized as confirmation without any deviation and is automatically approved. Order Confirmation cXML structure compatible with Supply chain monitor -- 4 of 10 -- PO confirmation business rules and implications Order Confirmation Transaction rules implications -- 5 of 10 -- Deviation approval is enabled by the following transaction rule in buyer’s account: If the rule Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval is checked, confirmation status is retained even if the item changed. This behavior is true even if the Retain confirmation status for unchanged line items on change orders rule is unchecked. There are two exceptions to this behavior: If the previously confirmed quantity for an item is higher than the item’s revised quantity in the change order, the confirmation status is NOT retained. If the previously confirmed price for an item is higher or lower than the revised price in the change order, the confirmation status is NOT retained More scenarios highlighted on the next slide Order Confirmation Transaction rules implications -- 6 of 10 -- Further scenarios with change order and impact to Confirmation status of PO and Approval status of OC: -- 7 of 10 -- If confirmation status is retained for a line item, the following logic also applies: The confirmation status (for example, Confirmed With Changes) is recalculated based on the new version of the item. All previous deviation alerts for order confirmation approval are deleted for the item. If the item hasn’t changed in the new version of the order, the approval status is retained. If this item had any deviation alerts, they’re regenerated. If an item price has changed, within tolerance or not, the approval status is not retained. Deviation alerts are not generated because the supplier must first reconfirm the item. If an item’s approval status changed and the supplier has configured notifications for approval status changes, the supplier receives a notification. -- 8 of 10 -- Please note this is not an official documentation, this guide was created by SCC SI EMEA team in order to help Suppliers during the integration project and after Hyper care period when SCC SI consultant is disengaged from the project. For more details and official documentation please refer to: Or please access the “Help center” from your SAP Business Network account and type key words to find the necessary information: You can also access to the official documentation following the link : SAP Help Portal Note -- 9 of 10 -- Thank you. Disclaimer -- 2 of 10 -- -- 3 of 10 -- Is confirmation required ? -- 4 of 10 -- The Order Confirmation message is allowed or required in SAP Business Network : By Instruction in the Purchase Order in <ControlKeys> part, within <OCInstruction value="allowed"> field 3 values are possible : allowed notAllowed requiredBeforeASN By rule defined in SAP Business Network which requires Order Confirmation “Require suppliers to create an order confirmation for the PO before creating an invoice.” “Require suppliers to fully confirm line items before fulfillment” “Require suppliers to create an order confirmation before creating a ship notice.” By rule defined in SAP Business Network, confirmation could have to be done at schedule line-item level “Require suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the schedule line-item level” In this case, tolerances can be set-up to be validated at schedule line-item level by the following rule : “Validate tolerance for quantity, delivery date, or both at the schedule-line level” Note : When attribute OCinstruction value is requiredBeforeASN, and/or the rule is set-up, Order Confirmation for the Purchase Order line Item is required before sending a Ship Notice for that line - Otherwise the Ship Notice will be rejected by SAP Business Network Is Confirmation requested ? -- 5 of 10 -- Order confirmation and Reconfirmation cases -- 6 of 10 -- Case 1 Confirmations usually include acceptance, change, merge or split of delivery dates. file://SBN/split/Order Confirmation Proc.content: Order Confirmation and Reconfirmation cases - at schedule-line level Confirmations usually include acceptance, change, merge or split of delivery dates. Multiple date changes can be sent using multiple Order Confirmation transmissions. Update Order Confirmation 1st Order Confirmation Purchase Order Case 1 -- 1 of 10 -- Case 2 1st Order Confirmation Purchase Order Update Order Confirmation -- 2 of 10 -- Case 3 1st Order Confirmation Update Order Confirmation Purchase Order -- 3 of 10 -- Order confirmation general rules -- 4 of 10 -- An Order Confirmation can only include items belonging to the same Purchase Order. (The message only allows to refer to a single Purchase Order number) The Purchase Order Id should be included in the Order Confirmation message : If a supplier has started generating Order Confirmations from his ERP, these Order Confirmations can’t be edited from SAP Business Network. Similarly, if an Order Confirmation is initially created from SAP Business Network subsequent Order Confirmations coming from a supplier ERP will not be accepted by SAP Business Network. If an Order Confirmation message gets blocked in error on SAP Business Network, it will not reach Buyer ERP. Rejection details can be found on the Ariba SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network* Transaction Tracker and could be checked and also received with the Status Update Request Message If an Order Confirmation failed due to a wrong value send by the supplier, which means Order Confirmation is rejected by business rules, then it’s possible to set up the following notification in SAP Business Network to receive it by email * SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network hereafter referred to as Managed Gateway for Spend&Network -- 5 of 10 -- Order confirmation Header -- 6 of 10 -- An Order Confirmation is always linked to a unique Purchase Order, and a Purchase Order can be confirmed several times (if it’s allowed by rule in SAP Business Network Portal) The Order confirmation Header indicates if the Purchase Order is confirmed for the first time or if previous Order Confirmation has been sent : <ConfirmationHeader> operation must equal : "new" for the first Order Confirmation sent against a Purchase Order "update" or the following ones The Order Confirmation number “confirmID” attribut of an update OC should be the same as the new OC. Summary of the rules on the “operation” attribute: The operation attribute with a “new” value is only used when one or more lines are confirmed for the first time. If an Order confirmation with the operation attribute with a “new” value is sent against a Purchase Order already confirmed or partially confirmed it will fail. The operation attribute with an “update” value in used when at least one of the line of the Purchase Order has already successfully been confirmed. Previous Confirmed line can be included but it’s not mandatory to include them. Example: -- 7 of 10 -- Reconfirmation of a Purchase Order : A Purchase Order can be reconfirmed several times for different reasons: It can be a reconfirmation initiated by the supplier due to a change in the delivery date, price, quantities (depending of what is allowed by the buyer by the control Keys or rules set up in SAP Business Network) It can also be a reconfirmation needed following a Change Purchase Order sent by the buyer. Although the last PO version received by the supplier reflects exactly a previously sent confirmation, another confirmation could be required depending on Buyer requirement (rules set-up) SAP Business Network portal will store the history of all confirmations made for each PO line. By reconfirming a Purchase Order, the supplier could have to confirm date in the past. It may be allowed or not by Customer per rule Reconfirmation initiated by a supplier: In this case, logic for the operation has to follow the one, that has been described in the slide « Order confirmation Header » Reconfirmation due to a change Order sent by the Buyer: In this case, logic to follow for the Order Confirmation header depends on the rules « Retain confirmation status for unchanged line items on change orders » and «Retain confirmation status for changed line items on change orders that match supplier confirmation” : If these rules are unchecked : The confirmation status of items on a previous order is not retained. Then each time when there is a change PO, the supplier can send a New or an Update OC. The confirmationId should remain the same. -- 8 of 10 -- If the rule « Retain confirmation status for unchanged line items on change orders » is checked : The confirmation status of unchanged line items on a previous order is retained on a subsequent change order. The confirmation status of changed line items is not retained in case of one of the following segment is changed in the Change Order Notes : A comparison between the PO versions must be performed on supplier side unless there is an indicator build by the buyer in the PO (if such indicator exists, it’s described in Delta samples provides with the Integration Guidelines) When this rule is checked, the confirmation status is also retained for any line item that has a rejected quantity (full or partial). Below you will find the different behavior when “Retain confirmation status for unchanged line items on change orders” is active -- 9 of 10 -- Reconfirmation Logic of a Purchase Order with “Retain confirmation status for unchanged line items on change orders” checked -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SCC EMEA Supplier integ.content: INTERNAL – SAP and Customers Only EMEA SCC Seller Integration – FAQ Emilia Stefan March , 2025 -- 1 of 3 -- 2 INTERNAL – SAP and Customers Only Important questions Question Answer Is SAP Business Network “touching” the internal back-end system / middleware of the supplier ? No it does not. Is there a specific requirement coming from SAP Business Network for the supplier to use a specific ERP / ERP version ? No. SAP Business Network does not have requirements or limitations related to the ERP / ERP version used by the supplier. That because the Supplier’s ERP / ERP version is basically not transparent to the SAP Business Network. As long as the supplier is able to process the files in the specification of BUYER* project and provide back files that comply with the BUYER* specification as requitements the actual back-end of the supplier is not transparent for the project. Is SAP Business Network requiring the suppliers to use / purchase a specific middleware / third party provider in order to complete the seller integration ? No. SAP Business Network does not have requirements or limitations related to the middleware / third party provider that the supplier is using. The suppliers are free to chose whatever integration solutions, applications, middleware's or service providers are better suited for their internal polices. As long as the supplier is able to process the files in the specification of BUYER* project and provide back files that comply with the BUYER* specification as requitements the actual middleware / third party provider of the supplier is not transparent for the project. Is the SAP Business Network team, the SI team, part of the internal mappings that take place internally on Supplier’s side ? No. Please note the SAP SI is not part of the internal mappings that take place on the supplier’s side. Please note that the SAP SI will not be in a position offer any type consultancy in terms or internal supplier mappings, supplier ERP processes, supplier middleware, etc. It will be the responsibility of the supplier to find and engage the necessary resources for their own internal project . Who can indicate the timeline of the Seller Integration Project? The Supplier Team Since all the developments and mapping are happening on the suppliers side, the supplier is the only one in a position to indicate how long these processes take on their side. Who has leverage to commit the supplier to a specific timeline, Project Scope and readiness moment (the exact start date of the Project) ? BUYER Team BUYER Team is the only one who has the necessary leverage to discuss, agree and commit the supplier to a specific timeline, Project Scope and readiness moment as per the requirements of the BUYER* organization -- 2 of 3 -- 3 INTERNAL – SAP and Customers Only Important questions related to BUYER* resources Question Answer Does the Buyer need to allocate dedicated resources for Supplier Integration ? Yes, the buyer needs to strategically approach supplier integration and plan to have dedicated resources for this part of their project. The resources must be allocated for the entire duration of the desired/intended supplier projects. Do the Buyer resources allocated to Supplier Integration need to be technical ? No, they do not. The Buyer resources will need to have a deep understating of the Buyer’s organization, business requirements and the Buyer scope within the SAP Business Network. From our experience we have noticed that the successful projects were the ones where the Buyer team had internal materials and procedures to ensure a scalable and controllable deployment of the Adoption project part ( enablement and supplier integration ) . Is supplier Integration a technical project/exercise ? No, it is not. From our experience we have noticed that the great majority of the efforts of the buyer and the supplier are spent on non-technical activities like ( not limited to ) : - Change management activities - Business and logistic requirements agreement alignment - Day to day activities alignment - Master data alignment The actual technical activities are a smaller part of the project that just help in place the business requirements aligned between the buyer and the supplier. Success factors ( macro view ) Avoid approaching the Buyer Solution Implementation only as a technical project. Clear/ complete business requirements fully documented in the Functional Design document. Include ALL Business Flavors ( per each buyer location in scope and each SCC process in the Functional Document and Buyer User Acceptance Testing. All business requirements must be locked at the moment of the Buyer User Acceptance Testing. Make sure that the Buyer UAT will include day to day real business scenarios that include all possible flavors (often different per each buyer location in scope ), refrain from testing using technical dummy files. A clear Buyer communication strategy that includes a compliance message for the suppliers in scope Buyer Internal Resources fully informed on the scope of the project and prepared to handle the discussions with the suppliers / clear compliance message. Buyer dedicated resources to Supplier Adoption ( both enablement and supplier integration ) -- 3 of 3 --

file://SBN/split/SCC Indirect Cross Trai.content: 1 INTERNAL ONLY SCC / Indirect Cross Training Purchase Order Collaboration -- 1 of 10 -- 2 Agenda 01 Purchase Order Collaboration 02 03 04 Practical Exam Scenarios Order Confirmation & Ship Notice Goods Receipt & Invoice -- 2 of 10 -- 3 SCC Purchase Order Collaboration Overview Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice Today we will be focusing on the SCC Process Purchase Order Collaboration. o PO Collaboration’s core function is facilitating the Buyer and Supplier’s Ordering, Shipment and Invoicing of Direct Materials required for their Supply Chain. This includes raw materials, finished goods, spare parts or components. o Normally PO Collaboration is not the only SCC process the Buyer would have in scope and is often used in combination with other SCC Process integral to the Buyer’s own Supply Chain. o It also provides a great starting point for Supplier Integration Specialists as it’s familiar in the sense of documents you may have worked with previously, but also extents it’s functionally and use of cXML elements to meet industry specific requirements within Supply Chain. -- 3 of 10 -- 4 SCC Purchase Order Collaboration Overview -- 4 of 10 -- 5 SCC Process Overview Consignment Collaboration In consignment collaboration, the supplier sends consignments to the buyer, but retains ownership of the consignments until the buyer pays for the assignment the buyer consumes. The transfer of ownership, and often of location, to the buyer at the time of consumption is called a consignment movement. The consignment movement information flows from Buyer to Supplier. Subcontract Collaboration This solution supports the following features for subcontract purchase orders and their associated documents, which are used in contract manufacturing collaboration. Forecast Collaboration Forecast collaboration allows buyers to send forecasts of future procurement to suppliers. Suppliers can send commitments to buyers based on forecast demand. Quality Collaboration Quality inspection collaboration supports buyer inspections of supplier facilities. Supplier Managed Inventory (SMI) This module provides suppliers with visibility into the buyer's inventory and demand levels so that they can replenish inventory based on established minimum and maximum stock levels. Schedule Agreement Collaboration Form of an outline agreement to procure items on predetermined dates according to an aligned Schedule. Returns Collaboration The returns process deals with the business process of returning goods to the Supplier. It also deals with receiving credit for the returned items. Material Traceability Capture complete material provenance from raw material to finished product to enhance safety, sustainability, and customer loyalty. Please note: Not a process for Supplier Integration but adds to the importance of correct Batch Information on Orders / Ship Notices. Supply Chain Collaboration Solutions Glossary A Supply Chain in the context of Buyers and Suppliers is the structured flow of materials, information, and commitments that allows suppliers to deliver goods, and Buyers to convert those inputs into finished offerings. This can be anything from; Electronics, Cars, Medicine, Food or Appliances. These are all industries that currently transact via SAP Business Network SCC. -- 5 of 10 -- 6 SCC Purchase Order Collaboration + Other SCC Processes Purchase Order Order Confirmation Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice o Please remember that when other SCC Processes are also in scope, the Purchase Order is often not the start of the procurement flow and other documents may be transacted (Integrated or Portal) before the PO even is sent to the Supplier. o A good example is the combination of Forecast Collaboration and Purchase Order Collaboration where the Forecasting of order quantity is completed before the PO is sent to the Supplier. This forecasting can either be integrated or completed via the Portal by Suppliers. o This is not limited to Forecast Collaboration and applies to all other SCC process that the Buyer may have in scope. Forecast Collaboration PO Collaboration Forecast Forecast Commit -- 6 of 10 -- 7 Purchase Order – Direct Materials -- 7 of 10 -- 8 Purchase Order Types – Quick Glance SCC Processes Purchase Order Type Comments Purchase Order Collaboration Direct Materials Purchase Order Ordering of direct materials based on the Material Master from the Buyer’s ERP. Subcontracting Collaboration Subcontract Purchase Order An order that contains Component Information for a Subtracting Supplier to create and/or finish the goods with. Consignment Collaboration Consignment Purchase Order Order of Consignment materials that are only purchased at time of movement / use. Returns Collaboration Returns Purchase Order Materials that are to be returned due to warranty or failed inspection. Schedule Agreement Collaboration Schedule Agreement / Schedule Agreement Release (JIT & Forecast) Order that’s based on a contractual agreement that outlines the frequency of deliveries. Service Process Service Orders Service Order for both planned and unplanned services. Indirect Processes Purchase Order Type Comments Buying and Invoicing Catalog Order, Free Text Order, Blanket PO Catalog Order based off Supplier Punchout or CIF. Not a part of SCC. Commerce Automation Catalog Order, Free Text Order, Blanket PO Not a part of SCC. Despite the overarching name, the use, information, and structure that defines the Purchase Order differs greatly per the process it’s a part of. Requirements that applies to the PO within the PO Collaboration may not be applicable to other processes. All POs within SCC are generated by the Buyer’s ERP. Please note: The below are just examples of the PO types only and is not representative of full SCC process. Please refer to appendix 2.a for a full overview of processes and documents. -- 8 of 10 -- 9 Supply Chain Terminology for PO Collaboration Term Explanation Material ID The material that is being procured by the Buyer from the Supplier. The material may be the stock / items required for the buyer’s production line, or the end-product itself. Normally this the Buyer PartID on the PO and used as the main identifier. It’s not common for the Supplier PartID to be maintained as well, only in specific cases. Production Plants, Warehouse, Distribution Centre or Store. Depending on the Buyer, ShipTo locations to them could mean a Production Plant, Warehouse, Distribution Centre or Store Front Location and would generally differ depending on the industry. • Some Buyer’s may have a combination of Production plants, warehouse and distribution centers that suppliers need to shipTo. • Production Plants should be treated as small entities within an organization. It’s common that a Buyer’s Production plant will have different requirements and processes in scope. For example: • Buyer Plant A: could be using Purchase Orders Collaboration as they just needs material parts for Repairs. • Buyer Plant B: could be using both SCC Processes Schedule Agreements and Purchase Orders as the plant is dedicated to mass production of the end product. Material requirements planning (MRP) Material requirements planning (MRP) is a software-based integrated inventory and supply management system designed for businesses. Companies use MRP to estimate raw material needs, manage inventory, and plan production and deliveries. This terminology is not specific to SAP Business Network SCC, but is general terminology used by Buyer’s that are experienced with Direct Materials Supply Chain. -- 9 of 10 -- 10 Purchase Order - Some differences, a quick glance Indirect SCC Buyer Part ID Usually optional. Mostly Supplier Part Ids are used. Free text Pos are also possible. Used by Buyer and supplier as main identifier of the materials. Data alignment of materials in scope are integral to the integration connection. Bill To , Ship To and Storage Locations Usually the buyer locations are head quarters / offices or delivery is indicted directly to the employee Each Buyer location has a unique identification code at the plant / shipTo level. For large plants or warehouses, the shipTo location may have designated locations where the Supplier / Carrier must deliver to once at the plant / warehouse location. For example; an order of vaccines can only be delivered to storage location “A” as it’s medical related. Batch Ids Not commonly utilized Used to identify specific production lots Revisions and Drawing numbers Not commonly utilized Used to identify different versions of product specifications Schedule Lines Not used. Usually the parent PO line is used. The PO Line is the parent of the Schedule lines. Used by Buyers to specify a schedule of deliveries for the PO line Quantity. Control Keys Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules if configured to do so. Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules Tolerances ( as per control keys ) date and quantity Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules if configured to do so. Used all the time In general for Supply Chain Collaboration, requirements are defined at either a material or plant level by the Buyer within their ERP. These requirements are shared with the Supplier using Purchase Order Control keys and Tolerances, when sent on the PO these supersede the Supplier level transaction rules. This allows Buyers the capability configure their requirements at either a material or plant level, which is extremally important for large or global organizations where these requirements will often differ throughout their various business entities, Supply Chain process, locations, material and vendors. -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SCC Indirect Cross Trai.content: 11 SCC Specific Considerations on the Purchase Order SCC Flow Material / Plant Specific Revision ID Provides and indicator for both buyers and supplier to help identify the part version needing to be produced. New revisions may have accompanying design specifications sent as an attachment on the Purchase Order. Material Specific Control Keys Document Instructions and tolerances supersede what is defined at the supplier group level. Control keys and tolerances are defined by the Buyer’s ERP and would need to be altered in the Buyer’s system there if there are conflicting keys or tolerances set for the OC or ASN as it’s overriding all respective transactional rules in the network. Yes Purchase Order Schedule Lines PO line is the Parent of the Schedule Lines, you can have multiples schedule lines on one PO Line. This provides a delivery schedule that the supplier would need to adhere to when supplying the requested goods. The OC confirming the Delivery date would need to include each of the scheduled lines for PO Line 10. Normally the ASN Shipments would be as per Schedule Line requested Quantity and DeliveryDate. Please Note the Schedule Line: Date&Time Timestamp, Quantity and UOM must match exactly when it's returned on the Order Confirmation. Schedule Line reference requirement is determined by Supplier Transactional rules. Yes Handling Unit Flag PO Flag that specifies if Handling Unit Information is Required on the ASN for this specific material. This is a material level flag and may not apply to all materials within the supplier's scope. The material Master Data must be aligned between the Buyer and Supplier as this requirement could also differ between Buyer plant / locations as well. Yes Quality Process Flag Certain Materials require additional certification documentation or must follow an additional quality process flow. Commonly this in the form of a PDF document (Certificate of Analysis) that's attached to the ASN / Ship Notice cXML message. More complex process a part Quality Collaboration would require additional cXML messages to be sent. Yes Batch Required Flag Flag to specify if Batch Information is required on the ASN. Depending on the material, this information could include BatchID, ExpiryDate, ProductionDate or UseByDate. This may also impact the ASN structure as different material Batches / BatchIDs are usually split into sperate ASN Lines when sent on a single ASN. Yes Purchase Order Attachments Attachments on POs are commonly utilized in specific industries. The two common types of suppliers that utilize attachments are; • Packaging Suppliers: Labeling and information that needs to be on the box of the end product (For example; Pharmaceutical or Health products). • Parts Suppliers: it's utilized in combination with the material revision ID. Attachments would be additional documentation, specifications, product drawings and dimensions that would be needed by the supplier to manufacture. Yes -- 1 of 10 -- 12 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice As we go through each of the documents within the PO Collaboration process, we will be using an example of a Grocery Store (Buyer) purchasing cartons of Milk from their largest Milk Supplier. Cartons of Milk will be delivered by the Supplier to each of the Buyer’s Distribution Warehouses based on the Purchase Order. The Buyer then internally transfers the Milk to each of their store locations daily. This should help with visualizing how different technical aspects within the cXML documents can affect the process in the real world when it comes to Supply Chain. If you prefer, you can apply the same scenario for Oat Milk instead. Supplier Buyer (DC101) Buyer Store Fronts -- 2 of 10 -- 13 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Schedule Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag As per a Standard Purchase Order to Invoice process, the Buyer has sent a Purchase Order from their ERP to the Integrated Supplier via the SAP Business Network. The Supplier received the PO into their ERP and converted it into their internal Sales Order to start processing the order. The PO was for 550 2 Liter Cartons (EA) of Milk The Supplier was expecting this demand of quantity for this location. A month prior to receiving the PO the Buyer and Supplier had Collaborated on the Forecast of Orders via the Portal. -- 3 of 10 -- 14 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Schedule Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag Upon review of the Purchase Order the Supplier had identified that the ShipTo location for this Order is for the Buyer’s Distribution Centre. It’s an extremely large Distribution Centre (DC101) and has multiple entrances that lead to different storage locations for specific goods. o Milk must be constantly refrigerated so delivery must go to storageLocation ”C” at this Distribution Centre (DC101). o If you were using the example of Oat Milk. The Buyer may want it delivered to StorageLocation “A” as refrigeration is not needed. The Purchase Order would reflect this requirement using the ShipTo and StorageLocation. It is critical this information is captured by the Supplier’s ERP so it can be informed to their carrier for this shipment to ensure the full delivery is correct. Note: Depending on the Buyer, ShipTo locations to them could mean a Production Plant, Warehouse, Distribution Centre or Store Front Location and would generally differ depending on the industry. -- 4 of 10 -- 15 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Schedule Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag Master Data Alignment It’s extremely important that the alignment of data between Buyer and Supplier is completed in addition to their integration, or on a regular basis as a part of their Business Relationship. This includes business specific information such as ShipTo / StorageLocation, BillTo, Material ID, UOM, Price ect... Within Supply Chain, there is a strong focus on Material level requirements, and business processes and logic based on each specific Material IDs. Any discrepancies lead to delayed materials that would impact the Buyer directly. If for example the shipTo and storage locations were not correctly aligned in the supplier’s system, delivery of goods may not have occurred, impacting available Milk for an entire city / region. -- 5 of 10 -- 16 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Schedule Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag For this specific DC Location, the Buyer would send Weekly orders for Milk every Thursday to the Supplier. If they received all 5500 cartons of Milk on Friday at the Distribution Centre, they would use valuable warehouse space to hold all the cartons until sold. Instead, the Buyer requests the delivery of PO Line 10 throughout the week using 3 different Schedule Lines. From past consumer trends, the Buyer knows that Monday and Friday are the busiest days at the Grocery Store locations, so the majority of the 5500 Cartons are split between those two days and is reflected as such at the Schedule Line level on the PO. -- 6 of 10 -- 17 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario - PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Scheduled Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag Control Keys and and Tolerances can be defined at either the vendor, plant and/or material level. When sent on the PO they supersede the related supplier transactional rules. o The Buyer requires both OC and ASN to be sent for the Purchase Order to ensure accurate delivery information. o As noted, the Buyer’s DC space is limited so the upper limited of delivered quantities is 10%. o There is no allowed tolerance on Delivery Date as it’s vital that there is enough milk for specific days. It’s also to ensure the freshest possible Milk for the end customers and limit any spoilage. In combination with the scheduled lines and Material level tolerances, the Buyer has a lean Supply Chain that’s able to cater to all customers in the City on a weekly basis. Note: If for this specific material the Tolerance was outside of the agreed percentage causing the documents to fail (OC / ASN), this tolerance would need to be amended by the Buyer within their ERP and Change Order sent with the updated tolerance at the line level. -- 7 of 10 -- 18 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – PO Purchase Order  ShipTo / Storage Location  Buyer Part ID  Schedule Lines  Control Keys  Tolerances  Handling Units Flag  Quality Flag  Batch Managed Material Flag o For food related Suppliers and Buyers, Lots / Batches are commonly documented by both the Buyer and Supplier. This is normally referred to as Batch Managed Materials. Batch Information is provided on the ASN for the shipped quantity. If there is a recall of Milk both parties know exactly what stores and locations are affected. o In accordance with local regulations, regular testing of the Milk is required. The Supplier is also aware of this Business requirement, so for this specific PO it’s flagged internally for testing and prepares the required Analysis documentation for the Quality Collaboration process. o To ensure that Buyer Distribution Centre (DC101) can efficiently unpack and receive the Milk delivery on the day, the Buyer requires Handling Unit / Packaging Information sent on the Ship Notice, this will detail in the cXML how the goods are shipped within the truck along with the order weight & dimensions. -- 8 of 10 -- 19 SCC PO cXML Examples / Comparison Purchase Order Line Example including; § Control Keys § Schedule Lines, § Handling Unit Flag § Quality Flag § Batch Managed Material Flag For the full comparison of an Indirect and SCC Purchase Order, please refer excel previously shared within the shared drive. -- 9 of 10 -- 20 Order Confirmation -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/SCC Indirect Cross Trai.content: 21 SCC PO Collaboration – Order Confirmation The Order Confirmation provides the Buyer with an indication of what to expect and when. This is particularly important for materials that are relevant for material requirements planning (MRP) in the ERP because data in the Order Confirmation impacts the planning for that material. o Due to this, there are often a heavy focus on ensuring that provides the latest status via the Order Confirmation regardless of if the Purchase Order has already been confirmed. In turn this may result in multiple PO versions and Order Confirmations. In SCC many Buyer’s have implemented Supply Chain Monitor and Order Confirmation with Approval. This monitoring feature sits within the Buyer’s SAP Business Network Account and allows the Buyer to respond to Order Confirmations from their Suppliers. If the Supplier Confirms the Purchase Order outside the agreed tolerance for quantity, price, or delivery date, an Order Confirmation Deviation Approval feature enables the Buyer to review the confirmation deviation and decide whether to approve or reject the Order Confirmation. Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice -- 1 of 10 -- 22 SCC PO Collaboration – Order Confirmation Approval Flow Example Order Confirmation Approval is only in scope for specific SCC Buyers. Please be aware it’s common for SCC Buyer’s to deploy this functionality as a part of their SCC solution. For Hybrid Buyers that have both SCC and Indirect Suppliers under the same SAP Business Network Buyer account, only Order Confirmations for SCC Direct POs will trigger the approval flow. -- 2 of 10 -- 23 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – Order Confirmation Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice Milk Supplier Buyer (DC101) Buyer Store Fronts -- 3 of 10 -- 24 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – Order Confirmation Order Confirmation 1 (New)  Accept  Schedule Line reference The Milk Supplier has since processed the PO and is ready to confirm supply. As they were expecting this demand, they have enough Milk stock to ship as per the schedule lines on the PO. The OC was automictically approved by the Buyer as it’s all within OC tolerance. Order Confirmation 2 (Update)  Accept with Quantity Change  Schedule Line reference Unfortunately, the morning of delivery a 3 pallets of Milk cartons had fell over in the Supplier’s Warehouse and they are not able to meet the expected demand for Friday. The Supplier Creates an additional OC (Update) to notify the buyer with a new delivery quantity of 50 instead. As this is outside of Tolerance, the OC is sent for approval. The OC is approved by the Buyer and a Change Order with the new Quanty is sent. Supplier Confirms (Update) the Change Order before the warehouse starts packing the goods. Order Confirmation 3 (Update)  Accept  Schedule Line reference -- 4 of 10 -- 25 SCC PO Collaboration – Order Confirmation Over the coming month, an additional SI Training session will by lead by my colleague Isabelle. • This session will go into detail Order Confirmation logic and key considerations when confirming / requesting changes at the Schedule Line level for Integrated Suppliers. Today’s focus was to understand the Importance of the Order Confirmation and its practical use in the Supply Chain. Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice Goods Receipt Invoice -- 5 of 10 -- 26 Advanced Ship Notice -- 6 of 10 -- 27 SCC PO Collaboration – Advanced Ship Notice Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice • Batch Information • COA (Quality Attachment) • Handling Units / Packaging Technical Acknowledgment Goods Receipt Invoice The ASN within SCC extends its current use to provide extra detail about the Shipped Quantity before it’s physically received by the Buyer’s Plant / Distribution Centre. This allows the Buyer’s warehouse to receipt the goods with reference to the ASN, thus automatically populating the details from the cXML ASN (IBD – In bound Delivery). o If the the ASN is not sent, the Buyer warehouse would have to check received stock and manually document the information into their own system to create the IBD internally. Batch Information is commonly utilized in many industries and includes additional for the shiped products such as BatchID, expiryDate, productionDate and Buyer batchID(Subcon). o For certain industries serialID for finished good may be used instead, or a GTIN / Barcode ID as an additional identifier for consumer products. Certificate Of Analysis (Quality Attachment) used by Buyer’s to ensure stock is periodically checked by Suppliers and meets certain industry standards before it’s shipped to the Buyer’s location. Handling Units / Packaging Information Provides the Buyer with a detailed packing structure of the goods being shipped on the ASN. This includes the SSCC ID of the Handling Units / Packages, Level of packing used (Pallet > Boxes > Goods), and the dimensions & weight for each of the packages. -- 7 of 10 -- 28 SCC PO Collaboration – Advanced Ship Notice Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice • Batch Information • COA (Quality Attachment) • Handling Units / Packaging Technical Acknowledgment Goods Receipt Invoice Technical Acknowledgments: For SCC Suppliers Integrating ASNs it’s extremely important that the Technical Acknowledgment (StatusUpdate) cXML message is enabled and integrated by the supplier. Majority of information sent on the ASN is not validated on the Business Network, but rather the Buyer’s Warehouse System so unless the the supplier checks each ASN history for each ASN or is setup to receive email notifications from the network to check, it’s incredibly difficult for the supplier to full visibility of their ASN status. Handling Units: An additional Training session will be designated to the structure of the ASNs with Handling Units / Packaging. -- 8 of 10 -- 29 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – Advanced Ship Notice Milk Supplier Buyer (DC101) Buyer Store Fronts Purchase Order Order Confirmation • With Approval Advanced Ship Notice • Batch Information • COA (Quality Attachment) • Handling Units / Packaging Technical Acknowledgment Goods Receipt Invoice -- 9 of 10 -- 30 SCC PO Collaboration Scenario – Advanced Ship Notice Ship Notice 1 Quantity 50 • Single Batch Packaging • 1 Pallets > Crates Certificate of Analysis (Attached) The Supplier is now ready to Pick and Pack the Order before it’s shipped to the Buyer DC(101) As per the Change Order Friday’s Schedule quantity is now 50 instead of 200. The Milk is normally packed into re- usable crates and loaded onto a pallet supporting 50 cartons. • Certificate of Analysis is completed for this shipment of 50 and attached as a PDF to the cXML ASN. cXML ASN is sent via the SAP Business Network and received by the Buyer’s ERP successfully. The Buyer’s system automatically creates an IBD (Inbound Delivery Note) ready for the actual receiving of goods. Supplier Receives the cXML Technical Acknowledgement from the Buyer’s system that Ship Notice was successfully. Technical Acknowledgment (From Buyer) “ShipNotice 1 Accepted – IBD created.” -- 10 of 10 --

The scenario discussed today was for only a single supplier, plant and material ID. Please consider that it takes many individual suppliers and materials to supply a large country wide Grocery Store. Please note this not information that you have to know about your Buyer and Supplier. Mostly Supplier Part Ids are used. Free text Pos are also possible Used by Buyer and supplier as main identifier of the materials. Free text Pos are not used. Bill To , Ship To and Storage Locations Usually the buyer locations are head quarters / offices or delivery is indicted directly to the employee Each Buyer location has a unique identification code at the plant / shipTo level. For large plants or warehouses, the shipTo location may have designated locations where the Supplier / Carrier must deliver to once at the plant / warehouse location. For example; an order of vaccines can only be delivered to storage location “A” as it’s medical related. Batch Ids Not commonly utilized Used to identify specific production lots Revisions and Drawing numbers Not commonly utilized Used to identify different versions of product specifications Schedule Lines Not used. Usually the parent PO line is used. The PO Line is the parent of the Schedule lines Control Keys Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules if configured to do so. Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules Tolerances ( as per control keys ) date and quantity Over-rule the validation / Transaction rules if configured to do so. Used all the time Blanket Pos In use Not part of the scope Catalogues In use Not part of the scope. All material master data is locally stored by buyer and supplier -- 4 of 10 -- 5 SCC PO cXML Examples / Comparison Purchase Order Line Example including; § Control Keys § Schedule Lines, § Handling Unit Flag § Quality Flag § Batch Managed Material Flag For the full comparison of an Indirect and SCC Purchase Order, please refer to the excel below. -- 5 of 10 -- 6 SCC Specific Considerations on the Purchase Order SCC Flow Material / Plant Specific Revision ID Provides and indicator for both buyers and supplier to help identify the part version needing to be produced. New revisions may have accompanying design specifications sent as an attachment on the Purchase Order. Material Specific Control Keys Document Instructions and tolerances supersede what is defined at the supplier group level. Control keys and tolerances are defined by the Buyer’s ERP and would need to be altered there if there are conflicting keys or tolerances set for the OC or ASN. Yes Purchase Order Schedule Lines This provides a delivery schedule that the supplier would need to adhere to when supplying the requested goods. The OC confirming the Delivery date would need to include each of the scheduled lines for PO Line 10. Normally the ASN Shipments would be split as per schedule line. Please Note: Date-Time Timestamp & UOM must match exactly when it's returned on the Order Confirmation. Quantity tolerance is per case. Yes Handling Unit Flag PO Flag that specifies if Handling Unit Information is Required on the ASN for this specific material. This is a material level flag and may not apply to all materials within the supplier's scope. The material Master Data must be aligned between the Buyer and Supplier as this requirement could also differ between Buyer plant / locations as well. Yes Quality Process Flag Certain Materials require additional certification documentation or must follow an additional quality process flow. Commonly this in the form of a PDF document (Certificate of Analysis) that's attached to the ASN / Ship Notice cXML message. More complex process a part Quality Collaboration would require additional cXML messages to be sent. Yes Batch Required Flag Flag to specify if Batch Information is required on the ASN. Depending on the material, this information could include BatchID, ExpiryDate, ProductionDate or UseByDate. This may also impact the ASN structure as different material Batches / BatchIDs are usually split into sperate ASN Lines when sent on a single ASN. Yes Purchase Order Attachments Attachments on POs are commonly utilized in specific industries. The two common types of suppliers that utilize attachments are; • Packaging Suppliers: Labeling and information that needs to be on the box of the end product (For example; Pharmaceutical or Health products). • Parts Suppliers: it's utilized in combination with the material revision ID. Attachments would be additional documentation, specifications, product drawings and dimensions that would be needed by the supplier to manufacture.
