as per SCC DD and methodology Outcome Purchase Order Collaboration Buy Side Education of the Buyer SIFL resource for SCC SI methodology ( includes buyer consultation ) Able to articulate / educate Buyer team / SIFL and /or internal teams on SCC methodology Purchase Order Collaboration with Order Confirmation Flow ASN with Handling Units Buy Side Guidelines creation - new Able to create / review/ revise / update SCC Guidelines OC Deviations , Tolerances , OC with Delivery lines reference , Invoices with ASN / GR reference Guideline update / modification Sell Side SCC SI project activities, calls, notes Able to conduct SCC SI projects as per SCC methodology Today’s session is meant to be an intro, a first step -- 4 of 10 -- 5 Indirect and SCC -- 5 of 10 -- 6 SCC • Purchased materials are directly part of the produced finished goods and the production process • Direct and critical impact in the production lines / finished goods / distribution / logistics • Buyers have multiple Locations / Plants with different scope flavors - impacting Scope, timelines, Go lives strategies • Multiple SCC processes covering different parts of production, manufacturing, planning, etc • Each buyer implements different combinations of the SCC processes • Buyers and suppliers have different teams/ procedures / materials etc per each SCC process Indirect • Purchased materials are not part of the produced finished goods • No direct impact on the production lines / finished goods • Buyer Locations have more impact when Invoices are in scope • One single Process Some differences – a quick glance Consultancy mindset & Pro- active approach -- 6 of 10 -- 7 Context: 2 Solutions Providing different value propositions and addressing different business work streams and requirements for our customers Supply Chain Collab ✓ Increasing visibility along the supply chain enabling margin growth and Inventory stock levels optimization. ✓ Enabling Business Transformation and driving operational excellence by optimizing manufacturing and asset performance and elevating product quality ✓ Business Critical operations Indirect Procurement ✓ Enabling control and monitoring allowing the Buyers to standardize their indirect procurement operations. ✓ Reducing error handling enabling faster invoice reconciliation and cash flow optimization Over 35 SCC processes combinations and 100+ document types variants One set of documents with approx 5+ types variances Specific Indirect : - Buyer Org and resources - Buyer internal procedures - Buyer compliance message - Buyer Supplier communication - Buyer Flight plan Specific SCC : - Buyer Org/resources and internal procedures, business and logistic requirements (+flavors per buyer location) - Buyer compliance message - Buyer Supplier communication and change management - Buyer Flight plan & Supplier segmentation per SCC process and per Buyer location Where ? Official list of all SCC processes and documents per each together with the availability in multiple file formats: Standard B2B Formats on SAP Integration Suite managed gateway.xlsx -- 7 of 10 -- 8 What are the Criteria that impact the effort/project plan/timeline of the BUYER and Suppliers during the entire project ? Change management and Business Transformation ▪ Change management is CRITICAL to the success of the project ▪ SCC projects have a critical Transformation Added Value within the Buyer and Supplier organizations. ▪ Day to day operations are changed / optimized and/or completely renewed ▪ We have noticed that the change management activities deeply impact a project timeline and require multiple resources on both BUYER and Supplier side Number of BUYER Plants in scope ▪ It is very usual that SCC buyers have multiple Locations in scope ▪ From our experience we noticed that it is very often that different flavors of business/logistic requirements are in scope Per Each Buyer Location ▪ Please note that Buyer / Supplier SIT/UAT testing needs to be done per each Buyer Location in conjunction with each SCC process in scope Number of SCC Processes in scope ▪ A Buyer may have in scope one ( e.g. Po collab ) or more processes ( e.g. SMI, Po Collab, Forecast Collab ,etc ) at the same time. ▪ From our experience we noticed that each SCC process has on the Buyer side different requirements that need to be designed/mapped and tested separately ▪ The more processes are in scope the larger the timeline SCC Business Scope Buyer locations Change management Number of Document type per SCC Process in scope ▪ The buyer may chose to implement a certain number of documents per SCC process or all. ▪ Impact in the number of needed mappings and the timeline ▪ Buyer may have internal requirements/ technical limitations that dictate his choice -- 8 of 10 -- 9 SCC Projects – Supplier integration – One glance Buyer Dedicated resources for supplier Integration Buyer SIFL resource as part of standard SCC DD Buyer SIFL resource is not technical and is leading the supplier integration project Supplier interest in supplier Integration approach Due to strategic collaboration with the buyer suppliers often pursue themselves the integration project and have internal commitment for resources and necessary budgets SCC Direct impact – day to day operations Supplier and Buyer resources Buyer Interest / commitment / strategy About 60 to 70% of SCC Buyers come to the network already having a plan/pipeline for integrated suppliers. Usually the strategic suppliers are pilots Buyer compliance message 60 to 70% of SCC Buyers have the necessary leverage to deliver strict compliance messaging to their suppliers Buyer internal interest Change management and Business Transformation About 70 to 90% of SCC Buyers implement /deploy completely NEW Business scope / processes/ requirements as part of an SBN project. New scope may come as part of : ✓ New / legacy Buyer locations / regions ✓ S4 projects / migrations from other back-end systems ✓ Buyer Internal business requirements Strategic impact within the buyer organization Critical impact in day to day operations. Buyers are committed and treat each supplier as an individual project that is basically a mini version if the Buyer deployment project with average durations of 6 moths to 1 year or more depending on scope complexity 1 2 Critical Business Transformation projects 90% of SCC Buyers / partners have the wrong expectation that change management for new Business scope/requirements is covered by the technical deployment project / SAP, both on buyer and supplier side -- 9 of 10 -- 10 SCC Complexity -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/Training Session 2 SCC.content: SCC Indirect Cross training – Session 2 SCC Supplier Integration Roles and responsibilities Name, SAP Business Network May, 2026 -- 1 of 10 -- All sessions will be recorded All materials presented or offered before/after sessions will be made available Sessions will cover : methodology, procedures, business aspects, SBN functional topics and technical We aim for approximately 10 sessions followed by a Q&A Training purpose Location of all materials : And in the On24 application as part of the sessions – access is provided individually after you register Please note that all materials are MANDATORY and INTERNAL -- 2 of 10 -- Focus for today What we aim to cover ? Session 1 covered more business aspects impacting the projects Today’s session will focus on SAP SCC Methodology General aspects valid for both Buy – side and Sell Side More focus on the Sell-side activities What is Buyer Solution Deployment ? SCC Buyer dedicated roles Responsibilities of Buyer, Supplier and SAP Supplier Integration KO CALL and general process Please note that Buy – Side activities and methodology ( including Buyer Integration SCC KO call ) will not be covered today . A separate session will be dedicated to this subject. Have in mind the bigger picture – facilitating continuous Adoption and project growth ( adopting new SCC processes for example ) is the target -- 3 of 10 -- SCC Buyer Solution Deployment Services Include SAP Roles like : Delivery Executive and Product Expert along side Buyer Integrator SCC Enablement Deployment Description Stipulates that : - Buyer needs to have Dedicated resources for Supplier Enablement and Supplier Integration - Supplier Integration ( and Enablement ) are driven by the Buyer resources - Pilot suppliers are pre-defined : maximum 7 for portal and maximum 3 for Supplier integration - Supplier Integration KO call is lead by the Buyer resources – Buyer SIFL ( not by the SAP SI ) End to End testing is lead by the Buyer SIFL ( SAP SI is only covering initial technical testing ) Due to business/ operational impact the buyer is deeply involved and driving the process Most suppliers using Supplier Managed Gateway Change management should be aligned between buyer and supplier BEFORE starting the actual supplier integration Indirect Buyer Solution Deployment involves the SAP Buyer Integrator There are no dedicated and official Buyer resources for supplier Integration SAP SI is usually driving the Supplier Integration SAP SI is usually trying to advertise the advantages of supplier integration SAP SI leads the Supplier Integration KO call Usually SAP SI is driving end to end testing between Buyer and supplier More focus on buyer hands-off approach More suppliers using legacy connection -- 4 of 10 -- Buyer Solution Deployment What is a Deployment Description and why it is important ? -- 5 of 10 -- Buyer Solution Deployment defines the full Buyer Scope in SAP Business Network (SBN) – across business, operational, logistic, functional, and technical dimensions. It outlines how the buyer will use SBN and applies uniformly to all suppliers – portal and integrated suppliers. For example, if Purchase Orders weren’t inlcluded in the Buyer Solution, no supplier – integrated or portal – will receive them via SBN. The Buyer Solution acts as the foundation for all supplier interactions on the Network. The Buyer Solution Design Document captures the entire Buyer Scope on SBN, covering both the buyer’s back-end systems and how these are integrated with SBN. It serves as the source of truth for both portal training materials and Supplier Integration Guidelines. For more detailed information, consult your SCC deployment description. What is Buyer Solution Deployment/Implementation? -- 6 of 10 -- IDoc or proxy Native connection Pre-defined mappings & customizations cXML cXML Translation CXML or EDI Supplier Managed Gateway Buyer Managed Gateway Buyer Solution Deployment Supplier Message Flow And Translation Points for Integrated (B2B) Documents Buyer’s ERP Supplier’s ERP Supplier Managed Gateway for Spend & Network does not “touch” the supplier’s internal back-end systems. For inbound documents (e.g., PO), the supplier provides a URL endpoint to receive files in real time. For outbound documents (e.g., ASN), the supplier prepares the file according to BUYER* Seller Integration Guidelines. Buyer Managed Gateway and Supplier Managed Gateways do not perform the same functionalities. If Buyer uses SAP – Buyer Managed Gateway will act as an out of the box product and includes Services with pre-defined duration as per purchased licenses -- 7 of 10 -- 01 SAP roles included in the SCC Buyer Solution Deployment Services, and only during purchased period : Delivery Executive, Product Exert centre of excellence ), BI, Functional / Technical Consultant 02 SAP Roles included in the Embedded Services : NxLs ( digital or none in some cases ), Sis ( Buy side and sell side ), CSM ( as per case ) 03 In SCC The Buyer resources are driving the Supplier Integration projects. The details are presented in the SCC Enablement Deployment description page 9 04 The number of pilot suppliers portal and integration is presented in the SCC Enablement Deployment Description. INTERNAL LINKS ONLY DO NOT SHARE EXTERNALLY -- 9 of 10 -- As per SCC Enablement Deployment Description SAP NxL and SAP SCC SI pro-actively collaborate, review any outline case / supplier, highlight to each other any project risks/ deviations from SAP methodology BUYER Dedicated SEFL BUYER Dedicated SIFL SAP NxL ( shared resource ) SAP SCC SI ( shared resource ) To ensure seamless execution, Buyer SELF must engage proactively with Buyer SIFL to align on the flight plan, key suppliers Buyer locations/Plants, Business Scope, prioritization, wave capacity, and scheduling Buyer SEFL collaborates with the SAP NxL to jointly define, align, and plan the flight plan, pipeline projections, strategic approach, wave design, and desired timelines Buyer SIFL collaborates Pro-actively with the SAPSCC SI to jointly define, align, and plan the next supplier to be started, any strategic cases and pipeline visibility Collaborative partnership driving joint success -- 10 of 10 --

file://SBN/split/Training Session 2 SCC.content: Seller Integration - Participating Roles Who are the key players that have a mandatory role in the integration project? -- 1 of 10 -- The same contact may take on multiple roles Assists in troubleshooting document failure on BUYER* side back-end system. Attend supplier calls as needed. Performs data mapping or modifications on BUYER* side back-end system if needed (on case by case basis). Provides technical details for the integration to BUYER* back-end systems Together with the BUYER* SIFL organizes the regular calls with the suppliers . Reviews and confirms test plan per supplier. Attends supplier calls as needed. Generates test documents. Downloads & validates applicable test transactions; load & process through ERP. Assists in other testing activities, coordinate go-live The main contact for supplier integration project coordination within Customer organization and with the suppliers. Participates in Customer enablement meetings, drives kick-off and regular status calls for supplier integration projects, creates custom reporting. Creates and approves Identified Supplier communications, education content and project plan Participates in Customer requirements gathering and Customer design workshops. Supports Internal Customer training sessions needed for the seller integration project as well with the integrated suppliers themselves. Reinforces Solution compliance with Identified Integrated Supplier and internal Customer department stakeholder as part of the change management program. Participates in the Customer User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and drives the individual end to end testing within the supplier integration projects. Conducts enablement related activities in the SAP Business network and Customer back-end system. Obtains supplier’s commitment for project Scope and Timeline. Coordinates, during pilot phase, internal activities with the Functional Lead to facilitate the project progress. Coordinates, during pilot phase, with the Technical Lead if technical issues from integration supplier testing require trouble soothing. Coordinates with Customer’s purchasing department to address Integrated Suppliers that are not following agreed upon integration Testing Contact -- 2 of 10 -- BUYER* SIFL - Activities - general overview - Project holistic activities Please note that we can not estimate all the activities needed on the BUYER* side since each Buyer project represents a specific case. file://SBN/split/What is Buyer and Suppl.content: 1 SCC Supplier Integration INTERNAL What is Buyer SCC SI KO call and SCC SI Supplier KO call -- 1 of 6 -- 2 Buyer SCC SE KO Call OPTIONAL SCC SI INTRO session Buyer SCC - SI KO call SCC SI Supplier KO call What is it? • As part of the SCC Buyer SE call the SI part should be an Introduction to Seller Integration in general – focused on SCC SI methodology and Buyer dedicated resources/responsibilities as per SCC Deployment Description • It should NOT be a Technical presentation • Buyer SCC SI KO call is done per each buyer scope/case • Buyer SI ko call is NOT a technical call • It is means to Introduce the SCC Seller Integration methodology to the buyer’s team, including the Buyer dedicated role and its responsibilities as per SCC Deployment Description (Please see the related screenshot below from Deployment Description) • It should continue the message that was delivered during the buyer SE KO call either by our NxL colleagues, DE or, if there was an Intro session, directly by the SCC SI • The Buyer SI KO call is supposed to mark the moment when the Buyer will start to work/commit/start consider seller integration as part of his entire project • During the call the SCC SI will present the seller integration methodology/best practices to the team of the buyer • KO call is done per each supplier in scope for SCC integration and will reflect the specific relation of that specific supplier with the buyer • Supplier SCC SI KO is NOT a technical call • Ko call represents the official start of the integration project for that specific supplier Pre-condition: buyer SIFL should have already discussed and agreed with the supplier on the Business change management / Business requirements / SCC processes in scope (and document types per process) per each buyer Location / Plant When? • When a buyer is interested to know more about supplier Integration but does not have a definitive commitment to start it, does not have allocated resources to the Si part, is confused on what supplier integration is. • Usually in the Explore phase of New Buyer Deployments but it is possible that the interest of the buyer appears in different stages and / or after the completion of the initial Go live • When a buyer already has a declared interest / commitment to start the SCC SI part • Buyer should already have a dedicated buyer SIFL resource allocated Usually in the Explore phase of New Buyer Deployments but it is possible that the interest of the buyer appears in different stages and / or after the completion of the initial Go live • For each Supplier Pilot • For each supplier in the run phase -- 2 of 6 -- 3 Buyer SCC SE KO Call OPTIONAL SCC SI INTRO session - consultation Buyer SCC - SI KO call SCC SI Supplier KO call How is the KO call slide deck created per each buyer project? • Buyer ko call deck is updated (from the general template) per each buyer case/scope • We should start with the general standard slides and customize per buyer scope / case • Customizations/adaptations; add the logo of the buyer, remove / add SCC processes / documents that are in scope (based on whatever information is available to the SI at that point in time). Consult with NxL, DE and COE involved with the buyer to obtain any information available at the time • Buyer KO call deck is adapted per each buyer scope / case • We should start with the general standard slides and customize/ adapt per buyer • Customizations/adaptations; add the logo of the buyer, remove / add SCC processes / document’s types that are in scope (based on whatever information is available to the SI at that point in time) etc. It is critical for a successful approach to adapt as per the case of the buyer and focus during the session on what seems to be more fitted: buyer role / responsibilities, methodology, expectations, scope, change management, etc. • Buyer SIFL has the responsibility to create the needed documentation / decks - general and adapted per each supplier case / scope • SBN SCC SI – usually offers best practices as part of the SCC SI methodology sessions Typical duration 1 hour Can be reduced to less according to case / time available etc. 1 hour Please note that multiple sessions may be needed on a case-by-case basis 1 hour (but multiple sessions may be needed on a case-by- case basis) -- 3 of 6 -- 4 Buyer SCC SE KO Call OPTIONAL SCC SI INTRO session Buyer SCC - SI KO call SCC SI Supplier KO call What is the aim of the call? At the end of the call the buyer’s team should know that: • There is something called Seller Integration that needs to be included in the general project plan in the Buyer wishes to have it in scope • That Seller integration might impact their timelines / targets What are the dependencies between buyer Solution Deployment and the Seller Integration part • The Buyer is responsible for allocating dedicated resources that will take ownership of the responsibilities mentioned in the SCC Deployment Description • That a separate call will be organized to get in detail and they should expect it Recommendation: ask buyer if they are comfortable to record the session. Buyer team should archive the recording for internal KT sessions At the end of the call the team of the Buyer should be clear on the following points: • what is SCC supplier integration • what is the difference between a supplier working on the portal and an integrated supplier • enablement for integrated suppliers, who do what, integration and portal work are possible for the same supplier. • what resources are needed from buyer side and what are the responsibilities as per SCC Deployment Description • what are integration guidelines, why they are needed and when they are created • what is the process that is followed together with the buyer’s team for each supplier. • best practices Important: the buyer should be clear that it is their responsibility to discuss and agree with the supplier on the business scope AND the Change Management part (ideally before the supplier ko call) Recommendation: ask buyer if they are comfortable to record the session. Buyer team should archive the recording for internal KT sessions 1. Buyer SIFL and supplier team Review and re-confirm the scope of the project based on the individual business relation between BUYER and SUPPLIER • Business change management / Business requirements / SCC processes in scope (and document types per process) per each buyer Location/Plant • From these documents, are there some that are completely new (change management)? • Also, from these documents some will be handled in the portal, and some will be integrated? which are the actual documents in scope of the integration? • Locations on buyer and supplier that we have in scope 2. Define the roles and contacts involved (buyer and supplier) 3. Buyer SIFL has the responsibility to Review and agree/commit the supplier to project scope, timeline and start moment 4. Discuss about the testing approach as per Business requirements and business cases 5. Agree on the regular calls 6. Agree on the next steps 7. At the end of the call buyer and supplier need to be crystal clear and completely in sync on the business scope, the integration scope, the portal scope, the change management and timelines -- 4 of 6 -- 5 Buyer SCC SE KO Call OPTIONAL SCC SI INTRO session Buyer SCC - SI KO call SCC SI Supplier KO call What should be the next step? The next step should be: • Buyer team to allocate necessary resources SAP SCC SI organizes the separate Buyer SI KO call Please note that it does happen often that Buyers do not follow/ respond/restart discussions after such an Intro call. From experience/lessons learned we have noticed that buyers requesting Intro calls (information calls) are not really interested in suppliers, are not in a position to allocate resources, do not have budgets/internal buy in or have other situations that prevent them to commit/start a seller integration at that moment in time. The next steps should be: • Buyer SIFL and SCC SI agree on following regular sessions to review in details SCC methodology and best practices, Buyer Scoping file, SCC SI guidelines creation, Please note that it is possible to Buyer will change the buyer resources and there will be a need to repeat the buyer KO call session multiple times The next steps should be: • Buyer SIFL should set in place the regular project management calls • SCC SI usually agrees with the supplier on the technical call or calls • It is possible that sometimes SCC SI has one technical intro with the supplier team prior to the o call – just to give a macro image on the cXML and HTTPS connection for example. Owner/ organizer NxL/DE - usually informs SCC SI manager of the interest of the buyer NxL/DE usually facilitate the session – this may vary per case SCC SI will drive the presentation / session and provide notes NxL/DE - usually informs SCC SI manager of the interest of the buyer NxL/DE may facilitate the session or just introduce the SCC SI to the buyer team/resources – this may vary per case SCC SI will drive the presentation/session and provide notes Buyer SIFL will drive the call and take notes – as per RACI mentioned in the SCC Deployment Description Buyer SIFL should inform the SCC SI prior to the call and provide the Scoping file agreed with the supplier -- 5 of 6 -- 6 Buyer SCC SE KO Call OPTIONAL SCC SI INTRO session Buyer SCC - SI KO call SCC SI Supplier KO call Mandatory participant resources Buyer resources: Technical, business, decision makers, Buyer Service provider SAP SBN resource: SI and the NDL/DE optional CSM and COE according to each case Note: the SCC SI is not necessarily the same resource that will actually take over the project. At this moment in time the Buyer is not yet committed to the SI part, so we allocate a resource that is available for a one-time session Buyer Resource: SIFL Optional: Buyer technical, business, decision makers, Buyer Service provider SBN SCC SI resource: SCC SI and the NDL/DE Optional: CSM and COE according to each case Buyer SIFL and supplier team are mandatory in the call. Buyer Resource: Buyer SIFL, also Buyer Business resources are often a part of the call. Supplier Resource: Supplier Business and technical resources are required. SBN SCC SI resource: SBN SCC SI in charge of the specific supplier Best practices SCC SI should discuss prior to the call with the NDL/DE/COE to get a better understanding of the background of the project SCC SI should discuss prior to the call with the NDL/DE/COE to get a better understanding of the background of the project, what are the targets/ Business case/ SCC scope / points of interest of the buyer, etc. If needed SCC SI and NDL should work on a strategy to highlight different aspects as needed (for example if the NDL knows that the buyer does not have resources/compliance message, this should be a point that will need to be insisted on) We have also noticed that in some cases, providing the slides prior to the call and as part of the invite, helps the buyer team to prepare or already have the notes/information available As a general best practice, we recommend a technical call with the supplier before the ko call. This will prepare the supplier and keep the focus of the ko call on business and project organization rather than on technical aspects. A good collaboration with the buyer SIFL resource to ensure clarity on the next supplier and their scope/situation is always a critical success key Recommend buyer to suggest recording the session so that both supplier and buyer have a clear history of the discussions -- 6 of 6 --

Business Network Buyer Administration Guide This guide describes how buyers can administer their SAP Business Network accounts. Use this guide to: • • • • • • • • • • Configure settings for your SAP Business Network account, such as default transaction rules. Manage suppliers by creating supplier groups. Generate reports of your SAP Business Network account's activity. Manage users and roles. Download and view supplier customer catalogs. Search and view network catalog products. Manage payment and discount processing for the SAP Ariba Payables solution. View incoming and outgoing documents. Manage SAP Business Network subscription services. Learn about the SAP Business Network technical infrastructure. This guide applies to: • • SAP Business Network SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Related Guides SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide 12 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers SAP Business Network is a hosted service that enables buying organizations and suppliers to form relationships and conduct transactions over the Internet. Buying organizations use SAP Business Network to find suppliers from which they want to purchase products or services and invite suppliers to form trading relationships. After the supplier accepts the invitation, the buying organization can look at the supplier’s customer catalogs and place orders. Buyers can also easily search for suppliers and their products on the network catalog irrespective of the trading relationship between buyer and supplier. Suppliers receive the orders and return invoices. As a buying organization, you can do the following on SAP Business Network: • Search for or invite suppliers that have the products and services you need to form trading partnerships (see Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network). • • Send orders and receive invoices [page 417]. Run reports [page 226] on your suppliers. How Buyers and Suppliers Connect [page 13] SAP Business Network Benefits at a Glance [page 17] Supplier Interactions [page 17] Understanding the Order Life Cycle [page 19] Account Administrator Responsibilities [page 21] Getting Started with the SAP Business Network User Interface for Buyers [page 22] How Buyers and Suppliers Connect This is the process to establish a business relationship between a buying organization and a supplier. 1. Buyer creates a vendor record and uploads the vendor details 2. Buyer navigates to Supplier enablement , Configure to customize the new template email body with a personalized invitation message 3. Buyer activates the template and invites the potential new supplier to enter into a business relationship. The template is pre-populated with the available vendor details such as the company address 4. Supplier receives the email invitation and clicks Get started 5. The supplier is redirected to the new registration landing page. SAP Business Network determines whether or not there is an existing user account or an existing supplier company account 6. The supplier user can view (and search for) existing accounts, use an existing account, or chose to create a new account SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers PUBLIC 13 7. In case the supplier choses to create a new account, they are redirected to a supplier registation form. The supplier is advized to fill out some more information such as provide product and categories, as well as to finalize the supplier profile 8. The supplier lands on the supplier portal Any supplier can register with SAP Business Network. However, a supplier can't obtain a fully-transactional account until at least one buying organization (a "sponsor") requests and approves a relationship with the supplier. There is only one template (Trading Relationship Request letter (SAP Business Network). This template should be activated by the buyer. If a buyer does not already have a logo in their Company Profile and does not add one before sending any business relationship request, suppliers will go to a registration landing page with no branding (No buyer brand logo / No SAP Brand logo) When a registered SAP Business Network buyer wants to initiate a business relationship with a supplier, the buyer activates and customizes the template mentioned above. The new template supports customization of the header logo, the invite body text, the company on the invite, and the contact on the invite. After customization the buyer can send the invitation email When buyers invite a supplier to collaborate and start a business relationship on SAP Business Network, suppliers are directed to a landing page. The landing page is the entry point for a supplier to establish a business relationship. From there potential suppliers can create a new SAP Business Networkaccount, use an existing account, or search for an existing account. SAP Business Network has a number of automated search and matching capabilities to surface existing accounts and avoid duplicate accounts creation When a supplier receives a business relationship email request from a buyer, a supplier can either create a new SAP Business Networkaccount, or use an existing SAP Business Network account. If a supplier is unsure how to proceed, there is a search function to determine if there is an existing SAP Business Network account that can be used. The search function uses an algorithm to show 20 results in a results table. If there is an existing user account, click Use this account. If there is an existing company account, click Contact administrator. This sends a message to the administrator to ask how to proceed and request a subuser account to be created. The search filters and the results table are optimized for ease of use and better understanding of the functionality. The initial search is the basic search. This provides three search filters: Company name, Corporate email / domain, and Country. Actions are: Search, Clear, and Cancel The advanced search adds four additional search filters: Tax/VAT ID , Ariba Network ID, DUNS number, and GLN (Global Location Number). You can return to the basic search window by clicking the Hide advanced Search link. Supplier Post Registration Experience • • The SAP Business Network user ID provides a sign in link allowing you to finish the registration process • Upon final email confirmation, you are asked to provide a last bit of information such as the product and services categories you provide and the ship to and service locations you support. This information helps you to be discovered by other potential customers and grow your business • Now the registration process is complete. You are redirected to the SAP Business Network supplier portal. 14 You can requests to resend the email in case you missed it or you want to change the email address used in the initial registration process PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers New Account Creation from the Landing Page Using the New Registration Form The registration form is integrated with the landing page. It supports the workflow outlined below: • • • Click on the link in the business relationship request email to launch the new landing page • • • Auto default the administrator user details Click the Create account button on the new landing page to launch the new registration form The registration form is auto-populated with the vendor information from the buyer. You can change it if necessary. Perform all field validations and country specific behavior Create the account and redirect the supplier to the supplier portal Automatch on the Landing Page Account auto match capabilities make it easy for invited suppliers to determine whether there is an existing SAP Business Network account for their company that they can use. This avoids having to search for an account or creating unnecessary duplicate accounts. The auto match function uses a ranking system using either the DUNS number and supplier email, the DUNS number, or an existing email. The DUNS number and email is based on vendor details from buyer's vendor master. If there is a match found, the supplier can then use this account to sign in by clicking the Use this account button. If the supplier is still not sure whether to use a matched account, they can contact the buyer administrator to inquire how to proceed by clicking the Contact administrator button. SAP SAP Business Network confirms whether or not the message was succesfully sent. Duplicate Acccount Check on the Registration Form There are automated checks for duplicate accounts on the SAP Business Network supplier registration form. There are two possible workflows for the duplicate check function as described below: Flow 1 1. A supplier receives an invitation email to establish a business relationship 2. The supplier clicks the Create Account button on the landing page which launches the registration form 3. The registration form is auto populated with vendor details available from the invitation 4. The supplier fills out any remaining fields on the registration form and enters the same email that was used in the invitation 5. The supplier submits the registration form 6. The check duplicate account process detects there is an existing account which is displayed on the screen 7. The supplier realizes there is an existing account and clicks the Use this account button to sign in Flow 2 1. A supplier receives an invitation email to establish a business relationship SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers PUBLIC 15 2. The supplier clicks the Create Account button on the landing page which launches the registration form 3. The registration form is auto populated with vendor details available from the invitation including the suppier's DUNS number 4. The supplier fills out any remaining fields on the registration form 5. The supplier submits the registration form 6. The check duplicate account process detects there is an existing account with the same DUNS number which is displayed on the screen 7. The supplier cannot proceed and must click the Contact administrator button. This triggers a message to the buyer's administrator asking on how to proceed 8. The supplier leaves the registration page and waits for further instructions to complete the registration process Address Validation on the Registration Form Address validation extends existing HCP/ICP address validations and all other country specific validations and behaviour on the registration form. It ensures that the company legal name and mandatory address fields are entered in valid Latin characters. Manage Multiple Buyer Entities During the Invite Process Some buying organizations like to have local entities to onboard suppliers. The From section of the invite letter and the landing page allows buyer user to specify a buyer entity at the vendor level. Note that the specified buying entity determines the company name, logo and address displayed to the user on the new registration experience. If no specific entity is provided, the details specified at the company profile level will be used. Configure a Buyer Contact per Vendor A supplier invited by a buyer to join SAP Business Network often does not know anything about SAP or SAP Business Network. They only know the buyer with whom they are already conducting business outside the SAP Business Network. As a buyer you can configure a buy-side contact(one contact) per vendor that is displayed both on the invite email and also the landing page. This instills confidence in the invited supplier that the invitation is coming from a trusted source and a contact that they can reach out to. 16 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers SAP Business Network Benefits at a Glance SAP Business Network offers the following benefits: • Business automation. SAP Business Network enables trading partners to automate part of their businesses, providing significant advantages. By processing transactions automatically on SAP Business Network, trading partners can speed order execution, increase accuracy, and reduce costs. • Easy supplier enablement. More than 4.6 million companies are already members of SAP Business Network, operating in nearly every country/region. You can easily search the list of suppliers to see which of yours are already enabled. Adding new suppliers is simple. You can invite new suppliers through several methods and you can even have SAP Ariba enable them for you. • Content distribution. You have access to validated customer catalogs from any supplier. You can manually download customer catalogs for inspection or subscribe to them so that you are notified of any future changes. • Access to contract prices. SAP Business Network allows buyers and suppliers to communicate content and pricing confidentially so that you can negotiate prearranged contract prices. Your suppliers are assured that no other buyers can see their prices. • Multi-protocol order routing. SAP Business Network automatically routes orders to suppliers through cXML (Commerce eXtensible Markup Language), email, fax, or EDI (Electronic Data Interchange). Suppliers specify their preferred order routing method, and SAP Business Network takes care of the format, protocol, and delivery details. • Order status tracking. You and your suppliers can track real-time status of your orders on SAP Business Network. Suppliers can set order status through order confirmations and ship notices. • Powerful invoicing. Suppliers can send you invoices, credit memos, and debit memos through SAP Business Network. They can use several methods to generate invoices, including an easy-to-use invoicing wizard. SAP Business Network routes invoices to you for reconciliation and payment. • Access to SAP Business Network Discovery. With the right permission, you can use your SAP Business Network user name and password to easily publish postings (formerly Public RFXs) on SAP Business Network Discovery. Anyone can search the SAP Business Network Discovery directory for suppliers. When you create a posting, you can direct SAP Business Network Discovery to automatically notify suppliers that provide the goods or services you seek, and you can invite any other suppliers you like. Supplier Interactions Suppliers register on SAP Business Network, configure their accounts, and store product and service content there. Buying organizations then download customer catalogs and use their procurement applications to generate orders. Procurement applications send purchase orders to SAP Business Network, which either stores them for suppliers to pick up or routes them to suppliers through one of several protocols. Suppliers can respond with order confirmations, ship notices, and invoices. Suppliers cannot see each other on SAP Business Network. They see neither the names nor the customer catalogs of other suppliers, so their business information and their relationships remain confidential. Buyers, however, can see the names and basic information of all suppliers on SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers PUBLIC 17 Supplier Order Routing Methods SAP Business Network allows you to see the order routing method that each supplier supports. Suppliers can use any of the following order routing methods, depending on their technical capabilities. Method Description Online SAP Business Network stores orders online. Suppliers must sign in and read them manually. Email SAP Business Network sends orders to the supplier’s email mailbox over the Internet. Fax SAP Business Network sends orders to the supplier’s fax machine. EDI SAP Business Network sends orders to the supplier’s EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) mailbox through a private VAN (Value Added Network). SAP Business Network supports both ANSI X12 and UN EDIFACT standards. cXML SAP Business Network sends orders as cXML (commerce eXtensible Markup Language) to the supplier’s website. XML (eXtensible Markup Language) is a standard for passing data between Internet applications. XML documents contain data in the form of tag/value pairs. XML has a structure similar to HTML (hypertext markup language), but Internet applications can extract and use data from XML documents more easily than from HTML. Supplier Subscriptions SAP Ariba subscriptions help suppliers to maximize the benefits of SAP Business Network for their business by providing added functionality and services tailored to their level of participation. Suppliers receive benefits based on their annual transaction volume. SAP Business Network calculates transaction service fees for each customer relationship based on the transaction volume and number of transactional documents. • Transaction volume is the total dollar value of either: • • • purchase orders (PO) and non-PO invoices, or invoices (both PO and non-PO) SAP Ariba distinguishes between PO invoices (invoices that have been generated from a purchase order issued through SAP Ariba) and non-PO invoices (invoices not associated with an SAP Ariba-managed purchase order) in order to ensure that fee calculations do not “double count” SAP Ariba-generated purchase order and invoice volumes. Document count is the number of purchase orders and all invoice documents (PO and non-PO invoices). Order confirmations, change orders, ship notices, ICS invoices (invoices sent from an invoice conversion service), and other documents are excluded from the document count, ensuring that suppliers can continue to transact these value-added transaction types at no additional cost. For more information on the different subscriptions and pricing by region, see the Supplier Subscription Overview Website 18 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers Suspended Supplier Accounts If your relationship with a supplier is chargeable, SAP Business Network can suspend your supplier’s ability to transact with you for one of the following reasons: • • The supplier fails to pay any required transaction service fees The supplier fails to replace an invalid credit card with a valid credit card for transaction service fees  Note Relationships below the total suspension threshold won’t be suspended unless there has been no payment during the last 12 months. Relationships with a $0 transaction service fee won’t be suspended. While a supplier’s account is suspended, they can't: • • • • Receive purchase orders sent to them through SAP Business Network Receive other incoming documents sent to them through SAP Business Network Send invoices or other outgoing documents to you Send new customer catalogs to you If you find a new supplier in a search and their account is suspended, you can’t establish a relationship with them. SAP Business Network shows suppliers with suspended accounts in the Suspended Relationships area of the Active Relationships page. You also see a message at the top of the supplier’s basic profile. Related Information Supplier Membership Status Reports [page 270] Viewing and Downloading a Supplier’s Basic Profile [page 166] Supplier Management [page 164] Supplier Contacts [page 214] Supplier Profile Reports [page 273] Supplier Membership Status Reports [page 270] Supplier Subscription Overview Understanding the Order Life Cycle During the life cycle of an order, buying organizations and suppliers communicate information about orders: 1. The supplier creates customer catalog files that describe products and services. 2. The supplier uploads the customer catalog files to SAP Business Network for validation. 3. The supplier publishes customer catalogs to specific customers. 4. SAP Business Network notifies buying organization by email that new customer catalogs are available. 5. Buying organizations download and approve customer catalogs for use with their procurement application. 6. Procurement application end users browse the customer catalogs for products and services and initiate purchase requisitions, which are routed through their organizations for approval. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers PUBLIC 19 7. Upon approval, the procurement application automatically sends purchase orders in cXML format to SAP Business Network. 8. SAP Business Network stores orders so that suppliers can view them in their account. Figure 1: Purchase Order Life Cycle All suppliers receive orders in their online accounts. However, they can also receive orders through a routing method. Related Information Supplier Customer Catalogs [page 340] SAP Business Network Documents [page 396] Invoice Conversion and PO Line Level Mapping If you subscribe to an SAP Ariba invoice conversion services (ICS) solution, and the service provider supports PO line level mapping rules, you can have SAP Business Network send a cXML copy of the PO to the service provider as a CopyRequest document. Copies of POs are sent for all types of POs (new, canceled, or changed). The Order History tab includes CopyRequest POs sent to service providers. 20 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: Related Information SAP Business Network Guide to Invoice Conversion Supply Chain Finance Capability You can unlock working capital by using supply chain finance, a tool that enables you to extend the payment terms and Days Payable Outstanding (DPO). The goal of supply chain finance is to optimize your accounts payable metrics, cash management, working capital, transaction costs, administration, and risk. On SAP Business Network, supply chain finance involves a third party financing organization connected to SAP Business Network that pays your supplier early at a discounted rate. The third party executes two separate agreements, one with you and one with your supplier. The agreement with you is a guarantee that you will pay the third party the full amount of the approved invoice at the term due date. The agreement with the supplier is a purchase agreement that transfers ownership of the supplier’s receivables to the third party when the early payment is settled. When the agreements are in place, the process works as follows: 1. You approve the invoices to pay and post them through SAP Business Network, which sends a copy to the third party provider. 2. The third party provider pays the supplier at the agreed upon discount rate. 3. You pay the third party provider the full amount of the invoice at the full term due date of the invoice. Related Information Ariba Working Capital Management Services datasheet Account Administrator Responsibilities One person in your organization acts as the account administrator. The administrator is responsible for: • • • Setting configuration options. See SAP Business Network Configuration [page 33]. (Optional) Adding additional users to the account. See SAP Business Network Users and Roles [page 293]. (Optional) Creating a test account for testing document flow with suppliers. See Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers PUBLIC 21 Getting Started with the SAP Business Network User Interface for Buyers The SAP Business Network application user interface for buyers has the following key components: 1. Home page [page 22]—The default page you see when you sign in to SAP Business Network. Click Home to access your home page from anywhere in the application. 2. Menu bar—Provides access to the various pages in the application. Some menus go directly to a page, while others provide a dropdown list of commands. The menu bar that you see may vary depending on your account’s entitlements. 3. Header bar—Provides helpful menus, commands, and information about you and your company. • Use the dropdown on the top-left corner of the header bar to switch between different SAP Ariba web applications. • Click the • Account Settings icon to choose one of the following commands from the dropdown: • ANID (Ariba Network ID)—A number that uniquely identifies your company on SAP Business Network. You might need this number to contact some support services. • • • • Switch to Test Account—Change from production to test account modes. • Settings—Access configurations for users and roles, self-service customization, the unit of measure master list, and your audit log. Also manage purge requests. • Logout—Exit SAP Business Network when you’re done with your session. Company Profile—Review and manage your company profile on SAP Business Network. Manage Services—Manage your SAP Business Network services. Manage Profile—Configure company settings such as locale settings, cXML settings, document routing preferences, system notifications, default transaction rules, country/region-based invoice rules, payment settings, application end points, and quote automation rules. Click the Help  icon to activate SAP Companion in-app help. 4. Search bar—Provides capabilities to search for trading partners and network catalog products on SAP Business Network. • • Trading partners search. See Searching for Trading Partners on SAP Business Network [page 335]. Discovery search. See Searching for Products in Network Catalog from Various Suppliers [page 338]. Figure 2: SAP Business Network User Interface for Buyers Home Page You can navigate back to the SAP Business Network home page by clicking Home on the menu bar. Depending on your permissions, the Home dashboard can display the following content items. Only the Alerts and Messages content item is not permission-based. 22 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers • Alerts and Messages. This content item displays important information about SAP Business Network, and reminders about your account. A yellow icon is shown for alerts that require your attention soon, and a red icon is shown for alerts that require your immediate attention. You can permanently delete any item that does not have an icon by clicking the trash can icon. • Shipment Tracking. See Tracking Shipments from the Home Dashboard [page 429]. Be sure to respond promptly to alerts in the Alerts and Messages content item. Overview Tile Bar The Overview tile bar displays the default tiles for your business role, or tiles that you have configured. On the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page, up to five tiles are displayed in the Overview tile bar by default. You can reveal an additional five tiles with the More button. You can also configure which tiles are displayed from the Workbench. For more information, see The Workbench [page 397] The Overview tiles are displayed intelligently: if one or more Pinned documents exist, that tile is displayed first. Otherwise, it is moved to the end of the order. Getting Started Tile Bar The Getting started tile bar offers you recommended tasks and information resources for first time users. The Getting started tile bar directs you to complete important configuration tasks for your account. For example, Update company profile, Upload company logo, or Upload vendors.  Note The tasks available to you depend on your permissions. Each Getting started tile includes an info icon that you can click to learn more about the task. You can mark Getting started tiles as complete to remove them from the tile bar. Marking a task complete increments the count on the Completed task tile. Click the Completed task tile to view tasks that were previously marked as complete, when, and by whom. Home Page Widgets Your Home page provides widgets to show at a glance current information for your business activities. The SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page displays role-based widgets. These widgets help you focus on important tasks, insights, key performance indicators, and benchmarks for your business. To customize the contents of your Home page, see Customizing Your Home Page Widgets. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers PUBLIC 23 Shipment Tracking Widget The Shipment tracking widget allows you to quickly track the status of shipments. Enter a purchase order number and click Track to view shipment status information. Purchase Orders Widget The Purchase Orders widget shows you the total value of purchase orders you have created in each month of the selected year. Data is displayed in your preferred currency. Click View all to view additional details on the Analytics dashboard. You must have the Analytics dashboard access permission and the analytics functionality must be activated to access the Analytics dashboard.  Note Purchase order and invoice amounts specified in non-USD currencies are converted to USD for the purpose of aggregation using the currency exchange rate at the time the transaction document is created. The aggregated amount is further converted to your user-specified currency for display in widgets. Therefore, you may see a difference between the original amounts displayed in the workbench and the aggregated amount displayed in widgets. Invoices Widget The Invoices widget shows you the total value of invoices you have received in each month of the selected year. Data is displayed in your preferred currency. Click View all to view additional details on the Analytics dashboard. You must have the Analytics dashboard access permission and the analytics functionality must be activated to access the Analytics dashboard. Delivery Execution Widget The Delivery execution widget displays the Perfect delivery, On time delivery, and In full delivery key performance indicators (KPIs) for your entire supply chain in the previous month. The KPIs are calculated by the underlying Delivery execution analytics story. You can click View all to view the full story in the Analytics dashboard. The KPIs are defined as follows: • 24 Perfect delivery: The percent of items delivered on time and in full, calculated by dividing the total count of line items delivered on time and in full by the total count of line items evaluated. PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers • On time delivery: The percent of items delivered on time, calculated by dividing the total count of line items delivered on time by the total count of line items evaluated. • In full delivery: The percent of items delivered in full, calculated by dividing the total count of line items delivered in full by the total count of line items evaluated. To view the widget, you must be enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. You must have the Analytics dashboard access permission and the analytics functionality must be activated to access the Analytics dashboard. Supplier Enablement Widgets The Enablement summary, Full enablement progress, and Light enablement progress widgets enable you to quickly check the real-time enablement progress for your potential suppliers that are planning to use either an enterprise account or a standard account. To view the widgets, you must have at least one of the following permissions assigned to your account: Supplier Enablement Configuration, Supplier Enablement Program Administrator, Supplier Enablement Report Administration, or Supplier Enablement Task Management For more information, see Supplier Enablement Widgets. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network for Buyers PUBLIC 25 Your Company Profile The buyer company profile on SAP Business Network provides information about your company and its business. You can review and manage information in the Company Profile to help suppliers learn about your company. Your Company Profile page consists of the following sections: Section Description Quick navigation pane Use the navigation pane on the left side of the Company Profile page to upload your company logo, jump to Contacts, or return to the Overview. Company Information An overview of your company information is displayed at the top of your profile. You can edit details such as the company name, website, DUNS number, number of employees, year founded, annual revenue, legal form, address, and business type. Categories, Locations, and Industries The data for Product and Service Categories and Receiving Locations are retrieved from your SAP Business Network Discovery activities and cannot be edited. You can specify Industries for your company. Marketing Collateral You can enhance your profile by adding marketing collateral in the form of attachments or external links. This helps suppliers learn more about your company. Activity Data Your activity data is displayed to provide transparency into your SAP Business Network Discovery posting history and build trust. Buyers with the Company Information permission can click the edit icon  beside each editable section to edit the information contained in the section. The  Options menu in the upper-right corner includes commands for viewing your public profile, obtaining a public profile URL, and setting profile visibility. Editing Your Company Profile [page 27] Uploading Your Company Logo [page 28] Editing the Main Contact [page 29] Showing or Hiding Your Company Profile in Discovery Postings [page 30] Profile Data Federation [page 30] 26 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile Editing Your Company Profile You can enter or revise information about your company so that suppliers can identify the company and contact you. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Company Profile . This opens the Company Profile page. 2. Click the edit icon  for the section that you want to edit information, enter or revise values as needed, and save your changes. Note the following constraints and guidelines: • • • • DUNS Number—A nine-digit number issued by Dun & Bradstreet, Inc. to identify each corporate location of an organization. You can obtain a DUNS number or look up your company’s existing number on Dun & Bradstreet’s website, https://www.dnb.com . Number of Employees—The approximate number of people who work for your organization. Year Founded—Enter the year in yyyy format. Revenue—Select a currency range. If you prefer not to state your annual revenue, scroll to the bottom of the list and select Contact company for information. • Legal Form—Choose the type of business entity or legal status of your company from the dropdown. The list of values varies per country/region. • • • Business Type—Check the business types that apply to your company. Industries—Select the industries your company serves. Marketing Collateral—Click Add marketing collateral. Choose Attachment to attach any files you want to make available to suppliers, such as customer presentations, case studies, and certifications. Choose External link to enter a URL and a description for each additional site. You must preface URLs with “https://”. For example: https://www.Your-Company.com/service. 3. If you want to share more details about your transaction requirements with trading partners, choose Account Settings and Information. Manage Profile . Then on the Configuration page, choose Extended Profile Settings a. Fill out the questions with the information you want to share with your suppliers. You do not need to answer all questions. Your suppliers will be able to see only the completed questions. b. Click Save. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile PUBLIC 27 Related Information Uploading Your Company Logo [page 28] Editing the Main Contact Uploading Your Company Logo SAP Business Network can display your organization’s logo on fax, email, and online Inbox purchase orders. Prerequisites Before uploading your logo, ensure the following: • You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. • Your logo file meets these requirements: • • • • Format: GIF (static only; no animation) Maximum size: 200 KB Dimensions: Up to 250 × 250 pixels Background: Remove any excess area surrounding your logo. Context You might want to add your logo so suppliers can tell who the customer is at a glance. Logos also appear on all emails and faxes sent to suppliers registering through the supplier enablement method. Logos do not appear on cXML or EDI orders. Your test account and production account each use their own logo. You might want to create a logo for your test account that clearly indicates that the orders are test orders. You cannot configure different logos to display to your suppliers. To save an existing logo on your computer, right-click it and select Save As in your web browser. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click your user initials at the top right of the home page and choose Company Profile from the menu. 3. Click the  (Edit company logo) icon in the top-left corner of the page. 28 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile 4. In the Upload Company Logo dialog box, click Browse to select your logo file. 5. Click Open to preview the logo. 6. Click Save to apply your changes. Your logo is updated immediately. Editing the Main Contact The main company contact represents the general contact information for your organization, including key details such as email, phone, and fax. Prerequisites You have the Company Information permission. If you're not an admin user, contact your account administrator to request access. Context By default, the main company contact is set to the account creator (administrator). However, you can update this information at any time to reflect your company’s most appropriate general contact. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click your user initials at the top right of the home page and choose Company Profile from the menu. 3. Click the Contacts tab. 4. In the Main Company Contact section, click Edit. 5. Update Email, Phone, Fax of your company as needed and click Save. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile PUBLIC 29 Showing or Hiding Your Company Profile in Discovery Postings When you create a public posting on SAP Business Network Discovery, your company profile information is by default visible to suppliers. If you want to prevent suppliers from viewing your company profile information, use this procedure to hide it. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Context Showing your company profile in postings can help potential suppliers feel more comfortable with doing business with your organization, resulting in increased responses to your posting. Although you can choose to hide your company profile information, SAP recommends that you show it. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Company Profile . 2. In the upper-right corner of the Company Profile page, choose the  Options menu, and the Profile settings command. 3. Toggle the Make my profile visible to supplier in postings option as needed. Profile Data Federation This feature enables your company profile data to be replicated across SAP Business Network's global data centers, making your profile visible to trading partners in different regions. For more information, refer to How Profile Data Federation Works [page 31] and Enabling Profile Data Federation. 30 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile
