file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: How Profile Data Federation Works Profile data federation replicates your company profile data across all global data centers of SAP Business Network, enabling trading partners in different regions to find and view your company profile, thereby facilitating potential business opportunities. To understand how profile data federation works, consider two trading partners located in diﬀerent regions: • • Trading Partner A is based in the United States (US) data center. Trading Partner B is based in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) data center. For Trading Partner B to view Trading Partner A’s profile, Trading Partner A’s profile data must be replicated from the US data center to the KSA data center. To make this happen, Trading Partner A must enable profile data federation. For details about how to enable profile data federation, refer to Enabling Profile Data Federation. Once enabled, an initial replication synchronizes your company profile data across all global data centers of SAP Business Network. Future updates are automatically synchronized to ensure your profile remains consistent and up to date across all data centers.  Note Profile data federation is only available to companies that are not sole proprietors. Enabling Profile Data Federation Profile data federation allows your company profile to be visible across all global data centers of SAP Business Network. This makes it possible for trading partners in different regions to view your company profile, facilitating potential business opportunities. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Company Profile. This opens the Company Profile page. 3. Click the Options menu in the upper-right corner of your profile and select Profile settings. 4. On the Profile Settings page, locate the section labeled Search Results Visibility, and toggle Replicate to global regions of SAP Business Network to enable profile data federation. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile PUBLIC 31 This setting determines whether your profile data will be replicated to other data centers of SAP Business Network. Once enabled, this setting cannot be reversed. 5. Click Save to confirm your settings. Results • • 32 Your company profile will be replicated and visible across all data centers of SAP Business Network. Future updates to your profile will be automatically synchronized globally. PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Your Company Profile SAP Business Network Configuration On the Configuration page of your SAP Business Network account, you can review and update company settings such as contact information, locale settings, cXML settings, document routing preferences, system notifications, default transaction rules, country/region-based invoice rules, payment settings, application end points, and quote automation rules. To see the Configuration page, choose Account settings Manage Profile . The options available on the Configuration page depend on the features that have been enabled for your SAP Business Network account.  Note For additional configuration instructions related to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, see the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide. Timezone and Currency Settings [page 34] cXML Setup [page 35] Configure Your SAP Business Network Account to Access SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network [page 38] Notifications for Buyers [page 40] Data Deletion Criteria for Buyers [page 44] Default Transaction Rules [page 53] Currency Precision and Rounding [page 107] Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules [page 110] External Tax Invoice Rules [page 120] Using Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) Payment [page 122] Catalog Validation Preferences [page 123] Document Number Preferences for Invoices and Service Sheets [page 125] Supplier Profiles and Other Supplier Customizations [page 130] Link Multiple Business Applications [page 133] End Points Integration [page 135] Configuring the End Point URL to Access the Catalog Content Management System (CMS) [page 144] Quote Automation Rules [page 145] Tracking and Auditing Transaction Rule, Group Membership, and Other Account Configuration Changes [page 147] Audit Logs for Buyers [page 151] Audit Log Management on SAP Business Network on BTP [page 152] Unit of Measure Data for Your Account [page 155] Activating the Analytics Functionality in Your SAP Business Network Buyer Account [page 158] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 33 Setting Default Decimal and Digit Group Separators for Peru [page 159] Timezone and Currency Settings In the Locale Settings area, you can set the following options: • Preferred Timezone controls how SAP Business Network displays dates and times on purchase orders routed by fax or email. Date and time stamps are displayed as GMT (Greenwich Mean Time) +/-. • Default Currency is the currency that SAP Business Network uses for all entered and displayed monetary amounts in your account. These settings affect how SAP Business Network displays date/time stamps and currency to all account users. Users cannot see these settings—only the Administrator can see and change the timezone and default currency.  Note The currency that SAP Business Network uses in the Manage Services area of your account is controlled by your organization’s location, which you specify in Account settings Manage Profile Company Profile . Updating Locale Settings You can set the timezone and currency for your account. To convert from GMT (Greenwich Mean Time) to your local time, go to http://www.timezoneconverter.com . Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Locale Settings. The Locale Settings page appears. 34 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Figure 3: Locale Settings Page 3. Choose a timezone from the Preferred Timezone list. 4. Choose a currency from the Default Currency list. 5. Click Save. Changes take effect for users at the next sign in. cXML Setup Several SAP Ariba applications, both on premise and cloud, communicate with SAP Business Network over the Internet using cXML (commerce eXtensible Markup Language). To enable this communication, you specify an authentication method and the profile URL of your application. Authentication Method For secure access, all cXML applications authenticate cXML documents they receive. This authentication ensures that the documents are legitimate because they were sent from recognized organizations. You can choose shared secret authentication or digital certificate authentication. Profile and PunchIn URLs Ariba Buyer on premise and Ariba Sourcing on premise support the cXML Profile transaction. You need to specify these URLs only if you use Ariba Buyer with the collaboration site, or Ariba Sourcing with the Public RFX feature. SAP Business Network uses the cXML Profile transaction to check the capabilities of Ariba Buyer and Ariba Sourcing and the URLs of services they offer. SAP Business Network sends a ProfileRequest when it needs to send a cXML document, but not more than once in 24 hours. Ariba Buyer and Ariba Sourcing respond with a ProfileResponse, which SAP Business Network caches. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 35 SAP Business Network uses the cXML Profile transaction immediately before it sends a ProviderSetupRequest document to initiate a PunchIn session with Ariba Buyer or Ariba Sourcing. PunchIn sessions are initiated by suppliers in the following situations: Target Application PunchIn Initiated By Ariba Buyer Suppliers generating invoices from contracts Suppliers responding to collaboration requests Ariba Sourcing Suppliers inquiring about public RFX events Document Download Your application can optionally download documents from SAP Business Network: Document Can Be Downloaded By Order Confirmations Ariba Buyer, SAP Business Network adapter, SAP Ariba Buying solutions Ship Notices Ariba Buyer, SAP Business Network adapter, SAP Ariba Buying solutions Invoices Ariba Buyer, SAP Business Network adapter, SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, SAP Ariba Invoice Management Status Update Requests Ariba Buyer, SAP Business Network adapter Payment Schedules SAP Business Network adapter When these documents are downloaded into your application, you can use the data within them, such as using invoice data to reconcile orders. SAP Ariba Support controls whether your SAP Business Network account can download some or all of these documents. To request to have this feature activated for your account, click Help Help Center Support Center . Fill out the SAP Business Network Email Support Form. Indicate which documents you want to download. You can request to download each document type separately. As a best practice, enable this feature first with your test accounts and thoroughly test the process before enabling the feature with your production accounts. For more information, see Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network. When SAP Ariba Support activates this feature, SAP Business Network queues some or all of the following cXML documents for downloading by your application: ConfirmationRequest, ShipNoticeRequest, InvoiceDetailRequest, or StatusUpdateRequest. Note that if you use Ariba Buyer and request a status update, the status is “ordering.” When you download the StatusUpdateRequest, the status changes to “ordered.” 36 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Configuring cXML Setup To enable communication between your SAP Business Network account and Ariba Buyer, SAP Ariba Sourcing, and applications that use the SAP Business Network Adapter, you must specify cXML (commerce eXtensible Markup Language) options. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the cXML Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose cXML Setup. The cXML Setup page appears. Figure 4: cXML Setup Page 3. In the Authentication Method section, choose the authentication method from the dropdown: • Shared Secret. (Default) You enter a confidential text string as your shared secret. The shared secret is used to authenticate all cXML transactions between your organization and SAP Business Network. If you change your shared secret, you must also make the same change in your cXML-enabled application. If the values do not match, your documents cannot be delivered. To change your shared secret, you must enter the current value in the Current Shared Secret text box. If you forget your shared secret, SAP Business Network Customer Support must reset it. Choose Contact Support from the Help menu, and in the Support page set Category of Issue to “Reset Shared Secret” and click Submit. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 37 • Certificate. You purchase and maintain a digital certificate signed by a trusted certificate authority. Paste the signed client certificate into the Certificate text box. Your website and SAP Business Network use this certificate for cXML authentication. You can also uses the backup certificate if your primary certificate becomes invalid. Backup certificates are useful when your primary certificate expires or when you need to perform certificate maintenance. Digital certificates require more setup steps, they cost money, and they expire over time. However, they might be more compatible with your organization’s security strategy.You can also use a backup digital certificate. For a list of SAP Business Network’s trusted certificate authorities, see the cXML Solutions Guide. 4. In the Profile URL and Public RFX PunchIn URL sections, do one of the following: • If you use Ariba Buyer with contract collaboration, SAP Ariba Sourcing to create SAP Business Network Discovery postings, or SAP Business Network Adapter, enter the externally accessible URL of your SAP Ariba application or SAP Business Network Adapter application in the Profile URL section. Specify a URL with an https prefix so communication is encrypted. For example: https://procure.bigbuyer.com:443/Buyer/cxmlchannel Click Reset Profile to clear your cXML profile cached on SAP Business Network. The next time SAP Business Network needs to send you a cXML document, it gets your cXML profile instead of using the cached profile, which can be up to 24 hours old. This function is helpful when developing support for the Profile transaction. • If you use both Ariba Buyer with contract collaboration and SAP Ariba Sourcing with the Public RFX feature, enter your Ariba Buyer cXML channel URL in the Profile URL section and your SAP Ariba Sourcing cXML channel URL in the Public RFX PunchIn URL section. Specify a URL with an https prefix so communication is encrypted. For example: https://yourdomain.com/Sourcing/CXMLChannelServlet 5. Click Save. Configure Your SAP Business Network Account to Access SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Buyers using SAP Business Network can send and receive transaction documents using the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. As a buyer administrator, you can set up the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network to send and receive transaction documents to SAP Business Network. You need to assign roles and permissions for users to access the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network.  Note You can use the trusted certificate authorities (CA) listed in SAP Note 2801396 for your connection to SAP Business Network. Your certificate must be from one of the authorities in the SAP Note, as SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network does not support loading any new certificate authorities. 38 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Related Information Enabling the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network on SAP Business Network Signing into the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Assigning User Permissions for the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network Switching to the US Data Center of SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network for Existing SAP Business Network Buyers SAP Business Network Users and Roles [page 293] Audit Logs Audit logs for switching data centers and enabling or disabling SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network routing in SAP Business Network • Entries are added to the audit log when a user enables or disables SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network routing in SAP Business Network. • Entries are added to the audit log when a user switches between SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network data centers in SAP Business Network. • • Only SAP Business Network users with administrator or viewer privileges can view the audit log entries. Audit logs for test and production accounts are separate and independent of each other. The following are the functional features: When users switch data centers and enable or disable SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network routing, these comments are entered in the SAP Business Network audit log. Table 1: Audit Log Operations and Comments Operation Comments in the Audit Log Description User enables SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network routing X Data Center was enabled for SAP Ariba X is the default data center for selected location Cloud Integration Gateway SSO to SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway X Data Center was enabled User disables SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network routing X Data Center was disabled for SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway SSO to SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway X Data Center was disabled User switches between SAP Inte- X Data Center was disabled for SAP Ariba gration Suite, managed gateway Cloud Integration Gateway for spend management and SAP SSO to SAP Ariba Cloud Integration GateBusiness Network data centers way X Data Center was disabled SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration X is the currently configured data center PUBLIC 39 Operation Comments in the Audit Log Description Y Data Center was enabled for SAP Ariba Y is the new data center that the user switches to Cloud Integration Gateway SSO to SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway Y Data Center was enabled Viewing Audit Log Entries How to view audit log entries • • To view the audit log information go to Settings Audit Log . To generate the audit log in PDF format click the Export to PDF button. Notifications for Buyers You specify which notifications you want to receive to stay informed about different events and activities that affect your SAP Business Network account. You can use notifications to monitor account activity, such as customer catalog updates, and to resolve issues related to your account. Notifications are triggered by events that occur on SAP Business Network. For example, you can choose to be notified by email whenever an invoice is received or updated. SAP Business Network sends notifications to two places: on SAP Business Network, and to the specified email addresses for a particular notification type. Only notifications related to transaction documents (for example, purchase orders, order confirmations, ship notices, and invoices) are delivered on SAP Business Network. You can view them on the Quick links Notifications tab.  Note To update notification email addresses for your SAP Ariba subscriptions, click the then click Manage Services to go to the My Services area of your account. Account Settings icon, Unsubscribing to Notifications When a user unsubscribes from a notification by clicking the Unsubscribe link in the email, SAP Business Network sends a notification to inform the account administrator of the request to unsubscribe and provides the email address involved. The administrator then fulfills the request, removing the email address from the notification subscription. 40 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: Entering Email Addresses for Notifications Use notifications to monitor account activity, such as customer catalog updates, and to resolve issues related to your account. By default, all notifications are sent to your administrator’s email address. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Notifications. The Notifications page appears. Figure 5: Notifications Page 3. Enter up to three email addresses per notification type. Use a comma between addresses. For example: joe@brass.com,john@esm.com,mark@sfs.com  Tip To send one notification type to more than three email addresses, create a distribution list in your email system and enter the name of that distribution list in the appropriate field on the Notifications page. 4. Check the box for each notification type you want to receive. 5. Click Save. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 41 Notification Types for Buyers Describes notification types for SAP Business Network buyers. Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Order An order is undeliverable, a supplier has updated an order’s status, or a supplier has generated an order confirmation or a ship notice. If you request a notification when a supplier updates the status of an order, SAP Business Network sends an email to the order requester, not to the email address specified for the notification. You can also include all line item details from the status update in the notification. SAP Business Network also sends an email to the order requester when a supplier acknowledges the order. By default, this option is enabled. If you do not want the order requester to receive a notification when the order is acknowledged, clear the check box for “Send a notification to the requester on the order when the order status changes.” Service Sheet A supplier has sent a new or updated service sheet. Data Identification and Deletion Transaction documents have been identified for deletion, or they have been deleted. Current Transaction Download Requested transaction documents are ready for download. Invoice An invoice has arrived or been updated by a supplier. If you subscribe to an invoice conversion service, you can also receive notification when an unassigned invoice is waiting for you. An unassigned invoice is an invoice on which the supplier does not match any of the suppliers with which the buying organization has a trading relationship. For information about working with unassigned invoices, see the SAP Business Network Guide to Invoice Conversion. Duplicate Invoice A supplier sends you multiple invoices with the same amount and date. SAP Business Network excludes rejected, invalid, and canceled invoices when checking for duplicates. Invoice An unregistered supplier creates a non-PO invoice that includes your customer code. You can accept or reject the invoice. If you accept it, the supplier’s account changes to production mode. This is called Invoice Quick Enablement. Time Sheet A time sheet is undeliverable. Request for Quotations A request for quotations is undeliverable. Quotes Quotes are undeliverable. RFQ Failure An RFQ failed. Purchase Requisition Request A purchase requisition is undeliverable. Payment Remittance A remittance advice is undeliverable. Payment Remittance Status Updates A remittance status has changed to Paid or Failed. You have the option of receiving only notifications of Paid status or only notifications of Failed status. 42 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Catalog Service A supplier publishes, updates, or removes a customer catalog to which you have subscribed. Order Confirmation An order confirmation is rejected. Supplier A supplier you invited has registered on SAP Business Network or a supplier with which you already have a relationship has changed their routing methods. Supplier-Initiated Relationships A supplier requested a trading relationship with you. Network Service SAP Business Network has a planned or unplanned downtime or an upcoming software release. Pending Queue You have documents in your account that SAP Business Network has not been able to download to you for more than three days. SAP Business Network sends an email notification titled “Documents Delivery Delay” that lists the unacknowledged documents in an email attachment. See Re-Queuing Documents Automatically Using Batch Document Resend [page 440]. Supplier Payment Proposal A supplier sends you a payment proposal. Payment Proposal A payment proposal is undeliverable. Payment Cash Limit Used cash amount is approaching configured payment cash limit. Certification Expiration Supplier certification information has expired. Examples of company certifications include Small and Disadvantaged Business, Minority-Owned Business, and VeteranOwned Business. Certification Supplier certification information has changed. Transport A transport confirmation is received. Other Notifications SAP Business Network sends other important notifications that do not belong to any of the specified notification categories, to the email address specified here.  Note SAP Business Network sends all other important notifications to the email address you specify here. You cannot clear the check box to stop receiving these notifications. Related Information Notification Types for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 43 Data Deletion Criteria for Buyers On the Configuration page, the administrator for your SAP Business Network account and other users with appropriate permission can specify the retention period for transaction documents. Additionally, SAP Business Network automatically deletes buyer master data after a period of inactivity following contract termination. You may need to delete old transaction documents to satisfy regulatory needs in your country/region or business requirements in your organization. If you request recurring deletion of transaction data, any transaction document sets older than the retention period are subject to deletion every month. Each document set includes transaction documents and any associated attachments. You can also request one-time deletion of transaction data. This operation is similar, but happens only once, not every month. For example, you can delete your transaction data older than January 1, 2018.  Note If a buyer account is deleted from the SAP Business Network, the posted RFx transactions get automatically deleted. Suppliers associated with the deleted RFx now can't view any of the deleted RFx transactions. Types of Transaction Documents That Can Be Deleted The following transaction documents can be deleted: • • • • • • • • • • • 44 Purchase orders (orders and blanket orders) Order confirmations Ship notices Receipts Service sheets Invoices, credit memos, and debit memos Payment documents SAP Business Network for Supply Chain transaction documents Notifications Quote requests and quote messages Associated attachments PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Workflow for Deleting Transaction Documents The following diagram shows the workflow for deleting transaction documents from SAP Business Network: Figure 6: Workflow for Deleting Transaction Documents from SAP Business Network  Note SAP Ariba retains transaction data for a reasonable time after the 30-day grace period. About Transaction Document Sets Each transaction document is part of a larger transaction document set, a sequence of related documents sent between the buyer and supplier (for example, purchase order, order confirmation, ship notice, receipt, invoice, and so on). Buyers and suppliers maintain their own data retention period. When all documents in a particular set are older than the specified data retention period, only then are they ready to be deleted. If any document in a set isn't older than the data retention period, the entire set is retained. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 45 Figure 7: Transaction Document Set For example, say that your company retains transaction documents for 36 months. A purchase order was created 60 months ago. However, an invoice associated with the purchase order was created only 30 months ago. Since the document set (the purchase order and invoice) isn't older than the retention period of 36 months, both the purchase order and the invoice are retained, not deleted. Documents are identified for deletion according to the data retention period that you specify (for example, 18 months). The age of a document is based on its creation date or the date of its last status update, whichever is later. On the first day of each month, the system finds any document sets older than the data retention period. If all documents in a particular set are older than the data retention period, that set is identified for deletion. The identified set is queued for deletion and deleted within 1 month after being identified. When the system deletes a document, it’s deleted permanently; it can’t be restored. You can’t perform any operations against deleted documents (for example, searching).  Note Documents that have been identified for deletion can still be searched until they're deleted. Data Deletion Restrictions • • • • 46 This feature doesn't affect archived invoices, which are stored separately. Once a document has been identified for deletion, it’s deleted regardless if you later opt out of data deletion. Please carefully configure the retention period for transaction documents. Deletion of transaction documents is an irreversible process. You can’t retrieve any transaction documents after they're deleted by the system. If you're using long-term archiving services, we strongly recommend that you specify a retention period for transaction documents that is greater than or equal to the longest archiving retention period legally required by countries/regions where you operate. If the system deletes your invoices, you can't search for those invoices in SAP Business Network. Your archived invoices, however, continue to be retained by TrustWeaver or Sovos (third-party systems that SAP Business Network uses to archive invoices) for the full legal retention period. PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Data Deletion Notifications You can enable the following notifications for data deletion: Notification Type Notifications Data Identification and Deletion • Send a notification when the transaction documents have been identified for deletion • Send a notification after deletion of transactions Automatic Deletion of Master Data for Inactive Buyer Accounts Buyer accounts and their data are automatically deleted when their contract with SAP Ariba is terminated.  Note Accounts that have used archiving services at any time are not subject to the automatic deletion of master data due to inactivity; the account is expired but the master data is maintained.  Note Buyers who only use SAP Business Network Discovery are considered inactive after 3 years of inactivity. When a buyer account's contract with SAP Ariba is terminated, the account status becomes Expired and SAP Business Network sends a notification to the buyer account administrator. The buyer account administrator can request reactivation of their account at this time. After 60 days of expiry, if the account has not been reactivated, the buyer account and all of its data is permanently deleted. Account deletion is irreversable.  Note When a buyer account is deleted, they're still visible to their suppliers with the identifier Deleted by SAP Ariba, and suppliers can still access transactions involving the deleted buyer. No company is able to perform new transactions with a deleted buyer. When the buyer and all its related suppliers are deleted, all remaining retained data is permanently deleted. To download a ZIP file, go to the Action column and click the  Download icon.  Tip You can filter the table of ZIP files to show files for which download has not yet started. 52 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Default Transaction Rules SAP Business Network default transaction rules control how suppliers submit transaction documents that meet the buyer’s content requirements. Buyers must ensure that documents comply with their processes and procedures. With invoice documents, buyers and suppliers must ensure that documents are tax-compliant and align with country/region-specific rules. If the documents are not compliant, buyers and suppliers alike can have costly and lengthy exception handling. When configuring business rules on the SAP Business Network, buyers can reduce exceptions and ensure that documents are compliant by identifying problems before documents are sent to the buyer’s back-end system. Suppliers can address and resolve issues before their customers receive the document.  Note SAP Business Network applies the rules to the documents in the native language, cXML. Documents not initially created in this format are translated into cXML first, then the rules are applied. If the documents comply with the buyer's rules, the documents are sent to the buyer in real-time through the integration methods specific to that buyer. The rules may then be applied to transactions entered manually by suppliers on the SAP Business Network portal and to those automatically integrated into the network. For documents entered on the SAP Business Network portal, the transaction rules are applied when the documents are created. If there are errors or incomplete information, the user cannot move to the next stage to submit the document to the buyer. For integrated documents, the rules are applied after the documents are received and processed. The network sends the relevant error messages as notifications on the SAP Business Network portal and the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network if the supplier investigates the document's status. To ensure consistency, the configured transaction rules must be identical in the buyer’s SAP Business Network account in both Test and Production. Buyers can configure default transaction rules on the Default Transaction Rules page in their SAP Business Network account ( Account settings Manage Profile override them for specific suppliers and supplier groups. Default Transaction Rules ). However, they can In the case of invoices, buyers can also override the invoice rules for the country/region from which the invoice is sent. For more information, go to Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules [page 110]. Rule Categories  Note For additional default transaction rule information related to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, see the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 53 The Default Transaction Rules page has rules grouped in the following categories: • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • Payment Batch Transmission Rules [page 56] Purchase Order Rules [page 57] Blanket Purchase Order Rules [page 60] Scheduling Agreement Release Setup Rules [page 61] Ariba Buyer Contracts Site Setup Rules [page 62] Attachment Rules [page 63] Quick Enablement of SAP Business Network Suppliers [page 64] Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules [page 65] Service Sheet Rules [page 84] Invoice Rules [page 91] Invoice Archiving [page 93] Long-Term Archiving of Tax Invoices [page 98] Sales Order Rule [page 101] D-U-N-S Number Rule [page 101] Work Order Information [page 101] Quality Collaboration Rules [page 104] Allow vs. Require Rules Generally, there are two types of transaction rules: • Allow rules—When these rules are checked, suppliers have the option to enter values per rule setting or not. If these rules are not checked, the rule behavior is enforced. • Require rules—When these rules are checked, the buyer mandates that the supplier provides certain information on the document. When these rules are not checked, suppliers have the option to leave that information blank. • Other rules—There are some rules that don’t start with Allow or Require, but that are processed as Require rules. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the Transaction Configuration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Default Transaction Rules. The Default Transaction Rules page appears. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 55 Figure 11: Default Transaction Rules Page 3. In each section of the Default Transaction Rules page, specify rules that either require or allow suppliers to include specific kinds of information on transaction documents. 4. Click Save. Payment Batch Transmission Rules Payment batch transmission rules allow you to choose whether your payment batches are immediately sent for processing or held until the daily cut-off time. SAP Business Network offers one payment batch transmission configuration option: Hold payments until the daily cut-off time. By holding payment batches until the daily cut-off time, you can cancel an entire payment batch or individual payments within a payment batch before the processing day cut-off time. If you choose to hold payment batches until the daily cut-off time, you can still force the transmission of a pyament at any time. You can generate a daily report containing information about all the payments canceled that day. The Cancelled Payment Transactions report is sent as a CSV file attachment in an email notification at the end of each day. When deciding whether or not to hold payment batches until the daily cut-off time, consider the following: • If you hold payment batches until the daily cut-off time, payment batches will be transmitted to the payment provider after the daily cut-off time. • If you submit a payment batch after the daily cut-off time, the payment will be transmitted after the cut-off time of the following day. • If you set a payment batch to process at a future date, and that date is a holiday, the payment will be transmitted after the cut-off time of the day following the holiday. • The projected settlement date for SAP Ariba Payables payments is based on the transmission date of the payment and the processing time of the payment provider. 56 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Purchase Order Rules By default, SAP Business Network doesn't accept change orders or cancel orders for orders that suppliers have updated to Shipped status. You can override this behavior so your organization can send change and cancel orders for partially shipped or fully shipped orders. Override the following default purchase order rules. Check this rule to override default rules for purchase orders. These rules do not affect scheduling agreement releases. When this rule is checked, you can override the following rules: • • • • • • • • • Allow change orders for fully shipped orders. Allow change orders for partially shipped orders. Retain confirmation status for unchanged line items on change orders. Enable ship notice tracking on change orders. Allow change orders in invoice aggregation. Allow cancel orders for fully shipped orders. Allow cancel orders for partially shipped orders. Override supplier's routing method for orders that match buyer's conditions. Check this rule to let buyers submit change orders for fully shipped orders. Default setting: No Allow change orders for partially shipped orders. Check this rule to let buyers submit change orders for partially shipped orders. Default setting: No Retain confirmation status for unchanged line items on change orders. This rule applies only if you have allowed suppliers to send order confirmations on the line item level. If this rule is checked, the confirmation status of unchanged line items on a previous order is retained on a subsequent change SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 57 order. If this rule is unchecked, the confirmation status of items on a previous order is not retained on a subsequent change order. The following purchase order fields are evaluated for changes: Section Line Items Schedule Lines Field • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • Quantity Requested Delivery Date Unit Price Supplier Part ID Auxiliary Part Number Estimated Delivery Date Description Unit of Measure Price Basis Quantity (Price Unit, Unit Conversion, and Price Unit Quantity) Ship Date Buyer Part Number Manufacturer Part ID Manufacturer Name [Schedule line added] [Schedule line removed] Quantity Requested Delivery Date Unit of Measure When this rule is checked, the confirmation status is also retained for any line item that has a rejected quantity (full or partial). For suppliers who are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, this rule when checked applies only to purchase order confirmations. This rule does not apply to confirmations of scheduling agreements or scheduling agreement releases, which SAP Business Network for Supply Chain supports. Instead, previous confirmation of unchanged line items is always retained in scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases, except in the following cases: • If a schedule line is dropped from the new version, the confirmation for the dropped schedule line is not retained. • When the quantity of a schedule line changes in the new version, the confirmation for that schedule line is not retained, and the supplier needs to reconfirm that schedule line.  Note There's one exception to this case. When the quantity of a schedule line changes in the new version, the confirmation for that schedule line is retained if there's a confirmation status that matches the schedule line's quantity and date. When a schedule line has more than one confirmation status related to it, the system matches one of the confirmation statuses to the new schedule line. To match, both the quantity and the delivery date must be the same. Default setting: No 58 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Enable ship notice tracking on change orders. Such orders include purchase orders, change orders, scheduling agreements, scheduling agreement releases, or blanket orders. If all of the following information in a new order is the same as in an existing order, this rule rejects the new order as a duplicate: • • • • • • Buyer ANID Supplier ANID System ID Order number Order version Order type When SAP Business Network rejects a duplicate order, the buyer receives a status message that the document was rejected as a duplicate. The message provides the reason for rejection, and includes certain information from the duplicate order, such as the order ID, payload ID, and supplier ANID.  Note • • This rule does not remove existing duplicate orders. Scheduling Agreement Release Setup Rules You can configure these transaction rules for scheduling agreement releases, which define the quantities and dates for the shipments desired for a specific item. Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration. Check this rule to allow this account to share scheduling agreement release documents with suppliers. Default setting: No When this rule is checked, the following rules appear: Allow suppliers to use only JIT for shipping. For suppliers that have both JIT (Just In Time) and Forecast release capability, choose this option to restrict suppliers to using JIT for shipping. Allow suppliers to use only Forecast for shipping. For suppliers that have both JIT (Just In Time) and Forecast release capability, choose this option to restrict suppliers to using Forecast for shipping. Scheduling Agreement Release Concepts Buyers often want to procure pre-defined quantities of materials in releases to be received on pre-determined dates. For example, a buyer might order 100 items, but want them delivered 10 items at a time on a weekly basis. A buyer would, in this case, send a scheduling agreement release to a supplier. A scheduling agreement release can have multiple schedule lines for any single line in a purchase order or other business document. A single schedule line contains fields for delivery date and time, and for scheduled quantity and unit of measure. Buyers create schedule agreement releases with external ERP systems. Suppliers can view scheduling agreement releases in the SAP Business Network user interface. Buyers can periodically communicate releases to their suppliers, and suppliers can create ship notices for materials requested through a scheduling agreement release. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 61  Restriction Scheduling agreement releases do not support order confirmations. The processing of non-scheduled items is not affected by scheduling agreement relases. Ariba Buyer Contracts Site Setup Rules If you use Ariba Buyer 8.1 or later or an SAP Ariba cloud solution, you can allow suppliers to access your contracts site to create invoices against contracts (master agreements) or bids for service line items. Allow suppliers to access your Ariba procurement applications for collaborative invoicing, requisitioning, managing time and expense sheets, and creating service sheets. Check this rule to let suppliers access their contracts (master agreements) on your contract compliance site. Default setting: No Contracts are agreements between trading partners to exchange services for payment over a period of time. Suppliers can create invoices for some types of blanket purchase orders, such as supplier-, commodity-, and customer catalog-level BPOs, only by accessing your contracts site. The process of enabling suppliers to access your contracts site for collaborative invoicing or requisitioning includes the following steps: 1. Configure your cXML setup [page 35], which requires you to change your shared secret. Make the same change to the cXML shared secret in your SAP Ariba procurement application. 2. Enable all suppliers or individual suppliers to sign in to your contracts site.  Restriction You cannot use contract collaboration if you use certificate-based authentication. SAP Ariba cloud procurement applications use only shared secret authentication. You can override this option for specific suppliers. See Overriding Your Rules and Preferences for a Supplier [page 201]. 62 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Attachment Rules You can configure several types of transaction rules for attachments. Attachment File Extension Rules Choose one of the following options: Allow all attachment file extensions. Suppliers can upload attachments from the user interface with any file extension, except executable file extensions. Default setting: Yes Allow these file extensions only. Suppliers are only allowed to upload or send attachments with the specified list of file extensions. Enter a commaseparated list of file extensions using alphanumeric characters only. Do not allow these file extensions. Suppliers are not allowed to upload or send attachments with the specified list of file extensions. Enter a commaseparated list of file extensions using alphanumeric characters only.  Note Executable file extensions are automatically disallowed. Attachment Filename Rule By default, all characters are allowed in the filenames of attachments. You can disallow certain characters in the filenames of attachments, particularly if an external system does not allow certain characters. Do not allow these characters in filename of attachments. Check this rule to prevent suppliers from uploading an attachment with the specified characters in the filenames. Default setting: No  Note The maximum number of disallowed characters you can specify is 25. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 63 Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Attachment Rules You can check the following rules to allow suppliers to include attachments with orders confirmations and ship notices: Allow suppliers to include attachments with order confirmations. Check this rule to allow suppliers to attach files to order confirmations. Default setting: No Allow suppliers to include attachments with ship notices. Check this rule to allow suppliers to attach files to ship notices. Default setting: No For both order confirmation and ship notices attachments, you can leave attachments online or send URLs for them: Leave attachments online. Check this rule to route attachments to your online account. Uncheck it to view attachments in SAP Business Network. If you can't uncheck this rule, then your account does not allow you to download order confirmations or ship notices to SAP Business Network. Contact SAP Ariba Customer Support for assistance. Default setting: Yes Send URLs to view attachments on Ariba Network. This option is available if you are an SAP Business Network Adapter customer. Check this rule to include a URL to open the attachment on SAP Business Network. Default setting: No Quick Enablement of SAP Business Network Suppliers SAP Business Network supports multiple supplier enablement methods for establishing trading relationships with suppliers. These methods allow you to create new SAP Business Network accounts on behalf of suppliers. The quick enablement setting allows you to initiate trading relationships and create new SAP Business Network accounts on behalf of suppliers through purchase orders, payment proposals, CC invoices (invoices sent from the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions or the ERP system), ICS invoices (invoices sent from an invoice conversion service provider), and requests for quotation. If you want to receive non-PO invoices from suppliers that don't have an SAP Business Network account, you can generate a customer code for them. Before you receive a non-PO invoice from an unregistered supplier, you must provide your unique customer code to the supplier. You can provide your customer code in an email, over the phone, or by fax. The quick enablement setting and the invoicing rule Allow suppliers to send invoices to this account are required for you to generate the customer code. 64 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Related Information Supplier Enablement Process [page 164] Non-PO Invoices [page 420] Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules You can configure these transaction rules for order confirmations and ship notices.  Note Estimated shipping and delivery dates are attributes of the cXML itemOut element. Therefore, any estimated shipping and delivery date, even when defined at the header level, is applied at the line-item level without consideration of any transaction rules that prevent suppliers from editing line items. To prevent suppliers from editing estimated shipping and delivery dates, you must request a customization project to hide the Est. Shipping Date and Est. Delivery Date fields in order confirmations. Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders When this rule is checked, your suppliers can send order confirmations for material orders to you. To restrict your suppliers from sending you order confirmations for material orders, click to clear this rule setting. You can also specify this rule for your supplier groups.  Note When you change the default setting and clear this rule, SAP Business Network automatically unchecks the Require suppliers to create an order confirmation for the PO before creating an invoice rule. Default setting: Yes Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the line-item level When this rule is checked, SAP Business Network allows your suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the line-item level or at the header level. If you don't check this rule, your suppliers can only confirm or reject the entire order. Since SAP Business Network doesn’t match between accumulated service sheets and partial order confirmations for an order, SAP Ariba recommends that you uncheck this rule for suppliers who fulfill service orders so that they have to confirm or reject the entire order and then create service sheets to accumulate against it. Default setting: Yes SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 65 Allow suppliers to reject quantities for material orders at the line-item level in order confirmations This rule is available only when the following two rules are first checked: • • Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders. Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the line item level. (This rule is visible only after Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders is enabled.) This rule has three options: • • • No – Prevents suppliers from rejecting quantities at the line-item level. Partially – Allows suppliers to reject partial quantities at the line-item level. Fully – Allows suppliers to fully reject the line item. Partial rejections aren't allowed. When Fully is selected for this rule, suppliers can still partially confirm a line item that was fully rejected in a previous order confirmation. When an order is for material items only and the Allow suppliers to reject quantities for material orders at the line-item level in order confirmations rule is unchecked, suppliers can't reject an entire order. For orders containing material items only, the rule must be checked for the Reject Entire Order button to be enabled in SAP Ariba pages that create an order confirmation. If an order is for services, or a mixture of service and material items, this rule doesn't apply, and suppliers can reject an entire order, whether the rule is checked or not. Buyers can have a notification email sent to them automatically when a supplier rejects or partially rejects a quantity in an order confirmation, or when they reject an entire order. The order confirmation details are included in the email body. Default setting: Partially Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for service orders When this rule is checked, your suppliers can send order confirmations for service orders to you. To restrict your suppliers from sending you order confirmations for service orders, click to clear this rule setting. You can also specify this rule for your supplier groups. Default setting: Yes Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for service orders at the line-item level When this rule is checked, SAP Business Network allows your suppliers to send order confirmations for service orders at the line-item level or at the header level. If you don't check this rule, your suppliers can only confirm or reject the entire order. Since SAP Business Network doesn’t match between accumulated service sheets and partial order confirmations for an order, SAP Ariba recommends that you uncheck this rule for suppliers who fulfill service orders so that they have to confirm or reject the entire order and then create service sheets to accumulate against it. Default setting: Yes 66 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Allow suppliers to confirm an order multiple times The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release. This rule has the following options: • • Yes No – Allows suppliers to confirm the order only once, for the entire order. Suppliers can't confirm the order at the line-item level. • Confirm only once at line-item level. – Available when No is first checked. Allows suppliers to confirm the order only once, either for the entire order or at the line-item level. This rule applies to material orders and service orders independently. If you don't check this rule, your suppliers can only confirm the entire purchase order once. For your suppliers to reconfirm an order when this rule is turned OFF, you must send a changed order to the supplier. If the rule Retain confirmation status for unchanged line items on change orders is also enabled, and a supplier receives a new version of an order and the order status is not Confirmed, Backordered, or Rejected, the supplier can create an order confirmation. In that new order confirmation, the supplier can change previously confirmed items that kept their confirmation status. Default setting: blank (disabled) Send suppliers an automatic reminder of unconfirmed orders after a specified number of days. Sends suppliers up to three automatic reminders for orders that are unconfirmed after the specified number of days from the order date. To send reminders, enter a number from 1 to 10. At the beginning of every week, SAP Business Network sends to the primary email address for your account a report of unconfirmed orders that have generated these notifications within the last 30 days. This rule doesn't apply to scheduling agreement and scheduling agreement release confirmation. Default setting: blank (disabled) Send suppliers an automatic reminder for non-shipped items a specified number of days before the delivery date. Sends suppliers up to three automatic reminders for purchase order items that haven't been shipped a specified number of days before the delivery date. To send reminders, enter a number from 3 to 10. SAP Business Network sends to the primary email address for your account a report of non-shipped purchase order items that have generated these notifications within the last 30 days. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 67 Send suppliers an automatic reminder for non-received items a specified number of days after the delivery date. Sends suppliers up to three automatic reminders for purchase order items that haven't been received a specified number of days after the delivery date. To send reminders, enter a number from 1 to 10. At the beginning of every week, SAP Business Network sends a report of non-received purchase order items that have generated these notifications within the last 30 days to the primary email address for your account. Default setting: blank (disabled) Require suppliers to fully confirm line items before fulfillment. The order confirmation can be for a purchase order, scheduling agreement, or scheduling agreement release. When this rule is checked, it enables a subrule called Check Delivery Date. • Check the Check Delivery Date subrule to evaluate whether the supplier’s delivery or completion date for a line item matches the buyer’s need-by date from the order. If the dates are different, the line item isn't considered fully confirmed. When this rule is enabled with the subrule Check Delivery Date, a supplier can't create a service entry sheet or invoice from an order confirmation that has the status Confirmed With New Date or Confirmed With Changes. • Uncheck this subrule to not consider the delivery date when evaluating whether a line item is fully confirmed. For scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases, this rule is only applied to Firm schedule lines. • Only confirmation statuses against Firm schedule lines need to be different from Confirmed With Changes or Confirmed With New Date. • The overall confirmed quantity for Firm schedule lines needs to be equal to or greater than the item’s quantity. Default setting: No Require suppliers to create an order confirmation before creating a ship notice. When this rule is checked, your suppliers are required to submit an order confirmation against a purchase order before sending a ship notice. Default setting: Yes Allow suppliers to send ship notices to this account. When this rule is checked, your suppliers can send you ship notices. To restrict your suppliers from sending you ship notices, click to clear this rule setting. You can also specify this rule for your supplier groups. 68 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration  Note When this rule is unchecked, SAP Business Network automatically unchecks the rules Require suppliers to create a ship notice for the PO before creating an invoice and Require suppliers to include only shipped quantities on invoices. Default setting: Yes Require delivery dates for order confirmations and ship notices. When this rule is checked, your suppliers must provide delivery dates on order confirmations and ship notices. The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release.  Note This rule is not enforced for unplanned lean-service items or material items in an order confirmation. Default setting: No Require an estimated shipping date on order confirmations. When this rule is checked, your suppliers must specify estimated shipping dates when changing order confirmation line items. The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release. Default setting: No Require an actual or estimated shipping date on ship notices. When this rule is checked, your suppliers must specify an actual or estimated date on ship notices. Default setting: No Require ship notice type on ship notices. Ship notices that lack a type aren't allowed. For the type, the supplier must choose either actual or estimated. Default setting: No SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 69 Allow suppliers to add delivery and transport information to ship notices. When this rule is checked, your suppliers can add the delivery and transport information to a ship notice when the order doesn't contain this information. Default setting: No Require all items in a ship notice to have the same transport terms value. When this rule is checked, your suppliers must use the same transport terms value for all line items of a ship notice. Default setting: No Allow suppliers to send non-PO ship notices through cXML. When this rule is checked, your suppliers can send non-PO ship notices through cXML. Default setting: No Allow zero-quantity line items in ship notices sent through cXML. When this rule is checked, your suppliers can add zero-quantity line items in ship notices sent through cXML. Default setting: No Allow multiple orders and scheduling agreement releases in ship notices. When this rule is checked, your suppliers can include multiple orders and scheduling agreement releases in ship notices. Default setting: No Require suppliers to provide a unique asset serial number for each purchase order line item on a ship notice. When this rule is checked, suppliers that maintain asset serial numbers must provide a unique asset serial number for each PO line item on a ship notice. If a supplier doesn't maintain asset serial numbers, this rule doesn't apply. Default setting: No 70 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration
