Configure a guided buying end point for your buying solution from SAP Ariba. See Configuring the Guided Buying Endpoint. Related Information Default Transaction Rules [page 53] Configuring the End Point URL to Access the Catalog Content Management System (CMS) If you use the content management system (CMS) to manage customer catalogs in your procurement application, then you must configure the end point URL of your data center to enable the flow of customer catalog data from SAP Business Network to your procurement application. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Content Management System (CMS) Settings. 3. In the End Point URL section, enter the URL of your data center. 144 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration 4. Click Save to save your changes. Quote Automation Rules You can configure rules for Request for Quote (RFQ) postings in SAP Business Network Discovery. You can configure rules to specify which suppliers are invited to RFQ postings based on the product and service categories in those events. For example, you can configure a rule to specify that if commodities in the Chemicals category are specified in the RFQ posting, only vendors in your approved vendor database are invited, and if commodities in the Office Suppliers and Printing category are specified, all public SAP Business Network suppliers are invited. You can also configure a default supplier matching rule for any category that might not have a rule. By default, SAP Business Network Discovery matches commodities with approved vendors. SAP Business Network applies these rules to an RFQ posting if the SupplierSelector element in the QuoteRequest document does not include the matchingType attribute. Therefore, you can choose to do one of the following: • Include the matchingType element in the QuoteRequest document that is sent to SAP Business Network; SAP Business Network uses the specified matching type for the RFQ posting as a whole. Any configured quote automation rules are ignored. • Remove the matchingType attribute before the QuoteRequest document is sent to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network applies the quote automation rules to the commodities in the RFQ postings and selects an appropriate matching type for the event as a whole. Configure quote automation rules from the Quote Automation page by choosing Profile Account settings Manage Quote Automation . Configuring Supplier Invitation Rules [page 145] Configuring the Supplier Invitation Default Rule [page 146] Deleting a Supplier Invitation Rule [page 147] Configuring Supplier Invitation Rules You can configure category-specific supplier invitation rules for RFQ postings. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 145 Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Quote Automation. 3. Click Quote Automation Rules. 4. Click the Browse link provided beside the Product or Service Category text box. The Product and Service Category Selection page is displayed. 5. Add all the product or service categories for which you want to create a rule, and then click OK. 6. Click Create Rule. A rule is created for each category that you selected. The rules are listed in the Categories table. By default, the rules are set to All Suppliers. 7. In the Categories table, in the Matched Suppliers column, for each category that you added, set the supplier matching type that you prefer. 8. Click Save. Related Information Quote Automation Rules [page 145] Configuring the Supplier Invitation Default Rule You can configure the category-specific supplier invitation default rule for RFQ postings. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Quote Automation. 3. Click Quote Automation Rules. 4. In the Configure Quote Request Flow section, from the Default Rule drop-down menu, choose the matching type that you want to apply to categories for which a supplier category matching rule is not configured. 5. Click Save. 146 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Related Information Quote Automation Rules [page 145] Deleting a Supplier Invitation Rule You can delete a category-specific supplier invitation rule for RFQ postings. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Quote Automation. 3. Click Quote Automation Rules. 4. In the Categories table, in the row that displays the rule that you want to delete, click Delete. 5. Click Save. Related Information Quote Automation Rules [page 145] Tracking and Auditing Transaction Rule, Group Membership, and Other Account Configuration Changes You can use the Intelligent Configuration Manager to track and audit the changes that users make to your accounting settings configuration. Transaction rules are subjected to changes based on the buyer requirements and the different transaction scenarios. Changes to the transaction rules settings impact the existing buyer configuration and can result in document validation and processing errors. Auditing and tracking of the transaction rules enable buyers to track the changes applied to the various sets of the transaction rules in their SAP Business Network account. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 147 There are three levels of transaction rules you can track: • • • Default transaction rules Country/region-based invoice rules Supplier group transaction rules Buyers can also track and audit when users • • • • create a new supplier group add suppliers to a supplier group remove suppliers from a suppler group deactivate a supplier group Searching for Changes to Account Settings You can use the Intelligent Configuration Manager to search for recent changes to your account settings. Prerequisites You must be assigned the Administrator role. Context You can search for data about various events, impacted applications, and actions and operations taken within the last 90 days. Procedure 1. Click the account settings icon and choose Settings Audit Log . 2. On the Events tab, reveal More options, choose your Search filters as desired, then click Apply. Results The Search results table is displayed. 148 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Creating a New Audit Report to Track Changes to Account Settings You can use the Intelligent Configuration Manager to create reports that help you audit changes to your account settings. Prerequisites You must be assigned the Administrator role. Context You can generate reports on up to 3 years worth of data about various events, impacted applications, and actions and operations taken. Procedure 1. Click the account settings icon and choose Settings Audit Log . 2. Click the Reports tab. 3. In the bottom right corner, click Create report. 4. Enter a Report name, optionally enter a Description, click More options to expand the available filters, then configure the Search filters as desired. 5. Click Generate report. It may take several minutes to generate the report. 6. When the Audit reports table appears, click Download for the report you just created If the Audit reports table does not appear after several minutes, you can refresh the page and then search for the report you just created using the Search filters. Results Your report downloads as a ZIP file that contains a CSV.GZ file that contains the report CSV. The report displays information such as TIME, USER, ACTION, and old and new values. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 149 Example To generate a report for changes to your account's default transaction rules, configure the following: Filter Selection Event type Data modification From Any date To Any date within 3 years of your From date Action Update Operation DefaultRules You can replace the DefaultRules Operation with SupplierGroupRules or CountryBasedRules to generate reports for changes to those rule categories instead. Generate a report without Event type, Action, or Operation to view more potential report parameters. Searching for Audit Reports You can search for audit reports that you've previously created with the Intelligent Configuration Manager. Prerequisites You must be assigned the Administrator role. Context You can generate reports on up to 3 years worth of data. Procedure 1. Click the account settings icon and choose Settings Audit Log . 2. Click the Reports tab. 3. Choose Search filters as desired, then click Apply. 150 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration

Click Download to download a ZIP file that contains the audit report. Purging Audit Logs Customer administrators can use the Intelligent Configuration Manager workspace to purge audit log data older than a specified date or configure recurring data purges based on the retention policy in your site. For more information, see Data Purge Capabilities in Intelligent Configuration Manager in the Intelligent Configuration Manager Administration guide. Audit Logs for Buyers You can access classic and standard audit logs. To view audit logs, click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings. Under Audit Log, choose Classic for the legacy audit log or Standard for the Intelligent Configuration Manager audit log. These are the available classic audit logs: • • • • Transaction Rule Changes – This log tracks changes to default transaction rules. Supplier Group Membership Changes – This log tracks changes to supplier groups. Profile Changes – This log tracks changes to user profiles. User Access – This log tracks user access activity, which includes the number of failed access attempts since the last successful sign in and their reasons.  Note This log can be exported to a PDF file with a maximum of 500 records. If you need additional records, change the search criteria to filter for a specific time period, user, or other field. • Currency Preference Changes – This log tracks changes to currency preferences. For more information about the standard audit log, see Managing SAP Ariba Audit Information. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 151 Audit Log Management on SAP Business Network on BTP Business Details The SAP Business Network audit service, logs selected user and administration actions performed in SAP Business Network applications. It also logs user interface audit actions like create, download, purge, or delete audit reports. The audit actions are divided into the following categories: • • Generic audit actions - purge, delete and download audit reports Inegrated audit actions - create audit reports For more information about audit logs for buyers, see Audit Logs for Buyers [page 151]. For more information about audit logs for suppliers, see Audit Logs for Suppliers. The SAP Business Network on BTP audit service enables administrators and security personnel to take a detailed look at what occurs in their SAP Business Network site, reproduce potential malicious activities of users and administrators, monitor administrative activities, like configuration changes, and retrieve forensic evidence if a security breach occurs. The SAP Business Network audit service records activities and events relevant for security auditing. You can access audit service records for evaluation in the form of security audit reports. In legacy SAP Business Network Audit Classic is where you can view the audit logs. In SAP Business Network on BTP, all audit logs are now written to BTP and retrieved from BTP. The main difference of audit between SAP Business Network on BTP and legacy SAP Business Network is that in legacy SAP Business Network the audit events were generated in a synchronous manner, providing a real-time view of the audit trail. Whereas in SAP Business Network on BTP you first need to create an audit repor, download it to view them. To view audit logs, click Compliance section. Account Settings Settings and then choose Audit Log Standard from the Implementation Details General Prerequisites Ensure that the user have the following permissions to access audit logs: • • User Administration Audit Log Administration Business End User Tasks The SAP Business Network audit service log entries contain identifying information, such as user, event type, date, and time. When users change data, the SAP Business Network audit service records both the old and new value. The SAP Business Network audit service creates a log entry when a user, integration tool, or scheduled event performs the following actions: 152 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration • • • • • • Changes a user's authorization Exports or downloads data Creates, edits, or deletes data Authenticates a user Changes system configuration Accesses or changes sensitive information The SAP Business Network audit service also records user consent to privacy policies, including the version number of the policy and whether the policy was a custom privacy policy or the SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Privacy Statement. For information about the types of actions recorded by the SAP Business Network audit service, refer to Audit Log Criteria for SAP Business Network. Audit Events and Reports The Audit events and reports page is where you view the list of audit reports that are created. The audit log report has filters for filtering the reports. Creating an Audit Report Follow these steps to create an audit report: 1. Click Create. 2. The Create Audit Report page displays the following fields: Fields Description Name This is a mandatory field. Enter a name for the report. Event type This is a mandatory field. Choose the type of logged audit events for which you want to create a report. For example, choose Security to view security critical events. Choose Data access to view data access related activities. The available event types are: • • • • • • Security Data access Data modification Configuration modification Generic action Integration From This is a mandatory field. Choose the start date for the events. You can choose a valid date (within the last 3 months) using the calendar tool. To Choose the end date for the events. You can choose a valid date (within the last 3 months) using the calendar tool. 3. Click Create to create an audit report with the specified name. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 153 Viewing the List of Audit Reports The Audit Events and reports page displays the list of reports that have been generated. In this page, you can use the search filters to look for a particular report, download a report, or delete a report. Search a report User the search filters to search for a report. The available fields are: • • • Name Event Type Status After entering the required search criteria, click Apply to search for audit reports based on the search filters. Click Clear to clear the search filter fields. The Audit Reports Log section shows all generated reports. Each row in the table displays information for the generated report such as name of the report, who created it, when it was created, type of the event, and the status. The following table explains the statuses that appear on the Status column. Status Description PROCESSING Indicates that the report creation is in progress. COMPLETED Indicates that the report is successfully generated and can be downloaded. An email is sent to the user when the report is generated. FAILED Indicates that the report generation has failed. An email notification is sent to the user when the report generation fails. PURGE SCHEDULED Indicates that the report will be purged. An email notification is sent to the user one day before the report is automatically purged. From the day the notification is sent to the user and till the report is purged, the report will be in purged scheduled status. There is no retention period for the purged report. PURGED Indicates that the report has been purged. SAP Business Network purges the generated report after 30 days. A reminder email is sent to the user one day before the actual purge. If the user wishes to download the report can do so. The status of the report is changed to Purged scheduled. The purged reports are permanently deleted and there is no retention period. Audit Reports The Audit Report Logs section lists all generated reports. • • Click Download to download the generated report in XLS format. Click Delete to delete a generated report.  Note If a user offboards from SAP Business Network, all the associated audit reports are deleted automatically. • 154 Click Create to create a new audit report. PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Audit Event Types The following table describes the types of events: Event Type Description Security Security-related events for discovery and analysis of security critical incidents. For example, server start or stop, failed sign-in attempts, failed authorization checks, critical system parameter changes, and so on. Data access Data access-related events, such as successful and unsuccessful attempts to access personal identifiable data and confidential data, access to different services or applications, read access of confidential data, and so on. Data modification Personal data modification events and auditing reasons. This includes personal and confidential data updates, changes to group membership, or contact information. Configuration modification Administrative actions and events in your site and all configuration modifications. Generic action Actions generated or occurring in the system, such as: • • Integration Actions that transfer data to or from the system. For example, file uploads or downloads. Scheduled integration tasks. Actions related to integration events such as data import and export, inbound or outbound API calls, and events related to configuration files. Unit of Measure Data for Your Account You can use the unit of measure CSV template to define the unit of measure codes that you use in your business, as well as provide additional information such as the symbol, name, and description for each code. Unit of measure codes can be based on ISO or UN/CEFACT standards, or they can be any arbitrary codes defined by your company. If unit of measure codes are company-specific, it's important to provide additional information about the codes to suppliers so they can understand what the codes mean in purchase orders and other SAP Business Network documents. The unit of measure CSV template has the following four header rows at the top of the template: • • • • Row 1: Character encoding (for example, 8859_1). Row 2: Field names (Code, Name, Symbol, and Description). Row 3: Whether the field is required or optional. Row 4: Data type and maximum length (for example, "String 100"). The first three fields in the template, Code, Name, and Symbol, are required. The Description field is optional. The fields can be rearranged in any order as long as the field names are not changed.  Note If there is no symbol for a code, we recommend that you repeat the Code value in the Symbol field. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 155 The following table shows an example of unit of measure information that you can add to the CSV template: Code Name Symbol Description 2N dB decibel decibel 2P kbyte kilobyte kilobyte 2Q kBq kilobecquerel kilobecquerel 2R kCi kilocurie kilocurie DZN dozen DOZ dozen PK pack PK pack TP ten pack TP ten pack Language Support The unit of measure master list supports multiple languages. Fill in the template in a separate CSV file for each locale. To activate a master list, upload strings for at least the English locale. Downloading the Unit of Measure Template You can download a CSV template to populate it with unit of measure codes to upload to your SAP Business Network account. To support different locales, save a different version of the file for each locale. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . The Master List page appears. 156 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Figure 17: Master List Page 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Download template, and save the file to your computer. Uploading Unit of Measure Data You can use the unit of measure CSV template to upload additional unit of measure information to your account for use in SAP Business Network documents. Prerequisites • • You are assigned the Administrator role. Fill in the CSV template with information about unit of measure information codes for one or more locales. To activate the list in your account, upload strings for at least the English locale. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Upload or download master list. 3. For the locale of the CSV file you are uploading, click Upload. 4. Click Browse to select a CSV file, and then click Upload. 5. Repeat steps 3 [page 157] and 4 [page 157] for other locales, as needed.  Note To verify the data you uploaded, click Download. 6. Click Done. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 157 Enabling or Disabling Unit of Measure Codes You can disable and enable unit of measure codes that you uploaded to your account. If you disable a unit of measure code, suppliers can't find it anymore in the application, although they can still enter it. Prerequisites • • You are assigned the Administrator role. Before you can enable or disable unit of measure codes, you must first upload them to your account. When you upload unit of measure codes, they are enabled by default.  Restriction Once you upload a unit of measure code to your account, you cannot delete it. However, you can update the Name, Symbol, and Description fields for a unit of measure code. Procedure 1. Choose Settings Master List . 2. For the Unit of Measure master list, click Enable or disable codes. The Enable or disable unit of measure codes page appears. 3. Select Code or Name from the list. 4. Type the start of a code or name, and then click Search. 5. Select one or more codes. 6. Click Enable to enable the selected codes, or click Disable to disable them. 7. Click Done. Activating the Analytics Functionality in Your SAP Business Network Buyer Account You activate the analytics functionality in your SAP Business Network buyer account from the Configuration page. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. 158 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Analytics Configuration. 3. Click Submit to configure and activate the analytics functionality. If the operation fails, click Retry. You can retry the operation for a maximum of 4 times. Contact SAP Ariba Customer Suppor for help if the operation fails after the maximum number of tries. Setting Default Decimal and Digit Group Separators for Peru SAP Business Network buyers whose addresses are set to Peru can set default decimal and digit group separators. For some locales, including Spanish-Peru, the default Web browser setting is to use the comma (,) as a decimal separator and the dot (.) as a digit grouping separator. This can lead to errors on SAP Business Network in locales that actually use the dot as a decimal separator and the comma as a digit group separator. As a buyer, you can set default decimal and digit group separators in SAP Business Network that override the defaults that apply to your preferred browser in your locale. These defaults can be set by administrators to be applied at organization level or at individual user level. Preferences set at individual user level override those set at the organization level. Separator preferences are reflected in all fields that use separators in SAP Business Network reports. Enabling This Feature This feature is disabled by default. To enable this feature, please have your Designated Support Contact log a service request. An SAP Ariba Support representative will follow up to complete the request. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 159 Setting Default Decimal and Digit Group Separators at Organization Level You can set default decimal and digit group separators at the organization level. These settings override the defaults that apply to your preferred browser in your locale. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. • The default decimal and digit group separators feature must be enabled for your account. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Company Profile. 3. Add the required defaults for the Decimal Separator and Digit Grouping Separator fields in the Separator Preference area. 4. Click Save. Results Your changes take effect at the next sign in. Setting Default Decimal and Digit Group Separators at Individual User Level You can set default decimal and digit group separators at the individual user level, which override settings at the organization level. Prerequisites • 160 You are assigned a role with the Company Information permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Results Your changes take effect at the next sign in. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Configuration PUBLIC 161 Updating Your Personal Information The Personal Information page includes the user name, password, name, and other information about the current user. Only the account administrator’s name and email address are included in the company profile. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, choose Personal Information. The Personal Information page appears. Figure 18: Personal Information Page 3. Update values on the Personal Information page as necessary, noting the following constraints and guidelines: 162 • User Name is a value you enter when you sign in to SAP Business Network. A user name must be in the format of an email address (name @ domain .com); however, SAP Business Network does not send messages to the address. User names are case-sensitive, can contain any English character, and cannot contain any punctuation except the ampersand and period required by the name @ domain .com format. • Email Address is where SAP Business Network sends account notifications. By default, SAP Business Network sends all notifications to the account administrator. If you change your email address, SAP Business Network sends an email to the newly updated email address requesting you to confirm the email address. You must use the link in the email to activate and sign in to the account. • Password is a case-sensitive value you enter when you sign in to SAP Business Network. For increased security on SAP Business Network, passwords expire every 90 days for users who have PCard access (granted with Payment Activities permission). For all other users, including administrators, passwords expire after 5 years (1,826 days). PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Updating Your Personal Information Passwords are case-sensitive, must be at least eight characters long, and can include only alphabetic letters (without accents), numbers, and common symbols. You cannot reuse your recent passwords. As a best practice, you should include at least one numeral between the first and last characters and at least one letter. To change your password, you must enter your current password as well as the new one, then confirm the new password.  Note The number of asterisks that appear onscreen after you have typed in your password might differ from the number of characters in your password. This does not indicate a typing error. The difference results from password encryption and occurs randomly. • Secret Question and Answer are values that SAP Business Network uses to verify your identity if you forget your password. SAP Business Network provides a set of pre-determined secret questions for you to select from. Select a secret question and provide an appropriate answer that you will easily remember in the future. • Preferred Language is the language of notifications that SAP Business Network sends you. This is different than your web browser’s language setting, which controls the user interface and actions you initiate there. 4. Click Save. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Updating Your Personal Information PUBLIC 163 Supplier Management To manage SAP Business Network suppliers better, you can assign them to groups, which associate them with a customization project, define invoice rules, assign discount offers, or assign custom PDF layouts. Supplier Enablement Process [page 164] Verified Business and Active Supplier [page 165] Supplier Profiles [page 166] Supplier Organizational Hierarchy [page 168] Supplier IDs [page 169] Supplier Relationships [page 199] Creating a Supplier Group [page 204] Custom Routing Method for Suppliers [page 212] Commodity and Sales Territory Mappings [page 213] Supplier Contacts [page 214] Custom PDF Layouts [page 217] Application Gateway for Supplier Access to Non-SAP Ariba Applications [page 222] Supplier Enablement Process You enable your suppliers on SAP Business Network in order to exchange business documents with them. Through SAP Business Network, your organization or an assigned third-party service provider can enable suppliers efficiently in a self-serviced manner. You can assign specific activities to suppliers, determine how many suppliers are ready to transact on SAP Business Network, identify the suppliers that haven't completed their tasks, and evaluate the overall status of your organization's supplier enablement effort. The supplier enablement process on SAP Business Network involves the following high-level steps. Initial Setup for Supplier Enablement 1. Configure your trading relationship request and quick enablement letters. 2. View supplier enablement activities and tasks. 3. Set up the supplier information portal. 4. Set up reminder notifications for your organization. Suppliers can also set up reminder notifications for their organizations. 164 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Ongoing Steps for Supplier Enablement 1. Export your vendor data. 2. Upload your vendor data to SAP Business Network. 3. Assign activities to vendors. 4. Start enablement for vendors. 5. Take action on pending tasks. 6. Manage supplier enablement tasks. 7. Monitor the status of suppliers. 8. Assign additional activities to vendors. Related Information Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Verified Business and Active Supplier When evaluating suppliers on SAP Business Network, two key indicators on their company profiles can help you make informed, confident decisions: the Verified Business badge and the Active Supplier status. These indicators provide valuable insights into a supplier’s authenticity and engagement—helping you identify trustworthy and reliable partners. Verified Business Badge The Verified Business badge, represented by a blue checkmark , indicates that a supplier's company details have been validated by a trusted third-party provider—CDQ or Dun & Bradstreet (D&B) . Verified details include: • • • • Company Name Primary Address (Country, State, City, Address Line 1, and Postal Code) Tax ID or VAT ID DUNS Number (if verified by D&B) You can use the Verified filter to easily find suppliers with this badge when searching for suppliers.  Note SAP does not verify the accuracy of Third-Party Verification Information and is not responsible for any losses, direct or indirect, that may arise from it. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 165 Active Supplier Status The status highlights a supplier's ongoing engagement on SAP Business Network. A supplier earns this status by meeting both of the following criteria: • • Complete at least one successful transaction (invoice or order) within the last three years. Maintain at least one active trading relationship. By focusing on these two indicators, you can quickly identify suppliers who are both verified and actively engaged, ensuring strong and reliable business partnerships. Supplier Profiles Suppliers enter both basic and extended profile data in their SAP Business Network accounts. Basic supplier profile data is available online to all buying organizations. The extended profile, which includes both basic and extended information, is provided in a downloadable report. You can view a supplier’s extended profile if they configured their account to display it. You might want to review suppliers’ extended profiles in order to plan your implementation for doing business with them. By reviewing this information early, you can establish effective communication and set reasonable expectations with your trading partners before you begin transacting business with them. To prevent unrestricted access and potential overuse of Dun & Bradstreet (D&B) data by trading partners, SAP Business Network monitors the total number of supplier profiles downloaded from the SAP Business Network platform, which contain DUNS numbers fetched from Dun & Bradstreet (D&B). When the total number of downloaded supplier profiles with D&B-provided DUNS numbers reaches 100,000 records in a given year, the D-U-N-S Number column in newly downloaded profiles is left blank. The number of downloaded supplier profiles is counted at the organization level and this limit includes instances where the same record has been downloaded multiple times. The start date of each year is determined by the date when a buyer organization first downloads supplier profiles. Viewing and Downloading a Supplier’s Basic Profile The basic profile enables buying organizations to locate a supplier by company when searching by commodity, industry, territory, or other criteria. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. 166 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . The Active Relationships page appears. Figure 19: Active Relationships Page 2. Click the name of a supplier displayed as a Current Supplier or Pending Relationship. SAP Business Network displays summary information, including company contact information, classifications, preferred order routing methods, and other information. 3. Click Actions and choose Download Basic Profile to download a supplier’s basic profile. Results If a supplier’s account has been suspended, SAP Business Network displays a message to this effect at the top of the page. You cannot establish relationships with a supplier if their account is suspended. Related Information Supplier Membership Status Reports [page 270] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 167 Viewing and Downloading a Supplier’s Extended Profile Suppliers can choose whether to make their extended profile data available to all buying organizations on SAP Business Network or only to those buying organizations that have sent them a trading partner relationship request. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Context Supplier profiles are saved as CSV (comma separated value) files, which are viewable in spreadsheet applications, such as Microsoft Excel. SAP Ariba Sourcing can import SAP Business Network supplier profiles directly from SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Click the name of a supplier displayed as a Current Supplier or Pending Relationship. SAP Business Network displays the supplier’s basic profile. 3. Click Download Extended Profile. The browser displays a File Download dialog. 4. Click one of the following: • • Open to view the report. Your browser starts Microsoft Excel and displays the report. Save to save the report to your hard disk. The profile is in comma separated value (.csv) format.  Note You can also download the supplier’s extended profile using the Actions button. Supplier Organizational Hierarchy Buyers can view the organizational hierarchy of suppliers on SAP Business Network. This enhances visibility and understanding of supplier relationships and can be used to improve collaboration and decision-making within SAP Business Network. To view the organizational hierarchy of suppliers, you can search for the supplier from the trading partner portal, open the public profile of the supplier from the search results by clicking on the supplier name, and then choose Organization Structure from the left pane. 168 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management You can view their suppliers' organizational hierarchy at the following two levels: • • Parent organization Linked child organizations Clicking an element at the parent or child organization levels displays the following details: • • Name of the organization Address of the organization Supplier IDs Business applications can assign unique supplier IDs to suppliers. These IDs are called private IDs. For buyers using on-demand SAP Ariba Procurement solutions or SAP Business Network Commerce Automation, there is another type of unique supplier ID called the vendor compound key. The vendor compound key is uniform way to identify supplier sites in communications across the SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, and ERP systems, using values that already exist in ERP vendor master data. This key includes the vendor ID (which is often the same as the supplier private ID on SAP Business Network) plus two optional keys with additional supplier site data. For more information, see Supplier ID Normalization [page 177]. SAP Business Network can use private IDs and vendor compound keys to create private suppliers on behalf of buying organizations in cases where the vendor compound key is not supported (for example, when the quick enablement document comes from an ICS provider or an Ariba Buyer installation). On SAP Business Network, you can add and delete unique supplier IDs for suppliers. If you have multiple private IDs to add, you can specify them in a single file and upload them to SAP Business Network. Private Suppliers [page 170] Supplier ID Maintenance with Multiple Procurement Applications [page 170] Multiple Unique Supplier IDs for One Supplier [page 171] Editing or Deleting a Unique Supplier ID [page 173] Deleting Unique Supplier IDs [page 174] Uploading Multiple Unique IDs for Suppliers in Your Test Account [page 174] Creating a Supplier File [page 176] Uploading a Supplier File [page 176] Supplier ID Normalization [page 177] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 169 Private Suppliers If you send an order or other document to a supplier that does not have an SAP Business Network trading relationship with you, or if an unregistered supplier routes an invoice to you, SAP Business Network creates a private supplier account. This supplier appears as a Private Supplier. SAP Business Network can create private supplier accounts using one of the following values: • • Unique supplier ID from the procurement application Vendor compound key values, if available (cloud SAP Ariba Procurement solutions or SAP Business Network Commerce Automation) SAP Business Network classifies private suppliers in the following categories: • • After a private supplier takes ownership of their account, they appear as a Current - Former Private Supplier. • If a private supplier declines your trading relationship, SAP Business Network displays the supplier as a Declined Private Supplier. If a supplier without an SAP Business Network account routes an invoice to you that fails or you send them an order that fails, SAP Business Network cannot create a private account on the supplier’s behalf. The supplier appears as a Failed Private Supplier. Related Information Supplier IDs [page 169] Supplier ID Maintenance with Multiple Procurement Applications If your organization has more than one procurement application, you define an application system ID to uniquely identify each procurement application on SAP Business Network. You can identify suppliers in your procurement application by: • Private ID, a supplier ID that identifies the supplier as unique within each of your procurement applications. These IDs can have any alphanumeric value, but they must be unique for each procurement application. • The values that automatically form the SAP Business Network vendor compound key, a unique supplier ID that reflects the supplier ID information in the back end ERP system (applicable to cloud SAP Ariba Procurement solutions). • • ANID, a globally unique identifier. D-U-N-S number, a globally unique identifier. By defining an application system ID for each procurement application, you can easily manage all transactions with suppliers using a single SAP Business Network account. For each application’s system ID, the unique supplier IDs are mapped to the supplier’s ANID to ensure correct document routing. 170 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: Related Information Supplier IDs [page 169] Link Multiple Business Applications [page 133] Multiple Unique Supplier IDs for One Supplier If your organization has more than one procurement application, and you use unique supplier IDs to identify suppliers, you can configure SAP Business Network to map multiple supplier IDs from your procurement applications to the ANID of the supplier.  Note This SAP Business Network feature is available only if your application is enabled to allow multiple unique supplier IDs (formerly called private IDs) per supplier. To enable this feature, contact SAP Ariba Support. Mapping multiple supplier IDs to the supplier’s ANID prevents SAP Business Network from creating multiple supplier accounts for each buyer–supplier relationship through Purchase Order, Payment Proposal, CC Invoice (invoices sent from the SAP Ariba procurement solution or the ERP system), or Request for Quotation Quick Enablement and ensures that all documents are sent to one supplier account. The following explains the process flow: 1. You configure your unique supplier IDs to map to the supplier’s ANID. 2. You choose one supplier ID as the default. 3. When users anywhere in your organization create orders, payment proposals, CC invoices (invoices sent from the SAP Ariba procurement solution or the ERP system), or request for quotation for a supplier identified by a unique supplier ID from the procurement application, SAP Business Network determines the supplier’s ANID and routes the document to the supplier. 4. If the supplier issues a non-PO invoice, SAP Business Network routes the document to your procurement application using the default unique supplier ID. Each procurement application has a system ID associated to the unique supplier ID. SAP Business Network identifies your procurement application with the Bill To address associated with each application system ID. Configuring Unique Supplier IDs You can configure SAP Business Network to map multiple supplier IDs from your procurement applications to the ANID of the supplier. Prerequisites • You are assigned the Administrator role. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 171 • This SAP Business Network feature is available only if your application is enabled to allow multiple unique supplier IDs (formerly called private IDs) per supplier. To enable this feature, contact SAP Ariba Support. • • You must specify a unique supplier ID for each supplier relationship. Don’t append “-T” to supplier ID values for test accounts. You can use the same value in both test and production accounts, because test environments cannot communicate with production environments.  Restriction • Once you enter a supplier ID for a supplier, you can edit but not delete it. You can delete unique supplier IDs [page 174] only when the supplier declines a relationship request. • On the Edit Preferences for Supplier page, the Application System ID column in the Unique Supplier ID Configuration section is displayed only if your organization has configured system IDs. • SAP Business Network does not map these supplier ID values for documents exchanged between SAP Business Network and suppliers. Suppliers must identify themselves with NetworkId, DUNS number, or a sign in name in order to exchange documents. • If you try to assign a supplier ID that is already in use, SAP Business Network might display this message: “This ANID is already assigned to ANID0000xxxx.” This appears because the supplier ID is already assigned to a supplier in another trading relationship. • When a supplier ID cannot be assigned for a particular trading relationship, you can edit the supplier ID (or delete it if the supplier has declined your relationship request). Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Select the supplier that requires multiple unique supplier ID configurations, click More Actions and then click Edit.. SAP Business Network displays the Edit Preferences for Supplier page. 3. In the Unique Supplier ID Configuration section, click Add. The Add Supplier Unique Key dialog box opens. 4. Enter the supplier ID information in the dialog box. • • The Vendor ID field can be used for private IDs or for the Vendor ID portion of the vendor compound key. The remaining fields are for buyers using SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. Site ID and Site Auxiliary ID are part of the vendor compound key. Legacy Supplier Private ID holds the private ID that existed before the supplier ID was converted to the vendor compound key. It is for backward compatibility. 5. Click Save. 6. Click Save to close the Edit Preferences for Supplier page. Related Information Supplier IDs [page 169] 172 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Editing or Deleting a Unique Supplier ID After you define a unique supplier ID, you can edit it. If the supplier declined the relationship request, you can delete the supplier ID. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. In the Current Suppliers text box, enter the ANID specified in the error message and click Search. 3. Do one of the following: • If the search returns the ANID, click More Actions and then Edit to edit the preferences for the supplier. Edit the unique supplier ID of the supplier. • If the search does not return the ANID, delete the supplier’s private ID. [page 174] How Editing Unique Supplier IDs Affects Existing Documents Your SAP Business Network account can be configured to include the vendor compound key values in outbound documents. This configuration option has the following effects on editing unique supplier IDs on SAP Business Network: • If your account is configured to include vendor compound key values in outbound documents, when you edit the vendor compound key under Unique Supplier ID Configuration on the Edit Preferences for Supplier page, the changes are applied to supplier responses to orders (order confirmations, advance ship notices, and invoices) that were received prior to the edit. These documents are enriched with the modified key. • If your account is not configured to include vendor compound key values in outbound documents, and you edit the vendor compound key, the behavior is the same as it was before this feature was released: The edited ID is added as a completely new ID. It is not linked with supplier responses received prior to the edit. Related Information Supplier IDs [page 169] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 173 Deleting Unique Supplier IDs If a private supplier declines a relationship request, you can delete the supplier’s unique ID (or private ID) from SAP Business Network. This allows you to continue sending orders to the supplier, and possibly later establish a trading relationship. If you do not delete these supplier IDs, SAP Business Network rejects orders sent to the supplier. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Click Supplier Selector and select Declined Private Suppliers. SAP Business Network displays a list of private suppliers that have declined your relationship requests. 3. Click Delete Private ID.  Note You can use the link in the Alerts and Messages section to view information about your declined relationships. Related Information Supplier IDs [page 169] Multiple Unique Supplier IDs for One Supplier [page 171] Uploading Multiple Unique IDs for Suppliers in Your Test Account You can specify multiple supplier IDs and system IDs for suppliers that have an active trading relationship with you. Using a single file, you can quickly add multiple IDs for suppliers. You can add up to 1,000 unique entries in a single file.  Note This feature is available only in your test account. To upload multiple unique supplier IDs in your production account, see Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network. 174 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management You use the following process to upload multiple supplier IDs in your test account: 1. Create a comma-separated values (CSV) file [page 176] with supplier ANID, system ID, and private ID information. 2. Upload the file [page 176] to SAP Business Network. Basic Syntax Rules for Creating a Supplier File A supplier file containing supplier IDs and system IDs has the following requirements: • • The file must be saved in CSV format. The file must have four columns using the fields described in Supplier File Fields [page 175]. If the values or number of columns are incorrect, file validation fails. Supplier File Fields The following table specifies requirements for each field in the supplier file:  Restriction This supplier file does not support the vendor compound key. Field Description Required/Optional Content Type ANID Supplier ANID Required 13 digits number prefixed with AN. For example, ANxxxxxxxxxx. SystemID An identifier assigned to each of your procurement applications Optional Alphanumeric values PrivateID An identifier used to define the suppliers in your procurement application. It must be unique per buyer–supplier relationship per system ID. Required Alphanumeric values IsDefault Required Controls routing of nonPO invoices for each procurement application. You can only dedicate one supplier private ID as a default for each application system ID. Y to indicate Yes N or Blank to indicate No Related Information Supplier IDs [page 169] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 175 Creating a Supplier File You can create your file using a spreadsheet application such as Microsoft Excel. Procedure 1. Create a new blank CSV file and enter the following headings in the first four columns: • • • • ANID SystemID PrivateID IsDefault 2. Enter appropriate values in each of the columns. 3. Ensure that the file maintains the correct syntax and values. 4. Save the file. Related Information Supplier IDs [page 169] Uploading a Supplier File After you create the supplier file, you must upload it. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. • Your application must be enabled to allow multiple unique supplier IDs (private IDs) per buyer–supplier relationship. Context If there are no syntax errors when you upload the supplier file, SAP Business Network puts your file into the queue to validate and process it. SAP Business Network validates the syntax and values specified in the supplier file. When validation is complete, SAP Business Network changes its status to Completed. In case there are errors, an 176 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management error message is displayed. You can view the list of events and the status of the supplier file in the Upload Events table. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network test account. 2. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 3. Click Upload Private IDs. 4. Enter a name in the text box to identify the uploaded event. 5. Browse for your CSV file and click Upload. The supplier file can have two kinds of errors: • Syntax errors. If the file contains syntax errors, an error message is displayed on the Upload Supplier Private IDs page. Click Download Error Log to download the error log file. Events with syntax errors are not queued and they are not available in the Update Event table. • Database or event errors. In case there are database or event errors while uploading the supplier file, the file is queued and this event appears in the Update Event table. Click the event name to download the error log and supplier file to view and make changes. Results You receive notifications on the status of the uploaded file. Related Information Supplier IDs [page 169] Supplier ID Normalization Supplier ID normalization provides a uniform way to identify supplier sites in communications across SAP Business Network, on-demand SAP Ariba procurement and invoicing solutions, and ERP systems, using values that already exist in ERP vendor master data. Supplier ID normalization identifies supplier sites using a vendor compound key. This key includes the vendor ID (which is often the same as the supplier private ID on SAP Business Network) plus two optional keys with additional supplier site data. Supplier ID normalization includes automatic and manual conversion to the vendor compound key. This feature also provides backward compatibility by preserving legacy supplier site IDs for use in configurations that do not use the vendor compound key, for example, SAP Ariba invoice conversion services (ICS) and on-premise SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 177 With supplier ID normalization: • • Transaction document routing maps to ERP master data without using SAP Ariba internal IDs. • Quick-enabled suppliers are matched to the vendor IDs used in the supplier enablement process. For example, when you quick enable a supplier through a purchase order, and you upload the same supplier to SAP Business Network in a CSV file, SAP Business Network recognizes that the suppliers are the same and combines the information in one supplier record based on the common vendor compound key. • It is easier for organizations using the invoice automation feature to integrate with ERP vendor sites for inbound and outbound documents and to migrate to SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing or SAP Ariba Invoice Management, if desired. For existing SAP Business Network supplier accounts that are linked to ERP vendor IDs, quick enablement transactions no longer trigger the creation of a duplicate SAP Business Network account. Supplier ID normalization enablement [page 178] Prerequisites [page 178] Backward compatibility [page 179] Limitations [page 179] Supplier ID Normalization Enablement Some aspects of supplier ID normalization are available to all buyers. • The vendor compound key is available for managing vendors in supplier enablement automation and in the SAP Business Network user interface. • Documents sent from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to SAP Business Network include the vendor compound key when that information is available. • For buyers using SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, SAP Ariba Buying, or SAP Ariba Invoice Management, existing supplier private IDs on SAP Business Network are converted to the new vendor compound key automatically through transaction documents sent from the SAP Ariba solution to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites • Buyers using the Oracle Fusion Middleware adapter must use a version of the adapter that supports the supplier ID normalization feature (adapter version 12s2 and later). • If buyers using Oracle Fusion Middleware with a document automation feature (and without SAP Ariba Procurement solutions) want to use the vendor compound key, they must convert their SAP Business Network vendor IDs. • There is a setting in SAP Business Network buyer accounts for including the vendor compound key in outbound documents sent to the ERP system. This setting must be either enabled or disabled, depending on how your site is configured.  Note Transactions continue to flow regardless of whether you take full advantage of supplier ID normalization by configuring your site. 178 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Vendor compound keys and multi-ERP support For SAP Business Network accounts with multi-ERP support, each vendor compound key is mapped to an application system ID. System IDs uniquely identify different buyer-side business applications. For details about system IDs, see the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. Backward Compatibility Supplier ID normalization is backward compatible with SAP Ariba solutions that are unchanged (such as SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing and SAP Ariba invoice conversion services). Legacy supplier site keys still work as they did before, making sure that transactions flow regardless of whether the new vendor compound key or the legacy key is used. The vendor CSV file template includes columns for the vendor compound key and legacy vendor ID values, but you can still import vendors without including these columns. Restrictions • In some circumstances, such as when duplicate supplier accounts previously existed for the same supplier site, or when using SAP Ariba invoice conversion services (ICS), supplier normalization IDs may not be used to link accounts. • If duplicate supplier accounts were already created for the same supplier site, those duplicate accounts still exist. The supplier ID normalization feature does not link the accounts. Review your vendor list on SAP Business Network and remove any accounts that are duplicated and not used. • • • The payment batch upload CSV file format does not incorporate the vendor compound key values. SAP Ariba invoice conversion services does not yet include the vendor compound key values in ICS invoices. For suppliers that use a single SAP Business Network account for multiple fulfillment sites, this feature does not link specific fulfillment sites to the buyer-maintained supplier sites (supplier locations) on SAP Business Network. (This limitation pertains to suppliers for whom the buyer specified multiple supplier locations.) Vendor Compound Keys and Legacy Vendor IDs The vendor compound key is the ID of the supplier site as it is stored in the ERP system. The previously used vendor ID, called the legacy vendor ID, still exists for backward compatibility. The fields used in your configuration depend on the type of ERP system used. The following table lists the fields available in the vendor compound key: Field Description Notes Vendor ID Vendor ID from the ERP system Vendor ID is always required on SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 179 Field Description Notes Site ID Vendor location ID Maps to a field in Oracle and PeopleSoft ERP systems. Not used in SAP ERP. Site Auxiliary ID Holds an additional ID of the vendor key, often used for address ID or contact ID Maps to a field in PeopleSoft ERP systems. Not used in SAP and Oracle ERP systems. The previously used vendor ID (sometimes referred to as the supplier private ID) is still used to identify supplier sites when the vendor compound key is not present. This ID is now called the legacy vendor ID. In some cases, the legacy vendor ID is the same as the vendor ID. Field Description Legacy Vendor ID Formerly used vendor ID / private ID, used for backward compatibility. Legacy Vendor ID is a separate field from the vendor compound key fields, and is not a required field on SAP Business Network. However, it is required for successful transacting in environments that combine the previous and new approaches to supplier IDs. For example, SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing uses supplier ID normalization, but SAP Ariba invoice conversion services does not. So, if you are using both of these solutions, all existing and new vendors must have the new key and the legacy vendor key. Vendor compound keys and multi-ERP support For SAP Business Network accounts with multi-ERP support, each vendor compound key is mapped to an application system ID. System IDs uniquely identify different buyer-side business applications. For details about system IDs, see the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. Related Information Vendor Compound Keys Mapping to Vendor IDs in External Systems [page 180] Supplier ID Normalization Workflow [page 182] Vendor Compound Keys Mapping to Vendor IDs in External Systems Fields in the vendor compound key in SAP Business Network map differently to the vendor identification information in SAP, PeopleSoft, and Oracle ERP systems and in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. For buyers using SAP as their external ERP system, only the Vendor ID field is used to identify the supplier site on SAP Business Network. 180 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management
