file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: Field on SAP Business Network Field in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions Field in SAP ERP System Vendor ID Supplier.UniqueName Vendor ID For buyers using PeopleSoft as their external ERP system, all three parts of the vendor compound key are used to identify a supplier site in SAP Business Network. Field on SAP Business Network Field in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions Field in PeopleSoft ERP System Vendor ID Supplier.UniqueName VendorID Site ID SupplierLocation.UniqueName VendorID:LocationID Site Auxiliary ID SupplierLocation.ContactID VendorID:AddressID:ContactID For buyers using Oracle (which corresponds to the Simple Generic variant in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions), Vendor ID and Site ID are used to identify a supplier site in SAP Business Network. Field on SAP Business Network Field in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions Field in Oracle ERP System Vendor ID Supplier.UniqueName VENDOR_ID Site ID SupplierLocation.UniqueName VENDOR_SITE_ID If your ERP system and your SAP Ariba variant use different vendor identifiers, and you use SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, SAP Ariba Buying, or SAP Ariba Invoice Management, an optional customization is available to have the SAP Ariba solution include only the applicable values in transaction documents. Regardless of whether this customization is implemented, transactions still flow successfully between SAP Ariba Procurement solutions and SAP Business Network. Vendor compound keys and multi-ERP support For SAP Business Network accounts with multi-ERP support, each vendor compound key is mapped to an application system ID. System IDs uniquely identify different buyer-side business applications. For details about system IDs, see the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. Related Information Vendor Compound Keys and Legacy Vendor IDs [page 179] Supplier ID Normalization Workflow [page 182] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 181 Supplier ID Normalization Workflow Supplier ID normalization provides a uniform way to identify supplier sites using values from your ERP system to identify supplier sites uniquely. The following figure illustrates the workflow of supplier ID normalization: Figure 20: Supplier ID Normalization Workflow In SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, supplier master data fields correspond to the vendor compound key as follows: • • • The UniqueName field of a supplier maps to the Vendor ID field on SAP Business Network. The UniqueName field of a supplier location maps to the Site ID field on SAP Business Network. The ContactID field of a supplier location maps to the Site Auxiliary ID field on SAP Business Network. Matching Enabled Suppliers The additional supplier data included in purchase orders makes it possible for SAP Business Network to find suppliers that you already enabled. If an account already exists for the supplier site, SAP Business Network does not create an additional account. Instead, SAP Business Network matches the new information to the existing account. The following figure shows what happens on SAP Business Network when a purchase order without an Ariba Network ID comes in for a supplier site that was already enabled. The ERP system is Oracle, so only Vendor ID and Vendor Site ID are used. 182 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Figure 21: Matching Account Information on SAP Business Network for a Supplier Site Already Enabled Related Information Vendor Compound Keys and Legacy Vendor IDs [page 179] Vendor Compound Keys Mapping to Vendor IDs in External Systems [page 180] Impact of Supplier ID Normalization on SAP Ariba Procurement solutions [page 183] Impact of Supplier ID Normalization on SAP Ariba Procurement solutions All documents sent from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions include the vendor compound key information. This information enables identification of the supplier and supplier location. The supplier location private ID (called Ariba Network Private ID in the user interface), which is auto-generated for each supplier location in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, is included in documents sent from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. The value is sent using the SSPPrivateID domain. To ensure backward compatibility, SAP Business Network uses both SSPPrivateID and PrivateID to look up suppliers in cXML documents from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. Therefore, legacy documents that use the PrivateID domain for specifying the auto-generated supplier-location-level private ID are properly routed. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 183 Related Information Supplier ID Normalization Workflow [page 182] Supplier Credentials in cXML Documents Outbound documents from SAP Business Network to an ERP system can include vendor information based on your SAP Business Network configuration. For information about credentials in cXML documents, see the SAP Business Network cXML solutions guide. Documents Sent from SAP Business Network to the ERP System Your SAP Business Network account can be configured to include Vendor ID, Site ID, and Site Auxiliary ID credentials in documents sent from SAP Business Network to the ERP system. If your account is not configured to send these values, outbound documents do not include them. Outbound documents do not include the SSPPrivateID domain. Instead, outbound documents include the legacy private ID using the PrivateID domain. For configuration information, see Configuring Supplier ID Normalization on SAP Business Network [page 185]. Vendor compound keys and multi-ERP support For SAP Business Network accounts with multi-ERP support, each vendor compound key is mapped to an application system ID. System IDs uniquely identify different buyer-side business applications. For details about system IDs, see the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. SAP Business Network Transaction Matching Order SAP Business Network uses supplier credentials in transaction documents to find a matching supplier among your trading relationships. When SAP Business Network finds a match, no further matching or validation occurs. SAP Business Network uses the credentials to find a match in the following order: 1. Supplier Ariba Network ID 2. Vendor compound key (Vendor ID, Site ID, Site Auxiliary ID)  Note SAP Business Network rejects documents when the combination of legacy vendor ID and vendor compound key in the document conflicts with an existing combination on SAP Business Network. 184 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management 3. Supplier organization private ID corresponds to Vendor ID on SAP Business Network (if no vendor ID is provided) 4. Ariba Network Private ID (SSPPrivateID domain) corresponds to Vendor ID on SAP Business Network 5. Ariba Network Private ID (SSPPrivateID) and PrivateID correspond to Legacy Vendor ID on SAP Business Network (for example, ICS uses the PrivateID domain to send a legacy private ID) If SAP Business Network does not find a match, and the document is of a type that can be used for quick enablement, SAP Business Network creates a private supplier account using the vendor compound key. Related Information Supplier ID Normalization Troubleshooting [page 196] Management of Supplier ID Normalization Managing supplier ID normalization involves configuring it on SAP Business Network, optionally including the vendor compound key in SAP Business Network documents sent to your ERP system, and converting existing supplier/vendor IDs automatically or manually. Configuring Supplier ID Normalization on SAP Business Network [page 185] Including the Vendor Compound Key in Documents Sent from SAP Business Network to the ERP System [page 186] Converting Existing Vendor/Supplier IDs [page 187] Converting Vendor IDs Manually [page 191] Configuring Supplier ID Normalization on SAP Business Network Full adoption of supplier ID normalization for existing suppliers may involve several steps. The following steps provide an overview of the process for fully adopting supplier ID normalization for existing suppliers: 1. If you use an adapter to integrate with an ERP system other than SAP ERP, update the adapter to the latest version. 2. For buying organizations using on demand SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, vendor IDs on SAP Business Network are converted automatically through transaction documents. 3. For vendor IDs that were not converted automatically, we recommend that you convert the IDs manually to maintain a clean vendor data set on SAP Business Network. 4. To have SAP Business Network include the vendor compound key values in documents sent to the ERP system, have SAP Ariba Customer Support turn on the entitlement option called Send VendorID, SiteID and SiteAuxID in outgoing documents. For some buying organizations, this option is enabled automatically. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 185 Related Information Conversion Using Transaction Documents from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions [page 187] Converting Vendor IDs Manually [page 191] Including the Vendor Compound Key in Documents Sent from SAP Business Network to the ERP System [page 186] Including the Vendor Compound Key in Documents Sent from SAP Business Network to the ERP System You can optionally include the vendor compound key in documents sent from SAP Business Network to an ERP system. SAP Business Network buyer accounts include an entitlement option called Send VendorID, SiteID and SiteAuxID in outgoing documents that can be enabled at your request by SAP Ariba Customer Support. The entitlement option determines whether the vendor compound key values are included in documents sent from SAP Business Network to the ERP system. If this option is not enabled for your account, documents sent from SAP Business Network include only the legacy vendor ID, which is sent using the PrivateID domain. The Send VendorID, SiteID and SiteAuxID in outgoing documents option affects what happens to existing transaction documents when you edit a unique supplier ID. Depending on how your site is configured, the option Send VendorID, SiteID and SiteAuxID in outgoing documents must be either enabled or disabled: • For SAP Business Network buyers using SAP ERP, this option must not be enabled. The SAP adapter has not been updated to consume values sent using the VendorID domain. • For SAP Business Network buyers using Oracle Fusion Middleware, this option is not enabled automatically. Oracle Fusion Middleware sends only Vendor ID unless you set a parameter to have Site ID sent, too. If you configure the adapter to send Site ID, the option Send VendorID, SiteID and SiteAuxID in outgoing documents must be enabled. • For SAP Business Network buyers using SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing and not using SAP Ariba Invoice Management, SAP Ariba enables this option automatically, with the following exception: • • • 186 If the Enable end point support option is turned on in the SAP Business Network account, the option is not enabled automatically. For SAP Business Network buyers whose SAP Ariba sites include both SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing and SAP Ariba Invoice Management (as a merged SAP Ariba solutions environment), SAP Ariba Customer Support confirms whether your adapter can process the new keys at the same time that they configure the merged site: • If your adapter can process the new keys, the SAP Business Network option for including the vendor compound key in outbound documents must be left on. • If your adapter cannot process the new keys, SAP Ariba Customer Support disables this option, giving you time to upgrade the adapter. To enable supplier ID normalization fully, have your designated support contact log a service request. An SAP Ariba Customer Support representative follows up to complete the request. For all other existing SAP Business Network buyers, this option is disabled by default to give organizations that use adapters sufficient time to upgrade to the latest version of the adapter. To enable supplier ID normalization fully, have your designated support contact log a service request. An SAP Ariba Customer Support representative follows up to complete the request. PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management For information on what happens to existing transaction documents when you edit a unique supplier ID, see the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide [page 12]. Related Information Integrating with SAP ERP [page 194] Integrating with Oracle [page 194] Converting Existing Vendor/Supplier IDs Existing vendor IDs and supplier private IDs on SAP Business Network can be converted to the vendor compound key automatically for SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, SAP Ariba Buying, and SAP Ariba Invoice Management, or buyers can convert the IDs manually. • For buyers using SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, SAP Ariba Buying, or SAP Ariba Invoice Management, the supplier private IDs configured on SAP Business Network are automatically converted using the information in transaction documents sent from the SAP Ariba solution. • Buyers can convert vendor IDs manually. Related Information Conversion Using Transaction Documents from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions [page 187] Conversion of Suppliers with Multiple Supplier Locations [page 188] Suppliers Quick Enabled Through ICS Invoices [page 188] Examples of Transaction-Based Vendor Identifier Conversion [page 189] Conversion Using Transaction Documents from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions SAP Business Network uses the supplier credentials in documents from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions (SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, SAP Ariba Buying, or SAP Ariba Invoice Management) to convert existing supplier private IDs on SAP Business Network to the new vendor compound key. The conversion process consists of the following steps: 1. SAP Ariba Procurement solutions send a document to the supplier using SAP Business Network. 2. SAP Business Network looks for a supplier record that matches the supplier credentials in the document. 3. If a matching supplier is found, SAP Business Network checks whether the supplier private ID for that supplier has to be converted to the vendor compound key format. (If there is a value in the Legacy Vendor ID field, conversion has already occurred. If the matching supplier was found using the vendor compound key, no conversion is necessary.) SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 187 4. If the supplier private ID has not been converted, SAP Business Network converts it. SAP Business Network converts the existing value in the Vendor ID field into the Legacy Vendor ID field and enters the vendor compound key values into the appropriate fields (Vendor ID, Site ID, Site Auxiliary ID). Related Information Conversion of Suppliers with Multiple Supplier Locations [page 188] Suppliers Quick Enabled Through ICS Invoices [page 188] Conversion of Suppliers with Multiple Supplier Locations For suppliers with multiple supplier locations, automatic conversion of the supplier private ID depends on whether a private ID is configured at the supplier organization level or the supplier level (partitioned supplier) in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. • For suppliers that have both a private ID at the partitioned supplier level and multiple supplier locations, the supplier private ID on SAP Business Network is converted to the vendor compound key for each of the supplier locations. • For suppliers that have both a private ID at the supplier organization level and multiple supplier locations, the supplier private ID on SAP Business Network is not automatically converted to the vendor compound key. This is to ensure backward compatibility with external ERP systems. SAP Business Network sends documents to the supplier using the supplier organization private ID. Related Information Conversion Using Transaction Documents from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions [page 187] Suppliers Quick Enabled Through ICS Invoices [page 188] Suppliers Quick Enabled Through ICS Invoices For buyers who subscribe to SAP Ariba invoice conversion services (ICS) and use on demand SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, ICS might not use the new vendor compound key values for initial identification of suppliers who are quick enabled through ICS invoices. Invoices sent by ICS providers use either the supplier organization private ID or the auto-generated supplier location private ID (SAP Business Network Private ID) to identify suppliers. For suppliers that are quick enabled through ICS invoices, when the supplier is first quick enabled on SAP Business Network, it has a legacy vendor ID but not the vendor compound key. SAP Business Network receives the vendor compound key values later, from subsequent transaction documents sent from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to the supplier (for example, CC invoices). 188 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management  Note When the ICS provider supports vendor compound keys, buying organizations can stop using the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions Export Vendor Master File v2 data export task to export vendor details for the ICS provider. They can use the vendor details from their ERP system. Related Information Conversion Using Transaction Documents from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions [page 187] Conversion of Suppliers with Multiple Supplier Locations [page 188] Examples of Transaction-Based Vendor Identifier Conversion Transaction-based vendor identifier conversion differs depending on your external ERP system. The following figure shows an example of transaction-based conversion for a buying organization that uses SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, SAP Ariba Buying, or SAP Ariba Invoice Management configured to work with SAP ERP: Figure 22: Transaction-Based Conversion for a Buyer Using SAP Ariba Procurement solutions with SAP ERP SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 189 The following figure shows an example of transaction-based conversion for a buying organization that uses SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, SAP Ariba Buying, or SAP Ariba Invoice Management configured to work with PeopleSoft: Figure 23: Transaction-Based Conversion for a Buying Organization Using SAP Ariba Procurement solutions with PeopleSoft The following figure shows an example of transaction-based conversion for a buying organization that uses SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, SAP Ariba Buying, or SAP Ariba Invoice Management configured to work with Oracle (the Simple Generic variant in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions): Figure 24: Transaction-Based Conversion for a Buying Organization Using SAP Ariba Procurement solutions with Oracle 190 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: Related Information Vendor Compound Keys Mapping to Vendor IDs in External Systems [page 180] Converting Vendor IDs Manually Vendor ID conversion is optional. However, we recommend that you manually convert the vendor IDs that were not automatically converted through transaction documents from SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. When all vendors use the new vendor compound keys, SAP Business Network does not create duplicate accounts and supplier relationships during quick enablement.  Note If buying organizations using Oracle Fusion Middleware with SAP Business Network document automation features (and without SAP Ariba Procurement solutions) want to use the vendor compound key, they must convert their SAP Business Network vendor IDs. There are two ways to convert vendor IDs manually: • • Mass conversion using the vendor CSV file Converting vendor IDs from the active relationships page  Tip To find out which SAP Business Network vendors have not been converted, run the Vendor Data Export report. If the Site ID column or the Legacy Vendor ID column has no value, then the vendor ID has not been converted. Related Information Converting Vendor IDs in the SAP Business Network User Interface [page 192] Mass-Converting Vendor IDs Using the Vendor CSV File [page 192] Converting Supplier Identifiers Used by SAP Ariba Procurement solutions [page 193] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 191 Mass-Converting Vendor IDs Using the Vendor CSV File To convert existing vendor IDs to the vendor compound key manually, you edit and upload the vendor CSV file. The Legacy Vendor ID column is used to look up the old vendor ID. You can add the vendor compound key values in the appropriate columns as needed. Context You can edit the CSV output from a full vendor data export report to move values in the Vendor ID column to the Legacy Vendor ID column. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Download a full vendor data export report from the Reports tab, and open the resulting CSV file. 3. For the vendors you want to convert, move the values in the Vendor ID column to the Legacy Vendor ID column in the vendor CSV file. 4. Enter values in the Vendor ID column. If applicable for your ERP system, enter values in the Site ID and Site Auxiliary ID columns, too. 5. Save and upload the file. (Choose Supplier Enablement for the upload operation, and specify the file.) Manage Vendors , click Upload, provide a name Related Information Converting Vendor IDs in the SAP Business Network User Interface [page 192] Converting Supplier Identifiers Used by SAP Ariba Procurement solutions [page 193] Converting Vendor IDs in the SAP Business Network User Interface You can convert vendor IDs in the user interface by editing the supplier identifiers for suppliers on the Active Relationships page. These IDs were formerly called supplier private IDs and are the IDs used by SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. Related Information Mass-Converting Vendor IDs Using the Vendor CSV File [page 192] 192 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Converting Supplier Identifiers Used by SAP Ariba Procurement solutions [page 193] Converting Supplier Identifiers Used by SAP Ariba Procurement solutions You can convert vendor IDs from the Active Relationships page. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 3. For the vendor whose supplier identifier you want to convert, choose More Actions Edit . 4. In the Edit Preferences for Supplier page, scroll down to the Unique Supplier ID Configuration section. 5. Click Convert for an ID that you want to convert. The Convert Supplier Private ID dialog box opens. The value you are converting is in the Legacy Supplier Private ID field. 6. Enter a value in the Vendor ID field. If applicable, enter values in the Site ID and Site Auxiliary ID fields, too. 7. Click Save. Related Information Mass-Converting Vendor IDs Using the Vendor CSV File [page 192] Converting Vendor IDs in the SAP Business Network User Interface [page 192] Integration of Supplier ID Normalization with ERP Systems Buyers can integrate supplier ID normalization with their existing SAP or Oracle ERP systems. No action is required for buyers that use a PeopleSoft ERP system. With PeopleSoft, there is no integration with the ERP system through SAP Business Network. Integrating with SAP ERP [page 194] Integrating with Oracle [page 194] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 193 Integrating with SAP ERP For buyers using SAP ERP, integration is easy because SAP ERP uses only one field to identify suppliers. If your organization uses SAP ERP, consider the following: • Buyers that use SAP ERP do not need to do anything to integrate the new vendor compound key with their ERP system, because SAP ERP uses only one field, Vendor ID, to identify supplier sites. • The SAP Business Network entitlement option Send VendorID, SiteID and SiteAuxID in outgoing documents is not turned on for buying organizations using SAP ERP, because the SAP ERP adapter has not been updated to consume values sent using the VendorID domain. • New SAP Business Network buyers do not need to fill in the Legacy Vendor ID column when uploading vendors to SAP Business Network using the vendor upload CSV file. • When vendor IDs are converted, the vendor ID and legacy vendor ID values are identical. Related Information Vendor Compound Keys Mapping to Vendor IDs in External Systems [page 180] Integrating with Oracle Buyers using the Oracle Fusion Middleware adapter must use a version of the adapter that supports the supplier ID normalization feature (adapter version 12s2 and later). For Buyers Using SAP Ariba Invoice Management Buyers using Oracle Fusion Middleware with SAP Ariba Invoice Management must decide which credentials to use, Vendor ID only, or Vendor ID and Site ID. If you chose to use Vendor ID only, then you must configure the private IDs at the supplier organization level in SAP Ariba Invoice Management. If you chose to use Vendor ID and Site ID, you are not required to configure the private IDs in SAP Ariba Invoice Management, but you must manually convert existing supplier IDs configured on SAP Business Network. For Buyers Using the SAP Business Network Document Automation Feature for Invoices or Purchase Orders If buying organizations using Oracle Fusion Middleware with Ariba Invoice Automation or Ariba Purchase Order Automation (and without SAP Ariba Procurement solutions) want to use the vendor compound key, they must convert their SAP Business Network vendor IDs. 194 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Related Information Vendor Compound Keys Mapping to Vendor IDs in External Systems [page 180] Configuring the Oracle Fusion Middleware Adapter to Send the Vendor Site ID [page 195] Configuring the Oracle Fusion Middleware Adapter to Send the Vendor Site ID By default, the 12s2 Oracle Fusion Middleware adapter only sends the vendor ID, not the vendor site ID to the ERP system. Therefore, existing buyers get time to learn about supplier ID normalization details, and to convert their SAP Business Network vendor IDs to use the vendor compound key. If you want the adapter to send the vendor site ID to the ERP system, you must: • Configure the adapter to send the vendor site ID. To configure the adapter to send the vendor site ID, you must populate the MAP_TYPE, MAP_KEY, and MAP_VALUE columns in the VALUE_MAP table using Insert/Update SQL commands. To send the vendor site ID, run the following insert command: insert into value_map values ('COMP_VENDOR_KEY','VENDOR_SITE_ID','YES') The following table explains the values in the preceding command: Field Value MAP_TYPE COMP_VENDOR_KEY MAP_KEY VENDOR_SITE_ID MAP_VALUE YES  Note This value tells the adapter to send the vendor site ID. If you do not insert the record in VALUE_MAP, or if you set MAP_VALUE to NO, the adapter sends only the vendor ID and not the vendor site ID. • Manually convert existing SAP Business Network vendors to use the vendor compound key (Vendor ID and Site ID). • Contact SAP Ariba Customer Support to enable the SAP Business Network option Send VendorID, SiteID and SiteAuxID in outgoing documents. Related Information Converting Vendor IDs Manually [page 191] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 195 Supplier ID Normalization Troubleshooting Issues related to supplier ID normalization may include transaction routing failure, ID conflicts, and legacy IDs that need correcting. Transaction Routing Failures [page 196] Handling ID Conflicts on SAP Business Network [page 196] Correcting Legacy Vendor IDs [page 199] Transaction Routing Failures If transaction routing fails from the buyer to SAP Business Network, check the related SAP Business Network vendor details to confirm the keys used. Handling ID Conflicts on SAP Business Network ID conflicts may occur when a supplier network ID does not match, and sometimes, even when the ID matches. Related Information Supplier Network ID Matches but Vendor Compound Key Conflicts [page 197] Supplier Network ID Matches but Legacy Vendor ID Conflicts with Vendor Compound Key [page 197] Missing Supplier Network ID and Vendor Compound Key Conflicts with Legacy Vendor ID [page 198] 196 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Supplier Network ID Matches but Vendor Compound Key Conflicts An error may occur when SAP Business Network receives a document in which the supplier network ID of the document matches an existing vendor on SAP Business Network, but the vendor compound key in the document is different from the one on SAP Business Network. Supplier Network ID Matches but Legacy Vendor ID Conflicts with Vendor Compound Key SAP Business Network attempts to resolve conflicts between the legacy vendor ID and the vendor compound key, when the supplier network ID in an incoming document matches an existing vendor record on SAP Business Network. Different processing scenarios are possible depending on existing data. The following table shows how SAP Business Network handles the conflicts. The table lists the IDs in the following format: VendorID, (SiteID, SiteAuxiliaryID), LegacyVendorID, NetworkID IDs on SAP Business Network IDs in Incoming Document V1,_,_,_,AN101 Explanation and SAP Business Network Behavior IDs in SAP Business Network Return Document V1,_,_,_,L1,AN101 The legacy vendor ID in the document gets priority, for backward compatibility in return documents. L1,_,_,_,AN101 V1,_,_,_,L1,AN101 The legacy vendor ID of the V2,_,_,L1,AN101 enriched vendor record gets priority, for backward compatibility in return documents. V1,_,_,_,L1,AN101 Due to the mismatch in legacy _,_,_,_,AN101 vendor IDs, only the network ID is included in the return document. V1,_,_,_,L1,AN101 SAP Business Network assoL1, _, _, _,AN101 ciates the vendor ID of a different network ID in the return documents based on a legacy match. L1,_,_,_,AN101 (Neither ID has been converted; there is no value in the Legacy Vendor ID field.) V1,_,_,_,AN101 V2,_,_,L1,AN101 (The second ID has been converted; there is a value in the Legacy Vendor ID field.) V1,_,_,_,AN101 L1,_,_,L2,AN101 (The second ID has been converted.) V1,_,_,_,AN101 L1,_,_,_,AN102 (Neither ID has been converted.) SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 197 Missing Supplier Network ID and Vendor Compound Key Conflicts with Legacy Vendor ID SAP Business Network attempts to resolve conflicts where an incoming document has no supplier network ID and contains vendor compound keys and legacy vendor IDs that are different from the IDs in the existing vendor record. Different processing scenarios are possible depending on existing data. The following table shows how SAP Business Network handles the conflicts. The table lists the IDs in the following format: VendorID, SiteID, SiteAuxiliaryID, LegacyVendorID IDs on SAP Business Network IDs in Incoming Document V1,_,_,_ V1,_,_,L1 Explanation and SAP Business Network Behavior Resulting IDs on SAP Business Network No change: L1,_,_,_ The legacy vendor ID in the document matches the vendor ID of a different vendor. (Neither ID has been con- SAP Business Network rejects L1,_,_,_ verted; there is no value in the the document. Legacy Vendor ID field.) V1,_,_,_  Tip To allow transactionbased conversion, delete V1 on SAP Business Network. V1,S1,A1,L1 V1,S1,A1,L2 V2,S2,A2,L2 Both of the possible unique IDs in the document (the vendor compound key and the legacy vendor ID) already exist in two different vendor records. No change: V1,S1,A1,L1 V2,S2,A2,L2 SAP Business Network rejects the document. V1,S1,A1,L1 V1,S1,A1,L2 The legacy vendor ID is upThe vendor compound key in dated: the document already exists on SAP Business Network with V1,S1,A1,L2 a different legacy vendor ID. SAP Business Network updates the legacy vendor ID in the vendor record to reflect the value in the document. V1,S1,A1,L1 V2,S2,A2,L1 The legacy vendor ID in the document already exists in a different vendor record. No change: V1,S1,A1,L1 SAP Business Network rejects the document. 198 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management When a rejection occurs, buyers can resolve the conflict manually in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions or on SAP Business Network. Correcting Legacy Vendor IDs You can correct the legacy vendor ID in three ways: by editing preferences for the supplier, by editing vendor details, and by uploading corrected legacy vendor ID. • Edit preferences for the supplier from the Active Relationships page. In the Unique Supplier ID Configuration section of the Edit Preferences for Supplier page, the Legacy Supplier Private ID field is always editable. • Edit the vendor details from the Manage Vendors page. On the Vendor Details page, the Legacy Vendor ID field is always editable. • Upload corrected legacy vendor IDs in the CSV vendor upload file. Supplier Relationships After you establish a relationship with a supplier, you can manage and view details of suppliers. On the Supplier Enablement management tasks: • • • • Active Relationships page, you can perform the following supplier Use filters to group suppliers and view status and details for them. Resend email invitations to private suppliers. Override default transaction rules and catalog validation preferences for suppliers. Remove a vendor from the list of active suppliers. Viewing Supplier Relationships [page 199] Overriding Your Rules and Preferences for a Supplier [page 201] Terminating Active Supplier Relationships [page 203] Viewing Supplier Relationships You can view your organization’s supplier relationships on the Supplier Enablement tab. You can view your invited and current suppliers, as well as pending and declined relationships. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 199 Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Click Supplier Selector and select a category of suppliers [page 200] to view. Supplier Status Information The Alerts and Messages section displays the status information about your suppliers. You can use this section to quickly view detailed information about the suppliers you have a relationship with. The next section on the page displays the different status information you can view by clicking these corresponding links in the Alerts and Messages section: • • The Chargeable Suppliers link displays the number of suppliers you have a chargeable relationship with. • The Failed Private Suppliers in the last 30 days link displays the number of your private suppliers that SAP Business Network could not enable. • The New Suppliers added in the last 30 days link displays the number of your suppliers that have been added in the last 30 days. • • The Suspended Suppliers link displays the number of your suppliers that are currently suspended. The Declined Private Suppliers in the last 30 days link displays the number of your private suppliers who declined to take ownership of their account in the last 30 days. The Declined Relationships link displays the number of suppliers that have declined to establish a trading relationship with you. Supplier Selector Categories The Supplier Selector button on the Active Relationships page displays the different supplier categories. Click this button and select a category to view the supplier information. SAP Business Network has the following supplier categories: • Private Suppliers displays suppliers with SAP Business Network accounts that were created on your behalf and of which the supplier has not taken ownership. You can resend the sign in information to private suppliers so that they can register and take ownership of their account. You can use the supplier enablement process on SAP Business Network to manage and track enablement activities for private suppliers. See Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network for more information. • • Current-Former Private Suppliers displays private suppliers that have taken ownership of their account. • 200 Declined Private Suppliers displays the private suppliers that have declined to establish a trading relationship with you. Failed Private Suppliers displays the private suppliers for which SAP Business Network cannot create a private account. You can resend the sign in information to private suppliers so that they can register and take ownership of their account. PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: • Invited Registered Suppliers displays registered suppliers that have not responded to relationship requests you have sent. You cannot yet transact with these suppliers. After SAP Business Network enables these suppliers, they are classified as Current Suppliers. If you invite a registered supplier and their account is set up to accept relationship invitations automatically, the supplier appears as a Current Supplier. If a registered supplier’s account is set up so that a user must review and respond to relationship requests manually, the relationship appears as a Pending Relationship until the supplier approves your request. • Invited Unregistered Suppliers displays unregistered suppliers to which you have sent relationship requests. You cannot yet transact with these suppliers. Suppliers might delay accepting requests so they can configure their order receiving systems before receiving purchase orders from new buying organizations. This process helps ensure that a supplier can receive your orders effectively. • Current Suppliers displays suppliers with which you have active relationships. Unless a current supplier’s account has been suspended, you can transact with these suppliers. • Suspended Suppliers displays suppliers with suspended accounts, which means you cannot transact with them. • Declined Relationships displays the suppliers that have declined your relationship requests. When a supplier declines your relationship request, SAP Business Network sends email notifications to you and the supplier. Suppliers might temporarily reject your relationship request if they are having trouble with your orders or to configure their order receiving systems to handle orders in a different manner. If you feel the supplier has declined the relationship in error, contact them directly. If you decide to establish a relationship, you can send them another relationship request. • Pending Relationships displays the suppliers you have invited and that have configured their accounts to review relationship requests manually. You cannot yet transact with these suppliers. Related Information Suspended Supplier Accounts [page 19] Supplier Membership Status Reports [page 270] Supplier Subscriptions [page 18] Private Suppliers [page 170] Supplier Relationships [page 199] Overriding Your Rules and Preferences for a Supplier You can edit the supplier relationship to override your default transaction rules and catalog validation settings. These overrides affect only the selected supplier. The Edit Preferences for Supplier page has the following categories of supplier preferences that you can override: • • • • Purchase order rules Scheduling agreement release setup rules Contracts, invoices, time and expense sheets site setup Invoice rules SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 201 • • • • Unique supplier ID configuration Catalog validation preferences Sales order rules Forecast collaboration Figure 25: Edit Preferences for Supplier Page Invoice Rules By default, the invoicing rules you set in Configuration govern all your suppliers. You can choose not to apply your customized invoice rules to individual suppliers. For example, if you allow some suppliers to change the unit price during invoicing, but want to block other suppliers from changing the unit price, you can override the invoicing rules for suppliers who should not be allowed to change the unit price during invoicing. If you click Enable invoice rules, SAP Business Network uses your invoicing rules [page 91] from this supplier.  Note If you clear Enable invoice rules, SAP Business Network does not use any invoicing rules except the following (these rules cannot be turned off and are set to Yes or whatever is appropriate): • • Allow suppliers to reuse invoice numbers. Allow suppliers to send invoices with service information. You can also override invoice rules for supplier groups [page 204]. 202 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Overriding Rules and Preferences for Suppliers SAP Business Network enables you to set catalog validation preferences so that suppliers can qualify their customer catalogs for your organization before publishing them to you. You can override these settings on a per-supplier basis to enforce or unenforce certain rules. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose 2. Click Supplier Enablement More Actions Edit Active Relationships . for a supplier. 3. Select a check box for each rule you want to override. 4. Click Save. Results Your updates take effect the next time the supplier logs in to their account on SAP Business Network. Related Information Catalog Validation Preferences [page 123] Terminating Active Supplier Relationships If you have already enabled a supplier’s account and are no longer buying from their organization, you can remove them from your list of current suppliers. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 203 Context When you delete an active supplier, you • • Remove your company from the list of companies to which that supplier can publish private customer catalogs Cancel any customer catalog subscriptions you have with that supplier Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Click Supplier Selector and select Current Suppliers. 3. Click More Actions and then Delete in the Supplier column. SAP Business Network removes that supplier from your list of current suppliers. 4. Click Continue. Results SAP Business Network sends an email notification to suppliers you delete from your list of current suppliers. Creating a Supplier Group You can group suppliers in specific supplier groups to associate them with a customization project, define invoice rules, assign discount offers, or assign custom PDF layouts. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Context You can use supplier groups for the following purposes: • 204 Customization projects—With the help of an SAP representative, you can customize the SAP Business Network supplier user interface by creating a customization project [page 130]. You can then assign the customization project to specific supplier groups. A customization project can be used to do several things, such as customize supplier profile requirements, add invoice or ship notice fields, control the behavior of order confirmation fields, or enable CSV invoices. PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management • Transaction rules—You can use supplier groups to organize your suppliers according to different order confirmation and ship notice rules [page 65], service sheet rules [page 84], and invoicing rules [page 91], including country-based rules [page 110]. If you subscribe to an SAP Ariba invoice conversion services (ICS) solution, you can create supplier groups for the suppliers who send paper invoices to the ICS provider. Typically, buying organizations want the invoice rules for ICS invoices to be less stringent than the rules for non-ICS invoices, to prevent some of the automatic validation that occurs with the default rules. For more information about invoice conversion, see the SAP Business Network Guide to Invoice Conversion. • Discount management—If your organization uses SAP Ariba Invoice Management or SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing with an SAP Ariba payment module, and discount management is enabled for these solutions, you can define multiple discount offers and then assign them to supplier groups. • Custom PDF layouts—With the help of an SAP representative, you can define custom PDF layouts for purchase orders [page 218] and ship notices [page 219] and then assign them to supplier groups. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . The Supplier Groups page appears. Figure 26: Supplier Groups Page 2. Click Create. The Supplier Group page appears. 3. Enter a meaningful group name and description and click OK. Suppliers do not see your group names or descriptions. 4. To change transaction rules for the group, click Supplier Group Transaction Rules. The Supplier Group Transaction Rules page appears. The settings you make here affect only this group of suppliers. 5. When you are finished configuring transaction rules, click OK to save your settings and close the Supplier Group Transaction Rules page. 6. Click OK to save the supplier group. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 205 Related Information Custom PDF Layouts [page 217] Modifying Supplier Groups You can modify a supplier group by adding or removing suppliers from them. You can also search for suppliers within a group. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. • If you defined a custom PDF layout for purchase orders or ship notices, an SAP Ariba Support representative must upload the PDF layout file (an XSLT file) to your account and configure the layout before you can assign it to supplier groups.  Restriction You cannot delete supplier groups after creating them, but they can be disabled and hidden. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . SAP Business Network lists your supplier groups. 2. Click the name of the group you want to modify. 3. To add suppliers to this group: a. Click Add Members. b. Search for suppliers to add to the group. You can search only for your current suppliers. You can search for the supplier’s company name or ANID. c. When you find the supplier you want to add, select it and click OK. SAP Business Network adds the supplier to the group. 4. Locate suppliers to remove from this group or assign group members to another group: a. Enter the name of a supplier at the top right of the Group Members table and click Search. SAP Business Network performs a match based on exactly the value you specify. For example, entering “acme” returns all suppliers listed as “acme” or “ACME.” This field is not case-sensitive. you can search only for your current suppliers. b. Scroll down through the list of displayed group members. The list includes only the first 200 suppliers in the group. If you do not see the supplier you are looking for, use the Search feature. 206 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management 5. Select the suppliers you want to remove or assign to another group. 6. Do one of the following: • • To remove suppliers, click Remove Members. To assign suppliers to another group, click Assign Group. Assign the suppliers to another group and click OK. 7. To change invoice rules for the group, click Supplier Group Transaction Rules. The settings you make here affect only this group of suppliers. If you subscribe to an ICS solution, you can configure one supplier group as the group to which SAP Business Network adds new suppliers created through ICS quick enablement. The check box Use this group for suppliers created through the Invoice Conversion service can be selected for one supplier group only. For details, see the SAP Business Network Guide to Invoice Conversion. If you want to change invoice rules for suppliers that belong to a country/region that requires specific invoice rule, specify them. Click View Invoice Rule Results to view invoice rules based on a supplier group level, default transaction group level, or country/region level. 8. In the Custom PDF Layouts section, find Purchase Order Layouts or Ship Notice Layouts and click Assign Layouts. a. Select one or more layouts to assign to the group.  Note If the Assignment List is empty, there are no custom PDF layouts configured for your account. b. Click Save. c. Click Done to close the Supplier Group Layout Assignment page. 9. Click OK. Related Information Invoice Rules [page 91] Overriding Your Rules and Preferences for a Supplier [page 201] Custom PDF Layouts [page 217] Assigning Suppliers to a Supplier Group For easier configuration, you can assign suppliers to a supplier group. The group's transaction rules apply to all its members. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 207 Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . SAP Business Network lists your supplier groups. 2. Select suppliers you want to assign to a group. 3. Click Actions and choose Assign Supplier Group. 4. Click the supplier group to assign the selected supplier and click OK. Assigning Multiple Vendors to a Supplier Group On the Manage Vendors page, you can assign multiple vendors to a supplier group. The vendors can include active suppliers. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure Supplier Enablement 1. Choose Manage Vendors . SAP Business Network displays the Manage Vendors page. 2. Select the vendors you want to assign to a supplier group. 3. Click Actions Assign to Supplier Group . SAP Business Network displays the Assign to Supplier Group dialog box. 4. Choose the supplier group to which you want to assign the selected vendors. 5. Click Assign. 6. Click Done. The vendors are now members of the assigned supplier group. You must refresh the Manage Vendors page to view the updated information. 208 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Assigning Suppliers and Vendors to a Supplier Group Using Vendor CSV Upload You can assign suppliers and vendors to a supplier group by uploading a vendor CSV file. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308].  Restriction If multiple vendors are uploaded with different supplier groups specified, and each vendor corresponds to the same supplier account, the supplier account is assigned to the last-specified supplier group. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . SAP Business Network displays the Manage Vendors page. 2. Click Upload. SAP Business Network displays the Upload Vendors page. 3. Complete the following steps if you do not have a completed vendor CSV file: a. Click Download Template on the Upload Vendors page to download the vendor CSV file template. b. Enter supplier details, including supplier group information in the AN Supplier Group column, in the vendor CSV file template. c. Save the vendor CSV file. 4. Enter a name of the vendor CSV file you are uploading in the Name field. 5. Click Choose File and browse for your saved vendor CSV file, then click Open. SAP Business Network displays the warning, “Existing supplier groups might get replaced with the newly uploaded supplier group if present in the Vendor row” if values have been entered in the Group column of the CSV file. 6. Click Upload. SAP Business Network validates the uploaded vendor CSV file and displays its name, status and other information in the Upload Details table. You must click Refresh Status to view any updated changes. If the vendor CSV file is valid and does not create any errors, suppliers without a supplier group are assigned to the supplier group in the vendor CSV file, and suppliers that are members of a different supplier group are reassigned to the supplier group in the vendor CSV file. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 209 Configuring Invoice Rules by Supplier Group Supplier groups can have different invoice rules than those defined in the Default Transaction Rules for your SAP Business Network account. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . 2. Click a supplier group link or click Create to create a new supplier group. 3. On the Edit Supplier Group page, click Supplier Group Transaction Rules. 4. The default rule settings are displayed. Select Enter supplier group specific transaction rules and override the default rules. 5. Click Done. 6. Click OK to save the supplier group. Removing a Supplier from a Supplier Group You can remove a supplier from a supplier group at any time. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Select the supplier you want to remove from the group. 3. Click Actions and choose Remove From Supplier Group. 210 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: Deactivating Unused Supplier Groups If a supplier group isn’t used anymore, you can deactivate it. You can’t delete a supplier group after creating it.  Restriction Before they can be deactivated, supplier groups must not contain any supplier or vendor members and they must not be used for suppliers created through Invoice Conversion Services (ICS). Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . 2. Click Deactivate in the row of the supplier group you want to deactivate. 3. Click Yes to confirm the deactivation. Hiding Supplier Groups To simplify the Supplier Groups page, you can hide supplier groups that have been deactivated. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308].  Restriction Supplier groups must be deactivated before they can be hidden. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . 2. Click Hide Deactivated Supplier Groups. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 211 Reactivating Supplier Groups If you deactivated a supplier group temporarily, you can reactivate it and assign suppliers to it again. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Groups . 2. Click Show Deactivated Supplier Groups if the Deactivated Supplier Groups table is hidden. 3. Click Activate in the row of the deactivated supplier group you want to activate. 4. Click Yes to confirm the activation. Custom Routing Method for Suppliers You might have suppliers that have invested in a non-SAP Business Network business-to-business integration data format system and protocol to support their existing customer integrations. You can continue to standardize your business processes using SAP Business Network while allowing these suppliers to retain their existing infrastructure and processes to transact with you on SAP Business Network. Using an intermediary between SAP Business Network and the supplier, you can map cXML documents from SAP Business Network to the format required by the supplier and route documents between the supplier and SAP Business Network. To route your documents to the intermediary, you configure a custom routing method. The following overview describes the process to set up custom routing: 1. Identify the suppliers that require a custom routing method. 2. Contact SAP Ariba Support and request enablement for custom routing. 3. SAP Ariba Support obtains the list of your suppliers that require custom routing and set up these suppliers on SAP Business Network. SAP Ariba Support then configures your account to use the custom routing method. 4. Choose the suppliers that require the custom routing method in your SAP Business Network account. 5. Your suppliers are contacted and provided instructions on setting up their account. Once the supplier's account is configured, they receive a confirmation notification. 6. The supplier configures their SAP Business Network accounts to send and receive documents from their business application to you over SAP Business Network using the custom routing method. You can view details on the custom routing methods when you generate a Supplier Profile report. 212 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Configuring Your Account to Use a Custom Routing Method You can enable a custom routing method to support suppliers that require it. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Contact SAP Ariba Customer Support and request enablement for custom routing. Once your account is configured, sign in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . SAP Business Network lists your current suppliers. 3. Select the suppliers that require a custom routing method. 4. Click Actions and choose Activate Custom Routing. Commodity and Sales Territory Mappings You can bulk upload commodity and sales territory information to Vendor profiles in your SAP Business Network Vendor Master. After the supplier takes ownership of their account, further commodity and sales territory uploads do not impact the supplier’s profile. Uploaded commodities should be in UNSPSC version 14 format. To upload non-UNSPSC taxonomy commodities to SAP Business Network, corresponding mappings must exist in your sourcing realm. Uploading Commodity and Sales Territory Mappings You can map the custom commodity, currency, and unit of measurement values in your ERP system to values in SAP Business Network. A commodity code map translates custom commodity codes in one domain to another domain, such as UNSPSC. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with supplier enablement permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 213  Restriction If a vendor’s profile has missing commodity and sales territories information, then the vendor may not be matched to the RFQ posting in the Matched Vendor case. Context This mapping ensures that the custom taxonomy in your ERP system is mapped to values in SAP Business Network when you upload your suppliers from your ERP system. During vendor matched supplier enablement, the mapping allows existing suppliers in your vendor master to be matched to RFQ postings based on commodity and sales territories. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement 2. Choose Upload Manage Vendors . Supplier Commodity Codes and Sales Territories . The Upload Supplier Commodity Codes and Sales Territories page appears. 3. Click Download Template to download the supplier commodity codes and sales territories template. 4. Upload a CSV file with the supplier commodity codes and sales territories you want to add to your SAP Business Network profile. Details uploaded will be added incrementally to your existing commodities and sales territories.  Note The maximum recommended upload file size is 10MB. Your browser might time out for larger files.You can use a zip utility to compress CSV File before uploading it. Zipped files must have a .ZIP file extension. 5. Click Done. Supplier Contacts Individuals within your company can serve as contacts for current and potential trading partners. Before you can assign individuals in your company as specific contact types, you must create a pool of contact personnel. Suppliers need to know whom to contact within your company with various inquiries, ranging from initial contacts to technical questions related to your SAP Business Network account. Managing Contact Assignments [page 215] Managing Supplier Contact Types [page 216] 214 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Managing Contact Assignments You can assign individuals in your company to serve as contacts for current and potential trading partners. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the Contact Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. • For each individual, you must provide a first and last name, and either a valid email address or a phone number. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Contacts . The Contacts page appears. Figure 27: Contacts Page 2. To create a new contact person, do the following: a. Click Create. The Create New Contact page appears. b. Enter the first and last names of the contact. The Business Title field is optional. c. Enter a valid email address or a phone number, or both, and click Save. SAP Business Network returns to the Contact Personnel page. Your new contact is displayed.  Note When specifying an email address or telephone number, you might want to ask employees which contact method they prefer, to ensure they are prepared to handle inquiries effectively. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 215 3. To edit a person’s contact information, do the following: a. Select the person and click Edit. b. Update the person’s name, contact information, or select a different contact type. To create new contact types, see Managing Supplier Contact Types [page 216]. c. Click Save. 4. To delete a person from your contact personnel pool, select the person and click Delete. Managing Supplier Contact Types You can create custom contact types that suit the way your organization does business. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the Contact Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. • You must add personnel to your list of contact personnel before you make contact assignments. See Managing Contact Assignments [page 215]. Context SAP Business Network provides one standard contact type—Business Contact. You cannot rename or delete this standard contact type. However, you can create custom contact types. Your companywide contact types are visible to all suppliers on SAP Business Network. The individuals who are assigned to these contact types should be prepared to respond to high-level inquiries. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Contacts . 2. Click Companywide Assignments. SAP Business Network displays a list of standard and custom companywide assignments. 3. To create a new type, do the following: a. Click Create. The Create Companywide Assignment page appears. b. Enter a name for the new contact type. This contact type is visible to supplier organizations on SAP Business Network and to others within your company. c. Select an individual from the Contact Person list. d. Click Save. SAP Business Network returns to the Companywide Assignments page and displays the new assignment. 216 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management 4. To edit a contact type, do the following: a. Click the contact type. b. Select a different individual to assign to this contact type. If this is a custom contact type, you can also modify the contact type name. c. Click Save. 5. To delete a custom contact type, click Delete in the Actions column.  Note If you click the Delete link for a standard contact type, SAP Business Network removes the individual who is assigned. You cannot delete standard contact types. Custom PDF Layouts With the help of an SAP Ariba representative, you can define custom PDF layouts for purchase orders and ship notices and then assign them to supplier groups. Enabling This Feature This feature is disabled by default. To enable this feature, please have your Designated Support Contact log a service request. An SAP Ariba Support representative will follow up to complete the request. This feature requires custom XSL-FO stylesheets to be developed before the feature is turned on. You must engage SAP Ariba Services for help with this. Contact your Customer Success Partner (CSP) or Account Manager for more information about SAP Ariba Services. After a custom PDF layout has been configured by SAP Ariba Support for your account, an administrator for your account can assign the layout to supplier groups. See Modifying Supplier Groups [page 206]. Prerequisites • SAP Business Network buyers must request help from SAP Ariba Services to develop XSL-FO stylesheets for custom PDF layouts.  Note If you engage with SAP Ariba Services to develop custom XSL-FO stylesheets for custom PDF layouts, you will incur additional fees. • When XSL-FO stylesheets for custom PDF layouts are ready to be deployed, an SAP Ariba Support representative must upload them to your account. • Suppliers must belong to a supplier group that has been assigned a custom PDF layout to download and print it. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 217 Custom PDF Layouts for Orders [page 218] Ship Notice Barcode Labels [page 219] Custom PDF Layouts for Quality Inspections [page 222] Custom PDF Layouts for Orders You can define custom PDF layouts for purchase orders to • • • Make them consistent with orders that originate from your ERP systems Provide a familiar PDF layout for suppliers Include only required information on the PDF, thus saving paper when printing  Note A custom PDF layout for orders can also include barcode labels. See Supported barcode types [page 220]. Workflow for Custom PDF Layouts for Orders The following describes the workflow for custom PDF layouts for orders: 1. An SAP Business Network customer contacts SAP Ariba Support to engage with SAP Ariba Services to define one or more custom PDF layout templates for orders. The templates are XSL-FO stylesheets. 2. An SAP Ariba Support representative uploads the custom XSL-FO stylesheets to the customer's account. Each custom PDF layout configuration should have a name that clearly identifies its intended purpose (for instance, an intended supplier, industry, or order format). 3. An administrator for the SAP Business Network customer assigns the custom PDF layout to a supplier group. Members of the supplier group can now print an order using the assigned PDF layout. 4. A supplier that belongs to the supplier group opens an order, and clicks Download PDF > LayoutName in the header to download the custom PDF format.  Note LayoutName is a placeholder for the name assigned to the custom PDF layout configuration for orders. There could be multiple PDF layout configurations for different types of orders. 218 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management Figure 28: Custom PDF Layout for Orders Workflow Ship Notice Barcode Labels Buyers can provide suppliers with barcode labels to use for shipments. To facilitate the shipping of goods, SAP Business Network allows suppliers to print barcode labels directly from a ship notice in PDF format. The barcode label is generated from a custom PDF layout that customers can implement for their suppliers with the assistance of SAP Ariba Services. Ship notice barcode labels help buyers and suppliers to accelerate their logistics processes. They can use barcode scanners to quickly scan the barcodes for shipment information for their systems. Barcode label layouts can be applied at the header and the item level of the ship notice, giving suppliers the ability to print a single set of labels containing all the items of a ship notice or a label containing the information for a single line item. The specific fields needed on ship notice barcode labels can vary per customer. The ship notice barcode label layout can gather needed information at runtime from the ship notice cXML, related documents (such as a purchase order), and the buyer's and supplier’s SAP Business Network profile. For information about cXML data you can access from a ship notice or other related SAP Ariba documents, see the cXML reference guide at http:// www.cxml.org . Barcode Label Scenarios for Different Industries This feature flexibly supports different industry scenarios for ship notice barcode labels. For instance, suppliers in the automotive industry may need to generate one barcode label per item, a master barcode label for a grouping of items in a pallet, or a mixed barcode label for a grouping of a set of mixed items in a pallet. At the same time, suppliers in the food industry may require a single barcode label per shipping container. All of these scenarios can be supported by designing and configuring multiple barcode label layouts. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management PUBLIC 219 Figure 29: Barcode Label Scenarios: Automotive Industry Figure 30: Barcode Label Scenario: Food Industry Supported Barcode Types SAP Business Network uses Barcode4J 2.1 to generate barcodes. The Barcode4J library supports the following 1D and 2D barcode types: • • • • • • Codabar 220 PUBLIC Interleaved 2 of 5 ITF-14 Code 39 Code 128 EAN-128, GS1-128 (based on Code 128) SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Supplier Management
