file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: Supplier Remittance Information Reports Supplier remittance information reports provide a summary of your suppliers requested payment details, including the remit to information, preferred payment method, ACH pre-note status, and financial institution account information. These reports are helpful to track changes your suppliers make to their address, preferred payment method, and bank account information.  Note To run this report, you must have the Supplier Remittance Information Report permission and have set up your SAP Business Network account for ACH payment. Supplier Remittance Information Report Criteria Field Description Date Range From/To Select the range of accepted dates you want to include in the report. By default, the report includes one week preceding today’s date. The narrower the range, the quicker the search. Max Results Returned Select the maximum number of records returned by the report. By default, the report returns up to 100 records. Related Information SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308] Setting Up ACH Payment [page 360] Payment Transactions Reports [page 255] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers PUBLIC 281 Tax Book Reports Tax book reports contain tax information from invoices, including information related to VAT. Suppliers can also generate this report. Tax Book Report Criteria Field Description Supplier By default all suppliers are selected for inclusion in the report. To limit the report to specific suppliers, click Select and then select suppliers for the report. Created Date Select the range of creation dates you want to include in the report. Tax Book Report Fields Field Description Invoice # The unique invoice number. Date The date and time of the invoice. Buyer The name and address of the buying organization. Derived from the Sold To Address in the invoice. If Sold To information is not available, SAP Business Network uses BillTo information. Buyer VAT ID The buying organization’s VAT ID. Supplier The name and address of the supplier. Derived from the IssuerOfInvoice address in the invoice. If the IssuerOfInvoice information is not available, SAP Business Network uses From information. Supplier VAT ID The supplier’s VAT ID. Tax Representative The name and address of the tax representative. Tax Representative VAT ID The tax representative’s VAT ID. Report Line ID The source of the tax data: • • • 0, which indicates a header field 1, which indicates the first tax rate and location 2, which indicates the second tax rate and location Tax Rates The rate used to calculate the amount of tax. Currency The default currency for the tax amount. Tax Amount The amount of tax in the default currency. Alternate Currency When suppliers use a different currency to calculate tax, this second tax amount is displayed in the Tax Amount in Alternate Currency column. The currency used for this is displayed in the Alternate Currency column. 282 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers Field Description Tax Amount in Alternate Currency The amount of tax in the alternate currency, if any. Shipping Amount The shipping amount. Special Handling Amount The special handling amount, if any. Discount Amount The discount amount, if any. Net Amount The net amount. Due Amount The due amount. Tax Point Date The date of supply. Tax Description An optional description of the tax. Used to explain zero-rate VAT. Ship From Country The country/region from which the transaction occurred. Ship To Country The country/region to which the transaction occurred. Cross Border Trade Indicates whether the transaction is across a country/region’s border. Intra EU Trade Indicates whether the transaction is within the EU. Converted Data Indicates whether the invoice was generated electronically or created manually by the buyer. Status The invoice document status level [page 418], such as sent. Vendor Data Export Reports Vendor Data Export reports contain all vendor profiles. The profile details also include changes made online to the existing saved data. To run this report, you need the Supplier Enablement Program Administrator permission.  Restriction • • Suppliers cannot generate this report. This report is not available for test accounts. The Vendor Data Export Report fields are the same as in the vendor CSV file [page 175]. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers PUBLIC 283 Messaging Reports A messaging report contains messages exchanged between you and your trading partners on SAP Business Network. Messaging Report Criteria Field Description Supplier (or Buyer) Select the trading partner with whom you had the conversation with. Context Select Context Free or Purchase Order. Context Free means the conversation is not associated with any documents. Purchase Order means the conversation is associated with specific purchase orders. Status Select Open or Closed. Initial Participant From Select the originating source of the message, whether the message is initiated from SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba Procurement Solution, or SAP Ariba Sourcing. Created On Select the date when the conversation was initiated. Maximum Results Returned Select 100, 200, 500, 1000, or 10000. Messaging Report Fields Field Description Date Date of the initiation of the conversation. Subject Subject of the conversation. Message Content of the message. Context Context of the message, whether it is related to an invoice or purchase order, or if it is a context-free message, or a broadcast message. Document Reference Invoice number or the purchase order number to which the message is related. For contextfree messages, this field is blank. Created By ANID of the creator of the post. 284 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers Generating Messaging Reports Context A messaging report contains messages exchanged between you and your trading partners on SAP Business Network. To generate a messaging report, follow the steps below: Procedure 1. Sign in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Analytics Reports . 3. On the Reports page, in the Report Templates section, click Create. 4. In the Select report type popup, select the required report type. 5. In the New Object, go to the Report Description tab and enter the following details: • • • • • • Report Type: You already added this in the previous step. Title: Add a title for the report. This is a mandatory field. Description: Provide additional details about the purpose of the report. Format: Select the output format for the generated report. Comma-Separated Values (*.csv) and Microsoft Excel (*.xlsx) are supported. Time Zone: Choose the time zone applicable for the report data. Language: Select the language in which the report is generated. 6. Go to the Report Criteria tab and select the required values for the following fields: • • • • • • Supplier (or Buyer): Select the trading partner with whom you had the conversation with. Context: Select Context Free or Purchase Order. Context Free means the conversation is not associated with any documents. Purchase Order means the conversation is associated with specific purchase orders. Status: Select Open or Closed Initial Participant From: Select the originating source of the message, whether the message is initiated from SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba Procurement Solution, or SAP Ariba Sourcing. Created On: Select the date when the conversation was initiated. Maximum Results Returned: Select 100, 200, 500, 1000, or 10000.  Note 7. This step is available only to buyers. On the Report Schedule tab, select one of the following: • • Manual Report Scheduled Report: • • If you select this, enter the Date Range and Automatically Run schedule. Add your email address under Email Notification to receive notifications when the report is generated.  Note The Report Schedule setting is only available to buyers. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers PUBLIC 285 8. Click Save. 9. Click Back to return to the Reports page. 10. Select the created Report Template and click Run. 11. Click Go to execute the report. The task is queued for processing. Wait until the status changes to Processed. 12. Once processed, click the download icon in the Action column to retrieve the report file. Generate and Download Reports SAP Business Network generates reports in the order in which they enter the queue. When the report is finished, its status is “Processed.” Regardless of the actual start time, the report will collect information for the date range and time zone specified in the template. The exact timing of a report run might differ from one run to the next, but the coverage period is always determined by the criteria in the template. To keep a record of report files, download each report file to your computer hard disk before running the report again. You can download any report to your local drive that SAP Business Network has generated successfully. The next time you generate the report, SAP Business Network overwrites the current version with a new report file. SAP Business Network saves reports in CSV (comma separated value) or XLSX format, viewable in spreadsheet applications, such as Microsoft Excel. If a report file is larger than 1 MB, SAP Business Network stores it in zip format and displays a zip icon in the Size column for that report. Generating and Downloading Reports [page 286] Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters [page 287] Generating and Downloading Reports When you generate a report or edit and save an existing report, SAP Business Network puts the report into the queue and displays the report status as “Processing” on the Reports page.  Restriction • • Your organization can generate a maximum of 100 reports, including up to 20 scheduled reports. SAP Business Network deletes generated reports from your account after 30 days. Procedure 1. Choose Reports from the menu bar. 2. To generate a report, select the report that you want to generate and click Run. If you want to download the existing version of the report, skip this step and go to step 3. 286 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers SAP Business Network adds your report to the queue and returns you to the Reports page. To update the statuses of reports on the Reports page, click Refresh Status. You can view and download the report when its status changes to “Processed.” 3. To view and download the report, select the report template and click Download. Click one of the following: • • Open to view the report. Your browser starts Microsoft Excel and displays the report. Save to save the report to your hard disk. Related Information Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters [page 287] Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters Use this procedure to change encoding and delimiter settings of files that include double-byte or accented characters, which prevent correct display in some applications. Context To keep a record of a scheduled report, save the report to your hard disk each time the report runs. If a report file is over 1 MB, SAP Business Network stores it in zip format and displays a zip icon in the Size column for that report. SAP Business Network deletes generated reports from your account after 30 days. Procedure 1. Choose Reports from the menu bar. 2. Select the report and click Download. Start a text viewer. 7. Click to open a file. 8. Choose All Files in the Files of type list. 9. Select the file you want to open. 10. Choose Unicode in the Encoding list. If your browser prompts you to overwrite the existing file of the same name, click Yes. 13. Close the file and close the text viewer. 14. Start a spreadsheet application. 15. Click to open a file. 16. Choose All Files in the Files of type list. 17. Open your saved report file. 18. The file displays in the spreadsheet application 288 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Reports for SAP Business Network Buyers Data Analytics SAP Business Network, powered by SAP Analytics Cloud, offers data analytics related to your procurement activities. Information is presented as predefined stories (presentation-style documents that describe data) in the Analytics dashboard in the SAP Business Network user interface for buyers. A story is a presentation-style document that uses charts, visualizations, text, and images to describe data. Users can use the available filters in each story to view the data that they want. The following Predefined Stories [page 289] are displayed: • • • • Purchase Orders Overview Invoices Overview Transactions Overview Delivery execution Users with the Analytics dashboard access role permission can access the predefined stories in the Analytics dashboard under Reports on the menu bar. Users can only view the predefined stories. They cannot edit them or create new stories. Buyer administrators add the Analytics dashboard access permission to one or more roles, and assign the roles to users to grant them access to the Analytics dashboard. Buyer administrators must first activate the analytics functionality before they can grant Analytics dashboard access to users. Related Information Activating the Analytics Functionality in Your SAP Business Network Buyer Account [page 158] Predefined Stories Predefined stories offer data analytics related to your procurement activities. For information on accessing the stories, see Data Analytics [page 289]. Purchase Orders Overview The Purchase Orders Overview story presents a high-level overview of data related to purchase orders as a series of charts. You can choose to view either the number of orders or total order amounts in relation to the following dimensions: SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Data Analytics PUBLIC 289 • • • • • • • • • Order Date Supplier Name Supplier Country Order Status Company Code Purchasing Group Purchasing Organization System ID Vendor ID You can also filter data by these dimensions and their attributes or hierarchies. For customers that have a high volume of data, the date filter includes quarter as the only filtering option. Invoices Overview The Invoices Overview story presents a high-level overview of data related to invoices as a series of charts. You can choose to view either the total invoice amounts or number of orders in relation to the following dimensions: • • • • • • • • • • Invoice Date Supplier Name Original Currency Invoice Status Company Code Purchasing Group Purchasing Organization System ID Vendor ID Reference You can also filter data by these dimensions and their attributes or hierarchies. For customers that have a high volume of data, the date filter includes quarter as the only filtering option. Transactions Overview The Transactions Overview story presents a high-level overview of data related to all transactions sent to and received from suppliers, as a series of charts. You can view data aggregated by the following measures and dimensions: 290 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Data Analytics

For customers that have a high volume of data, the date filter includes quarter as the only filtering option. You can filter the data by year (for customers with high volume of data only filter by quarter is available), supplier name, company code, purchasing org and purchasing group, system ID and vendor ID. Delivery Execution Prerequisite To view the Delivery execution story, you must be enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Description The Delivery execution story presents a high-level overview of the suppliers in terms of delivery of ordered goods measured against requested delivery dates and ordered quantities. Delivery execution is measured by the Items delivered on time, Items delivered in full, and Perfect delivery key performance indicators (KPIs). Dates and quantities in receipts are compared against requested delivery dates and quantities in purchase orders to calculate the KPIs and assess delivery execution. A delivery is considered to be on time if the receipt date is earlier than or same as the requested delivery date, and it is considered to be in full if the received quantity is same as the requested quantity. A delivery is considered to be perfect if it is both on time and in full. For orders with multiple receipts, the latest receipt’s date is taken into consideration to assess whether an order is on time, and the sum of the received quantity of all the receipts is taken into consideration to assess whether an order is delivered in full. In case the buyer sends goods receipts of type return or reversal, then the sum of received quantity to be used for in full metrics calculation will be calculated net of any returns or reversals. However the return and reversal goods receipts will not impact the on time delivery KPI as they do not represent actual deliveries. The story displays delivery execution metrics for your entire supply chain and at a supplier level for the previous month by default. Please note you will not be able to see supplier level data for more than 3000 suppliers at once. You can also filter data by supplier and by month using the Supplier Name and Requested delivery month filters. The delivery execution KPIs per supplier per month are calculated as follows: • Items delivered on time: The percent of items delivered on time, calculated by dividing the total count of line items delivered on time by the total count of line items evaluated. • Items delivered in full: The percent of items delivered in full, calculated by dividing the total count of line items delivered in full by the total count of line items evaluated. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Data Analytics PUBLIC 291 • Perfect delivery: The percent of items delivered on time and in full, calculated by dividing the total count of line items delivered on time and in full by the total count of line items evaluated. The following types of line items are excluded from the calculations: • • • • • 292 Line items without goods receipts Line items with multiple schedule lines Blanket purchase order line items Service line items Line items associated with product returns PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide Data Analytics SAP Business Network Users and Roles By creating roles and then adding users to them, the SAP Business Network administrator controls who can sign in to your organization’s account and which areas of the service each user can access. SAP Business Network Roles [page 293] SAP Business Network Users [page 298] SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308] Revoke User Access and Remove a User's Personal Information [page 317] Configure Retention Period and Manage Deletion of Revoked Users in SAP Business Network [page 320] Prevention of Manual Sign In by SAP Business Network Buyer Users [page 321] Multifactor Authentication [page 322] SAP Business Network Roles A user with the Administrator role can create a role with certain permissions and assign the role to a buyer user. A role defines a user function within SAP Business Network, such as Purchase Order Generator. Each role has a unique name and set of associated permissions that specify what users who are assigned to the role can see and do in SAP Business Network. A role can be assigned to any number of users. Using the Administrator Role After you complete registration, SAP Business Network creates a single default role named Administrator. The Administrator role is automatically linked to the user name and sign in that you entered during registration. The Administrator role should be assigned to the individual at your organization who is responsible for setting configuration options, managing supplier relationships and contacts, and maintaining the account over time. The account administrator serves as the primary point of contact for users with questions or problems. As the SAP Business Network account administrator, you control who can sign in to your organization’s SAP Business Network account and which areas of the service each user can access. To do this, you create roles and then add users. As a best practice, create roles that reflect the way your company does business to prevent confusion for your account users and maximize the efficiency of your team once roles are in place. Only one SAP Business Network user can be assigned to the Administrator role. You cannot modify this role, but you can assign it to another user. The account administrator can assign user management capabilities to non-administrator buyer users, called user administrators. For more information, see the following topics: • • Transferring Administration Ownership [page 305] Assigning User Management Capabilities to Users [page 306] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 293 SAP Business Network Predefined Roles Predefined roles are visible only in accounts that were created before roles and permissions were introduced on SAP Business Network. If you registered with SAP Business Network after roles and permissions were implemented, Administrator is the only predefined role. To minimize disruption to these older users, SAP Business Network provides a small set of predefined roles to be used as templates for custom roles. SAP Business Network assigned the Full Access role to all preexisting users when it introduced roles and permissions. Administrators for these older supplier accounts should review the predefined roles and their permissions and consider using them as the basis for custom roles. The predefined roles are listed in the following table: This Role… Grants a User Access To… Administrator All areas of the account, including Catalog Manager Catalogs Settings Users and test account management Customer Catalogs Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Catalog Service Full Access All areas of SAP Business Network, except areas that are reserved for administrators Purchasing Manager Give access to incoming and outgoing transaction documents and the following configuration pages: Vendor Manager Account Settings Manage Profile Default Transaction Rules Account Settings Manage Profile cXML Setup Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Supplier Enablement Current Relationships Supplier Enablement Contacts Account Settings Manage Profile Account Settings Company Profile Product Manager Catalogs Network Catalog Product Approver Catalogs Network Catalog Notifications (transaction-related notifications only) Supplier The Administrator role includes all available permissions. These permissions grant the Administrator role access to all areas of your SAP Business Network account. Creating a Role [page 295] Modifying a Role [page 296] Reassigning Users to a Different Role [page 297] Deleting a Role [page 298] 294 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles Creating a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can define new roles with a specific set of user permissions that determine what the assigned users can see or do in SAP Business Network. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. • Before creating your first role, you might want to review the list of permissions. This list is useful for planning your approach to roles. Some companies create broadly defined roles that include all or most of the available permissions, while others create specialized roles that include narrow sets of permissions. By planning your approach to roles, you can prevent confusion for your account users and maximize the efficiency of your team after roles are in place. • Before creating new roles, use the Permission dropdown menu to filter the Roles table for existing roles that already include that permission. Context A role defines a user function within SAP Business Network. You assign roles when you create users.  Restriction • • You can create no more than 25 custom roles. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Before you make changes, you might want to inform users who will be affected. Procedure 1. Choose The Account Settings Account Settings Users SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles Settings Users . page appears with the Manage Roles tab selected by default. PUBLIC 295 Figure 34: Manage Roles Tab 2. Click the Create Role icon  at the top right of the role results table. 3. Enter a distinctive name for the role. 4. Enter a description to record your intentions for this role. Descriptions can be useful later, if you want to review or revise the structure of your roles. 5. Select one or more permissions for the new role. Each role must have at least one permission.  Note You can also select all permissions by clicking on the checkbox at the top left of the list of permissions. 6. Click Save. Results SAP Business Network creates the role and returns you to the Manage Roles page. Modifying a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can edit a role's name, description, and assigned permissions. Prerequisites • 296 You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles • You have informed users about role changes that can affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, search for a Permission using the search filters, or scroll down and locate the role you want to modify. 3. In the Role Name column of the search results table, select the role you want to modify. 4. Check Show me all the available permissions and select the permissions you want or uncheck the permissions you don't want for that role. 5. Choose Save. SAP Business Network applies your changes to all users assigned to the role. Changes take effect for each user at their next sign in. Reassigning Users to a Different Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can change the role assigned to users. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. • You have informed users about role changes that will affect them.SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, scroll down to the role you want to investigate. 3. Click the role in the Role Name column. 4. Scroll down to the Assigned Users table. 5. Using the checkboxes, select the users you want to move to another role. 6. Click Move to another role. 7. Click Save to return to the Manage Roles page. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 297 Deleting a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can delete roles that they no longer need. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. • You have informed users about role changes that will affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. • No users can be assigned the role you want to delete. To change a user to another role, see Reassigning Users to a Different Role [page 297]. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, you can perform a search for the role you want to delete, if necessary. Search for a Permission using the search filters. Or, scroll down and locate the role you want to delete. 3. In the Actions column of the roles results table, click the Delete  icon. Results SAP Business Network deletes the role and returns to the Users page. SAP Business Network Users Access to a buyer account is secured with individual user identities and levels of permissions. A user is an SAP Business Network sign in (user name and password) that enables one individual in your organization to sign in to your account. The administrator adds users to the SAP Business Network account and assigns each user exactly one role, which typically corresponds to the user’s real-world job responsibilities. 298 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles Best Practices in Managing User Accounts When the administrator of an SAP Business Network account creates users and assigns roles, it is mandatory that the administrator assigns a unique user name with an appropriate assigned role for each individual who needs to access the account. Users must not share their user name or password with other users. This is important for SAP Business Network and your company in managing data privacy and integrity on SAP Business Network. For security, account administrators and users who have PCard access but are not the PCard owner are required to update their password every 90 days. As a best practice, users should not share their secret question and secret answer. To ensure your organization and users have secure accounts on SAP Business Network, create individual user accounts for different roles in the organization. By default, add one role per user. Users can have multiple related roles, depending on the tasks assigned to the user. How Roles Control User Interface Access Every user can see the Configuration Personal Information area, which contains basic contact information and a preferred language setting for that specific user. Beyond that, the only areas that a user is permitted to see are those allowed by their role permissions. For example, if the administrator created a role that included the Contact Administration permission, a user assigned to that role could see only the Information area and the Supplier Enablement Configuration Personal Contacts area of your SAP Business Network account. While users can update their own personal information, the administrator is responsible for overall user maintenance, which includes deleting users or reassigning user sign ins when individuals leave the company, and resetting user passwords. Enter a user name, email address, first and last name, and optionally a phone number for this user. 5. Select a role in the Role Assignment section. 6. Scroll down and click Done. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 301 • The Table Options Menu controls what columns to show in the user results table. After you create a user, SAP Business Network sends an email message to that user with a randomly generated password. Each new user should sign in and change the password to something they can remember. Next Steps • • Remind users to store their user names and passwords in a safe place. • If a user forgets their password, an administrator can reset it. You can change a user’s role assignment at any time. See Changing a User’s Role and Resetting the Password [page 302]. • If an employee leaves your company or changes jobs, and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account, an administrator can delete the user. See Deleting a User [page 304]. Users who forget their user name can go to the Sign In page, click Forgot User Name and follow the instructions for regaining access to their account. Changing a User’s Role and Resetting the Password You can select a different role for an existing user or reset the password. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Context Users can forget their sign in information if they do not sign in to SAP Business Network regularly. SAP Business Network provides a secure and relatively quick way for users to recover sign in information. However, even with this process in place, loss of user names and passwords can cause frustration and lost productivity for you and your users. If you do not want to reset a user’s password, instruct him or her to click Forgot Your Password? on the SAP Business Network Sign In page. After a user submits a user name, SAP Business Network Accounts Services sends the user an email containing steps to reset the password. 302 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Cick Edit for the user whose password you want to reset. 4. Do one of the following: • • To change a user’s role, select a different role in the Role Assignment section and click Save. To reset the user’s password, click Reset Password. 5. Click Save. SAP Business Network returns to the Users page. Results If you reset the user’s password, SAP Business Network sends an email to the user containing a new randomlygenerated password. The password update takes effect immediately. Reassigning a User Sign In If a user has left the company, you can reassign that user’s sign-in to another individual, to retain the user setup and data. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Context When an employee leaves the company or changes jobs and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account in their name, the administrator should either delete the user or reassign the user’s sign-in to another individual. If you want to retain the user’s setup and data, reassign the sign-in. If you want to delete the user’s setup and data, delete the user. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 303 Procedure 1. Sign in using the user’s user name and password. If you do not know the password, click 2. Choose Account Settings Help Support to contact SAP Business Network Support. Manage Profile . 3. On the Configuration page, choose Personal Information. 4. Change the user name and password and optionally other information. 5. Click OK. 6. On the Configuration page, choose Notifications. 7. Make any modifications to notification emails based on the user sign in reassignment. 8. Click OK. Deleting a User If a user has left the company, you can delete the user to prevent its further use to access SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Context When an employee leaves the company or changes jobs and no longer uses the SAP Business Network account, the administrator should either delete the user or reassign the user’s sign in to another individual. • • If you want to retain the user’s setup and data, reassign the sign in. See Reassigning a User Sign In [page 303]. If you want to delete the user’s setup and data, perform this procedure. User deletion is permanent. There is no way for SAP Business Network or you to recover a deleted user. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Search for the user you want to delete. See Creating a User [page 300] for the steps to perform. 304 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles 4. In the user results table, check the checkbox for the user you want to delete. 5. In the Actions column, click the Delete  icon in the row of the user you want to delete. Results SAP Business Network deletes the account and refreshes the page content. It does not maintain a record of deleted users. Transferring Administration Ownership The current account administrator can reassign ownership of the SAP Business Network account to another person. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Context Account administrators can quickly and easily transfer the Administrator role to another user. After the Administrator role is transferred to a new user, SAP Business Network sends a notification to the new account administrator, alerting them that they now have the Administrator role.  Note If you do not know who the account administrator is, contact SAP Business Network Support. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Select the user you want to transfer the Administrator role to. 4. Choose Actions Make Administrator . The Assign a Role page opens. 5. Select a new role for your account, and click Assign. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 305 Assigning User Management Capabilities to Users The current account administrator can create a role with the User Administration permission and assign it to nonadministrator buyer users, called user administrators. User administrators can perform administrative functions, such as tasks relevant to user management and buyer user access to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles page, click the  icon. 3. Enter a distinctive name for the role. Enter a description to record your intentions for this role. 4. Go to the last page of permissions, and select the User Administration permission. 5. Click Save. 6. Click Manage Users. 7. On the Manage Users page, select the user you want to assign the user administrator role to. 8. Choose Actions Edit . 9. In the Role Assignment area of the Edit User page, select the user administrator role you created. 10. Click Save. Mass Uploading Users Using an Excel Template Account and user administrators can create and update users through mass upload using an Excel template. Using an Excel template, user administrators can perform the following actions: create or update users, assign roles, assign business units, authorization profile assignments. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. • For the mass upload capability using an Excel template, all required fields must be filled out in the Excel template before uploading it. • List of the required fields in the Excel template: 306 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles • • • • • • • • • Action User Name Corporate User Name (if SSO is enabled) Email Address First Name Last Name Has Limited Access; if this value is set to "No", at least one role must be assigned Only Excel files in the .XLSX format can be uploaded Only five roles, business units, and authorization profiles can be assigned using an Excel template. These roles, business units, and authorization profiles must exist already, and cannot be created using Excel upload. If additional ones are needed, they can be added from the user interface. • Change of first name, last name, or email address fields is not allowed when updating user details using Excel upload, consistent with the handling in the user interface. • The number of users entered in the Excel file must not exceed 500. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Click the Upload Users button on the Manage Users page. 4. Click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 5. Click the Download template link on the Upload File dialog box. 6. Open the Excel template and fill out the required fields. 7. Click the Browse button on the Upload Files dialog box, choose the filled out Excel template from your computer and enter a descriptive name. 8. Click the Upload button. 9. Click the Refresh Status button on the Upload Users page and wait until it shows status Completed. If the status is Completed With Errors or Failed, select the download icon ( reasons for errors and to correct them. ) in the Log column to see the 10. Click the Done button. This opens the Manage Users page where you can see the uploaded users. Updating Users Using an Excel Template Account and user administrators can update multiple users using an Excel template. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 307 Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. Click the Upload Users button on the Manage Users page. 4. Click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 5. Click the Download template link on the Upload File dialog box. Alternatively, if you already have an uploaded Excel template you can reuse it by selecting the download icon ( page ) in the File column on the Upload Users 6. Open the Excel template and fill out or update the required fields and click the Upload button on the Upload Users page. 7. Click the Browse button on the Upload Files dialog box, choose the Excel template from your computer and enter a descriptive name. 8. Click the Upload button. 9. Click the Refresh Status button on the Upload Users page and wait until it shows status Completed. If the status is Completed With Errors or Failed, select the download icon ( reasons for errors and to correct them. ) in the Log column to see the 10. Click the Done button. This opens the Manage Users page where you can see the updated users. SAP Business Network Permissions A permission grants access to a certain area of the SAP Business Network user interface. Each role includes one or more permissions. For example, the Archive Access permission grants access to the Archived Invoices tab and the functionality of the Invoices area. Any user who is assigned a role that includes the Archive Access permission can access the Archived Invoices tab. You can view the list of available permissions while creating a role. See Creating a Role [page 295]. The Administrator role, which can be assigned to only one user for your account, includes all permissions. Some permissions are exclusive to the Administrator role, and only the user assigned the Administrator role can see them. Grants access to this area: Account Settings Quick Links 316 PUBLIC Manage Announcements Create Announcement SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles Revoke User Access and Remove a User's Personal Information SAP Business Network users can request the administrator for their account to remove their personal information from the system. If approved, the user can’t sign in to SAP Business Network any longer, and their personal information is no longer visible to users, including in transaction documents shared and exchanged with business partners.  Note For audit and compliance purposes, the user's personal information is still visible to the user who is the administrator for your SAP Business Network account. Restrictions • Comments or attachment files associated with transaction documents aren’t affected when users remove personal information. Therefore, avoid entering personal information in comments or attached files. • After a user’s revocation of user access request is approved, their personal information is pseudonymized in SAP Business Network transaction documents. However, transaction documents that were integrated with other systems (such as an ERP) or downloaded before the request was approved may still have the user’s personal information. The customer needs to take additional action, including informing impacted business partners, to remove it. • If a customer needs to re-identify a user that has been pseudonymized for legal purposes, the administrator of the account can provide that information. Workflow for Removing Personal Information for a User from SAP Business Network [page 317] Requesting Removal of Personal Data for a Buyer User [page 318] Approving or Rejecting a Buyer User's Request to Remove Their Personal Information [page 319] Viewing and Exporting Revoked Buyer Users [page 319] Workflow for Removing Personal Information for a User from SAP Business Network This procedure describes the workflow for removing personal information for an SAP Business Network user: Figure 35: Workflow for Removing Personal Information for a User SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 317 1. A user signs in to the SAP Business Network portal to request the removal of their personal information. 2. The administrator for the account receives an email notifying them of the user's request. 3. The administrator signs in to the SAP Business Network portal and approves or rejects the user's request. 4. If the administrator approved the request, the user's personal information is removed. 5. If the administrator approved the request, the user can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Requesting Removal of Personal Data for a Buyer User SAP Business Network users can request the administrator for their account to remove their personal information from the system. If your request is approved, your personal information is removed, and you can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites If you are currently assigned the Administrator role for your account, you can't perform this task until after you transfer the Administrator role to another user. See Transferring Administration Ownership [page 305]. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Manage Profile. 2. Click Personal Information. The Personal Information page opens. 3. In the Personal information usage section, check the Request to remove my personal information option. 4. Click Save. Results The administrator is notified of your request, and they can approve or reject it. 318 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles Approving or Rejecting a Buyer User's Request to Remove Their Personal Information As an administrator, you can approve or reject a user's request to remove their personal information from SAP Business Network. If you approve the request, the user's personal information is removed, and they can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage Users. 3. In the Users table, select the user who requested revocation of access. In the AN Access column, the value is Revocation request pending. 4. Click Actions, and choose one of the following actions: • • Accept Revocation Request Reject Revocation Request 5. Click OK. Viewing and Exporting Revoked Buyer Users As an administrator, you can view the list of revoked users and export the table to an XLS file. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Revoked Users. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 319 3. The Revoked Users table lists all users whose access to SAP Business Network has been revoked.  Tip You can filter the table by User Name, Email Address, or First or Last Name. 4. To export the table, click the  Table Options Menu icon, and choose Export All Rows. Results An XLS file containing the list of revoked users downloads to your computer. Configure Retention Period and Manage Deletion of Revoked Users in SAP Business Network As a buyer administrator, configure a retention period for revoked users. SAP Business Network users can request the administrator of their account to remove their personal information from the system. This is called a revocation request. If the request is approved, users cannot sign in to SAP Business Network any longer, and their personal information is no longer visible to other users. As an administrator, you can configure a retention period for the user data of all the revoked users in your organization. The data of revoked users is automatically removed from SAP Business Network after this retention period is reached. In the meantime, you can view the list of revoked users in the Revoked Users tab. You must have configured the retention period before accepting or rejecting any revocation request. If the retention period for an organization is not configured, SAP Business Network prompts you to configure the retention period before you can act on a revocation request. You can change the retention period at any time before the previously configured retention period is reached. The newly configured retention period takes effect immediately. The retention period must be configured in months, and must be between 1 and 999 months.  Note 320 • Only users with non-administrator roles can request revocation of their access from SAP Business Network. Administrators cannot raise a revocation request. If administrators want to request revocation of their access from SAP Business Network, they must transfer their administrator role to another user. For more information, see Transferring Administration Ownership [page 305]. • Transaction documents such as purchase orders and invoices created by users before they were revoked will remain unchanged in SAP Business Network even after revocation and subsequent permanent deletion of such users. PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: Configuring Retention Period for Revoked Users in Your Organization As an administrator, you can configure the retention period of user data for revoked users in your organization. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Users . 3. Click Manage User Deletion. 4. Enter a retention period between 1 and 999 in the Retention period in months box. The data of all revoked users in your organization will be retained for a period that you configure here. 5. Click Save. • • • • After the retention period is over, user data will be deleted permanently from SAP Business Network. You cannot act upon a revocation request unless you configure the retention period first. Revoked users' data is available for you to view for purposes such as regulatory audits. All the data of an organization (including users' data - both revoked as well as deleted) is deleted when an organization is permanently deleted. Prevention of Manual Sign In by SAP Business Network Buyer Users Buyers whose SAP Business Network accounts are configured for single sign-on (SSO) corporate authentication can prevent users from signing into the SAP Business Network manually, outside of the single sign-on (SSO) configuration. This SAP Business Network feature is applicable to all buyers who use single sign-on (SSO) corporate authentication for accessing the SAP Business Network. This feature does not affect SAP Business Network suppliers. Preventing users from signing in manually enhances the security of SAP Business Network accounts using single sign-on (SSO) authentication. When this feature is enabled, users cannot sign in to the SAP Business Network in any way other than through single sign-on (SSO). They cannot sign in by entering the URL buyer.ariba.com directly into a browser. Even users with the Administrator role cannot sign in manually. Users who try to sign in manually will receive an error message that says The user name and password pair you entered was not found. If this feature is not enabled, users can use their user name and password to manually sign in to the SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 321 Enabling This Feature This feature is disabled by default. To enable this feature, ask your Designated Support Contact to log a case (formerly Service Request). An SAP Business Network Support representative will follow up to complete the request. Enabling the feature involves SAP Business Network setting an option in the single sign-on (SSO) configuration for the SAP Business Network account to disable manual sign in. Multifactor Authentication Multifactor authentication is a two-step verification process where you are required to authenticate yourself a second time using a time-based verification code. As compared to the single step authentication process, the multifactor authentication process provides enhanced security. If multifactor authentication is enabled for critical fields, you are required to perform the two-step verification process while attempting to update the values of critical fields such as email addresses, phone numbers, remittance information and so on. With multifactor authentication enabled for sign in, you are required to perform the two-step verification process to sign in to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network administrators can now enable the following functionalities for users in their organization by selecting the desired users from a table: • • Require multi-factor authentication for critical fields Require multi-factor authentication for login  Note • • Only buyer administrators with the required permissions can disable multifactor authentication for sign ins. SAP Business Network does not prompt newly created users to complete the multifactor authentication setup immediately after a successful sign in. New users are recommended to set up multifactor authentication for sign in after they change their initial password. Prerequisites When multifactor authentication is enabled for your organization, you must install an authenticator application such as SAP Authenticator from iTunes (for iOS devices) or from Google Play (for Android devices) in your hand-held devices to generate a time-based verification code (also called time-based one-time password). The time-based verification code setup is also compatible with third-party authenticators such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator. Enabling Multifactor Authentication for Sign In [page 323] Configuring Multifactor Authentication Settings [page 323] Managing Multifactor Authentication for Users [page 324] Setting Up Multifactor Authentication (Buyer User) [page 325] 322 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles Setting Up Multifactor Authentication Using a New Device (Buyer User) [page 326] Enabling Multifactor Authentication for Sign In Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage User Authentication. The Multi-factor Authentication User Setup page is displayed. 3. Select the box Require multi-factor authentication for sign in. 4. Click Yes in the dialog box that appears. 5. Select the desired users by checking the boxes against their user names from the table, and click Enable.  Note Only the selected users are enabled for "multifactor authentication for sign in". If you do not select any user from the table, none of the users in your organization will be enabled for multifactor authentication. Configuring Multifactor Authentication Settings Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage User Authentication. 3. Click Configure MFA Settings. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 323 The Configure Multi-factor Authentication Settings page appears. 4. Enter a value in the Time allowed to skip multi-factor authentication setup box. This field specifies the maximum number of days the user can skip the multifactor authentication setup when an administrator has enabled it for that user. The default value is 5 days. 5. Enter a value in the Number of invalid multi-factor authentication attempts allowed box. This field specifies the maximum number of invalid multifactor authentication attempts that the user can make. The default value is 5 attempts. After the number of invalid attempts specified in this field, the user account is locked. It can be unlocked only by an administrator. 6. Enter a value in the Retry period for locked out users box. • After the number of minutes (the default value is 120 minutes) specified in this field, the user account is automatically unlocked and can be re-used. • If the user gets locked a second time, the default value becomes 240 minutes, and the user is unlocked only after 240 minutes. • If the user gets locked a third time, the user account is locked for good, and can be unlocked only by an administrator.  Note Users can contact their administrator at any time during this period to get their account unlocked. 7. Select the Enable the Remember me option check box. This checkbox (unchecked by default) specifies if users can choose the Remember me option for multifactor authentication in the one-time password input screen. If this box is checked, an input box Remember device for is displayed. 8. Enter a value in the Remember device for box. This field specifies the maximum number of days the user's device and browser will be remembered, during which they will not be prompted for the multifactor authentication passcode during login. The default value is 5 days. 9. Click Save. Managing Multifactor Authentication for Users Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 308]. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. Click Manage User Authentication. 324 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles 3. Select the desired multifactor authentication check boxes. 4. Select the users (from the table) for which you want to manage multifactor authentication. 5. Click the following buttons depending on what you wish to do: • • • • • Enable: Enables multifactor authentication for the selected users. Disable: Disables multifactor authentication for the selected users. Reset: Resets multifactor authentication for the selected users. These users must either enter the secure key displayed on the user interface, or scan a new QR code during their next sign in session. Send Email Reminder: Sends a reminder email to the selected users. Unlock: Unlocks the selected users. 6. Click Save. Setting Up Multifactor Authentication (Buyer User) Context You can set up multifactor authentication after your SAP Business Network administrator has enabled the feature. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Personal Information. The Personal Information page appears. 3. Below the User Name text box, click the Set up multi-factor authentication link. The Set up Multi-factor Authentication page appears. 4. Download and install SAP Authenticator or any compatible authenticator application such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator on your hand-held device. 5. Open the authenticator application that you have installed on your mobile device and do either one of the following: 1. Scan the QR code displayed on the page, and enter the code in the Time-based Verification Code input box, or 2. Enter the secure key displayed on the page in the Time-based Verification Code input box. 6. Click Done. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 325 Setting Up Multifactor Authentication Using a New Device (Buyer User) Context When you change your mobile device, you can reset the multifactor authentication that had been configured using your old device. Using the verification code from the old device, you can set up multifactor authentication on your new device. Procedure 1. Choose Account settings Manage Profile . 2. On the Configuration page, click Personal Information. The Personal Information page appears. 3. Below the User Name text box, click the Reset multi-factor authentication link. 4. Enter the verification code from your old mobile device. 5. Set up multifactor authentication again, using a new QR code on your new mobile device. 6. Click Done. 326 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass Description This section covers onboarding an SAP Fieldglass supplier on SAP Business Network and vice versa. Buyers can onboard the suppliers either in SAP Fieldglass or SAP Business Network ensuring unified user experience for suppliers across SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network. If SAP Ariba Buying that is part of SAP Ariba Procurement solutions uses SAP Fieldglass (restricted access) for service procurement, buyer cannot onboard a supplier on SAP Fieldglass. The buyer can leverage the SAP Business Network onboarding feature to onboard and manage suppliers. For more information on buyers and suppliers connection, see the How Buyers and Suppliers Connect section in the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide.  Note • • • • Buyer can invite a supplier on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass only if the buyer exists on both. • Only one remote external identity provider (IDP) is allowed to login to SAP Business Network. Therefore, while connecting to SAP Fieldglass, use only the SAP Fieldglass IDP. • • The Copy SES option on SAP Business Network is not supported in this integration scenario. Only the active supplier accounts can be integrated. Synchronization of supplier profile is not supported between SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. After the supplier registers in SAP Fieldglass by approving the collaboration type as Service and establishes a connection with the buyer in SAP Fieldglass, a situation may arise wherein the buyer deletes the relationship or the supplier rejects the approved releationship in SAP Business Network. In that case, the relationship in SAP Fieldglass continues and it is not automatically deleted, you must manually deactivate the relationship. Creation of service sheets from Orders tile is not supported for SAP Fieldglass suppliers. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass PUBLIC 327 Onboarding SAP Fieldglass Supplier on SAP Business Network Description This section covers onboarding an SAP Fieldglass supplier on SAP Business Network. If a supplier fulfilled both material and services, the supplier is required to log in to SAP Business Network as well as SAP Fieldglass separately for different processes. SAP Fieldglass now has the ability to initiate the onboarding of SAP Fieldglass suppliers on to SAP Business Network. The supplier can switch between the applications using single sign-on (SSO). Prerequisites • • Ensure that the buyer exists on both SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. • Ensure that the SAP Fieldglass supplier is subscribed to Fieldglass Onboarding Service permission to get the option to register with SAP Business Network. • We recommend that you set the relationship acceptance type to auto-approved. Ensure that you enable the Allow multiple private IDs per supplier buyer entitlement for the SAP Fieldglass buyer. Contact the Designated SAP Support contact to enable this feature. Restrictions • • • • • • The supplier accounts on SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network must be present on US data centre. The supplier accounts on SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network must be active. SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network account integration does not support profile synchronization. Only one remote external identity provider (IDP) is allowed to login to SAP Business Network and in this flow it is SAP Fieldglass IDP. While using this flow, you cannot use any another IDP. Creation of service sheets from Orders tile is not supported for SAP Fieldglass suppliers. Supplier must create the custom role FIELDGLASS_REMOTE_USER_DEFAULT_ROLE with the following three permissions before registering with SAP Fieldglass: • • • Invoice Generation Inbox Access Outbox Access Otherwise, the users that are created using the SCIM API are not granted the role. For more information on permissions, see Permissions You Can Assign to Users. 328 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass How the Integration Benefits the Customer • Supplier does not need to create an account of SAP Fieldglass user again on SAP Business Network. The supplier sub-users from SAP Fieldglass are automatically replicated in SAP Business Network. • • A user can perform actions on both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network using single-sign-on. When a new supplier is onboarded on SAP Fieldglass by a buyer that exists on both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network, the supplier is onboarded on to SAP Business Network too. User Interface Changes for Fieldglass Suppliers When a new supplier gets registered on SAP Fieldglass, the system displays an option as Complete SBN Registration. Clicking this option redirects the supplier to SAP Business Network to create a new account or integrate with an existing account on SAP Business Network. For existing suppliers, SAP Fieldglass displays the Complete SBN Registration option if the account is not already integrated with an account on SAP Business Network. When a service order is sent to SAP Fieldglass, SAP Business Network displays the statement of work number as a hyperlink. On clicking the hyperlink, the corresponding statement of work document gets displayed on SAP Fieldglass. SAP Fieldglass provides the option to return to SAP Business Network purchase order page. Workflow of Onboarding a SAP Fieldglass Supplier on SAP Business Network The following steps explain the workflow of onboarding a SAP Fieldglass supplier on SAP Business Network . 1. SAP Fieldglass buyer invites a supplier to onboard on SAP Fieldglass. 2. A new registration link is sent to the supplier via an email. 3. Supplier registers on SAP Fieldglass using the link. 4. The registration page displays a link to Complete SBN Registration. Suppliers on SAP Fieldglass that have the relationship with a buyer on both SAP Fieldglass and SAP Business Network, are displayed a link to Complete SBN Registration. The link is displayed until the supplier's account on both the applications are linked. 5. Complete SBN Registration provides the following two options: • • Create New Account Use Existing Account 6. Clicking the Create New Account opens the Registration page on SAP Business Network that pre-populates with the supplier's profile data from SAP Fieldglass. Modify the necessary fields on the SAP Business Network page, except the UserID field. 7. When a new supplier account is created on SAP Business Network, a relationship is created with the buyer ANID, account is enabled for single-sign-on, and a default role is assigned to that supplier. 8. When a supplier uses an existing account on SAP Business Network, the system does one of the following: • If the supplier exists and relationship with SAP Business Network buyer does not exist, then the relationship is created, account is enabled for single-sign-on, and the default role is assigned to the user. • If the supplier exists and relationship with SAP Business Network buyer is already established, then the account is enabled for single-sign-on and the default role is assigned to the user. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass PUBLIC 329 • If the supplier exists and the remote login and default role is assigned, but the relationship with the SAP Business Network buyer is not established, then only the relationship is created. 9. All the sub-users of the supplier on SAP Fieldglass are migrated to SAP Business Network.  Note The sub-users are migrated only when the scheduled job is run. Onboarding SAP Business Network Supplier on SAP Fieldglass Description This section explains onboarding a SAP Business Network supplier on SAP Fieldglass, which is mandatory in the following situations: • If a buyer that uses SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass sends a purchase order containing serviceable items, to a supplier in SAP Business Network • If a buyer uses SAP Ariba Buying to manage service orders, then the buyer can leverage the SAP Business Network onboarding feature to onboard and manage suppliers. The suppliers on SAP Business Network can create a new account or use the existing account and link that to a new or existing account on SAP Fieldglass. SAP Ariba Buying that is part of SAP Ariba Procurement solutions uses SAP Fieldglass (restricted access) for service procurement. After the supplier is registered on SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass, the supplier can use the SAP Business Network portal to view the service orders and navigate to SAP Fieldglass to manage the statement of work. If the buyer has a trading relationship with a supplier, then they can send a service collaboration request to the supplier to onboard them on SAP Fieldglass. The supplier can approve or reject the request. On approval, the supplier gets a notification to either create a new account or use an existing account on SAP Fieldglass. When the supplier creates a new account or uses an existing account, the supplier account in SAP Business Network is linked to the supplier account in SAP Fieldglass and single-sign-on is enabled. Prerequisites • • Ensure that the buyer exists on both SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass. • Ensure that the buyer Fieldglass ID (FGID) is included in SAP Business Network in the Fieldglass configuration section. 330 Ensure that the buyer has a trading relationship with a supplier. Only then the buyer can send a service collaboration request to the supplier to onboard them on SAP Fieldglass. PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Ariba Buying Integration with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: • In the buyer profile, ensure that the Enable Supplier Onboarding option is selected while configuring SAP Fieldglass.
