file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Bu.content: SAP Business Network Technical Infrastructure Provides information about the SAP Business Network technical infrastructure, including physical location and access, availability, reliability, communication and routing methods, authentication and encryption, backups, and preventive maintenance. SAP Business Network Physical Location [page 461] SAP Business Network Availability and Reliability [page 461] SAP Business Network Communication [page 462] Authentication [page 467] Backups and Maintenance [page 468] Technical Acknowledgment Messages Reference [page 469] SAP Business Network Physical Location The computers that run SAP Business Network are located at a secure co-location facility in California. A backup facility in Pennsylvania is available for disaster recovery. SAP Business Network uses heavy-duty servers with redundant features to ensure maximum availability. Only certified SAP Business Network representatives have direct access to these computers and the data they contain. Outside organizations cannot access your transactions or customer catalogs. Only the organizations involved in a transaction can see that transaction. The only parties that can see customer atalogs are buying organizations to whom suppliers have given permission. SAP Business Network uses a high-speed connection to an Internet Service Provider (ISP). A firewall prevents unauthorized access. SAP Business Network Availability and Reliability SAP Ariba recognizes that you need the highest possible availability and reliability. The procurement application/SAP Business Network transaction model is designed so you can depend on it for your business. To provide high availability and reliability, SAP Business Network has extensive error handing and fail-over features. Error Handling SAP Ariba Procurement solutions and SAP Business Network have built-in order error handling at all stages of the transaction process. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Technical Infrastructure PUBLIC 461 1. When SAP Business Network receives a transaction from SAP Ariba Buying, it first stores the transaction within a secure database before any processing takes place. This action ensures that no transactions are lost. 2. SAP Business Network sends an acknowledgment to SAP Ariba Buying that it received the transaction. If this acknowledgment does not take place, SAP Ariba Buying considers the transaction transmission to have failed. If an error occurs during transaction transmission, SAP Business Network notifies the SAP Ariba Buying administrator and SAP Ariba Buying automatically resends the transaction. 3. If the supplier selected the cXML order-routing method, SAP Business Network sends the transaction to the supplier’s website. 4. The supplier’s website sends an acknowledgment to SAP Business Network that it received the transaction. If this acknowledgment does not take place, SAP Business Network considers the transaction transmission to have failed and it automatically resends the transaction. At any time, both the supplier and its customer can view the status of orders on SAP Business Network. Fail-Over SAP Business Network runs redundant copies of all critical software subsystems related to transaction routing. This redundancy enables automatic fail-over in the event of an error so that there is no disruption of service. Even if automatic fail-over for order routing does not work, you can view orders online on SAP Business Network. Operational Status SAP Business Network hosts a user-accessible Trust Center platform that disseminates notifications about operational issues of cloud services. It also contains archived notifications from the previous 60 days. The trust center displays the same event notifications sent through email. Users can view the current availability and performance history of SAP Business Network by going to the Trust Center at https://www.sap.com/about/trust-center/cloud-service-status.html . The website is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. SAP Business Network Communication For increased security, SAP Business Network communicates using HTTPS, which is Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure. HTTPS uses TLS encryption to protect web communications. The TLS security protocol provides RSA data encryption, server authentication, message integrity, and optional client authentication for TCP/IP connections. TLS is built into both Microsoft’s and Mozilla’s web browsers.  Note SAP Ariba does not support using TLS 1.0, and it supports using TLS 1.1 through January 13, 2021. Starting January 14, 2021, SAP Ariba recommends that you use TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3. 462 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Technical Infrastructure For information about enabling TLS for external cXML sites, such as PunchOut sites and order receiving systems, see the cXML Solutions Guide. Interactive Sessions and Customer Catalog Uploading Users use web browsers to initiate interactive sessions on SAP Business Network. Buying organizations go to buyer.ariba.com and suppliers go to supplier.ariba.com. SAP Business Network redirects interactive sessions to https URLs, which instruct web browsers to encrypt all communication. The level of encryption is determined by the web browser. Suppliers upload customer catalogs while logged on to interactive sessions. Customer catalogs are encrypted for transport like all other data in the sessions. Communication with SAP Ariba Procurement solutions SAP Ariba Procurement solutions post data in the form of cXML documents to SAP Business Network through HTTPS using 128-bit encryption. SAP Business Network authenticates the received data to ensure that it comes from a valid buying organization. See these topics for additional information about communication: • • • • • cXML Routing [page 464] Fax Routing [page 464] Email Routing [page 464] Online [page 465] EDI Routing [page 466] SAP Business Network web servers use a server digital certificate to enable TLS connections. SAP Business Network supports 40-bit, 56-bit, and 128-bit encryption. The longer the key, the more difficult it is to break the encryption code. Both Mozilla Firefox and Microsoft Internet Explorer can support 128-bit keys. Related Information Authentication [page 467] SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Technical Infrastructure PUBLIC 463 cXML Routing The cXML order routing method posts cXML documents to the web URL that the supplier specifies during account configuration. Because this URL has an https prefix, SAP Business Network encrypts all communication. The level of encryption is determined by the supplier’s web server. If the supplier’s web server is down or if it rejects the cXML post, SAP Business Network retries the post every hour. After 10 retries, SAP Business Network holds the transaction and labels it “Failed.” HTTPS connections require TLS. For information about enabling TLS for external cXML sites, such as PunchOut sites and order receiving systems, see the cXML Solutions Guide. Related Information Authentication [page 467] Fax Routing The fax order routing method sends faxes to the supplier’s fax machine or fax modem using standard Group III protocol. Faxes transmit at speeds up to 14.4 kbps and have a resolution of 200 x 200 dpi. SAP Business Network uses a fax service provider to send faxes. SAP Business Network submits fax messages to the fax service provider securely over the Internet through HTTPS using TLS. Faxes are then sent to the supplier’s fax machine over private telephone lines. SAP Business Network does not fax orders and releases larger than 1 MB or that have more than 1,000 line items. It indicates that these orders exceed the maximum limit for display. It can transmit these orders and releases through email, cXML, and EDI routing. SAP Business Network prints only the last four digits of credit card and PCard numbers in fax and email orders and releases. SAP Business Network hides these numbers for increased security as suppliers already have them on file. Suppliers continue to see credit card and PCard numbers in cXML and online orders and releases. SAP Business Network correctly handles routing or fax problems. If the fax machine does not connect, SAP Business Network tries calling it 10 more times. Email Routing The email order routing method uses standard SMTP (Simple Mail Transport Protocol) Internet electronic mail. SAP Business Network sends email to the addresses specified by the supplier. Suppliers can specify up to five email addresses. Each email order contains both a plain-text message and a duplicate message in HTML format. The email recipient should use an HTML-aware email reader such as Microsoft Outlook for the best looking results. 464 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Technical Infrastructure Suppliers can optionally configure SAP Business Network to attach the cXML OrderRequest document to all email purchase orders. SAP Business Network prints only the last four digits of credit card and PCard numbers in fax and email orders and releases. SAP Business Network hides these numbers for increased security as their suppliers already have them on file. Suppliers see full credit card and PCard numbers in cXML and online orders and releases. When SAP Business Network sends orders and releases to mailboxes that respond automatically with “Out of Office” messages, it does not fail the orders if it detects one of the following phrases in the auto-reply message: • • • • • • • • • Out of office OOTO On vacation on holiday out of town away from the office away until out of the country/region at an off site meeting When SAP Business Network detects an auto-reply containing one of these phrases, it indicates that it received the auto-reply in the order history log. Email is not considered secure, because it is sent as clear text. However, suppliers can configure SAP Business Network to send just a brief email notification for each order. Then, they can sign in to and read their orders online, which is more secure. Online Order Routing The online order routing method requires suppliers to sign in to SAP Business Network with a web browser to manually read transactions. To connect to SAP Business Network, the supplier uses the URL supplier.ariba.com. SAP Business Network redirects the session to an HTTPS connection, so all communication for that session is encrypted. SAP Business Network does not display orders and releases larger than 1 MB or that have more than 1,000 line items. It indicates that these orders exceed the maximum limit for display. It can transmit these orders and releases through email, cXML, and EDI routing. The level of encryption is determined by the supplier’s web browser. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Technical Infrastructure PUBLIC 465 EDI Routing Suppliers can select the type of EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) routing when they configure their SAP Business Network accounts. SAP Business Network supports two kinds of EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) document routing: • • ANSI ASC X12 EDI v004010 UN EDIFACT version D98A with syntax version 3 SAP Ariba recommends that suppliers subscribe to the Supplier Technical Support (STS) service. STS membership offers an enhanced level of support that a standard account does not include, such as the ability to view online case status, extended support hours, guaranteed response times, and an escalation path. EDI Routing Options There are two routing options for EDI documents: • • Value Added Network (VAN) routing through Inovisworks from Inovis, Inc. EDI over the Internet (EDIINT) routing using the Applicability Statement 2 (AS2) method. Suppliers choose one of these methods when setting their EDI configuration. Inovis, Inc. (formerly Harbinger and Extricity) has provided B2B solutions to the world’s most successful companies since 1984. The Inovisworks network provides mission critical and flexible connectivity to electronic B2B trading communities. For more information, see www.inovis.com . EDI Setup When suppliers select X12 or EDIFACT document routing in their SAP Business Network accounts, they enter data about their EDI profile, including their EDI IDs and VAN names. Suppliers must also contact SAP Ariba Support, specifying their NetworkId and their customers’ NetworkIds and names. EDI Document Mapping SAP Business Network performs EDI mapping according to its published guidelines, not a supplier’s preferred guidelines. It does not customize mapping for each customer. When SAP Business Network maps data between cXML and EDI documents, it passes as much of the sender’s original data as possible. For example, the EDI order generated by SAP Business Network is as complete a rendering of the cXML OrderRequest that can be produced within the confines of the X12 or EDIFACT standards. So, generated documents might contain what appears to be verbose optional content, such as currency declarations, redundant postal addresses, and text comments, because that data is present in the original document. For EDI and EDIFACT implementation guidelines, see the help center. 466 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Technical Infrastructure Retrieving EDI Orders Suppliers can establish EDI mailboxes with Inovis or any other VAN. Suppliers set up their own mailbox services, and they are responsible for any interconnect fees between VANs. Suppliers retrieve orders and releases using the medium their VAN supports—usually private telephone lines. They use EDI retrieval and translation software to read their EDI mailboxes and to translate orders for their order fulfillment system. Related Information EDI Configuration Guide Authentication For secure access, SAP Business Network and supplier organizations perform authentication of both interactive user sessions and cXML documents. Authentication of Interactive Sessions SAP Business Network authenticates online sessions by requiring users to sign in with a unique user ID/password pair. SAP Business Network encrypts account passwords before storing them. Each organization can view only its own information. Some buyer/supplier data can be viewed by other organizations. Suppliers can explicitly publish customer catalogs to make them visible to specific customers. Transactions between a supplier and its customer can be seen by both parties. Supplier company profiles can be viewed by buying organizations when they search for new suppliers. Authentication of cXML Documents For secure access SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba Buying, SAP Ariba Sourcing, and external cXML-enabled sites (such as PunchOut sites) authenticate cXML documents they receive. This authentication ensures that the senders are recognized organizations. SAP Business Network provides two methods for authenticating received cXML documents: • Shared Secret (default)—You enter a confidential text string into a field in your SAP Business Network account. All documents passed between you and SAP Business Network are authenticated using this shared secret. • Digital Certificate—Organizations purchase and maintain a digital certificate from a trusted Certificate Authority and then enter that certificate into their SAP Business Network account. SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Technical Infrastructure PUBLIC 467 uses the digital certificate for authentication. SAP Business Network supports backup certificates, which are useful when the primary certificate expires or when you need to perform certificate maintenance. For instructions on setting up digital certificates, see the cXML Solutions Guide. Related Information cXML Setup [page 35] Backups and Maintenance SAP Ariba performs regular backups of your SAP Business Network data—registration and account information, uploaded customer catalogs, transactions, and discrete data (uploaded files). Backups do not interrupt the normal operation of SAP Business Network. Database Backups • • Database transaction logs are copied from disk to tape four times per day in each datacenter. • Database physical disk backups are completed once per week in each datacenter, copied to physically separate disks from the database data and transaction log volumes. Database transaction logs are saved to disk and to tape from the point in time of each database disk backup in each datacenter. • Full database backup copies are written to tape once per week in each datacenter. Database copy-on-write snapshot disk backups are completed twice per day in each datacenter. Database transaction logs are saved to disk and to tape from the point in time of each database disk backup in each datacenter. Discrete Data Backups • • • Copy-on-write snapshot disk backups are completed four times per day in each datacenter. Discrete data full backup copies are written to tape once per week in each datacenter. Discrete data incremental backup copies are written to tape daily in each datacenter. SAP Business Network receives periodic preventive maintenance. This preventive maintenance is scheduled for low-use times, such as weekends and late at night. Transaction queues wait while maintenance occurs, and they resume processing when maintenance concludes. SAP Ariba usually lists planned preventive maintenance times on the Event Website. 468 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Technical Infrastructure Related Information Operational Status [page 462] Technical Acknowledgment Messages Reference Buyers receive notifications, such as functional acknowledgments and status messages, which keep them current with the technical status of the documents they send. This reference gives the definitions for the messages. Definitions for the technical acknowledgment messages follow: Received The document reached SAP Business Network at the respective technical interface. The document is syntactically correct and has valid AN IDs. The document was parsed and can be loaded into the queue for processing. Successfully processed The document was successfully processed and validated in both buyer and supplier communities, including successful third-party processing and flow-extensions, but has not yet been sent to the integration layer. Processing failed Propagation of the document from the buyer community to the supplier community failed. Ariba Operations was notified, prior to buyer notification, after 10 retries. Processing delayed Because of temporary errors, the document is not yet successfully propagated. Sent The document could be transferred to the integration layer without any technical issue. The data are no longer in the SAP Business Network sphere of responsibility. Delivery to gateway delayed Delivery of the document to the integration layer was delayed, perhaps because of a short outage in the connection between SAP Business Network and the integration layer. Ariba Operations and administrators will perform retries. Delivery to gateway failed The document could not be transmitted to the integration layer, even after retries. The data quality is good, and you can retrieve the data from the SAP Business Network user interface. Ariba Operations and network administrators will retry the transfer. Delivery successful After successful mapping into the target format the message was transmitted to the supplier. This is a technical acknowledgment on the transmission level. Delivery failed An error prevented the delivery of the document. The error could be a mapping error, an addressing error, the permanent unavailability of the target system, or another type of error. Delivery delayed Indicates the first delivery attempt failed. Another attempt to deliver will happen automatically. Delivery confirmed The target system received, validated and loaded the data. The business data arrived in the recipient processing landscape. The data were accepted, but have not yet been processed. Negative confirmed The target system received and validated the data. This status is based on a negative functional acknowledgment. SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Technical Infrastructure PUBLIC 469 Processing acknowledged When a buyer and a supplier officially confirm the processing of the business data, the confirmation results in the status processing acknowledged. A document reaches this status only when the supplier actively confirms the successful processing with a positive acknowledgment. Buyers and suppliers should first make an agreement whether or not to employee this status. Receiving successful This status defines the beginning of the message tracking for inbound documents. The message from the supplier was received, and could be stored on the integration layer. Passed This status defines the beginning of the message tracking for inbound documents. The message from the supplier passed, and could be stored on the integration layer. Delivery to AN failed The integration layer could not post the data to SAP Business Network, even after all retries.Notice of the failure will be sent back to the supplier. Msg queued The document was queued to get retrieved by the buyer organization. Only the buyer is responsible for the further document life cycle. Delivery processing acknowledged The message now was queued to get retrieved by the buyer organization. Only the buyer is responsible for the further document life cycle. Message never disclosed The message was placed in the queue for the buyer, but the buyer has not retrieved the data from the queue. The file has not been picked up. 470 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide SAP Business Network Technical Infrastructure

Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide This guide is for an SAP Business Network buyer user or buyer administrator who is enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. You configure and use SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality for additional ways to collaborate with your suppliers. This guide applies to: • • SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network Related Guides: SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide cXML Solutions Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide PUBLIC 7 SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network for Supply Chain is an extension of SAP Business Network that enhances the ability of buyers to collaborate with suppliers in supply-chain tasks such as ordering, invoicing, and shipping. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Overview This extension of SAP Business Network provides additional capabiities for buyers and suppliers. With SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enabled, an array of features become available to buyers and suppliers on SAP Business Network. These features facilitate collaboration between buyers and suppliers, for example on transactions pertinent to direct material supply chains. As a buyer, the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain solution allows you to do the following: • • Collaborate efficiently with all supply chain partners through a single global solution. • Easily manage all direct materials procurement and typical retail and manufacturing collaborative processes including consigned inventory, rolling delivery schedules, and contract manufacturing - all in one place • • • Improve visibility into supply with continuous monitoring, benchmarking, and enhancement of supplier performance Respond intelligently to changes in supply and demand with real-time visibility into supply chain metrics Rapidly connect to thousands of suppliers with minimal IT costs Instantly identify errors through configurable business rules with automated validation and reconciliation  Note SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration features entail enhancements to the SAP Business Network user interface. Fields and tabs that do not appear in the regular SAP Business Network interface may appear in the SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration user interface. Also, the same tab may be labeled with one name in the regular SAP Business Network user interface, and with another in the SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration user interface. Users should take note of these differences, especially when they first switch from the regular SAP Business Network user interface to the SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration user interface. Alternate cXML Document Routing You might need alternate cXML document routing enabled for you and your suppliers to use certain features. Many SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features require enablement of alternate cXML document routing, which allows cXML documents to be routed to alternate paths specified in the cXML. If you haven’t already enabled alternate cXML document routing, ask your Designated Support Contact to log a case (formerly Service Request). An SAP Business Network Support representative follows up to enable alternate cXML document routing for each supplier-buyer relationship that you request. 8 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network Overview SAP Business Network is a cloud-based business network where buyers and suppliers establish business relationships and run their business transactions. SAP Business Network has a number of advantages for customers. On the technical level, customers only have to connect to a single service in the cloud, instead of having to set up and operate technical integration to all their business partners, using different protocols and technologies. On the business level, customers not only save costs with automated procurement processes, but they can also use the network to find new business partners and opportunities. For more information about SAP Business Network, see SAP Business Network - Supplier Help Roadmap. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain PUBLIC 9 Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers This section provides topics that describe the configuration of SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features for deployment. Buyer System Configuration [page 10] Supplier Relationship Configuration [page 12] Advanced Packaging Configuration [page 18] Freight Carrier List Configuration [page 27] Replenishment Order Configuration [page 29] Rejection Code Configuration for Order Change Requests [page 31] Planning and Forecast Configuration [page 33] Supply Chain Monitor Configuration [page 58] Buyer System Configuration This section provides topics that describe how buyer administrators can configure SAP Business Network for Supply Chain systems for buyer users. Deployment Process for SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network for Supply Chain [page 10] Buyer System Integration with SAP Business Network [page 11] Buyer System Entitlement for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain [page 12] Deployment Process for SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network for Supply Chain You need to plan, configure, and test your system to prepare it for deployment. The SAP Business Network for Supply Chain solution sits within SAP Business Network, so, as a buyer, you can set it up as part your initial SAP Business Network setup, or you can set it up after the initial SAP Business Network setup. The table below provides an overview of the SAP Business Network deployment process, with emphasis on areas that are particularly relevant to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain setup.  Note When setting up either SAP Business Network or the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain solution it is important to engage at least some suppliers as early as possible. The recommendation is to engage with at least one supplier who uses EDI documents and one who can accommodate cXML documents. 10 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Deployment Process Overview Stage Description High level design • • • Explore the ERP starting point of the buyer organization Discuss the documents and processes that the buyer wants to support Identify the connection types and authentication methods the buyer wants to implement • • Identify the exact documents and processes that the buyer wants to support • Set up and configure the buyer’s SAP Business Network account and test account. Generic SAP Business Network business rules and rules specific to supply chain collaboration can be configured. • Enable suppliers on SAP Business Network. Suppliers might also be enabled for supply chain collaboration functionality at this stage. Mapping • Create mappings between fields used by buyers in their business documents and messages and cXML elements and attributes that can be passed through SAP Business Network. Installation and configuration of adapters • Buyer organization installs and configures the adapter Unit testing • End-to-end (buyer ERP through SAP Business Network to supplier and back) testing performed for each document type. UAT testing • System tested internally by buyer organization users Production • System goes live for collaboration between the buyer and their suppliers Technical design Plan in detail for the installation and configuration of an adapter to connect the buyer’s ERP system with SAP Business Network Buyer System Integration with SAP Business Network Hardware and software solutions enable SAP Business Network to communicate with different buyer systems. Organizations communicate with SAP Business Network using commerce eXtensible Markup Language (cXML) documents. Unless a buyer is using an SAP Business Network procurement solution, they will create these cXML documents on an ERP system that is external to SAP Business Network. The buyer’s ERP system, therefore, must be integrated with SAP Business Network in order to communicate over SAP Business Network and make use of its extensions. For enterprise customers of SAP Business Network using SAP Netweaver, SAP Business Network offers out-of-thebox adapters that allow the exchange of cXML documents with SAP Business Network. The adapters also provide complete mapping services between SAP Netweaver and SAP Business Network. An adapter is software that is installed at the customer site, behind the customer's firewall. For more information about integrating ERP systems with SAP Business Network, see the Integrating SAP Business Network for Supply Chain with SAP ERP and and SAP S/4HANA guide and the Transport Adapter Implementation Guide. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 11 For more information about integration services, contact your SAP Business Network Account Manager. Buyer Integration Options The SAP Business Network Adapter for SAP NetWeaver is an add-on module for SAP business applications. This adapter enables integration between SAP Business Network and your SAP ERP system. It enables your SAP ERP system to send and receive cXML documents to and from SAP Business Network by mapping data elements between IDoc and cXML documents. Buyer System Entitlement for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network Support enables your account to access SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality. To have your SAP Business Network account entitled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features, ask your Designated Support Contact to log a case (formerly Service Request). An SAP Business Network Support representative will follow up to entitle your company to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. For buyers using external ERP systems, such as SAP ERP, adapter support for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain is available. Contact your SAP Business Network Account Manager for more information about integration services. Supplier Relationship Configuration This section provides topics that describe how buyer administrators can configure SAP Business Network for Supply Chain relationships with suppliers. Enabling or Disabling SAP Business Network for Supply Chain for Suppliers [page 13] Using a Vendor CSV File to Enable or Disable SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Relationships [page 14] Requesting a Logistics Relationship with a Supplier [page 15] Configuring Buyer-Controlled Routing of Orders [page 16] 12 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers Enabling or Disabling SAP Business Network for Supply Chain for Suppliers Use this procedure to grant a supplier access to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality. Prerequisites To enable suppliers for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain and industry-specific functionality, buyer administrators must have the Supplier Enablement Task Management permission. Context Buyer administrators who are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enable suppliers for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality. Buyer administrators can also enable suppliers for industryspecific functionality, which is an additional layer of SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality that sits on top of the base SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality. When a supplier is enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality by one buyer, they are automatically enabled for that functionality with all other buyers with which they have an active relationship.  Note You can alternatively use a CSV file to enable or disable suppliers in bulk. See Using a Vendor CSV File to Enable or Disable SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Relationships [page 14]. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account as an administrator. Supplier Enablement 2. Choose Active Relationships . 3. Choose the suppliers for whom you want to enable or disable collaborative supply chain or retail-industry functionality. 4. Choose the Actions menu at the bottom of the supplier table, then choose Enable/Disable Supply Chain Collaboration. 5. Check or uncheck the relevant boxes to enable or disable collaborative supply chain functionality for the selected suppliers: • Collaborative supply chain • • Retail industry fields Aerospace and Defense fields 6. Click OK. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 13 Using a Vendor CSV File to Enable or Disable SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Relationships Use this procedure to grant SAP Business Network for Supply Chain access to multiple suppliers in one operation. Prerequisites • • Assume a role with the Supplier Enablement Program Administrator permission. Have available one of the following vendor CSV files, populated with vendor records: • Vendor Data Export report – This report prepopulates all fields that have existing data, including SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enablement settings. For more information, see Generating and Downloading Reports in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. • Upload Vendor template – Add vendor data to the template before you perform this procedure. For more information, see Creating a Vendor CSV File in Enabling suppliers on SAP Business Network . Context Buyer administrators can use a vendor CSV file to enable or disable multiple SAP Business Network for Supply Chain relationships in one operation.  Note You can alternatively enable or disable suppliers from the user interface. See Enabling or Disabling SAP Business Network for Supply Chain for Suppliers [page 13]. Procedure 1. Open the vendor CSV file for editing. 2. Enter in the Proposed Enablement Mode column your desired enablement settings, then save the file. Valid values are the following: Enablement Value Description EnableSCCWithRetail Enables the vendor for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, including retail industry fields. EnableSCCWithoutRetail Enables the vendor for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, excluding retail industry fields. DisableSCC Disables the vendor for all SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enablement. Observe these guidelines: 14 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers • To include other text in the same field, enter that text first, followed by a pipe character (|) and the enablement value. For example: Your comment | EnableSCCWithRetail  Tip To avoid setting the wrong enablement value, enter only one enablement value in the field. Because this field accepts free text, more than one enablement value could be entered, but only the last value in the field is applied when you upload the file. • You can set provisional enablement values for standard account suppliers and private suppliers. The setting becomes active after the supplier is fully registered. • If the vendor CSV file has multiple records with the same Network ID value but different enablement values, the value of the record nearest the end of the file is applied. • Enablement values for a private supplier are ignored if the private supplier consolidates to an existing vendor. The private supplier inherits the enablement values of the existing supplier. 3. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 4. Click Upload, then choose Vendors from the dropdown. 5. On the Upload Vendors page, choose your edited CSV file and click Upload. Results On the Supplier Enablement Active Relationships page, the Supply Chain Collaboration column reflects the updated SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enablement settings. Requesting a Logistics Relationship with a Supplier Use this procedure to enable an SAP Business Network for Supply Chain relationship with a third-party logistics provider. Prerequisites Before you can request logistics services from a third-party logistics provider, you must do the following: • • Be an administrator with the Supplier Enablement Task Management permission. Establish a logistics relationship with the supplier. A logistics relationship allows a supplier to receive transport requests and to send and receive transport confirmations. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 15 Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account as an administrator. 2. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 3. Click Search For Suppliers. 4. Enter information in the Company name, Company name starts with, or ANID fields, then click Search. Matching suppliers appear in the Search Results table. 5. In the Search Results table, find the supplier you're looking for, then in that row choose Request Relationship in the Actions column. The Supplier Detail page opens. 6. Check I have reviewed and verified the profile of SupplierName. 7. Click Request a Logistics Relationship. A message appears saying that the logistics relationship has been established. 8. Click Done. Configuring Buyer-Controlled Routing of Orders Use this procedure to override the default routing method of one or more suppliers. Prerequisites You must be an administrator with the Supplier Enablement Task Management permission. Context As a buyer administrator, you can override the supplier’s default routing method for orders that match one or more conditions. Doing this prevents those orders from being routed to an external integration channel. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • To override the order routing method for an individual supplier, choose Relationships , find the desired supplier, then in that row choose Preferences for Supplier page opens. • To override the order routing method for all suppliers, choose Supplier Enablement More Actions Administration Active Edit . The Edit Configuration Default Transaction Rules . The Default Transaction Rules page opens. 16 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers 2. In the Purchase Order Rules section, make sure Override default purchase order rules is checked. Checking this rule shows the override rules you can set. 3. Check Override supplier's routing method for orders that match buyer's conditions, then click Configure. The Routing conditions for orders page opens. 4. Specify a value for one or more conditions. In the Condition column, select is or is not from the dropdown. For the Planning Type setting, the is empty condition is also available. Type Value cXML mapping Order Type Type of order. Select one of the following values: Request.OrderRequest.Order- • • regular – Standard order RequestHeader.orderType • blanket – Blanket purchase order release – Release against a master agreement or against a blanket purchase order External Document Enter a string for a document type from an external system. Type Request.OrderRequest.OrderRequestHeader.OrderRequestHeaderIndustry.ExternalDocumentType.docType Planning Type Item Category Item-level planning strategy. Select one of the following values: Request.OrderRequest.Item- • • • • Out.ItemOutIndustry.planning- MTO – Make to Order MTS – Make to Stock Type ATO – Assemble to Order CTO – Configure to Order Item-level category, which indicates how a component or material Request.OrderRequest.Item- is procured. Select one of the following values: Out.itemCategory • subcontract – Procuring a material by providing component information to a contract manufacturer that makes the finished product. • consignment – Managing a material through a special process where the payment to supplier is withheld until the material or service is consumed by the buyer. • thirdParty – Procuring a material from a third-party vendor. Extrinsic Enter the cXML extrinsic Transaction Category Type Transaction (transactionCategoryOrType). You can enter multiple val- derRequestHeader.Extrin- Request.OrderRequest.Or- Category Type ues separated by commas. sic.name="transactionCategoryOrType" 5. To enable a condition, check its Enable box. 6. Click OK to save the conditions. 7. Click Save to save purchase order rules. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 17 Next Steps To avoid communication interruption, be sure to tell suppliers which orders are subject to buyer-controlled routing of orders. Suppliers aren’t notified by email when their default routing method for an order is overridden by the buyer. Advanced Packaging Configuration Buyer administrators can enable suppliers to specify a packing plan for ship notice items as they create a ship notice. The advanced packaging with handling units feature provides suppliers with a packaging wizard, to guide them through the steps of packing ship notice items. As a buyer administrator, this feature enables you to do the following tasks, to provide your requirements for the packaging wizard to use: • • • • • Upload packaging instructions for the supplier and configure automatic numbering of handling units. Provide multiple packing instructions when a single packing instruction can't cover all materials. Use a template to create packaging instructions. Provide handling unit labels for suppliers to print. Configure profiles to grant extra capabilities to suppliers when using advanced packaging for handling units. Workflow for Handling Unit Labels [page 18] Automated Transfer of Updated Handling-Unit Packaging Instructions [page 19] Configuring Auto-Numbering of Handling Units [page 20] Configuring GTL Numbering [page 22] Creating Packaging Instructions [page 23] Creating a Handling Unit Profile [page 26] Workflow for Handling Unit Labels The end-to-end workflow for handling unit labels starts with a buyer contacting SAP Ariba Services to define a template, and ends with the supplier printing labels for a ship notice. The following describes the workflow for printing handling unit labels: 1. An SAP Business Network customer engages with SAP Ariba Services to define a custom layout template for handling unit labels. The template is an Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations, or XSLT, file. 2. SAP Ariba Services uploads custom PDF layout templates to the customer account. When more than one version of a template has been uploaded, the latest uploaded file is active. 3. A supplier opens a ship notice in the SAP Business Network user interface and clicks the printer icon in a handling unit line item to print a handling unit label in PDF format. Handling unit labels are available to all suppliers. 18 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers Automated Transfer of Updated Handling-Unit Packaging Instructions Buyers can configure their ERP system to send packaging instructions to SAP Business Network for them whenever any instructions are added or updated. When a buyer creates or updates packaging instructions in their SAP S/4HANA ERP system, this feature coordinates with SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network the automatic transfer of those instructions to SAP Business Network. This feature doesn't change or interact with packaging instructions that are manually uploaded to SAP Business Network with an Upload/Download template in Excel. The manual creation and upload of packaging instructions using Upload/Download remains supported. For details about this manual upload method, see Creating Packaging Instructions [page 23]. In addition, a buyer who uses more than one type of ERP system can receive automatic transfers of updated packaging instructions on SAP S/4HANA systems, and manually update SAP Business Network with changes made in their other ERP systems. Prerequisites To activate automated transfer of new or updated packaging instructions, a buyer system must meet the following configuration requirements. • • The buyer ERP system uses SAP S/4HANA. • The buyer has followed instructions in the following SAP Notes: The buyer ERP system is configured with SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. For details, see High-Level Steps for Integrating SAP ERP with SAP Business Network. • • • 3230454 3261333 3265218 Restrictions • Quantities in the capacity fields in packaging instructions must be whole numbers. Quantities with decimal places aren't supported. • This feature doesn't automatically transfer generic packaging instructions. Details of the Automated Transfer Process • This SAP Business Network feature coordinates with other functionality to support automatic import of updates in packaging instructions from the buyer ERP. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 19 When a buyer ERP system that uses SAP S/4HANA receives additions or changes to packaging instructions, SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network automatically retrieves those instructions and updates the data in SAP Business Network. The transferred instructions are then available to suppliers who use the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain advanced packaging wizard to create ship notices for that buyer. • This feature supports buyers with packaging instructions in more than one supported ERP system. Packaging instructions transferred to SAP Business Network include the systemID of the source ERP system. When revisions to packaging instructions are automatically transferred to SAP Business Network, this feature verifies that the instructions to update have the same systemID as the source ERP system. • When a supplier creates a ship notice with the advanced packaging wizard, this feature ensures that the wizard provides the right packaging instructions. When the wizard searches for valid packaging instructions to use, this feature chooses packaging instructions whose systemID and order number matches the systemID and order number of the purchase order to be shipped.  Note Buyers can still upload packaging instructions manually when desired. • This feature automatically populates the values for vendor ID, plant, and validity period in packaging instructions in the ERP system. You can select the Handling Unit level structure from the following options: • • • Single Level Packing Multi Level Packing Mixed Multi Level Packing Issuing Agency Code You can enter the agency code. Rolling From the dropdown, select Yes or No.  Note You can set GTL, handling unit, and advance ship notice numbering for documents from 1 to 100. If document 100 is reached, expect the following scenarios: • If you have rolling enabled, the document rolls back to 1. This results in duplicate document numbering. • If rolling is disabled, the following document must be created with a manually entered unique value— for example, Document 120. Context You can configure how the advanced packaging wizard for ship notices will automatically number handling units. Suppliers can choose to override this configuration with their own auto-numbering settings. Procedure 1. Choose Administration Configuration Document Number Preferences . 2. In the Handling Units section, click Create. 3. On the Configure Numbering page, enter the desired numbering criteria and constraints and click OK. 4. Verify the configuration and click Save. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 21 Next Steps • Enable transaction rule Allow suppliers to use advanced packaging on ship notices for the suppliers you want to use this feature. • Provide your packaging instructions. See Create and upload packaging instructions [page 23]. Configuring GTL Numbering Use this procedure to set GTL numbering for handling units in a ship notice. Prerequisites You must be a buyer administrator. Context As a buyer administrator, you can configure Global Transport Level (GTL) numbering for the Handling Unit number range. Procedure 1. Sign in as a buyer administrator. 2. Go to Manage Profile. 3. Select Document Number Preferences from the list. 4. In the Handling Units tab, click Create. 5. In the Configure Numbering page, choose GTL as the configuration type.  Note You can set GTL, handling unit, and advance ship notice numbering for documents from 1 to 100. If document 100 is reached, expect the following scenarios: • • 22 If you have rolling enabled, the document rolls back to 1. This results in duplicate document numbering. PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers Creating Packaging Instructions Use this procedure to provide suppliers their requirements for packing items for shipment. Prerequisites • Enable the Allow suppliers to use advanced packaging on ship notices rule for the suppliers you want to use the advanced packaging wizard.  Note When this rule is enabled, transaction rule Require suppliers to provide a unique Global Individual Asset ID for line items on ship notices is ignored. To allow GS1 numbering, enable the Require suppliers to provide a Global Individual Asset ID for line items on ship notices that conforms to the Serial Shipping Container Code (SSCC) format rule. • (Optional) Configure auto-numbering. See Configure auto-numbering of handling units [page 20]. Context You can download an Excel template to create packaging specifications for different types of material. You then upload the files for suppliers to use with the advanced packaging wizard. Procedure 1. Choose Quick links Upload/Download Uploads , then click Upload. 2. In the Upload File popup, choose Packaging Instructions from the Type dropdown. The Download template link displays. 3. Click Download template and choose where to save the file. The Packaging Instructions template downloads. 4. Open the template file and enter data for all desired material types. Only the most recently uploaded instructions are used. 5. Choose Quick links Upload/Download Uploads , then click Upload. 6. In the Upload File popup, enter a name to call the upload and choose Packaging Instructions from the Type dropdown. Then browse to choose the desired file and click Upload. The • • • Uploads page opens and shows your uploaded file. If the upload status is Processing, choose Refresh Status to update the status. If the upload status is Completed, processing is finished. If the upload status is Failed, choose the download icon  in the Log column for troubleshooting information. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 23 Related Information Packaging Instructions Fields [page 24] Packaging Instructions Fields The following fields appear on the Instructions sheet of the Packaging Instructions template: Field Description Packaging Specification ID A unique ID for the packaging specification. Capacity Not used. Capacity information is taken from the Maximum Capacity field. Material The customer product ID of the product to be packed. Material Description Unit Required. The value of Unit from the ship notice. Packaging Level Packaging Material The packaging material to contain the product. Packaging Material Description Maximum Capacity The capacity value used by the system. Minimum Capacity Length Unit Length Height Unit Height Width Unit Width Volume Unit Volume Net Weight The total weight, excluding packaging. Gross Weight The total weight, including packaging. Unit Gross Weight Total Volume Unit Total Volume Parent Packaging Material 24 PUBLIC The next larger packaging material that can contain a number of the packaging materials. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers Field Description Create Handling Unit Set to Yes to generate handling units automatically, based on these specifications. Valid values are Yes, No, and blank, which is the same as No. Default is blank. Allow Mixed Required. Set to Yes to allow different materials in the same innermost handling unit. Valid values are Yes, No, and blank, which is the same as No. Default is blank. Is Auxiliary Required. Set to Yes if the item as an auxiliary material, or set to No if the item is a handling unit. Valid values are Yes and No. A blank field is not valid. Is Printable Controls whether a printer icon  displays in the SAP Business Network user interface for printing the handling unit label. Valid values are Yes and No. If an entry has no value set, that entry is processed as having Is Printable set to No. Is Default Identifies whether the packaging instruction is preselected for the supplier by the packaging wizard. Valid values are Yes and No. If an entry has no value set, that entry is processed as having Is Default set to No. The following rule is introduced in the Handling Unit supplier profile that enables default packaging instructions as a default in addition to specific instructions: The Allow suppliers to choose default packaging instructions for buyer parts that already have part specific instruction rule is added to the handling unit supplier profile in Create handling unit profile for Ship Notice. When buyers check this rule, their suppliers can determine how to pack items that the buyers have already provided partspecific instructions about. These enhancements provide the capability to use the assignment information for generic packaging instructions. Earlier, this was limited to material specific packaging instructions. There are now more determination options available for generic packaging instructions, like those based on Vendor ID or Plant information. The following fields appear on the Supplier and Plant Assignment sheet of the Packaging Instructions template: Field Description Packaging Specification ID A unique ID for the packaging specification. Supplier ANID Ariba Network ID for the supplier. Plant ID Plant ID. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 25 Creating a Handling Unit Profile Use this procedure to assign advanced packaging tasks to suppliers. Context As a buyer administrator, you can create handling unit profiles to assign to one or more suppliers or supplier groups. A profile enables the specified suppliers to do one or more of the following advanced packaging tasks: Handling-unit profile capability Description Enable suppliers to add handling unit Enabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can add a new handling unit to the advanced packaging wizard. Enable suppliers to move and rearrange the handling units on the Confirm Packing screen Enabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can move materials from one handling unit to another available handling unit. Enable suppliers to edit items on the Confirm Packing screen Enabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can edit the quantity of a handling unit. Enable suppliers to edit values on Define Instructions screen Enabled by default. Enable suppliers to edit the dimension values of handling units Disabled by default. When enabled, supplers can change the following values for a handling unit: • On the Define packaging instructions page, suppliers can change Length, Height, and Width. • On the Confirm packing plan page, suppliers can change Length, Height, Width, Gross weight, and Net weight.  Note The supplier cannot change dimension values on the Print labels page. Enable suppliers to add empty packaging material to a handling unit Disabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can add empty packaging material, such as boxes, to handling units in a packaging plan, except to the highest-level handling unit. The empty packaging material can be used to help stabilize items in a partially filled handling unit, with or instead of auxiliary material. Show auxiliary materials in auto packaging Disabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can see on the Confirm packaging page the auxiliary materials in an automatically generated packaging plan, and make any desired changes. When disabled, suppliers can still add or remove auxiliary materials to a packaging plan that is not automatically generated. 26 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers Handling-unit profile capability Description Enable suppliers to remove auxiliary materials in auto packaging This task requires that the task Show auxiliary materials in auto packaging is also enabled. When enabled, suppliers can delete auxiliary materials from automatically generated packaging plans on the Confirm packaging page. Enable suppliers to add auxiliary materials in auto packaging This task requires that the task Show auxiliary materials in auto packaging is also enabled. When enabled, suppliers can add auxiliary materials to an automatically generated packaging plan on the Confirm packaging page. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Manage Profile Manage Handling Unit Profile for Ship Notice . 2. Click Create Profile. 3. Enter a profile name, specify which suppliers the profile includes or excludes, and choose what capabilities to assign. You can specify to include or exclude one or more suppliers, supplier groups, or a combination. In the Include or Exclude field, start typing a name, then choose one from the list. 4. Click Save. The new profile name and list of suppliers displays on the Manage Handling Unit Profile for Ship Notice page, with Edit and Delete actions for the profile. Freight Carrier List Configuration As a buyer administrator, you can upload customized freight carrier lists for your suppliers. Buyer administrators can upload any number of customized freight carrier lists. The most recently uploaded list is made available to suppliers when creating ship notices. If you use preferred carriers for shipments from your suppliers, you can upload them to your account from a CSV file. Otherwise, suppliers must select one of the following default freight carriers: • • • • • • Airborne Express DHL FedEx UPS US Postal Service Other SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 27 Uploading a Customized List of Freight Carriers Use this procedure to upload freight carrier lists for supplier use in ship notices. Context As a buyer administrator, you can upload any number of customized freight carrier lists. The most recently uploaded list is made available to suppliers when creating ship notices.  Note If you upload an empty list, the uploaded file is ignored and the default list of all carriers is displayed to suppliers in the Carrier Name field when creating ship notices. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Choose Supplier Enablement > Manage Vendors. 3. Click Upload > Carrier Codes. 4. Click Download template on the Upload Carrier Codes page. 5. Starting on row six of the template file, enter the carrier information.  Caution Do not change or delete the information in rows one to five of the template. • • You can add details for up to 2500 carriers to the file. You can upload the file as a CSV file, or you can upload a ZIP file that contains the CSV file. a. In column A, enter carrier codes. b. In column B, enter matching carrier names. c. Save the file. 6. Enter a name for the upload file in the Name field on the Upload Carrier Codes page. 7. Click Browse and browse for the saved CSV file or ZIP file. 8. Click Upload. If an error is found during upload, an error message appears, and the Upload button changes to Reload. Correct the file, browse for it again, and click Reload. Results The uploaded file displays in the Upload Details table. 28 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers Editing a Freight Carrier List Use this procedure to edit carrier lists. Prerequisites You have signed in to your SAP Business Network buyer account as an administrator. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement > Manage Vendors. 2. Click Upload > Carrier Codes. 3. (Optional) Enter the name of the relevant CSV file in the Name field under Search Filters and click Search. 4. Click the name of the relevant CSV file in the Upload Details table. 5. Click Download File, make the required changes to the carrier list, save the file, and then upload it. Related Information Freight Carrier List Configuration [page 27] Uploading a Customized List of Freight Carriers [page 28] Replenishment Order Configuration Use this procedure to configure how suppliers manage their planned replenishments. Prerequisites • • You must be a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Planning Settings Authorization permission. If you plan to change the Replenishment time bucket setting in an existing custom configuration, prepare all affected suppliers for the change: • • • Tell all suppliers when you plan to make this change. Tell suppliers to publish all their planned replenishments for existing time buckets, to avoid data loss. Make sure all suppliers have completed publishing their planned replenishments before you change the setting. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 29 Context By creating a custom configuration of settings, you can apply to certain suppliers a set of replenishment-order business rules that differ from the System default settings. Procedure 1. Choose Planning Settings Assign suppliers . 2. Click the edit ( ) icon of the desired custom configuration for the Replenishment orders process type. If you instead want to create a new custom configuration, click the Add configuration button in the upper right corner. Then in the section that opens, do the following: • • Enter a name for the new configuration. Set the Process type field to Replenishment orders. 3. Make your configuration choices in the Planning process section: Option Description Suppliers or Supplier groups Add the suppliers or supplier groups the custom configuration applies to.  Restriction A mix of individual suppliers and supplier groups in the same custom configuration is not supported. If a member of a supplier group that is assigned a custom planning configuration is assigned as an individual supplier to another configuration, settings are applied to that supplier in the following priority: 1. Individual-supplier configuration 2. Supplier-group configuration 3. System default settings Replenishment horizon, in number of days Enter the replenishment horizon. The default is 180 days. Replenishment time bucket Choose Daily (default) or Weekly. Refresh planning data from current date Choose Yes or No (default). When this setting is enabled, a product activity message with changes for planning collaboration information clears all planning information between the current date and the earliest date in the message. Allow suppliers to edit price Choose Yes or No (default). Require suppliers to replenish within the proposed Choose Yes or No (default). range of minimum and maximum quantities Allow suppliers to send planned replenishment Choose Yes or No (default). Maximum number of line items allowed in replenishment orders Enter the maximum number to allow. The default is 1,000 line items. 4. Click Save. 30 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers

Rejection Code Configuration for Order Change Requests Buyer administrators can use CSV templates to upload rejection codes for their suppliers. The Upload dropdown on the templates: • • • Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors page provides the following CSV Priority Codes Reason Codes Rejected Reason Codes Buyer administrators can download these templates, populate them with values for their suppliers to use, and upload the information to SAP Business Network. Their supplliers can then use these codes when rejecting a change request. All codes are maintained in the buyer's ERP system. For details, see Uploading Priority, Reason, and Rejected-Reason Codes [page 31]. Uploading Priority, Reason, and Rejected-Reason Codes Use this procedure to upload change-request rejection codes to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer user assigned a role with the User Administration permission. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 31 Context Buyer administrators can use CSV templates to import to SAP Business Network the lists of codes to use in a buyer's change request or in a supplier's change-request rejection. You can upload codes multiple times. Each upload replaces the previous codes. Procedure 1. Go to Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 2. Choose Upload, then choose one of the following code types from the dropdown: • • • Priority Codes – Used by buyers in change requests. Reason Codes – Used by buyers in change requests. Rejected Reason Codes – Used by suppliers in change-request rejections. The Upload File page for the code type opens. 3. Click Download latest template version and save the template file.  Note To download a Rejected Reason Code template, first select Change Request Rejected reason codes from the Description field. 4. Open the downloaded template file for editing. 5. Starting on row 5 of the template file, enter each code and its description.  Caution Do not change or delete the information in rows 1 to 4 of the template. 6. For the Priority Codes, Reason Codes, and Rejected Reason Codes templates, enter in the Code Language column all languages that are valid for each code. The en value (English) is required for all codes. A list of the available language codes is provided in the template. 7. Save the edited template. 8. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 9. Choose Upload and select the code type to upload. The upload page for the code type opens. 10. Enter a name in the Name field to give to the file you're uploading. 11. Click Browse and select the saved template file you want to upload. 12. If you are uploading the Rejected Reason Codes template, click Description and choose Change Request Rejected reason codes. 13. Click the Upload button. The uploaded file's name is added to the Upload Details table at the end of the upload page. If necessary, click Refresh Status to update the file's upload status. If an error occurs during upload, an error message appears, and the Upload button changes to Reload. Correct the error in the file, browse for the file again, and click Reload. 32 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers Planning and Forecast Configuration Buyer administrators can set up key figures, attributes, and views to use in planning and forecast collaboration. Key Figures [page 33] Attributes for Planning Views [page 46] Forecast and Planning Collaboration Views [page 52] Key Figures Buyers and suppliers can use key figures in planning and forecast collaboration. Key figures contain numeric data that is represented either as a quantity or as a monetary value. Buyers and suppliers use key figures for planning and forecast collaboration to communicate about goods and materials. Typically, buyers want information about a set of key figures, not just one or two. A set of key figures is referred to as a view. Suppliers provide buyers with information about key figures, either through the user interface from the Planning Collaboration page or from the ... Upload/Download Jobs Planning tab using Excel files. There are two types of key figures: • Standard – A standard key figure is a figure that cannot be derived or calculated from other figures, such as the number of employees in a company. Other examples are sales, fixed costs, variable costs, and quantity produced. One example of a standard key figure used in planning collaboration is ORDER_FORECAST. This key figure contains the order forecast quantity. • Calculated – A calculated key figure is a figure that is derived or calculated using other figures. For example, if you have the SALES_REVENUE and EMPLOYEES key figures, you can create a calculated key figure with the sales revenue per employee using formula SALES_REVENUE/EMPLOYEES. Key figures used in a formula for a calculated key figure can be either standard or calculated key figures. One example of a calculated key figure used in planning collaboration is FORECAST_DEVIATION. This key figure is a calculation of the accuracy of the actual forecast demand from the committed forecast demand. It is calculated by subtracting the order forecast quantity (ORDER_FORECAST) from the forecast committed quantity (FORECAST_COMMIT). The formula is FORECAST_COMMIT-ORDER_FORECAST. See Key Figures Reference for Planning and Forecast Collaboration Views [page 34] for a list of the key figures defined for the planning and forecast collaboration views. See Key Figures Reference for the Component Planning Collaboration View [page 37] for a list of the key figures defined for component planning collaboration. These key figures populate from purchase order, ship notice, and goods receipt transactions. For these key figures to populate, their related transactions must arrive on SAP Business Network after the planning or forecast records are created. Transactions that arrive before the planning or forecast records are created do not populate any key figures. Also, for these transaction key figures to populate, the transaction's system ID and vendor ID must match the system ID and vendor ID of an existing planning or forecast record. • • You can edit key figure display names. The Supplier managed inventory, Supplier managed inventory days-of supply, Supplier managed replenishment, and Supplier managed replenishment days-of supply views all have Maximum proposal and Minimum proposal key figures. The default key figure display name for these key figures is identical in all these views, but the configuration IDs are different. Creating Custom Key Figures Use this procedure to create key figures for planning collaboration views. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Planning Settings Authorization permission. Context Buyer administrators can create custom key figures for planning collaboration views. You can create up to 100 custom key figures across all views. Procedure 1. Select Planning Settings Manage views . 2. Choose a view. The view's details page displays with the Key figures tab open. 3. Click Create new. The New key figure popup opens. 4. Enter information in the Key figure display name field and optionally in the Description field. The Key figure display name value automatically populates the Configuration ID field. 5. Choose Buyer or Supplier as the data source. 6. To enable any of the following key figure options, move its toggle switch to the On position. • • • Visible - Makes the key figure visible in the view. Editable by supplier - Allows suppliers to edit the key figure. Show in Excel - Includes the key figure in the Microsoft Excel file. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 39 • Time-based formula - Indicates the Expression field value is time-based. 7. Example: Time-based formula when a divisor value might be less than 1 A key-figure value used to divide a number in a formula might be zero or a negative number. Dividing by zero or a negative number causes an error in the formula calculation. To prevent this error, you can construct your formula to test for such values and, if found, divide instead by a number you specify in the formula. D[i] : 1) This added syntax first tests whether the value of D[i] is greater than 0. If D[i] is not greater than 0, the formula is instead divided by 1, the number that is specified in the formula. Example: Time-based formulas that reference past key figure values You may need to show a calculated key figure in a planning view that is calculated by the value of the same key figure in the previous time bucket, or the value of another key figure in the previous time bucket. For example, suppose you are customizing formulas for MY_KEY_FIGURE. When editing the formula for future time buckets, you want to reference the value of ORDER_FORECAST in the previous time bucket. In this case, the formula is as follows: MY_KEY_FIGURE = i === CURRENT_DATE ? ORDER_FORECAST[i] : ORDER_FORECAST[i-1] + 100 If the date is the current date, the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE is equal to the value of ORDER_FORECAST in the current time bucket; if the date is a future date, the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE is equal to the value of ORDER_FORECAST in the previous time bucket plus 100. Using the previous example, suppose you want to reference the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE in the previous time bucket in the formula for future time buckets. In this case, the formula is as follows: MY_KEY_FIGURE = i === CURRENT_DATE ? ORDER_FORECAST[i] : result[i-1] + 200 If the date is the current date, the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE is equal to the value of ORDER_FORECAST in the current time bucket; if the date is a future date, the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE is equal to the value of MY_KEY_FIGURE in the previous time bucket plus 200. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 45 Attributes for Planning Views Buyers can use attributes to define characteristics of planning items. Attributes can be included in views along with key figures. There are two types of attributes: • Standard – Standard attributes are predefined. Some examples of standard attributes are the following: • • • • Customer location Customer part no. Lead time Planner code Planning items are defined by the unique combination of the standard attributes Customer part no. and Customer location. The display name and behavior of standard attributes is fixed and cannot be altered. • Customer-defined – You can use customer-defined attributes to add information to planning items. You can also use customer-defined attributes as additional identifiers for planning items. For example, you could add a customer-defined attribute called Promotion and use the value of this attribute to help identify planning items.  Note Unlike key figures, customer-defined attributes included in views are not automatically updated by transactions like purchase orders, ship notices, goods receipts, and so on. See Creating a Customer-Defined Attribute for a View [page 47].  Caution Customer-defined attributes are not set up with data protection measures that are appropriate for sensitive data. Do not use customer-defined attributes for sensitive personal data (for example, Social Security numbers) or personal data (for example, addresses).
