SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 51 Forecast and Planning Collaboration Views Buyers use views to help visualize planning data. Views are used in planning and forecast collaboration to share information between buyers and suppliers. A view is a collection of key figures (standard, calculated, and custom) and attributes (standard and customer-defined) that provide a window into the planning data. The following table lists the standard views: View Description Aggregated forecast across locations Aggregated version of the forecast view across multiple locations Component planning collaboration view Component planning collaboration data for a finished good and its components.  Note The Component planning collaboration view does not support customer-defined attributes. External manufacturing visibility Data about external manufacturing items Forecast Forecast data for planning items Supplier managed inventory Information about supplier-managed inventory Supplier managed inventory days-of-supply Information about the days of supply left on the supplier's inventory Supplier managed replenishment Information about supplier-managed replenishment Supplier managed replenishment days-of-supply Information about the days of supply of replenishment You can configure views to contain the exact information you need. Some example configurations are hiding key figures, renaming key figure display names, adding custom key figures, and adding customer-defined attributes. See Customizing Key Figures and Attributes for a View [page 53] for more information about configuring views. In addition to the standard views, you can create custom views, each containing customized key figures and attributes. Custom views help make planning collaboration more efficient since only the fields that are needed for planning items are included. Tailoring multiple planning views to fit specific business needs, and assigning the most appropriate view to each planning item, ensures easier adoption for suppliers. It also minimizes errors and improves communication between trading partners. For example, you could create custom views for forecast planning items belonging to the Wholesale line of business and for forecast planning items belonging to the Retail line of business. Each of these views would have a different set of key figures and attributes. See Custom Views [page 54] for more information about custom views. You can set the key figure order for both standard and custom views. This order is visible in all the view's planning records, both in the user interface and in downloaded Excel files created from running Upload/Download jobs. See Changing Key Figure Order in a View [page 42]. To view product aggregation with the Aggregated forecast across locations view, go to Manage views 52 PUBLIC Aggregated forecast across locations Planning Settings and select the Enable this view on Excel checkbox. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 61 Supplier-Managed Inventory Alerts Settings Buyers can configure what supplier-managed inventory alerts Supply Chain Monitor generates. The Supply Chain Monitor supplier-managed inventory alerts feature provides a Supplier managed inventory exceptions section to the Administrator settings page accessed from the Supply Chain Monitor settings  popup. Buyers with the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission configure the alerts to generate for the following supplier-managed inventory exception types: • • • • Out of stock Above maximum Below minimum Replenishment orders out of tolerance As soon as changes to the Administrator Settings page are saved, the settings are in effect for newly sent product activity messages, product replenishment messages, and replenishment orders. Past alerts that were generated for different alerts settings aren't changed or removed. Forecast Alerts Settings Buyers can configure what forecast alerts Supply Chain Monitor generates. The Supply Chain Monitor forecast alerts feature provides a Forecast exceptions section to the Administrator settings on the Supply Chain Monitor settings  page. Buyers with the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission can configure which alerts to generate for the forecast exception types: • • • Missing commits Commit shortages Decommits As soon as changes to the Administrator Settings page are saved, the alerts settings are in effect for future forecasts and forecast commitments. Past alerts that were generated by different alerts settings aren't changed or removed. 62 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers Configuring Supply Chain Monitor Access Use this procedure to enable buyers to use Supply Chain Monitor. Prerequisites You must be a buyer administrator. For more information about creating and assigning roles, see SAP Business Network Users and Roles [page 99]. Context As a buyer administrator, you can create a role to grant permissions to buyer users for Supply Chain Monitor. Procedure 1. Choose Administration Create Role . 2. Enter a name for the role and a description. 3. Check the permissions you want to assign to the role, then choose Save. Permission Name Supply Chain Monitor Capability Buyer Dashboard For Supply Chain Collaboration Viewing Inbox and Order Access Viewing Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration Making setting changes 4. Assign the new role to users you want to have access to Supply Chain Monitor. Configuring Supply Chain Monitor Alerts Display Use this procedure to set what alerts information to show in Supply Chain Monitor. Prerequisites You are assigned a role with the permissions you need to configure Supply Chain Monitor alerts. For more information, see Supply Chain Monitor Component Requirements [page 58]. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 63 Context Buyers can configure filters that refine which alerts data is visible in Supply Chain Monitor. Procedure 1. On the Supply Chain Monitor page, choose the more ( ) icon of an exceptions group tile. A popup window opens that shows the list of alerts for the tile. 2. Check the alerts that you want to show in the tile, then dismiss the popup. 3. Hover over an alert name in the tile and choose the filter icon  that appears to the right of the name. The Configure your alerts page opens. 4. Configure alerts settings as desired, then close the window. Setting changes are saved and applied immediately.  Caution Setting Apply to all alerts overrides all existing alerts settings throughout the exception group. Allowing Suppliers to Submit Order Confirmations with Line-Item Deviations That Require Approval Use this procedure to control when suppliers can send order confirmations with deviations. Context You can enable transaction rules that allow suppliers to submit order confirmations with deviations from defined tolerances. A buyer can approve, approve with updates, or reject the deviations. Procedure 1. Choose Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules . 2. Scroll to the Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules section. 3. Check the following rules, to allow suppliers to send order confirmations: • • Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the line-item level 4. Optional: Configure the following rules to specify line item tolerances: 64 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers • • • • Apply line item quantity tolerance to order confirmations Apply line item unit price tolerance to order confirmations Allow suppliers to increase item quantities on order confirmations Apply line item delivery date tolerance to order confirmations 5. Check the following rule to allow suppliers to submit order confirmations with deviations from tolerances: • Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval  Note This rule applies only to material items, not service items. 6. Choose Save. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Setup for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers PUBLIC 65 SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration SAP Business Network business rules allow buyer administrators to control aspects of how order confirmations, ship notices, and other documents are created and how they flow between suppliers and buyers. Two categories of SAP Business Network business rules are important for the supply chain collaboration solution: • Default Transaction Rules These rules are available on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules they are applied to all suppliers who are enabled for supply chain collaboration functionality. • page, and Supplier Group Rules These rules are supplier-group specific rules that are enabled on the Supplier Group Transaction Rules page. Supplier group rules allow you to set confirmation and ship notice rules differently for specific sets of suppliers. For suppliers who are added to a group, rule settings that are created at the supplier group level override rule settings at the default transaction level. Suppliers can see the rules that were specified by the buyer on the Customer Details page of their SAP Business Network account. Notification Event That Triggers Notification Method General Notification Options A transmission failure has occurred. Online and email If you request immediate notification, SAP Business Network sends an email to the email addresses you set, without awaiting multiple retries. Notifications tell whether you can resolve issues on the local system, and provide the date/time stamp, document type, payload ID, document business number, last technical status, classification and severity, exception information, and a link to the affected document. You can also request a daily summary of notifications and choose whether to include notification of transient failures. You can choose to receive notifications of supplier-initiated document transactions that failed. Order An order is undeliverable, a supplier has updated an order’s status, or a supplier has generated an order confirmation or a ship notice. Online and email If you request a notification when a supplier updates the status of an order, SAP Business Network sends an email to the order requester, not to the email address specified for the notification. You can also include all line item details from the status update in the notification. SAP Business Network also sends an email to the order requester when a supplier acknowledges the order. By default, this option is enabled. If you do not want the order requester to receive a notification when the order is acknowledged, clear the check box for “Send a notification to the requester on the order when the order status changes.” Service Sheet A supplier has sent a new or updated service sheet. Online and email Invoice An invoice has arrived or been updated by a supplier. Online and email If you subscribe to an invoice conversion service, you can also receive notification when an unassigned invoice is waiting for you. An unassigned invoice is an invoice on which the supplier does not match any of the suppliers with which the buying organization has a trading relationship. For information about working with unassigned invoices, see the SAP Business Network guide to invoice conversion. Description Do not allow consumption to exceed balance quantity in component inventory. No When this rule is checked, an error message appears if consumption of component inventory that is managed in batches exceeds the available batch quantity. To allow suppliers to send a ship notice or a component consumption report with a negative stock quantity, leave this rule unchecked. Require the quantity of a consumed component in a ship notice to not exceed the component quantities in the related order No When this rule is checked, it prevents a ship notice from consuming a greater quantity of a component than is authorized in the subcontracting order. This rule applies to purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and scheduling agreement releases.  Note For this feature to validate a component as authorized for shipment, the component's information must be identical in both the subcontracting order and the ship notice. The following scenarios describe possible actions taken when this rule is enabled: Scenario Action taken • The components to be consumed are verified as not exceeding the component quantities that are authorized for consumption. Checks are made in the line items and schedule line items of the purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and scheduling agreement releases that are included in the ship notice or in reported consumption. If there are any errors, the rule displays messages that explain the reasons for the errors. • 70 PUBLIC A ship notice is created from the Create ship notice page of the SAP Business Network user interface. A Component Consumption Document is created with the Report Consumption button on a purchase order details page of the SAP Business Network user interface. The quantities of components consumed in that ship notice are automatically restored to the available quantity in the subcontracting purchase order. Or they're restored to the quantities for those components that are referenced in a ship notice that isn't in the Obsolete state. The quantity of components consumed in a ship notice is changed. The new version of the ship notice shows the revised quantities. Require buyer batch matching in component inventory. No When this rule is checked, the buyer batch number of a consumed component must match the buyer batch number that is defined in component inventory. Require suppliers to provide a unique asset serial number for each purchase order line item with consumed components. No When this rule is checked, an error message appears if component consumption contains a duplicate serial number in more than one line item. Require the total count of shipment serial numbers to not exceed the total quantity shipped for line items with consumed components. No When this rule is checked, an error message appears if component consumption contains more serial numbers for an item than the purchase order quantity of that line item. Require suppliers to provide asset serial numbers for the total shipped quantity of line items with consumed components. No When this rule is checked, an error message appears if component consumption contains a higher or lower number of serial numbers for an item than the purchase order quantity of that line item. Component Consumption Download and Upload via Excel Files Business Details This feature adds the Component Consumption job type to Upload/Download in SAP Business Network. Buyers and suppliers can create and run Component Consumption jobs to download prepopulated Excel files with component consumption data. Buyers can review the component consumption data in these downloaded Excel files. Suppliers can also review these downloaded Excel files and can additionally edit and add data to them and then upload them. This provides suppliers with the capability to process component consumption data in bulk.  Note A supplier can upload up to 600 rows per Excel file. If a supplier tries to upload a file with more than 600 rows, the upload fails and an error message displays. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 71 Changes to the User Interface When you create Upload/Download jobs from the Upload/Download Jobs page, the Create/Edit Job popup includes Component Consumption in the Type dropdown list. When you choose this type, the search criteria appear for a component consumption job. For details, see Component Consumption Template for Upload/ Download [page 73]. The supplier can edit the Excel file and add data to it based on individual needs, and then upload the Excel file to report component consumption in bulk. Restrictions A supplier can upload up to 600 rows per Excel file. If a supplier tries to upload a file with more than 600 rows, the upload fails and an error message displays. Component Consumption Template Criteria The Upload/Download job type: • • • • • page provides the following search criteria for the Component Consumption Name – (Required) The name to give the job. Type – (Required) Choose Component Consumption. Customer (Required, supplier view only) or Supplier (Required, buyer view only) The name of the buyer (supplier view) or supplier (buyer view) whose data you want in the Excel file. Order number – The ID of the purchase order. Line-item level • • • • • Jobs Supplier part number Supplier batch Buyer part number Buyer batch Component level • Supplier part number SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 73 • • • Supplier batch Buyer part number Buyer batch Editing the Component Consumption Excel File • The Item Serial Numbers column in the Component Consumption Excel file accepts multiple values, separated by pipe ( | ) characters. The multiple serial numbers are separated and assigned to the component consumption items. When there is a direct linkage of the serial number at the component level with the serial number at the line-item level, rows in the Excel file may need to be repeated for a specific line item with a single quantity to allow reference to related serial numbers for one or multiple components consumed for the line item. When rows are repeated in the Excel file, the Component Line Group column is used to clarify the assignment of the component serial number to specific line item serial numbers; this column is needed because the line item's serial number cannot be used to indicate this assignment. The value in the Component Line Group column is a number used once only for each upload. The following figure shows some example data. • The Item Schedule Line and Component Line Number columns in the the Component Consumption Excel file are read only. The values in these two columns are populated from the orders for informational purposes. These columns are not evaluated by SAP Business Network when the supplier uploads the Excel file. Uploading the Component Consumption Excel File • When the buyer enables certain component consumption transaction rules or sets the requiresRealTimeConsumption control key in the corresponding line item of the cXML file for the order, SAP Business Network performs additional validation during upload that may result in a validation failure. For example, if a buyer enables the Do not allow consumption to exceed balance quantity in component inventory rule, an uploaded Component Consumption Excel file fails validation if its entries do not all meet this rule. • After a supplier uploads a Component Consumption Excel file, its entry on the Uploads • • • Upload/Download page shows one of the following statuses: Completed – The upload processed without any errors. Completed with Errors – The upload contained errors. The rows without errors were processed. Failed – All rows had errors. The entry also displays a link to a log file that reports the upload status for successful and failed rows. • 74 When a supplier uploads a Component Consumption Excel file, if there are any empty Consumption ID fields, a unique ID is autogenerated, and the empty Consumption ID fields are filled with this unique ID. The autogeneration of the unique ID occurs in the backend system. The unique ID is not added to the Excel file. PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Order Change Request Rules Buyer administrators enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure additional transaction rules for order change requests. The following order change request rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Order Change Requests Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. • Allow suppliers to respond to a change request with a different quantity than the buyer proposed. When this rule is checked, suppliers can propose another quantity when they respond to a change request from a buyer for a purchase-order schedule line. Suppliers can request a different quantity only once per change request. • Allow suppliers to respond to a change request with a different delivery date than the buyer proposed. When this rule is checked, suppliers can propose another delivery date when they respond to a change request from a buyer for a purchase-order schedule line. Suppliers can request a different delivery date only once per change request. • Allow suppliers to request an additional cost when responding to a buyer request to change a schedule line. When this rule is checked, suppliers can request an additional charge for accepting a buyer's requested change to a purchase-order schedule line. Suppliers can request an additional charge only when the buyer has proposed a different quantity or delivery date. The supplier can split the response created by a change request. The supplier can send up to 2 responses corresponding to a change request. The split allows the supplier to propose 2 different dates when the deliveries can be made. The supplier can enter any one of the following values: • • • Supplier proposed delivery quantity Estimated cost A newly split change request can be deleted using the Delete action. When the user selects the split action for a change request, a new row is introduced below the selected change request which is being split. The Split action is available under the Actions column for each change request.The supplier can enter the following information for both the response lines (main and the split lines) • • • • Supplier proposed delivery date Supplier proposed delivery quantity Estimated cost Comment The only way to uniquely identify a parent and its split line or child is by entering 'one' and 'two'. If the change request is not split, there is empty data for it. If any change request has been split, the parent is shown using SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 75 'one' and the split using 'two'. There is a dedicated column for it called the Change request response line number which is also present in the Excel file the is uploaded by the supplier. To simulate a 'split' on the Excel file, the supplier will have to enter value in that column as 'one' and 'two'. Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure these transaction rules for order confirmation. The following order confirmation rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide.  Note Estimated shipping and delivery dates are attributes of the cXML itemOut element. Therefore, any estimated shipping and delivery date, even when defined at the header level, is applied at the line-item level without consideration of any transaction rules that prevent suppliers from editing line items. To prevent suppliers from editing estimated shipping and delivery dates, you must request a customization project to hide the Est. Shipping Date and Est. Delivery Date fields in order confirmations. Rule Require suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the schedule line-item level. Default Setting Description No This rule is available only when the following two rules are also checked: • • Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders. Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the line item level. (This rule is visible only when the rule before it's enabled.) When this rule is checked: • • Every supplier confirmation must reference a specific schedule line. Suppliers can't use the following methods to upload mass order confirmations: • From the … Upload/Download Uploads page, an Order Confirmation Excel file. • From … Order Confirmation , in the CSV Upload sec- tion, a CSV file that is missing any schedule-line information. Suppliers can still upload a CSV file with complete schedule-line information. 76 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration Rule Default Setting Validate tolerance for quantity, No delivery date, or both at the scheduleline level. Description This rule is available only when Require suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the schedule line-item level is checked. This rule has two validation options. You can set one or both options: • Quantity tolerance – Set this tolerance value with order confirmation control key QuantityTolerance or by enabling the rule Apply line item quantity tolerance to order confirmations. • Date tolerance – Set this tolerance value with order confirmation control key TimeTolerance or by enabling the rule Apply line item delivery date tolerance to order confirmations. For further information, see Calculation of Quantity Tolerance Compliance and Tolerance Hierarchy for Quantity, Delivery Date, and Unit Price. Allow suppliers to edit components in order confirmations. When this rule is checked, suppliers can edit subcontracting component assignments and batch information as part of the order confirmation process. Otherwise, suppliers can't edit subcontracting components on order confirmations. Allow suppliers to send a ship notice No for a material in an open quality notification with no purchase order reference, only after the quality notification is closed or the buyer has accepted the quality inspection for the purchase order. This rule only applies to quality notifications without a purchase order reference. When enabled, suppliers must resolve the defect for a material (Customer part no.) referenced in an open quality notification before they can create a ship notice for a purchase order that contains the material. Suppliers can create a ship notice only when the quality notification for the material is closed or when the buyer accepts a quality inspection for the purchase order. This rule must be set to apply to buyers, suppliers, or both. Allow suppliers to edit estimated shipping dates, delivery dates, and quantities on the Items to Confirm tab. This rule allows buyers to permit suppliers to edit the estimated shipping and estimated delivery dates, and quantity, for line items when creating an order confirmation on the Items to Confirm tab.  Note This rule, whether enabled or disabled, doesn’t affect suppliers' ability to edit estimated shipping and delivery dates when confirming orders in the SAP Business Network mobile app or when confirming entire orders at the header level. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 77 Default Setting Rule Allow check for estimated shipping or Yes delivery dates in the past when order confirmations are submitted. Description This rule allows buyers to control whether suppliers can submit order confirmations with estimated shipping or delivery dates that are in the past. The order confirmation can be for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release. When the rule is checked, SAP Business Network validates the estimated shipping and delivery dates on order confirmations when the order confirmation is created. By default, if either date is in the past, an error is triggered.  Note This rule isn't enforced for unplanned lean service items or material items in an order confirmation. When the rule is unchecked, SAP Business Network doesn't validate these dates, so a supplier can submit an order confirmation with an estimated shipping or estimated delivery date that is in the past. Allow suppliers to send order confirmations on line item level. Yes This rule allows buyers to enable or disable the visibility to suppliers of purchase order line items in the Items to Confirm table. This rule is checked by default. When this rule is unchecked, purchase orders between the buyer and the supplier remain visible, but not actionable, in the supplier's Items to Confirm table. Allow suppliers to send order confirmations to this account. Yes This rule is checked by default. When this rule is unchecked, no purchase orders from this buyer are visible in supplier Items to Confirm tables. 78 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration Rule Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval. Default Setting Description No This rule only applies to purchase orders. When this rule is checked, suppliers can send order confirmations with line items that are out of quantity, delivery date, or price tolerance. Such line items are updated with a status of Awaiting Approval. The quantity, delivery date, or price deviation from the order must be approved or rejected by the buyer.  Restriction This rule applies only to material items. This rule doesn't apply to purchase orders that are excluded from the deviation approval process in the cXML (<Extrinsic name="OCDeviationApproval">notAllowed</ Extrinsic>). This rule isn't enforced for unplanned material items in an order confirmation. This rule has two levels of deviation approval for order confirmations: • Single-level deviation approval – Provides a single level of approval. Customers approve deviations directly in the buyer portal. Default setting. • Multilevel deviation approval – Provides multiple levels of approval. Customers approve deviations first in the buyer portal, then in the customer’s back-end ERP system. When enabled, this rule shows the following checkboxes, which set exceptions to the rule for their individual deviation types. If a supplier enters a value that is outside the permitted tolerance for an excepted deviation type, a message displays to indicate an error.  Caution A buyer who wants to set an exception to any deviation type needs to first reject from all partially confirmed orders any existing deviations of that type. This task prevents possible unexpected behavior that can be caused by conflicts after you set an exception rule. • Except quantity deviations – When checked, the rule isn't applied to quantity deviations in an order confirmation. • Except delivery date deviations – When checked, the rule isn't applied to delivery-date deviations in an order confirmation. • Except price deviations – When checked, the rule isn't applied to unit-price deviations in an order confirmation. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 79 Rule Allowed actions for order confirmation deviation approval. Default Setting Description No When this rule is checked, you can configure the available deviation approval actions to Approve, Approve and update, or both. By default, both actions are checked. The actions apply for both single-level and multilevel deviation approvals. If only Approve is checked, for a single-level deviation approval of a price deviation, the new supplier-proposed price can't be updated in the buyer's back-end system, because price information can't be updated in the Confirmations tab.  Note Allow suppliers to send ship notices only after receiving acceptance of inspection results. No • The Approve and Approve and update actions apply only to purchase orders. The actions don't apply to scheduling agreements or scheduling agreement releases. • When you configure multilevel deviation approval, the Approve and update action is checked by default, and you can't uncheck it. When this rule is checked, suppliers can’t send ship notices for goods that require inspection, unless the buyer has accepted the inspection results. Otherwise, suppliers can send ship notices for goods that require inspection without receiving acceptance of inspection results. Require the quantity of a component receipt item to not exceed the component ship notice quantity. No When this rule is checked, a component receipt must report item quantities that are equal to or less than the item quantities in the component ship notice. This rule excludes from a component receipt all flipped items that are already received, and shows an error message.  Note For this functionality, you need to set the frequency that your ERP system sends goods receipts to SAP Business Network to the shortest interval that is feasible for your organization. For example, you can choose to set your ERP to send goods receipts every 15 minutes. This ERP setting ensures that SAP Business Network can update a component ship notice to Partially received or Received in close to real time. SAP Business Network depends on these statuses to help determine whether a new component goods receipt would be a duplicate. 80 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: Rule Require the quantity of a component receipt item to not exceed the multitier ship notice quantity. Default Setting Description No When this rule is checked, a component receipt must report item quantities that are equal to or less than the item quantities in the multitier ship notice. When Allow suppliers to create a component receipt for multiple multi-tier ship notices is also checked, this rule excludes from a component receipt all flipped items that are already received, and shows an error message.  Note For this functionality, you need to set the frequency that your ERP system sends goods receipts to SAP Business Network to the shortest interval that is feasible for your organization. For example, you can choose to set your ERP to send goods receipts every 15 minutes. This ERP setting ensures that SAP Business Network can update a component ship notice to Partially received or Received in close to real time. SAP Business Network depends on these statuses to help determine whether a new component goods receipt would be a duplicate. Do not allow suppliers to create a ship notice for order lines that have a change request. When this rule is checked, if a purchase order line item or schedule line has a change request, suppliers can't use the Releases Items to Ship Orders Orders and page to create a ship notice for that line item or schedule line. However, the supplier can still use other methods to create a ship notice for that item or schedule line, such as by using cXML or a spreadsheet upload. Order Confirmation, Ship Notice, and Component Receipt Attachment Rules Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure these transaction rules for attachments in order confirmations, ship notices, and component receipts. The following attachment rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Order Confirmation, Ship Notice, and Component Receipt Attachment Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 81 Rule Default Setting Description Allow suppliers to include Disabled Check this rule to allow suppliers to attach files to component receipts. Disabled When this rule is checked, suppliers must attach required quality certifi- attachments with component receipts Require suppliers to provide a quality certificate on ship notices cates to a ship notice. Purchase Order Rules Buyer administrators enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure an additional transaction rule for purchase orders. The following purchase order rule is available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Purchase Order Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. • Override supplier's routing method for orders that match buyer's conditions If this rule is checked, the supplier’s default routing method is overridden for orders that match any of the specified conditions, thus preventing it from being routed to an external integration channel. Click Configure to specify one or more conditions. If an order matches any of the conditions, it is routed to the supplier on SAP Business Network. Quality Collaboration Rules Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure transaction rules for quality collaboration. To use quality collaboration, buyers must be entitled for the quality collaboration component, and suppliers must have a trading relationship with a buyer entitled for the quality collaboration component. The following quality collaboration rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page in the Quality Collaboration section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide. 82 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration Rule Allow suppliers to create non-PO quality notifications in a multi-ERP environment Default Setting Description No If this rule is checked, suppliers can create non-PO quality notifications and select which system they apply to when there are multiple routing end points. Otherwise, quality notifications are always sent to the default routing end point.  Note The buyer's account must be configured for multi-ERP support. Allow suppliers to send quality notifications for indirect orders without part numbers No Do not allow suppliers to send nonPO quality notifications No If this rule is checked, suppliers can send quality notifications for line items without specifying a customer part number or customer location. This rule makes those two quality notification fields optional. If this rule is checked, suppliers can only create quality notifications that reference an order. Otherwise, suppliers can create non-PO quality notifications from the Quality tab. Activate DocuSign for quality inspection documents No If this rule is checked, suppliers must electronically sign quality inspection results before submitting them. Currently DocuSign is the only supported electronic signature provider. Scheduling Agreement Release Setup Rules Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure these transaction rules for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. The following scheduling agreement and scheduling agreement release rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Scheduling Agreement Release Setup Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. Rule Default Setting Description Allow scheduling agreement collaboration No When this rule is checked, the buyer can send scheduling agreement documents for collaboration with suppliers. And suppliers who are enabled for supply chain collaboration functionality can create ship notices from scheduling agreements. This rule is unchecked by default. Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration No When this rule is checked, the buyer can send scheduling agreement release documents for collaboration with suppliers. And suppliers who are enabled for supply chain collaboration functionality can create ship notices from scheduling agreement releases. This rule is unchecked by default. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 83 Default Setting Rule Description Allow suppliers to use only JIT for shipping This subrule is visible only when the Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration rule is checked. For suppliers that have both JIT (Just In Time) and Forecast release capability, make sure this rule is checked to restrict suppliers to using JIT for shipping. Allow suppliers to use only Forecast for shipping This subrule is visible only when the Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration rule is checked. For suppliers that have both JIT (Just In Time) and Forecast release capability, make sure this rule is checked to restrict suppliers to using Forecast for shipping. 84 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration Rule Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases Default Setting Description No This rule can be enabled only when the Allow scheduling agreement collaboration rule, the Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration rule, or both, are checked. This rule also requires that the Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the line-item level rule is checked. When this rule is enabled, suppliers can confirm scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. Suppliers can only confirm Firm schedule lines. Rules related to purchase order confirmation also apply to scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. This rule provides the following subrule: Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval. Values are Yes or No. When enabled, suppliers can send order confirmations that are out of tolerance for delivery date and/or quantity. Line item status is updated to Awaiting Approval, and the buyer must approve or reject the order confirmation. This subrule provides the following subrules: • Except quantity deviations. Values are Yes or No. When enabled, the rule is not applied to quantity deviations in an order confirmation for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. • Except delivery date deviations. Values are Yes or No. When enabled, the rule is not applied to delivery-date deviations in an order confirmation for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases.  Restriction SAP Business Network does not support order confirmations for scheduling agreements or scheduling agreement releases that are generated by using a release creation profile in the SAP ECC or SAP S/4HANA system. Schedule-line numbers in such order confirmations are incompatible with the SAP Business Network logic for retaining a confirmation, which is based on the schedule-line number. When a supplier submits a changed order confirmation from SAP Business Network , the new order confirmation overwrites the previous confirmation that was stored in the SAP ECC or SAP S/4HANA system. Retain schedule-line confirmations in a new version of a scheduling agreement or scheduling agreement release No When this rule is checked, confirmed schedule lines in a scheduling agreement or scheduling agreement release remain confirmed when a new version of the document is received. In the past, the retain logic was executed by default, but it is now controlled by this new rule. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 85 Ship Notice Rules Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can configure these transaction rules for ship notices. The following ship notice rules are available for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers on the Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules page, in the Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules section. For additional transaction rules available to all SAP Business Network buyers, see Default Transaction Rules in the SAP Business Network buyer administration guide. Default Setting Rule Description Allow third-party suppliers to send multi-tier ship notices to this account When this rule is enabled, third-party suppliers can create ship notices for multitier orders. Require suppliers to close a quality If this rule is checked, suppliers must resolve a reported defect for an notification for an item before they item and close the quality notification before they can create a ship notice can create a ship notice for the to replace the complaint quantity for that item. complaint quantity Require suppliers to provide a unique asset serial number for each purchase order line item on a ship notice This rule applies within the scope of the order line item. Using the same serial number on any of the ship notice line items for this order line item is not allowed. If validation fails, the error message you receive is Asset serial numbers for item shipments must be unique. Require the total count of shipment serial numbers not to exceed the total quantity shipped for line items on ship notices Within a ship notice item, the number of serial numbers must be less than or equal to the quantity shipped. If validation fails the error message you receive is The total number of shipment serial numbers exceeds the quantity shipped for the line item. Require suppliers to provide asset serial numbers for the total shipped quantity of line items on ship notices This rule applies within the scope of the order line item. When this rule is checked, suppliers must provide an asset serial number for the total shipped quantity of line items. Require the Packing Slip ID to be unique on ship notices Duplicate shipment notice numbers (Packing Slip IDs) are not allowed. This rule is validated against all ship notice numbers for the particular supplier without time window restriction. If validation fails the error message you receive is This Packing Slip ID has already been used. Please enter a unique ID. Require ship notice type on ship notices When this rule is checked ship notices lacking a type are not allowed. For the type, the supplier must choose either actual or estimated. Allow suppliers to create invoice number automatically from Packing Slip ID when creating a ship notice When this rule is checked, it ensures that the Packing Slip ID value is copied to the Invoice # field automatically when a supplier is creating a ship notice. Require suppliers to provide a Global Individual Asset ID for line items on ship notices that conforms to the Serial Shipping Container Code (SSCC) format Requires that the asset IDs for line numbers on ship notices use the SSCC format used to identify logistics units, such as a case or pallet. The SSCC code is an 18-digit number, and the last digit is a check digit that ensures that the data is entered correctly. When this rule is checked, SAP Business Network uses the check digit algorithm to validate the number. For more information about SSCC, see http://www.gs1.org/ Require suppliers to provide a unique Global Individual Asset ID for line items on ship notices 86 PUBLIC . Requires that when suppliers provide an asset ID for line items on ship notices, the ID must be unique for the customer-supplier relationship. It cannot be used on ship notices from other suppliers to that same customer. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration Default Setting Rule Description Allow suppliers to create a component receipt for multiple multitier ship notices When this rule is checked, suppliers can create a component receipt that references multiple multitier ship notices. Otherwise, each component receipt must reference only one multitier ship notice. Require all items in a ship notice to contain at least one consumed component When this rule is checked, suppliers must provide at least one consumed component in a ship notice. Setting Default Transaction Rules Use this procedure to set the business rules for submitted transaction documents. Prerequisites You have signed in to your SAP Business Network buyer account as an administrator or a buyer enabled for the Transaction Configuration permission. Context Buyer administrators enable or disable business rules by managing their profiles. Procedure 1. Go to Administration Configuration . 2. Choose Default Transaction Rules. 3. Check the boxes to enable any of the business rules in the Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules section. Uncheck the boxes to disable them. 4. Click Save. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 87 Setting Supplier Group Rules Use this procedure to set rules for a selected set of suppliers. Prerequisites You have signed in to your SAP Business Network buyer account as an administrator or a buyer with the Transaction Configuration permission. Context You can apply SAP Business Network business rules to specific groups of suppliers. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement > Supplier Groups. 2. Do one of the following: • • To create a new group, choose Create and add group details. To edit an existing group, select the group name. 3. Choose Supplier Group Transaction Rules. 4. Check Enter supplier group specific transaction rules and check the appropriate rule in the Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Rules section. 5. Choose OK to return to the Edit Supplier Group page, then choose OK on that page to save your suppliergroup configuration. Configuring Quality Review Auto-Numbering Use this procedure to automatically assign custom numbering to quality reviews. Context When auto-numbering is configured, quality review numbers are auto-generated. 88 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration Procedure 1. Choose Administration Configuration Document Number Preferences . 2. In the Quality Review section, click Create.  Note If you reach the maximum limit, a warning message displays. 3. On the Configure Numbering page, enter the desired numbering criteria and constraints and click OK. 4. Verify the configuration and click Save. 5. Click Edit to modify the desired numbering criteria, then click Save. Uploading Quality Notification Codes Use this procedure to upload the codes to be used in quality notifications. Context Quality notification codes define the metadata values used by your quality notification system. A buyer administrator must upload quality notification codes to populate the system with values that reflect your quality notification process. If you are integrating with an SAP ERP with Quality Notifications (QM-QN), upload the same quality notification codes used by your SAP ERP system. You can upload quality notification codes multiple times. Each upload replaces the previous codes. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 2. Click Upload > Quality Notification, Review Codes. The Upload Quality Notification and Review Codes page opens. 3. In the Description field, click Select and choose Notification codes from the dropdown. 4. Below the Upload button, click the Download latest template version link. 5. Save the template (a CSV file) to your computer. 6. Open the template file for editing. 7. Starting with the 6th row, add your quality notification code data in the following columns.  Caution The first 5 rows are headings and must not be edited. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 89 • • • • • Code Group – This field is optional if Code Type is Reason, Type, or Revision. Code Group Description – This field is optional if Code Type is Reason, Type, or Revision. Code Name – If this field contains data, the Quality Code Group, Quality Code Type, and System ID fields are ignored. Code Description Code Type – Valid values are: • • • • • • • • • • • • • Subject Activity Defect Cause Task Reason Type Revision Code Language Quality Code Group Quality Code Type System ID Quality Review Template 8. Save the CSV file. 9. On the Upload Quality Notification and Review Codes page, enter a name for the upload in the Name field. 10. In the Description field, click Select and choose Notification codes from the dropdown. 11. Click Browse, select the CSV file you saved, and click Open. 12. Click Upload. 13. In the Upload Status section, click Refresh Status to refresh the status of the upload. • • If the Status is Done, the upload was successful. If the Status is Error, there were errors in your file. Correct the errors in the file and upload it again. Related Information Example of Quality Notification Codes [page 91] 90 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration

Prerequisites • • Buyers: Your account is entitled for the quality collaboration component. Suppliers: You have a trading relationship with a buyer entitled for the quality collaboration component. Context Buyers and suppliers can enable notifications for different types of documents and different events. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Settings . The Quality Settings page opens. 2. Click Edit. 3. If you are a supplier, choose one of the following options: • • Same rule for all customers – Applies these quality settings to all of your customers. Separate rules for each customer – Applies separate quality settings to each customer. If you choose this option, click Add customer to specify a customer to define settings for. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 93 For quality reviews only, when a quality review event occurs, all users who have their settings configured to receive quality review notifications from you for that type of event will receive them. 4. If you are a buyer, choose one of the following options: • • Same rule for all suppliers – Applies these quality settings to all of your suppliers. Separate rules for each supplier – Applies separate quality settings to each supplier. If you choose this option, click Add supplier to specify a supplier to define settings for. For quality reviews only, when a quality review event occurs, all users who have their settings configured to receive quality review notifications from you for that type of event will receive them. 5. Check the email notification options you prefer for Quality inspections, Quality notifications, and Quality reviews. 6. Click Submit. Overriding the Rule Determining Release Type for Shipping Use this procedure to override scheduling agreement release rules for a supplier. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Transaction Configuration permission. Context For a specific supplier, a buyer can override the rule determining the release type suppliers use for shipping. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. In the Current Suppliers table, for a supplier for whom you want to override the rule, click More Actions Edit . 3. Under the heading Scheduling Agreement Release Setup Rules, check Override the following default scheduling agreement release rules.  Note Make sure Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration remains checked. 94 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration 4. Check either of these rules to enable that rule for this specific supplier. • • Allow suppliers to use only JIT for shipping. Allow suppliers to use only Forecast for shipping. 5. Click Save. Prerequisites You must be an administrator. Context You can create a custom configuration of settings for the Forecast, and Manufacturing Visibility planning processes. Procedure 1. Choose Buyer User Profile Settings Transactions Supplier Group Rules Supplier Rules . 2. In the upper right corner of the page, choose Add to create a new custom configuration. Configuration fields appear for the configuration's name, type of supplier and their names, and rules to set in Planning process and Forecast sections. 3. Enter your configuration choices. a. Type the name to give the new configuration. b. Add the suppliers or supplier groups the custom configuration applies to.  Restriction A mix of individual suppliers and supplier groups is not supported. c. Set the desired Forecast, and Manufacturing Visibility settings. The following table shows the available settings and their default values, if any. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 95 Planning Process Setting Default Value Supplier managed inventory Process type Planned shipments Replenishment horizon, in number of days 180 Replenishment time bucket Daily Refresh planning data from current date No Match transaction quantities to transactional key figures even No if coming from a different system ID No Allow suppliers to edit supplier stock on hand When this rule is set to Yes, suppliers can update their stock-onhand levels. Forecast No Allow suppliers to view forecast data When this rule is set to Yes, suppliers can view forecast data from buyers. No Allow suppliers to commit to forecast data When this rule is set to Yes, suppliers can commit to forecast data to buyers. The Allow suppliers to view forecast data setting must be Yes to be able to change this setting. Forecast commit horizon, in days (does not affect B2B mes- 1095 sages) To limit the period for which the supplier can commit to quantities forecast, enter a number into the days field for the transaction rule. The Allow suppliers to view forecast data setting must be Yes to be able to change this setting. Forecast commit lock horizon, in days (does not affect B2B 0 messages) Once a time series reaches the commit lock period, the supplier can no longer change that quantity. Forecast commit lock horizons are enforced in Forecast downloads from the Quick Links Upload/Download Jobs tab, when the job criteria uses the Daily time period. A supplier is prevented from editing commit key figures for a time series that is within the locked period. The Allow suppliers to view forecast data setting must be Yes to be able to change this setting. 96 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration Planning Process Setting Default Value Use Time series end date to populate Forecast data No When set to Yes, each forecast quantity is posted to the end date of its time period, instead of the start date. The Allow suppliers to view forecast data setting must be Yes to be able to change this setting. Forecast commit time bucket Daily If the buyer selects All, the supplier can choose the time series granularity to use for each planning item. When the buyer selects a specific time series granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly), the supplier is only allowed to commit forecasts using that time series granularity. Refresh forecast data from current date No When this setting is enabled, a product activity message with changes to forecast information clears all forecast information between the current date and the earliest date in the message. The Allow suppliers to view forecast data setting must be Yes to be able to change this setting. Match transaction quantities to transactional key figures even No if coming from a different system ID When this setting is enabled, the transactional key figures no longer check for matching System ID values in their calculations. Instead, they validate that a product activity message has the same values for Customer part no., Supplier part no., Vendor ID, and Customer location as the purchase order it's for, before performing their calculations. Clear buyer-sent key figures in forecast when planning item No with no time-series data is received When this rule is set, if the buyer sends a forecast-type product activity message in cXML that does not include data in its details section for the ORDER_FORECAST key figure or any buyersourced custom key figures, SAP Business Network clears the key figure data for those missing key figures from both the buyer’s and the supplier's planning tables.  Caution Buyers should be careful when clearing key figure data from planning tables with cXML. After SAP Business Network processes the cXML message, the key figure data is gone and cannot be retrieved. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration PUBLIC 97 Planning Process Setting Default Value Manufacturing Visibility Planning horizon, in number of days 180 The number of days in the future that suppliers can send Manufacturing Planning Visibility planning items, from 0 to 1095 days. Must match Customer part ID and Customer location with No existing records When this setting is Yes, Manufacturing Planning Visibility planning items must match at least one existing planning item created by the buyer for a planning process. Component planning collaboration Enable component planning collaboration No When this setting is set, if a planning item matches a finished good or a component stored in a BOM in SAP Business Network, its corresponding component planning collaboration item is created or updated. 4. Click Save. Next Steps If a member of a supplier group that is assigned a custom planning configuration is assigned as an individual supplier to another configuration, settings are applied to that supplier in the following priority: 1. Individual-supplier configuration 2. Supplier-group configuration 3. System default settings 98 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Business Rules and Configuration SAP Business Network Users and Roles By creating roles and then adding users to them, the SAP Business Network administrator controls who can sign in to your organization’s account and which areas of the service each user can access. SAP Business Network Roles [page 99] SAP Business Network Users [page 104] SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113] Prevention of Manual Sign In by SAP Business Network Buyer Users [page 122] SAP Business Network Roles A user with the Administrator role can create a role with certain permissions and assign the role to a buyer user. A role defines a user function within SAP Business Network, such as Purchase Order Generator. Each role has a unique name and set of associated permissions that specify what users who are assigned to the role can see and do in SAP Business Network. A role can be assigned to any number of users. Using the Administrator Role After you complete registration, SAP Business Network creates a single default role named Administrator. The Administrator role is automatically linked to the user name and sign in that you entered during registration. The Administrator role should be assigned to the individual at your organization who is responsible for setting configuration options, managing supplier relationships and contacts, and maintaining the account over time. The account administrator serves as the primary point of contact for users with questions or problems. As the SAP Business Network account administrator, you control who can sign in to your organization’s SAP Business Network account and which areas of the service each user can access. To do this, you create roles and then add users. As a best practice, create roles that reflect the way your company does business to prevent confusion for your account users and maximize the efficiency of your team once roles are in place. Only one SAP Business Network user can be assigned to the Administrator role. You cannot modify this role, but you can assign it to another user. The account administrator can assign user management capabilities to non-administrator buyer users, called user administrators. For more information, see the following topics: • • Transferring Administration Ownership [page 113] Assigning User Management Capabilities to Users SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 99 SAP Business Network Predefined Roles Predefined roles are visible only in accounts that were created before roles and permissions were introduced on SAP Business Network. If you registered with SAP Business Network after roles and permissions were implemented, Administrator is the only predefined role. To minimize disruption to these older users, SAP Business Network provides a small set of predefined roles to be used as templates for custom roles. SAP Business Network assigned the Full Access role to all preexisting users when it introduced roles and permissions. Administrators for these older supplier accounts should review the predefined roles and their permissions and consider using them as the basis for custom roles. The predefined roles are listed in the following table: This Role… Grants a User Access To… Administrator All areas of the account, including Catalog Manager Catalogs Settings Users and test account management Customer Catalogs Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Catalog Service Full Access All areas of SAP Business Network, except areas that are reserved for administrators Purchasing Manager Give access to incoming and outgoing transaction documents and the following configuration pages: Vendor Manager Account Settings Manage Profile Default Transaction Rules Account Settings Manage Profile cXML Setup Account Settings Manage Profile Notifications Supplier Enablement Current Relationships Supplier Enablement Contacts Account Settings Manage Profile Account Settings Company Profile Product Manager Catalogs Network Catalog Product Approver Catalogs Network Catalog Notifications (transaction-related notifications only) Supplier The Administrator role includes all available permissions. These permissions grant the Administrator role access to all areas of your SAP Business Network account. file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: Creating a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can define new roles with a specific set of user permissions that determine what the assigned users can see or do in SAP Business Network. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. • Before creating your first role, you might want to review the list of permissions. This list is useful for planning your approach to roles. Some companies create broadly defined roles that include all or most of the available permissions, while others create specialized roles that include narrow sets of permissions. By planning your approach to roles, you can prevent confusion for your account users and maximize the efficiency of your team after roles are in place. • Before creating new roles, use the Permission dropdown menu to filter the Roles table for existing roles that already include that permission. Context A role defines a user function within SAP Business Network. You assign roles when you create users.  Restriction • • You can create no more than 25 custom roles. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Before you make changes, you might want to inform users who will be affected. Procedure 1. Choose The Account Settings Account Settings Users Settings Users . page appears with the Manage Roles tab selected by default. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 101 Figure 1: Manage Roles Tab 2. Click the Create Role icon  at the top right of the role results table. 3. Enter a distinctive name for the role. 4. Enter a description to record your intentions for this role. Descriptions can be useful later, if you want to review or revise the structure of your roles. 5. Select one or more permissions for the new role. Each role must have at least one permission.  Note You can also select all permissions by clicking on the checkbox at the top left of the list of permissions. 6. Click Save. Results SAP Business Network creates the role and returns you to the Manage Roles page. Modifying a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can edit a role's name, description, and assigned permissions. Prerequisites • 102 You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles • You have informed users about role changes that can affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, search for a Permission using the search filters, or scroll down and locate the role you want to modify. 3. In the Role Name column of the search results table, select the role you want to modify. 4. Check Show me all the available permissions and select the permissions you want or uncheck the permissions you don't want for that role. 5. Choose Save. SAP Business Network applies your changes to all users assigned to the role. Changes take effect for each user at their next sign in. Reassigning Users to a Different Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can change the role assigned to users. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. • You have informed users about role changes that will affect them.SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, scroll down to the role you want to investigate. 3. Click the role in the Role Name column. 4. Scroll down to the Assigned Users table. 5. Using the checkboxes, select the users you want to move to another role. 6. Click Move to another role. 7. Click Save to return to the Manage Roles page. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles PUBLIC 103 Deleting a Role Buyer administrators and users assigned a role with the User Administration permission can delete roles that they no longer need. Prerequisites • You are assigned a role with the User Administration permission. See SAP Business Network Permissions [page 113]. • You have informed users about role changes that will affect them. SAP Business Network does not notify users of changes to roles. • No users can be assigned the role you want to delete. To change a user to another role, see Reassigning Users to a Different Role [page 103]. Procedure 1. Choose Account Settings Settings Users . 2. On the Manage Roles tab, you can perform a search for the role you want to delete, if necessary. Search for a Permission using the search filters. Or, scroll down and locate the role you want to delete. 3. In the Actions column of the roles results table, click the Delete  icon. Results SAP Business Network deletes the role and returns to the Users page. SAP Business Network Users Access to a buyer account is secured with individual user identities and levels of permissions. A user is an SAP Business Network sign in (user name and password) that enables one individual in your organization to sign in to your account. The administrator adds users to the SAP Business Network account and assigns each user exactly one role, which typically corresponds to the user’s real-world job responsibilities. 104 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network Users and Roles Best Practices in Managing User Accounts When the administrator of an SAP Business Network account creates users and assigns roles, it is mandatory that the administrator assigns a unique user name with an appropriate assigned role for each individual who needs to access the account. Users must not share their user name or password with other users. This is important for SAP Business Network and your company in managing data privacy and integrity on SAP Business Network. For security, account administrators and users who have PCard access but are not the PCard owner are required to update their password every 90 days. As a best practice, users should not share their secret question and secret answer. To ensure your organization and users have secure accounts on SAP Business Network, create individual user accounts for different roles in the organization. By default, add one role per user. Users can have multiple related roles, depending on the tasks assigned to the user. How Roles Control User Interface Access Every user can see the Configuration Personal Information area, which contains basic contact information and a preferred language setting for that specific user. Beyond that, the only areas that a user is permitted to see are those allowed by their role permissions. For example, if the administrator created a role that included the Contact Administration permission, a user assigned to that role could see only the Information area and the Supplier Enablement Configuration Personal Contacts area of your SAP Business Network account. While users can update their own personal information, the administrator is responsible for overall user maintenance, which includes deleting users or reassigning user sign ins when individuals leave the company, and resetting user passwords.
