file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: Configuring DocuSign for Electronic Signatures Buyer administrators must set up three fields on the DocuSign Integration Setup page before using DocuSign for electronic signatures. Prerequisites You have a license from DocuSign. Additionally, if you want your suppliers to comply with FDA 21 CFR Part 11 regulations, you must subscribe to the DocuSign Part 11 module. For more information about this module, refer to How the DocuSign Part 11 Module Fits with 21 CFR Part 11 . Procedure 1. Sign in to your DocuSign account. 2. Choose Settings from the DocuSign account top menu. 3. Go to Admin > INTEGRATIONS. 4. Find your DocuSign API Account ID. a. Click Apps and Keys. b. Locate your API Account ID in the My Account Information section. c. Copy your API Account ID to a file. 5. Set up a secret key.  Note The following instructions are from DocuSign's How to set up HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) security with your app page. a. Click Connect. b. Choose Connect Keys. c. Choose + ADD SECRET KEY. The screen shows the added secret key. d. Copy the secret key to a file. 6. Set up a generic user to handle creating electronic envelopes in DocuSign. a. Click Users. b. Click ADD USER. c. Create a user. Refer to the User Management instructions. section of the DocuSign eSignature Admin Guide for  Note You must assign the user the DS Sender permission to allow the user to create electronic envelopes in DocuSign. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 151 d. From the Users page, click the row for the newly-created generic user to display the user profile. e. Copy the User ID to a file. 7. In the SAP Business Network user interface, go to Integration Setup. Administration Configuration and choose DocuSign 8. Copy your API Account ID from the file where you saved it, paste that ID in the API Account ID field, and click Submit. 9. Copy your secret key from the file where you saved it, paste that key in the Secret key field, and click Submit. 10. Copy your User ID from the file where you saved it, paste that ID in the User ID field, and click Submit. DocuSign opens a popup window for you to grant consent for the generic user. 11. Grant consent for the generic user in DocuSign. a. Sign in to DocuSign with the generic user. b. Click ACCEPT to permit that user to create and send electronic envelopes in DocuSign. c. Exit DocuSign. 12. In the SAP Business Network user interface, click Close. The Administration Configuration page opens. Quality Notification Collaboration for Buyers Viewing Quality Notifications [page 153] Customized Quality Notifications [page 153] 152 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits Viewing Quality Notifications Buyers can view quality notifications submitted by their ERP system or by suppliers. Prerequisites The buyer system is enabled for the quality collaboration component. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Notification . The Quality Notifications page opens. 2. To search for a quality notification, expand the Search filters, enter values in the search fields, and then click Search.  Note When you choose the Exact match radio button below the Customer deviation no. or the Supplier deviation no. filter, only that filter and the Supplier filter display. 3. Click a quality notification number to open it.  Note You cannot edit the quality notification. It is read-only. Customized Quality Notifications Buyers can apply customizations to quality notification documents. A customization project for quality notifications contains one or more customizations. These customizations help buyers obtain better requirements compliance and reduce unnecessary communications with their suppliers. The following are examples of customizations that buyers can add to a customization project: • • • Set a default value for a field. Make a field required. Provide a tooltip message for a field. Buyers can define customizations for their suppliers to use, both when creating new and editing existing quality notifications. For example, buyers can make a field required when suppliers create a quality notification, but make the field read only after that. Buyers specify which mode (Create mode or Edit mode) to apply a customization to when defining rules for their customization project. For details, see Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161]. By default, customizations apply to both modes when buyers do not add rules to define the mode. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 153 Buyers edit and test their customization project until they have set up all of the customizations correctly. When they are done editing and testing, they publish their customization project and assign it to selected suppliers. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Restrictions Customizations are available only for quality notifications, not for quality inspections or quality reviews. Customization Project Workflow The tasks involved in the customization process are divided into two parts, editing tasks and publishing tasks. 1. The editing tasks are done by the Editor from the buyer test account. The Editor creates or updates customization projects and tests them. For details, see Creating a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 156]. 2. The publishing tasks are done by the Publisher from the buyer production account. The Publisher publishes customization projects. For details, see Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 172]. For more information about creating customization projects, see Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 155]. Working with Customization Projects You can create a new version of a customization project and make changes to it. For details, see Creating New Versions of Customization Projects [page 173]. You can delete customization projects that have not been published yet. For details, see Deleting Unpublished Customization Projects [page 175]. Available Customizations You can make the following customizations to a quality notification document: • • 154 Customize fields – For details, see Adding Field Customizations to a Customization Project [page 159]. Add rules – For details, see Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161]. PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits • • • • Add new fields – For details, see Adding Fields to a Customization Project [page 165]. Customize sections – For details, see Customizing Quality Notification Sections [page 167]. Hide tabs – For details, see Hiding Tabs in a Customization Project [page 170]. Hide sections – For details, see Hiding Sections in a Customization Project [page 171]. Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 155] Creating a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 156] Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications [page 172] Creating New Versions of Customization Projects [page 173] Deleting Unpublished Customization Projects [page 175] Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications The Editor creates the customization project from the buyer test account, and the Publisher publishes it from the buyer production account.  Restriction The Editor can only use a test account, not a production account, to develop and test customizations for quality notifications. 1. The Editor logs on to the buyer test account and creates a new or edits an existing customization project to apply to suppliers when they create quality notifications. 2. The Editor edits the customization project to add customizations to fields, rules to fields, and new fields. 3. The Editor pushes the customization project to the supplier test account. 4. The Editor logs on to the supplier test account and validates the customization project. 5. From the buyer test account, the Editor requests to publish the customization project to the production system. 6. The Publisher logs on to the supplier test account and validates the customization project.  Note When the Editor is also the Publisher, this step is skipped. 7. The Publisher logs on to the buyer production account and assigns suppliers to the customization project. 8. The Publisher publishes the customization project. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 155 Creating a Customization Project for Quality Notifications Buyers can create, edit, and test customizations for quality notifications. Prerequisites • • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. The supplier groups that you want to assign your customization project to already exist in your account. Procedure 1. Sign in to your buyer test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 3. Choose Create Project to create a new customization project. The Create Project page opens showing the first step, What project do you want to create? 4. Enter your information in the customization project fields. The following fields are required. 156 Field Description Project name Enter a unique name. Project description Enter a description. PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits Field Description Document type Choose Quality notification.  Note By default, the Create option is selected. Customizations will be applied to the creation of the quality notification. Suppliers Choices are: • • All (default) None  Note If you choose None, you will not be able to check your customizations in the supplier test account since the customization project will not be assigned to any suppliers. • Selected supplier groups – When chosen, a dropdown arrow shows. Click the arrow to show the list of supplier groups. Customization area By default, the Create option is selected. Customizations will be applied to the creation of the quality notification. Customized languages English (en) is required and always chosen. To add other languages, click the add ( ) icon to choose the languages. Click Done when you finish selecting languages.  Note When you add new fields to your project, to better support your customers, you should also add translations for the field labels. Field label translations are provided for standard fields, but not for added fields. The translations you add will be available for all future customization projects. If the translations for one or more standard field labels need to be enhanced, you can add translations for them too. Field label translations also affect the filters for quality notifications and the table where the quality notifications are listed. 5. Choose Next or Save. If you choose Next, continue with Step 7. If you choose Save, the Customization – Self Service page opens in the Projects tab, showing your project in the list of customization projects. 6. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit customization. The Create quality notification page for your customization project opens. Create quality notification refers to the quality notification creation page that suppliers use when creating quality notifications. You are creating customizations for this page for your suppliers. 7. Make one or more of the following customizations. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 157 • • • Add customizations for fields. Refer to Adding Field Customizations to a Customization Project [page 159]. Add rules for fields. Refer to Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161]. Add new fields. Refer to Adding Fields to a Customization Project [page 165]. On the quality notification design page, customized fields display a blue dot to the right of the field label. Additionally, the following customization changes are visible for customized fields: • • • Field label Default value Tooltip message  Note The quality notification design page does not provide a real-time view of the customized report, which means some customizations are not visible. To view all customizations, push your customization project to test and sign in to the supplier test account to create a document. 8. When you finish making your customizations, click the back arrow ( ). The Customization – Self Service page displays. 9. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Push to supplier test account. The Push project to supplier test account popup displays. 10. Choose Push. The customization project is pushed to the supplier test account. The project Status changes to Pushed to Test. 11. Optional: Assign the project to suppliers for testing. This step is only needed when no suppliers have been assigned to the project. a. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit project details. b. Select the suppliers. c. Click Save. The Suppliers popup displays asking if you want to save the updates you made. d. Click OK. 12. Check your customizations. a. Sign in to a supplier test account you have assigned the customization project to. b. Go to Quality Notification . c. Create a quality notification. d. Review the fields you customized to confirm they are set up correctly. 13. Return to your buyer test account and click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service . The Customization – Self Service page opens. 14. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for your customization project and select Request to publish. The Request to publish to production popup opens. 158 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits 15. Click OK. Your customization project is sent to production for the Publisher to review and publish. The project Status changes to Requested to Publish. Adding Field Customizations to a Customization Project [page 159] Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161] Adding Fields to a Customization Project [page 165] Customizing Quality Notification Sections [page 167] Hiding Tabs in a Customization Project [page 170] Hiding Sections in a Customization Project [page 171] Adding Field Customizations to a Customization Project Buyers can add customizations for fields in a customization project. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, hover over the dropdown ( ) icon of a field you want to customize, then click the edit ( ) icon that appears. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 159 The Edit field panel opens with the Properties tab displayed. 2. Make your customizations. Examples of customizations you can make include: • • • • • • • Set a default value for a field – you may want to set default values for some fields. Make a field required – some fields are already set as required. A required field displays with an asterisk. Hide a field – required fields display with an asterisk and cannot be hidden. Add a field – you can add custom fields. Rename a field label – the field label helps the user determine the purpose of the field. Set a minimum and maximum length for a field – you can enter a minimum length, a maximum length, or both. Provide a tooltip message for a field – you can provide a tooltip message in all the languages selected for your customization project. 3. Click Save. Results On the quality notification design page, customized fields display a blue dot to the right of the field label. Additionally, the following customization changes are visible for customized fields: • • • Field label Default value Tooltip message  Note The quality notification design page does not provide a real-time view of the customized report, which means some customizations are not visible. To view all customizations, push your customization project to test and sign in to the supplier test account to create a document. 160 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project Buyers can add rules to a customization project for quality notifications. You can apply these rules to creating a quality notification, editing a quality notification, or both. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context You add rules to enforce certain characteristics for customizations of quality notifications. For example, if you create a rule to hide a field when the value of the Quality notification type is Q7, the field will not be included in the quality notification when the Quality notification type has this value. Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, hover over the dropdown ( ) icon of a field you want to customize, then click the edit ( ) icon that appears. The Edit field panel opens with the Properties tab displayed. 2. Click the Rules tab, then click the add ( ) icon to add a new rule. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 161 3. Choose a property: Hide, Read only, or Required.  Note By default, the chosen property applies both when creating and when editing quality notifications. 4. Enter a condition for the rule by selecting values from each dropdown menu. 162 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits a. In the first setting for the condition, configure the type. Choose Field to add a field rule or System to add a system rule. b. In the second setting for the condition, configure the field. Choose the appropriate value for your choice in the first setting: • • Field rule – Choose Quality notification type. System rule – Choose Document mode. c. In the third setting for the condition, choose contains. d. In the fourth setting for the condition, configure the value. Perform the following instructions for the type of rule you are adding. • Field rule – Choose one or more values for the Quality notification type field.  Remember If you add a rule for the Quality notification type field with a value that is a custom quality notification code, you need to make sure that the custom quality notification code is uploaded to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 163 the buyer test account and actual account. Refer to Uploading Quality Notification Codes [page 89]. • System rule – Choose one or both document modes: • • Create mode – Define a rule for creating quality notifications. Edit mode – Define a rule for editing quality notifications.  Note Suppliers cannot edit any of the following fields after the quality notification is created: Customer Quality notification type Supplier deviation no. Customer location Customer part no. Customer routing identifier – This field only appears if the buyer has a multiple-ERP environment. Supplier part no. Purchase order no. Purchase order line item no. Ship notice no. Ship notice line item no. Subcontracting component 5. Optional: If you want to enter a second condition for the rule, click the add ( ) icon and choose the And if or Or if conditional operator. Follow the procedure described in the previous step to define the second condition. 6. Click Save. 164 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits The new rule displays in the Edit field window. 7. Click Save to save the new rule and exit the Edit field window. Adding Fields to a Customization Project Buyers can add fields to a customization project. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, click the edit ( ) icon in the section where you want to add a field. A window titled with the section name opens. 2. Click the add ( ) icon to the right of the Fields label to add a new field. The Create field popup opens. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 165 3. Enter the information about the field. Existing fields are referred to as intrinsics, meaning they are intrinsic to the document. New fields are referred to as extrinsics. Extrinsic fields add additional information to the document. The new field has the same properties and rules as existing fields. If a rule is needed for the field, configure it first. Refer to Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161]. The field information includes: 166 • New field name – the extrinsic name that is displayed in the cXML. In the cXML, the new field is added as the name element in an Extrinsic tag. Each new field is unique per cXML element (header, task element, and so on), and spaces are not allowed in field names. For example, if the New field name is RevisionLevel, and the revision level is 11, the corresponding cXML is: <Extrinsic name="RevisionLevel">11</Extrinsic>. • • • • • • • Label – the label that is displayed for the field. Hide Read only Required Tooltip message Default value Character length PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits The legal disclaimer at the bottom of the window reminds you that new fields cannot include sensitive personal data (for example, Social Security numbers) or personal data (for example, phone numbers) since they are not set up with appropriate data protection measures. 4. When you are done entering the field information, click Save.  Note The added field is available for any future customization projects you create. To use the field in another customization project, follow the steps to add a field, and when prompted for the New field name, enter the field's extrinsic name. The translations for the field are also available when you use the field in another customization project. Results The new field displays on the quality notification design page at the end of the section where it was added. The blue dot to the right of the field label indicates it is a customized field. When you generate a quality notification report, new fields are added as columns to the end of the report. The column name for each new field is its corresponding extrinsic name. Customizing Quality Notification Sections Buyers can customize certain sections in a quality notification. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context You can customize the following sections in a quality notification: • • • • • • Required tasks Activity log Defects Defects-Causes Defects-Required tasks Defects-Activity log SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 167 Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, click the edit ( ) icon of the section you want to customize. 2. Click the Rules tab. 3. Choose a property. You can only choose one property: • • Hide – The section will be hidden. • Limit creation – When selected, the Cannot be created more than field displays. Enter a number from 1 to 99 to specify the maximum number of sections of this type. Read only – The section will be read only. For example, if you select this property when customizing the Activity log section, your suppliers will be unable to either create new Activity log sections or remove existing Activity log sections when editing quality notifications.  Note The limit you enter is the total number of sections. For example, if you specify to create a maximum of 10 Required tasks sections and the supplier already entered 7 of these sections, they can only enter a maximum of 3 more. • Cannot be removed while editing – Your suppliers will be restricted from removing this type of section when they edit quality notifications. The customization shown in the screenshot applies to suppliers when they edit quality notifications with a Quality notification type of Q6. A maximum of 10 Activity log sections can be created. 168 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 169 4. Enter a condition for the rule by selecting values from each dropdown menu. For information about entering conditions for a rule, see Step 4 and Step 5 in Adding Field Rules to a Customization Project [page 161]. 5. Click Save. The new rule displays in the Edit field window. 6. Click Save to save the new rule and exit the Edit field window. Hiding Tabs in a Customization Project You can customize a quality notification document to hide tabs. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, click the more ( ) icon in the upper right corner of the page, and then select the Page editor link that displays. A side panel opens, showing checkboxes for the four tabs of a quality notification document. 2. To hide a tab, uncheck its checkbox.  Restriction Only the Defects and Partner info tabs can be hidden. Tabs that cannot be hidden show a grayed-out checkbox. 3. Click Save. 170 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: Hiding Sections in a Customization Project You can customize a quality notification document to hide sections. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission.  Restriction • Only sections that do not contain required fields can be hidden. For example, the Activity log and Required tasks sections do not have any required fields, so these sections can be hidden. • The Customer and part section can be hidden only when transaction rule Allow suppliers to send quality notifications for indirect orders without part numbers is enabled. When this transaction rule is not enabled, the Customer location and Customer part no. fields in this section are required fields, so the section cannot be hidden. Procedure 1. From the customization project's Create quality notification page, click the edit ( ) icon of the section you want to hide. 2. Check Hide under the Properties tab. 3. Click Save. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 171 Publishing a Customization Project for Quality Notifications After the Editor requests publication of a customization project, the Publisher can test and publish it. Prerequisites • • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Publisher permission. The supplier groups that you want to assign your customization project to already exist in your account. Procedure 1. Validate the customization project.  Note If you are both the Editor and the Publisher, you can skip this step since you already validated the project. a. Sign in to your supplier test account. b. Go to Quality Notification . c. Create a quality notification. d. Review the customized fields to confirm they are set up correctly. 2. Sign in to your buyer production account. 3. Click Administration Customization – Self-Service . The Customization – Self Service page opens. 4. Optional: Assign suppliers to the customization project.  Note You can assign suppliers to the customization project before or after publishing it. a. From the Customization – Self Service page, click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for your customization project, and select Edit project details. The Edit Project page opens. 172 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits b. Edit the Suppliers section to assign suppliers to the customization project. Select All, None, or Selected supplier group(s) and click Save. • • • All – customization project added to all suppliers. None – customization project removed from all suppliers. Selected supplier group(s) – customization project added to the suppliers in the supplier group(s) and removed from all other suppliers. The Suppliers popup opens asking you if you want to save the updates you made to the suppliers assigned to the customization project. Click OK to save the updates. 5. From the Customization – Self Service page, click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the customization project you want to publish, and select Publish. The Publish to production popup opens. The popup reminds you that your customization project will apply to your chosen suppliers in your production account. 6. Click OK to publish the customization project. Creating New Versions of Customization Projects Buyers can create a new version of an existing customization project and make changes to it. The existing customization project must have the Published status. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 173 Procedure 1. Sign in to your test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 3. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the Published customization project you want to create a new version for, and choose Create new version from the Project section. The following actions occur when you create a new version: • A warning message displays stating that the new version will be generated and the currently published version will not be affected. • The new version's major number is incremented. For example, if a new version is created from published version 1.3, the new version's number is 2.00. • The new version initially has status In Progress.  Remember Follow the normal workflow for projects to move the new version from In Progress to Pushed to Test and then to Requested to Publish. Results Suppliers assigned to a customization project always use the latest published version of the project. When you request to publish a new version, a warning message displays to remind you that this will affect all suppliers assigned to the project. After a new version of a customization project is published, suppliers will see this version in the user interface. For example, consider a new version of a customization project for quality notifications. The default behavior for the Serial no. field in the quality notification is to display the field. Since the Serial no. field is not a mandatory field, it can be hidden. If the field is hidden in the latest published version of a customization project, suppliers will not see the field when editing an existing quality notification, even though they may have previously inserted a value in the field. However, the Serial no. field information is still visible when suppliers download the cXML for the quality notification. 174 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits Deleting Unpublished Customization Projects Buyers can delete customization projects that have the status Draft, In Progress, Pushed to Test, or Requested to Publish. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context You can only delete a customization project when it is not yet published; that is, the project has the status Draft, In Progress, Pushed to Test, or Requested to Publish. You cannot delete a customization project that has the Published status. Procedure 1. Sign in to your test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 3. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the customization project you want to delete, and select Delete project from the Project section. A warning message displays to inform you that the version of the customization project will be permanently deleted. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 175 Results When you delete a customization project, only the latest version of the project is deleted. The table on the Customization – Self Service page has one row for each customization project, which shows information about the latest version of the project. • • When you delete a customization project that was never published, the row is removed from the table. When you delete a customization project that was previously published, the row for that project now shows information about the previously published version. For example, if you create version 2.0 and then delete it, and the previously published version is 1.3, the row for the project shows information about version 1.3. Planning and Forecast Collaboration Features This section describes SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features for planning and forecast collaboration. Component Planning Collaboration [page 176] Component Planning Collaboration Component planning collaboration lets buyers and suppliers view the forecast planning data for a finished good and its components together. Forecast planning items are created or updated when buyers send product activity messages and when suppliers send product replenishment messages. When component planning collaboration is enabled, in addition to forecast planning items, component planning collaboration items are also created or updated. For a component planning collaboration item to be created or updated, the item must be included in a Bill of Materials (BOM) stored in SAP Business Network. Each finished good has a component planning collaboration record. These records are created from Bill of Materials (BOM) records extracted from SAP Business Network. A BOM contains the list of components needed to manufacture a finished good. For more information about how BOM data is used for component planning collaboration, see Component Planning Collaboration Use of BOM Data [page 181]. To enable component planning collaboration, the buyer administrator edits the settings to toggle Enable component planning collaboration on. When this setting is set, if a planning item matches a finished good or a component stored in a BOM in SAP Business Network, its corresponding component planning collaboration item is created or updated. Component planning collaboration items are only created or updated when there is a match. Component planning collaboration uses the Component planning collaboration view. This view has two sections, Finished good section and Component section. Each section has its own key figures. For more information about the key figures in the Component planning collaboration view, see Key Figures Reference for the Component Planning Collaboration View [page 37]. Buyer administrators can also add custom key figures to both sections. Component planning collaboration data displays on the component planning collaboration list and details pages. • 176 For more information about the component planning collaboration list page, see Component Planning Collaboration List Page [page 177]. PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits • For more information about the component planning collaboration details page, see Component Planning Collaboration Details Page [page 178]. Prerequisites • • You must have both the Supply chain collaboration and Planning collaboration entitlements enabled. • The buyer administrator has imported the Bill of Materials (BOM) for the finished goods from the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. Refer to Importing Bill of Materials from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. • To view the Component planning collaboration tile in the Workbench tab, you must have the Component planning collaboration permission. The buyer administrator has set the Enable component planning collaboration setting on the Settings Assign suppliers Planning page. Restrictions • • The Component planning collaboration view does not support customer-defined attributes. Component planning collaboration does not support Planning Collaboration authorization profiles. Component Planning Collaboration List Page [page 177] Component Planning Collaboration Details Page [page 178] Component Planning Collaboration Use of BOM Data [page 181] Component Planning Collaboration List Page On the component planning collaboration list page, you can view a table of component planning records for finished goods. To view the component planning collaboration list page, click Workbench, then click the Component planning collaboration tile.  Note If the Component planning collaboration tile does not display, follow the instructions on Customizing Tiles on Your Workbench [page 209] to add it. You must have the inventory collaboration entitlement enabled for the Component planning collaboration tile to display in the list of tiles you can add.  Restriction You cannot download information from the list view of the Component planning collaboration table to a spreadsheet file such as Excel. The page displays a table of component planning collaboration records. Each record represents a finished good. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 177 The Component count column lists the number of components for each finished good and includes the number of active components in parenthesis. You can use the following filters to filter the finished goods: • • • • • Customer (supplier view) or Supplier (buyer view) Customer location Supplier part no. Customer part no. Components used – Select one or more components from the pulldown to list only finished goods that include one of the selected components. You can also sort the table by any column. Component Planning Collaboration Details Page On the component planning collaboration details page, you can view the planning items for a finished good and its active components. To open the component planning collaboration details page for a finished good, from the component planning collaboration list page, click the detail-view ( ) icon from the Actions column.  Restriction A maximum of 30 components are supported for each finished good. If a finished good has more than 30 components, only the first 30 components (in alphabetical order) display. General information about the finished good displays in the section at the top of the page. If the customer has uploaded a company logo, it displays in this section. Click the dropdown ( ) icon to expand this section. 178 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits The Bill of materials section displays the details of the BOM for the finished good. Click the feeder arrow ( ) icon to expand this section. When you open the details page, the Finished good section is expanded and the key figures for the finished good display with the standard planning time series table format. The time series tables on the component planning collaboration details page have the same functionality as they do on other planning pages. The only difference is that, when you click Send data, data is sent for both the finished good and its components. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 179 The Components with shortage key figure shows the count of the components used by the finished good that have a shortage on each date in the time bucket. Values greater than or equal to 1 display in red.  Note The Components with shortage key figure row only appears in the planning table when you use Daily granularity. You can view component planning items using any available granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly). However, you can only edit component planning items using Daily granularity since component planning is used for planning shorter timeframes. The header lines for the finished good and its components list the finished good or component name, description, and amount of stock on hand. Component header lines also include the following: • Vertical status bar – The status bar is green if the component does not have any shortages. The status bar is red if the component has one or both of the following shortages: • • Current stock on hand – The component is out of stock. Projected stock – The component will run out of stock on a future date based on the component's inflow and outflow. • Newspaper icon – Click the newspaper ( ) icon in the component header line to open the Where used? popup. This popup shows which finished goods use the component. • Message-warning icon – If a component has a shortage, a message-warning icon ( ) displays on its header line. Click the icon to view the shortage information.  Note The message-warning icon and shortage information display only for shortages that will occur in the next 30 days. Click the feeder-arrow ( ) icon next to a component to open its time series table to view and edit its key figures. 180 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: Standard calculated key figures that have values less than or equal to 0 display in red.  Caution Forecast commit locks are not supported for component planning. If you set Forecast commit lock horizon, in days to a value other than 0, you will not be able to commit from the component planning collaboration details page. To navigate back to the component planning collaboration list page, click the back-arrow ( ) icon at the top of the page. Component Planning Collaboration Use of BOM Data Component planning collaboration records are created using Bill of Materials (BOM) records in SAP Business Network. A BOM is a list of components needed to manufacture a finished good. Each component planning collaboration record contains one finished-good planning item and zero or more component planning items. Prerequisites The buyer administrator has imported the Bill of Materials (BOMs) for finished goods from the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. Refer to Importing Bill of Materials from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 181 Creating and Updating Component Planning Collaboration Items Component planning collaboration items are created for finished goods and components when a product activity message is sent by the buyer and the following two conditions are true: • The buyer or supplier has the Enable component planning collaboration setting set. This setting is set by the • The values of the Material ID and Plant ID in the message match the values of the Material ID and Plant ID in an active BOM at the header or component level. buyer administrator on the Planning Settings Assign suppliers page. When both items are true, if the match of the Material ID and Plant ID values is at the header level, a finishedgood planning item is created. If the match of the Material ID and Plant ID values is at the component level, a component planning item is created. Before creating a new planning item, SAP Business Network checks whether a planning item already exists. • • If one exists, SAP Business Network updates it. If one does not exist, SAP Business Network creates a new finished-good or component planning item.  Note • If the component data arrives before the finished-good data, the component planning item is created, but it is not displayed, until its finished-good planning item is created. A component planning item only displays on its finished good's component planning collaboration details page. • The component planning item is included in the component planning collaboration records of all finished goods that use it, and its data is always in sync in these records. • A planning item can be both a finished good and a component as illustrated in Example 3 below. Examples These are the BOM records used in the examples: BOM: Header Material: Plant ID: Components: 0001 Classic promo pack 1000, 2000 BBQ chips, Peanuts BOM: Header Material: Plant ID: Components: 0002 Party pack 2000, 3000 BBQ chips, Salt chips, Pistachios BOM: Header Material: Plant ID: Components: 0003 Wholesale pallet 3000 Party pack, Variety pack The product activity messages are shown for each of the following examples. The bullets after each message list the BOM where SAP Business Network finds the match and what action SAP Business Network takes as a result of the match. 182 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits Example 1: Simple component planning collaboration item generation These examples show simple generation of component planning collaboration items. • Message 1: Forecast for Material ID Classic promo pack/Plant ID 1000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 1 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. • Message 2: Forecast for Material ID Peanuts/Plant ID 1000 Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 1 component. 1. Create and populate the component planning item for Peanuts under the finished-good planning item for Classic promo pack/1000. Example 2: Component used in multiple finished goods These examples show the generation of component planning collaboration items for a component used in more than one finished good. • Message 1: Forecast for Material ID Classic promo pack/Plant ID 2000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 1 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. • Message 2: Forecast for Material ID Party pack/Plant ID 2000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 2 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. • Message 3: Forecast for Material ID BBQ chips/Plant ID 2000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with both BOM 1 and BOM 2 components. 2. Create and populate component planning items for BBQ chips for finished-good planning items Classic promo pack/2000 and Party pack/2000. The data for the BBQ chips component planning item in the component planning collaboration records for these two finished goods is always in sync. Example 3: Material is both a component and a finished good These examples show the generation of component planning collaboration items when a material is both a component and a finished good. • Message 1: Forecast for Material ID Party pack/Plant ID 3000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 2 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. 3. Since the Material ID/Plant ID also matches the BOM 3 component, a component planning item for Party pack is also created. This planning item is not visible until the finished-good planning item for Wholesale pallet/3000 is created. • Message 2: Forecast for Material ID Pistachios/Plant ID 3000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 2 component. 2. Create and populate the component planning item for Pistachios under the finished-good planning item for Party pack/3000. • Message 3: Forecast for Material ID Wholesale pallet/Plant ID 3000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 3 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. 3. The Party pack/3000 component planning item previously created (see Message 1 in this example) is now visible as a component in the component planning collaboration record for the Wholesale pallet/3000 finished good. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 183 Quality Review Collaboration for Buyers Buyers and suppliers can exchange information though SAP Business Network to facilitate quality reviews. With the quality review collaboration feature, SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enables buyers to do the following: Batch records Collaborate on batch-record reviews, finalize batch record information, and allow quality releases of product bulk materials. The supplier can initiate the batch record process after the quality inspection process is completed for the final batch documentation. Complaints Collaborate on product complaint investigations from the buyer’s customer. Buyers usually receive complaints through a third-party system but reports them to suppliers and CMOs through quality reviews. Change requests Collaborate on material changes, processes, or equipment. General Collaborate on quality process-type definitions. Buyers can create or update quality review requests by choosing Quality Review . Quality reviews can reference purchase orders, ship notices, quality inspections, and quality notifications. Quality Review Request Statuses SAP Business Network for Supply Chain displays one of the following statuses for each quality review request: New The default status, set automatically when the quality review request is created. In process Indicates that the other party responded to the quality review request.  Note Either the supplier or the buyer can change Complete to In process. Complete The status selected by the supplier to indicate a review has been completed. Only the supplier can choose this status. Close The status selected by the buyer when a review has been closed. Only the buyer can set this status.  Note A closed review can no longer be edited. 184 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits Creating a Quality Review Request Use this procedure to request quality reviews for goods. Prerequisites The buyer system is enabled for the quality collaboration component. Context Suppliers can report quality issues that need investigation and resolution. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Review . The Quality review page opens. 2. Click Create Quality Review. The Create quality review page opens. 3. Fill in the Subject field, and choose details as desired from the drop-down menus. 4. Write your comment in the Comment field. Click Submit. Responding to a Quality Review Notification by Email Buyers and suppliers can post a comment through email or attach files to the associated quality review. Prerequisites • • • Buyers: Your account is entitled for the quality collaboration component. Suppliers: You have a trading relationship with a buyer entitled for the quality collaboration component. Buyers and suppliers: Your SAP Business Network account is configured to receive quality review notifications. See Configuring Quality Collaboration Notifications [page 93].  Restriction • You can’t reformat or delete parts of the original quality review notification message. Otherwise, SAP Business Network can’t process the message. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 185 • • • • • You can’t change the To address in the reply email. However, you can add recipients. In your reply email, don’t enter line breaks or exceed 1024 characters. SAP Business Network removes line breaks and excess characters before posting your comment to the quality review. Files you attach to the reply email can’t exceed 1 GB in total size. When the quality review status changes to Closed, no more notification responses can be received. You can send a reply to a quality review notification only within 30 days of receiving it. After 30 days, replies to the quality review notification won’t be posted, though you can still edit the quality review in the SAP Business Network portal. Procedure 1. Open the email notification in your email client. 2. Create a reply to the email, observing the above restrictions. 3. Send the email. The text from your email reply is encrypted for transport and is posted as a comment to the quality review. Any files you attached to the email are automatically attached to the quality review. Supply Chain Monitor Feature The Supply Chain Monitor feature provides a simple and flexible way to access the transaction alerts information you want. The Supply Chain Monitor filters and settings give you greater control of which criteria generates an alert, which alerts data you see, and how the information is presented. Prerequisites • The buyer user is granted permissions by the buyer administrator to view Supply Chain Monitor and, if appropriate, to change its administration settings. For more information about Supply Chain Monitor access requirements, see Supply Chain Monitor Component Requirements [page 58]. • The buyer user is enabled for any collaboration component required by a particular Supply Chain Monitor exceptions group or chart. • For an exception group or chart whose functional area requires an additional permission, the buyer user is granted that permission. For more information about permission requirements, see the documentation for the exception group or chart. • For an exception group or chart whose functional area requires a collaboration component, the buyer user is entitled for that collaboration component. For more information about collaboration component requirements, see the documentation for the exception group or chart. • Each exception group or chart that the buyer user wants to see is checked in the Supply Chain Monitor settings  popup. 186 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits Restrictions • The maximum combined number of alerts that can exist, across all alert types, is 1 million. When new alerts are generated after this limit is reached, an equal number of the oldest alerts are automatically deleted. Otherwise, alerts are kept for 90 days, then automatically deleted. • Excel download is not available for alert type details pages. Order Confirmation Deviation Alerts [page 187] Order Confirmation Deviation Approval Alerts [page 188] Supplier-Managed Inventory Alerts [page 197] Quality Notification Chart [page 199] Forecast Alerts [page 200] Related Information Supply Chain Monitor Configuration [page 58] Order Confirmation Deviation Alerts Order confirmation deviation alerts in the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard inform you immediately when order confirmations deviate from certain purchase order requirements. Buyers, planners, and other stakeholders within a buying organization need visibility into the incoming supply. The order confirmation deviation alerts tile of the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard can identify immediately: • • • Orders at risk of being late Quantities that deviate from the purchase order Missing order confirmations Prerequisites This feature requires that: • SAP Ariba Support has enabled this tile. Have your Designated Support Contact log a case (formerly Service Request), and an SAP Ariba Support representative follows up to complete the request. • The buyer user is granted the Buyer Dashboard for Supply Chain Collaboration and Inbox and Order Access permissions by the buyer administrator. See Configuring Supply Chain Monitor Access [page 63]. • The buyer user is also granted the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission, to permit changes to Supply Chain Monitor administration settings. • Confirmation alerts is checked in the Supply Chain Monitor settings  popup. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 187 Restrictions • • • • Date deviations alert types are not generated for purchase order line items with multiple schedule lines. Excel download is not available for alert type details pages. Date deviations alerts might be generated in error due to time zone differences. Confirmation alerts are not generated for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. User Interface • On the Supply Chain Monitor page, the Supply Chain Monitor order confirmation deviation alerts feature has a tile for order confirmation exceptions group alerts. The tile contains an interactive donut chart and list of alert types. • Buyers without the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission can see, but not set, order confirmation alerts. • When you hover over an alert type name in the list, a filter icon  displays to the right of the name. Clicking this icon opens a filter popup to refine which alerts data is displayed. Certain fields have a type-ahead feature that lists known valid choices as you type. You can set each filter to apply to the individual alert type or apply for all alert types in the exceptions group.  Caution Setting Apply to all alerts in this exception group overrides existing settings for that filter in all alert types of the same exceptions group. • Clicking the donut chart or an alert type opens a details page for that data. This page has a dropdown to select which alert type data to show, and has an Export CSV download link. Buyers can select and clear an alert from the details page.  Note An alert is removed for all buyers when: • • A buyer clears an alert. The generation date of an alert becomes more than 90 days before today. Order Confirmation Deviation Approval Alerts The Supply Chain Monitor dashboard can notify buyers when an order confirmation does not meet certain approval requirements. Suppliers can submit an order confirmation for a purchase order even when it is out of tolerance (for quantity, delivery date, or price). Suppliers can also submit an order confirmation for a scheduling agreement or a scheduling agreement release even when it is out of tolerance for quantity and/or delivery date; price deviations are not possible because the unit price cannot be changed in SAP Business Network for these documents. When a deviation occurs in the order confirmation process, an alert is automatically generated in the Supply Chain Monitor tab of the SAP Business Network buyer portal. 188 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits If you want to receive email notifications of deviation alerts, you can configure email settings in the Administration Configuration Notifications Order Confirmation Deviation Approval page of the SAP Business Network buyer portal. You can choose to receive emails every hour, three hours, six hours, 12 hours, or 24 hours. Each email notification contains a maximum of 100 of the most recently confirmed orders with deviations. By default, the emails are sent to the purchasing agent indicated in the purchase order cXML document. This information is received under the element Contact in the purchase order cXML document and it must have the Role attribute equal to purchasingAgent. You can include up to five email addresses under the Contact element, with each address under its own Email element. You can configure up to three alternative email addresses to send the emails to when the purchasing agent is missing. You can decide whether to approve or reject an order confirmation deviation from the Order confirmation deviation approval alerts page of the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard. As a result, order confirmation deviations do not go to your backend ERP system until you proactively resolve them. Deviation alerts are generated per line item. An item can have multiple deviations (for example, both a date deviation and a quantity deviation). The order type filter on the Order confirmation approval alerts page can be set to Orders, Stock Transport Orders, or Scheduling agreements. The confirmation statuses shown on this page display the schedule line number information. For purchase orders, this information is only displayed when it is available. Schedule line information is always available for scheduling agreement and scheduling agreement release confirmations. The following screenshot shows an example Order confirmation approval alerts page. Prerequisites • Buyers must enable the order-confirmation approval process for suppliers by checking the following rule and one of its approval-process levels: Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval • • • Single-level approval process Multilevel approval process To limit which types of deviations this rule allows to exceed defined tolerances, buyers can set one or more of the rule's exceptions. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 189  Caution Before enabling an exception rule, the buyer first needs to reject from all partially confirmed orders any existing deviations that the desired exception rule does not allow. This task prevents possible unexpected behavior due to conflicts after an exception rule becomes enabled. Except quantity deviations Except delivery date deviations Except unit price deviations • For scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases, the Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases rule must be set. One or both of the following subrules must also be enabled: • • Allow scheduling agreement collaboration Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration Restrictions • The order confirmation deviation approval process only supports material items; service items are not supported. • The order confirmation deviation approval process does not apply to purchase orders that contain the cXML element <Extrinsic name="OCDeviationApproval">notAllowed</Extrinsic>. • When single-level deviation approval is used, buyers cannot approve and update orders with line items that have more than one unit price. • The Approve deviation and update order action is only available for purchase orders. It is not available for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases. • Since deviations are approved at the line-item level, if an item has a deviation, it is not possible to ship or invoice the item until the deviation is cleared. Behavior Differences for Order Confirmation Deviations That Are Allowed with Buyer Approval [page 191] Configurations for Deviation Approval [page 192] Workflows for Order Confirmation Deviation Approval [page 195] Approving or Rejecting Confirmation Deviations [page 196] Related Information Approving or Rejecting Confirmation Deviations [page 196] 190 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: Behavior Differences for Order Confirmation Deviations That Are Allowed with Buyer Approval The result of a deviation approval varies for the types of item changes and conditions. Purchase Orders If the rule Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval is checked, confirmation status is retained even if the item changed. This behavior is true even if the Retain confirmation status for unchanged line items on change orders rule is unchecked. However, there are two exceptions to this behavior: • If the previously confirmed quantity for an item is higher than the item’s revised quantity in the change order, the confirmation status is NOT retained. • If the previously confirmed price for an item is higher or lower than the revised price in the change order, the confirmation status is NOT retained. The following matrix further explains this behavior: Condition of Line Item in a Change Order Confirmation Status Approval Status Confirmed quantity is higher than the quantity in the new version of the order Not retained Not retained Item price in the new version of the order is higher or lower than the confirmed item price Not retained Not retained Item delivery date or quantity has changed and is not within tolerance Retained, but requires reconfirmation Changed to Awaiting supplier reconfirmation Item hasn’t changed in the new version of the order Retained Retained Item has changed, other than a change to unit price, and is within tolerance Retained Changed to Approved • If confirmation status is retained for a line item, the following logic also applies: • The confirmation status (for example, Confirmed With Changes) is recalculated based on the new version of the item. • • All previous deviation alerts for order confirmation approval are deleted for the item. If the item hasn’t changed in the new version of the order, the approval status is retained. If this item had any deviation alerts, they’re regenerated. • If an item has changed, other than the price, and it’s within tolerance, the approval status is changed to Approved. • If an item price has changed, within tolerance or not, the approval status is changed to Awaiting supplier reconfirmation. Deviation alerts are not generated because the supplier must first reconfirm the item. • If an item's delivery date or quantity has changed and it's not within tolerance, the approval status is changed to Awaiting supplier reconfirmation. Deviation alerts are not generated because the supplier must first reconfirm the item. • If an item’s approval status changed and the supplier has configured notifications for approval status changes, the supplier receives a notification. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 191 Scheduling Agreements and Scheduling Agreement Releases If the rule Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval is checked, when a new version of a scheduling agreement or scheduling release agreement is received, previous confirmations for schedule lines are retained except when: • • • The schedule line is dropped in the new version. The schedule line quantity changes in the new version. The schedule line delivery date changes in the new version. The exception to this is when a confirmation status matches the schedule line's quantity and delivery date. When this occurs, the confirmation of the schedule line is retained. The confirmation of a schedule line with a changed quantity in the new version is retained if there is a confirmation status that matches the schedule line's quantity and date. When a schedule line has more than one confirmation status related to it, the system matches one of the confirmation statuses to the new schedule line. To match, both the quantity and the delivery date must be the same in the confirmation and the new schedule line. In either case, the confirmation status must be recalculated. This logic is applied even when the Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval rule is not set. If the rule is set, the buyer confirmation approval status is also recalculated. If a line item changes and the confirmation remains within tolerance (at line-item level or schedule-line level, depending on how rules are configured), the line-item confirmation approval status is changed to Approved. If a line item changes and the confirmation is not within tolerance (at line-item level or schedule-line level, depending on how rules are configured), the line item's confirmation approval status is changed to Awaiting supplier reconfirmation. Related Information Approving or Rejecting Confirmation Deviations [page 196] Configurations for Deviation Approval Buyers can customize how they approve order confirmations and handle approval deviations. Customers can choose between two configurations for deviation approval: • Single-level deviation approval—Provides a single level of approval. Customers approve deviations directly in the buyer portal. • Multilevel deviation approval—Provides multiple levels of approval. Customers approve deviations first in the buyer portal, then in the customer’s backend ERP system. Multilevel approval only applies to quantity and/or price deviations. The configuration type defines which actions are allowed per deviation type. The following actions are available: • 192 Approve—Buyer approves the deviation and updates the item’s confirmation in their ERP. PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits • Approve and Update—Buyer approves the deviation and updates the order in their ERP with the confirmation information.  Note A line item with more than one unit price cannot be updated with single-level deviation approval.  Note This action is only supported for purchase orders. It is not supported for scheduling agreements or scheduling agreement releases. • Reject—Buyer rejects the deviation and nothing is updated in the ERP. Items revert to being unconfirmed in SAP Business Network. By default, both actions are checked. The selected approval actions apply for both single-level and multilevel deviation approval. The following list describes what happens when one or both actions are checked. • Both Approve and Approve and update are checked. The Purchase Orders tables in the Configuration Settings for Single-Level Deviation Approval and the Configuration Settings for Multilevel Deviation Approval sections show which deviations can be approved or rejected. • Only Approve is checked. The following table shows which deviations can be approved or rejected. The table is the same for single-level and multilevel deviation approval. Prerequisites • You are assigned the following permissions: • • • • • Permission to approve or reject date deviation Permission to approve or reject price deviation Permission to approve or reject quantity deviation Access to order confirmation approvals You have access to Supply Chain Monitor and to the Confirmation alerts tile. For more information, see Supply Chain Monitor Component Requirements [page 58] and Order Confirmation Deviation Approval Alerts [page 188]. Procedure 1. Go to Supply Chain Monitor. 196 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits 2. View the chart of confirmation alerts to see the number of deviations you received. 3. Above the chart, click You have order confirmation approvals due. The Order confirmation approval alerts page appears. 4. Optional: Filter deviations by Supplier, Part number, Purchase order, Purchasing group, Purchasing org, Planner code, and order type, or click tiles to show a subset of deviations. Types of deviations include date deviations, quantity deviations, price deviations, and deviations awaiting ERP approval. 5. Reject deviations by following these steps: a. Select one or more deviations in the table. b. Click Reject. A popup window appears. c. Optional: Enter a comment. d. Click Save. Rejected items revert to being unconfirmed. 6. See Configurations for Deviation Approval [page 192]. • • Approve deviation – Approves the deviation and updates the item’s confirmation in your ERP. Approve deviation and update order – Approves the deviation and updates the order in your ERP with the confirmation information.  Note Line items with more than one unit price cannot be updated with single-line deviation approval. d. Optional: Enter a comment. e. Click Save. Supplier-Managed Inventory Alerts Buyers can use the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard to monitor alerts for supplier-managed inventory, including replenishment orders. With supplier-managed inventory alerts tile on the Supply Chain Monitor dashboard, also called the supply-chain dashboard, you can configure and monitor supplier-managed inventory alerts. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 197 Prerequisites This feature requires that: • SAP Ariba Support has enabled this tile. Have your Designated Support Contact log a case (formerly Service request), and an SAP Ariba Support representative follows up to complete the request. • The buyer user is granted the Buyer Dashboard for Supply Chain Collaboration and Planning Collaboration Visibility permissions by the buyer administrator. See Configuring Supply Chain Monitor Access [page 63]. • The buyer user is granted the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission, to be able to change Supply Chain Monitor administration settings. • • The buyer user is entitled for the inventory collaboration component. Supplier managed inventory alerts is checked in the Supply Chain Monitor settings  popup. Restrictions Excel download is not available for alert type details pages. User Interface • On the Supply Chain Monitor page, the Supply Chain Monitor supplier-managed inventory alerts feature provides a tile of exceptions group alerts for supplier-managed inventory. The tile contains an interactive donut chart and list of alert types. • Buyers without the Supply Chain Monitor Settings Administration permission can see, but not set, suppliermanaged inventory alerts. • When you hover over an alert type name in the list, a filter icon  displays to the right of the name. Clicking this icon opens a filter popup to refine which alerts data is displayed. Certain fields have a type-ahead feature that lists known valid choices as you type. You can set each filter for an individual alert type or set it for all alert types in the exception group.  Caution Setting Apply to all alerts in this exception group overrides existing settings for that filter in all alert types of the same exception group. • Clicking the donut chart or an alert type opens a details page for that data. This page has a dropdown to select which alert type data to show and an Export CSV download link. Buyers can select and clear an alert from this page.  Note An alert is removed for all buyers when: • • • 198 A buyer clears an alert. PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits • • If a material status becomes Inactive, existing related alerts are deleted. When a product activity message, product replenishment message, or sales order is sent and an individual planning item has a combination of Out of Stock, Below Minimum, and Above Maximum deviations in different weeks, only one alert is generated. That alert is based on the following priority ranking: 1. Out of Stock alerts 2. Below Minimum alerts 3. Above Maximum alerts Quality Notification Chart The Supply Chain Monitor dashboard can identify which materials or suppliers were issued the most quality notifications in a given period.
