Freight Collaboration Feature This topic studies in detail, the relationship and collaboration between SAP Business Network for Supply Chain and SAP Business Network for Logistics. Overview In a supplier managed transportation scenario, shipment visibility turns out to be a key issue as the buyer often does not have reliable information about cargo movement or planned delivery timeline. This makes appointment scheduling, or goods receipt a challenge. Small suppliers do not enjoy economies of scale with Logistics Service Providers (LSP) / Carriers and therefore, pay relatively higher freight charges that ultimately inflates the landed cost of the product for the buyer. Inflated transportation bills can also be a reality in extreme cases. To overcome these supply chain issues, large buyers are increasingly turning their focus towards managing the transportation themselves with the help of partner LSPs (Logistics Service Provider) and carriers. Efficient management of the process directly and positively impacts the bottom line. By using economies of scale in transportation and enhanced supply chain visibility, the process can be made cost-effective. Prompt exception management and optimum resource allocation across the supply chain are ensured. Therefore, buyer managed transportation for inbound materials using LSP or carriers is expected to grow rapidly as a key differentiator in increasingly competitive supply chains. In short, the buyer organizations now need to create an end-to-end ‘source to stock’ process that seamlessly merges their procurement collaboration process with inbound transportation management. This is a singularly difficult collaboration where multiple business partners (such as supplier, LSP, Carrier) dispersed in a distributed supply chain need to strike a precise supply chain cadence. SAP Business Network, with a large partner ecosystem and extensive connectivity, can effortlessly deliver this critical capability SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 201 Related Information For more information, see Integration with SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration Prerequisites • • The buyer and supplier must share a CSC relationship type. • Enable BN4L integration for Ship Notices must be enabled for the buyer account. Contact SAP Support to get this entitlement enabled. • The buyer must set a partner function called “ShippingNetwork,” with the value ‘BN4L’, on their system. This indicator is then included in the Purchase Order document. • The buyer must also provide, as part of the Purchase Order document, the Logistics Service Provider (LSP) identifier, by setting an additional partner function called “ForwardingAgent.” This value is flipped to the Ship Notice document generated from the Order, after which, it is transmitted to BN4L. Doing this enables the corresponding LSP to be assigned to the Transport Request. The buyer is also onboarded on SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L). Contact SAP Support, provide your SAP Business Network for Supply Chain ANID and your SAP Business Network for Logistics LBN ID, to establish the relationship between both networks Process Flowchart Flowchart illustrating the process: 202 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits Feature Benefit Through the seamless fusion of procurement and logistics collaboration, using the Ship Notice document as the key connector, the buyer can monitor and manage the blended networks collaboration in a single unified flow. Procedure Context Perform the following steps: 1. The buyer sends the Purchase Order (PO) to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain with two indicators: the BN4L flag (which allows the application to route the ASN* to BN4L) and the LSP identifier (for SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L) to know to which LSP the ASN must be sent). *ASN = Advance Shipping Notification. 2. The supplier receives the PO in the Business Network (BN) portal, where the new BN4L indicator is visible and confirms the PO, depending on the configured business rules (configured by the buyer). 3. The supplier creates the ASN including all the required information. This ASN is sent to the buyer (backend) system, where an Inbound delivery is created. At the same time, the ASN is also routed to BN4L. 4. In SAP Business Network for Logistics (BN4L), a Transportation Requirement is created and propagated from the Shipper (who is the same SCC (Supply Chain Collaboration) Buyer in this scenario) to the corresponding LSP tenant. 5. The Transportation Requirement is forwarded from BN4L to the assigned carrier through an external API. 6. The carrier plans the shipment and sends this shipment plan to BN4L  Note A shipment plan carries the following statuses as a progress marker to the plan: - • In Planning: Status assigned after the ASN is being created and sent to LBN (Logistics Business Network) so the shipment can be planned • • Planned: Status assigned when the shipment plan is generated by the carrier and comes from LBN Planning not started: This status is assigned when the ship notice is not submitted, but there is a draft saved. 7. BN4L forwards the shipment plan to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain (SCC) and updates the following header information in the ASN: • • • • • Bill Of Lading Service Level Carrier Transit Direction Delivery Date 8. In the portal, the suppliers can visualize all the shipment details under a new tab in the ASN document. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 203 9. An updated version of the ASN (with the updated values) is also sent to the buyer and the inbound delivery is updated. 10. Optional Step: - An update or cancellation of the shipment plan can be done by the carrier for several reasons. For example: If the carrier updates the shipment plan by providing a different delivery date or if the assigned carrier cannot handle transportation and a new carrier is assigned, then a Shipment Plan Update is generated and BN4L sends it to SCC. 11. After every change to the shipment plan, the SCC creates a new ASN version and sends it to the buyer, where the inbound delivery is also updated. 12. On the planned pick-up date, the carrier picks up the items from the supplier warehouse and delivers it to the buyer warehouse. 13. Finally, the buyer can issue the goods receipt (GR) confirming receipt of the requested goods. Limitations • This new functionality applies to online Ship Notices and Ship Notices created through the Excel mass upload template only. B2B Ship Notices are not covered. • Only one shipment plan per Ship Notice is supported. UI Changes Table 1: New Fields / Filters Introduced UI Section New Fields / Filters Purchase Order page The Shipping Network: BN4L indicator is shown at the document level. Ship Notices created from this type of POs, are routed to SAP Business Network for Logistics. Orders and Items to Ship Workbench The Shipping Network filter and column have been added. They help suppliers to tiles identify this specific type of orders and items that belong to these orders, to facilitate the creation of the corresponding Ship Notice. Ship Notice page The Shipping Network: BN4L indicator is shown at the document level. • The Shipment Planning Status is displayed. Possible statuses are: In Planning, Planned and Planning Not Started. • Additionally, a new Shipment Details tab has been added to the Ship Notice UI. This new tab displays all the details related to the shipment plan that is generated (externally) by the carrier and comes from SAP Business Network for Logistics. Buyers and suppliers can see the planned pickup date, planned delivery date, information on all the transport stages, and more. 204 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits UI Section New Fields / Filters Ship Notice Workbench tile A new workbench tile that lists all available ship notices has been introduced. New tile filters include: Customers/Suppliers, Packing Slip ID, Order Number, Creation Date, Ship Notice Type, Shipping Date, Delivery Date, Completion Status, Receipt Status, Routing Status Shipping Network, and Shipment Planning Status. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Features and Benefits PUBLIC 205 Tasks for Regular Business Users This section provides topics describing how regular business users, rather than administrators, use the system to perform supply chain collaboration tasks. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home Page Components [page 206] The Workbench [page 208] Documents for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Buyers [page 215] Resending a Document That Was Not Received [page 221] Resending Failed Orders for Private Suppliers [page 222] SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home Page Components Home page features help you access and manage your transactions. Your SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page features simple navigation, a powerful search bar, an instant overview of your transactions in a tile-based design, and a My widgets section that you can customize. Overview Tile Bar [page 206] Home Page Widgets [page 207] Customizing Your Home Page Widgets [page 207] Overview Tile Bar The Overview tile bar displays the default tiles for your business role, or tiles that you have configured. On the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page, up to five tiles are displayed in the Overview tile bar by default. You can reveal an additional five tiles with the More button. You can also configure which tiles are displayed from the Workbench. For more information, see The Workbench [page 208] The Overview tiles are displayed intelligently: if one or more Pinned documents exist, that tile is displayed first. Otherwise, it is moved to the end of the order. 206 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users Home Page Widgets Your Home page provides widgets to show at a glance current information for your business activities. The SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page displays role-based widgets. These widgets help you focus on important tasks, insights, key performance indicators, and benchmarks for your business. To customize the contents of your Home page, see Customizing Your Home Page Widgets [page 207]. Customizing Your Home Page Widgets Use this procedure to choose what displays on your SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Home page. Context You can add, remove, and rearrange widgets on your Home page from the Customize my widgets page. Procedure 1. On the Home page, click Customize in the My widgets area. 2. On the Customize my widgets page, do any of the following: • • • Click the plus sign icon ( ) to add a widget. Click the minus icon ( ) to remove a widget. Select the two line icon in the center of the widget to move the widget. 3. Click Save. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users PUBLIC 207 The Workbench The workbench displays configurable tiles based on transaction documents, statuses, and additional filters. Overview of the Workbench The workbench is a customizable page that allows you to get a quick overview of transaction documents and take action on them. It displays up to 25 customized tiles. When more tiles are available that can fit on your screen (based on your screen resolution), the tile bar displays a right arrow button ( ) to scroll through the tiles. Each tile displays a count or amount, title, and subtitle. 1. The count is the number of transactions, action items, or events that match the tile filter criteria, up to 1000; if the count is greater than 1000, the count displays 1000+. The amount is the total value of scheduled payments, remittances, or early payment offers contained in the tile. It is displayed in your local currency. 2. The title is the name of the base tile, a label describing the type of transaction, action item, or event that matches the tile criteria, such as Invoices. 3. The subtitle is a configurable label to further describe the contents of the tile, which is particularly useful when you create your own variant of a tile based on a complex combination of filters. Custom attributes Custom attributes you create with a customization project can be extended to workbench tiles, allowing you and your suppliers to view them as filters and columns. The actions column The Actions column displays a more button ( ) that allows you to complete actions on documents. The actions available are based on the document type and status. Some workbench tiles also support multi-select and bulk actions. Column grouping You can group workbench columns for many tiles. Grouping workbench columns is helpful when you need to perform bulk edits on similar line items. When you group columns for a workbench tile, the search results show documents that have the same values for the filters you've selected. For example, you can look for documents with the same description, order number, and item number. 208 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users The export button The workbench also features an export button ( ), which allows you to download the information displayed in the table as an .xlsx file. The download includes only the information currently displayed in the list view. Any lines or columns that are hidden from your current list view are not included in the .xlsx file. Customizing Tiles on Your Workbench [page 209] Filtering Workbench Tiles [page 210] Customizing Workbench Columns [page 212] Grouping Workbench Columns [page 213] Workbench Tile Reference [page 214] Customizing Tiles on Your Workbench Use this procedure to add workbench tiles, add custom subtitles to the tiles, and remove or rearrange tiles as needed. Procedure 1. On the Workbench page, click the Settings icon ( ) in the top-right corner. 2. Do any of the following: • Click the plus symbol ( ) to add a new tile. The value for the tile populates after you save your changes. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users PUBLIC 209 • Click the delete symbol ( ) to remove a tile. • Select the three lines icon ( ) in the center of the tile to move the tile. 3. Click Apply to save your changes. Next Steps Further customize your tile by adding filters. For more information, see Filtering Workbench Tiles [page 210]. Filtering Workbench Tiles When you open a workbench tile, all of the documents associated to that tile are displayed, but you can apply filters and refine which documents are shown. For example, you can choose to only see orders from a specific customer by using the Customers filter. Context When a tile is selected, SAP Business Network displays filter tags for any filters configured for that tile. The screenshot of the Orders tile below has the following filters and their values applied, Creation date: Last 365 days, Routing status: Sent, Max amount: 10,000, and Currency: USD. 210 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users

Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended collaboration and navigate to the component receipts. 2. Use search filters to refine the records shown. Viewing Component Ship Notices Buyers can see the component ship notices sent by component suppliers on the shipment of goods. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Component Shipments . 2. Use search filters to refine the results shown.. Viewing Forecast Commitment Information from Suppliers Buyers can monitor their projected stock needs and what quantity their suppliers commit to deliver. Context To effectively collaborate with suppliers on forecast quantities, buyers must see the same forecast demand and forecast commitment data that their suppliers see. With the buyer view of forecast application feature, buyers can see the same forecast demand and forecast commit data their suppliers see. Procedure 1. Choose Planning Forecast . 2. Enter information in the Search filters fields to refine the information shown in the Forecast table. 216 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users Related Information Search Filters in Order and Forecast Collaboration [page 132] Viewing Multitier Orders Multitier orders are sent from an OEM buyer to multiple suppliers in different tiers in the supply chain, for example, contract manufacturers and component suppliers. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Orders and Releases . 2. Look in the Multi-Tier column. Any orders that request copies to be sent to other supply chain partners have a green checkmark . 3. To view details on copy documents, click the Copies link for a multitier order. 4. To open the order, click an order number. Viewing and Exporting Serial Number Lists in Orders If serial numbers are included with an order, you can view serial number details for each line item. Prerequisites The cXML file for the order must include serial number information. Procedure 1. Open an order that contains serial numbers for line items. 2. For any item contained in the order, click Details. 3. Find the Information on Ship Notice [Optional] > Serial Numbers section. • • If serial numbers are specified as a profile or a range, they appear under Serial Numbers. If the format is a list, click Details to open the Items serial number popup and see the list of serial numbers for the item. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users PUBLIC 217  Restriction The Items serial number window can display up to 500 serial numbers. If there are more than 500 serial numbers for the item, download the full list. • • • • To advance to the next page, click the  icon. To download the list, click the Download Serial Numbers  icon. To print the list, click the Print Screen  icon. When you are finished, click Done. file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: Resending a Document That Was Not Received Administrators can resend some documents that were not received because of errors. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Context Occasionally, documents sent through SAP Business Network are not received at their final destination because of errors in the documents or their lack of compliance with relevant business rules. Administrators can often resend these documents after correcting the errors. Procedure 1.  Note The path to the Documents to Resend feature is as follows: • • For buyers – For suppliers – Quick links … Documents to Resend Documents to Resend Choose Documents to Resend. The documents search results are displayed, with details about the causes of the failures. The Resolution Status search filters Show unresolved entries and Show resolved entries control which of the failed documents that meet the other search results are included. 2. Review the failed document's error message, make the correction, then click Resend in the Actions column.  Note Alternatively, you can choose these other actions in the Actions column: • Click Export cXML to export the affected document in cXML, then mark the document transmission issues as resolved. • Click Mark as Resolved if you do not want to resend the failed document. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users PUBLIC 221 Resending Failed Orders for Private Suppliers If copies of orders failed to be delivered to suppliers, you can resend them. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Orders and Releases . 2. Click View Failed Orders to Private Supplier. The Resend Failed Orders for Private Suppliers window appears. 3. Enter the supplier's Ariba Network ID (optional) and a date range, and then click Search. 4. In the result table, click a supplier's Ariba Network ID to view the failed multitier orders for that supplier. 5. Select one or more orders, and click Resend to resend the selected orders, or click Resend All to resend all failed orders. 6. Click Done twice to return to the Orders and Releases page. 222 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Tasks for Regular Business Users Serial Numbers Enabled in Component Receipts Serial numbers are supported within subcontracting processes in Component Receipts whenever they are present in the Component Ship Notice. • The following business rules are enabled and are available at the default transaction and supplier group level: • Require serial numbers to be mandatory in the Component Receipt whenever they occur in the Component Ship Notice. • Require the serial numbers that are a part of the Component Ship Notice to be included in the Component Receipt. • Require the total count of component receipt serial numbers to match the total quantity received for line items in a component receipt. • • Serial numbers can be entered while creating the Component Receipt (CR) for the Component Ship Notice (CSN) in the user interface at the line item level. • When the supplier selects Add Serial Numbers in the Component Receipt (CR) page, a popup for the creation of the serial number is displayed with the possibility to change the serial numbers. • • • • • Serial numbers can be removed by selecting the Remove option. • The supplier can click on Browse to select the Excel file and then choose Upload Excel to upload the Excel file with the serial numbers. When the supplier selects Autofulfill Quantity, the serial numbers populate the system. The supplier can use the Reset button to clear all the serial numbers in the popup. The Close button allows the supplier to return to the Component Receipt (CR) page. The supplier can select Download template to download an excel templated of all the line items in the component creation screen. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Serial Numbers Enabled in Component Receipts PUBLIC 223 Document Customization You can create custom attributes and include these attributes in customization projects for certain document types. Custom Attributes Custom attributes contain additional information relevant to your business and add to the standard SAP Business Network pages, Upload/Download job types, and Workbench tiles. You can create custom attributes for purchase orders, ship notices, and order confirmations. See Custom Attributes for Customization Projects [page 224]. Customization Projects You can create customization projects to add custom attributes to the Ship Notice Excel template for Upload/ Download and to the Items to Confirm, Orders, and Items to Ship tiles of the Workbench. See Customization Projects [page 229]. Custom Attributes for Customization Projects [page 224] Customization Projects [page 229] Custom Attributes for Customization Projects You can create custom attributes for purchase orders, ship notices, and order confirmations to be used in customization projects. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Restrictions You can create a maximum of thirty custom attributes to use across all document types. Custom attributes help you communicate information with your suppliers that is not already included on standard SAP Business Network pages, Upload/Download job types, and Workbench tiles. For example, you can create 224 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization Size and Color custom attributes, and then create a customization project for the Items to Ship tile for the Workbench that includes these attributes. Applying these custom attributes to the Items to Ship tile for the Workbench lets your suppliers view this information on the list page and filter ship notices by these custom attributes. For details on creating custom attributes, see Creating a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 225]. You can also edit and delete existing custom attributes. See Editing a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 227] and Deleting a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 228]. Creating a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 225] Editing a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 227] Deleting a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 228] Creating a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project Use this procedure to create custom attributes to apply to document types. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission.  Restriction You can create a maximum of thirty custom attributes to use across all document types. Context Buyers can create custom attributes and add them to a centralized library of attributes. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 225 The Customization – Self Service page opens. 2. Click on the Create pulldown menu and select Attribute. The Create Attribute page displays. 3. Fill in the attribute fields. Field Description Attribute name Enter the display name for the attribute. Attribute description Enter a description for the attribute. Attribute type Choose Extrinsic or Characteristic. Data type Choose String. Level (Extrinsic only) Choose Header or Line item depending on whether the custom attribute is a header or a line-item extrinsic. Domain (Characteristic only) Enter the name of the domain attribute of the Characteristic element in the cXML. Extrinsic name (Extrinsic only) Enter the name of the extrinsic used in the cXML. Document type The Purchase order document type is always selected. You can also select one or both other document types. By selecting a document type, you indicate that the attribute can be used in a customization project for this type of document. SAP Business Network automatically builds and displays the cXML paths. For example, if you create an attribute that is a line-item level extrinsic, and you select all three document types, SAP Business Network displays the following cXML paths: • • • Order confirmation: ConfirmationRequest/ConfirmationItem/Extrinsic Purchase order: OrderRequest/ItemOut/ItemDetail/Extrinsic Ship notice: ShipNoticeRequest/ShipNoticePortion/ShipNoticeItem/Extrinsic What language(s) do you want to Choose what languages to support and enter the attribute name for each chosen support? language. English (en) is supported by default. Click the add  icon to choose more languages. 4. Click Save. The attribute is saved, and the attribute library page displays. 226 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization Related Information Document Customization [page 224] Editing a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project Use this procedure to make changes to a custom attribute. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context Buyers can edit a custom attribute in the attributes library. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service . The Customization – Self Service page opens. 2. Click the Attributes tab. The list of custom attributes in the attributes library displays. 3. In the Actions column, click the more ( ) icon for the attribute you want to edit, and click Edit. The Edit Attribute window opens. 4. Make your edits. 5. Click Save. The attribute is saved, and the attribute library page displays. Related Information Document Customization [page 224] SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 227 Deleting a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project Use this procedure to remove a custom attribute from the attributes library. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context Buyers can delete a custom attribute from the attributes library. Procedure 1. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service . The Customization – Self Service page opens. 2. Click the Attributes tab. The list of custom attributes in the attributes library displays. 3. In the Actions column, click the more ( ) icon for the attribute you want to delete, and click Delete. A popup displays asking you to confirm the deletion.  Caution You cannot delete an attribute that is included in a customization project with either the Requested to Publish or Published status. If you try to do that, a popup displays that includes a list of projects that have either status. 4. Click Delete. The custom attribute is deleted from the attributes library. Related Information Document Customization [page 224] 228 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization Customization Projects You can create customization projects for the Ship Notice and Order Confirmation Excel templates for Upload/ Download and for some Workbench tiles. Prerequisites • • • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. The supplier groups that you want to assign your customization project to already exist in your account. To publish a customization project, you must be a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Publisher permission. You can create customization projects to add custom attributes to the Ship Notice and Order Confirmation Excel templates for Upload/Download. Customization projects for these templates might include the following changes: • • • Choose which customer-defined columns to include or omit from the template. Set an alternative name for a customer-defined column. Change the order of the columns in the Excel template. You can also create customization projects to add custom attributes to the Workbench tiles for Items to Confirm, Orders, and Items to Ship. A customization project for one of these Workbench tiles might include the following changes: • • • Add a custom attribute as a column. A maximum of five columns can be added. Add a custom attribute as a filter. A maximum of three filters can be added. Edit custom attributes to display a different column name, including translations. The tasks involved in the customization process are divided into two parts, editing tasks and publishing tasks. 1. Editing tasks are done by the Editor from the buyer test account. The Editor creates or updates customization projects and tests them. For details, see Creating a Customization Project [page 231]. 2. Publishing tasks are done by the Publisher from the buyer production account. The Publisher verifies and publishes customization projects. A buyer who is both an Editor and a Publisher can publish their own customization projects. For details, see Publishing a Customization Project [page 242]. For an overview of the complete workflow, see Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project [page 230]. Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project [page 230] Creating a Customization Project [page 231] Publishing a Customization Project [page 242] Creating New Versions of Customization Projects [page 244] Deleting Unpublished Customization Projects [page 245] SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 229 Workflow for Creating and Publishing a Customization Project The end-to-end workflow for a customization project starts with an Editor creating or editing a project, and ends with a Publisher assigning suppliers to the published project.  Note The Editor creates the customization project from the buyer test account, while the Publisher publishes it from the buyer production account.  Restriction The Editor can only use a test account, not a production account, to develop and test customization projects. 1. The Editor logs on to the buyer test account. 2. The Editor creates a new or edits an existing customization project to apply to suppliers when they do one of the following: • • • • • • Create or edit a quality notification. Generate a Ship Notice Upload/Download job template in Excel. Generate an Order Confirmation Upload/Download job template in Excel. Review orders in the Workbench tile for Orders. Create order confirmations in the Workbench tile for Items to Confirm. Create ship notices in the Workbench tile for Items to Ship. 3. The Editor edits the customization project to add customizations. 4. The Editor pushes the customization project to the supplier test account. 5. The Editor logs on to the supplier test account and validates the customization project. 6. From the buyer test account, the Editor requests to publish the customization project to the production system. 7. The Publisher logs on to the supplier test account and validates the customization project.  Note When the Editor is also the Publisher, this step is skipped. 8. The Publisher logs on to the buyer production account and publishes the customization project. 9. The Publisher assigns suppliers to the customization project. 230 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: Creating a Customization Project Use this procedure create a customization project for a Ship Notice or Order Confirmation Upload/Download template, or for Workbench tiles for Items to Confirm, Orders, or Items to Ship. Prerequisites • • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. The supplier groups that you want to assign your customization project to already exist in your account. Procedure 1. Sign in to your buyer test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 3. Choose Create Project to create a new customization project. The Create Project page opens showing the first step, What project do you want to create? 4. Enter your information in the customization project fields. The following fields are required. Field Description Project name Enter a unique name. Project description Enter a description. Document type Choose Order confirmation, Purchase order, Quality notification, or Ship notice. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 231 Field Description Suppliers Choices are: • • All (default) None  Note If you choose None, you will not be able to check your customizations in the supplier test account since the customization project will not be assigned to any suppliers. • Selected supplier groups – When chosen, a dropdown arrow shows. Click the arrow to show the list of supplier groups. Customization area Choose Workbench/Items to Confirm, Workbench/Orders, or Workbench/Items to Ship to customize the Workbench tile for the selected Document type. Or, when the Document type is Ship notice or Order confirmation, choose Excel to customize the Ship Notice or Order Confirmation Excel template for Upload/Download. Customized languages English (en) is required and always chosen. To add other languages, click the add ( ) icon to choose the languages. Click Done when you finish selecting languages. 5. Choose Save. The Customization – Self Service page opens in the Projects tab, showing your project in the list of customization projects. 6. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit. The Edit Project page opens with the second step, How do you want to customize your project, expanded. 7. Make your customizations. • For details about customizing an Excel template for Upload/Download, see Customizing an Excel Template for Upload/Download [page 233]. • For details about customizing Workbench tiles, see Customizing a Workbench Tile [page 239]. 8. When you finish making your customizations, click Save. The Customization – Self Service page displays. 9. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Push to test. The Push project to supplier test account popup displays. 10. Choose Push. The customization project is pushed to the supplier test account. The project Status changes to Pushed to Test. 11. Optional: Assign the project to suppliers for testing. This step is only needed when no suppliers have been assigned to the project. a. In the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit. b. Click the edit ( ) icon in the What project do you want to create? section. c. Select the suppliers. 232 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization d. Click Save. 12. Sign in to a supplier test account you have assigned the customization project to and check your customizations. See Testing a Customization Project [page 241]. 13. Return to your buyer test account and click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service . The Customization – Self Service page opens. 14. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for your customization project and select Request to publish. The Publish to production popup opens. 15. Click OK. Your customization project is sent to production for the Publisher to review and publish. The project Status changes to Requested to Publish. Customizing an Excel Template for Upload/Download [page 233] Customizing a Workbench Tile [page 239] Testing a Customization Project [page 241] Customizing an Excel Template for Upload/Download Use this procedure to edit a customization project to customize an Excel template for Upload/Download. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context If you completed the first step (What project do you want to create?) on the Create Project page and clicked Save to save your project information, start with Step 1. If you completed the first step and clicked Next, start with Step 2. Procedure 1. From the Customization – Self Service page, in the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit. The Edit Project page opens with the second step, How do you want to customize your project, expanded and active. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 233 2. Optional: Customize the standard attributes in the template. See Customizing Standard Attributes in an Excel Template [page 234]. 3. Optional: Create additional custom attributes. If you need to create additional attributes to add to your customization project, click Create in the Available Attributes column next to Custom Attributes. For details, see Creating a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 225]. 4. Optional: Customize the custom attributes in the template. See Customizing Custom Attributes in an Excel Template [page 236]. 5. Optional: Change the display order of columns. In the Selected attributes list, click the drag ( ) icon of an attribute you want to move, then drag and drop the attribute to the desired place in the list. 6. When you finish making your customizations, click Next. The page expands and makes active the third step, What will your project look like? 7. Review the preview of your customization project applied to the Upload/Download Excel template. 8. Optional: If you need to make any changes, click the edit ( ) icon in the section for the second step, How do you want to customize your project, and go back to Step 2 [page 234] to edit your project. Customizing Standard Attributes in an Excel Template You can customize standard attributes in an Excel template. Context Make one or more of the following customizations to the standard attributes you include in the template. Procedure 1. Optional: Add optional standard attributes. a. If the Standard Attributes section in the Available Attributes column is not expanded, click the feeder arrow ( ) icon to expand it. b. Click the blue add ( ) icon next to All to add all optional standard attributes, or separately select the optional standard attributes to add by clicking the blue add ( ) icon next to each one.  Note Required standard attributes are always included. 2. Optional: Remove optional standard attributes. In the Selected Attributes column, optional standard attributes display with a blue checkmark and required standard attributes display with a greyed-out checkmark as shown in the following screenshot. Uncheck any 234 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization optional standard attributes you do not want to remove them from your customized template and hide them in the Excel file. 3. Optional: Edit standard attributes. a. In the Selected Attributes column, scroll to the standard attribute you want to edit. b. Hover over the standard attribute, then click the edit ( ) icon when it appears. The Edit Standard Attribute window displays. c. Optional: Make the standard attribute required. Click the Required checkbox under the Properties tab to make the standard attribute required.  Note For required standard attributes, the Required checkbox is always checked and the field is greyed out because it cannot be changed. d. Optional: Provide an alternative label and translation. The supported languages display under the Alternative label and translation dropdown menu. Enter the new column name in English and for any other selected language. Changes made to the standard attribute's label and translations will apply to all customization projects for that type of Upload/Download Excel template that include the standard attribute. e. Click OK. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 235 When you customize a standard attribute, a blue circle displays after its name in the Selected Attributes column. Customizing Custom Attributes in an Excel Template You can add custom attributes to the template and customize them as needed. Context Make one or more of the following customizations to the custom attributes you want to include in the template. Procedure 1. Optional: Add custom attributes. a. If the Custom Attributes section in the Available Attributes column is not expanded, click the feeder arrow ( ) icon to expand it. b. Click the blue add ( ) icon next to the All label to add all custom attributes, or separately select the custom attributes to add by clicking the blue add ( ) icon next to each one. 2. Optional: Remove custom attributes. In the Selected Attributes column, custom attributes and optional standard attributes display with a blue checkmark. Uncheck any custom attributes you do not want to remove them from your customized template. 236 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization 3. Optional: Edit custom attributes. a. In the Selected Attributes column, scroll to the custom attribute you want to edit. b. Hover over the custom attribute, then click the edit ( ) icon when it appears. The Edit custom attribute window displays. c. Optional: Make the custom attribute read only. Check the Read only property to define custom attributes to be read only. You can only select this property when the Custom attribute's default value field is Purchase order since when this is the case, the custom attribute’s default value is taken from the purchase order. When the Custom attribute's default value is None, the supplier must fill in a value, which is why you cannot make the custom attribute read only. d. Optional: Make the custom attribute required. Check the Required checkbox under the Properties tab to make the custom attribute required. The supplier will be required to enter a value for this custom attribute in the Excel file. When you select the Required property for a custom attribute, its Include custom attribute in resulting cXML document field is checked automatically. e. Optional: Provide an alternative label and translation. The supported languages display under the Alternative label and translation dropdown menu. Enter the new column name in English and for any other selected language. Changes made to the custom attribute's label and translations will apply to all customization projects for that type of Excel template for Upload/Download that include the custom attribute. f. Optional: Provide an alternate data length. When the custom attribute was defined, the minimum and maximum length of its string value was set. If needed, you can change these lengths in the Alternate data length field. g. Optional: Enter a default value. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 237 The Custom attribute's default value field indicates which document the custom attribute’s default value is taken from. You can choose Purchase order or None. h. Optional: Include the custom attribute in the resulting cXML document. Check the Include custom attribute in resulting cXML document option to include the custom attribute in the cXML document that is generated when a supplier uploads the Excel template for that document type. i. Click OK. When you customize a custom attribute, a blue circle displays after its name in the Selected Attributes column. 238 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization Customizing a Workbench Tile Use this procedure to create a customization project to customize the Workbench tile to include custom attributes as columns and filters. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context You can customize the following Workbench tiles: • • Items to Confirm Orders  Note When you customize the Orders tile, the other tiles related to orders (New Orders, Changed Orders, Orders to Invoice, and Orders with service line) are also affected. • Items to Ship If you completed the first step (What project do you want to create?) on the Create Project page and clicked Save to save your project information, start with Step 1. If you completed the first step and clicked Next, start with Step 2. Procedure 1. From the Customization – Self Service page, in the row for your customization project, choose the more ( ) icon in the Actions column, then from the dropdown choose Edit. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 239 The Edit Project page opens with the second step, How do you want to customize your project, expanded and active. 2. Select up to five custom attributes to add to the Workbench tile. You can select all attributes, or you can individually select attributes from the Custom Attributes list. You can also click Create to create a new custom attribute; see Creating a Custom Attribute for a Customization Project [page 225] for instructions. 3. Optional: Edit your selected attributes. a. Click the edit ( ) icon next to an attribute to edit it. The Edit custom attribute popup opens. The attribute name displays on the second header line in the popup. 240 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization

Testing a Customization Project Use this procedure to check how an applied customization project will look before publishing it. Prerequisites • You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the permission. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 241 • You have completed steps 1 through 11 in Creating a Customization Project [page 231]. Procedure 1. If you have not already done so, sign in to a supplier test account that you have assigned the customization project to.Customization Editor 2. To test a customization project for the Upload/Download Ship Notice or Order Confirmation Excel template, proceed to Step 3 [page 242]. To test a customization project for a Workbench tile, proceed to Step 4 [page 242]. 3. Test customizations to the Upload/Download Ship Notice or Order Confirmation Excel template. a. Go to Quick Links Upload/Download The Create/Edit Job popup opens. Jobs and click Create. b. Create a job, run the job, and download the generated Excel template. For details, see Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] and Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267]. When you generate the customized Upload/DownloadCustomization job template, the new fields show as columns in the Excel spreadsheet. c. Open the Excel template download and confirm that your customizations are correct. 4. Test customizations to a Workbench tile. a. Click Workbench, and then click the tile (Items to Confirm, Orders, or Items to Ship) you want to test. The list page for the tile displays. b. Optional: Filter the results using any of the available filters. c. Optional: Configure the display listing. You can change which columns display in the table. Click the table ( ) icon to view the available columns and select the ones you want to display in the table. Publishing a Customization Project Use this procedure to test and publish a customization project. Prerequisites • • 242 You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Publisher permission. The supplier groups that you want to assign your customization project to already exist in your account. PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization Context After the Editor requests publication of a customization project to production, the Publisher can test and publish it. Procedure 1. Validate the customization project by logging on to your supplier test account and checking your customizations. See Testing a Customization Project [page 241].  Note If you are both the Editor and the Publisher, you can skip this step since you already validated the project. 2. Log on to your buyer production account. 3. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 4. Optional: Assign suppliers to your customization project. You can assign suppliers before or after publishing the project. a. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the customization project you want to assign suppliers to and select Edit. The Edit Project page displays. b. Click the edit ( ) icon in the What project do you want to create? section. c. Select the suppliers. Choices are: • • • All (default) None Selected supplier groups – When chosen, a dropdown arrow shows. Click the arrow to show the list of supplier groups. d. Click Save. e. The Suppliers popup displays. Click OK. Your edits are saved, and the Customization – Self Service page displays. 5. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the customization project you want to publish and select Publish. The Publish to production popup opens. The popup reminds you that your customization project will apply to your chosen suppliers in your production account. 6. Click OK. The customization project is published. The Status column for the project shows Published. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 243 Creating New Versions of Customization Projects Buyers can create a new version of an existing customization project and make changes to it. The existing customization project must have the Published status. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Procedure 1. Sign in to your test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. 3. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the Published customization project you want to create a new version for, and choose Create new version from the Project section. The following actions occur when you create a new version: • A warning message displays stating that the new version will be generated and the currently published version will not be affected. • The new version's major number is incremented. For example, if a new version is created from published version 1.3, the new version's number is 2.00. • The new version initially has status In Progress.  Remember Follow the normal workflow for projects to move the new version from In Progress to Pushed to Test and then to Requested to Publish. 244 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization Results Suppliers assigned to a customization project always use the latest published version of the project. When you request to publish a new version, a warning message displays to remind you that this will affect all suppliers assigned to the project. After a new version of a customization project is published, suppliers will see this version in the user interface. For example, consider a new version of a customization project for quality notifications. The default behavior for the Serial no. field in the quality notification is to display the field. Since the Serial no. field is not a mandatory field, it can be hidden. If the field is hidden in the latest published version of a customization project, suppliers will not see the field when editing an existing quality notification, even though they may have previously inserted a value in the field. However, the Serial no. field information is still visible when suppliers download the cXML for the quality notification. Deleting Unpublished Customization Projects Buyers can delete customization projects that have the status Draft, In Progress, Pushed to Test, or Requested to Publish. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Customization Editor permission. Context You can only delete a customization project when it is not yet published; that is, the project has the status Draft, In Progress, Pushed to Test, or Requested to Publish. You cannot delete a customization project that has the Published status. Procedure 1. Sign in to your test account. 2. Click Account Settings Settings Customization – Self Service .  Note Account Settings is the user icon on the top right of the page. The Customization – Self Service page opens. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Document Customization PUBLIC 245 3. Click the more ( ) icon in the Actions column for the customization project you want to delete, and select Delete project from the Project section. A warning message displays to inform you that the version of the customization project will be permanently deleted. Results When you delete a customization project, only the latest version of the project is deleted. The table on the Customization – Self Service page has one row for each customization project, which shows information about the latest version of the project. • • 246 When you delete a customization project that was never published, the row is removed from the table. When you delete a customization project that was previously published, the row for that project now shows information about the previously published version. For example, if you create version 2.0 and then delete it, and the previously published version is 1.3, the row for the project shows information about version 1.3. Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Consignment Template for Upload/Download You can generate an Upload/Download report in Excel format to help reconcile your consignment records.  Note The path to the Upload/Download feature is as follows: • • For buyers – For suppliers – Quick links … Upload/Download Upload/Download This template consolidates goods receipt and consignment movement data for a specified supplier or buyer. When a line item in a goods receipt and a consignment movement share the same consignment tracking ID, the Consignment template retrieves the related purchase order, line item, and ship notice numbers. If no tracking ID is provided, the template attempts to find line items with other matching data, such as purchase order number and ship notice number. The Consignment template also shows stock-on-hand and consignment stock values. These values are derived from cXML ProductActivityMessage documents with a matching buyer part number, supplier part number, SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update PUBLIC 249 location, and process type, and which contain ConsignmentInventory or ConsignmentMovement elements with the processType attribute set to Consignment.  Restriction The stock-on-hand value is only populated if the user has the Planning collaboration entitlement or the Inventory collaboration entitlement. A Consignment job can generate data for up to the last 60 days. A maximum of 60,000 consignment report records can be downloaded. Reports with more than 60,000 records are truncated when downloaded. The Consignment job retrieves data for a single specified supplier or customer. Records in the download file are in alphanumeric order by a combination of Customer Part No., Supplier Part No., and Location values, in that order. Blank fields are sorted last. Each set of sorted records is then grouped by document type: goods receipt (Consignment In) and consignment movement (Consignment Out). Within each set of related goods receipt and consignment movement records, color highlighting identifies rows with the following calculations: • • Blue highlighting—The total quantity of goods receipts or consignment movements for the record set. Yellow highlighting—The most recent value of consignment inventory on hand for the record set. file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: Copy Partner Addition Template for Upload/Download Buyers can use an Excel file to add a copy partner or logistics partner to multiple scheduling agreements, scheduling release agreements, and purchase orders in one operation. When you create and run a Copy Partner Addition type job from the Quick links Upload/Download Jobs page, you can download the generated Excel file and use it to add a copy partner to multiple orders: scheduling agreements, scheduling agreement releases, and purchase orders. The downloaded file can contain a maximum of 10,000 records. Files with more than 10,000 records are truncated when downloaded. Buyers send documents to the primary supplier, also copying the third-party logistic provider (copy supplier). Sometimes, the buyer might need to add the third-party logistics provider for the same documents, keeping the previous transaction data intact. The new copy partner has access and visibility to the new versions of the documents, while continuing business with the customer seamlessly. The former copy partner can no longer access the new versions of the documents. After adding or replacing the copy partner, an updated change purchase order with the latest copy partner information needs to be sent to the network, to replicate the current and subsequent documents for the new copy supplier.  Note Multiple copy suppliers cannot be added or replaced for the same purchase at the same time. A single updated change purchase order with the latest copy partner information must be processed successfully in the network before you can submit another new copy partner addition or replacement request. For each order you want to add the copy partner to, you change the value in the Partner to Use column of the Excel file to the supplier ANID of the copy partner. Then you upload the file using the Copy Partner Addition job type to submit your changes. The log for the uploaded file can contain a maximum of 10,000 records. Prerequisites You are a buyer administrator or a buyer with the Copy Partner Update permission. Requirements The copy partner or logistics partner you want to add to the orders must be enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Partner to add – (Required) The supplier ANID of the copy partner that you want to add to the orders. A supplier is prevented from editing commit key figures for any time series within the locked period. You can create Forecast type jobs using any time series granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly). When the buyer sets the preferred time series granularity to All, you can edit and commit Excel files in any time series granularity. However, when the buyer sets a specific preferred time series granularity, you can only edit and commit Excel files using that granularity. Restrictions • The Order Change Requests template for Upload/Download does not support change requests for scheduling agreements or scheduling agreement releases. • Buyers cannot upload responses with the Order Change Requests template. Order Change Request Template Criteria The Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Order Change Request job type: • • • • • • • • • • Name – (Required) A name to give the job. Type – Choose Order Change Request. Supplier – (Required) The name of the supplier whose data you want in the report. Order number – The ID of the purchase order. Company location Company code Order line-item number Schedule-line number Customer part number Creation date – The creation date or range of creaiion dates to include. Field choices are: • • • • • • • • Current Date Minus, with a Days field for the desired number of days before the current date Current Date (default) Current Date Plus, with a Days field for the desired number of days after the current date Other, with fields to choose the Start date and End date of the time period Customer-proposed delivery date – Field choices are the same as for Creation date. Priority code Reason code Change by number of days – The number of days that a Customer proposed delivery date is earlier or later than the order's current Delivery date. Filter choices are None (the default), Days earlier, or Days later. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update PUBLIC 261 For the Days earlier and Days later choices, the filter shows Min and Max fields. In these fields, you specify the minimum and maximum number of days difference that you want to include in the search results. The Min and Max fields have the following requirements: • At least one of these fields, Min or Max, must contain a value. Valid values are a number from 0 to 999. Both fields can be the same number. • The value of Min must not be greater than the value of Max. Uploads tab using any time If planning items contain attributes, attribute data is included when you download these items from the Upload/Download Jobs Upload/Download Uploads … tab. Suppliers can also upload planning items containing attributes from the … tab. Prerequisites To access this job type from the Upload/Download you must have one of the following permissions: • • • • 262 Jobs and Upload/Download Downloads tabs, Inbox and Order Access Outbox Access Forecast Visibility Planning Collaboration Visibility PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update Suppliers may also access this job type from the Upload/Download Uploads tab if they have any of the permissions listed above. Buyers, however, must have one of the following permissions to access this job type from the Upload/Download • • Inbox and Order Access Uploads tab: Outbox Access  Note Buyers cannot access the Uploads tab with only the Forecast Visibility or Planning Collaboration Visibility permission. Restrictions When the template Excel file is uploaded, it is converted to one or more cXML documents in the backend. Each cXML document is limited to 500 items. If the template Excel file has more than 500 items, multiple cXML documents are created. Replenishment Template Criteria The • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Replenishment job type: Name – (Required) The name to give the job. Type – (Required) Choose Replenishment. Customer – (Required, supplier view only) The name of the customer whose data you want in the report. Supplier – The name of the supplier whose data you want in the report. To retrieve information for all suppliers, leave this field blank. Supplier part number Buyer part number Product family Product sub-family Location Program code Planner code Part category Part type Manufacturing type Line of business Time bucket – (Required) Values are Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly. The following table shows the maximum date range for each time bucket. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update PUBLIC 263 • Time Bucket Maximum Date Range Daily 1825 days Weekly 260 weeks Monthly 60 months Quarterly 20 quarters Yearly 10 years Start – The starting date in the time window. You can define the starting date in the following ways: • • • • Current – The starting date is the current date for the time bucket. Previous – The starting date is a previous date in the time bucket. An additional field displays for you to enter a numeric value. Custom – The starting date is a custom date. An additional field displays for you to enter a custom date. End – The ending date in the time window. You can define the ending date in the following ways: • After – An additional field displays for you to enter a numeric value. The ending date is the date after the number of time buckets specified by this value. For example, if the Time bucket is Daily, and you enter 250 for the value, the ending date is after 250 days. If the time bucket is Weekly, and you enter 26 for the value, the ending date is after 26 weeks. • Custom – The ending date is a custom date. An additional field displays for you to enter a custom date. • • Download planning item attributes on all rows – Check to populate all cells in the Excel file with data. • • • Buyer last modified – Date field. • Only download planning records with positive or negative time series data – Check to only include planning records that have at least one positive or negative value in the specified time window. Supplier last modified – Date field. Customer view – Choose All Views or choose a specific view. Downloaded Excel files contain the key figures and attributes included in the view. Sort by planned projected stock status – When this checkbox is checked, the records in the downloaded Excel file display in priority order based on their stock situation. The planning records in the planning horizon (defined by the Replenishment horizon, in number of days setting) are first sorted by their stock status severity using the following order: 1. Out of Stock. 2. Below Minimum (no Out of Stock). 3. Above Maximum (no Out of Stock or Below Minimum). 4. On Track. The planning records are then sorted within each of these four groups based on the date when the stock problem will occur.  Note Planning records not occurring in the defined planning horizon appear in the Excel file after the ones in the planning horizon even when their stock status severity is Out of Stock, Below Minimum, or Above Maximum. 264 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Transaction Document Report Template for Upload/ Download Buyer administrators can generate a custom list to show the status of of multiple types of transaction documents.  Note You must have buyer administrator authorizations.  Restriction The downloaded Transaction Document Report Excel file is for information only. You cannot use it to change and upload any values the file contains. The Transaction Document Report job type lets you retrieve information from multiple document types. A Transaction Document Report job can generate up to 20,000 records for download in Excel. The generated file displays each document, its status, error codes and error messages for failed documents, and other information. Transaction Document Report Template Criteria The Quick links Upload/Download Document Report job type: Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Transaction Transaction Document Report Field Field Choices Supplier Specify a supplier name or leave blank to include all suppliers. Start date and End date Choose the dates during which included documents had any activity. • • • Monitoring status SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update The date range can cover no more than seven days. The Start Date can be no earlier than 180 days before the current date. The default is 7 days before the current date. The End Date can be no later than the current date. The default is the current date. Choose from the dropdown menu. The default All includes all document statuses. Other possible values, listed in order of severity, are: Failed on Arrival, Failed, Delayed, In Process, and Successful. PUBLIC 265 Transaction Document Report Field Field Choices Document type Choose from the dropdown menu. The default All includes all document types. Report level Choose from the dropdown menu. • • Default – Include the standard information. Order Line Reference – Include the line-item number and buyer part number from the related purchase order. This filter only supports the Invoice, Order Confirmation, and Ship Notice document types. • Order Reference – Include the related purchase order number. This filter only supports the Component Consumption, Invoice, Order Confirmation, Quality Notification, and Ship Notice document types. Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Creating an Upload/Download Job Use this procedure to save customized queries to retrieve in spreadsheet form the transaction information you want from SAP Business Network. Prerequisites Review information about the Upload/Download job type you will use and what search information you will provide. See Upload/Download Templates [page 247]. Procedure 1. Click the  Create icon and choose Upload/Download Jobs. 2. The Jobs list is displayed. Click Create. 3. Enter a name for the job and select the job type from the Type dropdown. 4. Enter your search criteria and click Next Step. 266 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update  Note For some filters, you can enter the first few letters of the term you want to search, instead of the exact term. The search result shows all the terms starting with the letters you entered. Multiple values can be selected for most of the filters. 5. If the Job needs to be executed On Demand by the user, then Run on Demand needs to be selected. If the Job needs to be executed by the system automatically in the background with specific schedules, then Schedule needs to be selected. 6. Once the schedule type is selected, then choose Next Step for Destination and Notification emails. Destination emails notify the users after the job is completed, with the link to download the file. Notification emails notify the users about the job status. If the job fails, the user can rerun, if required. Emails are not applicable to Run on Demand. 7. Click Review to go to the Review page to review your search criteria. Use Previous Step to go back to update any search criteria if needed. 8. Choose Create from the Review page to save the job definition. 9. When the schedule is selected, the frequency, start and end dates must be specified. Next Steps See Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 267]. Related Information Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload Use this procedure to generate a spreadsheet of transaction data to use to update information in SAP Business Network. Prerequisites The Upload/Download job you want to use is created. See Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 266]. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update PUBLIC 267 Procedure 1. Click the  Create icon and choose Upload/Download Jobs. 2. On the Jobs tab, locate the created job from the list, then click the  icon and choose Run from the menu.  Note The processing status will be updated automatically every 30 seconds because of auto refresh. 3. Switch to the Download tab. 4. Click the download icon  and open the file with your preferred editor. The template opens, already containing data from the selected transactions. The template spreadsheet is in Excel or CSV format, depending on the template type. If the query results exceed the maximum number of lines for the template, only the first lines up to the maximum amount are included. The rest of the lines are not included and no notification of excluded data is given.  Note All dates in an Upload/Download job download are shown by default in the user preferred time zone. This occurs regardless of the time zone used in the originating document, or the preferred time zone setting in your SAP Business Network account or operating system. 5. Enter values as desired. Make sure that required columns have values for each entry.  Note For some columns, you can enter the first few letters of the term you want to enter, instead of the exact term. The cell shows all the terms starting with the letters you entered. 6. Save the file. 7. Click the  Create icon and choose Upload/Download Jobs. 8. Click the Upload tab and choose Upload. The Upload file popup opens. 9. Upload your file. a. Choose the name of your template from the Type dropdown. b. Click Browse to choose the file to upload. c. Click Upload. The processing status will be updated automatically every 30 seconds because of auto refresh. Processing is finished when Completed shows in the Status column.  Note If the upload file has been Completed With Errors or failed , user can use the status column to view the log file and download as well, if required. 268 PUBLIC SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide Upload/Download Templates for Data Retrieval and Update Related Information Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 269] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/ Download Job Use this procedure to delete accumulated download files for a specific Upload/Download job, and optionally delete the job that created those files. Context Performing this procedure deletes all files on the Download tab of the Download and Upload page that were created by the same job. You can delete downloads for one job at a time. You can also choose to delete the job.  Note Deleting job downloads, or deleting job downloads plus the job, cannot be undone. Procedure 1. Click the  Create icon and choose Upload/Download Jobs. 2. On the Jobs tab, locate the job whose downloads you want to delete, then click the  icon and choose Delete from the menu. A confirmation popup appears with two options: • • Delete the job with downloads Delete only downloads 3. Select the desired option and click Delete. 4. To delete a specific download, go to the Download tab and choose the  Delete icon for the corresponding download. file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network fo.content: Component Shipment Report Buyers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain can create a Component Shipment report in Excel format to show selected information from multiple component ship notices. Component Shipment Report Criteria Field Description Customer Choose a customer name, or use the default value (All Customers) Component Ship Notice No. To report on a component ship notice with a specific number, enter the number in the text box. This field is case sensitive. Tracking Number Enter the tracking number associated with the component ship notice. Order Number To report on an order with a specific number, enter the number in the text box. This field is case sensitive. Shipping Organization Code Enter the code for the organization that ships the components. Receipt Status Choose one or more statuses (Open, Partially Received, or Fully Received), or use the default value (All). Show Ship Notice By Choose which type of date from the ship notice to show and the date range to include. Choices are either Ship Notice Date, Estimated Delivery Date, or Actual Shipping Date. Maximum Results Returned Choose the maximum number of records returned by the report. The report supports up to 30,000 records. Component Shipment Report Sheets The Component Shipment Excel report organizes the information it retrieves in the following sheets: • Component Shipment – Lists all component shipments sent to suppliers at item level. Details include the names of the customer, supplier, and carrier, component details, and shipping details. • Serial Numbers – Lists the serial numbers associated with specific component shipments. Details include component ship-notice information, customer and supplier batch IDs, and component serial numbers. • Component Receipt Line Item – Includes component receipt numbers, line numbers, quantities, dates, and status.
