file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Gu.content: Viewing X-Rechnung Invoice Learn to download and view X-Rechnung invoice. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. 2. Choose Invoices Invoices . The list of invoices sent to buyers appears. 3. Select the required invoice sent to the German buyer. The Detail tab opens by default. 4. Go to the Attachment(s) section. The X-Rechnung format of the invoice is available as X_RECHNUNG.XML file. 5. Double-click the X_RECHNUNG.XML file to view it. The file is automatically downloaded to your local system. Handling External Invoices This feature allows non-SAP Business Network suppliers to send external invoices (invoice created in supplier's system) to buyers in Germany through email. When the supplier sends the external invoice through email, the document is sent to SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition. The validated UBL invoice received from SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition is converted into cXML invoice in SAP Business Network. Both the UBL and the cXML invoices are then sent to the buyer as attachments, the system identifies the relevant buyer using the buyer’s VAT ID/Tax ID in the invoice.  Note Only invoices that have the buyer tax identification will be processed in SAP Business Network. Suppliers can send the following invoice types through email: • • An X-Rechnung invoice (UBL) or CII format ZUGFeRD (hybrid PDF with attached CII) invoice Suppliers can send the external invoice to the following email IDs based on the type of account: Document Type Account Type Email ID CII and UBL Test invoicereceiver-test@ansmtp.ariba.com Production invoicereceiver-prod@ansmtp.ariba.com Test PdfTaxInvoice-test@ansmtp.ariba.com Production PdfTaxInvoice-prod@ansmtp.ariba.com ZUGFeRD Buyers must configure the SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition details in SAP Business Network. For more information, see Configuring External Document Service Details [page 302]. Buyers must maintain your Vat ID in your SAP Business Network buyer account. Please contact your admin and create a support ticket for the component SBN-AN-TX-ADM-INV to add the Vat ID. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 301 SAP Business Network uses the following customization IDs to accept the external invoice. This is applicable for all types of invoice formats (UBL/CII/ZugFeRD). • • urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017#compliant#urn:xeinkauf.de:kosit:xrechnung_3.0 urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017#compliant#urn:xoev-de:kosit:standard:xrechnung_2.3 Ensure that the External Tax Invoice Rules are enabled to handle external invoices. The External Tax Invoice Rules apply a specific set of SAP Business Network transaction rules to all the external invoices irrespective of the supplier that is referenced in the invoice. For more information, see External Tax Invoice Rules. If you as a buyer has configured the attachment rules in your SAP Business Network buyer account under Default Transaction Rules Attachment File extension Rules , ensure that you allow the attachment extensions for the type of invoice format sent in the email. If the attachment rules are not set correctly, then the invoice sent as attachments to the buyer will be rejected by the system. Prerequisites • • An enterprise global account on SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP). A subscription to SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition.  Note You can reuse the SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition license if you already have a subscription for using Peppol related transactions in SAP Business Network. Configuring External Document Service Details Procedure 1. Login to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Navigate to Manage Profile Configuration External Document Service Configuration . The External Document Service Configuration page opens. 3. Under the External System Configuration tab, choose Create. The Create Configuration screen appears. The Service Provider field displays the default service provider, SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, and the Authentication Type field displays the authentication method for the service provider. Here, OAuth. 4. In the Authentication section, enter the Client ID, Client Secret, and Token URL of SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition instance. These details are created in the SAP BTP cockpit. For more information, see section Integrating Peppol Exchange with SAP Business Network. 5. Choose Save. 302 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process The SAP Business Network system validates the credentials that are provided. If the connection with SAP Document Reporting and Compliance is not established then the configuration will not be saved. Results The service provider configuration is displayed under the Service Provider section on the External System Configuration tab. You can also Edit and Delete the configuration. Click the Action option to choose the required action. Tax Invoicing in Japan The tax authority in Japan will follow the new invoice format, TEKIKAKU SEIKYUSHO TOU HOZON HOUSHIKI, effective October 2023. Supplier organizations need to register with the tax authority in Japan. The tax authority issues a unique ID for each supplier called as Tax Registration Number. This Tax Registration Number enables the buyers and suppliers using the SAP Business Network to continue business transactions and identify the business transactions with qualified invoices to claim VAT returns. The invoice created by the supplier must contain the Tax Registration Number that is used as an identifier in SAP Business Network to route it to the relevant buyer. During invoice creation, the tax amount is calculated for the line items that belong to the same tax Category and Rate. SAP Business Network then rounds-off the total taxable amount based on the round-off rule configured in the system for Japan. This enables buyers to receive invoices with accurate round-off value for the total tax amount, which is displayed on the Tax Summary section of the invoice. Thus, invoices created in the SAP Business Network system will have the tax summarization calculated at the header level during invoice creation. The tax rounding (round up, round half-up, round down) occurs only once per tax rate in a single invoice. To know more about the tax calculation, see Sample Tax Calculation [page 305]. You as a buyer, can configure your own precision and round-off value rules for the invoices that the suppliers can create in SAP Business Network. See Configuring Currency Precision and Round-Off Rules [page 308].  Note If you do not wish to apply any round-off rule, SAP Business Network applies the default round-off rule Round-half up for tax calculations. SAP Business Network recommends domestic suppliers to create and maintain a country configuration in your SAP Business Network supplier account. Additionally, buyers can generate reports to verify if the supplier has a country configuration in SAP Business Network. As a buyer, you can generate reports for all the suppliers with whom you have established a business connection in the system. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 303 Prerequisites • Buyer Prerequisite • You must enable the rule Require suppliers to send tax invoice documents under Manage Profile Configuration Country-based Invoice Rules General Invoice Rules section in your SAP Business Network buyer account. This rule enables supplier to send invoices as per the new invoicing method. • If multiple tax types are used at the header in SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, ensure that you use the same configuration in SAP Business Network. See Configuring Tax Types [page 309].  Note This is to overcome the restrictions of SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing to allow only one tax type and tax rate at the header. • Ensure that you disable the rule Ignore country-based invoice rules in your SAP Business Network buyer account under Account Settings Manage Profile Configuration Default Transaction Rules . Disabling this rule allows the country-specific rules configured for the country to precede over the default rules configured for your account on SAP Business Network. • Supplier Prerequisite • You must create and maintain a country configuration in your SAP Business Network supplier account. See Country Configuration for Suppliers in Japan [page 310]. Restrictions Country configuration is required only for domestic suppliers with registered addresses in Japan. Related Links • Invoicing Process in Japan for SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing. Supplier Information If you are a registered supplier, then you need to add the Tax Registration Number to the cXML invoice to send the invoice to the buyer on SAP Business Network. The following cXML sample code snippet describes the tag where you can add your Tax Registration Number details.  Sample Code <InvoicePartner><Contact role="billFrom"><Name 304 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process xml:lang="en-US">dev3sup06</Name><PostalAddress><Street>Aguascalientes</ Street><Street>Aguascalientes</Street><Street/><Street/><City>Aguascalientes</ City><Municipality>Aguascalientes</Municipality><State isoStateCode="MX-AGU">Aguascalientes</ State><PostalCode>10119</PostalCode><Country isoCountryCode="MX">Mexico</Country></PostalAddress><IdReference domain="taxID" identifier="T1234567890111"/></Contact></InvoicePartner> On SAP Business Network, you can view the supplier Tax Registration Number under the section of the invoice. BILL FROM Tax ID You need to send the tax summarization per tax rate and category in the cXML invoice as required by the buyer's system. During invoice creation, the following field is displayed under the Additional Japan Specific Information section. • Supplier Tax Registration Number - Displays the Tax Registration Number that is used for the country configuration. You can also edit the field to update the Tax Registration Number. This field displays a value only when a supplier enters a Tax Registration Number when creating additional entities. Sample Tax Calculation Here is an example of how SAP Business Network performs the tax calculations for Japan. The table below displays the three line items and their corresponding values added by the supplier during invoice creation. Line Item Unit Price (Yen) Category Rate (%) Line Item 1 5000 SalesTax_10 10 Line Item 2 10000 SalesTax_10 10 Line Item 3 2000 SalesTax_8 8 The line items 1 and 2 belong to the same Rate and Category, hence the total amount of line items 1 and 2 sums upto 15000. The total tax value of both the line items sums upto 1500. The line item 3 belong to a different Rate and Category, hence the total amount of line item 3 is 2000. The total tax value is 160. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 305 The SAP Business Network system sums up the total amount of the three line items as 17000 and the total tax amount as 1660. The summarized value is then displayed on the Invoice Summary section. Buyer Task Generating Reports for Country Configuration Context Buyers in Japan can generate reports to view the country configuration status in SAP Business Network. Follow the steps to create and download a report: Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Click the Reports tab. 3. Choose Create. 4. Enter a unique report title in the Title field in the Report Description section. 5. Enter a description. 6. Choose a value from the Time zone dropdown. The date and time on the report uses the time zone you select here, expressed as GMT +/-. In addition, SAP Business Network uses the time zone to determine the range of information collected for the report. 7. Choose a language. SAP Business Network uses this language for labels in the resulting report file. It displays report data in the language in which the information was entered into the system. 8. Choose Supplier Legal Profile from the Report Type drop-down. 306 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process 9. Choose Next. The Report Schedule section appears with details of the report type you selected. 10. Choose Manual Report or Scheduled Report. • • To generate a manual report, choose Manual Report, and click Next. To generate scheduled reports, choose Scheduled Report and enter the following details. • • Choose a Start Date and End Date. • Enter an email ID to receive email notifications in the Email notification. Choose a schedule from the Automatically Run drop-down. The possible values are Monthly, Weekly, Daily, and Daily (Except Sat, Sun). SAP Business Network automatically generates scheduled reports using the frequency that you specify. 11. Click Next. The Criteria section appears. 12. Select the Country/Region as Japan. 13. Choose Submit. 14. Choose Run to generate a report. The system displays the report status as Queued. Refresh the page to change the status as Processed for the report. Now, you will be able to view and download the report. 15. Select the required report template and choose Download to download the report. Results The generated report contains the following columns and corresponding details of the supplier: • • • • • • Company Profile Name Supplier ANID Address Name City Country Country configuration Status - For a domestic supplier with a country configuration, this column displays the status as Accepted. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 307 Configuring Currency Precision and Round-Off Rules Context To set the round-off value for all the items on the invoice, perform the following configuration:  Note It is recommended to set the rounding rule as Round down to meet the Japanese qualified invoice system requirements. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. On the Administration tab, choose Configuration Currency Precision and Rounding . The Configure currency precision and rounding rules page appears. 3. Choose Add currency. The Add currency overrides for Default (All systems) screen appears. 4. In the Currency drop-down list, select JPY. 5. In the Decimal place for amounts drop-down list, select 00 (recommended value). 6. In the Decimal places for unit price drop-down list, select 00 (recommended value). 7. In the Rounding rule drop-down list, select Round down. 8. In the Tax drop-down list, select Round down. 9. In the Allowances drop-down list, select Round down. 10. In the Charges drop-down list, select Round down. 11. Choose Save. The JPY round-off rule is added on the Configure currency precision and rounding rules page. 12. Select the Enable currency precision and rounding overrides checkbox. A confirmation dialog box appears. 13. Choose Yes to confirm the changes applied. 308 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process Configuring Tax Types Context Follow the steps to configure the tax types in SAP Business Network: Procedure 1. Go to Account Settings Manage Profile Configuration Country-based Invoice Rules . The Country-based Invoice Rules page is displayed. 2. Under PO and Non-PO Invoice Rules section, go to the rule Require suppliers to choose list from your list of valid tax values. 3. Select YES and click Configure. The Configure Tax page is displayed. 4. Add the tax values. 5. Select Create. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 309 Supplier Task Country Configuration for Suppliers in Japan Learn how to create country configuration for suppliers in Japan. Procedure 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. 2. Navigate to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Country Configuration from the left navigation pane. 4. Choose Create. 5. Select the Country/Region as Japan and the Company Name. 6. Choose Continue. For the selected country and company name, some of the fields are prepopulated. This information is captured from the company details provided under Additional Entities. 7. The Tax Identification Numbers section displays the tax type and tax ID related information of the supplier organization. 8. In the Access Information section, choose the required Tax Registration Type. The following tax registration type options are available: • Registered - Select this option if you are a registered supplier with Japanese tax authority and have a Tax Registration Number. • Non-Registered - Select this option if your transactions are below the taxable threshold limit as per Japan tax regulations. As a result, you have not registered with Japanese tax authority and do not have a Tax Registration Number. • Exempted - Select this option if your transactions do not require registration with the Japanese tax authority and do not have a Tax Registration Number. For example, NGOs. 9. Choose Create to complete the configuration process. You can also delete the configuration by choosing Discard Draft. Results The Japan configuration is displayed on the Country Configuration entry page. The configuration works when the Status column displays as Accepted. Related Information Editing a Country Configuration [page 186] 310 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Gu.content: Deleting a Country Configuration [page 186] Timestamp Verification of Invoices in Japan Invoices in Japan must be timestamped and verified by government approved service providers to ensure authenticity and integrity of invoices. SAP Business Network interacts with timestamp service providers such as Seiko to timestamp and verify invoices in Japan. Suppliers, buyers, or auditors appointed by the National Tax Authority can submit invoices from SAP Business Network to timestamp and further verify the invoices. In addition, buyers and suppliers enable auditors to verify invoices by creating special user profiles for them in SAP Business Network. Cross Border and Domestic Transactions Transactions in SAP Business Network are considered 'cross border' transactions if either the buyer or the supplier is outside of a country/region. If both the buyer and supplier are from within the country/region, the transactions are considered domestic transactions. According to the eDocument Act in Japan, every invoice that is associated with a cross border transaction or a domestic transaction must be timestamped and verified by a service provider. Invoices in Japan are required to be: 1. Timestamped 2. Made available for verification Timestamping of Invoices Invoices are automatically sent to Seiko when administrators configure a rule in SAP Business Network to enable timestamping and verification of invoices. The timestamping vendor, Seiko, attaches a timestamp token to each invoice and sends the invoices back to SAP Business Network. The timestamp token can be used in future to detect any tampering of invoice data. Verification of Invoices Seiko sends the timestamped invoices back to SAP Business Network. These invoices are now ready to be verified. Buyers, suppliers, or auditors can select a group of invoices and send them for verification. Seiko verifies the timestamps and sends them back to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network displays the verification status in the Timestamp Verification tab of invoices. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 311  Note It is not possible to initiate timestamp verification of invoices from other systems. Integrated suppliers also must sign in to SAP Business Network to initiate verification of invoices. Validity of Invoices The invoices that are timestamped have a validity of 10 years. Enabling the Timestamp Rule for Buyers [page 312] Enabling the Timestamp Rule for Suppliers [page 313] Batch Verifying Timestamped Invoices [page 313] Enabling the Timestamp Rule for Buyers The timestamp rule for invoices is disabled by default. Buyer administrators can enable this rule in SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Choose Administration Configuration . 2. On the Configuration page, click Default Transaction Rules. 3. Scroll down to Timestamp Rules. 4. Check the box Apply a timestamp to invoices from Japan. For this rule to be visible, at least one of the following conditions must be true: • • The buying organizations' primary address in their SAP Business Network profile must be located in Japan. At least one of the Sold to addresses must be located in Japan. This condition allows buying organizations with headquarters outside of Japan to enable timestamping without having their primary address changed to Japan. 5. Click Save. Results After the Apply a timestamp to invoices from Japan rule is enabled, an invoice that has either a Sold to or Ship to address located in Japan will be timestamped. 312 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process Enabling the Timestamp Rule for Suppliers The timestamp rule for invoices is disabled by default. Supplier administrators can enable this rule in SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Electronic Invoice Routing . 2. Click the Tax Invoicing and Archiving tab. 3. Scroll down to the Timestamp Rules check box. 4. Check the Apply a timestamp to invoices from Japan box.  Note For this rule to be visible, the address in the Company Profile must be a Japan address. 5. Click Save. Batch Verifying Timestamped Invoices Context Invoices that have been timestamped can be sent to Seiko for verification as a batch. If you wish to send more than ten invoices for verification at a time: Procedure 1. Go to the Timestamp Verification tab. 2. Select the date range of invoices to be sent for timestamp verification. 3. Click Verify. The verification process is initiated and an entry with details such as the user who created the report, the start and end dates of invoices, and the status of the verification request is added to the table. The total document count is also displayed, regardless of the number of results returned. 4. To download a batch verification report, select the report and click Download. The batch verification report is downloaded as a CSV file to your local computer. This file can be opened with any spreadsheet editor, for example, Microsoft Excel. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 313 Next Steps An email notification is sent to users after the verification report is processed. Tax Invoicing in Poland Tax invoicing in Poland provides an electronic invoicing solution that includes receiving, validating, transforming, and transmitting tax invoices to buying organizations through SAP Business Network for inbound invoices (invoices created by suppliers in a system outside SAP Business Network). Workflow of Inbound Invoices [page 314] Workflow of Outbound Invoices [page 321] Workflow of Inbound Invoices Buyers can receive the inbound invoices directly from the tax authority portal of Poland known as Krajowy System e-Faktur (KSeF). These invoices are then processed in SAP Business Network for further business transactions. SAP Business Network uses SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition to get the required invoices from the KSeF portal. The system then converts the invoice to the cXML format.  Note The Polish mandated XML invoice format is further referred as FA e-invoice in this document. As per the regulations, FA(3) invoice formats will be supported for e-invoicing in Poland for inbound flow of invoices, effective from February 2026. SAP Business Network shall support the transition of FA(2) to FA(3) invoice format from February 2026. Buyers need to configure the external document provider details in the SAP Business Network buyer account. This enables you as a buyer to establish a connection with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition and the frequency at which the invoices must be retrieved from KSef portal to your buyer account. The configurations include information about country/region, Service Provider, and scheduling details. Prerequisites • General Prerequisite • • Buyers and suppliers must register their organizations at the KSeF portal. The Tax ID (NIP) is the relevant identifications for the KSeF portal. Buyer Prerequisites • To activate this feature, you must have: • 314 PUBLIC An enterprise global account on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP). SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process • A subscription to SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition. This allows you to receive invoices from the KSeF portal to your SAP Business Network buyer account. For more information, contact your SAP Account Executive.  Note You can reuse the SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition license if you already have a subscription for using Peppol related transactions in SAP Business Network. Restrictions • For corrective invoices, SAP Business Network maps/converts the data either to a header credit memo or to a debit memo based on the corrective document type. Overview The following graphic is an example of the workflow of e-invoicing in Poland where supplier creates a purchase order (PO) in SAP Business Network using the external invoice. Prerequisite • Buyer has configured the country/region-specific and Service Provider details in SAP Business Network. This enables the buyer to receive the required external invoice. Click here [page 317] to perform the configurations. 1. The supplier creates the FA.xml e-invoice in the respective backend system and submit it to the KSeF portal for issuance. 2. The KSeF portal validates the invoice and approves or rejects based on the authenticity of the invoice. 3. The SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition retrieves the FA.xml e-invoice format from KSeF portal and sends it to SAP Business Network. 4. SAP Business Network converts the FA.xml e-invoice format into cXML format. 5. The Buyer in SAP Business Network can view the external invoice validations, and archive the invoice. The original FA e-invoice is also received as an attachment. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 315 6. The invoice is sent to the buyer's backend system.  Note The workflow of e-invoicing process is the same for both SAP Business Network suppliers and non-SAP Business Network suppliers. Buyer Information Ensure that the External Tax Invoice Rules are enabled to handle the external invoices. The External Tax Invoice Rules apply a specific set of SAP Business Network transaction rules to all the external tax invoices irrespective of the supplier that is referenced in the invoice. For more information, see External Tax Invoice Rules.  Note The Poland tax portal does not support invoice rejections, hence the standard SAP Business Network rules cannot be used. You as a buyer can view the extrinsic fields of the cXML in the invoice inbox. Open the required cXML to view them. <Extrinsic name="taxInvoiceVerification"/> <Extrinsic name="buyerVatID">3781736133</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="supplierVatID">3426417844</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="taxInvoiceRepresentation">Tax</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="taxInvoiceAttachmentName">cid:FA_VAT</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="invoiceSubmissionMethod">LegalDocumentViaXML</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="taxInvoiceFormat">FA_VAT</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="taxInvoiceNumber">9519085102-20240108-E0551478959C-F4</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="originalInvoiceNumber">PL_IN_FEB15-06</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="referenceTaxInvoiceNumber">7998033294-20240201-B8DD68CA97A0-56</ Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="originalInvoiceDate">2023-08-31</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="externalDocumentType">KOR</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="paymentMethod">cash</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="isSplitPayment">Yes</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="splitPaymentDescription">mechanizm podzielonej płatności</ Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="isReverseCharge">Yes</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="discountInformation">you get discount if you pay early</Extrinsic> The extrinsic fields that are specific for corrective invoices are given below. <Extrinsic name="originalInvoiceNumber">PL_IN_FEB15-06</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="referenceTaxInvoiceNumber">7998033294-20240201-B8DD68CA97A0-56</ Extrinsic> <Extrinsic name="originalInvoiceDate">2023-08-31</Extrinsic> 316 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process Configuring External Document Service Details This topic describes the procedure for buyers to configure external document service details to receive external documents. Context Follow these steps to configure the external document service details to receive external documents in SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Navigate to Manage Profile Configuration External Document Service Configuration . The External Document Service Configuration page appears. 3. Choose Create. The Create Configuration screen appears. 4. In the Country/Region field, select a country/region name. Here, Poland. The Create Configuration screen is populated with more fields. The Service Provider field displays the default Service Provider, SAP Document Reporting and Compliance. 5. In the Tax ID field, enter the tax ID. 6. In the Authentication Type field, select the authentication method for the Service Provider. Here, select OAuth. 7. In the Authentication section, enter the Client ID, Client Secret, and Token URL of the Service Provider. These details of the Service Provider are created in the SAP BTP cockpit. For more information, see section Integrating the Cloud Edition with SAP Business Network.  Note Ensure that you append ?grant_type=client_credentials at the end of the Token URL that you copy from the SAP BTP cockpit. For example, if the Token URL in the SAP BTP cockpit ishttps://**************.com/oauth/ token, you need to configure in the Buyer account as https://**************.com//oauth/token? grant_type=client_credentials. 8. In the Scheduling Details section, enter t section, select the start date from when you wish to retrieve the external invoices from the KSeF portal. 9. Specify the start time. 10. Choose Save. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 317 Results The Status column on the External Document Service Configuration page displays the status as NEW. You need to activate the created external document service configurations to start receiving the external documents in your SAP Business Network buyer account. This configuration is activated only once per country. For more information, see Activating External Document Service Configurations [page 318]. Activating External Document Service Configurations This topic describes the procedure to activate the external document service configurations created to receive external documents. Context Follow the steps to activate the external document service configurations. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Navigate to Manage Profile Configuration External Document Service Configuration . The External Document Service Configuration page appears. 3. On the External Document Service Configuration page, for the required country/region, choose Actions Activate . The Activate Configuration screen appears. 4. Enter the time interval at which the documents must be retrieved from the KSeF portal to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 5. Choose Save. Results The Status column on the External Document Service Configuration page displays the status as ENABLED. 318 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process Editing External Document Service Configurations Prerequisites The Status column on the External Document Service Configuration page for the specific country/region must be displayed as Enabled. Context Follow the steps to edit the external document service configurations. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Navigate to Manage Profile Configuration External Document Service Configuration . The External Document Service Configuration page appears. 3. On the External Document Service Configuration, for the required country/region, choose Actions Edit . The Edit Configuration screen appears. 4. On the Edit Configuration screen, edit the required fields. You can edit only the Authentication Detail section of the Service Provider. 5. Choose Save to save the changes. Disabling External Document Service Configurations This topic describes the procedure to disable the external document service configurations created for a specific country/region to receive external documents. Prerequisites You can disable the the external document service configurations if you have activated it. Thus, the Status column on the External Document Service Configuration page for the specific country/region must be displayed as ENABLED. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 319 Context Follow the steps to disable the external document service configurations. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Navigate to Manage Profile Configuration External Document Service Configuration . The External Document Service Configuration page appears. 3. On the External Document Service Configuration page, choose Actions Disable . The CONFIRMATION dialog box appears. 4. Choose Yes to disable the external document service configurations. Results The Status column on the External Document Service Configuration page displays the status as DISABLED. Enabling External Document Service Configurations This topic describes the procedure to enable the external document service configurations created for a specific country/region to receive external documents. Prerequisites You can enable the external document service configurations if you have disabled them. Thus, the Status column on the External Document Service Configuration page for the specific country/region must be displayed as DISABLED. Context Follow the steps to enable the external document service configurations. 320 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Gu.content: Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Navigate to Manage Profile Configuration External Document Service Configuration . The External Document Service Configuration page appears. 3. On the External Document Service Configuration page, choose Actions Enable . The CONFIRMATION dialog box appears. 4. Choose Yes to enable the external document service configurations. Results The Status column on the External Document Service Configuration page displays the status as Enabled. Workflow of Outbound Invoices This topic describes the outbound flow of invoices for suppliers in Poland. Suppliers in Poland can submit the invoices that are created in SAP Business Network directly to the Polish tax authority portal, Krajowy System e-Faktur (KSeF). SAP Business Network converts the system readable cXML invoice into the Polish FA xml e-invoice format and sends it to the KSeF portal for validation of the invoice. Only valid FA xml e-invoice from the KSeF portal will be processed in the SAP Business Network system. Buyers will receive the cXML invoice along with the FA xml e-invoice and a PDF version of the invoice as attachments.  Restriction Outbound flow of invoices is applicable only for domestic and cross-border/intra EU transactions. SAP Business Network supports generation of certificate in the tax authority portal. Support for token generation will be notified with upcoming releases. Prerequisites • Buyer Prerequisites • You must enable the rule Require suppliers to send tax invoice documents under Configuration Select the Country as Poland Country-based Invoice Rules Manage Profile General Invoice Rules section in your SAP Business Network buyer account. This rule enables suppliers to send Polish invoices to the KSeF portal. • Ensure that you disable the rule Ignore country-based invoice rules in your SAP Business Network buyer account under Account Settings Manage Profile Configuration Default Transaction Rules . Disabling this rule allows the country-specific rules configured for Poland to precede over the default rules configured for your account on SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 321 • Supplier Prerequisites • You need to have a KSeF registered Tax ID/NIP, and a valid KSeF token. Both these particulars can be obtained in the KSeF portal. • You must create a country configuration for your supplier organization in your SAP Business Network supplier account. For more information, see Country Configuration for Suppliers in Poland [page 322]. Invoices created without a maintained country configuration will: • • Be processed in SAP Business Network if the rule is not enabled by the buyer. Not be processed in SAP Business Network if the rule is enabled by the buyer. Therefore the invoice will not be sent to the KSeF portal. Buyer Information You can view the FA xml e-invoice under the Invoice inbox in your SAP Business Network buyer account. Supplier Information During invoice creation, note the following points: • You will be able to enter the tax rate allowed by the KSeF as Line Level taxes. Header level taxes are not supported for Polish invoices. • Once you select the required country configuration, the Supplier NIP field under the Additional Poland Specific Information section is auto-populated with the Tax ID/NIP entered during creation of the country configuration.  Note Ensure that you maintain only the Tax ID(NIP) for the SoldFrom address on the Additional Entities tab. • The Buyer NIP field under the Additional Poland Specific Information section is auto-populated with the Tax ID/NIP when you select the buyer's address from the Choose Address Customer drop-down.  Note If the FA xml e-invoice fails the validation process in the KSeF portal, then the status of the invoice is available on the invoices's History page. Country Configuration for Suppliers in Poland Context Follow the steps to set up the country configuration for suppliers in Poland. 322 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process Procedure 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. 2. Navigate to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Country Configuration from the left navigation pane. 4. Choose Create. 5. Select the Country/Region as Poland and the Company Name. 6. Choose Continue. For the selected country and company name, some of the fields are prepopulated. This information is captured from the company details provided under Additional Entities. 7. The Tax Identification Numbers section displays the tax type and tax ID related information of the supplier organization. 8. In the Supplier KSeF Registration Information section, choose the Registration Type. 9. If you select the KSeF Token type, then enter the token number. If you select the KSeF certification type, then upload the certificate. 10. Choose Create to complete the configuration process. You can also delete the configuration by choosing Discard Draft. Results The Poland configuration is displayed on the Country Configuration entry page. The configuration works when the Status column displays as Accepted. Once the Poland configuration is in the accepted state, it is recommended to not delete it. If you delete it, then you have to create a Service Now ticket to create country configuration for the same tax details and credentials. Poland Split Payment Mandate Overview Poland introduced a split payment mechanism for certain categories of goods and services. Polish and cross border (foreign) suppliers selling goods or offering services from those categories must mark an invoice, which documents the delivery of such goods or services, as subject to the mandatory split payment method. The invoice is then applicable for split payment if at least one product or service falls under the defined categories, and if a certain threshold is exceeded. This feature is applicable only to suppliers from Poland. To determine whether the supplier is from Poland, SAP Business Network first checks the VAT ID/TAX ID of the supplier. If VAT ID/TAX ID is not present, SAP Business Network checks the "From" address.  Note The buyer VAT ID/TAX ID does not have any impact on the split payment functionality. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 323 To maintain regulatory consistency in its Poland operations, SAP Business Network provides suppliers an option to indicate whether an invoice is subject to the split payment mandate or not. The section, Additional Poland Specific Information, contains a mandatory question 'Invoice subject to split payment mechanism?' Suppliers must choose either Yes or No in the drop-down box. If suppliers do not answer this question and try to submit the invoice, they are prompted to provide an answer with a message "Please select Yes/No for the Split Payment mechanism." The cXML invoice contains the extrinsic splitPayment:  Sample Code <InvoiceDetailRequest> <InvoiceDetailRequestHeader> <Extrinsic name="splitPayment">Yes</Extrinsic> </InvoiceDetailRequestHeader> </InvoiceDetailRequest> If the extrinsic element splitPayment is present in the cXML invoice, it's value must be either 'Yes' or 'No'. If suppliers leave this vaue empty or enter any value other than 'Yes' or 'No', the invoice might fail. Suppliers can view the invoice status in the History tab of the invoice. Tax Invoicing in Romania Tax invoicing in Romania provides an electronic invoicing solution that includes receiving, validating, transforming, and transmitting tax invoices to buying organizations through SAP Business Network. Workflow of Outbound Invoices [page 324] Workflow of Inbound Invoices [page 327] Workflow of Outbound Invoices Outbound invoices are the invoices generated on SAP Business Network. They are validated against the Romanian tax authority known as National Agency for Fiscal Administration (ANAF) portal and then the UBL invoice is received as an attachment. This workflow is applicable for domestic transactions. The following graphic shows the workflow of e-invoicing for outbound invoices in Romania. 324 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process 1. The supplier flips a PO or creates a non-PO invoice in SAP Business Network. 2. SAP Business Network performs business validations against the created invoice and converts the invoice into cXML format. It is then submitted to the ANAF portal through the authorized service provider. 3. The authorized service provider enables connectivity with the ANAF portal and also converts the cXML invoice into Romanian-specific invoice format, RO_UBL. 4. The ANAF portal validates the invoice, and approves or rejects based on the authenticity of the invoice. 5. The status of the RO_UBL invoice, validated UBL invoice and the PDF version of the invoice are captured by the service provider and sent to SAP Business Network. 6. SAP Business Network routes the cXML version, UBL version and the PDF version of the invoice to the relevant buyer. 7. The Buyer in SAP Business Network can view the external invoice validations, and archive the invoice. Prerequisites • Buyer Prerequisite • You must enable the rule Require suppliers to send tax invoice documents under Configuration Select the Country as Romania Manage Profile Country-based Invoice Rules General Invoice Rules section in your SAP Business Network buyer account. This rule enables suppliers to send invoices to the ANAF portal. • Enable the rule Allow suppliers to add allowances and charges to invoices and its subrule Require suppliers to provide negative tax on allowances on invoices in your SAP Business Network buyer account under Invoice Rules • Account Settings Manage Profile General Invoice Rules Configuration Default Transaction Rules section. Disable the rule Require customer's VAT/Tax ID in your SAP Business Network buyer account under Account Settings Manage Profile SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process Configuration Default Transaction Rules Invoice Rules PUBLIC 325 VAT Rules Romania • section and under VAT Rules Configuration Country-based Invoice Rules Select country as section. Ensure that you disable the rule Ignore country-based invoice rules in your SAP Business Network buyer account under Account Settings Manage Profile Configuration Default Transaction Rules . Disabling this rule allows the country-specific rules configured for Romania to precede over the default rules configured for your account on SAP Business Network. • Supplier Prerequisite • You need to have a ANAF registered Tax ID/CUI, and a valid ANAF Acess token, Refresh token, Client ID and Client Secret. These particulars can be obtained in the ANAF portal. • You must create and maintain Romania country configuration in your SAP Business Network supplier account. For more information, see Country Configuration for Suppliers in Romania [page 326]. Invoices created without a country configurations will: • • Be processed in SAP Business Network, if the rule is not enabled by the buyer. Not be processed in SAP Business Network, if the rule is enabled by the buyer. Therefore the invoice will not be sent to the ANAF portal. Supplier Information During creation of an invoice, consider the following points: • If you are a Romanian supplier and have selected the State as Bucharest, then enure that you enter the City as SECTOR1, SECTOR2,….SECTOR6. • The Invoice number should have at least one numeric value. Country Configuration for Suppliers in Romania Learn how to create country configuration for Romania. Procedure 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. 2. Navigate to Account Settings Company Profile . 3. Select Country Configuration from the left navigation pane. 4. Choose Create. 5. Select the Country/Region as Romania and the Company Name. 6. Choose Continue. For the selected country and company name, some of the fields are prepopulated. This information is captured from the company details provided under Additional Entities. 7. The Tax Identification Numbers section displays the tax type and tax ID related information of the supplier organization. 326 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process 8. In the ANAF Registration Information section, enter the Access Token, Refresh Token, Client ID and Client Secret that are generated by ANAF during tax registration in the respective fields. 9. Choose Create to complete the configuration process. You can also delete the configuration by choosing Discard Draft. Results The Romania configuration is displayed on the Country Configuration entry page. The configuration works when the Status column displays as Accepted. Once the Romanian configuration is in the accepted state, it is recommended to not delete it. If you delete it, then you have to create a Service Now ticket to create country configuration for the same tax details and credentials. Related Information Editing a Country Configuration [page 186] Deleting a Country Configuration [page 186] cXML Information SAP Business Network generates the following extrinsic in the cXML invoice specifically for Romania. When SAP Business Network suppliers send the the invoice, the extrinisc must be available in the invoice. Extrinsic taxInvoiceNumber Sample code <InvoiceDetailRequest> .... <InvoiceDetailRequestHeader> <Extrinsic name="taxInvoiceNumber">3013238232</ Extrinsic> </ InvoiceDetailRequestHeader> .... </InvoiceDetailRequest> Workflow of Inbound Invoices Buyers can receive invoices directly from the tax authority portal of Romania, National Agency for Fiscal Administration (ANAF). These invoices are then processed in SAP Business Network for further business SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 327 transactions. SAP Business Network uses SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition to get the required invoices from the ANAF portal. Buyers need to configure the external document provider details in the SAP Business Network buyer account. This is required to establish a connection with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition and maintain the frequency at which the invoices must be retrieved from the ANAF portal. The following graphic describes the workflow of e-invoicing in Romania for inbound invoices. 1. The supplier creates a local e-invoice format in the respective backend system and submit it to the ANAF portal. 2. The ANAF portal validates the invoice and approves or rejects the invoice. 3. The SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition retrieves the validated e-invoice from ANAF portal and then send it to SAP Business Network. 4. SAP Business Network converts the local e-invoice into the cXML format. 5. The SAP Business Network validates the invoice as per the business rules and archive the invoice. The original local e-invoice and the signature file are received as attachments. 6. The invoice along with the attachment are sent to the buyer's backend system.  Note The workflow is the same for both SAP Business Network suppliers and non-SAP Business Network suppliers. Emailing Inbound Invoices Buyers can receive the legal RO_UBL invoices from external suppliers through email. The supplier issues the external RO_UBL invoice for cross-border and domestic transactions and submit them to the Romanian tax authority portal. The buyer can then download the external invoice from the tax authority portal and then email it to the respective buyer account in SAP Business Network Buyers can use the following email IDs to receive the external invoice to the test or prod accounts. Account Type Email ID Test invoicereceiver-test@ansmtp.ariba.com 328 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process Account Type Email ID Prod invoicereceiver-prod@ansmtp.ariba.com You can upload up to three RO_UBL invoice as attachments. The tax ID must be maintained in the SAP Business Network buyer account. Based on the tax id maintained in the UBL, the invoice is routed to the corresponding buyer. Prerequisites • General Prerequisite • • Buyers and suppliers must register their organizations with the ANAF portal. The VAT ID/TAX ID is the relevant identifications for the ANAF portal. Buyer Prerequisites • To activate this feature, you must have: • • An enterprise global account on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP). A subscription to SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition. This allows you to receive invoices to your SAP Business Network buyer account. For more information, contact your SAP Account Executive.  Note You can reuse the SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition license if you already have a subscription for using Peppol related transactions in SAP Business Network. Buyer Information Ensure that the External Tax Invoice Rules are enabled to handle the external invoices. The External Tax Invoice Rules apply a specific set of SAP Business Network transaction rules to all the external tax invoices irrespective of the supplier that is referenced in the invoice. For more information, see External Tax Invoice Rules.  Note SAP Business Network recommends to use External Tax Invoice rules over the standadrd invoice rules as the Romanian tax portal does not support invoice rejections. You can see the extrinsics in the cXML invoice.  Sample Code <Extrinsic Name="buyerVatID">R041179133</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic Name="supplierVatID">RO34104693</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic Name="taxInvoiceRepresentation">Tax</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic Name="taxInvoiceAttachmentName">cid:RO_FACTURA</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic Name="invoiceSubmissionMethod">LegalDocumentViaXML</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic Name="taxInvoiceFormat">UBL</Extrinsic> SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 329 <Extrinsic Name="taxInvoiceNumber">54354354353</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic Name="paymentMethod">wire</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic Name="deliveryDate">deliverydate1234</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic Name="LegalStatus">CompanyLegalForm654</Extrinsic> <Extrinsic Name="paymentReference">76767586</Extrinsic> Configuring External Document Service Details Context Follow these steps to configure the external document service details to receive external invoices in SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Navigate to Manage Profile Configuration External Document Service Configuration . The External Document Service Configuration page appears. 3. Choose Create. The Create Configuration screen appears. 4. In the Country/Region field, select a country/region name. Here, Romania. The Create Configuration screen is populated with more fields. The Service Provider field displays the default Service Provider, SAP Document Reporting and Compliance. 5. In the Tax ID field, enter the CIF number. 6. In the Authentication Type field, select the authentication method for the Service Provider. Here, select OAuth. 7. In the Authentication section, enter the Client ID, Client Secret, and Token URL of the Service Provider. These details of the Service Provider are created in the SAP BTP cockpit. For more information, see section Integrating the Cloud Edition with SAP Business Network.  Note Ensure that you append ?grant_type=client_credentials at the end of the Token URL that you copy from the SAP BTP cockpit. For example, if the Token URL in the SAP BTP cockpit ishttps://**************.com/oauth/ token, you need to configure in the Buyer account as https://**************.com//oauth/token? grant_type=client_credentials. 8. In the Scheduling Details section, select the start date from when you wish to retrieve the external invoices from the ANAF portal. 9. Specify the start time. 330 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process

SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 333 Results The Status column on the External Document Service Configuration page displays the status as Enabled. Tax Invoicing in Australia and New Zealand Tax invoicing in Australia and New Zealand provides an electronic invoicing solution that includes receiving, validating, transforming, and transmitting tax invoices to buying organizations through SAP Business Network. Inbound flow of invoice is supported through Peppol. For more information, see Peppol Integration for SAP Business Network [page 355]. To understand the outbound flow, see Workflow of Outbound Invoices [page 334]. Workflow of Outbound Invoices When suppliers create an invoice in SAP Business Network, a cXML format of the invoice is generated. The invoice is then sent to the relevant buyer using the ANID as the identifier. Ensure that as a buyer, you apply appropriate default rules and country-specific rules to complete transactions with suppliers. You must also enable the entitlement Label both CXML and PDF invoice documents as 'Tax Invoice' for Australia and New Zealand. To enable the entitlement, contact your SAP support team.  Remember This flow is applicable for domestic and cross-border transactions. Related Information Invoice Rules [page 119] Invoice Creation [page 23] Tax Invoicing in Belgium SAP Business Network supports creating and processing of EN-16931 compliant invoices to address relevant Belgian B2B regulations, if the buyer activates this feature. In this case, the UBL invoice issued in SAP Business Network shall constitute as the legal invoice, whereas the cXML file is used only for data transfer and processing purposes. 334 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process As per the e-invoice mandate in Belgium, the default approach is for suppliers to send invoices to buyers through Peppol network. As of January 2026, Belgian invoices must be based on the European Norm EN-16931, for example, UBL BIS 3.0 format. If you as a supplier want to use an alternative invoice format and/or send invoices outside of the Peppol network it must be based on mutual agreement between the buyer and the supplier. The UBL invoice is available under the Attachment(s) section. As the cXML invoice does not constitute as a legal invoice, it will not be digitally signed.  Note Domestic invoices based on the UBL format is not supported for self-billed invoices. If Long Term Archiving is activated, then the UBL invoice is also archived. The required SAP Business Network rules such as country-based rules, and default transaction rules are also applicable for Belgium. As a buyer, ensure that the rules are thoroughly checked and applied for the country if you are adding the invoice rules for the first time for Belgium. For more information, see Country/Region-Based Invoice Rules [page 122]. Buyer Tasks Enable the following rules • • Default rules: • For outbound flows: Allow suppliers to add allowances and charges to invoices to ensure the UBL structure is correct. Discounts or additional costs such as transport cost should use allowances and charges to ensure alignment with the UBL structure. • For inbound flows: Allow these file extensions only and enter xml and html as file extension formats to allow as attachments. Country-based rules: • • Require suppliers to send tax invoice documents Require suppliers to provide net term information on the invoice to ensure that the payment term information is available. Disable the following rules • Default rules: • • Ignore country-based invoice rules to precede the configured country-specific rules over the default rules for Belgium. Country-based rules: • Require explanation for zero-rate VAT  Remember Ensure that the UOM on POs and invoices are based on Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 recommendations. For more . information, see https://docs.peppol.eu/poacc/billing/3.0/codelist/UNECERec20/ SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process PUBLIC 335 Supplier Tasks • During invoice creation, navigate to the Line items section. If the Tax rate is zero rated, then choose the required option for the Reason for exemption drop-down list. • To download and view the invoices sent to buyers, see Viewing a UBL Invoice [page 336]. Viewing a UBL Invoice Learn to download and view a UBL invoice. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network supplier account. 2. Choose Invoices Invoices . The list of invoices sent to buyers appears. 3. Select the required invoice sent to the Belgian buyer. The Detail tab opens by default. 4. Go to the Attachment(s) section. The UBL format of the invoice is available as UBL.XML file. 5. Double-click the UBL.XML file to view it. The file is automatically downloaded to your local system. 336 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Country/Region-Specific Tax Invoicing Process SAP Business Network Invoice Rules and Fields Suppliers are responsible for providing invoices on time and ensuring that all required invoice content is present (same as for paper invoices). Buyers are responsible for enabling specific rules for that cover how suppliers create invoices, as many rules determine the allowed values for certain fields. Buyers can enable rules in the Invoice Rules section of the Default Transaction Rules page in their SAP Business Network account (Manage Profile > Default Transaction Rules). However, they can override them for specific suppliers, supplier groups or the country/region from where the invoice is sent. Suppliers can review the rules that have been specified by the buyer for invoice transactions in the Customer Details page of their SAP Business Network account (Customer Relationships > Customer Details). SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing SAP Business Network Invoice Rules and Fields PUBLIC 347 Global E-Invoicing Requirements Electronic tax invoicing (e-invoicing) is the sending, receipt and storage of invoices in electronic format without the use of paper-based invoices as tax originals. For e-invoices to be recognized on an equivalent audit basis as paper invoices for value-added tax (VAT) or similar indirect taxes, most countries require e-invoices to meet the requirements for content, authenticity, integrity, and archiving. Failure to meet such requirements can lead to sanctions, including fines and the possibility of buyers having to repay already deducted VAT. Implementing a cost-effective tax compliant e-invoicing system requires a holistic approach that takes into account technical, process, and legal aspects of a corporation's invoice processes throughout the relevant disciplines in the company. However, the approach must be driven by a tax perspective, which means first deciding on the desired outcome of an audit process and then designing the system from the resulting requirements. Trading Partner Tax Responsibilities and Liabilities SAP Ariba does not play a tax advisor role. When a Trading Partner uses a Service Provider, it does not transfer its tax responsibilities or liabilities to the Service Provider. Tax authorities offer system audits to the taxable customer. These audits typically address the “end to end” process. SAP Ariba supports reviews of its components by offering process documentation and technical advisory services. However, SAP Ariba cannot support non-SAP Ariba components or processes such as tax reports generated in the Trading Partners’ AP/ERP systems. In Europe, local Tax Authorities don't deliver formal certification/authorization letters to providers of e-invoicing features like SAP Ariba. For legal and regulatory compliance, each Trading Partner needs to, at its own expense, perform the following tasks: • • Obtain all necessary regulatory approvals applicable to its business. Obtain any necessary permits for its business and comply in all material respects with all laws and regulatory requirements applicable. SAP Ariba makes no representation as to whether its e-invoicing features satisfy the applicable legal requirements regarding tax. Customers should consult with their tax and legal advisor on such issues. 348 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Global E-Invoicing Requirements Invoice Status Portal Configuration Buyers transacting with different suppliers receive invoices through different channels such as email, fax, and more. These invoices are processed based on location and buyer configuration. The status of an invoice can be received, approved, paid, or rejected. Throughout the invoice lifecycle, suppliers can have multiple queries regarding the status of the invoices and payments. Buyers spend a significant amount of resources to manually communicate with suppliers on such queries regarding the status of invoices and payments. The invoice status portal is a self-service platform that allows suppliers to view the status and details of their invoices at any time. Suppliers can create a new account on your invoice status portal or use an existing account on SAP Business Network to view invoice details. Suppliers can also look up a single invoice without signing into your invoice status portal. You configure the invoice status portal to suit your requirements and profile. The invoice status portal you configure is unique and contains your company name and logo. While setting up the invoice status portal, you can specify the logo, criteria for invoice search, and the portal URL. When the invoice status portal is set up and an ERP copy invoice is received on the invoice status portal, a customized invitation email is also sent to the supplier to visit the portal to view status of their invoices.  Note • Once the invoice status portal is set up, when an ERP copy invoice is received, a quick enablement email invitation to SAP Business Network are not sent to suppliers. Instead, they are invited to your invoice status portal. • Email invitations for your invoice status portal are also sent to suppliers for invoices of legacy purchase orders. • Invitation to the invoice status portal is triggered when an ERP copy invoice is sent to a new supplier. If the supplier is already registered on SAP Business Network via trading relationship request or other relationship methods, they can continue using the invoice status update on the workbench. On the invoice status portal, a supplier can either look up the status of a single invoice or register on to your invoice status portal to view the status of the invoices the supplier has sent to you. When a supplier receives an invitation email to your invoice status portal, the supplier can access the invoice status portal from the link in the email. When suppliers click on the link to the invoice status portal, they will land on your invoice status portal sign in page. Suppliers can perform the following actions on the invoice status portal: • Register for your invoice status portal: Suppliers can register on your invoice status portal to view invoices that they have sent to you. On registration, they get access to invoices in different statuses categorized in the form of tiles. Clicking on each tile displays the list of invoices with the same status. Suppliers can also edit the filters to view invoices that meet specific criteria. They can sort the list of invoices, hide and display columns, and export the results into an Excel file. Invoice tiles available on the portal include statuses for: all invoices, paid, rejected, invoices pending approval, approved invoices pending payment, overdue invoices - approved, and overdue invoices - not approved, and remittances. • Sign in using existing SAP Business Network credentials: Suppliers who already have an account on SAP Business Network can log into the invoice status portal using the same credentials. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Invoice Status Portal Configuration PUBLIC 349 • Single invoice lookup: Suppliers can look up the status of a single invoice without having to create an account on the invoice status portal or SAP Business Network. The status of a single invoice is displayed based on supplier vendor ID, email address, and the invoice number given by suppliers. You can integrate support for net payment due date in ERP-initiated invoices and Invoice Status Update (ISU) messages using SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. Prerequisites • You must have a license to SAP Business Network Commerce Automation, SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, or SAP Business Network Commerce Automation, foundation option. • To give suppliers access to remittance details on invoices, you must configure payment remittance requests. For more information, see Configuring payment remittance request in SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA. • You must configure SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. You must configure ERP copy invoices to send those invoices to SAP Business Network. For more information on configuring ERP copy invoices, seeConfiguring ERP-initiated invoice in SAP ERP and SAP S/ 4HANA .  Note When SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing retries invoice copy requests due to a missing confirmation response from Ariba Network, it generates a new payload ID for each retry. Since Ariba Network identifies requests by payload ID, this behavior can result in duplicate invoices and payment processing errors. To reuse the same payload ID during retries and prevent duplicates, enable the Reuse invoice payload ID for copy requests to Ariba Network (Application.Invoicing.ReuseInvoicePayloadIDForCCToAN) parameter. For more information, see Reuse existing invoice payload ID for copy requests to Ariba Network. • You must enable the transaction rule to set up the invoice status portal. For more information, see Enabling the Invoice Status Portal [page 351]. • You must configure the invoice status portal URL to activate the invoice status portal for suppliers. For more information, see Setting Up the Invoice Status Portal [page 352].  Note You must ensure that the email address they keep for the supplier in your vendor master data is the email address that should receive the invitation to your invoice status portal. Restrictions To know the restrictions of invoice status portal, refer to the chapter Restrictions in SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway Overview Guide. 350 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Invoice Status Portal Configuration
