file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Gu.content: Workflow for the Invoice Status Portal The following is the workflow for the invoice status portal: • • • You deploy and configure SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway. • Suppliers can create an account on your invoice status portal. If a supplier already has an account on SAP Business Network with a trading relationship with you, they can use the existing account to sign in to your invoice status portal. Suppliers can also sign in to SAP Business Network to create users and update their company profile. Suppliers can view the invoices they have sent to you. They can view the details of invoices including invoice status, invoice date, received date, and net payment due date. • Alternatively, suppliers can look up details of a single invoice without registering or logging into your invoice status portal. The invoice details are retrieved based on the invoice number and the supplier vendor ID that you keep in your vendor master data for suppliers. Suppliers can view header-level details of the invoice including invoice status, invoice date, and net payment due date. Suppliers can also view the timeline of the status of an invoice. You configure the invoice status portal on SAP Business Network. When an ERP copy invoice is received on SAP Business Network, an invitation email is sent to suppliers to visit your invoice status portal for status and header-level details of invoices.  Note For suppliers to look up details of a single invoice, you must enable single invoice lookup while configuring the invoice status portal. Enabling the Invoice Status Portal Context You must enable the transaction rule for the invoice status portal to configure your invoice status portal. Procedure 1. Click Administration > Configuration. 2. Click Default Transaction Rules. This opens the Default Transaction Rules page. 3. In the Invoice Status Portal Rules section, check the rule Enable invoice status portal. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Invoice Status Portal Configuration PUBLIC 351 4. Click Save. Setting Up the Invoice Status Portal Context You can set up the invoice status portal for suppliers and configure the portal to reflect your requirements. You can also configure the invitation email to the supplier. Procedure 1. Sign in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Administration > Configuration. 3. Choose Invoice Status Portal Configuration. This opens the Invoice Status Portal Configuration page. 4. Under the General tab, add the company information under the following fields: • Company Name: The name of your organization configured under Configuration > Company profile on SAP Business Network is displayed. • Company Logo: The company logo configured under Configuration > Company profile on SAP Business Network is displayed. For more information, see How to upload your logo. • Buyer Email: Add the email address shared with suppliers on invoice status portal for help and additional information. • URL: Give a name to the endpoint of the invoice status portal URL to be shared with suppliers. 5. Under the Invitation email tab, configure the email invitation for the invoice status portal. The invitation email content in English has to be set up first. • • Language: English is chosen as the default language. Content: Enter the content for the email invitation. You can also set up email invitation content in other languages. For the detailed process to add language and content, see Setting Up the Invoice Status Portal Invitation Email [page 353]. 6. Under the Registration tab, you can manage the information displayed to suppliers on the registration page of the invoice status portal. For the detailed process to set up the invoice status portal registration page, see Setting Up Registration Page for the Invoice Status Portal [page 353]. 7. Under the Single invoice lookup tab, you can choose to allow or not allow suppliers to look up a single invoice without registering on your invoice status portal. For the detailed process to set up single invoice lookup, see Setting Up Single Invoice Lookup [page 354]. 8. Click Save to save the invoice status configuration. 352 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Invoice Status Portal Configuration Setting Up the Invoice Status Portal Invitation Email Context You can configure the email invitation to suppliers for the invoice status portal. The invitation email content has to be set up in English first. If no content has been set up for a specific language, the invitation is sent in English. If the Enable email invitation toggle is turned off, suppliers will not automatically receive an invitation to the invoice status portal when ERP copy invoices are sent to SAP Business Network. However, you can manually invite suppliers to your invoice status portal by navigating to Manage Vendors, selecting suppliers, and adding the suppliers by clicking Add > Invite to Invoice Status Portal. Suppliers added to your invoice status portal will receive an email invitation. You can also use this functionality to resend the invitation email to suppliers. Procedure 1. On the Invoice Status Portal Configuration page, choose the Invitation email tab. 2. Turn on the Enable email invitation toggle to enable email invitation to suppliers for the invoice status portal. 3. Enter the maximum number of times the invoice status portal invitation email is to be sent to a supplier under the Email Invitation Threshold section. By default, an email invitation is sent to the supplier for every ERP copy invoice unless you configure a maximum threshold number. This email is sent to the supplier email address to which the invitation email was sent. 4. Choose language from the Choose language dropdown. 5. Choose country/region from the Choose country dropdown. 6. Enter the subject of the invitation email in the Title field. 7. Enter the body of the email invitation in the Description field. 8. Enter the help text to help suppliers access/locate their vendor ID. For instance, you can explain how suppliers can access the vendor ID from a purchase order or from the invitation email. 9. Click Add. Setting Up Registration Page for the Invoice Status Portal Context You can manage the information displayed to suppliers on the registration page of the invoice status portal. The registration page content has to be set up in English first. If no content has been set up for a specific language, the informtaion is displayed in English. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Invoice Status Portal Configuration PUBLIC 353 Procedure 1. On the Invoice Status Portal Configuration page, choose the Registration tab. 2. Enter the title of the registration page in the Title field. 3. Enter the description for the registration page in the Description field. 4. Enter the help text to help suppliers access/locate their vendor ID. Setting Up Single Invoice Lookup Context You can choose to allow or not allow suppliers to look up details of a single invoice. Procedure 1. On the Invoice Status Portal Configuration page, choose the Single invoice lookup tab. 2. Allow single invoice lookup by enabling the Allow single invoice lookup toggle. 3. Choose the fields to be displayed on the single invoice lookup page. Invoice number is mandatory and it cannot be removed during configuration. Invoice amount and Invoice date are the other two available fields. You can choose to make these fields visible and mandatory. The selected fields are displayed on the single invoice lookup page and are used, along with the supplier's vendor ID and email address, to retrieve the details of the requested invoice. If the supplier has sent more than one invoice with the same invoice number, the most recent invoice is displayed to the supplier. 4. Enable the Allow supplier users listed in the Contact section of an invoice to look up the invoice to allow supplier users listed in the Contact section of an invoice to look up that particular invoice. 354 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Invoice Status Portal Configuration Peppol Integration for SAP Business Network Learn how Peppol is integrated with SAP Business Network. Description SAP Business Network supports integration with Peppol network. This allows buyers using SAP Business Network to receive invoices from Peppol network, provided both the buyer and supplier are registered with Peppol network. This feature is available for buyers and suppliers in Germany, Australia, New Zealand, Belgium, Norway, Japan, Singapore and the Netherlands. Peppol integration with Singapore, Australia and New Zealand is supported only for inbound flow of invoices, that is, as a buyer, you can only receive invoices from suppliers through Peppol network. PINT format invoices are supported for Australia and New Zealand.  Note Peppol in the Netherlands supports invoices in SI-UBL 2.0 and BIS Billing 3.0 formats. While SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition (Peppol Access Point) supports both the required formats, SAP Business Network as the receiving business system (Corner 4), currently supports BIS Billing 3.0. Prerequisites • You must have: • • An enterprise global account on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) A subscription to SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition • To enable this feature, contact your SAP Ariba Customer Success Partner, Customer Engagement Executive, or Account Executive. • You have already completed the initial steps to setup SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition. For more information, see Integrating Peppol Exchange with SAP Business Network. • Your peppol participant ID must be maintained in SAP Business Network buyer account under Manage Profile Configure External Network Identifiers . Based on the participant ID maintained in the UBL, the invoice is routed to the corresponding buyer. • The following rules must be enabled under Rules • • Default Transaction Rules Invoice Rules General Invoice section: Allow suppliers to send invoices to this account Allow suppliers to send invoice attachments The following additional prerequisites are applicable for Japan only. • Buyers must establish connection between Peppol Exchange service for SAP Document and Reporting Compliance and SAP Business Network. This is a one-time activity. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Peppol Integration for SAP Business Network PUBLIC 355 For more information, see Setting Up Connectivity (Relevant Only for Japan). Click here [page 362] to see the procedure to setup Peppol connectivity with SAP Business Network for Japan. • Buyers must have credentials to access the Open API to receive external documents from SAP Document and Reporting Compliance. • To create an application and request access to use the SAP Ariba APIs relevant to this feature, you must have access to the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. For details refer to Steps to Start Using the SAP Ariba APIs in Help for the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. • All queries made to this API must be authenticated using OAuth authentication. For details refer to SAP Ariba Developer Portal Authentication in Help for the SAP Ariba Developer Portal.  Note Ensure that you use OAuth version 2.0 for authentication. Restrictions • Buyers will be able to receive invoice documents only. SAP Business Network as a receiving business system (Corner 4) only supports BIS Billing 3.0. Information for Buyers • Invoices created by supplier contain identifiers such as the Peppol participant ID. SAP Business Network depends on this identifier to link the buyer and supplier. • When you quit, you must delete your corresponding Peppol profile in SAP Business Network and SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, and then exit. • The standard digital signature will not be applied for Peppol invoices. Related Information What Is SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition Integrating Peppol Exchange with SAP Ariba Peppol Page 356 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Peppol Integration for SAP Business Network Workflow of Peppol Integration with SAP Business Network Describes an inbound flow of an invoice from Peppol network to SAP Business Network. The image below depicts a typical inbound flow of an invoice through Peppol network. In this scenario, the supplier is the sender and is not a user of SAP Business Network. The buyer is a registered user of SAP Business Network and is a part of the receiving entity. 1. Supplier is a registered participant of Peppol network and uses a Peppol registered Access Point to send an invoice in the UBL format. 2. The supplier Access Point communicates with Peppol network to identify the buyer in the network. The supplier Access Point also validates the UBL invoice. 3. Peppol network sends the invoice to the relevant buyer who is also a registered participant of Peppol network. The buyer is identified by the buyer's Peppol participant ID available in the UBL invoice. 4. SAP Business Network uses SAP Document and Reporting Compliance as the Access Point to receive the invoice from Peppol network. SAP Document and Reporting Compliance routes the UBL invoice to CIG, and CIG converts the UBL to cXML format.  Note Incase of Japan, SAP Document and Reporting Compliance routes the UBL invoice to SAP Business Network through the SAP Open Application Programming Interface (API) called externaltaxdocservice. This API allows buyers to receive the external tax documents directly in SAP Business Network from supplier's backend system or third-party application or SAP partners like Document Reporting and Compliance. 5. Buyer receives the invoice in cXML format and the UBL invoice as an attachment. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Peppol Integration for SAP Business Network PUBLIC 357  Note The workflow of an invoice from Peppol network to SAP Business Network remains the same if the supplier is a user of SAP Business Network. Buyer Tasks Tasks that a buyer must perform to work with Peppol. 1. Set up the connection between SAP Business Network and SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition. For more information, see Setting Up Connectivity. 2. Configure the same Peppol participant details on SAP Business Network. Enter other information such as, Network Type, Country/Region, and so on. This enables you to receive invoices. • Configuring Peppol Participant Details to Receive an Invoice [page 358]  Note Ensure that the information added in SAP Business Network is the same as entered in SAP Document and Reporting Compliance. You can also modify and delete your peppol profile details configured on SAP Business Network . • • Modifying Peppol Profile Configuration [page 359] Deleting a Peppol Profile Details [page 360] 3. Add the supplier master data in the vendor upload template. This enables the SAP Business Network system to identify the supplier and map the Peppol invoice to the relevant buyer. • Uploading Supplier Master Data [page 360] 4. View the invoice received from the Peppol network. • Viewing an Invoice Received from Peppol Network [page 362] Configuring Peppol Participant Details to Receive an Invoice Learn to configure Peppol participant details to receive an invoice in SAP Business Network and view your external network details. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Navigate to 358 PUBLIC Administration Configuration Configure External Network Identifiers . SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Peppol Integration for SAP Business Network The Configure External Network Identifiers page appears. 3. Choose Create. The Create Configuration screen appears. 4. Select the Network Type as Peppol. 5. Enter your company name in the Company Name field. 6. Select the Country/Region, Scheme Type, and System ID.  Note The list items in the System ID dropdown list is populated when you configure multi-ERP systems on Configure Business Application IDs page in SAP Business Network. 7. Enter the Peppol participant ID (uppercase only) in the Network Identifier field.  Note Ensure that the supplier also maintains the buyer Peppol Participant ID in uppercase only in the incoming invoice. 8. Choose Save. Results The Configure External Network Identifiers page displays the configured details. The External Identifier is used as an identifier to map the invoice coming from Peppol to the buyer in SAP Business Network. Modifying Peppol Profile Configuration Learn to edit your Peppol profile details in SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Navigate to Administration Configuration Configure External Network Identifiers . The Configure External Network Identifiers page appears. 3. On the Configure External Network Identifiers page, for the required profile, choose Action Edit . The Edit Configuration screen appears. 4. Edit the required fields.  Note You cannot edit the Network Type, Country/Region and Scheme Type dropdown lists. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Peppol Integration for SAP Business Network PUBLIC 359 5. Choose Save to save your changes. Deleting a Peppol Profile Details Learn to delete a your Peppol profile details in SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Navigate to Administration Configuration Configure External Network Identifiers . The Configure External Network Identifiers page appears. 3. On the Configure External Network Identifiers page, for the required profile, choose Action Delete . A confirmation message appears. 4. Choose Yes to delete the profile. Results The peppol profile is deleted from Peppol network and SAP Business Network's configuration. You will not be able to receive any invoices from suppliers on Peppol network. Uploading Supplier Master Data Learn how to upload supplier master data to receive invoices from Peppol network. Context Supplier master data upload activity enables SAP Business Network to map the supplier Peppol participant ID to the correct vendor ID in SAP Business Network when the Peppol invoice is routed through SAP Business Network.  Note If the supplier is a user of SAP Business Network, then mention the supplier's Ariba Network ID in the vendor upload template. 360 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Peppol Integration for SAP Business Network

file://SBN/split/SAP Business Network Gu.content: Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Choose Supplier Enablement Upload Vendors . The Upload Vendors page appears. 3. In the Upload File section, choose Download latest template version The Upload_Vendor_Template.csv file is dowloaded to your local system. 4. Enter the required supplier master data in the downloded template. 5. In the External Network Type field, enter PEPPOL as the external network provider. 6. In the Partner Scheme Type field, enter the scheme type for the external network. For example, DE:VAT. The table below describes the country and its supported partner scheme types. Country Partner Scheme Type Germany DE:VAT DE:LWID Australia AU:ABN New Zealand GLN Norway NO:ORG Belgium BE:VAT BE:EN Netherlands NL:KVK NL:OINO NL:VAT 7. In the Partner Identifier field, enter the supplier's Peppol participant ID in uppercase only.  Note Ensure that the supplier also maintains the Peppol participant ID in uppercase only in the incoming invoice. 8. Choose Upload. The uploaded supplier details are available under the Upload Details section. 9. Choose Done. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Peppol Integration for SAP Business Network PUBLIC 361 Viewing an Invoice Received from Peppol Network Buyers learn to view the invoice sent from Peppol network. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Select Invoices Invoices . A list of all the received invoices are displayed. 3. Select the required invoice to view it. 4. Scroll down to the Attachment(s) section to view the attachments sent by the supplier.  Note PeppolUBL.xml is the invoice sent by the supplier among the other attachments such as PDF. Setting Up Peppol connectivity with SAP Business Network for Japan Context This topic describes the over all procedure to setup Peppol connectivity with SAP Business Network for Japan. Procedure 1. Get the credentials to access the SAP API externaldocservice a. Open the SAP Ariba developer portal to create an account in the portal to access the SAP APIs. Your organization’s SAP Ariba administrator can create this request. b. In the SAP Ariba developer portal, choose the externaldocservice API. c. Follow the steps as given in the guide Steps to Start Using the SAP Ariba APIs. 2. Setup SAP Business Network connectivity with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance. Use the credentials generated in step 1 and follow the steps as given in the topic Setting Up Connectivity (Relevant Only for Japan). 3. Register your participant ID in the Peppol Access Point. a. Create a Peppol participant for your company. See Integrating Peppol Exchange with SAP Business Network. You can contact your administrator to help set up a Peppol participant for your company. b. Enable your company to receive electronic documents in the Peppol network. See Registering Your Company to Receive Electronic Documents in the Peppol Network. 362 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Peppol Integration for SAP Business Network 4. Maintain the Peppol participant ID in your SAP Business Network buyer account. a. Configure the Peppol participant details in SAP Business Network. See Configuring Peppol Participant Details to Receive an Invoice [page 358]. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Peppol Integration for SAP Business Network PUBLIC 363 Externaldocservice Open API for SAP Business Network  Restriction With the upcoming transition to SAP Business Network on BTP, we will be introducing a more streamlined and standardized process to use this feature. The current functionality will evolve to support the canonical UBL format to ensure a consistent and harmonized approach globally. Suppliers must ensure that the country-specific format is converted to a canonical UBL format before sending it to the buyer in SAP Business Network. We appreciate your patience and will share the updates when they are available. The externaltaxdocservice is an open Application Programming Interface (API) designed for SAP Business Network to provide a secure, standardized way to post external tax documents to SAP Business Network. This API serves as an additional inbound channel within SAP Business Network, complementing existing methods such as email and manual upload. This feature supports the following types of external documents for the respective countries: • • • • FA xml - Poland DTE xml - Chile CFDI xml - Mexico NFe, CTe, CCe xmls - Brazil The endpoint of the externaltaxdocservice API uses the Post method and expects a multipart request to send the tax document to SAP Business Network. Method Endpoint Description POST {{runtime_URL}}/v1/taxdocument Entry point for accepting external legal tax documents. The endpoint v1/taxdocument is a part of the "externaltaxdocservice" rest service. The runtime URL varies based on your data center. Replace {{runtime_URL}} with the desired runtime URL from the Environment details table on the SAP Ariba developer portal discovery page for this API. When the tax document is successfully accepted at SAP Business Network, the endpoint sends a response as a message. 202 "Accepted" In case of an error, the endpoint sends a response as a message to the backend system/third-party application/ SAP partner. The code below displays an example of the error response. 400 { 364 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Externaldocservice Open API for SAP Business Network "errors": [ "Document processing failure. No matching customer was found on the Ariba Network. Correct the customer information and resend the document." ], "errorId": "11032" } The error can be caused due to the following reasons: Error HTTP Response Error codes Bad request 400 Unauthorized 401 Forbidden 403 Internal Server Error 500 Prerequisites • To create an application and request access to use the SAP Ariba APIs relevant to this feature, you must have access to the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. For details refer to Steps to Start Using the SAP Ariba APIs in Help for the SAP Ariba Developer Portal. • All queries made to this API must be authenticated using OAuth authentication. For details refer to SAP Ariba Developer Portal Authentication in Help for the SAP Ariba Developer Portal.  Note Ensure that you use OAuth version 2.0 for authentication. • Buyers must configure the client ID in the SAP Business Network buyer account. For more information, see Buyer Configuration [page 367].  Note For some countries, the relevant country-specific add-on might be required. This may involve activation and additional licensing costs. Buyers are recommended to confirm entitlements and pricing with your SAP account representative before using this feature with the suppliers. Configuration of the externaltaxdocservice API The Multipart/formdata request of the externaltaxdocservice API contains two parts: • First part - JSON definition Type JSON Name json SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Externaldocservice Open API for SAP Business Network PUBLIC 365 Required True When you define the JSON part of the request to integrate the externaltaxdocservice API in your third-party system / backend system, update the JSON input parameters with the following information: JSON Element Type Required Description Validation additionalInfo String Optional Important note regarding the tax document NA documentName String Mandatory Name of the tax document Legal document (XML) name should match with the name of the attached countryspecific document documentType String Mandatory The following Only valid document type for specific country is allowed document types are supported: • NFe , CTe, CCe (Brazil) • CFDI33 and CFDI40 (Mexico) • • environment String Mandatory DTE (Chile) FA_VAT (Poland) Supports the following Only supported values values: are allowed and it is case sensitive • TEST • PRODUCTION issuerCountryCo de String Mandatory ISO Alpha-2 country code Only valid ISO country code is allowed receiverCountry Code String Optional ISO Alpha-2 country code Only valid ISO country code is allowed Here is an example of a JSON code.  Sample Code { "issuerCountryCode": "MX", "environment": "TEST", "documentType": "CFDI", "additionalInfo": "The tax document has been validated according to the local regulations", "documentName": "tr_pay_rcpt_2.xml" } • Second part - File attachment Type 366 PUBLIC Binary SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Externaldocservice Open API for SAP Business Network Name file Required True. At least one file attachment of the legal tax document. Additionally, you can send a PDF attachment. Maximum size of each file attachment is 10MB. You must attach the country-specific tax document with the same name that you define in the JSON part of the request as mentioned in the element documentName. Additionally, you must add the following HTTP header in your backend system. HTTP Header Name Value X-ARIBA-NETWORK-ID Enter your SAP Business Network ID Buyer Configuration Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network buyer account. 2. Go to Manage Profile API Client ID Configuration Add Updated Client ID . 3. Copy the OAuth ID from the SAP Ariba Developer Portal and paste the ID in the Client ID field. 4. Choose Save. SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Externaldocservice Open API for SAP Business Network PUBLIC 367 Integration with SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition You want to understand the process and tasks involved when integrating SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition with SAP Business Network to receive external invoices. Here's some information on where and how to start. SAP Business Network supports integration of SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition for inbound flow of invoices. This enables buyers to receive external invoices from suppliers that are generated outside of SAP Business Network. SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition retrieves invoices from the country/region-specific tax authority portal. Currently, the integration is supported for countries like Poland and Romania. Prerequisite: • • An enterprise global account on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP). A subscription to SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition. The graphic below describes the over all process flow and the sequence of tasks that must be performed in the tax portal, SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition, and SAP Business Network. 368 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Integration with SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Integration with SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition PUBLIC 369 • • • • • • • #unique_416/unique_416_Connect_42_subsection-im1 [page 370] #unique_416/unique_416_Connect_42_subsection-im2 [page 370] #unique_416/unique_416_Connect_42_subsection-im3 [page 370] #unique_416/unique_416_Connect_42_subsection-im4 [page 370] #unique_416/unique_416_Connect_42_subsection-im5 [page 370] #unique_416/unique_416_Connect_42_subsection-im6 [page 371] #unique_416/unique_416_Connect_42_subsection-im7 [page 370] Generate Credentials for Authentication in the Tax Authority Portal You need to generate credentials for authentication from your country/region-specific tax authority portal. This parameter is required while configuring SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition. For more information, see: • • Generating an Authorization Token in the Test Environment in Poland’s KSeF Portal Generating an Authorization Token in Romania’s ANAF Portal Using Postman . . Set Up Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition You need to perform few tasks in SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition. Configure External Document Service You need to configure external document service in SAP Business Network to establish connection with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition to start receiving external invoices. For more information, see: • • Configuring external document service for Romania [page 330] Configuring external document service for Poland [page 317] Initial Set Up To use SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition with other applications, you perform several tasks on SAP BTP. You can either use the booster to perform the tasks automatically or you can perform all steps manually. For more information, see Initial Setup. Activate Country/Region-Specific Process To enable a specific business scenario for the SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition, you first activate the relevant process. When it is active, the cloud edition enables the relevant configuration options. For more information, see Activating Process. Create a Service Binding You specify client credentials required to enable your SAP Business Network system to communicate with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition, using OAuth 2.0 client authentication. For more information, see Creating Service Bindings Using OAuth 2.0 Client Authentication. Get Credentials for oAuth After creating the client credentials required for the communication between your SAP Business Network system and SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition, you find the credentials in the service binding details. You use them to configure the OAuth 2.0 client. 370 PUBLIC SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Integration with SAP Document Reporting and Compliance, cloud edition

Your customers send you collaboration requests to invite you to collaborate on a request for products or services. This guide applies to: • SAP Business Network Related Guides Introduction to SAP Business Network Collaborating with Customers Collaborating with Customers PUBLIC 3 About Collaborating with Customers Your customers send you collaboration requests to invite you to collaborate on a request for products or services.  Example You and your customer collaborate to find, evaluate, and hire temporary labor or to determine the printing specifications for a marketing brochure. In addition to service line items, collaboration requests can contain products and fees for services.  Example A request for a database administrator contains a material line item for a new-hire kit that includes a computer, a phone, and office supplies, and it also contains a fee line item for a background check. During the collaboration process, customers send summary information about collaboration requests to your online inbox on SAP Business Network. You then view collaboration requests [page 5] and assign collaboration requests [page 9] in your online inbox, and you access your customer’s procurement site to view summary information, collaboration proposals, and history information and participate in the collaboration process [page 10]. SAP Business Network shows the document status for collaboration requests to reflect updates made during the collaboration process. Your customer can make changes to a collaboration request after you have already received the final purchase order. 4 PUBLIC Collaborating with Customers About Collaborating with Customers Finding Collaboration Requests and Organizing Results Use this procedure to view your collaboration requests regularly to track activity and troubleshoot errors efficiently. You can scroll through the collaboration requests in your online inbox or search for requests by customer, ID, or date range. Prerequisites You must have the Inbox Access permission to view collaboration requests. You need to have an active relationship with your customers on SAP Business Network.  Limitations If your account is suspended, you can't receive collaboration requests or other incoming documents from your customers. Accounts are suspended if you fail to pay your subscription fees. Context You can create a filtered list that shows only those collaboration requests meeting various criteria you specify. You can also customize the way SAP Business Network sorts and displays your search results. Procedure 1. Do one of the following • From the search bar on the Home tab, choose Collaboration Requests, optionally choose a specific customer and whether you want to exact or partial search, and enter a request number.  Note Request numbers are case-sensitive, so CLR123 is not the same as clr123. • Click Opportunities Collaboration Requests to view all collaboration requests. 2. If you don't see the collaboration request you're looking for, use the search filters to refine your search: • Choose a customer, date range, or collaboration request status from the dropdowns.  Note The maximum date range is 31 days. Collaborating with Customers Finding Collaboration Requests and Organizing Results PUBLIC 5 • • • Enter a particular collaboration request number. Use the Assigned To search filter to search for collaboration requests assigned to a particular user. Choose the number of results to show.  Tip If you're looking for an updated version of a collaboration request, such as one that contains "V2" in the request number, you need to access the associated purchase order to find the changed collaboration request. To view a changed collaboration request: 1. Click the Inbox tab, and then click Collaboration Requests in the navigation bar. 2. From the list of collaboration requests, find the previous version of the collaboration request. 3. Click the corresponding link in the Purchase Order column. 4. Scroll down to the bottom of the page, and go to the Change Order Requests section. 5. Click the Request# link to view the changed collaboration request. 3. Click Search. 4. After you run the search, click any column heading link in the collaboration request display table to sort the table by that column. If you want to undo your search and start again, you have the following options: • • Click Reset, which blanks out all search filters except date range. Click the Inbox tab and navigate to the Collaboration Requests section again to view the results for the default date range. 5. To change the column display and groupings, click the table options menu icon ( • • ) at the top of the table. In the Show / Hide Columns section, click the columns you want to show or hide. In the Group by Column section, choose how you want to group the results. Use the Grouping Expansion toggle to control your initial display. If you group your results you can then use the expansion triangle to expand or collapse the display per grouping. 6. Click a link in the Request # column to view the collaboration request in your customer's procurement application. 7. Click Search. 8. In the Inbox, click a link in the Request # column to view details. Next Steps Assign the collaboration request [page 9] to a user in your company's account. Review and respond to the collaboration request [page 10] in your customer's procurement application. 6 PUBLIC Collaborating with Customers Finding Collaboration Requests and Organizing Results Collaboration Request Statuses The collaboration request document status lets you know where a collaboration request is in the process. The final status is Some Proposals Accepted and Request Closed or Request Closed. Status Description Search Filter Option Awaiting Response from Buyer Your customer is considering the proposal. Response Needed Awaiting Response from Supplier for Some Requests Your customer sent additional requests and is awaiting your response. Response Needed Buyer Response Required for Some Proposals You created alternate proposals. Your customer is considering your alternate proposals. Response Needed  Note You can create alternate proposals only for those items that are defined to allow alternate proposals. Proposal Rejected by Buyer Your customer rejected the proposal. You can make a new proposal. Response Needed Request Received - Supplier Response Required A new collaboration request is in your Inbox. Your customer is awaiting your response. Response Needed Some Proposals Withdrawn by Supplier You withdrew some proposals. Response Needed Some Proposals Rejected by Buyer Your customer rejected some proposals. Response Needed Request Sent - Waiting for Supplier to Enable Response Needed Your customer is waiting for you to register on SAP Business Network and accept the terms and conditions by using the collaboration request email invitation you received. Request Sent - Waiting for Response You have registered on SAP Business Network through the collaboration request invitation. Your customer is waiting for you to respond to the request. Response Needed Proposal Accepted and Request Closed Your customer accepted the proposal and closed the request. Collaboration Accepted Proposal Accepted by Buyer Your customer accepted the proposal. Collaboration Accepted Proposal Partially Accepted by Buyer Your customer accepted one or more items in the proposal. Collaboration Accepted Some Proposals Accepted and Request Closed Your customer accepted some proposals and closed the request. Collaboration Accepted Some Proposals Accepted by Buyer Your customer accepted some proposals. Collaboration Accepted Proposal Withdrawn by Supplier You withdrew the proposal. Collaboration End Request Canceled by Buyer Your customer canceled the request. No further action is allowed. Collaboration End Request Closed The request is closed. No further action is allowed. Collaboration End Request Declined by Supplier You declined to collaborate on the request. Collaboration End Request Expired The request has expired. No further action is allowed. Collaboration End Collaborating with Customers Finding Collaboration Requests and Organizing Results PUBLIC 7 Status Description Search Filter Option Request Routing An error occurred while routing your response. Contact your customer for further action. Collaboration End Some Proposals Closed Some proposals are closed. Collaboration End Some Proposals Declined by Supplier You declined some proposals. Collaboration End Collaboration Request Notifications You receive collaboration request email notifications in the following situation: Event Recipient Your account receives a new collaboration request Email addresses listed in the Notifications Company Settings Network section. A collaboration request is assigned to you Email address listed in the Account Information section. Click your name in the upper right corner, and then choose My Account to update this email address. One of your collaboration requests is updated Assigned request: Email address listed in the Account Information section. Click your name in the upper right corner, and then choose My Account to update this email address. Unassigned request: Email addresses listed in the Settings 8 PUBLIC Network Notifications Company section. Collaborating with Customers Finding Collaboration Requests and Organizing Results Assigning a Collaboration Request Use this procedure to view and assign collaboration requests to users in your company's account. Prerequisites You must have the Inbox Access permission to view collaboration requests. You must be the account administrator to assign collaboration requests to users. Procedure 1. Click Opportunities Collaboration Requests 2. Check the box for each request that you want to assign to a single user. 3. Choose the user in the Assign To dropdown.  Note You can assign collaboration requests to users who have the Collaboration Request Access permission. If a user doesn't show up in the list, you need to assign this permission to their user account. 4. Click Assign. Results Users receive an email notification when a collaboration request is assigned to them. Collaborating with Customers Assigning a Collaboration Request PUBLIC 9 Reviewing and Responding to a Collaboration Request Use this procedure to review collaboration requests and respond with proposals, send messages to customers, decline requests, or change proposals. Prerequisites You must have the Inbox Access permission to view collaboration requests. Context When you open a collaboration request, SAP Business Network passes your authenticated credentials to your customer’s procurement site. When you punch in to your customer's procurement site for the first time to access collaboration requests, you see the following error: Cannot access customer's site. Your buying organization must approve your access to their system before you proceed with this action. Please try again later. This error occurs only when your customer hasn't yet approved your access to their procurement site. Contact your customer to request access. You can participate in the collaboration process in the procurement site and then return to your SAP Business Network account. If your session on SAP Business Network has timed out before you return, sign in to to your account again. Procedure 1. Click Opportunities Collaboration Requests 2. From the list of collaboration requests, click a link in the Request # column for the collaboration request you want to review. You are taken to your customer's procurement application to review and respond to the collaboration request. 3. Do one of the following: 10 PUBLIC Collaborating with Customers Reviewing and Responding to a Collaboration Request

After you choose Respond with Proposal, take the following actions: 1. Click Included > View Details for a more detailed look at the request. Click OK when finished. 2. Click Included > Edit to update any of the details in your proposal. 3. To submit a candidate in response to a request to fill a job opening, click Add in the Candidates section, enter candidate information on the Contractor Candidate Details page, and then click OK. Click Add again to add additional candidates. 4. Click Next. 5. Enter any message that you want to include, or add any attachments. 6. Click Submit.  Note At any point during the response process, you can save or delete your proposal by clicking Exit and choosing the desired option. Respond > Send Message Enter the subject and the message, and then click Send. Respond > Decline Request Select a reason for declining the request, and then click OK. Respond > Revise Proposal Edit the proposal, and then click Submit. Respond > Withdraw Proposal Enter a reason for withdrawing the proposal, and then click OK. Back Before you respond to a collaboration request, you can click the Back link in the lower left corner to return to your SAP Business Network account. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 72 4 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Content Configuring Document Routing This guide is for SAP Ariba administrators responsible for configuring, testing, and maintaining the connection between SAP Business Network and a supplier's business for the purpose of routing business documents. SAP Business Network can send and receive different types of business documents through multiple channels. It also supports payment through AribaPay, allows you to specify a detailed business profile, and manage the queue of documents awaiting transmission. This guide applies to: • • • SAP Business Network SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network Discovery Related Guides Introduction to SAP Business Network Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network How to Guide for Suppliers cXML Solutions Guide Configuring Document Routing Configuring Document Routing PUBLIC 5 Electronic Order Routing Introduction to Routing Orders and Releases [page 6] About Selecting an Order Routing Method [page 7] Online Order Routing [page 8] Email Order Routing [page 9] Fax Order Routing [page 11] cXML Order Routing [page 12] cXML Pending Queue Routing [page 13] EDI Order Routing [page 14] Order Document Types [page 15] Order Document Restrictions [page 20] Configuring Electronic Order Routing [page 22] Order Routing Problems [page 30] Introduction to Routing Orders and Releases Orders and releases are generated by customer procurement applications and sent electronically to SAP Business Network as cXML documents. SAP Business Network essentially functions as a hub to receive customer order documents and send (route) them to you for review and order processing (fulfillment) using a supported order routing method. You select order and release routing methods when you set up your account, and you can change them anytime afterward. If you change an order routing method, the change takes effect immediately. Buying organizations can view the order routing methods that you configured and can request notification if you change them. SAP Business Network supports the following order routing methods: • • • • • • 6 Online Order Routing [page 8] Email Order Routing [page 9] Fax Order Routing [page 11] cXML Order Routing [page 12] cXML Pending Queue Routing [page 13] EDI Order Routing [page 14] PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing About Selecting an Order Routing Method You can select routing methods for incoming documents if you are the administrator, if you have Transaction Configuration permission, or if you have cXML Configuration permission (only for suppliers using cXML). You can specify order routing methods for incoming documents if your account is either in preview or production mode. When selecting a routing method, consider your infrastructure, technical capabilities, purchase order volume, and order fulfillment systems. You can select different routing methods for different types of order documents. SAP Business Network stores all transactions (including orders and releases) online regardless of routing methods you select. Users can always view transactions by logging on to their user account. Online order routing is the best choice for some suppliers, because it requires only an Internet connection and a supported browser. The most common order routing methods are fax and email, because most suppliers already have a fax machine or email account. Suppliers with advanced order-receiving infrastructures can choose cXML or EDI routing. These methods send electronic documents to suppliers' order receiving systems. They require suppliers to have technical personnel available to set up and maintain their cXML or EDI systems. All routing methods are free, except for EDI routing through a Value Added Network (VAN). VANs typically charge suppliers for membership and a per transaction fee. EDI suppliers can avoid this cost by using EDI over the Internet (AS2 transport). Contact SAP Ariba Support if you want to implement EDI routing using AS2 transport. Additional order routing methods are available if your customer has requested SAP Business Network to provide you with custom routing methods. If you choose a custom routing method, documents are sent through a mapping process to or from cXML. To learn more about custom routing methods, contact your customer. About Testing Routing Methods Testing a selected routing method after initial configuration, after changing routing methods, or when there are substantial changes to existing infrastructure. Test your selected routing method to ensure that your users can read and process purchase orders. To perform testing, sign in to your SAP Business Network test account, upload your customer catalogs to SAP Business Network, and send test purchase orders to yourself using items from those customer catalogs. For example, if a new fax machine becomes available, make sure the telephone lines and the fax machine are working by sending a test purchase order to it. Test purchase orders are maintained in a separate test account so they cannot be confused with production purchase orders. Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing PUBLIC 7 Required Acknowledgments for Fax, cXML, and EDI Routing Methods Fax, cXML, and EDI routing methods require supplier acknowledgments, which are document receipt replies confirming that your backend system received an order or release. Acknowledgments confirm the reliability of document delivery and allow for failure notifications in case a delivery fails. SAP Business Network must receive the required acknowledgment within a specific period of time or it considers routing to have failed. Language Support for Routing Methods Your customers determine the language of the order and release content, such as line item descriptions or comments. Order and release section titles and labels on the user interface are dependant on the routing method you select. Routing Method Language Setting Online Uses user’s web browser language setting. If language is not supported, user interface titles, messages and field names are displayed in English. Fax and email Configured in your SAP Business Network account. If you are the account administrator, then the preferred language setting also controls the section headings and field labels on orders and releases routed through Email or Fax. cXML and EDI Determined by your order-receiving systems Online Order Routing Online order routing is the default order routing method. A buying organization sends all incoming documents, such as orders, releases, payments, and notifications, over the Internet to the SAP Business Network, where they are visible in the appropriate menu in the supplier portal. If you do not see documents received from buying organizations in the supplier portal, either you do not have any customer relationships in your account or your account administrator did not grant you the necessary permission. There are no acknowledgments or retries for online orders and releases. Your customer’s procurement system and the SAP Business Network ensure that all orders and releases are routed online to your SAP Business Network account. 8 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing Email Order Routing SAP Ariba can use standard Simple Mail Transport Protocol (SMTP) for order routing between buyer and supplier by email. Email routing is similar to online order routing. A buying organization sends all incoming documents, such as orders, releases, payments, and notifications over the Internet the Ariba Network, and Ariba Network forwards the documents to the supplier’s email accounts, You can enter up to five email addresses to route your orders and releases. Each email message contains both a plain-text message and a duplicate message in HTML format. For the best looking results, make sure the recipient uses an HTML-aware email reader. There are no acknowledgments or retries for email orders and releases. If an email purchase order bounces back to SAP Business Network, its status is set to “Failed” in the Comments field.  Caution Email is not considered secure, because it is sent as clear text. However, you can configure SAP Business Network to send just a brief email notification for each purchase order and read the contents of the purchase order in your online account. Allow Email Messages from SAP Ariba If you want to receive orders as email messages and your organization uses software to block unwanted email messages, you need to configure it to allow messages from Ariba Network. The SAP Business Network uses the following address as its From email address. ordersender-prod@ansmtp.ariba.com Setting Auto-Reply Message Text If you will be out of the office you can use your mail client’s auto-reply (“Out of Office” or vacation) feature to respond to orders. Include one of the following phrases in auto-reply messages to prevent SAP Business Network from failing orders and releases sent to mailboxes responding using an auto-reply feature: Out of office OOTO On vacation on holiday Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing PUBLIC 9 out of town away from the office away until out of the country at an off site meeting When SAP Business Network detects an auto-reply containing one of these phrases, it indicates that it received the auto-reply in the order history log and does not fail the order. About Receiving cXML Documents as Email Messages When you configure Email as a routing method, you can select the option Attach cXML document in the email message. This option routes cXML OrderRequest documents as attachments to email change/cancel orders. Use this option to receive cXML orders without having to set up a cXML-enabled website. When you receive the attached cXML OrderRequest documents, you can parse and process them as if they were sent through an HTTP POST transaction. Order Routing to Email Addresses Not Specified by Suppliers Buyers sometimes want to route purchase orders to a direct supplier sales contact within a supplier organization. To allow this, a buyer might have their SAP Ariba Buying or SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing solutions configured to allow buyer-defined email addresses for order routing. In this situation, SAP Business Network receives the purchase order cXML and routes it using the following logic. For private suppliers (those who are not registered on SAP Business Network): • SAP Business Network routes the order email to the buyer-specified email address in the existing "Correspondent" section of the purchase order cXML. The content of the email depends on the buyer’s entitlement. • If the purchase order cXML contains an additional correspondent (directSupplierContact), SAP Business Network also sends an interactive email for the purchase order to this correspondent. This email contains two buttons, Confirm Order and Create Invoice, that the recipient can use to process the order. Regardless of whether the supplier is registered or not with SAP Business Network, this email does not provide links for the recipient to register for an SAP Business Network account or to sign in to an existing account. • If the additional correspondent email address is the same as that for the existing correspondent, then the email is routed only to the existing correspondent using the logic mentioned in the previous bullet point. 10 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing

The content of the email depends on the buyer’s entitlement. • If the purchase order cXML contains an additional correspondent (directSupplierContact), the SAP Business Network also sends the purchase order to that correspondent. This interactive email contains two buttons, Confirm Order and Create Invoice, that the recipient can use to process the order. Regardless of whether the additional supplier is a private or public supplier, the email does not provide links for the recipient to register for an SAP Business Network account or to sign in to an existing account. • If the additional correspondent email address is the same as the one configured by the supplier in their SAP Business Network account, the email is routed to the supplier-specified email addresses.  Note In all cases, if the email fails to be delivered to any of the addresses it is marked as FAILED for all addresses. When a buyer adds an additional correspondent for a purchase order, the following text is included on purchase order emails to let users know that the email will be sent to other users at the supplier organization: "If you or your customer have more than one email address associated with your organization for purchase order delivery, a copy of this purchase order will be sent to the other email addresses." Fax Order Routing You can select fax order routing to have SAP Business Network send orders and releases to your fax machine. The contents of the fax reflect the order sent to your account. With fax order routing, a buying organization sends all incoming documents, such as orders, releases, payments, and notifications over the Internet to SAP Business Network , and SAP Business Network forwards the documents over the Internet to a third-party fax service. The fax service faxes the documents over private telephone lines to the supplier’s fax machine. SAP Business Network sends faxes using the standard Group III fax protocol. It submits fax messages to the fax service provider securely over the Internet through HTTPS using SSL v3.0. SAP Business Network uses two fax service providers: a primary provider and a backup provider. If the SAP Business Network Operations Group detects a systemic problem with the primary provider, it switches SAP Business Network to use the backup provider, so that orders continue to flow. No action is required by SAP Business Network users. Fax telephone numbers must be entered as if you were called from the United States. Each SAP Business Network account can accept only one number, so high-volume suppliers might want to use multiple fax machines connected to multiplexed telephone lines. Alternatively, high-volume suppliers can use Rule-Based Routing. Fax machines acknowledge orders by sending “confirmation of receipt” messages automatically before disconnecting. If your fax machine does not connect or the fax does not go through, SAP Business Network Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing PUBLIC 11 attempts again every hour to fax the order. If the 10th retry fails, SAP Business Network marks the order as “Failed” in its Comments field. Fax Order Routing Configuration Options If you select fax order routing, you can configure your account to receive an optional cover sheet, you may also choose to receive only a brief order notification via fax instead of the full order details. When a fax machine is shared with other groups, suppliers might want to include cover pages. If the machine is dedicated to an order-receiving department, suppliers probably do not need cover pages. When a fax machine is shared among groups suppliers might want to keep order contents private. They can do so by configuring fax order routing to receive a brief order notification rather than full order details. After receiving the fax notification, suppliers must log into their account to view the full order. Fax Routing Restrictions SAP Business Network does not fax orders larger than 1 MB or that have more than 1,000 line items. Fax routing also does not support attachments. When an order exceeds size limits, SAP Business Network indicates so, It can send large orders can be sent by email, cXML, and EDI routing. Orders with attachments are routed without the attachments. SAP Business Network indicates that attachments are visible only online. cXML Order Routing To use the cXML (commerce eXtensible Markup Language) order-routing method, you must implement a website that can initiate and accept XML posts. cXML is an open standard for communicating commerce-related data across the Internet. When you chose cXML order-routing, a buying organization sends all incoming documents, such as orders, releases, payments, and notifications over the Internet to SAP Business Network , and SAP Business Network posts the documents over the Internet to your supplier cXML application on the web. Suppliers must acknowledge cXML orders within five minutes by transmitting an XML response document in the same HTTP session as the order. If your web server is down or if it rejects the cXML post, SAP Business Network retries the post every hour. If the 10th retry fails, SAP Business Network marks the order as “Failed” in its Comments field.  Note SAP Business Network queries cXML applications to find out their supported transactions and their URLs. If you leave the Profile URL field empty when you configure your account, SAP Business Network routes cXML documents to one of the following destinations, in this order: 12 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing • • An end point destination configured for your account For orders: a cXML routing method configured for your account Related Information Configuring an SAP Business Network Account for cXML Routing [page 34] cXML Order Routing Security Considerations If you select cXML order routing, you must provide a secure (HTTPS) URL for your cXML application. HTTPS connections employ Secure Socket Layer (SSL), which requires you to have a Web server digital certificate issued by a trusted Certificate Authority. cXML Pending Queue Routing You can configure your SAP Business Network accounts to retrieve cXML documents in a pending documents queue. To use this method, you must also configure your external ERP system and your SAP Business Network account to use the GetPending/DataDownload transaction method. When you choose the pending queue routing method, a buying organization sends all incoming documents, such as orders, releases, payments, and notifications over the Internet to SAP Business Network. Your cXML application must poll SAP Business Network for pending documents and download them. You configure your SAP Business Network accounts to retrieve cXML documents using the cXML Pending Queue routing method. Using this routing method, your application polls SAP Business Network for the pending documents. You can poll by document type and then download them. Your application then issues a StatusUpdateRequest document to indicate that it received the document. The Pending Queue page lists the pending documents that your application can download from your SAP Business Network account. You must configure your account to specify the authentication method and Profile URL Your supplier application must use the Profile URL request document to obtain the URLs for sending the GetPendingRequest and the DataRequest document. SAP Business Network uses MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) envelopes to send documents with attachments in an HTTP document through this retrieval method. The supplier’s application must decode the MIME envelopes. You can use this routing method to retrieve the following transactions: • • • • New Orders and Releases Changed/Canceled Purchase Orders Blanket Purchase Orders Status Update Requests Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing PUBLIC 13 Related Information cXML Solutions Guide EDI Order Routing You can configure SAP Business Network to send orders and blanket purchase orders as ANSI X12 850, EDIFACT, or OAGIS v9.2 EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) documents using Applicability Statement 2 (AS2) Internet routing, Value Added Network (VAN) routing, or the cloud integration gateway. With EDI order routing using a VAN, a buying organization sends all incoming documents, such as orders, releases, payments, and notifications over the Internet to SAP Business Network (where they are visible in your account), and SAP Business Network sends the documents over the Internet to the VAN. The VAN sends the documents to your supplier EDI mailbox. With EDI order routing using AS2, you purchase AS2 software and set it up on your own web server. Then contact SAP Ariba Support to implement AS2 transport support for EDI routing with SAP Business Network. Then when a buying organization’s documents are received by SAP Business Network, SAP Business Network sends them over the Internet to the EDI mailbox on your server. EDI routing does not support attachments. Orders with attachments are routed without the attachments to your SAP Business Network account. Suppliers that use AS2 routing must make sure their EDI mailboxes are available all the time or purchase orders might fail to route. Your system must acknowledge EDI orders and blanket purchase orders within 72 hours by sending EDI acknowledgements (X12 997 or EDIFACT CONTRL documents); otherwise SAP Business Network marks the order or blanket purchase order as “Failed” in their Comments fields. SAP Business Network does not retry EDI orders and blanket purchase orders. Related Information EDI Configuration Guide EDI Order Routing Configuration Options When you configure EDI order routing, you choose between the EDI standard you want to use, and you select a transport option. There are three EDI standards to choose from: • • • OAGIS v9.2 14 PUBLIC ANSI ASC X12 EDI v004010, most often used in the United States UN EDIFACT version D98A syntax version 3, most often used in Asia and Europe Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing Transport options specify how EDI orders are routed. There are two choices: • • • Value-Added Network (VAN) Applicability Statement 2 (AS2) Cloud integration gateway [page 37] If you choose to use AS2 for transport, you must: • Create a digital certificate for document authentication and security. The certificate acts as both a client certificate for authentication and a server certificate for Secure Sockets Layer (SSL). It can be signed by a public Certificate Authority or it can be self-signed. • • Purchase and maintain AS2 software on your own web server. Contact SAP Ariba Support to configure SAP Business Network to route documents over the Internet to your EDI mailbox. Once set up and configured, AS2 is free to use. If you prefer a ready-made transport option you can choose the VAN option. SAP Business Network sends orders to the Inovis VAN. Inovis can route the order directly to the supplier or to the supplier's own VAN through VAN-to-VAN interconnect. The final routing method is determined by agreement between the VAN and the supplier. In most cases, suppliers use private telephone lines to download waiting orders. VANs typically charge suppliers for membership and per transaction. Order Document Types You can configure order routing methods for new orders, change and cancel orders, and other documents related to orders. New Orders New catalog and non-catalog orders, also called regular purchase orders, are those initially placed by customers. They may include attachments that provide explanatory or supporting order information. New orders include: • • • • • Catalog orders without attachments Catalog orders with attachments Non-catalog orders without attachments Non-catalog orders with attachments Non-catalog orders with manually-entered part numbers Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing PUBLIC 15 Customer Catalog Orders Customer catalog orders are purchase orders where the buyer selects items from your online catalog. Customers can attach external files to purchase orders to provide more information about the order. Attachments can be in any format, such as Word documents, AutoCAD drawings, or Excel spreadsheets. SAP Business Network always stores attachments online. Routed purchase orders indicate that attachments can be viewed online. You can view attachments by logging in to SAP Business Network. Non-Catalog Orders Non-catalog orders are purchase orders containing items not selected from your online catalog. These items are manually entered by the purchasing agent, and often do not have corresponding part numbers. Non-catalog orders might require special validation and processing, so you might want to route these purchase orders to a special department in your organization before shipping them. To detect non-catalog items, SAP Business Network examines incoming orders and looks for either: • • The isAdHoc attribute (in a cXML OrderRequest, an isAdhoc=”yes” attribute) Supplier Part IDs that are blank or set to “not available.” A non-catalog order may contain Supplier Part IDs entered by the purchasing agent. In this case, the order items include the isAdHoc attribute and Supplier Part IDs that are not blank. You can set your configuration to process these orders as if they were regular orders. Change and Cancel Orders Buying organizations can modify previously sent customer catalog and non-catalog purchase orders by sending a subsequent change order. They can also cancel a pending purchase order by sending a cancel order. You might want to configure routing for change or cancel orders so they get immediate attention of your order fulfillment group. Other Electronic Order Routing Document Types Just as you can select purchase order routing methods, you can also configure routing methods for supporting electronic order routing documents, including time sheets, order response documents, and document status updates. On the Electronic Order Routing page, you can configure routing for these additional document types: • • • 16 Blanket Purchase Orders Time Sheets Order Response Documents PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing • • • • • • • Payment Remittances and Payment Proposals Status update requests (Order Status Requests and Document Status Updates) Receipts Product Activity Message, Return Ship Notices, and Component Ship Notice Transport Requests and Transport Confirmations Copy documents (Copy Order, Copy Confirmation, Copy Ship Notice, and Copy Approval) Quality-related documents (Quality Notification Document, Quality Inspection Request, Quality Inspection Decision Request)  Note Available document types depend on your SAP Ariba solutions and your configuration. Time Sheets If you are a supplier of services and intend to receive electronic time sheets from your customers for work completed, you can configure a routing method for time sheets. If you specify cXML as the routing method for time sheets, cXML TimeCardInfoRequest messages are routed to the URL you specify. If you specify Email as the routing method for time sheets. by default, Ariba Network sends only a brief notification containing a hyper link to the time sheet to prevent transmission of unencrypted order content. To include the full time sheet in email, click Include document in the email message. Order Response Documents Order response documents include order confirmation and ship notices. You can select routing methods for these documents. If you do not have an automated order management system that generates cXML or EDI order responses, select Online as the routing method. You can view orders and releases online and use the Create Confirmation and Create Ship Notice buttons to create and send order responses. If you have an automated order management system that can generate and send cXML or EDI order response documents to SAP Business Network, select cXML or EDI as the routing method. The order management system generates and sends order response documents to SAP Business Network. When SAP Business Network receives the order response documents, it applies the information in them to the affected line items. Customers can see updated line item status by logging on to SAP Business Network, by punching out to SAP Business Network from their procurement applications, or by receiving order confirmation or ship notice information automatically to their buying solution from SAP Ariba. Select cXML as the routing method if your order management system sends the following cXML messages: ConfirmationRequest (purchase order confirmation) ShipNoticeRequest (advance ship notice) Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing PUBLIC 17 Select EDI as the routing method if your order management system sends the following ANSI X12 or EDIFACT fulfillment status documents: • • • X12 855 (Purchase Order Acknowledgment) X12 856 (Ship Notice/Manifest) EDIFACT DESADV (Despatch Advice)  Note You cannot update order confirmation status manually if you send order confirmations through cXML or EDI. but you can update shipping status manually using the Create Ship Notice button. Status Update Requests Status Update Request documents contain information about orders, releases, or blanket purchase orders, and the status of invoices and payments. If you specify cXML as the routing method, the cXML StatusUpdateRequest messages are routed to the URL you specify. If you use the cXML Pending Queue routing method, your application sends status update request documents when it receives documents from SAP Business Network. Blanket Purchase Orders If you are a supplier of goods or services and intend to receive blanket purchase orders, you can configure a separate routing method for them. A blanket order is a purchase order that is valid for a specified period of time and authorizes multiple orders during that time period, as long as the total dollars on the PO are not exceeded. Blanket POs limit the types of goods or services that can be ordered, and may also limit the order amounts. Blanket purchase orders may include attachments that provide explanatory or supporting order information. 18 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing Payment Remittances You can specify a separate routing method for payment remittances you receive. Payment remittances are notifications to you from your buyers that they have paid an invoice. Receipts You can specify a routing method for receipts you receive from buyers. Although receipts can have attachments, SAP Business Network doesn’t send them to suppliers. The following routing options can be selected for receipts: • • Online (default)—Receipts are visible in your SAP Business Network account. cXML—Receipts are visible in your SAP Business Network account, and the SAP Business Network posts them to your supplier cXML application on the Web. • Email—Receipts are visible in your SAP Business Network account, and SAP Business Network also routes them to up to five email addresses. • cXML Pending Queue—Receipts are visible in your SAP Business Network account.Your cXML application must poll SAP Business Network for pending documents and download them. • Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway—You receive non-cXML receipts (UN-EDIFACT or ASC-X12) from the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. Receipts are visible in your SAP Business Network account.  Note To send and receive non-cXML transaction documents from SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network, you must set up and enable the SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network on SAP Business Network. Transport Requests and Transport Confirmations If you have a logistics relationship with an SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyer, you can select routing options for transport requests and transport confirmations. The following routing options can be selected for transport requests and transport confirmations: • Online (default)—Transport requests and transport confirmations are visible in the SAP Business Network supplier portal. • cXML—Transport requests and transport confirmations are visible in the SAP Business Network supplier portal, and the SAP Business Network posts them to your supplier cXML application on the Web. Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing PUBLIC 19 Order Document Restrictions Order documents have restrictions depending on document type, size, and age. Maximum Document and Attachment Size Maximum Document Sizes The maximum size of a cXML order, ship notice, order confirmation, or invoice document is 40 MB or 10,000 line items. All other cXML documents are limited to a maximum size of 4 MB or 1,000 line items. These maximums do not include the size of any attachments. The maximum size of an Excel file created by running an Upload/Download job for a planning process job type is 40 MB or 10,000 rows. Maximum Attachment Sizes Attachment maximums are for the combined total size of all attachments to the same document.  Note During attachment upload, original attachment files are converted to plain ASCII text, using base64 encoding. This conversion increases the file size by approximately 35%. Therefore, the actual file size limit is 65% of the configured maximum limit. For example, if the maximum allowed limit is set to 10,000 KB (10 MB), then the actual total attachment file size that users can add is 6,500 KB. If you attempt to upload an attachment that exceeds this limit, SAP Business Network displays an error and doesn’t allow the upload. With the exception of one document type, 10 MB is the default setting for the maximum size of attachments. The highest possible setting is 100 MB. For users enabled for the quality collaboration component under SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, a quality review document has by default a maximum attachment size of 100 MB. The highest possible setting is 200 MB. To change the maximum size of attachments, buyers can ask their Designated Support Contact to log a service request. An SAP Ariba Support representative follows up to make the change. The buyer's maximum attachment size applies to all documents that are sent between that buyer and their suppliers. Size Limits in the SAP Business Network User Interface The SAP Business Network user interface doesn't display a document that is larger than 1 MB (or 2 MB for buyers and suppliers enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain) or that has more than 1,000 line items. 20 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing

Order Routing Problems Each time the status of a order changes, SAP Business Network logs the change. If you encounter order routing problems you can view the order history to help troubleshoot the problem. The following table describes common reasons for order failures based on the order routing method, and offers possible solutions for those problems. Routing Method Problem Solution Fax Your fax machine might not be turned on or responding, or you might have provided the wrong fax number. Turn on your fax machine and resend the order from SAP Business Network. See Resending Failed Orders [page 32]. SAP Business Network is sending orders to the wrong fax Make sure the telephone number of your machine in your company. fax machine is the same one entered into your SAP Business Network account. 30 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Electronic Order Routing
