file://SBN/split/Configuring Document Ro.content: Routing Method Problem Solution Email Your mailbox might have sent an auto-response that caused the order failure. SAP Business Network scans auto-responses and attachments for phrases that indicate the recipient is away. If one of these phrases is found, SAP Business Network does not fail the purchase order. Instead it logs the auto-response in the order history log. To prevent order failure, ensure that your email auto-response contains one of these phrases: Your email system incorrectly interprets the email as spam and rejects it, or stores it in a spam folder. • • • • • • • • • Out of office OOTO On vacation On holiday Out of town Away from the office Away until Out of the country At an off site meeting If your organization uses software to block the receipt of unwanted email messages, configure it to allow messages from SAP Business Network’s email address: ordersender- prod@ansmtp.ariba.com cXML Check your responses. You did not respond within the time out limit, you did not return a valid cXML Response document, or you returned a cXML Response document with a status code indicating failure. If SAP Business Network receives a 4xx status code, the order fails immediately since this code indicates a fatal error. SAP Business Network does not retry the order. If there is no response from the supplier or SAP Business Network receives a 5xx status code, then SAP Business Network tries resending the order up to 20 times, roughly once every half an hour, before failing the order. EDI You did not send back a Functional Acknowledgment (FA) within 72 hours of receipt of a purchase order, as required by the EDI protocol. If the FA is not received within this timeframe, the order fails. The order history log indicates why the order failed. Alternatively, the FA from the supplier might not contain a document level acknowledgment. You must generate transaction-level, not group-level functional acknowledgments. Make sure your ANSI X12 997 FA contains an AK2/AK5 segment for each document in the functional group. If you use EDIFACT, the CONTRL FAs must contain a UCM segment for each document in the interchange. An EDI order can also fail due to any translation error encountered while processing the EDI document. Order numbers are case-sensitive, so DO123 is not the same as do123. Date The date on which SAP Business Network received the order. By default, the report includes today’s date and the preceding 14 days. 4. Click Search to look for failed orders. 5. Do one of the following: • • 32 Select one or more failed orders and click Resend. Click Resend All. Orders marked for resending are put into a queue, and are sent in the background. Check your account after several minutes to verify the current status of the orders you resent. Even if you accept cXML or EDI invoices, you can also generate invoices online as needed. Prerequisites To specify the routing method for outgoing documents, such as invoices, your account must be in production mode. Context You can generate invoices manually in the SAP Business Network user interface or programmatically receive electronic invoices that your users generate in an external ERP system for distribution to your customers on the SAP Business Network. Electronic invoices can be enabled using either the cXML or EDI routing methods. When SAP Business Network receives invoices, it creates an online invoice visible to both you and your customer. Your customers can configure SAP Business Network to route invoices to their procurement applications for reconciliation and payment. Procedure 1. In the right corner of the header bar, click the Account Settings icon and choose Settings Electronic Invoice Routing . Configuring Document Routing Invoice Routing and Archiving PUBLIC 47 2. Selecting a Routing Method for Customer Invoices You can choose how to route self-billing invoices sent to you from customers based on an agreement made outside SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. In the right corner of the header bar, click the Account Settings icon and choose Settings Electronic Invoice Routing . 2. For the Customer Invoices option, choose one of the following values from the dropdown: • • • Online—enables routing of customer invoices to your SAP Business Network account. cXML—enables acceptance of cXML InvoiceDetailRequest documents sent from customers. Enter the https URL of your website. Email—enables routing of customer invoices by email. Enter up to five email addresses separated by commas. 3. If you chose the Email option, configure these optional settings: • Attach cXML document in the email message—Check this option to attach a cXML version of the customer’s self-billing invoice to the email message. • Include document in the email message—Check this option to include the customer’s self-billing invoice in the email message. 4. Click Save. About Archiving Invoices You can configure SAP Business Network to archive your invoices in zip format and store them for three months. You specify an archiving frequency interval that SAP Business Network uses to queue invoices for archiving. 30 days after queuing invoices, SAP Business Network archives them. The archiving frequency interval determines how often SAP Business Network queues recent invoices for archiving. You can specify a weekly, biweekly, or monthly frequency. When the specified interval is complete, SAP Business 48 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Invoice Routing and Archiving Network queues invoices for archiving 30 days later. The 30-day waiting period is designed to accommodate the completion of a typical invoice cycle. If you want SAP Business Network to archive invoices immediately at the end of each archiving frequency interval, you can override the default 30-day waiting period when you configure invoice archiving. You can download archived invoices from the Archived Invoices page or configure SAP Business Network to send archived invoices to the pending queue, or automatically deliver them via HTTPS as soon as they are available. The Archived Invoices page is available only after you configure and start invoice archiving.  Note Users must have the Archive Access permission to view archived invoices. Invoice Archive Zip File Contents An invoice archive zip file contains both invoice information and meta attributes for easy data retrieval. Invoice information includes: • • • • • Raw invoice data in cXML format A human-readable copy of the invoice A copy of the invoice in PDF format if your account is enabled for PDF invoices A log text/history file that includes key Ariba Network invoice processing dates such as signing and verification-related events, start of processing at the receiver side, and approval and payment status Any related file attachments Zip file meta attributes allow easy retrieval of stored/archived invoices and provide the following data: • • • • • Invoice or credit memo date Buyer AN-ID / Supplier AN-ID (for supplier download) Invoice or credit memo number Copy of CCs or invoice conversion “From” and “To” countries or regions if the credit memo or invoice has been digitally signed Automatic Archived Invoice Delivery When you configure invoice archiving, you can enable automatic delivery of archived zip files as soon as they are available. You can specify your own archiving solution on a web server you pre-configure, specify a separate e-archival provider, or specify an SAP Ariba partner service. Before enabling automatic delivery of archived invoices, the following steps should be taken: • • • Your buyers must enable you to submit online invoices. You must configure and subsequently maintain a web-server to receive the archived invoice files. You must be able to extract the archive file from the data portion of the HTTP post request that contains the archived invoice file, Configuring Document Routing Invoice Routing and Archiving PUBLIC 49 • You must be able to store the archived on your file system. To enable automatic delivery of archived invoice files, you specify an HTTPS-prefixed URL to which SAP Business Network posts the file. SAP Business Network uses HTTPS POST to deliver invoice archives. You can authenticate an HTTPS post request based on the client certificate available for SAP Business Network. For a list of certificate authorities trusted by SAP Business Network, see the cXML Solutions Guide.  Note Even if your organization enables automatic delivery of archived invoice files, SAP Business Network continues to store them for three months in your account. You can view automatic delivery information in the Delivery Status and Delivery Date columns on the Archive Invoices page. If a delivery attempt of an archive fails, then SAP Business Network sends you an email notification explaining the failure. As an alternative, you can check the status in the Delivery Failure Reason column of the Archived Invoices page.  Note SAP Ariba Support assistance is required for those organizations that need to include old invoices (created prior to AN49) in automatically delivered ZIP files. Download Archived Invoice Files from the Pending Queue You can choose to automatically send archived invoice files to the pending queue, facilitating secure download. If archived invoice files are sent to the pending queue, you can download them over an HTTPS connection from your external ERP system to the SAP Business Network using a GetPendingRequest and DataRequest pair. Only one archived invoice file can be downloaded per GetPendingRequest and DataRequest pair. When using a GetPendingRequest to query for archived invoice files in the pending queue, you must set the maxMessages value to 1 to prevent failure in the case of excessive attachment sizes. If you choose to send archived invoices to the pending queue, you cannot also have archived invoice files automatically delivered via HTTPS. Example GetPendingRequest for Archived Invoice Files <GetPendingRequest lastReceivedTimestamp="2015-02-13T16:00:00-08:00" maxMessages="1"> <MessageType>InvoiceArchive</MessageType> </GetPendingRequest> For additional information about archived invoices and the pending queue, see the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide. 50 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Invoice Routing and Archiving

file://SBN/split/Configuring Document Ro.content: Configuring Invoice Archiving Configuring invoice archiving allows you to specify the frequency, immediacy, and delivery of zipped invoice archives. Click how often you want SAP Business Network to automatically archive your invoices: • • • Weekly Biweekly Monthly  Note If you choose any of the options, SAP Business Network collects invoices for one month before posting the first archive in Invoices Archived Invoices , so that any invoices that arrive just before the first period starts can be included in the first archive. 4. Click Save Delivery Option. Next Steps You can return to the Invoice Archival section to change automatic archiving frequency at any time. Click the desired invoice archival frequency and click Update Frequency To stop SAP Business Network from automatically archiving your invoices, click Stop. You can also check the Invoice Archival section to see when the next archive file will be available. In the right corner of the header bar, click the Account Settings icon and choose Settings Electronic Order Routing . 2. Choose one of the following the routing methods for payment proposals and remittances in the Other Document Types section: Method Required Values Optional Values Notes Online None None Choose this method to receive payment remittances in your SAP Business Network account. cXML The https URL of your website. SAP Business Network does not display this URL to customers or other suppliers. None Choose this method to receive payment remittances through cXML. See cXML and EDI Routing Options [page 33]. 54 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Payment Routing Method Required Values Optional Values Notes Email Enter the email address of your Internet mailbox. Attach cXML document in the email message To ensure that someone in your Include document in the email Choose this method to receive payment remittances through email. company has access to payment message remittances when the primary order receiver is absent, provide an email alias. EDI Click the Click here... link to set configuration options. None Choose this method to receive payment remittances through EDI. Until Ariba activates EDI order routing for your account, you receive orders on SAP Business Network. See cXML and EDI Routing Options [page 33] cXML Pending Queue None None Choose this method to send payment documents to the cXML Pending Queue. See the cXML Solutions Guide.  Note Routing options for payment proposals are limited to Online and cXML Pending Queue. Remittance Addresses and Preferred Payment Methods for Non-AribaPay Payments Your customers use your remittance addresses to send payment electronically and by mail. You can specify multiple remittance addresses and payment method preferences. SAP Business Network shows your remittance address information under “Remit To” on generated invoices and in your company profile, which is visible to customers.  Note The remittance addresses you specify in Ariba Network do not apply to AribaPay payments. AribaPay payments use the remittance address associated with your AribaPay Merchant ID. For additional information about AribaPay, see Activating and Managing AribaPay [page 60]. Some customers may require you to include bank account details on invoices. If required, SAP Business Network automatically includes your Bank Account Number and Bank ID values on invoices. customers can further require IBAN on invoices if you are based in a country or region that uses IBAN. Configuring Document Routing Payment Routing PUBLIC 55  Note If your customer requires bank details on invoices but you haven't added bank information to your remittance address, you'll receive an error message on the invoice. Below the error on the invoice you're creating, you can click Add bank accounts details to configure your remittance address with bank information. After you add bank information, you are returned to the invoice entry page and can submit the invoice to your customer. If you don't have permission to update remittance information, you'll see a link to contact your account administrator. In North America if your customers invite you to use it, you can facilitate payment receipt by including ACH or wire transfer information in your SAP Business Network account. SAP Business Network includes this information on invoices you generate. About EFT Payments EFT stands for Electronic Funds Transfer. EFT payments involve the removal of funds from a single account and then immediate payment to another account. EFT transactions verify the availability of funds prior to authorizing the transaction; if you do not have enough funds in your account at the time you make a transaction, the transaction will fail. About the ACH Payment Method ACH is a specific form of EFT payment. ACH stands for the Automated Clearing House, a federally regulated network that processes electronic payments. The ACH network, including each transaction and its accompanying data, is governed by the NACHA Operating rules. The ACH network acts as a transfer point for funds between different banks. ACH payments function similarly to paper checks: the signature of a person or institution authorizes the transaction, and if funds are not available there may be a fee or legal penalty. If you update your remittance address and ACH information, SAP Business Network sends an ACH pre-notification (pre-note) to your bank. A pre-note is a zero dollar transaction used to verify the accuracy of the bank account information. The bank verifies the information in the pre-note and, if necessary, sends a notification of change (NOC) to SAP Business Network. In that case, Ariba updates the remittance information in your account and sends you a notification informing you of the change. If the bank reports an error in the remittance information, SAP Business Network sends you a notification requesting you to correct the information. About Access to Credit Card Account Numbers For security purposes, account administrators can create or modify a user role that grants access to complete credit card numbers. Users without the user role see partial, masked credit card account numbers. Users whose roles have the Credit Card Number Access permission can view complete credit card numbers. For additional information, see SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide. 56 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Payment Routing Configuring Remittance Addresses and Payment Methods Configure remittance addresses and payment methods to define how your customers send you payments. Context  Note Some customers require their suppliers to provide bank details on invoices. You'll receive an error message on the invoice if your customer requires it but you haven't added bank information to your remittance address. If see you an error, you can click Add bank accounts details directly from the invoice you're creating to configure your remittance address with bank information. After you add bank information, you are returned to the invoice entry page and can submit the invoice to your customer. If you don't have permission to update remittance information, you'll see a link to contact your account administrator. Procedure 1. In the right corner of the header bar, click the Account Settings icon and choose Settings Remittances . The Network Settings page appears, with the Settlement tab selected. 2. In the EFT/Check Remittances section, click Create. 3. On the Create Remittance Address/Payment Info page, enter a complete mailing address. 4. In the Default field, indicate whether you want to designate this address as the default. 5. Assign remittance IDs for this address for each of your customers. Customers might ask you to assign IDs to your addresses so they can refer to them uniquely. You can assign different IDs for each customer. 6. If you are setting up payment using ACH or wire transfers, click Include Bank Account Information in invoices. 7. In the Payment Methods section, do the following: 1. Choose a preferred payment method from the pull-down menu. The options are ACH (Automated Clearing House), Check, Credit Card, and Wire. 2. Enter information for each payment method you support. Your customers use this information when they set up electronic payments. A beneficiary bank is your primary bank. A corresponding bank is an intermediate bank that facilitates international transactions. 3. In the Credit Card field, indicate whether you accept credit card payments. 8. Click OK to create the remittance address and save payment method information. 9. Create a remittance entry for each type of payment you accept. A remittance address is required for each entry. 10. Click Save to return to the Settlement page. Configuring Document Routing Payment Routing PUBLIC 57 Acceptance Rules for Early Payment Offers You can create rules to accept early payment offers from your customers automatically. SAP Business Network compares the early payment offers you receive from your customers to your auto-acceptance rules and accepts offers that meet all the pre-defined rule criteria.  Note If you have already established standing early payment terms with a customer, the auto-acceptance rule does not apply. Accepting Early Payment Offers Automatically To allow your customers to offer you early payment of remittances, you can configure your account to accept these offers automatically. Procedure 1. In the right corner of the header bar, click the Account Settings icon and choose Settings Remittances . The Network Settings page appears, with the Settlement tab selected. 2. In the Supplier Auto Acceptance Rule section, click Create. The Create Supplier Auto-acceptance Rule page appears. 3. Provide the following information to create an early payment offer auto-acceptance rule: 58 Field Description Name A descriptive name for this rule. The name appears in the Supplier Auto Acceptance Rule table on the Settlement page. Description (Optional) A brief description of the rule’s purpose and what it covers. The description displays in the Supplier Auto Acceptance Rule table on the Settlement page. Effective Date The date this rule becomes active. The default is the current date. Rule End Date (Optional) The date this rule becomes inactive. Amount (low) Amount (high) (Optional) The lowest and highest net transaction amount to which this rule applies. For example, to specify a rule that applies to transaction amounts greater than $5,000, enter 5000 in the Amount (low) field. APR (low) APR (high) (Optional) The lowest and highest annual percentage rate to which this rule applies. PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Payment Routing Field Description Active? (Optional) Click Yes to activate this rule for all early payment offers from your customers. Click No to deactivate this rule.  Note Only one rule can be active at a time, even if the date ranges do not overlap. 4. Click OK. Configuring Document Routing Payment Routing PUBLIC 59 Activating and Managing AribaPay About Activating and Managing AribaPay [page 60] Activating AribaPay in a Supplier Account [page 61] About Activating and Managing AribaPay AribaPay is a fast, reliable way for your customers to pay you through SAP Business Network. Customer must request to pay you through AribaPay before you can activate it. AribaPay is only available for transactions that originate from and settle in banks in the United States of America, transactions that originate from and settle in banks in Canada, and transactions that originate from and settle in banks in Germany. AribaPay delivers: • Perfect visibility into payments: AribaPay’s track and trace display on the Remittance Advice page allows you to track each payment’s progress. If a payment fails, you can see the stage at which it failed and the error that caused the failure so that you can address problems quickly. • • Faster reconciliation: matching between payments and invoices clearly shows what each payment is for. Faster payment dispute discovery: richer remittance information for every payment highlights differences between expected invoice and payment amounts so that you can identify discrepancies and resolve them quickly. AribaPay uses the bank holiday calendar, business day, and transmission cut-off information for the payment provider to calculate settlement dates. Payments that a customer transmits before the 7pm EST cut-off time settle in 3 banking days. Payments transmitted after the 7pm EST cut-off time settle in 4 banking days. Payment sent in Euro (EUR) in accordance with Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) standards and processes are submitted to the payment provider for processing each business day at 11 AM CET. You activate AribaPay in your account after the first customer requests to pay you that way. AribaPay activation in a supplier account is a one-time activity. Once you have activated it, you can receive AribaPay payments from any customer who requests to pay you that way. AribaPay Requirements AribaPay requires coordination between a customer who requests it as a payment method and you, who must set up your account to support AribaPay features. You must be set up to receive electronic payments through a merchant acquirer in order to receive payments through AribaPay. You cannot activate AribaPay until a customer has requested to pay you that way. At that time, you must mark the Agree to Enable AribaPay enablement task complete and accept the AribaPay Terms of Use, then click the Enroll with AribaPay Payment Provider enablement task to start the process of acquiring an AribaPay Merchant ID. An 60 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Activating and Managing AribaPay

file://SBN/split/Configuring Document Ro.content: AribaPay Merchant ID is a unique identifier that your customers and SAP Business Network use to direct payments to your specified bank account. The AribaPay provider assigns you an AribaPay Merchant ID after you provide qualifying financial information, including a bank account number for payment settlement. The bank account you provide must be authorized to receive settlements for the SAP Business Network accounts you wish to use it with. The AribaPay provider assigns the bank account a unique AribaPay Merchant ID.  Note The bank account that you designate for AribaPay payments during the activation process is maintained by the AribaPay provider outside of the SAP Business Network and is not necessarily the same bank account that you designated in your payment information on the SAP Business Network. AribaPay Restrictions Because AribaPay is a fast, reliable payment method there are a few restrictions regarding its use. AribaPay does not receive status updates from supplier banks. AribaPay shows payments with status Paid, and shows the Funds Paid stage of payment tracking complete on the Remittance Advice page, when SAP Business Network receives notification that the AribaPay provider has credited the supplier’s bank. It does not know whether or not the supplier’s bank has credited funds to the supplier’s account. The remittance address for AribaPay payments is the remittance address associated with your AribaPay Merchant ID, rather than the remittance address you specify in SAP Business Network. Misdirected payments should never occur with AribaPay. In the unlikely event of a misdirected payment from a customer, you must work with SAP Ariba Support to address it. For each SAP Business Network account where you enable AribaPay, it’s important to maintain records of the bank account, AribaPay Merchant ID, and SAP Business Network ID combination configured for the account. Activating AribaPay in a Supplier Account Once a customer has requested to pay you through AribaPay, you can activate it. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • • Click the link in your AribaPay welcome notification and sign in to SAP Business Network Go to supplier.ariba.com and sign in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Enablement from the menu bar. 3. In the AribaPay area, click Enable AribaPay. 4. If applicable, choose the country or region in which you would like to get paid from the list provided. Configuring Document Routing Activating and Managing AribaPay PUBLIC 61 The list of countries and regions is provided to the payment provider by your buyer. Please contact your buyer if the correct country or region does not appear in this list. 5. Accept the Terms of Use and click Continue. 6. Click Enroll with AribaPay Payment Provider. Results You are automatically redirected to the payment provider portal and logged in via single sign-on. The payment provider displays a list of information that you need to have to continue enrollment with AribaPay. If you are not prepared to complete enrollment at this time or are not the appropriate person to complete enrollment, you can provide the payment provider with an email address for followup. The payment provider sends an email notification to the email account you provided. After you complete the AribaPay enrollment process on the payment provider portal, an AribaPay Merchant ID is assigned to your account. 62 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Activating and Managing AribaPay Extended Profile Maintenance Maintaining Extended Profile Information [page 63] Extended Profile Reference for Order Processing Capabilities [page 64] Extended Profile Reference for Catalog Capabilities [page 66] Maintaining Extended Profile Information You create and update your extended profile information to keep your current and potential customers ware of your business policies. Context SAP Business Network enables you to provide business policy and implementation information to your current and potential customers. Your customers use this information to learn how you do business so that they can configure their procurement applications accordingly. As part of the extended profile information, you can provide details about the following capabilities: • Invoicing Capabilities: Let your customers know if you provide invoices through SAP Business Network or if you have any plans to do so. Provide additional information about your invoice processes and policies, and enter default comment text that appears on all invoices and credit memos. • Payment Options: SAP Business Network lets you indicate whether you support PCards, and, if so, which PCard types you support. In addition, you can provide detailed information for customers about your PCard support and about other payment methods you support. Ghosted PCards are accounts that do not have a physical card; they are used by organizations to process charges for corporate expenses. Ghosted PCard account numbers are usually communicated between suppliers and their customers ahead of time, not within purchase orders. • • Order Processing Capabilities. Catalog Capabilities:  Note Providing extended profile information is optional and serves informational purposes only. It does not affect the way that SAP Business Network functions. Configuring Document Routing Extended Profile Maintenance PUBLIC 63 Procedure 1. In the right corner of the header bar, click the Account Settings icon and choose Settings Electronic Order Routing . 2. Scroll to the end of the page and click Extended Profile Information to expand the section. 3. Enter the order processing and customer catalog information and click Save. 4. Click the Electronic Invoice Routing tab, enter information about your invoicing capabilities in the Extended Profile Settings and Information section, and click Save. 5. Click the Settlement tab, and enter information about the payment options you support. Extended Profile Reference for Order Processing Capabilities To provide customers with information about your order processing capabilities, you can specify implementation time frame, shipping address options, policies for returns and credits, policies for cXML or EDI Order Request Documents, policies for change and cancel orders, and policies for order response documents. • • • • • • Implementation Time Frame [page 64] Shipping Address Options [page 65] Policies for Returns and Credits [page 65] Policies for cXML or EDI Order Request Documents [page 65] Policies for Change and Cancel Orders [page 66] Policies for Order Response Documents [page 66] Implementation Time Frame SAP Business Network enables you to specify the length of time it takes your organization to integrate new customers into your customer catalog creation and order processing systems. The information you enter helps potential customers determine how quickly they can begin buying from you. Choose options and enter additional information where necessary to specify your implementation time frame policies. • • • • • 64 Choose an option from the menu for the question How long does it take you to perform production…. (Optional) Enter additional information about your implementation time in the text box. Choose an option from the menus for the questions on CIF catalogs. Click an answer to the question Do you provide a detailed supplier implementation guide? If you have clicked Yes, enter a contact name or URL. PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Extended Profile Maintenance Shipping Address Options You can choose options and enter additional information whenever necessary to specify your shipping address policies. • Indicate whether your order processing system can accommodate different Ship To addresses for line items. Some buying organizations allow requisitioners to order items for employees at other locations. • Indicate whether you accept drop ship addresses (ad hoc Ship To addresses without an associated address identifier). Buying organizations usually assign unique IDs to their addresses; ad hoc addresses do not have these IDs. • (Optional) Enter additional information about how you process drop ship addresses. Policies for Returns and Credits You can choose options and enter additional information where necessary to specify your policies for returns and credits. • • • Indicate whether you accept returned shipments. (Optional) Provide detailed information on your return policy, such as an address for return shipments, the circumstances under which returns are accepted, and what supporting documentation customers must send with return shipments. (Optional) Provide detailed information on your procedures so customers know what to provide and what to expect, without having to contact your company directly. You might enter Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) contact information. Policies for cXML or EDI Order Request Documents You can specify your organization’s special requirements for the content or format of cXML OrderRequest (order and release) documents. For example, some suppliers, such as distributors and aggregators, require that purchase orders identify the supplier of each line item. Choose options and enter additional information where necessary to specify your order request document requirements. • If you receive orders and releases by cXML or EDI, indicate any specific requirements for cXML OrderRequest documents sent by procurement applications. Include information such as required fields or field length restrictions. For example, you might request that customers always include a Ship To address, with no more than three street lines, and each address having fewer than 50 characters. • Indicate whether you require customers to specify a SupplierID for each line item. Configuring Document Routing Extended Profile Maintenance PUBLIC 65 Policies for Change and Cancel Orders You can specify whether or not you accept change and cancel orders. Change orders modify a previously sent purchase order. Cancel orders cancel a previously sent purchase order. Change and cancel orders often require special processing, so not all suppliers accept them. Choose options and enter additional information where necessary to specify your policies for change and cancel orders. • • • Indicate whether you accept change orders. Indicate whether you accept cancel orders. (Optional) Enter additional information about these policies. Policies for Order Response Documents You can choose options and enter additional information where necessary to specify your policies for order response documents. Indicate whether you send or plan to send: • • • • Order confirmation, messages that confirm or reject line items on received purchase orders Back order notifications Notifications of rejected orders Ship notices, messages that indicate when you shipped items and how they will be delivered You can optionally provide additional information about your policies for order status updates and ship notices. For example, if you provide order status updates through another means, you might indicate how customers can access this information. Also, if you provide shipment information on a website, you might want to give the URL. You can send these messages through cXML or EDI, or generate them online from your account. Extended Profile Reference for Catalog Capabilities To provide customers with information about your catalog capabilities, you can specify general catalog, classification, CIF, and PunchOut capabilities. Related Information Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Customer Catalog Format Reference 66 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Extended Profile Maintenance General Customer Catalog Capabilities You can choose options and enter additional information to specify your catalog capabilities: • Indicate whether you have published customer catalogs in the Catalog Interchange Format (CIF), and which version of CIF you support. • • • Indicate whether you have published customer catalogs in cXML format. Indicate whether you have published PunchOut customer catalogs. Choose an option that indicates how frequently you update your customer catalogs. Customer Catalog Classification Capabilities You can choose options and enter additional information to specify details about your customer catalog content. Customers use this information to prepare their procurement applications for your customer catalogs. • Specify whether you support the United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (UNSPSC) classification system. SAP Business Network uses ECCMA version 13.5 and UNSPSC version UNSPSC v9.0501. The UNSPSC codes used in catalogs support version 13.5. • • • If you support UNSPSC, indicate what level of classification you provide (how many digits). • Click all the languages you use for item descriptions in your customer catalogs. Indicate what other product classification schemes you support. Specify the unit of measure coding system you use to indicate how you package items. United Nations Units of Measure (UN/UOM) is preferred. CIF Catalog Capabilities You can choose options and enter additional information to specify details about your CIF catalogs. • • Click all of the CIF fields you include in your catalogs. For example, SupplierID, SupplierPartID. Specify whether your catalog updates are partial or complete. PunchOut Capabilities You can choose options and enter additional information to specify details about your cXML PunchOut site. • • • • • Indicate whether it provides tailored, customer-specific content and pricing for each buying organization. Indicate whether items can be configured before ordering. Indicate whether the website contains extended product information or detailed specifications. Indicate whether the website offers real-time availability checks and pricing information. Indicate whether the website offers order status information. Configuring Document Routing Extended Profile Maintenance PUBLIC 67 • Provide information on how your site supports the PunchOutSetupRequest message. Your site can use the SelectedItem element in PunchOutSetupRequest documents to display the appropriate subset of your offerings. Procurement applications use the ItemID value from your PunchOut index catalog as the SelectedItem. Without aisle-level PunchOut, users see your entire (store-level) offerings. • • • Indicate whether your site supports aisle-level PunchOut. 68 Indicate whether your site offers secure browsing through SSL (Secure Sockets Layer). Indicate what is required from a customer to authenticate a PunchOutSetupRequest message. For example, you might require customers to provide their NetworkId and a more specific location ID in order to provide customized content to a targeted purchasing division. PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Extended Profile Maintenance Pending Queue SAP Business Network suppliers that integrate their SAP Business Network accounts with their external ERP system using cXML can access the Pending Queue from the More menu ( ... ). It lists documents pending for download to your application from your SAP Business Network account. SAP Business Network allows you to monitor the pending document queue, remove documents from the queue, and re-queue them. To use these services, you must configure your external ERP system and SAP Business Network account to use the GetPending/Data Download transaction method. If you have documents that your application has not been able to download for more than three days, SAP Business Network sends you a notification that lists the unacknowledged documents in an attachment. Make sure you have configured your account to send you email notifications to the people in your company responsible for resolving integration issues if documents remain in the pending queue for three or more days. You configure notification settings in your company settings. Your cXML application sends a GetPendingRequest to SAP Business Network, and SAP Business Network sends a GetPendingResponse that contains information about any pending documents. If there are pending documents, your application sends a DataRequest to SAP Business Network and SAP Business Network returns a DataResponse containing the attached pending documents. Your application then issues a StatusUpdateRequest document to indicate that it received the document. You can download documents by document type, such as by purchase order/blanket purchase order and status update documents. You can configure your SAP Business Network accounts to retrieve cXML documents through the pending queue using the GetPending/Data Download transaction method. Viewing the Pending Queue [page 69] About Re-Queuing Documents [page 70] Re-Queuing Documents Manually [page 71] Re-Queuing Documents Automatically [page 71] Example CSV File for Automatic Re-Queuing of Documents [page 72] Viewing the Pending Queue You can view any documents awaiting download to your application from your Ariba Network account. Procedure 1. Choose ... Pending Queue in the Track section. 2. Choose Purchase Order or Status Update as the document type. Configuring Document Routing Pending Queue PUBLIC 69 3. Click Search. To narrow the search to a specific document, enter a document number and then click Search. SAP Business Network displays the document that matches your criteria. 4. Select and open a file to view the document online in your web browser. If your web browser does not recognize a file format, it prompts you to save the file to disk instead. Removing a Document from the Pending Queue When you view documents in the pending queue, you can remove them from the queue, for example, because they failed to download to your application automatically from SAP Business Network. • Select the documents to remove, and click Remove From Queue. Removing a document from the pending queue does not delete them from SAP Business Network. You can re-queue them either manually or automatically. About Re-Queuing Documents After you remove a document from the pending queue in your account because it failed to download, you can re-queue the document to try downloading it again. When your application fails to download a document, SAP Business Network does not create a corresponding object representing that document on SAP Business Network. Furthermore, SAP Business Network does not create corresponding objects for any other documents of that type until you remove them from the queue and re-queue them. Documents that fail to download may have format or data problems that your application cannot process. View failed documents in the pending queue to check for problems before re-queueing them for download. To find documents that failed to downloaded you can: • • Check your application’s log for error messages. Compare the document date in the Pending Queue page to the last date your application attempted to download documents. If the last download date is later than the document date in the Pending Queue, then the document might not exist on Ariba Network. You can re-queue up to 1000 documents at a time manually or automatically. You can re-queue all document types by uploading a document resend file. When your application fails to download documents, Ariba Network creates a resend file and sends you an email notification. When documents fail in your receiving system, however, Ariba Network does not create a resend file or send you a notification. You must create a resend file yourself. 70 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Pending Queue

file://SBN/split/Configuring Document Ro.content: Re-Queuing Documents Manually You can manually re-queue documents that failed after you remove them from the queue and your system re-flows the documents. You can manually re-queue orders, releases, and blanket purchase orders. Procedure 1. Do one of the following • • • For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Orders Purchase orders . Orders and Releases . Navigate to an order-based workbench tile. 2. Select the order you want to resend and click the order number link.  Note SAP Business Network displays a list of orders using default filters. If you cannot find the order, release, or blanket purchase orders you are looking for, use the available search filters to widen or narrow your search. 3. On the Order Detail tab, go to the right side of the toolbar, click the ellipsis icon  , and then select Resend. Re-Queuing Documents Automatically You can re-queue documents automatically using a resend file. When documents remain in the pending queue for three days or more, SAP Business Network sends you an email notification with a resend file attachment. In other cases you must create the resend file yourself. Procedure 1. If you received an email notification from SAP Business Network, view it and save the attached document resend file to your computer. 2. Edit the saved resend file, or create it from scratch in a spreadsheet application: a. List only the problem documents. b. Save the file in CSV format. 3. Choose ... Pending Queue in the Track section. 4. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Create. SAP Business Network displays the Upload Batch Document Resend File page. 5. Click Browse to select the document resend file on your computer. Configuring Document Routing Pending Queue PUBLIC 71 6. Click Upload to add the document resend file to the queue for processing. SAP Business Network processes batch document resend files individually. You can upload multiple files. Next Steps • • Click Refresh Status to see the latest status of the resend file. Delete the resend file after SAP Business Network processes it. Example CSV File for Automatic Re-Queuing of Documents A resend file used to automate re-queueing of documents is a CSV file in UTF-8 character formatting. You can edit a resend file emailed to you by Ariba Network or create your own. The following example illustrates fields for a recored in a CSV file for resending documents automatically: UTF-8 From,Document Number,Type,Created,Payload ID,Network ID KSTsupplier@ariba.com,Inv_0134,InvoiceDetailRequest,3/25/2010,1ty12345,AN000000333. Field Description From Identifies the organization that sent the document. In the CSV file sent in a pending queue notification, this value is an Identity attribute. (Optional) Document Number The Document ID used by the organization identified in the From field. (Required if the Payload ID is not specified) Type The type of cXML request or the document type. (Required if the Payload ID field is not specified) Created The date the document was created on SAP Business Network. (Optional) Payload ID Payload ID is a unique document identifier used for document logging and tracking. If Payload ID is specified, SAP Business Network uses it to find the matching document. (Required if the Document Number, Type, and Network ID fields are not specified. Network ID The SAP Business Network ID of the organization specified in the From field. (Required if the Payload ID field is not specified.) Each row in the file must unique key identifying the document. This key is either the Payload ID or the combination of the Document Number, Document Type, and Network ID fields. If a row contains a Payload ID, the Document Number, Document Type, and Network ID fields are optional. Ariba Network uses the Payload ID for document matching. If no match is found, Ariba Network logs an error message. If a row does not contain a Payload ID, the Document Number, Document Type, and Network ID fields are required. Ariba Network uses the combination of these three fields for document matching. The Type field must 72 PUBLIC Configuring Document Routing Pending Queue be the cXML name of the document type. For example, if a document is a purchase order, the Type field must be OrderRequest. PUBLIC Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy This guide is for SAP Ariba administrators responsible for uploading and managing a master content file that contains comprehensive information about all of the items that their organization wants to sell through the Spot Buy Network Sellers marketplace in any country/region. The SAP Ariba Spot Buy capability allows users to search for and buy non-sourced goods from their SAP Ariba Buying solution. This guide applies to: • SAP Business Network Related Guides SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide About Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy [page 3] Groups for Managing Master Content and Supplier Pricing Files [page 4] Uploading Spot Buy Catalog Master Content [page 4] Uploading Catalog Supplier Pricing and Shipping Files for a Specific Country/Region [page 5] Master Content and Supplier Pricing Files Management [page 10] Configuration of Daily Updates by API [page 21] Catalog Master Content File Formats [page 22] About Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy You can upload a single master content file that contains comprehensive information about all of the items that you want to sell through Spot Buy in any country/region. You can then upload smaller supplier pricing files for individual countries/regions that contain additional information for a subset of the master content file. A shipping policy file must also be uploaded when uploading a supplier pricing file. A single pricing file can be uploaded for each of the countries/regions that are currently available. When Spot Buy buyers search in their SAP Ariba systems, they see items from your supplier pricing file for their country/region, and not items from your full master content file. Separate master content files are uploaded for each available language, and each language has a different set of master content. The language that is displayed to buyers depends on the buyer’s locale. Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy PUBLIC 3 Groups for Managing Master Content and Supplier Pricing Files The following groups allow you to manage access to master content and supplier pricing files: • Content Manager Membership of this group allows you to manage master content files, preparing product information as individual SKU’s. • Catalog Manager Membership of this group allows you to prepare and maintain pricing tables according to contract or market channel requirements. Uploading Spot Buy Catalog Master Content Use this procedure to upload Spot Buy catalog master content. Context You must upload a catalog master content file before you can upload supplier pricing files. Master content files can be in CSV, CIF, or XML format. ZIP format is also supported for master content upload. The zip file must contain a valid CIF, CSV, or XML master content file. It is recommended that suppliers select and stick with one of these formats. Files can be up to 2GB in size.  Note Spot Buy catalog master content is uploaded to Spot Buy, and not to SAP Business Network. Catalog validation is performed by Spot Buy. Spot Buy and SAP Business Network have different format specifications and validation rules. Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select Upload master content. 5. Select the language of the catalog content file from the Language pull-down menu. 6. Drag and drop your content file to the box as indicated or select the browse button to browse for and upload the file. You can download template files from the list at the bottom of this page or by selecting Download templates on the dashboard. For information about file formats, see Catalog Master Content File Formats [page 22]. 4 PUBLIC Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy 7. If you are uploading your first master content file or if you want to completely replace an existing file for the selected language, you can select the Replace all for this language checkbox. However, if you are updating only a few items in an existing file, make sure this checkbox remains unchecked. 8. Click on Submit. The file is uploaded and sent for validation. 9. Depending on the size of your file, if might take a while to upload. If you want to receive notifications regarding the file processing status, enter your email address in the field provided and click on Submit. Results The contents of the file you uploaded are displayed on the Content manager tab. For information about file upload statuses, see see Master Content and Supplier Pricing File and Item Processing Statuses [page 11]. Related Information Downloading File Templates [page 11] Viewing Upload File Errors [page 12] Uploading Catalog Supplier Pricing and Shipping Files for a Specific Country/Region Use this procedure to upload catalog supplier pricing and shipping files for a specific country/region. Context Supplier pricing files allow you to create catalogs for specific countries/regions by referencing items to be pulled from master content and adding additional details. Supplier pricing files must be in CSV format. Files can be up to 2GB in size.  Note • Before uploading a supplier pricing file for a specific country/region you must have uploaded master content for the items referenced in the pricing file. For information about uploading master content files, see Uploading Spot Buy Catalog Master Content [page 4]. • As part of the procedure described below, you are required to upload two files, for the shipping policy for the country/region in question, as well as the actual pricing file for that country/region. The shipping policy is only required the first time a pricing file is uploaded. If you want to, you can download templates for these files and populate them with the required content before you begin the following procedure. For more information, see Downloading File Templates [page 11]. Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy PUBLIC 5 • The Returns policy field is not editable. The maximum days to return of 30 days is set forth in the SAP Ariba Network Spot Buy Program Terms. Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Catalog manager tab. 5. Select Upload marketplace catalog. 6. Select the country to which the catalog is to apply from the Country/Region pull-down menu. 7. (Required) Browse for the shipping policy file for that country/region or drag it to the location indicated. The shipping policy file must be in CSV format and cannot be greater than two gigabytes (GB). You can download a shipping policy template file at the bottom of the current page. For more information about the shipping policy template, see Shipping Policy File Fields [page 7]. 8. In the Excluded buyer list field, enter the ANIDs of any users that you do not want to see the current catalog. 9. Select Continue. 10. Browse for the pricing file or drag it to the location indicated. The pricing file must be in CSV format and cannot be greater than two gigabytes (GB). You can download a pricing file template at the bottom of the current page. For more information about the pricing file template, see Pricing File Fields [page 8]. 11. IMPORTANT: Only select the Replace all for this country/region checkbox if you want to completely replace an existing file for the selected country/region with the file that you are currently uploading. 12. Select Submit. Related Information Shipping Cost Handling with Spot Buy [page 10] Shipping Policy File Fields [page 7] 6 PUBLIC Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Shipping Policy File Fields The following table describes the column headings on the shipping policy CSV file. Each row in the file represents a separate policy item: Field Name Description COMMODITY_CODE The UNSPSC commodity code for the product or product category to which the policy item applies. All catalog items that have this code or sit under this code in the commodity hierarchy are covered by this policy item. To apply a policy to all catalog items, enter "All" for this column. SHIPPING_METHOD The shipping method that applies to this policy item. Use the below standard format for consistency between suppliers. • • • • 1 Business Day 2 Business Days 1-3 Business Days 2-5 Business Days MINIMUM_ORDER_VALUE The minimum order value required for this policy item to apply. Must be whole numbers; decimals are not allowed. MAXIMUM_ORDER_VALUE The maximum order value to which this policy item will apply. Must be whole numbers; decimals are not allowed. SHIPPING_COST The shipping cost for this policy item. Example COMMODITY_CODE,SHIPPING_METHOD,MINIMUM_ORDER_VALUE,MAXIMUM_ORDER_VALUE,SHIPPING_COST All,2-5 Business Days,1001,,0 All,2-5 Business Days,501,1000,15 All,2-5 Business Days,0,500,25 In this example, assuming the items are priced in USD, ground shipping to the US for all items is free when the item costs $1001 or more, $15 for orders between $501 and $100, and $25 for items up to $500 in value.  Note Add the field names, separated by a comma (,), on the first line of the CSV file and shipping policy details, separated by commas, on subsequent lines. A default shipping policy is required even if shipping is included in the catalog. Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy PUBLIC 7 Pricing File Fields The following table describes required and optional fields for supplier pricing files: Field Name Required/ Optional Data Type/ Length (In Characters) Required Order Used in Temin File plate Type Supplier ID Yes String/255 1 CSV Description The SAP Business Network ID of the supplier account. This should be the same as in the master content file. Example: AN05460017766 Supplier Part ID Yes String/255 2 CSV Unique SKU number assigned to the item by the supplier. Example: CAHDPE6BIASE Supplier Part Auxiliary ID No String/255 3 CSV Any additional part number to uniquely identify the product within the supplier’s inventory. Each Supplier Part ID and Supplier Part Auxiliary ID combination is unique within a supplier’s inventory system. Can be used to distinguish similar items with varied properties. Market Price Recommended Decimal/No limit 4 CSV The list or suggested retail price of the item. Must be in currency, with two significant digits. Example: 249.99 Unit Price Yes Decimal/No limit 5 CSV The current price of the item per unit in Spot Buy. Must be in two significant digits. Example: 100.00 8 PUBLIC Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Field Name Required/ Optional Data Type/ Length (In Characters) Required Order Used in Temin File plate Type Currency Yes String/3 6 CSV Description ISO 4217 currency name. The currency in which the item price is quoted. This value overrides Currency in the header. Example: USD Quantity Yes Integer/No limit 7 CSV The quantity of the item available in inventory or available to be ordered. Example: 2478 Quantity Sold No Integer/No limit 8 CSV The quantity of the item that have been sold. Example: 478 Unit of Measure Yes String/255 9 CSV The unit of measure in UNUOM (United Nations Unit of Measure) standards. Example: EA (for each) Item Shipping No • 10 Shipping Method: String/255 • Shipping Cost: Decimal/No limit CSV The shipping policy for the item. A list of shipping method name and cost pairs. Example: {One Day Shipping=50;Two Day Shipping=30} When shipping information is included in the pricing file this takes precedence over the calculation using the shipping policy file. Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy PUBLIC 9 Shipping Cost Handling with Spot Buy There are three possible approaches for handling shipping with Spot Buy: 1. Offer free shipping and build freight costs into the price for each item. To do this, a supplier can enter 0 shipping cost for all commodities in the shipping policy file, which is required. The Item Shipping field in the pricing file can be left blank for each item. 2. Use the shipping policy file to establish freight cost rules for all commodities. 3. Use the shipping policy file to set general shipping rules for commodities, and use the Item Shipping field in the pricing file to overwrite these rules wherever necessary for specific items. file://SBN/split/Content Management for.content: Downloading File Templates Use this procedure to download file templates. Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Select the Catalogs tab. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select either the Content manager or Catalog manager tab. 5. Select Download Templates. Master Content and Supplier Pricing File and Item Processing Statuses File and item processing statuses are displayed on the Activity page for each file type. File Statuses The file status is listed in the Status column. The following table describes the file upload statuses: Status Description Uploading Upload in progress. This can take up to 30 minutes depending on size and upload volume. Uploaded The file was upload and the contents of the file are being validated. Upload error Upload failed so no items are processed. Processing Processing in progress. This can take a few hours depending on size and upload volume. Processed The contents of the file were processed. This status means that all items were validated, or some items were successfully validated and remaining items failed to validate. Process Failed There was a fatal validation error and no items were validated. Click the Download Error Report link to download a list of validation errors. Publishing Publishing in progress. This can take up to 15 minutes. Catalogs start publishing once they are processed. Published The catalog was published. The catalog is now available for users to search. Publish Failed Publish failed with internal error. Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy PUBLIC 11 Item Statuses There are three possible item processing statuses: Status Description Valid The item was validated and it is available for use in master content. The number of valid items is listed in the Valid items column. Error The item was already saved to the database, but there is an error in the version of the item that you are attempting to upload. The previously saved version of the item is retained in master content and is not overwritten by the error version. The number of error items is listed in the Items with errors column. Unprocessed The item was not added to the database because it was unreadable for some reason, such as an incorrect ANID. The number of unprocessed items is listed in the Unprocessed items column. Viewing Upload File Errors Use this procedure to view upload file errors. Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Content manager tab. This should be displayed by default. 5. Select Activity. 6. If you entered an email address to receive notifications regarding file upload status when uploading the master content file, copy the File ID from the email, select File ID in the search drop-down menu at the top of the page and paste the file ID into the text field. This filters the activities list to show only the file you are looking for. 7. Select Download in the Errors report column. 8. Scroll to the right of the error file to find the error reason listed in the Errors column. 9. You can fix the errors in the original upload file and re-upload the file. To download the original file, click on the file name in the File name column on the Activity page. When uploading the file, ensure that the Replace all for this language field is unchecked so that only the fixed items are uploaded. For more information, see Uploading Spot Buy Catalog Master Content [page 4]. 12 PUBLIC Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Replacing a Master Content File Use this procedure to replace a master content file. Context You can completely replace your existing master content for a language with a new master contents file.  Note This removes everything that was updated previously for that language and replaces your content with that in the new master content file. Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Content manager tab. This should be displayed by default. 5. Select the Upload master content button. 6. Select the language of the catalog content file from the Language pull-down menu. 7. Drag and drop your content file to the box as indicated or select the browse button to browse for and upload the file. 8. Select the Replace all for this language check box. 9. Select Submit. Updating Items in a Master Content File Use this procedure to update items in a master content file. Context You can update specific items in your master content by downloading the existing file, making edits in it and re-uploading the file.  Note Be careful to NOT select the Replace all for this language button when uploading the edited file. Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy PUBLIC 13 Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Content manager tab. This should be displayed by default. 5. Select the Activity button. 6. Click on the file name of the file you want to edit. 7. Save the file to your local device, make your changes, and re-upload the file. For information about uploading master content files, see Uploading Spot Buy Catalog Master Content [page 4]. Replacing a Supplier Pricing File Use this procedure to replace a supplier pricing file. Context You can replace an existing supplier pricing file for a country/region with a new supplier pricing file.  Note This removes all pricing that was updated previously for that country/region and replaces the pricing information with that in the new file. Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Catalog manager tab. 5. Select the vertical ellipsis button to the right of the country/region catalog name and click on Re-upload. 14 PUBLIC Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Replacing Items in a Supplier Pricing File Use this procedure to replace items in a supplier pricing file. Context You can update specific items in a supplier pricing file by downloading the existing file, making edits in it and re-uploading the file.  Note Be careful to NOT select the Replace all for this country/region button when uploading the edited file. Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Catalog manager tab. 5. Select the vertical ellipsis button to the right of the country/region catalog name and click on Activity. 6. Click on the file name of the file you want to edit. 7. Save the file to your local device, make your changes, and re-upload the file. For information about uploading marketplace pricing files, see Uploading Catalog Supplier Pricing and Shipping Files for a Specific Country/Region [page 5]. Viewing Uploaded File History for Master Content Use this procedure to view uploaded file history for master content. Context You can view all uploaded file activity for master content files on the Activity page. The Activity page refreshes automatically, so any file activities that occur while you are looking at the page are displayed automatically. Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy PUBLIC 15 Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Content manager tab. This should be displayed by default. 5. Select the Activity button. 6. From here you can do the following: • • To download a specific version of a file, click on a file name. • To download an error report for a file, select Download in the Errors report column. To search for a specific file based on an email notification, copy the file id from the notification email, select File ID in the search field pull-down menu and enter the file id in the text field. Viewing History for Supplier Pricing Files Use this procedure to view history for supplier pricing files. Context You can view all uploaded file activity for individual supplier pricing files. Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Catalog manager tab. 5. Select the vertical ellipsis button to the right of the country/region catalog name and click on Activity. 16 PUBLIC Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Searching for Items in Master Content Use this procedure to search for items in master content. Context You can search for items in master content by Supplier Part ID and other attributes. Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Content manager tab. This should be displayed by default. 5. Select one of the available item attributes in the pull-down menu beside the search text box and enter your search term in the box. The items list is filtered to show your search results. Modifying Shipping Policy or Excluded Buyers List for a Supplier Pricing File Use this procedure to modify shipping policy or excluded buyers list for a supplier pricing file. Context You can edit some of the settings you entered when you uploaded a supplier pricing file. These include the shipping policy and the excluded buyers list. Procedure 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Catalog manager tab. Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy PUBLIC 17 5. Select the vertical ellipsis button to the right of the country/region catalog name and click on Settings. Previewing a Catalog Use this procedure to preview a catalog. Context When you upload a supplier pricing file for a country/region, you can preview how that catalog will look in Spot Buy. Procedure 1. Sign into your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Catalog manager tab. 5. Select the vertical ellipsis button to the right of the country/region catalog name and click on Preview catalog. Suspending Catalogs Use this procedure to suspend catalogs. Context You can suspend catalogs for specific countries/regions so that buyers no longer see search results from those catalogs. This can be useful if you cannot fulfil orders during a specific period or if a business has closed. When the switch button for a country/region is off, catalog items for this country/region will not show up in buyer search results. You can reinstate suspended catalogs at any time.  Note When you suspend a catalog, any order that is already moving through the buyer workflow will still be submitted. 18 PUBLIC Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Procedure 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Search suspend tab. 5. Switch the On/Off button to off to suspend catalogs for all countries/regions or for specific countries/regions. Downloading Master Content Data Use this procedure to download master content data. Context You can download master content data in CSV format. Procedure 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Content manager tab. 5. Select Generate master content file. 6. A message is displayed asking you to return to this page later to download the master content file. Click on Close. 7. On the Content manager page, click on the download icon ( under the page name. ) for the last downloaded file, which is listed 8. Open or save the file. Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy PUBLIC 19 Downloading Pricing Data Use this procedure to download pricing data. Context You can marketplace pricing data in CSV format. Procedure 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Catalog manager tab. 5. Click on the pricing file that you want to download. 6. Select Generate pricing file. 7. A message is displayed asking you to return to this page later to download the master content file. Click on Close. 8. On the marketplace pricing file page, click on the download icon ( listed under the page name. ) for the last downloaded file, which is 9. Open or save the file. Deleting a Marketplace Catalog Use this procedure to delete a marketplace catalog for a country/region in the user interface. Procedure 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Catalog manager tab. 5. Select the vertical ellipsis button to the right of the country/region catalog name and click on Delete marketplace. 6. Select Delete to confirm your action. 20 PUBLIC Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy

file://SBN/split/Content Management for.content: Configuration of Daily Updates by API An API can be set up to push catalog updates from the Spot Buy supplier to Spot Buy automatically on a daily basis. The API involves a request from the Spot Buy supplier and a response from SAP Ariba. The request contains a file attachment that contains details of what item information is to be updated and the response lets the Spot Buy supplier know if the update was successful. The request file for master content can be in CIF, CSV, XML or ZIP format. The request for supplier pricing files can be in CSV or ZIP format. The request file is subject to a size limit of 2GB. To establish a connection with Spot Buy, Spot Buy supplier organizations must connect to the following endpoint: https://mu.ariba.com/sellerdirect/marketplace/dailyUpdateFile The API POST request form requires the following: • A request string that identifies the supplier and catalog to which the request applies. This should be in one of the following formats: {"ANID":"addYourANIDHere","User": " addYourUserIDHere ","language":"en","uploadType":"MasterContent", "Location":"US","Locale":"en_US", "SharedSecret":"addYourSharedSecretHere", "Email":" addYourEmailHere "} {"ANID":"addYourANIDHere","User": " addYourUserIDHere ","uploadType":"Pricing", "Location":"US","Locale":"en_US", "SharedSecret":"addYourSharedSecretHere", "Email":" addYourEmailHere "} The uploadType must be either MasterContent or Pricing. Location, Locale and language can be changed. • The file attachment containing the catalog updates. Ensure that the file attachment has the correct extension, either .cif, .csv, .xml, or .zip. If you would like to try out the API, go to the following location, and add a request string and a daily upload file: https://mu.ariba.com/sellerdirect/marketplace/swagger-ui.html#/fileupload-controller/updateCatalogStartUsingPOST For more information about using the daily updates API, see the Spot Buy for Network Suppliers Feature Administration Guide. Related Information Configuring Endpoint Shared Secrets [page 22] Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy Content Management for SAP Ariba Spot Buy PUBLIC 21 Configuring Endpoint Shared Secrets Use this procedure to configure endpoint shared secrets. Context A shared secret allows Spot Buy to authorize users when they call the External Daily Update API. Whenever users call this API, they must include their shared secret in the request to be verified and authorized. You can add or edit shared secrets for endpoints. Procedure 1. Log in to your SAP Business Network account as an administrator. 2. Click Catalogs. 3. Click the Ariba Spot Buy Catalog Console link. 4. Select the Endpoint configuration tab. 5. If you are adding a new shared secret, enter the following details: • • Shared secret Confirm shared secret 6. If you are editing an existing shared secret, enter the following details: • • • Old shared secret New shared secret Confirm new shared secret 7. Select Submit.
