and Managing Customer Catalogs This guide is for SAP Business Network suppliers and describes how to create, upload, and manage customer catalogs of the products and services that their company offers. Customer Catalogs are text files that describe the products and services offered by suppliers. Suppliers publish catalogs on the SAP Business Network for customers to subscribe to. This guide applies to: • SAP Business Network Related guides Customer Catalog Format Reference Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs PUBLIC 3 Getting Started with Customer Catalogs Customer Catalogs are text files stored on SAP Business Network or on your own company’s website that describe the products and services your organization offers and the prices you charge. You can create customer catalogs for any product or service, regardless of how it is measured, priced, or delivered. Your customers access your catalogs through their procurement solutions to see what you offer and to make purchases from you. Catalogs are the main communication channel between you and your customers. SAP Business Network supports the following customer catalog types: • CIF (Catalog Interchange Format): You can create CIF catalogs [page 28] with any word processor, text editor, or spreadsheet application. • cXML (Commerce eXtensible Markup Language) format: You can create cXML catalogs using any XML or text editor. • PunchOut catalogs: PunchOut catalogs [page 31] are interactive catalogs that use cXML to support two-way communication of electronic commerce details. A PunchOut catalog resides on your website; you provide your customers with a URL with which to access it. • BMEcat (Bundesverband Materialwirtschaft, Einkauf und Logistik e. V. catalog): You can publish BMEcat catalogs [page 12] only to customers who use the content management system (CMS) in SAP Ariba solutions to manage their catalogs. • Excel (Microsoft Excel): You can publish Excel catalogs [page 12] only to customers who use the content management system (CMS) in SAP Ariba solutions to manage their catalogs. SAP Business Network supports any customer catalog in CIF or cXML format. A CIF catalog can be either a text file saved with a .cif extension or an Excel file saved with a .xls extension. You can upload a customer catalog using either the SAP Business Network catalog wizard or the cXML CatalogUploadRequest transaction. The cXML CatalogUploadRequest transaction supports CIF, cXML, BMEcat, and Excel catalogs. It also supports both new catalogs and updates to existing catalogs. For help in deciding which catalog format is best for your company, see the Customer Catalog Format Reference. Customer Catalog Workflow The following is a typical example of the interaction between customer catalogs and your customer's purchasing solution: 1. You create catalog files [page 9] that describe products and services. You can download the CIF file template [page 28] or the CIF and CXML example files that are available in the SAP Business Network customer catalog wizard to create catalogs. 2. You specify how to publish the customer catalog. In the SAP Business Network customer catalog wizard, you: 1. Designate a customer catalog as either private or public. 2. View your customer’s catalog preferences [page 17]. 3. You upload the catalog files for a customer that has an active trading relationship on SAP Business Network. If your account is suspended, you can't publish catalogs to specific customers. SAP Business Network doesn't show your customers at the bottom of this page. 4 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Getting Started with Customer Catalogs After the customer catalogs are validated, SAP Business Network publishes them to customers. You can verify the status [page 17] for your uploaded customer catalogs. 4. If your uploaded customer catalog has errors, correct the errors [page 20], and upload the catalog again. 5. SAP Business Network notifies the customer by email that new catalogs are available. 6. Your customer’s purchasing site downloads and approves catalogs for use. 7. Users in your customer's organization browse the customer catalogs for products and services and initiate purchase requisitions, which are routed through their organizations for approval. 8. Upon approval, the purchasing site automatically sends purchase orders to SAP Business Network. Benefits of Uploading Customer Catalogs Storing your customer catalogs on SAP Business Network provides the following benefits: • Security: SAP Business Network offers robust catalog security. After you upload customer catalogs, you publish them to individual customers or groups of customers. No other customers or suppliers can see them. For additional security, SAP Business Network uses Secure Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTPS) so customer catalogs are encrypted across the Internet. SAP Business Network also uses HTTPS when customers download catalogs. • Versioning: SAP Business Network stores all versions of your customer catalogs, so you don't have to maintain local copies on your computer. Catalog versions are maintained on a "last in/first out" basis. When you upload a new customer catalog version, SAP Business Network maintains it as the current version. When you delete a version, SAP Business Network removes the most recently uploaded customer catalog.  Note While uploading a customer catalog, you must ensure that you always use the same filename for all versions of the selected customer catalog. Using the same name makes catalog management easier for customers.  Note Catalogs published for CMS-enabled customers [page 12] aren't stored on SAP Business Network. Making Catalogs Available to Your Customers After you create your CIF or cXML catalog, you store it on SAP Business Network and publish it to your customers. Your catalogs don't automatically appear in your customers’ purchasing systems immediately after you publish them. Your customer’s administrator must first validate, approve and activate catalogs before users can view them. A customer catalog subscription creates a link between your customer and your catalog so that you can send updated versions directly to your customer’s purchasing system. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Getting Started with Customer Catalogs PUBLIC 5 Customer Catalog Notifications If customers request notification of catalog changes, any future modification you make to that catalog automatically triggers another notification to the customer. For private catalogs, customers receive notification only if you select them and they request notification. Customers that you don't select won't receive notification, even if they request it. Publishing a customer catalog sends an automatic notification to the selected customer. Customers can download catalogs manually from SAP Business Network, or you can set up subscriptions so that SAP Business Network automatically updates your customer’s existing catalogs when new versions are available. Customer Catalog Expiration and Deletion Customer catalogs that have never been published and contain more than one version expire 180 days after they were last viewed by the supplier. If a customer catalog has been published or contains only one version, it never expires. When SAP Business Network deletes customer catalogs, it deletes them permanently. There is no way to retrieve deleted customer catalogs, either through the SAP Business Network user interface or by contacting SAP Ariba. Deleting a customer catalog from SAP Business Network doesn't delete the catalog from your customer’s purchasing system. Customers that previously downloaded these catalogs and imported them into their purchasing system can still use them. To ensure that customers don't continue to use old catalogs, add an expiration date to your customer catalogs (available in CIF 3.0 and cXML catalog formats). Test Customer Catalogs Test accounts are optional and complementary SAP Business Network accounts that allow customers and suppliers to test catalogs and purchase order generation, routing, and receiving. Test accounts enable transaction partners to send and receive test purchase orders without the risk of actually shipping products or disrupting production transactions. The catalog tester, which is available only in your test account, lets you see how a customer would see the catalog contents. You can examine your item descriptions and other catalog fields to see how they appear. You can choose customer catalog items and add them to test purchase orders. You can also submit these test purchase orders to exercise the order routing method you configure in your test account. For more information on test accounts, search for Using test accounts in Ariba Network in the help center.  Note You cannot test customer catalogs published for customers who use the content management system (CMS) available in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to manage their catalog data. 6 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Getting Started with Customer Catalogs Pricing and Availability Updates If your customer’s purchasing site supports PunchOut catalogs in both CIF and cXML formats, your customers can go directly to your website to search for and choose items and services. In the case of a PunchOut item, the customer can click a link to punch out directly to your website and receive live pricing and customer-specific information. Level 2 PunchOut enables customers to search for and find PunchOut items within their purchasing site, instead of having to search your website directly. If you use Level 2 PunchOut, SAP Business Network allows you to configure and specify a cXML URL for pricing updates, where customers can request for updates on price and availability of catalog items. After you have published a catalog on SAP Business Network, you might change the price or availability of your catalog items. However, your published customer catalog continues to show the older information on SAP Business Network until you upload a newer version of the catalog. When you configure a cXML URL for the price and availability updates, customers can view the updated prices of customer catalog items in their purchasing site. Maintenance of Customer Catalog Versions for Different Customers Customers that use SAP Ariba Buying solutions can define customer catalog validation rules to support unique codes in their purchasing systems. You might have customers using a unique set of Unit of Measure (UOM) codes or commodity codes in SAP Ariba Buying solutions. SAP Business Network supports customer-specific catalog validation rules [page 17] and transforms the values provided by the customer to the equivalent values supported by SAP Business Network. This greatly eliminates the need for suppliers to maintain separate catalogs to support a different set of UOM, country code, commodity code, and currency code values for each customer. Suppliers can use a single set of values for the customer catalog each time an update is made. For example, customer A supports “Each” as the UOM code and customer B supports “EA." The supplier supports “Each” as the UOM code. In order to support both the customers, the supplier had to create and maintain two sets of customer catalogs for these UOM codes. SAP Business Network allows customers of SAP Ariba Buying solutions to define specific catalog validation rules that allow suppliers to maintain a single set of UOM code to support both these customers. Using the customer catalog rules specified in SAP Ariba Buying solutions, SAP Ariba transforms the UOM code “EA” to “Each” allowing both the customers to receive their value of the UOM code each time the customer catalog is updated. Additional Resources The following table lists the resources available for customer catalog creation: Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Getting Started with Customer Catalogs PUBLIC 7 If You Want To… See This Guide… Create CIF or cXML catalogs Catalog format reference (available in the help center) Explains how to work with the CIF (Catalog Interchange Format) 3.0 and cXML (commerce eXtensible Markup Language) catalog formats. It also describes how to use customer catalog features to reflect your business model and to differentiate your product and service content. Implement a PunchOut website cXML Solutions Guide (available in the help center) Describes how to implement a PunchOut-enabled website, receive cXML purchase orders, and send cXML invoices. Learn about cXML cXML User’s Guide (available at http://www.cxml.org ) The definitive source for information on the cXML language. Describes how to send and receive cXML documents. 8 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Getting Started with Customer Catalogs Creating and Publishing a Static Customer Catalog Static customer catalogs are text files stored on SAP Business Network that describe the products and services your organization offers. To create a static customer catalog, use the catalog creation wizard. It guides you through the process of choosing customers, adding catalog details, uploading catalog files and publishing the catalog to selected customers. Prerequisites • • You have a role with the Catalog Management permission on SAP Business Network. • Prepare your catalog file. Note the customer catalog file types supported by SAP Business Network, download a template, and fill in your catalog content. Your catalog file name must contain only the following characters: A–Z, a–z, 0–9, period (.), dash (-), and underscore (_). • If your account is suspended, you can't publish catalogs to customers. We recommend that you view customers' catalog validation preferences before preparing catalog files. Validation checks customer catalogs for syntactic and semantic errors and also for compatibility with customer-specified requirements. If your customer requires advanced pricing details, ensure that those catalog fields comply with all syntactic, semantic, and customer-specific validation rules. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network supplier homepage, choose Catalogs Customer Catalogs . 2. Click Create. The system displays the Select Visibility & Type page of the catalog creation wizard. 3. Select the catalog visibility and type. Visibility - Choose one of the following: • Private: Your catalog will be visible only to specific customers you choose. Ideal for tailored offers or contract pricing. You will select customers later in the wizard. • Public: Your catalog will be visible to all customers on SAP Business Network who have an established relationship with you. No customer selection is required. Type - Choose Static Catalog. A static catalog is a fixed catalog stored directly on SAP Business Network that contains product and service information you upload. If you selected Private visibility, the system displays the Choose Customer(s) page. This page lists the customers you have trading relationships with on SAP Business Network. 4. On the Choose Customer(s) page, select the customer(s) to whom you want to publish the catalog. Note the following: Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Creating and Publishing a Static Customer Catalog PUBLIC 9 • To find a specific customer, enter customer name in the search box or click the  (Filter) icon to filter customers by country/region. Click CMS Customers or Non-CMS Customers to filter customers based on whether they have enabled content management system (CMS) in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to manage catalog content.  Note If you know that customers are registered on SAP Business Network but you can't see them, contact them directly and ask them to grant you permission to see them. • When you select a customer, the Catalog Validation Preferences table appears on the right side of the page, showing preferences specified by the customer on SAP Business Network. These include the preferred UNSPSC code version and whether to bypass UNSPSC or UoM checks or ignore zero price values. Use this information to ensure your catalog complies with customer requirements. To view catalog content rules on a customer's procurement site, click Request to View in the Catalog Validation Preferences table. After viewing the rules, return to SAP Business Network. • You can select either CMS or non-CMS customers, but not a combination of both. When selecting multiple customers, it's best to choose those with the same catalog validation preferences, which helps reduce potential validation errors. 5. Choose Next Step to reach the Add Catalog Details page. 6. On the Add Catalog Details page, add a unique catalog name, a brief description, and the commodity codes to classify your catalog. Your customers can find your catalog by searching with this information. To add commodities, proceed as follows: 1. Click the  icon inside the Commodities box. SAP Business Network shows the Product or Service Categories dialog box, which lists product and service categories, based on the United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (UNSPSC). 2. If needed, enter a category name or code in the search box and click Go. The search results will list the categories that match your search criteria. 3. Under Select Categories or Search Results, expand the list and select the product or service categories you want to add. The categories are displayed in the Selected Categories box. You can add up to 20 categories.  Limitations If you are a supplier of all the items in a given product and service category level, choose the name of the higher-level product and service category instead of adding all of the lower-level categories. For example, a furniture supplier should choose the category “Furniture and Furnishings” not the hundreds of individual items it sells. Customers can search for this information. 4. To remove a selected category, deselect it from the Selected Categories box. 5. Click Apply. 7. Choose Next Step. The Important File Requirements page opens and displays supported file format, sizes, and upload instructions. Read the information and click Close to proceed to the Upload File page. If you prefer not to see this page again, click Don't show this again. The Upload File page shows brief file requirements at the bottom, along with a Show More link. You can click Show More to reopen the Important File Requirements page. 8. On the Upload File page, proceed as follows: 10 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Creating and Publishing a Static Customer Catalog

In the File Type box, select a catalog file type. 3. Click the Browse button beside Upload Catalog File to locate the catalog file you've prepared.  Note Large catalog files may upload slowly. To speed up the upload, you can zip a large file and upload the zip file (.zip) instead. 4. If you are creating a catalog for CMS customers and would like to add product images by uploading images to SAP Business Network, click the Browser button beside Upload Image File to locate the image zip file (.zip) you've prepared.  Tip You can link images to products in one of the following ways: • Upload a zipped folder of images as described above (for CMS customers only, max 200 MB for image folder), or directly share the zip with your customer. Specify the image path (e.g., Image/ image1.jpg) in your catalog file. • If your images reside on a public website, enter the image URLs in your catalog file. Ensure the URLs start with https:// and end with the full file name, including the file extension. 5. Choose Submit. Your web browser uploads the catalog to SAP Business Network, validates it and publishes it to the customer(s) you've chosen in the previous step. You'll see a pop-up displaying the upload progress. Do not navigate in the browser window until the next page shows up, as interrupting your web browser aborts the upload process. When the process completes, your customers receive the current version of the catalog. The new catalog is added to your catalogs list under the customer's name. You can find it anytime by entering the catalog name or customer name in the search box or using the filters above the list. Next Steps After SAP Business Network uploads the customer catalog, you can do the following: • Check catalog status and validation errors (if any). For more information, see: • • • • Customer Catalog Validation for CMS Customers Customer Catalog Validation for Non-CMS Customers) Publish the customer catalog to more customers. Perform catalog management tasks, such as editing, downloading, and deleting catalogs. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Creating and Publishing a Static Customer Catalog PUBLIC 11 Customer Catalogs for CMS-Enabled Customers Some customers use the content management system (CMS) avaialble in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to manage customer catalog data. You can upload and publish customer catalogs in CIF and BMEcat format for customers who use CMS to manage catalogs. You can punch in to your customer's site to view content rules and validation errors [page 15] of catalogs that fail these rules. You can also edit and revalidate the customer catalog content within the customer's CMS. Keep the following in mind when publishing customer catalogs for CMS-enabled customers: • • • • You can't upload customer catalogs in cXML format for CMS-enabled customers. When uploading private customer catalogs on SAP Business Network, you can choose either CMS-enabled customers or customers who haven't enabled the CMS feature, but not a combination of both. You can't upload public customer catalogs for CMS-enabled customers. You can upload customer catalogs manually using the SAP Business Network customer catalog wizard or programmatically using the cXML CatalogUploadRequest transaction. Publishing customer catalogs to CMS-enabled customers involves the following high-level steps: 1. An SAP Ariba Customer Support representative enables this feature for your site and the customer's procurement site. 2. You create customer catalog files that describe products and services. You can download the CIF and BMEcat file templates or the example files that are available in the SAP Business Network customer catalog wizard to create the catalogs. 3. You set the customer catalog visibility to Private and choose the CMS-enabled customers that you want to publish the catalog to. 4. You can punch in to each of your customer's sites to view their customer catalog content rules. 5. You return to the customer catalog creation wizard on SAP Business Network, choose the catalog format, and upload the required customer catalog and image files.  Note SAP Business Network doesn't check the customer catalog for syntactic and semantic errors. 6. The customer catalog file isn't uploaded to SAP Business Network but is sent to the CMS in the customer's procurement site. The customer catalog is processed according to the content rules in the CMS. 7. Customer catalogs that fail any catalog rules set up by the customer in the CMS have a Validation Errors Found by Customer status on SAP Business Network . 8. You can punch in to the customer's CMS, fix the errors, and revalidate the catalog. 9. Validated content documents are pushed from the CMS to the Catalog Manager workspace in the customer's site for master data validation, approval and activation. 10. The status of approved and activated customer catalogs is updated in the CMS and on SAP Business Network. 12 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Customer Catalogs for CMS-Enabled Customers Uploading and Publishing Customer Catalogs for CMS-Enabled Customers You upload and publish private customer catalogs for your customers who use the CMS in SAP Ariba Buying solutions. Prerequisites • • • • We recommend that you view your customer's catalog rules before you upload a catalog. When entering filenames for the catalog, you must ensure that the filenames don't contain any spaces or special characters. Ensure that the customer catalog file size doesn't exceed 200 MB. Ensure that the customer catalog images ZIP file size doesn't exceed 200 MB. Procedure 1. On the home dashboard, click the Catalogs menu. 2. Select the Customer Catalogs option. 3. Click Create to create a standard customer catalog. 4. Enter a unique customer catalog name and a brief description of your catalog. Customers can search for customer catalogs using this information. 5. To classify the products and services in your customer catalog, do the following: a. Click Add in the Commodities section. SAP Business Network shows the Product and Service Category Selection page, which lists product and service categories, based on the United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (UNSPSC). b. On the Search tab, enter a keyword or search phrase and click Search, or click the Browse the Categories tab to drill down through commodity families, classes, and individual commodities. c. Choose a product and service category level, and click Add. The My Selections area shows the selected product and service category level.  Limitations If you are a supplier of all the items in a given product and service category level, choose the name of the higher-level product and service category instead of adding all of the lower-level product and service categories. For example, a furniture supplier should choose the category “Furniture and Furnishings” not the hundreds of individual items it sells. Customers can search for this information. d. To search for a product and service category by keyword, click the Search tab. e. Enter a search keyword and click Search. Choose a check box to select a search result, and click Add. The My Selections area shows the selected product and service category segment. f. To remove a selected product and service category segment, choose the check box next to the product and service category segment in the My Selections area, and then click Remove. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Customer Catalogs for CMS-Enabled Customers PUBLIC 13 g. Click OK. h. Click Next. The Subscriptions page in the catalog wizard lists only customers for whom the catalog is qualified. If you know customers are registered on SAP Business Network, but you can't see them, contact them directly and ask them to grant you permission to see them. 6. Set the customer catalog visibility to Private, and choose the customers that you want to publish the customer catalog to. This step creates the customer catalog subscription and automatically notifies the customers by email. You can choose either CMS-enabled customers or customers who have not enabled the CMS feature, but not a combination of both. 7. To punch in to your customer's site and view the customer catalog content rules specified by your customer, click the View link in the Catalog Validation Rules column. Click Done to return to the customer catalog creation wizard on SAP Business Network. 8. Click Next to reach the Content page. 9. Choose the format of the customer catalog that you want to publish from the Catalog File Format dropdown. 10. Click Browse to navigate to, and choose a customer catalog file. You can compress and upload large catalog files in ZIP file format to avoid time-out errors. The maximum size of a catalog file is 200 MB. 11. Click Browse to navigate to and choose a customer catalog image file. You can upload the customer catalog images file in ZIP file format only. Ensure that the path names you provide in your customer catalogs match the image directory structure. If you choose to zip the folder containing the images, the paths of the image files in the customer catalog file must contain the folder name. For more information, see the Customer Catalog Format Reference. The maximum size of a catalog images ZIP file that can be uploaded is 200 MB. 12. Click Validate And Publish.  Caution Don't navigate in your browser window until the next page appears. Interrupting your web browser stops the upload process. Next Steps The customer catalog file isn't uploaded to SAP Business Network but is sent to the CMS in your customer's procurement site. The customer catalog is then processed according to the content rules in the CMS and moves to one of the following statuses. Customer Catalog Subscription Status Description Pending Buyer Validation The customer catalog is uploaded successfully in SAP Ariba Buying solutions and is pending processing by the CMS. Validation Errors Found by Customers 14 PUBLIC The customer catalog violates one or more content rules specified in the CMS. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Customer Catalogs for CMS-Enabled Customers Customer Catalog Subscription Status Description Validated The customer catalog is successfully uploaded in SAP Ariba Buying solutions and has passed all content rules, but isn't approved by the customer yet. Approved The customer catalog is approved by the customer. Rejected The customer catalog is rejected by the customer. Activated The customer catalog is activated and available in SAP Ariba Buying solutions. Deactivated A previously activated customer catalog version is now deactivated in SAP Ariba Buying solutions. Deleted The customer catalog is deleted by the customer. Changed The customer made some changes to the catalog. Viewing Customer Catalog Validation Errors You view customer catalog validation errors in order to find out why a customer catalog failed and how to fix it. Procedure 1. On the Catalogs Customer Catalogs page, click the Validation Errors Found by Customer link in the Status column to punch in to your customer's site. The page shows the total number of items that have been imported and the number of items that failed content rules, grouped by the following statuses: Validation Error, Validation Warning, Cleansed, and Enriched. 2. Expand each item status group to view the list of rules that caused failures and the item count per rule. 3. Click an item status link to view the items that are in that particular status. For example, click the Validation Error link to view the list of items with validation errors. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Customer Catalogs for CMS-Enabled Customers PUBLIC 15 Fixing Errors and Revalidate a Customer Catalog in Your Customer's Site You can punch in to the customer's site to edit customer catalogs that have errors and revalidate them. Procedure 1. On the Catalogs Customer Catalogs page, click the Validation Errors Found by Customer link in the Status column to punch in to your customer's site. The page shows the total number of items that have been imported and the number of items that failed content rules. 2. Expand each item status group to view the list of rules that caused failures and the item count per rule. 3. Click Edit Content to edit the customer catalog. The page shows the list of items in the customer catalog. Items that failed one or more customer catalog rule conditions are indicated by icons, and the associated field values are shown in red boxes. 4. You can use the options in the See All Items dropdown to narrow the list and view items that are in a particular status. For example, choose See All Items > See Enriched Items to see only the list of items that have been enriched. 5. Click the value of the field that you want to edit, enter a new value, and click OK. Your changes are saved automatically.  Note You have to fix errors in each line individually. There is no provision to select multiple lines to edit catalog fields. 6. (Optional) Click Save to save your changes. 7. Click Revalidate to run the rules again and revalidate the entire customer catalog. 16 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Customer Catalogs for CMS-Enabled Customers Validation and Statuses for Catalogs After you upload a customer catalog, SAP Business Network validates the customer catalog to ensure that the catalog content is correctly formed. Then, SAP Business Network publishes and qualifies the catalog for the designated customers. You can view the status of each customer catalog in the list on the Catalogs Catalogs Customer page. Validation by SAP Business Network SAP Business Network validates the syntax and semantics of your customer catalog files: • • Syntactic validation ensures that a customer catalog’s content is correctly formed. For example, every catalog entry must have the correct number of fields and the content of each field must match the field’s data type. Every customer catalog file must be syntactically correct before you can publish it. During syntactic validation, SAP Business Network checks that: • • • • • • • All required fields are present. • • No invalid characters are present in any fields. No field exceeds its maximum field length. All integers and decimals are formatted correctly. Price formats are correct and a currency specified. No two items have the same combination of Supplier ID, Supplier Part ID, and Supplier Part Auxiliary ID. The character set specified in the file is valid. CIF file headers begin with a CIF version number and end with a DATA token. The DATA and ENDOFDATA tokens must exist and be in the correct locations. The lines between must be of the form key:value. Additionally, SAP Business Network displays an error if the itemcount field does not match the number of items in the file. Descriptions are present. SAP Business Network issues a warning if it encounters invalid characters in the Description field. Semantic validation ensures that a customer catalog’s content is compatible with specified customer catalog standards, such as UNSPSC commodity codes or standard unit of measure (UOM) codes. If you choose to qualify your catalog for a specific customer, SAP Business Network validates it against that customer’s catalog rules. For example, if the customer’s procurement system uses a custom commodity code set and the customer catalog uses a standard commodity code set, SAP Business Network can't validate the catalog for that customer. Your customers can choose to relax validation rules for UNSPSC, UOM, or zero price values. During semantic validation, SAP Business Network checks the units and codes listed below for each customer catalog item to ensure they are compatible with specified customer catalog standards. • Currency: An item’s currency must be valid. SAP Business Network maps currencies to translate the incoming currency names into the customer’s procurement system’s standard currency terminology. A currency is not valid unless it meets the following criteria: The value to which the code is mapped in the simple map has a corresponding Currency object. There are no empty values. SAP Business Network generates an alert for items with zero or no cost. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Validation and Statuses for Catalogs PUBLIC 17 • Unit of measure (UOM): An item’s unit of measure must be valid based on the UOM code specified in the catalog header. If a customer catalog doesn't use the customer’s canonical units of measure, the customer must define a mapping file to be sure that the incoming terminology is interpreted correctly. • Commodity code: An item must have at least one domain-specific commodity code that maps to a supported commodity code specified in the catalog header. You can override the commodity code at the line-item level. SAP Business Network supports UNSPSC, eCl@ss, NAICS, and ISICS commodity codes, but only validates UNSPSC commodity codes. As of 2024-05-24, the supported UNSPSC version was updated to v25.9. You can download the UNSPSC Codeset v25.9 from UNSPSC Codeset Downloads . Free version: Link (login needed) • Supplier ID: An item’s Supplier ID must match the ANID or D-U-N-S number of your supplier organization as specified in the customer catalog header file. • • • URL formats: The Supplier URL and Manufacturer URL must have http:// along with the URL string. Start/Expiration Dates: The item’s Start Date must be before the expiration date. Territory and Language: The Territory and Language codes must validate against the ISO 3166-1 and 3166-2 codes and Java locale codes. Your Customers' Catalog Validation Rules To view your customers’ catalog validation rules, go to the Subscriptions page of the SAP Business Network customer catalog wizard, and then click the View link in the Catalog Validation Rules column next to the customer's name. Alternatively, you can punch into the customer's site to view the customer catalog preferences. In some cases, when you punch in to the customer's site for the first time, you might see the following error message: Cannot access customer's site. Your buying organization must approve your access to their system before you proceed with this action. Please try again later. This error occurs when your customer hasn't approved your access to their procurement site. You should contact your customer to ask for access to their site.  Note SAP Business Network doesn't validate customer catalogs published for CMS-enabled customers. Validation Errors on Customer Catalogs After you upload a customer catalog file, the catalog might have errors that prevent it from being published to your customers. To view details of the validation errors, do one of the following: • • 18 Go to your customer's site to view the error details. Check the error information in email notifications sent by SAP Business Network. PUBLIC Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Validation and Statuses for Catalogs • On the Catalogs column. Customer Catalogs page, click the Errors Found by Customer link in the Status To resolve a catalog error [page 20], you can either upload a modified version of the customer catalog that meets your customer’s requirements or contact your customer to ask them to disable a requirement. After correcting customer catalog errors on SAP Business Network, you must ensure that you make the same changes to the customer catalog file on your computer so the errors don't reappear.  Limitations For cXMLcustomer catalogs, you can't fix problems within your account. Instead, fix the file locally on your computer and click Update content to upload the updated version [page 24]. Customer Catalog Statuses Use the following table to interpret the different customer catalog subscription statuses. Status Description Received, Pending Buyer Validation The customer catalog is uploaded successfully in SAP Ariba Buying solutions and is pending validation from your customer. Customer catalogs published to all other procurement customers have a Published status. Validation Errors Found by Customers The customer catalog failed during validation against your customer’s catalog rules in SAP Ariba Buying solutions. To view details of the error, click the Validation Errors Found by Customer link for this catalog on the catalog dashboard and view details of the error message by punching into your customer’s site. Validated The customer catalog is successfully uploaded in SAP Ariba Buying solutions and has passed validation, but your customer hasn't approved it yet. Approved Your customer approved the catalog. Rejected Your customer rejected the catalog. Activated Your customer activated the catalog and made it available in SAP Ariba Buying solutions. Deactivated A customer catalog version activated earlier is now deactivated. Customer catalogs can change back and forth between Activated and Deactivated statuses. Deleted Your customer deleted the catalog. Changed Your customer made some changes to the catalog. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Validation and Statuses for Catalogs PUBLIC 19 Correcting Errors in CIF Files You fix errors in yourcustomer catalog files so you can reload them and publish them successfully to your customers. Procedure 1. On the home dashboard, click the Catalogs Customer Catalogs . 2. Click a customer catalog name to view more information about it, or choose a customer catalog and click View/Edit. 3. Click the Errors Found status link. 4. To customize your view of the error list, click the table options icon in the upper right of the Catalog Validation Errors table, and then do one or all of the following: • To add or remove columns from view, check or uncheck them in the Show/Hide Columns section of the table menu. • To group errors by a specific column, choose the column name in the Group by Column section of the menu. • To export the errors to Excel, choose an option in the Export to Excel section of the menu. 5. When you are ready to view an error, click a line number or an error description. If the error is in the customer catalog body, you're taken to a page where you can edit the line item. If the error is in the customer catalog header, you'll see a text box for editing just the header. 6. For each error, enter a new value to replace the old value.  Tip For information about syntax for CIF files, see the Catalog format reference. 7. Click Update to submit your changes. SAP Business Network validates your changes and, if you selected a customer during upload, qualifies the catalog for that customer. It also revalidates the customer catalog against all qualified customers to ensure that you have introduced no new errors. 8. To delete a line from the customer catalog, do the following: • • Click the Content page to view all the catalog items. Click Delete in the Action column for the item that you want to delete. The line is deleted and the status of the customer catalog is updated in the customer catalog dashboard. 20 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Correcting Errors in CIF Files

Prerequisites • If you use Windows Notepad to edit customer catalogs, do not click the “Save as Unicode” check box. For the same reason, if you use Microsoft Word, do not select “Unicode Text” as the file type. Raw Unicode (also known as UCS-2) is not file-safe because its byte order varies depending on the operating system.  Limitations • You can't edit customer catalogs over 4 MB in size online. Download large catalogs [page 26], edit them on your computer [page 22], and then upload them to SAP Business Network. • • You can't view or edit cXML catalogs online. You can't edit Excel customer catalogs online; edit them on your computer in Microsoft Excel and upload them to your account. Procedure 1. On the home dashboard, click Catalogs Customer Catalogs . 2. Click the name of the customer catalog you want to edit, or choose the customer catalog and click View/Edit. 3. Click Next to view the Content step of the customer catalog wizard. SAP Business Network shows a list of line items in the catalog. 4. If the customer catalog you want to edit has already been published, you must create a new version to edit it. Click Create New Version, update the information on the Details page, and click Next. 5. Do one of the following: • • To delete an item, click Delete in the Action column next to the item. To add an item, click Add Item. You'll see a page where you can enter field values for the new item.  Tip For information about CIF syntax and format, see the Customer Catalog Format Reference. 6. If you added or deleted any items, click Update Header Data on the Contents page to edit the catalog header details. 7. After updating the customer catalog header details, click Next. 22 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Editing CIF Catalogs Online  Note If SAP Business Network finds any errors, they are indicated on the Errors page. Click the item number of the item with the error to correct it. 8. On the Subscriptions page, configure the customer catalog visibility. 9. Click Validate and Publish to publish the new version of the customer catalog. Next Steps After editing customer catalogs directly in your SAP Business Network account, be sure to make the same changes to the customer catalog files on your computer so the old values don't reappear. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Editing CIF Catalogs Online PUBLIC 23 Updating or Deleting Your Customer Catalog Files You can update customer catalog files when there are updates to your offerings or pricing. When a customer catalog subscription no longer applies, you can delete if from SAP Business Network. Context Keep the following points in mind when editing and uploading customer catalogs: • You change the customer catalog by uploading another customer catalog. A new version of a customer catalog is created on SAP Business Network when a customer catalog is edited or a new customer catalog file is uploaded. SAP Business Network continues to store the previous versions of your customer catalog, but only the latest version is visible. • Upload the entire updated customer catalog, not just the changes; SAP Business Network doesn't merge partial customer catalogs. • Avoid changing customer catalog formats (CIF or cXML). While SAP Business Network doesn't prevent you from changing customer catalog formats during an update, it's important to use the same format for all versions of a customer catalog subscription. • If the customer catalog contains numerous errors, it's easier to fix the original file and upload it again. If you update an existing customer catalog that SAP Business Network validated in the past, it might no longer pass validation when you upload it because of one or both of the following: • • • SAP Business Network’s semantic validation checking was less sophisticated. Your customer’s catalog validation rules changed after you last validated the catalog. When updating a customer catalog, you don't need to create a new standard customer catalog.You can use an existing customer catalog, but make sure not to change the existing name for the customer catalog subscription when you upload a new version. This step is critical for your customer to be able to accurately update existing catalogs when a new version is available. You can access previous versions of a customer catalog by deleting the current version. Deleting customer catalogs removes them from SAP Business Network. Customers can no longer view them online or download them. When a new version is created or a current version is deleted, SAP Business Network sends an automatic notification to all customers that subscribed to it. Publishing your updated customer catalog sends automatic notification to any customers that subscribed to it. For private catalogs, customers receive notification only if you select them and they request notification. Customers that you don't select won't receive notifications, even if they request it. Procedure 1. On the home dashboard, click 24 PUBLIC Catalogs Customer Catalogs . Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Updating or Deleting Your Customer Catalog Files 2. Choose a catalog, and do one of the following: • • To edit a customer catalog, click View/Edit. To delete only the latest version of a customer catalog, choose Delete > Latest Version Only. SAP Business Network reverts to the previous version of the customer catalog, if one exists.  Note Use this feature if the latest version you uploaded has problems and you want to go back to the previous version or upload a new version. • To delete all versions of a customer catalog, choose Delete > All Versions. SAP Business Network deletes all versions of the customer catalog and removes the customer catalog name. 3. To add product and service categories, click Add in the Commodities section, and then choose from the available product and service categories on the Product and Service Category page. 4. Click Next to view the Content step of the catalog wizard. SAP Business Network shows a list of line items in the customer catalog. 5. Click Upload Catalog File to replace the existing customer catalog file. 6. Click Browse to find the location of the customer catalog file on your computer.  Tip Use the same customer catalog filename for all versions of a catalog subscription. Using the same name makes catalog management easier for customers. 7. Click Validate and Publish to publish a new version of the customer catalog. Related Information Editing CIF Catalogs Online [page 22] Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Updating or Deleting Your Customer Catalog Files PUBLIC 25 Viewing and Downloading Your Customer Catalogs You can view details and validation errors for your created and published customer catalogs. You can download catalog files from SAP Business Network if you’ve lost your local copies or need to verify their contents. Prerequisites • You have a role with the Catalog Management permission on SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network supplier homepage, choose Catalogs Customer Catalogs . The Customer Catalogs page opens and lists your customer catalogs, grouped by customer name. 2. To show or hide columns in the catalogs table, click the  (Settings) icon and select or deselect columns in the dialog box. The following table columns are available: Column Name Description Customer The name of the customer to whom the catalog has been published. If a catalog is published to multiple customers, the catalog row shows up multiple times for each customer. Catalog Name The unique name of the customer catalog. File Name The name of the customer catalog file. Version The version number of the customer catalog. When you edit or update an existing customer catalog, SAP Business Network creates a new version and assigns a version number. SAP Business Network continues to store the previous versions of your catalog, but only the latest version is visible. You can access previous versions by deleting the current version. Full/Incremental The load mode of a split catalog file. When uploading a large catalog file, you can split it into smaller files and set the Loadmode column to "F" (full) for the first file and to "I" (incremental) for subsequent files. SAP Business Network combines these split files and processes them as a single catalog. Catalog Type 26 PUBLIC The customer catalog file type. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Viewing and Downloading Your Customer Catalogs Column Name Description Created By The name of the customer catalog creator. Created On The date the customer catalog was uploaded to SAP Business Network. Status The status of the customer catalog, including: • Status on SAP Business Network: Whether the customer catalog was uploaded and published successfully on SAP Business Network. • Status received from customer's system: Whether the customer catalog passed validation in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions. When the customer catalog fails validation in SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, a status update is sent to SAP Business Network and shown on the Customer Catalogs page. If SAP Business Network doesn't receive a status update for the customer catalog, the SAP Business Network catalog status remains. 3. To search for a customer catalog, enter a catalog name or customer name in the search box, set values in the Catalog Type, Customer, Created On filters, and click Go. You can also use the quick status filters to locate catalogs based on their current status. The number next to each icon shows the number of catalogs with that status. For example, click the Errors icon to list all catalogs with errors. 4. Click the name of a customer catalog to open its details page. You can do the following on the details page: • View general catalog information, including catalog description, relevant commodity codes, item count, and catalog status, etc. • • • Download the customer catalog file by clicking the Download button under Content. View the customers to whom the catalog is published, and check their catalog validation preferences. View error details such as line number, field, and description in the error tables, or export the error list for offline review. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Viewing and Downloading Your Customer Catalogs PUBLIC 27 Excel CIF Template If you prefer to manage customer catalog content with spreadsheets, SAP Ariba provides a Microsoft Excel template containing the required information and an Excel-to-CIF converter. The Excel format CIF template helps you fill in the various fields for items in your customer catalogs.  Note Your customer's purchasing system recognizes CIF files, but not Excel catalogs. To convert Excel catalogs to CIF, you can either use the SAP Business Network Excel-to-CIF converter, or you can convert them yourself. It can also convert CIF files back to Excel format for downloading. Editing the Excel CIF Template Procedure 1. To get the CIF file template, create a new standard customer catalog, and find the template on the Content step of the customer catalog wizard. 2. After you download and save the template, open the file in Excel.  Tip The CIF template contains useful descriptions of each field. To read them, put your pointer on the red comment markers. 3. Review the customer catalog header to make sure the fields are correct. For example: CODEFORMAT: UNSPSC CURRENCY: USD SUPPLIERID_DOMAIN: NETWORK ID  Note Specify currency names with ISO 4217 three-letter (CodeA) currency codes. 4. Enter your customer catalog data into the body fields.  Remember For each customer catalog item, you must enter values for the first seven fields (or columns). Ensure that your entries don't exceed the field sizes (the Excel CIF template contains comments that indicate the field size). 5. To calculate the number of customer catalog items for the ITEMCOUNT field, subtract the number of the last line of data from the number of the first line of data, and then add one. 28 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Excel CIF Template 6. Save the file as an Excel (.xls) file. Opening CIF Files in Excel Procedure 1. In Excel, choose File > Open. 2. Choose the CIF file. Excel shows the Text Import Wizard. 3. Select Delimited and then click Next. 4. Select Comma as the delimiter and quote (") as the text qualifier. 5. Uncheck Tab. 6. Click Next. 7. Select all columns in your spreadsheet, select Text as the column data format, and then click Finish.  Tip Treat all columns as text so that Excel retains any leading or trailing zeros. 8. To make the resulting spreadsheet more readable, select all cells and choose Format > Column > AutoFit Selection. Saving Excel Files as CIF To convert to CIF manually, you save the Excel file to CSV format and delete extra commas with a text editor. Procedure 1. In Excel, choose File > Save As. 2. Select CSV (MS-DOS) as the file type. Excel inserts a comma between each field. 3. Enter an meaningful name for the file.  Example The recommended format is < catalog_description >_< customer_name >; for example, workchairs_acme. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Excel CIF Template PUBLIC 29 4. Click Save. 5. To remove extra commas in the CIF file, open the file in Notepad, Wordpad, or another ASCII text editor. 6. Delete extra commas from the header and the body. 7. Ensure that the leading or trailing zeros weren't deleted. 8. Save the file. 9. Change the file extension from .csv to .cif. Excel CIF Template Fields The following table provides an overview of the fields that are available in the CIF template. For each customer catalog item, you must enter the following values: Field Description Supplier ID Your SAP Business Network ID (ANID) or D-U-N-S number: • View your ANID at the bottom of any SAP Business Network page or by clicking Company Settings in the upper right corner of your dashboard. • Look up your organization’s D-U-N-S number on the Dun & Bradstreet website . Item Description A description of the customer catalog item. Don't use abbreviations. SPSC Code Enter the catalog item’s United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (UNSPSC). To find the appropriate code, search for catalog standards in the help center. As of 2024-05-24, the supported UNSPSC version was updated to v25.9. You can download the UNSPSC Codeset v25.9 from UNSPSC Codeset Downloads . Free version: Link (login needed) The commodity codes used in catalogs support ECCMA version 13.5. However, SAP Business Network can translate any earlier version to 13.5 and vice versa. Unit Price Enter the price per unit for the customer catalog item. Specify numbers as you want them to appear to users. For example, for $19.50, enter “19.50” (include the trailing zero). Do not include the currency symbol ($). Unit of Measure Enter the unit of measure for the customer catalog item using the United Nations Units of Measure (UNUOM) standard 30 PUBLIC . For a list of UNUOM codes, search for UN UOM in the help center. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Excel CIF Template

file://SBN/split/Creating and Managing C.content: Setting Up a PunchOut Catalog Creating PunchOut Configuration Context PunchOut catalogs are interactive catalogs stored on your website that use the pre-defined PunchOut configuration to enable two-way communication of electronic commerce details. A PunchOut catalog allows your customer's purchasing system to communicate with live catalog content on your website, which often provides a better shopping experience for your customers and reduces your workload. In your customer's purchasing system, PunchOut catalogs show a hyperlink instead of product or pricing details. When users click this hyperlink, their web browser leads them to a page from your local website. Depending on how you implement this page, users can browse product options, specify configurations, and choose delivery methods. Your customer's system passes organization IDs to your website, and you can use them to look up previously agreed-upon prices (contract prices). When users finish with this page, they click a button that returns the order information to their purchasing system. The fully configured products and their prices appear within the purchasing system on users’ purchase orders. PunchOut catalogs allow you to leverage existing resources from simple online catalogs to advanced e-commerce sites. PunchOut catalogs can also use search engines to find items on your website. Use PunchOut catalogs for: • Products with a large number of configurations and options; for example, many colors or sizes, or many delivery methods (overnight, two-day, or five-day). • • • Inventories containing more than a few thousand items. • • Products whose specifications or prices change often. Products whose prices are based on prearranged contracts (custom pricing). Products, such as nameplates or business cards that must be customized for each customer. (Alternatively, your customers can implement custom catalog forms in the purchasing system, which allow users to attach personalized data to a purchase order). Products with advanced pricing details. When deciding whether to use PunchOut catalogs, consider the following tradeoffs: • • They require all users to have full Internet access, which some companies don't allow. They require you to implement and maintain an interactive website, accessible 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Even if your account is suspended, your customers can still access your PunchOut catalogs, shop for products and services, and create a purchase order; however, SAP Business Network doesn't send you the purchase order. For more information about suspended accounts, see Managing Subscription Services. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Setting Up a PunchOut Catalog PUBLIC 31 PunchOut catalog users don't need to enter a user password for your site. They are pre-authenticated by SAP Business Network. For information on how to implement a PunchOut website, see the cXML Reference Guide Solutions Guide. and the cXML  Note You must ensure that your PunchOut website’s use of cookies and online tracking is compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the ePrivacy Regulation (ePR). SAP Ariba recommends that you use appropriate tools to test your site to ensure that it is GDPR and ePR compliant. These tools might indicate you to make changes such as, removing all external http references, and having a single cookie policy for site visitors. Procedure 1. On the home dashboard, click the Catalogs menu. 2. Select Customer Catalogs option. 3. Click PunchOut Configuration Create . 4. Enter information about your PunchOut configuration. Customers can search each of these fields. Note the following: a. In the PunchOut URL section, you must enter the prefix https:// for the PunchOut URL value.  Note If the Profile URL is already specified on the cXML Setup page, then SAP Business Network uses the Profile URL instead of the PunchOut URL. b. In the Visibility section, choose who should see your catalog: • Public: SAP Business Network makes your catalog visible to all customers. To receive a catalog, a customer must establish a relationship with you. • Private: SAP Business Network makes your catalog visible only to customers that you specify. You can choose this option for catalogs that contain contract prices. c. In the Authentication section, select an authentication type, either Default authentication or Customized authentication. • Default authentication: SAP Business Network uses the authentication type specified on the Settings Electronic Order Routing Configure cXML (native) integration cXML Setup page. For more information about how to configure authentication type on the cXML Setup page, see How to configure an Ariba Network account for cXML routing section in the Configuring Document Routing Guide. • Customized authentication: SAP Business Network allows you to select a customized authentication type to access the PunchOut catalog. In the Authentication method dropdown, select either Shared Secret or Certificate option. • 32 PUBLIC Shared Secret: To use this option, enter a confidential text string to use as the shared secret. Make certain your shared secret is different from your account password. All cXML documents passed between SAP Business Network and your cXML application contain this shared secret for authentication. Shared secrets are simple to set up, are free, and require little maintenance. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Setting Up a PunchOut Catalog If you forget your shared secret, SAP Ariba Support must reset it. Choose Contact Administrator from the Help menu, and request your administrator to reset your shared secret. • Certificate: To use this option, purchase and maintain a digital certificate signed by a trusted certificate authority. Paste the signed client certificate into the Certificate text box. Your website and SAP Business Network use this certificate for cXML authentication. You can also provide a backup digital certificate. SAP Business Network uses the backup certificate if your primary certificate becomes invalid. Backup certificates are useful when your primary certificate expires or when you need to perform certificate maintenance. Digital certificates require more setup steps, cost money, and expire, but your organization’s security strategy may require that you use them. d. In the Pricing updates section, choose an option to the enable the customer to receive pricing updates (applies only to Level 2 PunchOut items). Choose one of the following: • • Use the PunchOut Site URL: If you want to specify the same URL as the PunchOut URL. Custom URL: If you want to enter a specific URL for customers to punch in and view the pricing updates for the catalog items. e. Enable the Server name indication toggle button to use SNI for establishing connection to the specified PunchOut URL. 5. Click OK.  Note SAP Business Network now forwards all PunchOut requests to the specified URL. Results You can review the status of the catalog that has been published. If the catalog contains errors, correct the errors and try to publish it again. For more information see Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs [page 3]. Creating and Publishing PunchOut Catalogs To create PunchOut catalogs, you can define the level 1 index file settings that are applicable across buyers either on the PunchOut Configuration listing page or on the PunchOut catalog creation page to pre-fill the required fields automatically while creating a PunchOut catalog. Prerequisites • We recommend that you view your customer's catalog validation rules [page 17] before you upload a catalog. Validation checks the catalog for syntactic and semantic errors and also for compatibility with the catalog rules set by specific customers. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Setting Up a PunchOut Catalog PUBLIC 33 • Catalog filenames must contain only the following characters: A – Z, a – z, 0 – 9, period (.), dash (-), and underscore (_). Procedure 1. On the home dashboard, click the Catalogs menu. 2. Select Customer Catalogs option. 3. Click Create to create a PunchOut catalog. SAP Business Network displays the first page of the SAP Business Network create catalog wizard. 4. Enter a unique catalog name and a brief description of your PunchOut catalog. Customers can search for catalogs using this information. 5. To classify the products and services in your catalog, do the following: a. Click Add in the Commodities section. SAP Business Network shows the Product and Service Category Selection page, which lists product and service categories, based on the United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (UNSPSC). b. On the Search tab, enter a keyword or search phrase and click Search, or click the Browse the Categories tab to drill down through commodity families, classes, and individual commodities. c. Choose a product and service category level, and click Add. The My Selections area shows the selected product and service category level.  Limitations If you are a supplier of all the items in a given product and service category level, choose the name of the higher-level product and service category instead of adding all of the lower-level product and service categories. For example, a furniture supplier should choose the category “Furniture and Furnishings” not the hundreds of individual items it sells. Customers can search for this information. d. To search for a product and service category by keyword, click the Search tab. e. Enter a search keyword and click Search. Select the required check box to select a search result, and click Add. The My Selections area shows the selected product and service category segment. f. To remove a selected product and service category segment, choose the check box next to the product and service category segment in the My Selections area, and then click Remove. g. Click OK. 6. Select PunchOut Level 1 check box to use the specified index file settings for your PunchOut catalog. 7. To add the index file settings if not defined earlier or to edit the existing index file settings that are defined already, do the following: a. Click You can add/edit your index file settings here link. You can also add or edit the index file settings on the PunchOut Configuration listing page before creating a PunchOut catalog. Click Level 1 Index File Settings: Add link before creating a PunchOut catalog to add the index file settings. Click Level 1 Index File Settings: View/Edit link to view and make changes to the defined index file settings. b. Choose your supplier ID. • • 34 PUBLIC ANID: Your Ariba Network ID (ANID) will be displayed by default on selecting the ANID option. DUNS: Your organization’s D-U-N-S number will be displayed by default on selecting the DUNS option. Creating and Managing Customer Catalogs Setting Up a PunchOut Catalog c. Enter a keyword that can be used for searching a supplier in SAP Ariba Buying. d. Enter a short name for your catalog file which will be displayed as a button in the procurement system. e. Click OK. 8. Click Next. The Subscriptions page in the catalog wizard lists only customers for whom the catalog is qualified. If you know that customers are registered on SAP Business Network, but you can't see them, contact them directly and ask them to grant you permission to see them. 9. Enter the keyword filter (Supplier Part ID) that is used to filter your webshop catalog views. 10. Choose who should see your catalog: • Private: SAP Business Network makes your catalog visible only to customers that you specify. You can choose this option for catalogs that contain contract prices. This option automatically creates a subscription to the catalog for all customers you choose. • Public: SAP Business Network makes your catalog visible to all customers. To receive a catalog, a customer must establish a relationship with you.  Note If you set the visibility to Private, you can choose customers or customer groups, which creates the catalog subscriptions and automatically notifies the selected customers by email. 11. Choose your catalog item’s code from the Catalog code list box and enter the version of the specified catalog code. SAP Business Network supports UNSPSC, ECLASS, and Custom codes, but only validates UNSPSC codes. 12. To punch in to your customer's site and view the catalog content rules specified by your customer, click the View link in the Catalog Validation Rules column. Click Done to return to the catalog creation wizard on SAP Business Network. 13. Click Next to display the Content page. The details on the Content page are displayed automatically as per the specified index file settings. 14. Click Validate And Publish. SAP Business Network, validates and publishes the catalog. The created catalog will be displayed on the catalog files listing page. Your customers are subscribed to the current catalog version and are notified of its availability. Next Steps After SAP Business Network completes validation, it changes the catalog status from Validating to one of the following statuses: • • • Validated means that your catalog is error-free. Published means that your private catalog has been validated and published. Errors Found by means that SAP Business Network detected catalog content that violates syntactic validation rules, standards-based semantic validation rules, or a customer’s catalog rules. Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Content PUBLIC 5 Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos This guide is for SAP Ariba users responsible for creating and managing invoices, credit memos, and debit memos on SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network is a hosted service that connects suppliers to buying organizations, allowing them to conduct transactions over the internet. This guide applies to: • • • • • SAP Business Network SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing SAP Ariba Invoice Management SAP Ariba Contract Invoicing Related Guides SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Integration and Configuration Guide 6 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Invoicing in SAP Business Network SAP Business Network supports the creation, validation and routing of electronic invoices and credit memos. Invoices are detailed statements of products delivered or services rendered, and associated charges for one or more purchase orders or contracts. In SAP Business Network, the buyer (your customer) sets the invoicing rules that determine which fields and actions are available when you create an invoice. For more information, see the SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Features and Functions. Buyers allow their suppliers to create the following types of invoices: • • • • • • Invoices against purchase orders. [page 10] Invoices against contracts [page 31] by accessing the buyers’ contract collaboration sites. Service invoices against service purchase orders. [page 40] Non-PO invoices. [page 28] PO-based and non-PO credit memos. [page 61] Invoices in comma-separated values (CSV) format [page 75] and import them into SAP Business Network. You can then create an invoice by: • • • • Posting a cXML (via HTTPS) or EDI message (via VAN or AS2) to the SAP Business Network. Using the Generate Invoice feature to create an online invoice form (PO Invoice, non-PO Invoice, service invoice, or a credit memo). Uploading a CSV file with invoice data. Punching into your customer’s procurement site and creating a contract-based invoice. PO-based and service invoices are both considered standard invoices. For information on how to implement EDI or cXML invoice transmittal, please see the respective documentation resources available in the Product Documentation For Administrators section of the Learning Center.  Note Some countries/regions require suppliers to digitally sign invoices to assure authenticity. If you or your customer are located in one of those countries/regions, the invoices you submit are automatically digitally signed on your behalf. A message at the top of the invoice entry page indicates when an invoice will be digitally signed, and after you submit the invoice, you receive a confirmation message of the signature. Prerequisites for Creating Invoices Buyers must specifically allow suppliers to submit invoices through the SAP Business Network to them. If a buyer has disabled the invoicing feature for you, then you will not have access to the invoicing functionality when reviewing the buyer’s purchase orders and you will not be able to enter non-PO invoices for those buyers. If you attempt to send automated invoices using cXML or EDI to those buyers, those invoices will be automatically rejected. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Invoicing in SAP Business Network PUBLIC 7 Buyers can configure their own specific set of invoice rules which might differ by supplier or originating country/ region of the invoice. After a buyer has enabled you for invoicing, you can view that buyer’s invoice rules in the Customer Relationship section in your account. If you want to add pricing details to line items when creating non-PO invoices, buyers must configure rules that allow you to do so. Restrictions When Creating Invoices You cannot create either PO-based header-level or line item credit memos against purchase orders that contain item groups unless the purchase order contains at least one service line. You must create credit memos against those purchase orders either using non-PO credit memos, in a third-party system, or as part of the service invoice flow based on service sheets. Temporary Pricing in PO-Based Invoices Your customer might send you purchase orders with temporary pricing to allow you to start the order fulfilment process while the final price negotiations are still going on. Depending on the specific business practices, the entire purchase order might be flagged for temporary pricing, or pricing might not be final for one or more line items. If the entire purchase order is flagged to indicate that pricing is not final, you cannot create an invoice for it until you receive a change order with the final price. If the purchase order includes line items where the price is not final, you can invoice only the line items with final prices, and the line items with temporary prices are not transferred to the invoice document when you create a PO-based invoice. You can invoice the remaining line items only after receiving a change order with the final price for them. SAP Business Network provides indication and messaging to help you identify purchase orders and line items where the pricing is not final. Related Information Taxes, Shipping, Special Handling, and Discounts on Invoices [page 53] Allowances and Charges on Invoices [page 57] Existing Invoices [page 83] Invoice Attachments Depending on each customer’s invoice rules, you may be allowed or required to attach files to an invoice. Attachments can give more explanation or supporting information for an invoice, such as proof of delivery or terms and conditions. 8 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Invoicing in SAP Business Network  Note Do not attach a file to an invoice unless your customer has specifically requested the information. Invoice-Based Workbench Tiles Create custom invoice-based workbench tiles to more easily find and take action on your invoices. Invoices is the most basic tile for users who manage invoices. Invoice-based tiles contain invoices and the list view displays information such as customer, invoice number, reference document, invoice amount, and status. On the workbench, depending on your customer's transaction rules, your user permissions, and document status, you can view the invoices and any referenced documents, create line-item credit and debit memos, and edit or copy invoices. The workbench offers the following invoice tiles: • • • • • • • • • • • Invoices Rejected invoices Invoices pending approval Invoices pending payment Invoice Conversions Invoice Conversions Draft Invoice Conversions for Review Draft invoices Paid invoices Overdue invoices (Approved) Overdue invoices (Not approved) You can filter invoice tiles on values such as Customers, Invoice number, Order number, Creation date, Invoice status, Invoice type, Routing status, Min amount and Max amount (with Currency), External invoice number, Payment net due date, From country, To country, Status change date, Approved date, Rejected date, and Paid date. Related Information The Workbench Workbench Tile Reference Customizing Tiles on Your Workbench Filtering Workbench Tiles Customizing Workbench Columns Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Invoicing in SAP Business Network PUBLIC 9 PO-Based Invoices When your customer sends you a purchase order through SAP Business Network, you can create a standard PO-based invoice from the purchase order if it does not contain item groups or require service sheets. When you create a PO-based invoice, you “flip” the purchase order information into an invoice and then add taxes (and other charges, as required) and make any necessary line item modifications. This is also called PO-Flip. The figure below shows the basic flow for purchase order based invoicing: Figure 1: Basic Flow for PO-Based Invoicing When you create an invoice, SAP Business Network validates the invoice with the invoice rules set by your customer. For more information on invoice rules, see SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing. Prerequisites You must have Inbox Access, Outbox Access, and Invoice Generation user permissions to be able to create and manage invoices. Your customer must also enable certain invoice rule settings to allow you to add or edit the line items with advanced pricing details. Restrictions You cannot create a PO-based invoice for any purchase order that contains item groups. You must invoice those purchase orders either using non-PO invoices or in a third-party system instead. If the purchase order contains service lines that require service sheets, you must create a service invoice [page 40] instead. Helpful Hints Useful tips to follow for service lines and Evaluated Receipt Settlements while creating PO-based invoices.
