file://SBN/split/Creating and Managing I.content: • General and labor service lines do not require service sheets, and you invoice them using PO-based invoices. You can also add general and labor service lines to PO-based invoices; these lines are line items with a specific type for services. • Service lines in service orders involve a separate workflow. Service lines generally require service sheets, which are then used to create service invoices. [page 40] • If you are unable to create an invoice for a blanket purchase order, it may be past the expiration date of the purchase order, and your buyer does not accept transactions against expired blanket purchase orders. ERS items • You cannot create invoices against purchase orders flagged for ERS at the header level. However, if a purchase order does not have items flagged for ERS at the header level, but has items at the line-level, you can create an invoice for non-ERS items at the line level in SAP Business Network. • Buyers can send purchase orders with both ERS and non-ERS items to SAP Business Network. However, while creating a PO-based invoice against this purchase order, SAP Business Network automatically removes the ERS-based items and keeps only the non-ERS items on the invoice. Creating a PO-Based Invoice [page 11] Creating or Modifying PO-Based Invoice Line Items [page 13] Creating a PO-Based Invoice for Shipped or Received Quantities Only [page 14] Creating an Invoice or Credit Memo Based on a Receipt Reversal [page 18] Creating PO-Based Invoices Automatically from Receipts [page 19] Creating PO-Based Invoices Automatically from Service Entry Sheets [page 22] Searching for a Unit of Measure on an Invoice [page 24] Self-Billing Invoices [page 25] Creation of Invoices Against Enhanced-Limit Material Items [page 27] Creating a PO-Based Invoice Use this procedure to create a standard PO-based invoice from the purchase order. Prerequisites See PO-Based Invoices [page 10]. Procedure 1. To create an invoice, perform one of the following actions: Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices PUBLIC 11 • Choose Orders Standard Invoice • Choose Orders Purchase Orders or Orders Orders and Releases , and then click Purchase Orders or Orders Orders and Releases , and then choose the radio button next to the purchase order or blanket purchase order, and then choose Standard Invoice Actions to the right of the purchase order or blanket purchase order. Create Invoice at the bottom of the page. • On an order-based workbench tile, such as Orders, New orders, or Orders to invoice, choose Standard invoice from the Actions column to the right of the purchase order. • While viewing an invoice, choose Create Invoice Standard Invoice .  Note If your customer has masked certain values (masked fields show a value of Undisclosed on the blanket purchase order), the values in the Quantity, Subtotal, and Price fields are also masked in the Create Invoice page. If you create an invoice that exceeds the amount in the blanket purchase order, SAP Business Network shows an error message. 2. On the Create Invoice page, enter an invoice number (Invoice #), invoice date and other header-level information about the invoice in the Summary area.  Note The invoice number uniquely identifies the invoice, typically with a value from an internal system such as a billing application. The invoice number is case-sensitive, and it can include numbers and letters. 3. (Optional) Enter header-level taxes, shipping, special handling, and discounts [page 53]. 4. (Optional) Enter allowances and charges [page 57]. 5. Click View/Edit Addresses in the Summary, Shipping, and Additional Fields sections to review or edit address details. 6. Add other elements such as payment terms, comments, or attachments by clicking Add to Header and choosing from the available options. 7. In the Additional Information section, enter any other information that your customer requests. 8. Click Update on the top or bottom of the page to update any calculated fields if you add or modify any amount or rate fields. 9. Enter or modify line item information [page 13] for the invoice. If you are creating an invoice for a blanket purchase order with advanced pricing details, you need to specify advanced pricing details for the line items. 10. Click Next.  Note If your customer requires bank details on invoices but you haven't added bank information to your remittance address, you'll receive an error message on the invoice. Below the error on the invoice you're creating, you can click Add bank accounts details to configure your remittance address with bank information. After you add bank information, you are returned to the invoice entry page and can submit the invoice to your customer. The remittance address is also saved for future invoices. If you don't have permission to update remittance information, you'll see a link to contact your account administrator. 11. Review the invoice and make any final changes. 12. Click Submit. 12 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices Creating or Modifying PO-Based Invoice Line Items Use this procedure to add or remove line items for a PO-based invoice. You also can add tax lines, discounts, or special handling for line items. Prerequisites See PO-Based Invoices [page 10]. Procedure 1. If you have not already created an invoice for the PO, create one [page 11]. If the Create Invoice or Edit Invoice page is not already open for the invoice you want to work with, find the invoice [page 83], and click the invoice number to open it. 2. Review the invoice detail lines displayed from the purchase order. PO line items with a green check mark in the Include column have not been previously invoiced or have been partially invoiced. These line items will be included in the invoice you are creating. • To exclude a line item from the invoice you are creating, click the green check mark (the check mark turns gray and details are no longer visible). This removes the item from the invoice you are creating but retains it on the invoice entry page so you can include the line item in later invoices. • Select a line and click Delete to remove it completely from the Create Invoice page. You cannot add a deleted line back to the current invoice without starting the invoice creation process over again. • To add line item details for a fully invoiced line item (Quantity is 0), such as shipping charges, click the icon in the Include column to include information about the line item in the current invoice.  Note If the buyer has enabled a rule preventing a change of the line-item description, you cannot change the line-item description from the one provided in the purchase order. Similarly, you cannot enter zero as the line-item quantity or line-item price, if the buyer has enabled rules preventing the use of zero for either of these. 3. To quickly add tax lines, discount and/or special handling to all included line items, do the following: 1. Make sure that Line level tax is selected in the Tax area of the invoice header. 2. Under Insert Line Item Options in the line level service table, select Tax Category. 3. Select a tax type from the Tax Category pull-down menu and enter tax information. 4. Click the check boxes next to Discount and Special Handling as required. 5. Click Add to Included Lines to add the selected types of detail lines to all lines with a green check mark in the Included column. For tax lines, it adds the specific tax information to each included line. 4. To add sections to selected detail lines, do the following: 1. Select one or more line items for which you want to add additional data entry sections. You can add additional line item details, such as special handling, individual items that are in the invoice. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices PUBLIC 13 2. Click Line Item Actions and select the types of fields to add from the available options. 3. Enter information in the fields for the selected lines. 5. To add additional line items to the invoice, click Add Item. This button is only available if your customer’s invoicing rules allow you to add additional line items to a PO-based invoice. 6. To add accounting reference information or an inspection date to one or more line items, select the line items and select Line Item Actions Edit . You can also add discount, special handling and comments if you haven’t done so on the previous page. 7. The following fields are pricing details for line items: • • • • • • Price Unit Price Unit Quantity Unit Conversion Description To add or edit pricing details: For regular (non-blanket) purchase orders, click Line Item Actions and select Pricing Details. For blanket purchase orders: 1. Locate the Blanket PO Items area at the bottom of the page. 2. Mark the checkbox for the line item. 3. Click Create and select Goods or Service according to the contents of the line item. When you create an invoice for a purchase order that has at least one line item with advanced pricing details, SAP Business Network allows you add pricing details for all line items, regardless if they included advance pricing details or not. You can add or edit these values for line items based on the invoicing rules specified by your buyer. However, you can enter pricing details in a PO-based invoice or an invoice for blanket purchase orders only if your buyer: • • Allows you to edit the unit price of a line item AND Enables the rule to allow you to add pricing details at line item level OR the purchase order has at least one line item with pricing details. 8. Click Update on the top or bottom of the invoice entry form to update any calculated fields if you add or modify any amount or rate fields. 9. Click Next. 10. Review the invoice and make any final changes as necessary. 11. Click Submit. Creating a PO-Based Invoice for Shipped or Received Quantities Only Business rules allow SAP Business Network customers to require that you invoice only for quantities that have been shipped or received. Customers can also require that you include references to ship notices or receipts on invoices. When customers enable rules to require invoicing against shipped or received quantities, you can quickly flip a purchase order to an invoice whenever goods have been shipped or received. You and your customers can open the invoice and see the associated ship notice or receipt for each line item. 14 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices In the invoicing scenarios for shipped or received quantities, you can invoice up to the balance of items either shipped or received for that order. However, the SAP Business Network enforces invoice business rules, country/ region-based invoice rules, and PO invoice tolerances. Prerequisites To invoice for shipped quantities only, your customers must enable the following business rules on the Default Transaction Rules page: • • Require suppliers to include only shipped quantities on invoices Require references to ship notices on invoices To invoice for received quantities only, your customers must enable the following business rules on the Default Transaction Rules page: • • Require suppliers to include only received quantities on invoices Require references to receipts on invoices Restrictions This feature has the following restrictions: • Service Orders - This feature is designed to support invoicing of material items that have been shipped or received. It does not support flipping a PO that contains both service items that require a service sheet and material items to an invoice. • Line Item Credit Memos - This feature does not allow you to create line item credit memos against receipts for returned goods. • Referencing Receipts for Returns or Corrections on Invoices - Only receipts with positive received items can be referenced on invoices. If you create an invoice after the buyer submits a receipt for returned goods or a correction receipt (a receipt with a negative amount), the invoice does not reference the receipt even though it is used to calculate the balance of received items for billing. • Receiving Types – Many ERP systems have a concept of a two-way match between an invoice and the associated orders for items that do not require a receipt. The extrinsic ReceivingType indicates whether a receipt is required for an item. If any items on the order have the extrinsic ReceivingType=4 (no receipt required, reconciliation is based on quantity) or ReceivingType=10 (no receipt required, reconciliation is based on amount) in the ItemDetail element, then you cannot invoice for them if the customer business rule Require suppliers to include only received quantities on invoices is enabled. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices PUBLIC 15 Invoicing from the Ordered or Received Quantity Based on Control Keys Specified at the Line Item Level Invoicing based on control keys at the line item level SAP Business Network offers a special entitlement to buyers that allows them to apply receipt-based invoice verification at the line item level. Buyers that enable this entitlement force a three-way match between PO, receipt, and invoice quantities for any PO line items in which the following control key is present: <ControlKeys> <InvoiceInstruction verificationType="goodsReceipt" /> </ControlKeys> PO line items without this control key do not require a receipt for invoicing. You can invoice the ordered quantity for such items. Creating a PO-Based Invoice for Shipped Items An SAP Business Network customer can require that you invoice on shipped quantities only and include references to ship notices on invoices. If so, when you flip a PO to an invoice, only shipped items can be added to the invoice. If there are multiple ship notices associated with a purchase order, you can select which ones to invoice against. Prerequisites See Creating a PO-Based Invoice for Shipped or Received Quantities Only [page 14]. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Purchase Orders or Inbox Orders and Releases . 2. Open a purchase order. 3. Click Create Invoice.  Note If a ship notice has been received by the customer for any items on the purchase order, the Create Invoice button is available. Otherwise, it is unavailable. If the customer received multiple ship notices related to the purchase order, the Select Ship Notices To Be Invoiced wizard appears. 4. If the Select Ship Notices To Be Invoice wizard is displayed, select ship notices to include in the invoice, and then click Next. Otherwise, complete the first page of the Create Invoice wizard, and click Next. 5. Complete the Create Invoice wizard, and click Submit. The invoice includes only shipped quantities, and it has references to ship notices for each line item. 16 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices Creating a PO-Based Invoice for Received Items An SAP Business Network customer can require that you invoice on received quantities only and include references to receipts on invoices. If so, when you flip a PO to an invoice, only received items can be added to the invoice. If there are multiple receipts associated with a purchase order, you can select which ones to invoice against. Prerequisites See Creating a PO-Based Invoice for Shipped or Received Quantities Only [page 14]. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Purchase Orders or Inbox Orders and Releases . 2. Open a purchase order. 3. Click Create Invoice.  Note If a receipt has been received by the supplier for any items on the purchase order, the Create Invoice button is available. Otherwise, it is unavailable. If the customer sent multiple receipts related to the purchase order, the Select Receipts To Be Invoiced wizard appears. 4. If the Select Receipts To Be Invoice wizard is displayed, select receipts to include in the invoice, and then click Next. Otherwise, complete the first page of the Create Invoice wizard, and click Next. 5. Complete the Create Invoice wizard, and click Submit. The invoice includes only received quantities, and it has references to receipts for each line item. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices PUBLIC 17 Creating an Invoice or Credit Memo Based on a Receipt Reversal Use this procedure to create an invoice or credit memo based on a receipt reversal, which updated an earlier receipt. Prerequisites The following buyer invoice rules are enabled: • • • • Require suppliers to include only received quantities on invoices Require references to receipts on invoices Allow suppliers to send line-item credit memo Allow suppliers to send invoices to this account Context A receipt reversal occurs when a receipt corrects quantities from a previous receipt, either for received items or returned items. It has negative quantities, thereby reversing positive quantities from the earlier receipt. You can create an invoice or a line-item credit memo for a reversal receipt the same way you create one for receipts with positive quantities. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • • For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: Orders Orders Purchase Orders Orders and Releases 2. Open a purchase order. 3. Do one of the following: • • To create an invoice for a Returned Reversal receipt, click Create Invoice To create a line-item credit memo for a Received Reversal receipt, click Standard Invoice . Create Invoice Line-Item Credit Memo . 4. If the Select Receipts To Be Invoiced wizard is displayed, select receipts to include in the invoice or credit memo, and then click Next. Otherwise, complete the first page of the Create Invoice wizard or Create LineItem Credit Memo wizard, and then click Next. 5. Complete the wizard, and click Submit. The invoice or credit memo includes includes a reference to a receipt for each line item. 18 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices Creating PO-Based Invoices Automatically from Receipts Creating PO-based invoices automatically from receipts SAP Business Network customers in the United States, Australia, and South Africa can enable the following country/region-based invoice rule to let you invoice automatically whenever the customer sends a receipt for received quantities: • Enable automatic invoice creation from receipts This rule is effective only when the default transaction rule Require suppliers to include only received quantities on invoices is selected. The Enable automatic invoice creation from receipts rule causes the SAP Business Network to automatically create an invoice when the customer sends a receipt for material goods. The rule ensures that invoices are based on goods that the customer has received. This makes the invoicing process more efficient, and it reduces the possibility of invoices not matching goods receipts. The feature automates invoice creation for material goods and it reduces the possibility of invoices being rejected for not matching goods receipts. Before invoices can be automatically generated based on receipts sent from a customer, you must agree to automatic invoicing by completing the Automatic Invoice Creation Acceptance page for each customer that has enabled the country/region-based rule. When you log into the SAP Business Network, an alert notifies you of the need for confirmation of automatic invoicing against receipts. When a customer sends a receipt for received quantities, the SAP Business Network automatically generates a standard invoice or line-item credit memo based on the type of receipt. Table 1: Invoices Generated from Receipts Receipt Type Invoice Type Received items with positive quantities Standard invoice Received items with negative quantities (a correction) Line-item credit memo Returned items with positive quantities Line-item credit memo Returned items with negative quantities (a correction) Standard invoice If a customer includes comments in a receipt with negative received quantities to explain the reason for a correction, the comments are flipped to the automatically-generated line-item credit memo. Partial invoicing is supported. In other words, if the customer ordered 10 of an item and received only 5, the receipt will generate an invoice for the 5 items. The date assigned to the invoice is the system date. Each automatically-generated invoice has references to the related receipt and purchase order. Invoice Number for Automatically-Generated Invoices There are two methods the SAP Business Network uses to assign invoice numbers to invoices created automatically from receipts: • Receipts with Delivery Note Information: If the buyer uses the SAP ERP to create a receipt from a ship notice coming from SAP Ariba, the Delivery Note field on the receipt is auto-populated with the packing slip ID from Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices PUBLIC 19 the SAP Business Network. In that case, the invoice number for an automatically-generated invoice or line-item credit memo is based on the delivery note information, with a four-digit number appended to it. • Receipts without Delivery Note Information: If a receipt does not include delivery note information, the invoice number is a system-generated unique number that starts with "A" (for example, "AI7VCKN40"). Prerequisites Before a supplier can automatically create invoices from receipts for a buyer, the supplier and the buyer must meet these requirements: • • The buyer must be in the United States, Australia, or South Africa, where this feature is supported. The buyer must enable the following rule on the Default Transaction Rules page: Require suppliers to include only received quantities on invoices. This default transaction rule can be enabled for a group of suppliers rather than for all suppliers. If the rule is not enabled, automatic invoice creation from receipts does not work. • The buyer must enable the following country/region-based invoice rule: Enable automatic invoice creation from receipts. • The buyer and cXML-enabled supplier must upgrade to cXML 1.2.030 (or later) to support the ShipNoticeIDInfo child element in the ReceiptRequestHeader element. • The supplier must confirm automatic invoice creation for the buyer [page 22]. Restrictions This country/region-based invoicing feature is supported for the following countries/regions only: • • • United States Australia South Africa Additionally, the feature only applies if you invoice through the SAP Business Network and not through an integrated ERP system. The following receipts do not result in an automatically-generated invoices: • • • • • 20 Receipts for items from multiple purchase orders Receipts for items from a purchase order that contains both services and material goods. Receipts for ERS (self-billing) orders. Receipts for consignment orders. Receipts for orders with a temporary price indicator at the header level. PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices

file://SBN/split/Creating and Managing I.content: SAP Business Network does not generate an invoice in the following scenarios: Scenario The receipt is for an order that has an ERS indicator at the header level. The receipt is for an item that has an ERS indicator at the item level on the order. The receipt is for an item that has a consignment indicator at the item level of the order. The receipt is for an order for which the buyer doesn't allow invoicing. The receipt is for an order with a temporary price indicator at the header level. cXML example <OrderRequestHeader ... > <ControlKeys> <InvoiceInstruction value="isERS"/> </ControlKeys> </OrderRequestHeader> <ItemOut ... > <ControlKeys> <InvoiceInstruction value="isERS"/> </ControlKeys> </ItemOut> <ItemOut itemCategory="consignment" lineNumber="10" quantity="30.000" requestedDeliveryDate="2017-12-08T12:00:00+02:00"</ ItemOut> <OrderRequestHeader ... > <Extrinsic name="Ariba.invoicingAllowed">No</ Extrinsic> </OrderRequestHeader> <OrderRequestHeader ... > <ControlKeys> <InvoiceInstruction value="notAllowed"> <TemporaryPrice value="yes"/> </InvoiceInstruction> </ControlKeys> </OrderRequestHeader> All items in a receipt must have either positive or negative quantities and must be either of type "received" or "returned". Otherwise, the receipt will be rejected. All taxes, allowances, and charges must be specified on the purchase order as a percentage rate, not as a flat amount. Confirming Automatic Invoice Creation from Receipts for a Customer [page 22] Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices PUBLIC 21 Confirming Automatic Invoice Creation from Receipts for a Customer Before the SAP Business Network can automatically create invoices from receipts for a customer, you must agree to the invoicing rule. Otherwise, you must create invoices manually for goods the customer received. Prerequisites Creating PO-Based Invoices Automatically from Receipts [page 19] Procedure 1. On the Enablement tab, look for a notification that a customer has requested you to confirm automatic invoice creation from receipts. Click the notification. The Account Settings > Customer Relationships > Automatic Invoice Creation Acceptance page appears, listing customers that have requested confirmation to automatically create invoices from receipts. 2. For each customer whose status is Not Responded, click Actions > Confirm Automatic Invoice Creation to respond. The Confirm Automatic Invoice Creation page appears. 3. Click Yes to agree to the terms and conditions, and then select the By selecting Yes... check box, which acknowledges that you authorize Ariba to automatically create and submit invoices for the selected customer. 4. Click OK. Creating PO-Based Invoices Automatically from Service Entry Sheets Invoices can be automatically generated from approved service entry sheets in SAP Business Network in the Service Procurement with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass (4R2) integration scenario. Automating the invoicing process increases efficiency and reduces the possibility of invoices not matching service entry sheets. Buyers can enable the automatic generation of invoices from approved service entry sheets feature by enabling the Enable automatic generation of invoices from approved service entry sheets invoice rule. Before invoices can be automatically generated based on service entry sheets, you, as a supplier, must confirm automatic invoice creation for each buyer that has enabled the rule. You must also specify whether you want the invoices to be saved as drafts or submitted for approval. However, if tax information is not specified at the purchase order line-item level, the generated invoices are saved as drafts even if you have specified that the invoices be submitted for approval. This feature is applicable only in the Service Procurement with SAP Business Network and SAP Fieldglass (4R2) integration scenario. The 4R2 integration scenario involves integration between SAP S/4HANA Cloud, 22 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices SAP Fieldglass, and SAP Business Network for services procurement and supports the exchange of documents such as orders, service sheets, and invoices. All data is routed through SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network.  Note Invoices are generated only for those service entry sheets that are associated with purchase order line items containing planned lean-service items. Prerequisites Before a supplier can automatically create invoices from service entry sheets for a buyer, the supplier and the buyer must meet these requirements: • The buyer must ensure that the following integration scenarios have been implemented: • • Automation of Source-to-Pay with Ariba Network (42K) Service Procurement with Ariba Network and SAP Fieldglass (4R2) • The buyer must ensure that the Enhanced order confirmation integration capabilities for hosted and integrated suppliers entitlement is enabled. • The buyer must ensure that the following transaction rules are enabled in the SAP Business Network buyer account: • Allow exchange of documents between Ariba Network, SAP Fieldglass, and SAP S/4HANA or SAP S/4HANA Cloud, for services procurement • • Require suppliers to fully confirm line items before fulfillment Require delivery dates for order confirmations • The buyer must ensure that the country-region-based invoice rule, Enable automatic generation of invoices from approved service entry sheets is enabled. • The buyer must ensure that the Ignore country-based invoice rules transaction rule is disabled in the SAP Business Network buyer account. • The buyer must ensure that the Auto-generate service sheets from service invoices transaction rule is disabled in the SAP Business Network buyer account. • The supplier must confirm automatic invoice creation for the buyer [page 24] . Restrictions • • • • • Tax information in purchase orders is not sent from SAP S/4HANA Cloud to SAP Business Network. This feature is not applicable to suppliers who invoice through an integrated ERP system. Automatic generation of credit memos from correction service entry sheets is not supported. Allowances and charges information in the purchase orders is not carried over to the automatically created invoices. Service entry sheets originating from SAP Fieldglass cannot be edited in SAP Business Network. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices PUBLIC 23 • Enabling the Allow suppliers to create invoices directly from service POs without a service sheet rule takes no effect when the Allow exchange of documents between Ariba Network, SAP Fieldglass, and SAP S/4HANA or SAP S/4HANA Cloud, for services procurement rule is enabled. Confirming Automatic Invoice Creation from Service Entry Sheets for a Customer Before SAP Business Network can automatically create invoices from service entry sheets for a buyer, you, as a supplier, must agree to the invoicing rule. You must also specify whether you want the invoices to be saved as drafts or submitted for approval. If you do not confirm automatic invoice creation, you must create invoices manually from approved service entry sheets. Procedure 1. On the Enablement tab, look for a notification that a customer has requested you to confirm automatic invoice creation from receipts. Click the notification. The Account Settings > Customer Relationships > Automatic Invoice Creation Acceptance page is displayed, listing buyers that have requested confirmation to automatically create invoices from service entry sheets. 2. For each customer whose status for Automatic invoice generation from service sheets request is Not Responded, click Respond to respond. The Confirm Automatic Invoice Creation page appears. 3. Click Yes to confirm that you accept automatic creation of invoices from approved service entry sheets and specify whether you want the invoices to be saved as drafts or submitted for approval. 4. Select the By selecting Yes... check box, which acknowledges that you authorize SAP Ariba to automatically create and submit invoices for the selected buyer. 5. Click OK. Searching for a Unit of Measure on an Invoice If a buyer allows you to edit the unit of measure on invoices, you can type a unit of measure symbol, select one from a list, or search for a unit of measure. Procedure 1. On an invoice, select the Unit field for a line item or a header field. 2. Start typing a unit of measure symbol. A dropdown list of matching unit of measure symbols appears. 24 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices 3. Do one of the following: • • Select a unit of measure symbol. Click Search for more to search for a unit of measure. 4. If you clicked Search for more, do the following: a. Select Name, Symbol, or Code, and then type a value. b. Click Search. The search results appear in the table. If there are more than ten results, use the page controls above the table to page through more units of measure. c. Click Select to select a unit of measure. Self-Billing Invoices SAP Business Network can automatically transmit self-billing invoices to suppliers and buyers based on data in purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and goods receipts using an automated process called Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS). The buyer creates a self-billing invoice in an external business system and sends it to the supplier over SAP Business Network. The ERS/self-billing process supports the following features: • An agreement is presumed to exist outside SAP Business Network between buyer and supplier approving the usage of ERS/self-billing. • The buyer transfers ERS/self-billing data from the ERP system to SAP Business Network and makes sure all country/region-required mandatory content is included on self-billing documents. • If applicable, SAP Business Network adds country/region-specific signatures to the cXML self-billing document based on the supplier’s location (country/region) and optionally creates a human-readable PDF based on the cXML data. • • • • A self-billing invoice is labeled “Self-Billing” in the user interface and in the human-readable PDF. • ERS/self-billing is available for the following countries/regions: Australia, Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, UK, and USA. • Based on the buyer’s and supplier’s configuration, self-billing documents optionally can be archived using the SAP Business Network long-term document archiving feature. SAP Business Network sends signed self-billing invoices to the buyer’s account. SAP Business Network sends signed self-billing invoices to the supplier’s account and notifies that supplier. Suppliers can download self-billing invoices through their network accounts or optionally configure their accounts to receive them through email. Prerequisites To use this feature, a buyer must have an ERS/self-billing agreement in place with a supplier. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices PUBLIC 25 Workflow for Self Billing SAP Business Network automatically transmits self-billing invoices to suppliers and buyers based on data in purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and goods receipts using an automated process called Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS). The following describes the workflow for a self-billing process: 1. The buyer and supplier enter a written agreement on ERS/self-billing. 2. The buyer creates an order with the ERS flag in the buyer's ERP, which sends the order to the supplier on SAP Business Network. 3. Optionally, the supplier sends an order confirmation to the buyer. 4. Optionally, the supplier sends a ship notice to the buyer. 5. Outside SAP Business Network, the supplier ships material or provides services to the buyer. 6. The buyer creates a goods receipt in the ERP. 7. The buyer creates a self-billing invoice in the ERP, which sends it to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network makes the self-billing invoice available to the supplier through the user interface, cXML, and PDF. 8. Optionally, the buyer and supplier can archive the self-billing invoice. Figure 2: Workflow Process for Self Billing 26 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices Creation of Invoices Against Enhanced-Limit Material Items You can create invoices against enhanced-limit material items in purchase orders without the necessity of ship notices or goods receipts. The enhanced-limit material items in SAP Business Network correspond to product type group Material (1) items in SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud. You can create invoices against enhanced-limit material items in purchase orders without the necessity of ship notices or goods receipts, in the Automation of Source-to-Pay with SAP Business Network (42K) integration scenario. The 42K integration scenario involves integration between SAP Business Network (with SAP Business Network Commerce Automation) and SAP S/4HANA or SAP S/4HANA Cloud, for procurement and supports the exchange of documents such as requests for quotations, orders, ship notices, and invoices. All data is routed through SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network. Supplier users are prevented from creating ship notices and service entry sheets for enhanced-limit material items in purchase orders. When creating invoices, supplier users can create multiple invoice lines against a single enhanced-limit material line in the purchase order. However, the subtotal of the amounts of all the invoice lines must not exceed the expected amount limit specified for the associated purchase order line item. Prerequisites Ensure that the buyer has: • • implemented the Automation of Source-to-Pay with Ariba Network (42K) integration scenario. Enabled the Enhanced order confirmation integration capabilities for hosted and integrated suppliers entitlement. If your orders contain both material and lean-service items, then ensure that the buyer has: • • Implemented the Service Procurement with Ariba Network and SAP Fieldglass (4R2) integration scenario. Enabled the Allow exchange of documents between Ariba Network, SAP Fieldglass, and SAP S/4HANA or SAP S/4HANA Cloud, for services procurement transaction rule. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos PO-Based Invoices PUBLIC 27 Non-PO Invoices Creating a Non-PO Invoice [page 28] Adding Invoice Line Items to a Non-PO Invoice [page 29] Creating a Non-PO Invoice Use this procedure to create an invoice without a corresponding purchase order. Prerequisites You must have Inbox Access, Outbox Access, and Invoice Generation user permissions to be able to create and manage invoices. Your customer controls whether or not you can create non-PO invoices for them with an invoice rule setting. Your customer must also enable certain invoice rule settings to allow you to add or edit the line items with advanced pricing details. Context You create non-PO invoices either for purchase orders that are not routed through SAP Business Network or that do not reference any purchase orders. Your customer’s invoice rules determine if you can create non-PO invoices and if order information is required on non-PO invoices. When you create an invoice, Ariba Network validates the invoice with the invoice rules set by your customer. For more information on invoice rules, see the Ariba Network Guide to Invoicing Features and Functions in the Product Documentation For Administrators section of the Learning Center. If you submit a non-PO invoice through cXML, it can have item groups, which contain items grouped under them. Procedure 1. Choose Create Non-PO Invoice . 2. On the Create Non-PO Invoice page, select a customer from the pull-down menu, select Standard Invoice, and click Next. 28 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Non-PO Invoices 3. On the Create Invoice page, enter an invoice number (Invoice #), date and other header-level information about the invoice in the SUMMARY area. 4. Enter header-level taxes, shipping, special handling, and discounts [page 53] as needed. 5. Enter allowances and charges [page 57] as needed. 6. Click View/Edit Addresses in the SUMMARY, Shipping, and Additional Fields sections to review address details and edit them as needed. 7. Add other elements such as payment terms, comments, or attachments by clicking Add to Header and selecting from the available options. 8. Enter any other information your customer requests in the Additional Information area. 9. Click Update on the top or bottom of the invoice entry form to update any calculated fields if you add or modify any amount or rate fields. 10. Add line items [page 29] to the invoice. 11. Click Next.  Note If your customer requires bank details on invoices but you haven't added bank information to your remittance address, you'll receive an error message on the invoice. Below the error on the invoice you're creating, you can click Add bank accounts details to configure your remittance address with bank information. After you add bank information, you are returned to the invoice entry page and can submit the invoice to your customer. The remittance address is also saved for future invoices. If you don't have permission to update remittance information, you'll see a link to contact your account administrator. 12. Review the invoice and make any final changes as necessary. 13. Click Submit. Adding Invoice Line Items to a Non-PO Invoice Use this procedure to add line items for a non-PO invoice. You also can add tax lines, discounts, or special handling for line items. Prerequisites See Prerequisites [page 28]. Procedure 1. If you have not already created a non-PO invoice, create one [page 28]. If the Create Invoice or Edit Invoice page is not already open for the invoice you want to work with, find the invoice [page 83], and click the invoice number to open it. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Non-PO Invoices PUBLIC 29 2. Add items to the invoice. To invoice goods, go to the bottom of the Line Items section and click Add > Add Material. To invoice services, go to the bottom of the Line Items section, click Add and select Add General Service or Add Labor Service. 3. To quickly add tax lines, discount and/or special handling to all included line items, do the following: 1. Make sure that Line level tax is selected in the Tax area of the invoice header. 2. Under Insert Line Item Options in the line level service table, select Tax Category. 3. Select a tax type from the Tax Category pull-down menu and enter tax information. 4. Click the check boxes next to Discount and Special Handling as required. 5. Click Add to Included Lines to add the selected types of detail lines to all lines with a green check mark in the Included column. For tax lines, it adds the specific tax information to each included line. 4. To add sections to selected detail lines, do the following: 1. Select one or more line items for which you want to add additional data entry sections. You can add additional line item details, such as special handling, individual items that are in the invoice. 2. Click Line Item Actions and select the types of fields to add from the available options. 3. Enter information in the fields for the selected lines. 5. To add accounting reference information or an inspection date to one or more line items, select the line items and select Line Item Actions Edit . You can also add discount, special handling and comments if you haven’t done so on the previous page. 6. The following fields are pricing details for line items: • • • • Price Unit Price Unit Quantity Unit Conversion Description To add or edit pricing details, click Line Item Actions and select Pricing Details: 7. Click Update on the top or bottom of the invoice entry form to update any calculated fields if you add or modify any amount or rate fields. 8. Click Save. 30 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Non-PO Invoices

file://SBN/split/Creating and Managing I.content: Contract-Based Invoices A contract is a legal document that allows a buyer to establish a commitment with a supplier for products or services. Contracts can be specific or open-ended. They contain: pricing information for specific goods, commodities, or customer catalogs; minimum and maximum order levels; optional minimum and maximum commitment levels; and effective and expiration dates. Funds from contracts are either released when a purchasing agent places an order for items governed by a release order contract, or they can be released directly through the invoicing process and don’t require a purchase or release order (for invoiceable contract or no-release order contracts). An example of an invoiceable contract might be a janitorial service supplier that invoices monthly for a predefined amount of services against a yearly contract. Buyers can configure different levels of contracts: • • • • Item-level contracts that apply to specific customer catalog or non-catalog items. Commodity-level contracts that apply to all goods and services for specific commodity groups. Catalog-level contracts that apply to all items in a customer catalog. Supplier-level contracts that apply to all items ordered from a supplier. Buyers that use an SAP Ariba invoicing solution can allow their suppliers to transfer to their site and create invoices against invoiceable contracts either directly in the buyer’s account, or by retrieving certain contract header information and line item details from the buyer’s site. This is also called collaborative invoicing. The specific workflow that applies to you depends on your customer’s contract configuration and their site configuration. If you have trading relationships with multiple customers, you might have a different workflow for each customer: • Create the entire invoice in the customer’s site After selecting the customer, you are transferred into the customer’s invoicing site to create the entire invoice there. After the invoice has been approved by a customer’s invoice agent, you receive a copy of your invoice in your SAP Business Network account. This invoice is not validated against the invoicing rules configured by the customer in their SAP Business Network account and this workflow assumes that the customer has trained you on their invoice entry procedures. • Create an SAP Business Network-validated contract invoice After selecting the customer, you are transferred into the customer’s invoicing site to retrieve the contract and add line items only. You finalize the invoice in your SAP Business Network account using the Ariba Create Invoice pages and you submit the invoice from your SAP Business Network account, which means it is subject to the invoicing rules your customer has configured. For countries/regions that require a digital signature, the invoice is digitally signed if the customer’s account has been enabled for digital signing. • Use PO-Flip to create a standard invoice for item level blanket purchase orders For blanket purchase order (BPO) type contracts, your customer can disallow collaborative invoicing. In that case, for item level BPOs, you can create a standard invoice using purchase order to invoice flip (PO-flip) as you do with regular purchase orders. See PO-Based Invoices [page 10] for more information on creating invoices from purchase orders. For any other BPO type (supplier, customer catalog, or commodity level contracts), you must enter a non-PO invoice providing the contract ID on the invoice. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Contract-Based Invoices PUBLIC 31 Prerequisites You must have the Inbox Access, Outbox Access and Contract Access permissions to be able to review contracts and create collaborative invoices. Helpful Hints • Contract data (except BPO type contracts) is not stored on SAP Business Network, so you cannot search for contracts or run reports on contracts from your SAP Business Network account. • You might create invoices for customers with the SAP Business Network-validated contract invoicing flow and for other customers that continue to require you to create the contract invoice entirely in their invoicing site. In that case, remember that draft invoices will be in two different areas: On the Business Network-validated contract invoices) and the page (contract invoices created in the customer’s site). • Orders Contracts Invoices Drafts tab (SAP View contracts invoices When you are transferred to your customer's SAP Ariba invoicing site for the first time to access contracts, the following error might be displayed: “Cannot access customer's site. Your buying organization must approve your access to their system before you proceed with this action. Please try again later.” This error occurs only when the buying organization has not yet approved access to their procurement site. Contact your customer and ask them to grant you access. Finding Contracts to Create Invoices [page 32] Creating an SAP Business Network-Validated Contract Invoice [page 34] Adding or Modifying Line Items on an SAP Business Network-Validated Contract Invoice [page 35] Creating a Contract Invoice in the Customer’s Site [page 38] Finding Contracts to Create Invoices Use this procedure to find a contract to create a contract-based invoice. Prerequisites See Contract-Based Invoices [page 31]. 32 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Contract-Based Invoices Procedure 1. Choose Orders Contracts . 2. On the Contracts page, click View contracts. SAP Business Network opens a page with a list of customers that have enabled you to access their contract collaboration sites. Select the customer for which you want to view your contracts and click Next. 3. If your customer has multiple procurement applications, select the business unit address whose contracts you want to access by the Bill To address ID and the contact person and click Next. SAP Business Network passes your authenticated credentials to the customer’s site, opens a new session there and displays contracts available for direct invoicing. 4. Click the contract’s ID to view the contract summary and pricing terms. Click the Invoice button if you want to create an invoice for this contract. 5. To return to SAP Business Network, close your browser window. If your session on SAP Business Network has timed out, log back in to your account. On the Create Contract Invoice: Select Customer page, select the customer from the list of displayed customers and click Next. If your customer has multiple procurement applications, select the business unit address whose contracts you want to access by the Bill To address ID and the contact person. If the list is very long, you can search for your customer by typing the full or partial customer name into the Customer text box and clicking Search. If your customer has enabled their site for SAP Business Network-validated contract invoicing, the Create Contract Invoice: Select Contract page is displayed. Continue to the next step. [page 38] 3. On the Create Contract Invoice: Select Contract page, locate the Contract field and click the select link to open the contract chooser. 4. In the contract chooser, find the contract you want to create the invoice for and click Select. On the Create Contract Invoice: Select Contract page, enter an invoice number, invoice date, and any other information as required. Depending on how your customer has configured the contract, the Sold To email address might be defaulted from the contract. You can overwrite the Sold To email address and select different payment terms if required. The choices on the Bill To dropdown menu all match the contract. You are now on the SAP Business Network Create Invoice page. Click Edit Header to modify any of the attributes you specified when selecting the contract. To view the details of the contract, locate the Contract # field and click on the contract number link (such as C123). 7. Complete any other invoice header information as you do for any invoice you create on the SAP Business Network. 8. Add line items [page 35] to the invoice. 9. After adding the items to the invoice, finalize the invoice by adding all required taxes and special charges, comments, attachments or any other information following the same process to you use to enter a standard invoice. Prerequisites See Contract-Based Invoices [page 31]. Procedure 1. If you have not already created an invoice for the contract, create one [page 34]. If the Create Invoice or Edit Invoice page is not already open for the invoice you want to work with, find the invoice [page 83], and click the invoice number to open it. 2. Locate the Line Items section of the invoice entry form. At the bottom of this section, click Add Items. 3. The Create Contract Invoice: Add Contract Item page opens to display items configured on the contract for invoicing. Depending on the type of contract and the way your customer has configured the customer catalog, the Add Contract Item page either displays the catalog main view or the item list view. For example, an item Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Contract-Based Invoices PUBLIC 35 level contract displays all available items for invoicing directly in item list view mode, while a supplier level contract displays the catalog main view for browsing and searching. 4. On the catalog main page, narrow the list of items for invoicing. You can: • • • Enter a search term, such as ‘keyboard,’ and search the customer catalog to list available items. Browse the catalog items by clicking a category name in the Browse By Category column or below an image for a category. If the list of items is very long, you can search within the categories using keywords or part numbers. View the contract details by clicking on the contract ID in the upper left corner. 5. On the customer catalog’s item listing page, select the items you want to add to your invoice. Note that the price you see on this page reflects the price before the contract pricing terms are applied. Contract pricing terms are applied when you add the item to the invoice. • Click the check box next to the Add Item button in the header line above the items to select all items displayed on this page. You can then unselect any items you don’t want to add. Add the quantity for all selected items, then click Add Item on the header line or at the bottom of the page to add the selected items. • If you want to add only one item to the invoice, find the item, enter the quantity in the Qty field and click the Add Item button.  Note For no-release contracts and blanket purchase orders, when you click the Add Itembutton, the catalog item is added to a shopping cart in the catalog page. You can add multiple catalog items to your shopping cart and review them in the Review Cart page. Click Done to return to the Create Invoice page in the SAP Business Network. 6. In the Create Invoice page, review the items in the Goods section and do one of the following: • • • Click Change Items to make modifications to the line items [page 37]. Click Add Items to add additional items to the invoice. Add line item detail information such as taxes, special handling, comments or attachments to each line item. 7. To add non-catalog items to an SAP Business Network-validated contract invoice (if allowed), click Add Items at the bottom of the Goods section of the Create Invoice page. You may be able to click the add non-catalog items icon ( ), which is only available if your customer has configured the contract to allow you to enter non-catalog items. Depending on the type of contract and the contract’s definition, the contract pricing terms might be applied to non-catalog items. 8. Enter information for the item. The fields that are available for data entry depend on how your customer has configured the contract. For example, if you are not allowed to edit accounting information, then the accounting fields (and the calculator icon) are not displayed. Your customer might also require additional information that you provide in custom fields. 9. Click Save. This returns you to the SAP Business Network Create Invoice page. 10. To add additional item to the invoice, click Add Items again in the Goods section on the Create Invoice page. 36 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Contract-Based Invoices Modifying Line Items on an SAP Business NetworkValidated Contract Invoice Use this procedure to modify line items for an SAP Business Network-validated contract invoice. Prerequisites See Contract-Based Invoices [page 31]. Procedure 1. If you have not already created an invoice for the contract, create one [page 34]. If the Create Invoice or Edit Invoice page is not already open for the invoice you want to work with, find the invoice [page 83], and click the invoice number to open it. 2. On the Create Invoice or Edit Invoice page, locate the Line Items section and click Change Items. 3. On the Create Contract Invoice: Change Items page, do the following: • To mass edit accounting information or other custom fields, select at least two items and click Edit. For example, if your customer expects you to enter accounting information, and you are invoicing the same department for different items, you can mass edit the accounting information for all these items in one simple step. • To edit accounting information or other specific information for each line item, click the triangle next to More. • • • To edit accounting information only for each line item, click the calculator icon. To delete items from the invoice, select the item or items for deletion and click Delete. If needed, modify the quantity, unit of measure, and, if allowed, the unit price for the invoiced item. Click Update Amount. 4. Click Save. Prerequisites See Contract-Based Invoices [page 31]. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • • Choose Orders Contracts , and then click Create contract invoice. Choose Create Contract Invoice . 2. Select the customer for which you want to create a contract-based invoice and click Next. You are now punching into your customer’s invoicing site. 3. In the Invoice Entry page, click the down arrow in the Contract field. If the contract you are looking for is shown, click it. If you do not see the contract you need, click Search for more, which opens up the Contract Chooser to display all available contracts. 4. In the Contract Chooser, find the contract you want to create the invoice for. If the list is very long, you can click anywhere in the Field text box to select a search filter and then type a search criteria to narrow the list. For example, if you know the month of the expiration date of the contract, choose Expiration Date and enter the case-sensitive three letter abbreviation, for example: Jan. Click Search. 5. Click Select next to the contract you are creating the invoice for. 6. Enter the invoice information into the Invoice Entry form as follows: 1. Enter all required fields and any optional fields. 2. In the Invoice Header section, click Header Actions. This lets you add sections to enter tax, shipping, special handling, discount, comments and attachments. 3. In the Line Items section, click Line Item Actions and add items from the catalog or add ad hoc items (non-catalog items) as required. 4. Click the triangle next to More to expand the line item detail section and enter any required fields. 5. Click the check box for the line items for which you need to add additional details, such as line level tax, discount, special handling charges, comments or attachments. 7. When you are ready to submit the invoice to your customer, click Submit. You might get validation errors that you must correct before you can submit the invoice. After you have submitted your invoice, the Invoice Draft page is displayed. If you have any unfinished invoices for this customer, they are listed here. Click on the invoice ID link to view and finalize them. To return to your SAP Business Network session, click Logout or simply close your browser window. 38 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Contract-Based Invoices 9. If you exit the page without submitting the invoice, you can save the draft invoice by choosing Save this request on the Confirm Exit page. Orders Contracts Related Information Finding Contracts to Create Invoices [page 32] Creating an SAP Business Network-Validated Contract Invoice [page 34] Adding or Modifying Line Items on an SAP Business Network-Validated Contract Invoice [page 35] Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Contract-Based Invoices PUBLIC 39 Service Invoices Service invoices are typically based on one or more approved service sheets created from a service order. Customers place service orders for one-time services or large projects with multiple stages. A service order contains at least one service line that requires a service sheet to describe the services delivered. Service orders can contain lines for both material items and services. The following types of line items are supported in a service purchase order: • • • • • Material Service Lean Service - Lean services simplify the process of procuring low-value service items. Limit Service - Limit items for unplanned lean services, also known as Limit Services, are used to procure unplanned low-value services costing up to a predefined spend limit. Limit Order - A Limit Order line item is defined as the fulfillment of a service or material delivery at a price limited by a predetermined amount within a time period specified by the buyer. The person in your company who fulfills the service at the work site (the field contractor) creates service sheets to describe service and goods fulfillment. In case questions arise during invoicing, service sheets can include contact information for the field contractor, field engineer (the person in your customer’s organization who supervised the work), and approver (the person in your customer’s organization who approved the service sheet). You invoice those service sheets in the service invoice. Service invoices have a single table for material and service line items. The Line Items table maintains the same sequence and hierarchy as the order. The Service Sheet # column shows the corresponding service sheet for each line. Figure 3: Standard Workflow for Service Invoicing Suppliers can create multiple service sheets against an amount-based service line type if the transaction rule Allow suppliers to create multiple invoices for an amount-based service item is enabled. However, the sum of the subtotal amount from all the service sheets created for an amount-based service line purchase order must not exceed the tolerance limit. Depending on a business rule enabled by your customer, you can also create invoices directly from a service order without automatically generating a service sheet. Suppliers are also allowed to create service invoice from a service purchase order that does not require service sheet, and has a service hierarchy. When a buyer sends service orders indicating that a supplier does not need to send service sheets for invoicing, SAP Business Network flips the outline items from the service purchase order to create a service invoice, maintaining the hierarchy. For customers who allow automatically generated service sheets, you can create service invoices for each service line on a service order, and the corresponding service sheets are automatically generated and sent to the customer. 40 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices
