file://SBN/split/Creating and Managing I.content: Figure 4: Automatic Generation of Service Sheet Workflow for Service Invoicing In some business environments, buyers allow suppliers to modify (in service sheets and invoices) the unit price for line items coming from the service purchase orders or contracts. Buyers can send service orders toSAP Business Network from their backend procurement system (such as SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA) where the purchase order cXML document includes line-item control keys that allow unit price changes by suppliers. Now, if buyers specify that the unit price is editable in service orders, suppliers can identify the control keys for changing the unit price in the service orders. Suppliers can then change the unit prices in service sheets and invoices. SAP Business Network fails the service order under the following scenarios: • • Scenario 1 In Invoice In Service Entry Sheet Buyer allows changes to the unit price Yes No Supplier modifies the unit price No Yes In Invoice In Service Entry Sheet Buyer allows changes to the unit price No Yes Supplier modifies the unit price Yes No Scenario 2 If buyers allow unit price change, on the service order page, SAP Business Network displays Unit Price Editable control keys for both the invoice and the service entry sheets. The control key indicates whether changing the unit price is allowed or not. Service invoices are fairly flexible. You can consolidate invoicing by: • • Creating service invoices based on multiple service sheets from the same service order. Adding ship notices from standard, non-service purchase orders to a service invoice. Prerequisites You must have Inbox Access, Outbox Access, and Invoice Generation user permissions in order to create and manage service invoices. You do not see any features related to services invoicing in your SAP Business Network account until the first time one of your customer sends you a service purchase order. At that time, all Services Invoicing features are automatically enabled. You can invoice only service sheets that have the status Approved or Partially Invoiced.  Note Alternatively, if no service sheets have been created for the order and the customer allows automatic generation of service sheets, you can create an invoice from the service order. In this case, the SAP Business Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices PUBLIC 41 Network generates a corresponding service sheet automatically and sends it to the customer for approval. The invoice is sent once the customer approves the service sheet.  Note If the customer has configured the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to enable simplified procurement of services, service purchase orders from these customers can be invoiced directly without service sheets. Restrictions: Standard Service Invoice Workflow You cannot edit quantities for service sheet lines on invoices. In some cases, you can create service invoices from a service purchase order that does not require a service sheet, and has a service hierarchy. When a buyer sends service orders indicating that the supplier does not need to send service sheets for invoicing, SAP Business Network flips the outline items from the service purchase order to create a service invoice, maintaining the hierarchy. For planned lines in service purchase orders with hierarchy, you cannot edit outline items and the subtotal flipped from the service purchase order. You cannot edit the unit price of children items. You can edit only the quantity for children items, and include taxes, allowance, and charges. Ariba Network validates the quantity against the quantity limit specified in the purchase order considering the quantity tolerance set by the buyer.  Note Buyer users can create service sheets based on copy orders only in SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing (merged with SAP Ariba Invoice Management) when the Allow creation of service sheets based on copy orders: (Application.Procure.EnableServiceSheetForCopyOrder) parameter is enabled. For more information, see Allow creation of service sheets based on copy orders. If your customer has changed the underlying service order on which an already-approved service sheet is based and has removed a service line, you cannot invoice that line on the service sheet, even though its status shows as Approved. If your customer has configured the SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to enable simplified procurement of services, you cannot add unplanned items to the invoices for the service purchase orders from that customer. For Lean Service line items, only the following fields can be edited - Qty/Unit, Start Date, End Date, and Add comments. For Limit Service line items, only the following fields can be edited - Description, Quantity, Unit, Price, Start Date, and End Date. The Quantity for a Limit Order line item is always 1 and it is not editable. The Subtotal for a Limit Order line item should not exceed the limit set by the buyer for that line item in the purchase order. 42 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices Restrictions: Automatic Generation of Service Sheets Workflow • By default, the Invoice Date of invoices created in the automatic generation of service sheets workflow is populated automatically when the customer approves the corresponding service sheet. However, if the customer sets the rule named Allow suppliers to edit service invoice dates and retain them when using auto-generated service sheets, you can enter an invoice date and SAP Business Network will use that date in the corresponding service sheet. • Buyer users can create service sheets based on copy orders only in SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing (merged with SAP Ariba Invoice Management) when the Allow creation of service sheets based on copy orders: (Application.Procure.EnableServiceSheetForCopyOrder) parameter is enabled. For more information, see Allow creation of service sheets based on copy orders. • In the automatic generation of service sheets workflow the Rejected status is final and it cannot be changed. If an automatically generated service sheet is approved but the corresponding invoice is rejected, then the service sheet cannot be flipped into an invoice. As a best practice, buyers should reject automatically generated service sheets if they reject the corresponding invoice. • You cannot add a line level attachment in PO-based invoices when they use the automatic generation of service sheets workflow. • The automatic generation of service sheets workflow should not be used if you issue invoices from a VAT country/region and you trade with customers who have a different local currency. This is because the automatically generated invoices may have an invalid exchange rate but they will still be sent to you automatically after you approve the corresponding service sheet. • The automatic generation of service sheets workflow is not compatible with SAP Ariba invoice conversion services and therefore should not be used for suppliers who submit paper invoices. • • The automatic generation of service sheets workflow should not be used for summary invoices. • The automatic generation of service sheets workflow should not be used for POs that contain SESInstruction ControlKeys element. The automatic generation of service sheets workflow should not be used for POs that contain both planned and unplanned items at the top level. Multi-Level Service Hierarchy [page 43] Automatic Generation of Service Sheets [page 45] Maximum Limits for Unplanned Service Lines [page 46] Service-Based Invoice Verification [page 47] Creating a Service Invoice [page 47] Creating or Modifying Service Invoice Line Items [page 49] Correction Service Entry Sheet [page 51] Multi-Level Service Hierarchy The SAP Business Network supports a multiple-level hierarchy for the following document types: • • Service orders Order confirmations Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices PUBLIC 43 • • • Order inquiries Service sheets Service Invoices The maximum number of levels supported depends on your back-end ERP system, not on the SAP Business Network. Within the service hierarchy, items with children are called outline items. An outline item is a container item that does not have a price or quantity, and it typically has a subtotal only at the top level. It can contain nested outline items, service items, and material items. When you confirm or reject an outline item, you also confirm or reject all its children. The SAP Business Network user interface displays up to 10 top-level items per page. For orders with more than 10 top-level items, you can use page controls at the upper right of the Line Items table to display other pages. By default, only one parent purchase order line is allowed per service sheet. However, buyers can configure their transaction rules to allow you to add multiple parent purchase order lines on a single service sheet. The ability to add multiple parent PO lines to a service sheet is supported in both the standard service sheet workflow and in the auto-generation of service sheets workflow. Service Hierarchy Terms The following terms are used to describe a service hierarchy: Service hierarchy An outline structure representing items in a PO, order confirmation, order inquiry, service sheet, or invoice. If any of these documents has outline items with children, it has hierarchy, and an outline item exists at the top level of the hierarchy. Each top-level outline item represents a different hierarchical structure that can have a different number of levels than other outline items on the same order. For instance, one outline could consist of four levels, but another might have only two. Top level The highest level in a hierarchical structure. Branch A portion of the hierarchy representing an outline item and all of its subitems (or children). Line item An element of the service hierarchy. Outline item A container item in a service hierarchy. It does not show values for Quantity or Price fields, and it typically has a Subtotal value only for top-level outline items. An outline item can contain nested outline items, service items, and material items. When you confirm or reject an outline item, you also confirm or reject all its children. For planned line items in service purchase orders with hierarchy, suppliers cannot edit outline items and the subtotal flipped from the service purchase order. Service item A line item in a PO that represents a service to be performed. Material item A line item in a PO that represents material goods. Item group An item with children that is not an outline item and does not require a service sheet. Child item Item nested below an outline item. Also called a subitem. Child items can include outline items and functional items. 44 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices Unplanned items Ad hoc items added to a service sheet or invoice by the supplier. Unplanned items are not on the PO. Planned items Items in a service sheet or invoice that were flipped from the PO and were therefore planned by the buyer. Figure 5: Parts of a Service Hierarchy Related Information Creating a Service Invoice [page 47] Creating or Modifying Service Invoice Line Items [page 49] Automatic Generation of Service Sheets Service sheets are meant to be created by field workers to record task lists or work breakdowns as they complete the work from field tickets or service requests. However, field workers often complete the service sheets without taking into account any financial or tax issues. This is why some suppliers prefer to have a billing clerk gather the information when creating service invoices. In such cases creating a service sheet is an unnecessary step for the supplier but it still may be required by the buyer. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices PUBLIC 45 Some customers allow service sheets to be generated automatically. With those customers, you can skip the unnecessary manual service sheet generation and directly generate invoices for each service line. Furthermore, both the manual and automatic workflows are available, so that you can choose which workflow to use per service order, as long as all service lines from the same service PO are processed with the same workflow. The workflows that are distinguished on the SAP Business Network are: • Standard workflow, in which you manually generate service sheets. You can generate a service invoice for each service sheet only after the customer approves the service sheet. • Automatic generation of service sheets workflow, in which you can directly generate service invoices for each service line, and the corresponding service sheets are generated automatically and sent to the customer for approval. Automatically generated service sheets can contain more information than regular service sheets, including: • • • • • • • An extended header summary Allowances and charges Taxes Shipping information Sold To and Bill To addresses Special handling Discounts The additional information contained on automatically generated service sheets allows customers to preview all of the details from the corresponding service invoice. Maximum Limits for Unplanned Service Lines For service invoices submitted without a service sheet, SAP Business Network validates unplanned service items against maximum limits specified in the order. The total amount of unplanned services can’t exceed the hidden overall limit specified on the order.  Note The purchase order limits for unplanned service lines are hidden from suppliers. Only buyers can see them. Service Invoice Scenarios That Don’t Require a Service Sheet The following scenarios don’t require a service sheet before invoicing: 1. Buyer service sheet rules (for vendor or group) specify that a service sheet is not required: • • Allow suppliers to create invoices from service POs without a service sheet rule is checked. Allow suppliers to auto-generate service sheets rule is unchecked. 2. Purchase order has a control key specified at the outline level that indicates that a service sheet is not required: <ControlKeys> <SESInstruction value="notAllowed"/> <InvoiceInstruction value="allowed"/> 46 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices </ControlKeys> or <ControlKeys> <SESInstruction value="notAllowed"/> </ControlKeys> 3. Buyers have configured their SAP Ariba Procurement solutions to enable simplified procurement of services. Service purchase orders from these buyers can be invoiced directly without service sheets. Service-Based Invoice Verification Buyers can allow you to create invoices directly from service orders without a service sheet. They can also include control keys in a service order to specify whether an item requires a service sheet for invoice verification. Service order control keys take precedence over invoice rules. Creating a Service Invoice Use this procedure to create a service invoice from a service order or a service sheet. Prerequisites See Service Invoices [page 40]. Context There are several ways to create a service invoice depending on the workflow you use for service invoicing. You can create invoices for all types of service lines except information service lines, which are for information purposes only. If the buyer allows service sheets to be generated automatically, a service sheet is created automatically when you create an invoice against a service order. The invoice is submitted with the status Pending Approval. If the buyer allows invoicing without service sheets, the invoice is submitted with the status Pending Approval. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices PUBLIC 47 Procedure 1. Perform one of the following actions: • Depending on whether you have SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders or Orders service order. • or Orders Purchase Orders and Releases , then click the Create Invoice icon ( ) to the right of the Depending on whether you have SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Orders Orders Orders and Releases , then select the service order and select Purchase Create Invoice Standard Invoice . • Depending on whether you have SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders or Orders Create Invoice Orders Purchase Orders and Releases , then click the purchase order to open it, then select Standard Invoice .  Note If you create a service invoice directly from the service order, either in the Inbox or on the Orders and Releases page, it automatically includes all service lines that have not already been invoiced from all of the service sheets associated with the purchase order. You can edit the invoice and delete or exclude any lines you do not want to include in the invoice. • Depending on whether you have SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Purchase Orders or Orders Orders and Releases , then click the triangle next to Search Filters to expand it. Choose Search only service purchase orders and click Search. Click the service order number for which you want to create a service sheet, and then click Create Service Sheet at the top of the order. To proceed further, see Creating a Service Sheet. • Choose Create Service Entry Sheet . Click the service order number for which you want to create a service sheet, and then click Create Service Sheet at the top of the order. To proceed further, see Creating a Service Sheet. • If you submitted a service sheet for the order, go to service sheet, and click Create Invoice. Fulfillment Service Sheets , select the approved 2. If the service order has multiple top-level outline items, and the customer allows you to generate service sheets automatically, select the desired item on the Select Item to Create Invoice with Auto-Generated Service Sheet page, and then click Next. By default, you can include only one parent PO line per service sheet. However, if the customer has enabled the business rule Allow suppliers to include multiple parent PO lines per service sheet, you are not prompted to select an outline item when you create a service sheet or an invoice for the order. Instead, all parent PO lines are automatically added to the service sheet and the invoice. 3. On the Create Invoice page, enter an invoice number (Invoice #), invoice date and other header-level information about the invoice in the Summary area. 4. Enter header-level taxes, shipping, special handling, and discounts [page 53] as needed. 5. Enter allowances and charges [page 57] as needed. 6. Click View/Edit Addresses in the Summary, Shipping, and Additional Fields sections to review address details and edit them as needed. 7. Add other elements such as payment terms, comments, or attachments by clicking Add to Header and selecting from the available options. 48 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices 8. Enter any other information your customer requests in the Additional Information area. 9. Click Update on the top or bottom of the invoice entry form to update any calculated fields if you add or modify any amount or rate fields. 10. Enter or modify line item information [page 49] for the invoice. 11. Click Next. 12. Review the invoice and make any final changes as necessary. 13. Click Submit. Results SAP Business Network transmits the service invoice to your customer. You can see it in the related documents for the associated purchase order and service sheets. Creating or Modifying Service Invoice Line Items Use this procedure to invoice remaining lines of a partially invoiced service service sheet. You also can add unplanned items to the invoice, and add tax lines, discounts, or special handling for line items. Prerequisites See Service Invoices [page 40]. Context You can invoice one or more lines from a service sheet that contains multiple lines and exclude the lines you do not want to invoice. A service sheet that is invoiced this way has the status Partially Invoiced. You can continue to create invoices on remaining lines until the service sheet is Fully Invoiced. Procedure 1. If you have not already created an invoice for the PO or service sheet, create one [page 47]. If the Create Invoice or Edit Invoice page is not already open for the invoice you want to work with, find the invoice [page 83], and click the invoice number to open it. 2. Review the detail lines displayed in the Line Items table for the invoice. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices PUBLIC 49 3. Add or remove lines on the invoice by performing one of the following actions: • Click the green check mark in the Include column to exclude it from the invoice. Excluded lines are indicated by a gray check mark in the Include column and their details are no longer visible. The invoice you submit does not contain any excluded lines, but they are still visible on the Create Invoice page and you can add them back if you need to. • Click the gray check mark in the Include column to include a previously excluded line in the invoice. Included lines are indicated by a green check mark and their details are visible. • Select a line and click Delete to remove it completely from the Create Invoice page. You cannot add a deleted line back to the current invoice without starting the invoice creation process over again. 4. Add unplanned items to the invoice: • To add unplanned items to the bottom of the invoice, scroll to the bottom of the Line Items table and click Add Add General Service , Catalog Item , or Add unit price, and so forth. • Add Add Labor Service , Add/Update Add Contract/ Add Material . Enter information for the line such as description, quantity, If you created the invoice directly from the purchase order without creating a service sheet, you can add unplanned items to any outline item (previously called an item group). To the right of an outline item, click Add/Update Add General Service , Add/Update Add Contract/Catalog Item , or Add/Update description, quantity, unit price, and so forth. Add Labor Service , Add/Update Add Material . Enter information for the line such as 5. Add line item detail information such as taxes, special handling, comments, or attachments to each line item. 6. To quickly add tax lines, discount and/or special handling to all included line items, do the following: a. Make sure that Line level tax is selected in the Tax area of the invoice header. b. Under Insert Line Item Options in the Line Items table, select Tax Category. c. Select a tax type from the Tax Category pull-down menu and enter tax information. d. Click the check boxes next to Shipping Documents, Special Handling, or Discount and as required.  Note Shipping Documents and Special Handling apply only to material items. e. Click Add to Included Lines to add the selected types of detail lines to all lines with a green check mark in the Include column. For tax lines, it adds the specific tax information to each included line. 7. To add sections to selected detail lines, do the following: a. Select one or more line items for which you want to add additional data entry sections. You can add additional line item details, such as special handling, individual items that are in the invoice. b. Click Line Item Actions and select the types of fields to add from the available options. c. Enter information in the fields for the selected lines. 8. To reset the tax for selected lines to tax values specified on the purchase order, select the line items and click Reset Tax from PO. 9. To add accounting reference information or an inspection date to one or more line items, select the line items and select Line Item Actions Edit . 10. Click Update on the top or bottom of the invoice entry form to update any calculated fields if you add or modify any amount or rate fields. 50 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices

Suppliers must enter a negative quantity value in the correction entry sheet. While creating a correction entry sheet, suppliers cannot: • • • Copy a line item. Edit details of the Price, Part# / Description, and Subtotal fields. Delete line items.  Note • • Suppliers cannot copy or create an invoice for an approved correction service entry sheet. • Use correction service entry sheets, not credit memos, to make adjustments for over-invoiced item quantities on service sheets. Suppliers cannot enter a negative quantity per line item which exceeds the total quantity value of the original service entry sheet. Creating a Correction Service Entry Sheet Use this procedure to create a correction service entry sheet to make adjustments for over-invoiced item quantities on service sheets. Prerequisites Suppliers can create correction service entry sheets only for those service entry sheets which are invoiced. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Service Sheets . 2. Click the service entry sheet for which you want to create a correction service entry sheet. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices PUBLIC 51 Ariba Network displays the details of the service entry sheet. 3. Click the Create Correction Service Sheet button. 4. If required, modify the Start Date and End Date fields. 5. Modify the Quantity or Unit field as required. You can only enter a negative value in this field. 6. Click Next. 7. Click Submit. Related Information Service Invoices [page 40] 52 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Service Invoices Taxes, Shipping, Special Handling, and Discounts on Invoices You add taxes, shipping, special handling, and discounts to invoices at either the header level or the line level, but not both. Prerequisites To add taxes, shipping, special handling, and discounts to invoices: • • You must have Inbox Access, Outbox Access, and Invoice Generation user permissions. You must have created an invoice or have a invoice open for editing. Your customer’s business rules determine whether you can: • • • • • • Add special handling taxes to an invoice. Add shipping taxes to an invoice. Edit line-item tax added from the purchase order. Enter discounts at the header level. Enter taxes at the header level (your customer might require you to enter line-level taxes). Enter your own tax categories or choose from the customer’s list. Restrictions If you add discounts or special handling at the line level of an invoice, you cannot switch back to header level discount or special handling even if you remove all line level discount or special handling sections. You cannot add line-level special handling or shipping to service lines. You can apply taxes to shipping costs or special handling at the header level, but not at the line level. Helpful Hints • If you manually enter a tax rate and a tax amount, and the entered tax rate does not match the calculated tax rate, the tax rate you entered will be overridden with the calculated tax rate based on the taxable amount and tax amount. • You can only enter withholding tax at the line level. To add withholding taxes to an invoice, select the line item to which you want to add withholding tax, select Tax from the Line Item Actions pull-down menu and then select Withholding Tax from the Category pull-down menu. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Taxes, Shipping, Special Handling, and Discounts on Invoices PUBLIC 53 • To apply the same line-level tax to all included line items, select Tax Category under Line Item Options on the line item table. Select the tax category from the pull-down menu, enter tax information, and click Add to Included Lines. • To add withholding taxes to an invoice, use line-level taxes. Adding Taxes, Shipping, Special Handling, and Discounts to an Invoice [page 54] Related Information French Parafiscal Taxes on Invoices [page 58] Adding Taxes, Shipping, Special Handling, and Discounts to an Invoice Use this procedure to add taxes, shipping, special handling, and discounts to invoices at either the header level or the line level. Prerequisites See Taxes, Shipping, Special Handling, and Discounts on Invoices [page 53]. Entering Taxes on an Invoice Procedure 1. In the Tax area of the invoice header, select Header level tax or Line level tax. 2. Perform one of the following actions to add a tax to the invoice at the selected level: • • To add header-level taxes, click Add to Header and select Tax. To add a line-level tax to a specific line item, select the line item, click Line Item Actions, and select Tax. 3. Select a tax type from the Tax Category pull-down menu. 4. Enter tax information such as taxable amount and rate. 5. Click Update to calculate tax totals for the invoice. 54 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Taxes, Shipping, Special Handling, and Discounts on Invoices Entering Shipping Charges and Taxes for Shipping in an Invoice Header Procedure 1. In the Shipping area of the invoice header, select Header level shipping. 2. Review the Ship To and Ship From information for the invoice and click View/Edit Addresses to make any changes. 3. Click Add to Header and select Shipping Cost. 4. Enter the charge for shipping all of the items on the invoice. 5. Select the date on which you will ship all of the items on the invoice. 6. To add taxes on shipping, do the following: 1. In the Tax section of the invoice header, select Line level tax. 2. Click Add to Header and select Shipping Tax. 3. Enter tax information [page 54] for the special handling. 4. Repeat as needed to add more shipping taxes. 7. Click Update to calculate shipping totals and taxes for the invoice. Entering Shipping Charges for Invoice Line Items Procedure 1. In the Shipping area of the invoice header, select Line level shipping. 2. For each invoice line: 1. Review the Ship To and Ship From information for the invoice and click View/Edit Addresses to make any changes. 2. Enter the charge for shipping that line. 3. Select the date on which you will ship that line. 3. Click Update to calculate shipping totals for the invoice. Entering Special Handling and Taxes on Special Handling in an Invoice Header Procedure 1. Click Add to Header and select Special Handling. 2. Enter the amount of the special handling charges and a description. 3. To add taxes on special handling, do the following: Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Taxes, Shipping, Special Handling, and Discounts on Invoices PUBLIC 55 1. In the Tax section of the invoice header, select Line level tax. 2. Click Add to Header and select Special Handling Tax. 3. Enter tax information [page 54] for the shipping. 4. Repeat as needed to add more special handling taxes. 4. Click Update to calculate special handling totals and taxes for the invoice. Entering Special Handling for Invoice Line Items Procedure 1. Perform one of the following actions: • To add a line-level discount to all included items in a line item table, select Special Handling and click Add to Included Lines. • To add a line-level discount to specific line items, select them, click Line Item Actions, and select Special Handling. 2. Enter a description and special handling charges. 3. Click Update to calculate special handling totals for the invoice. Entering Discounts on an Invoice Procedure 1. Perform one of the following actions: • • • To add a header-level discount, click Add to Header and select Discount. To add a line-level discount to all included items in a line item table, select Discount and click Add to Included Lines. To add a line-level discount to specific line items, select them, click Line Item Actions, and select Discount. 2. Enter a discount amount and an optional discount percentage. Discount percentage is only for information; the discount amount is applied to the invoice. 3. Click Update to calculate discount totals for the invoice. 56 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Taxes, Shipping, Special Handling, and Discounts on Invoices Allowances and Charges on Invoices Allowances and charges refer to the deductible and non-deductible expenses added to an invoice along with the total cost of the ordered products. Suppliers add the allowances and charges details at the header and line item levels of an invoice. Depending on the configurations of your buyer, you can add allowances and charges either at the line level, or at unit price level. Allowances and charges are added at unit price level in case your buyer has enabled an additional rule, which requires line item modifications to be applied only on the unit price. Otherwise, you can only add allowances and charges at the line level. In SAP Business Network, you add and modify allowances and charges in PO-based invoices, service invoices, non-PO invoices, and credit memos. In addition, you can also apply taxes to allowances and charges at the header and line item levels of an invoice.  Note • When you create a PO-based invoice, allowances and charges information within the purchase order is carried over to the new invoice. However, you can add new allowances and charges, and modify or remove allowances and charges carried over from the corresponding purchase order. Allowances and charges information in the purchase order is also carried over to documents such as change orders, credit memos, and order confirmations. • Allowances and charges functionality overlaps with Ariba shipping, special handling, and discount capabilities. You must apply these cost details accurately based on the buyer’s preference. Suppliers can also apply compound allowances and charges in a certain order by posting a cXML invoice with the corresponding elements and structure. Compound allowances and charges can be added on different levels, similar to compound interest rates. Invoices with compound allowances and charges cannot be copied or edited. For example, the initial price of an item is 10 USD and the following allowances and charges have to be added: • • • 10% charge on level 1 20% charge on level 2 5% allowance on level 2 In this case the 10% charge on level 1 will be added first to the 10 USD base amount. The result will be 11 USD. The level 2 charge and allowance will be added to the base amount of 11 USD, so a total of 15% (20 - 5 = 15) will be added to 11 USD. The result will be 12.65 USD. As you can observe from this example, several taxes can be added on the same level. This feature allows the user to see on invoices how the allowances and charges have been calculated. This is done with two columns in the Allowances and Charges table on the invoice: • • Level - used to display on which level an allowance or charge is added. Base Amount - used to display the base amount, on which allowances and charges are added for the corresponding level. The base amount is a result from calculations on previous levels. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Allowances and Charges on Invoices PUBLIC 57 Prerequisites To enter allowances and charges to invoices: • • • You must have Inbox Access, Outbox Access, and Invoice Generation user permissions. • To apply allowances and charges at the unit price instead of the line level, your customer must enable the rule “Include allowances and charges in the unit price.” • To enter French parafiscal taxes on non-PO invoices and credit memos, you must satisfy the following additional requirements: You must have created an invoice or open one for editing. Your customer must enable the rule “Allow suppliers to add allowances and charges to invoices.” (Note that this rule does not need to be enabled for you to add discounts, shipping, and special handling charges to invoices. For more information about the rule, see SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing.) • • You must have a French address. Your customer must enable the following country/region-based invoice rule for France: Allow suppliers to include parafiscal taxes. French Parafiscal Taxes on Invoices [page 58] Entering or Modifying Allowances and Charges on Invoices [page 59] Entering Charges on Credit Memos [page 60] French Parafiscal Taxes on Invoices Parafiscal taxes are specific taxes used in France. They are enforced by French law. The idea of the parafiscal taxes is to create dedicated funds for different causes. When selling particular products, French sellers are obliged to collect parafiscal taxes for specific purposes, which they ultimately pay to a third party, responsible for investing the funds according to their purpose. For example, if a customer buys a polluting product from a French seller, then this customer has to pay an environment tax. If you are a French supplier and your customer allows you to include parafiscal taxes on invoices, you can add parafiscal taxes to non-PO invoices and credit memos at the line level or header level in the Allowances and Charges section. Furthermore, as parafiscal taxes are subject to VAT taxes, you can add a VAT tax to parafiscal taxes. If you enter multiple parafiscal taxes for a line item, they are grouped in a Parafiscal Tax Summary. 58 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Allowances and Charges on Invoices Entering or Modifying Allowances and Charges on Invoices Use this procedure to enter allowances and charges on invoices. Prerequisites See Allowances and Charges on Invoices [page 57]. Procedure 1. If you are working with a PO-based invoice, open the Create Invoice page, review any allowances and charges sections displayed from the purchase order. 2. To modify the allowances and charges, click the specific field text box and enter the desired value. 3. To add allowances to an invoice header, select in the Allowances section: • • • • Allowance and enter the following details Service Code Description Start Date and End Date Allowance Amount 4. To add charges to an invoice header, select Charge section: • • • • Add to Header Add to Header Charge and enter the following details in the Service Code Description Start Date and End Date Select Rateor Amount from the pull-down menu and enter the corresponding value. 5. To apply tax on allowances or charges, click Add Tax in the ALLOWANCES AND CHARGES section. 6. Select the specific type of tax applicable on the allowances from the Category pull-down menu and enter any required information. 7. To apply allowances, charges, and taxes on allowances and charges at the line-item level, click the Line Item Actions link. Related Information Entering Charges on Credit Memos [page 60] Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Allowances and Charges on Invoices PUBLIC 59 Entering Charges on Credit Memos Use this procedure to enter charges on credit memos. Prerequisites See Allowances and Charges on Invoices [page 57]. Procedure 1. In the Create Credit Memo page, scroll down to the ADJUSTMENTS IN CHARGES section and click the Create Charge button. 2. Enter the following details: • • • • • Service Code Select Rateor Amount from the pull-down menu and enter the corresponding value. Description Start Date End Date 3. To add additional charge details, click Create Charge button. 4. To enter taxes on charges, click the Create Tax pull-down menu and choose Configure Tax Menu. 5. In the Configure Tax page, enter the following details: • • • Tax Category Rate (Optional) Tax Description 6. Click OK. 7. Click Submit to go to the next step. file://SBN/split/Creating and Managing I.content: Credit and Debit Memos Order Collaboration Returns for Suppliers [page 61] Credit Memos [page 63] Creating Credit Memos [page 66] Debit Memos [page 71] Creating a Line-Item Debit Memo to Increase Prices for an Invoice [page 73] Order Collaboration Returns for Suppliers Suppliers can use SAP Business Network to handle credit for goods returned by buyers. SAP Business Network supports the capability to process return orders. Buyers can return goods that they've purchased from a vendor and receive credit for them. Purchase orders can now include return items, that is, items that are being returned to the supplier. Returns can occur for many different reasons, including: • • • • • • • Warranty returns Non-compliance by the supplier (goods failed quality inspection) Reaching the end of life of equipment Damaged or defective product Equipment upgrade Overstock Delivery error Return items can be included on regular orders. To process return items, you can create a line-level credit memo called a Return Item Credit Memo. The Return Item Credit Memo is always PO-based. You can create a Return Item Credit Memo only for return items on a single order. Before items can be returned, buyers usually must submit a Returned Materials Authorization (RMA), which must be approved by the supplier. The RMA process is managed outside SAP Business Network, but the order can reference the Return Authorization Number for the return items. The Return Authorization Number field appears in the Return Information section of the Details view of a line item. If an order includes at least one return item, you cannot confirm or reject the entire order. When you confirm individual line items, only regular items are flipped to the order confirmation; return items are not flipped. When you create a ship notice for an order, the ship notice cannot include return items. Only regular items can be shipped to the buyer. After receiving return authorization, the buyer submits a Return Ship Notice to you, which indicates the items in the return shipment. A Return Ship Notice can include items from multiple orders. Based on a buyer's invoicing rules, you can be allowed to include return items on a standard invoice. If you flip an order with return items to an invoice, quantities for return items are negative. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos PUBLIC 61  Note You can create an invoice for purchase orders that have return items if the transaction rule Ignore return items when creating an invoice is disabled. You can cancel a Return Item Credit Memo with the Sent status if the buyer allows them to cancel invoices. Workflow Process for Returns The following describes the workflow for the returns process: 1. The buyer requests a Returned Material Authorization (RMA) from the supplier. The RMA process is managed outside the SAP Business Network. 2. The supplier authorizes the RMA. 3. The buyer submits a return purchase order to the supplier. The return purchase order references the RMA number. 4. The buyer submits a Return Ship Notice to the supplier, and ships the goods to the supplier’s location. 5. The supplier creates a Credit Memo for Return Items to reimburse the buyer for the returned goods. 6. In the credit memo, the supplier edits the price for return items that were damaged. Figure 6: Workflow Process for Returns Viewing Return Items Use this procedure to view items that have been marked as return items by buyers. Context Return items will be shipped back to you after RMA authorization, and you can issue a credit for them to the buyer. Procedure 1. Navigate to a Return items workbench tile 62 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos 2. To locate a specific return item, expand the search filters, enter the criteria desired, and click Apply. Viewing a Return Ship Notice Use this procedure to view a return ship notice sent from the buyer. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended Collaboration The Return Shipments page appears. Return Shipments . 2. To search for a specific ship notices from a particular customer or for a particular date range, click the triangle next to the Search Filters heading, enter the criteria desired, and click Search. 3. To open a ship notice, click one of the Ship Notice # fields. Credit Memos Credit memos let your customers know that you are issuing them a credit. Send credit memos for ordering, shipping, or billing problems you encounter in your day-to-day operations. You might issue credit for an ordering or shipping problem, such as: • • • • Your customer ordered the wrong items. Your company shipped incorrect items. Items were lost or damaged during shipping. The buyer decided not to use ordered items or services.. You can also issue credit for billing problems, such as: • • • • The customer was overbilled. There were changes in tax or shipping amounts after you sent invoices. Item prices were reduced before or after you sent invoices. Your customer remitted too much money. In many countries/regions with Value Added Tax (VAT) or other similar indirect taxes, suppliers are required to issue credit memos when a buyer and supplier agree to an early payment discount after a tax invoice has been issued. Credit memos allow your customers to adjust their accounts so that they match your own. They enable account reconciliation and balancing required due to problems that trading partners regularly encounter. They do not automatically move money from your company to your customer. You can use credits to reduce the cost of future orders from the customer or you can proactively send money back to the customer (through any method, such as EFT or check). Any movement of money back to the customer Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos PUBLIC 63 occurs outside of SAP Business Network and is typically performed manually. The specific process you use for issuing credits should be stated in your agreement with your customer. Types of Credit Memos SAP Business Network supports four types of credit memos: • • • • PO-based header-level credit memo PO-based line-item credit memo Non-PO credit memo Dynamic discounting credit memos A PO-based header-level credit memo is created against a purchase order routed through SAP Business Network. A PO-based line item credit memo is created against a specific item in a purchase order or invoice. A non-PO credit memo is created against a purchase order that is not routed through SAP Business Network (or when there is no purchase order at all). You manually fill in details when you create a non-PO credit memo. For PO-based and service credit memos, SAP Business Network pre-fills the credit memo entry form with details from the purchase order. Dynamic discounting credit memos are automatically generated on your behalf when you and your buyer agree to an early payment discount after a tax invoice has been issued. Automatic generation of dynamic discounting credit memos is limited to supplier-submitted invoices on SAP Business Network in countries/regions that requires credit memos. These credit memos are generated at the time of payment, upon receipt of the buyer remittance, and align to your original tax invoice. The credit memo: copies content from the original tax invoice; adjusts taxable amount, prices, and tax amount using the discount percentage; and applies any country/region-specific e-signatures or business rules.  Note Automatic generation of dynamic discounting credit memos is limited to supplier-submitted invoices on SAP Business Network in countries/regions that requires credit memos. You can use the Early Payment (details) report to make tax adjustments. You can archive the credit memo files (automatically generated cXML and PDF files) through the Archive Zip process or SAP Ariba's Archive service. The dynamic discounting credit memo feature is enabled by your buyer and confirmed by you. For more information, see Managing Discounts. The Credit Memos Workbench Tile The Credit memos workbench tile displays a count of credit memos that you have created. When you select a Credit memos workbench tile, the workbench displays them in a list, in addition to filters, default columns, and based on your customer's transaction rules, your user permissions, and document status, allows actions as follow: 64 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos Tile Filters Default Columns Actions Credit memos Customer Credit memo number Edit Credit memo number Credit memo date External credit memo Customer number Credit memo date Credit memo status Credit memo status change date Routing status Reference From country To country Invoice type Credit memo status Credit memo status date change Routing status Reference From address To address Amount Min amount Max amount Currency Submitted by View Invoice type Prerequisites You must have Inbox Access, Outbox Access, and Invoice Generation user permissions to be able to create and manage invoices. Each buying organization determines whether suppliers can send credit memos (invoices with negative amounts). If the Create Line-Item Credit Memo button is disabled, your customer does not accept line-item credit memos. To edit quantity in PO-based line-item credit memos, your customer must enable the business rule of Allow suppliers to edit quantity in line-item price adjustment credit and debit memos. Restrictions There are a few restrictions on how you can use credit memos. A few of these are natural restrictions of the feature, but there are also special considerations for certain situations, such as grouping and dynamic discounting. Restrictions related to header- and line-level credit memos You cannot create header-level or line item credit memos based on purchase orders that contain item groups. You must create credit memos against those purchase orders either using non-PO credit memos or in a third-party Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos PUBLIC 65 system, or create a correction service entry sheet as part of the service invoicing flow based on service sheets against a service purchase order. SAP Business Network does not support advanced pricing details on header-level credit memos. You can create a line-item credit memo only for an existing standard invoice. You cannot create one for an order that hasn’t been invoiced. You cannot edit quantities when creating a line-item credit memo for a service invoice. To make adjustments for over-invoiced item quantities on service sheets, use correction service entry sheets if enabled by the buyer. Some buying organizations have agreements with trading partners that do not allow partial credit memos for invoices. To support these buyers (in United States and Australia only), SAP Business Network provides a country/ region-based invoicing rule that requires suppliers to credit for the full invoice amount when they send a line-item credit memo. When this rule is checked, you cannot create partial credit memos for material invoices and service invoices. Restrictions related to dynamic discounting Auto generation of dynamic discounting credit memos is limited to supplier-submitted invoices on SAP Business Network. Dynamic discounting credit memos cannot be generated for service invoices, service entry sheets, invoices with allowances, nor deleted, rejected, or failed invoices. The dynamic discount credit memo feature does not apply to SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing; buyers must integrate via cXML through SAP PI Netweaver or their own middleware. Related Information Creating Credit Memos [page 66] Creating Credit Memos Creating a PO-Based or Service Header Level Credit Memo [page 67] Creating a PO-Based or Service Line Item Credit Memo [page 67] Creating a Non-PO Credit Memo [page 68] Flipping a Purchase Order to a Line-Item Credit Memo for Returned Items [page 69] Creating a Credit Memo for Return Items [page 70] Creating a Line-Item Credit Memo to Reduce Quantities or Prices for an Invoice [page 71] 66 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos Creating a PO-Based or Service Header Level Credit Memo Use this procedure to create a purchase order based credit memo or a service header level credit memo. Prerequisites See Prerequisites [page 65].  Restriction See Restrictions [page 65]. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • • For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: 2. Select the purchase order, and select Create Invoice Orders Orders Purchase Orders Orders and Releases Credit Memo . 3. Enter the invoice number and adjustment amounts (in negative numbers) in the fields provided. If your purchase order is set up for PCard or credit card payments, your credit memo is labeled Information Only. 4. Click Next to review the credit memo details. 5. Click Previous to make changes to the credit memo. Clicking Previous is necessary only if you need to change your input. 6. Click Submit. Creating a PO-Based or Service Line Item Credit Memo Use this procedure to create a purchase order based credit memo or a service line level credit memo. Prerequisites See Prerequisites [page 65].  Restriction See Restrictions [page 65]. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos PUBLIC 67 Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • • For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: 2. Select the purchase order, and select Create Invoice Orders Orders Purchase Orders Orders and Releases Line Item Credit Memo . 3. From the list of invoices, select an invoice and click Create Line Item Credit Memo. 4. Click Next to review your memo. 5. Click Previous to make any changes. Clicking Previous is necessary only if you need to change your input. 6. Click Submit. Creating a Non-PO Credit Memo Non-PO credit memos are invoices that are not based on a purchase order. These are the result of a sale outside of a regulated procurement process. Prerequisites See Prerequisites [page 65].  Restriction See Restrictions [page 65]. Procedure 1. Choose Create Non-PO Invoice . 2. Select a customer name from the dropdown menu. 3. In the Type of Invoice section, select Credit Memo. 4. Click Next. 5. Click Previous to make any changes. Clicking Previous is necessary only if you need to change your input. 6. Click Submit to go to the next step. 68 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos Related Information Credit Memos [page 63] Flipping a Purchase Order to a Line-Item Credit Memo for Returned Items Depending on the buyer's invoice rules, you can create a line-item credit memo for receipts with returned items directly from a purchase order. You can also create the line-item credit memo from the invoice for the received items. In that case, the invoice contains references to the receipts, and when you create the line item credit memo the receipt references are copied to it. Prerequisites The buyer must enable rules that require suppliers to include the following on invoices: • • Received quantities only References to receipts Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • • For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: Orders Orders Purchase Orders Orders and Releases 2. Open a purchase order. 3. Click Create Invoice > Line-Item Credit Memo.  Note If there are no returned items to be credited, the Line-Item Credit Memo command is not available. 4. If the Select receipts to be credited page appears, select receipts to include in the credit memo, and then click Next. Otherwise, complete the first page of the Create Line-Item Credit Memo wizard, and click Next. 5. Complete the Create Line-Item Credit Memo wizard, and click Submit. The credit memo includes only returned quantities, and it has references to receipts for each line item. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos PUBLIC 69 Creating a Credit Memo for Return Items Use this procedure to reimburse the buyer for goods they have returned. Prerequisites To create a credit memo for return items, the buyer must allow you to send line-item credit memos. Restrictions • • • The quantity for a credit memo for return items cannot exceed the return quantity on the order. All return items on a Return Item Credit Memo must be from the same order. You cannot create a Return Item Credit Memo for return items from multiple orders. If a return item or the entire order is flagged for Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS) or the order does not allow Ariba invoicing, then a credit memo cannot be created for that return item. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • • Orders For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: Orders Purchase Orders Orders and Releases 2. Click the Return Items tab.  Note You can also create a credit memo for return items on a particular order by opening the order and selecting Create Invoice > Credit Memo for Return Items. 3. To search for a specific return item, click the triangle next to the Search Filters heading, enter the criteria desired, and click Search. 4. Select one or more return items from the same order. 5. Click Credit Memo for Return Items.  Note If you selected only one item, you can also select Actions > Credit Memo for Return Items. 6. Enter a Credit Memo #. 7. If any return items were damaged, adjust the Price to the actual return value for the items. 8. Click Next to review your memo. 9. Click Previous to make any changes. Clicking Previous is necessary only if you need to change your input. 10. Click Submit. 70 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos

file://SBN/split/Creating and Managing I.content: Creating a Line-Item Credit Memo to Reduce Quantities or Prices for an Invoice Use this procedure to create a line-item credit memo to reduce quantities or prices at the line level for an invoice. Prerequisites See Prerequisites [page 65].  Restriction See Restrictions [page 65]. Procedure 1. Choose Invoices Invoices . 2. Select an invoice and click Create Line-Item Credit Memo. 3. If your customer allows you to make quantity and price adjustments, choose the credit memo type, either Quantity Adjustment or Price Adjustment.  Note • • • If you change the credit memo type, the Line Items section is reloaded. If you are reducing the quantity for a line item, the new quantity must be negative. If you are reducing the price for a line item, the new unit price must be negative. 4. Click Next to review your memo. 5. Click Previous to make any changes. Clicking Previous is necessary only if you need to change your input. 6. Click Submit. Debit Memos Debit memos are invoices that inform your customers of a corrected price after invoice acceptance. You can issue line-item debit memos for billing problems, such as: • • • The price for an item in an invoice is less than the agreed upon price. The price for an item in an invoice increased due to fluctuations. There were increases in tax or shipping amounts after you sent an invoice. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos PUBLIC 71 Types of Debit Memos SAP Business Network supports the following types of debit memos: • • PO-based line-item debit memo Non-PO line-item debit memo The Debit Memos Workbench Tile The Debit memos workbench tile displays a count of credit memos that you have created. When you select a Debit memos workbench tile, the workbench displays them in a list, in addition to filters, default columns, and based on your customer's transaction rules, your user permissions, and document status, allows actions as follow: Tile Filters Default Columns Actions Debit memos Customer Debit memo number Edit Debit memo number Debit memo date External debit memo number Customer Debit memo date Debit memo status Debit memo status Debit memo status date Debit memo status change change date Routing status Routing status Reference Reference From address From country To address To country Amount Min amount Invoice type Max amount Currency Submitted by View Invoice type Prerequisites You must have Inbox Access, Outbox Access, and Invoice Generation user permissions to be able to create and manage invoices. 72 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos Each SAP Business Network customer selects business rules that define the types of transactions that are allowed, including whether suppliers can send line-item debit memos. If the Create Line-Item Debit Memo button is disabled, the customer does not accept line-item debit memos. To edit quantity in PO-based line-item debit memos, your customer must enable the business rule of Allow suppliers to edit quantity in line-item price adjustment credit and debit memos. Restrictions Debit memos have following restrictions: • • • SAP Business Network does not support header-level debit memos. • • • You can’t use line-item debit memos to increase quantities for an invoice. You can't create line-item debit memos against invoices generated from SAP Ariba invoice conversion services. You can create a line-item debit memo only for an existing standard invoice. You can’t create one for an order that hasn’t been invoiced. You can’t create a line-item debit memo by uploading a CSV file. You can’t create a line-item debit memo against a service invoice based on service sheets. Creating a Line-Item Debit Memo to Increase Prices for an Invoice Use this procedure to create a line-item debit memo to adjust the price by an increased amount at the line level for an invoice. Prerequisites See Prerequisites [page 72].  Restriction See Restrictions [page 73]. Procedure 1. Choose Invoices Invoices . 2. From the list of invoices, select an invoice and click Create Line-Item Debit Memo. 3. Complete the debit memo. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos PUBLIC 73  Note If you are making a price adjustment for a line item, the new unit price must be positive. 4. Click Next to review the debit memo. 5. To make any changes, click Previous. Otherwise, click Submit. 74 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos Credit and Debit Memos CSV Invoices A CSV file is a Comma Separated Value file that represents a structured method of storing data. A CSV invoice enables suppliers with a large number of invoices to submit their invoices to customers in one consolidated file. If you cannot create cXML or EDI invoices and do not want to create invoices in SAP Business Network manually, CSV invoice import provides you with a convenient way of routing invoices to your customers. Another advantage of including multiple invoices in a single CSV file is that you can save significant time and effort.  Note You can import CSV files into SAP Business Network only if your customer has enabled this feature. To import CSV invoices into SAP Business Network, you perform three steps: 1. Download [page 76] your customer’s CSV invoice. 2. Fill in the field values in the CSV invoice. 3. Import [page 77] the properly formatted CSV invoices into SAP Business Network. Correctly formatted invoices will be imported successfully. If your invoice is incorrectly formatted, you will receive an error message. You can then correct the formatting error and repeat the import process. Helpful Hints to Populate CSV Invoices Given below are a few dos and don'ts to help you prepare CSV invoices before you import them into SAP Business Network . • • • Ensure that you are using the current version of the CSV template provided by your customer. • Do not enter special characters prohibited by your customer. If you are not sure of characters that are not allowed, contact your customer. • If the CSV invoice displays unrecognizable characters, save the CSV invoice, re-open it with the CSV editor, and save the file with character code set “UTF-8” and set the BOM flag. • • • • Do not save the CSV invoice as a workbook. • Do not include the terminology "script" anywhere in the CSV file name. Use a supported CSV file editor to edit the CSV invoice. For example, use Ron's Editor. Do not alter or update the original CSV invoice format that you download from SAP Business Network. This will cause the import process to fail. Always preserve the downloaded CSV invoice in its native format. Do not add macros to the CSV invoice. Do not add or delete columns. The first three rows of the CSV template are read-only. Contact your customer if you have queries on read-only rows. Downloading a Customer's CSV Invoice Template [page 76] Downloading the Original CSV and the CSV Invoice Errors Files [page 77] Importing CSV Invoices and Invoice Attachments [page 77] Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos CSV Invoices PUBLIC 75 Checking Status of an Invoice That Is Part of a CSV File [page 79] Navigating to the Invoice Detail Page of an Invoice [page 79] Troubleshooting Possible Issues with CSV Invoices [page 80] Downloading a Customer's CSV Invoice Template Use this procedure to download a customer’s CSV invoice template. Prerequisites Your customers must configure their accounts before you can download their CSV invoice templates. Context SAP Business Network converts each invoice in your CSV file to a cXML invoice. Customers use this invoice data in many ways, and may need to specify different CSV invoice formats. You can learn more about each customer’s CSV invoice format by downloading their CSV invoice template from SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. In the right corner of the header bar, click the user icon then choose Settings Customer Relationships . 2. In the Current table on the Customer Relationships page, click the customer name. 3. On the Customer Details page, scroll down to the CSV Invoice Fields area and click Download CSV Invoice Template. 4. Save the file to your computer. 5. Open the template in a CSV editor (such as Ron's Editor) and enter your invoice data in the appropriate fields. Related Information CSV Invoices [page 75] Importing CSV Invoices and Invoice Attachments [page 77] 76 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos CSV Invoices Downloading the Original CSV and the CSV Invoice Errors Files Context Use this procedure to download the original CSV file that was uploaded previously and the CSV Invoice Errors files. Procedure 1. In the CSV Files page, click the CSV file that you want to download. 2. In the CSV File Information page, click the Download option. 3. Click Original CSV. 4. Save the file to your local computer. 5. If you want to download the CSV Invoice Errors file, click the Download option, and then CSV Invoice Errors. 6. Save the file to your local computer. Importing CSV Invoices and Invoice Attachments Use this procedure to import CSV invoices and invoice attachments Prerequisites • • • Your customers must configure their accounts before you can import CSV invoices. Download a customer's CSV invoice template. [page 76] Ensure that you have populated all the required fields. See CSV Invoices [page 75] for a few helpful tips while working with CSV invoices.  Restriction For importing CSV invoices, the following limitations apply: • • • • Maximum lines per file: 10000 Maximum number of invoices per file: 2500 Maximum file size: 40MB Maximum attachment file size: 10MB-100MB Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos CSV Invoices PUBLIC 77  Note • By default, the cumulative size of attachments associated with a document cannot exceed 10 MB. Customers can request to change that limit, which can be changed from 10 MB to 100 MB. • During file upload, attachment files are converted to plain ASCII text using base64 encoding. This conversion increases the file size by approximately 35%. Therefore, the actual file size limit is 65% of the configured maximum limit. For example, if the maximum allowed limit is set to 10 MB (10000 KB), the actual total attachment file size that users can add is 6500 KB. • SAP Business Network stores attachments for a maximum period of eighteen months, after which the attachments expire and are no longer available online. • Attachments can be added to CSV invoices at the header level only. You can include multiple invoices for a customer in a single CSV invoice, but you cannot include invoices for different customers in the same CSV invoice. Your invoice template must match your customer's current template. Procedure 1. Choose ... Invoice , in the CSV Upload section. The Import CSV Invoice page appears. 2. Choose the customer name from the dropdown menu. 3. Click Browse to select an invoice CSV file. 4. Select a file, and click Open. 5. Click Import CSV Invoice. The page displays a list of invoices uploaded from the CSV file. 6. (Optional) For each invoice, click Browse to select an attachment.  Note The Browse button for attachments is visible only if the customer allows you to send attachments for invoices. a. Select a file, and click Open. b. Click Upload Related Document to upload the file. c. Upload other attachments as needed. 7. Click Submit.  Note The CSV invoice and its attachments are not saved on the SAP Business Network until you click Submit. 78 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos CSV Invoices Results The CSV invoice, with its attached files, appears on the Invoices Invoices page.  Note After you import a CSV file into SAP Business Network, you may not be able to view the invoice immediately. If you want to view the CSV invoice immediately, use the Search option. Checking Status of an Invoice That Is Part of a CSV File Use this procedure to check the status of an individual invoice that is part of a CSV file. Procedure 1. In the CSV Files page, click the CSV file you want to view the details of. 2. In the CSV Invoice Details section, click the link in the Invoice Status column for the individual invoice (for which to view the status). The invoice history is displayed on your screen. This is the same page that is displayed in the History tab of the invoice detail page. Navigating to the Invoice Detail Page of an Invoice Use this procedure to navigate to the invoice detail page in SAP Business Network from the CSV File Information page. Procedure 1. In the CSV Files page, click the CSV file you want to view the details of. 2. In the CSV Invoice Details section, click the link in the Invoice # column for the individual invoice (for which to view the invoice detail page). The invoice detail page is displayed on your screen. This is the same page that is shown when you open an invoice in your SAP Business Network Outbox. To navigate back to the CSV File Information page, click the Back button. Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos CSV Invoices PUBLIC 79 Troubleshooting Possible Issues with CSV Invoices You might encounter the following problems when trying to view, create, and submit CSV invoices on SAP Business Network. The table below describes a few possible problems and their solutions. Table 2: Troubleshooting Possible Issues with CSV Invoices Problem Solution I am unable to import the CSV invoice to SAP Business Net- Does your file meet the basic CSV requirements? Look for work. specific error messages to help identify fields that may need to be corrected. For example, review the CSV invoice for: • • • Missing header information Missing data in required fields Incorrect formatting in fields Correct errors if any, and import the CSV invoice again. My file was imported successfully, but a few invoices show a Do your invoices meet your customer-configured invoice rules? "Failed" status in my outbox. When invoices are converted from the CSV file type to individual invoice documents on SAP Business Network, they are validated based on the invoice rules set by customers in their SAP Business Network accounts. • Click the History tab for error messages or additional status information about the invoice. • Correct any customer-configured invoice rule violations that you detect in the invoice, and resend the invoice.  Note Resend only those invoices that show a "Failed" status. My file was imported successfully, but a few invoices show a "Rejected" status in my outbox. This means that the invoices passed the CSV and SAP Business Network checks, but were rejected either by your customer's invoicing system or by your customer manually. • Click the History tab for error messages or additional status information about the invoice. • Correct any problems with individual invoices and resend them.  Note Resend only those invoices that show a "Rejected" status. 80 PUBLIC Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos CSV Invoices
