The Registered and Received Interactive Email columns can be used to view interactive email-order suppliers and their registration status. Workflow The following is the one-time password workflow associated with interactive email-orders: 1. Your procurement system sends a purchase order to a supplier through SAP Business Network. 2. If the routing method is email (the cXML purchase order shows Email name = "routing"), SAP Business Network chooses the appropriate interactive email-order template, and sends the supplier an interactive email-order based on that template. 3. If needed, a new private SAP Business Network supplier account is created and vendor details are defaulted. 4. When the supplier receives an interactive email-order, the supplier reviews the order and takes any of the following actions: • • • • • • Confirms the entire purchase order. Creates a partial or full invoice. Registers a new account or logs in using an existing account. Asks your organization a question. Declines the relationship request. Forwards the interactive email-order to another person in their company.  Note Some actions might not be available. 5. If the supplier creates an invoice, SAP Business Network sends them a PDF copy of the invoice, and the invoice data in cXML format with the invoice confirmation email. 6. Depending on how the buyer integration to SAP Business Network is configured, suppliers might also receive invoice status updates as email notifications from SAP Business Network. Letter Templates SAP Business Network uses different criteria to select a letter template for the one-time password flow. If the routing method for the supplier is email and the one-time password flow is enabled for the buyer, SAP Business Network uses the interactive email-order templates. SAP Business Network bases the selection of the template on the status of the supplier (registered or unregistered), and on whether the supplier owed SAP Ariba subscription fees earlier. The Supplier Enablement Configure templates for the email routing method: • • Letter Content tab includes the following purchase order letter Interactive Email-Order Letter (Supplier Registered) Interactive Email-Order Letter (Supplier Unregistered) The following table shows which interactive email-order template is used in various scenarios: Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 11 Registration Status Received PO from Earlier Release Incurred Subscription Fees Interactive Email-Order Letter Template Unregistered No - Supplier Unregistered Unregistered Yes No Supplier Unregistered Unregistered Yes Yes Supplier Unregistered Registered Yes No Supplier Registered If the routing method for the supplier is fax, SAP Business Network uses one of the existing purchase order templates. SAP Business Network bases the selection of the template on the thresholds that the buyer configures for the templates. Reporting The following reports include a Received Interactive Email column: • • • Supplier Enablement Status Report Supplier Enablement Task Status Report Supplier Membership Status Report If suppliers receive an interactive email-order, the Received Interactive Email column shows Yes. Restrictions The one-time password flow has the following restrictions: • Help: The user community capability (the help center) isn't available for suppliers that use the one-time password flow to process purchase orders. Instead, a dedicated help page is available for suppliers at this time. • SAP Ariba invoice conversion services (ICS): ICS can be used in combination with interactive email-orders. However, if the ICS quick enablement welcome letter is activated, suppliers will be directed to register, which may trigger fees for suppliers. • Purchase orders: • • 12 • Legacy purchase orders are not supported. Legacy POs aren't routed to supplier email. Suppliers must register on SAP Business Network to access and invoice legacy POs. • For PCard interactive email-orders, the PO and HTML attachments show a masked PCard number (only the last 4 digits of the PCard number are shown). The supplier must have access to the full PCard number on file. Invoice creation through the direct action button is automatically blocked. Order confirmations: Suppliers can only create full order confirmations directly from interactive email-orders. Invoices: • If an invoice is rejected, a new invoice must be created. Non-registered suppliers cannot access previous invoices like registered suppliers can. • • Draft invoices cannot be saved or stored. Contract invoicing through punch-in isn't supported. PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement • • • • • • The attribute display for blanket purchase orders are limited. Suppliers cannot change the remit-to address. The remit-to ID can't be prepopulated. Suppliers cannot add bank details. Cancellation invoices and credit memos aren't supported. Interactive email-orders: • Registered suppliers continue to receive subscription invoice fees for purchase orders that are delivered to them. • Buyers can't send interactive email-orders to suppliers in the following countries: • • • • • Brazil Chile Colombia Mexico Africa (all countries)  Note Suppliers in these countries receive quick enablement purchase orders instead. • Suspended suppliers: SAP Ariba doesn't allow transaction types, including interactive email-orders, or status updates to be sent to suspended suppliers. • POs for SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing : Supplier Name is based on the supplier name in SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, not on Supplier Location Name. • Invoices for SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing: Suppliers receive manually entered invoice status comments only when provided on the invoice, not from the invoice reconciliation (IR) rejection. • Fax PO routing • • The existing threshold based quick enablement purchase order letter is used. • Interactive email-orders can be sent only through email. Interactive email-orders don't work when purchase orders are sent using fax as the routing method for the purchase order. Suppliers can't create order confirmations, ship notices, or take other direct actions until the routing method is changed to Email and the buyer sends another purchase order. Standard Account Capability for SAP Business Network The standard account capability for SAP Business Network provides buyers with a quick and touchless way to onboard all their suppliers and eliminate manual transaction processes. Standard accounts are free, easy-to-use accounts on SAP Business Network that allow suppliers to exchange an unlimited number of basic documents. After a buyer is set up to enable suppliers through standard accounts, all existing quick enablement flows and the non-PO invoice creation with customer code flow will direct suppliers to register an SAP Business Network standard account. All these flows are listed in the Supplier Enablement Configure with a Supplier Registration Type of Quick Enablement or Standard Account. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement Letter Content section PUBLIC 13 When buyers enable suppliers through the standard account capability, suppliers receive one of the following to get started: • • • • • An interactive email-order that contains the purchase order details A carbon copy (CC) invoice email The buyer's customer code to create a non-PO invoice A payment proposal email A quote request email From an interactive email-order notification, suppliers can take the following actions: • Add the purchase order to an existing account: If suppliers have already registered an account on SAP Business Network, they can sign in with their existing administrator account information. Any interactive email-orders the buyer sent to them are merged with their existing account. • Register a standard account and create documents against the purchase order: When suppliers receive their first interactive email-order, they click Process order to register a free, standard account on SAP Business Network. After registering their company, they are taken to the purchase order details page to create documents like order confirmations, ship notices, service sheets (for service orders), invoices, or credit memos. When they click Process order in the future, suppliers are taken directly to the login page so they can sign in and view the purchase order in their standard account.  Tip After registering a standard account, if suppliers misplace an interactive email-order notification, they can resend the purchase order email to the configured email address from their home dashboard. • Contact the buyer: If suppliers have questions, they can click the link for the buyer's name in the Frequently Asked Questions section of the interactive email-order notification to send an email message to the buyer. • Decline the relationship request: If suppliers don't want to transact with the buyer on SAP Business Network, they can click the stop receiving emails link in the Frequently Asked Questions section of the interactive email-order notification to tell the buyer that they are declining the request. All subsequent documents sent to the supplier will fail. • Forward the interactive email-order notification: The person who receives the interactive email-order can forward the notification to another person in their company. If the person who forwarded the email already registered the standard account, that person is the account administrator. On the login page, other users have the option to send a message to the account administrator to request a new user account. After suppliers submit invoices, SAP Business Network sends them PDF and cXML copies of the invoice in the invoice confirmation email. Suppliers can retain these files to support their local business records storage and archiving requirements. Suppliers may also receive invoice status updates from buyers, sent as email notifications from SAP Business Network. Because suppliers are registering a standard account on SAP Business Network, they also get access to SAP Business Network Discovery to find new business opportunities and, if used by their buyers, they get access to SAP Ariba Sourcing and SAP Ariba Contracts.  Note Suppliers may incur optional fees for participating in certain leads on SAP Business Network Discovery. Suppliers also have the power to choose if and when to upgrade to an enterprise account to run reports or integrate with external systems. Suppliers can choose to upgrade from a standard account to an enterprise account at any time by clicking Learn More at the top of any page in their standard account or by clicking Learn 14 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement More when hovering over any grayed out area of their standard account, such as the Purchase Orders menu. Both the buyer and the supplier are notified by email when the supplier upgrades to an enterprise account.  Note Upgrading to an enterprise account on SAP Business Network may lead to subscription fees for suppliers. For information about the different subscription levels and the pricing by region, visit the SAP Ariba subscriptions and pricing page and choose a region from the Download Datasheet area along the right side of the page. When suppliers upgrade to an enterprise account in production, their test account also gets upgraded automatically. However, if they upgrade from the test account, the production account isn't upgraded.  Tip Suppliers might want to upgrade their test account first in order to explore the additional features before they commit to upgrading their production account. Suppliers have access to help content and videos in the SAP Ariba help center, which is accessible along the right side of each page and by opening the help center in a new window. Suppliers have access to submit a web form to request help from SAP Ariba Support, but this option becomes visible only after they search for help on the Support Center page of the help center.  Restriction Suppliers can contact SAP Ariba Support only in cases where they experience technical issues with their standard accounts. Buyers are expected to handle all questions related to transactions and functionality in standard accounts. When to choose the standard account method Standard accounts are intended for suppliers with limited annual transactions. We recommend that buyers target a subset of their suppliers for standard account registration, which allows all their suppliers to derive value according to their size and volume. This makes supplier enablement more efficient by allowing buyers to focus on actively enabling suppliers that need enterprise accounts first, followed by the group of suppliers targeted for standard accounts. We recommend using the standard account method in the following situations: • • • Large capital spend suppliers (high value, low document count) Smaller suppliers that transact fewer than 100 documents per year (purchase orders and invoices) Suppliers who don't have e-commerce capabilities but utilize email (must have a valid email address) Buyers should continue to target the following suppliers for enterprise account registration: • • Strategic suppliers Legacy, EDI-integrated suppliers Enterprise account suppliers need more automated, efficient ways to transact or are too important not to proactively manage. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 15 Enabling the standard account capability If your organization was never enabled for interactive email-orders, please have your Designated Support Contact log a service request to enable the standard account capability. An SAP Ariba Support representative will follow up to complete the request. Prerequisites Buyers need to meet the following prerequisites to enable suppliers through standard accounts: • Your organization needs to be set up to send quick enablement cXML documents to SAP Business Network using email routing, as documented in the cXML Solutions Guide. • SAP Ariba Procurement solutions send quick enablement documents when the supplier location Preferred Ordering Method is set to Email. • For buyers who use an SAP Ariba adapter to connect from their ERP to SAP Business Network, see the SAP Ariba adapter documentation for details on configuring this workflow. Restrictions The standard account capability has the following restrictions: • Purchase orders: • If you want to send legacy orders to standard account suppliers, you need to enable them through another document type first. After the supplier registers a standard account, you can send legacy orders to them. From their standard account home dashboard, they can send a copy of the legacy order through email, which gives them access to the Process order option. The email notification indicates to the supplier that the order was already fulfilled. • Blanket purchase orders (BPOs) are supported, but some BPO details aren't displayed in interactive email-order notifications, such as minimum and maximum quantities.  Recommendation Test the end-to-end BPO flow to understand what standard account suppliers see in the email notification versus what they see while logged in to their standard account. • Purchase orders for SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing: • Supplier Name is based on the supplier name in SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, not on the supplier location Name value. • SAP Ariba Contract Invoicing isn't supported by default for standard accounts. Buyers need to request the activation of this flow if needed. • Invoices for SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing: Suppliers receive manually-entered, invoice-status comments only on the invoice (INV) document. They don't receive comments from the invoice reconciliation (IR) document when you reject the IR. • Carbon copy (CC) invoices: You can send additional CC invoices after the supplier registers a standard account, but the supplier will receive only the invoice status email notification. Suppliers can click View invoice in the notification to access the CC invoice. 16 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement • SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: Standard accounts can't be enabled for documents like consignment collaboration, forecast collaboration, or manufacturing planning visibility. If you send scheduling agreement releases to standard account suppliers, the documents aren't sent. If you send scheduling agreement releases to unregistered suppliers, SAP Business Network follows the enterprise account registration flow. • Suspended supplier relationships: SAP Ariba doesn't allow transaction types, including interactive emailorders, or status updates to be sent to suspended supplier relationships. • Supplier account configuration: • Suppliers can choose only Email for their electronic order routing configuration method. They can upgrade to an enterprise account to use the cXML, EDI, fax, or CSV methods. Viewing and reporting on suppliers with standard accounts You can distinguish between standard account suppliers and enterprise account suppliers by using the filters and column headers on the supplier enablement pages: • The Manage Vendors and Monitor pages on the Supplier Enablement tab have an Account Type filter and an Account Type column in the list of suppliers. You can also use the Registered column to find out the registration status of suppliers that you're enabling through the standard accounts method. • The Supplier Enablement Active Relationships page has a Standard Account Suppliers filter in the Supplier Selector menu and an Account Type column in the list of suppliers. • The Search Suppliers page has an Account Type column in the search result list. The following reports include Account Type and Received Interactive Email columns: • • • Supplier Enablement Status Report Supplier Enablement Task Status Report Supplier Membership Status Report If a supplier has registered a standard account, the Account Type column shows Standard account. All other suppliers and any suppliers who have upgraded are indicated as a Enterprise account. If suppliers receive an interactive email-order, the Received Interactive Email column shows Yes. Registration and Document Workflow for Standard Accounts After suppliers register a standard account on SAP Business Network, the workflow skips the account creation and registration steps. The following diagram describes the standard accounts workflow for your organization and your suppliers, once you're set up to use the standard account supplier enablement method.  Note Suppliers can choose to upgrade to an enterprise account at any point during the process. The lower portion of the diagram provides the enterprise account registration flow for comparison. 18 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement Figure 2: Standard Account Registration Methods Migrating Suppliers from the One-Time Password Flow to Standard Accounts If your organization has already sent interactive email-orders to suppliers through the SAP Business Network one-time password flow, you can follow this self-service migration process to transition existing suppliers and enable new suppliers through the standard account method. Context The self-service migration allows your organization to decide when it's the right time to transition your existing suppliers over to standard accounts. Your organization controls the change management, and your suppliers are informed about the benefits and change impact of standard accounts. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Configure . 2. On the Letter Content tab, locate the Alternate Supplier Invitation Letters (not in use) section. You'll see 3 letter templates related to standard accounts: • • • Interactive Email-Order Letter (Supplier Registered) Interactive Email-Order Letter (Supplier Suspended) Interactive Email-Order Letter (Supplier Unregistered) 3. Do the following for one of the 3 letter templates related to the Standard Account supplier registration type: Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 19 a. Click the letter template name, and choose Activate This Letter. b. When you see the confirmation message, click OK. Results After your migration to the standard account method, all suppliers who receive interactive email-orders will need to sign up for a free standard account on SAP Business Network the next time you send a purchase order to them. Existing suppliers who used the one-time password flow will see the following message in their first interactive email-order notification: There's a new way to process orders on SAP Business Network. Previously, without an account you had to use a one-time password for each order response. Now, just sign up for a FREE SAP Business Network standard account to process orders and do more on the network. See all benefits. Click Process order to sign up for a free standard account. Letter Template for Standard Accounts If a supplier's routing method is email and the standard accounts feature is enabled for your organization, SAP Business Network uses the standard account template to send purchase orders to the supplier. The Supplier Enablement Configure Letter Content tab includes the following purchase order letter template for supplier enablement through standard accounts: • Interactive Email-Order Letter (Direct Supplier Contact) Workflow to Create and Edit Letter Templates 1. As a buyer on the SAP Business Network dashboard, choose Supplier Enablement tab and click Configure. Select a template and click Actions to activate. Once the letter is active, click Actions to edit. Customize the new template letter body with a personalized invitation message.  Note If you are a long-term customer, you find new purchase order templates in the Alternate Supplier Invitation Letters (not in use) section. 2. The buyer sends a purchase order document. 3. The supplier receives the order and clicks the button in the email. 4. The supplier is redirected to the registration landing page. SAP Business Network determines whether or not there's an existing user account or an existing supplier company account. 20 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement

Supplier Enablement Permissions to Assign to Account Users The account administrator configures user accounts with the specific permissions to manage the supplier enablement process. Account administrators automatically have all of these permissions.  Note For information about how to create users and to assign permissions to them, see SAP Business Network Users and SAP Business Network Permissions in the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide. Permission Description Supplier Enablement Program Administrator This permission includes all the other permissions available for managing the supplier enablement process. Configure supplier enablement thresholds, upload vendors, start supplier enablement, manage supplier enablement tasks, and access vendor data export reports. Supplier Enablement Configuration Allows you to configure supplier invitation letters, tasks, and activities for supplier enablement. Supplier Enablement Task Management Allows you to manage and monitor tasks for supplier enablement and edit vendor details (vendor name, preferred language, email, contact information, address, vendor comments, enablement status). Supplier Enablement Report Administration Allows you to access and run supplier enablement reports: Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement • • Supplier Enablement Task Status Supplier Enablement Status PUBLIC 21 Turning On Quick Enablement Your organization can configure your SAP Business Network account to allow for quick enablement of suppliers. Context Quick enablement refers to sending a document, such as a purchase order, through SAP Business Network to create a placeholder account for an unregistered supplier. The supplier can then register to take ownership of the account. Procedure 1. Choose Administration Configuration . 2. On the Configuration page, click Default Transaction Rules. 3. In the Quick Enablement Rules section, choose Allow Quick Enablement. 4. Click Save. Related Information Standard Account Capability for SAP Business Network [page 13] Supplier Invitation Letters Supplier invitation letters are sent to vendors and quick-enabled suppliers when you initiate a relationship with them. You can choose to use the standard letter content or create custom content [page 24] for the different letters. You can view the standard content for each letter by going to and then choosing Actions Preview Template Supplier Enablement Configure Letter Content next to a letter. SAP Business Network supports multiple supplier enablement methods that allow you to initiate trading relationships. When you invite suppliers to join SAP Business Network, they receive a trading relationship request invitation letter by fax or email. A supplier invitation letter is sent when you invite a vendor through the following supplier enablement methods: • 22 Trading relationship requests: Guides suppliers to register your choice of enterprise [page 96] or standard [page 13] account. PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement For this enablement method, you can choose between three letters on the Letter Content tab: • • • Trading Relationship Request Letter (Option 1) Trading Relationship Request Letter (Option 2) Trading Relationship Request Letter (Option 3) If you want to switch which letter SAP Business Network sends on your behalf, scroll down to the Alternate Supplier Invitation Letters (not in use) section, and choose inactive option. • Actions Activate This Letter next to the Quick enablement: Sends a document to the supplier and creates a private account. If your organization has the standard account capability [page 13] enabled, this process guides suppliers to register a free, standard account. Otherwise, suppliers register an enterprise account. For more details about the difference between standard accounts and full-use accounts, see Supplier Enablement Terms [page 96]. • ICS invoice (invoices sent from an invoice conversion service provider)  Note You can configure thresholds for ICS invoice welcome letters [page 28]. • • • Invoice copy (invoices sent from SAP Ariba Buying solutions or an ERP system) Payment proposal Purchase order  Note You can configure thresholds for purchase order welcome letters [page 26]. • • Quotation request Trading relationship request for quick enabled suppliers For this enablement method, you can choose between two letters on the Letter Content tab: • • Trading Relationship Request for Quick Enabled Suppliers Trading Relationship Request for Quick Enabled Suppliers (Basic) The Trading Relationship Request for Quick Enabled Suppliers (Basic) template contains only minimal SAP Ariba content and allows buyer administrators to customize almost all of the request template. For best results, add content details that help suppliers to understand the context, any buyer-specific expectations, and the value of establishing the trading relationship. If the buyer organization logo is available, it's included automatically in the template. If it's not available, the buyer organization name displays where the logo would be. If you want to switch which letter SAP Business Network sends on your behalf, scroll down to the Alternate Supplier Invitation Letters (not in use) section, then choose inactive option. • Actions Activate This Letter next to the Interactive email - order: Sends a purchase order through email to the supplier. If your organization is set up for the one-time password flow [page 10], suppliers remain unregistered and use the action buttons in the purchase order email notification to process and invoice the purchase order. If your organization has the standard account capability [page 13] enabled, suppliers are prompted to register a free, standard account before they can take action on the purchase order. After the vendors register and accept the SAP Business Network terms of use, a dedicated supplier account is created on SAP Business Network and a relationship is established with your organization. Creating Custom Supplier Invitation Letters [page 24] Configuring Thresholds for Purchase Order Welcome Letters [page 26] Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 23 Configuring Thresholds for ICS Invoice Welcome Letters [page 28] Creating Custom Supplier Invitation Letters Custom content can improve the chances that suppliers review the invitation letters carefully and comply with your requirements. Prerequisites You have the Supplier Enablement Program Administrator or Supplier Enablement Configuration permission to configure invitation letters. Context You can optionally customize the content in the supplier invitation letters that ask suppliers to register on SAP Business Network.  Tip If you don't customize the welcome letters, the standard SAP Ariba content is included in invitations sent to suppliers. The following guidelines and hints apply to custom content in supplier invitation letters and in the supplier information portal [page 31]: • • You can create custom content for any combination of supported languages and countries/regions. • • For every country/region, the default country/region-specific content is the English content. Global custom content must exist in English before you can create content for another language or for a specific country/region. For any given country/region, English custom content must exist for that location before you can create content in any other language.  Example Before you can create Spanish content for Mexico, you must create English content for Mexico. • If you want to delete the global English custom content (that is, English content that isn't country/regionspecific), you must first delete the custom content for all other languages and countries/regions.  Caution For the supplier information portal, if you delete English country/region-specific content, SAP Business Network also deletes all other custom content for that location. A confirmation message gives you a chance to confirm or cancel the action. 24 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement • When you create country/region-specific content, it's a good idea (but not a requirement) to create custom content in all potential language and country/region combinations. Doing so ensures that suppliers receive the correct, customer-specific content. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Configure . 2. On the Configure page, click the Letter Content tab. 3. On the Letter Content tab of the Configure page, find the letter template you want to edit, and choose Actions Create/Edit Custom Content. 4. Choose a language to customize the custom-specific content in the preferred language of the supplier. 5. (Optional) Choose a country/region to create country/region-specific content in the selected language. 6. Enter the content in the text editor. 7. Click Save. Results SAP Business Network checks whether your welcome letters are customized and references the supplier's country/region and language to determine which content to send to the supplier in any given situation. Next Steps You can preview the custom content you created by choosing customized template. Actions Preview Template next to a How Does SAP Business Network Select Custom Content? When custom content exists in multiple languages and countries, SAP Business Network uses a selection process to determine which content to use in any given situation. This process applies to trading relationship letters and the supplier information portal. To determine which custom content to use, SAP Business Network: • • Checks the country and language of the supplier. • Uses a set of priorities to select the most appropriate content to use: Checks for custom content that matches the supplier’s country and language: After determining the supplier’s country and language, SAP Business Network checks whether custom content exists that matches the country and language of the supplier. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 25 1. Supplier's preferred language and country 2. Supplier's country, in English language 3. Supplier's preferred language 4. Default (global) English custom content Country and Language SAP Business Network gets country and language information in different ways, depending on the situation: • For trading relationship requests and discount letters, SAP Business Network gets country and language information from the existing supplier record. • For quick-enablement invitations, SAP Business Network gets country and language information from the document sent from the buyer. • For supplier information portal content, SAP Business Network gets the supplier’s country and language information as follows: • To get country information for the supplier, SAP Business Network first checks the main address in the supplier profile (the main address in the supplier’s company profile). If the supplier profile is not available (for example, in the case of private suppliers), SAP Business Network checks the default address of the vendor (the address specified on the Vendor Details page). If no country information is available for the supplier, SAP Business Network displays the global custom content. • For language information, SAP Business Network checks the locale setting of the supplier’s browser. Configuring Thresholds for Purchase Order Welcome Letters You can configure thresholds to manage which type of purchase order welcome letter is sent to a supplier. Prerequisites • • • • Your account must be enabled for quick enablement [page 22]. • You must have the Supplier Enablement Program Administrator or Supplier Enablement Configuration permission to configure thresholds. 26 If you haven't configured a threshold for the letter, the default threshold is used. If you have a test account, you must configure thresholds for your test account also. You can specify only a template for the Purchase Order Welcome Letter Threshold 1. You can't edit values in the other fields. PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement Context A threshold defines the number and total value of the purchase order sent. When one of the defined threshold parameters is met, the associated letter is sent to the supplier. The welcome letter section is a part of each quick enabled purchase order sent to suppliers. The content of the welcome letter differs depending on the number and total value of the purchase orders sent. The welcome letter section is included with the purchase order until the supplier registers on SAP Business Network and accepts the terms of use. SAP Business Network defines three default thresholds, and you can specify up to two additional thresholds. The following table shows the default threshold settings for quick enablement purchase order welcome letters: Purchase Order Welcome Letter Threshold Number of Purchase Orders Total Purchase Order Value - - - Purchase Order Letter 1 Contains only the purchase order and doesn't contain the link to register on SAP Business Network. This template isn't used by default. 1 1 0 Purchase Order Letter 2 Contains the purchase order and the link to register on SAP Business Network. Use this template to send suppliers a welcome letter to sign in using the temporary ID and secure code and register on SAP Business Network. 2 3 25,000 Purchase Order Letter 3 Contains the purchase order and the link to register on SAP Business Network. Use this template as a follow-up to the earlier welcome letters that invited the supplier to sign in using the temporary ID and secure code and register on SAP Business Network. 3 5 50,000 Purchase Order Letter 4 Contains the purchase order and the link to register on SAP Business Network. Use this template if the supplier hasn't registered after multiple reminders. 4 8 75,000 Purchase Order Letter 4 Contains the purchase order and the link to register on SAP Business Network. Use this template if the supplier hasn't registered after multiple reminders. 5 10 100,000 Purchase Order Letter 4 Contains the purchase order and the link to register on SAP Business Network. Use this template if the supplier hasn't registered after multiple reminders. Letter Template Template Contents Threshold settings are defined for a year. Thresholds are evaluated each time a purchase order is received based on the current purchase order count. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 27 You can preview the letters by clicking the Preview Template link. However, this preview doesn't include the actual purchase order details. If you have added custom content [page 24], you can also preview this information.  Example You have configured Purchase Order Welcome Letter Threshold 2 and specified the number of purchase orders as 3, total purchase order value per year as 4,000, and selected the welcome letter template 2. When you configure the next purchase threshold, you must ensure that the value is incremental to the previous value specified for Purchase Order Welcome Letter Threshold 2. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Configure . 2. On the Configure page, click the Quick Enablement Thresholds tab. 3. In the Document Type list, choose Purchase Order.  Note If you don’t subscribe to ICS, the Document Type field is read-only and Purchase Order is already selected. 4. Click Configure Threshold. 5. For each threshold other than threshold 1, specify the number of purchase orders you allow per year. Threshold 1 is set to 1 purchase order. 6. For each threshold other than threshold 1, specify the total value of the purchase orders you allow per year. Threshold 1 is set to a total value of zero (0). 7. For each threshold, choose the welcome letter template. 8. Optional: Click Add Buyer Threshold to define up to two more thresholds. 9. Click Save. Configuring Thresholds for ICS Invoice Welcome Letters You can have SAP Business Network send an invitation letter to a supplier as soon as you receive a specified number of invoices from that supplier through SAP Ariba invoice conversion services (ICS). Prerequisites • • • • 28 Your account must be enabled for quick enablement [page 22]. If you have a test account, you must configure thresholds for your test account also. There's only one ICS invoice threshold. You can't add more ICS invoice thresholds. You must have the Supplier Enablement Program Administrator or Supplier Enablement Configuration permission to configure thresholds. PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement Context ICS eases conversion of paper invoices to an electronic format. A service provider receives invoices on behalf of the buying organization and converts them to an electronic format for posting to SAP Business Network.  Example If the ICS invoice threshold is set to 5, when SAP Business Network receives the fifth invoice from a given supplier, it sends an invitation letter to the supplier. The supplier uses the link in the invitation to register on SAP Business Network and view the status of invoices. For more information about invoice conversion, see SAP Business Network Guide to Invoice Conversion.  Tip You can start supplier enablement manually for a supplier that was quick enabled through ICS but hasn't yet reached the ICS invoice volume threshold. Doing so sends the supplier the trading relationship request for quick-enabled suppliers. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Configure . 2. On the Configure page, click the Quick Enablement Thresholds tab. 3. In the Document Type list, choose ICS Invoice. If you don’t subscribe to ICS, the Document Type field is read-only and Purchase Order is selected. 4. Click Configure Threshold. 5. Enter a number in the Number of ICS Invoices field. 6. Click Save. Activities and Tasks SAP Business Network allows you to track suppliers based on key events that take place during the lifecycle of supplier enablement. Events in the supplier-enablement lifecycle are called tasks and are broadly grouped into activities. Activities and tasks are used to monitor and track the progress of suppliers on SAP Business Network. An activity is a method by which suppliers transact with a buying organization through SAP Business Network, for example, Purchase Order, Invoice, or Catalog. Each activity has a set of predefined tasks for supplier enablement. For example, when a supplier is supposed to receive purchase orders through SAP Business Network the activity is called Purchase Order Activity and it includes a task called Configure Purchase Order Routing and Notifications. Tasks have two closure types – system or manual. The system tasks are closed automatically by SAP Business Network, while the manual tasks are closed manually by the task owner after the requested action has been completed. Both your organization and the supplier have tasks associated with them. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 29 After you have uploaded vendors through a CSV file or by manually adding vendors, you can assign activities to selected vendors and start the enablement. Managing Activities and Tasks An activity can have a group of tasks associated with it and these tasks are monitored through supplier enablement. Each task has a description and configured logic to track when the task can be marked completed. Tasks are closely linked to each other. If a task is dependent on another, the corresponding task must be completed before the following task is due for completion. SAP Business Network automatically calculates the target date for the task based on preconfigured offset days. When new activities are assigned to vendors, an email notification is sent out to them. Adding a New Activity to the List New activities must be added to the list to be able to start them. Prerequisites You must have the Supplier Enablement Program Administrator or Supplier Enablement Configuration permission to configure activities. Context If you haven't yet started activities for any suppliers, you see all the available activities on the Supplier Enablement tab. However, if you're already running activities for suppliers and SAP Business Network adds a new activity, you must add the new activity to the list before you can start it. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Configure . 2. On the Configure page, click the Activities tab. 3. Click Add Activity next to the new activity. 30 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement

file://SBN/split/Enabling Suppliers on S.content: Previewing, Enabling, or Disabling Activities and Tasks You can view the preconfigured activities and tasks before you start enabling suppliers. You can choose to disable activities and tasks for supplier enablement. Context When you disable activities and tasks, suppliers that are already assigned to them aren't impacted. If you want to push the changes to existing vendors, you need to remove and reassign activities to them on the Manage Vendors or Monitor pages. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Configure . 2. On the Configure page, click the Activities tab to view all activities and tasks. 3. Optional: Expand an activity to see its tasks.  Note The Days to Complete and the Escalate on Day fields show the preconfigured dates for a task. 4. Choose or clear the check box for an activity or any of its tasks. When you choose the check box for an activity or task, its status changes to Enabled. Similarly, when you clear the check box for an activity or task, its status changes to Disabled. Supplier Information Portal You can create a supplier information portal to allow your suppliers to view information about your organization, such as specific content about your organization's processes. With the supplier information portal, you can do the following: • Create customized content [page 33] for suppliers using the rich-text editor that supports common formatting like bold, colors, underline, and bullets. • • Paste text from Microsoft Word into the rich-text editor. • • Enable extended profile settings [page 36] to share more detailed company information with suppliers. Upload [page 35] and share reference documents [page 36], such as your supported extrinsics, guides, and information like ship-to and bill-to addresses. Translate your supplier information portal into several different languages that are supported by SAP Business Network. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 31 Besides the shared customized content and reference documents, suppliers can also view your business transaction rules [page 37] in the supplier information portal. Suppliers can choose to receive email notifications [page 37] every time you update your shared company profile or share reference documents. You can create custom content in the following languages: • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • Brazilian Portuguese Danish Dutch English French French Canadian German Greek Hungarian Italian Japanese Korean Norwegian Polish Romanian Russian Simplified Chinese Spanish Swedish Turkish Country/Region-Specific Custom Content In addition to creating custom content in multiple languages, you can also create country/region-specific content in any combination of the languages and countries/regions that SAP Business Network supports.  Example If you want to customize the information sent to suppliers in different Spanish-speaking countries/regions, such as Spain, Mexico, and Argentina, you can create several versions of Spanish content: Spanish–Spain, Spanish–Mexico, Spanish–Argentina, and global Spanish content (for Spanish-speaking suppliers that aren't located in Spain, Mexico, or Argentina). For any given language, custom content that doesn't have a country/ region specified is called global custom content.  Note When determining which content to show in the supplier information portal [page 25], SAP Business Network first checks for country/region information in the supplier profile. If country/region information exists in the supplier profile, SAP Business Network doesn't check the country/region on the vendor details page. Therefore, if multiple SAP Business Network vendors are linked to the same public supplier, the country/region SAP Business Network uses might not match the actual vendor country/region. 32 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement How Suppliers View Supplier Information Portal Content Suppliers must have an SAP Business Network supplier account to access the supplier information portal, or they can use a secure link in the trading relationship request letter. A link to the supplier information portal is available to suppliers on the following pages: • • • • Enablement tasks Task details Customer relationships Trading relationship request letter These links give suppliers easy access to the supplier information portal if they need more information about your supplier enablement processes. Managing Custom Content for the Supplier Information Portal [page 33] Downloading a Reference Document Template [page 34] Uploading Documents to the Supplier Information Portal [page 35] Sharing or Stop Sharing a Reference Document [page 36] Filling Out Extended Profile Settings [page 36] Viewing Configured Invoicing Rules [page 37] Workflow for Notifying Suppliers About Updated Reference Information [page 37] Managing Custom Content for the Supplier Information Portal You can create custom letter content for the supplier information portal. Context You can edit or delete custom letter content at any time. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Information Portal . 2. Do one of the following: • Create and save custom new content in English. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 33  Note English content is the default content. You can't specify another language or country/region until English content exists. • • Edit custom content by clicking View, choosing the language, and clicking Edit. Delete custom content by clicking View, choosing the language, and clicking Delete. 3. To create custom content in other languages, choose a language on the Create/Edit tab, and enter and save the content.  Tip You can also add a language from the View tab by clicking an entry in the Country column, then choose Add Language. This option takes you to the Create/Edit tab, where you enter and save the content. 4. To create country/region-specific content, choose a country/region and a language on the Create/Edit tab, and enter and save the content.  Note You must first create English content for a country/region before you can create content for that location in any other language. 5. To add another language for the country/region-specific content that you just configured, return to the Create/ Edit tab, choose a language, and enter and save the content. Downloading a Reference Document Template You can download your reference document templates as your suppliers see them. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Information Portal . 2. Click Download Template and choose one of the following: • • Extrinsics Template for sharing information about the extrinsics you use Ship-To and Bill-To Template for sharing information about your shipping and billing addresses Your browser downloads the selected template in XLS format. 34 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement Uploading Documents to the Supplier Information Portal You can upload files containing additional information in several document formats. Prerequisites • • Ensure that the format for the uploaded documents is supported by the commonly used viewers. Don't exceed the maximum file size for each uploaded file, which is 4 MB. Context Document formats you can upload include PDF, Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, and Microsoft PowerPoint. A secure web address URL is generated by SAP Business Network for each uploaded document. Use a text editor like Microsoft Word to create the hyperlink, then copy and paste the hyperlink into the rich-text editor. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Information Portal . 2. On the Create/Edit tab, find the Reference Content Files section. 3. Choose the type of document you're uploading from the Document Type dropdown. If you choose Other for the document type, you must complete the Upload Reference Name field. This field isn't available for the other document types. 4. Click Choose File and browse for the desired file. If you're uploading an Extrinsics Used or Ship To/Bill To Addresses document type, we strongly recommend using the corresponding reference document template [page 34] . 5. Optional: If you want to share any additional comments related to the reference document, enter them in the Comments to Seller field. 6. Click Upload. Results The uploaded reference document shows up in the Reference Files table. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 35 Sharing or Stop Sharing a Reference Document You can share files so that your suppliers can view and download them from your supplier information portal. You can stop sharing a file to hide it from your suppliers. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Information Portal . 2. Find the file you want to share or stop sharing in the Reference Files table, and do one of the following: • If you want to share the file, make sure that the tick sign in the Shared with Suppliers column is green. If the sign is white, click on it so it becomes green. • If you want to stop sharing the file, make sure that the tick sign in the Shared with Suppliers column is white. If the sign is green, click on it so it becomes white. Next Steps To view your shared reference documents: 1. Click Supplier Information Portal. 2. Click the View tab. 3. Click the Reference Documents tab. 4. You can see a list of your shared reference documents as your suppliers see them. 5. Download any of the shared reference documents by clicking one of the names. Filling Out Extended Profile Settings Fill out your extended profile to share more detailed company information with your suppliers. Procedure 1. Choose Administration Configuration . 2. On the Configuration page, click Extended Profile Settings and Information. 3. Fill out the questions with information you want to share with your suppliers.  Note You don't need to answer all questions. Your suppliers can see only the completed questions. 36 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement 4. Click Save and then Close. Next Steps To view and export shared extended profile information: 1. Click the View tab. 2. Click the Extended Profile Information tab. 3. You can view the shared information as your suppliers see it. 4. (Optional) You can export the extended profile information by clicking Export to CSV. Viewing Configured Invoicing Rules You can view your Default Transaction Rules, Country-based Invoicing Rules and Supplier Group configurations in read-only format, as your suppliers see them. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Information Portal . 2. Click the View tab. 3. Click the Transaction Rules tab. Workflow for Notifying Suppliers About Updated Reference Information This workflow starts with the supplier enabling the Customer Requirements Change tab, and ends with the supplier able to view information you share.  Note You have a trading relationship with the supplier. 1. Your supplier signs in to SAP Business Network, clicks the chooses Settings notification tab. Network Notifications Account Settings icon, and then General , and enables the Customer Requirements Change 2. You sign in to SAP Business Network as an administrator, and go to Administration Configuration Extended Profile Settings and Information , and respond to the questions. 3. You go to Supplier Enablement Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement Supplier Information Portal and do the following: PUBLIC 37 • • Configure information to be shared with suppliers. Upload and shares one or more reference documents, containing extrinsics, shipping and billing addresses, an EDI guide, non-ISO units of measure, or other information. 4. Your supplier receives an email notification about your updates and opens your supplier information portal. 5. Your supplier views the extended profile information, reference documents, transaction rules, and other information that you shared. Supplier Enablement Notifications People in your organization and in the supplier organizations you are enabling can choose to receive email notifications, which helps to keep the enablement process on track. Setting Up Supplier Enablement Notifications for Your Organization An SAP Business Network account administrator can specify which email addresses receive reminder notifications. Context As an administrator, you can configure notifications to remind a supplier when one of your organization's tasks is overdue, or when a supplier task is escalated. You can also configure the reply-to email address and choose whether to show your organization's name in the email. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Configure . 2. On the Configure page, click the Notifications tab. 3. Choose the Send notifications when supplier enablement tasks are overdue or escalated check box, and enter up to three email addresses, separated by commas. 4. In the Configure supplier notifications section, for each Notification type: a. Check the Sender name check box to use SAP Business Network as the sender name instead of your company name. b. Enter an email address in the Reply-to email box. 5. Click Save. 38 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement Setting Up Supplier Enablement Notifications (For Suppliers) Suppliers can configure users to receive notifications about supplier enablement activities and task reminders. Context By default, notifications of supplier enablement activities and tasks are sent to the account administrator of the supplier account. But the account administrator can add more users to receive the notifications. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network supplier account as an administrator. 2. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Network Notifications . 3. In the Relationship section of the General tab, choose the Send a notification when a supplier enablement activity is assigned or a task is overdue check box. 4. Enter up to three comma-separated email addresses. 5. Enable SAP Business Network to send a notification when a customer has shared or updated a Reference Document on your Supplier Information Portal by checking the Customer Requirements Change box. 6. Optional: Update the email address for the notification in the To email addresses column. 7. Click Save. Enabling Notifications for New Purchase Orders and Changes in Purchase Orders Suppliers can enable email notifications for new and changed purchase orders. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Network Notifications . 2. Go to the section Electronic Order Routing. 3. Check the Send notifications for new purchase orders to suppliers. checkbox. 4. Click Save. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Initial and Ongoing Setup of Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 39 Vendors You can manage all your vendors and existing trading relationships on the Manage Vendor page. You can upload thousands of vendors [page 41] using a single CSV file and later invite them to register on SAP Business Network. You can also manually create a single vendor [page 44] at a time in your account. The CSV file template upload is incremental, and SAP Business Network creates new vendors if their vendor ID is not yet available on the SAP Business Network buyer account. You can then start supplier enablement for the new vendors, and the Account activity task is automatically assigned to them. All Account activity tasks are immediately completed. If you assigned no other activities to them, the enablement status is set to Tasks Completed.  Tip You can view the enablement status on the Monitor page or on supplier enablement reports [page 88]. For existing vendors, the vendor information is updated with the information present in the newly uploaded CSV file. The CSV vendor upload links your vendor records with suppliers that are already registered on SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba Sourcing, SAP Business Network Discovery, or SAP Ariba Contracts when you provide the supplier's Network ID or D-U-N-S number.  Note Buyer customer developers can also use the Supplier Invite API to create a client application that creates vendor records in SAP Business Network. For more information, see the Supplier Invite API guide. Option to Ignore D-U-N-S Number for Supplier Matching By default, D-U-N-S numbers are checked when you send documents to SAP Business Network. SAP Business Network looks for an existing supplier account with a matching D-U-N-S number. If a matching account is found, one of the following happens: • If your organization has a trading relationship with the supplier on SAP Business Network, the document is sent to the existing account. • If your organization doesn't have a trading relationship with the supplier, the document fails and doesn't reach the supplier. If no matching account is found, SAP Business Network creates a new, private supplier account and sends the document to that account. Your organization can choose to ignore the D-U-N-S credential in cases where the D-U-N-S check fails on SAP Business Network. With this configuration, if a matching account is found based on the D-U-N-S number, one of the following happens: • 40 If your organization has a trading relationship with the supplier on SAP Business Network, the document is sent to the existing account. Creating a Vendor CSV File [page 41] Adding a Single Vendor in the Supplier Enablement Interface [page 49] Viewing and Editing Vendor Details [page 50] Creating and Linking Vendors to a Quick-Enabled Supplier [page 51] Creating and Uploading a Supplier ID File [page 51] Synchronization of Supplier Contact Information [page 53] Creating a Vendor CSV File You can upload new vendor data for multiple unregistered suppliers at a time through a CSV file. You can also update vendor data for existing suppliers. Prerequisites • • • • • You can include up to 100,000 records in the CSV template. The CSV file must conform to basic syntax rules [page 43]. The maximum recommended upload file size is 10 MB. Your browser might time out for larger files. You can use a ZIP utility to compress the CSV file before uploading it. Zipped files must have a ZIP file extension and must contain only one CSV file. ERP administrators should export vendor data from their backend systems in the CSV vendor file format. Context For each CSV file you upload for supplier enablement, you must specify a name. SAP Business Network processes the file and creates new vendors. For vendors already existing on SAP Business Network, the vendor information is updated. The Upload page shows the counts for new and updated vendors. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Vendors PUBLIC 41 Procedure 1. Download the vendor CSV template: a. Do one of the following: • • Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . Choose Supplier Enablement Monitor . b. Choose Upload Upload Vendors . c. Click the Download Template link. d. Click Save. e. Choose a location to save the Upload_Vendor_Template.csv file, and then click Save. 2. Use the template to create a CSV file containing information on vendors to upload on SAP Business Network.  Note The language used for the trading relationship request invitation letter is determined by the Preferred Language field. This field is not case-sensitive. This language setting is only used for notifications until the supplier has registered and taken account ownership. If the Preferred Language field is blank in the CSV vendor file, SAP Business Network uses English as the default language. 3. On the Upload Vendors page, enter a name in the Name field to identify the uploaded CSV file. 4. Click Browse and choose the vendor CSV file.  Note You can upload the vendor CSV files in ZIP format. However, the ZIP file must contain only one vendor CSV file. 5. Click Upload. The CSV file is validated first and then new vendors are created or previously imported vendors are updated. Results If the vendor CSV file contains syntax errors, you'll see an error message in the Upload Details table section. Click the upload name to view details and download the error file. Correct the vendor CSV file and upload it again. 42 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Vendors Vendor CSV File Syntax and Encoding Understand the requirements for uploading multiple vendors through a comma-separated values (CSV) file. Vendor CSV File Basic Syntax Rules The basic syntax rules are as follows: • • • The file must be saved in CSV format (.csv extension). String values in a CSV file can have commas, but quotes must be used around the string. The following fields are required in the CSV file: • • • • • • • • • • Vendor Name Vendor ID (required only if Tax ID is not included in the CSV file) Tax ID (required only if Vendor ID is not included in the CSV file) Vendor City or Vendor Postal Code Vendor Country Code Vendor Province/State/Region (required only if Vendor City or Vendor Postal Code is in a U.S. state) System ID (required only for multi-ERP buying organizations) Buyer ANID (required only for third parties managing supplier enablement on behalf of a buying organization using a Provider account The template also provides details on the available fields [page 44]. The file must specify the file encoding in the first row. You can leave optional fields blank or delete the column. The CSV file can contain multiple vendors linked to the same Ariba Network ID if your organization is enabled to allow multiple unique supplier IDs (formerly called supplier private IDs) per supplier. Contact SAP Ariba Support to enable this option in your SAP Business Network account. Vendor CSV File Encoding The CSV file must explicitly specify the encoding character set as defined in the following table. Enter the code in the first field of the first row. Be sure to leave the remaining columns in the first row blank.  Note If your CSV upload template file contains only ASCII (7bit) text, you can leave the encoding field empty. The file is processed based on the assumption that it is encoded for 8859_1. (Replaced by the vendor compound key: Vendor ID, Site ID, Site Auxiliary ID.) Account Type Optional String 256 Account type for vendor invite (FULL/LIGHT). FULL invites the supplier to register an enterprise account, while LIGHT invites the supplier to register a standard account. Adding a Single Vendor in the Supplier Enablement Interface You can provide required vendor details and optional details. Context Vendor information includes routing information for the invitation letterand order routing information. When you start supplier enablement for the newly added vendor, the vendor receives a trading relationship request letter. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 2. Click Add. 3. On the Add a Vendor page, enter the vendor details. 4. Click Add. Related Information Supplier Invitation Letters [page 22] Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Vendors PUBLIC 49 Viewing and Editing Vendor Details Buying organizations can view and edit the vendor details available in the Manage Vendors and Monitor pages. Prerequisites You must have the Supplier Enablement Program Administrator or Supplier Enablement Task Management permission to view and edit vendor details. Context You can edit the following vendor details at any time: • • • • Vendor name Vendor email address, fax number, phone number, and vendor address Contact first and last name Contact phone number You can edit the following vendor details until the supplier has registered and taken account ownership: • • Invitation letter routing email or fax Order routing email or fax If the vendor is linked to an existing supplier account on SAP Business Network, the Network ID column shows the Network ID of the vendor. The Network ID also shows up after supplier enablement has started for the vendor. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • • Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . Choose Supplier Enablement Monitor . 2. Optional: Filter the page [page 75] by specifying one or more filters. 3. Choose a vendor. 4. In the Actions column, choose Actions View/Edit Details .  Note You can delete a vendor if you don't want to track and manage the vendor for supplier enablement any longer by choosing Actions Delete Vendor . The vendor must not have started enablement, or must have a supplier enablement status of Closed. To delete other vendors, first change the enablement status to Closed. 50 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Vendors
