file://SBN/split/Enabling Suppliers on S.content: 5. View or edit fields on the Supplier Details and Vendor Details tabs. 6. Click Save. Creating and Linking Vendors to a Quick-Enabled Supplier You can link quick-enabled suppliers to the corresponding vendor records. When you invite suppliers through a quick enablement method, a private supplier account and a corresponding vendor are created on SAP Business Network. The Account activity is automatically associated to the quickenabled suppliers, and the enablement status is set to Active. For quick enablement through purchase orders, the Purchase Order activity is also added automatically. If your organization uses quick enablement with SAP Ariba Buying solutions, you can use the supplier Network ID to establish a link with the vendor ID in your ERP or other back-end systems. This additional step is required when the quick-enablement document uses a supplier private ID to identify the supplier and doesn't include vendor compound key information. When vendors are uploaded using the vendor CSV file [page 41], you can add the supplier Network ID to the respective vendor that links the vendor ID with the SAP Business Network supplier. If you assign supplier groups in the vendor CSV file, any vendors whose corresponding supplier accounts were already members of a supplier group other than that specified in the vendor CSV file are now members of the supplier group specified in the vendor CSV file instead.  Note This process creates two vendors linked to the same SAP Business Network supplier. To allow this, your organization must be enabled to allow multiple unique supplier IDs (formerly called supplier private IDs) per supplier. Contact SAP Ariba Support to enable this option in your SAP Business Network account. Creating and Uploading a Supplier ID File You can specify multiple supplier IDs and system IDs for suppliers that have an active trading relationship with you. Prerequisites Your application must be enabled to allow multiple unique supplier IDs (private IDs) per buyer–supplier relationship. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Vendors PUBLIC 51 Context Using a single file, you can quickly add up to 1000 supplier IDs in a single file.  Note This feature is available only in your test account. To upload multiple unique supplier IDs in your production account, see Creating a Vendor CSV File [page 41]. A supplier file containing supplier IDs and system IDs has the following requirements: • • The file must be saved in CSV format. The file must have the four columns indicated in the steps that follow. If the values or number of columns are incorrect, the file validation fails. The supplier file can have two kinds of errors: • Syntax errors: If the file contains syntax errors, an error message is displayed on the Upload Supplier Private IDs page. Click Download Error Log to download the error log file. Events with syntax errors are not queued and they are not available in the Update Event table. • Database or event errors: In case there are database or event errors when uploading the supplier file, the file is queued and this event appears in the Update Event table. Click the event name to download the error log and supplier file to view and make changes. You receive notifications on the status of the uploaded file. Procedure 1. Create a new blank CSV file, and enter the following headings in the first four columns:  Note The supplier file doesn't support the vendor compound key. 52 Column Header Description Required/Optional ANID Supplier ANID Required 13 digits number prefixed with AN. For example, ANxxxxxxxxxx. SystemID An identifier assigned to each of your procurement applications. Optional Alphanumeric values PrivateID An identifier used to define the suppliers in your Required procurement application. It must be unique per buyer–supplier relationship per system ID. Alphanumeric values PUBLIC Content Type Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Vendors Column Header Description IsDefault Controls routing of non-PO invoices for each procurement application. You can only dedicate one supplier private ID as a default for each application system ID. Required/Optional Content Type Required Y to indicate Yes N or Blank to indicate No 2. Sign in to your SAP Business Network test account. 3. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 4. Click Upload Private IDs. 5. Enter a name to identify the uploaded event in the text box. 6. Browse for your CSV file, and then click Upload. Results If there are no syntax errors when you upload the supplier file, SAP Business Network puts your file into the queue to validate and process it. SAP Business Network validates the syntax and values specified in the supplier file. When validation is complete, SAP Business Network changes its status to Completed. If there are errors, you'll see an error message and you can view the list of events and the status of the supplier file in the Upload Events table. Synchronization of Supplier Contact Information The contact information in the trading relationship request is synchronized with the quick enablement letters and the information on the Vendor Details page (under Invitation Letter Routing Information). Here is the flow SAP Business Network follows for updating contact information in the letters and user interface: • First, when the supplier is quick enabled, the supplier routing information used in the document that triggered quick enablement (for example, the purchase order or ICS invoice) is added to the vendor details available from the Manage Vendors page. (This occurs only if the Vendor Details page does not already contain that information.) The invitation letter routing information on the Vendor Details page supports both email and fax. • Whenever a manual or automatic reminder is sent to the supplier, SAP Business Network uses the letter routing information on the Vendor Details page. The letter is sent by email, if an email address is available, or by fax, if the only routing information available is a fax number. • After enablement has started for a private supplier, when you select Edit on the Active Relationships page for that supplier, SAP Business Network takes you to the Vendor Details page to edit the information. (A confirmation message explains that this is happening.) This is to keep routing information on the Vendor Details page in sync with the information on the Active Relationships page once enablement has started. On the Vendor Details page, the vendor contact information in the Vendor Account Details and Invitation Letter Routing Information sections are populated from the quick enablement invitation letter only if the fields are empty. This means: • Vendor details loaded via CSV vendor upload or entered manually are not overwritten with information from quick enablement documents. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Vendors PUBLIC 53 • Existing contact information on the Vendor Details page is not automatically updated from subsequent quick enablement documents. This is to ensure that the CSV vendor upload data stays the source of truth. For example, suppose a supplier is quick enabled through a purchase order. The supplier email address from that purchase order is added to the Vendor Details page. Ten days later, another purchase order is sent to the supplier, this time with different email information. The Vendor Details page is not updated with the new information. You must update the routing information manually. Following are some details to keep in mind regarding supplier contact information: • The contact information used by the new invitation (the trading relationship request for quick enabled suppliers) is based on the information in the Invitation Letter Routing Information section of the Vendor Details page. This contact might be different from the contact used by the quick enablement invitation letters for each quick enablement method. • If you edit the routing email for a private supplier on the Active Relationships page before the supplier enablement process has started, the updated email address is not carried over to the Invitation Letter Routing Information section on the Vendor Details page. 54 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Vendors Manage Supplier Enablement After you upload multiple vendors or add individual vendors, you can start and track enablement for them.  Remember Complete the one-time setup activities [page 6] before starting enablement for vendors. The Manage Vendors page lists all vendors available for supplier enablement. You can assign activities [page 55] and start enablement [page 57] for selected vendors and monitor the enablement [page 71]. You can also view and edit the vendor details [page 50] and resend the trading relationship request letter [page 66]. Assigning or Unassigning Activities [page 55] Starting Supplier Enablement for a Vendor [page 57] Putting a Supplier on Hold [page 58] Stopping Enablement for a Supplier [page 59] Trading Relationships [page 59] Extend a Relationship with an Existing Supplier [page 69] Supplier Enablement Monitoring [page 71] Assigning or Unassigning Activities You can assign supplier enablement activities to vendors based on the types of transactions they wish to enable. Context You assign activities based on the desired transactions. You can then monitor and track these activities. If you don't want to track previously assigned activities for vendors, you can unassign the activities. You can assign the following supplier enablement activities to vendors: • • • • • • Account (automatically assigned by the system) Purchase Order Invoice Catalog Payment Discount Management Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 55 • • • AribaPay (available only in accounts where the payment capability is enabled) Supply Chain Financing Dynamic Discounting Credit Memos These activities are preconfigured and include a set of associated tasks. When an activity is assigned, the corresponding grouped tasks are automatically associated. Activities and tasks are started once the Account activity has been completed. Buying organizations can mass-assign one or more activities for vendors based on filter options available on the Manage Vendors and Monitor pages. For example, buying organizations can choose vendors based on an enablement mode, spend value, or spend range and assign activities. This helps in managing and monitoring supplier enablement for vendors easily. An activity can also have the following exception statuses: • • Overdue Escalated/Failed Buying organizations are notified about exceptions through email and these activity statuses can be viewed on the Monitor page. Suppliers invited through quick-enablement methods (inviting suppliers through purchase orders, payment proposals, CC invoices sent from SAP Ariba Buying solutions or the ERP system, request for quotation, or ICS invoices) are automatically added to the Account activity and are monitored on the Supplier Enablement tab. For quick enablement purchase orders, the Purchase Order activity is added automatically.  Note • If activities are assigned to vendors who have already completed all earlier tasks, the supplier enablement status for the vendor changes from No pending tasks to Active. • Deactivated activities are not available while assigning activities and tasks for vendors. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • • Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . Choose Supplier Enablement Monitor . 2. Select a vendor. 3. Click Assign or Unassign. 4. Choose the activities to assign or unassign for the selected vendors. 5. Click Assign or Unassign. 56 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement Starting Supplier Enablement for a Vendor If the supplier enablement has not been started for a vendor, the buying organization can start it manually on the Manage Vendors or Monitor pages of the Supplier Enablement tab. Prerequisites Before buying organizations start supplier enablement, they should use the e-Contact column in the Manage Vendor and Monitor pages to verify that the vendor has configured an email address or fax number to send the trading relationship request letter. A trading relationship request letter is sent out when supplier enablement is started for a vendor. Context The supplier enablement status shows Not Started or blank if supplier enablement isn't yet started for a vendor. When supplier enablement is started, the status changes to Active. Buying organizations can refine the vendors list by using filters available on the Manage Vendors or Monitor pages. They can then start enablement for multiple vendors at once. For example, you can use the supplier enablement status None to filter vendors that haven't started supplier enablement and don't have any activity assigned. After the supplier enablement is started for vendor, the Account activity is automatically assigned. Other assigned activities are started after the Account activity has been completed. Suppliers invited through quick enablement methods are automatically added to the Account activity and the enablement is started.  Tip You can get accustomed with the SAP Business Network supplier enablement process by working on a pilot project with a small number of vendors. By using a pilot project, a buying organization can complete a full supplier enablement life cycle, to ensure that all their configuration settings are accurate and that the integration to their back-end system is complete. Later, they can start the supplier enablement process for all remaining vendors with whom they want to start a trading relationship on SAP Business Network.  Remember You can't test supplier enablement configurations using your test account. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 57 • • Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . Choose Supplier Enablement Monitor . 2. (Optional) Filter the page [page 75] by specifying one or more filters. 3. Choose one or more vendors whose status is not Active. 4. Click Start. Putting a Supplier on Hold You can temporarily pause the supplier enablement process. Context When a vendor requires follow-up action before supplier enablement can continue further, the buying organization can put the vendor on hold. The buying organization can later change the enablement status back to Active. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Tasks . 2. In the View dropdown, choose a view (for example, Escalated Supplier Tasks. 3. (Optional) Filter the page [page 82] by specifying one or more filters. 4. Find the supplier to put on hold, and choose Actions View Task Details . 5. In the Supplier Enablement Status field on the task details page, choose Escalated. 6. In the Status Reason field, choose a value. If you choose Other - Details in Vendor Comments, add a comment describing the reason in the Vendor Comments field. 7. In the Action Required By field, choose the person designated for follow-up action. 8. Click OK. 58 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement Stopping Enablement for a Supplier You can cancel the supplier enablement process. Context Buying organizations can discontinue supplier enablement for a vendor after the supplier enablement was started by changing the supplier enablement status from Active to Closed. The vendor is no longer tracked for supplier enablement. A buying organization can restart supplier enablement for a vendor in Closed status by changing the supplier enablement status back to Active in the Vendor Details page. Alternatively, they can delete the vendor (which deletes existing activity assignments), reload the vendor, and then restart supplier enablement again. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . 2. (Optional) Filter the page [page 75] by specifying one or more filters. 3. Find the supplier, and click the vendor name. The Vendor Details tab of the Supplier and Vendor Details page appears. 4. For the Enablement Status field, choose Close. 5. In the Status Reason field, choose a value. If you choose Other - Details in Vendor Comments, add a comment describing the reason in the Vendor Comments field. 6. Click Save. Trading Relationships You can use multiple methods to initiate a trading relationship with suppliers. The following tasks are ways you can start a trading relationship: • • • Search for and add registered suppliers [page 60]. Invite unregistered suppliers through email [page 62]. Quick enable [page 63] suppliers through purchase order, payment proposal, CC invoice (invoices sent from SAP Ariba Buying solutions or the ERP system), ICS invoice, or request for quotation. Post a supplier self-nomination project [page 68] so that suppliers can proactively initiate a relationship request with you. Searching for and Requesting a Relationship with Registered Suppliers [page 60] Inviting Suppliers Through Email [page 62] Inviting Suppliers Through Quick Enablement [page 63] Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 59 Sending a Quick Enablement Trading Relationship Request [page 65] Resending Trading Relationship Request Letters [page 66] Generating an Invoice Quick Enablement Customer Code [page 67] Deleting Invited Unregistered Suppliers [page 68] Creating a Supplier Self-Nomination Project [page 68] Searching for and Requesting a Relationship with Registered Suppliers You can search for and request a relationship with suppliers that are already registered on SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba Sourcing, SAP Business Network Discovery, or SAP Ariba Contracts. You can also review your current supplier relationships through the search. Context  Note To invite new suppliers that are not yet registered on SAP Business Network use one of the quick enablement methods [page 22]. To add more than 500 suppliers at a time, upload a vendor CSV file [page 41]. To search only suppliers with which you have established relationships, click Search only my trading partners. SAP Business Network refreshes the page to display additional options. You can search for suppliers using a wide range of business criteria: Use This Area… To Do This… Search only my trading partners Search only suppliers with which you have established relationships. If you do not select this check box, SAP Business Network searches all suppliers with visible profiles, including those with which you have relationships. When you select this option, SAP Business Network displays additional check boxes that let you limit the search to: • • • 60 PUBLIC Only suppliers for which you have set up custom order routing rules Only suppliers for which you have set up custom invoicing rules Only suppliers for which you have configured custom contracts site setup Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement

file://SBN/split/Enabling Suppliers on S.content: Use This Area… To Do This… Basic Profile Search by company name, NetworkId, state, or country/region. Note these guidelines for Basic Profile fields: Classifications • Company name and Company name starts with: You can enter a partial name—SAP Business Network finds similar names. • NetworkId (also known as Ariba Network ID or ANID): Enter a value starting with “AN” followed by 11 digits; for example, AN02000012345. SAP Business Network performs exact matching for this field. • D-U-N-S Number: You can enter a partial number—SAP Business Network finds similar numbers. Search by commodity, territory served, and industry served. Note these guidelines for Classifications fields: Additional Company Profile • Commodity supplied: Select UNSPSC (United Nations Standard Products and Services Code) categories to narrow your search. The more specific the commodity classification you select, the fewer potential suppliers SAP Business Network returns. • Territory served: Select a country/region to narrow your search. For some locations, SAP Business Network displays a Region list that allows you to select a more specific area, such as a state. • Industry served: Select an industry to narrow your search. Search by year founded, annual revenue, number of employees, and minority information. If you use the Annual Revenue parameter, SAP Business Network does not return suppliers that specified “contact company for information” for that field. Some private and nonprofit suppliers do not specify their annual revenue for business reasons. After you locate suppliers of interest, you can download their basic or extended profile. Basic profiles include limited data, such as company contact information and the supplier’s supported routing methods. Extended profiles include all available information about suppliers. For enhanced security, you cannot view the tax IDs of a supplier that you do not have a trading relationship with when you search for them. In the Supplier Details Company Profile page, SAP Business Network masks the Tax ID, State Tax ID, Regional Tax ID, and VAT ID fields when you do not have a trading relationship with the supplier. The Tax ID is only visible after you establish a trading relationship with the supplier on SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Click Search for Suppliers. 3. Enter values in any of the fields.  Tip You can search by the supplier name, D-U-N-S number, country/region, industry, or commodity. The more search criteria you enter, the narrower the search results. 4. Click Search. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 61 SAP Business Network shows matching suppliers. SAP Business Network doesn't show suppliers that are already in your list of current or pending suppliers. You can view any supplier's profile or public customer catalogs. 5. Click a supplier to see the supplier's account information. 6. Check the information for accuracy. SAP Ariba doesn't check the validity of the information provided by suppliers. Do one of the following: • • If the information is accurate, continue to the next step. If the information contains errors, do not continue. Contact the supplier's representative directly by telephone or email and ask that person to fix the problem on SAP Business Network. Wait for another email from SAP Business Network indicating that the supplier reregistered, and start at step 1 again. 7. Click Request Relationship. 8. Read the responsibility statement and, if you agree, choose the check box. 9. Click Request a relationship to finish the review and send the supplier a relationship request. 10. Click Done. SAP Business Network shows the supplier either as a Current Supplier or Pending Relationship, depending on whether their account is configured to accept all requests automatically or to review each individually. Results SAP Business Network sends you and the supplier an email notification with further information and instructions on finalizing the relationship request. Inviting Suppliers Through Email The following overview describes the steps you use to invite an unregistered supplier to register on SAP Business Network and establish a trading relationship. Suppliers who register by email invitation are registering an enterprise account. 1. Enter the supplier's email address and company name. SAP Business Network sends the invitation as an email message and shows this supplier as an Invited unregistered supplier on the Active Relationships page. 2. The supplier receives an email invitation from SAP Business Network and clicks the link provided in the email to start the registration process. Once registered, the supplier gains immediate access to the account. The supplier can't transact until you establish a trading relationship with them. 3. You receive an email notification from SAP Business Network indicating that your invited supplier has registered and requesting that you review the supplier's account information. When you go to your Active Relationships page, the supplier now appears as an Invited Registered Supplier. 4. You review the supplier's registration information and request a relationship. 5. The supplier accepts your request in one of the following ways: 62 • If the supplier account is configured to automatically accept all relationship requests (the default), your request is accepted immediately. • If the supplier account is set up so that a user must review and approve or reject relationship requests manually, the supplier shows as a Pending Relationship on your Active Relationships page until they have PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement approved the request. This enables them to configure their order routing systems to handle orders from a specific buyer or reconfigure their order routing systems to fix a receiving problem. 6. The supplier receives an email notification from SAP Business Network confirming that they are ready to transact with your organization. After the supplier accepts your request, their organization shows as a Current Supplier on your Active Relationships page. Now, you can send orders to the supplier through SAP Business Network. Resending an Email Invitation to a Private Supplier In some cases, the email invitation fails to reach the private supplier or you may want to resend the temporary user ID and secure code to a private supplier using a different email address. In such cases, you can resend the sign-in information to private suppliers. Private suppliers can use the information in the email invitation to sign in to SAP Business Network and take ownership of their account. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . SAP Business Network lists your current suppliers. 2. Click Supplier Selector and select Private Suppliers. 3. Do one of the following: • To edit the email address before sending the email notification, click More Actions and then click Edit. Enter the new email address.  Note If enablement has started for the private supplier, SAP Business Network takes you to the Vendor Details page to edit the email address. (A confirmation message explains that this is happening.) This is to keep routing information on the Vendor Details page in sync with the information on the Active Relationships page once enablement has started. • To send the email notification, click More Actions and then click Send Invitation.  Note You can also resend the sign-in information to failed private suppliers. Inviting Suppliers Through Quick Enablement Quick enablement allows you to create new SAP Business Network accounts on behalf of suppliers. Before you can use the quick enablement methods to invite suppliers, you need to turn on quick enablement [page 22] in your account. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 63 Quick Enablement Through Purchase Orders, Payment Proposals, CC Invoices, and Requests for Quotation The following overview describes the steps you use to invite suppliers through purchase orders, payment proposals, CC invoice (invoices sent from the SAP Ariba procurement solution or the ERP system), and request for quotation: 1. You enable your account for quick enablement. 2. You send a purchase order, payment proposal, CC invoice (invoices sent from the SAP Ariba procurement solution or the ERP system), or request for quotation to suppliers with whom you do not have an existing relationship. SAP Business Network creates a private account for this supplier. 3. The supplier receives an email invitation from SAP Business Network and clicks the link provided in the email to start the registration process. 4. If the supplier is not yet registered, they can accept the invitation by completing the registration process. 5. If the supplier is already registered, they can accept the invitation and combine their new relationship request with their existing account. 6. Once registered, the supplier gains immediate access to the account.  Note Quick enablement through payment proposals, CC invoices (invoices sent from the SAP Ariba procurement solution or the ERP system), and request for quotation is available to buyers using SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, SAP Ariba Invoice Management, Ariba Purchase Order Automation, or Ariba Invoice Automation. For more information on purchase orders, payment proposals, CC Invoice (invoices sent from the SAP Ariba procurement solution or the ERP system), and request for quotation, see the SAP Business Network cXML solutions guide. Quick Enablement Through Invoices The following overview describes the steps you use to invite suppliers through invoices. You can use this method to allow unregistered suppliers to enter non-PO invoices, which, if you accept them, establish the trading relationship with them. You can also use this method to invite registered suppliers who don't have a trading relationship with you. 1. You enable your account for this enablement method and generate a unique customer code [page 67]. After you generate the customer code, you can send this information to your supplier. 2. After the supplier receives your customer code, the supplier can send you a non-PO invoice through the SAP Business Network. The supplier enters this code when creating the invoice. 3. After you receive the invoice, you can choose to accept or reject it. If you accept it, you establish a relationship with the supplier on SAP Business Network. 64 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement Quick Enablement Through Invoice Conversion Service Invoice conversion services (ICS) facilitate conversion of paper invoices to an electronic format using a process that includes validation. A service provider receives invoices on behalf of the buying organization and converts them to an electronic format for posting to SAP Business Network. If you subscribe to an ICS solution, you can have SAP Business Network send an invitation to suppliers once they reach specified invoice volume thresholds. SAP Business Network sends an email invitation, and suppliers can use the link in the invitation to register on SAP Business Network and view the status of invoices. You can also send an invitation manually before the volume threshold is met. For more information about invoice conversion, see the SAP Ariba guide to invoice conversion. Sending a Quick Enablement Trading Relationship Request You can send a new trading relationship request to a quick-enabled supplier. Context When you manually invite a quick-enabled supplier or when SAP Business Network automatically starts the enablement process, SAP Business Network sends the invitation called Trading Relationship Request for Quick Enabled Suppliers. The letter is generic to all types of quick enablement; it doesn't mention which type of quick enablement occurred. Also, the letter lets the supplier know that the private supplier account already contains at least one document. You can add custom content to the letter if desired. When the supplier enablement process starts automatically for a supplier that was quick enabled through any method except purchase orders, the supplier receives two letters: • • The invitation letter specific to the quick enablement method used The trading relationship request for quick enabled suppliers, which informs the supplier that at least one document from BuyerName exists in a new account. Sending both letters is beneficial in that it reminds the supplier in multiple ways to take account ownership. Suppliers that were quick enabled through purchase orders receive only one letter, the invitation letter that is specific to purchase order quick enablement. You can also resend a trading relationship request letter [page 66] on the Vendor Details page. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Choose a quick enabled supplier. 3. Click More Actions Send Invitation . Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 65  Note Because the invitation used for manual resending is also used for reminders, the secure code is not regenerated every time the buying organization manually resends the invitation. This way, suppliers don't have to keep track of which invitation is the most recent. Resending Trading Relationship Request Letters When you start supplier enablement for vendors and the trading relationship request letter is sent to the vendor, it may fail to reach them. In such cases, you can resend the trading relationship letter to the vendor. Context You can resend a trading relationship request letter only if the vendor has: • • Not yet registered and taken ownership of the account on SAP Business Network and The supplier enablement status is Active or On Hold Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • • Choose Supplier Enablement Manage Vendors . Choose Supplier Enablement Monitor . 2. (Optional) Filter the page [page 75] by specifying one or more filters. 3. Choose a vendor. 4. In the Actions column, click Actions View/Edit Details . 5. Edit the Invitation Letter Routing Information and Order Routing Information sections. 6. Click Send Now.  Note You can also resend the trading relationship request from the Manage Vendors or Monitor pages. On either of those pages, choose a vendor, and then click 66 PUBLIC Actions Resend Trading Relationship Request . Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement Generating an Invoice Quick Enablement Customer Code You can generate a new code for suppliers to send a non-PO invoice. Procedure 1. Choose Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules . 2. In the General Invoice Rules section, check Allow suppliers to send invoices to this account. 3. In the Quick Enablement Rules section, check Allow Quick Enablement. 4. To generate a new customer code, click Regenerate.  Note The Regenerate button is available only if the Allow Quick Enablement check box and the invoicing rule “Allow suppliers to send invoices to this account” are selected. 5. Click OK. Receiving Non-PO Invoices from Unregistered Suppliers You can use the invoice quick enablement process to receive non-PO invoices from an unregistered supplier. Procedure 1. Turn on quick enablement for your account. 2. Generate your unique customer code [page 67] for invoice quick enablement. 3. Provide your customer code to the supplier. a. If they don't already have an account, the supplier registers on SAP Business Network. b. The supplier creates a non-PO invoice and enters your customer code. c. SAP Business Network determines where to route the invoice based on the customer code. The invoice arrives on your Invoices page as an unassigned invoice. 4. Click Invoices Unassigned Invoices . 5. Click an invoice number. SAP Business Network shows the invoice details and allows you to approve the supplier or reject the invoice. 6. Enter the private ID of the supplier. 7. Click Approve Supplier. 8. SAP Business Network asks you to confirm that you want to approve the supplier. 9. Click OK. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 67 Results • SAP Business Network sends you an email notification saying that the supplier can transact business with you. You now have a trading relationship with the supplier. Deleting Invited Unregistered Suppliers If you invite an unregistered supplier and then decide to rescind the invitation, you can delete the supplier from your list of invited suppliers before activating their account. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . 2. Click Supplier Selector, and then choose Invited Unregistered Suppliers. 3. Select the supplier, and choose More Actions Delete . Results SAP Business Network removes the supplier from your list of invited unregistered suppliers. Creating a Supplier Self-Nomination Project You can create a supplier self-nomination project so that suppliers can request a trading relationship with your company. Context A supplier self-nomination project allows you to create a project with specific criteria so that registered suppliers can respond with a relationship request. You can configure your account and create a project so that suppliers can request a trading relationship with your company. These projects allow registered suppliers already doing business with you outside SAP Business Network, and any other registered suppliers, to request a trading relationship with you. In your project, you specify the criteria required from suppliers to establish a trading relationship with you. After you publish the project, it is available to all suppliers on SAP Business Network. Suppliers can view the project and send a relationship request to you. After you view the supplier’s response, you can accept or decline their trading relationship request. 68 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement You can remove a project at any time by clicking the Remove Project radio button, and the project will no longer be available to suppliers. All pending relationship request are automatically declined. Procedure 1. Choose Administration Configuration Supplier Self-Nomination . 2. Enter a project name in the Project Name text box. 3. Enter a brief description in the Description text box, specifying any criteria you require from prospective suppliers. 4. Click the Post Project radio button. 5. Click the Require suppliers to confirm that they already do business with your company and require them to provide the name or email address of their primary contact in your company check box if you want only suppliers that do business with you to respond to this request. 6. Click the notification check box and enter up to three email addresses. 7. Click Save. Extend a Relationship with an Existing Supplier Buying organizations can add a further collaboration to their existing relationship with a supplier. Prerequisites • • • • • • You’re an active buyer on SAP Business Network. You use SAP Business Network Commerce Automation. You have a relationship with a supplier. You're assigned a role with the required permissions. See SAP Business Network Permissions. You've set the collaborationRole and collaborationType Supplier Invite API. Depending on the collaboration you want to add, there can be further collaboration-specific prerequisites. Context You can add an SAP S/4HANA for product sourcing collaboration. This function is available via API. To add a collaboration, buyers use a specified API that makes it possible for them to invite their suppliers on SAP Business Network to participate in SAP S/4HANA for product sourcing collaboration. Once the supplier accepts the request, they have extended their relationship with an additional collaboration. This table shows the options that the function offers for managing collaborations. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement PUBLIC 69 Table 1: Options for Managing Collaborations Options Description Add a collaboration You can add a collaboration to your relationship. Delete a collaboration You can delete a collaboration. For more information, see Deleting a Relationship Extension [page 70]. Results You receive a system notification about the acceptance or rejection of the collaboration request. To view established relationships, click Supplier Enablement Active Relationships . In the Supplier Selector dropdown menu, choose Current suppliers. The table displays your collaborations sorted by types in separate rows, which allows you to manage them independently. You can filter by pending, declined, and suspended suppliers. You can also generate a collaboration type status report. SAP Business Network sends an e-mail notification about the deletion to the participants. Supplier Enablement Monitoring You can see the details of a supplier's enablement progress. Supplier Enablement Statuses [page 72] Vendor Filtering Options [page 75] Enablement Milestones [page 77] Supplier Enablement Widgets [page 78] Supplier Enablement Statuses You can track the overall supplier enablement status per vendor. Along with the supplier enablement status, a Reason for Status Update and an Action Required By option are used for certain statuses. The status details are also provided in both the supplier enablement status reports. Status changes are system-driven, or a buying organization can decide to change the enablement status for vendors. The following supplier enablement statuses are available: Supplier Enablement Status Description None The buying organization hasn't assigned any activity or started supplier enablement for the vendor. Not Started The buying organization has assigned activities but hasn't yet started supplier enablement. Active The buying organization has started supplier enablement for the vendor and pending tasks exist Escalated The enablement is put on hold by the buying organization for follow-up action. 72 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Manage Supplier Enablement Supplier Enablement Status Description Escalated (Supplier) The vendor is put on hold due to any of the following reasons: • The supplier raised a question when responding to the trading relationship request. In this case the task for terms of use acceptance is also escalated. • • The supplier account is locked as the company verification failed during login. • The supplier has rejected the trading relationship request with the buying organization. The supplier account is suspended because they didn't pay their subscription fees.  Note In this case, the buying organization can't resend a trading relationship request to this supplier again. • The supplier declined the trading relationship request letter sent through a quick enablement method. Pending Approval The trading relationship with the buying organization is pending and awaiting approval In Progress - At Risk Project time lines are on track but the supplier has not responded to the calls or shared the needed details. The supplier could also also be at risk due to external dependencies. Ready to Transact The buying organization is ready to transact business with the supplier. Buyer PO Pending The buying organization has a Purchase Order Sent task pending. Supplier Transaction Pending The supplier has an Invoice Sent task pending. Buying organizations can choose from the preconfigured reasons available. file://SBN/split/Enabling Suppliers on S.content: Supplier Enablement Tasks Tasks for supplier enablement are tracked and closed by two methods. There are two types of supplier enablement tasks: • Automatic: These tasks have built-in logic to track when the task can be marked completed by SAP Business Network. • Manual: These tasks are manually closed by the user when the task is complete. Each task has a description. Tasks are closely linked to each other. If a task is dependent on another, the corresponding task must be completed before the following task is due for completion. SAP Business Network automatically calculates the due date and the escalation date for the task based on the preconfigured task values [page 31]. These values are displayed in the task details page. When a task has crossed the due date (number of days to complete the task), reminders are sent to the task owner. When a supplier-owned task is still pending, even after all the reminders are sent out, the task is escalated to the buying organization and the buying organization receives a consolidated email of all the escalated supplier tasks. The Escalate on Day field specifies the number of days after which an incomplete task is escalated. The escalation date is calculated based on the task due date plus the number of days specified for the Escalate on Day field. You can also view the escalated tasks for your suppliers. When a supplier fails to complete an overdue task even after receiving all the reminder notifications, SAP Business Network escalates the task and sends an email notification to you. Using the Escalated Supplier Tasks view, you can view the escalated tasks for suppliers with an Active supplier enablement status. SAP Business Network doesn't close the Invoice Sent task for invoice conversion services (ICS) and carbon copy (CC) invoices. The Invoice Sent task is automatically completed only for true electronic invoices that are transacted through SAP Business Network: • • • • • • • PO and non-PO invoices Invoices against contracts Invoices against timesheets Invoices against release and nonrelease blanket purchase orders (BPO) Invoices through CSV file upload Credit memos (PO and non-PO) Information-only invoices Task Lists, Statuses, and Filters [page 82] Viewing, Deferring, or Reopening a Task [page 84] How Suppliers Can Access Supplier Enablement Tasks [page 85] Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Tasks PUBLIC 81 Task Lists, Statuses, and Filters The Tasks tab allows you to view your tasks and your suppliers' tasks. The Tasks tab lets you: easily view pending and escalated tasks and take the necessary action. You can use the task list filters and views to filter tasks for a specific group of tasks. The Tasks page provides the following views: View Name Description Pending Buying Organization Tasks and All pending, escalated, or failed tasks for your organization. This view also shows the Escalated Supplier Tasks escalated supplier tasks. (default view) All tasks for suppliers with an Active or On Hold enablement status are shown in this view. Pending Buying Organization Tasks Overdue, escalated, and failed tasks for your organization. Tasks are shown only for suppliers with an Active supplier enablement status. Escalated Supplier Tasks Escalated tasks for suppliers, including failed tasks. Tasks are shown only for suppliers with an Active supplier enablement status. All Buying Organization Tasks All tasks for your organization, including tasks that are completed. All Tasks All tasks for both your organization and your suppliers. Task Status A task can move to one of the following statuses during the supplier enablement process: Task Status Description Not Started Task hasn't yet started. Pending Task is pending action. Overdue Task has passed the due date. Escalated Supplier task has passed the due date and is still pending, even after all the reminders have been sent. Completed Task is completed. Failed Task failed. The following tables explain the failure reasons for the tasks related to trading relationships: Table 6: Task Failure Reasons for the Relationship Request Task Status Reason Description Email failed during invite A trading relationship request letter is sent by email to suppliers. Because of errors, the email failed. Fax failed during invite A trading relationship request letter is sent by fax to suppliers. Because errors, the fax failed. 82 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Tasks Table 7: Task Failure Reasons for the Accept Trading Relationship Task Status Reason Description Trading relationship declined for this sup- The supplier declined the trading relationship with the buying organization. plier account Trading relationship request declined The supplier declined the trading relationship request letter that was sent through a quick-enablement method. Task Filters Task filters allow buying organizations to view tasks that are related to a specific group, such as tasks based on an activity, task name, or supplier name. To view, click Add Filters. The Tasks page has the following filters: Filter Name Use This to Filter By... Dropdown filters: Assigned Activities Activity assigned to the vendor. Supplier ANID Network ID of the supplier on SAP Business Network. Enablement Status The supplier enablement status of the vendor. Date Range Due Date range during which the task is due to be completed. Supplier Country Country/region of the supplier. Relationship Method The relationship method by which the vendor was registered on SAP Business Network. Supplier Name The name of the supplier. Date Range Escalated Date range during which the task was escalated. System ID Vendor master ID for the supplier in the procurement system. Text filters (supports partial string search): Vendor/Supplier Name The name of the vendor or supplier. Site Aux ID An additional ID of the vendor key, often used for address ID or contact ID. (Part of the vendor compound key used with SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, and with Ariba Invoice Automation and Ariba Purchase Order Automation using Oracle Fusion Middleware adapters.) Vendor ID The vendor ID from the ERP system. Legacy Vendor ID Formerly used vendor ID /supplier private ID used with SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, and with Ariba Invoice Automation and Ariba Purchase Order Automation using Oracle Fusion Middleware adapters. This filter is now used for backward compatibility. (Replaced by the vendor compound key: Vendor ID, Site ID, Site Aux ID.) Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Tasks PUBLIC 83 Filter Name Use This to Filter By... Site ID The ID of the vendor location. (Part of the vendor compound key used with SAP Ariba Procurement solutions, and with Ariba Invoice Automation and Ariba Purchase Order Automation using Oracle Fusion Middleware adapters.) Task Comments You can add comments to tasks. For example, if you change the status of a task for a supplier, you can add a comment to explain why. When you reopen a task that was already completed, you must enter a comment to explain why the task was reopened. Task comments are useful to capture exceptions for a task during the supplier enablement process and to make them available to other users and on supplier enablement reports. Viewing, Deferring, or Reopening a Task You can view a task to see its details. When you want to hold back a task until a later time, you can defer the task. If a manually tracked task is closed, you can reopen it if the subsequent task is in Pending status. Prerequisites • • View the preconfigured values [page 31] for each supplier enablement task. You must have the Supplier Enablement Program Administrator or Supplier Enablement Task Management permission to manage and monitor tasks. Context The task details page on the Tasks tab provides the following detailed information for a task: • • • • • • 84 Whether the task is buyer-owned or supplier-owned Task name Activity name Supplier details Vendor details Date when the status was changed PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Tasks • • • Person who modified the task parameters Comments (entered by the supplier and buying organization Companywide contact information (for the supplier) You can defer a task for the following statuses: • • • • Pending Overdue Escalated Failed When a task is deferred, the due date of the task is recalculated and the remaining pending reminders aren't sent out. The task is also removed from the pending task list. However, when the task again reaches the due date and is pending, it shows in the task list and reminders are sent. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Tasks . 2. In the View dropdown, choose a view. 3. Optional: Filter the page [page 82] by specifying one or more filters. 4. Find a task and do one of the following: • • • To view details about the task, choose Actions View Task Details . To defer the task, choose Actions Defer Task . In the Defer By field, choose a value (for example, 1 Day, 2 Days, or 5 Days) and click OK. To reopen a task, choose Actions Reopen Task . Enter a comment that explains why you're reopening the task, and click Reopen. How Suppliers Can Access Supplier Enablement Tasks Your suppliers can view, complete, and set reminders for enablement tasks. Viewing Tasks Suppliers can view the supplier enablement tasks from their SAP Business Network supplier account. The Enablement Tasks page lists all the tasks associated to an activity. If a supplier has multiple customers, the tasks for each customer are grouped together. The task list allows easy access to all the pending, overdue, and escalated tasks. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Tasks PUBLIC 85 1. Selected customer 2. Activities for the selected customer 3. Tasks for the selected activity 4. Link to complete a task Suppliers can also view the supplier information portal [page 31] to access more information about the customer’s company processes. The task meter on the Home page lists out the number of pending tasks for a supplier. Suppliers can also use the link in the task meter to navigate to the Enablement Tasks page. Completing a Task On the Enablement Tasks page, the supplier enablement activities. A tasks table lists the task status and description, grouped by each activity assigned to the supplier. Tasks have a link that allows a direct task completion, depending on the following task closure type: • System tasks: The task link opens the relevant configuration page. On completion, the task link lets you review the configuration. • Manual tasks: The task link prompts the supplier to complete the task. On completion, the task link lets you reopen the task only if the subsequent task hasn't yet been completed.  Remember Suppliers must have the necessary permissions to complete a system task. Additionally, a supplier can also view the following summary for each activity per customer: • • • • • 86 Activity name Date due (to complete the whole activity) Count of total tasks Count of supplier pending tasks Count of pending buyer tasks PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Tasks By default, the Enablement Tasks page shows activities that have pending suppliers tasks in the expanded task level view mode. Reopening a Task Suppliers can reopen any of the manually tracked tasks for supplier enablement by finding a completed task and clicking Reopen Task. A task can be reopened only when the subsequent task hasn't been completed. Suppliers can reopen their tasks from the SAP Business Network supplier account. Reminder Notifications Suppliers receive overdue task reminders. By default, these reminders are sent to the account administrator of the supplier account. Suppliers can configure additional users to receive the notifications. If the supplier doesn't take action, even after all preconfigured reminders have been sent out, the task is escalated to the buying organization.  Note Reminders aren't sent to suppliers quick enabled through purchase orders. However, as a buying organization, you can send the trading relationship request for quick-enabled suppliers manually [page 65]. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Tasks PUBLIC 87 Supplier Enablement Reports You can generate several different types of reports to track the supplier enablement process. When you create a new report [page 93] or edit and save an existing report [page 94], SAP Business Network puts the report into the queue and shows the report status as Processing on the Reports page. SAP Business Network generates reports in the order in which they enter the queue. When the report is finished, its status is Processed. Regardless of the actual start time, the report can collect information for the date range and time zone specified in the template. The exact timing of a report run might differ from one run to the next, but the coverage period is always determined by the criteria in the template. To keep a record of report files, you can download each report file to your computer before running the report again. The next time you generate the report, SAP Business Network overwrites the current version with a new report file. Creating Supplier Enablement Report Templates [page 93] Generating and Downloading Existing Supplier Enablement Reports [page 94] 92 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Reports Creating Supplier Enablement Report Templates You can create supplier enablement report templates that define what information is included in reports. Prerequisites You must have the Supplier Enablement Program Administrator or Supplier Enablement Report Administration permission to access and run reports. Context The Reports tab allows you to create, edit, and delete report templates, as well as to run and download reports. When you generate a report from a template, SAP Business Network creates a report file in comma-separated values (CSV) format with UTF-8 encoding, and it overwrites the last report you ran from that template. You can view reports or download them to your computer to save a record of your account activity over time. You can generate a maximum of 100 reports, with a maximum of 20 scheduled reports. Procedure 1. Choose Reports Reports . 2. Click Create. 3. Enter a unique title that helps you and other users easily identify this report from a list. For example, Supplier Enablement Status Report. 4. Enter a description. The description is useful for identifying the scope and target of the report for all account users. For example, Supplier Information report of all suppliers in a project. 5. Choose a value from the Time zone list. Dates and times in your report file use the time zone you choose here, expressed as GMT +/-. In addition, SAP Business Network uses the time zone to determine the range of information collected for the report. 6. Choose a language. SAP Business Network uses this language for labels in the resulting report file. It shows report data in the language in which the information was entered. 7. Choose a supplier enablement report type [page 88]. 8. Click Next. 9. On the Schedule page, choose either Manual Report or Scheduled Report. • • To generate a manual report, go to the Reports page and click Run. SAP Business Network automatically generates scheduled reports using the frequency that you specify. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Reports PUBLIC 93 10. If you choose Scheduled Report, SAP Business Network refreshes the page and shows the Scheduling section. Do the following: a. Set a date range. b. Choose a value from the Automatically Run list to set the report generation frequency. c. Enter up to three email addresses, each separated by a comma. SAP Business Network sends a notification to these addresses when the report status is Processed. 11. Click Next. 12. On the Criteria page, choose the parameters for the report. 13. Click Submit. SAP Business Network puts your report into the queue. You can view and download the report when its status is Processed. 14. To view and download the report, choose the report template, and then click Download. Then, do one of the following: • • Click Open to view the report. Your browser opens the report in Microsoft Excel. Click Save to save the report to your computer. Generating and Downloading Existing Supplier Enablement Reports You can run supplier enablement reports, or download reports that have already been scheduled and processed. Prerequisites You must have the Supplier Enablement Program Administrator or Supplier Enablement Report Administration permission to access and run reports. Context  Caution Report files that include double-byte or accented characters might not show up correctly in all viewer applications. You can change the encoding and delimiter settings for these files. For more information, see Viewing a Generated Report with Double-Byte or Accented Characters. 94 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Reports Procedure 1. Choose Reports Reports . 2. To generate a report, choose the report that you want to generate, then click Run.  Tip If you want to download the existing version of the report, skip this step and go to step 3. SAP Business Network adds your report to the queue and returns you to the Reports page. To update the statuses of reports on the Reports page, click Refresh Status. You can view and download the report when its status changes to Processed. 3. To view and download the report, choose the report template and click Download. Then, click one of the following: • Open to view the report. Your browser opens the report in a program associated with CSV files (typically Microsoft Excel). • Save to save the report to your computer. If a report file is larger than 1 MB, SAP Business Network stores it in ZIP format, and displays a ZIP icon in the Size column for that report.  Caution SAP Business Network deletes generated reports from your account after 30 days. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Reports PUBLIC 95 Supplier Enablement Terms This topic defines the terms relevant to the supplier enablement process. Term Definition Activity The method, by which suppliers transact with buying organizations through SAP Business Network. For more information, see Activities and Tasks [page 29]. Buying organization reminders A notification sent to a buying organization that contains a consolidated list of tasks that require action. The tasks are grouped into two types of reminders: • • Tasks for a buying organization that are pending Escalated supplier tasks CC invoice (carbon copy invoice) A cXML copy request document that contains an attached invoice sent from SAP Ariba Buying solutions or the ERP system. eContact The field to identify the vendors that have the relationship request routing as email, fax, or both, before starting supplier enablement. If supplier enablement is started for a vendor that doesn't have the email or fax routing details, the buyer task Provided Email or Fax for the Trading Relationship Request becomes pending. The task is marked complete once the buyer has provided a routing email address or fax number for the vendor. This can be done online or by reloading the updated vendor details. The trading relationship request letter is automatically sent once the buyer has provided the details.  Note If both email and fax routing types are specified, email is used to send the relationship request letter. Escalated task A task that is given increased importance when all reminders have been sent to the task owner but the task isn't yet completed. Once a supplier task is escalated, a notification is sent to only the buyer. This consolidated notification contains a list of counts per escalated task for all suppliers. Enterprise account An account that provides access to all supplier functionality on SAP Business Network and might lead to supplier subscription fees. These accounts are your suppliers who need a more automated, efficient way to transact, or are too important not to proactively manage. Consider targeting the following suppliers for enterprise account registration: • • 96 PUBLIC Strategic suppliers Legacy, EDI-integrated suppliers with over 500 documents a year Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Terms Term Definition Standard account A free, easy-to-use account on SAP Business Network. These accounts allow suppliers to exchange an unlimited number of basic documents. Standard accounts provide limited access to SAP Business Network functionality. The standard account capability [page 13] for SAP Business Network provides buyers with a quick and touchless way to onboard all their suppliers and eliminate manual transaction processes.  Note After you start enabling suppliers through the standard account method, this process affects all quick enablement flows, including purchase order, CC invoice, payment proposal, and quick enablement customer code. Payment proposal An email sent by Procurement applications to create an SAP Business Network accounts for suppliers. Predefined tasks A default set of tasks that take place during supplier enablement on SAP Business Network. These tasks are further linked to predefined activities. For example, when a supplier creates an account, the task is called Accept Trading Relationship, which is associated with the Account activity. Private supplier account A type of account that is created for the following scenarios: • A buying organization sends a purchase order, CC invoice, or payment proposal to a supplier that doesn't have an SAP Business Network account. • An unregistered supplier routes an invoice to the buying organization by using the quick-enablement customer code. Quick enablement through purchase order A supplier-enablement method by which procurement applications send a purchase order by email to create SAP Business Network accounts for suppliers. Supplier enablement methods The multiple ways used to initiate a trading relationship for the following types of suppliers: • • • Suppliers already registered on SAP Business Network. Suppliers not yet registered and who don't have an SAP Business Network account. Private suppliers (defined previously in this table) – For these suppliers, you can link multiple unique supplier IDs (from the procurement application) to a single ANID/Vendor ID on SAP Business Network. Available methods: • • Searching and adding registered suppliers Quick Enablement – Purchase Order, Payment Proposal, CC Invoice (invoices sent from SAP Ariba Buying solutions or the ERP system), ICS Invoice (invoices sent from invoice conversion service providers), and request for quotation. • • Request trading relationship with suppliers. Posting a supplier self-nomination project so the supplier can proactively initiate a relationship request with you. Supplier information portal A portal that buying organizations create for vendors to view information about their company’s trading processes. Supplier notification A notification is sent when a new activity is assigned to a supplier. Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Terms PUBLIC 97 Term Definition Supplier reminders A reminder sent when a task for a supplier is overdue. Tasks Actions that a buyer or supplier must complete to establish supplier enablement. There are two types of tasks: • Automatic: Tasks that are system generated and are automatically tracked for closure. For example, acceptance of SAP Business Network terms and conditions or accept-trading-relationship tasks. • Manual: A task that isn't directly related to an SAP Business Network configuration setting and is therefore set to complete manually. For example, when a supplier needs to configure their order receiving process to receive purchase orders from SAP Business Network, the specified task for this action is called Ready to Receive Purchase Orders. This task needs to be completed manually. Trading relationship request letter A letter [page 22] sent to the newly created suppliers and existing suppliers by fax or email when enabling a trading relationship with a buying organization. Vendors A supplier in the customer’s back-end system. Vendors are identified on SAP Business Network with unique vendor IDs. A buying organization stores details of their vendors in their ERP systems. The vendor ID on SAP Business Network typically reflects the vendor ID used in the ERP system. For buyers using SAP Ariba Procurement solutions (or Ariba Invoice Automation and Ariba Purchase Order Automation with Oracle Fusion Middleware adapters), a vendor is identified on SAP Business Network with a unique vendor compound key. The vendor compound key consists of up to three fields: Vendor ID, Site ID, and Site Auxiliary ID. The fields used in your configuration depend on the type of ERP system used. (These fields reflect the ID of the supplier site as it's stored in the ERP system.) See Supplier ID Normalization. A buying organization can upload vendor information to SAP Business Network using their SAP Business Network account. After the upload, they can assign Supplier Enablement activities containing specific tasks and start the enablement for selected vendors. First a trading relationship request email is sent out to these vendors. Once they register and accept the terms of use, a dedicated supplier account is created on SAP Business Network and a relationship is automatically established with the buying organization that sent the request. Afterwards, all supplier account details are maintained by the suppliers themselves and all vendor details continue to be managed by the buying organization. Wave A form of identifier used to group vendors for supplier enablement activities, based on various criteria. For example, you could group all vendors that have high saving/ROI potential into the first wave or group vendors that belong to a specific region into another dedicated wave. Once you've grouped vendors in waves, it's easy to start supplier enablement by a wave and also to track the enablement progress by waves.  Note Wave values can't exceed 256 characters. Waves are entered in the format WaveN, where N is any positive integer. A zero (0) can't prefix positive integers N, except where N is a value from one to nine. You can only assign waves to your vendor through the Vendor CSV file. The Manage Vendors and Monitor pages allow you to filter by wave. 98 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Enablement Terms Supplier Self-Assessments In today's fiercely competitive business environment, companies rely heavily on robust supply chains to gain a competitive edge. However, managing larger supply chains exposes businesses to greater risks, especially when partnering with unvetted suppliers, which can result in regulatory violations. These violations not only lead to financial losses but can also damage a company's reputation. To effectively address these challenges, SAP Business Network offers standardized supplier self-assessment questionnaires. These questionnaires are invaluable tools for gathering essential information for procurement activities, helping mitigate uncertainties within the supply chain. This proactive approach not only safeguards against potential risks but also enhances a company's reputation with both new and existing business partners. With SAP Business Network, you can easily request assessments from suppliers to collect required information. Suppliers can also proactively complete the assessments and share them with you and other buyers. Initiating Assessment Requests You have the flexibility to initiate assessment requests either from the Supplier Self-Assessments page or from supplier profiles. Initiating requests from the Supplier Self-Assessments page requires an established trading or sourcing relationship between you and the supplier. However, requesting assessments from supplier profiles doesn't have this requirement. If you're using SAP Ariba Supplier Risk, specific conditions must be met, including having established trading or sourcing relationships with your suppliers and selecting SAP Business Network as the data source for responses to modular questionnaires. Notifications and Updates When you send an assessment request, your suppliers are notified through both emails and notifications on the SAP Business Network portal. You are also notified through emails and portal notifications when your suppliers share or update their assessments. However, you won't be notified if suppliers unshare their assessments. SAP Business Network supports version update of the self-assessment questionnaires. You will receive a notification on the Supplier Self-Assessments page if a new version is available, and the supplier has not yet upgraded. In such cases, you can request the supplier to upgrade promptly. About the Human Rights Assessment The human rights assessment questionnaire inquiries about the processes a supplier has in place to identify, assess, prevent, and remedy human rights and environmental risks and impacts in their supply chain and operations. Examples of the risks that companies must address are as follows: • • • • • • • Forced labor Child labor Discrimination Violations related to freedom of association Unethical employment Unsafe working conditions Environmental degradation Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Self-Assessments PUBLIC 99 Requesting Assessments from the Supplier Self Assessments Page Prerequisites • • Both you and your suppliers use SAP Business Network. You've established a transaction or sourcing relationship with your suppliers.  Note If you have an account of SAP Ariba Supplier Risk, you can also request an assessment from this portal. Context To assess the supply chain due diligence of suppliers, request them to take an assessment. You can initiate your request either from the Supplier Self Assessments page of the SAP Business Network portal or from the supplier profiles. This task explains how to request supplier assessments from the Supplier Self Assessments page. For details about requesting assessments from supplier profiles, refer to Requesting Assessments from the Company Profile of Suppliers [page 102] You can send an assessment request to suppliers with the assessment status Not requested. You can resend an assessment request to suppliers in the following two scenarios: • You've already sent the assessment request to a supplier, but the supplier hasn't shared the assessment answers with you. In this case, the assessment status is Requested. • A supplier has shared the assessment answers with you but later decided to cancel the sharing of the assessment. In this case, the assessment status is Not available - Unshared. After the supplier has shared the assessment with you, the assessment status changes to Available. In this case, you're unable to resend the assessment request. Procedure 1. Choose Supplier Enablement Supplier Self Assessments in the menu bar. 2. Click Request assessment. 3. Click Request for the target assessment. 4. Enter values in any of the fields to search for suppliers to whom you want to send the assessment request.  Tip You can search by supplier name and country/region. The more search criteria you enter, the narrower the search results are. 100 PUBLIC Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Supplier Self-Assessments
