file://SBN/split/Managing Network Catalo.content: Units and Codes Validation SAP Business Network uses standard coding systems for commodity, currency, unit of measure, state, country, and language codes. • • • • • Commodity Codes [page 11] Currency Codes [page 12] Unit of Measure Codes [page 12] State and Country Codes [page 13] Language Codes [page 15] Commodity Codes The United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (UNSPSC) standard is the SAP Business Networkpreferred commodity coding system. The UNSPSC contains descriptions of more than 12,000 products and services. The UNSPSC coding structure is hierarchical. It combines similar items in standardized groups. The finer the granularity of the item description, the more digits in the UNSPSC code, up to 8 digits. For example, the UNSPSC code for wooden pencils is 44121706, which is composed of the following categories: 44 Office equipment, accessories, and supplies 12 Office supplies 17 Writing instruments 06 Wooden pencils SAP Business Network supports only 6-digit or 8-digit UNSPSC codes. A 6-digit code represents a classification at level 3, the Class level (e.g., 441217). An 8-digit code represents a classification at level 4, the Commodity level (e.g., 44121706). SAP Business Network uses UNDP version - UNSPSC v25.9 by default. You can download the UNSPSC Codeset (login needed) v25.9 from UNSPSC Codeset Downloads . For example, English text that is the same for US English and UK English can be labeled with the shortened code “en”. 16 PUBLIC Managing Network Catalog Validation for Network Products Managing Staged Products Supplier users with the product manager role or an administrator role can perform the following actions on staged products in the network catalog: view product information, edit product details, delete products, preview the Product Details page, and send products for internal approval. Users with both the product manager and product approver roles or an administrator role can also publish staged products to the online version.  Note Suppliers without a promote subscription can perform up to 1000 publishing actions. A "publishing action" refers to any instance of publishing or approving a product, which includes initial publishing, republishing, approving, or re-approving a product in the network catalog. To exceed this limit, you need to purchase the promote subscription for SAP Business Network. For more information, see Network Catalog Experience for Promote Subscribers [page 4]. Action Description View complete product information After uploading the product files, you can view complete product information such as product name, ID, status, description, validity period, manufacturer name and ID, lead shipping time, classification system, pricing, and images. To view complete product details, choose View Edit product details ... on the Action column of the required staged product. To edit product details: 1. Choose ... Edit on the Action column of the required product.  Note You cannot edit products with the pending approval status. 2. Make changes as per your requirement.  Note If you are using a supplier account with the promote subscription, you can generate product summary and description using AI. For detailed steps, see Generating Product Summary and Description Using AI [page 19]. 3. Click Preview to view the latest changes on the Product Details page. 4. Go back to the edit page and click Save to save your changes.  Note You can also edit product data using product templates. To do that, download the required product template, add all the details, and upload it again. The uploaded file will replace the existing data of the respective staged product. Preview You can preview the Product Details page that will be displayed for buyers when they search and view the respective product. To preview the product details page, choose on the Action column of the desired staged product. Managing Network Catalog Managing Staged Products ... Preview PUBLIC 17 Action Description Send products for approval You can send staged products to the product approver for internal approval. Only products with the complete or rejected status can be sent for approval. Do the following to send products for internal approval: 1. To send a single product for approval, select the product in the staged products table and click the Send for Approval button above the table, or choose Approval ... Send for on the Action column of the desired product. 2. To send multiple products for approval, select the target products in the staged products table and click the Send for Approval button above the table. 3. To send all the products with the complete or rejected status and matching the page filter criteria for approval, choose ... Send all Products for Approval at the top right-hand side of the staged products table. Delete products You can only delete staged products from the network catalog. You cannot delete online products. Do the following to delete staged products: • To delete a staged product from the network catalog, choose ... Delete on the Action column of the desired product. • To delete multiple staged products, select the target products in the staged products table and click the Delete button above the table. Also, the Bulk Deletion Template allows you to delete multiple products using the Product ID's of your network products. Do the following to delete multiple staged products from the network catalog using Bulk Deletion template: • • • On the top right-hand side of the Network Catalog page, click ... icon. Select Download Bulk Deletion Template. In the downloaded template, add the Product ID's of the staged products which must be deleted and save the file. Product ID is the unique product identifier or Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) number assigned to the product by the supplier. • • • On the top right-hand side of the Network Catalog page, click ... icon. Click Upload Bulk Deletion File and add the bulk deletion file. Click Upload.  Note While uploading the bulk deletion file, only the file name with the 'deleteproduct+{file info}+{language code}.xlsx' format is allowed. The file information string in the file name must contain only alphanumeric characters and the maximum length is 20 characters. The language code must be as detailed in the SAP Business Network Standards and Guidelines. 18 PUBLIC Managing Network Catalog Managing Staged Products Action Description Publish Suppliers with both the product approver and product manager roles or an administrator role can directly publish staged products to the online version. Only products with the complete status can be published. 1. To publish a single product, select the product in the staged products table and click the Publish button above the table, or choose ... Publish on the Action column of the desired product. 2. To publish multiple products, select the target products in the staged products table and click the Publish button above the table. 3. To publish all the products with the complete status and matching the page filter criteria, choose ... Publish all Products at the top right-hand side of the staged products table. This saves you time and enhances the readability and appeal of your catalog entries. Prerequisites • • You've subscribed to SAP Business Network, promote subscription. A supplier administrator must have enabled the generative AI functionality for network catalog as described in Enabling Generative AI Functionality. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. From the menu bar, choose 3. Choose ... Edit Catalogs Network Catalog . on the Action column of the required staged product. 4. To generate product summary with AI, click the Generate with AI button above the Product Summary section to display the Generate Product Summary dialog, where you can view the product name, product description, product category, and manufacturer name.  Note A consent message must be acknowledged before using generative AI functionality. Managing Network Catalog Managing Staged Products PUBLIC 19 5. In the Character Limit field, set the total character length of the product summary to your preferred value. 6. In the More Details text box, provide additional details as inputs or instructions to develop product summary. 7. Click Generate. 8. Click Apply to use the generated content for your network catalog product. 9. To generate product description with AI, click the Generate with AI button above the Product Description section. Then proceed with the steps similar to steps 5 to 8.  Note It is important to remember that while AI generally produces high-quality content, there is a chance that it may not be entirely accurate, or it may generate text that doesn't meet your needs. Generated content should always be thoroughly reviewed. 20 PUBLIC Managing Network Catalog Managing Staged Products

file://SBN/split/Managing Network Catalo.content: Approving or Rejecting a Network Catalog Product As a product approver, you validate and approve the network catalog products that are sent for internal approval. When the product is in a pending approval status (awaiting internal approval), you need to view all the productrelated information and validate it. If you approve the product, it will be moved to the online version and can be searched by all buyers. If you reject the product, it will remain in the staged version. Staged products are not visible to buyers. If you have both the product manager and product approver roles, you can add products and subsequently approve them. Prerequisites  Note Suppliers without a promote subscription can perform up to 1000 publishing actions. A "publishing action" refers to any instance of publishing or approving a product, which includes initial publishing, republishing, approving, or re-approving a product in the network catalog. To exceed this limit, you need to purchase the promote subscription for SAP Business Network. For more information, see Network Catalog Experience for Promote Subscribers [page 4]. To approve or reject a network catalog product, you must have the product approver role or an administrator role. Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. From the menu bar, choose Catalogs Network Catalog . 3. Choose the Pending Approvals tile to display the pending approvals table. 4. Choose … View on the Action column of the desired pending approval product to review complete product information. 5. Choose … Preview on the Action column of the desired product to preview the Product Details page that is displayed for buyers when they search and view the respective product. 6. If the product data is complete without any errors, choose … Approve on the Action column of the desired pending approval product to approve and move the product from the staged version to the online version. You can approve multiple products at once by selecting them in the pending approvals table and clicking the Approve button above the table. You can also choose … Approve all Products at the top right-hand side of the pending approvals table to approve all pending approval products that match the page filter criteria. Managing Network Catalog Approving or Rejecting a Network Catalog Product PUBLIC 21 7. If the product data is incomplete or contains errors, choose … Reject on the Action column of the desired product to reject and move the product from the pending approval status to the rejected status. Enter the rejection reason in the Comments field of the Reject dialog and click Reject. You can reject multiple products at once by selecting them in the pending approvals table and clicking the Reject button above the table. The products selected for rejection at once must have the same rejection reason. 22 PUBLIC Managing Network Catalog Approving or Rejecting a Network Catalog Product Managing Online Products Product managers and supplier administrators can perform the following actions on an online product: Action Description Move products from the online version to the staged version You can move the products from the online version to the staged version. Staged products are not visible to buyers. Do the following to move products from the online version to the staged version: 1. ... Click Move to Staged on the Action column of the required online product. 2. Click Move. 3. To send multiple products from the online version to the staged version, select each check box at the beginning of the respective product row and click the Move to Staged button at the top right-hand side of the online products table. Preview You can preview the Product Details page that will be displayed for buyers when they search and select the respective online product. To preview the product details page, click Preview View complete product information ... on the Action column of the desired product. You can view complete product information such as product name, ID, status, description, validity period, manufacturer name and ID, lead shipping time, classification system, pricing, and images. To view complete product details, click View Managing Network Catalog Managing Online Products ... on the Action column of the required staged product. PUBLIC 23 Overview of Product Detail Template The product detail file allows you to add the detailed product description, specifications, supplier information, and manufacturer information that the buyer seeks before making the purchase. This is the first template that must be uploaded while adding a product. While uploading the product detail file, only ".xls" and ".xlsx" file formats are supported. File name with the 'product+{language code}+{file info}.xlsx' format is allowed.  Note Do not specify the geographic region in the language code. For example, English text that is the same for US English and UK English must be labeled with the shortened code “en” instead of “en-US” or “en-GB”. For the list of language codes, go to Language Codes [page 15]. Example of product detail file format: product+en+test.xlsx. The file information string in the file name must contain only alphanumeric characters and the maximum length is 20 characters. The file size must not exceed 2 MB. Product Detail Template Fields The following table lists the product template fields in order, describes each field, indicates if a field value is required or can be left blank, the field's data type, and the maximum field length.  Note Do not change the label names of the columns and tabs present in the template. All the mandatory fields in the template are marked with an asterisk (*) symbol. Field Name Data Type/Length (In Characters) Description Product ID* String/255 Unique product identifier or Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) number assigned to the product by the supplier. The product ID field must contain only the following characters: A – Z, a – z, 0 – 9, dash (-), and underscore (_). Short Name* String/80 A brief title associated with this product. It will be displayed as the product title on the search results page. Do not include quotes, HTML, symbols, or commas. Description* String/1000 Detailed description of the item. Generally only shown on the product details page. Do not include quotes, HTML, symbols, or commas. 24 PUBLIC Managing Network Catalog Overview of Product Detail Template Field Name Data Type/Length (In Characters) Description Summary String/1000 Brief description of the product providing additional information about various product attributes. Do not include quotes, HTML, symbols, or commas. UNSPSC Number* String/6 or 8 United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (UNSPSC) of the product. You can enter either an L3 - Class level code (6 digits) or an L4 - Commodity level code (8 digits). For example, enter 44121706 to represent wooden pencils, or 441217 to represent writing instruments. SAP Business Network uses UNDP version - UNSPSC v25.9 by default. You can download the UNSPSC Codeset v25.9 from UNSPSC Codeset Downloads Free version: Link . (login needed) EAN String/13 International Article Number. UPC String/12 Universal Product Code. Unit of Measure* String Select the unit of measure in UNUOM (United Nations Unit of Measure) standards which will be considered as the base unit of measure or sales unit. Product URL String/255 Product URL to provide more information about the product. URL must be https. Valid From Date (YYYY-MM-DD) Date in YYYY-MM-DD format from which the product becomes valid. This date is based on UTC time and must be prior to the product expiration date that is, Valid To date. Valid To Date (YYYY-MM-DD) Future date in YYYY-MM-DD format from which the product is no longer valid. This date is based on UTC time. Manufacturer Part ID String/255 A unique number assigned to the part by the manufacturer or brand. Manufacturer String/255 The name of the manufacturer or brand name. Manufacturer URL String/255 URL to the product manufacturer's website. URL must be https. Lead Shipping Time Integer Number of days required to ship the item. Decimal values are not allowed. Recycled Content Percentage Integer The total percentage of recovered material in a product, including pre-consumer and postconsumer materials. Managing Network Catalog Overview of Product Detail Template PUBLIC 25 Field Name Data Type/Length (In Characters) Description Renewable Energy Used Percentage Integer The total percentage of clean energy or green power used to build the product. Carbon Emission Enabled* Boolean (True/False) Enter the value "True", if you want to provide product specific carbon emission information. Entering a value of "True" in this field will enable mandatory field checks for other fields in the sustainability information section of this template. CO2e Emission Decimal (10,2) It is defined as the carbon footprint of a product. It considers the amount of GreenHouse Gas (GHG) emissions that are released throughout the production supply chain to produce a material or product. It is often measured with the boundary conditions of cradle to gate, cradle to site, or cradle to grave. CO2e Emission Unit String Select the unit of measure in UNUOM (United Nations Unit of Measure) standards for CO2e emission. Quantity per Unit Integer Reference quantity of the product for CO2e emission Accounting Standard String/20 Carbon accounting involves recognizing, evaluating, and monitoring GHG emissions and their effects on ecosystems. The most commonly used standard for carbon accounting is the GHG Protocol Product Standard, ISO Standard 14067, and ISO Standard 14044. Boundary Condition String/20 Boundary conditions are used to define what constraints are included in the emission calculation. The common boundary conditions are cradle to gate, cradle to site, and cradle to grave. Emission Accuracy String/20 Accuracy level of CO2e emission calculation. Emission Calculation Valid From Date (YYYY-MM-DD) Date in YYYY-MM-DD format from which the emission calculation value becomes valid. This date is based on UTC time. Emission Calculation Valid to Date (YYYY-MM-DD) Future date in YYYY-MM-DD format from which the emission calculation value is no longer valid. This date is based on UTC time. Additional Information String/1000 Additional sustainability-related information about CO2e emission calculation. 26 PUBLIC Managing Network Catalog Overview of Product Detail Template Overview of Price Template The pricing template allows you to add product pricing information based on quantity, geographic location, currency, price validity, discount, and units of measurement. SAP Business Network offers flexible pricing models such as: • Date-dependent pricing: It is useful for offering seasonal or holiday discounts. In the downloaded template, you will need to add the price, the date from which the price is valid, and the date from which the price is no longer valid. For date-dependent prices, SAP Business Network displays the current valid price in product details based on the server timezone. End users do not see information indicating that the price is date-dependent or when it will no longer be valid. • Quantity-dependent pricing: You can define different levels of pricing for products based on different quantities. For example, the product price is 100.22 USD if the product quantity is between 1 and 19 and 99.22 USD if the product quantity is 20 or more. In the downloaded template, you will need to add the price in the Price column and the minimum order quantity for which the pricing is effective in the Scale column. • Geography based pricing: You can define the product pricing based on the delivery location of the buyer. For example, if the delivery location is the United States of America, the product price is 50 USD and if the delivery location is Japan, the product price is 7200 JPY. You must upload the price template after uploading the product detail template. The instructions sheet on the downloaded price template provides an overview of the fields that are available in the template. While uploading the price file, only ".xls" and ".xlsx" file formats are supported. The file name with the 'price+{file info}.xlsx' format is allowed. The file size must not exceed 2 MB. The file information string in the file name must contain only alphanumeric characters and the maximum length is 20 characters. Example of price file format: price+test.xlsx. Price Template Fields The following table lists the price template fields in order, describes each field, indicates if a field value is required or can be left blank, the field's data type, and the maximum field length.  Note Do not change the label names of the columns and tabs present in the template. All the mandatory fields in the template are marked with an asterisk (*) symbol. Managing Network Catalog Overview of Price Template PUBLIC 27 Field Name Data Type/Length (In Characters) Description Product ID* String/255 Unique product identifier or Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) number assigned to the product by the supplier. The product ID field must contain only the following characters: A – Z, a – z, 0 – 9, dash (-), and underscore (_). Price Price of the product. Listing a valid price in the catalog increases the chance of potential buyers contacting you or making a purchase. If a price is unavailable or you’d rather respond to a check price request, leave the field blank. Currency* String/3 ISO 4217 currency codes. The currency in which the product price is quoted. Unit of Measure* String Select the unit of measure in UNUOM (United Nations Unit of Measure) standards. Quantity* Long Minimum order quantity for which the pricing is effective. For example, the product price is 100.22 USD if the product quantity is between 1 and 19 and is 99.22 USD if the product quantity is 20 or more. Valid From Date (YYYY-MM-DD) Date in YYYY-MM-DD format from which the price becomes valid. This date is based on UTC time and must be prior to the price expiration date that is, the Valid To date. Valid To Date (YYYY-MM-DD) Future date in YYYY-MM-DD format from which the price is no longer valid. This date is based on UTC time. Country/Region* String Select the country or region for which the product pricing is applicable from the drop-down list. Based on the selected geography, the product visibility will be determined for the buyers. State/Province String Select the state or province within the specified country/region for which the pricing is applicable. 28 PUBLIC Managing Network Catalog Overview of Price Template Overview of Media Templates There are two types of media templates namely, URL and .zip media templates. The media URL template allows you to add image URLs for uploading the product media. The media ZIP template allows you to add product images and paths to the location of images. You can add product images to give requisitioners a visual representation of your network products. They provide customers with a rich network catalog-browsing experience, similar to buying products on the Web. Recommended sizes for images: • • Full Size: 820 x 820 pixels or 568 x 426 pixels Thumbnail image: 160 x 160 pixels Ensure that the below criteria are met before adding images to the network catalog: • • • • • Images must be in JPEG, JPG, or PNG format. Your images can be in black-and-white or in color. They can be photographs or drawings. For best visual results, images should have a neutral background. The image URLs must be HTTPS only. The file names and filename extensions for images are case-sensitive. It is advised to compress the images before uploading the media file for a better experience. When you download the media ZIP template, a ZIP file containing the CSV file, images folder, and other documents will be downloaded. You need to add information to the CSV file and product images to the images folder. Also, you need to compress all the files into a single ZIP file. While uploading the meida ZIP file, only the file name with the 'media+{file info}.zip' format is allowed. The entire media ZIP file size must not exceed 200 MB. Example of media ZIP file format: media+test.zip. When you download the media URL template, an image URL file will be downloaded. You need to add information to the image URL file. While uploading the image URL file, only the file name with the 'imageurl+{file info}.xlsx' format is allowed. The file information string in the file name must contain only alphanumeric characters and the maximum length is 20 characters. The image URL file size must not exceed 2 MB. Example of image url file format: imageurl+test.xlsx.  Note Media file is optional. If the media file is not added for a product, a default image (blank page icon) is displayed for the respective product. . . 64 Managing Your User Account Content PUBLIC 3 Managing your SAP Business Network This guide describes how suppliers can customize their homepage and workbench, update their user information, link accounts, change their password, and configure their notification preferences. Suppliers periodically need to change their password for security reasons, link accounts with other users in their company, and change their notification settings to better monitor the transaction documents most important to them. This guide applies to: • • • SAP Business Network SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network Discovery Related Guides SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide 4 PUBLIC Managing Your User Account Managing your SAP Business Network The Supplier Homepage The SAP Business Network supplier homepage features navigation consistent with other SAP cloud solutions, a powerful search bar, an instant overview of your transactions in a tile-based design, and a widgets section that you can customize with various insights and promotional widgets. Figure 1: The Supplier Homepage 1. Document type: You can choose the type of document you are searching for: Orders and Releases, Order Confirmations, Ship Notices, Invoices, Service Sheets, Payments, Remittances, Time & Expense Sheet, or Collaboration Requests. 2. All customers or a specific customer: You can specifiy who the document is for. 3. Exact match or Partial match: You can choose whether the search results yield an Exact match or a Partial match. 4. Order number: You can enter the order number or other identifying number related to the document. 5. Overview tile bar. 6. Getting started tile bar. 7. My widgets displays widgets based on your role. Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage PUBLIC 5 Overiew Tile Bar Overview tile bar displays the default portal tiles, or tiles that display Rejected invoices and Service sheets, for example. The Overview tiles are displayed intelligently: if one or more Rejected invoices or Service sheets exist, those tiles are displayed first; otherwise, they are moved to the end of the order. Up to five tiles are displayed in the Overview tile bar by default, you can reveal additional tiles with the More button ( ). Getting Started Tile Bar 6 PUBLIC Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage • Quick start: Opens a new browser window and directs you to the Getting Started on SAP Business Network web page, which includes information about becoming an SAP Business Network supplier. • • • • • Add users: Directs you to your Account Settings, where you can manage users and roles. Set up order routing: Directs you to the Electronic Order Routing page. Set up invoice processing: Directs you to the Electronic Invoice Routing page. Set up email notifications: Directs you to the Notifications page. Review subscriptions: Directs you to the Subscriptions page. Homepage Widgets [page 7] The Workbench [page 18] Homepage Widgets The homepage displays role-based widgets that help you focus on important tasks, insights, key performance indicators, and benchmarks for your business. Homepage Widgets Figure 2: Example of Possible Widgets on the Homepage • Company profile widget: Shows you a percentage of how complete your company profile is. Complete your company profile to increase your chances of being discovered by new buyers. • Download app widget: Directs you to Google Play or the Apple App Store to download the SAP Business Network Supplier mobile app, so you can continue to focus on important tasks and insights for your business on-the-go. The widget includes a Learn more link if you want more information about the mobile app. • Activity feed widget: Displays real-time transaction activity and offers you a way to quickly navigate to those transactions. You can use the customer filter to display data for All customers or a specific customer, filter the widget by document type, and configure it to include specific events. Click the settings icon ( ) to choose which documents and statuses are displayed. For example, you can choose to only monitor the events Order cancelled or Orders changed. Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage PUBLIC 7 Figure 3: Screenshot of the Activity Feed Widget Settings Figure 4: Example of Possible Widgets on the Homepage • SAP Supplier Financing widget: Gives access to and displays information regarding the SAP Supplier Financing solution. SAP Supplier Financing gives you access to pre-qualified offers personalized for your business, based on your digital footprint on SAP Business Network. Its mission is to improve the financial health of small- and medium-sized businesses on SAP Business Network by simplifying access to working capital finance. As an SAP Business Network supplier, you simply activate SAP Supplier Financing using your existing SAP Business Network credentials, gaining access to your pre-qualified offers in a few short clicks. When you are approved for funding, the widget allows you to compare your Funded amount and Total Invoice Amount over the Last 7 days, Last quarter, Last 6 months, or Last 12 months. For more information, see SAP Supplier Financing user guide. • Invoice aging widget: Displays a bar graph of the value of Sent, Rejected, and Approved invoices from the last 0-30, 31-60, and 61-90 days. You can use the customer filter to display data for All customers or a specific customer. • My leads widget: Displays any open leads that match the commodities and territories in your company profile. 8 PUBLIC Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage Figure 5: Example of Possible Widgets on the Homepage • Purchase orders widget: Displays a line graph of the total value of purchase orders you've received from your customers in the Last 3 months, Last 14 days, or Last 7 days. You can use the customer filter to display data for All customers or a specific customer.  Note Purchase order and invoice amounts specified in non-USD currencies are converted to USD for the purpose of aggregation using the currency exchange rate at the time the transaction document is created. The aggregated amount is further converted to your user-specified currency for display in widgets. Therefore, you may see a difference between the original amounts displayed in the workbench and the aggregated amount displayed in widgets. • Application gateway widget: If your buyer has configured any external applications for your use, you can access them via single sign-on through the Application gateway widget. KPI and Benchmarking Widgets [page 9] Customizing Your Home Page Widgets [page 17] KPI and Benchmarking Widgets A Key Performance Indicator, or KPI, is a measurable value that demonstrates how effectively a company is achieving key business objectives. Organizations use KPIs at multiple levels to evaluate their success. Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage PUBLIC 9 A benchmarking widget gives you information about the performance being achieved by groups of companies in aggregate across SAP Business Network. You can view a particular facet of performance in all or specific industries during a selected time range (last 12 months, last quarter, or last month). Benchmarking widgets eliminate costly data collection activities that would have otherwise been required to share data with a benchmarking service provider, and enable you to make fair comparisons between your customers. KPI and benchmarking widgets include a history icon ( ) that displays the latest data refresh. This data is refreshed monthly, and as needed, for accurate calculation and to remove irrelevant data. KPI and benchmarking widgets should be used in conjunction to support your customer relationship management strategy. You can compare the performance of your specific customer (KPI) to the aggregate performance of others on SAP Business Network (benchmarking) and leverage this information in evaluations and negotiations with your customer. A benchmarking widget provides benchmarking information by buyer industry, supplier region, and buyer performance quartile. The figures are only presented if there are seven or more companies in the region, industry, or group; otherwise, SAP Business Network combines the figures into a group named Others. • Buyer Industry - Buyer industry is determined by the buyer's account representative and assigned to the buyer's account on SAP Business Network. Industries aren't determined by the business unit of the underlying transaction. • Supplier Region - Region is determined by the country/region of the supplier's account on SAP Business Network, not the country/region of the underlying transaction. Regions include Americas, APAC, and EMEA. • Buyer Performance Quartile - A quartile is a statistical term that describes a division of observations into four defined intervals. SAP Business Network calculates buyers' monthly performance, orders the buyers by performance, and groups the buyers into four performance quartiles. Best in class is a term for the top performing results in a particular metric. To understand best-in-class performance on SAP Business Network, choose Top 25% in the Buyer Performance Quartile chooser. Requirements Most KPI and benchmarking widgets require an enterprise account with bronze level or above, except the Paid invoices and On-time payment rate KPI widgets. Restrictions • The value of transactions is displayed in USD only. The intent of KPI and benchmarking widgets is to compare the customers performance to the aggregated behavior of the network. As such, the comparison and the standard for comparison is in USD. • The data is not real time and is presented for prior complete periods only. This ensures the performance calculations are fair and not just based on a few days in the opening of a new period. • • The widgets do not include data from test accounts. 10 KPI and benchmarking widgets are not available in FedRAMP environment. file://SBN/split/Managing your SAP Busin.content: Considerations • Some widgets use the remittance data or scheduled data uploaded by buyers, but not all buyers load such data to SAP Business Network. • A scheduled payment is the buyer's representation of the supplier invoice in the buyer's accounts payable system. The payment relevant KPIs calculated by SAP Business Network may therefore differ from those calculated by the supplier receivable system. Understanding the buyer’s perception of the KPIs can be a powerful tool in business reviews as both parties work together to improve process performance. • The accuracy of the widgets may be impacted by problems with the buyer's integration with SAP Business Network. • The SAP Business Network KPI framework includes intelligence to identify and exclude data outliers that may be bad data, test data, or otherwise interfere with the KPI calculation. Therefore, KPI calculations may not fully reconcile with the scheduled payments listed on SAP Business Network. In-app Help As soon as you can access the widgets, you can find more information in the in-app help. Open it by selecting the help icon ( ) in the upper right corner of the window. On-time Payment Rate Widget The On-time payment rate widget measures the number of invoices paid before or on the date defined by the payment terms of the invoice, as a percentage of the total number of invoices paid by customer's Accounts Payable (AP) department over the same period of time. On-time payment rate categorizes payments as Accelerated, Paid on time, or Paid late, and presents this information as a donut chart. You can display the data for All customers or a specific customer, and for payments received in the Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. SAP Business Network calculates on-time payment rate by comparing the remittances and scheduled payments sent to you by your customers. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Payment Activities, Inbox and Order Access, or Supplier Treasury Agent. Definitions Paid on time: The percent of remittance line items that match to a scheduled payment, where remittance Payment date is less than or equal to scheduled payment Payment date. Paid late: The percent of remittance line items that match to a scheduled payment, where remittance Payment date is greater than the scheduled payment Payment date. Accelerated: The percent of remittance line items that match to a scheduled payment where remittance Payment date is less than or equal to the scheduled payment Payment date and the scheduled payment is the result of a discount offer (buyer-initiated, standing early payment term offer, or payment term offer). Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage PUBLIC 11 Paid Invoices Widget The Paid invoices widget displays a line chart that shows the quantity (right-side axis) and value (left-side axis) of the invoices paid in the Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. You can use this widget together with the On-time payment rate widget to identify the extent to which you are paid on time. It also helps you understand, at a glance, the degree to which you are benefiting from your early payment discount program. Consult the widget in conjunction with the Early Payment (details) report for a more complete understanding. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Payment Activities, Inbox and Order Access, or Supplier Treasury Agent. Payment Days Late Widget The Payment days late widget calculates the average payment days late KPI and displays the number of paid invoices by the number of payment days late on a bar chart. You can display the data for All customers or a specific customer, and for payments received in the Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. Payment days late, in conjunction with the On-time payment rate and Paid invoices widgets, helps you identify the extent to which you are paid late and understand the payment behaviors and patterns of your customers. You must have the Payment Activities permission to view the widget. Definitions Average days: The average number of days late that invoices are paid. This is calculated by comparing the payment date on remittances with the scheduled payment date defined in the invoices. Late payments have a positive value. Early payments have a negative value. On the bar chart, the y-axis represents the number of paid invoices, and the x-axis shows the number of payment days late as defined below: Category Number on x-axis Definition Paid on time 0 Invoices paid on the scheduled payment date Paid late 7 Invoices paid 1-7 days later than the scheduled date 14 Invoices paid 8-14 days later than the scheduled date 30 Invoices paid 15-30 days later than the scheduled date 60 Invoices paid 31-60 days later than the scheduled date 90 Invoices paid 61 or more days later than the scheduled date 12 PUBLIC Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage Category Number on x-axis Definition Paid early -7 Invoices paid 1-7 days earlier than the scheduled date -14 Invoices paid 8-14 days earlier than the scheduled date -30 Invoices paid 15-30 days earlier than the scheduled date -60 Invoices paid 31-60 days earlier than the scheduled date -90 Invoices paid 61 or more days earlier than the scheduled date Benchmarking On-time Payment Widget The Benchmarking: On-time payment widget calculates the on-time payment rate, payment days late, and paid invoices KPIs across SAP Business Network by supplier region, buyer industry, and buyer performance quartile. You can use this benchmarking widget in conjunction with the On-time payment rate, Payment days late, and Paid invoices KPI widgets to compare the benchmark to your specific customer's performance. Both sets of widgets use the same source data and KPI calculation method, including intelligence to identify and exclude data outliers that may be bad data, test data, or otherwise interfere with the KPI calculation. On the donut chart that shows on-time payment rate, accelerated payments refer to the on-time payments accelerated through the use of SAP Business Network discount solution for which buyers early payment offers to suppliers. You must have the Payment Activities permission to view the widget. Approved Invoices Widget The Approved invoices widget displays a line chart that shows the quantity (right-side axis) and value (left-side axis) of the invoices approved in the Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. The calculation is made by counting the scheduled payments that were sent to you by your customers. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Payment Activities, Outbox Access, or Invoice Generation. Invoice Cycle Time Widget The Invoice cycle time widget enables you to track the invoice processing performance of your customers and identify potential credit and collection issues. The invoice cycle time KPI measures the number of business days required to process an invoice from when the invoice is received by customer's Accounts Payable (AP) department until it is approved and scheduled for Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage PUBLIC 13 payment. In the line chart, the y-axis represents the number of invoices approved and scheduled to pay. The x-axis represents invoice cycle time in days. You can display the data for All customers or a specific customer and for invoices approved in the Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. The KPI calculation excludes failed, canceled and on-hold scheduled payments. Some data outliers that may distort the graphical presentation of cycle times are filtered out from the graphical display, but they are still included in the KPI calculation. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Payment Activities, Outbox Access, or Invoice Generation. Benchmarking Invoice Cycle Time Widget The Benchmarking: Invoice cycle time widget calculates the invoice cycle time KPI and the number of approved invoices across SAP Business Network by supplier region, buyer industry, and buyer performance quartile. The chart on the left displays the invoice cycle time, which measures the number of business days required to process an invoice from when the invoice is received by the buyer's accounts payable system until it is approved and scheduled for payment. The chart on the right shows the value and volume of approved invoices over the same period of time. You can use this widget in conjunction with the Invoice cycle time and Approved invoices widgets to compare the benchmark to the performance of your specific customers. Both sets of widgets use the same source data and KPI calculation method. You can display the data for Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Payment Activities, Outbox Access, or Invoice Generation. Days to Pay Widget The Days to pay widget displays the average days it takes your customers to pay an invoice. You can use it in conjunction with the Paid invoices widget to identify customer payment patterns and behaviors. The widget also helps you understand the impact of accepting early payment offers on your organization. The more early payment you accept, the greater reduction in days to pay is achieved. You can display the data for All customers or a specific customer and for payments received in the Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Inbox and Order Access, Payment Activities, or Supplier Treasury Agent. Definitions Average days to pay: The average number of days required to process an invoice between the invoice date and payment date. This is calculated by taking the difference between the invoice date on a scheduled payment and the payment date on the related remittance sent to you by your customer. 14 PUBLIC Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage Benchmarking Days to Pay Widget The Benchmarking: Days to pay widget calculates the days to pay KPI across SAP Business Network by buyer industry, supplier region, and buyer performance quartile. The KPI measures the average number of days required to process an invoice between the invoice date and payment date. This is calculated by taking the difference between the invoice date on a scheduled payment and the payment date on the related remittance. You can use this widget in conjunction with the Days to pay widget to compare the benchmark to the performance of your specific customers. Both widgets use the same source data and KPI calculation method. You can display the data for Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Inbox and Order Access, Payment Activities, or Supplier Treasury Agent. Invoice Exceptions Widget The Invoice exceptions widget displays a line chart of the total number of invoice exceptions in the Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months, which includes the number of rejected, canceled and failed invoices plus the number of debit and credit memos. You can use it in conjunction with the Invoice exception rate widget to understand customer performance. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Payment Activities, Outbox Access, or Invoice Generation. Invoice Exception Rate Widget The Invoice exception rate widget measures the percentage of invoices sent by suppliers to their customer's Accounts Payable (AP) department that contain an error of some kind and are rejected by AP. You can display the data for All customers or a specific customer and for invoices in the Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Payment Activities, Outbox Access, or Invoice Generation. Definitions Invoice exception rate: the number of invoices sent to AP that are rejected, canceled or failed plus the number of credit/debit memos, divided by the total number of invoices received by AP over the same period of time, as a percentage Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage PUBLIC 15 Benchmarking Invoice Exception Rate Widget The Benchmarking: Invoice exception rate widget calculates the invoice exception rate KPI and the number of invoice exceptions across SAP Business Network by buyer industry, supplier region, and buyer performance quartile. The donut chart on the left displays the invoice exception rate, which measures the number of invoice exceptions (rejected, canceled and failed invoices plus debit and credit memos) as a percentage of the total number of invoices received by buyer's accounts payable system. The line chart on the right counts the invoice exceptions over the same period of time. Use this widget in conjunction with the Invoice exception rate and Invoice exceptions widgets to compare the benchmark to the performance of your specific customers. Both sets of widgets use the same source data and KPI calculation method. You can display the data for Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Payment Activities, Outbox Access, or Invoice Generation. Change Orders Widget The Change orders widget displays a line chart of the quantity of change orders that were sent to you by your customers in the Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. You can use it in conjunction with the Change order rate widget to understand customer performance. You can use the customer filter to show data for All customers or a specific customer. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Inbox and Order Access, Purchase Order Report Administration, or Invoice Generation. Change Order Rate Widget The Change order rate widget displays a bar chart to show the percentage of purchase orders sent by your customers that have subsequent changes. The Change order rate KPI is calculated by dividing the number of change orders by the total number of new purchase orders sent by your customers over the same period of time, as a percentage. Scheduling agreements are excluded from the KPI calculation. You can display the data for All customers or a specific customer and for purchase orders in the Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Inbox and Order Access, Purchase Order Report Administration, or Invoice Generation. 16 PUBLIC Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage Benchmarking Change Order Rate Widget The Benchmarking: Change order rate widget calculates the change order rate KPI and the number of change orders across SAP Business Network by buyer industry, supplier region, and buyer performance quartile. The bar chart on the left displays the change order rate, which measures the number of change orders as a percentage of the number of original purchase orders. The line chart on the right shows the quantity of change orders over the same period of time. Use this widget in conjunction with the Change order rate and Change orders widgets to compare the benchmark to the performance of your specific customers. Both sets of widgets use the same source data and KPI calculation method. You can display the data for Last month, Last quarter, or Last 12 months. To view the widget, you must have one of the following permissions: Inbox and Order Access, Purchase Order Report Administration, or Invoice Generation. Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage PUBLIC 17 The Workbench The workbench displays configurable tiles based on transaction documents, statuses, and additional filters. Overview of the Workbench The workbench is a customizable page that allows you to get a quick overview of transaction documents and take action on them. It displays up to 25 customized tiles. When more tiles are available that can fit on your screen (based on your screen resolution), the tile bar displays a right arrow button ( ) to scroll through the tiles. Each tile displays a count or amount, title, and subtitle. 1. The count is the number of transactions, action items, or events that match the tile filter criteria, up to 1000; if the count is greater than 1000, the count displays 1000+. The amount is the total value of scheduled payments, remittances, or early payment offers contained in the tile. It is displayed in your local currency. 2. The title is the name of the base tile, a label describing the type of transaction, action item, or event that matches the tile criteria, such as Rejected invoices. 3. The subtitle is a configurable label to further describe the contents of the tile, which is particularly useful when you create your own variant of a tile based on a complex combination of filters. Editing fields in the table The documents associated to each tile are listed in the table below the workbench tiles. Each row represents a document associated to that tile, each column represents a field and their value from the document. Based on your buyer's transaction rules, some of the fields in the table may be editable. In the screenshot below, you can edit the Estimated shipping, Estimated delivery, Quantity to confirm, and Unit price fields for orders associated to the Items to confirm tile. This would allow you to make edits before the items on an order are confirmed. The fields you can edit are based on the tile selected, not every tile has editable fields. 18 PUBLIC Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage If an editable field isn't selected or entered, it is automatically included in the Others column; you can click Others to display and edit these hidden fields. Customer-specific attributes Buyers create custom attributes for various customization projects and can extend them to workbench tiles to allow their suppliers to view them as filters and columns. You must configure their workbench tiles to view these customer-specific attributes. You can customize your workbench tile tables to display or group customer-specific columns the same way you do with standard columns. If you work with only a single customer who provides additional columns, they are selected by default. Otherwise, you can choose a customer in the Customize table dialog to manage their columns. Customer-specific filters and columns are only available when you filter for a single customer. If you filter for two or more Customers, any customer-specific filters are removed. Documents that you pin are available on the Pinned documents tiles on the workbench and in the SAP Business Network Supplier mobile app. The pin action is supported on the following tiles: • • • • • • • • • Orders New orders Orders to invoice Changed orders Orders with service line Invoices Rejected invoices Invoices pending approval Approved invoices pending payment Choose the Pin column from the Table setting dialog on supported tiles to add the pin action to your tile. The actions column The Actions column displays a more button ( ) that allows you to complete actions on documents. The actions available are based on the document type, status, and your buyer's transaction rules. For example, when viewing the New orders tile, the Actions column may allow you to confirm or reject the order. Some workbench tiles also support multi-select and bulk actions. 20 PUBLIC Managing Your User Account The Supplier Homepage

Updating Your User Account Information [page 31] Updating Your User Account Information You can change your contact information, preferred language, preferred timezone, and other information related to your account from the My account page. Procedure 1. In the right corner of the header bar, click the Account Settings icon ( The My Account page appears. ) and choose My Account. 2. Update values in the Account Information section as necessary, noting the following constraints and guidelines: • User name is a value you enter when you sign in to SAP Ariba. User names may be in the format of an email address (name@domain.com); however, SAP Ariba does not send messages to the address. User names are not case-sensitive and can contain any English character, but cannot contain any spaces or punctuation except the @ sign and period required by the name@domain.com format. • Email Address is where SAP Ariba sends user level account notifications. By default, SAP Ariba sends all notifications to the account administrator. In addition, the account administrator’s and SAP Ariba Sourcing users email addresses are part of the seller account profile, which is visible to your customers or to all buying organizations, depending on your account setting. If you change your email address, SAP Ariba sends an email to the newly updated email address requesting you to confirm the email address. You must use the link in the email to activate and sign in to the account.  Note Your account administrator serves as the primary point of contact if you need help updating your user information, or if you have any other questions or problems. To view your account administrator’s contact details, click Help Contact Administrator . 3. To change your password, click Change Password. For more information, see Changing your Password [page 34]. 4. Update values in the Preferences section as necessary, noting the following constraints and guidelines: • Preferred Language is the language used when SAP Ariba sends you configurable notifications. This is different from your web browser's language setting, which controls the user interface and actions you initiate there. If you are the account administrator, then the preferred language setting also controls the section headings and field labels on purchase orders routed through email or fax. • Preferred Timezone controls how SAP Ariba displays date and time on purchase orders routed by fax or email. Date and time stamps are displayed as GMT (Greenwich Mean Time) +/-. Managing Your User Account User Account Information PUBLIC 31 SAP Business Network uses this setting for documents sent by your administrator and user accounts, such as invoices. In addition, SAP Business Network uses the time zone for dates and times entered by users. Procedure 1. Sign in to SAP Business Network. 2. In the header bar, click the Account Settings icon ( ) and choose My Account. The My Account page appears. 3. Below the User name text box, click the Set up two-factor authentication link. The Enable Two-factor Authentication page appears. 4. Download and install the SAP Authenticator or Google Authenticator on your mobile phone. 5. Open the authenticator app that you have installed on your phone and do either one of the following: 1. Type the secure key displayed on the Enable Two-factor Authentication page. Or 2. Use your phone to scan the bar code displayed on the Enable Two-factor Authentication page. Passwords are case-sensitive, must be at least eight characters long, and can include only alphabetic letters (without accents), numbers, and common symbols. For increased security, you should include at least one numeral between the first and last characters and at least one common symbol. You can update all your user account information, including changing your password, from the user profile menu. To change your password, you must enter your current password as well as the new one, and then confirm the new password. Managing Your User Account Searching for Trading Partners PUBLIC 39 Data Analytics SAP Business Network offers data analytics to help suppliers better understand their customers and business. Analytics Dashboard The Analytics dashboard on the SAP Business Network user interface for suppliers offers predefined analytics views on purchase order and invoice data, presented in tiles, charts, and tables. Access to the dashboard requires a SAP Business Network Enterprise account at the Platinum subscription level for suppliers. Enter up to three email addresses, separated by commas, for each notification type you want to activate. For example: johnc@abccompany,natalies@abccompany,nelss@abccompany  Note To send one notification type to more than three email addresses, create a distribution list in your email system and enter the name of that distribution list in the appropriate field on the Notifications page. 54 PUBLIC Managing Your User Account Notification Preferences 3. Select the check box for each notification type you want to activate. If you want SAP Ariba to stop sending a notification type, click to clear the check box. SAP Ariba retains your email addresses for your convenience, but does not send notifications. Related Information Notification Types [page 47] Managing Your User Account Notification Preferences PUBLIC 55 Linking User Accounts If you have multiple user accounts, you can link them together. Context Linking your multiple user accounts together enables you to quickly transfer between accounts with a single-click. Linking your multiple accounts also helps to eliminate the need to remember multiple user names and passwords. You must have access to the user name and password of the user account with which you want to link to your account.  Restriction You cannot unlink user accounts. Procedure 1. In the right corner of the header bar, click the Account Settings icon ( ) and choose Link User IDs. The Link Accounts page appears. 2. Enter the user name and password of the user account you want to link with and click OK. SAP Ariba displays a confirmation message, indicating that your user accounts are now linked. 3. Click Done. Results The user profile menu displays multiple User Account IDs in the Switch To section. 56 PUBLIC Managing Your User Account Linking User Accounts Removing Your Personal Information and Revoking User Access to SAP Business Network SAP Business Network users can request the administrator for their account to remove their personal information from the system. If approved, the user can’t sign in to SAP Business Network any longer, and their personal information is no longer visible to users, including in transaction documents shared and exchanged with business partners.  Note For audit and compliance purposes, the user’s personal information is still visible to the user who is the administrator for your SAP Business Network account. Restrictions • Comments or attachment files associated with transaction documents aren’t affected when users remove personal information. Therefore, avoid entering personal information in comments or attached files. • After a user’s revocation of user access request is approved, their personal information is pseudonymized in SAP Business Network transaction documents. However, transaction documents that were integrated with other systems (such as an ERP) or downloaded before the request was approved may still have the user’s personal information. The customer needs to take additional action, including informing impacted business partners, to remove it. • If a customer needs to re-identify a user that has been pseudonymized for legal purposes, the administrator of the account can provide that information. Workflow for Removing Personal Information for a User from SAP Business Network This procedure describes the workflow for removing personal information for an SAP Business Network user: Figure 6: Workflow for Removing Personal Information for a User 1. A user signs in to the SAP Business Network portal to request the removal of their personal information. 2. The administrator for the account receives an email notifying them of the user's request. Managing Your User Account Removing Your Personal Information and Revoking User Access to SAP Business Network PUBLIC 57 3. The administrator signs in to the SAP Business Network portal and approves or rejects the user's request. 4. If the administrator approved the request, the user's personal information is removed. 5. If the administrator approved the request, the user can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Requesting Removal of Personal Data for a Supplier User SAP Business Network users can request the administrator for their account to remove their personal information from the system. If your request is approved, your personal information is removed, and you can't sign in to SAP Business Network. Prerequisites If you are currently assigned the Administrator role for your account, you can't perform this task until after you transfer the Administrator role to another user. See Transferring the Account Administration Role. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose My Account. The My Account page opens. 2. In the Personal information usage section, check the Request to remove my personal information option. 3. Click Save. Results The administrator is notified of your request, and they can approve or reject it. 58 PUBLIC Managing Your User Account Removing Your Personal Information and Revoking User Access to SAP Business Network Contacting Your Account Administrator Contact your account administrator with questions or problems related to your account. The account administrator role is assigned to the individual at your organization who is responsible for setting configuration options, managing customer relationships, subscribing to services, and maintaining the account over time. The administrator serves as your primary point of contact if you need a password reset, if you require additional permissions, or if you have any other questions related to your user account. To view your account administrator's contact details, click your name at the top of the page and select Contact Administrator. Managing Your User Account Contacting Your Account Administrator PUBLIC 59 About the SAP Business Network Supplier Mobile App The SAP Business Network Supplier mobile app gives users mobile access to SAP Business Network, including some features of SAP Business Network Discovery. SAP Business Network Supplier Overview [page 60] SAP Business Network Supplier Supported Devices and Restrictions [page 61] SAP Business Network Supplier Security Features [page 62] Managing the SAP Business Network Supplier Mobile App [page 63] SAP Business Network Supplier Overview You can use SAP Business Network Supplier to view, track, and pin purchase orders and invoices, confirm standard purchase orders at the header level, create invoices and credit and debit memos, and view graphical representations of your transaction data. SAP Business Network Supplier includes the following features: • Biometric authentication: SAP Business Network Supplier uses biometric authentication for enhanced security and usability. Sign in to SAP Business Network Supplier quickly with your fingerprint. • SAP Business Network Supplier home dashboard: The SAP Business Network Supplier home dashboard displays permissions-based tiles for important transaction documents, collaboration requests, and enablement tasks, and various widgets that help you focus on important tasks and insights for your business. • Document search: Search for specific orders and invoices or filter by status, customer, or pinned documents. SAP Business Network Supplier uses the powerful HANA infrastructure to allow users to search for orders and invoices from the last 12 months. Alternatively, users can browse recent orders and invoices from the last 31 days. • Configurable alerts: Choose specific document types and statuses for which you want to view notifications and receive push alerts on your mobile device. • Pin orders and invoices: Mark important documents from your mobile device to more quickly access them from a desktop workstation. • Orders and invoices: View order and invoice details, status changes, and histories. Create invoices, credit memos, and debit memos. Share orders and invoices with your colleagues using any app on your device that can share documents, such as email, text messages, or Google Docs. • • • Order confirmation: Confirm standard purchase orders at the header level. • Account switch: Switch to linked user IDs, allowing you to efficiently monitor activity on all of your accounts. 60 Receive and respond to leads: Monitor, respond to, and bid on SAP Business Network Discovery postings. Company profile management: Track your company profile completeness. Complete your company profile to increase your chances of being discovered by new buyers. file://SBN/split/Managing your SAP Busin.content: Mobile Gateway The mobile gateway is a set of features that allow you to access the full functionality of SAP Business Network from within the SAP Business Network Supplier mobile app. Mobile gateway features allow you to: • • • • • update your company profile view the web version of orders and invoices create non-PO invoices create standard PO-based invoices create credit memos, line-item credit memos, and line-item debit memos SAP Business Network Supplier Supported Devices and Restrictions SAP Business Network Supplier supports Apple iOS and Android devices. SAP Business Network Supplier supports the following operating systems and devices: • iOS versions 15.4 or higher: • • iPad Air, mini, and mini with Retina display iPhone 8x or higher  Note For iOS, SAP Business Network Supplier works best when viewed on the iPhone 8, 8 Plus, 9, iPhone X, iPhone XS, iPhone 11, iPhone 12, iPhone 12 Pro, and iPad Air. • Android versions 13.x or higher.  Note For Android, SAP Business Network Supplier works best when viewed on Samsung Galaxy S9, S10, and S11 devices. SAP Business Network Supplier works best with the latest versions of iOS and Android; users with older operating systems may encounter bugs.  Restriction SAP Business Network Supplier is not compatible with jailbroken or rooted devices. Caveats Users with iOS devices might encounter the following issues: • Users viewing the app on an iOS device other than those mentioned above might experience slower performance and irregularities in the display. The functionality of the app is unaffected. • Due to technical limitations, iOS does not support some Microsoft Word formatting features. Attachments viewed using iOS might have a different appearances. Users might also see irregularities in the display of Microsoft PowerPoint attachments. For example, slide numberings might not be displayed correctly. Managing Your User Account About the SAP Business Network Supplier Mobile App PUBLIC 61 • Biometric authentication is only supported on iOS versions 9.x or higher and iPhone 6 or later. Restrictions You can not use SAP Business Network Supplier on devices that are not passcode protected. You can not share orders and invoices with 100 or more line items. Though SAP Business Network Supplier supports and expands many of the features and functionality of SAP Business Network, it does not support all features and functionality of SAP Business Network. For example: • You can not use SAP Business Network Supplier to view and respond to leads created by buyers using the quote automation feature. • You can not use SAP Business Network Supplier to view custom implementations applied to SAP Business Network. If your buyer uses custom order confirmation layouts, you should perform the related tasks on SAP Business Network • You can not use SAP Business Network Supplier to view or download attachments to collaboration requests. SAP Business Network Supplier does not support the features and functionality of SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. SAP Business Network Supplier Security Features Security features in the SAP Ariba mobile apps help protect your data and the communication between the app and SAP Ariba. SAP Ariba mobile apps include the following security configuration options and controls. Security configurations: • • User authentication - user name and password credentials are required to sign in to SAP Ariba mobile apps. • Fingerprint recognition - users can use fingerprint recognition instead of their user name and password to sign into SAP Ariba mobile apps. • Face ID support for iOS devices - users can use facial recognition on devices that support it to access SAP Ariba mobile apps. • Password reset - users can reset their password, and administrators can reset passwords on behalf of a user, from the web application. Users must enter their user name and new password after password reset to re-enable Face ID or Touch ID features. • Device deactivation - if a user's mobile device is lost or stolen, the user or administrator can deactivate SAP Ariba mobile apps via the web application. User authorization - SAP Ariba mobile app functionality is controlled by user authorizations and permissions defined in the web application. Security controls: • Data encryption - all data is encrypted, including data transmitted over the network and limited data stored on the device. • 62 All communication between the device and the server is over TLS 1.2. PUBLIC Managing Your User Account About the SAP Business Network Supplier Mobile App • Data stored on mobile devices is encrypted using AES 256. • • Device passcode - SAP Ariba mobile apps can only be launched on a passcode-protected device. • Screen focus - SAP Ariba mobile apps show a blank screen when the user focus is moved away from the app. Jailbroken and rooted devices - SAP Ariba mobile apps aren't supported on jailbroken and rooted devices. If a device is jailbroken or rooted after an app is installed and activated, the app is deactivated and all data is wiped when the app is reopened. Choose On or Off for each notification as needed. 4. Click Save.
