. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 19 2 PUBLIC Messaging on SAP Business Network Content Messaging on SAP Business Network This guide describes how to communicate with trading partners to get clarifications on purchase order details or follow up on orders, invoicing, or payment status. This guide applies to: • • SAP Business Network SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Related guides Introduction to SAP Business Network Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Overview of the Messaging Feature The Messaging feature enables buyers and suppliers on SAP Business Network on BTP to communicate directly with each other using online messaging and email messaging. It supports structured, auditable communication related to procurement and invoicing activities by ensuring that all message exchanges are centrally stored, traceable, and accessible in one place. The feature is available to all buyer users and all supplier users. Buyers and suppliers can use Messaging to clarify purchase order details, follow up on order status, and resolve invoicing or payment issues. By moving these conversations from offline channels into SAP Business Network, the feature improves visibility, accountability, and collaboration efficiency. Online Messaging Online messaging allows buyers and suppliers to communicate directly within SAP Business Network using the Message Center. It provides a centralized, real-time workspace for all conversations, ensuring full message history and visibility for all participants. There are two types of online conversations: • In-Context Conversations: Linked to a specific business document (including purchase orders and invoices) and initiated from the document's Details page. These conversations allow users to discuss and resolve document-related issues while maintaining a clear audit trail. • Context-Free Conversations: General, document-independent conversations initiated directly from the Message Center, allowing users to communicate more broadly with trading partners. Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network PUBLIC 3 All online conversations, regardless of type, are stored and managed in the Message Center for easy tracking, access, and follow-up. Email Messaging Email messaging allows users to participate in message conversations directly from their email clients while keeping all communication synchronized with the Message Center in SAP Business Network. When a new message is posted, SAP Business Network sends an email notification to all conversation participants who have an SAP Business Network account. By default, SAP Business Network includes the latest two messages of a conversation in the email. Recipients can reply directly from email, and their responses are processed by SAP Business Network and added to the corresponding conversation thread. For more information, see Email Messaging [page 6]. Benefits Using the Messaging feature helps trading partners: • • • Reduce processing delays and manual coordination in procurement and invoicing workflows. Resolve disputes more efficiently with centralized, traceable message history. Maintain a complete audit trail of buyer–supplier interactions across online and email channels. Availability and Prerequisites • • The Messaging feature is available to buyer and supplier organizations using SAP Business Network on BTP. • To allow unregistered and registered suppliers to respond to interactive email-order emails, ensure that standard enablement using interactive email-order is turned on for the SAP Business Network buyer account. For buyers, the Messaging feature must be enabled by the account administrator before use. For enablement steps, see Enabling the Messaging Feature for a Buyer Account [page 17]. Glossary of Messaging Terms Term Definition Conversation A collection of one or more messages grouped by a common subject. Each conversation includes the subject, participants, and the sequence of exchanged messages. 4 PUBLIC Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network Term Definition In-context conversation A conversation linked to a specific business document, such as a purchase order or invoice. It enables trading partners to communicate directly about that document. Context-free conversation A general conversation not tied to any business document. It is initiated from the Message Center and used for broader or document-independent communication. Message / Post The content exchanged within a conversation. Messages (also knows as posts) appear in chronological order within the Message Center, forming a single communication thread. Message Center The central workspace where users can create, view, and manage all conversations. It is accessed by clicking the  icon in the top-right corner of the SAP Business Network portal. Related Information The Messaging User Interface [page 5] The Messaging User Interface The following example shows the Message Center user interface: Element on Screen Description Search bar Allows you to search for specific messages. Create Starts a new conversation. Delete Deletes a conversation. Available only to administrators in the initiator’s organization. Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network PUBLIC 5 Element on Screen Description Conversation list on the left panel Displays all conversations, including: • In-context conversations: Linked to a specific business document. The Reference field on the conversation details screen indicates the document linked to the conversation. • Context-free conversations: General conversation not linked to any business document. Edit Subject Edits the subject of a conversation. Close Conversation Makes a conversation read-only. Available only to the initiator or administrators in the initiator’s organization. Reopen Reopens a closed conversation open for further communication. Available only to the initiator or administrators in the initiator’s organization.  Note The data shown in this example screenshot is for testing purposes only and does not represent real customer data. Email Messaging Email messaging extends the SAP Business Network Messaging capability by allowing buyers and suppliers to participate in message conversations directly from their email clients. In addition to the online messaging channel, users can receive email notifications for newly created messages and send responses by replying to those emails. All email-based responses are captured and displayed in the corresponding online message thread, ensuring that all communication remains contextual, auditable, and accessible to all conversation participants. This capability is available to all buyer users and supplier users and supports both document-related conversations, such as those initiated from purchase orders or invoices, and context-free conversations. Buyer and supplier administrators can configure the email addresses that should receive message notifications. When a new message is posted, SAP Business Network sends an email notification to all conversation participants who have an SAP Business Network account. By default, SAP Business Network includes the latest two messages of a conversation in the email. Recipients can reply directly from email, and their responses are processed by SAP Business Network and added to the corresponding conversation thread. Adding a Participant to an Email Conversation Buyers and suppliers can include participants who don't have access to SAP Business Network by including the email address of the participant in the carbon copy (Cc) field of an email client. When the participant responds, buyers and suppliers can continue the conversation by responding to the emails. When a participant is included in 6 PUBLIC Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network an email, it must contain the Messaging Policy consent statement to ensure that the participant consents to the Messaging Policy of the SAP Ariba Cloud Services.  Note When a user initiates a message from SAP Business Network, the user can add only one participant. However, when the responding participant replies to a message via an email client, multiple participants can be added. When any subuser is deleted, SAP Business Network deletes all personal information of the subuser and stops sending any email notifications to the subuser. In this scenario, when a participant (either a buyer subuser or a supplier subuser) of a conversation is deleted, the Messaging feature deletes the details of the participant. SAP Business Network doesn't delete any conversation. Any other user having access to the document in SAP Business Network can participate in the conversation. Adding Attachments to a Message While initiating a message or responding to a message, a buyer or supplier can add attachments to the message. You can also add attachments while replying to an email message. All participants of a conversation can view the list of attachments either online in SAP Business Network or in the email message. You can download attachments either in SAP Business Network or from the email message. You can add a maximum of 5 attachments to a message. The size of each attachment can't exceed 10 MB. SAP Business Network rejects all email messages containing more than 5 attachments or if the size of any attachment exceeds 10 MB. Attachments having executable file extensions aren't allowed. Standard account suppliers can also add attachments while replying to a message via email. Management of Messaging Conversations Users can close, reopen, and delete messages and conversations, depending on their role and permissions. Closing and Reopening Conversations Organizations may choose to close conversations that are no longer needed. If necessary, the initiator or the initiator’s administrator can also reopen a closed conversation. Deleting Conversations After a conversation is deleted, it is permanently purged according to the system’s data retention schedule. Only the administrator of the organization that initiated the conversation can delete it. For example: Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network PUBLIC 7 • • If a supplier user initiated a conversation, only the supplier’s administrator can delete that conversation. If a buyer user initiated it, only the buyer’s administrator can delete it. Deleting Posts (or Messages) Buyer administrators and supplier administrators can delete individual posts created by their subusers within a conversation. Buyer and Seller Tasks • • • • Closing a Conversation [page 12] Reopening a Conversation [page 13] Deleting a Conversation [page 14] Deleting a Message from a Conversation [page 15] Notifications for Messaging The Messaging feature provides notifications for buyers and sellers. Table 1: Messaging Notifications Type of Notification Description Consent Confirmation Messaging feature sends a Consent Confirmation notification to the message sender for the first time, if the email contains the Messaging Policy consent statement. Missing Consent Messaging feature sends a Missing Consent notification if the message sender's email doesn't contain the Messaging Policy consent statement, and the consent doesn’t exist for the email address. Messages Messaging feature sends notifications when messages are received. Invoice messages Messaging feature sends notifications when invoice-related messages are received. Purchase order messages Messaging feature sends notifications when purchase order-related messages are received. Related Information Configuring a Buyer Account to Receive Email Notifications [page 16] Configuring a Supplier Account to Receive Email Notifications [page 15] 8 PUBLIC Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network Buyer and Supplier End User Tasks Initiating a Context-Free Conversation [page 9] Initiating an In-Context Conversation [page 10] Viewing and Replying to Online Messages [page 11] Unsubscribing from Email Notifications for Online Messages [page 11] Initiating a Context-Free Conversation You can start a conversation that is not linked to any specific business document. These are called context-free conversations and are created directly from the Message Center. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. In the left panel of the Message Center, click Create. The Create New Conversation dialog opens. 3. Enter the following details: • Recipient: Enter the name of the organization you want to contact. You can also click the  value-help icon to choose from a list of organizations with active trading or sourcing relationships. • • Subject: Provide a brief subject for your conversation (maximum 20 characters). • Start Message: Type your initial message (maximum 1024 characters). Message content must not include lewd, harassing, discriminatory, or illegal material. Attachment: Select files to attach, if needed. You can attach up to five files, with a maximum size of 10 MB per file.  Note Files attached to messages cannot be deleted or recalled once sent. 4. Click Create to start your conversation. Results The conversation is created and displayed in the Message Center You can continue exchanging messages with the recipient within this thread. Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network PUBLIC 9 Initiating an In-Context Conversation After a business document is created and sent, you can start a conversation with your trading partner in the context of that document. These are called in-context conversations. Context You can exchange in-context messages for the following document types: • • • Purchase Orders PO-Based Invoices Non-PO Invoices Procedure 1. Open the required document, such as a purchase order or invoice. 2. On the document Details page, click Send Message. The Messages popup appears. 3. Click New message. The Create New Conversation dialog opens. 4. Enter the following details: • Recipient: Enter the name of the organization you want to contact. You can also click the  value-help icon to choose from a list of organizations with active trading or sourcing relationships. • • Subject: Provide a brief subject for your conversation (maximum 20 characters). • Start Message: Type your initial message (maximum 1024 characters). Message content must not include lewd, harassing, discriminatory, or illegal material. Attachment: Select files to attach, if needed. You can attach up to five files, with a maximum size of 10 MB per file.  Note Files attached to messages cannot be deleted or recalled once sent. 5. Click Create to start your conversation. Results You can start exchanging messages with the recipient within this thread. If you click Send Message again from the document’s Details page, the existing conversation opens automatically. You can also access the same conversation from the Message Center. 10 PUBLIC Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network

file://SBN/split/Messaging on SAP Busine.content: Viewing and Replying to Online Messages You can view and reply to online messages directly from the Message Center. Context Any user in your organization can access the Message Center and participate in a conversation. Within each conversation thread, participants are identified by their user name followed by the name of their company. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, select the conversation you want to view. The conversation thread appears on the right. 3. Enter your reply in the text box and click the  Send icon to send it. 4. Optional: To attach files, click the  Attachment icon and select the files you want to upload.  Note You can upload up to 5 files, and each file can be up to 10 MB in size. Files attached to messages cannot be deleted or recalled once sent. Unsubscribing from Email Notifications for Online Messages As a supplier, you can unsubscribe from email notifications that are sent when new conversation messages are posted. Context By default, when buyers and suppliers communicate using the Message Center, the Messaging feature sends an email notification for each message. If you do not want to receive an email for every message, you can unsubscribe using the steps below. Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network PUBLIC 11 Procedure 1. Open the notification email. 2. Click the Unsubscribe link for email message notification. Results After unsubscribing, you will no longer receive email notifications for new conversation messages. To resume receiving email notifications, contact your SAP Business Network account administrator and ask them to add your email address back to the notification list. Buyer and Supplier Administrator Tasks Closing a Conversation [page 12] Reopening a Conversation [page 13] Deleting a Conversation [page 14] Deleting a Message from a Conversation [page 15] Configuring a Supplier Account to Receive Email Notifications [page 15] Configuring a Buyer Account to Receive Email Notifications [page 16] Enabling the Messaging Feature for a Buyer Account [page 17] Closing a Conversation To prevent accidental replies, the conversation initiator or an administrator from the initiator’s organization can close a conversation, making it read-only. Prerequisites You are either the conversation initiator or an administrator from the initiator’s organization. 12 PUBLIC Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. In the left panel of the Message Center, select the conversation that you can close. 3. Click Close Conversation in the top-right corner of the screen. 4. In the confirmation dialog, click Close to confirm. Results The conversation becomes inactive and you’re not able to send new messages until reopened. Related Information Reopening a Conversation [page 13] Reopening a Conversation You can reopen a closed conversation if you need to continue communicating with the recipient. Prerequisites You are either the conversation initiator or an administrator from the initiator organization. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, click the closed conversation you want to reopen. 3. Click Reopen Conversation at the top-right corner of the conversation details screen. 4. In the confirmation dialog, click OK to confirm. Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network PUBLIC 13 Results The conversation is active again, and you can continue exchanging messages with the recipient. Deleting a Conversation If a conversation is no longer needed, an administrator from the initiator organization can delete it. Once deleted, the conversation cannot be resumed and will be permanently removed from the system in accordance with the system’s data retention policy. Prerequisites You are an administrator from the initiator organization. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, select a conversation that you want to delete.  Note Checkboxes are disabled for conversations that were not initiated by your organization. 3. Click Delete at the top right of the panel. Results The conversation is removed from the conversation list and cannot be resumed. 14 PUBLIC Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network Deleting a Message from a Conversation An administrator from the initiator organization can delete individual messages from a conversation. Prerequisites You must be an administrator from the initiator organization. Procedure 1. On the SAP Business Network portal, click the  Message icon in the top-right corner of the screen. The Message Center is displayed. 2. From the left panel of the Message Center, open a conversation that was initiated by a user from your organization. 3. Under the message you want to remove, click Delete. Results The selected message is deleted from the conversation. The recipient can no longer view the message. Configuring a Supplier Account to Receive Email Notifications As a supplier administrator, use this procedure to configure email addresses for a supplier account to receive certain kinds of email notifications. Context Supplier accounts can receive email notifications for the following types of messages: • Document-specific messages • • • Purchase order-related messages. Invoice-related messages Default email notifications for all messages You can specify a maximum of three comma-separated email addresses to receive the notifications. Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network PUBLIC 15 Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Account Administration Notifications . 2. On the Notifications page, click the Messaging tab. 3. Choose your next step. • Send notifications when purchase order messages are received. In the Global document-specific settings section, check the Send notifications to these addresses checkbox, and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. • Send notifications when invoice messages are received. Check the Send notifications when invoice messages are received checkbox, and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. • Send notifications for all types of buyer messages received. In the Global default settings section, check the Send notifications when customer messages are received checkbox and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. If global document-specific settings aren't defined, or if those email addresses are unsubscribed from receiving notifications, the Messaging feature sends the notifications to the specified email addresses. • Send all notifications to the SAP Business Network administrator. Check theSend all notifications to the SAP Business Network administrator checkbox. If you enable both global default settings, the Messaging feature sends notifications to the SAP Business Network Supplier Administrator only when the email addresses in Global document-specific messages are unsubscribed. • Send notifications when context-free messages are sent or received. In the Context-free settings section, check the Send context-free message notifications to these addresses checkbox and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. 4. Click Save. 5. Click Close. Configuring a Buyer Account to Receive Email Notifications As a buyer administrator, use this procedure to configure email addresses for buyer accounts. Context The buyer administrator can configure email addresses for a buyer account to receive the following types of email notifications: • Document-specific • • • Purchase order-related messages Invoice-related messages Global default You can specify a maximum of 3 comma-separated email addresses to receive notifications. 16 PUBLIC Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Account Administration Notifications . 2. On the Notifications page, click the Messaging tab. 3. Choose your next step. • Send notifications to the Ship To email address on the purchase order. In the Global document-specific settings section, check the Send notifications to the Ship to email address on the purchase order (if available) checkbox. • Configure an email address for a scenario where the Ship To email address isn't specified on the purchase order. Check the If there's no Ship to email address, send notifications to these addresses checkbox and type the email addresses in the textbox next to it. • Configure separate email addresses for different countries/regions based on the Sold to address of a purchase order. • Send notifications when invoice messages are received. Check the Send notifications when invoice messages are received checkbox, and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. • Configure separate email addresses for different countries/regions based on the Bill To address of an invoice, • Send notifications for all types of document-specific supplier messages received. In the Global default settings section, check the Send notifications when customer messages are received checkbox and enter the required email addresses in the accompanying textbox. If global document-specific settings aren't defined, or if those email addresses are unsubscribed from receiving notifications, the Messaging feature sends the notifications to the specified email addresses. • Send all notifications to the SAP Business Network Buyer Account Administrator. Check the Send all notifications to the SAP Business Network administrator checkbox. If you enable both global default settings, the Messaging feature sends notifications to the SAP Business Network Buyer Account Administrator only when the email addresses in All document-specific messages are unsubscribed. • Send notifications when context-free messages are sent or received. In the Context-free settings section, check the Send context-free message notifications to these addresses checkbox and enter the required email addresses in the textbox next to it. 4. Click Save. Enabling the Messaging Feature for a Buyer Account To use messaging, your account administrator must enable it for your organization Prerequisites You must be an account administrator. Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network PUBLIC 17 Procedure 1. Sign in to your SAP Business Network account. 2. Click your user initials in the top-right corner and select Settings. 3. Go to Account Administration Messaging . 4. Click Edit, and select the checkbox Allow this account to use messaging in SAP Business Network. 5. Click Save. Results The Messaging feature is now enabled. All users in your organization can communicate with trading partners through messages in SAP Business Network.  Note To disable messaging, return to the Messaging Configuration page and clear the same checkbox. Messaging Reports A messaging report contains messages exchanged between you and your trading partners on SAP Business Network. Messaging Report Criteria Field Description Supplier (or Buyer) Select the trading partner with whom you had the conversation with. Context Select Context Free or Purchase Order. Context Free means the conversation is not associated with any documents. Purchase Order means the conversation is associated with specific purchase orders. Status Select Open or Closed. Initial Participant From Select the originating source of the message, whether the message is initiated from SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba Procurement Solution, or SAP Ariba Sourcing. Created On Select the date when the conversation was initiated. Maximum Results Returned Select 100, 200, 500, 1000, or 10000. 18 PUBLIC Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging Report Fields Field Description Date Date of the initiation of the conversation. Subject Subject of the conversation. Message Content of the message. Context Context of the message, whether it is related to an invoice or purchase order, or if it is a context-free message, or a broadcast message. Document Reference Invoice number or the purchase order number to which the message is related. For contextfree messages, this field is blank. Created By ANID of the creator of the post. Generating Messaging Reports Context A messaging report contains messages exchanged between you and your trading partners on SAP Business Network. To generate a messaging report, follow the steps below: Procedure 1. Sign in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Analytics Reports . 3. On the Reports page, in the Report Templates section, click Create. 4. In the Select report type popup, select the required report type. 5. In the New Object, go to the Report Description tab and enter the following details: • • • • • • Report Type: You already added this in the previous step. Title: Add a title for the report. This is a mandatory field. Description: Provide additional details about the purpose of the report. Format: Select the output format for the generated report. Comma-Separated Values (*.csv) and Microsoft Excel (*.xlsx) are supported. Time Zone: Choose the time zone applicable for the report data. Language: Select the language in which the report is generated. 6. Go to the Report Criteria tab and select the required values for the following fields: • • • Supplier (or Buyer): Select the trading partner with whom you had the conversation with. Context: Select Context Free or Purchase Order. Context Free means the conversation is not associated with any documents. Purchase Order means the conversation is associated with specific purchase orders. Status: Select Open or Closed Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network PUBLIC 19 • Initial Participant From: Select the originating source of the message, whether the message is initiated from SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba Procurement Solution, or SAP Ariba Sourcing. • • Created On: Select the date when the conversation was initiated. Maximum Results Returned: Select 100, 200, 500, 1000, or 10000.  Note 7. This step is available only to buyers. On the Report Schedule tab, select one of the following: • • Manual Report Scheduled Report: • • If you select this, enter the Date Range and Automatically Run schedule. Add your email address under Email Notification to receive notifications when the report is generated.  Note The Report Schedule setting is only available to buyers. 8. Click Save. 9. Click Back to return to the Reports page. 10. Select the created Report Template and click Run. 11. Click Go to execute the report. The task is queued for processing. Wait until the status changes to Processed. 12. Once processed, click the download icon in the Action column to retrieve the report file. 20 PUBLIC Messaging on SAP Business Network Messaging on SAP Business Network

file://SBN/split/Receiving and Fulfillin.content: 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Receiving and Fulfilling Orders Generated on: 2026-07-10 02:06:09 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network for Trading Partners | 2605 Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/ARIBA_NETWORK_SUPPLIERS/45abc7c531754929a19c6a844bd5d6ec?locale=enUS&state=PRODUCTION&version=2605 Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 1 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Receiving and Fulfilling Orders This guide is for SAP Business Network suppliers who use SAP Business Network to process purchase orders from their buyers. You use SAP Business Network to view purchase orders from your buyers and to confirm, deliver, and invoice for the goods or services you supply. This guide applies to: SAP Business Network Related Guides: SAP Business Network - Supplier Help Roadmap Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Purchase Orders This section provides topics describing types of purchase orders and the processes to fill orders. What Are Purchase Orders and Service Orders? Order Routing Work Order Information Typical Purchase Order Life Cycle What Are Purchase Orders and Service Orders? Purchase orders and service orders are documents that your customers send you to request goods or services from your company. Your customer’s procurement application assigns a unique number to each order it generates. SAP Business Network tracks transactions by these assigned numbers. Purchase orders you receive through SAP Business Network can contain the following types of information: Material items, such as raw materials or furniture General service items, such as janitorial services, or labor service items, such as contract labor, that do not require separate tracking Service items that require separate tracking Lean Service type items for planned lean services Limit Service type items for unplanned lean services Limit Order type items that are service or material items at a price limited by a predetermined amount within a time period specified by the buyer Travel and expense items, such as airline flights or car rentals This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 2 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Blanket purchase order items, such as any frequently purchased items or services Total landed cost details, such as allowances and freight charges Material Orders Material orders can contain lines for both material items and general-service items or labor items that don’t require separate tracking. The typical order fulfillment cycle for a material order is as follows: Limit Orders A Limit Order type line item is defined as the fulfillment of a service or material delivery at a price limited by a predetermined amount within a time period specified by the buyer. It focuses on improving customer experience by optimizing the use of resources. It reduces the time, user effort, and processes involved in procuring low-value materials and services. The source of a purchase order with a limit-order line item can be SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing or SAP Ariba Buying. Limit Order type line items can be materials or services in SAP Business Network. For example, cleaning of office premises can be considered as a limit-order service line item. This service will be carried out regularly at a price and within a period that is previously agreed upon by the buyer and supplier. When either of the following entitlements is enabled, SAP Business Network supports a mixed order of both limit-order and regular material or service line items: Enhanced order confirmation integration capabilities for hosted and integrated suppliers Enhanced order confirmation integration capabilities  Note The Quantity for a limit-order line item is always 1 and it is not editable. The Subtotal for a limit-order line item should not exceed the limit set by the buyer for that line item in the purchase order. Service Orders Based on your customer's configuration, service orders contain at least one line item that requires a service sheet. A service sheet is a document that you fill out to describe the services you performed to fill the order, as well as any material goods you used for the service. Service orders can contain lines for both material items and services. The following types of line items are supported in a service purchase order: Material Service This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 3 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Lean Service Limit Service Lean services simplify the process of procuring services. They can be either Lean Service type items for planned lean services or Limit Service type items for unplanned lean services. Planned lean services focus on improving the customer experience by optimizing the use of existing resources. They reduce the time and effort involved in procuring low-value items, and reduce the steps involved, such as ordering, receiving, processing invoices, and so on. For example, regular cleaning of office premises can be considered a lean service. The buyer does not need to know the specific details of the regular cleaning process, such as the exact time when the cleaning is done or the details on supplies used per day. Here, the buyer purchases the service item as a lean service. Limit items for unplanned lean services, also known as limit services, are used to procure unplanned low-value services costing up to a predefined spend limit. They reduce the time and effort involved in procuring low-value items, and reduce the steps involved, such as ordering, receiving, processing invoices, and so on. Limit services can be purchased like planned lean services. The buyer does not need to specify all the details at the time of purchase. The purchased service will be carried out until the buyer-specified predefined spend limit is reached. For example, regular cleaning of office premises can be considered as a limit service. The buyer does not need to know the specific details of the regular cleaning process, such as the exact time when the cleaning is done or the details on supplies used per day. Here, the buyer purchases the service item as a limit service, specifying the spend limit as the value for the Expected Value for Unplanned Spend field in the service purchase order. As a result, the cleaning service is carried out until that spend limit is exhausted. For more information about planned and unplanned lean-service line items, see Manage Service Entry Sheets - Lean Services in the SAP S/4HANA Sourcing and Procurement guide. The main difference in fulfillment cycle between a material order and a service order is that, when you are fulfilling a service order, the service sheet takes the place of a ship notice to describe the parts of the order that have definitely been fulfilled and to provide a basis for invoicing. The typical order fulfillment cycle for a service purchase order is as follows:  Note Observe the following guidelines and restrictions for service orders: Based on your customer's configuration, you might not have to create service sheets as a prerequisite to be able to create service order-based invoices. The Lean Service and Limit Service item types in SAP Business Network correspond to and support SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud standard and enhanced limit-item categories for services. SAP Business Network supports a mixed order with materials and lean services. In such cases, a ship notice is valid for the material items in the order. SAP Business Network also supports mixed orders with materials and service items including both Lean Service and Limit Service line items. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 4 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Order confirmation is not supported for Limit Service item types (unplanned lean services), unless one of the following entitlements is enabled: Enhanced order confirmation integration capabilities for hosted and integrated suppliers Enhanced order confirmation integration capabilities However, order confirmation is supported for planned lean services (Lean Service item types). See Service Order Confirmations for more information. Cancellation of service sheets with Limit Service items is not supported. Attachments are not supported. Quick enablement of suppliers is not supported. Blanket Purchase Orders A blanket purchase order (BPO) is a purchase order issued to one supplier for multiple purchases of specific goods or services, for a specific time period and a not-to-exceed predetermined amount. The BPO allows purchases, within the terms of the order, to be charged to that specific BPO. The transaction rule Allow adding a child item to an invoice for blanket purchase orders under Blanket Purchase Order Invoice Rules allows the supplier to choose whether to add child items while creating an invoice from a BPO from SAP Ariba Buying or from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Viewing a BPO on the Orders Purchase Orders page (or Orders Orders and Releases if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain) is similar to viewing a standard purchase order, with some differences. Customers can hide some information, and change orders might be displayed differently. If any values in a BPO are Undisclosed, then your customer has elected to mask certain field values from their suppliers. Typically, the Order Detail page contains additional BPO-related information for BPO status, amount available, minimum and maximum amounts, and BPO type, but customers have the option not to disclose amounts, quantities, or prices on BPOs. Customers can choose to hide completely the Amount field label and value in the BPO header and the Sub-total field label and value in the BPO footer, along with the following related fields, when used: Total Tax, Est. Total Tax, Total Freight, Est. Total Freight, then your customer has, Est. Grant Total. If your customer sends a change order for a BPO containing advanced pricing details, the changes are not highlighted for the line item in the Pricing Details table. The Change column displays Edited for the line item that changed.  Note Service sheets are not supported for blanket purchase orders in SAP Business Network. Legacy Purchase Orders Customers who are transitioning to SAP Business Network frequently have purchase orders that have been fulfilled but not yet invoiced. In that case, your customer might send you a legacy purchase order. Legacy purchase orders appear online in Orders Purchase Orders (or Orders Orders and Releases if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain) and contain the comment, This purchase order has already been fulfilled. You can use a legacy purchase order to create a standard invoice through SAP Business Network. Related Information This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 5 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Order Confirmations Order Routing When a customer sends an order to you through SAP Business Network, you have different options that you can configure for receiving it. You can always view orders on the Orders and Releases Orders Purchase Orders page of your SAP Business Network account (or Orders if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain), even if your account is configured for additional routing methods. You can also route it to an email account or fax machine. If you are using an order fulfillment system that can be integrated with SAP Business Network, you can configure your account to send orders to your order fulfillment system through cXML or EDI. For more information about the different order routing options and how to resolve order routing problems, see Electronic Order Routing in the Document routing guide. Work Order Information Suppliers can view work-order information in certain documents transacted in SAP Business Network. Work-order information originating from the Plant Maintenance component of SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA is displayed in documents transacted on SAP Business Network. The two work-order information fields are WorkOrder ID and Equipment ID. These fields are auto-populated in documents that are displayed on SAP Business Network. The work-order information is derived from purchase orders received into SAP Business Network from the buyers' SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. Certain buying organizations that have SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP as their back-office system use maintenance work orders to procure maintenance and repair services for their plants and machinery. These work orders originate from the Plant Maintenance component in SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP, and describe the materials and services required to fulfill such orders. If one or more items listed in those work orders are not available in the inventory, SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP generates purchase requisitions for those items. Planned-maintenance work orders or ad-hoc maintenance work orders originating from the Plant Maintenance component in SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP can include services or material goods. Planned maintenance work orders are scheduled orders for regular maintenance work, for example, maintenance of machinery. Ad-hoc work orders are 'for the purpose' in nature to perform urgent or unplanned repairs in the plant. Workflow for Adding Work Order Information 1. A work order is created in the Plant Maintenance component of SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP. 2. A purchase order is created in SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP if one or more items in the work order are not available in the inventory. 3. SAP Business Network receives the purchase order cXML document from SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP. The purchase order contains the following information at the line level, under the section Work Order Information: WorkOrder ID Equipment ID This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 6 7/10/26, 2:06 AM 4. A supplier hosted on SAP Business Network logs in to SAP Business Network and creates one or more of the following documents from the purchase order: Invoice Credit memo Debit memo Line-item credit memo Line-item debit memo Service entry sheet Order confirmation Ship notice 5. SAP Business Network displays work-order information fields on the document that is created from the purchase order. The work-order information fields are displayed only if buyers have enabled the Allow supplier to view work order information rule in their SAP Business Network accounts. Scope of Feature After a purchase requisition is approved by authorized personnel, a purchase order is created in SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP. The purchase order cXML document contains work order-related information and is sent from the buyer's SAP S/4HANA or SAP ERP to SAP Business Network. This feature includes the WorkOrder ID and Equipment ID fields in documents transacted in Ariba Network. The following are the transaction documents that display work-order information, for suppliers hosted on SAP Business Network and buyer users: Purchase order Invoice Credit memo Debit memo Line-item credit memo Line-item debit memo Service entry sheet Order confirmation Ship notice Goods receipt note Prerequisite To enable suppliers hosted on SAP Business Network and buyer users to view work-order information fields, buyers need to enable the Allow supplier to view work order information rule in Administration Configuration Default Transaction Rules . To send purchase orders with work-order information to your suppliers, your organization must use one of the following: This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 7 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Your organization uses either of the following SAP Ariba procurement solutions: SAP Ariba Buying with procurement operations desk capability SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing with procurement operations desk capability SAP Business Network is integrated with the buyer’s SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to send purchase orders to suppliers. In this case, buyers need to enable the Integration to support sending work order-based purchase orders to Ariba Network feature on SAP Ariba Cloud Integration Gateway. Typical Purchase Order Life Cycle When you create a customer catalog of your products and services, your customers can issue a purchase order based on your customer catalog. Purchase orders can include catalog or non-catalog items. The following diagram shows the typical life cycle of a catalog-based purchase order on SAP Business Network. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 8 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Details for Orders and Releases This section provides topics describing where and how to view details for purchase orders, scheduling releases, and scheduling agreement releases. Management of Orders and Releases Pages on Which You Can Save Search Filter Preferences Viewing Orders or Releases Viewing Order Attachments Downloading a Custom PDF for an Order Responding to Order Inquiries Tracking Shipments Order Statuses Order View Settings and Options Management of Orders and Releases View your orders and releases regularly to track activity and troubleshoot errors efficiently. You can scroll through the orders and releases on the Orders Purchase Orders page (or Orders Orders and Releases if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain), create custom orders-based workbench tiles, or use the search filters to find specific purchase orders. Additionally, you can customize the way SAP Business Network sorts your search results. Order-Based Workbench Tiles Searching for Orders and Releases Search Filters for Orders and Releases Order-Based Workbench Tiles Create custom order-based workbench tiles to more easily find and take action on your orders. Orders is the most basic tile for users who work with customer orders. Orders-based tiles contain orders and scheduling agreement releases and the list view displays information such as customer, ship to address, and amount. On the workbench, depending on your buyer's transaction rules and your user permissions, you can confirm, ship, and invoice the orders, or create credit memos, line-item credit memos, or line-item debit memos against them. The workbench offers the following order tiles: Orders New orders Changed orders Orders to invoice Orders with service line Items to confirm This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 9 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Items to ship Return items You can filter order tiles on values such as Customers, Order numbers, Creation date, Order status, Company codes, Purchasing organizations, Customer locations, Order type, Routing status, Min amount, Max amount, and Currency. Use the Visibility to search for all orders, hidden orders, or orders that are not hidden. The Show orders with inquiries only checkbox allows you to filter for orders for which you've received customer inquiries. Customer-Specific Attributes Buyers create custom attributes for various customization projects and can extend them to workbench tiles to allow their suppliers to view them as filters and columns. You must configure their workbench tiles to view these customer-specific attributes. You can customize your workbench tile tables to display or group customer-specific columns the same way you do with standard columns. If you work with only a single customer who provides additional columns, they are selected by default. Otherwise, you can choose a customer in the Customize table dialog to manage their columns. Customer-specific filters and columns are only available when you filter for a single customer. If you filter for two or more Customers, any customer-specific filters are removed. Customer-specific attributes can be created by your customers for the following tiles: Orders New Orders Changed Orders Orders to Invoice Orders with service line Items to confirm Items to ship Column Grouping Order-based tiles support column grouping, which allows you to display similar lines together. For example, you can create a column grouping to display all schedule lines under the line item to which they belong. Configure column groupings from the Table setting menu. Related Information The Workbench Workbench Tile Reference Customizing Tiles on Your Workbench Filtering Workbench Tiles Customizing Workbench Columns Searching for Orders and Releases Use this procedure to use search filters on the Purchase Orders page. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 10
