file://SBN/split/Receiving and Fulfillin.content: 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Context If you want to search for one or more purchase orders or releases, you can search by customer name, order number, or date range. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Orders Purchase Orders . Orders and Releases . By default, the page initially shows all orders created in the past 1 year. If you received more than 100 orders in the past 1 year, the search results show only the 100 most recent orders. 2. Click the expand arrow ( ) to open the Search Filters section. 3. Set your search criteria.  Tip If you know the order number, click the Exact number radio button and enter the number in the Order Number field. If you don't know the order number, use the other search filters to refine your search. If you’re searching for orders that are older than 1 year, choose Other for the Date Range field, and then choose a start date and end date. You can either use the calendar icon or enter a date into the Start Date and End Date boxes using a valid date format for your locale, such as 9/1/2016 or 1 Sep 2016. Start and end dates can't be more than 31 days apart. 4. Click Search. 5. Click any column heading in the search results to sort by that column.  6. To change the column display and groupings, click the Table Options Menu icon ( ) at the top of the table and perform any of the following actions: In the Show / Hide Columns section, choose what columns you want to show or hide. Click More if you want to change the display settings for more than one column. In the Group by Column section, choose how you want to group the results. Use the Grouping Expansion section to control your initial display. If you group your results, you can then use the expansion triangle to expand or collapse the display per grouping. In the Export to Excel section, you can export the first page of search results or download all the search results (up to 500 rows of data). To see time information in addition to date information, choose Show Time in the Date Display section. In the Table Size section, choose how many orders and releases to show in the results. 7. If you want to undo your search and start again, do either of the following actions: Click Reset to blank out all search filters except the date range. Repeat step 1 to show the original list of purchase orders and releases. Next Steps After you find the order you're looking for, you can create an order confirmation, send a ship notice, or create a PO-based invoice.  Tip This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 11 7/10/26, 2:06 AM If you want to close an order or release that's no longer active, you can hide it from your view. Click Actions Hide to the right of the document you want to hide. After you hide documents, you can find them by using the View All or View Only hidden orders search filter options. When searching for hidden orders, it's helpful to know either the exact order number or the date on which you received the order. Related Information Search Filters for Orders and Releases Search Filters for Orders and Releases You can refine which records display on the Purchase Orders tab. The following table describes how to use each search filter on the Releases Orders Purchase Orders page (or Orders Orders and if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain) to refine your purchase order and release search results: Filter Description Customer Choose a customer from the list to view purchase orders from that customer. To add another customer to the selection, click Add More to the right of the field, and then select another customer from the list. To remove a selected customer, click the x button to the right of the customer's name. Order Number Search by purchase order number. Purchase order numbers are case-sensitive. For example, PO123 is different from po123. Your customer's purchasing system assigns order numbers.  Note You can specify whether you're searching for a partial or exact order number. When you choose Exact number, all hidden orders with this purchase order number also show up. Buyer Location Code Find all purchase orders with particular location codes. You can enter multiple buyer location codes separated by commas. Your customers can add a location code to purchase orders to help you identify the exact delivery location for an address. Invoice Number Locate a purchase order by its corresponding invoice number. Invoice numbers are case-sensitive. For example, INV123 is different from inv123. Date Range Search by the date the purchase order reached SAP Business Network. You can choose one of the following ranges: Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 14 days, Last 31 days, or Other. Use Other to search for orders that are older than 31 days.  Note If you choose Other, you need to specify the start and end dates. This custom date range is limited to 14 days. Start Date and End Date Search by the date on which SAP Business Network received the order. The maximum date range is 14 days. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 12 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Filter Description Min. Amount and Max. Amount Search by the purchase order's total amount. Don't enter currency symbols. To search above or below a given amount, enter only one amount. To search within a range, enter both amounts. Order Status Search by purchase order document status. View Search for purchase orders by choosing one of the following options: All, All except hidden orders, Only orders with inquiries, or Only hidden orders. Search only blanket purchase Search only for blanket purchase orders (BPOs). A BPO is identified in SAP Business Network by the orders prefix “BPO,” for example BPO123.  Note Customers have the option to hide certain field values on blanket purchase orders (BPOs). Typically, these are amount fields, such as amount available, minimum and maximum amount, price, and quantity. To search for BPOs that have masked values, enter the customer name or exact order number. If you search for purchase orders using the Min. Amount and Max. Amount fields, you won't see orders with masked values in the search results. Search only scheduling Confine the search to scheduling agreement releases. agreement releases Search only service purchase Search only for purchase orders that contain at least one line requiring a service sheet. orders Search only pinned orders Search for purchase orders that you pinned in the SAP Ariba mobile app. Routing Status Search by purchase order routing status. Number of Results Request more than the default number of search results (100). Company code Search using company code search filters and table columns. Purchasing organization Your company is divided into various purchasing organizations that do business with your suppliers. Search using the purchasing organization. Pages on Which You Can Save Search Filter Preferences If your account allows you to save search filter preferences, you can save them on several transaction document pages. The following SAP Business Network supplier portal pages allow users to save search filter preferences: Orders Purchase Orders (or Orders Orders and Releases if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain) Items to Ship Items to Confirm Time & Expense Sheets Early Payments Scheduled Payments Remittances This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 13 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Inquiries Receipts Invoices Order Confirmations Ship Notices Service Sheets Allowing Your Search Filter Preferences to Be Saved Saving and Clearing Search Filter Preferences for a Page Allowing Your Search Filter Preferences to Be Saved Before you can save search filter preferences, you must enable the feature for your account. The feature is not automatically enabled for all users. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon and choose My Account from the dropdown. The My Account page opens. 2. In the Preferences section, check Allow me to save filter preferences in the Inbox/Outbox. 3. Click Save. At the top of the page, SAP Business Network displays a message indicating that your account settings have been successfully updated. 4. Click Close. Related Information Saving and Clearing Search Filter Preferences for a Page Saving and Clearing Search Filter Preferences for a Page You can save search filter preferences for each document type. Your filter preferences are saved in your user account, and only you can use them. Prerequisites Update your account settings to allow you to save filter preferences. See Allowing Your Search Filter Preferences to Be Saved.  Restriction You can save only one set of filter preferences per page. When you save filter preferences, any previously saved filter preferences for that page are overwritten and cannot be retrieved. Procedure This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 14 7/10/26, 2:06 AM 1. Choose a transaction document page that lets you save search filter preferences. See Pages on Which You Can Save Search Filter Preferences. 2. Click the triangle to the left of Search Filters to show the filters. 3. Specify search filters for the page. 4. Click Save Preferences. 5. In the Save Preferences window, enter a nickname (up to 100 characters) for the filter preferences, and then click OK. The preferences nickname appears at the top of the Search Filters section. 6. Click Search to perform a search using the saved filter preferences. 7. If you want to clear your filter preferences, click the Clear Preferences link at the top of the page. A message window appears asking whether you want to clear your preferences. Click Yes. Viewing Orders or Releases Use this procedure to view details and status information for orders, releases, and blanket purchase orders. Context On the Orders Purchase Orders page (or Orders Orders and Releases if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain), each document is identified by a unique number. This number is based on the order number assigned by your customer's procurement application. The available information depends on the purchase order type and your customer's procurement application. Different customers might include different line-item detail fields. For example, if you receive purchase orders for temporary labor, the details might include the contractor name, start date, and end date for the service.  Restriction SAP Business Network doesn't show purchase orders that are larger than 1 MB or that have more than 1,000 line items. SAP Business Network indicates that these purchase orders exceed the maximum limit for on-line display, but it can transmit these purchase orders through email, cXML, and EDI routing. The Amount Invoiced column in the Orders Purchase Orders table and order-based workbench tiles shows order settlement status. It lists how much money you’ve invoiced or charged against the order. Additionally, in the Order Detail and Order History tabs of an order's details page, you can view information about the goods received or returned for each line item. If you have multiple locations with different ordering addresses, you can use the Ordering Address field or column on the Purchase Orders Orders and Items to Confirm pages or workbench tiles to sort and group orders to process them quickly.  Tip When viewing a purchase order, you can use the related documents links to view the documents that are matched to the purchase order, such as order confirmations, ship notices, or invoices. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Orders Purchase Orders Orders and Releases Navigate to an order-based workbench tile. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 15 7/10/26, 2:06 AM 2. Review the order status and routing status information. 3. Review the order fulfillment status icons for a quick indication of the current fulfillment status. Each order and release offers various Actions, which allow you to create order confirmations, ship notices, service entry sheets, or invoices. You can also use this menu to Hide the order or release. 4. Click the order number link to open it.  Note SAP Business Network hides purchase order line-item details and expands item groups by default. The quantity for an item group is always 1, and the price for the item group is the sum of price * quantity for all of its grouped items. Only top-level item groups show quantity and price values; grouped items within an item group don’t show quantity or price. 5. To view line item details, perform one of the following actions: Click Show Item Details above the Line Items section to show details for all individual and grouped line items at once. Use the table options menu icon  to choose which types of information to show or hide. Click the Details link for a specific line item to show only that line item's details.  Note SAP Business Network lists multiple schedule lines for line items having more than one delivery date. 6. To hide item details, perform one of the following actions: Click Hide Item Details above the Line Items section to hide details for all line items. Click the Summary link for a specific line item to hide its details. 7. Click the arrow next to an item group to collapse it and hide its grouped items for a more compact review format. 8. If the order has been changed, you can view the order with or without the changes. By default, a changed order highlights the changes. SAP Business Network indicates these changes using color, styles, and icons. For a monochrome view of the order (print, fax and emails without colors), use the icons and font formats to locate the differences. You can view header-level changes, and newly added, deleted, or updated line items. If desired, click Hide Changes at the top of the page to view the purchase order without the changes. For large purchase orders (purchase orders exceeding 1 MB or more than 1,000 line items), only header changes are shown. No line-item differences are shown. You can also print the purchase order with or without changes. Next Steps When viewing a purchase order, you can create order confirmations, ship notices, service sheets, or invoices. Related Information The Workbench Viewing Order Attachments Use this procedure to view attachments associated with purchase orders. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 16 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Context Orders and order line items with attachments are identified by a paper clip icon next to the order number or order line number. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Orders Purchase Orders . Orders and Releases . Navigate to an order-based workbench tile. 2. Click an order number link to open the order. 3. Do one of the following: For header-level attachments, go to the Attachments area. For line-level attachments, click the Details link within a line item to show its attachments. 4. Click the name of an attachment. 5. Do one of the following: Save the file if you want to send it to someone or review it later. Large files can take several minutes to download. Open the file to view it online. Your web browser starts the process to show the attachment. If your web browser doesn't recognize a file format, it prompts you to save the file.  Note Attachments expire 18 months after SAP Business Network receives them. After they expire, they are no longer available online. If you need attachments that have expired, contact your customer directly. Related Information The Workbench Downloading a Custom PDF for an Order Use this procedure to download custom PDF layouts that your customer defined. Context If your customer has defined custom layouts for orders and assigned them to your SAP Business Network account, you can download a custom PDF for each order. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Orders Purchase Orders . Orders and Releases . Navigate to an order-based workbench tile. 2. Click an order number link to open it. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 17 7/10/26, 2:06 AM 3. At the top of page, click the Download icon. Select the print or download option you want  Note If the Download PDF link doesn't display a dropdown list of layouts, your customer hasn't provided any custom order layouts to you. 4. Your browser downloads a PDF file containing the order. You can open it in a PDF application (for example, Adobe Reader) or save the file to your computer. Related Information The Workbench Responding to Order Inquiries Use this procedure to reply to an order inquiry from your customer. Context An order inquiry provides customers with information that falls outside of an order confirmation or ship notice. After sending you an order, customers can send you order inquiries to ask about the status of a specific order. Order inquiries are tracked with orders so that both you and your customers can keep track of them. The number of inquiries you have received against a specific order is shown in the Inquiries column of the Orders Purchase Orders page or order-based workbench tile. You also receive alerts to let you know when you have received an order inquiry. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Orders Purchase Orders . Orders and Releases . Navigate to an order-based workbench tile. 2. In the Inquiries column, click the number link for the order that has an inquiry to which you want to respond. The Inquiry Detail page opens. 3. Click Reply. 4. Do one of the following: To reply to an inquiry about the order as a whole, enter your reply in the Comments field at the header level. To reply to inquiries about specific line items, enter your replies in the Comments fields for the respective line items.  Note In cases where your customer has not allowed line-item-level responses, the order inquiry message that appears on the Inquiry Detail tab states that your customer requires an order confirmation as reply. 5. Click Next. 6. Review your comments, then click Submit. Related Information The Workbench This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 18 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Tracking Shipments Use this procedure to track shipments that have a tracking number. Context You can track the progress of a shipment with the Purchase order tracking page. This page consolidates all relevant information about a purchase order's status, history, and execution.  Restriction The Purchase order tracking page supports only shipments for material purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and scheduling agreement releases. The feature does not support service orders or orders that have a mix of material and service items. If you know the purchase order number for the shipment you want to track, you can use the Home Shipment tracking widget to go directly to the Purchase order tracking page for that order. In the widget, enter the desired purchase order number and press Track. Alternatively, you can go to the purchase order’s details page and click Track Order. Procedure 1. Search for the purchase order whose shipment you want to track. If you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, go to Orders If you are not enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, go to Orders and Releases . Orders Purchase Orders . 2. Click the link in the Order Number column for the desired purchase order. The purchase order details page opens. 3. In the Order Detail tab, click the desired ship notice number in the Related Documents field. The ship notice details page opens. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 19 7/10/26, 2:06 AM 4. Click the Track Ship Notice button in the Ship Notice Tracking section. SAP Business Network opens the carrier’s Web site, where you can review information about your shipment. 5. On the Purchase order tracking page, click the Track Order button. The Purchase order tracking page opens, showing information about the shipping progress of your order. 6. To return to the purchase order details page, click the purchase order number at the top left of the Purchase order tracking page. Results The Purchase order tracking page includes the following sections: A milestones timeline – A timeline of the 10 most recent event milestones and their dates, from order creation through invoicing. The milestones that show depend on the type of document being created. For example, when a ship notice is generated, the milestone is either Partially shipped or Shipped.  Note There is no milestone to track return shipments. Also, if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, there are no milestones to track component shipment, component receipt, or component consumption of subcontracting orders. You can set the milestone filters for the number of milestones and the types of documents you want to see. When a milestone has previous documents of the same type, it shows a View history dropdown that shows up to 10 of the most recent versions of the document. For each previous document, the dropdown shows its status, date and time, and an active link. Tracking information section – This section contains a table of ship notices. In the Actions column, you can select the … icon and choose View detail to go to that ship notice's details page. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 20

file://SBN/split/Receiving and Fulfillin.title: Receiving and Fulfilling Orders_Part3
file://SBN/split/Receiving and Fulfillin.content: 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Related Information Order Status Order Statuses This topic describes the possible routing, processing, and settlement statuses for purchase orders and service orders. Routing Status Routing Status indicates whether a purchase order or service order is queued, sent, acknowledged, or if routing failed. SAP Business Network displays the following routing statuses for orders: Routing Status Definition Queued Initial state. SAP Business Network received the order but no further action was taken. Sent SAP Business Network sent the order to your account. Acknowledged You received the order. Failed SAP Business Network experienced a problem routing the order to your preferred order routing method. For example, your back end order fulfillment system could have experienced a problem that prevented SAP Business Network from successfully routing the order. You can resend orders that have a Failed routing status. Order Status Order Status indicates where the order stands in regard to your processing of the order. SAP Business Network displays the following statuses for orders and releases: Order Status Definition New Initial state. You have not updated the order status. Changed Your customer canceled or replaced the order by a sending a subsequent (changed) order. Confirmed You agreed to ship all line items. Confirmed With New Date The order confirmation has a different Start Date or End Date than the order, but no other change. Confirmed With Changes The order confirmation has a different Expected Value than the order, and also has a different Start Date, End Date, or both. Partially Confirmed The order is in progress. Partially Shipped If you update part of a purchase order, SAP Business Network reports the partial status for the Partially Serviced Partially Invoiced entire purchase order. For example, if you partially confirmed an order and then you partially ship either the previously confirmed order line or a different order line, the purchase order status is set to Partially Shipped. You can still continue to confirm order line items regardless of the shipping status until you have confirmed all order lines. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 21 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Order Status Definition Partially Rejected For service orders, you can continue to create service sheets for unplanned service lines up to their hidden maximum amounts (which might be larger than their subtotals) or planned service lines up to their subtotals. The service order status is set to Partially Serviced until all of the service lines are serviced. Serviced The order is fully serviced. You cannot create any more service sheets for any more service lines in the order. Shipped Final state. You shipped the entire order. Invoiced The order is fully invoiced. The Amount Invoiced column shows how much money you have invoiced or charged against the purchase order. For older purchase orders, SAP Business Network displays Yes to indicating that you have submitted invoices. Received Statuses for receipts that are sent by the buyer from their ERP system. The purchase order status is updated based on this information. On the Order Detail page, each line item-detail Partially Received section displays the quantity of goods received or returned for that line item, based on the Returned information in the receipts. Failed SAP Business Network experienced a problem routing the order to your account. You can resend failed orders. Settlement Statuses Settlement status indicates how you can settle payment for an order you fulfilled. The Settlement column shows whether you need to create an invoice or charge a purchasing card (PCard) for a given order: Settlement Description Invoice Create an invoice to settle the order. PCard Charge a PCard through your own charging system. The Amount Invoiced column shows how much money you have invoiced or charged against the order. Order View Settings and Options Some order information shows up based on customer language and currency settings. Other information depends on how you set up your customer catalogs and what viewing permissions you have. Language and Currency Your customers determine the language of the purchase order content, such as line item descriptions or comments. SAP Business Network doesn't perform currency conversion for purchase orders. All monetary amounts show up in the currencies chosen by your customers. Your customers’ choices of language do not affect purchase order section titles, messages, tool tips, hint text, and field labels in the SAP Business Network interface. Those are controlled by the language you configured for your web browser. If your web browser is configured for a language that isn't supported by SAP Business Network, you'll see everything in English. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 22 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Credit Card Numbers SAP Business Network masks credit card numbers in purchase orders sent by email or fax. For increased security, SAP Business Network masks card numbers by printing only the last four digits of credit card and PCard numbers in fax and email purchase orders. To view the full credit card account number, you can either click the link in the email or sign in to your SAP Business Network account and go to your Inbox.  Note You need to have the Credit Card Number Access permission to view complete credit card numbers. SAP Business Network always passes full credit card and PCard numbers when sending purchase orders through cXML or EDI. Advanced Pricing Details Suppliers can provide advanced pricing details for items in their customer catalogs. When you include advanced pricing details for items in a customer catalog you provide to your customers, your customers can send you purchase orders that include these items. When viewing a purchase order, the Pricing Details table shows the Price Details and Unit Details sections for a line item. You can view the Unit Details section only when the unit of measure for the ordered item differs from the unit of measure for the price unit quantity specified or if the pricing is based on a different price unit quantity than 1. The advanced pricing details are also available when printing the purchase orders. If you receive a change order for a blanket purchase order, the changes are not highlighted for the line item in the Pricing Details table. The Change column shows Edited for the line item that was changed.  Note SAP Business Network doesn't support advanced pricing details on contract documents. Expected Value and Overall Limit for Unplanned Line Items Customers can pass expected value and overall-limit values for unplanned line items by using extrinsics. Order Confirmation Deviations and Tolerances A buyer might include tolerances when creating a purchase order, a scheduling agreement, or a scheduling agreement release. For purchase orders, buyers can include tolerances for delivery date, quantity, and price. For scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases, buyers can include tolerances for delivery date and quantity.  Note Price deviations are not possible for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases because the unit price cannot be changed in SAP Business Network for these documents. Buyers must set one or both of the following rules to activate the order confirmation deviation approval process: Purchase orders: Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval. Scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases: Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases and its subrule Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval. The buyer can also check the Except quantity deviations or the Except delivery date deviations subrule to further specify which deviations the rule applies to. If you submit an order confirmation that is out of any tolerance set by the buyer, the buyer can decide whether to approve or reject the deviation. SAP Business Network validates date and quantity both at the header level and the line-item level for purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and scheduling agreement releases. For purchase orders, SAP Business Network also validates price deviations. For example, a delivery-date tolerance is the maximum number of days the actual delivery can differ from the delivery date requested on an order. If you provide a delivery date for the entire order that is out of tolerance, an error message informs you to provide delivery dates at the line-item level instead. When an item has confirmation deviations, an alert icon appears to the left of the item on the Confirming PO page before you submit the confirmation. The alert icon also appears on the submitted confirmation. When you click the alert icon, a popup window displays with the message: The order confirmation for this item needs buyer approval. When you submit an order confirmation with deviations, SAP Business Network automatically generates an approval request and attaches the confirmation to the approval request. You can reconfirm items that are still awaiting approval. When an item’s approval status is not Approved, the system does not allow you to ship or invoice the item. If an order has at least one item with the approval status Approved awaiting change order, you cannot create an order confirmation for it. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 31 7/10/26, 2:06 AM The copy of the approval request is always routed to the copy supplier. Related Information Order Confirmation Approval Requests Unit Price Tolerance for Order Confirmations SAP Business Network enforces unit price tolerances (over and under) specified by control keys in an order when you submit an order confirmation. By specifying control keys in an order, customers can define different upper and lower unit price tolerances per order. You can’t specify a unit price outside of the order’s unit price tolerances. This gives buyers more control over price deviations from the original order. Unit price tolerances specified through control keys also apply to quantity-based pricing. When you change unit conversion or price unit quantity, SAP Business Network validates the unit price tolerance based on the new calculated price. Confirmation control keys in an order always take precedence over business rules. Therefore, an upper unit price tolerance specified by a control key in the order overrides the upper unit price tolerance specified by the rule Apply line item unit price tolerance to order confirmations.  Note Unit price tolerances don’t apply to items with an undisclosed price. In that case, unit price tolerances are ignored. Related Information The Workbench The Items to Confirm List As a supplier, the Items to Confirm list feature enables you to confirm incoming purchase orders efficiently across multiple customers.  Note Planned lean-service items, unplanned lean-service items, and unplanned material items are not supported to be confirmed from the items to confirm list. See Service Order Confirmations for more information. In the order collaboration process for direct materials, suppliers typically strive to establish long-term, repeat business with their customers. From the supplier perspective, a successful business model involves a continual flow of incoming purchase orders from a number of buying customers. The supplier must efficiently process these incoming purchase orders: confirm line items when confirmation is required, create ship notices, and ship goods. Also, the supplier must process purchase orders that have been changed. Further, the supplier must not confirm orders for quantities or delivery dates that are not achievable. Therefore, the process of confirming orders quickly and correctly can be challenging because of the volume of data and the level of detail required. The Orders Orders and Releases Items to Confirm list displays a list of purchase orders that includes information critical for you to confirm many order details accurately and simultaneously.  Note Some functionality of the Items to Confirm list is changed if a purchase order has temporary unit prices. See Temporary Unit Prices for more information. Reconfirmed Items The View dropdown in the Items to confirm tile has two views: Items to be confirmed (default) and Confirmed items for editing. The Confirmed items for editing view contains a Reconfirmed Items section that shows all line items that are eligible to reconfirm. By default, this view shows all confirmed and partially confirmed items. This view also puts into edit mode all line-item fields that were editable when their order confirmation was created. Suppliers can use the Confirmation status filter to choose which confirmation status types to exclude. Filter choices in the Confirmed items for editing view are Exclude confirmation not allowed and Exclude unconfirmed. The default for both filters is Yes, Suppliers can reconfirm any line item that has status Backordered, Confirmed, Rejected, or Unconfirmed. To do this, the supplier chooses the desired line items, then from the Confirm dropdown chooses one of the following options: Confirm entire order This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 39 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Confirm entire item Confirm schedule line In the same operation, suppliers can confirm multiple line items that may have different statuses. If a supplier reduces the quantity of an item before sending it for reconfirmation, the confirmation status changes as follows: The reduced quantity becomes Confirmed. The remaining quantity becomes Unconfirmed. For example, suppose that an item has a Confirmed quantity of 100. If the supplier changes the confirmed quantity to 90, the reconfirmed item quantity becomes 90 Confirmed and 10 Unconfirmed. Items that are submitted for reconfirmation are validated again. Search for purchase-order line items. 2. View purchase-order line items, with the default sort showing the items that should be confirmed first. 3. Confirm purchase orders in one of the following ways: Confirm one or more entire purchase orders at the header level. Confirm or reject single purchase-order line items, or modify quantities before confirming a line item, using the Update Line Item option. Confirm or reject multiple purchase-order line items, including line items from different purchase orders. Items to Confirm Workbench Tiles Create custom Items to confirm workbench tiles to more easily find and take action on your orders. The Items to confirm tile contains all material orders and scheduling agreement releases that can be confirmed. The Items to confirm list view displays information such as customer, item number, and need-by date. On the workbench, depending on your customer's transaction rules, you can confirm or reject the orders and create quality notifications. Items to confirm tiles allow you to filter by the following values: Customers, Order numbers, Customer locations, Need by date, Ship by date, Creation date, Company codes, Purchasing organizations, Purchasing groups, Ordering address IDs, Part numbers, Customer part numbers, Product group, Planner codes, Order type, Category, Stock transfer type, Ship from location, Supplier batch ID, Confirmation approval status, Confirmation status, Shipping status, Receiving status Invoicing status, and External document type. Tax Cost are hidden when the following conditions exist: The default transaction rule Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the line-item level is enabled. Check the checkbox for the line item, and click Confirm Requested Quantities. Order Confirmation Troubleshooting Following are some examples of possible issues with order confirmations. Example 1: The buyer creates a purchase order with two line items and sends it to the supplier. 1. The supplier creates an order confirmation with confirmID OC-A01 for line item 1 (operation type is new). 2. The supplier creates an order confirmation with confirmID OC-B01 for line item 2 (operation type is new). 3. The supplier creates an order confirmation with confirmID OC-A01 for line items 1 and 2 (operation type is update). This order confirmation is rejected. An error message displays to let the supplier know they cannot send a new order confirmation for a line item that was already confirmed. Example 2: Supplier sends a new order confirmation for a previously confirmed line item. 1. The buyer creates a purchase order with two line items and sends it to the supplier. 2. The supplier creates an order confirmation with confirmID OC-A01 for line item 1 (operation type is new). 3. The supplier creates an order confirmation with confirmID OC-B01 for line item 2 (operation type is new). 4. The supplier creates an order confirmation with confirmID OC-C01 for line items 1 and 2 (operation type is new). This order confirmation is rejected. An error message displays to let the supplier know they cannot send a new order confirmation for a line item that was already confirmed. Ship Notices for Customers This section provides topics describing how to create, edit, and send ship notices to customers. Ship Notices Draft Ship Notices Ship Notice Updates Creating and Ship Notice Creating a Ship Notice from a Scheduling Agreement Release Creating a Ship Notice from Several Orders and Releases Creating a Ship Notice with One Ship-to Address for All Items Uploading Serial Numbers for Ship Notices Ship Notice Barcode Labels Purchase Order Priority Reporting Creating a Draft Ship Notice Editing a Draft Ship Notice Editing a Submitted Ship Notice Cancelation of Submitted Ship Notices This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 45 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Ship Notices You can generate ship notices manually or send them automatically from your external order management system to SAP Business Network though cXML or EDI. When you create a ship notice, SAP Business Network applies the information to the affected line items and sends the information to your customers. You can review ship notices that you submitted on the Fulfillment Ship Notices page. Whether you can send ship notices to your customers depends on your customers' settings for default transaction rules, also called business rules. For information about these rules and how suppliers can view the rules set by a customer, see Default Transaction Rules. Your customers can: Prevent you from sending ship notices altogether. SAP Business Network disables the Create Ship Notice option. Prevent you from including attachments with ship notices. Prevent you from sending ship notices that contain items with different delivery dates and times. Restrict the kinds of files you can provide as attachments to ship notices. You can view the file extensions that your buyer allows or disallows in the Attachment File Extension Rules section of their Customer Details page. Allow you to create ship notices at the line-item level. If so, you create ship notices for individual items within an item group rather than for the entire item group as a unit. Allow you to ship partial orders when you create ship notices at the line-item level. Allow you to include terms of delivery on ship notices even when the customer's purchase order does not provide this information. If the customer provides terms of delivery, you can change this information on your ship notice. Allow you to add terms of delivery fields at either header or line-item levels. Allow you to include transport information on ship notices even when the customer’s purchase order does not provide this information. You can add transport information and additional fields only at the header level. If the customer provides transport information, you can change this information on your ship notice. Allow you to enter the actual shipping or estimated shipping date in your ship notices.  Note If a customer sends you a blanket purchase order (BPO) with masked values for certain fields (for example, amountrelated fields, price, or quantity), the value for the masked fields is set to Undisclosed on the BPO. You can't create ship notices for BPOs with undisclosed fields. Even if you set the shipping status through cXML or EDI, you can update the shipping status manually on SAP Business Network using the Create Ship Notice button for that order. If you change the order shipping status manually for these orders, make sure that you keep your external order management system updated with the order information stored on SAP Business Network.  Note Suppliers can create ship notices against the material line items of a purchase order containing both material and service line items, if the related default transaction rule Allow suppliers to send ship notices to this account is enabled to allow suppliers create ship notices. However, the buyer can use purchase order control keys at a line item level to override the default transaction invoice rule. Service order control keys take precedence over invoice rules. If a customer has uploaded their own unit of measure data, you can search for units of measure for packaging dimensions on a ship notice. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 46 7/10/26, 2:06 AM  Note Ensure that all units of measure (UOMs) in the ship notice are valid. When a ship notice is submitted, SAP Business Network validates the UOMs against the master list of UOMs that the buyer uploaded. If no master list is uploaded, SAP Business Network validates UOMs against the standard UN/CEFACT list. If the ship notice contains an invalid UOM, it fails submission. If your customer allows it, you can attach files to ship notices to provide more explanation or supporting information. Attachments can be in any format allowed by your customer, such as Word documents, fax images, or Excel spreadsheets. Observe the following rules for file attachments:  Note By default, the cumulative size of attachments associated with a document cannot exceed 10 MB. Customers can request to change that limit, which can be changed from 10 MB to 100 MB. During file upload, attachment files are converted to plain ASCII text using base64 encoding. This conversion increases the file size by approximately 35%. Therefore, the actual file size limit is 65% of the configured maximum limit. For example, if the maximum allowed limit is set to 10 MB (10000 KB), the actual total attachment file size that users can add is 6500 KB. SAP Business Network stores attachments for a maximum period of eighteen months, after which the attachments expire and are no longer available online. Items to Ship Workbench Tiles Items to Ship Workbench Tiles Filters for the Items to ship workbench tile help you more easily create online ship notices. The Items to ship tile contains all material orders and scheduling agreement releases that can be shipped, allowing you to view all items from orders and agreements with the status New, Changed, or Confirmed, and take action on them. Depending on your customer's transaction rules, you can create quality notifications for each line item and schedule line, and create ship notices for one or more line items and schedule lines. In addition, as a supplier you can download a PDF version of a draft ship notice if the download PDF functionality has been configured for them by the buyer. Draft ship notices can be edited, deleted, or submitted. SAP Business Network automatically deletes draft ship notices 60 days after it was last edited. If the draft is edited and saved again during this time period, the time limit resets to 60 days from the most recent edit session. If a draft new or revised ship notice is in Composing status while a change order is made against the related order document, the ship notice status doesn’t change. You can continue to edit the draft with no loss of data.  Note Draft ship notices are not considered in balance tracking or for validations, such as the ability to invoice up to shipped quantity. Related Information Creating a Draft Ship Notice Editing a Draft Ship Notice Ship Notice Barcode Labels Ship Notice Updates Suppliers can edit a ship notice that is already created. After a ship notice update is submitted, the status of the original ship notice is changed to Obsoleted. The global individual asset IDs in the original ship notice can optionally be used again in the ship notice update. Observe the following guidelines and restrictions: A ship notice must be edited using the same system it was created in. A ship notice created in the supplier ERP system must be edited only in the supplier ERP system. And a ship notice created with the SAP Business Network user interface can be edited only in SAP Business Network. A ship notice update must use the same Packing Slip ID as the ship notice it is updating. A ship notice cannot be edited when: The transaction rule Require references to ship notices on invoices is enabled and the ship notice has lines referenced by an invoice. The ship notice is canceled. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 48 7/10/26, 2:06 AM The ship notice is a component ship notice. A purchase order with line items in the ship notice has the ASNInstruction control key set to notAllowed. A ship notice with a goods receipt can be edited if the following items are both true: Its goods receipt is fully reversed on the buyer's system. It does not have any other related goods receipts. Related Information Editing a Submitted Ship Notice Creating and Ship Notice Use this procedure to create a standard ship notice. Context Ship notices keep your customers informed about when they can expect to receive the items they ordered from your company. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Purchase Orders , choose the number of the order you plan to ship, then choose Create Ship Notice at the top of the purchase order. For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Orders and Releases , choose the number of the order you plan to ship, then choose Create Ship Notice at the top of the purchase order. Navigate to an order-based workbench tile, then choose Create ship notice from the Actions column of the order you plan to ship. 2. In the Ship Notice Header section, enter the information for this shipment. Observe the following requirements: At minimum, provide a Packing Slip ID, Tracking No., and the address where you’re shipping from. If you’re providing transport terms and the transaction rule Require all items in a ship notice to have the same transport terms value is enabled, all line items of a ship notice must use the same transport term. 3. Optional: To help you identify and search for documents you send out, add an internal reference code in the Supplier Reference field. This code can take any form. For example, it might be a number or the name of a person who is dealing with that order. 4. In the Item section, do one of the following: For each line item, enter in the Ship Qty field the number of that item that is included in this shipment. To indicate that none of a particular item is included in this shipment, click the Remove link to the right of that line item. This link removes the item from the current ship notice, but not from the source purchase order. The item remains available for future ship notices.  Note This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 49 7/10/26, 2:06 AM If the order contains advanced pricing details, SAP Business Network shows the pricing details for the line items when you create ship notices. If the customer flagged an item on the order as completed, the following warning appears for the item: The buyer has marked this as Completed. This warning doesn’t prevent you from submitting the ship notice. 5. Optional: Enter into the Batch ID field the ID number for the batch in which each item was made. 6. If you need to add shipping information on line item level, click Details for the line item to show the Create Ship Notice Shipping Details page. 7. To enter hazardous materials instructions, enter a description of the hazardous materials to be shipped, select a hazardous materials code system from the Code Type menu, and enter the code. 8. To change the terms of delivery, enter the necessary information in the Delivery Information section. 9. To enter serial numbers or asset information, enter the item’s serial number or asset tag and click Add. Repeat as necessary to add more serial numbers or asset tags. 10. Click Next. The ship-notice review page opens. 11. Confirm the information on the review page. To make changes, click Previous. 12. Click Submit. SAP Business Network sends the ship notice to your customer and returns you to your Inbox. Next Steps After you create a ship notice, you can: Review copies of ship notices you’ve sent on the Fulfillment Ship Notices page. Review order status information: For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, go to Orders Purchase Orders , and check the Order Status column. For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, go to Orders Orders and Releases , and check the Order Status column. Create invoices against the order. If the ship notice contains an invalid UOM, it fails submission. The following table lists default fields available when creating ship notices. Field Description Ship From and Deliver To Contact Person This field appears for the Ship From and Deliver To sections only and shows up only when imported from cXML. Shipping Packing Slip ID The packing slip number from your shipping system or carrier. Invoice No. The associated invoice number. Requested Delivery Date Delivery date requested by the buyer. Ship Notice Type Choose a value: Actual: Lets you specify the Actual Shipping Date and Actual Delivery Date. Estimated: Lets you specify the Estimated Shipping Date and Estimated Delivery Date. Actual Shipping Date/Estimated Actual or estimated date the goods shipped. Shipping Date Actual Delivery Date/Estimated Actual or estimated date for delivery of goods. Delivery Date Hazard Type Select one of the following classifications of dangerous goods: Unitied Nations Dangerous Goods International Marine Organization Dangerous Goods North American Hazardous Goods Code Enter the appropriate hazard code for the item. Is Divisible Check this option for any cargo that can be separated into units of legal weight without affecting the physical integrity of the load. Dimensions Gross Volume/Unit Total cubic volume of a shipment of goods. Gross Weight/Unit Total weight of a shipment of goods. Includes their packaging, such as crates, pallets, and so on. Total Length/Unit Total length of a shipment of goods. Total Width/Unit Total width of a shipment of goods. Total Height/Unit Total height of a shipment of goods. Tracking Carrier Name Choose a carrier from the list. If your carrier isn't listed, choose Other and enter a name in the text box. If you choose a carrier, complete the additional fields. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 51 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Field Description Tracking No. Only available when you choose a carrier. The tracking number provided by your carrier. Tracking Date Only available when you choose a carrier. The tracking date provided by your carrier. Bill of Lading No. Bill of lading number provided by your carrier. It may be identical to the tracking number. This field appears for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain suppliers only. Shipping Method Only available when you choose a carrier. The shipping method, for example, air, motor, rail, or ship. Or, click Save to save it as a draft, to finish and send within the next 60 days. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 58 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Ship Notice Barcode Labels To facilitate the shipping of goods, SAP Business Network allows suppliers to download barcode labels directly from a ship notice in PDF format. Ship notice barcode labels help buyers and suppliers to accelerate their logistics processes. They can use barcode scanners to quickly scan the barcodes for shipment information for their systems. Barcode label layouts can be applied at the header and the item level of the ship notice, giving suppliers the ability to print a single set of labels containing all the items of a ship notice or a label containing the information for a single line item. The specific fields needed on ship notice barcode labels can vary per customer. Barcode Label Scenarios for Different Industries This feature flexibly supports different industry scenarios for ship notice barcode labels. For instance, suppliers in the automotive industry may need to generate one barcode label per item, a master barcode label for a grouping of items in a pallet, or a mixed barcode label for a grouping of a set of mixed items in a pallet. At the same time, suppliers in the food industry may require a single barcode label per shipping container. All of these scenarios can be supported by designing and configuring multiple barcode label layouts. Barcode Label Scenarios: Automotive Industry Barcode Label Scenario: Food Industry This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 59 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Supported Barcode Types SAP Business Network uses Barcode4J 2.1 to generate barcodes. The Barcode4J library supports the following 1D and 2D barcode types: Interleaved 2 of 5 ITF-14 Code 39 Code 128 EAN-128, GS1-128 (based on Code 128) Codabar UPC-A and UPC-E (with supplementals) EAN-13 and EAN-8 (with supplementals) POSTNET Royal Mail Customer Barcode (Four State) USPS Intelligent Mail (4-State Customer Barcode) PDF 417 (ISO/IEC 15438:2001(E)) DataMatrix (ISO/IEC 16022:2000(E)) For more information about Barcode4J, go to http://barcode4j.sourceforge.net/ . Purchase Order Priority Reporting You can use the Items to Ship tab to help you prioritize shipments and inventory. Suppliers often want to know when the inventories of their buyers start to fall below target levels. When this occurs, suppliers can raise the priority of the related purchase orders to prevent inventory shortages. On the Ship tab (or Orders Orders and Releases Items to Ship Orders Purchase Orders Items to if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain), you can filter and sort items by shipment priority and other criteria. The Inventory Level field in the Items to Ship table shows the current level of the inventory compared, as a percentage, with the target inventory. Editing a Submitted Ship Notice Use this procedure to edit a ship notice after you send it. Prerequisites The ship notice was created using SAP Business Network. The transaction rule Allow suppliers to edit existing ship notices is enabled. You have verified that the ship notice can be edited. Refer to Ship Notice Updates. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Ship Notices . 2. Click the ship notice you want to edit. The ship notice details page opens. 3. Click Edit. 4. In the Edit Ship Notice page, enter the corrected information.  Note The Packing Slip ID must be the same as in the original ship notice. 5. Click Save. The Review Ship Notice page opens. 6. Cancelation of Submitted Ship Notices In certain circumstances, you can cancel a ship notice that you've submitted. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 65 7/10/26, 2:06 AM If permitted by the buyer in their business rules configuration, a supplier can cancel a submitted ship notice for business or technical reasons, where the goods were not yet fully received. This applies to all ship notices, including those that were created without reference to a purchase order (non-PO ship notices). Additionally, a supplier can cancel a ship notice if its goods receipt is fully reversed on the buyer's system and it does not have any other related goods receipts. A ship notice can be canceled from the supplier user interface, by using the Cancel button at the top of the ship notice details page, or through cXML. For information about canceling ship notices through cXML, see the cXML Solutions Guide. When a ship notice is canceled, its status is updated to Canceled. The canceled ship notice is retained as part of the document history associated with the purchase order for which the ship notice was created originally. A message is displayed on the canceled ship notice to indicate that it was canceled, and SAP Business Network sends an email notification of the canceled ship notice to the buyer. The supplier can create a new ship notice for the purchase order. The earlier version of the component ship notice (CSN) can be deleted now. When a canceled component ship notice is received in the SAP Business Network, the earlier version of component ship notice is deleted and the text Canceled Component Ship Notice is displayed in the component ship notice. Whenever there is a need to change or cancel the CSN, the buyer triggers a CSN from ERP with the relevant operation (update / delete). Once the new CSN is received in SAP Business Network with operation value, the old CSN is deleted. Once the component receipt is created for a CSN, the component ship notice cannot be cancelled unless the component receipt is reversed.  Note A draft ship notice cannot be canceled. Upon cancellation of a ship notice, SAP Business Network does not consider the quantities of the ‘canceled’ ship notice in any validations, such as the ability for the supplier to invoice only up to the shipped quantity. Prerequisites You can cancel a ship notice that has the Sent status only if your customer’s business rules allow you to cancel ship notices. You must have the Inbox and Order Access and Outbox Access user permissions to be able to create and manage ship notices. Restrictions A ship notice cancellation is a transaction that can be executed only at header level; individual line items cannot be canceled. The CSV upload for ship notice does not support the option to cancel a previously created ship notice. It is not possible to cancel a ship notice where line items are associated with an invoice. Context Suppliers and buyers often collaborate in the creation of invoices for direct-material orders. This collaboration requires the exchange of information specific to direct material orders. This feature facilitates the invoice collaboration process by allowing more detailed description of materials being procured. This feature also allows the supplier to perform invoice collaboration through the SAP Business Network user interface. This is particularly helpful for suppliers that do not have EDI, cXML, or other integrated business-to-business mechanisms in place. Direct material suppliers can view direct material fields and can enter data into many of them directly in the SAP Business Network user interface. The direct material fields appear in purchase orders, ship notices, invoices, and goods receipt notifications for direct material suppliers.  Note Direct material includes all items, such as raw materials and parts, required to assemble or manufacture a complete product. Direct Material Fields for Purchase Orders Direct material fields appear in purchase orders to facilitate purchase order collaboration between buyers and suppliers. Purchase Order Header Suppliers and buyers often collaborate in the creation of purchase orders for direct-material orders. This collaboration requires the exchange of information specific to direct material orders. This feature facilitates the purchase order collaboration process by allowing more detailed description of materials being procured. This feature also allows the supplier to perform order collaboration through the SAP Business Network user interface. This is particularly helpful for suppliers that do not have EDI, cXML, or other integrated business-to-business mechanisms in place.  Note Direct material includes all items, such as raw materials and parts, required to assemble or manufacture a complete product. The purchase order header displays shipping data, and purchase order line items display retail details and product details. The following section and fields appear in the purchase order header. Shipping Dates section Requested Delivery Earliest Delivery Latest Delivery Goods Pick Up Contact Information This section may include any number of fields of contact information, such as fields labeled manager, accountStatus, or accountID. However, SAP Business Network automatically formats the field label for a contact person to Contact Person. Purchase Order Line Items The following section and fields appear in the purchase order line items: Retail Details section Promotion Deal ID Promotion Variant ID This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 69 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Product EAN/UPC European Waste Catalog ID Product Details section This section may include any number of fields of product details, such as fields labeled weight, style, or volume. However, SAP Business Network automatically formats the field labels for eight common characteristics, as follows: Size Size Code Quality Quality Code Grade Grade Code Color Color Code Customer Part #, Revision Level, and Customer Location Fields The Customer Part #, Revision Level, and Customer Location fields appear as table column headers in the following locations, starting from an open purchase order: Order Details Create Order Confirmation > Update Line Items > Update Item Status Create Order Confirmation > Confirm Entire Order > Confirm Entire Order Create Order Confirmation > Confirm Entire Order > Review Order Confirmation Order History Create Ship Notice, in the Order Items area of the summary page.
