file://SBN/split/Receiving and Fulfillin.content: 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Use this procedure to create ship notices from scheduling agreement releases, for more efficient shipments. Context Buyers can periodically communicate releases to their suppliers; and suppliers can create ship notices for materials requested through scheduling agreement releases. From the Items to Ship tab, a supplier can create a single ship notice containing items from several purchase orders that all are due by the same date.  Note Direct material includes all items, such as raw materials and parts, required to assemble or manufacture a complete product. Scheduling agreement releases are included in the list of documents on the Orders and Releases Orders Purchase Orders page (or Orders if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain). Suppliers can create ship notices from scheduling agreement releases. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Purchase Orders for Supply Chain). (or Orders Orders and Releases if you are enabled for SAP Business Network 2. Expand Search Filters and check Search only scheduling agreement releases or scheduling agreements. 3. Click the order number of a scheduling agreement release to open it. 4. Click Create Ship Notice. 5. Select an item to include in the ship notice, click Next, and fill in required fields in the Create Ship Notice page. 6. For each line in the list of purchase order items, enter the number of items to ship in Ship Qty. 7. To add retail details or asset details to the line, click Add Details, enter the information, and click OK. 8. To add a line to the ship notice, click Add Ship Notice Line. 9. When done adding lines, click Next. Confirm the information in the document, then click Submit. 10. Click Done. Viewing Details for Previous Scheduling Agreement Releases Use this procedure to view previous scheduling agreement releases. Context A scheduling agreement release defines the quantities and dates for the shipments desired for a specific item. For detailed tracking of previous shipments, view the details of previous releases.Scheduling agreement releases appear in the list of documents on the Orders Purchase Orders page (or Orders Orders and Releases if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain).  Note Direct material includes all items, such as raw materials and parts, required to assemble or manufacture a complete product. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Purchase Orders (or for Supply Chain). Orders Orders and Releases This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. if you are enabled for SAP Business Network 71 7/10/26, 2:06 AM 2. Expand Search Filters and check Search only scheduling agreement releases or scheduling agreements. 3. Click the order number of a scheduling agreement release to open it. 4. Click the Previous Releases tab. 5. To view additional details, click Show Release Detail. Searching on Customer Part Number or Customer Location Use this procedure to search for a specific purchase order or scheduling agreement release by customer part number or customer location. Context  Note A search by either of these fields will only return purchase orders and scheduling agreement releases that contain a value for the search field. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Purchase Orders for Supply Chain). (or Orders Orders and Releases if you are enabled for SAP Business Network 2. Click the Items to Ship tab. 3. If the search filters are not visible, click the arrow icon to view the Search Filters area. 4. In the Customer Part # or Customer Location field, type the first letters in an order or release name to return all documents whose names start with those letters. You can enter multiple search terms separated by commas. For example, type C, D in the Customer Location field to return all orders and releases where the customer location begins with C, c, D, or d. 5. To search for a customer location, click Lookup to display the Customer Location window. a. Type a value in the Plant Location / Description or Storage Location field and click Search. b. Check the box for a customer location and click Select. Customer Part Number, Release Level, and Customer Location Fields Suppliers can find customer part number and location information in multiple parts of an open scheduling agreement release. The Customer Part #, Revision Level, and Customer Location fields appear as table column headers in the following locations, from an open scheduling agreement release: Release Detail Processing History Release History Create Ship Notice > Add Details (for a line item) Create Ship Notice, in the Order Items area of the summary page. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 72 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Related Information Searching on Customer Part Number or Customer Location Sending Service Sheets to Customers This section provides topics describing what service sheets are, how to create and edit them, and how to view attachments included with status update requests. Service Sheets Contract and Ad Hoc Limits in Service Sheets Creating a Service Sheet Editing and Resubmitting a Failed or Rejected Service Sheet Downloading a Service Sheet PDF Viewing Status Update Request Attachments Searching for a Unit of Measure on a Service Sheet Service Sheet Statuses Service Sheets A service sheet (sometimes called a “service-entry sheet”) describes one or more line items you fulfill in response to a service purchase order (also called a service order). Service orders can contain lines for both material items and services. The following types of line items are supported in a service order: Material Service Lean Service Limit Service People in your company who fulfill services at a work site create and send service sheets to customers to describe the services they performed. Service sheets can include contact information for the field contractor, field engineer, and approver. You can create service sheets on SAP Business Network or transmit them from third-party systems using cXML. If your customer supports service sheet CSV upload, you can also upload service sheet CSV files. SAP Business Network doesn't let you submit service sheets until you receive your first service order from a customer. Depending on the nature of the order and your company’s business processes, you might create one service sheet to describe a one-time service or periodic service sheets for service projects that span longer time frames. You might be the only person at your company creating service sheets for the order, or there might be different people at your company creating service sheets for different parts of the order. A service sheet needs to contain at least one service line from the purchase order on which it is based. You can create a service sheet for one or more service lines in a service order. Service sheets can contain both service and material goods lines. On the Create Invoice page for suppliers, SAP Business Network displays the service description field only when service and mixed purchase orders are flipped to create invoices. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 73 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Buyer administrators can enable a default transaction rule Require suppliers to create service entry sheets where the line item quantity is not zero that prevents suppliers from creating service-entry sheets where the line-item quantity is zero. When this rule is enabled, suppliers can enter either a positive or a negative value in the quantity field.  Note You can't create service sheets for purchase orders with lines that have the type “service” but don’t require a service sheet. Service orders can contain separate, individual lines for goods that aren’t part of a service line.  Note When SAP Business Network receives a purchase order from an SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA system, and it contains both material and service line items, suppliers can create service-entry sheets against the service line items. Suppliers can create ship notices against the material line items of a purchase order containing both material and service line items, if the related default transaction rule Allow suppliers to send ship notices to this account is enabled to allow suppliers to create ship notices. However, the buyer can use purchase-order control keys at a line-item level to override the default invoice transaction rule. Your ability to send service sheets to your customers and to perform the following actions depends on the customer's configuration: If your customer allows attachments for service sheets, you can add attachments only at the header level. Edit quantity, unit of measure, unit price, or subtotal amounts for service-order lines. Add ad hoc items. Add contract or catalog items. Your customer might require start and end dates either at line level or the header of service sheets. If so, the start and end date fields are required on the Create Service Sheet page. SAP Business Network provides an option for suppliers to copy the service start and end date information specified in the service header, to automatically populate the service start and end dates of service-sheet line items (including ad hoc service-sheet line items). You can create service sheets against blanket (unplanned) service lines in service orders, but you can't create them against blanket purchase orders (BPOs). For BPOs, you need to create a ship notice. If the customer flagged an item as completed on the order, the following warning appears for the item: The buyer has marked this as Completed. This warning doesn’t prevent you from submitting a service sheet. If the supplier specifies the email address in the approver details section that is within the Additional Details section on the service-entry sheet page, SAP Business Network sends email notifications to the approver. Notifications are sent whenever modifications are made to the service-entry sheet, or if the status of the service-entry sheet changes. Planned and Unplanned Service Lines Service lines on service orders are either planned or unplanned. Planned service lines describe specific pieces of work and have set quantities and amounts as well as a hidden maximum amount. Your customers use planned lines for orders where they know exactly what work they want performed. When you create a service sheet for a planned line, all of the grouped items under it are automatically added to the service sheet. If your customer’s business rules allow you to add ad hoc items to service sheets and the hidden maximum amount is larger than the line’s subtotal, you can also add line items under a planned line to describe additional goods or services you needed to perform the work. Your customer might also specify tolerances to limit how much you add to a planned line. Suppliers cannot edit the item description field. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 74 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Unplanned service lines are blanket purchase order lines; the subtotal might be visible or hidden, and they always have a hidden maximum amount. Your customers use unplanned lines for orders where they know the overall piece of work they want performed, but they want you to provide the detail of the services and goods you needed for it. If your customer places orders with unplanned lines, they need to enable the business rule that allows you to add ad hoc items to service sheets. You then add material goods and service lines under the unplanned line on the service sheet to describe how you performed the work. When an unplanned ad hoc line item is added in a service-entry sheet, suppliers can specify any unit of measure (UOM) specified in the UOM file uploaded by the buyer. If a buyer didn’t upload a UOM master file, then suppliers must mandatorily specify the unit of measure, and it is mandatory for the suppliers to specify the UOM. Buyers can use default transaction rules to: Prevent suppliers from specifying part numbers that exceed 18 characters for ad hoc line items. Require suppliers to provide part descriptions for ad hoc line items. Require suppliers to provide line item quantities for ad hoc line items. Service sheets accumulate against purchase orders in the same way that ship notices do. Service sheets for unplanned service lines accumulate against the unplanned line’s subtotal only, not its unit price or quantity. Determining if a service line is planned or unplanned helps you know what information you may be allowed to provide to the customer in your service sheet. Use the following guidelines for determining whether a service line is planned or unplanned: Service Line Characteristics Examples Planned The service line is an item group with grouped Planned line: items under it. If the unit price is visible, the subtotals of the grouped item add up to the unit 1 Service Line A $300 (max amount $300) price. 1.1 Service Item A1 $200 If your customer allows you to add ad hoc items to 1.2 Goods Item A2 $100 an order and the service line specifies a (hidden) maximum amount that is larger than the unit price, Planned line to which you can add you can add unplanned or ad hoc items to a unplanned or ad hoc items: planned service line, up to tolerance limits. 2 Service Line B $300 (max amount $500) 2.1 Service Item B1 $200 2.2 Goods Item B2 $100 Unplanned The service line is an item group with no items grouped under it. The unit price might be visible or hidden. You must add items to the unplanned service line. Unplanned line with unit price: 1 Service Line A $300 (max amount $300) Unplanned line with hidden amount: The subtotal of those items can add up to the unit 2 Service Line B undisclosed (max amount price, if it is visible, and must not exceed the $500) (hidden) maximum amount. Service Sheets for Purchase Orders with Tolerances, Expected Value, and Overall Limit Customers can pass quantity and price tolerances for planned line items and Expected Value and Overall Limit values for unplanned line items. You can see the Expected Value for unplanned items on the purchase order, but not the Overall Limit. If you This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 75 7/10/26, 2:06 AM attempt to submit a service sheet that includes planned line items that exceed the customer's defined quantity or price tolerances, or unplanned line items that exceed the Overall Limit, you receive an error that prevents you from submitting the service sheet. SAP Business Network displays the allowed and accumulated quantity information in the tooltip provided for the Qty/Unit field. Lean Service and Limit Service Service orders can also include Lean Service and Limit Service item types. Lean services simplify the process of procuring services. They can be either Lean Service items for planned lean services or Limit Service items for unplanned lean services. Planned lean services focus on improving the customer experience by optimizing the use of existing resources. Limit items for unplanned lean services, also known as limit services, are used to procure unplanned low-value services costing up to a predefined spend limit. Both the lean service and limit service reduces the time and effort involved in procuring low-value items, and reduces the steps involved, such as ordering, receiving, processing invoices, and so on. Limit services can be purchased like planned lean services. The buyer doesn’t need to specify all the details at the time of purchase. The purchased service is carried out until the buyer-specified predefined spend limit as the value for the Expected Value for Unplanned Spend field is reached. The Other information section under Line Items in a purchase order displays the field Expected Value for Unplanned Spend, which is the predefined limit set by the buyer for the limit-service item. While creating a service sheet or an invoice from a purchase order with Lean Service or Limit Service items, all the line items are flipped together. This action is unlike a purchase order with several Service line items, where a service sheet or a standard invoice can be created for only one line item in the purchase order. The supplier can create a single service sheet or an invoice for all the Lean Service or Limit Service line items. The supplier can choose to exclude one or more Lean Service or Limit Service line items by deselecting the radio button Include against each line item. By default, all Lean Service and Limit Service line items are included in the service sheet or invoice. There is no parent-child structure for Lean Service and Limit Service items. Each line item exists independently. Contract and Ad Hoc Limits in Service Sheets Buyers can set contract and ad hoc limits in the line-item detail of a purchase order. While creating purchase orders in a procurement system like the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, buyers can specify different types of limits in the purchase item detail. If you have other ERPs, this feature can be supported with the necessary mapping in the cXML data. In some procurement systems, buyers can also specify the following sub-limits at the item level: Contract – Contract limit refers to the allowed limit for planned services with reference to a contract. Ad hoc – Ad hoc limit refers to the allowed limit for unplanned services without reference to a contract. In SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA, an ad hoc limit is called an other limit. When buyers specify these sub-limits in a purchase order item detail, suppliers can charge for ad hoc unplanned services and planned services from a contract by adding service lines. The total value of unplanned services and planned services from a contract cannot exceed the hidden overall limit (MaxAmount) specified in the purchase order.  Note The purchase order limits for unplanned service lines are hidden from suppliers. Only buyers can see them. When suppliers create unplanned service lines with or without reference to a contract, SAP Business Network applies and validates the sub-limits specified in the purchase orders. SAP Business Network applies and validates the following rule: This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 76 7/10/26, 2:06 AM If the contract limit is not specified in the unplanned lines of a purchase order, the contract value must not exceed the overall limit. The total value must not exceed the overall limit. If the contract limit is specified in the unplanned lines of a purchase order, the contract value must not exceed the contract limit. The total value must not exceed the overall limit. When the Allow suppliers to add ad hoc line items to service sheets default transaction rule is enabled, and the ad hoc limit is set in the purchase order created in the SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA system, then SAP Business Network applies and validates the following rules: If the ad hoc limit is not specified in the unplanned lines of a purchase order, the unplanned ad hoc service value must not exceed the overall limit. If the ad hoc limit is specified in the unplanned lines of a purchase order, the value of unplanned ad hoc services with no reference to a contract must not exceed the ad hoc limit. The ad hoc limit set must not exceed the overall limit. If both the contract and ad hoc limits are set in the unplanned service lines of a purchase order, SAP Business Network validates value of each spend against the corresponding limits, however the sum of the ad hoc service spend and the unplanned contract spend cannot exceed the set overall limit.  Note Sometimes the overall limit could be lower than the contract and/or ad hoc limit. In such scenarios, SAP Business Network validates the contract and/or ad hoc items against the overall limit. SAP Business Network applies and validates these rules against invoices, service sheets, and proforma invoices. Creating a Service Sheet Use this procedure to create service sheets or update service sheets that were originally created in your external order management system. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Purchase Orders and click the triangle next to Search Filters to expand it. Then check Search only service purchase orders and click Search. For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Orders and Releases and click the triangle next to Search Filters to expand it. Then check Search only service purchase orders and click Search. Choose Create Service Entry Sheet . Navigate to an Orders with service line workbench tile. 2. Click the service order number for which you want to create a service sheet. The order's details page opens. 3. Click Create Service Sheet at the top of the order. The Select Item to Create Service Sheet page opens.  Note The Select Item to Create Service Sheet page shows only if your customer allows it. 4. Select an item to add to the service sheet. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 77 7/10/26, 2:06 AM  Note While creating a service sheet from a service purchase order with Limit Service or Lean Service items, all the line items are flipped together. This behavior is unlike a service purchase order with several Service line items, where a service sheet can be created for only one line item in the service purchase order. The supplier can create a single service sheet for all the Limit Service or Lean Service line items. 5. In the Service Sheet Header area, perform the following actions: Enter information such as the service sheet number, service dates, and contact information for the field contractor, engineer, and approver. To add a comment, click Add Comment and enter comment text. To add one or more attachments, click Add Attachment, browse to the attachment file, and click Add Attachment. You can only add attachments to service sheets at the header level; customers can set a business rule to require you to add at least one attachment per service sheet. 6. (Optional) To help you identify and search for documents that you send to customers, add an internal reference code in the Supplier Reference field. For example, you could enter a number or the name of a person who is dealing with that order. 7. In the Service Sheet Line Items area, select any purchase order lines you don't want to include in the service sheet and click Delete.  Note A service sheet needs to include at least one service line. You can exclude one or more Limit Service or Lean Service line items by deselecting the radio button Include against each line item. By default, all Limit Service and Lean Service line items are included in the service sheet. 8. Enter details of the services you performed for the included lines, such as quantities, unit prices, and service period start and end dates. By default, service lines use the service period start and end dates specified on the purchase order.  Note For Lean Service line items, only the following fields can be edited: Qty/Unit, Start Date, End Date, and Add comments. For Limit Service line items, only the following fields can be edited: Description, Quantity, Unit, Price, Start Date, and End Date. 9. If your customer’s business rules allow you to add ad hoc items to service sheets, choose a purchase-order item group and click Add Add Unplanned Item to add the item under it, then perform the following steps: a. Choose the type of line you want to add: Service for a service line Lean Service for a planned lean service line Limit Service for an unplanned lean service Material for a material goods line b. Enter a part number and description for the item. c. Enter the Quantity, Unit, Unit Price, and Subtotal for the item.  Note Unit and Subtotal are required for service lines. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 78 7/10/26, 2:06 AM d. (Optional) Add or edit the service period start and end dates. You can edit any default service dates for ad-hoc lines. By default, the individual ad-hoc lines you add to a service sheet use the service period from the service sheet’s header, if it has them. Otherwise, the dates are blank. By default, ad-hoc lines you add as grouped items under an item group use the item group’s service period dates, if it has them. Otherwise, they use the header dates. e. (Optional) Click Comments and enter comment text for the line. 10. If your customer allows you to punch in to their SAP Business Network procurement site to add contract or catalog items to service sheets, choose a purchase-order item group. Then click Add Contract/Catalog Item to add the item under it, and perform the following steps. a. The Add Item page opens to display items configured for invoicing on the related contract. On the catalog main page, browse by category, follow the category links, or search by keyword or part number to narrow the list of items. Depending on the type of contract and the way your customer has configured the customer catalog, the Add Item page either displays the catalog main view or the item list view. For example, an item-level contract displays all available items for invoicing directly in item list view mode, while a supplier-level contract displays the catalog main view for browsing and searching. b. On the catalog item's listing page, click Add Item to add the item to the shopping cart.  Note The price on the listing page reflects the price before contract pricing terms are applied. Contract pricing terms are applied when you add the item to the service sheet. c. If your customer allows you to add non-catalog items to service sheets during punch in, click Add Non-Catalog Item and enter information for the item. d. Click the shopping cart icon in the upper right corner of the screen at any time to edit your shopping cart contents. e. Click Done.  Note You can save service sheets as drafts to work on them at different times before you submit them. SAP Business Network stores draft service sheets for 14 days after the last time you edited them. To save a service sheet, click Save at the top of the service sheet page. To open a saved draft service sheet, choose Outbox Drafts and click the Service Sheets tab. 11. Click Next. 12. Review the information you entered and click Submit.  Caution You can't cancel a service sheet once it’s submitted. Results SAP Business Network sends the service sheet to your customer. You can view the service sheet in the related documents for the purchase order, and on the Outbox Service Sheets page. The status of a service line in a purchase order is set to Serviced once you create service sheets against it up to the subtotal amount. If the line is unplanned and has a hidden maximum amount larger than the subtotal, you can continue to create service sheets against it up to that maximum amount. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 79 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Related Information The Workbench Service Sheet Header Fields When you create, edit, or resubmit a service sheet you need to be familiar with the data fields available to you. Default service sheet header fields provide general information about the service sheet. Your customers can customize the labels for the default fields or remove them from the service sheet header. The following table describes the default header fields for service sheets: Field Description Service Sheet # A unique identifier for the service sheet. Service Sheet Date The date on which the service sheet was created. The default date is the current date. Service Start Date The start and end dates for the time in which you performed the service. If you specify Service End Date these dates at the header level, they become the default service start and end dates for each line in the service sheet that does not have its own start and end dates set separately. You can also edit the start and end dates for individual lines at the line level. Field Contractor Name, Email, Phone Contact information for the person in your company who manages or performs the service work. This could be you or a site supervisor. Field Engineer Name, Email, Phone Contact information for the person in your customer’s organization who manages or supervises the service work at the work site. Approver Name, Email, Phone Contact information for the person in your customer’s organization who approves the service work. The approver is not necessarily the person who ordered the work. Your customers can set a business rule to require the approver name and email address; phone number is always optional. Correction Service Entry Sheet You can create correction service entry sheets to modify information in service sheets that have been invoiced. By doing so, you can avoid the service sheets from being rejected by your customers. Use correction service entry sheets, not credit memos, to make adjustments for over-invoiced item quantities on service sheets. For more information, see Creating a Correction Service Entry Sheet. Editing and Resubmitting a Failed or Rejected Service Sheet Use this procedure to correct any errors on a failed or rejected service sheet and then resubmit it to your customer. Context A service sheet can fail when service sheet line items don't match the information from the purchase order. Your customer provides a reason when rejecting a service sheet. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 80

file://SBN/split/Receiving and Fulfillin.content: 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Procedure 1. Do one of the following: Choose Fulfillment Service Sheets . Navigate to a Service sheets workbench tile. 2. Choose the failed or rejected service sheet and click Edit. 3. If the service sheet was rejected, enter a new service sheet number. 4. Edit the service sheet to correct any errors. 5. Review the information you entered, and then click Submit. Results SAP Business Network sends the updated service sheet to your customer. The rejected service sheet is still available in your Outbox and in the purchase order’s related documents with a status of Rejected and a routing status of Obsoleted. Related Information The Workbench Downloading a Service Sheet PDF Use this procedure to download a PDF copy of a service sheet to print or save for your records. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: Choose Fulfillment Service Sheets . Navigate to a Service sheets workbench tile. 2. Click a service sheet number to open it. 3. Click the Download  icon and choose the print or download option you want. The document number of the service sheet becomes the file name of the PDF. Related Information The Workbench Viewing Status Update Request Attachments Use this procedure to view and download attachments that are included with status update requests from your customers, regardless of the status. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: Choose Fulfillment Service Sheets . This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 81 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Navigate to a Service sheets workbench tile. 2. Click a service sheet number to open it. 3. Choose the History tab of the service sheet. 4. Click a status update request attachment under the Comments section to view or download it. Related Information The Workbench Searching for a Unit of Measure on a Service Sheet Use this procedure to find the unit of measure you want to use in a service sheet. Context If a buyer allows you to edit the unit of measure on service sheets, you can type a unit of measure symbol, select one from a list, or search for a unit of measure. Procedure 1. On a service sheet, select the Unit field for a line item or a header field. 2. Start typing a unit of measure symbol. A dropdown list of matching unit of measure symbols appears. 3. Do one of the following: Select a unit of measure symbol. Click Search for more to search for a unit of measure. 4. If you clicked Search for more, do the following: a. Select Name, Symbol, or Code, and then type a value. b. Click Search. The search results appear in the table. If there are more than ten results, use the page controls above the table to page through more units of measure. c. Click Select to select a unit of measure. Service Sheet Statuses Service sheet routing and document statuses let you know where each service sheet is in the process. Routing Statuses The Routing Status field describes whether a document made it successfully to its destination system. For documents you create, such as invoices and service sheets, the routing status informs you whether your document reached your customer's system. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 82 7/10/26, 2:06 AM For documents from your customer, such as orders, releases, time sheets, and remittances, the routing status lets you know whether the document reached SAP Business Network and any additional systems that you configured to accept incoming documents. SAP Business Network shows the following routing statuses: Status Description Acknowledged The document reached its destination system. This is the final routing status for documents. Duplicated This status applies only to remittance advice documents. A remittance advice document has this routing status if it's a duplicate of another remittance advice. Failed SAP Business Network could not send the document. In the case of a purchase order from your customer, SAP Business Network couldn't send the order to you through email, fax, cXML, or EDI. For example, your order fulfillment system could have experienced a problem that prevented SAP Business Network from successfully sending the order. You can resend orders that have a Failed routing status by clicking Resend at the top of the order. For failed invoices or service sheets, you need to correct any errors and resubmit them to your customer. For any other failed documents, contact your customer to resend them. Obsoleted After you cancel an invoice or edit and resubmit an invoice or service sheet, the original document moves to Obsoleted status, which indicates that you don't need to take any further action on the original document. Once a document has this routing status, you can't make any changes to it. Queued SAP Business Network is in the process of sending the document. Contact SAP Business Network Support if a document remains in this status for more than 30 minutes. Sent SAP Business Network sent the document successfully. For invoices or service sheets, SAP Business Network sent the document to your customer, but your customer hasn't yet acknowledged that they received it. If your document stays in this status for an extended period of time, contact your customer to see what needs to happen next.  Note If your customer allows it, you can cancel an invoice with a routing status of Sent. Document Statuses A document's status, such as Order Status or Invoice Status, describes where the document stands in its processing. If you update part of a document, SAP Business Network reports the partial status for the entire document, such as Partially Invoiced. For documents you create, such as invoices and service sheets, the document status lets you know where your customer is in the approval process for that document. For documents from your customer, such as orders and releases, the document status tells you where you are with regard to processing the document. SAP Business Network shows the following document statuses: This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 83 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Status Description Approved This status applies to invoices, service sheets, and time sheets. If the document doesn't have any errors, your customer approves it. After a document reaches Approved status, you can't make any changes.  Note An approved invoice means that your customer has approved it for payment. If you made a mistake, you need to send a credit memo to your customer. Canceled This status applies to invoices, service sheets, and remittance advice documents. After a document reaches Canceled status, you can't make any changes. In the case of a remittance advice document, your customer canceled the payment transaction. When a payment transaction fails, it needs to be canceled to allow for a subsequent attempt to complete the payment. Changed This status applies to orders and releases. Your customer sent a new version to replace the original document. Confirmed / Partially Confirmed These statuses apply to orders, releases, and time sheets. For orders and releases, Confirmed means that you agreed to ship all line items, while Partially Confirmed means that you agreed to ship some items. Failed This status applies to orders, releases, and remittance advice documents. SAP Business Network experienced a problem routing the document to your account or any additional systems that you configured to accept incoming documents. You can resend orders that have a Failed status by clicking Resend at the top of the order. For remittance advice documents, a Failed status means that the payment transaction failed. Invalid This status applies only to time sheets. Contact your customer to find out how to handle an invalid time sheet. Invoiced / Partially Invoiced These statuses apply to orders, releases, and service sheets. You have invoiced for the full amount of the document. Partially Invoiced means that you invoiced for only a part of the document amount. The Amount Invoiced column shows how much money you have invoiced or charged against the document. New This status applies to orders and releases for which you haven't yet updated the status. Obsoleted This document status applies only to time sheets that were replaced by an updated version. SAP Business Network shows only the updated version of the time sheet. On Hold This status applies only to remittance advice documents whose payment transaction was put on hold. Paid / Partially Paid These statuses apply to invoices and remittance advice documents. For invoices, your customer paid the invoice or is in the process of issuing payment.  Note Not every customer sends remittance information to SAP Business Network. If your invoice doesn't move past Approved status, you'll need to contact your customer to find out when to expect payment. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 84 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Status Description For remittance advice documents: Paid status means that the payment transaction was completed successfully. Partially Paid status means that payment is still due for the remaining amount shown on the remittance advice. Received / Partially Received These statuses apply to orders and releases. Your customer creates receipt documents in their system to acknowledge the products they physically received. The information from these receipts causes your purchase order status to update. When viewing a purchase order's details in your account, each line item shows the quantity of goods received. Rejected / Partially Rejected These statuses apply to invoices, service sheets, remittance advice documents, and time sheets. Invoices and service sheets are rejected in two cases: They fail validation on SAP Business Network. Your customer rejected the document in their processing system.  Note You can edit and resubmit rejected invoices or service sheets. Returned This status applies to orders and releases. Your customer creates receipt documents in their system to acknowledge the products they need to return. The information from these receipts causes your purchase order status to update. When viewing a purchase order's details in your account, each line item shows the quantity of goods returned. Sent This status applies to invoices and service sheets. The document reached your customer's system, but they haven't yet approved or rejected it. If your document stays in this status for a while, contact your customer to see what needs to happen next.  Note If your customer allows it, you can cancel invoices in Sent status. Serviced / Partially Serviced These statuses apply to service orders and releases. When a document reaches Serviced status, you can't create any more service sheets against planned service lines items. You can continue to create service sheets for unplanned service lines up to their hidden maximum amounts (which may be larger than their subtotals). The document status is set to Partially Serviced until all of the service lines are serviced. Shipped / Partially Shipped These statuses apply to orders and releases. Shipped status means that you shipped the entire order, while Partially Shipped means that you shipped only some of the items from the order.  Note You can still continue to confirm order line items regardless of the shipping status until you have confirmed all order lines. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 85 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Status Description Submitted This status applies only to time sheets that were submitted to your SAP Business Network account. Proof of Service This section provides topics describing what a proof of service is, related permissions, and how to view proof-of-service reports. Proof of Service in SAP Business Network Roles with Permissions for Users Related to Proof of Service Proof of Service Personas Proof of Service Workflows Proof of Service API for Suppliers Proof of Service Reports Proof of Service Using SAP Field Service Management Proof of Service in SAP Business Network Proof of service (PoS) is a digital document that acts as a proof of completion of a service line item in the service order. The ability to create a proof of service is important for organizations to create a digital record as the proof of a completed service. This feature helps organizations increase efficiency and save time required to process hard copies of receipts as proof of service. For example, a field contractor of a supplier, who has completed a line item from the service order for the buyer, can now create a PoS as digital proof of completion of a service line item. The PoS includes details for field contractor, document reviewer, service duration, location, materials, and other details of the service or material.  Restriction A PoS can correspond to only one line item in the purchase order. A PoS can be created only at the purchase-order line-item level. A PoS can be created only for service items. Prerequisites The buyer and supplier organizations must have an active trading relationship. Roles with Permissions for Users Related to Proof of Service To ensure that users perform only those roles that are assigned to them, SAP Business Network provides five permissions related to proof of service (PoS). An administrator can assign these permissions to different roles and then assign these roles to the users. The following are the five PoS-related permissions: Proof Of Service Create Access Supplier users having this permission can create a PoS. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 86 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Proof Of Service Create On Behalf Access Supplier users having this permission can create a PoS on behalf of the contractor. This is useful in a business scenario where the supplier contractor does not have the resources to create PoS. Proof Of Service Review Access Once a supplier user or a contractor creates a PoS, a supplier supervisor with this permission can review the PoS and reject it or submit it for approval. These supplier users can view the details only for the PoS for which they are specified as reviewers. Proof Of Service Approval Access Buyer users having this permission can approve or reject the PoS sent by the supplier. Proof Of Service Report Access Users having this permission can create the report of all PoS based on specified criteria such as start date or status.  Note Only the Proof Of Service Create On Behalf Access permission in the SAP Business Network proof of service workflow is applicable while creating service calls (proof of service) using SAP Field Service Management. Related Information Creating a Supplier Role Related to Proof of Service Creating a Supplier Role Related to Proof of Service Use this procedure to create roles related to proof of service (PoS) and assign these roles to users. Prerequisites You are assigned a supplier administrator role. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Users. 2. In the Manage Roles section, click the Create Role icon  at the top right of the role results table. 3. Enter a distinctive name for the role. 4. Enter a description for this role. 5. Select one or more of the following permissions for the new role: Proof Of Service Create Access Proof Of Service Create On Behalf Access Proof Of Service Review Access Proof Of Service Report Access  Note Each role must have at least one permission. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 87 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Avoid giving other proof-of-service-related access permissions, except Proof Of Service Report Access, to a user who already has Proof Of Service Create Access permission. 6. Click Save. Proof of Service Personas The proof-of-service lifecycle involves different personas. In some business scenarios, a supplier may choose to hire one or more contractors to execute the service order. In the absence of digitalized processes, the supplies or the supplier's contractors create manual documents which act as proof to completion of a service. With proof of service (PoS), SAP Business Network allows suppliers and their designated contractors to create a PoS as a digital proof. The following table describes the different personas involved in the PoS lifecycle: Proof of Service Personas Persona Description Contractor Supplier user who completes a service for a supplier. A contractor can directly create a PoS or the supplier can create it on behalf of the contractor. PoS Assigner Supplier user who can create and assign a PoS to a contractor. This user can also create and submit a PoS on behalf of the contractor. Supervisor Supplier user who reviews the PoS created by a contractor or a supplier administrator. The reviewer can send the PoS for the buyer's approval. Supervisors with the Proof Of Service Create On Behalf Access permission can create a PoS for the contractor. Approver Buyer user who approves or rejects a PoS sent by a supplier. Proof of Service Workflows The end-to-end workflow of proof of service can develop in different ways, depending on the persona who creates it. The following are few of the different ways in which a proof of service (PoS) workflow can develop: A contractor who works for the supplier creates a PoS. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 88 7/10/26, 2:06 AM A supervisor creates a PoS from the purchase order and assigns it to a contractor. A PoS assigner creates a PoS from the purchase order and assigns it to a contractor. A supervisor creates and submits a PoS for a contractor. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 89 7/10/26, 2:06 AM A PoS assigner creates and submits PoS for contractor and the reviewer is a different supplier user. Proof of Service API for Suppliers Suppliers can use an API to create, view, and update proofs of serivce. The Proof of Service (PoS) is a digital document that acts as a proof of completion of a service line item in the service order. The Proof of Service API for suppliers allows suppliers to create, view, update a single PoS or a list of PoS (based on specific filter criteria), retrieve the list of all users of an organization with the specified role, add an attachment to a PoS, or download a specified attachment from a PoS. For more information, see Proof of Service API for Suppliers. Proof of Service Reports You can generate reports for proof of service (PoS) based on start date, end date, and status. You can create a report template and generate reports for proof of service data. For more details, see Generating Proof of Service Reports. Related Information Reports and Report Templates Proof of Service Using SAP Field Service Management Suppliers can use the service call feature in SAP Field Service Management as proof of service. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 90

file://SBN/split/Receiving and Fulfillin.content: 7/10/26, 2:06 AM SAP Field Service Management is a business solution that helps you speed up issue resolution and makes the service experience easier and more effortless. With SAP Field Service Management solution, you can support your technicians with mobile tools to provide proactive customer service, leading to greater customer satisfaction. You can use the service call feature in SAP Field Service Management as proof of service in integration with SAP Business Network. The service call created in SAP Field Service Management acts as proof of service in SAP Business Network. Technicians can use SAP Field Service Management to manage and fulfill the service call and the corresponding information gets reflected in SAP Business Network against the service on the purchase order for which the service call is created. For more information about SAP Field Service Management, see the SAP Field Service Management documentation. Related Information Creating a Service Call (Proof of Service) from a Purchase Order Adding a Service Call as Proof of Service to a Service Sheet Default Transaction Subrule to Mandate Proof of Service Buyers can require that suppliers to attach a proof of service to a service sheet. When buyers enable the Require suppliers to create a proof of service (PoS) before submitting a service entry sheet (SES), suppliers need to create at least one proof of service (PoS) and attach it to the service sheet before submitting it. Creating a Service Call (Proof of Service) from a Purchase Order Suppliers can use purchase orders to create service calls (proofs of service). Suppliers can create a service call (proof of service) from a purchase order (PO) as part of the integration with SAP Field Service Management. SAP Business Network provides suppliers the option to create a service call (PoS) from a PO. For more information about proof of service, see Proof of Service in SAP Business Network. Prerequisites You must meet the following requirements to create a service call (PoS) from purchase order using SAP Field Service Management: You must have the Proof Of Service Create On Behalf Access permission in the SAP Business Network proof of service workflow. For more information about the different permissions related to proof of service, see Roles with Permissions for Users Related to Proof of Service. The default transaction rule Allow suppliers to send service sheet attachments must be enabled. The default transaction rule Allow suppliers to create proof of service using SAP Field Service Management must be enabled.  Note If the default transaction rule Do not allow suppliers to manually create service entry sheets for service orders is enabled, its subrule Allow suppliers to create proof of service using SAP Field Service Management does not show. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 91 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Creating a Service Call (Proof of Service) from a Purchase Order Suppliers can create service calls (proofs of service) using a purchase order. Procedure 1. Perform one of the following actions: For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Orders Purchase Orders . Orders and Releases . Navigate to an order-based workbench tile. 2. Click a purchase order. The purchase order details page opens. 3. Click Create Service Call (proof of service). The line-items selection page opens, listing all line items that are eligible for creation of a service call. 4. Choose the line items for which a service call should be created. If you choose a parent line item, all the corresponding child items are selected by default. To exclude a child item, uncheck the box corresponding to that specific child item. 5. Click Create Service Call (proof of service). A popup displays the number of service calls to be created. If you have selected a parent line item with two child items, two service calls are created in SAP Field Service Management. 6. Click Proceed. The service calls are created for the selected line items. 7. (Optional) To view and manage the service calls you have created, log on to SAP Field Service Management by clicking View and manage service calls from SAP Field Service Management mobile application. 8. To return to the order details page, click Back to purchase orders. Related Information The Workbench Default Transaction Subrule to Allow Suppliers to Create Proof of Service Using SAP Field Service Management Buyers can ensure that suppliers use SAP Field Service Management for service completion. Suppliers need to use SAP Field Service Management for service completion when either of the following conditions exists: The Do not allow suppliers to manually create service entry sheets for service orders transaction rule is enabled. The Do not allow suppliers to manually create service entry sheets for service orders transaction rule is disabled and the Allow suppliers to create proof of service using SAP Field Service Management transaction rule is enabled. For more information about proof of service, see Proof of Service in SAP Business Network.  Note This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 92 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Only the Proof Of Service Create On Behalf Access permission in the SAP Business Network proof of service workflow is applicable while creating service calls (proof of service) using SAP Field Service Management. For more information about the different permissions related to proof of service, see Roles with Permissions for Users Related to Proof of Service. SAP Field Service Management has its own user authentication and authorization management. The Proof of Service Report does not include service calls (proof of service) that are created using SAP Field Service Management. Adding a Service Call as Proof of Service to a Service Sheet Suppliers can attach the service call for a line item as proof of service, when creating the service sheet for that line item. When a supplier creates a service sheet from a purchase order in which at least one line item has completed service calls (proof of service), the attachments corresponding to the selected and completed service calls (proof of service) are automatically uploaded to the Attachments section in the service sheet. This is in addition to the existing option of adding attachments to the service sheet. To exclude a service call (proof of service) attachment from the service sheet, suppliers choose the attachment from the Attachments section and click Delete. Suppliers can also remove a service call (proof of service) attachment from the service sheet by turning off the Include toggle against the corresponding line item. When the default transaction rule Require proof of service to create service sheet is checked, suppliers can create the service sheet only if at least one purchase order line item has completed service calls (proof of service). When the default transaction rule Require proof of service to create service sheet is unchecked, suppliers can create the service sheet irrespective of whether the purchase order line item has completed service calls (proof of service). Prerequisites To enable suppliers to add a service call as proof of service to a service sheet: The default transaction rule Allow suppliers to send service sheet attachments on the Default Transaction Rules page must be checked. The subrule Allow suppliers to create proof of service using SAP Field Service Management under the Do not allow suppliers to manually create service entry sheets for service orders transaction rule on the Default Transaction Rules page must be checked.  Note If the Do not allow suppliers to manually create service entry sheets for service orders transaction rule is checked, the subrule Allow suppliers to create proof of service using SAP Field Service Management is not displayed. Changes in Purchase Orders with Service Calls SAP Business Network provides buyers the option to make changes to a purchase order (PO) with service calls attached to it. Cancellation of a PO This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 93 7/10/26, 2:06 AM It is not possible for suppliers to cancel a PO when there is at least one service call associated with a service line item in a PO. This applies regardless of whether the service call status is Completed or Ready to Plan. Updates to a PO Deletion of a service line item: It is not possible for suppliers to delete a service line item in a PO when there is a service call associated with it. Change in quantity of a service line item: It is not possible for suppliers to change the quantity of a service line item in a PO when there is a service call associated to it. Change in unit of measure for a service line item: It is not possible for suppliers to change the unit of measure for a service line item in a PO when there is a service call associated to it. Change in other attributes of a service line item: Both buyers and suppliers can change other attributes of a service line item in a PO even when there is a service call associated to it.  Note When a change is successfully made in a PO, the service calls associated to the PO, along with the service call status, gets automatically associated to the updated PO. Changes made to attributes of material line items are not reflected in service calls associated to the PO. Changes made in a PO with service calls are not reflected in SAP Field Service Management. Handling Service Calls Deleted in SAP Field Service Management Service calls deleted in SAP Field Service Management can affect SAP Business Network. There are two possible scenarios in SAP Business Network related to service call deletion in SAP Field Service Management: Deletion of service call with status Completed: When a service call in Completed status is deleted in SAP Field Service Management, no change is recorded in SAP Business Network. Deletion of service call with status Ready to plan: When a service call in Ready to plan status is deleted in SAP Field Service Management, the service call gets deleted in SAP Business Network. This is displayed in the Order History tab of the corresponding purchase order. When a service call in Ready to plan status is deleted, suppliers can create a service call again for the purchase order line item. Individual Buyer Cloud Account in SAP Field Service Management Service call information is managed through a buyer's individual SAP Field Service Management account. You can complete actions and operations in SAP Field Service Management by owning and managing your own SAP Field Service Management account. Buyers can configure their SAP Field Service Management account details in SAP Business Network which is then used by SAP Business Network in completing any SAP Field Service Management operation. Service call (proof of service) information for an individual buyer account is managed through their own individual SAP Field Service Management account. Buyers can sign in to the SAP Field Service Management web application and can approve the This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 94 7/10/26, 2:06 AM service call using the web application or the field technician's SAP Field Service Management mobile application. Since the buyer owns the SAP Field Service Management account, they have access to all SAP Field Service Management features. Suppliers can sign in to each individual buyer account and can view, schedule, or update service calls for the individual buyer owning the account. Prerequisites To use individual buyer cloud account for the integration of SAP Field Service Management with SAP Business Network, the buyer must enable and configure the use of proof of service using SAP Field Service Management, and the supplier must be invited by the buyer to register with SAP Field Service Management. Using CSV Files to Respond to Large Orders This section provides topics describing how to download orders in CSV or use CSV templates to respond to large orders. Guidelines for Responding to Large Orders with CSV Templates Changing the Routing Method for Order Response Documents in CSV Format Downloading Large Orders in CSV Format Downloading Empty CSV Templates Guidelines and Field Reference for Uploading Order Confirmations in CSV Format Schedule-Line Confirmations in CSV Format Uploading Order Confirmations in CSV Format Guidelines and Field Reference for Uploading Ship Notices in CSV Format Uploading Ship Notices in CSV Format Guidelines for Responding to Large Orders with CSV Templates You can use CSV templates to respond to orders with more than 1,000 line items. Although SAP Business Network supports documents with up to 10,000 line items, you can't view or edit documents with more than 1,000 line items in the user interface. If a document has more than 1,000 line items (such as a large order), the document shows only the header when you open it; you can't view the line item details. To download the complete order, you can open the order and download it in CSV format.  Note You also can't view line item details for large orders received through email or fax. You can submit large order confirmations or ship notices (up to 10,000 line items) by uploading CSV files using standard templates. You can download CSV templates to help you create these documents and upload them to SAP Business Network. Each standard CSV template has the following 6 header rows at the top of the template: Row 1: Character encoding (for example, 8859_1). Row 2: Template information (for example, version and template type). Row 3: Field names. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 95 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Row 4: Whether the field is required or optional. Row 5: Data type (for example, Boolean, String, Integer, or Decimal). Row 6: Field description explaining the data to enter in the field. Starting at row 7, you can enter data in the template. When you upload the CSV file, SAP Business Network imports data from row 7 and below.  Note Although the header rows (rows 1 through 6) aren't imported, be sure that you don't remove them. If you do, you'll receive errors when you try to upload the CSV file. Changing the Routing Method for Order Response Documents in CSV Format Use this procedure to set the electronic order routing method to support uploading order response documents in CSV. Context Before you can upload order confirmations or ship notices in CSV format, you need to change the routing method for order response documents to cXML. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings ( ) icon and choose Electronic Order Routing. 2. On the Electronic Order Routing page, find the Other Document Types section. 3. For Order Response Documents, choose cXML. 4. Click Save. Downloading Large Orders in CSV Format Use this procedure to download information from a large order to a CSV spreadsheet. Context When you download a large order in CSV format, the file contains all items from the order. You can use the file as the basis for an order confirmation, ship notice, or invoice. The file doesn't include header-level taxes, allowances, or charges. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, choose Orders Orders Purchase Orders . Orders and Releases . Navigate to an order-based workbench tile. 2. Click the order number of the large purchase order you want to download. The order's details page opens. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 96 7/10/26, 2:06 AM 3. Click the download  icon in the upper right corner and choose Download CSV. 4. Follow the instructions in your browser to save or view the file.  Note You can open CSV files in your preferred spreadsheet application. Related Information The Workbench Downloading Empty CSV Templates Use this procedure to download a CSV template that is not prepopulated with data. Context When you download CSV templates for order confirmations, ship notices, and invoices, you can use the templates to upload CSV files for large documents. Your customers might offer customized templates for you to use. Otherwise, SAP Business Network offers standard templates to suppliers. Procedure 1. Click ... and choose Templates in the CSV Download section. 2. Choose a template, and then click Download. 3. Choose a location where you want to save the CSV file, and then click Save. Guidelines and Field Reference for Uploading Order Confirmations in CSV Format Suppliers can respond to multiple purchase-order confirmations using the standard order-confirmation CSV template.  Note This template is not prepopulated with data. If you're enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, you can alternatively use a prepopulated template in Excel format. For details, see Order Confirmation Template for Upload/Download. When you upload order confirmations from a CSV file, observe the following guidelines: You must first update the routing method for order response documents to cXML. Use the order-confirmation CSV file to confirm, reject, or backorder line items from the purchase order. You can confirm or reject an entire order in the SAP Business Network user interface.  Note You cannot use the order-confirmation CSV file to update line items on a previously submitted order confirmation. Supply all required fields for each order confirmation. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 97 7/10/26, 2:06 AM The order confirmation requires the purchase order date. You can copy the date from the purchase order cXML. You can upload several order confirmations from one CSV file, but they must be for the same customer. Enter the header information in the first row for the order confirmation. You don't need to repeat the header fields on subsequent rows. For information about the valid values for certain fields, see the Description column in the table. For example, the valid values for Item Type are accept, detail, backordered, or reject. If you enter detail for Item Type, the item is confirmed with changes detailed in the other fields for this item (such as shipping and tax amounts).  Note For order confirmation files with temporary unit prices, suppliers must enter detail in the Item Type column of each item with a temporary unit price. Otherwise, when you upload the file, any item with a temporary unit price that has accept in the Item Type column fails with an error message. For Boolean values, enter Yes or No. The order-confirmation CSV template has the following fields: Field Description Confirmation Number Order confirmation ID Order Number (Required) Purchase order ID Type Purchase order type Order Date Purchase order date; format: YYYY-MM-DD T hh:mm:ss Customer Location Item customer location Shipping Currency Shipping currency Shipping Money Estimated shipping cost Tax Currency Tax currency Tax Amount Tax amount Comment Comments about the order confirmation Item Line Number (Required) Purchase order line number for the item Schedule Line Number Item schedule line number Commitment Level Schedule-line commitment level Item Type (Required) Order confirmation type for the item (accept, detail, backordered, or reject) Item Quantity (Required) Item quantity Item Unit Of Measure (Required) UN/CEFACT unit of measure code; for example, EA for each, PK for pack, MO for Month, or HUR for Hour Item Delivery Date Item delivery date Item Shipment Date Item shipment date This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 98 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Field Description Item Shipping Currency Item shipping currency Item Shipping Amount Item shipping cost Item Tax Currency Item tax currency Item Tax Amount Item tax amount Item Comment Comments about the order confirmation for an item Item Supplier Batch Number Item supplier batch ID Item Supplier Part ID Supplier part ID; requires that transaction rule Allow suppliers to edit the Supplier Part ID and Auxiliary Part ID fields on order confirmations at the line-item level is enabled, for upload to succeed. Item Unit Price Currency Item price currency; requires that transaction rule Allow suppliers to change the currency for unit price on order confirmations is enabled, for upload to succeed. Item Shipping Instructions Instructions describing how to pack the item for shipment Item Unit Price Amount Item unit price; requires that transaction rule Apply line item unit price tolerance to order confirmations is enabled and the new value is within the set tolerance, for upload to succeed. Schedule-Line Confirmations in CSV Format Guidelines and requirements to upload multiple order confirmations at the schedule-line level. You can use the Order Confirmation CSV template to perform mass confirmations of purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and scheduling agreement releases at the schedule-line level. This topic describes the additional requirements when you use this template to make multiple schedule-line confirmations.  Note If you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, you can instead use an Excel template. For details, see Schedule-Line Confirmations in Excel Format. Restrictions CSV upload does not support confirming or rejecting an order than has unplanned lean-service items or unplanned material items. Prerequisites To upload order confirmations for scheduling agreement and scheduling agreement releases, the following rules must be enabled: Allow scheduling agreement collaboration Allow scheduling agreement release collaboration Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 99 7/10/26, 2:06 AM If you want to upload a CSV order confirmation file when the rule Require suppliers to send order confirmations for material orders at the schedule line-item level is enabled, the Schedule Line Number column is mandatory. Buyers configure the quantity and delivery-date tolerances by sending confirmation control keys in the purchase order. If no confirmation control keys are sent in a purchase order, the following rules are used: Apply line item delivery date tolerance to order confirmations. Apply line item quantity tolerance to order confirmation. When the rule Validate tolerance for quantity, delivery date, or both at the schedule-line level is enabled, the tolerances set by the control keys or the preceding rules are evaluated at schedule-line level. Related Information Using CSV Files to Respond to Large Orders Guidelines and Field Reference for Uploading Order Confirmations in CSV Format Uploading Order Confirmations in CSV Format Use this procedure to upload order confirmations with the CSV template. Prerequisites Review the guidelines for the order confirmation template: Guidelines and Field Reference for Uploading Order Confirmations in CSV Format Update the routing method for order response documents to cXML. Context To confirm a purchase order with more than 1,000 lines, you can use a CSV template to upload the order confirmations to SAP Business Network.  Restriction You cannot confirm orders with at least one service line item by using the Order Confirmation CSV template. See Service Order Confirmations for more information.  Note This template isn't prepopulated with data. If you're enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, you can alternatively use a prepopulated template in Excel format. For details, see Order Confirmation Template for Upload/Download. Procedure 1. Open the downloaded order confirmation CSV template with your preferred editor. 2. Enter values as desired. Make sure that required columns have a value for each entry. 3. Save the file. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 100

Supply all required fields for each ship notice. You can upload several ship notices from one CSV file, but they need to be for the same customer. Enter the header information in the first row for the ship notice. You don't need to repeat the header fields on subsequent rows. file://SBN/split/Registration and Signin.content: 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Registration and Signing In Generated on: 2026-07-10 02:06:36 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network for Trading Partners | 2605 Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/ARIBA_NETWORK_SUPPLIERS/ddd75910f67b4212b1c83f9d68cd2f01?locale=enUS&state=PRODUCTION&version=2605 Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 1 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Registration and Signing In This guide describes how suppliers can register as sellers on the SAP Business Network. This guide applies to: SAP Business Network SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network Discovery SAP Ariba Contracts SAP Ariba Sourcing Related Guides SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide Before You Register You can register by responding to an invitation or welcome letter from your customer, or you can create an account that's not yet linked to a customer by going to the SAP Business Network sign in page to register. If you have an existing supplier account, registering on SAP Business Network allows you to consolidate your company profile information and provides you with a centralized location to access all your SAP Ariba Sourcing events. During registration, the SAP Business Network requires you to enter basic information about your company and your account administrator. After you complete registration, you can enter additional information about your company, including: Company information: Enter information about your company, including a company description, contact information, and website URL. User account information: Enter additional contact information for yourself (the account administrator or user), such as your user name, email address, password, and other values. Administrators can also enter your company’s default currency in this section. Certifications: Enter company certification information, such as Small and Disadvantaged Business or Minority-Owned Business status. Profile visibility: Select options to make your business profile visible to all buying organizations or to allow potential new customers to contact you. Registering with Assistance from Your Customer Typically, your company is already in contact with a customer that transacts with their suppliers through SAP Business Network. The customer logs in to SAP Business Network and invites your company to join. SAP Business Network sends an email message to you that contains a link for starting the registration process. SAP Business Network notifies you through email when the account is active and ready to transact with your customer. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 2 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Registering Without Assistance from Your Customer If you are not already in contact with a buying organization on SAP Business Network, you can create a free, standard account at supplier.ariba.com . You can use this account to learn how to conduct e-commerce through SAP Business Network, create a company profile, and find new business through SAP Business Network Discovery. Completing a company profile allows buying organizations to locate your company when searching for suppliers by product and service category, industry, ship-to or service location, or other criteria. After reviewing basic company information, a buying organization can then request a relationship with your company. After you accept a relationship request, your account is ready to transact with the buying organization. Unified Terms of Use SAP Ariba has a unified Terms of Use for all SAP Ariba seller-facing solutions. The unified Terms of Use are available for review at any time on the Ariba Terms Center page. You must accept the unified Terms of Use before using Ariba seller-facing solutions.  Note SAP Ariba records the date on which you accept the Terms of Use Agreement as the effective date of service. The Ariba Terms Center Page displays the unified Terms of Use, Data Policy and Privacy Statement. Click Terms of Use at the bottom of any page to access the Ariba Terms Center page. Choosing a Secure Password Passwords are case-sensitive, must be at least eight characters long, and can include only alphabetic letters (without accents), numbers, and common symbols. For increased security, you should include at least one numeral between the first and last characters and at least one letter. To change your password, you must enter your current password as well as the new one, then confirm the new password. Passwords for users who have access to customer PCard numbers expire every 90 days. Selecting the Right Account Administrator The person whose name is entered when the account is created becomes the account administrator automatically. The account administrator plays a key role in the value your company realizes through SAP Ariba, so it is important you choose the appropriate person in your organization. The right person will have the time and capabilities to add users with appropriate roles, set configuration options, manage customer relationships, subscribe to services, respond to user questions or problems, and maintain your SAP Ariba account in a consistent manner. If you currently use SAP Ariba, you already have an account administrator, so assess whether they meet the qualifications. Selecting the Right Business Role About Business Roles Your Business Role determines the default action tiles displayed on the SAP Business Network dashboard. New SAP Business Network users are asked to select a Business Role during account creation. Existing SAP Business Network users who have not yet selected a business role will be prompted to select one the next time they sign in. You can select or change your Business Role from the My Account page at any time. For more information see Business Roles Reference. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 3 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Business Roles Reference Business Role Description Default Workbench Tiles Accounts Receivables An Accounts Receivables role represents a Orders to invoice, Orders, Rejected invoices, user focused on money owed to the Remittances, Early payment opportunities, company.
