You can invoices, Remittances customize the name of this role. Registering as a Supplier on SAP Business Network Use this procedure to register an SAP Business Network account to transact with your customers and potentially find new business opportunities. Context  Note To avoid potential confusion, SAP Business Network checks for duplicate accounts as part of the registration process. This applies to both standard and enterprise accounts as well as accounts created in SAP Business Network Discovery (so called walk up registrations). Suppliers can register non-public email domains to get notified whenever a new account is created or a relationship is established using this email domain. Procedure 1. You can use one of the following methods to register a new or existing seller account on SAP Business Network: If you received an email invitation from a buying organization, click the link in the email message. When SAP Business Network shows the welcome page, do one of the following: If you already have an account, click Sign in. If you don't already have an account, click Sign up. If you received a purchase order welcome letter that contains a temporary ID and secure code, you can use a web browser to go to the web address contained in the welcome letter. Enter your temporary ID and secure code to activate the account. After you activate your account, the temporary ID becomes your user name. If you received a purchase order or other first-time document from your customer, click the action button in the email, such as Process order. From the landing page, choose Sign up to register a free, standard account, or choose Sign in to add the document to your existing SAP Business Network account.  Note You must be the account administrator to move the document to an existing account. If you didn't receive an invitation, you can use a web browser to go to supplier.ariba.com . Click Register Now to register a free, standard account on SAP Business Network. 2. Follow the steps in the registration wizard. SAP Business Network asks for basic information about your business, such as your company name, address, and email address. You also create a user name and password. The wizard performs automatic address validation to detect and correct any wrong or misspelled portion of a mailing address. A pop up window shows a recommendation, which you can accept or reject. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 5 7/10/26, 2:06 AM There is an ISO-based country- or region-specific drop-down list for state/province in the address section of the supplier profile. Select from the drop-down list (where available) instead of entering free text.  Note The person whose name is entered in the user account information section becomes the account administrator automatically. Account administrators can transfer the administrator role to another user later.  Note When double byte non-Latin characters (such as Chinese) are detected in an address, a warning displays and a Latin character translation has to be provided by the user which is then also validated for correctness. 3. Read the terms of use, and choose the check box if you agree to the terms. 4. (Optional) Print the Summary page for your records. You can also print the terms of use. 5. Click Continue. SAP Ariba shows the Activate Your Account Now page. SAP Business Network sends you an email confirming registration of your account. You must click the link in the email to activate your account and start transacting with your customer. If you change your email address, SAP Business Network sends an email to the newly updated email address requesting you to confirm the email address. You must use the link in the email to activate and sign in to the account. You can also resend the email containing the link to activate your SAP Business Network account in case the previous email did not reach you. If for any reason, you are unable to launch a browser using this link, you can copy the link and paste it into the address bar of any of the supported Web browsers to form a single-line URL. 6. To activate your account, click the link in the email sent to you. SAP Business Network shows the Welcome to Ariba page, where you can view your company profile completeness meter. 7. Choose one of the following options: Click Go to Company Profile to enter additional information about your company.  Note To increase your visibility to buying organizations, be sure your company profile is completed accurately, and consider subscribing to the SAP Business Network Discovery Advantage Program to further distinguish your organization in SAP Ariba’s publicly-accessible supplier directory. When registering on SAP Business Network following an invitation initiated from SAP Ariba Supplier Lifecycle and Performance or SAP Ariba Sourcing, the Product and Service Categories and Ship-to or Service Location fields listed under Tell us more about your business are mandatory. Click Complete my Company Profile later, to access the Home dashboard. Related Information SAP Business Network Duplicate Account Check Process After You Register When you are finished with basic configuration, you can do the following: This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 6 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Manage Your SAP Ariba Profile Complete additional information about your company, such as website information, and set options for extending business profile visibility. You may need to update this information periodically, such as when a different individual at your company becomes the administrator. Manage your profile in a way that maximizes exposure for your business. Potential and existing customers rely on the information in your SAP Ariba profile when deciding whether to do business with you, so it is essential to keep your profile complete and accurate. In addition to completing requested fields, frequently review and update your profile to ensure it is current. While every section is important, pay special attention to the following four sections: Addresses: Buying organizations use your company name and main address to transact with you through SAP Business Network Discovery, SAP Ariba Sourcing, SAP Ariba Contracts, and the SAP Business Network, so ensure this information is always up to date. You should also add any addresses served by your account, such as your company’s subsidiaries, since these are exposed to SAP Ariba Sourcing and can be used by your own team members when creating e-invoices online. Product and Service Categories, Ship-to or Service Locations, and Industries: As the key criteria used to match your company to potential buyers through SAP Business Network Discovery, these three categories are vitally important in helping you obtain new business opportunities, so ensure to select these values carefully. Contacts: By assigning specific contacts for particular business activities (such as accounts payable, catalog management, and sales), you can ensure that buyers are able to contact the correct person quickly and easily. You have the option to designate both company-wide contacts and customer-specific contacts (only for SAP Business Network relationships). Marketing: Subscribing to the SAP Business Network Discovery Advantage program increases your visibility to potential buyers. The SAP Business Network Discovery Advantage program gives your company preferential placement in search results along with the option to display enhanced sales and marketing information—including a detailed company description, logos, URLs, attachments, and more—in your Ariba Network for Suppliers profile. You can assign a marketing team member to be the user responsible for completing and maintaining this section of your profile. Complete Customer-Requested Profile Information SAP Ariba profile information can include additional profile information requested by buyers as part of the Supplier Profile Questionnaire. If you are the administrator for your organization’s account, you see information about company profile fields requested specifically from the buyer. Buyers may require that you complete all requested profile information before you can participate in their events. Define User Roles and Create Users Assign user roles and permissions to employees based on their functional roles in your company, such as: Company profile manager Leads creator/manager Proposal and contract manager Order manager Invoice manager This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 7 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Inform individual users and teams in your company about the SAP Ariba account to which they are assigned, so they can be well prepared to respond to and collaborate with buyers. If you participate in sourcing events, be sure to assign the appropriate users in your company the Access Proposals and Contracts permission so that SAP Ariba Sourcing buyers can view and approve them to join events.  Note By default, users are not visible to or searchable by your customers. SAP Ariba recommends that you regularly review, identify, and eliminate or reassign unapproved users added to your account as a result of SAP Ariba Sourcing buyers asking them to participate in sourcing events. Access Web Assistant and Review Additional Product Documentation and Tutorials Click the question mark icon in the upper right-hand corner to activate Web Assistant in-app help and explore the field-level help, guided tours, and learning content. Click the Documentation tile to access product documentation or the Support tile to access the Help Center. Link Multiple SAP Ariba Seller Accounts If you have more than one SAP Ariba seller account, you can link accounts to consolidate your company's account management and service management tasks. You can create a parent-child account hierarchy. For example, link one parent account to any number of child accounts. Creating an account hierarchy allows parent account administrators to manage settings and components (including instant access to solution-specific dashboards and related child account services) for all accounts. Both parent and child accounts are visible in buyer searches, however you have the option to make child accounts invisible by configuring the Allow buyer organizations to search this account setting. After an account hierarchy is created, parent account administrators can sign in and access child accounts with a single click. If your company has created duplicate accounts by mistake, it’s important to keep these accounts current, since transactions have already been processed through them. To help reduce the amount of time spent on managing multiple accounts, you can enable Profile Sharing, allowing you to automatically synchronize your parent account profile with selected child accounts. Profile sharing reduces the need for separate profile updates.  Note Profile sharing synchronization does not occur for all fields and settings, (for example, not for electronic order/invoice routing), so you may need to maintain these settings individually for each account. You can use the User Account Navigator to link and quickly navigate among multiple user accounts. Verify Your Email Address To avail yourself of the full benefits of the SAP Business Network, you must validate your email addresses. To expedite registration, SAP Ariba allows you to register without validating your email addresses in some cases. For example, if you are moving your existing account from your buyer’s SAP Ariba Sourcing application to the SAP Business Network, SAP Ariba does not require you to validate your email addresses immediately. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 8 7/10/26, 2:06 AM The User Email Address Validation feature reminds suppliers without validated email addresses to validate their email addresses. SAP Ariba automatically marks the email addresses of suppliers invited to sourcing events as valid. If you sign in with a non-validated email address, an alert icon appears in the upper-right portion of the screen. A popup message appears when the cursor hovers over this icon. Follow the instructions in the message to verify your email address. Receive Relationship Requests, Receive Orders, and Send Invoices When you register for an SAP Ariba account through SAP Ariba Sourcing, SAP Business Network Discovery, or SAP Ariba Contracts, you are automatically enabled to receive orders and send invoices on SAP Business Network. Buyers on SAP Business Network can see your company profile in search results and send you trading relationship requests. SAP Ariba Sourcing and SAP Ariba Supplier Lifecycle and Performance relationship requests are set to “manual approval” by default. All other relationship requests are automatically accepted by default, but your account administrator can choose to manually review all relationship requests. An indicator appears in the right corner of the header bar in all solutions if there is a pending relationship request waiting to be approved, and email notifications are sent to you as a reminder. If you accept a relationship request from a buyer, a popup is displayed, prompting you to configure your preferred order routing method. You are not obliged to accept trading relationship requests. For more information about managing customer relationships, see SAP Business Network Supplier Administration Guide. You can enable the Do not expose my company in search results to Ariba Discovery users and Ariba Network buyers preference on the Profile Visibility page if you do not want to appear in search results to SAP Business Network Discovery users and SAP Business Network buyers. Extend a Relationship with an Existing Buyer A supplier organization that has a relationship with a buyer, can accept the buyer's additional collaboration request. Upon acceptance of the request, they have extended their relationship with a further collaboration. Prerequisites You’re a registered supplier on SAP Business Network and you have a relationship with a buyer. You've received a request from a buyer. You're assigned a role with the required Customer Administration permission. See Permissions You Can Assign to Users. You've read Manually Reviewing All Relationship Requests. Context You can extend an existing relationship with an SAP S/4HANA for product sourcing collaboration. This table shows the options that the function offers for managing collaborations. Options for Managing Collaborations Options Description This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 9 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Options Description Accept a collaboration You can accept a collaboration request. Reject a collaboration When a supplier rejects a collaboration, the collaboration status is updated to rejected. You can reject a current or pending collaboration. Rejection applies to collaboration type level. Rejecting the selected additional collaboration doesn't affect the unselected collaborations or the existing relationship. You can't reject a fulfillment collaboration if your relationship is suspended. Procedure 1. On the Ariba Network dashboard, click your profile and choose Settings Customer Relationships . 2. In your Account Settings, click Customer Relationships Current Relationships requests. You can see your requests listed by collaboration type and role. Pending to view your collaboration  Tip You can also navigate to this page by clicking the Review request button in the invitation e-mail. 3. Select a customer and click approve to accept, or reject to decline a collaboration request.  Note Based on your account type, you may have to accept additional fees and Terms of Use to enable the relationship extension. Automatically accept all relationship requests function is only applicable for those request types where you have already accepted the associated Terms of Use. Results The relationship extension is now established. SAP Business Network sends an e-mail notification. You can view the updated list of your relationships in Account Settings Customer Relationships Current Relationships . Click Current to show established, or Rejected to show declined relationships. The table displays your collaborations sorted by types and roles in separate rows, which allows you to manage them independently. Related Information Configuring a Supplier Account to Receive Email Notifications Creating and Resetting Passwords Use this procedure to create or reset the password for your SAP Business Network user name. Context Your password is case-sensitive and must be at least eight characters long. It can only include unaccented alphabetic characters, numbers, and common symbols. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 10

file://SBN/split/Registration and Signin.content: 7/10/26, 2:06 AM For increased security on SAP Business Network, passwords expire every 90 days for users who have PCard access but are not the PCard owner. These users receive email notifications that indicate how many days remain before their password expires. You cannot reuse your recent passwords.  Note For users without PCard access, passwords are valid for five years. You have a limited number of attempts to enter your password. After too many failed attempts, your account will be locked. Your account will automatically unlock after a few hours. You can initiate the password reset process to unlock your account immediately. If you cannot remember your user name or the email address you used to register, you must contact your account administrator to reset your password. You can contact your account administrator by clicking the user icon, then Contact Administrator. When your account administrator resets your password, SAP Business Network sends an email notification to you that contains a link to confirm your email address and enter a new password. If you cannot remember your user name or the email address you used to register, and you are the account administrator, you must call SAP Business Network Customer Support or log a service request. Click the question mark icon in the top right corner to access Web Assistant in-app help, then click the Support tile; you are redirected to the Help Center. In the Help Center, click Support Center to access support content, phone numbers, or create an online service request. Procedure 1. If your SAP Business Network password is not working or if you forget your password, click Password on the Sign In page. 2. Click Continue. 3. Enter your user name or email address in the User name or Email Address field and click Submit. SAP Business Network sends an email notification that contains instructions on how to reset your password to the email address you used to register your SAP Business Network account. 4. Click the link in the Password Reset email.  Note Links in password reset notifications are only valid for 24 hours. If you receive a password reset notification, but the link provided is invalid or expired, contact your account administrator and have them initiate the password reset process for you. If you are the account administrator, initiate the password process again.  Note If you don’t receive a password reset email from SAP Business Network: Check your junk mail folder or spam filter settings to verify that automated emails from SAP Business Network are not blocked from your email account. You might have multiple SAP Business Network user names with different email addresses. Make sure you check the correct email account. You might have recently changed your email address without updating the email address in your SAP Business Network account. Check the email account associated with your SAP Business Network account. You might have mistyped your user name. 5. Enter and confirm your new password on the Password Reset page. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 11 7/10/26, 2:06 AM 6. Click Submit. Results You can now use your user name and new password to sign in to SAP Business Network. Retrieving User Names If you forgot your SAP Business Network user name, use this procedure to request that SAP Business Network send you an email with instructions for retrieving your user name. Context The user name retrieval email notification is sent to the email address you entered when you registered your SAP Business Network account. If your email address is registered with multiple SAP Business Network accounts, the email will contain all the user names associated with your email address. Procedure 1. If you forget your SAP Business Network user name, click Forgot User name on the sign in page. 2. Enter the email address you used when you registered your SAP Business Network account. 3. Click Submit. Results SAP Business Network sends an email listing all the user names associated with your email address.  Note If you do not receive a user name retrieval email from SAP Business Network, check the following: Did you enter the correct user name that is registered with the SAP Business Network? If you have more than one user name, you can try to enter the other user names. Does your email configuration allow you to receive automated emails from SAP Business Network? Check your junk mail folder or email filter settings to verify automated emails from SAP Business Network are not blocked from your inbox. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 12

For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 1 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Reports and Report Templates This guide is for SAP Ariba supplier users and administrators seeking to collect transaction information in the form of reports in their SAP Business Network accounts. This guide applies to: SAP Business Network SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Related Guides SAP Business Network Guide to Invoicing Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Introduction to SAP Business Network Reporting Report Generation and Downloads Introduction to SAP Business Network Reporting You use reports to collect information on the transaction activity in your Ariba account. A report is a snapshot of data generated at a particular point in time. A report template defines what information is included in reports that are generated from it. Reports can be either manual reports or scheduled reports. You use manual reports to choose your data and generate the report. With scheduled reports, the data included in the report is based on a report template. For example, a purchase order report template defines which customers and amount ranges are to be included in the report. A manual report can be generated any time you want to see the results. A scheduled report is automatically generated from a template at scheduled intervals by SAP Business Network. Users with appropriate permissions can carry out all reporting tasks, including creating, editing, and deleting report templates, as well as running and downloading reports. To access the reporting area of your account, choose Reports from the menu bar. When you generate a report from a template, SAP Business Network creates a report file in comma-separated values (CSV) format and overwrites the last report you ran from that template. You can view and download reports to your local drive to save a record of your account activity over time.  Note To keep a record of report files, download each report file to your computer hard disk and save it under a different name before running the report again. You can download any report to your local drive that SAP Business Network has generated successfully. The Reports page allows you to do the following: This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 2 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Run generates a report from the selected template. Each time you select a report template and click Run, SAP Business Network overwrites the previously generated report. Download lets you save a generated report in CSV format to your local drive. Edit lets you to modify a report template’s name, description, and/or reporting criteria. Copy lets you copy a template, edit report criteria, and save it as a new report template. When you save a new template, SAP Business Network automatically puts a new report into the queue. When your organization reaches the maximum limit of twenty templates, SAP Business Network disables the Copy and Create buttons. Delete removes a report template and its corresponding report from your account. You might delete a template if your organization has reached the maximum of 20 templates and you want to create a new template rather than use Edit to modify an existing template. Create lets you to create a report template. Refresh Status refreshes the on screen display of report status. You might want to see the latest status when a report has been in Queued or Processing status for some time. Only users with a reporting permission can see the Reports area in your SAP Business Network account and any report types for which they have permission. Changes that you make to reports affect all account users. You must have an active SAP Business Network account to create scheduled report templates; however, SAP Business Network continues to generate your existing scheduled reports until they expire. The report templates that users can create depend on the permissions users have. For example, a user needs to have the Invoice Report Administration permission to access the Reports area and create an invoice report. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 19 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Report Generation and Downloads Exporting Report Document Header Information Use this procedure to export document information for reports. Procedure 1. On the tab of the documents you want to export, click the table options menu. 2. Choose one of the following: To download a maximum of 500 rows, choose Export all Rows. To download only the current page, choose Export Current Page. 3. Follow the instructions in the application window that appears. 4. To view the report in a format that is easy to read, save it to your computer hard disk. Then, open the saved file using a spreadsheet application, such as Microsoft Excel. The content of the output file is determined by the Show / Hide Columns settings in the table options menu. 5. To create a space-separated or csv file, open and export the file in Excel. Results Files created by exporting document information from the user interface are UTF-8 encoded. If your application does not read UTF-8, it might not correctly display all Asian and accented characters in the file. Related Information Report Generation and Downloads Downloading Reports Use this procedure to download reports to open or save them. Procedure 1. Choose Reports from the menu bar. 2. To generate a report, choose the report on the Reports page that you want to generate, and click Run. If you want to download the existing version of the report, skip this step and go to step 3. SAP Business Network adds your report to the queue and returns you to the Reports page. To update the statuses of reports on the Reports page, click Refresh Status. You can view and download the report when its status changes to “Processed.” 3. To view and download the report, click Download. Click one of the following: Open to view the report. SAP Business Network starts your spreadsheet application and displays the report. Save to save the report to your disk and view it later. Results This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 20

SAP Business Network deletes generated reports from your account after 30 days. Related Information Report Generation and Downloads Viewing Generated Reports with Double-Byte or Accented Characters Use this procedure to view generated reports with double-byte (for example, Japanese or Chinese) or accented characters. Procedure 1. Choose Reports from the menu bar. 2. On the Reports page, choose a report template, and click Download. Your browser prompts you to indicate whether you want to view the report or save it to disk. 3. Click Save. 4. Modify the file location and name, if necessary, and click Save. 5. Click Close. 6. Start a plain text viewer, such as Microsoft Notepad. 7. Click to open a file. 8. Choose All Files from the Files of type pull-down menu. 9. Select the file you want to open. 10. Choose Unicode from the Encoding pull-down menu. 11. Select All Files in the Save as type list. 12. Click Save. If the browser prompts you to overwrite the existing file of the same name, click Yes. 13. Close the file and quit Microsoft Notepad. 14. Start Microsoft Excel. 15. Click to open a file. 16. Choose All Files from the Files of type pull-down menu. 17. Open the report file you saved. 18. In Step 1 of the Text Import Wizard, choose Delimited as the Original data type, and click Next. 19. In Step 2 of the Text Import Wizard, click the check box for Comma in the Delimiters section, and click Next. 20. Click Finish. The file is displayed in Microsoft Excel. Results Regardless of the actual start time, the report collects information for the date range and time zone you specified in the template. The exact timing of a report run might differ from one run to the next, but the coverage period is always determined by the criteria in the template. Related Information This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 21 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Report Generation and Downloads Field Information for Tax Book Reports Tax book reports contain tax information from invoices, including information related to VAT. Buying organizations can also generate this report. The following table describes the information collected in the tax book report: Field Description Invoice # The unique invoice number. Date The date and time of the invoice. Buyer The name and address of the buying organization. Derived from the Sold To Address in the invoice. If Sold To information is not available, SAP Business Network uses Bill To information. Buyer VAT ID The buying organization’s VAT ID. Supplier The name and address of the supplier. Derived from the IssuerOfInvoice address in the invoice. If the IssuerOfInvoice information is not available, SAP Business Network uses From information. Supplier VAT ID The supplier’s VAT ID. Tax Representative The name and address of the tax representative. Tax Representative VAT ID The tax representative’s VAT ID. Report Line ID The source of the tax data: 0, which indicates a header field 1, which indicates the first tax rate and location 2, which indicates the second tax rate and location Tax Rates The rate used to calculate the amount of tax. Currency The default currency for the tax amount. Tax Amount The amount of tax in the default currency. Alternate Currency When suppliers use a different currency to calculate tax, this second tax amount is displayed in the Tax Amount in Alternate Currency column. The currency used for this is displayed in the Alternate Currency column. Tax Amount in Alternate Currency The amount of tax in the alternate currency, if any. Shipping Amount The shipping amount. Special Handling Amount The special handling amount, if any. Discount Amount The discount amount, if any. Net Amount The net amount. Due Amount The due amount. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 22 7/10/26, 2:06 AM Field Description Tax Point Date The date of supply. Tax Description An optional description of the tax. Used to explain zero-rate VAT. Ship From Country The country/region from which the transaction occurred. Ship To Country The country/region to which the transaction occurred. Cross Border Trade Indicates whether the transaction is across a country/region’s border. Intra EU Trade Indicates whether the transaction is within the EU. Converted Data Indicates whether the invoice was generated electronically or created manually by the buyer. Status The invoice status level, such as Sent. This is custom documentation. file://SBN/split/Tracking Temporary Labo.title: Tracking Temporary Labor Time_Part1
file://SBN/split/Tracking Temporary Labo.content: 7/10/26, 2:07 AM Tracking Temporary Labor Time Generated on: 2026-07-10 02:07:23 GMT+0000 SAP Business Network for Trading Partners | 2605 Public Original content: https://help.sap.com/docs/ARIBA_NETWORK_SUPPLIERS/b62ba04e48ff49df99e4e78a720f0c72?locale=enUS&state=PRODUCTION&version=2605 Warning This document has been generated from SAP Help Portal and is an incomplete version of the official SAP product documentation. The information included in custom documentation may not reflect the arrangement of topics in SAP Help Portal, and may be missing important aspects and/or correlations to other topics. For this reason, it is not for production use. For more information, please visit https://help.sap.com/docs/disclaimer. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 1 7/10/26, 2:07 AM Tracking Temporary Labor Time This guide is for suppliers responsible for managing time sheets or time cards submitted to SAP Business Network from contractors. Time sheets can be created by a contractor or a contractor’s supervisor in a procurement application, or by a supplier on SAP Business Network. This guide applies to: SAP Business Network Related Guides Introduction to SAP Business Network About Time Sheets A time sheet (also called a time card) is a statement of hours worked by a contractor. Time sheets include details such as start time, end time, hours worked, pay rate, and basic information about the contractor, customer, supplier, and submitter. Time sheets can be created by a contractor or a contractor’s supervisor in a procurement application, or by a supplier on Ariba Network. As a supplier, when you receive a time sheet, you see a Time & Expense Sheets link in your Ariba Network inbox. The submitter’s procurement application assigns a unique number to each time sheet. Ariba Network tracks time sheets by these assigned numbers. You can track the progress of work on a job by reviewing time sheets and associated purchase order line items on Ariba Network. Each time sheet is associated with exactly one labor line item in a purchase order, and it serves as a partial receipt for the associated labor line item.  Example If the purchase order contains a time entry for an administrative assistant for a total of 500 hours, each time sheet that contractor filled out would be a partial receipt toward those 500 hours. The task flow for time sheets on Ariba Network is as follows: 1. A time sheet is created and submitted in one of the following ways: By a contractor’s supervisor on behalf of a contractor in a procurement application By a contractor in a procurement application By a supplier on behalf of a contractor on Ariba Network 2. The procurement application routes the time sheet to the supplier’s Ariba Network account. 3. The supplier reviews the time sheet and associated purchase order. 4. The supplier creates an invoice against the purchase order. 5. (Optional) The customer updates the invoice status, triggering the electronic payment process. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 2 7/10/26, 2:07 AM Finding Time Sheets and Organizing Results Use this procedure to view your time sheets regularly to track activity and troubleshoot errors efficiently. You can scroll through the time sheets or search for time sheets by customer, ID, or date range. Prerequisites You need to have the Inbox Access and Time Sheet Management permissions to search for or view time sheets. Contact your account administrator if you don't see the Fulfillment Time and Expense Sheets page after logging in to your account.  Restriction If your account is suspended, you can't receive time sheets or other incoming documents from your customers. Accounts are suspended if you fail to pay your subscription fees. Context You can create a filtered list that shows only those time sheets meeting various criteria you specify. You can also customize the way SAP Business Network sorts and displays your search results. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: From the search bar on the Home tab, choose Time & Expense Sheet and search by a particular customer or time sheet ID. Choose Fulfillment Time and Expense Sheets to view all time sheets. 2. If you don't see the time sheet you're looking for, use the search filters to refine your search: Choose a customer, date range, or time sheet status from the dropdowns. Enter a particular time sheet ID. Choose the number of results to show. 3. Click Search. 4. After you run the search, click any column heading link in the time sheet display table to sort the table by that column. If you want to undo your search and start again, you have the following options: Click Reset, which blanks out all search filters except date range. Choose Fulfillment Time and Expense Sheets again to view the results for the default date range. 5. To change the column display and groupings, click the table options menu icon  at the top of the table. In the Show / Hide Columns section, click the columns you want to show or hide. In the Group by Column section, choose how you want to group the results. Use the Grouping Expansion toggle to control your initial display. If you group your results you can then use the expansion triangle to expand or collapse the display per grouping. Decide if you want to see the time in your date display, or the date only. 6. Click a link in the ID column to view details of the time sheet. 7. To view associated purchase orders, click a link under Related Documents. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 3 7/10/26, 2:07 AM 8. To view the previous version of the time sheet click Previous Version. To return to the current version click Previous. Next Steps You can create invoices against associated purchase orders. See Creating and Managing Invoices, Credit Memos, and Debit Memos. Time Sheet Search Fields To find specific time sheets, you can filter new or existing searches by various criteria. To narrow a search, add criteria to any of the following fields listed under Search Filters: Search Field Description Customer Choose one of your customers from the dropdown. ID Time sheet number assigned by your customer’s procurement application. Time sheet numbers are case-sensitive. For example, TS123 is different from ts123. Date Range The date on which Ariba Network received the time sheet. You can choose one of the following ranges from the dropdown: Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 14 days, Last 31 days, or Other. The maximum date range is 31 days. Start Date End Date (For Other search) The dates on which the time sheet was received by Ariba Network. By default, the report includes today’s date and the preceding 14 days. Contractor The full name of the temporary employee. You can enter the first several letters of the employee’s name. Status The time sheet document status. Number of Results The number of search results to return. By default, the search returns up to 100 records. Creating a Time Sheet Use this procedure to create a time sheet on behalf of a contractor from your Ariba Network account. You don't need to complete this task if the contractor or contractor's supervisor submits time sheets from the customer's procurement application. Prerequisites You need to have the Time Sheet Management permission to create time sheets. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: In the upper right corner, choose Create Time & Expense Sheets . On the Orders and Releases page click Manage Time & Expenses 2. Search for or choose the appropriate customer from the list, and then click Next. 3. If the customer has more than one site, choose the appropriate business unit or location, and then click Next. 4. On the Manage Time Sheets and Expense Sheets page, do one of the following:, c This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 4 7/10/26, 2:07 AM To create time sheets individually, click Time Sheet under Create. To import multiple time sheets at a time, click Time Sheet under Import. 5. If you are importing time sheets, click Import next to the Import Time Sheets task and upload your time sheet files. Any time sheets in the import files are submitted for approval automatically.  Tip Click Download Data Dictionary to find out how to build your time sheet import files. 6. If you are creating an individual time sheet, choose the contractor for the On Behalf Of field, and then click Create Time Sheet. If the contractor is associated with more than one purchase order, choose the purchase order against which you are submitting this time sheet. If a contractor is associated with more than one line item in a purchase order, choose the line item against which you want to create the time sheet. 7. Click the Previous Time Sheet or Next Time Sheet buttons to navigate to a different time sheet. You won't see these buttons for time sheets configured for custom time periods. If the time sheet that you have navigated to is in a status other than Composing, you can only view the time sheet. You might see all or some of the following buttons: Create Time Sheet, Edit, Withdraw. You won't see the Edit and Withdraw buttons for time sheets that are approved. Time sheets that are denied also show a Resubmit button.  Note When using the Previous Time Sheet button to browse through previous time sheets, a time sheet may be created automatically for any period that didn't already have a time sheet. If you want to save an automatically generated time sheet, you need to click Save. If you don't click Save, the time sheet is deleted when you move away from it. If you click Save, the next time you open that time sheet, any changes you make are saved automatically. 8. Specify the pay code for each entry, and the start and stop times or the total hours worked, depending on your configuration. If needed, enter the name of the project and the task performed during the time entry. Create a line item for each day that the contractor works. 9. Do one or more of the following: To update entries, choose one or more entries and click Update. To add more entries, click Add or choose one or more entries, and then click Copy. 10. To enter more detailed information about an entry, click Show Details, and then enter the information in the Notes field. 11. Click Submit to submit the time sheet for approval. Time Sheet Statuses Ariba Network shows the current routing and processing statuses for each time sheet. Routing Statuses The Routing Status field describes whether a document made it successfully to its destination system. For documents you create, such as invoices and service sheets, the routing status informs you whether your document reached your customer's system. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 5 7/10/26, 2:07 AM For documents from your customer, such as orders, releases, time sheets, and remittances, the routing status lets you know whether the document reached SAP Business Network and any additional systems that you configured to accept incoming documents. SAP Business Network shows the following routing statuses: Status Description Acknowledged The document reached its destination system. This is the final routing status for documents. Duplicated This status applies only to remittance advice documents. A remittance advice document has this routing status if it's a duplicate of another remittance advice. Failed SAP Business Network could not send the document. In the case of a purchase order from your customer, SAP Business Network couldn't send the order to you through email, fax, cXML, or EDI. For example, your order fulfillment system could have experienced a problem that prevented SAP Business Network from successfully sending the order. You can resend orders that have a Failed routing status by clicking Resend at the top of the order. For failed invoices or service sheets, you need to correct any errors and resubmit them to your customer. For any other failed documents, contact your customer to resend them. Obsoleted After you cancel an invoice or edit and resubmit an invoice or service sheet, the original document moves to Obsoleted status, which indicates that you don't need to take any further action on the original document. Once a document has this routing status, you can't make any changes to it. Queued SAP Business Network is in the process of sending the document. Contact SAP Business Network Support if a document remains in this status for more than 30 minutes. Sent SAP Business Network sent the document successfully. For invoices or service sheets, SAP Business Network sent the document to your customer, but your customer hasn't yet acknowledged that they received it. If your document stays in this status for an extended period of time, contact your customer to see what needs to happen next.  Note If your customer allows it, you can cancel an invoice with a routing status of Sent. Document Statuses A document's status, such as Order Status or Invoice Status, describes where the document stands in its processing. If you update part of a document, SAP Business Network reports the partial status for the entire document, such as Partially Invoiced. For documents you create, such as invoices and service sheets, the document status lets you know where your customer is in the approval process for that document. For documents from your customer, such as orders and releases, the document status tells you where you are with regard to processing the document. SAP Business Network shows the following document statuses: This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 6 7/10/26, 2:07 AM Status Description Approved This status applies to invoices, service sheets, and time sheets. If the document doesn't have any errors, your customer approves it. After a document reaches Approved status, you can't make any changes.  Note An approved invoice means that your customer has approved it for payment. If you made a mistake, you need to send a credit memo to your customer. Canceled This status applies to invoices, service sheets, and remittance advice documents. After a document reaches Canceled status, you can't make any changes. In the case of a remittance advice document, your customer canceled the payment transaction. When a payment transaction fails, it needs to be canceled to allow for a subsequent attempt to complete the payment. Changed This status applies to orders and releases. Your customer sent a new version to replace the original document. Confirmed / Partially Confirmed These statuses apply to orders, releases, and time sheets. For orders and releases, Confirmed means that you agreed to ship all line items, while Partially Confirmed means that you agreed to ship some items. Failed This status applies to orders, releases, and remittance advice documents. SAP Business Network experienced a problem routing the document to your account or any additional systems that you configured to accept incoming documents. You can resend orders that have a Failed status by clicking Resend at the top of the order. For remittance advice documents, a Failed status means that the payment transaction failed. Invalid This status applies only to time sheets. Contact your customer to find out how to handle an invalid time sheet. Invoiced / Partially Invoiced These statuses apply to orders, releases, and service sheets. You have invoiced for the full amount of the document. Partially Invoiced means that you invoiced for only a part of the document amount. The Amount Invoiced column shows how much money you have invoiced or charged against the document. New This status applies to orders and releases for which you haven't yet updated the status. Obsoleted This document status applies only to time sheets that were replaced by an updated version. SAP Business Network shows only the updated version of the time sheet. On Hold This status applies only to remittance advice documents whose payment transaction was put on hold. Paid / Partially Paid These statuses apply to invoices and remittance advice documents. For invoices, your customer paid the invoice or is in the process of issuing payment.  Note Not every customer sends remittance information to SAP Business Network. If your invoice doesn't move past Approved status, you'll need to contact your customer to find out when to expect payment. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 7 7/10/26, 2:07 AM Status Description For remittance advice documents: Paid status means that the payment transaction was completed successfully. Partially Paid status means that payment is still due for the remaining amount shown on the remittance advice. Received / Partially Received These statuses apply to orders and releases. Your customer creates receipt documents in their system to acknowledge the products they physically received. The information from these receipts causes your purchase order status to update. When viewing a purchase order's details in your account, each line item shows the quantity of goods received. Rejected / Partially Rejected These statuses apply to invoices, service sheets, remittance advice documents, and time sheets. Invoices and service sheets are rejected in two cases: They fail validation on SAP Business Network. Your customer rejected the document in their processing system.  Note You can edit and resubmit rejected invoices or service sheets. Returned This status applies to orders and releases. Your customer creates receipt documents in their system to acknowledge the products they need to return. The information from these receipts causes your purchase order status to update. When viewing a purchase order's details in your account, each line item shows the quantity of goods returned. Sent This status applies to invoices and service sheets. The document reached your customer's system, but they haven't yet approved or rejected it. If your document stays in this status for a while, contact your customer to see what needs to happen next.  Note If your customer allows it, you can cancel invoices in Sent status. Serviced / Partially Serviced These statuses apply to service orders and releases. When a document reaches Serviced status, you can't create any more service sheets against planned service lines items. You can continue to create service sheets for unplanned service lines up to their hidden maximum amounts (which may be larger than their subtotals). The document status is set to Partially Serviced until all of the service lines are serviced. Shipped / Partially Shipped These statuses apply to orders and releases. Shipped status means that you shipped the entire order, while Partially Shipped means that you shipped only some of the items from the order.  Note You can still continue to confirm order line items regardless of the shipping status until you have confirmed all order lines. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 8 7/10/26, 2:07 AM Status Description Submitted This status applies only to time sheets that were submitted to your SAP Business Network account. This is custom documentation. For more information, please visit SAP Help Portal. 9

on SAP Business Network Content Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network This guide is for SAP Ariba users seeking a general understanding of test accounts that provide a safe way for new and established buying organizations and suppliers to configure and exercise SAP Business Network in a non-production environment. This guide applies to: • • SAP Business Network SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Related Guides Introduction to SAP Business Network Enabling Suppliers on SAP Business Network Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network PUBLIC 3 SAP Business Network Test Accounts Test accounts provide a safe way for new and established buying organizations and suppliers to configure and exercise SAP Business Network in a non-production environment. Test accounts are optional and complementary SAP Business Network accounts that allow buying organizations and suppliers to test customer catalogs, purchase order generation, routing, and receiving before implementing the same settings on their production accounts. New buying organizations typically spend several days testing their SAP Business Network solution and SAP Business Network configurations. Similarly, new suppliers spend several days testing their order receiving system and SAP Business Network configuration. Buying organizations and suppliers can also use test accounts when starting new relationships on SAP Business Network. Test accounts and production accounts are entirely separate. They do not share account data or configuration settings, nor do they communicate with each other. Because account administrators have the Test Account Administration permission, they can set up and administer a test account. Account administrators can also create users on the test account, just as they do on the production account. To perform testing, buying organizations and suppliers must both agree to use either test accounts or production accounts. Buying organizations control testing by changing their procurement or invoicing application’s configuration settings to use either test accounts or production accounts. Suppliers can use test accounts by themselves to generate test orders from their customer catalogs and also test their PunchOut catalogs. Suppliers can also generate order confirmations, ship notices, and invoices against test purchase orders. These documents can be generated online or sent through cXML. To test cXML documents, suppliers can use the automatic validation that SAP Business Network performs when it receives cXML documents. When buying organizations and suppliers are confident that their business processes are working in their test accounts, they can switch to their production accounts and replicate their test account settings in their production accounts.  Note • If a supplier’s SAP Business Network account is suspended, buyers can send documents to and receive documents from the supplier’s test account, but not the supplier’s production account. • • Test accounts cannot be used to create an account hierarchy and link child accounts. Buying organizations and suppliers can test their Internet connections and the transaction load capabilities of their software provided they follow SAP Business Network’s performance testing policy. For more information, see the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide in the Learning Center. 4 PUBLIC Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Test Accounts Test Account Tools for Suppliers Two tools are available to suppliers to test account settings: the catalog tester and the EDI Tester. The catalog tester allows suppliers to display customer catalog contents as buyers would see it. Suppliers can examine their item descriptions and other customer catalog fields to verify they appear correctly. Suppliers can select customer catalog items and add them to test purchase orders and also submit these test purchase orders to exercise the order routing method they configure in their test account. The EDI Tester helps with EDI integration by allowing suppliers to test their inbound X12 EDI documents (order confirmations, ship notices, and invoices). This tool uploads supplier’s implemented EDI documents and validates them against SAP Business Network EDI implementation guidelines to ensure that their documents are error-free when sending them to their buyers. For more information, see the Account Settings and Profile Configuration and EDI Integration guides in the supplier's Learning Center. Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network SAP Business Network Test Accounts PUBLIC 5 Test Account Creation Buyer and supplier account administrators can create their test accounts in SAP Business Network in one of two ways: by choosing to switch to a test account for the first time, or automatically when a supplier accepts a buyer’s relationship request. Account When buyer and supplier account administrators click the Switch To Test Account link from the Settings icon menu on SAP Business Network for the first time, SAP Business Network creates a test account. When a buyer searches for and requests a relationship with a supplier that is already registered on SAP Business Network, SAP Business Network sends the supplier an email notification with information and instructions to accept the relationship request. Once the supplier accepts and completes the trading relationship request, a test account for the buyer and supplier is automatically created on SAP Business Network. Organizations can have only one test account, and only the account administrator can create it. Account administrators signed into a test account can create additional user accounts for testing and assign permissions to them.  Note Before a supplier can create a test account, the production account must be fully enabled by a buying organization. The following table lists the default notation used for test account user name, company name, and organization ID (you can change any of these values except organization ID): Property Notation Example User name Prepended with “test-” test-judy@workchairs.com Company Name Appended with “- TEST” Work Chairs, Inc. - TEST Organization ID Appended with “-T” D-U-N-S: 94-288-8710-T NetworkID: AN100000123-T  Note Production purchase orders can be sent only to supplier production accounts, not to test accounts. This restriction prevents the loss of production purchase orders. For more information, see the SAP Business Network Buyer Administration Guide (for buying organizations) and Account Settings and Profile Configuration (for suppliers) guides. 6 PUBLIC Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Test Account Creation Creating and Accessing the Test Account as a Buyer A buyer account administrator can access the test account from the Home dashboard. Other users (and the account administrator) can log in directly to the test account using their account user names and passwords. After a buyer signs in, the buyer can add other users, add suppliers, and subscribe to customer catalogs. Prerequisites To test orders and customer catalogs, you must have a relationship with a supplier that also has a test account. Procedure 1. Sign into your production account on SAP Business Network. 2. Click your name and choose Switch to Test Account. 3. In the Changing Account Mode dialog box, click OK. If you have not used your test account before, SAP Business Network prompts you for a new user name and password. 4. Enter and confirm your test account user name and password. Click OK. SAP Business Network signs you in to your test account and displays the label Test Mode at the top of the pages. The test account ANID is your production account ANID appended with a -T. Click on your name and choose Switch to Production Account to switch back to the production account. SAP Business Network copies company profile information from your production account to your test account. The rest of your test account settings are set to their default values. You can change these settings at any time, and they do not affect your production account. 5. Click Manage Profile in the user name menu to check your test account setup. Next Steps After you have created the test account, you can add users and suppliers, and subscribe to customer catalogs. After users have activated their test account, they can directly log into their test account. Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Test Account Creation PUBLIC 7 Creating and Accessing the Test Account as a Supplier A supplier account administrator can access the supplier test account from the user name drop-down on SAP Business Network. Account administrators and other users (and ) can directly sign into the test account using their test account user names and passwords. Prerequisites To use a test account, you must be the account administrator. Procedure 1. Sign into your production account on SAP Business Network. 2. Click the Account Settings icon and choose Switch to Test ID. 3. In the Changing Account Mode dialog box, click OK. If you have not used your test account before, SAP Business Network prompts you for a new user name and password. 4. Enter and confirm your test account user name and password. Click OK. SAP Business Network signs you in to your test account and shows Test Mode at the top of each page. SAP Business Network copies company profile information from your production account to your test account. The rest of your test account settings are set to their default values. You can change these settings at any time. They do not affect your production account. 5. In the top right of the page, click Company Settings to check your test account setup. To identify the current account mode, check the area at the top of the page. If Test Mode shows at the top of the page, your account is in test mode. Otherwise, your account is in production mode. Next Steps After account administrators sign into the test account, they can add other users. Supplier account administrators can switch back to the production account by clicking Switch To Production in their user menu unless they signed in directly to the test account. 8 PUBLIC Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Test Account Creation Testing Methods for Suppliers Suppliers can test their systems with or without customer interactions. Usually suppliers test first without customer interactions, and then progress to testing with them. Which testing method you use depends on the type of testing you perform. You must weigh the advantages and limitations of both types of testing. You can perform both types of testing, one after the other. Test Method Benefits and Limitations Without customer • This testing method does not depend on customers, so you can perform testing iterations more rapidly. • To use the catalog tester, you do not need to modify your customer catalogs. Simply upload them to your Test account. • The catalog tester tests only customer catalogs that are smaller than four MB and displays only the first 300 customer catalog items. The catalog tester ignores partial catalog items, those that do not have values for all required fields. • Testing through a customer’s procurement application provides the most realistic and thorough testing, but requires the customer to coordinate with you. • To test through a customer, you must manually modify your customer catalogs by appending “-T” to the Supplier ID for all customer catalog items before uploading and publishing them to your SAP Business Network Test account. This modification ensures that the Supplier ID in your customer catalogs matches the Supplier ID used by SAP Business Network and procurement applications. With customer Most suppliers first test on their own to check basic functionality, then they ask their customers to send orders and test customer catalogs and PunchOut. Testing Without a Customer Testing without a customer enables you to learn the CIF or cXML catalog formats, debug PunchOut websites, and demonstrate customer catalogs or PunchOut. Your test account has a built-in catalog tester for sending yourself simple purchase orders. The catalog tester acts as a simple procurement application, allowing you to search and browse customer catalog contents, create simple requisitions, and send purchases through SAP Business Network. The catalog tester also allows you to debug your interactive PunchOut website and demonstrate it to prospective customers. The catalog tester sends out cXML 1.1 messages, and can receive both cXML 1.0 and 1.1 messages. It allows you to view and edit these cXML messages. Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Testing Methods for Suppliers PUBLIC 9 Testing with a Customer Testing with a customer lets you simulate the buying experience using the customer’s procurement system. Perform this type of testing after debugging your customer catalogs. You need to upload customer catalogs to your test account, unless your buyer’s test account already has them. Customer catalogs in a supplier’s test account are only visible to their buyer’s test accounts, not to the buyer’s production accounts. Switching between testing and production requires action only on the buyer’s side. Buyers need to modify Ariba Buyer settings. 10 PUBLIC Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Testing Methods for Suppliers

file://SBN/split/Using Test Accounts on.content: Customer Catalog Testing The catalog tester allows a supplier to test static catalogs, PunchOut catalogs, and order routing without requiring customer interactions. The catalog tester simulates a user buying experience, allowing suppliers to demonstrate catalogs and PunchOut sites. Testing a Customer Catalog After suppliers specify an order routing method and upload a functional customer catalog to their test accounts, supplier should test their customer catalogs with the catalog tester. Prerequisites The catalog tester cannot test customer catalogs larger than 4 MB. Context Once suppliers choose a customer catalog strategy, they can test uploading customer catalogs by switching to their test account and using the catalog tester. When using the catalog tester to perform catalog testing and detailed debugging of their PunchOut websites suppliers do not need to coordinate with their buyers. SAP Business Network supports customer catalogs in CIF and cXML formats. Suppliers can examine and edit cXML messages passed to and from their PunchOut websites, and they can modify the cXML as they step through all the phases of cXML PunchOut and OrderRequest transactions. Some buyers might request custom catalog content for their procurement systems. More advanced suppliers can host PunchOut sites where they provide catalog items through Web storefronts. Using a test account and the catalog tester, suppliers can debug these customer catalogs before publishing them. After suppliers test a sample customer catalog, they can upload the final customer catalog to SAP Business Network and publish it either as a private catalog to specific buyers or as a public catalog to all buyers. The catalog tester simulates the following SAP Ariba applications in basic test mode: Ariba Buyer 8.2.2 and later, SAP Ariba Buying and SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing. Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Customer Catalog Testing PUBLIC 11 Procedure 1. Sign into your test account. 2. Click Catalogs to display a list of all your catalogs. Only the catalogs in your test account are visible. You can test catalogs before or after publishing them, but they must first pass validation. SAP Business Network displays an error message if you attempt to test a catalog that has not been validated. 3. Select the customer catalog you want to test and click Test. SAP Business Network displays the first 300 items in the customer catalog. Partial items (items that do not have values for all required fields) do not appear. You can display additional items by clicking the column heading to sort the customer catalog. 4. To search for an item by description, click the expand arrow next to Search. 5. Click View Item Details to see the complete customer catalog information for all items. To return to the regular view, click Hide Item Details. Related Information Testing a Non-PunchOut Item [page 12] Testing a PunchOut Item [page 13] Testing a Non-PunchOut Catalog Item Test non-PunchOut items to verify that they are handled as you expect. Procedure 1. In the catalog tester, click a check box next to an item and click Add to Cart to display the Submit Cart page. 2. You can edit the quantity or delete items. If you change the quantity, click Update Quantity to update the total amount. 3. Click Submit Cart to display the View Order page. The View Order page contains the Purchase Order cXML Code and the Response cXML Code tabs, where you can view the cXML contents and the cXML response from SAP Business Network. Next Steps • • 12 Click Edit cXML Purchase Order to make changes to the test purchase order. Click Create New Test to start a new test for the same catalog and to generate additional purchase orders. PUBLIC Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Customer Catalog Testing Related Information Switching to a Buyer Test Account [page 7] Testing a PunchOut Item [page 13] Testing a PunchOut Catalog Item Test PunchOut items to verify that they are handled as you expect. Procedure 1. From the catalog tester, choose the procurement product to simulate: • • • • • Ariba Buyer 7.0 Ariba Buyer 8.0 Ariba Buyer 8.1 Ariba Buyer 8.2.x SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing 2. Select a credential setting in the Use Credential Set pull-down menu or click Search for more on the dropdown menu. 3. Click Shop to open a browser window that displays the web page for customer catalog. 4. Select items and check out. SAP Business Network returns to the catalog tester and displays the items you selected under the Submit Cart section. 5. If necessary, initiate Edit or Inspect sessions to punch out again. 6. If desired, click View/Edit PunchOut Cart to view and modify the cXML PunchOut order message details for your shopping cart. If you edit the cXML message, click Update PunchOut Cart. 7. Click Submit Cart to display the View Order page. The View Order page contains the Purchase Order cXML Code and the Response cXML Code tabs, where you can view the cXML contents and the cXML response from Ariba Network. Viewing cXML content can be extremely useful when you are developing and debugging PunchOut websites. Next Steps Next Steps • • Click Edit cXML Purchase Order to make any changes to the test purchase order. Click Create New Test to start a new test for the same customer catalog and to generate additional purchase orders. Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Customer Catalog Testing PUBLIC 13 . Related Information Switching to a Buyer Test Account [page 7] Testing a Non-PunchOut Item [page 12] Viewing and Editing Outgoing and Incoming cXML Documents The catalog tester allows you to edit the contents of outgoing cXML documents and view the contents of incoming cXML documents. It simulates the PunchOut behavior of SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing, Ariba Buyer 9r1, 8.2.x, 8.1, 8.0, or 7.0. Ariba Buyer 9r1, 8.2.x, 8.1, 8.0, and 7.0 generate slightly different PunchOutOrderMessage and OrderRequest documents: • SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing: • Ariba Buyer 9r1: • • • The DOCTYPE element refers to http://xml.cXML.org/schemas/cXML/1.2.009/cXML.dtd. There is an orderVersion attribute added to the OrderRequestHeader in the OrderRequest. This attribute specifies the order version number of change orders, starting with “1” for the original order. The DOCTYPE element refers to http://xml.cXML.org/schemas/cXML/1.2.008/cXML.dtd. There is a quoteStatus attribute added to the PunchOutOrderMessageHeader in the PunchOutOrderMesssage. This attribute specifies if the order is “pending” or “final.” If quoteStatus is “final,” the transaction is complete. Ariba Buyer 7.0: • • • • 14 There is a PaymentTerm element added to the OrderRequestHeader element in the OrderRequest. This element defines either the net term (without discount) or the discount term (with discount). Ariba Buyer 8.0: • • • The DOCTYPE element refers to http://xml.cXML.org/schemas/cXML/1.2.011/cXML.dtd. Ariba Buyer 8.1: • • • The DOCTYPE element refers to http://xml.cXML.org/schemas/cXML/1.2.019/cXML.dtd. Ariba Buyer 8.2.x: • • • The DOCTYPE element refers to the latest version of cXML available on http://www.cxml.org. The DOCTYPE element refers to http://xml.cXML.org/schemas/cXML/1.1.010/cXML.dtd. The included Extrinsics are “UserEmail,” “UniqueName,” and “CostCenter.” There is a Contact element. There are Shipping and Tax elements in the OrderRequest PUBLIC Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Customer Catalog Testing Customizing a Credential Set for PunchOut Catalogs Suppliers might want to create a credential set for each trading relationship. Context The catalog tester enables suppliers to create multiple credential sets. Proceed through each step in the process to review and, if desired, edit each cXML document. Suppliers can edit both outgoing and incoming documents by: • Selecting additional credentials for the From element. cXML documents sometimes contain multiple credentials, so suppliers might want to exercise their PunchOut site’s credential-domain recognition. Supplier’s PunchOut sites must recognize the NetworkID of the catalog tester: AN01000002779-T. • Changing the parts of cXML documents that appear in text-edit boxes. For example, in PunchOutSetupRequest documents, suppliers can edit or add Extrinsic elements to simulate additional data passed by procurement applications. Another example that suppliers might try is to enter different values in the SelectedItem element. Procedure 1. In the catalog tester, click Customize Set to display the customize credentials page, where you can create a custom credential setting for your PunchOut catalog. 2. If you make any changes, click Save Custom Credential. 3. Click Preview to review the cXML PunchOutSetupRequest. 4. Click Shop if you want to PunchOut to the shopping website and select items. 5. Click Send Request to view/edit the cXML PunchOutSetupResponse document. 6. Click Process Response. A new browser window opens and displays the web page for that item. Navigate your website, select items, and check out. SAP Business Network returns to the catalog tester and displays the items you selected on the Submit Cart page. 7. Click View/Edit Punchout Cart to view/edit the cXML PunchOut Order Message. 8. Click Update PunchOut Cart if you make any changes and then click Submit Cart. 9. Click Submit Cart to display the View Order page. The View Order page contains the Purchase Order cXML Code and the Response cXML Code tabs, where you can view the cXML contents and the cXML response from SAP Business Network. 10. Click Edit cXML Purchase Order to make any changes to the test purchase order. 11. Click Create New Test to start a new test for the same catalog. 12. If you configured your account to send cXML orders, examine the orders in your order receiving system. SAP Business Network routes purchase orders to you through your preferred order routing method within a few minutes. 13. Delete the purchase orders from your order receiving system. Do not allow your system to execute test orders. Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Customer Catalog Testing PUBLIC 15  Note You cannot delete test orders from SAP Business Network, but you can set their status to Shipped so you can ignore them. For the most realistic testing, use the same order routing method as you use for production, including an order receiving system if you have one. Warn order processing personnel not to fill orders sent from the test customer. Troubleshooting Order Routing Problems During Catalog Testing If you encounter order routing problems, you can troubleshoot the order in a series of logical steps. Procedure 1. Do one of the following: • • For suppliers without SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: Choose For suppliers with SAP Business Network for Supply Chain: Choose Orders Orders Purchase Orders . Orders and Releases . 2. View your account’s transactions. 3. Find the test transaction in the list to ensure that it was logged. Test transactions always list “Catalog Tester” as the customer. 4. Click the order number for the test transaction to display the details of the purchase order. 5. Click the Order History tab to display processing information for the purchase order. 6. Click Status History to see additional processing information. 7. Click the Account Settings icon, and choose Settings Electronic Order Routing . 8. On the Electronic Order Routing tab, examine your order routing configuration. Ensure that your email address or website URL is correct, and click Save. 9. After correcting the problem, click Resend on the Order Detail page to resend the order, and then check that there are no remaining problems. 10. Delete the purchase order from your order receiving and management system so that your system does not execute the test order.  Note You cannot delete test orders from SAP Business Network. 16 PUBLIC Using Test Accounts on SAP Business Network Customer Catalog Testing Important Disclaimers and Legal Information Hyperlinks Some links are classified by an icon and/or a mouseover text.
