file://SBN/split/SCC : Indirect Cross Tr.content: SCC / Indirect Cross Training Advanced Ship Notice INTERNAL ONLY 1 Agenda 01 Advanced Ship Notice Overview 02 Handling Units & Summary ASN 03 Technical Acknowledgments 04 Practical Exam Scenarios 2 SCC Advanced Ship Notice Overview Today we will be focusing on the SCC Advanced Ship Notice Document. Advanced Ship Notice (ASN) Summary ASN ASN with Handling Units Return ASNs Component ASNs o We’ll be looking at it’s common use cases within Supply Chain, and its extended capability within SCC SAP Business Network for Suppliers and Buyers. o This includes, Summary ASNs, ASN with Handling Units. But we will touch on the Component ASNs and Return ASNs briefly. 3 SCC Advanced Ship Notice 4 Supply Chain Collaboration Solutions Glossary A Supply Chain in the context of Buyers and Suppliers is the structured flow of materials, information, and commitments that allows suppliers to deliver goods, and Buyers to convert those inputs into finished offerings. This can be anything from; Electronics, Cars, Medicine, Food or Appliances. These are all industries that currently transact via SAP Business Network SCC. For a full breakdown of processes and documents: SAP Help Standard B2B Formats SCC Process Overview Consignment Collaboration In consignment collaboration, the supplier sends consignments to the buyer, but retains ownership of the consignments until the buyer pays for the assignment the buyer consumes. The transfer of ownership, and often of location, to the buyer at the time of consumption is called a consignment movement. The consignment movement information flows from Buyer to Supplier. Subcontract Collaboration This solution supports the following features for subcontract purchase orders and their associated documents, which are used in contract manufacturing collaboration. Forecast Collaboration Forecast collaboration allows buyers to send forecasts of future procurement to suppliers. Suppliers can send commitments to buyers based on forecast demand. Quality Collaboration Quality inspection collaboration supports buyer inspections of supplier facilities. Supplier Managed Inventory (SMI) This module provides suppliers with visibility into the buyer's inventory and demand levels so that they can replenish inventory based on established minimum and maximum stock levels. Schedule Agreement Collaboration Form of an outline agreement to procure items on predetermined dates according to an aligned Schedule. Returns Collaboration The returns process deals with the business process of returning goods to the Supplier. It also deals with receiving credit for the returned items. Material Traceability Capture complete material provenance from raw material to finished product to enhance safety, sustainability, and customer loyalty. Please note: Not a process for Supplier Integration but adds to the importance of correct Batch Information on Orders / Ship Notices. 5 Advanced Ship Notice Overview 6 SCC Advanced Ship Notice Use Cases Subcontract PO Direct Material PO Order Confirmation Order Confirmation Component Ship Notice (Buyer) Ship Notice (Supplier) Receipt Request Goods Receipt Component Consumption Invoice o The Advanced Ship Notice is a core document for many of the Supply Chain flows and is utilized in different ways depending on the SCC Process. o Using the Subcontracting Supply Chain process as an example, the Ship Notice acts as both a Buyer and Suppler issued Document. o A more familiar scenario would be Purchase Order Collaboration + Return’s Collaboration where the Buyer can also an issue an ASN for the goods needing to be returned. o Returns could also be a part of the Subcontracting flow as well, so there could technically be three different types of ASNs being sent a part of the full process. Component Inventory Status Ship Notice (Supplier) Goods Receipt Goods Receipt (Negative Value) Invoice Return Ship Notice (Buyer) Credit Memo 7 SCC Advanced Ship Notice Use Cases Advanced Ship Notice (ASN) o The two type of Ship Notices that we’ll be focusing on today is the Summary ASN, and ASN with Handling Units as they’re both commonly utilized in Purchase Order Collaboration. o These two types of ship notices are often used together to meet Buyer specific Supply Chain requirements where a single shipment needs to cover multiple orders due to the high daily volume of materials being supplied by the Supplier. o Other SCC Processes can also utilize these two forms of shipNotices in addition the specific SCC process requirements that would be needed. Summary ASN ASN with Handling Units Return ASNs Component ASNs 8 Advanced Ship Notice – Handling Units 9 What are Ship Notice Handling Units? o A handling unit (HU) is a logistic unit consisting of packaging materials and goods (materials). o Typically, a company does not move individual pieces of different materials, rather, it moves quantities of materials grouped together as packages. o Within Supply Chain, the HU’s being shipped to fulfil the Order quantity is detailed within the ASN by the Supplier. This allows the Buyer to automate the receipting process when the individual HUs labels are scanned into the Buyer’s Warehouse. o Handling Units can also be nested within other Packaging materials to ensure that each level of the package (Pallet > Carton > Box) is detailed by the Supplier to the degree of detail needed by the Buyer’s warehouse / logistics team and the Buyer’s systems. 10

file://SBN/split/SCC : Indirect Cross Tr.content: SAP Business Network: Handling Units (HU) If enabled by the Buyer’s solution, Suppliers can send Handling Unit (HU) information on the Ship Notice via the Business Network. This configuration is completed by the SCC Buyer Integration team during the deployment of the Buyer’s Solution. Please remember that is not configured by the SCC Supplier Integration team. Once implemented, the HU information on the Ship Notice can be created in two ways: • Fully inside the Supplier’s ERP and sent as a cXML shipNotice to the Buyer via the SAP Business Network (passing through the Supplier’s account). • Manually via the Supplier’s SAP Business Network account – Portal interface using the packing functionality when creating the Ship Notice. (Screenshot example). Suppliers must confirm the scope of Handling Units with their Buyer contact directly as not all materials may require HU information on the Ship Notice. 11 SAP Business Network: Handling Units (HU) Hierarchy - Example Buyer’s packaging instructions are maintained within their Buyer ERP. Below here is an example of the packaging instructions. Please note, each Buyer will have different variations and flavors of the packaging instructions, this could be generic for all materials, or for specific Buyer materials. Packaging Hierarchy Pallet Packing instruction specifies that the pallet contains the carton. The pallet is a handling unit. Carton Packing instruction specifies that the carton contains the box. The carton is a handling unit. Box Packing instruction specifies that the bottle is packed in the box. Each small box is also a handling unit. Auxiliary material can be associated with any of the levels of packaging. For example: foil, wrapping, lids, crates, ect… 12 ShipNotice with Handling Units: cXML Example o Example structure of a ShipNotice Line including Handling Unit information for a single pallet. o The packaging information highlighted must be created by the Supplier’s system and populated as per the Buyer’s cXML requirements and logistical requirements. o The packaging segment is repeated for each Handling Unit sent. For nested / low level handling units, the individual package must reference the Parent package SSCC / HU Number and the Parent PackID. o SSCC / HU Number values should be generated by the Supplier and must align with your Buyer’s logistic requirements and format: character, length, sequencing and character casing as examples. This not something that is defined by the SAP Business Network. For Example: Handling Unit Number Buyer Requirement SAP BN Portal Integrated Supplier 0008000000121 0008000000121 0008000000121 [0008000] - Company Pre-fix [000121] – Serial Reference [0008000] - Company Pre-fix [000121] – Serial Reference [0008000] - Company Pre-fix [000121] – Serial Reference 13 ShipNotice with Handling Units: cXML Example cont. o To add perspective; the cXML segment shown is for a single Pallet only. The packaging segment for each ASN Line is repeated for each separate pallet, box, carton needing to be sent to fulfil the shipment. 14 ShipNotice with Handling Units: cXML Example cont. o The next packaging Segment for the ASN line details the Carton on the pallet. This packaging segment is also repeated as many times as there is Cartons on the single Pallet. o For example, if the material quantity being shipped is 500, the supplier would need to ship 10 pallets. This is because the pallet can hold 5 Carton and each Carton contains 20 Materials. For this scenario, the packaging segment would need to be repeated 30 times within the ASN Line each of the HUs being sent. 15 Integrated Suppliers: Handling Units (HU) – Common cXML Fields Below are a list of common fields that are expected on the cXML Ship Notice when Handling Units are sent. Packaging Codes, Descriptions, and dimensions is MasterData that must be shared by the Buyer with each of their Suppliers. Without this Master data alignment, incorrect packaging detail in the ASN will cause the document to fail once received by the Buyer’s ERP. Specific cXML requirements will be flagged in the Supplier Integration Guidelines. Field Value PackagingCode Commonly the Buyer’s Material ID but may differ per your Buyer’s Logistical requirements. Dimensions Handling Unit Dimensions & Quantity for: • Length • Height • Width • Volume • Gross Weight • Unit Net Weight Each dimension requires the expected unit of measure being maintained by your Buyer. Type, Description The handling Unit type being sent. • Package • Material (HU should be flagged as type “Material” if the HU contains actual goods) Buyer’s description of the Handling Unit package type. Must align exactly. For example: • Test Pallet 001 • Carton PackagingLevelCode Level of packaging. Used when there are multiple packages for a material item, (1, 2 or 3). • • “1” as the highest level of the packing hierarchy. “Auxiliary” for auxiliary packaging materials. Field Value PackageTypeCodeIdentifierCode Packaging Code of the Handling Unit. For example: • MBPALLET001 • SPACINGCARTON ShippingContainerSerialCode Shipping Container Serial Code / Handling Unit Number. Value must be generated by your ERP for each Handling Unit as per your Buyer’s logistical requirements. ShippingContainerSerialCodeReference Reference to the parent Handling Unit for nested packages. OrderedQuantity Ordered quantity- Quantity of the original ordered quantity. DispatchedQuantity Dispatched Quantity – Number of items the HU package contains. Package Extrinsics required for Business Network Generated Labels • • • • AribaNetwork.packId – Package ID Value AribaNetwork.parentPackId – Parent Pack ID AribaNetwork.mixedInstruction – To pack multiple materials in the same packaging material and in a single handling unit. AribaNetwork.shipNoticeLineIndex – Ship Notice Line Number 16 Integrated Suppliers: cXML shipNotices with Handling Units The Buyer’s handling unit and specific packaging instructions for the materials in scope must be maintained by the Supplier’s system and populated on the cXML shipNotice as per the Buyer’s logistical and technical requirements. o This ensures the HU information and packaging instructions align between the Buyer’s ERP and Supplier’s system. o The SAP Business Network does not populate HU Information on the integrated cXML ShipNotice once received by the Supplier’s or Buyer’s account (Please note that network does not alter the cXML data being sent by the supplier). In some instances, Packaging instructions for Orders are provided by Buyers in the form of an attachment on the Purchase Order when sent to the SAP Business Network. o If considering integrating both the Purchase Order and Ship Notice that contain attachments, please ensure you’re able to receive and send MIME envelopes via your HTTPs connection. Your Buyer may send a HU flag at the Purchase order line level. If an ASN without HU Information is sent against a PO Line with the below flag, the ASN will fail when attempting to send to the SAP Business Network. 17 ShipNotice with Handling Units: cXML Example – Nested Pallet and Carton relationship o The Pallet SSCC / HU Value is referenced on the inner level (Carton) Package. This would represent a nested Handling Unit where there are two levels of packages are detailed by the Supplier. A third level can be detailed, but its not common due to added complexity. o Depending on the Buyer’s Solution and Logistic requirements, nested Packaging / HU may not be required and only a single level (pallet) could be required on the ASN. But this Buyer and supplier specific, so please refer to the Supplier Integration Guidelines for that Buyer. 18 Shipment Labels 19 Shipment Labels o Although the Package / HU Label is not a direct part of the Supplier Integration project and cXML connection, it is still an important aspect to understand as it can impact how the supplier will interact with the Network / Buyer once the Ship Notice flow is integrated. o This is be a generic sample of a HU label. Each Buyer would have their own layout and requirements that would be aligned with the Supplier as part of their Business Relationship. Depending on the Buyer packaging requirements, this label would be physically taped to each of the Handling Units / Packages being shipped similar how you would post a parcel. o Shipping labels are used in combination with the Handling Unit information populated in the Ship Notice by the Supplier. o For example; the SSCC Code / HU Code is converted into the barcode that can be interpreted by the the Buyer’s own warehouse scanning solution. This barcode is used to automatically receipt the goods into the system once physically received. This is why it’s integral that the Business Logistic requirements are aligned directly between the Buyer and Supplier as it has flow on affect with the movement of physical goods and not it’s not requirements that an SAP SI would know. 20

file://SBN/split/SCC : Indirect Cross Tr.content: Shipment Labels If configured by the Buyer’s SCC solution, labels for each of the Handling Unit’s / Packages based off the ASN can be downloaded and printed by the Supplier via the portal. This is only once the ShipNotice is received successfully by the Network. This applies to both Portal and Integrated Suppliers. o Alternatively, the Integrated Supplier may wish to generate the labels themselves in alignment with Buyer’s label requirements to avoid having manually print it from the Business Network. Please Remember: Not all Buyer’s will have labels in the Network or may choose to keep this process outside of the Network. There is no mechanism to integrate the Packaging / HU label or receive the label via a HTTPs integrated connection. 21 Integrated Suppliers Exception Handling 22 Integrated Suppliers Exception Handling – Common HU Statuses & Errors The table provides an overview of common response’s that the Supplier may receive on the cXML Status Update message from your Buyer’s ERP once the ASN is received. Scenario Status Detail Successful Ship Notice with HU Information. Success – 200 (OK) code="200" text="OK">0001 inbound delivery/deliveries created (nos. 180005612 to 180005612) Incorrect HU Package Type Code used “MyPallet” Failed - 406 (Not Acceptable) code="406" text="Not Acceptable">Material MyPallet does not exist Error while generating packaging data Due to the of range errors, it is highly recommend that the error detail is consumed by the receiving system (Supplier) and made visible to the relevant end users that would action the changes to the Ship Notice. Main / Parent HU Number previously used on a different Ship Notice. Failed - 406 (Not Acceptable) code="406" text="Not Acceptable">Handling unit 700000945 already in existence Error while generating packaging data o If further investigation of the Ship Notice error is required, the supplier would need to contact the Buyer directly as they would have insight into the failure reason. Reference to a Main / Parent HU number previously used on a different Ship Notice. Failed - 406 (Not Acceptable) code="406" text="Not Acceptable">Handling unit 700000945 already in existence Error while generating packaging data. Incorrect HU number format. Failed - 406 (Not Acceptable) code="406" text="Not Acceptable">InccorrectHU1 is not in interval that is provided for this pack.material type Error while generating packaging data. o Please note: this table is to be used as a guide only as your Buyer may have different or additional responses configured within their individual ERP. 23 Handling Units: Portal and Integrated comparison Handling Unit Information Portal Supplier Integrated Supplier Packaging Instructions, Package Dimensions and Handling Unit Information. Preconfigured by the Buyer within the SAP Business Network and available to the supplier during the Ship Notice creation and packing process for the material. Detailed packaging instructions, package dimensions, and HU information for each material must be maintained by the supplier within their own system/ERP. Please work with your Buyer directly to ensure the alignment of packaging instructions for each of the materials in scope. Shipping Container Serial Code (SSCC) / Handling Unit Number Automatically generated by the Business Network, based on the buyer’s packaging instructions during the ship notice creation process within the supplier portal. The packaging instructions are defined by the Buyer in the network. Ship notice status (Acknowledged, Failed, or Rejected). Visible within the Supplier Portal with exception reason visible via the document history. Ship notice exception / failure and reason relating to Handling Units when it is received by the Buyer’s ERP (after the network). Email notifications can be configured for Ship Notice Failures. Packaging Labels Labels Pre-configured by the Buyer in the network can be downloaded manually via the Supplier portal after the Ship Notice with HU information has been created. Supplier system must generate the SSCC / Handling Unit Number and populate it on the cXML shipNotice document. Please note: the handling unit number for each package must meet the Buyer’s logistic requirements. An incorrect SSCC value will affect both the barcode and receipting process within the Buyer’s ERP. cXML Status Update document is sent from the network to the Supplier’s system and will include error information if the Ship Notice with handling units fails in the Buyer’s ERP (after the network). Email notification for Ship Notice Failures can be enabled as well. Can be manually downloaded from the portal after the integrated cXML ShipNotice has been sent to the SAP Business Network. Packaging labels can not be sent via HTTPs connections or email. 24 Integrated Suppliers: Document Validation & Exception Handling • HU values are not validated by the SAP Business Network itself. The Ship Notice will successfully route/delivered to the Buyer’s ERP if the cXML syntax structure of the file is valid. • Validation of the HU information is done on the Buyer ERP level (after the network) and is validated against the Buyer’s own internal masterdata and material master. • Please be aware that the processing of the HU information occurs after the first successful acknowledgement by the SAP Business Network. A subsequent Status Update Request will be sent from the Buyer ERP to the SAP Business Network advising on the Ship Notice’s new Status (Accepted, Rejected or Failed). • Example: If the Ship Notice fails validation within the Buyer’s ERP, the Buyer will send a Status Update message changing the Ship Notice’s “Acknowledged” Status to “Failed”, along with the reason. • It is highly recommend that Integrated Suppliers consume the asynchronous Status Update cXML message that is sent from the Buyer’s ERP when HU validation occurs. This ensures that the status of the Ship Notice is aligned between both the Supplier and Buyer. For more information, please refer to the cXML Technical Acknowledgment guide (PDF): https://support.ariba.com/item/view/199235. • cXML example below: Status Update sent to the Supplier as the Buyer’s ERP was unable to process the HU information on the Ship Notice. 25 Buyer & Supplier Scenario 26 Buyer & Supplier Scenario: Ship Notice with Handling Units Purchase Order Received Materials are Picked for Shipment Labels Generated Battery Co Ltd Technical Acknowledgment & Goods Receipt Goods Shipped, cXML ASN sent Technical Acknowledgment Goods Receipt Supplier Warehouse ASN & Shipment of Goods Buyer (DC101) 27 Buyer & Supplier Scenario: Ship Notice with Handling Units Purchase Order Received Materials are Picked for Shipment Labels Generated Goods Shipped, cXML ASN sent Technical Acknowledgment Goods Receipt The Supplier “Battery Co Ltd” receives the Purchase Order. It’s been agreed previously with the Buyer that due to weight limits when moving materials within the warehouse, only 5 Cartons of Batteries can be loaded onto a single pallet. The specific Carton’s used must be the double walled cardboard variant. The Battery Supplier’s Warehouse team starts to pick the goods needed to fulfil the order of 700 batteries. As it’s an order for 700 Batteries the Supplier’s warehouse system knows that to fulfill the order they would need 7 pallets, each with 5 cartons containing 20 batteries. 28 Buyer & Supplier Scenario: Ship Notice with Handling Units Labels Generated Once the goods are prepared, the supplier’s Warehouse system / ERP would generate the respective Handling Unit Codes / SSCC codes for each of the Pallets and Cartons being shipped. Based on the supplier’s own master data, the dimensions, packaging weights, HU hierarchy will also be determined at this stage and populated on the cXML Ship Notice. Goods Shipped, cXML ASN sent o If a supplier is creating the ASN on the Portal or just downloading the labels; it’s at this stage where the supplier will manually create the ASN, and/or download the labels from the portal to stick onto each of the Handling Units being shipped on this ASN. o Alternatively, the Battery Co Ltd Supplier has an agreement with the buyer to use labels generated from their own system rather than the SAP Business Network. Purchase Order Received Materials are Picked for Shipment Technical Acknowledgment Goods Receipt 29 Buyer & Supplier Scenario: Ship Notice with Handling Units Purchase Order Received Materials are Picked for Shipment Labels Generated Goods Shipped, cXML ASN sent The labels are printed by their system and are physically taped to each of the Cartons and Pallets and loaded into the truck ready for shipment to the Buyer. Normally, it’s at this stage the cXML Ship Notice that we see in the Network is sent via the Integrated Connection Technical Acknowledgment Goods Receipt Supplier Warehouse ASN & Shipment of Goods Buyer (DC101) 30

file://SBN/split/SCC : Indirect Cross Tr.content: Buyer & Supplier Scenario: Ship Notice with Handling Units Purchase Order Received Materials are Picked for Shipment Labels Generated Goods Shipped, cXML ASN sent Technical Acknowledgment Goods Receipt Once it passes the SAP Business Network validation successfully, it is then received by the Buyer’s ERP for final validation of the Handling Unit’s / Packing Information populated on the ASN. o If there any exceptions relating to the ASN packaging / HU information, the Technical Acknowledgment from the Buyer’s system will state the failure reason (for example: duplicate HU ID used). The goods are physically received by the Buyer and scanned into the warehouse using the labels. The Goods receipt is generated based off what as been scanned into the Warehouse and the GR is sent to the Supplier’s ERP to close the delivery flow. Technical Acknowledgment & Goods Receipt Battery Co Ltd Buyer (DC101) 31 Summary Advanced Ship Notice 32 Summary Advanced Ship Notice Purchase Order 1 Summary Ship Notice PO Line 1 Purchase Order 1 PO Line 2 ShipNotice Line 1 PO Line 3 ShipNotice Line 2 ShipNotice Line 3 Purchase Order 2 Purchase Order 2 PO Line 1 Schedule Agreement Release SAR Line 1 ShipNotice line 4 ShipNotice line 5 (Split batch) Schedule Agreement ShipNotice line 6 The Summary ASN allows the Supplier to create a single shipment for all materials going to the same Buyer Ship To Location. Instead of Supplier creating 3 separate ASNs, only a single ASN is created. o If any of the materials required packing information / Handling Units then it would be sent at the line level like a standard ASN. This is incredibly useful for Buyer and Supplier relationships where there are normally a large volume of orders that are all for the same day and can be delivered within a single shipment. The Summary ASN can also reference Schedule Agreement type Orders. This is a common combination in SCC where PO collaboration and Schedule Agreement SCC processes are in scope. Summary ASNs are Buyer specific and may not supported by all Buyer’s due to specific Business or tehcincal requirements. 33 Supplier Integration Project 34 Supplier Integration: Key considerations to remember during your integration project Integration Project Packaging Instructions, Package Dimensions and Handling Unit Information. Detailed packaging instructions, package dimensions, and HU information for each material must be maintained by the supplier within their own system/ERP. The Supplier and Buyer must align directly to ensure packaging instructions are correct for each of the materials in scope. Packaging information is not validated by the Network, and is Buyer specific requirements that is validated within the Buyer’s ERP / Warehouse Management System. Shipping Container Serial Code (SSCC) / Handling Unit Number Supplier’s system must generate the SSCC / Handling Unit Number and populate it on the cXML shipNotice document. Please note: the Handling Unit number for each package must meet the Buyer’s logistic requirements. An incorrect SSCC / HU value will affect both the barcode and receipting process within the Buyer’s ERP. Ship notice status (Acknowledged, Failed, or Rejected). cXML Status Update document is sent from the network to the Supplier’s system and will include error information if the Ship Notice with handling units fails in the Buyer’s ERP (after the network). From experience, It’s recommended that suppliers integrate the full flow of technical acknowledgments to ensure full visibility of the ASN status as failures relating to packaging. Ship notice exception / failure and reason relating to Handling Units when it is received by the Buyer’s ERP (after the network). As part of you Supplier integration project please advocate for testing an ASN exception process as it’s likely ASNs will fail due to incorrect Packaging Information. Email notification for Ship Notice Failures can be enabled as well, but it may lack the full detail of the error and the supplier would need review the error in the portal as well. Packaging Labels Can be manually downloaded from the portal after the integrated cXML ShipNotice has been sent to the SAP Business Network. Packaging labels can not be sent via HTTPs connections or email. Summary Ship Notice As the Ship Notice is referencing multiple Orders, if there is an error blocking the ASN for one of the POs the entire ASN fails until it’s resolved and resent. Please keep this mind if you have buyer requiring fully confirmed PO Lines. 35 Homework 36 Appendix 1.a Alternative Formats EDIFACT D96A & ANSI X12 37 Where to find Information Internal documentation : Standard B2B Formats on SAP Integration Suite Managed Gateway.xlsx (please download for full access) External Documentation: SAP Help Standard B2B Formats 38 Your perspective matters Join the conversation You ask. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Overview [page 9] SAP Business Network Overview [page 10] Configuration Support for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain [page 10] Integration of Supplier Systems with SAP Business Network [page 11] Alternate cXML Document Routing [page 11] Configuring Email Notification for Document Delay or Failure [page 11] SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Overview SAP Business Network for Supply Chain is an extension of SAP Business Network that enhances the ability of suppliers to collaborate with buyers in supply-chain tasks such as ordering, invoicing, and shipping. With SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enabled, an array of features become available to buyers and suppliers on SAP Business Network. These features facilitate collaboration between buyers and suppliers, for example on transactions pertinent to direct material supply chains. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enables you, as a supplier, to do the following: • • • • Collaborate efficiently with all supply-chain partners through a single global solution Easily manage all direct materials processes, including consigned inventory, rolling delivery schedules, and contract manufacturing Respond intelligently to changes in supply and demand with real-time visibility into supply-chain metrics Rapidly connect to thousands of buyers with minimal IT costs  Note SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration features entail enhancements to the SAP Business Network user interface. Fields and tabs that do not appear in the regular SAP Business Network interface may appear in the SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration user interface. Also, the same tab may be labeled with one name in the regular SAP Business Network user interface, and with another in the SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration user interface. Users should take note of these differences, especially when they first switch from the regular SAP Business Network user interface to the SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration user interface. Buyers can enable and disable SAP Business Network for Supply Chain for individual suppliers with whom they have an active relationship. After enabling a supplier, buyers can enable and disable the retail-industry functionality for individual suppliers. When at least one buyer enables a supplier to use the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain functionality, that supplier is always directed to the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain supplier user interface portal for all buyers. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network for Supply Chain PUBLIC 9 Figure 1: SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Processes SAP Business Network Overview SAP Business Network is a cloud-based business network where buyers and suppliers establish business relationships and run their business transactions. SAP Business Network has a number of advantages for customers. On the technical level, customers only have to connect to a single service in the cloud, instead of having to set up and operate technical integration to all their business partners, using different protocols and technologies. On the business level, customers not only save costs with automated procurement processes, but they can also use the network to find new business partners and opportunities. For more information about SAP Business Network, see SAP Business Network - Supplier Help Roadmap. Configuration Support for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain EDI support is provided via Boomi. file://SBN/split/Supplier Guide to SAP B.content: Integration of Supplier Systems with SAP Business Network Hardware and software solutions enable SAP Business Network to communicate with different supplier systems. Depending on their needs and technical capabilities, suppliers may choose to integrate with SAP Business Network to transfer EDI or cXML documents, or they can use the SAP Business Network supplier portal to manage documents. For more information about supplier integration options for EDI and cXML documents, see the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Overview Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers, SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network Installation Guide for ERP Integration for Suppliers, and the SAP Integration Suite, Managed Gateway for Spend Management and SAP Business Network configuration guide for ERP integration for suppliers. Alternate cXML Document Routing Some features require that you be enabled for alternate cXML document routing. Many SAP Business Network for Supply Chain features require enablement of alternate cXML document routing, which allows cXML documents to be routed to alternate paths specified in the cXML. SAP Business Network Support must enable alternate cXML document routing for each supplier-buyer relationship. Configuring Email Notification for Document Delay or Failure You can receive email notifications when documents you sent are delayed or failing. Context You can enable your system to receive email notifications for document types you send through the SAP Business Network for Supply Chain solution. The system sends you notification when a document you sent is delayed or failing. You can receive notifications for the following document types: • • • • • • Component consumption Component receipt Invoice Order confirmation Product replenishment Quality collaboration Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network for Supply Chain PUBLIC 11 • Ship notice Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon in the upper right corner, then in the dropdown, click Settings Network Notifications . 2. Go to the Error Email Notification section and check Send immediate notification upon failure. If desired, you can also enable an option to send a notification digest. 12 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Self-Assessment Questionnaire The self-assessment questionnaires are out of the box, standard questionnaires that you can use to share your human rights due diligence responses with your buyers. You can respond to an assessment request from buyers or proactively complete the assessment and share your responses with multiple buyers. With the self-assessment questionnaire, you eliminate the need to answer similar questions from different buyers. When you receive an assessment request, you are notified through both emails and notifications on the SAP Business Network portal. When you share or update your assessments, your buyers are also notified through emails and notifications on the SAP Business Network portal. Note that your buyers are not notified if you unshare your assessments. Your administrators can view and download assessment-related audit logs by choosing on SAP Business Network. Settings Audit Log The following table describes the self-assessment status on the SAP Business Network portal. Status Description New Before you start an assessment, the assessment is in the New state. In this state, if a buyer sends an assessment request, you receive a notification to start the assessment. Draft You have drafted assessment answers but have not completed it yet. In this state, you can only edit the assessment. If a buyer sends an assessment request,you receive a notification to complete the assessment. Completed You have completed the assessment. In this state, you can edit, view, share, or unshare the assessment. If a buyer sends an assessment request, you receive a notification to share the assessment. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Self-Assessment Questionnaire PUBLIC 13 Status Description Editing This status appears in either of the following cases: • You completed the assessment and is editing the assessment again before sharing it with buyers. In this scenario, you can edit, view, or share the last version of the assessment. • You have already shared the assessment with buyers, and now is updating assessment answers. In this scenario, you can edit, view, share, or unshare the last version of the assessment. Once the editing is finished, you can view, edit, share, or unshare the latest version of the assessment. Version Update SAP Business Network supports version update of self-assessment questionnaires. When SAP Business Network releases a new version, a New version available message will appear on the Assessments page. You can distinguish between the old and new versions by the version indicator displayed on the View and Edit pages. When a new version becomes available, you may encounter the following scenarios: • • If you have not yet started any assessment, you will automatically begin working on the new version. • If you have completed and submitted the previous version, you will be prompted to update to the new version when attempting to view, edit, or share the previous version. However, you can still review your responses from the previous version by clicking "View" before submitting the new version. If you have initiated an assessment but have not yet submitted it, you will be prompted to switch to the new version. Your answers from the previous version will be transferred to the new version. Please note that some of your answers from the previous version may be lost if certain questions have been removed in the latest version. Taking an Assessment SAP Business Network provides you with an assessment so that you can fill it in and show your supply chain due diligence to your buyers. This topic describes how to take an assessment. Context You can proactively take the assessment and share it with your buyers with an established trading partner or sourcing relationship. For details about how to take the assessment, refer to the Procedure section in this topic. Buyers (with an account on SAP Business Network or a license of SAP Ariba Supplier Risk) might also send an assessment request to you. 14 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Self-Assessment Questionnaire When a buyer sends an assessment request, you receive an email notification and also a notification on SAP Business Network. In this case, you can access the assessment by clicking the link in the notification email or clicking  on your SAP Business Network. Procedure 1. Log in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Assessments in the menu bar. All assessments are listed. 3. Locate an assessment in the New state, and choose  (more options) > Start assessment. Before starting the assessment, you can also click the assessment name to check background information about the assessment, and then click Start assessment in the upper right corner to fill in the assessment questionnaire.  Tip Once you start the assessment, its status changes to Draft. Later, you can choose  (more options) > Edit to continue finishing it. 4. Click Submit when you finish the assessment. 5. Click Continue to confirm your submission. A message is prompted indicating that you have successfully completed the assessment.  Note Completing an assessment does not mean you have shared it. Under this message, you can click Send assessment to share the assessment with your buyers now or you can do it later. Results The status of the finished assessment changes to Completed. The certificates that you upload to your assessment will be synchronized to the Certifications section of your profile, eliminating the need to upload them again to your profile. You can choose  (more options) to edit, view, or share the assessment with buyers. Related Information Editing an Assessment [page 16] Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Self-Assessment Questionnaire PUBLIC 15 Manually Sharing an Assessment with Buyers [page 17] Editing an Assessment After you complete an assessment and the assessment status has changed to Completed, you can edit the assessment to change your answers before sharing it with buyers. This topic describes how to edit a non-shared assessment. Context The assessment to be edited is in the Editing or Completed state. For a completed but non-shared assessment, there is no person or view icon in the Status column. Procedure 1. Log in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Assessments in the menu bar. All the assessments are displayed. 3. Locate an assessment in the Editing or Completed state without any person or view icon in the Status column. 4. Choose  (more options) > Edit. 5. Click Continue to confirm that you want to edit the assessment. 6. Edit the assessment. 7. Click Submit when you have finished the editing. A message is prompted indicating that the assessment is successfully updated. Results The assessment status changes to Completed, and you can edit, view, or share the assessment. The certificates that you upload to your assessment will be synchronized to the Certifications section of your profile, eliminating the need to upload them again to your profile. Related Information Manually Sharing an Assessment with Buyers [page 17] 16 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Self-Assessment Questionnaire Manually Sharing an Assessment with Buyers After finishing an assessment, you can share it with your buyers to let them know your supply chain due diligence as soon as possible. You have the flexibility to share your assessment manually or automatically. This topic describes how to manually share an assessment with your buyers. Context You can share an assessment in the Completed or Editing state. When you share an assessment in the Editing state, you share the last completed version of this assessment with your buyers. If you update an assessment that has been shared with buyers, the updates are automatically published to these buyers. Therefore, you don't need to share the updates. Procedure 1. Log in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Assessments in the menu bar. 3. Locate an assessment in the Completed or Editing state. 4. Choose  (more options) > Share to share the assessment. Before sharing, you can choose  (more options) > View to view the assessment. After you have viewed the assessment, click Share assessment at the bottom of the assessment dialog box. 5. Select the buyers that you want to share the assessment with. You can search the desired buyers based on their name, country, or region. The buyer who requested you to take the assessment is preselected. 6. Click Share. A message is prompted indicating that your assessment has been successfully shared. Results Your buyers receive an assessment sharing notification. For an assessment in the Editing state, the last completed version is shared. In the Status column, the number besides a person icon and the number besides a view icon might change accordingly based on the number of buyers you shared the assessment with. You can update and unshare the assessment. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Self-Assessment Questionnaire PUBLIC 17 Related Information Updating an Assessment [page 19] Unsharing an Assessment with Buyers [page 21] Automatically Sharing an Assessment with Buyers [page 18] Automatically Sharing an Assessment with Buyers After finishing an assessment, you can share it with your buyers to let them know your supply chain due diligence as soon as possible. You have the flexibility to share your assessment manually or automatically. This topic describes how to automatically share an assessment with your buyers. Prerequisites • • Your buyers have accounts on SAP Business Network or SAP Ariba Supplier Risk. You have established a trading partner or sourcing relationship with your buyers. Context You can automatically share assessments with your buyers in two ways: immediately upon completion of the assessment, or upon request from the buyers. This saves time and effort for both parties while ensuring that assessments are shared promptly. Procedure 1. Log in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Assessments in the menu bar. 3. Click Settings in the upper right corner of the Assessments page and turn on either the Auto share assessments with my buyers upon completion or Auto share completed assessments with my buyers upon request setting. The Auto share assessments with my buyers upon completion setting automatically shares both existing and future completed assessments with all your buyers, regardless of whether they specifically request access to the assessments or not. Note that assessments will not be automatically shared with buyers from whom you have previously chosen to unshare assessments. The Auto share completed assessments with my buyers upon request setting ensures that completed assessments are automatically shared with your buyers only when a sharing request is received from them. Assessment sharing requests received before this setting is enabled must be manually handled. 18 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Self-Assessment Questionnaire  Note You will need to share assessments manually for sharing requests from buyers without an existing relationship. The introduction of a new version of the supplier assessment questionnaire impacts the assessment auto share function as follows: • If the Auto share assessments with my buyers upon completion setting is enabled and you have a completed assessment using the previous version of the questionnaire, the completed assessment won’t be automatically shared with your buyers until you've finished the new version. Once the new version assessment is completed, the auto-share function will resume. The newly completed assessment, using the upgraded version, will be automatically shared with all your buyers. • If the Auto share completed assessments with my buyers upon request setting is enabled, the completed assessment of the previous version won’t be automatically shared with your buyers when they make a request. Instead, you’ll need to complete the new version of the assessment. Once the new version is completed, it will be automatically shared with buyers upon their new requests. For any requests received before you complete the new version, you will need to manually share the new version once it is completed. Results Your assessment will be automatically shared with your buyers. Your buyers receive an email notification and also a notification on SAP Business Network. Related Information Manually Sharing an Assessment with Buyers [page 17] Updating an Assessment [page 19] Unsharing an Assessment with Buyers [page 21] Updating an Assessment After you share a completed assessment with your buyers, you can still update the assessment regardless of whether the buyers have viewed it. Context The shared assessment is in the Completed state with person and view icons. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Self-Assessment Questionnaire PUBLIC 19 Once you submit your updates, all updates are published to buyers with whom the assessment was shared earlier.  Caution If you don't want to share further updates, unshare the assessment with buyers. Procedure 1. Log in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Assessments in the menu bar. All the assessments are displayed. 3. Locate an assessment in the Completed state with person and view icons. 4. Choose  (more options) > Edit. 5. Click Continue to confirm that you want to update the shared assessment. 6. Update the assessment answers. 7. Click Submit when you have finished the update. 8. Click Continue to confirm the submission. It is recommended to add a comment about the change you have made. This comment is displayed to your buyers so that they can easily identify the updated part. 9. Click Send. A message is prompted indicating that the assessment is successfully updated. Results Your assessment is updated and the updates are automatically published to your buyers who have already received the last version of your assessment. The certificates that you upload to your assessment will be synchronized to the Certifications section of your profile, eliminating the need to upload them again to your profile. Now, you can share the new version of the assessment to other buyers, or unshare the latest version of the assessment. Related Information Manually Sharing an Assessment with Buyers [page 17] Unsharing an Assessment with Buyers [page 21] 20 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Self-Assessment Questionnaire

file://SBN/split/Supplier Guide to SAP B.content: Unsharing an Assessment with Buyers After sharing an assessment with buyers, you can cancel the sharing of an assessment. This topic describes how to unshare an assessment. Context You can unshare an assessment in the Editing or Completed state with person and view icons. If you unshare an assessment in the Editing state, you cancel the sharing of the last version of the assessment. Procedure 1. Log in to SAP Business Network. 2. Choose Assessments in the menu bar. All the assessments are displayed. 3. Choose  (more options) > Unshare for the target assessment. A buyer list is displayed. Alternatively, you can go to the Status column and click the number besides the person icon to display the buyer list. 4. Click Unshare for the target buyer. 5. In the Unshare assessment dialog box, choose other buyers from the drop-down list and add a comment. It is recommended to add a comment about the reason of unsharing. This comment is displayed to your buyers after you unshare the assessment. 6. Click Unshare. Results The supplier-side assessment is still in the original status (Editing or Completed). The buyer-side assessment changes to Not available - Unshared with your comment. The assessment changes to unavailable to buyers, and the buyers can request the assessment again. You are navigated back to the assessment list page. In the Status column, you can see that the number of buyers you shared the assessment with is reduced by the number of buyers you selected. After you recover the business relationship with buyers, you can share the assessment again. Purchase Order Line Items [page 43] External Information Sources [page 45] Carbon-Copy Updates for Suppliers [page 46] Loss Prevention for Failed Documents [page 46] Search Filters in Order and Forecast Collaboration [page 48] Stock Transport Orders [page 49] Order change requests Tile for the Supplier Workbench [page 50] Related Information Receiving and Fulfilling Orders Purchase Order Line Items A purchase order contains one or more line items. Deleting Line Items Buyers can select which of their integrated suppliers should receive delete indicators when they delete line items in a purchase order. To select suppliers, buyers follow the steps documented in Enabling PO Line Item Delete Indicator [page 44]. Buyers only select suppliers who have not already implemented their own logic to determine which line items were deleted in a purchase order. The operation attribute in an ItemOut element in a cXML OrderRequest document defines actions associated with line items in purchase orders. When a buyer deletes a line item from a purchase order, they include operation="delete" in the ItemOut element. When a line item is deleted, it is crossed out on the Purchase Order Order Details page, and the Change column shows the line item as Deleted. Note that the information about deleted line items is visible even if the user clicks Hide Changes. Information about deleted line items is included in emails about updated purchase orders and in downloaded PDF files for purchase orders. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases PUBLIC 43  Note If the buyer undoes the deletion of a line item in a purchase order, that line item is still mapped to a new line item in the supplier's sales order since the supplier mapped the line item to a new line item in the sales order before the buyer undid the deletion. Retaining Order Confirmations for Purchase Order Line Items Buyers can retain their order confirmations when they match the supplier's confirmation even if the item has changed. The supplier is not required to reconfirm fulfilled items with conditions set at the schedule line level. If the rule Retain confirmation status for changed line items on change orders that match supplier confirmation is active and the order confirmation deviation approval is deactivated the confirmation status of unchanged line items on the previous order is retained on change orders. When this rule is applied, the following requirements are met: • • Validate if the change order items have changed and match the confirmation status at the schedule line level. • • • New and old versions of the order confirmations are retained. The order confirmation is retained if the change order items have changes that match any confirmation status items from the last order confirmation. Items with Confirmed and Backordered status are retained. Items with Rejected status are not included in the evaluation. When this rule is active and applied, the following schedule line-item level fields are evaluated to determine if the new version of the order matches the order confirmation: • • Line Items: Requested Quantity, Requested Delivery Date, Unit Price Schedule Lines: Quantity, Requested Delivery Date Enabling PO Line Item Delete Indicator Buyer can select suppliers who should receive the purchase order with the Deleted line items indicator, as follows: Procedure 1. Run the transaction code SPRO. The Customizing: Execute Project screen appears. 2. Click SAP Reference IMG. The Display IMG screen appears. 3. Navigate to Integration with Other SAP Components SAP Business Network Integration 44 PUBLIC General Settings Managed Gateway for Spend&Network for Buyer Enable Vendors Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases 4. Click the IMG-Activity icon for Enable Vendors. The Change View "SAP Business Network Vendor Table": Overview screen appears. 5. Enter X in the Send PO Del Ind field for the integrated supplier who should receive purchase order with the Deleted line items indicator. External Information Sources Suppliers can access information that buyers securely share with you through links to external sources. Buyers can provide you with links to external information sources in line items of purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and scheduling agreement releases. External information sources can include anything that the buyer wants to add to support an order item. Examples of such sources are a technical drawing or a link to a Web site containing item specifications. You can use the links that are included in the order to access external-information sources using single sign-on (SSO). When you click a link, SAP Business Network sends a single sign-on token (using SAML 2.0) through the supplier web browser to the target system for authentication. The supplier web browser is then redirected to the specific URL.  Note It is the responsibility of the buyer to provide a supplier with access to an external information source. There is no SAP Business Network involvement in opening an external information source. Access is handled between the buyer and the supplier only. A share icon indicates that a line item in an order has one ore more links to external information sources. The share icon shows on the following pages: • Next to the order number: • • • • Orders Orders and Releases Orders Orders and Releases Items to Confirm Orders Orders and Releases Items to Ship In the Line Items section of an order details page, next to the line item's part number. When an order has line items with external information sources, the order details page also shows an Additional Sources table with the following fields: • Source Name – The name of the document or other external information source. If the buyer provides a URL for an information source, the source name is an active hyperlink that you can click to view the source. When you click a link, a dialog box displays to warn that you are leaving SAP Business Network to view the source. You click Confirm and Proceed to continue. • • Version – The source version. Description – A description of the additional source. Up to 10 external information source links can show in the Additional Sources area. If a line item has more than 10 external information sources, the feature instead creates separate pages, one for every 10 source links, and shows links to those pages in the Additional Sources area. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases PUBLIC 45 If a change order creates a new version of an order with links to external information sources, any source names that are active links are made inactive in the obsoleted order version, but retained as active links in the new version. Carbon-Copy Updates for Suppliers Suppliers who received purchase order copies automatically receive copies of buyer updates to the original purchase orders. With carbon-copy updates: • • • • • A monitor displays throughput statuses for updated copy documents that were sent. Buyers can manually resend copy documents that are not sent successfully by automatic retries. Suppliers can create ship notices from updated copy documents. SAP Business Network sends an alert email when there are no copy documents created for purchase orders that should have a copy. SAP Business Network sends a Failed on Arrival notification, including the document number and document type, to buyers when a delivery fails. Loss Prevention for Failed Documents Suppliers can retrieve documents with transmission failures to make corrections and resend them. Sometimes, for any of several reasons including syntax errors, documents fail to get transmitted through SAP Business Network. With the resend document feature, SAP Business Network for Supply Chain lets you know of specific syntax errors, and enables you to resend these documents after correcting their errors. To prevent loss of important documents, SAP Business Network for Supply Chain does the following when documents fail to arrive at their destinations: • • • Captures document contents when they fail on arrival at SAP Business Network Provides a user interface for triggering the reprocessing of these documents Informs users of delivery failures caused by non-compliance with transaction rules, whether the cause lies with the document or with the transaction rule • • Provides detailed error messages and suggests potential solutions • Enables buyer administrators and supplier administrators to export cXML files for the affected documents, and to mark document transmission issues as resolved Enables buyer administrators and supplier administrators to discard or resend documents that previously failed to be delivered Resending a Document That Was Not Received [page 47] Resending a Purchase Order from Purchase Order Details [page 48] 46 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases Resending a Document That Was Not Received Administrators can resend some documents that were not received because of errors. Prerequisites You are assigned the Administrator role. Context Occasionally, documents sent through SAP Business Network are not received at their final destination because of errors in the documents or their lack of compliance with relevant business rules. Administrators can often resend these documents after correcting the errors. Procedure 1.  Note The path to the Documents to Resend feature is as follows: • • For buyers – For suppliers – Quick links … Documents to Resend Documents to Resend Choose Documents to Resend. The documents search results are displayed, with details about the causes of the failures. The Resolution Status search filters Show unresolved entries and Show resolved entries control which of the failed documents that meet the other search results are included. 2. Review the failed document's error message, make the correction, then click Resend in the Actions column.  Note Alternatively, you can choose these other actions in the Actions column: • Click Export cXML to export the affected document in cXML, then mark the document transmission issues as resolved. • Click Mark as Resolved if you do not want to resend the failed document. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases PUBLIC 47 Resending a Purchase Order from Purchase Order Details An administrator can resend a purchase order that failed transmission. Procedure 1. Open the details for the purchase order you want to resend. 2. Click Resend. SAP Business Network resends the purchase order and records the action in the log on the History tab. Search Filters in Order and Forecast Collaboration You can use filters to aid in searching orders and forecast documents. Users search differently for different kinds of items. Here are three examples: • • A buyer searches forecasts for a product based on the product internal program code • A supplier getting ready to send ship notices searches for all items belonging to a certain product family A supplier getting ready to send order confirmations searches for line items for a certain customer by the customer planner code On the Planning confirmations: • Forecast page, you can filter searches for items to confirm, items to ship, and order For planner code  Note Information for planner codes that you are not authorized to access are excluded from the search results. • For product group Additionally, you can browse for filters in the following product-grouping hierarchies: • • • • • • • 48 Line of business Product family Product subfamily Internal program code Program code Part type Part family PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases Stock Transport Orders Suppliers can identify and view stock transport orders. A stock transport order is a type of purchase order that is used to move stock between two plants within an organization or between different organizations. On the Orders Orders and Releases page, the search results table identifies stock transport orders by showing Stock Transport Order in the Type column, rather than Order for standard purchase orders. Search only stock transport orders in the page's Search filters limits the search results to stock transport orders only. The Orders Orders and Releases Items to Ship page also has the search filter Search only stock transport orders and shows Stock Transport Order in the Type column of the results table for stock transport orders. A Ship From column in the results table shows the location of the stock to be moved. On the Orders Orders and Releases Search only stock transport orders. Items to Confirm page, the View filters include the radio button When you open the details page of a stock transport order, the Line Items table includes a Stock Transfer Type column, which shows which kind of transfer to make for a line item. The column's values are: • • Intra – Intracompany. A stock transfer between plants in the same company. Inter – Intercompany. A stock transfer between plants in different companies. Restrictions • Only purchase orders are supported as stock transport orders. Scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases are not supported for stock transport orders. • The following capabilities are not supported for a stock-transport order: • • • Invoice creation Serial numbers Handling units • You cannot create an order confirmation from the details page for a stock transport order; the Create Order Confirmation button is grayed out. • In the Orders Orders and Releases results table, unit-price information is available only for intercompany (Inter) stock-transport orders. Unit-price information isn’t available for intracompany (Intra) stock-transport orders. • On the Orders Orders and Releases page, you cannot create the following documents: • An invoice for an intracompany stock-transport order. You can, however, create an invoice for an intercompany stock-transport order. • A service entry sheet, whether for an intracompany or intercompany stock-transport order. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases PUBLIC 49 Order change requests Tile for the Supplier Workbench Suppliers can manage MRP exceptions for purchase-order change requests. The Order change requests tile in the supplier Workbench reports the number of open change requests, shows request details, and provides filters to customize which information the tile reports. This information helps you collaborate with your buyers on changes to purchase-order quantity and date, based on Material Requirements Planning (MRP). In addition, you can use the tile to respond to these change requests.  Note SAP Integration Suite, managed gateway for spend management and SAP Business Network offers integration support that enables SAP Business Network and SAP S/4HANA Cloud to collaborate in handling purchase order change requests. This collaboration includes change-request follow-on documents, such as changerequest responses and change-request confirmations. This integration support is part of the larger MRP capabilities between SAP S/4HANA Cloud and SAP Business Network. For more information, see SAP Note 3101825 .  Restriction • The Order change requests tile does not support change requests for scheduling agreements or scheduling agreement releases. • • A supplier can make only one response or proposal per change request. A buyer can make only one response or proposal to a supplier response per change request. The Order change requests tile includes the following elements: • When the tile is active, the Edit filter dropdown below the tiles shows the tile's current filter settings. For details about the available filters, see Filters for the Order Change Requests Tile [page 52]. • The tile reports the number of change-requests that need a response and also meet the filter criteria that you configured. • The tile shows the following action buttons above its search results table: Accept Reject Propose 50 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases
