The Order change requests tile on the Workbench page provides search filters to refine what data it shows. Click Edit filter to show or hide the filters. • For filter fields that allow multiple values, do the following for each value you add: 1. Click an empty area of the filter field. 2. Type a value, which can have more than one word. 3. Click outside the entry field to complete that entry. • For filter fields that have the input hint Select or type selections and a value-help icon ( ), click in the field to show the dropdown, then select one or more of the available values. • When the Exact match box below the Order numbers field is checked, only the Customers and Order numbers fields are visible. Filter Description Customers One or more buyer names. Order numbers Purchase order ID. The filter has radio buttons to set the search by Partial match (default) or by Exact match. Customer locations Unique identifier for one or more locations in the buyer organization. Company codes One or more company-code IDs. Order line-item numbers Line number for the purchase-order item. Schedule-line numbers Schedule-line number for the purchase-order line item. Customer part numbers One or more part numbers used by the customer for the item. Creation date A range of dates when a change request was created. Values are Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last 14 days, Last 31 days (default), Last 90 days, Last 365 days, and Custom date range. Customer proposed delivery date A range of item delivery dates that a customer proposed as changes to original delivery dates. Values are None (default), Last 7 days, Today Next 7 days, Next 14 days, Next 31 days, Next 90 days, Next 365 days, and Custom date range. 52 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases Filter Description Priority The level of urgency for the requested change. Values are provided by the buyer. If no values are specified, the filter includes all possible values. Reason codes Numeric or text codes that provide a high-level reason for the requested change. Possible values are provided by the buyer.  Note If the filter has no choices of reason codes, the buyer does not require them and you can leave the filter empty. Customer response status The buyer's response to a change request from a supplier. Possible values are Pending, Accepted, and Rejected. Supplier response status The supplier's response to a change request from a buyer. Possible values are Pending, Accepted, Rejected, and Proposed. Change by number of days The number of days that a Customer proposed delivery date is earlier or later than the order's current Delivery date. Filter choices are None (the default), Days earlier, or Days later. For the Days earlier and Days later choices, the filter shows Min and Max fields. In these fields, you specify the minimum and maximum number of days difference that you want to include in the search results. The Min and Max fields have the following requirements: • At least one of these fields, Min or Max, must contain a value. Valid values are a number from 0 to 999. Both fields can be the same number. • The value of Min must not be greater than the value of Max. Related Information Filtering Workbench Tiles Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases PUBLIC 53 Responding to Change Requests Using the Supplier Workbench Suppliers can use the Order change requests tile of the supplier Workbench to manage purchase order change requests. Prerequisites • In the search results table of the Order change requests tile, each of the following columns requires enabling a transaction rule to make the column editable.  Note If a column is not shown, click the table's Settings icon ( ) and drag the column name into the Displayed columns list. Column name Required transaction rule for editing Supplier Proposed Quantity Allow suppliers to respond to a change request with a different quantity than the buyer proposed. Supplier Proposed Delivery Date Allow suppliers to respond to a change request with a different delivery date than the buyer proposed. Estimated Cost Allow suppliers to request an additional cost when responding to a buyer request to change a schedule line. Context If you have multiple change requests that you want confirmed, rejected, or to propose a different change, you can respond to all of them in a single operation by using the Order change requests tile in your Workbench.  Restriction You cannot use the Order change requests tile to respond to change requests for scheduling agreements or scheduling agreement releases. Procedure 1. Choose Workbench, then click the Order change requests tile. 2. If needed, choose Edit filters to refine the tile's search filters to locate the desired change requests. For more information, refer to Filters for the Order Change Requests Tile [page 52]. 54 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases 3. In the search results table, check the box for one or more change requests that you want to send the same type of response. 4. For each chosen change request, enter any desired changes in the editable fields. The following table fields are editable: • • • • Supplier Proposed Delivery Date – Select a date. Supplier Proposed Quantity – Enter a quantity. Estimated Cost – Enter an amount. The field allows a period (.) in the amount, but no commas (,). This field is valid only when the buyer has proposed a different delivery date or quantity. Comments – Enter any comments. 5. Above the top left of the results table, choose Accept, Reject, or Propose. A page opens with additional fields for the chosen response. 6. Review the information you want to send, then choose Submit. • The Accept change requests and Propose change requests pages have an optional Comment field above the table. This comment is applied to all change requests in the table. • On the Reject change requests page, the Rejected reason and Comment fields above the table are optional free-text fields. Entries in these fields are applied to all change requests in the table. The feature submits the response and returns you to the Workbench page. Results The following table describes the possible actions and results after a supplier responds to a change request: Submitted Response Actions Taken Accept 1. The buyer system accepts the confirmation. 2. The buyer system updates the change request with the supplier response. 3. The buyer system sends a change order with the accepted change to SAP Business Network. 4. The buyer system sends a change-request confirmation to the supplier, which describes what was done with the change request or change-request response on the buyer's backend system. Reject 1. The buyer system accepts the rejection. 2. The buyer system updates the change request with the supplier response. 3. No change order is sent to SAP Business Network. 4. The buyer system sends a change-request confirmation to the supplier, which describes what was done with the change request or change-request response on the buyer's backend system. Propose, accepted by the buyer 1. The buyer accepts the proposal. 2. The buyer system updates the change request with the supplier response. 3. The buyer system sends a change order with the accepted change to SAP Business Network. 4. The buyer system sends a change-request confirmation to the supplier, which describes what was done with the change request or change-request response on the buyer's backend system. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases PUBLIC 55 Submitted Response Propose, rejected by the buyer Actions Taken 1. The buyer rejects the proposal. 2. The buyer system updates the change request with the supplier response. 3. No change order is sent to SAP Business Network. 4. The buyer system sends a change-request confirmation to the supplier, which describes what was done with the change request or change-request response on the buyer's backend system. Related Information The Workbench 56 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Orders and Releases Order Confirmations This section provides topics about order confirmations. Additional Components and Batch in Order Confirmations [page 57] The Items to Confirm List [page 59] Order Confirmation Approval Requests [page 62] Order Confirmation Deviations and Tolerances [page 64] Additional Components and Batch in Order Confirmations Contract manufacturers can make additions and revisions while confirming components. Between the time a contract manufacturer receives a purchase order and the time the contract manufacturer begins manufacturing, the contract manufacturer might change the batches of components assigned to a particular order. Contract manufacturers need the ability to revise the batch and component information assigned to a purchase order, and to have those revisions delivered automatically to the relevant documents in their customers' ERP systems. With the adding components and batch in order confirmation feature, contract manufacturers can update order confirmations—including those for subcontracts—ship notices, and component consumption updates. In SAP Business Network for Supply Chain, adding components and batch in order confirmation includes the following functionalities: • Enables contract manufacturers to update component and batch information as part of the order confirmation process • Enables contract manufacturers to report the finished goods batches and quantities as part of component consumption reports • • • Enables suppliers to enter supplier batch, and confirm quantities during order confirmation Enables suppliers to add components for a subcontract order during order confirmation Enables suppliers to select one or more components and batches for a subcontract order during order confirmation • Enables suppliers to enter Reason Code data when the suppliers change delivery dates during order confirmation • Enables buyers to see current batch and quantity data in ship notices and component consumption tables as contract manufacturers and suppliers revise the data Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Order Confirmations PUBLIC 57 Updating Batch and Component Assignments for Purchase Orders You can revise component information in an order confirmation. Prerequisites The buyer must check the Allow suppliers to edit components on order confirmations rule. Otherwise, the Edit Components button on order confirmations is not visible. Procedure 1. Go to Orders Orders and Releases . 2. Select the desired order, then click Create Order Confirmation Update Line Items Edit Components . 3. In the Components dialog, check the Usage box for each component you want to edit. 4. Enter values into the Batch #, Quantity, and Unit fields as desired. 5. Optional: Do any of the following: • • • To add another component, click Add Component, and enter data for the additional component To copy the quantities from the purchase order, click Copy Order Quantities To replace any values you've entered with the original values from the purchase order, click Revert All Edits 6. Do one of the following: • • To save and confirm your changes, click OK To replace any values you've entered with the original values from the purchase order, click Remove Changes. 7. Complete the process for confirming a purchase order as usual. Confirmation Control Keys Some back-end enterprise systems use confirmation control keys to control processes that occur after the creation of a purchase order, specifically the creation of order confirmations and ship notices by the supplier. For example, in the SAP ECC (Enterprise Central Component) system, the control key is displayed at the purchase order item detail level and it controls whether or not confirmation orders and ship notices are required by the buyer, not required, or optional. SAP Business Network can receive order confirmation and ship notice control keys at purchase order line item level, and act on them to control the creation of order confirmations and ship notices. 58 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Order Confirmations The Items to Confirm List As a supplier, the Items to Confirm list feature enables you to confirm incoming purchase orders efficiently across multiple customers.  Note Planned lean-service items, unplanned lean-service items, and unplanned material items are not supported to be confirmed from the items to confirm list. See Service Order Confirmations for more information. In the order collaboration process for direct materials, suppliers typically strive to establish long-term, repeat business with their customers. From the supplier perspective, a successful business model involves a continual flow of incoming purchase orders from a number of buying customers. The supplier must efficiently process these incoming purchase orders: confirm line items when confirmation is required, create ship notices, and ship goods. Also, the supplier must process purchase orders that have been changed. Further, the supplier must not confirm orders for quantities or delivery dates that are not achievable. Therefore, the process of confirming orders quickly and correctly can be challenging because of the volume of data and the level of detail required. The Orders Orders and Releases Items to Confirm list displays a list of purchase orders that includes information critical for you to confirm many order details accurately and simultaneously.  Note Some functionality of the Items to Confirm list is changed if a purchase order has temporary unit prices. See Temporary Unit Prices for more information. Reconfirmed Items The View dropdown in the Items to confirm tile has two views: Items to be confirmed (default) and Confirmed items for editing. The Confirmed items for editing view contains a Reconfirmed Items section that shows all line items that are eligible to reconfirm. By default, this view shows all confirmed and partially confirmed items. This view also puts into edit mode all line-item fields that were editable when their order confirmation was created. Suppliers can use the Confirmation status filter to choose which confirmation status types to exclude. Filter choices in the Confirmed items for editing view are Exclude confirmation not allowed and Exclude unconfirmed. The default for both filters is Yes, Suppliers can reconfirm any line item that has status Backordered, Confirmed, Rejected, or Unconfirmed. To do this, the supplier chooses the desired line items, then from the Confirm dropdown chooses one of the following options: • • • Confirm entire order Confirm entire item Confirm schedule line In the same operation, suppliers can confirm multiple line items that may have different statuses. If a supplier reduces the quantity of an item before sending it for reconfirmation, the confirmation status changes as follows: Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Order Confirmations PUBLIC 59 • • The reduced quantity becomes Confirmed. The remaining quantity becomes Unconfirmed. For example, suppose that an item has a Confirmed quantity of 100. If the supplier changes the confirmed quantity to 90, the reconfirmed item quantity becomes 90 Confirmed and 10 Unconfirmed. Items that are submitted for reconfirmation are validated again. Workflow for the Items to Confirm List The end-to-end workflow for the Items to Confirm list starts with a supplier searching for purchase-order line items, and ends with the supplier confirming the purchase order in one of multiple ways. 1. Search for purchase-order line items. 2. View purchase-order line items, with the default sort showing the items that should be confirmed first. 3. Confirm purchase orders in one of the following ways: • • Confirm one or more entire purchase orders at the header level. • Confirm or reject multiple purchase-order line items, including line items from different purchase orders. Confirm or reject single purchase-order line items, or modify quantities before confirming a line item, using the Update Line Item option. Prerequisites  Restriction This task is not supported for planned lean services, unplanned lean services, or unplanned material items. Instead, see Order Confirmations for guidelines and alternative procedures to confirm these itmes. The buyer must enable the Allow suppliers to edit estimated shipping dates, delivery dates, and quantities on the Items to Confirm tab rule for these fields to be editable for line items. Search for the order for which you want to create an order confirmation. 4. For orders without schedule lines, edit one or more line-item fields: Line-item field Instructions Qty to Confirm Enter the quantity to confirm for the line item and press Enter .  Note The quantity you enter here cannot be greater than the figure in the Unconfirmed Qty field. Requirements to Reject an Entire Order for Material Items Buyers can enable or disable the rule that allows suppliers to reject an entire order for material items. If an order is for material items only, and the buyer does not have the rule Allow suppliers to reject quantities for material orders at the line-item level in order confirmations enabled with the Fully setting, suppliers cannot reject an entire order. The Reject Entire Order button is disabled in the following locations: • In the dropdown that displays when you click the Actions link of an order in the table on the Purchase Orders for Supply Chain). • page (or Orders Orders and Releases Orders if you are enabled for SAP Business Network In the dropdown that displays when you click Create Order Confirmation at the bottom of the table on the Orders Purchase Orders page (or Orders Orders and Releases if you are enabled for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain). In this instance, the Reject Entire Order button is not grayed out, but if you select an order and then choose Reject Entire Order, an error message displays to indicate that you cannot reject the entire order. • • In the dropdown that displays when you click Create Order Confirmation on a purchase-order details page. In the Actions menu on an order-based Workbench tile. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Order Confirmations PUBLIC 61 For orders containing material items only, the rule must be enabled for the Reject Entire Order button to be enabled.  Note If an order is for services, or a mixture of service and material items, this rule does not apply. Suppliers can reject an entire order whether the rule is enabled or not. If an order containing only material items includes unplanned material items, you can reject the order only from the Orders Purchase Orders page (or Orders Orders and Releases Network for Supply Chain) or from the purchase-order's details page. if you are enabled for SAP Business Order Confirmation Approval Requests Approval Requests To view approval requests related to an order confirmation, click the document link in the Related Documents area of the order confirmation header. The approval request has the same ID as the order confirmation, with the added suffix _AR. If the order confirmation does not have an ID, the format is MM/DD/YYYY_AR. Related Information Viewing an Approval Request for an Order Confirmation [page 62] Defining the Estimated Delivery Date at the Header Level [page 63] Viewing an Approval Request for an Order Confirmation If a buyer requires approval for order confirmation deviations, you can view automatically generated approval requests sent to buyers for approval and check the approval status. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Order Confirmations . 2. Click an order confirmation ID. The order confirmation opens. 62 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Order Confirmations 3. Find an approval request in the Related Documents section. Approval requests have the same ID as the order confirmation but with an added suffix _AR.  Note If a buyer has not approved a line item deviation yet, the approval status is Awaiting approval. Defining the Estimated Delivery Date at the Header Level Prerequisites • • • • • • You must be a part of the OCA (Order Confirmation Approval) Supplier Group. Your buyer has activated the order confirmation deviation approval on SAP Business Network. Your buyer has activated the order confirmation approval notification on SAP Business Network. Your buyer has activated the order confirmation approval at the schedule line level SAP Business Network. Your buyer has activated the required transaction rules. Ensure that you are selected to use SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration. Context Suppliers with order confirmation approvals can define an Estimated Delivery Date for all lines in their order confirmations. This saves time and reduces errors for suppliers confirming purchase orders. Procedure 1. Go to Orders Purchase Orders . 2. Choose and click on an order number. The selected purchase order details page opens. 3. At the purchase order header, choose Create Order Confirmation . 4. Choose how you want to confirm the purchase order: Confirm entire order or Confirm with information update in line. 5. Edit the Delivery Date. 6. Click Create. Your order confirmation is sent to your buyer for approval. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Order Confirmations PUBLIC 63 Related Information Editing Shipping Dates, Delivery Dates, or Quantity When Creating an Order Confirmation [page 60] Order Confirmation Deviations and Tolerances A buyer might include tolerances when creating a purchase order, a scheduling agreement, or a scheduling agreement release. For purchase orders, buyers can include tolerances for delivery date, quantity, and price. For scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases, buyers can include tolerances for delivery date and quantity.  Note Price deviations are not possible for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases because the unit price cannot be changed in SAP Business Network for these documents. Buyers must set one or both of the following rules to activate the order confirmation deviation approval process: • Purchase orders: Allow suppliers to send order confirmations that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval. • Scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases: Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases and its subrule Allow suppliers to send order confirmations for scheduling agreements and scheduling agreement releases that do not comply with defined tolerances and require buyer approval. The buyer can also check the Except quantity deviations or the Except delivery date deviations subrule to further specify which deviations the rule applies to. If you submit an order confirmation that is out of any tolerance set by the buyer, the buyer can decide whether to approve or reject the deviation. SAP Business Network validates date and quantity both at the header level and the line-item level for purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and scheduling agreement releases. For purchase orders, SAP Business Network also validates price deviations. For example, a delivery-date tolerance is the maximum number of days the actual delivery can differ from the delivery date requested on an order. If you provide a delivery date for the entire order that is out of tolerance, an error message informs you to provide delivery dates at the line-item level instead. appears to the left of the item on the Confirming PO When an item has confirmation deviations, an alert icon page before you submit the confirmation. The alert icon also appears on the submitted confirmation. When you click the alert icon, a popup window displays with the message: The order confirmation for this item needs buyer approval. When you submit an order confirmation with deviations, SAP Business Network automatically generates an approval request and attaches the confirmation to the approval request. You can reconfirm items that are still awaiting approval. When an item’s approval status is not Approved, the system does not allow you to ship or invoice the item. If an order has at least one item with the approval status Approved awaiting change order, you cannot create an order confirmation for it. 64 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Order Confirmations The copy of the approval request is always routed to the copy supplier. Enabling Notifications for Deviation Approvals [page 65] Related Information Order Confirmation Approval Requests [page 62] Enabling Notifications for Deviation Approvals You can choose to receive email notifications whenever buyers approve or reject order confirmation deviations. Context If notifications are enabled for deviation approvals, SAP Business Network sends an email whenever a buyer approves or rejects one or more deviations from tolerance on an order confirmation. The notification includes up to 20 items. If the buyer has a multilevel approval process, a notification is not sent after initial approval in SAP Business Network because the item is still awaiting final approval on the backend system. By default, only the account administrator has permission to configure all notifications. Other users can configure notifications based on the permissions assigned to them. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon in the upper right corner, then in the dropdown, click Settings Network Notifications . 2. Go to the Electronic Order Routing section and check Send a notification when order confirmation approval status changes. 3. Enter from one to three email addresses, separated by commas, for the notification type. 4. Click Save. SAP Business Network displays a confirmation message that your account settings are successfully updated. 5. Click Close. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Order Confirmations PUBLIC 65 Multitier Order Collaboration This section provides topics about multitier purchase orders, order confirmations, and ship notices. A multitier supply chain involves an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) buyer and multiple suppliers collaborating together to produce a finished product. Multitier order collaboration provides end-to-end visibility and collaboration features for a multitier ordering process. It allows supply chain partners to view copies of orders, order confirmations, and ship notices (with financial fields masked) and create component receipts after receiving shipments. OEM buyers can manage their copy documents and view component shipments and receipts from tiered suppliers. Multitier order collaboration allows supply chain partners to do the following: • Contract manufacturers can view copies of orders, order confirmations, and ship notices on the SAP Business Network. • Contract manufacturers can submit new component receipts on the SAP Business Network as well as cancel them. • All supply chain partners can specify a routing preference (cXML or Online) for order response documents and copy documents. Workflow for Multitier Orders, Order Confirmations, and Ship Notices [page 67] Workflow for Subcontracting Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul Scenarios [page 68] Extended Collaboration Tab [page 68] Multitier Order Collaboration with Integrated Suppliers [page 69] Information Masking on Copy Documents [page 70] Ship Notice Cancellation for Multitier Orders [page 70] Viewing a Copy of a Multitier Order [page 71] Viewing a Copy of a Multitier Order Confirmation or Ship Notice [page 71] Sending a Component Receipt for a Multitier Ship Notice [page 72] Cancelling a Component Receipt [page 73] Related Information Multi-Tier Order Report [page 224] 66 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Multitier Order Collaboration Workflow for Multitier Orders, Order Confirmations, and Ship Notices The end-to-end workflow for multitier orders, order confirmations, and ship notices starts with an OEM placing an order with the Contract Manufacturer, and ends with the OEM sending a receipt to the Contract Manufacturer. The workflows for multitier order collaboration involve several different types of users: Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Contract Manufacturer (CM), Component Supplier (CS), and Logistics Provider (LP). A typical multitier ordering process has the following workflow: 1. The OEM places an order with the Contract Manufacturer (CM). 2. The Contract Manufacturer sends an Order Confirmation to the OEM. 3. The OEM also places an order with the Component Supplier (CS) with a drop ship address of the Contract Manufacturer. 4. The Component Supplier sends an Order Confirmation to the OEM. 5. The Component Supplier arranges with the Logistics Provider to ship the goods to the Contract Manufacturer. 6. The Component Supplier sends a Ship Notice to the OEM for the drop shipment to the Contract Manufacturer. 7. The Contract Manufacturer sends a Component Receipt to the OEM for the drop shipment. 8. The Contract Manufacturer arranges with the Logistics Provider to ship the assembly to the OEM. 9. The Contract Manufacturer sends a ship notice to the OEM. 10. The OEM sends a receipt to the Contract Manufacturer. Figure 2: Multitier Order Collaboration Workflow Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Multitier Order Collaboration PUBLIC 67 Workflow for Subcontracting Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul Scenarios The end-to-end workflow for subcontracting maintenance, repair, and overhaul scenarios starts with a buyer creating a maintenance order, and ends with the buyer sending a goods receipt to the supplier who then creates an invoice. Workflow scenarios vary, depending on the individual requirements defined between buyers and suppliers.The following example describes a possible workflow: 1. The buyer creates a maintenance order. The order defines the type of service: • • A repair (no material change) An upgrade (material change) 2. In response to the maintenance order, the buyer system automatically sends a subcontracting purchase order to SAP Business Network. 3. The supplier assesses the defect material, makes a quote for the repair cost, and optionally determines a delivery date. 4. The supplier confirms the purchase order with the new date, if applicable, and with an updated price (the quote). 5. The supplier sends the order confirmation, which contains the added details, to enable the buyer to trigger related back-end processes. 6. The buyer can optionally send the subcontracting purchase order with the updated price to SAP Business Network. 7. After repair or maintenance of the material is done, the supplier ships the goods and informs the buyer by creating the ship notice. 8. The buyer creates a goods receipt based on the purchase order. 9. The buyer sends a goods receipt to the supplier, indicating that the supplier can create the invoice, the last step of the process. Extended Collaboration Tab The Extended Collaboration tab on the Fulfillment page for suppliers contains documents used to collaborate with your extended supply chain. Tab Description Multi-Tier Orders Shows orders sent to tier two (and lower) suppliers to provide products and services to a supplier at the next higher level in the chain. Component Shipments Shows the actual component issue date, quantity, tracking number, receipt status, and other information. You can select multiple component ship notices to perform an action, such as creating a component receipt. Component Inventory Shows a component inventory snapshot for a given point in time. Return Shipments Shows return shipments from the buyer. 68 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Multitier Order Collaboration Tab Description Consignment Movements Shows movements of material purchased on consignment. Multi-Tier Shipments Shows shipments to another supplier instead of to the OEM buyer. You can select multiple component ship notices to perform an action, such as creating a component receipt. Multi-Tier Quality Inspection Shows quality inspection reports to suppliers and multitier partners. Component Consumption Shows component consumption messages sent to the buyer. Component Receipts Shows receipts for subcontracting components sent to the buyer. You can click a receipt number to open it and access its attachments. Multitier Order Collaboration with Integrated Suppliers SAP Business Network supports routing copies of multitier orders, order confirmations, and ship notices through cXML to integrated suppliers. If no route nodes are included in the Path cXML element, then only copies of the documents are processed and sent to other tiered suppliers with all financial fields masked. Invoices are not routed. Copy Requests are created for each copy node. The Copy Request adds an OriginalDocument with the payload ID of the source document for the copy request. A copy node results in the system requesting a copy of the document. For example, the following excerpt illustrates a copy node in the cXML header, which results in a copy being sent to a contract manufacturer in a multitier supply chain: <Header> <From> <Credential domain="NetworkID"> <Identity>AN990000000168</Identity> </Credential> </From> <To> <Credential domain="NetworkID"> <Identity>AN990000000169</Identity> </Credential> </To> <Sender> <Credential domain="NetworkID"> <Identity>AN990000000168</Identity> <SharedSecret>welcome</SharedSecret> </Credential> <UserAgent>Ariba Buyer 7.0</UserAgent> </Sender> <Path> <!-- Contract Manufacturer --> <Node type="copy"> <Credential domain="NetworkId"> <Identity>AN01000000170</Identity> </Credential> </Node> Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Multitier Order Collaboration PUBLIC 69 </Path> <!-- Original order to copy --> <OriginalDocument payloadID="989280592595-5564367883689744433@10.11.128.149"/> </Header> Electronic Order Routing Settings for Integrated Multitier Suppliers Integrated multitier suppliers that collaborate with each other and an OEM buyer via cXML documents must set the appropriate document routing settings to cXML. The following table provides Electronic Order Routing settings for Tier 1 (Contract Manufacturer) and Tier 2 (Component Supplier). Tiered Supplier Electronic Order Routing Options Setting Contract Manufacturer (Tier 1) Copy Order, Copy Confirmation, Copy Ship Notice cXML (also specify the URL to send cXML documents) Component Supplier (Tier 2) Order Response Documents cXML Information Masking on Copy Documents Multitier order collaboration enables masking of information in copies of orders, order confirmations, and ship notices sent to tier-one suppliers, such as contract manufacturers. Consequently, contract manufacturers cannot see the following information on orders sent to component suppliers: • • • • • Prices Taxes Payment terms PCard Information BillTo Information Information masking allows the OEM buyer to protect sensitive information and maintain a competitive advantage with supply chain partners. Ship Notice Cancellation for Multitier Orders If a component supplier cancels a ship notice, the copy of that ship notice is also updated to Canceled for the contract manufacturer. Cancelling a ship notice for multitier orders has the following restrictions: • • 70 The contract manufacturer cannot create a component receipt from the canceled copy of a ship notice. If a component receipt exists for a ship notice, that ship notice cannot be canceled. PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Multitier Order Collaboration

file://SBN/split/Supplier Guide to SAP B.content: Viewing a Copy of a Multitier Order You can view a copy of a multitier order sent by a buyer. Context An OEM buyer can send a copy of an order to tiered suppliers. Such multitier orders mask all financial information. For more information, see Information Masking on Copy Documents [page 70]. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended Collaboration Multi-Tier Orders . 2. To open an order, click the order number. All financial fields on the order are masked. Related ship notices and order confirmation documents appear in the header under Related Documents. The only actions available at the top of the page are Print and Export cXML. Viewing a Copy of a Multitier Order Confirmation or Ship Notice Copies of multitier order confirmations and ship notices are listed as related documents of the copy of the order. Context Copy documents mask all sensitive information, such as pricing and taxes. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended Collaboration Multi-Tier Orders . 2. To open an order, click the order number. 3. Under Related Documents click a related order confirmation or ship notice to open it. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Multitier Order Collaboration PUBLIC 71  Note You can also view copies of component ship notices on the Fulfillment > Extended Collaboration > Component Shipments page. All sensitive fields, such as prices and taxes, on the copy document are masked. The only actions available at the top of the page are Print and Export cXML. Sending a Component Receipt for a Multitier Ship Notice If you receive a drop shipment from a component supplier, you can create a component receipt to notify the OEM buyer. Context  Note If transaction rules Require the quantity of a component receipt item to not exceed the multitier ship notice quantity and Allow suppliers to create a component receipt for multiple multi-tier ship notices are enabled when you create a component receipt, any items that are already received are automatically removed from the items being flipped. This action prevents the creation of another receipt for an already-received item. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended Collaboration Multi-Tier Shipments . 2. Select one or more multitier ship notices, and then click Create Component Receipt. 3. Click Next. Confirm the information on the review page. To make changes, click Previous. 4. Click Submit. Related Information Informing a Buyer of Receipt of Components [page 132] 72 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Multitier Order Collaboration Cancelling a Component Receipt Cancelled component receipts have the Obsoleted status. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended Collaboration Component Receipts . 2. To open a receipt, click a receipt number. 3. Click Cancel. 4. To confirm that you want to cancel the component receipt, click Yes. The status of the receipt changes to Obsoleted. 5. Click Done. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Multitier Order Collaboration PUBLIC 73 Shipping This section provides topics about shipping and ship notices. The Items to Ship Tab [page 74] Items to Ship Tile [page 75] Batch Assignments to Shipments [page 77] Creating a Ship Notice with Advanced Packaging [page 78] Uploading Serial Numbers for Ship Notices [page 81] Viewing and Exporting Serial Number Lists in Orders [page 82] Attaching a Quality Certificate to a Ship Notice [page 83] Configuring GTL Numbering as a Supplier [page 83] Uploading Certificates When Using the Advance Ship Notice Upload File [page 84] Related Information Ship Notice Barcode Labels Ship Notices for Customers The Items to Ship Tab You can use the Items to Ship tab to create and organize shipments. Suppliers often need to create shipments of items their buyers want by specific dates, sometimes grouping items into the same shipment that were ordered through different purchase orders. From the Orders Orders and Releases Items to Ship tab, you can create shipments based on dates due, and can create ship notices from multiple purchase orders and scheduling agreement releases. You can also create shipments for stock transport orders.  Note On the Items to Ship page, all line items for the same purchase order are hidden if either of the following conditions exist: 74 • A purchase-order line item or schedule line item has a quality inspection Usage Decision that isn't accepted, and transaction rule Allow suppliers to send ship notices only after receiving acceptance of inspection results is enabled. • A purchase-order line item has a quality notification that isn't in the Closed status, and transaction rule Require suppliers to close a quality notification for an item before they can create a ship notice for the complaint quantity is enabled. PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Shipping For items in an order with a specified unlimited quantity tolerance, you can generate unlimited shipments until the expiration date is reached. Similarly, items that have reached the underdelivery quantity tolerance specified in the order don't appear on the Items to Ship tab.  Tip For long-term purchase order agreements that typically are valid for a year and have line items with unlimited overdelivery, use the Order Number: Exact number filter on the Items to Ship tab to create ship notices for the order until the expiration date is reached. cXML Elements for the Items to Ship Tab The following elements support the Items to Ship tab: • ScheduleLine For more information, see the cXML Reference Guide . Items to Ship Tile You can use the Items to Ship Workbench tile to filter purchase order items and generate ship notices from SAP Business Network. Filter your purchase order items using the following parameters: • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • Customers Order numbers Creation date Need by date Customer locations Ship by date Company codes Purchasing organizations Purchasing groups Product group Ordering address IDs Part numbers Customer part numbers Planner codes Order type Category Stock transfer type Ship from location Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Shipping PUBLIC 75 • • • • • • • • Supplier batch ID Confirmation status Shipping status Receiving status Invoicing status External document type Transport terms Storage locations The following table columns are available in the Items to Ship tile:: • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • Customer Creation Date Cumulative Received Quantity Manufacturer Name Manufacturer Part ID Category Customer Part No. External Document Type Order No. Item No. Supplier Part No. Description Schedule Line No. Need By Ship By Commitment Level Requested Quantity Shipped Quantity Received Quantity Due Quantity  Note The Confirmation, Shipping, Receiving, and Invoicing status filters operate at the line-item level rather than the schedule-line level. For example, if a purchase order item contains three schedule lines where two are shipped and one is pending, the item’s overall shipping status is evaluated as Partially Shipped. Therefore, when a user applies the Exclude fully shipped filter, all three schedule lines—including the two already shipped—will appear in the search results. However, the shipped schedule lines are displayed in a disabled (grayed-out) state to indicate they are not selectable, as the filter logic is based on the parent line-item status, not individual schedule-line statuses. 76 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Shipping Related Information The Workbench Batch Assignments to Shipments You can link a supplier batch to orders and shipments, and search for items by batch IDs. On the Items To Confirm and Items To Ship tabs of the Orders Orders and Releases page, the Customer Batch ID and Supplier Batch ID fields appear on the More list of fields that you can add to the table. The list shows the supplier batch from the order, if it's present, or from the order confirmation. To view confirmed supplier batch IDs, click the View Confirmed Batch ID link. You can search for items by Supplier Batch ID on the Items To Confirm and Items To Ship tabs. A batch lookup component allows suppliers to search for batches based on the currently selected customer and part number (one or more) or customer part number (one or more). Looking Up Orders and Shipments by Supplier Batch You can track customer or supplier batches in orders, order confirmations, ship notices, and component inventory. Context When you create a ship notice from an order, the Supplier Batch ID and Customer Batch ID values are automatically copied from the order. You can also click Lookup to search for and select a different batch ID using the same batch lookup component from the Items To Ship page. When you create a ship notice, the customer batch and consumed quantity are validated based on the component inventory. If the customer batch is in component inventory, the consumed quantity can't exceed the available quantity in inventory. Procedure 1. Find the Supplier Batch ID field. 2. Click Lookup to display the Batches window. 3. Start typing a batch ID, then click Search. 4. In the results list, check boxes for batches, then click Select to select them. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Shipping PUBLIC 77 Creating a Ship Notice with Advanced Packaging When creating a ship notice, you can use the advanced packaging wizard to pack ship-notice items. Prerequisites • • • The transaction rule Allow suppliers to use advanced packaging on ship notices is enabled. When GS1 numbering is used, the buyer has enabled the Require suppliers to provide a Global Individual Asset ID for line items on ship notices that conforms to the Serial Shipping Container Code (SSCC) format rule. The buyer has uploaded packaging instructions. Context  Note To create a ship notice without the advanced packaging feature, see Creating and Ship Notice and Ship Notice Barcode Labels in Receiving and fulfilling orders. With the ship-notice advanced packaging wizard, you can: • Use a wizard to guide you through steps to create handling units, define handling unit hierarchies, and print labels. The wizard uses the packaging instructions provided by buyers to help you plan how to pack items. You can also edit the packaging instructions and build handling units on the fly. • Set your own auto-numbering settings, which override buyer auto-numbering settings if any were made. And support of multiple same-level packaging materials enables you to define those instructions. • On a ship notice details page, the Packed Items tab is visible to integrated suppliers, so they as well as hosted suppliers can print handling unit labels, when labels are available. A buyer is also able to assign additional capabilities that you can use and to make certain tasks required. For more information, see Tasks for Handling-Unit Profiles [page 79]. Procedure 1. Go to Orders Orders and Releases . 2. Choose the purchase order, then on the purchase order details page click Create ship notice. 3. Verify the items to ship. 4. Click Pack Items. • 78 If packaging instructions exist for all items, the Confirm packing plan page opens. Skip to Step 6 [page 79]. PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Shipping • If some items do not have packaging instructions, the Define packaging instructions page opens. Proceed to Step 5 [page 79]. 5. To create packaging instructions, click Define instructions, add your instructions, and click Next. • Line items that must be packed in a handling unit are identified with the message Handling Unit (required). • If the buyer enabled one or more advanced packaging tasks in your handling unit profile, complete the required tasks plus any other tasks as desired. For details, see Tasks for Handling-Unit Profiles [page 79]. The Confirm packing plan page opens. 6. Review packing plan details. • To put an item in a different handling unit, click the Move to link for that item and choose the desired handling unit from the dropdown. The dropdown list shows only the handling units with sufficient free space to add the item. • To change packed quantities for a handling unit, click Edit for the handling unit you wish to edit.  Note Make sure that the packed quantities are equal to the ship notice quantities. The Packed percentage for each handling unit must be 100% before you can proceed to the next step to Print labels. • If auxiliary materials are available in the packaging instructions, you can add auxiliary materials to a handling unit. Click the add  dropdown for the handling unit, choose Add Auxiliary Material, and choose the material type. If fields for the material are prepopulated by the packaging instructions, you can edit the fields to use your own data. 7. Click Next to approve the packing plan. The Print labels page opens.  Note To make more changes, click Define instructions to return to the Define packaging instructions page. 8. Print the desired labels, then click Next. A printer icon  shows only for handling unit types that are set to allow printing a label. The Review Ship Notice page opens. 9. Verify the ship notice content, then click Submit. Tasks for Handling-Unit Profiles Suppliers can be assigned additional capabilities by a buyer to customize handling units for a shipment. Buyers can create handling unit profiles to assign to one or more of their suppliers or supplier groups. A profile enables the specified suppliers to do one or more advanced packaging tasks when they create a ship notice with the advanced packaging wizard. Some tasks can be required by the buyer. The following tasks are available to include in a handling unit profile. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Shipping PUBLIC 79 Handling-unit profile capability Description Enable suppliers to add handling unit Enabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can add a new handling unit to the advanced packaging wizard. Enable suppliers to move and rearrange the handling units on the Confirm Packing screen Enabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can move materials from one handling unit to another available handling unit. Enable suppliers to edit items on the Confirm Packing screen Enabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can edit the quantity of a handling unit. Enable suppliers to edit values on Define Instructions screen Enabled by default. Enable suppliers to edit the dimension values of handling units Disabled by default. When enabled, supplers can change the following values for a handling unit: • On the Define packaging instructions page, suppliers can change Length, Height, and Width. • On the Confirm packing plan page, suppliers can change Length, Height, Width, Gross weight, and Net weight.  Note The supplier cannot change dimension values on the Print labels page. Enable suppliers to add empty packaging material to a handling unit Disabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can add empty packaging material, such as boxes, to handling units in a packaging plan, except to the highest-level handling unit. The empty packaging material can be used to help stabilize items in a partially filled handling unit, with or instead of auxiliary material. Show auxiliary materials in auto packaging Disabled by default. When enabled, suppliers can see on the Confirm packaging page the auxiliary materials in an automatically generated packaging plan, and make any desired changes. When disabled, suppliers can still add or remove auxiliary materials to a packaging plan that is not automatically generated. Enable suppliers to remove auxiliary materials in auto packaging This task requires that the task Show auxiliary materials in auto packaging is also enabled. When enabled, suppliers can delete auxiliary materials from automatically generated packaging plans on the Confirm packaging page. Enable suppliers to add auxiliary materials in auto packaging 80 PUBLIC This task requires that the task Show auxiliary materials in auto packaging is also enabled. Related Information Serial Number Report [page 235] 82 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Shipping Attaching a Quality Certificate to a Ship Notice You can attach quality certificates at the header level or item level of ship notices. Context In the header of a ship notice, there is a section called Quality Certificates. It lists all quality certificates (required and optional) that have been attached at the header level. If a file has not been attached for a certificate yet, it reads, “No attachment yet.” Quality certificates can also be attached to line items. Procedure 1. In the Quality Certificates section of the header or a line item, click Attach file. 2. Select a certificate. 3. Click Choose file. 4. Select the file, and click Open. 5. Click Add attachment.  Note • By default, the cumulative size of attachments associated with a document cannot exceed 10 MB. Customers can request to change that limit, which can be changed from 10 MB to 100 MB. • During file upload, attachment files are converted to plain ASCII text using base64 encoding. This conversion increases the file size by approximately 35%. Therefore, the actual file size limit is 65% of the configured maximum limit. For example, if the maximum allowed limit is set to 10 MB (10000 KB), the actual total attachment file size that users can add is 6500 KB. • SAP Business Network stores attachments for a maximum period of eighteen months, after which the attachments expire and are no longer available online. Logistics Providers and Transportation of Goods [page 86] Supplier Copies of Transport Requests and Transport Confirmations [page 87] Workflows for Transport Processes [page 88] Workflow for Ship Notices by Third-Party Suppliers [page 89] Viewing Transport Requests [page 90] Viewing Transport Confirmations [page 91] Accepting or Rejecting a Transport Request [page 92] Collecting or Cancelling a Consignment [page 93] Logistics Providers and Transportation of Goods SAP Business Network for Supply Chain supports integrated third-party logistics providers in a buyer-initiated transport process. Third-party logistics providers transport goods from one buyer location to another, or from a supplier to the buyer. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain buyers can request a logistics relationship with you instead of a standard trading relationship. The logistics relationship allows you to receive transport requests from the buyer and send and receive transport confirmations. When a buyer requests a logistics relationship, the SAP Business Network sends new logistics relationship request letter to you. Logistics transactions can be conducted using an integrated process through cXML or online in the SAP Business Network portal. You can create transport confirmations to accept or reject a transport request, fully or partially. Later, you can send additional transport confirmations to indicate when the consignment is collected or the transportation service has been canceled.  Note Only buyers can create transport requests. Fulfillment > Transport Requests Page The Transport Requests page lists all transport requests received.  Note Only suppliers with a logistics relationship with an SAP Business Network for Supply Chain customer can see this page. 86 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Logistics When you open a transport request, the Transport Request page appears. It has header information about the requester and the carrier, and the following sections for each consignment: • • • • • • • • • Status Ship From Deliver To Transport Dates Terms of Delivery Transport Information Packaging Comments Packaging Details At the top of the page, you can click Create Confirmation to create a confirmation for the request. Options include: • • • Confirm Entire Request Reject Entire Request Update Consignments Fulfillment > Transport Confirmations Page The Transport Confirmations page lists all transport confirmations sent from your company to companies that requested logistics services. When you open a transport confirmation, the read-only Transport Confirmation page appears. It has header information, including From and To information, and detailed information about each consignment.  Note Only suppliers with a logistics relationship with an SAP Business Network for Supply Chain customer can see this page. Supplier Copies of Transport Requests and Transport Confirmations A buyer can send copies of transport requests and associated transport confirmations to suppliers, to inform them of the current status of the request. There are routing options for copies of transport requests and transport confirmations. Suppliers that select the default Online routing option for copies of transport requests and transport confirmation can view current transport information on the Transport Details tab of the Ship Notice page. For more information about routing options, see the Configuring Document Routing guide. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Logistics PUBLIC 87 Workflows for Transport Processes A logistics provider can respond to transport requests, either online on SAP Business Network or through cXML sent from an external system. Transport Process Initiated by the Buyer to Transport Goods to Another Buyer Location The following describes the workflow for a transport process initiated by the buyer to transport goods to another buyer location.. 1. The buyer sends a transport request to the logistics provider. It includes details about consignments, origin and destination information, commercial terms, means and methods of shipment, transport equipment needed, required conditions for transport, summary information, and more. 2. The logistics provider sends a transport confirmation back to the buyer to either accept or reject the request for each consignment. If the request is accepted, the logistics provider confirms the shipping date, price, and so on. 3. The logistics provider picks up the goods from the buyer's warehouse and informs the buyer by sending a transport confirmation with a consignment status of "collected". Similarly, if the logistics provider is unable to pick up the goods for a consignment, they send a transport confirmation with a status of "canceled". Figure 3: Transport Process, Goods Between Buyer Locations Transport Process Initiated by the Buyer to Transport Goods from a Supplier to the Buyer The following describes the workflow for a transport process initiated by the buyer to transport goods from a supplier to the buyer. 88 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Logistics 1. The buyer sends a purchase order to the supplier. 2. The supplier sends a ship notice indicating the goods are ready to be collected. 3. The buyer sends a transport request to the logistics provider. 4. The logistics provider sends a transport confirmation to the buyer to either accept or reject the request for each consignment. If the request is accepted, the logistics provider confirms the shipping date, price, and so on. 5. The logistics provider picks up the goods from the buyer's warehouse and informs the buyer by sending a transport confirmation with a consignment status of "collected". Similarly, if the logistics provider is unable to pick up the goods for a consignment, they send a transport confirmation with a status of "canceled". Figure 4: Transport Process, Goods Moved from Supplier to Buyer Workflow for Ship Notices by Third-Party Suppliers The end-to-end workflow for ship notices by third-part suppliers starts with an OEM issuing an order or scheduling agreement, and ends with settlement by the OEM or the supplier. 1. An original equipment manufacturer (OEM) issues a purchase order or scheduling agreement to a supplier. 2. The buyer sends a copy of the purchase order or scheduling agreement to the third-party logistics provider (LP), or specifies the LP in the purchase order or scheduling agreement cXML file. 3. The supplier sends an order confirmation to the OEM. 4. The supplier advises the LP, outside of the system, that the product is available for transport to the OEM. 5. The LP sends the OEM a ship notice on behalf of the supplier, and the supplier automatically receives a copy ship notice. 6. If needed, the OEM sends a status update request to the LP, which automatically updates the ship notice status in the supplier system. 7. The OEM issues a goods receipt notification to the supplier, which automatically updates the LP system. 8. One of the following actions triggers settlement: • The OEM buyer performs the evaluated receipt settlement process. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Logistics PUBLIC 89 • The supplier generates an invoice. Key Figures [page 95] Views for Planning Collaboration [page 103] Updating Stock-on-Hand Levels [page 104] Configuring Email Notifications for Buyer Planning Collaboration Updates [page 105] Forecast Collaboration [page 106] Component Planning Collaboration [page 112] Supplier-Managed Inventory [page 120] Product Replenishment [page 121] The Direct-Material Sales Report [page 125] Key Figures Buyers and suppliers can use key figures in planning and forecast collaboration. Key figures contain numeric data that is represented either as a quantity or as a monetary value. Buyers and suppliers use key figures for planning and forecast collaboration to communicate about goods and materials. Typically, buyers want information about a set of key figures, not just one or two. A set of key figures is referred to as a view. Suppliers provide buyers with information about key figures, either through the user interface from the Planning Collaboration page or from the ... Upload/Download Jobs Planning tab using Excel files. There are two types of key figures: • Standard – A standard key figure is a figure that cannot be derived or calculated from other figures, such as the number of employees in a company. Other examples are sales, fixed costs, variable costs, and quantity produced. One example of a standard key figure used in planning collaboration is ORDER_FORECAST. This key figure contains the order forecast quantity. • Calculated – A calculated key figure is a figure that is derived or calculated using other figures. For example, if you have the SALES_REVENUE and EMPLOYEES key figures, you can create a calculated key figure with the sales revenue per employee using formula SALES_REVENUE/EMPLOYEES. Key figures used in a formula for a calculated key figure can be either standard or calculated key figures. One example of a calculated key figure used in planning collaboration is FORECAST_DEVIATION. This key figure is a calculation of the accuracy of the actual forecast demand from the committed forecast demand. It is calculated by subtracting the order forecast quantity (ORDER_FORECAST) from the forecast committed quantity (FORECAST_COMMIT). The formula is FORECAST_COMMIT-ORDER_FORECAST. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 95 See Key Figures Reference for Planning and Forecast Collaboration Views [page 96] for a list of the key figures defined for the planning and forecast collaboration views. See Key Figures Reference for the Component Planning Collaboration View [page 99] for a list of the key figures defined for component planning collaboration. For these key figures to populate, their related transactions must arrive on SAP Business Network after the planning or forecast records are created.
