file://SBN/split/Supplier Guide to SAP B.content: Key Figure Display Name Configuration ID Type Description Components with shortage (Finished good section only) COMPONENTS_WITH_SHORTAG E Calculated The total count of components used by the finished good that have a shortage for each time bucket in the next 30 days. This key figure only displays when you use the Daily time bucket. Beginning inventory for component (Component section only) BEGINNING_INVENTORY_COMP ONENT Calculated For the current date, the value is the STOCK_ON_HAND. For all other time buckets, the value is the ending inventory of the previous day. Ending inventory for component (Component section only) ENDING_INVENTORY_COMPONE Calculated NT The ending inventory for the component. Key Figures for Unreceived Orders and Optional Matching for Certain Criteria Description This feature lets buyers display to their suppliers what firmed or replenishment order quantities aren't yet received. This feature also enables buyers and suppliers to ignore the supplier part number or system ID for part matching. And, this feature can allow suppliers to populate certain key figures without having a planning record. Prerequisites • • The buyer is enabled with the Supply chain collaboration and Planning collaboration entitlements. On the Planning Settings Assign suppliers System default settings page, the Match transaction quantities to transactional key figures setting has the subsetting Ignore the Supplier Part no. set to Yes. Buyer Administrator Interface Changes This feature makes the following changes for key figures: • On the Planning Settings Assign suppliers System default settings page, this feature adds the setting Match transaction quantities to transactional key figures to the Supplier Managed Inventory and Forecast sections. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 101 • This setting has two subsettings: • • • • Ignore the System ID – Settings: Yes or No This setting supports the following transactional key figures: • • • • • • Ignore the Supplier Part no. – Settings: Yes or No ASN received Firmed orders Goods received Order received Total shipment When a subsetting is set to Yes, purchase orders, ship notices, and goods receipts can include in transactional key figures any items that have no match for the field named by the subsetting. Items must still have a matching Buyer Part ID and Plant ID to be included. This feature adds the following transaction-based key figures: Key Figure Display Name Configuration ID Type Description Open firmed order OPEN_FIRMED_ORDER Calculated The total quantity that isn't received, per shipment item in a firmed order. When the setting Match transaction quantities to transactional key figures has subsetting Ignore the Supplier Part no. set to Yes, this key figure includes items that have no matching Supplier Part no. in related transaction documents. This key figure is available in the following planning collaboration views: • • Forecast Supplier managed replenishment (standard and days-of-supply) • Supplier managed inventory (standard and days-of-supply) 102 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration Key Figure Display Name Configuration ID Type Description Open replenishment order OPEN_REPL_ORDER Calculated The total quantity that isn't received, per shipment item in a replenishment order. This goods-receipt number is calculated by subtracting the Order received quantity from the Published replenishment quantity. When the setting Match transaction quantities to transactional key figures has subsetting Ignore the Supplier Part no. set to Yes, this key figure includes items that have no matching Supplier Part no. in related transaction documents. This key figure is available in the Supplier managed replenishment (standard and days-of-supply) view. Supplier Changes to Functionality With this feature, suppliers no longer need a planning record before they can populate key figures with transaction document data. Views for Planning Collaboration Suppliers can use views for planning collaboration to help visualize planning data. Views are used in planning and forecast collaboration to share information between buyers and suppliers. A view is a collection of key figures (standard, calculated, and custom) and attributes (standard and customer-defined) that provide a window into the planning data. The following table lists the standard views: View Description Aggregated forecast across locations Aggregated version of the forecast view across multiple locations Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 103 View Description Component planning collaboration view Component planning collaboration data for a finished good and its components.  Note The Component planning collaboration view does not support customer-defined attributes. External manufacturing visibility Data about external manufacturing items Forecast Forecast data for planning items Supplier managed inventory Information about supplier-managed inventory Supplier managed inventory days-of-supply Information about the days of supply left on the supplier's inventory Supplier managed replenishment Information about supplier-managed replenishment Supplier managed replenishment days-of-supply Information about the days of supply of replenishment In addition to the standard views, buyers can create custom views. Buyers configure views to contain the exact information they need. Some example configurations are hiding key figures, renaming key figure display names, adding custom key figures, and adding customer-defined attributes. Each view, whether standard or custom, has its own set of key figures and attributes. Custom views also have conditions defined for them. SAP Business Network evaluates these conditions to determine which view to use for a planning item. If a planning item does not match the conditions of any of the custom views for the process type, the standard view is used. Buyers can set the key figure order for both standard and custom views. This order is visible in all the view's planning records, both in the user interface and in downloaded Excel files created from running Upload/Download jobs. SAP Business Network assigns a planning item to a view when cXML updates are made. If the planning item's view was deleted since the last cXML update, the standard view is used for the planning item. When a planning item's view is modified, the next time a cXML update occurs, the view criteria are reevaluated. The planning item’s view always matches the existing criteria at the last cXML update. Updating Stock-on-Hand Levels Suppliers can update stock-on-hand levels for planning items in the supplier-managed inventory, manufacturing visibility, replenishment, and forecast processes. 104 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration Prerequisites For the supplier-managed inventory and replenishment processes, the rule Allow suppliers to edit supplier stock on hand must be enabled. Procedure 1. Go to the Planning Planning Collaboration page. This page lists entries for supplier managed inventory, manufacturing visibility, replenishment, and forecast. 2. Open the Stock on hand popup from either the Status column or a View Details icon. • In the Status column of the Stock on hand section, click the status for the part number you want to update. • At the end of the row for the part number you want to update, click the View Details ( ) icon. In the part-number details page that opens, click the Stock on hand link. The Stock on hand popup opens. 3. At the bottom of the popup, click the Edit button. 4. Update the desired stock-on-hand levels. 5. When finished editing, save your changes. • • Choose Save to save your changes and exit the page. Choose Save and Send from the dropdown to save and submit the changes to your customer. Configuring Email Notifications for Buyer Planning Collaboration Updates You can receive email notifications when your buyers make planning collaboration updates for the Forecast, Replenishment, and Supplier managed inventory planning process types. Procedure 1. Click the Account Settings icon in the upper right corner, then in the dropdown, click Settings Network Notifications . 2. Go to the Planning Collaboration Updates section. 3. Enter a minimum of one and a maximum of three email addresses to use when sending the notifications. 4. Specify when to send the notifications. • Immediate notifications – Choose Send an immediate notification when buyers share planning collaboration updates. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 105 When a buyer makes planning collaboration updates, an email notification is sent to the specified address. This notification contains the number of planning records the buyer created or updated. • Digest notifications – Choose Send a digest notification about planning collaboration at this frequency, in hours:, and choose the number of hours from the pulldown menu. If there are planning collaboration updates during the selected time period, an email notification is sent to the specified address. This notification lists the buyers who sent updates. For each of these buyers, the number of planning records the buyer created or updated for each planning process type is also listed. Forecast Collaboration Suppliers can plan and commit to future goods deliveries using forecast information from their customers. The forecast collaboration feature enables suppliers to make commitments to deliver quantities of goods to supply upcoming demands forecast by buyers. This allows suppliers to schedule operations and plan capacity accordingly. For example, a supplier could build commonly-used subassemblies based on an anticipated demand. For another example, a supplier could schedule deliveries of parts in advance of an anticipated increase in demand, minimizing last-minute rush shipments and stock run-outs. Additionally, forecast collaboration enables suppliers to make commitments to deliver quantities of goods specified in buyer forecast demands. Alternatively, suppliers can send comments to buyers about forecast quantities and can request revisions. The forecast collaboration feature provides the following to suppliers: • • • • A simple table view of buyer forecast demand The ability to commit to forecast quantities based on supplier capacity and inventory Daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly time-bucket views of forecast demand Integration with other ERP and planning systems, both for buyers and for suppliers Workflow for Forecast Collaboration [page 107] Editing Forecast Quantities Before Committing [page 107] Committing to Given Forecast Quantities [page 108] Viewing Forecast Collaboration Data [page 109] CSV Upload for Forecast Commit [page 110] Multitier Forecast for Integrated Suppliers [page 112] Related Information Forecast Template for Upload/Download 106 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration Workflow for Forecast Collaboration The end-to-end workflow for forecast collaboration starts with a buyer sending forecast demand data, and ends with the buyer receiving commitments or comments from suppliers. 1. The buyer extracts net demand data after material requirements planning or forecast planning, and transmits this data to SAP Business Network via cXML. 2. The supplier logs on to SAP Business Network to view forecast demand data, enter comments, or download the forecast demand data to an Excel or CSV file. 3. If the supplier downloads the Excel or CSV file, the supplier can edit the comments in it to show supply commitments or proposed changes, including upside commitments. Editing Forecast Quantities Before Committing You can change the quantities committed any number of times before you send the commitment to the buyer. Context The buyer can either choose a preferred time series granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly) or allow you to choose one. If the buyer chooses one, you can only edit and commit data in that time series. The preferred time series granularity is shown when you open the planning item and also when you click on the Part details popup. Procedure 1. View the Planning Forecast table containing the forecast quantities to which you want to commit. 2. To edit a forecast quantity, click the editing pencil icon  in the Actions column. 3. Optional: In the Forecast Commit dialog that opens, fill in a value for inventory, and add a comment as desired.  Note The Forecast Commit popup shows the commit lock horizon period in the header's Commit Horizon field. When a forecast time series is within the commit lock horizon, you can no longer edit those quantities or use the Copy Forecast to Commit button. 4. Click the calendar icon and select the month of forecasts desired. 5. Do one of the following: • Enter quantities to which you want to commit into one or more Committed fields.  Note As you edit the value in a Committed field, Forecast Commit automatically recalculates the related Difference value. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 107 • To commit to a quantity greater than the forecast quantity, enter the quantity into the desired Upside field.  Note This entry communicates to the buyer how much capacity the supplier has beyond the forecast demand. This information allows the buyer to capture the additional supplier capacity as desired. • To commit to all the quantities forecast, click Copy Forecast to Commit.  Note This button can’t be used for a forecast time series that is within the commit lock horizon. 6. Do one of the following: • • • To close the Forecast Commit dialog without saving your revisions, click Close. To commit to a quantity you entered, and keep the Forecast Commit dialog open, click Commit. To commit to a quantity you entered, and close the Forecast Commit dialog, click Commit And Close. Commit or Commit And Close records the commitment quantities, but does not send the commitment to the buyer. You can change the quantities committed any number of times before you send the commitment to the buyer. 7. To send the commitment details to the buyer, in the Forecast table, click the page icon in the Actions column. 8. In the Commit Forecast Data dialog, click Yes. SAP Business Network sends the commitment to the buyer and disables the page icon so that you can’t send the commitment again. You can view the details of the commitment in the Replenishment Fulfillment Product tab. Committing to Given Forecast Quantities The buyer receives your commitment for the number of goods you will supply during the forecast period. Context You can commit quantities using any time-series view: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly. If a buyer sets a commit freeze horizon, you can see the freeze in effect in all time-series views.  Note When a forecast time series is within the commit lock horizon, you can no longer edit those quantities or use the Copy Forecast to Commit button. To see the commit lock horizon for forecast item, hover over the page icon in the Actions column. Or, go to the item's details page and click Part details, which shows the Planning horizon period. 108 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration Procedure 1. Go to Planning Forecast . 2. View a forecast table containing the forecast quantities to which you want to commit. 3. To make a commitment to supply a forecast quantity, unchanged, for the next 365 days, click the circled checkmark icon  in the Actions column. 4. To confirm the quantities committed, in the Commit Forecast Data dialog, click Yes. This step records the commitment quantities, but does not send the commitment to the buyer. You can change the quantities committed any number of times before sending the commitment to the buyer, unless the forecast time series is within the commit lock horizon. 5. Optional: To change the quantities committed before sending the commitment, see Editing Forecast Quantities Before Committing [page 107]. 6. To send the commitment to the buyer, click the page icon in the Actions column. Then in the Commit Forecast Data dialog that opens, click Yes. SAP Business Network sends the commitment to the buyer. Also, the page icon becomes disabled so that you can’t send the commitment again. You can view the details of the commitment in the Replenishment Fulfillment Product tab. Viewing Forecast Collaboration Data You can customize the criteria to search and which data fields to display. Context  Note Alternatively, administrators can view forecast commitment documents by searching for the document numbers in the administrator user interface. Procedure 1. Choose Planning Forecast . SAP Business Network displays the forecast search filters and table. 2. Optional: To find specific forecasts, do the following: a. Click the triangle next to Search Filters to expand the display of filter fields. b. Enter search criteria into any of the filter fields as desired. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 109  Note Certain fields, such as Customer Planner Code and Customer Part #, have a type-ahead feature that lists known valid choices as you type. c. Next to Display Forecast By, select the time increment for the display, Day, Week, Month, or Year. d. Click Search. The Forecast table displays the results of the search.  Note Forecasts for a given lead time are highlighted with the same color used to highlight the respective lead time. Quantities committed in excess of forecast quantities appear as positive numbers on a green background in the Difference column. Committed quantities needed to meet a forecast demand appear as negative numbers on a dark gray background in the Difference column. 3. Optional: Optionally add or remove columns from the Forecast table. a. Click the Forecast button to the upper-right of the Forecast table. b. Check the box next to the name of each column you want to make visible. c. Uncheck the box next to the name of each column you want to not appear. d. Click Close. 4. Optional: To scroll the Forecast table for forecasts from a different period, do one of the following: • • For an earlier period, click the left-pointing arrow in the Forecast table header For a later period, click the right-pointing arrow in the Forecast table header 5. Optional: To page through additional pages of search results, either click the left or right arrow next to Page, or select a page number from the Page dropdown menu. 6. Optional: To select which columns appear in the Forecast table, do the following: a. Click the table icon that appears to the far right of the Forecast table header. b. In the Order Forecast Columns dialog, check the box next to the name of every column you want to make visible, and click Close. c. To sort the table by any of the following columns, click the column name: Customer Part #, Supplier Part #, Unit, Plant, Lead Time, Inventory, Last Modified. This toggles between ascending and descending sorts. SAP Business Network retains your preferences for viewing the Forecast table. 7. To download the data in the Forecast table into a CSV file, click Download CSV, select an option, and click OK. CSV Upload for Forecast Commit As a supplier, you can upload forecast commitments in bulk by using CSV files. Workflow for CSV Upload for Forecast Commit [page 111] Uploading Forecast Commitments in CSV Files [page 111] 110 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration

file://SBN/split/Supplier Guide to SAP B.content: Workflow for CSV Upload for Forecast Commit The end-to-end workflow for forecast commit starts with a supplier downloading a file of forecast quantities and ends with the buyer viewing the file with the supplier commitments. 1. The supplier downloads a CSV file containing forecast quantities. 2. The supplier enters values for commited quantities into the CSV file. 3. The supplier uploads the updated CSV file. 4. The buyer views the commitments of the supplier. Uploading Forecast Commitments in CSV Files You can download, modify, and upload forecast data in bulk. Context To instead use the … Upload/Download Template for Upload/Download [page 177]. feature to upload multiple forecast changes in Excel, see Forecast Procedure 1. View the Planning Forecast page table containing the forecast quantities to which you want to commit. 2. Click Download CSV. SAP Business Network downloads a forecast CSV template. 3. Open the CSV file, enter desired values into the cells in the Committed column, and save the CSV file. 4. Click Upload CSV. SAP Business Network opens the Forecast Commit Uploads popup window containing a search filter and a table of previous uploads. 5. Add a name for the revised CSV file. Click Choose File and browse to the revised CSV file. 6. Select the revised CSV file and click Open. 7. Click Upload. 8. Optional: Click Refresh to update the values in the Status column. The Status column displays the status of the uploads.  Note If an upload fails, click the download icon  to open a log file that reports the errors that caused the failure. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 111 Multitier Forecast for Integrated Suppliers Suppliers can enable routing of product activity messages to tiered suppliers using cXML. For product activity messages to be delivered to a tiered supplier, the following configurations must be made on that supplier's system. This configuration also allows suppliers to see product activity messages from the Product Activity • • … tab. The supplier has a trading relationship with the buyer. The Product Activity Message is set to Online or cXML. Check this setting by clicking the Settings icon in the upper right corner, then in the dropdown, click Settings Account Electronic Order Routing . Copy Process for Product Activity Messages Primary suppliers use cXML to send product activity messages to tiered suppliers, also called copy suppliers. A primary supplier specifies the number of tiered suppliers in the Path element of the cXML header ProductActivityMessage. For complete information about these elements and their attributes, see the cXML Reference Guide .  Note Sensitive data, like pricing, is omitted from a cXML document delivered to tiered suppliers. Tiered suppliers can view and access their product activity messages on the SAP Business Network user interface. • … Product Activity tab of the To search for product activity documents that are for only copy suppliers, check the Show copy documents search filter.  Note When the Show copy documents checkbox is unchecked, only documents for the primary supplier are displayed. Copy documents are not displayed. • If necessary, click the Show/Hide Columns  icon and click Multi-Tier to show that column, which identifies which table entries are multitier messages. • To download a product activity message and view its forecast details, click its Export cXML link. Component Planning Collaboration Component planning collaboration lets buyers and suppliers view the forecast planning data for a finished good and its components together. Forecast planning items are created or updated when buyers send product activity messages and when suppliers send product replenishment messages. When component planning collaboration is enabled, in addition to forecast 112 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration planning items, component planning collaboration items are also created or updated. For a component planning collaboration item to be created or updated, the item must be included in a Bill of Materials (BOM) stored in SAP Business Network. Each finished good has a component planning collaboration record. These records are created from Bill of Materials (BOM) records extracted from SAP Business Network. A BOM contains the list of components needed to manufacture a finished good. For more information about how BOM data is used for component planning collaboration, see Component Planning Collaboration Use of BOM Data [page 118]. To enable component planning collaboration, the buyer administrator edits the settings to toggle Enable component planning collaboration on. When this setting is set, if a planning item matches a finished good or a component stored in a BOM in SAP Business Network, its corresponding component planning collaboration item is created or updated. Component planning collaboration items are only created or updated when there is a match. Component planning collaboration uses the Component planning collaboration view. This view has two sections, Finished good section and Component section. Each section has its own key figures. For more information about the key figures in the Component planning collaboration view, see Key Figures Reference for the Component Planning Collaboration View [page 99]. Buyer administrators can also add custom key figures to both sections. Component planning collaboration data displays on the component planning collaboration list and details pages. • For more information about the component planning collaboration list page, see Component Planning Collaboration List Page [page 114]. • For more information about the component planning collaboration details page, see Component Planning Collaboration Details Page [page 115]. Prerequisites • • You must have both the Supply chain collaboration and Planning collaboration entitlements enabled. The buyer administrator has set the Enable component planning collaboration setting on the Settings Assign suppliers Planning page. • The buyer administrator has imported the Bill of Materials (BOM) for the finished goods from the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. Refer to Importing Bill of Materials from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. • To view the Component planning collaboration tile in the Workbench tab, you must have the Component planning collaboration permission. Restrictions • • The Component planning collaboration view does not support customer-defined attributes. Component planning collaboration does not support Planning Collaboration authorization profiles. Component Planning Collaboration List Page [page 114] Component Planning Collaboration Details Page [page 115] Component Planning Collaboration Use of BOM Data [page 118] Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 113 Component Planning Collaboration List Page On the component planning collaboration list page, you can view a table of component planning records for finished goods. To view the component planning collaboration list page, click Workbench, then click the Component planning collaboration tile.  Note If the Component planning collaboration tile does not display, follow the instructions on Customizing Tiles on Your Workbench to add it. You must have the inventory collaboration entitlement enabled for the Component planning collaboration tile to display in the list of tiles you can add.  Restriction You cannot download information from the list view of the Component planning collaboration table to a spreadsheet file such as Excel. The page displays a table of component planning collaboration records. Each record represents a finished good. The Component count column lists the number of components for each finished good and includes the number of active components in parenthesis. You can use the following filters to filter the finished goods: • • • • • Customer (supplier view) or Supplier (buyer view) Customer location Supplier part no. Customer part no. Components used – Select one or more components from the pulldown to list only finished goods that include one of the selected components. You can also sort the table by any column. 114 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration Component Planning Collaboration Details Page On the component planning collaboration details page, you can view the planning items for a finished good and its active components. To open the component planning collaboration details page for a finished good, from the component planning collaboration list page, click the detail-view ( ) icon from the Actions column.  Restriction A maximum of 30 components are supported for each finished good. If a finished good has more than 30 components, only the first 30 components (in alphabetical order) display. General information about the finished good displays in the section at the top of the page. If the customer has uploaded a company logo, it displays in this section. Click the dropdown ( ) icon to expand this section. The Bill of materials section displays the details of the BOM for the finished good. Click the feeder arrow ( ) icon to expand this section. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 115 When you open the details page, the Finished good section is expanded and the key figures for the finished good display with the standard planning time series table format. The time series tables on the component planning collaboration details page have the same functionality as they do on other planning pages. The only difference is that, when you click Send data, data is sent for both the finished good and its components. The Components with shortage key figure shows the count of the components used by the finished good that have a shortage on each date in the time bucket. Values greater than or equal to 1 display in red.  Note The Components with shortage key figure row only appears in the planning table when you use Daily granularity. You can view component planning items using any available granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly). However, you can only edit component planning items using Daily granularity since component planning is used for planning shorter timeframes. 116 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration The header lines for the finished good and its components list the finished good or component name, description, and amount of stock on hand. Component header lines also include the following: • Vertical status bar – The status bar is green if the component does not have any shortages. The status bar is red if the component has one or both of the following shortages: • • Current stock on hand – The component is out of stock. Projected stock – The component will run out of stock on a future date based on the component's inflow and outflow. • Newspaper icon – Click the newspaper ( ) icon in the component header line to open the Where used? popup. This popup shows which finished goods use the component. • Message-warning icon – If a component has a shortage, a message-warning icon ( ) displays on its header line. Click the icon to view the shortage information.  Note The message-warning icon and shortage information display only for shortages that will occur in the next 30 days. Click the feeder-arrow ( ) icon next to a component to open its time series table to view and edit its key figures. Standard calculated key figures that have values less than or equal to 0 display in red.  Caution Forecast commit locks are not supported for component planning. If you set Forecast commit lock horizon, in days to a value other than 0, you will not be able to commit from the component planning collaboration details page. To navigate back to the component planning collaboration list page, click the back-arrow ( ) icon at the top of the page. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 117 Component Planning Collaboration Use of BOM Data Component planning collaboration records are created using Bill of Materials (BOM) records in SAP Business Network. A BOM is a list of components needed to manufacture a finished good. Each component planning collaboration record contains one finished-good planning item and zero or more component planning items. Prerequisites The buyer administrator has imported the Bill of Materials (BOMs) for finished goods from the SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. Refer to Importing Bill of Materials from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to SAP Business Network. Creating and Updating Component Planning Collaboration Items Component planning collaboration items are created for finished goods and components when a product activity message is sent by the buyer and the following two conditions are true: • The buyer or supplier has the Enable component planning collaboration setting set. This setting is set by the buyer administrator on the • Planning Settings Assign suppliers page. The values of the Material ID and Plant ID in the message match the values of the Material ID and Plant ID in an active BOM at the header or component level. When both items are true, if the match of the Material ID and Plant ID values is at the header level, a finishedgood planning item is created. If the match of the Material ID and Plant ID values is at the component level, a component planning item is created. Before creating a new planning item, SAP Business Network checks whether a planning item already exists. • • If one exists, SAP Business Network updates it. If one does not exist, SAP Business Network creates a new finished-good or component planning item.  Note 118 • If the component data arrives before the finished-good data, the component planning item is created, but it is not displayed, until its finished-good planning item is created. A component planning item only displays on its finished good's component planning collaboration details page. • The component planning item is included in the component planning collaboration records of all finished goods that use it, and its data is always in sync in these records. • A planning item can be both a finished good and a component as illustrated in Example 3 below. PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration Examples These are the BOM records used in the examples: BOM: Header Material: Plant ID: Components: 0001 Classic promo pack 1000, 2000 BBQ chips, Peanuts BOM: Header Material: Plant ID: Components: 0002 Party pack 2000, 3000 BBQ chips, Salt chips, Pistachios BOM: Header Material: Plant ID: Components: 0003 Wholesale pallet 3000 Party pack, Variety pack The product activity messages are shown for each of the following examples. The bullets after each message list the BOM where SAP Business Network finds the match and what action SAP Business Network takes as a result of the match. Example 1: Simple component planning collaboration item generation These examples show simple generation of component planning collaboration items. • Message 1: Forecast for Material ID Classic promo pack/Plant ID 1000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 1 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. • Message 2: Forecast for Material ID Peanuts/Plant ID 1000 Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 1 component. 1. Create and populate the component planning item for Peanuts under the finished-good planning item for Classic promo pack/1000. Example 2: Component used in multiple finished goods These examples show the generation of component planning collaboration items for a component used in more than one finished good. • Message 1: Forecast for Material ID Classic promo pack/Plant ID 2000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 1 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. • Message 2: Forecast for Material ID Party pack/Plant ID 2000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 2 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. • Message 3: Forecast for Material ID BBQ chips/Plant ID 2000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with both BOM 1 and BOM 2 components. 2. Create and populate component planning items for BBQ chips for finished-good planning items Classic promo pack/2000 and Party pack/2000. The data for the BBQ chips component planning item in the component planning collaboration records for these two finished goods is always in sync. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 119 Example 3: Material is both a component and a finished good These examples show the generation of component planning collaboration items when a material is both a component and a finished good. • Message 1: Forecast for Material ID Party pack/Plant ID 3000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 2 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. 3. Since the Material ID/Plant ID also matches the BOM 3 component, a component planning item for Party pack is also created. This planning item is not visible until the finished-good planning item for Wholesale pallet/3000 is created. • Message 2: Forecast for Material ID Pistachios/Plant ID 3000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 2 component. 2. Create and populate the component planning item for Pistachios under the finished-good planning item for Party pack/3000. • Message 3: Forecast for Material ID Wholesale pallet/Plant ID 3000 1. Match Material ID/Plant ID with the BOM 3 header. 2. Create and populate the finished-good planning item. 3. The Party pack/3000 component planning item previously created (see Message 1 in this example) is now visible as a component in the component planning collaboration record for the Wholesale pallet/3000 finished good. Supplier-Managed Inventory Suppliers can manage the goods they own that are stored in customer warehouses for future ownership. With the supplier-managed inventory feature, suppliers can use SAP Business Network for Supply Chain to manage goods that are in their customers' warehouses, a process referred to as supplier managed inventory (SMI) or vendor managed inventory (VMI). If the supplier owns the stock until the customer consumes it, the stock is called consigned stock. If the customer takes ownership of the stock on receipt, the stock is called non-consigned stock. Buyers can configure the planning view based on their business requirements. Also, suppliers can view their inventory data all together, and can manage their commitments to forecast demand through a flexible user interface. Both buyers and suppliers can benefit from supplier-managed inventory, with benefits including: • • • Improved inventory turns Improved service Increased sales Workflow for Supplier-Managed Inventory The end-to-end workflow for supplier-managed inventory starts with a buyer designating materials for a supplier to manage, and ends with the supplier creating ship notices for managed materials. Typically, the supplier-managed inventory workflow follows these steps: 120 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration

file://SBN/split/Supplier Guide to SAP B.content: 1. The buyer designates the materials for the supplier-managed inventory program and shares the gross-demand information with the supplier. 2. The supplier-managed inventory conditions are translated and the buyer creates a blanket order or a scheduling agreement. 3. The buyer shares the inventory information, including various stock levels, and minimum and maximum stock information. 4. The supplier determines the need for replenishment of stock at the buyer location, based on the gross demand, inventory on hand, and minimum and maximum stock levels. The supplier communicates the following to the buyer: • • • Estimated shipment plans Updated shipment plans Shipment data 5. The supplier-planned shipments create schedule lines in the buyer system, which are communicated back to the supplier for creating ship notices. The following diagram describes the typical workflow for supplier-managed inventory (SMI): Product Replenishment Suppliers with visibility into their buyer's inventory and demand levels can replenish inventory based on established minimum and maximum stock levels. Viewing Replenishment Details [page 122] Creating a Replenishment Order [page 122] Sending Planned Replenishment Quantities for an Item [page 123] Cancelling a Replenishment Order [page 124] Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 121 Related Information Replenishment Template for Upload/Download Viewing Replenishment Details Suppliers can view information about the goods they provide and manage for a buyer. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Product Replenishment . SAP Business Network for Supply Chain displays the Supplier managed replenishment details page, containing Search Filters and Supplier managed replenishment details. 2. Enter criteria in Search Filters as desired, and click Search. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain displays the replenishment details for the documents found in the Supplier managed replenishment details table. Creating a Replenishment Order You can send planned replenishment data to your buyer. Prerequisites • • You are enabled for the inventory collaboration component. The buyer has set the Planning setting Allow suppliers to send planned replenishment to Yes. Context  Note You can instead use one of the following alternate methods to provide planned replenishment data:: Sending Planned Replenishment Quantities for an Item [page 123] Updates to Planned Replenishment Data [page 209] 122 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration Procedure 1. Choose Planning Planning Collaboration . 2. Click Details for the desired item, which has the Replenishment process type. The Supplier managed replenishment details page is displayed. 3. Click Edit. If the Edit button is not visible, change the View setting. Editing is restricted by the buyer to either the Daily or Weekly view. 4. Click cells in the Planned replenishment row to enter values, then click Save. The Create replenishment order button is displayed. 5. Click Create replenishment order. 6. Enter a name in the Replenishment order field, make any other desired changes, and click Create order.  Note Use a name that has no more than 12 alphanumeric characters, and does not contain spaces or special characters. The Supplier managed replenishment details page is displayed. 7. Click Refresh data to update the replenishment data with the replenishment order values. 8. Choose Fulfillment is sent to the buyer. Product Replenishment and click the replenishment order name to confirm that it Sending Planned Replenishment Quantities for an Item You can send planned replenishment data for a single item to a buyer without creating a new replenishment order. Prerequisites • • You are enabled for the inventory collaboration component. The buyer has set the Planning setting Allow suppliers to send planned replenishment to Yes. Context  Note You can instead use one of the following alternate methods to provide planned replenishment data: Creating a Replenishment Order [page 122] Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 123 Updates to Planned Replenishment Data [page 209] Procedure 1. Choose Planning Planning Collaboration . 2. Click Details for the desired item, which has the Replenishment process type. 3. In the Planned replenishment row, click the edit  icon. 4. Enter a replenishment value in one of the columns, and click Save. 5. To the right of the Create replenishment order button, click the down arrow  . 6. Click Send Data. The system sends a product replenishment message to the buyer. Next Steps To view product replenishment messages you sent to buyers, go to Fulfillment Product Replenishment . Cancelling a Replenishment Order Context Suppliers can cancel a replenishment order. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Product Replenishment . 2. On the desired replenishment order line, click Actions and choose Cancel Order from the dropdown. 124 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration The Direct-Material Sales Report This section provides topics about information on the Planning Sales Report tab. Direct-Material Sales Report for Suppliers [page 125] Workflow for the Direct-Material Sales Report [page 125] Viewing the Direct-Material Sales Report [page 126] Direct-Material Sales Report for Suppliers You can use your customer's sales information to anticipate your future production needs. Buyers can provide sales report information to their suppliers for forecast purposes, providing ongoing visibility into their demand forecast. Using the cumulative sales report information, suppliers can adjust their production plan and forecast to accommodate changing demand patterns and meet service levels. The Planning Sales Report tab shows cumulative sales and returned quantities for customer part numbers. The report can be filtered by Customer or Last Updated. The Sales Report does not affect existing Inventory and Consignment reports. Workflow for the Direct-Material Sales Report The workflow for the direct-material Sales Report begins with the buyer sending a product activity message with sales report information to their supplier, and ends with the supplier reviewing the sales report data. 1. Customers send ProductActivityMessage documents containing sales report information to their SAP Business Network suppliers using cXML. 2. The Forecast application polls the SAP Business Network database tables at regular intervals to read ProductActivityMessage documents relevant for forecast collaboration. 3. The SAP Business Network extracts the sales report data from the ProductActivityMessage documents. 4. Suppliers log in to their SAP Business Network supplier account to view the They can filter the report by Customer and Last Updated. Planning Sales Report tab. Related Information Viewing the Direct-Material Sales Report [page 126] Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration PUBLIC 125 Viewing the Direct-Material Sales Report If customers have provided direct-material sales information to you for forecast purposes, you can view it in the Planning Sales Report table. Procedure 1. Choose Planning Sales Report . The Sales Report table appears. 2. Filter the sales report by Customer or Last Updated fields. You can select an interval (for example, Last 14 Days), or select Other to specify any date range for the report. 126 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Planning Collaboration Inventory This section provides topics about managing inventory. High-Tech Industry Fields for Order Collaboration [page 127] Contract Manufacturing Collaboration [page 128] Consignment Collaboration [page 139] High-Tech Industry Fields for Order Collaboration High-tech industry fields for order collaboration support real-time supply-chain collaboration. With real-time visibility into the supply chain, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), contract manufacturers, and suppliers can match production orders to required materials and capacity. They can collaborate in real time to keep component inventories at optimum levels, and to reduce inventories of finished goods. SAP Business Network for Supply Chain includes the following capabilities supporting high-tech industry fields for order collaboration: • High-tech extensions to key fields in the following documents: • • • • • Purchase orders Purchase order confirmations Ship notices Component consumption documents High-tech extensions to key fields appear in the SAP Business Network user interface. Related Information Workflow for High-Tech Industry Fields for Order Collaboration [page 127] Workflow for High-Tech Industry Fields for Order Collaboration The end-to-end workflow for high-tech industry fields for order collaboration starts with a buyer sending an order to a supplier, and ends with the buyer receiving the goods receipt. With high-tech industry fields for order collaboration, the ordering process for contract manufacturing typically follows the following steps: Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory PUBLIC 127 1. A buyer sends a purchase order to a supplier via an ERP system. 2. The supplier receives the purchase order, and the component supplier receives a copy of the purchase order. 3. The buyer sends any changes to the purchase order to the supplier. 4. The supplier receives the purchase order revisions and sends a copy of them to the component supplier. 5. The supplier sends a purchase order confirmation to the buyer, and sends a copy of the purchase order confirmation to the component supplier. 6. The buyer receives the purchase order confirmation. 7. The supplier sends a ship notice to the customer, and sends a copy of the ship notice to the component supplier. 8. The component supplier sends a goods receipt to the buyer, based on the shipment from the supplier. 9. The buyer receives the goods receipt. Contract Manufacturing Collaboration Buyers and contract manufacturers can manage the supply of component materials and finished goods through SAP Business Network. Large organizations can reduce costs by transferring the manufacture, assembly, or processing of parts to thirdparty contract manufacturers. Contract manufacturers are suppliers who build the parts for these buyers. The contract manufacturing collaboration feature includes the following functionalities: • Buyers can create subcontract purchase orders which can be transmitted to contract manufacturers via SAP Business Network. • Contract manufacturers can view all the data of subcontract purchase orders, including all the component information under the purchase order line item, in the schedule line section. • • • • • Contract manufacturers can confirm orders for finished goods purchased by buyers. Buyers can create ship notices for subcontracting components, and can send them to contract manufacturers. Contract manufacturers can create receipts for subcontracting components, and can send them to buyers. Contract manufacturers can create ship notices for finished goods to be shipped to buyers. Contract manufacturers can send component consumption information to buyers for components used to manufacture the finished goods on the subcontract purchase order. To support these functionalities, the following types of messages are available for direct materials buyers and contract manufacturers: Subcontracting Purchase Order A subcontracting purchase order is a purchase order that is sent from a buyer to a contract manufacturer to request the production and delivery of finished goods. The subcontracting purchase order can carry not only item level and schedule line level information, but also subcontracting component information. Subcontracting components are the raw materials that are used for manufacturing the finished goods specified at the item level. Component Ship Notice 128 PUBLIC A component ship notice is a type of ship notice that informs the contract manufacturer of the shipment of subcontracting components. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory Suppliers can segregate the routing of the document sub types based on the supplier capability. This feature supports separate routing options for ProductActivity and OrderRequest message for SAP Business Network. The routing configuration enhances and supports the Resend option for component ship notices. This capability helps organizations meet supplier adoption in integration area. There are four routings options for the Product Activity Message as shown below: • • • • SMI Product Activity Message Consignment Product Activity Message Forecast Product Activity Message Product Activity Message Option The Product Activity Message Option is able to route the documents only if the above processTypes are not present in the message. Once this is enabled, the other options point to the same routing configuration of the actual Product Activity Message adjusted by supplier by default. This provides flexibility to the supplier to change the new routing options without impacting the current flow. Component Receipt A component receipt is a type of goods receipt that informs the buyer of the receipt of subcontracting components. The contract manufacturer can issue the component receipt against one or more component ship notices. Component Consumption (Backflush) Message The ship notice message can include consumption details in a backflush component message. A backflush component consumption message is a type of ship notice request that informs the buyer of the completion of finished goods from subcontracting components. Unlike real-time component consumption reporting, backflush reporting is done only once, at the end of the production process. Component Consumption (Realtime) Message A real-time component consumption message informs the buyer of consumption of components at any phase of the production cycle. Component Inventory Message A component inventory message can inform suppliers about quantities of components available for manufacturing. Restrictions If a subcontracting purchase order has been uploaded or downloaded via CSV, a supplier will not see the component level on the downloaded subcontracting purchase order. Workflow for Contract Manufacturing Collaboration The end-to-end workflow for contract manufacturing collaboration starts with a buyer creating a subcontracting purchase order, and ends with the supplier sending a ship notice for the finished goods, followed by standard follow-up processes. 1. The buyer creates a subcontracting purchase order requesting the production and delivery of a finished product. The subcontracting purchase order carries item level, schedule line level, and component information. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory PUBLIC 129 Components are the materials needed to manufacture the finished product. The subcontracting purchase order is sent to the contract manufacturer via SAP Business Network. 2. The buyer changes a subcontracting purchase order on the item, schedule, or component level. The changed subcontracting purchase order is sent to the contract manufacturer via SAP Business Network. 3. Contract manufacturers view subcontracting purchase orders in the SAP Business Network user interface or in their backend systems. 4. Suppliers confirm subcontracting purchase orders in the SAP Business Network user interface, or they send confirmations of subcontracting purchase orders from their backend systems. 5. The buyer, who owns and physically controls the components, issues the components to the contract manufacturer. The information about the components issue is sent to the contract manufacturer via one of the following: • • Component Ship Notice containing the actual component issue date, quantity, and other information Component Inventory containing a component inventory snapshot for a given point in time Outbound Delivery information and Inventory Summary are not mutually exclusive as they carry different data (detail vs. summary data). The data are complementary. 6. Suppliers view the component inventory in the SAP Business Network user interface. 7. Suppliers confirm the component receipt either in the SAP Business Network user interface or by issuing respective messages from their backend systems. 8. As contract manufacturers produce the finished product, they consume the components that were provisioned by the buyer. Suppliers report the component consumption back to the buyer, so that replenishment and costing can occur. Suppliers report component consumption in either of the following ways as specified by the buyer: • If the buyer has requested real-time component consumption, the contract manufacturer records component consumption at any given point in time during production, and sends the information to the buyer. For example, if the contract manufacturer has produced Batch One of a finished product, the contract manufacturer records the components that were consumed before moving on to producing Batch Two of the finished product. Suppliers capture the data in the SAP Business Network user interface, or send a consumption message from their backend systems. This provides the buyer with up-to-date information on the contract manufacturer's component inventory, and allows the buyer to execute product costing and component replenishment in a timely fashion. This method is preferred in industries such as pharmaceuticals, where components have a very short lifespan. Here, the buyer must monitor the consumption in real-time, since at the time of a backflush the components used already might have expired. The high-tech industry also deploys this method. There, components often carry a significant monetary value, and must be accounted for continuously. • If the buyer has requested backflush reporting, the contract manufacturers record the component consumption continuously, but the system sends the information to the buyer only when the contract manufacturer creates the ship notice for the finished good. Suppliers capture the data in the SAP Business Network user interface, or send consumption messages from their backend systems. This method is used by customers where expiration or value of components is not as critical, or who want to receive only one ship notice message, instead of multiple messages, to account for component consumption. 9. Suppliers create the ship notice for the finished goods in the SAP Business Network user interface, or by sending messages from their backend systems. The process is completed by the standard follow-up processes, such as contract manufacturer-created invoices in the SAP Business Network user interface, or through messages from contract manufacturer backend systems, or alternatively, by self-billing initiated by the buyer. 130 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory

file://SBN/split/Supplier Guide to SAP B.content: Viewing Component Ship Notices You can see all your component ship notices listed in one place. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended Collaboration , then click the Component Shipments tile. 2. To search for a specific component ship notice, click the triangle next to the Search Filters heading, enter the criteria desired, and click Search. 3. To see the details for a component ship notice, click its ship notice number. 4. To see and download the serial number list, click Show Serial Numbers List in the Asset Details section. The Items serial number popup opens. The popup can show up to 500 serial numbers. If there are more than 500 serial numbers for the item, click the download icon  to download the full list. For alternative ways to access the serial number list, see: Viewing and Exporting Serial Number Lists in Orders [page 82] Serial Number Report [page 235] Viewing the Component Inventory A supplier can view a snapshot of the component inventory available for use in manufacturing. Context  Note The component inventory snapshot is updated only as frequently as the buyer publishes the component inventory data to SAP Business Network. It does not display up-to-the-moment information, and should be used only as an approximation of the quantities of the components available for manufacturing. Always take note of the dates and times listed in the Last Updated column. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended Collaboration Component Inventory . SAP Business Network displays the component inventory. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory PUBLIC 131  Note Records that a buyer marks Inactive are not displayed. 2. Optional: Do the following: • To search for a specific component, click the triangle next to Search Filters, enter the search criteria, and click Search. • To display records with a quantity of 0, check the View all component inventory checkbox. Viewing Component Consumption Details Suppliers can view their component consumption documents in the SAP Business Network user interface. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended Collaboration Component Consumption . 2. Optional: To find specific consumption documents, click the triangle next to Search Filters to expand the filter options. Enter search data and click Search. 3. To view additional details for a component consumption document, click the order number for a document listed in the Component Consumption Documents table. Informing a Buyer of Receipt of Components Contract manufacturers can inform their buyers when they've received components by sending component receipt messages through SAP Business Network. Context • If transaction rule Require the quantity of a component receipt item to not exceed the component ship notice quantity is enabled when you create a component receipt, any items that are already received are automatically removed from the items being flipped. This action prevents the creation of another receipt for an already-received item. • If transaction rule Require the quantity of a consumed component in a component ship notice to not exceed the component quantities in the related order is enabled, you can't enter for consumption a component quantity greater than is authorized in the subcontracting order. This rule applies to purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and scheduling agreement releases. 132 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory  Note To perform this validation, this rule requires that the component's information is identical in both the subcontracting order and the ship notice. If you edit a draft component ship notice without first clicking the Add details link to go to the component consumption page, the ship notice you submit might consume component quantities that exceed the quantity allowed in the purchase order. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended Collaboration Component Shipments , and then search for a component ship notice by customer or ship notice number. 2. In the Component Ship Notices table, select the desired ship notice. Then, do one of the following: • • Click Create Component Receipt. Click a component ship notice in the list. On the ship notice details page, click Create Component Receipt. 3. Enter the necessary details. To add an attachment, go to the Attachment section, click Browse, choose the file you want, then click Add attachment. Click Next. 4. Review the details, and click Submit. The component receipt document is sent to the buyer. 5. To view the new component receipt document, choose Fulfillment Extended Collaboration Component Receipts . Related Information Sending a Component Receipt for a Multitier Ship Notice [page 72] Informing a Buyer of Component Consumption in Real Time Contract manufacturers can inform their buyers in real time when they have consumed components in manufacturing by sending component consumption documents through SAP Business Network. Context  Restriction For a buyer who has enabled transaction rule Require buyer batch matching in component inventory, the component consumption that you report is validated and acted on in the following ways: Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory PUBLIC 133 • The following values for a subcontracting component must match the same values for a component in the supplier's or vendor's component inventory: Customer Part No., Supplier Part No., Location, and Logical ID. If a match is not found, the subcontracting component cannot be reported as consumed. The Logical ID is a combination of the following values: Vendor ID, Site ID, Site Auxiliary ID, Legacy Supplier Private ID, and System ID (when available). The value of the Logical ID is displayed as Vendor_ID (System_ID). • If a subcontracting component matches a component in component inventory but has no buyer batch number, the component can be consumed, but a buyer batch number cannot be entered for the component. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Orders and Releases . 2. Browse to a purchase order containing components in one or more schedule lines, or search for a subcontracting component, and click the order number to open it. 3. On the desired line item, click Details. The Order Detail page opens. 4. On the desired schedule line, click Show Components. A Components list becomes visible for the schedule line. 5. Click Report Consumption. 6. Fill in the fields of the Component Consumption Document form, as desired, and click Next.  Note The Lookup link for the Customer Part No. field displays only those subcontracting components in component inventory that are authorized for consumption for a certain buyer. 7. Review the Component Consumption Document for correctness, and click Submit. Informing a Buyer of Component Consumption by Backflush Contract manufacturers can inform their buyers at the end of the production cycle about which components they have consumed in manufacturing. Context Contract manufacturers can transmit component consumption information to their buyers by backflush through SAP Business Network. Buyers might prefer this kind of batch end-of-cycle consumption information, for example, when components have long shelf lives, or when the aggregated information is all that is necessary. 134 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory You can create a ship notice to log the consumption of components that are later transmitted to the buyer by backflush.  Restriction For a buyer who has enabled transaction rule Require buyer batch matching in component inventory, the component consumption that you report is validated and acted on in the following ways: • The following values for a subcontracting component must match the same values for a component in the supplier's or vendor's component inventory: Customer Part No., Supplier Part No., Location, and Logical ID. If a match is not found, the subcontracting component cannot be reported as consumed. The Logical ID is a combination of the following values: Vendor ID, Site ID, Site Auxiliary ID, Legacy Supplier Private ID, and System ID (when available). The value of the Logical ID is displayed as Vendor_ID (System_ID). • If a subcontracting component matches a component in component inventory but has no buyer batch number, the component can be consumed, but a buyer batch number cannot be entered for the component. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Orders and Releases . 2. Browse to a purchase order that has components in one or more of its line items, and click the order number to open it. 3. Click Create Ship Notice. 4. For the line item that contains the components that were consumed, click Add Details. 5. Add the necessary details about component consumption, and complete the ship notice.  Note The Lookup link for the Customer Part No. field displays only those subcontracting components in component inventory that are authorized for consumption for a certain buyer. Resending a Component Consumption or Component Receipt Document You can send again a component consumption or component receipt message if the original submission failed. Procedure 1. Go to the list for the type of component document you want to resend. • For a component consumption document, go to Fulfillment Extended Collaboration Component Consumption . Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory PUBLIC 135 • For a component receipt, go to Fulfillment Extended Collaboration Component Receipts . 2. Choose the desired document. 3. Click Resend. SAP Business Network sends the document again to the buyer ERP system, and resets the current document to the initial state. Component Consumption Download and Upload via Excel Files Business Details This feature adds the Component Consumption job type to Upload/Download in SAP Business Network. Buyers and suppliers can create and run Component Consumption jobs to download prepopulated Excel files with component consumption data. Buyers can review the component consumption data in these downloaded Excel files. Suppliers can also review these downloaded Excel files and can additionally edit and add data to them and then upload them. This provides suppliers with the capability to process component consumption data in bulk.  Note A supplier can upload up to 600 rows per Excel file. If a supplier tries to upload a file with more than 600 rows, the upload fails and an error message displays. Changes to the User Interface When you create Upload/Download jobs from the Upload/Download Jobs page, the Create/Edit Job popup includes Component Consumption in the Type dropdown list. When you choose this type, the search criteria appear for a component consumption job. For details, see Component Consumption Template for Upload/ Download [page 137]. Technical Details Product SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Line of Business Supply Chain Action Information Type New Lifecycle Phase General Availability Enablement Automatically On 136 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory Category App Functional Localization No Localization Capability Not Applicable Component Not Applicable Environment Not Applicable Version SAP Ariba 2508 Valid as Of 2025-08-15 Reference Number CSC-13186 Sub Process (Modular Business Process) Not Applicable Application Component Not Applicable Area Not Applicable Link to Demo Not Applicable Solution Capability Not Applicable User Type Buyer Supplier Related Information Component Consumption Template for Upload/Download [page 137] Component Consumption Template for Upload/Download You can generate an Upload/Download file in Excel format for component consumption data.  Note The path to the Upload/Download feature is as follows: • • For buyers – For suppliers – Quick Links … Upload/Download Upload/Download After running a Component Consumption job, the supplier can download the generated Excel file that contains prepopulated component consumption data from related orders. The supplier can edit the Excel file and add data to it based on individual needs, and then upload the Excel file to report component consumption in bulk. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory PUBLIC 137 Restrictions A supplier can upload up to 600 rows per Excel file. If a supplier tries to upload a file with more than 600 rows, the upload fails and an error message displays. Component Consumption Template Criteria The Upload/Download job type: • • • • • page provides the following search criteria for the Component Consumption Name – (Required) The name to give the job. Type – (Required) Choose Component Consumption. Customer (Required, supplier view only) or Supplier (Required, buyer view only) The name of the buyer (supplier view) or supplier (buyer view) whose data you want in the Excel file. Order number – The ID of the purchase order. Line-item level • • • • • Jobs Supplier part number Supplier batch Buyer part number Buyer batch Component level • • • • Supplier part number Supplier batch Buyer part number Buyer batch Editing the Component Consumption Excel File • 138 The Item Serial Numbers column in the Component Consumption Excel file accepts multiple values, separated by pipe ( | ) characters. The multiple serial numbers are separated and assigned to the component consumption items. When there is a direct linkage of the serial number at the component level with the serial number at the line-item level, rows in the Excel file may need to be repeated for a specific line item with a single quantity to allow reference to related serial numbers for one or multiple components consumed for the line item. When rows are repeated in the Excel file, the Component Line Group column is used to clarify the assignment of the component serial number to specific line item serial numbers; this column is needed because the line item's serial number cannot be used to indicate this assignment. The value in the Component Line Group column is a number used once only for each upload. The following figure shows some example data. PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory • The Item Schedule Line and Component Line Number columns in the the Component Consumption Excel file are read only. The values in these two columns are populated from the orders for informational purposes. These columns are not evaluated by SAP Business Network when the supplier uploads the Excel file. Uploading the Component Consumption Excel File • When the buyer enables certain component consumption transaction rules or sets the requiresRealTimeConsumption control key in the corresponding line item of the cXML file for the order, SAP Business Network performs additional validation during upload that may result in a validation failure. For example, if a buyer enables the Do not allow consumption to exceed balance quantity in component inventory rule, an uploaded Component Consumption Excel file fails validation if its entries do not all meet this rule. • After a supplier uploads a Component Consumption Excel file, its entry on the Uploads • • • Upload/Download page shows one of the following statuses: Completed – The upload processed without any errors. Completed with Errors – The upload contained errors. The rows without errors were processed. Failed – All rows had errors. The entry also displays a link to a log file that reports the upload status for successful and failed rows. • When a supplier uploads a Component Consumption Excel file, if there are any empty Consumption ID fields, a unique ID is autogenerated, and the empty Consumption ID fields are filled with this unique ID. The autogeneration of the unique ID occurs in the backend system. The unique ID is not added to the Excel file. Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job Consignment Collaboration Suppliers can use SAP Business Network to track materials on consignment and send invoices for consignment movements. With consignment collaboration, the supplier sends consignments to the buyer, but retains ownership of the consignments until the buyer pays for the consignments the buyer consumes, through a pre-arranged purchaseorder method. Consignments stocked in the buyer’s warehouses or production facilities are not paid for until they have been used. The transfer of ownership, and often of location, to the buyer at the time of consumption is called a consignment movement. SAP Business Network for SAP Business Network for Supply Chain provides ways for suppliers to view lists of materials on consignment, for suppliers to create invoices for consignment movements, and for buyers to create self-billing invoices for consignment movements. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory PUBLIC 139 Workflow for Consignment Collaboration The end-to-end workflow for consignment collaboration starts with a buyer creating or changing a consignment purchase order, and ends with the buyer or supplier sending an invoice. 1. The buyer creates or changes a consignment purchase order, and sends it, via SAP Business Network, to a supplier. 2. The supplier finds a purchase order for a consignment item, clearly differentiated as such in the item category field. The supplier creates a consignment fill-up order, and sends a consignment purchase order confirmation, via SAP Business Network, to the buyer. 3. The supplier creates a ship notice for the consignment purchase order and sends it, via SAP Business Network, to the buyer, who receives notice of an inbound delivery. 4. The buyer reports the transfer of materials from consignment to the buyer's own stock, via SAP Business Network, to the supplier. 5. The supplier views consignment movements in SAP Business Network. 6. Either of the following: • The buyer executes a consignment settlement, and sends a settlement invoice, via SAP Business Network, to the supplier. • The supplier creates an invoice against one or more consignment movements, and sends the invoice, via SAP Business Network, to the buyer. Creating an Invoice for a Consignment Movement As a supplier, you can create an invoice for one or more movements of consignment materials to a buyer. Procedure 1. Choose Fulfillment Extended Collaboration Consignment Movements . 2. To find consignments for a specific product, expand Search Filters. 3. Enter information into the desired search fields. 4. To find only consignment movements awaiting settlement, select Show consignment movements that are not settled. 5. Click Search. 6. Select one or more desired consignment movements. Then, click Create Invoice. 7. Enter information into the fields in the Create Invoice form as appropriate, making sure the required fields are filled. 8. Click Next. 9. Review the information in the Create Invoice form. When correct, click Submit. 10. To print a copy of the invoice, click Print. 11. To exit invoice creation, click Exit. 140 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Inventory
