file://SBN/split/Supplier Guide to SAP B.content: Invoicing This section provides topics about invoices. Invoice Enhancements for Self Billing and Scheduling Agreement Releases [page 141] Creating a Supply-Chain Invoice [page 142] Goods-Receipt-Based Invoice Verification [page 143] Related Information Creating an Invoice for a Consignment Movement [page 140] Invoice Enhancements for Self Billing and Scheduling Agreement Releases SAP Business Network for Supply Chain supports invoice enhancements for self billing and scheduling agreement releases for direct materials suppliers. For SAP Business Network for Supply Chain suppliers and buyers, SAP Business Network can automatically transmit self-billing invoices based on data in purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and goods receipts. The buyer creates a self-billing invoice in an external business system and sends it to a supplier over SAP Business Network. Suppliers and buyers can deploy self-billing invoices when they have agreed to not require the supplier to manually create invoices for order transactions, but instead to use an automated routine called Evaluated Receipt Settlement (ERS). ERS determines the invoice amount for ordering transactions from the prices entered in the order, the terms of payment, the tax information, and the delivery quantity entered in the goods receipt. With invoice enhancements for self billing and scheduling agreement releases, suppliers and buyers can employ self-billing invoices for scheduling agreements as well as for purchase orders. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Invoicing PUBLIC 141 Workflow for Self-Billing Invoicing The end-to-end workflow for self-billing invoicing starts with a buyer creating a self-billing invoice, and ends with the supplier receiving payment. Buyers and suppliers can automate the creation of invoices for purchase orders and scheduling agreements with self-billing invoicing.The following describes the general workflow for self-billing invoicing: 1. A buyer creates a self-billing invoice for a purchase order or scheduling agreement release in an ERP system. 2. The buyer ERP system publishes the self-billing invoice to a supplier through SAP Business Network. 3. The supplier receives the self-billing invoice either through the SAP Business Network user interface, or through the supplier's ERP system. 4. The buyer's ERP system processes the self-billing invoice, generates payments, and publishes payment status updates to the supplier via SAP Business Network. 5. The supplier receives payment status updates through the SAP Business Network user interface, or through the supplier's ERP system. Creating a Supply-Chain Invoice Suppliers can create supply-chain invoices against purchase orders and scheduling agreement releases. Context You can create an invoice from the Orders and Releases list, or from within an individual scheduling agreement release record. Procedure 1. Choose Orders Orders and Releases . 2. Click the Items to Confirm list. 3. Click the order number for a purchase order or scheduling agreement release. 4. Click the Create Invoice button, and click either Standard Invoice or Credit Memo. 5. Enter the necessary details, and click Next. 6. Confirm the details, and click Submit. 142 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Invoicing Goods-Receipt-Based Invoice Verification You can match each invoice item uniquely with its related goods-receipt item. With goods-receipt-based invoice verification for purchase orders, scheduling agreements, and scheduling agreement releases you can match up each invoice item uniquely with its related goods-receipt item. Buyers can transfer invoice verification instructions, ship-notice reference visibility in goods-receipt documents, and enhancements of receipt statuses in ship notices. Suppliers might work with goods-receipt-based verification, for example, when they expect a delivery to be made and posted in several parts. With goods-receipt-based invoice verification, you can view scheduling agreements in the Orders Orders and Releases tab. For the scheduling agreements, you can view the requested quantity and the cumulative quantities already scheduled or already shipped. You can create ship notices based on scheduling agreements on the Items to Ship tab. When a goods receipt is received, the following changes are made to the related ship notice: • • • The ship notice line-item received quantity or returned quantity is updated. • • A link to the goods receipt appears in the Related Documents section. The ship-notice completion status at the header and item level is updated. If the goods receipt is for a line item that is already in the completed state, the line item remains in the completed state. When all line items for a ship notice are marked Completed, the completion status for the whole ship notice is marked Completed. Workflow for Goods-Receipt-Based Invoice Verification The end-to-end workflow for a supplier to base an invoice on a ship notice starts with the buyer setting the transaction rule, and ends with the supplier creating the invoice based on the ship notice. 1. The buyer sets the transaction rule that allows suppliers to create invoices based on ship notices. 2. The buyer sends a purchase order or scheduling agreement to a supplier through SAP Business Network. 3. The supplier views the document on the or scheduling agreement. Orders Orders and Releases tab by filtering the purchase order 4. The supplier views the Invoice Verification Type in the purchase order. 5. The supplier creates a ship notice. 6. The buyer receives the material and sends the receipt to the supplier with the goods-receipt price. 7. The supplier creates an invoice based on the ship notice. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Invoicing PUBLIC 143 Quality Issues This section provides topics about quality notifications, inspections, and reviews. Quality Inspection Collaboration [page 144] Quality Notification Collaboration [page 153] Quality Review Collaboration [page 167] Quality Inspection Collaboration Suppliers can use SAP Business Network to respond to a quality inspection request. During the delivery of components, buyers and suppliers can collaborate on quality inspection of finished goods or subcontracting components to achieve improved overall quality metrics. Quality inspection collaboration supports the following functionality: • • Buyers can request the supplier to perform a quality inspection based on a specified inspection lot. • • • • • Buyers can review the inspection results and lock them, preventing the supplier from making further changes. • Buyers using DocuSign can require suppliers to electronically sign quality inspection results before submitting them. Refer to Electronic Signatures for Quality Inspections for Suppliers [page 150]. Suppliers can perform the inspection and send inspection results and an attached certificate of analysis to the buyer. Buyers can respond to the inspection results by sending the usage decision for the inspection lot to suppliers. Buyers and suppliers can receive email notifications for quality inspection documents. Supplier managers can assign roles to users to view or edit inspection results. Buyers and suppliers can see links to the related quality inspection documents in the header of the purchase order under Related Documents. You can click the link to the quality inspection document to open it. Buyers create quality inspection documents outside SAP Business Network and submit them through cXML. However, they can view quality inspections on the Quality tab. Account Settings > Settings > Users > Create Role > Permissions The following supplier user permissions appear on the Create Role page, in support of quality inspection collaboration: Permission Description Notifications Quality Inspection Access View quality inspection documents. None 144 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues Permission Description Notifications Quality Inspection Creation Create quality inspection documents. None Account Settings > Settings > Notifications The following notifications appear in a section called Quality Collaboration: Notification Type Event That Triggers Notification Method Quality Inspection Request A new quality inspection request was received. Email only Quality Inspection Decision A new quality inspection decision was received. Email only Quality Inspection Page On the Quality Inspection page you can search for, open, and view quality inspections. The Quality Inspection table includes the following columns; you can add or remove columns to the table by clicking the Table Options  icon. Column Description Customer inspection no. Customer inspection request number Supplier inspection no. Supplier inspection request number Customer Name of customer Customer batch Buying organization’s batch number Supplier batch Supplier's batch number No. of characteristics Number of inspection characteristics Inspection status Status of inspection Inspection progress Bar chart showing progress of inspection Usage decision Usage decision on stock Inspection lot quantity Quantity of items in inspection lot Days to complete Days left to complete inspection Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 145 Column Description Inspection end date Date when inspection must be completed Customer part no. Buying organization’s part number Supplier part no. Supplier's part number Purchase order Purchase order number; click on order number to open related order Purchase order item Line number in purchase order Results description Comments on characteristics added when entering quality inspection results You can click the blue table columns labels to sort the table by those columns. Inspection Details Page When you click a customer inspection number, the Inspection Details page appears. This page lets you send quality inspection test results to the buying organization. It has the following tabs and sections: Tab Section Description Details Header Contains summary information for the quality inspection. List certificates and documents Contains a reference to the certificate of analysis for the inspection as well as any other related documents. Test results for characteristics Contains the values for test results for inspection characteristics. History History Contains a history of changes to the document. Click Edit to enter test results for inspection characteristics. When you are finished entering results, click Submit. Quality Inspection Decisions Routing The Account Settings Settings Electronic Order Routing page includes a Quality Inspection Decision Request setting. You can configure this setting to route all quality inspection decisions to your desired location. Routing choices are Online, cXML, or cXML Pending Queue. 146 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues Workflow for Quality Inspection The end-to-end workflow for quality inspection starts with a buyer sending an order to a supplier, and ends with the buyer sending a usage decision to the supplier for the inspection lot quantities. Buyers can initiate inspections for different types of goods movements. Inspection lots can be created automatically after a ship notice is sent for material goods or when a product is processed at goods receipt. They can also be created manually before the goods are shipped or received. The following is an example of a quality inspection done after a ship notice: 1. The buyer sends an order to the supplier. 2. Optionally, the supplier sends an order confirmation to the buyer. 3. The supplier sends a ship notice. 4. The buyer creates an inspection lot and sends an inspection request to the supplier, and optionally sends a copy to a third-party supplier. 5. The supplier sends inspection results either online or through cXML to the buyer. 6. The buyer updates the inspection request, locking it to prevent the supplier from making further changes. 7. The buyer sends a usage decision to the supplier, indicating what to do with the inspection lot quantities. Figure 5: Quality Inspection After Ship Notice The following is an example of a quality inspection done before goods are shipped or received: 1. The buyer sends an order to the supplier. 2. Optionally, the supplier sends an order confirmation to the buyer. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 147 3. The buyer creates an inspection lot and sends an inspection request to the supplier. 4. The supplier sends inspection results either online or through cXML to the buyer. 5. The buyer updates the inspection request, locking it to prevent the supplier from making further changes. 6. The buyer sends a usage decision to the supplier, indicating what to do with the inspection lot quantities. 7. The supplier sends a ship notice. Figure 6: Quality Inspection Before Ship Notice (Manual) Copy Suppliers Buyers can provide read-only copies of quality inspections to third parties, also referred to as copy suppliers. Buyers trigger copies by including the <Node type=”copy”> element when sending cXML inspection requests. Here is an example: <Path> <Node type="copy"> <Credential domain="SAPBusinessNetworkUserId"> <Identity>test-testPT1@sap.com</Identity> </Credential> </Node> </Path> Buyers may want to add a copy supplier if, for example, they have a contract manufacturer responsible for a finished good. Copying this supplier will provide them with visibility about what is happening during an inspection process with the component(s) needed to make the finished good. 148 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues Buyers view information about copy suppliers from the Quality Inspection page. If a quality inspection has one or more copy suppliers, the Multi Tier column is checked and the Copies column contains a link. When you click this link, a popup with information about the copies opens. Suppliers view information about copy suppliers from the Multi-Tier Quality Inspection tab on the Extended Collaboration Inbox page. Additional Steps for Electronic Signatures If the Activate DocuSign for quality inspection documents rule is set, these steps are added to the workflow after the buyer sends an inspection request to the supplier. 1. The supplier fills in the inspection results, selects signers, and sends the results to be electronically signed. SAP Business Network assembles a document packet, including the signer information and the PDF file with the results, and sends it to DocuSign. 2. DocuSign creates the signature envelope and emails all the selected signers to request they electronically sign the quality inspection document. 3. The signers review and sign the inspection results in DocuSign. 4. If the quality inspection results are successfully signed, SAP Business Network sends the PDF file with the results, including the signatures, to the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.  Note Only inspection results sent through the SAP Business Network user interface, not inspection results sent through cXML, can be electronically signed. Entering Test Results for Inspection Characteristics After you perform an inspection for a quality inspection request that you received from a customer, you can open the quality inspection document and record the test results for inspection characteristics. Context Use this procedure to enter test results for one inspection characteristic at a time. To streamline entering test results for multiple inspection characteristics, use the Quality Inspection Results template. See Quality Inspection Results Template for Upload/Download [page 203]. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 149 Procedure 1. Choose Quality Inspection . 2. Click a customer inspection number to open it. 3. Click Edit. 4. In the header, enter the Supplier inspection no. 5. In the List certificates and documents section, click Attach files to attach documents related to this inspection. a. Click the certificate type link (if available), or click Additional Documents. A required certificate is indicated by an asterisk. The File Upload window appears. b. Select a file, and then click Open.  Note • By default, the cumulative size of attachments associated with a document cannot exceed 10 MB. Customers can request to change that limit, which can be changed from 10 MB to 100 MB. • During file upload, attachment files are converted to plain ASCII text using base64 encoding. This conversion increases the file size by approximately 35%. Therefore, the actual file size limit is 65% of the configured maximum limit. For example, if the maximum allowed limit is set to 10 MB (10000 KB), the actual total attachment file size that users can add is 6500 KB. • SAP Business Network stores attachments for a maximum period of eighteen months, after which the attachments expire and are no longer available online. 6. In the Test results for characteristics section, enter results for the inspection characteristics.  Note The characteristics, which are defined by your customer, can be both qualitative and quantitative. Sample size, allowed values, and expected values can vary per characteristic. 7. When you are finished entering test results, click Submit. Electronic Signatures for Quality Inspections for Suppliers Buyers can require that you electronically sign quality inspections before submitting them. Prerequisites All suppliers who are potential signers have the Quality Inspection Signature permission. All electronic signers need the Quality Inspection Signature permission. Supplier administrators are assigned this permission by default. They can create supplier subusers and assign this permission to them to allow them to be electronic signers. 150 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues

file://SBN/split/Supplier Guide to SAP B.content: Supplier users with the Quality Inspection Signature permission can send quality inspection results to be signed by following these steps: • • Add signers. Refer to Adding Signers [page 152]. Click Send to sign.  Note The Send to sign button is active if at least one signer is added. After clicking Send to sign, the following occurs: • SAP Business Network assembles the document packet, including the signer information and the PDF file with the results, and sends it to DocuSign. • In the SAP Business Network user interface, the Inspection status for the quality inspection results is set to Awaiting Signature. • DocuSign creates the signature envelope and emails the signers to request their signatures.  Note All potential signers (that is, supplier users with the Quality Inspection Signature permission) should make sure their email addresses are correct in SAP Business Network since DocuSign sends its emails to those addresses. By default, when multiple signers are requested, all signers must sign. If the quality inspection results are successfully signed, SAP Business Network does the following: • Sends the PDF file with the signatures and the DocuSign certificate of completion to the buyer and to the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system. Buyers can review this certificate to examine the actions DocuSign did on the document.  Note This certificate displays as an attachment in the user interface. It is submitted to the ERP as an attachment in the inspection result cXML, along with the signed PDF file. • Sets the Inspection status to Signed and Submitted. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 151 Adding Signers You select supplier users to sign the quality inspection results. Procedure 1. Go to Quality Inspection . The Quality inspection page opens. 2. Select a Customer inspection no. from the table. The Inspection details page for that Customer inspection no. opens. 3. Click Edit. The following page displays. 4. Click Add signers. The Add signers popup opens. It shows a list of supplier users who have the Quality Inspection Signature permission. 152 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues 5. Search for and select all supplier users you want to sign the quality inspection results. 6. Click Add to add the selected supplier users as signers.  Note DocuSign will email all the suppliers you add to request they electronically sign the quality inspection document. 7. Click Done to exit. The Quality Inspection Inspection Details page displays. Results All selected signers are preselected the next time you request a digital signature for the same Customer inspection no. Quality Notification Collaboration As a supplier, you and your customers can record problems with goods or services and use this information to collaborate on solutions. Quality notifications can help you process internal or external problems such as: • Complaints filed by customers Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 153 • • • • Deviations reported by suppliers Complaints against vendors Company-internal problems Other user-specific problems You can use a quality notification to: • Describe a problem and identify the affected customer, customer location, part number, and other reference objects (purchase order and ship notice). • • • Record the names of all persons (partners) who are involved with the problem. • Record individual defect items that relate to the problem and analyze their causes. Define processing parameters for the quality notification (for example, assigning a priority to the notification and specifying a time range when the problem should be completed). Specify the corrective actions to be taken (for example, tasks that are implemented immediately or corrective tasks that are implemented after a thorough analysis of the defects). Parts of a Quality Notification [page 155] Quality Notification Status Values [page 155] Restrictions for Quality Notifications [page 156] Workflows for Quality Notification Collaboration [page 156] Creating a Quality Notification [page 157] Viewing and Editing a Quality Notification [page 163] Reporting the Same Quality Notification Defect for Multiple Batches or Parts [page 164] Configuring Quality Collaboration Notifications [page 165] Uploading Certificates When Using the Advance Ship Notice Upload File [page 165] Related Information Quality Notification Report [page 234] 154 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues Parts of a Quality Notification A supplier uses a quality notification to provide a buyer with detailed information about an item and the quality concern to report. Each quality notification can have the following tabs: Tab Description Details Provides basic details about the quality notification. The tab includes the following sections: • • • • • Customer and part Notification detail Problem description Return information Required tasks – A task describes the planning and organizational aspect within a notification. Using tasks, you can plan the way in which various people work together to process the notification and perform the activities within a specified period of time. You can enter multiple tasks for the notification header and for individual defects.  Note You can no longer edit a task after a buyer marks it as Closed. • Activity log – An activity describes the action performed within the framework of a notification. It documents an activity that someone has performed in the process of solving a notification problem. You can enter multiple activities for the notification header and for individual defects. Defects Contains defect item detail for the quality notification. You can have multiple defects per quality notification, and each defect must have a cause, and optionally can have tasks and activities. You can use the Reference Object section to apply a defect to multiple parts or batches. Partner info Contains From, To, Bill to, and Deliver to information. History Contains the history of changes to the quality notification. The history is empty until the quality notification is published. Quality Notification Status Values A quality notification goes through multiple status values during its lifecycle. The following are the possible status values for a quality notification: • • • • Draft New (default) In-process Completed Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 155 • Closed – Tasks with this status can no longer be edited. Restrictions for Quality Notifications • If a change order is submitted that changes the original purchase order, any in-process quality notifications associated with the original order are not affected. • SAP Business Network does not support multitier quality notifications. Therefore, quality notifications are not copied to tier-two suppliers or lower-tier suppliers in a multitier supply chain. • When a buyer sets the Allow suppliers to send a ship notice for a material in an open quality notification with no purchase order reference, only after the quality notification is closed or the buyer has accepted the quality inspection for the purchase order rule, you cannot create a ship notice for a purchase order with a faulty material that is referenced in a quality notification. Blocked purchase orders become unblocked when one of the following occurs: • • The buyer accepts a quality inspection for the specific purchase order. The buyer closes the quality notification that caused the ship notice blocking. All corresponding purchase orders are unblocked. However, if the buyer also set the Allow suppliers to send ship notices only after receiving acceptance of inspection results rule, until the buyer accepts the inspection results, you cannot send ship notices for goods that require that inspection. Workflows for Quality Notification Collaboration Quality notifications can be created by buyers or suppliers, with a different workflow for each. Buyer-Initiated Quality Notification After Problem Found During Goods Inspection 1. The buyer submits a purchase order to the supplier. 2. The supplier confirms the order. 3. The supplier produces the goods, ships them to the buyer, and sends a ship notice. 4. The buyer receives the goods, sends a goods receipt, and inspects the goods. 5. The buyer discovers issues with the goods, creates a quality notification in their ERP and sends it to SAP Business Network. The buyer returns the defective goods. 6. The supplier processes the quality notification, eventually resolving the defect. 7. The supplier produces the replacement goods, ships them to the buyer, and sends another ship notice. 8. The buyer receives the replacement goods, sends a goods receipt, and inspects the goods again. 9. The buyer sends confirmation of the quality notification. 10. The supplier closes the quality notification. 156 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues Supplier-Initiated Deviation Request 1. The buyer submits purchase order to a component supplier to ship goods to a contract manufacturer. 2. The component supplier confirms the order, ships the goods, and sends a ship notice to the buyer. 3. The contract manufacturer inspects the goods, recording defects during production or wrong components from the component supplier. 4. For any wrong components or components with defects, the contract manufacturer creates a quality notification in SAP Business Network, and sends it to the buyer. 5. The buyer reviews the quality notification in SAP Business Network or in their ERP. 6. Upon the quality manager's approval, the buyer creates a quality deviation in their ERP system and submits it to SAP Business Network, where it is routed to the component supplier. Creating a Quality Notification You can create a quality notification to report a problem with an item on a purchase order or ship notice. Procedure 1. To create a quality notification, do one of the following: • Choose Orders Orders and Releases Items to Confirm or Orders Orders and Releases Items to Ship . Then select a single item and click Create quality notification. • • Choose Quality Notification , and then click Create quality notification. Choose Orders Orders and Releases . Then click the Orders and Releases tab, click an order number to open it, and click Create Quality Notification.  Note A quality notification applies to one line item only. It can't apply to multiple items. 2. If you started the quality notification from a purchase order, a wizard page appears. Select a line item, and then click Create.  Note Skip this step if you started the quality notification from other pages. 3. In the Details tab, enter quality notification details. Provide at least the Customer, Title, Quality notification type, Supplier deviation no., and Priority, and also other fields that are required by the buyer’s rules. 4. If the buyer has a multi-ERP environment, the Customer routing identifier field appears. If so, select a system ID from a list to route the quality notification to one of the customer’s end points. 5. In the Customer and part section, complete the following fields: Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 157 Option Description Customer location Required. Customer location ID. Customer part no. Required. Customer part number. Customer batch Customer batch ID. Supplier part no. Supplier part number. Supplier batch Supplier batch ID. Purchase order no. Related purchase order number. Purchase order line item no. Corresponding purchase-order line item number. Ship notice no. Related ship notice number. Ship notice line item no. Corresponding ship-notice line item number. Serial no. Optional serial number for the part. Revision level Revision level. (varies per customer) Subcontracting component? Whether the affected part is a subcontracting component. 6. Optionally in the Problem description section, do any of the following: • • • Choose a Reason code and enter a description. Click Upload a file to attach a file. Under Add links to existing files on the Web, click + Add another link and enter the link name (File name) and the URL (Address). Repeat to provide additional Web links.  Note A URL must meet the following criteria to be displayed as a live hyperlink in a quality notification: • • The URL uses the https protocol. The URL goes to a registered domain. These are the registered domains approved for use in SAP Business Network: • • • • irasdev.blob.core.windows.net www.box.com www.google.com www.microsoft.com Buyers can ask their Designated Support Contact to submit a request to SAP Business Network Support to add secure domains to this list. 7. Optionally, click Return information to expand the section, then complete the following fields: Option Description Return quantity Number of items returned and the item unit. Return authorization no. Return authorization number. Return date Date items were returned. 8. Optionally, click Required tasks to expand the section, then click + Add task to add one or more tasks associated with the quality notification. Then complete the following fields: 158 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues Option Description Task category Required if there’s no title. The task grouping. Task subcategory Required. The task subgrouping. Title Required if there’s no task category. The name of the task. Description Optional description of the task. Multiple descriptions are supported. Start date The planned start date for processing this task. Start time The planned start time (in military time) for processing this task. Target date The desired date for the task to be completed. Target time The desired time (specified in military time) for the task to be completed. Status Required. The task status. Possible values are New, In Process, and Complete. Processor type The type of processor. Possible values are Supplier, Customer, or Customer user. Processor ID The ID of the person or organization responsible for this task. For a supplier, you can provide either the user ID or the Ariba Network ID. Processor name The name of the person or organization responsible for this task. For a supplier, you can provide either the user name or the company name. 9. Optionally, click Activity log to expand the section, then click + Add activity to add one or more activities associated with the quality notification. Complete the following fields: Option Description Activity category Required if there’s no title. The activity grouping. Activity subcategory Required if there’s an activity category. The activity subgrouping. Title Required if there’s no activity category. The name of the activity. Description Optional description of the activity. Multiple descriptions are supported. Start date The planned start date for this activity. Start time The planned start time (in military time) for this activity. End date The planned end date for this activity. End time The planned end time (in military time) for this activity. 10. Optionally, click the Defects tab, then click the add  icon to add a known defect for the item. Then complete the following fields: Option Description Defect category Required if there’s no title. The defect grouping. Defect subcategory Required if there’s a defect category. The defect subgrouping. Number of defects The quantity of items subject to complaints or defects. Title Required if there’s no defect category. The name of the defect. Description Optional description of the defect. Multiple descriptions are supported. 11. If you added a defect, click Causes to expand the section, and click + Add cause to add at least one cause for each defect. Then complete the following fields: Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 159 Option Description Cause category Required if there’s no title. The cause grouping. Cause subcategory Required if there’s a cause category. The cause subgrouping. Title Required if there’s no cause category. The name of the cause. Description Optional description of the cause. Multiple descriptions are supported. 12. Optionally, click Additional Impacted Batches to expand the section, and then click + Add line to add one or more additional batches associated with the defect. Then complete the following fields: Option Description Customer location Customer location ID. Customer part no. Customer part number. Customer batch Customer batch ID. Supplier part no. Supplier part number. Supplier batch Supplier batch ID. 13. Optionally, click Required tasks to expand the section, and then click + Add task to add one or more tasks associated with the defect. For information about the fields, see Step 8 [page 158]. 14. Optionally, click Activity log to expand the section, and then click + Add activity to add one or more activities associated with the defect. For information about the fields, see Step 9 [page 159]. 15. Optionally, click the add  icon at the top of the page to add more defects. For each defect you add, you must also define a cause. You can also add tasks and activities for each defect. 16. Click Review to review the quality notification. 17. Do one of the following: • Click Publish to publish the quality notification. Each published version of a quality notification contains the following information about the supplier who created or updated it: first and last name, email address, and user ID. • Click Back to go back to the previous page and make any changes. Results The published quality notification is sent to the buyer. You can review the published quality notification on the Quality tab. You can also open it and click Edit to revise it. 160 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues

file://SBN/split/Supplier Guide to SAP B.content: Adding Descriptions to a Quality Notification Document Use this procedure to add descriptions to quality notifications from the user interface. Prerequisites You have a trading relationship with a buyer entitled for the quality collaboration component. Context  Caution Descriptions added to quality notification description fields should not contain sensitive information.  Remember You cannot edit a quality notification after a buyer marks it as Closed.  Tip Refer to the cXML Reference Guide (version 1.2.054 or higher) available at http://cxml.org/ for more information about the QNNotes element, which is used to define descriptions for quality notifications. Multiple descriptions are allowed in the following quality notification sections: • • • Required tasks Activity log Defects and its Causes, Required tasks, and Activity log subsections When you add an additional description to one of these quality notification sections, the new description is appended to the bottom of the description history for the section, along with a time stamp. The new description becomes part of the description history and cannot be edited. Procedure 1. From the Quality Notification page, click the link to the quality notification you want to edit. The quality notification displays. 2. Click Edit to open the quality notification for editing. 3. Navigate to the section you want to edit. 4. Click + Add a new description. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 161 A box for the new description displays. 5. Enter the new description in the box. If you decide not to add the description, click the delete ( ) icon to remove the new description box. 6. Click Publish to publish the new version of the quality notification document. 162 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues Viewing and Editing a Quality Notification You can view and edit quality notifications that you or your customers created to record and process different types of problems with goods or services. Prerequisites Your user role includes the Quality permission. Context Quality notifications are listed on the Quality Notification page. You can also open a quality notification from the Related Documents list on the Purchase Order or Ship Notice pages. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Notification . The Quality notifications page opens. 2. To search for a quality notification, expand the Search filters, enter values in the search fields, and then click Search.  Note When you choose the Exact match radio button below the Customer deviation no. or the Supplier deviation no. filter, only that filter and the Supplier filter display. 3. To open a quality notification, click its number. 4. Click Edit and update the form. For information about the fields in a quality notification, see Creating a Quality Notification [page 157].  Note You cannot edit any of the following fields after the quality notification is created: • • • • • • • Customer Quality notification type Supplier deviation no. Customer location Customer part no. Customer routing identifier – This field only appears if the buyer has a multiple-ERP environment. Supplier part no. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 163 • • • • • Purchase order no. Purchase order line item no. Ship notice no. Ship notice line item no. Subcontracting component 5. When finished, click Publish. Reporting the Same Quality Notification Defect for Multiple Batches or Parts If a defect affects other customer or supplier batches, you can reference those batch IDs in the quality notification. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Notification and then open a quality notification. 2. Click Edit. 3. Click the Defects tab. 4. Click Reference object to open it. You can also click the plus + icon to the right. 5. Click Add line. 6. Complete the following fields for other parts or batches affected by this defect: Option Description Customer location Type the first few characters of the customer location, and then choose one from the list. Customer part no. The customer part number. Customer batch The customer batch ID. Supplier part no. The supplier part number. Supplier batch. The supplier batch ID. 7. Add additional lines as necessary. 8. Click Publish. 164 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues Configuring Quality Collaboration Notifications You can configure the notifications you want to receive for quality collaboration. Choose to enable notifications for different types of documents and different events. Prerequisites • You have a trading relationship with a buyer entitled for the quality collaboration component. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Settings . The Quality Settings page opens. 2. Click Edit. 3. Choose one of the following options: • • Same rule for all customers—Applies these quality settings to all of your customers. Separate rules for each customer—Applies separate quality settings to each customer. If you choose this option, click + Add customer to specify a customer to define settings for. 4. Check the email notification options you prefer for Quality inspections, Quality notifications, and Quality reviews. 5. Click Submit. Uploading Certificates When Using the Advance Ship Notice Upload File Customers can upload certificates when using the Advance Ship Notice (ASN) upload template. • The following rule name is changed from: • • The following new tool tip is added next to the rule: • • Require suppliers to provide a quality certificate on ship notice to Allow suppliers to provide a quality certificate on ship notice Certificates are only specified as required by the cXML element CertificateInfo with the attribute isRequired=yes as part of the line item in the purchase order. In the Supplier Group Transaction Rules page, the following section is added along with the rule Allow suppliers to provide a quality certificate on ship notice: • Order Confirmation, Ship Notice and Component Receipt Attachment Rules Customers can attach Quality certificates when using the upload/download process for ASNs. This will get enabled by the rule or if the line item in the purchase order (PO) has the certificate flag (even if the rule is off). The customer will see a new column with the Attach certificates button. The count (0/N) is based only in the required Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 165 certificates, optional certificates are not considered in the count. Certificates will be displayed as mandatory in SAP Business Network, only if they were specified as required in the certificate flag in the line item in the purchase order by the cXML element CertificateInfo with the attribute isRequired=yes.  Note Files in the Excel format can only be used to upload certificates. If the Certificate tag is not sent in the PO line-item and the Allow suppliers to provide a quality certificate on ship notice rule is enabled, you can optionally attach certificates. Once the Attach certificates button is clicked, the Quality certificates pop up dialog is opened: The following seven columns are introduced: • • • • • • • 166 Ship notice Order Order line no. Customer part no. Supplier part no. File size Attach Files can be used to attach the certificates PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues Quality Review Collaboration Suppliers can exchange information with buyers to evaluate and address quality issues. With the quality review collaboration feature, SAP Business Network for Supply Chain enables suppliers to do the following: Batch records Collaborate on batch-record reviews, finalize batch record information, and allow quality releases of product bulk materials. The supplier can initiate the batch record process after the quality inspection process is completed for the final batch documentation. Complaints Collaborate on product complaint investigations from the buyer’s customer. Buyers usually receive complaints through a third-party system but reports them to suppliers and CMOs through quality reviews. Change requests Collaborate on material changes, processes, or equipment. General Collaborate on quality process-type definitions. You can create or update quality review requests by choosing Quality Review . Quality reviews can reference purchase orders, ship notices, quality inspections, and quality notifications. Quality Review Request Statuses SAP Business Network for Supply Chain displays one of the following statuses for each quality review request: New The default status, set automatically when the quality review request is created. In process Indicates that the other party responded to the quality review request. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 167  Note Either the supplier or the buyer can change Complete to In process. Complete The status selected by the supplier to indicate a review has been completed. Only the supplier can choose this status. Close The status selected by the buyer when a review has been closed. Only the buyer can set this status.  Note A closed review can no longer be edited. Creating a Quality Review Request Use this procedure to request quality reviews for goods. Prerequisites The buyer system is enabled for the quality collaboration component. Context Suppliers can report quality issues that need investigation and resolution. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Review . The Quality review page opens. 2. Click Create Quality Review. The Create quality review page opens. 3. Fill in the Subject field, and choose details as desired from the drop-down menus. 4. Write your comment in the Comment field. Click Submit. 168 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues Configuring Quality Collaboration Notifications Use this procedure to define settings for quality documents. Prerequisites • • Buyers: Your account is entitled for the quality collaboration component. Suppliers: You have a trading relationship with a buyer entitled for the quality collaboration component. Context Buyers and suppliers can enable notifications for different types of documents and different events. Procedure 1. Choose Quality Settings . The Quality Settings page opens. 2. Click Edit. 3. If you are a supplier, choose one of the following options: • • Same rule for all customers – Applies these quality settings to all of your customers. Separate rules for each customer – Applies separate quality settings to each customer. If you choose this option, click Add customer to specify a customer to define settings for. For quality reviews only, when a quality review event occurs, all users who have their settings configured to receive quality review notifications from you for that type of event will receive them. 4. If you are a buyer, choose one of the following options: • • Same rule for all suppliers – Applies these quality settings to all of your suppliers. Separate rules for each supplier – Applies separate quality settings to each supplier. If you choose this option, click Add supplier to specify a supplier to define settings for. For quality reviews only, when a quality review event occurs, all users who have their settings configured to receive quality review notifications from you for that type of event will receive them. 5. Check the email notification options you prefer for Quality inspections, Quality notifications, and Quality reviews. 6. Click Submit. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues PUBLIC 169 Responding to a Quality Review Notification by Email Buyers and suppliers can post a comment through email or attach files to the associated quality review. Prerequisites • • • Buyers: Your account is entitled for the quality collaboration component. Suppliers: You have a trading relationship with a buyer entitled for the quality collaboration component. Buyers and suppliers: Your SAP Business Network account is configured to receive quality review notifications. See Configuring Quality Collaboration Notifications.  Restriction • You can’t reformat or delete parts of the original quality review notification message. Otherwise, SAP Business Network can’t process the message. • • You can’t change the To address in the reply email. However, you can add recipients. • • • In your reply email, don’t enter line breaks or exceed 1024 characters. SAP Business Network removes line breaks and excess characters before posting your comment to the quality review. Files you attach to the reply email can’t exceed 1 GB in total size. When the quality review status changes to Closed, no more notification responses can be received. You can send a reply to a quality review notification only within 30 days of receiving it. After 30 days, replies to the quality review notification won’t be posted, though you can still edit the quality review in the SAP Business Network portal. Procedure 1. Open the email notification in your email client. 2. Create a reply to the email, observing the above restrictions. 3. Send the email. The text from your email reply is encrypted for transport and is posted as a comment to the quality review. Any files you attached to the email are automatically attached to the quality review. 170 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Quality Issues

file://SBN/split/Supplier Guide to SAP B.content: Customized Documents Your buyers can customize the form and behavior of certain SAP Business Network pages and download files that you use. Your buyers can create custom attributes and include these attributes in customization projects for the Upload/ Download Order Confirmation and Ship Notice Excel templates and for the Items to Confirm, Orders, and Items to Ship Workbench tiles. Custom attributes help buyers communicate information with their suppliers that is not already included on standard SAP Business Network pages, Upload/Download job types, and Workbench tiles. For more information about customized Upload/Download Excel templates, see Working with a Customized Excel Template for Upload/Download [page 171]. For more information about customized Items to Confirm, Orders, and Items to Ship Workbench tiles, see Working with a Customized Workbench Tile [page 172]. Working with a Customized Excel Template for Upload/Download Your buyers can customize an Excel template for Upload/Download. Context When a buyer assigns you a customized template for Upload/Download, and you run that type of job, the downloaded Excel file shows the buyer's customizations of the template. These customizations might include a different order of the columns, additional columns that are not in the standard template, or other changes. Procedure 1. To view the customized template, go to Quick links Upload/Download Jobs and click Create. The Create/Edit Job popup opens. 2. Create a job, run the job, and download the generated Excel template. For details, see Creating an Upload/Download Job and Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload. 3. View the Excel template download to see the customized columns in the Excel spreadsheet. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Customized Documents PUBLIC 171 Working with a Customized Workbench Tile Your buyers can customize some Workbench tiles to add additional columns and filters. Procedure 1. Click Workbench, and then click the Items to Confirm, Orders, or Items to Ship tile. The list page for the tile displays. 2. Optional: Filter the results. Use any of the available filters to filter the results. 3. Optional: Configure the display listing. You can change which columns display in the table. Click the table ( ) icon to view the available columns and select the ones you want to display in the table. 172 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Customized Documents Upload/Download This section provides topics describing how to create custom transaction queries and generate spreadsheets to download, modify, and upload information updates to SAP Business Network. Upload/Download Templates [page 173] Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 218] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 219] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 221] Upload/Download Templates This section describes the search criteria and other information about each Upload/Download job template. Build priority Template for Upload/Download [page 173] Consignment Template for Upload/Download [page 175] Forecast Template for Upload/Download [page 177] Inventory Template for Upload/Download [page 179] Manufacturing Planning Visibility Templates [page 182] Manufacturing Visibility Template for Upload/Download [page 190] Order Change Requests Template for Upload/Download [page 192] Order Confirmation Template for Upload/Download [page 197] Quality Inspection Results Template for Upload/Download [page 203] Quality Notification Template for Upload/Download [page 206] Replenishment Template for Upload/Download [page 206] Ship Notice Template for Upload/Download [page 210] Block and closed line-item status during Ship Notice creation [page 213] Build priority Template for Upload/Download You can generate an Upload/Download report in Excel format with forecast demand and purchase order quantities.  Note The path to the Upload/Download feature is as follows: Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Upload/Download PUBLIC 173 • • For buyers – For suppliers – Quick links … Upload/Download Upload/Download The Build priority template file contains a row for each prioritized part, with the dates of the period in which the part is needed. The values for the first and last days of the week populate the Delivery Start date, Delivery End date, Shipment Start date, and Shipment End date fields for purchase order priorities, relative to the Requested Delivery date and Requested Ship date. Prerequisites To access this job type from the Upload/Download you must have one of the following permissions: • • • • Jobs and Upload/Download Downloads tabs, Inbox and Order Access Outbox Access Forecast Visibility Planning Collaboration Visibility To access this job type from the permissions: • • Upload/Download Uploads tab, you must have one of the following Inbox and Order Access Outbox Access  Note You cannot access the Uploads tab with only the Forecast Visibility or Planning Collaboration Visibility permission. Restrictions The Build priority template does not support: • • File uploads of the Build priority download file Reconfiguration of the download file layout or format Build priority Template Criteria The • • 174 Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Build priority job type: Name – (Required) The name to give the job. Type – (Required) Choose Build priority. PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Upload/Download • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • • Customer – (Required, supplier view only) The name of the buyer whose data you want in the report. Supplier – (Required) The name of the supplier whose data you want in the report. Demand type - Values are All (default), Forecast, or Purchase Order. Date type - Values are Need By or Ship By. Start date End date Location Supplier part number Buyer part number Product family Product sub-family Line of business Program code Planner code Part category Part type Manufacturing type Exclude zero forecast - Only for All or Forecast demand types. Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 218] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 219] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 221] Consignment Template for Upload/Download You can generate an Upload/Download report in Excel format to help reconcile your consignment records.  Note The path to the Upload/Download feature is as follows: • • For buyers – For suppliers – Quick links … Upload/Download Upload/Download This template consolidates goods receipt and consignment movement data for a specified supplier or buyer. When a line item in a goods receipt and a consignment movement share the same consignment tracking ID, the Consignment template retrieves the related purchase order, line item, and ship notice numbers. If no tracking ID is provided, the template attempts to find line items with other matching data, such as purchase order number and ship notice number. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Upload/Download PUBLIC 175 The Consignment template also shows stock-on-hand and consignment stock values. These values are derived from cXML ProductActivityMessage documents with a matching buyer part number, supplier part number, location, and process type, and which contain ConsignmentInventory or ConsignmentMovement elements with the processType attribute set to Consignment.  Restriction The stock-on-hand value is only populated if the user has the Planning collaboration entitlement or the Inventory collaboration entitlement. A Consignment job can generate data for up to the last 60 days. A maximum of 60,000 consignment report records can be downloaded. Reports with more than 60,000 records are truncated when downloaded. The Consignment job retrieves data for a single specified supplier or customer. Records in the download file are in alphanumeric order by a combination of Customer Part No., Supplier Part No., and Location values, in that order. Blank fields are sorted last. Each set of sorted records is then grouped by document type: goods receipt (Consignment In) and consignment movement (Consignment Out). Within each set of related goods receipt and consignment movement records, color highlighting identifies rows with the following calculations: • • Blue highlighting—The total quantity of goods receipts or consignment movements for the record set. Yellow highlighting—The most recent value of consignment inventory on hand for the record set. Consignment Template Criteria The • • • • • • • • • Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Consignment job type: Name – (Required) The name to give the job. Type – (Required) Choose Consignment. Customer – (Required, supplier view only) The name of the buyer whose data you want in the report. Supplier – (Required, buyer view only) The name of the supplier whose data you want in the report. Start date End date Supplier part number Buyer part number Location Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 218] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 219] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 221] 176 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Upload/Download Forecast Template for Upload/Download You can generate an Upload/Download file in Excel format for forecast data.  Note The path to the Upload/Download feature is as follows: • For both buyers and suppliers: Click the  Create icon and choose Upload/Download Jobs. To edit data in the Forecast spreadsheet, click the Aggregated - Supply Commit sheet if it exists, or click the Product sheet. Editable rows are highlighted, and also have the Forecast commit value in the Key figures column. Add values to the cells that are under date headings. If a buyer sets a commit freeze horizon (by setting Forecast commit lock horizon, in days to a value other than zero), a Forecast job downloaded by a supplier from the Upload/Download Downloads tab applies the freeze to any time-series view the download uses: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly. A supplier is prevented from editing commit key figures for any time series within the locked period. You can create Forecast type jobs using any time series granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly). When the buyer sets the preferred time series granularity to All, you can edit and commit Excel files in any time series granularity. However, when the buyer sets a specific preferred time series granularity, you can only edit and commit Excel files using that granularity. Suppliers can upload Forecast type jobs from the Upload/Download Jobs series granularity (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly). Uploads tab using any time If planning items contain attributes, attribute data is included when you download these items from the Download Jobs Download Uploads tab. Upload/Download Uploads tab if they have any of the Restrictions The Excel file cannot be uploaded if the value in the part number field is entered as "0". When the template Excel file is uploaded, it is converted to one or more cXML documents in the backend. Each cXML document is limited to 500 items. If the template Excel file has more than 500 items, multiple cXML documents are created. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Upload/Download PUBLIC 177 Forecast Template Criteria The Upload/Download Jobs page provides the following search criteria for the Forecast job type:  Note When a supplier selects the Forecast job type, the Prepopulate Commit time series quantities with Forecast quantities checkbox also appears. Select this checkbox to automatically copy the values from Order forecast to Forecast commit. Multiple values can be selected for most of the fields. • • • • Name: (Required) The name to give the job. • • • • • • • • • • • • Supplier part number • • Type: (Required) Choose Forecast. Customer: (Required, supplier view only) The name of the customer whose data you want in the report. Supplier: The name of the supplier whose data you want in the report. To retrieve information for all suppliers, leave this field blank. Buyer part number Product family Product sub-family Location Program code Planner code Part category Part type Manufacturing type Line of business Time bucket – (Required) Values are Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly. The following table shows the maximum date range for each time bucket. Time Bucket Maximum Date Range Daily 1825 days Weekly 260 weeks Monthly 60 months Quarterly 20 quarters Yearly 10 years Start: The starting date in the time window. You can define the starting date in the following ways: • • Current: The starting date is the current date for the time bucket. • Custom: The starting date is a custom date. An additional field displays for you to enter a custom date. End: The ending date in the time window. You can define the ending date in the following ways: • 178 Previous: The starting date is a previous date in the time bucket. An additional field displays for you to enter a numeric value. After: An additional field displays for you to enter a numeric value. The ending date is the date after the number of time buckets specified by this value. For example, if the Time bucket is Daily, and you enter 250 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Upload/Download for the value, the ending date is after 250 days. If the time bucket is Weekly, and you enter 26 for the value, the ending date is after 26 weeks. • Custom: The ending date is a custom date. An additional field displays for you to enter a custom date. • • Download planning item attributes on all rows: Check to populate all cells in the Excel file with data. • • • Buyer last modified: Date field. Only download planning records with positive or negative time series data: Check to only include planning records that have at least one positive or negative value in the specified time window. Supplier last modified: Date field. Customer view: Choose All Views or choose a specific view. Downloaded Excel files contain the key figures and attributes included in the view. Buyers, however, must have one of the following permissions to access this job type from the Upload/Download • • Inbox and Order Access Uploads tab: Outbox Access  Note Buyers cannot access the Uploads tab with only the Forecast Visibility or Planning Collaboration Visibility permission. Time Bucket Maximum Date Range Daily 1825 days Weekly 260 weeks Monthly 60 months Quarterly 20 quarters Yearly 10 years Start – The starting date in the time window. You can define the starting date in the following ways: • • • • Current – The starting date is the current date for the time bucket. Previous – The starting date is a previous date in the time bucket. An additional field displays for you to enter a numeric value. Custom – The starting date is a custom date. An additional field displays for you to enter a custom date. End – The ending date in the time window. You can define the ending date in the following ways: • After – An additional field displays for you to enter a numeric value. The ending date is the date after the number of time buckets specified by this value. For example, if the Time bucket is Daily, and you enter 250 for the value, the ending date is after 250 days. If the time bucket is Weekly, and you enter 26 for the value, the ending date is after 26 weeks. • Custom – The ending date is a custom date. An additional field displays for you to enter a custom date. • • Download planning item attributes on all rows – Check to populate all cells in the Excel file with data. • • • Buyer last modified – Date field. • Only download planning records with positive or negative time series data – Check to only include planning records that have at least one positive or negative value in the specified time window. Supplier last modified – Date field. Customer view – Choose All Views or choose a specific view. Downloaded Excel files contain the key figures and attributes included in the view. Sort by projected stock status – When this checkbox is checked, the records in the downloaded Excel file display in priority order based on their stock situation. The planning records in the planning horizon (defined by the Replenishment horizon, in number of days setting) are first sorted by their stock status severity using the following order: 1. Out of Stock. 2. Below Minimum (no Out of Stock). 3. Above Maximum (no Out of Stock or Below Minimum). 4. On Track. The planning records are then sorted within each of these four groups based on the date when the stock problem will occur. Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Upload/Download PUBLIC 181  Note Planning records not occurring in the defined planning horizon appear in the Excel file after the ones in the planning horizon even when their stock status severity is Out of Stock, Below Minimum, or Above Maximum. Related Information Creating an Upload/Download Job [page 218] Running an Upload/Download Job and Making Data Changes to Upload [page 219] Deleting Download Files Created by an Upload/Download Job [page 221] Manufacturing Planning Visibility Templates Suppliers can share contract manufacturing data with their OEMs. Typically, in contract manufacturing, Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) maintain only critical bills of material (BOMs) while their contract manufacturers maintain exhaustive lists of components. With the Manufacturing Planning Visibility templates, suppliers can search for manufacturing planning visibility information by document type: • • • Manufacturing Planning Visibility: Inventory template - Inventory snapshots Manufacturing Planning Visibility: Supplier Data template - Supplier planning data Manufacturing Planning Visibility: All template - Combination of inventory snapshots and supplier planning data Suppliers can use a Manufacturing Planning Visibility template to upload their information to the OEMs. Information uploaded in a Manufacturing Planning Visibility template routes a product replenishment message to the buyer's default end point or default logical system.  Note Suppliers who need to deliver a Manufacturing Planning Visibility upload to a different buyer ERP system can provide the target system's ID in the System ID field of the template. This field is available in all forms of the template. Leave the field empty to use the buyer default system. After a supplier uploads a Manufacturing Planning Visibility template, SAP Business Network generates a corresponding cXML document and triggers a transaction based on the cXML document. Manufacturing visibility Settings To configure the Manufacturing visibility settings, buyers must be enabled for one of the following: 182 PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Upload/Download • • • The inventory collaboration component. The forecast collaboration component. SAP Business Network Planning Collaboration, which does not also require SAP Business Network for Supply Chain. Buyers can set the two settings in the Manufacturing visibility section of the suppliers Planning Settings Assign page: 1. Planning horizon, in number of days – This setting controls the number of days in the future that suppliers can send Manufacturing Planning Visibility planning records. The default value is 180 days. 2. Must match Customer part ID and Customer location with existing records – When this setting is set to Yes, all incoming Manufacturing Planning Visibility planning items are validated to make sure they match at least one existing planning item with an active status sent by the buyer for a planning process. The validation check occurs when suppliers do one of the following: • Upload Manufacturing Planning Visibility planning items from the Uploads • ... Upload/Download tab. Send cXML product replenishment messages for Manufacturing Planning Visibility planning items. Prerequisites Suppliers with one of the following permissions can access the Manufacturing Planning Visibility templates from the • • • … Upload/Download Uploads tab: Inbox and Order Access Outbox Access Planning Collaboration Visibility Restrictions When the template Excel file is uploaded, it is converted to one or more cXML documents in the backend. The cXML documents for Manufacturing Planning Visibility: All and Manufacturing Planning Visibility: Supplier Data uploads are limited to 200 items. If the template Excel file has more than 200 items, multiple cXML documents are created. For Manufacturing Planning Visibility: Inventory Excel files, the limit is 1000 items; if the Excel file has more than 1000 items, multiple cXML documents are created. Workflow for Manufacturing Planning Visibility Upload [page 184] Updating an Upload/Download Template for Manufacturing Planning Visibility [page 184] Fields for Manufacturing Planning Visibility [page 185] Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Upload/Download PUBLIC 183 Workflow for Manufacturing Planning Visibility Upload The end-to-end workflow for the Manufacturing Planning Visibility template starts with a supplier downloading the desired template, and ends with the buyer using the information provided by the supplier. 1. The supplier downloads the Manufacturing Planning Visibility template designed for one of the manufacturing planning visibility types. 2. The supplier enters data into the file based on the template selected. 3. After the supplier uploads the Manufacturing Planning Visibility template and it has been successfully processed, SAP Business Network generates a corresponding cXML file and triggers a transaction based on the cXML file. 4. The buyer can use the information provided by the Manufacturing Planning Visibility template to drive the planning and supply of transaction elements to contract manufacturers. Updating an Upload/Download Template for Manufacturing Planning Visibility Suppliers can download a predesigned spreadsheet to send their information for inventory, supplier data, or both. Prerequisites • Have one of the following permissions to access the Manufacturing Planning Visibility templates from the … • • • • Upload/Download Uploads tab: Inbox and Order Access Outbox Access Planning Collaboration Visibility Review field requirements and guidelines in Fields for Manufacturing Planning Visibility [page 185]. Procedure 1. Go to … Upload/Download Uploads . 2. Click Upload at the end of the page. The Upload File page opens. 3. Leave blank the Name and Type fields. 4. Click Download templates. Respond to any prompt to save or open the templates.zip file. The expanded zip file contains the following template files: • • • 184 Manufacturing_Planning_Visibility_Inventory_data.csv Manufacturing_Planning_Visibility_Supplier_Data_data.csv Manufacturing_Planning_Visibility_All_data.csv PUBLIC Supplier Guide to SAP Business Network for Supply Chain Upload/Download • • • Manufacturing_Planning_Visibility_Inventory_semicolon_data.csv Manufacturing_Planning_Visibility_Supplier_Data_semicolon_data.csv Manufacturing_Planning_Visibility_All_semicolon_data.csv 5. Click Close to exit the Upload File popup. 6. Open the desired template with your preferred editor. 7. Enter values as desired. Make sure that required columns have values for each entry. Manufacturing Planning Visibility templates support all alphanumeric characters, including any special language characters used by a particular locale. The templates also support the following special characters: !@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}\/|;:,.'"<>? 8. Go to … Upload/Download Uploads and click Upload at the end of the page. The Upload File popup opens. 9. Upload your file. a. Choose the name of your template from the Type dropdown. b. Enter the name to give your upload in the Name field. c. Click Browse to choose the file to upload. d. Click Upload. The Upload File closes. Click Refresh Status to update the processing status.  Note If Completed With Errors displays in the Status column for your upload, click the download icon  in the Log column to open the log file. The log provides operation status for each confirmed purchase order, including the order confirmation number that was used. The log lists successful confirmation messages first, followed by failure messages.
